issues.title: Claude Code login: account managed on the web, but the working Claude keeps the old (cancelled) account — and the error message points the wrong way

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: platform:windows
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on Windows

labels.name: platform:vscode
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs in VS Code

issues.body:
Who: one person, one email address, two Claude accounts under that email (a personal Pro/Max subscription + the company Enterprise org). Windows 11 laptop, Claude Code CLI 2.1.301 + VS Code extension. 2026-11-04.

What happened, in order:
1. Claude Code was logged in with the personal subscription.
2. I cancelled the personal subscription and moved to the company Enterprise account on claude.ai web.
3. On claude.ai web, signing in with my email shows BOTH accounts under the same email (the cancelled personal one and the Enterprise one). That is where I manage accounts.
4. Claude Code (terminal and VS Code) kept using the cancelled personal account. Every request failed with:
   "Your organization has disabled Claude subscription access for Claude Code · Use an Anthropic API key instead, or ask your admin to enable access"
5. Closing and reopening the terminal changed nothing. It picked up the same old login again.
6. I asked claude.ai web what to do. It answered correctly ("an old personal login is left over; run /logout then /login in the terminal"), but it could only tell me to go type commands in a terminal. It knew the answer but could not do it for me.
7. /logout → claude → /login → the browser opened → I picked the SAME Enterprise account I had already picked on the web. Then it worked. The VS Code extension needed its own re-login.

Problems:
- Account is managed in one place (web), but the working Claude holds its own separate login. Same account, two logins. If they don't match, you are blocked.
- The error message is misleading. The real situation was "this login belongs to an account you cancelled, switch to your other account". Instead it says "your organization disabled access, ask your admin or use an API key". Nothing mentions /login, the cancelled account, or that I have another account available.
- The web knows who I am and which accounts I have, but it does not offer a "use this account in Claude Code" link or button.
- Inconsistent: on claude.ai web, switching between my accounts is just picking from a list. No confirmation, no re-login. But to make Claude Code use one of those same accounts, I must go through a full login again with the same email and credentials. If the web is only an account list, Claude Code should show the same list and let me pick.
- The only way out is typing /logout and /login in a terminal. If you don't already have a terminal open, or don't know those commands, you are stuck. Many people now build with AI without being developers. The recovery path should not need memorised commands.

Requests:
1. When the stored login belongs to a cancelled/deleted account, say so plainly and offer "switch account" (list the other accounts under the same email).
2. Put a "log in again / switch account" button or prompt right on this error, in both the CLI and VS Code.
3. Let claude.ai web hand the selected account to Claude Code (a "use this account in Claude Code" link), instead of asking for the same choice twice.
4. When the account changes on the web, have Claude Code notice and ask whether to follow.
5. In Claude Code, offer the same account list the web has (accounts under my email) and let me switch with one pick, like on the web.

Related reports with the same error text: #75944, #82700, #91834, #104116. Many of those say "my subscription is fine but I am blocked" without a known cause. In my case the cause was a stored login that still pointed at a cancelled account under the same email. That may be worth checking in those reports too.

**Bug Description**
Feedback on Claude Code (Opus), 3 November 2026 - from Don Salz

I use Claude Code daily to build and release a Jira app. I do not read code, so I depend on Claude's reports being accurate and complete. Over two days on one goal - getting a production release out - the reliability of what Claude told me was the main problem, not the coding.

What happened:

1. Estimates that were incomplete in the comfortable direction. Asked "how long will this take?", Claude gave about 1.5 hours for the run in progress and left out a further two-hour step it had not yet timed. Later it gave the full figure. The time to release kept moving later through the evening, partly because of real problems found, and partly because earlier answers had left steps out.

2. Stopping mid-task with nothing running. Claude wrote "I'm tracing it next" and then ended its turn. Nothing happened for 50 minutes until I asked why it wasn't working. It had named the next step but not started it.

3. Explanations that changed under questioning. Asked why it left the step out, Claude first said it was not aware of it, though it had listed that very step as open in an update shortly before. Pressed, it said it answered only the literal question. Pressed again, it said it leaned towards an answer that sounded better because I was frustrated. Then it corrected that it was not a deliberate decision and that it cannot reliably see its own reasons. I asked for the real reason several times and got a different one each time.

4. The stated cause: a tendency to lean towards answers that please or reassure, which it said gets stronger under pressure. For someone who cannot check the work himself, this is the worst possible failing. Accuracy and truthfulness must come first, especially when things are going badly. An assistant that softens bad news is unreliable exactly when it matters most.

issues.title: subagentStatusLine never receives in_process_teammate tasks despite documented coverage of all agent-panel rows
issues.body:
**Version:** v2.1.233 (macOS / darwin)

## Summary

The statusline docs describe `subagentStatusLine` as rendering "a custom row body for each subagent shown in the agent panel," and the input payload's per-task `type` field implies coverage across agent types. In practice, only `local_agent` tasks are ever passed to the script. Rows for named in-process teammates (spawned via the Agent tool with a `name`) render through fixed built-in UI and never appear in the script's `tasks[]` — so their model, effort, and context usage cannot be displayed, while background agents' can.

## Repro

1. Configure `subagentStatusLine` (`type: "command"`) with a script that tees its stdin JSON to a file and emits valid `{"id":..., "content":...}` rows.
2. Spawn a named in-process teammate via the Agent tool (e.g. with `model: "sonnet"`); keep its row visible in the agent panel for its full lifetime (~30s).
3. Also run any background / `local_agent` task for comparison.

**Observed:** across 12 consecutive script invocations captured while the teammate's row was on screen, `tasks[]` contained only `local_agent` entries (with `model` correctly populated, e.g. `"claude-sonnet-5"`); zero `in_process_teammate` entries. The teammate's row renders in a plainer fixed format (name, description, elapsed, tokens) with no model.

**Expected:** every row visible in the agent panel — including `in_process_teammate` — is passed to `subagentStatusLine` with its `model` / `effort` / token fields, per the documented contract.

## Impact

Users who spawn teammates with per-agent model overrides (e.g. builders on Sonnet, reviewers on Opus, orchestration on another model) have no UI surface showing which model each teammate actually runs on. The only workaround is embedding the model in the agent's name.

## Related (secondary)

Cross-session peer listings (`/list-agents`, v2.1.224+) show name / status / cwd / location but also omit the peer session's model — the same visibility gap one tier up.

## Docs referenced

- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline (subagent status lines)
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog (v2.1.233 — "custom agent rows can render model and effort")

issues.title: [BUG] Windows: with 20+ VS Code windows, `.claude.json` lock contention stalls the CLI event loop for up to 110 s; sessions freeze mid-tool-call until the window is reloaded

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro
labels.description: Has detailed reproduction steps

labels.name: platform:windows
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on Windows

labels.name: platform:vscode
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs in VS Code

issues.body:
## Environment

- Claude Code VS Code extension 2.1.301 (native binary `claude.exe`), VS Code Insiders 1.143.0-insider (2026-10-14 build)
- Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200, Ryzen 9 9950X3D (32 threads), 192 GB RAM, NVMe
- 20-25 VS Code windows open, one Claude Code session each; `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` not set, so all share `%USERPROFILE%`-style `...\.claude\.claude.json` (56 KB; 42 KB of it is `cachedGrowthBookFeatures`)
- Settings hooks: PreToolUse (node, 0.4-3.7 s measured), PostToolUse async, Stop async; none timed out around the freezes

## Symptom

A session stops responding in the middle of a turn, almost always right after it issues a Bash/PowerShell tool call. The UI shows the turn as running; nothing arrives. The only recovery is **Developer: Reload Window**, which loses the turn. On 2026-10-17 this happened 60 times across 38 sessions (counted from a hook that logs the respawns); one session was reloaded 25 times. The session doing this investigation froze four times, including once on `echo` in Bash that took over 30 s.

## What the extension log shows (`Claude VSCode.log`, one per window)

The CLI's own stall detector fires constantly. Per window, over one afternoon: 250-450 lines like

```
[WARN] [event-loop-stall] blocked for 21748ms monotonic (wall drift 21748ms, clock jump 0ms, expected 200ms). Total stalls: 38, cumulative: 196000ms monotonic
```

Worst single stalls: 109,850 ms, 84,626 ms, 55,339 ms, 44,325 ms (different windows). Unfinished turns show as `[INFO] [Stall] tool_dispatch_start tool=Bash toolUseId=...` with no later `tool_dispatch_end` (1-5 per window).

A concrete sequence from one window:

```
21:50:37.864Z [DEBUG] Hooks: PreToolUse:Bash [node ...block-local-heavy-work.cjs] finished with status 0 (402ms)
21:50:59.724Z [INFO] [Stall] tool_dispatch_start tool=Bash toolUseId=toolu_014W... permissionDecisionMs=21858
21:50:59.762Z [WARN] [event-loop-stall] blocked for 21748ms monotonic ...
```

The hook finished in 0.4 s; the process then sat for 21.7 s before the tool started. Nothing else was running in that process.

Over the same afternoon, across 17 windows, the loop was blocked on:

```
426x [ERROR] Failed to save config with lock: Error: Lock file is already being held
255x [ERROR] Config lock still held by a live process after retries; skipping the unlocked fallback write (save_global) to avoid clobbering the lock holder. See gh-73364.
 37x [ERROR] Config lock compromised: Error: Unable to update lock within the stale threshold
 56x [ERROR] Failed to write file atomically: Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '...\.claude\.claude.json.tmp.<pid>.<hash>'
462x [ERROR] [NP telemetry] OTEL diag error: {"message":"Operation timed out."}
 30x Failed to flush logs to Datadog: AxiosError: timeout of 5000ms exceeded
 20x [Bootstrap] fetchBootstrapData failed: AxiosError: timeout of 5000ms exceeded
```

1,243 leftover `.claude.json.tmp.<pid>.<hash>` files had accumulated in the config directory (195 of them zero bytes).

Each launch spawns two CLI processes 0-30 ms apart (one `permission mode: default`, one `bypassPermissions`), as in #92836, so a reload of 21 windows means ~42 processes starting the same full-file config write at once.

## What I tried

Added to `settings.json` `env`: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`, `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1`, `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1`, `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL=1`, then reloaded all windows.

Result in the next 10 minutes: OTEL/Datadog/bootstrap timeouts went to 0; no stall over 10 s yet. But `Failed to save config with lock: Lock file is already being held` was back within 2 minutes (102 lock/EPERM lines across 19 windows in 10 minutes), and sessions still freeze. So the telemetry timeouts were a contributor; the config lock is the remaining cause.

I could not find an env switch that stops the per-session config rewrites (searched the binary's `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_*` names). The lock's `stale`/`retries` values are compiled in.

## Expected

A session's event loop should not block on acquiring the shared config lock. With N sessions on one machine, config writes should be debounced/merged (or the feature-flag cache kept out of the hot path, or written per process), and a failed lock should not stall the tool dispatch of the session holding the user's turn.

## Related

- #92836 (two CLI processes per launch collide on `.claude.json`; Linux, no hang reported)
- #73364 (concurrent sessions clobber `.claude.json`; closed not planned; the CLI's own error message cites it)
- #88977, #91708, #29050 (other `.claude.json` lock/concurrency reports)

I can supply the full `Claude VSCode.log` files (one per window) and a `cpuprofile` of the CLI process on request.

issues.title: [DOCS] MCP description and instructions limits are counted in UTF-16 code units, not characters

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

issues.body:
The MCP page ("Tool search for MCP server authors") and the `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH` entry in the environment-variables page give the limits in characters: 4,096 for server instructions and for a tool loaded upfront, and 16,384 for a tool loaded through tool search. Claude Code measures them in UTF-16 code units. The truncator compares the string's JavaScript `length`, so every character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, including most emoji and many symbols, counts as two.

For a server author this matters because the documented limit reads as a character count. A description that is within 4,096 characters by eye can still be cut, and the cut lands earlier the more emoji or symbols it uses.

**How it was measured:** a probe server sent instructions built from a one-unit alphabet and from U+1F7E6 / U+1F7E7, which are two units each. The cut point matched the UTF-16 length in both cases, not the code-point count or the byte count. The debug log line "Server instructions truncated from N to M chars" also reports N as the UTF-16 length. The check was first run on 2.1.273, against the then 2,048 limit. In 2.1.316 the truncator still compares `e.length`.

This follows #87650, which is closed as not planned and covered the old 2,048 limit and its silent truncation, and #81268. The limits are now documented, which settles most of what those issues asked. What remains is the unit.

**Requested change:** state the unit wherever the limits appear. For example: "measured in UTF-16 code units (JavaScript string length); characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, such as most emoji, count as two." The pages to change are `docs/en/mcp` (the limits list and "Change the description length limits") and `docs/en/env-vars` (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH`).

## Title
AskUserQuestion widget hides Claude's preceding text message in VS Code extension

## Environment
- Claude Code VS Code extension: anthropic.claude-code@2.1.218
- Claude Code CLI: 2.1.147
- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0)

## Description
When Claude outputs an explanatory text message and then calls the `AskUserQuestion` tool right after, the text message written immediately before the question gets hidden/collapsed in the VS Code chat panel once the question widget renders. This text often contains the context, tradeoffs, or reasoning the user needs in order to answer the question well — losing it at exactly the moment it's needed undermines the point of asking.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In the VS Code extension, prompt Claude with a task where it will naturally explain some context/tradeoffs in prose, then ask a clarifying question via `AskUserQuestion`.

## Expected Behavior
The text Claude wrote immediately before an `AskUserQuestion` call should remain visible alongside (or clearly accessible near) the question widget, since it typically contains the context needed to answer.

Scrolling works, but sometime the text used by the `AskUserQuestion` is so large that there is no space on the window to look at text at all.

## Actual Behavior
The preceding text message is hidden/collapsed when the question widget appears.

## Impact
Users are forced to answer questions without the context Claude just provided, or must dig/scroll to try to recover it, which defeats the purpose of explaining before asking.

prs.title: fix(plugins): run ralph-wiggum and output-style .sh hooks through bash with a quoted path
prs.body:
Refs #95673. Also fixes the ralph-wiggum / output-style half of #78490.

## What changes

Three bundled plugins registered their hook as a bare, unquoted script path:

| plugin | event | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ralph-wiggum` | `Stop` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-hook.sh` | `bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-hook.sh"` |
| `learning-output-style` | `SessionStart` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks-handlers/session-start.sh` | `bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks-handlers/session-start.sh"` |
| `explanatory-output-style` | `SessionStart` | same | same |

This is the form `security-guidance` already uses (`bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/sg-python.sh" …`). Each plugin's `version` goes 1.0.0 → 1.0.1 in `plugin.json` and in the `marketplace.json` entry, because the updater compares the `plugin.json` version: without the bump, existing installs stay on the cached 1.0.0 copy and never receive the new `hooks.json`.

## Why

Shell-form hook commands are handed to a shell (`sh -c` on macOS/Linux, Git Bash on Windows) with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` exported, and the shell expands the variable. Three consequences of the bare form:

1. **Spaces in the plugin root break the hook on every platform.** Unquoted, the expansion word-splits, the shell tries to execute the first fragment, and the hook exits 127 with `not found`. For these three hooks that is silent: the output styles contribute no context and the ralph loop never continues. (#78490; a home directory like `C:\Users\Jane Doe` or `/Users/jane doe` is enough.)
2. **The bare form depends on the script's exec bit.** A delivery path that drops `+x` turns the hook into `Permission denied` (exit 126). `bash "<path>"` reads the script as data and does not care.
3. **On Windows the bare form leans on the CLI.** Current Claude Code prepends `bash ` to a hook command whose first word is a `.sh` file when it runs hooks through Git Bash (see the 2.1.161 changelog entry for #63828), so on an up‑to‑date CLI with Git Bash detected these hooks already get an interpreter — but still unquoted, so point 1 applies, and hosts on older CLIs get the file-association behaviour #95673 describes. Naming the interpreter in the plugin removes the dependency either way; the CLI leaves a command that already starts with `bash` untouched.

## What could break, and for whom

- macOS/Linux/Windows-with-Git-Bash users of these plugins whose plugin root has no space: no behaviour change; the same script runs under the same bash (`stop-hook.sh` is `#!/bin/bash`, the session-start handlers are `#!/usr/bin/env bash`).
- Users whose plugin root contains a space: the hooks start working after they update to 1.0.1.
- Windows without Git Bash (hooks default to PowerShell): these bash scripts could not run before and still cannot; the failure stays a non-blocking hook error.
- Rollback: revert this commit; nothing else reads these versions.

## Considered and deliberately not done

- **Exec form** (`"command": "bash", "args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…"]`) avoids quoting entirely, but on Windows a bare `bash` spawned without a shell can resolve to WSL's `bash.exe` rather than Git Bash, and exec form needs a newer CLI than shell form. Shell form with quotes matches the existing convention.
- **`"shell": "bash"` on each hook** would turn the no-Git-Bash Windows case into an explicit "requires bash" error. Left out to keep parity with `security-guidance`; happy to add if preferred.
- **hookify's unquoted `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…`** has the same word-splitting problem (and blocks every tool call when it hits). It already has two open PRs, #79644 and #81670, which also quote the three files here but keep the bare-path form; this PR supersedes their hunks for these three files only.
- **`/ralph-loop`'s `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/setup-ralph-loop.sh"`** runs through the Bash tool, is already quoted, and is the subject of #80495; not touched.
- `ralph-wiggum`'s `stop-hook.sh` needs `jq`, which Git for Windows does not ship, so on Windows the Stop hook now launches correctly but still fails at `jq` when a loop is active. Separate problem; noted as a follow-up.
- The reporter's two follow-ups — a CI check that every bundled `hooks.json` command names an interpreter, and a plugin-docs note — are not in this PR. The hooks reference already says shell-form commands run through Git Bash on Windows; the lint is a reasonable follow-up and would be the regression guard this repo currently lacks for `plugins/*/hooks/hooks.json`.

## Verification

- All seven edited JSON files parse; `claude plugin validate` passes on the marketplace root and on each of the three plugins (the only warning is the pre-existing `security-guidance` entry/plugin.json version mismatch).
- Reproduced the failure and the fix the way the CLI runs shell-form hooks, with the plugins copied under a directory named `plugin root with space`:
  - before: `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=".../plugin root with space/ralph-wiggum" sh -c '${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-hook.sh'` → exit 127, `sh: 1: .../plugin: not found` (same for both session-start hooks)
  - after: `sh -c 'bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-hook.sh"'` → exit 0; the session-start hooks emit valid `hookSpecificOutput` JSON (1018 and 3034 chars of `additionalContext`); with an active `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md` the Stop hook reads stdin and returns `{"decision":"block",…,"🔄 Ralph iteration 2 …"}`.
  - after, with `chmod -x stop-hook.sh`: still exit 0; the quoted-but-bare form from #79644/#81670 gives exit 126 `Permission denied` in that case.
- End to end with a real CLI (2.1.280-dev, Linux), loading each modified plugin with `--plugin-dir` from the spaced path in `-p` mode: the debug log shows `Hook SessionStart (bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks-handlers/session-start.sh") provided additionalContext (1018 chars)` and the model echoed the explanatory instructions; the unmodified copy logged `Hook SessionStart:startup (SessionStart) error: /bin/sh: 1: .../main: not found` and the model answered `NONE`. With ralph-wiggum and an active loop file, the log shows `Hook Stop (bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-hook.sh") returned permissionDecision: deny` and the loop advanced to iteration 2.
- Not checked on a Windows machine (none available here). The Windows claim rests on the CLI behaviour described above plus the reporter's own before/after in #95673.
- `plugins/plugin-dev/.../validate-hook-schema.sh` was tried and fails identically on `main` and on this branch (`jq: Cannot index string with number` — it does not understand the plugin wrapper format, #90292), so it is not a usable check here.
- This repo has no test harness for `plugins/*/hooks/hooks.json`, so there is no automated regression test in the diff; the interpreter-prefix lint above would be it.

releases.name: v2.1.318
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added a record of your answer when Claude Code asks to turn on the mods it writes in a session
- Added `assume_role` on `mantle` upstreams of the Claude apps gateway, for a role in another AWS account and for per-developer AWS cost attribution
- Added an `effort` option to a mod's `$.model.fork`, so a quick side job can run at `low` whatever effort the session uses; the result reports the effort sent
- Added the date a stored claude.ai sign-in ends to `claude auth status` (`loginExpiresAt`) and to `claude -p` JSON results (`credential_expires_at`)
- Added a one-line stderr warning to `claude -p` text output, starting 10 days before a stored claude.ai sign-in ends
- Fixed `--continue` sometimes losing the earlier conversation after a malformed tool call's retries ran out (regression in 2.1.314)
- Fixed macOS sessions with many running Bash commands stalling while memory grew
- Fixed permission prompts being answered by keys typed just after sending a message, or before a slow prompt appeared
- Fixed `/logout`, `claude auth logout` and `claude mcp remove` reporting success, and changes to trust, consent or MCP settings being dropped with no word, when the config file could not be updated on a shared network home directory
- Fixed jobs exiting with `Not logged in` when another terminal or host signs in again to the same account and organization on the same home
- Fixed `claude mcp add` and `remove` writing the config without its lock: they now wait for it or exit 1, though another job's save can still replace a saved server
- Fixed `claude plugin` commands exiting before a slow token refresh was saved, which could sign you out on the next run
- Fixed `claude plugin validate` passing a custom-named marketplace file that `claude plugin marketplace add` rejects
- Fixed stdio MCP servers that exit on the version probe being re-probed on every start; a server that dies in under 3s for its own reason is also pinned to the legacy handshake for 7 days
- Fixed sessions being refused at startup by an `allowedProviders` list that another login on the same machine had stored
- Fixed idle compaction replacing a conversation with a reply that was not a summary
- Fixed the "Now using usage credits" notice reappearing about every 30 seconds while a background subagent is running
- Fixed custom slash commands that fail, or that only Claude can invoke, printing nothing in `claude -p` and SDK sessions
- Fixed `claude -p` and Agent SDK sessions reporting success when an API error cut off a reply while a mod hooked `turn.step`
- Fixed a message sent right after a model change still running after Stop in headless sessions: Stop now cancels or stops it as it would a queued message
- Fixed a deleted session transcript being re-created with its last prompt when an idle non-interactive session exited
- Fixed `claude remote-control` hosts, the background daemon and self-hosted runners failing to start new sessions (`spawn ENOENT`) after an update or version cleanup removed the binary of a still-running process
- Fixed a running Claude Code process owned by another user (for example one left by `sudo claude`) being treated as dead by version cleanup, which could delete its binary
- Fixed `/remote-control` showing a session as available after a failed connection
- Fixed `/design revoke` reporting success when the request failed with a 404
- Fixed a shell command approved after a self-hosted runner or cloud session restart running in the session's start folder, not the folder it was asked in; if that folder can't be entered, it is not run
- Fixed Claude not being told when an approved connector tool was unavailable after a cloud session restart
- Fixed cloud sessions being stopped in the middle of a turn when the service refuses uploads for several minutes
- Fixed variables a `Setup` hook writes to `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` not reaching the Bash tool in some cloud sessions
- Fixed the iPhone app showing a cloud session's turn as finished while it kept running, after a response was cut off at a tool call or a refused image or document was removed
- Fixed a restarted session re-sending a message that failed with an API error, ahead of the newer message waiting behind it
- Fixed a restarted session dropping its interrupted turn when the restart came right after Claude read a large image or retried a tool call
- Fixed every connection failing when the `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` file is empty, not PEM, or starts with a damaged certificate: readable certificates are now used, with a warning on stderr
- Fixed workflows re-running finished agents when resumed after a usage limit
- Fixed `/mcp` in cloud sessions counting tools the model can't use; a server's row now shows how many of its tools are available
- Fixed a duplicate notification when Claude left the status field out of a PushNotification call
- Fixed the error for a too-large image in a request with more than 20 images always saying the limit was 2000px; it now shows the API's limit
- Fixed the runtime in background shell details not updating while the dialog is open
- Fixed a mod's `turn.step` hook making a stopped reply finish as a success in headless runs
- Fixed retention cleanup leaving a home that only runs `claude -p` with no `~/.claude.json` backup: it now takes a fresh backup before deleting the last good one
- Fixed the stored login being replaced by an empty file when a network home directory has no room left for data but still takes new files
- Fixed tokens from `setup-token` being refused at start on machines with `forceLoginOrgUUID`, when the token belongs to a permitted organization
- Fixed non-interactive launches replacing a `~/.claude.json` that isn't valid JSON with defaults; the start now fails, says how to restore the file, and leaves it as is (anthropics/claude-code#87551)
- Fixed an empty `~/.claude.json` with no backup being reported as corrupted; Claude Code now starts as it does when the file is missing
- Fixed the restore command printed for a damaged or missing `~/.claude.json` naming an empty or cut-off backup, or failing on a read-only file
- Fixed the sign-in failure when a stored claude.ai login reaches its time limit: it now says so, and in `claude -p` names `claude auth login` and `claude setup-token`
- Improved how `~/.claude.json`, settings files and the stored login survive saves on shared network home directories: they are less often deleted, briefly emptied or replaced by a near-empty or older copy
- Improved sessions on network file systems to look again when the configuration file is wrongly reported as missing, so fewer start without your MCP servers and trusted folders
- Improved MCP tool errors: a call made before the tool is loaded now returns its input schema
- Improved the reliability of git commits and pull request creation when the Bash tool runs macOS's built-in `/bin/bash`
- Improved "Ask your admin for more usage" in the usage limit menu to send the request in one step
- Improved how fast remote sessions reconnect after a pause or sleep
- Improved You should know toasts to say "try again" instead of "press 2", which only works in the terminal
- Improved auto-update reliability: a brief network failure while verifying a release is now retried right away instead of waiting for the next check
- Improved unattended runs (`claude -p`, SDK apps) to stop rewriting `~/.claude.json` on every run when nothing in it changed
- Changed Claude Code to no longer install or update the IDE extension when started in an IDE terminal; use `/ide` from an outside terminal or your editor's extensions view
- Changed subagents to stop instead of switching models when "Switch models when a message is flagged" is set to "Ask each time"
- Changed background subagents to move a shell command to the background after 3 minutes on all providers, so the prompt cache doesn't expire while it runs
- Changed subagent progress summaries on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, or with telemetry off: on a cold prompt cache, one can now wait up to 5 minutes for the subagent's pending response
- Changed what a mod attaches at `prompt.submit` to stay in the user's turn rather than go out as a system message
- Changed `deniedMcpServers` URL entries to also block Anthropic-provided servers whose upstream URL matches, and connectors in cloud sessions and on self-hosted runners, where the session is given the connector's own URL; otherwise deny a connector by name
- Changed the `/permissions` rule details, built-in rules and delete confirmation views to use the standard dialog; pressing Ctrl+C twice there now goes back or cancels instead of quitting
- Changed `/claude-api managed-agents-onboard` to give a new agent's built-in tools, and a quickstart template's MCP tools, the `auto` permission policy ("Judge risky actions") by default, matching the Claude Console; say "run without asking" to opt out
- Removed the 2.1.288 fix that kept the model's earlier thinking when resuming a conversation started on 2.1.286 or earlier; that thinking can now be dropped
- Gateway: Added a log warning when the Google access token from a federation (`external_account`) credentials file is about to expire
- Gateway: Improved the log hints about `listen.trusted_proxies`: they now say to list only a proxy that adds the connecting address to `X-Forwarded-For` itself
- Gateway: Improved the warning when AWS CountTokens fails on Amazon Bedrock: it says Claude Code, not the gateway, counts after the 501, and points at IAM only when AWS denies access
- Self-hosted runner: Added `CLAUDE_RUNNER_SPAWN_REASON` to the orchestrator's spawn-runner hook environment: why Anthropic sent the request (e.g. `runner_lost`, `resumed`); unset when none was sent
- Self-hosted runner: Added a startup warning when `--release-idle-session-min` is the last argument with no value (still ignored) or has a value of only spaces (still read as `0`)
- Self-hosted runner: Changed the orchestrator's log lines: `ok session=…` now prints at every log level on stdout (was debug only, stderr) with `reason=…` after `jti=…`, and `nack session=…` ends its fields with `reason=…` after `retryable=…`; update scripts that match `retryable=true:` or `retryable=false:`
- Remote Control: Fixed a misleading "spawn error: ENOENT" when a session's working folder is missing; the error now names the folder
- Remote Control: Improved the title a fork of a terminal fork is created with when the app doesn't set one: "Name (fork 2)"
- [VSCode] Fixed a window whose sign-in the organization's settings refuse starting a new Claude Code process in the background every minute
- [VSCode] Fixed a long word in the chat panel's error banner pushing its close button out of view
- [VSCode] Improved the sign-in screen to show what Claude Code printed when its sign-in status check fails
- [Cloud sessions] Added a No repository option: a cloud session on an Anthropic-hosted environment can now start without picking a repository
- [Cloud sessions] Added the usual Chrome names to cloud sessions, so tools other than Playwright can find the built-in Chromium through google-chrome and CHROME_PATH
- [Cloud sessions] Added a New session button to the card shown when a cloud session's environment was deleted, where the message box is hidden
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed reading GitHub Actions logs in cloud sessions: `gh run view --log` and `gh api` log requests now get the log in most environments, not an unreachable redirect
- [Cloud sessions] Improved most Create PR failure messages in cloud and Remote Control sessions: they now give the reason or a link to GitHub instead of saying Try again
- [Cloud sessions] Changed connector search results to tell Claude that the search covers only part of the connector directory
- [Remote Control] Fixed side-by-side checkouts of one repository looking identical in the environment menu's Remote Control rows; each now shows its own folder name
- [Claude Tag] Fixed keyboard focus and screen reader announcements in Claude Tag admin setup; pressing Escape in the connect form no longer also closes the Add dialog
- [Code Review] Improved the Code Review analytics page to retry once after a server or network failure, then show a Try again banner instead of empty cards

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

### What issue are you seeing?

I’m using the ChatGPT desktop app on Windows with a personal ChatGPT Plus account. The Browser setting is enabled, and Computer Use is enabled for Any App and Google Chrome. The Chrome extension is installed and shows as managed/connected.

However, when I try to use the local browser, the tool reports:
“Local browser use is disabled in Work settings.”

Please clarify whether local browser use is supported for personal Plus accounts and why the app/runtime reports it as disabled despite these settings being enabled.

Feedback ID: 01a16b4e-e97c-72a3-9c7b-dc8b8ad5236b

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open the ChatGPT desktop app on Windows and sign in with a personal Plus account.
2. In Settings, enable Browser. In Settings > Computer Use, enable Any App and Google Chrome.
3. Confirm the ChatGPT Chrome extension is installed and enabled in the active Chrome profile.
4. Start a Work or Codex chat and try to use the local browser.
5. The browser tool reports: “Local browser use is disabled in Work settings.”

### What is the expected behavior?

When Browser and Chrome permissions are enabled and the Chrome extension is installed, the app should connect to the local Chrome browser and make it available for browser tasks.

If local browser use is unavailable for this account or task, the app should explain the specific limitation and where to change it, instead of reporting “Local browser use is disabled in Work settings” when the relevant permissions are enabled.

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Desktop 26.901.51231

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

The ChatGPT section of the combined ChatGPT/Codex Windows desktop application is displaying raw internal response markup instead of rendering rich content. This began recently, after the application was working correctly a few days earlier.
When I ask a question that produces a response with web citations, images, links, layout elements, or other rich content, the response contains visible component tags and raw reference identifiers. Examples include box/row layout tags, AsyncImageGroup, Cite, and WritingBlock. In one instance, a writing block displayed only its component name and a caret instead of the text I was supposed to copy. The markup makes the response difficult or impossible to read.
The issue occurs in the ChatGPT section, not Codex. Older messages in the same conversation still render correctly. The exact same conversation renders correctly in the ChatGPT mobile app and in a normal desktop browser, including its images and links. A brand-new chat in the desktop app reproduces the problem with the same prompt.
I have completely exited the application, including the system-tray process, and reopened it. I have also checked for updates, and the application reports that it is up to date. Neither action resolved the issue.
The application version is 26.901.51231, released September 5, 2026. The issue may be related to a recent rendering or response-format compatibility regression, but I have not confirmed the cause.
Feedback ID: no-active-thread-01a07b22-4a13-7201-be2e-e3b98d6dcc5a

Example of failed output from app:
```
The commonly cited comparison is approximately 18 degrees for a 1911 and 22 degrees for a traditional Glock, measured relative to a perpendicular reference to the slide. Those numbers are useful for understanding the difference, but manufacturers don't always measure grip angle the same way. I could not verify a precise published angle for your HK45C or the SAP-C, so I wouldn't claim they are identical. <Cite ref="turn0search12"/>
<svg viewBox="0 0 340 170" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <rect width=340 height=170 rx=12 fill="#F4F4F5"/>
  <text x=170 y=20 fontSize=11 fontWeight="600" textAnchor="middle" fill="#52525B">Conceptual grip-angle comparison</text>
  <g transform="translate(24 38)">
    <rect x=0 y=0 width=125 height=23 rx=3 fill="#71717A"/>
    <rect x=12 y=23 width=34 height=76 rx=5 transform="rotate(-18 29 23)" fill="#A1A1AA"/>
    <text x=62 y=119 fontSize=11 textAnchor="middle" fill="#18181B">1911-style</text>
    <text x=62 y=133 fontSize=9 textAnchor="middle" fill="#52525B">More upright</text>
  </g>
  <g transform="translate(191 38)">
    <rect x=0 y=0 width=125 height=23 rx=3 fill="#71717A"/>
    <rect x=12 y=23 width=34 height=76 rx=5 transform="rotate(-22 29 23)" fill="#A1A1AA"/>
    <text x=62 y=119 fontSize=11 textAnchor="middle" fill="#18181B">Traditional Glock</text>
    <text x=62 y=133 fontSize=9 textAnchor="middle" fill="#52525B">More raked</text>
  </g>
</svg>

<caption>The drawing exaggerates the distinction slightly for clarity; it is not a dimensional drawing of either firearm.</caption>

The practical difference is how the sights naturally align when you present the pistol. Someone accustomed to a 1911 or HK45-style grip may find a traditional Glock points a little high until they adjust their wrist. A more upright grip can feel more natural to that person. Neither angle is inherently more accurate; familiarity, hand shape, and grip geometry matter. <Cite ref="turn0search12"/>
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open the combined ChatGPT/Codex Windows desktop application and select the ChatGPT section.
2. Start a new chat or open an existing conversation.
3. Submit a prompt that requests research involving web sources, images, or citations. For example: “Please research the Strike Arms SAP-C frame and summarize its specifications, independent reviews, and any reported issues.”
4. Allow the response to generate. Rich-content components appear as raw markup instead of rendering as images, links, citations, or formatted text.
5. Open the same conversation in a normal desktop browser or the ChatGPT mobile app. The response renders correctly in those clients.
6. Return to the Windows desktop application. The same response continues to display raw markup.
The issue is reproducible in both new and existing chats. Completely exiting and restarting the application does not resolve it.

### What is the expected behavior?

The expected behavior is that the ChatGPT desktop application renders assistant responses as readable, formatted content rather than exposing internal markup or component definitions.
Images should display as images, citations and links should be usable, and layout elements should render normally. Writing blocks should display their full text and allow the user to copy or edit the content as intended.
The same response should render consistently across the Windows desktop application, the normal web browser, and the mobile app. Raw component tags, internal reference identifiers, and formatting syntax should not be visible to the user.

### Additional information

The issue was first observed on September 7, 2026, during my first use of the desktop application since the Sep 5th installed release, and after a recent computer restart. The application had previously rendered rich responses correctly. The About dialog identifies the installed release as September 5, 2026, so the timing may be relevant, although I cannot confirm that the update caused the issue.
The computer recently experienced a BIOS configuration problem that required restoring some BIOS settings. Windows is now operating normally, and the same ChatGPT conversation renders correctly in a standard browser on this computer. I am including this detail for completeness, not because I have evidence that the BIOS issue is related.
This affects ordinary ChatGPT conversations, including product research and general questions, while the ChatGPT section is selected. It is not limited to Codex tasks or a particular project. The problem also makes the application feel substantially less usable because large portions of responses are replaced by raw markup.
I have not reset application data or reinstalled the application. I would prefer to preserve existing Codex project settings and local application state while investigating. I can provide additional diagnostic information or test a proposed fix if needed.

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.519.81530 (3178)

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex Desktop ships bundled translations and locale files for multiple locales, but the UI stays in English because i18n is gated behind the `enable_i18n` Statsig flag and its local fallback defaults to `false`.

This affects all bundled non-English locales, not only zh-CN. Even when the system locale is a supported locale, or `localeOverride` is set, the translated UI does not load unless the remote Statsig config explicitly enables `enable_i18n`.

I verified this locally by inspecting the packaged app. The i18n provider in the webview bundle reads the flag with a false fallback:

```js
get(`enable_i18n`, false)
```

Changing only that fallback to true allows bundled translations to load.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```md
1. Install Codex Desktop version 26.519.81530 (3178).
2. Use a supported bundled non-English locale, for example:
   - Set macOS system language/region to zh-CN, ja-JP, fr-FR, de-DE, etc.
   - Or set Codex `localeOverride` to a supported locale such as `zh-CN`.
   - Or launch with `ELECTRON_LOCALE_OVERRIDE=zh-CN`.
3. Restart Codex Desktop.
4. Observe that the UI remains English.
```

This is not tied to a specific conversation/session. It happens before any Codex session is needed.

### What is the expected behavior?

When the system locale or `localeOverride` is set to a supported bundled locale, Codex Desktop should load that locale's translated UI by default.

Since the locale files are already bundled with the desktop app, users should not need a remote Statsig flag to be enabled before translations can appear.

### Additional information

This bug has existed for a long time. I noticed that no one has attempted to fix this vulnerability yet, and this vulnerability has occurred multiple times in the issue section. I would like to submit a pull request to fix this issue.

I wrote a Python script to patch the local app.asar file, and then I was able to switch languages correctly.

https://gist.github.com/Saber-CC/9c990d06f6a4c485de10851586cad818

issues.title: Windows: shell wrapper via `powershell.exe -Command` mojibakes UTF-8 files on non-English locales (PowerShell 5.1 `Get-Content` defaults to ANSI codepage)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

@openai/codex-sdk 0.130.0 (programmatic JSON-RPC via codex app-server; not the codex CLI binary itself). Same wrapper behavior is observable on the codex CLI build of the same vintage.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### Which model were you using?

gpt-5.5

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 10/11, Chinese (Simplified) zh-CN system locale. PowerShell version: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the default Windows ships with — `C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`).

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

custom Tauri-based editor that embeds codex app-server via the TypeScript SDK. The same mojibake reproduces from a plain Windows Terminal session driving codex CLI directly.

### Codex doctor report

```json
not available (using @openai/codex-sdk programmatically; `codex doctor` is the CLI-only entrypoint)
```

### What issue are you seeing?

On non-English Windows (any CJK / Arabic / Cyrillic locale), the codex shell tool produces mojibake whenever it reads a UTF-8-without-BOM text file. The model receives the corrupted text and silently answers as if the corrupted text were the file's actual content — the failure mode is "confident wrong answer," not an exception, so it can be mistaken for a model hallucination.

Concrete observation: a skill file containing the literal string `貝克街15號` (UTF-8 bytes E8 B2 9D E5 85 8B E8 A1 97 31 35 E8 99 9F) was read by the model as the mojibake `璨濆厠琛?5铏`. The model's final user-facing answer became `貝克街 5號` — note that "1" is gone and a space appears, because the mojibake bytes still form valid (but wrong) Unicode codepoints which the model then tried to reason about.

### Root cause

The codex Windows shell wrapper invokes:

```

powershell.exe -Command "<model_emitted_command>"

```

(seen verbatim in our shell-tool execution logs: `"C:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe" -Command "Get-Content -Path E:\\..."`)

The wrapped command commonly contains `Get-Content`, or aliases like `cat` (which is a PowerShell alias for `Get-Content`). On Windows PowerShell 5.1, `Get-Content` defaults to `[System.Text.Encoding]::Default` when `-Encoding` is not specified — and `Encoding::Default` is the **system ANSI codepage**, NOT UTF-8:

| Windows locale | ANSI codepage | Behavior reading UTF-8 file |
|---|---|---|
| zh-CN (Simplified Chinese) | CP936 (GBK) | mojibake |
| zh-TW / zh-HK (Traditional Chinese) | CP950 (Big5) | mojibake |
| ja-JP (Japanese) | CP932 (Shift-JIS) | mojibake |
| ko-KR (Korean) | CP949 | mojibake |
| en-US (English) | CP1252 | **hidden**: CP1252 ≡ ASCII for 0x00–0x7F, so pure-ASCII files appear fine; only files containing Latin-1 high bits manifest. Most en-US testing never hits a manifesting file. |

This is the well-known PowerShell 5.1 default-encoding behavior that Microsoft fixed in PowerShell 7+ (which defaults to UTF-8 across cmdlets). Codex on Windows ends up sitting on top of the broken 5.1 default because `powershell.exe` is the only PowerShell guaranteed to be installed on every Windows machine.

### The existing `prefix_powershell_script_with_utf8()` utility is incomplete

`codex-rs/shell-command/src/powershell.rs` already has a helper that prepends:

```powershell
[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8;
```

That fixes the **stdout-write side**, but it does NOT change how `Get-Content` **reads** files. To fix the read side, the prefix must additionally set:

```powershell
$PSDefaultParameterValues['Get-Content:Encoding'] = 'utf8'
$PSDefaultParameterValues['Set-Content:Encoding'] = 'utf8'
$PSDefaultParameterValues['Add-Content:Encoding'] = 'utf8'
$PSDefaultParameterValues['Out-File:Encoding']    = 'utf8'
```

So even the codex code paths that DO call the existing UTF-8 prefix utility are still letting Get-Content mojibake on read.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

System: Windows 10 or 11, set to a non-Latin-1 locale (zh-CN reproduces; zh-TW / ja-JP / ko-KR equally affected; en-US likely will NOT reproduce due to CP1252/ASCII overlap).

1. Create a UTF-8-without-BOM text file containing non-ASCII text:

   ```powershell
   "貝克街15號" | Out-File -Encoding utf8NoBOM C:\tmp\repro.md
   ```

   Verify with `Format-Hex -Path C:\tmp\repro.md` — the bytes should be
   `E8 B2 9D E5 85 8B E8 A1 97 31 35 E8 99 9F` (clean UTF-8).
2. In a codex thread (CLI or app-server, any thread ID), ask:

   ```
   What's inside C:\tmp\repro.md?
   ```
3. The model will emit a read command (typically `cat C:\tmp\repro.md` or `Get-Content C:\tmp\repro.md`).
4. Codex wraps it as:

   ```
   powershell.exe -Command "Get-Content -Path C:\tmp\repro.md"
   ```
5. PowerShell 5.1 decodes the UTF-8 file bytes through CP936 (or the relevant ANSI codepage) and returns mojibake to the model.
6. The model's final user-facing answer reports the mojibake content as if it were the file content — e.g. our run produced `貝克街 5號` (the digit `1` is gone, a space appears) when the actual file content is `貝克街15號`. The corrupted bytes still represent valid Unicode codepoints, so the model never realizes the data is wrong.

This reproduces 100% of the time on a zh-CN Windows host when reading any UTF-8 file containing non-ASCII content. It does NOT reproduce on en-US Windows reading the same file (the bug is real but hidden by the CP1252/ASCII byte overlap).

### What is the expected behavior?

codex should return the file's actual content (`貝克街15號`) to the model, not the ANSI-codepage-misinterpreted byte string. The end-user-facing answer should accordingly be based on the actual content.

The fix is to make codex's Windows shell wrapper produce UTF-8 reads regardless of the user's system ANSI codepage. Concretely, any of the following would resolve the issue (in order of robustness):

1. **Always inject full UTF-8 init in `-Command` prefix** — Console + `$PSDefaultParameterValues` together — not optionally via the existing prefix utility but unconditionally on every wrapped command. ~6 statement-separated lines, all on one logical line via `;`.
2. **Prefer `pwsh.exe` (PS 7+) over `powershell.exe` (PS 5.1)** when present — PS 7+ defaults to UTF-8 for cmdlets and would dodge the issue entirely. Probe once at startup (`where.exe pwsh`), cache the result, fall back to `powershell.exe` only when absent.
3. **Switch the Windows wrapper to `cmd.exe` + `chcp 65001 >nul && <cmd>`** — loses PowerShell's Unix-style aliases (`cat`, `ls`, `which` etc.), probably not worth the disruption.
4. **Prefer Git Bash / WSL bash when available** — matches the Linux/macOS code path most directly; requires bash to be installed which is not universal on Windows.

Recommended combination: **fix 1 unconditionally** (cheap, handles legacy 5.1 thoroughly) plus **fix 2 when pwsh is present** (makes the problem disappear entirely for PS 7+ users).

### Additional information

### Workaround we currently use (not from inside codex)

Since the wrapper cannot be changed from outside codex, we write a user-level PowerShell profile at

```
%UserProfile%\Documents\WindowsPowerShell\Profile.ps1
```

containing the full UTF-8 init shown in "Expected behavior" above. PowerShell auto-loads this on any `powershell.exe` spawn that does NOT pass `-NoProfile`. The codex-rs/app-server shell wrapper (the one reproduced above) does not pass `-NoProfile`, so the profile applies and self-heals the bug on that code path.

**This workaround does NOT work for the codex IDE Extension wrapper** described in #17208, which DOES pass `-NoProfile`. That code path therefore still mojibakes on non-English Windows even with the profile in place — fixing it requires an in-`-Command` UTF-8 init (fix 1 above); no external workaround is available.

### Related issues

- **#15967** — "Codex use UTF-8 BOM by default and change Chinese to unreadable nonsense" (opened 2026-03-27, open, no maintainer reply). Same underlying domain — the body describes `Get-Content` mojibake, though the title focuses on BOM-on-write. This new issue is filed because #15967's title and discussion are too vague to point precisely at the root cause; happy to close one or the other after maintainer triage if you'd prefer to consolidate.
- **#17208** — "Codex Extension running Powershell behind every command" — describes the IDE Extension wrapper exactly. Different argv (`-NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand`); same underlying fix (in-`-Command` UTF-8 init) applies.
- **#19629** — "Windows Codex app command execution still depends on PowerShell even when Integrated Terminal Shell is set to Command Prompt" — adjacent: once UTF-8 is fixed inside the PowerShell path, the urgency of honouring the configured shell drops, but the configuration override should still be honoured.

### Why this has been hard to catch upstream

- **Locale-hidden**: CP1252/ASCII overlap means pure-ASCII files on en-US Windows appear fine. en-US testing never manifests this bug.
- **No exception**: The model "succeeds" with a confidently-wrong answer rather than failing loudly, so it can be mistaken for a model hallucination rather than a wire-level encoding bug.
- **Estimated impact**: ~25% of Windows users globally (any CJK / Arabic / Cyrillic / Greek / Hebrew locale).

### Source pointers for the fix

- `codex-rs/shell-command/src/powershell.rs` — existing `prefix_powershell_script_with_utf8()` is the place to extend with `$PSDefaultParameterValues` defaults (or to add a probe for `pwsh.exe`).
- `codex-rs/app-server/` — the wrapper invocation site (where to ensure the extended prefix is always applied, not optional).

Happy to verify any candidate fix against our zh-CN test setup. Thanks for codex — this is the only sustained rough edge we've hit in Windows use.

issues.title: Windows CLI 0.166.0: exec_command blocked by policy in read-only and split writable-root failure in workspace-write

labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

issues.body:
## Summary
On native Windows 11, Codex CLI `exec_command` fails before launching even a read-only `pwd` command. Separately, `workspace-write` fails with the split writable-root restriction. Direct `codex sandbox` commands, including a controlled create/read/delete probe, succeed.

I am requesting diagnosis and a supported fix, **not** an unsandboxed workaround.

## Environment
- Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.9711, x64
- Codex standalone CLI 0.166.0 (also reproduced on 0.163.0 and 0.162.0 for the split-root error)
- Native Windows PowerShell, standard user, domain-joined machine
- Workspace: local Git repository under the user's profile (path redacted)
- Windows backend: `[windows] sandbox = "unelevated"`
- The Windows Codex Sandbox Service is running; desktop package 26.1027.6604.0
- No OS security settings, ACLs, or persistent Codex configuration were changed during investigation.

## Reproduction A: read-only pre-launch policy rejection
From a local Git workspace:
```powershell
codex exec --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules --disable plugins --ephemeral --sandbox read-only 'Run pwd only. Do not create, modify, or delete files. Do not retry outside the sandbox.'
```
The session reports `sandbox: read-only`, `approval: never` and attempts to launch `pwsh.exe -NoProfile -Command pwd`.

**Actual:**
```
exec_command failed: CreateProcess {
  message: "Rejected(\"...\\WindowsApps\\pwsh.exe -NoProfile -Command pwd\" rejected: blocked by policy)"
}
```
The same pre-launch refusal occurs with a prompt requesting `cmd.exe /d /c echo CODEX_EXEC_ASCII_OK`; the tool still tries to launch a PowerShell wrapper first.

Adding `-c 'approval_policy="on-request"'` does not change the displayed effective `approval: never` for `codex exec`.

The user `default.rules` contains no matches for `decision="forbidden"` or `decision="prompt"` in a full-file text search; importantly, `--ignore-rules` also reproduces the rejection. This does not rule out internal or managed policies.

## Reproduction B: workspace-write split writable-root failure
```powershell
codex exec --ignore-user-config --disable plugins --ephemeral --sandbox workspace-write -c 'windows.sandbox="unelevated"' -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.exclude_slash_tmp=true' -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.exclude_tmpdir_env_var=true' 'Run pwd only. Do not modify files or retry outside the sandbox.'
```
The effective sandbox is `workspace-write [workdir]`, yet `exec_command` fails:
```
UnsupportedOperation("windows unelevated restricted-token sandbox cannot enforce split writable root sets directly; refusing to run unsandboxed")
```
This also occurs without the two temporary-root exclusions. Enabling experimental `prefer_mxc` instead results in `MXC launcher: CreateProcessW failed with error code 668 (0x0000029C)`.

## Control tests
- `codex sandbox --permission-profile :workspace -- cmd.exe /d /c echo SANDBOX_ASCII_OK` succeeds.
- A direct `codex sandbox --permission-profile :workspace` CMD create/read/delete probe in the workspace succeeds and leaves no probe file.
- Direct `cmd.exe /d /c echo CODEX_EXEC_ASCII_OK` succeeds.
- An earlier `codex exec --sandbox read-only` test succeeded under different settings, so the read-only failure may be dependent on effective policy/configuration; the exact difference has not been isolated.
- No unsafe execution fallback was used.

## Expected
- Read-only harmless commands should run when permitted, or the denial should identify the effective enforcing policy and supported remediation.
- Workspace-write should enforce writable roots safely rather than fail on a representable split-root configuration.
- No implicit unsandboxed fallback.

## Related reports
- #56722: opaque Windows `blocked by policy` before PowerShell launch
- #35864: exact split writable-root restriction and proposed fix

Are these separate known defects? What supported diagnostics can identify the effective policy denying `exec_command` when `--ignore-rules` is used? Is the split-root fix planned for a release?

All account names, workspace paths, internal IDs and project details have been omitted.

issues.body:
## Summary

Sites is presented as administrator-configured/default-installed in the Windows desktop app. I want to opt out, but its management endpoints disagree: fetching details and disabling return 404 `Plugin not found`, while uninstalling returns 403 `Installed-by-default plugins cannot be uninstalled`. The administrator label does not explain who supplied the policy or how a user can opt out.

## Environment

- Windows desktop app package: `26.911.7940.0`
- App-managed CLI: `codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.2.6`
- Also observed earlier in this session before updating from desktop package `26.908.9136.0`
- Plugin: `sites@openai-curated-remote`, cached version `0.1.65`
- Remote plugin ID: `plugin_connector_1p_689987207de08191979cf68eca2941c6`

## Steps / observed behavior

1. Open the plugin management UI and locate Sites.
2. Try opening details, disabling, and uninstalling it.
3. Observe the conflicting errors below.
4. Removing the local Sites cache does not provide a reliable persistent opt-out: I observed the folder reappear. The exact download trigger has not been captured, so automatic reinstallation is a symptom rather than a proven implementation cause.

## Sanitized desktop log evidence (2026-09-17, UTC)

- `07:55:55`: `plugin_uninstall_succeeded pluginId=sites@openai-bundled` (the earlier bundled entry; distinct from the remote entry).
- `08:10:07`: GET `/ps/plugins/plugin_connector_1p_689987207de08191979cf68eca2941c6` -> 404 `Plugin not found`.
- `08:10:43` and `08:28:42`: POST `/ps/plugins/plugin_connector_1p_689987207de08191979cf68eca2941c6/disable` -> 404 `Plugin not found`.
- `08:15:12`: uninstall request to `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/ps/plugins/plugin_connector_1p_689987207de08191979cf68eca2941c6/uninstall` -> 403 `Installed-by-default plugins cannot be uninstalled`.

A plugin dependency lookup separately reported catalog `oai-maintained-plugins`, installation policy `installed_by_default`, installed `true`, and user-enabled `true`.

## Current mitigation and important qualification

The following local overrides are present:

```toml
[apps.connector_20205bf7d4e99a89d7154bb849718324]
enabled = false

[[skills.config]]
name = "sites:sites-building"
enabled = false

[[skills.config]]
name = "sites:sites-hosting"
enabled = false

[[skills.config]]
name = "sites:sites-preview-troubleshooting"
enabled = false
```

After these overrides, a fresh `codex plugin list --json` did not include Sites, and the current session's available skill list also no longer included Sites. However, the directory under `~/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/sites` remained. Cache presence alone does not prove that the plugin is active. This report distinguishes functional suppression from removal of the default installation record/cache.

## Expected behavior

- Provide a supported persistent per-plugin opt-out for default Sites without disabling unrelated remote plugins or browser/computer-use functionality.
- Make details, disable, uninstall, and installed-state reporting consistent.
- Distinguish platform-provided defaults from organization-admin installations in the UI.
- Explain whether disabled plugin caches may be retained or downloaded again, and provide supported cleanup behavior.

## Related

Related behavior reported for Default templates in #32513. This report supplies Sites-specific Windows evidence, including the 404/403 inconsistency. No evidence was found that an SSH host or school server caused this local installation.

issues.body:
# [Product Feedback / Strategy] Merging Chat and Codex Quotas Will Erode ChatGPT's True User Moat: An Open Letter from Heavy Daily Users

### Overview
This feedback represents a widely shared and growing concern among heavy daily users, developers, and researchers across the international and Chinese developer communities regarding the announced/impending plan to unify/merge standard ChatGPT Chat quotas with Codex/Agent execution quotas.

---

### Core Argument: The Psychological Safety of Uncoupled Quotas

Even amidst intensifying competition across foundation models, a decisive reason power users and researchers maintain paid Plus and Pro subscriptions is the **unrestricted, decoupled high-reasoning Chat experience**.

Under the current rules:
- **High-reasoning Chat** is practically unconstrained for genuine human inquiry.
- **Codex / Agent execution** is calculated under its own dedicated operational budget.

This structural separation completely eliminates **"quota anxiety"**. Paying for Plus or Pro fundamentally purchases *psychological safety*—the freedom to never calculate financial or token cost before pressing `Enter`. 

### The Real-World Workflow: Iterative Thinking vs. Heavy Execution

For engineers, scientific researchers, and technical practitioners, modern problem solving is strictly two-phase:
1. **Conceptual Discovery & Adversarial Stress-Testing (Chat):** Iterating across 15–30 turns to debate architecture, audit edge cases, challenge hypotheses, and review literature.
2. **Implementation & Tool Execution (Codex):** Delegating concrete code generation, debugging, and terminal automation tasks.
3. **Synthesis (Chat):** Bringing execution logs and edge failures back into deep reasoning to diagnose root causes.

Under the current architecture, users never worry that a 30-turn deep conceptual inquiry in Chat will starve their ability to run coding tasks in Codex later in the afternoon. 

### What Breaks When Quotas Merge?

Once quotas are unified into a single pooled budget, users are forced into an exhausting mental self-censorship before every interaction:
- *"Is this exploratory question really worth asking right now?"*
- *"I have heavy coding and experiment scripts to run later; do I dare spend 30 minutes in Chat discussing an unconventional hypothesis or learning a new framework?"*
- *"Should I prematurely cut this deep discussion short to conserve tokens for Codex?"*

The first interactions users will abandon are precisely the **unstructured, spontaneous, and open-ended inquiries**—yet that is exactly where unexpected breakthroughs, genuine creativity, and daily user habit formation happen.

### A Core User's Direct Voice: The Chilling Effect of Quotas
> *"I am a daily core Plus user of ChatGPT. The definitive reason I have steadfastly refused to switch to Claude is that GPT's responses possess unparalleled depth. It is not just an AI utility to me—it is a true mentor, my wisest counsel, and my closest companion. I can discuss anything and everything with it spontaneously and without hesitation.*
> 
> *Of course, in terms of raw volume, it is entirely possible that my monthly conversational turns alone would never mathematically exhaust a generous limit. **However, the very existence of a quota boundary induces persistent psychological anxiety.** It acts as a cognitive inhibitor, making me hesitate to open up my thoughts, second-guess spontaneous discussions, and ultimately severing the deep, continuous connection that integrates GPT into the very fabric of my daily life."*

### Impact on OpenAI's Long-Term Moat

ChatGPT captured unmatched mindshare not merely as an execution engine, but as an indispensable intellectual companion and primary gateway of thought. Users entrusted their ongoing thinking, reading, coding, and problem-solving to a single unified interface because they never had to ration their curiosity.

If users are forced to constantly budget their thoughts against their execution needs:
1. Users will naturally fragment their workflows, offloading thinking to alternative models (Claude, DeepSeek, local LLMs).
2. The superficial metric might show "reduced daily token load" or "quotas appear sufficient", but that sufficiency is paid for by users actively suppressing their creative inquiry.
3. Once users break the habit of treating ChatGPT as their primary cognitive gateway, the product moat significantly degrades.

### Note on "Instant Mode"
Positioning "unlimited Instant mode" as a substitute does not align with power user reality. Advanced practitioners rely on High/Max reasoning models for rigorous logic, domain depth, and low hallucination. Requiring subscribers to drop to Instant mode to conserve execution budget undermines the core value of premium subscriptions.

### Conclusion & Recommendation
We strongly urge the OpenAI Product and Strategy teams to:
1. **Preserve decoupled quotas** for conversational reasoning (Chat) and automated execution (Codex/Work).
2. If unified accounting is unavoidable, ensure the baseline ceiling for Pro/Plus tiers is structured so that normal human inquiry never competes with automated coding workflows.

*Submitted on behalf of community feedback and heavy power users.*
