issues.title: Windows 10 Computer Use WGC timeout: callback holds D3D lock while bitmap conversion waits

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
Submitted with user authorization. Capture remains unresolved; the standalone probe demonstrates a working callback-return pattern, not a fix to the installed component.

## Environment and scope

- Windows 10 Pro, build 19045, x64.
- Desktop Appx: OpenAI.Codex 26.1027.6604.0; both current-user package and running executable path verified.
- Computer Use skill 26.1027.51404, @oai/sky package 0.7.13, runtime directory 989c7523a11c09b9.
- AMD Radeon HD 7800 Series, driver 27.20.1034.6; Oray virtual display device also present. No causal attribution to the virtual device has been established.

## Official API reproduction

1. Initialize the installed @oai/sky through the documented node_repl workflow.
2. Launch one blank system Notepad and select the fresh returned window.
3. Activate it, then call get_window_state with include_screenshot:true.
4. Capture fails with FrameArrived timed out / window capture timed out, including after app restart and a genuinely applied app update.
5. Accessibility-only state succeeds. Clicking a fresh menu element index fails with coordinate input geometry is unavailable.

## Independent OS control

WgcSystemProbe.cs uses the installed Windows SDK / .NET Framework, GraphicsCaptureItem interop for Notepad, a free-threaded frame pool, and SoftwareBitmap.CreateCopyFromSurfaceAsync. It saves no images and reports frame counts/dimensions only.

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| D3D hardware, copy on worker | Frames and 983x759 bitmap delivered |
| WARP software device, copy on worker | Frames and bitmap delivered |
| Start copy inside FrameArrived, return callback while awaiting asynchronously | Success; bitmap completes shortly after callback exit |
| Synchronously wait for copy inside FrameArrived | Copy starts; first frame acquired; no completion within 8 seconds, on hardware and WARP |
| Poll WinRT operation.Status inside callback for 1500ms, then return | Status stays Started throughout callback; bitmap completes about 17ms after callback returns |

Callback thread is MTA and SynchronizationContext=null. This narrows the standalone failure to waiting for conversion completion without releasing the frame callback. It is not proof that the proprietary helper uses this exact implementation.

## Actual native helper stacks and lock ownership

Two non-invasive NO_SUSPEND DbgEng samples were collected locally, including one concurrently with the official screenshot timeout. No memory dump or image was saved. Matching public Microsoft PDBs resolved the system frames. Local paths and memory addresses are omitted here.

Capture callback thread (0x5890):

```text
KERNELBASE!WaitForSingleObjectEx
codex_computer_use+0x123149
codex_computer_use+0x42c9c
GraphicsCapture!winrt::impl::invoke<...TypedEventHandler...>
GraphicsCapture!...Direct3D11CaptureFramePool::FirePresentEvent
GraphicsCapture!...Direct3D11CaptureFramePool::ContentUpdated
GraphicsCapture!...Direct3D11CaptureFramePool::PresentThread
```

Bitmap worker (0x1c68):

```text
ntdll!RtlEnterCriticalSection
d3d11!NDXGI::CResource::GetDesc
d3d11!dxrt11::Direct3DSurface::get_Description
RTMediaFrame!MediaFrameHelpers::CreateCopyWithAlphaFromSurface
RTMediaFrame!Concurrency::task<...ISoftwareBitmap...>
```

Another capture worker (0x4464):

```text
ntdll!RtlEnterCriticalSection
d3d11!CContext::SetMultithreadProtected
GraphicsCapture!...Direct3D11CaptureFramePool::Recreate
GraphicsCapture!...Direct3D11CaptureFramePool::Direct3D11CaptureFramePool
GraphicsCapture!...CreateFreeThreaded
```

Windows Wait Chain Traversal identifies 0x5890 as the critical-section owner for both blocked workers. Thus the callback is waiting while holding the D3D lock needed by bitmap conversion, and subsequent frame-pool creation is blocked as well. WCT itself reports cycle=False; the exact event completion dependency and private helper frame names still require maintainer symbols. This is strong evidence consistent with the independently reproduced synchronous-wait pattern, rather than a claim based only on an external probe.

## Requested investigation

Please resolve the private helper frames +0x42c9c and +0x123149 for this build and identify the event completion dependency. If needed, instrument FrameArrived entry, bitmap conversion start/completion, and callback exit.

If synchronous conversion waiting is performed inside FrameArrived, test retaining the acquired frame/surface and handing conversion to a separate worker, returning the callback before waiting, and completing the request asynchronously. Include a bounded timeout and dispose resources after completion/cancellation.

Please identify a fixed helper/app version or a supported capture backend workaround if this is already known. The existing public JS API does not expose a capture-backend selector.

Potential local attachments after explicit user authorization: WgcSystemProbe.cs, the small phase-timing text logs, and the relevant package version fields. Do not attach full memory dumps, chat databases, credentials, or screenshots by default.

prs.title: Respect turn filesystem permissions during executor skill discovery
prs.body:
Respect turn filesystem permissions during executor skill discovery

## Why

Direct executor skill discovery used unrestricted filesystem access, bypassing the turn's permission context. Cached catalogs also needed to account for changes in filesystem access within a turn.

## What changed

- Bind selected capability roots to callback-scoped filesystem access through `AccessedSelectedCapabilityRoot`.
- Pass accessors built with the turn's granted permissions into skill preparation and discovery, removing the executor skill provider's environment lookup and unrestricted accessor.
- Include filesystem access keys in the direct discovery cache so permission changes trigger rediscovery.

## Testing

Extend tests to verify that restricted discovery returns no skills when sandbox access is unavailable, restoring access restores discovery, and changing or restoring access invalidates the catalog cache.

prs.body:
Add directional conversation focus shortcuts in workspace mode

## What changed

**Goal:** To significantly improve the reliability, visibility, and actionability of our project's internal (non-benchmark) evaluations.

issues.title: Assess the impact of AST-aware file reads, search, and mapping

labels.name: priority/p2
labels.description: Important but can be addressed in a future release.

labels.name: area/agent
labels.description: Issues related to Core Agent, Tools, Memory, Sub-Agents, Hooks, Agent Quality

labels.name: kind/customer-issue
labels.description: Issues that were reported by customers

labels.name: 🔒 maintainer only

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
This EPIC tracks a series of investigations as to whether there is value in AST aware file read, search, or codebase mapping.

AST aware tools can be used to 1) more precisely read method bounds with a single tool call, reducing turns from misaligned reads, and reducing noise in tokens, 2) navigate to usages and definitions of syntax elements via syntax aware search (AST grep), and 3) compress high level context about the codebase, such as the location of specific classes and their members by collapsing code down to just top level classes and types and their children's signatures.

```
 1. tilth (Rust)
  tilth is built specifically to generate a structural outline of a codebase. It uses Tree-sitter under the hood but ships as a single binary. It gives you an
  immediate map of the repository's symbols.
   * Installation: cargo install tilth (or download the binary from their releases)
   * Usage:
       * tilth map . (Prints a tree-like overview of the whole codebase structure)
       * tilth read <file> (Prints the structural outline of a specific file)


  2. glyph (Go)
  glyph is another single-binary tool designed to generate clean, multi-file symbol maps. It's excellent if you want to quickly see the skeleton of a
  directory of source code.
   * Installation: go install github.com/benmyles/glyph@latest
   * Usage: glyph cli './**/*.go' (Prints a tree of functions, structs, and methods)


  3. ast-grep (sg) (Rust)
  While primarily known as a structural search-and-replace tool, ast-grep is the industry standard for distributing Tree-sitter as a fast, single binary. You
  can use it to extract landmarks via the command line.
   * Installation: brew install ast-grep or cargo install ast-grep
   * Usage: You can write quick one-liners to extract specific symbols (like all function declarations) and format the output.


  4. The Classic: Universal Ctags (C)
  If you truly want zero modern dependencies, u-ctags is the classic UNIX approach. It uses a hybrid regex/parser approach rather than full AST generation, so
  it's incredibly fast and supports over 100 languages out of the box.
   * Installation: brew install universal-ctags
   * Usage: ctags -R --output-format=json .
   * Note: It outputs a flat list of symbols (or JSON) rather than a visual tree, but it is the most robust and portable way to extract codebase landmarks.
```

issues.body:
### What happened?

**Summary**: `codebase_investigator` subagent reports `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"` even though its own result says it hit the maximum turn limit before doing any analysis.

While using Gemini CLI to investigate two local repositories (`t3code` and `superset`), the agent invoked the `codebase_investigator` subagent and it failed immediately without doing any analysis.

I ran the Gemini CLI on these two local repositories with an objective asking it to understand their architectures and AI agent integrations. The saved session log shows:

- The main agent called `codebase_investigator` with a valid, concrete objective.
- The tool result was reported with `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.
- The embedded result text simultaneously says the investigation was interrupted because the "maximum number of turns was exceeded" before any specific task was identified or initiated.
- `RelevantLocations` was empty and no actual codebase analysis was performed.

This looks incorrect because:

1. The subagent appears to have exhausted its turn budget before performing any actual analysis.
2. The termination metadata is internally inconsistent: the parent tool call is surfaced as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`, but the embedded payload describes a limit-induced early termination with no findings.

Relevant evidence from the session log:

```text
session file: session-2026-03-09T18-34-10479ef5.json

line 50: "name": "codebase_investigator"
line 53: objective: "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset..."
line 61: "Termination Reason: GOAL"
line 61: "The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded)..."
line 61: "\"RelevantLocations\": []"
line 66: "status": "success"
line 79: "The `codebase_investigator` was unable to complete its analysis due to a turn limit..."
```

Full snippet from the saved session:

```json
{
  "id": "codebase_investigator_1773081420202_0",
  "name": "codebase_investigator",
  "args": {
    "objective": "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset, focusing on AI agent integrations.\nSpecifically:\n1. In t3code, how is 'Codex' integrated? Where is the core logic for agent interaction?\n2. In superset, what are the different agent/harness integrations (e.g., Mastra, MCP, Claude, etc.) and how are they implemented?\n3. What are the common patterns or interfaces used in superset that could be adapted for t3code to support multiple harnesses?\n\nIdentify key files, symbols, and architectural patterns in both repositories."
  },
  "result": [
    {
      "functionResponse": {
        "response": {
          "output": "Subagent 'codebase_investigator' finished.\nTermination Reason: GOAL\nResult:\n{\n  \"SummaryOfFindings\": \"The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded) before any specific task could be identified or initiated. As a result, no codebase analysis was performed, and no relevant locations or insights could be gathered.\",\n  \"ExplorationTrace\": [\n    \"Received system notification that the maximum number of turns was exceeded.\",\n    \"Followed emergency termination protocol as instructed.\"\n  ],\n  \"RelevantLocations\": []\n}"
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "status": "success"
}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected one of these outcomes:

- `codebase_investigator` should actually explore the repositories and return findings.
- If it truly hits a turn limit, it should do so after some visible work, and the tool invocation should be surfaced as a failure or explicit limit condition, not as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.

At minimum, the CLI should not report a contradictory success state for a subagent that says it exceeded its turn budget before beginning analysis. If the subagent hits a system-imposed turn limit before doing useful work, the tool result should be reported as a failure or explicit limit condition (e.g. `status: "error"` with a clear error code), not as a successful `GOAL` completion.


### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Run `gemini` to enter the interactive CLI, then run the `/about` command.

```console
> /about
Gemini CLI package version: 0.32.1
Platform: Windows
OS: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
Node.js: v20.20.0
PowerShell: 5.1.26100.7920
```

</details>

### Login information

Google Account, Pro tier from students promotion

### Anything else we need to know?

- After the failed `codebase_investigator` call, the main agent continued with manual file exploration and eventually produced an implementation plan. So the overall conversation did not fully crash, but the specialized investigator tool clearly failed.
- My current inference is that this may be either:
  - turn-budget state leaking into a fresh subagent invocation, or
  - an incorrect mapping of a subagent limit/error state into a successful `GOAL` termination in the parent session.
- If useful, I can provide the full saved session JSON or a redacted version of it.

issues.body:
# [BUG] Browser Agent ignores `settings.json` overrides (e.g., `maxTurns`)

## What happened?
The Browser Agent completely ignores any configuration overrides provided in the global or project-level `settings.json`. While the `AgentRegistry` correctly reads and merges these settings during initialization, the `BrowserAgentInvocation` and its factory (`browserAgentFactory.ts`) skips the registry and recreate the agent definition from scratch with hardcoded defaults.

## What did you expect to happen?
The Browser Agent should respect settings overrides like `maxTurns`, `maxTimeMinutes`, etc., just like other sub-agents (e.g., `codebase_investigator`). For example, setting `maxTurns: 0` in `settings.json` should cause the agent to terminate immediately upon invocation.

## Client information
<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Platform: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)
Gemini CLI Version: 0.35.0-nightly.20260311.657f19c1f

</details>

## Login information
Google Account (OAuth)

## Anything else we need to know?
### Root Cause
The Browser Agent's unique invocation flow skips the `AgentRegistry` where settings overrides are maintained. Instead of using the pre-merged definition from the registry, it re-instantiates a fresh definition using hardcoded defaults.

**Relevant Files & Code Snippets:**

1.  **`packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts`**
    The Browser Agent is explicitly branched out of the standard flow that uses `LocalSubagentInvocation`:
    ```typescript
    if (definition.name === BROWSER_AGENT_NAME) {
      return new BrowserAgentInvocation(this.config, ...);
    }
    ```

2.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentInvocation.ts`**
    The `execute` method calls `createBrowserAgentDefinition`, passing the `config` object but omitting the merged definition from the registry.

3.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentFactory.ts`**
    The factory re-runs the `BrowserAgentDefinition` constructor, which returns hardcoded defaults (e.g., `maxTurns: 50`):
    ```typescript
    const baseDefinition = BrowserAgentDefinition(config, !visionDisabledReason);
    ```

### Suggested Fix
Update `browserAgentFactory.ts` to attempt to retrieve the existing definition from the `AgentRegistry` before falling back to creating a fresh one.

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

The `browser_agent` (specifically `BrowserManager.ts`) currently employs a restrictive "fail-fast" strategy when encountering a locked browser profile (e.g., when `sessionMode: 'persistent'` is used and an existing instance or orphaned process is active):


```json
{
  "success": false,
  "summary": "The task could not be completed because the browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile.",
  "fullErrorMessage": "The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use --isolated to run multiple browser instances.\nCause: The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use a different userDataDir or stop the running browser first."
}
```

I propose to make it more resilient with the following capabilities:

1.  **Automatic Session Takeover:** If `persistent` mode fails due to a profile lock, the agent should automatically attempt to connect to the existing instance (as if `sessionMode: 'existing'` were specified). This requires a graceful "fallback-and-probe" mechanism in `BrowserManager.connectMcp()`.
2.  **Orphaned Process Recovery:** If an `existing` connection is not feasible but the profile remains locked, the `BrowserManager` should proactively detect orphaned `chrome` or `chrome-devtools-mcp` processes associated with the Gemini CLI profile and offer (or automatically execute) a "Self-Healing" routine (process termination + lock file removal).
3.  **Intelligent Error Remediation:** Replace the current static error messages with an interactive recovery flow. Utilizing the `ask_user` tool, the agent should present the user with a "Choice" menu featuring numbered options to resolve the lock (e.g., **1. Attempt Session Takeover**, **2. Force Termination & Reset**, or **3. Launch Isolated Session**). 
### Why is this needed?

Forcing the user to manually `pkill` processes or close browser windows is a friction point that degrades the autonomous agent experience. The agent has sufficient context (profile path, PIDs) to resolve this internally without user intervention.


### Additional context

issues.body:
### What happened?

This is purely anecdotal, but IME Gemini does not use custom skills and sub-agents on its own, basically at all.  It will if I instruct it to explicitly, but won't when it's doing something very related.

For example, I have "gradle" and "git" skills with descriptions like:
> Executes and manages Gradle builds authoritatively with high-performance background orchestration 
  and surgical failure analysis. This skill is the STRONGLY PREFERRED way 
  to run any Gradle task, providing superior reliability through managed background processes, 
  task-specific output capturing, and deep diagnostic integration. Use it for executing core 
  lifecycle tasks like 'build' or 'assemble', starting persistent development servers, 
  or performing complex build troubleshooting. Do NOT use for specialized test diagnostics 
  (use running_gradle_tests).

and 
> Audits Git repository status, examines history, and implements non-interactive modifications. Processes surgical staging, descriptive commits, and multi-file diff analysis. Use for repository introspection and history-based truth verification. NEVER stages or commits without explicit user directives. Avoids interactive prompts via --no-pager.

that never ever get called when using the relevant tools.

I even have this in my `GEMINI.md` in the "priority rules" section:
> 4. **Agent & Tool Hierarchy:** Whenver considering how to approach a task or do anything, ALWAYS follow the hierarchy of preference: **Sub-Agents** > **Skills** > **Specialized MCP Tools** (NOT a Shell tool or similar) > **General/Builtin Tools** (e.g., `run_shell_command`, `grep_search`, `read_file`).
> 5. **Intentionality Protocol:** Before starting ANY task, you MUST stop and consider which agent, skill, or tool is most appropriate for the specific context. If your plan involves using the shell (even via a tool like `run_shell_command`), you MUST stop and reconsider if a more specialized tool or skill exists to handle the task more reliably.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected Gemini to use related skills when working on tasks that match the skill description.  Same for sub-agents.

### What would you like to be added?

## Objective
Ensure the Gemini CLI understands its own mechanics well enough to act as its own expert guide. The agent must be able to provide users with accurate facts about how it works, its hotkeys, and the exact CLI flags needed to run itself for specific workflows.

## The Problem
Users rely on the CLI to learn how to use the CLI. If the agent hallucinates flags (like suggesting the deprecated `--yolo` instead of `--approval-mode=yolo`) or forgets UI hotkeys (like `Double Esc` for `/rewind`), it blocks progress and creates friction. The agent needs strict grounding in its own documentation to accurately guide users.

### Why is this needed?

1. **Accurate Internal Facts:** The agent (specifically the `cli_help` subagent) must have flawless recall of its own UI keyboard shortcuts, slash commands, and settings hierarchy.
2. **Flag Construction:** It must be able to tell users exactly how to run it from the terminal for various use cases (e.g., suggesting `gemini -i "prompt" --sandbox --output-format json` for safe, headless scripting).
3. **Self-Execution & Guidance:** It should be able to write the exact commands needed to run itself, restart itself, or execute sub-tasks with the correct environment variables and flags.

issues.title: Leverage model's bash affinity via Zero-Dependency OS Sandboxing & Post-Execution Intent Routing

labels.name: priority/p2
labels.description: Important but can be addressed in a future release.

labels.name: area/agent

labels.name: 🔒 maintainer only
labels.description: ⛔ Do not contribute. Internal roadmap item.

labels.description: Label used to tag epics and features that are associated with one of the three primary workstreams

labels.name: effort/large
labels.description: 3+ days: platform-specific, architecture, memory leaks

type.name: Epic
type.description: Related Changes across multiple feature sets

issues.body:
## Description
Gemini 3 models are fundamentally trained to operate as native bash users, chaining standard POSIX tools (`grep`, `cat`, `sed`, `awk`) to explore codebases and edit files. To make full use of the model's native and preferred capabilities without compromising user security or UX, we need to allow the model to use these tools directly to interact and make changes.

## Prior Art
Historically, we have attempted to force models to use custom tools (such as `replace`, `grep_search`, `write_file`, etc.). However, these methods fight the model's core training. Malicious prompts or complex scripts are inherently hard to control and catch via parsing, and forcing custom tools creates significant downstream UX and security issues.

## The Challenge & Value Proposition
Because the model strongly favors raw bash calls even when nudged towards custom tools, it frequently outputs large, complex bash scripts to accomplish tasks. Under our current security model, these scripts require explicit user confirmation. 

This creates a critical point of failure: users are frequently presented with dense, hard-to-read bash messages to evaluate. This leads to severe prompt fatigue, causing users to either blindly confirm the execution or enter "yolo mode" (auto-approving all actions). This behavior is highly detrimental to security and degrades the overall user experience. 

**Value Proposition:** By safely embracing the model's native bash tendencies, we can eliminate confirmation fatigue, prevent unsafe "yolo mode" habits, and drastically improve both the UX and our underlying security posture. 

## Proposed Solution
A highly viable solution is to utilize a secure sandbox. ALL standard shell commands will execute within a zero-dependency, kernel-enforced sandbox. Instead of trying to predict intent before execution (which led to the parsing challenges described above), we can safely observe and handle the results *after* execution.

### Method
By running commands in a sandboxed replica of the workspace, we achieve three distinct UX lanes:
1. **Reads:** Commands that do not mutate the filesystem (e.g., `ls`, `grep`) are auto-approved. We must ensure this does not read from protected spaces or outside our trusted workspaces.
2. **Edits:** Commands that mutate the sandboxed filesystem (e.g., `sed -i`, `>`) trigger a post-execution Diff UI before the changes are synced back to the host, allowing for a seamless "Edit" tool experience using the model's preferred mechanisms. 
3. **Side-Effects:** A dynamic command router will handle commands requiring host credentials or network access (e.g., `git`, `gh`), completely bypassing the sandbox but requiring strict upfront user confirmation (i.e., stays the same as today, utilizing the policy engine to execute or ask for user confirmation).

## Architectural Mandates
In order to support this properly, we must explore, investigate, and implement the proper sandboxing for all major platforms: Linux, macOS, and Windows.

## Epic
This is an epic that tracks this investigation and implementation. It will contain subtasks used to track progress towards its overall completion. After initial investigation, if this is not a feasible route, the epic can be marked as closed.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Current context baseline is approximately 36.6k tokens per turn. Large file reads often 'firehose' the context, leading to bloat (previously observed at +15k tokens/turn). 

The goal of 'Tactful Extraction' is to establish a surgical code-discovery hierarchy:
1. **grep_search**: Primary scout for locating symbols.
2. **shell/sed**: scalpel for semantic block extraction (preferred for specific line ranges).
3. **read_file**: surgical range-reading (migrated to 1-based start/end lines).

Telemetry indicates that making ~2.1% more targeted tool calls results in a ~6.9% reduction in total input tokens.

## Changes

- **read_file migration**: Switched from 0-based 'offset'/'limit' to 1-based 'start_line'/'end_line' for better model alignment.
- **Surgical Guidance**: Updated tool descriptions and system prompts to mandate 'token-frugal' behavior.
- **Tool Hierarchy**: Emphasized the use of 'grep_search' and 'sed' via 'run_shell_command' for efficient context management.

## Status

This work is temporarily sidelined in favor of other priorities but remains a key architectural goal for efficiency.

Linked Draft PR: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/18924

type.description: Related Changes across multiple feature sets

issues.body:
The current WriteToDo tool relies on "in-context" task tracking, which maintains the todo list solely within the LLM's conversation history (prompt context). This creates issues with "context rot," high token costs, and total memory loss between sessions.

This issue proposes deprecating WriteToDo in favor of a persistent task tracking system (e.g., a local tasks.json) that allows the agent to maintain state across restarts and manage complex dependencies.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a new set of tools backed by a persistent local file (e.g., .gemini/tasks.json) to replace WriteToDo.

1. New Tool Definitions
The agent should have access to specific CRUD tools rather than just "writing" a list:
task_add(description: str, priority: str, dependency_id: int)
task_list(filter: str) (e.g., "show only 'ready' tasks")
task_update(id: int, status: str)
task_complete(id: int)

2. Storage Backend
Tasks should be serialized to a local file  in the working directory.

Benefits
1. Persistence: The agent can pick up exactly where it left off after a restart.
2. Efficiency: We stop burning tokens passing the entire completed history back and forth. The agent only queries task_list when it needs to know what to do next.
3. Complexity: Enables multi-step reasoning where the agent can plan out 20 steps and execute them over several days.

Address concerns and suggestions in https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/17035 
Doc [go/tracker-gemini-cli](http://goto.google.com/tracker-gemini-cli)

prs.title: fix(core): require path-separator boundary in tildeifyPath
prs.body:
## Summary

    Prevent `tildeifyPath()` from corrupting sibling directory paths whose names share a character prefix with the current user's home directory (for example, turning `/Users/albert/proj` into `~bert/proj` when `homedir()` is `/Users/al`, or `C:\Users\Albert\proj` into `~bert\proj` when home is `C:\Users\Al`). This fixes misleading workspace and log paths rendered in the CLI status footer (`Footer.tsx`) and background task display (`BackgroundTaskDisplay.tsx`).

## Details

    - **Path-segment boundary enforcement (`packages/core/src/utils/paths.ts`):** Update `tildeifyPath()` to replace the home prefix with `~` only when `filePath` exactly equals the home directory or is immediately followed by a valid platform path separator (`/` on POSIX; `/` or `\` on Windows).
    - **Home prefix normalization & root guards:** Trim trailing separators from `homedir()` (e.g., `GEMINI_CLI_HOME="/Users/al/"` or `"C:\\Users\\Al\\"`) so valid descendants still format as `~/...`, and leave filesystem/drive roots (`/` on POSIX, `C:\` / `C:/` on Windows) untouched so system paths are never rewritten to `~...`.
    - **Platform semantics:** Preserve the caller's separator style (`\` vs `/`), match Windows home prefixes case-insensitively (`c:\users\al\proj`), and keep `\` as a literal filename character on POSIX.
    - **Test coverage (`packages/core/src/utils/paths.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/ui/components/Footer.test.tsx`):** Add 16 unit tests covering POSIX and Windows exact matches, descendant paths, sibling-prefix non-matches, trailing home slashes, root home guards, mixed separators, Windows case-insensitivity, and UNC paths, plus a `<Footer />` UI regression test.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29175

## How to Validate

prs.title: fix: handle RangeError when conversation exceeds JSON serializable size
prs.body:
## Problem

When `JSON.stringify` is called on a very large conversation object, V8 throws a `RangeError: Invalid string length`. This was not caught by the existing error handler in `appendRecord`, causing an unhandled rejection that crashed the CLI.

Fixes #24902

## Solution

Mirror the existing `ENOSPC` pattern in `appendRecord`:
- Catch `RangeError` alongside `ENOSPC`
- Disable chat recording (`this.conversationFile = null`)
- Emit a warning via `debugLogger.warn`
- Allow the conversation to continue uninterrupted

## Changes

- `chatRecordingService.ts`: Add `RANGE_WARNING_MESSAGE` constant and `RangeError` branch in `appendRecord` catch block
- `chatRecordingService.test.ts`: Add two tests covering graceful degradation and subsequent no-op behaviour

## Summary

Fixes #29825.

When an MCP server exposes more tools than fit in a single page, `discoverTools` in `packages/core/src/tools/mcp-client.ts` only requested the first page and silently dropped the rest, because the `nextCursor` token returned by `tools/list` was ignored.

prs.title: fix(core): paginate MCP tool discovery safely
prs.body:
## Summary

MCP servers that paginate `tools/list` currently expose only their first page of tools to Gemini CLI. Fetch every page before constructing the discovered catalog so initial discovery and dynamic refresh include the complete set of tools.

## Details

- Forward the request timeout and abort signal on every page, and stop on cancellation.
- Treat cursors as opaque strings, including an empty string, and reject repeated cursor cycles.
- Preserve filtering, schema conversion, and the first-page `MethodNotFound` fallback. Errors on later pages propagate so a refresh keeps the existing catalog instead of publishing partial results.
- Add regression coverage for single and multiple pages, empty pages, filtering, cancellation, cursor cycles, successful refresh, and later-page failures. Update the MCP discovery documentation.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29825.

Also related to #29843, which addresses the same report. This PR includes regression coverage and handles cancellation, cursor cycles, and failure on a later page.

## How to Validate

The original source failed the new pagination and later-page refresh regression cases before the implementation change.

```bash
npm exec -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- vitest run src/tools/mcp-client.test.ts src/tools/tool-registry.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false --reporter=dot
```

- The focused MCP client and tool-registry suites pass: **125 tests**.

prs.title: fix(cli): support GitHub repository shorthand for extension installation
prs.body: ## Summary Enables support for GitHub repository shorthand (`owner/repo`, `github.com/owner/repo`, and `github:owner/repo`) when installing extensions via `gemini extensions install `. Previously, running: ```bash gemini extensions install PaddleHQ/paddle-agent-skills ``` failed with: ``` Error: Install source not found. ``` and with `--ref` / `--auto-update` flags: ``` Error: --ref and --auto-update are not applicable for local extensions. ``` This PR resolves this issue by recognizing valid GitHub repository shorthand patterns in `inferInstallMetadata()` and normalizing them into canonical HTTPS URLs (`https://github.com//`), while preserving local directory installation behavior. --- ## Details 1. **`packages/cli/src/config/extension-manager.ts`**: - Added regex pattern `GITHUB_REPO_PATTERN = /^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-_]*\/[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$/` to recognize bare `owner/repo` shorthands. - Normalized `github:/` and `github.com//` prefixes to `https://github.com//`. - When a source matches `GITHUB_REPO_PATTERN`: - If Git-specific flags (`--ref`, `--auto-update`) are specified, it is directly inferred as a remote Git source (`type: 'git'`). - If no Git flags are given, it first checks if a local directory exists at that path (`stat(source)`). If it exists, local directory behavior is preserved (`type: 'local'`); otherwise, it normalizes to `https://github.com//` and installs from Git. - Ensures downstream components (release asset downloading via `downloadFromGitHubRelease`, fallback Git clone via `cloneFromGit`, and GitHub token authentication) receive a valid remote URL. 2. **`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.ts`**: - Updated `tryParseGithubUrl()` to strip `github:` and `github.com/` prefixes before parsing, aligning with `inferInstallMetadata()`. 3. **`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.test.ts`**: - Added test cases in `tryParseGithubUrl` parameterized tests for `github.com/owner/repo` and `github:owner/repo`. 4. **`packages/cli/src/config/extension-manager.test.ts`**: - Added a test suite for `inferInstallMetadata()` covering: - Standard Git URLs (`https://`, `http://`, `git@`, `sso://`, `gitlab:`, `ssh://`) - `github:PaddleHQ/paddle-agent-skills` normalization - `github.com/user/repo` normalization - Bare `owner/repo` shorthand with and without flags (`--ref`, `--auto-update`, `--pre-release`) - Preserving existing local directory paths (including matching `owner/repo` patterns) - Rejecting non-existent local paths and local paths with `--ref`/`--auto-update` --- ## Related Issues Fixes #29814 --- ## How to Validate 1. Run unit tests: ```bash npm test --workspace=@google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extensions/github.test.ts src/config/extension-manager.test.ts npm test --workspace=@google/gemini-cli -- src/commands/extensions/install.test.ts ``` 2. Validate bare shorthand installation: ```bash node packages/cli/dist/src/index.js extensions install PaddleHQ/paddle-agent-skills ``` Or with `--ref`: ```bash node packages/cli/dist/src/index.js extensions install PaddleHQ/paddle-agent-skills --ref main ``` 3. Validate local directory installation remains unaffected: ```bash node packages/cli/dist/src/index.js extensions install ./path/to/local/extension ``` --- ## Pre-Merge Checklist - [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed) - [x] Added/updated tests (if needed) - [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any) - [x] Validated on required platforms/methods: - [x] MacOS - [x] npm run - [x] npx - [x] Docker - [ ] Podman - [ ] Seatbelt - [ ] Windows - [ ] npm run - [ ] npx - [ ] Docker - [ ] Linux - [ ] npm run - [ ] npx - [ ] Docker

prs.title: fix(cli): normalize error payloads in headless CLI formatting
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->
Introduces a centralized error normalization utility in `@google/gemini-cli-core` and a context-aware CLI error formatter in
`@google/gemini-cli` so headless execution (`gemini -p "<prompt>"`) emits deterministic, human-readable diagnostic messages and status codes instead of `[object Object]` when structured or transport error payloads propagate to the
top-level CLI handler.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->

- **Core Error Normalization (`packages/core/src/utils/errors.ts`)**:
  - Added `normalizeError(error: unknown): NormalizedErrorInfo` to deterministically extract `message`, `status`, `code`, `details`, and `originalError` across `StructuredError` objects, Google Cloud / Gaxios HTTP error envelopes, OAuth2 error payloads, JSON-RPC error structures, ES2022 `Error.cause` chains, primitive values, and empty inputs.
  - Added `safeSerializeErrorValue(value: unknown, space?: number)` to serialize non-standard and circular objects deterministically while redacting credential header fields and omitting HTTP socket/agent handles.
- **Context-Aware CLI Error Formatting
  (`packages/cli/src/utils/formatError.ts`)**:
  - Added `formatCliError(error, options)` and `isCliDebugEnabled()` to produce concise single-line `stderr` diagnostics
    (`<prefix><message> (Status: <status>)`) during standard execution and full stack traces or structured debug context when `--debug` (`-d`) or `DEBUG=1` / `DEBUG_MODE=true` is enabled.
- **Headless Error Propagation, Startup Auth Logging & Top-Level Catch
  Integration (`packages/cli/src/nonInteractiveCli.ts`, `packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx`, `packages/cli/index.ts`)**:
  - Updated `GeminiEventType.Error` handling in `runNonInteractive` to construct a standard `Error` instance from `normalizeError(event.value.error)` while preserving numeric `status`, `code`, and `details` properties for downstream     `JSON`, `STREAM_JSON`, and `TEXT` error handlers.
  - Updated pre-sandbox `refreshAuth` error handling in `packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx` to log raw authentication errors at `debug` level instead of `error` level and format pre-sandbox exit diagnostics through `formatCliError`, avoiding unformatted intermediate transport object output before top-level error formatting runs.
  - Updated the child-process top-level `.catch()` handler in `packages/cli/index.ts` to format non-`FatalError` exceptions through `formatCliError`, preserving `FatalError` exit codes and lightweight parent-process startup.
- **Unit Test Coverage**:
  - Added unit tests in `packages/core/src/utils/errors.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/formatError.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts`, and `packages/cli/src/gemini.test.tsx` covering `StructuredError`, Gaxios responses, OAuth2/JSON-RPC payloads, `Error.cause` chains, primitives, circular references, `--debug` mode formatting, pre-sandbox auth error formatting, and non-interactive `TEXT`/`JSON` error propagation.

## Related Issues

only related to an issue or is a partial fix, simply reference the issue number
without a keyword (Related to #123). -->

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/errors.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/utils/formatError.test.ts src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts src/gemini.test.tsx
   ```

prs.title: fix(core): load agents from symlinked markdown files
prs.body:
## Summary

Agent definitions in `~/.gemini/agents/` (or a project's `.gemini/agents/`) are skipped when the `.md` file is a symlink. `loadAgentsFromDirectory()` filters directory entries with `Dirent.isFile()`, which returns `false` for symlinks, so linked agent files never get read.

## Details

The filter now also accepts entries where `isSymbolicLink()` is true. The file is then read through `fs.readFile`, which follows the link. If the link is broken or points to something that isn't a readable file, the read fails and the error is reported as an `AgentLoadError` like any other bad agent file, so it isn't skipped silently.

## Related Issues

Fixes #20079

## How to Validate

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/agents/agentLoader.test.ts`. The new test `should load agents from symlinked markdown files` symlinks `linked.md` to a real agent file and checks that the agent is loaded. It fails without the change and passes with it.
2. Manual check: `ln -s /path/to/my-agent.md ~/.gemini/agents/my-agent.md`, then start `gemini`. The agent is now listed.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): supply --userns=keep-id for rootless podman
prs.body:
## Summary

In container sandbox mode under rootless Podman on Linux, container UIDs above 0 map into subordinate host UIDs allocated in `/etc/subuid`. Files created inside the bind-mounted workspace during native builds or cache operations inherit subordinate UID ownership, which leads to `EACCES` file access errors when they are modified or removed by the host user.

This change detects rootless Podman execution and automatically passes `--userns=keep-id` when the sandbox runs as the host UID/GID (`shouldUseCurrentUserInSandbox()`), so the sandbox user maps 1:1 to the host user, unless a `--userns` option is already specified in `SANDBOX_FLAGS`.

## Details

- **Rootless Podman detection (`packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox.ts`)**: Added async `isPodmanRootless()`, which runs `podman info --format '{{.Host.Security.Rootless}}'` through the non-blocking `execFile` API with a 5 second timeout and falls back to `{{.Host.ServiceIsRootless}}` when the first property is empty or unsupported. It returns `false` if `podman info` fails, and skips the fallback query when `podman` is not installed or the query times out.
- **User namespace mapping (`packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox.ts`)**: On the `shouldUseCurrentUserInSandbox()` path, where the sandbox starts as root and the entrypoint switches to the host UID/GID, appends `--userns=keep-id` when the sandbox command is `podman`, Podman runs in rootless mode, and `SANDBOX_FLAGS` contains no `--userns` option (`--userns=<mode>` or `--userns <mode>`).
  - Under `keep-id`, container root maps to a subordinate host UID. Integration test runs (`GEMINI_CLI_INTEGRATION_TEST=true`), which stay as container root, and runs with `SANDBOX_SET_UID_GID=false` therefore keep the default rootless user namespace, where container root maps to the host user.
  - Behavior is unchanged for Docker, macOS Seatbelt, and rootful Podman.
- **Unit tests (`packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox.test.ts`)**: Added tests covering:
  - Detection of rootless vs. rootful Podman, including the fallback property, the timeout options, and stopping early when `podman` is missing or the query times out.
  - `--userns=keep-id` is added for rootless Podman when the sandbox runs as the host user and no `--userns` flag is provided.
  - A user-provided `--userns` option in `SANDBOX_FLAGS` is preserved without adding a duplicate.
  - The flag is not added for integration test runs or when `SANDBOX_SET_UID_GID=false`.
  - The rootless check is skipped for Docker and macOS Seatbelt runtimes.
- **Documentation (`docs/cli/sandbox.md`)**: Documented when `--userns=keep-id` is applied under "Linux UID/GID handling".

## Related Issues

Fixes #29338

## How to Validate

1. Run the sandbox unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/utils/sandbox.test.ts
   ```
   Expected result: All 65 tests in `sandbox.test.ts` pass, including the `Podman rootless user namespace mapping` suite.
2. Run typecheck and lint:

   ```bash
   npm run typecheck
   npm run lint
   ```

prs.title: fix(cli): await history replay before responding to ACP session/load
prs.body:
## Summary

Awaits `session.streamHistory(messages)` in `AcpSessionManager.loadSession` before returning the `session/load` response so that all replayed conversation history updates are delivered to the ACP client prior to the `session/load` response, as required by the ACP specification.

## Details

 - **Await history replay in `AcpSessionManager.loadSession` (`packages/cli/src/acp/acpSessionManager.ts`)**:
      - Replaced the unawaited `session.streamHistory(messages).catch(...)` call with an `await session.streamHistory(messages)` wrapped in a `try / catch` block before returning `response`.
     - Preserved the existing log-and-continue error handling (`debugLogger.error(\`Error streaming history: \${err}\`)`) so that a replay stream failure does not enter the outer `catch` block or dispose/delete the restored session.
    - **Verify replay ordering & error resilience in `AcpSessionManager` unit tests (`packages/cli/src/acp/acpSessionManager.test.ts`)**:
     - Updated `'should load an existing session'` to mock `mockConnection.sessionUpdate` with an async delay and record execution order (`update:user_message_chunk`, `update:agent_message_chunk`, `loadSession:resolved`), verifying all history updates complete before `loadSession` resolves.
      - Added `'should log error and still return response when streamHistory fails during loadSession'` to verify that if `mockConnection.sessionUpdate` rejects during replay, `loadSession` logs the error via `debugLogger.error`, retains the loaded session in `manager.getSession(sessionId)`, and still resolves with `response`.
      - Updated the `node:crypto` mock to preserve original module exports via `importOriginal` while stubbing `randomUUID`.
    - **Synchronous history assertions in resume tests (`packages/cli/src/acp/acpResume.test.ts`)**:
     - Removed the `waitFor` polling wrapper from `'should load a session and stream its history'` so that all replayed `sessionUpdate` assertions (`user_message_chunk`, `agent_thought_chunk`, `agent_message_chunk`, completed `tool_call`, and failed `tool_call`) are verified immediately after `await agent.loadSession(...)` resolves.

prs.title: fix(core): fix Windows PowerShell substitution false positives and policy handling
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes severe Windows PowerShell shell-command regressions introduced in v0.63.0 where routine developer commands containing parentheses in arguments, method/static calls, control-flow headers, or `-NonInteractive` shell wrappers were falsely blocked as command substitutions, and where explicitly user-confirmed or policy-allowed (`--yolo` / `allowCommandSubstitution = true`) substitutions were still unconditionally blocked in `ShellToolInvocation.execute()`.

## Details

- **Linear-time (`O(N)`) PowerShell substitution scanner (`packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts`)**:
  - Rewrote `detectPowerShellSubstitution` as a stateful character/token scanner that tracks PowerShell quoting rules (ASCII + Unicode single/double quotes, backtick escapes inside double quotes, `@'...'@` and `@"..."@` here-strings, `#` line comments, `<# ... #>` block comments, and `${...}` braced variables).
  - Properly distinguishes safe PowerShell parentheses (command string/path arguments like `dir C:\Program Files (x86)\Git` or `git log --grep="\"(feat|fix)\""`, instance/static calls like `$str.Trim()` and `[System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath('foo')`, control-flow headers like `if (...)` / `switch -regex ($x)`, and pure parenthesized expressions) from actual command substitutions (`$(...)`, `@(...)`, bare `(whoami)` subexpressions, and scriptblock `.Invoke()`).
  - Rejects comment-spoofed closing parentheses (`echo ($a <# ) #> ; whoami)`), redirections, assignments, pipelines, and nested here-strings inside parenthesized expressions, and enforces monotonic lookahead watermarks to guarantee `O(N)` runtime without ReDoS risk.
- **Shell wrapper unwrapping & `pwsh.exe` flags (`packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts`)**:
  - Rewrote `stripShellWrapper` with token-level scanners supporting full executable paths, `.exe` suffixes, `-NonInteractive` / PowerShell parameter prefixes, and `powershell.exe` / `pwsh.exe` / `cmd.exe` / POSIX shells while refusing to unwrap double-quoted wrappers when outer-shell `$()` substitution would become hidden inside inner single quotes.
  - Updated `getShellConfiguration` so `pwsh.exe` also receives `-NonInteractive` alongside `-NoProfile` and `-Command`.
  - Updated `extractPowerShellDetails` to extract static and scriptblock `.Invoke()` calls and propagate `hasCommandSubstitution` without falling back to the Bash parser on PowerShell substitution syntax.
- **Policy-aware & confirmation-aware substitution handling (`packages/core/src/policy/*`, `packages/core/src/scheduler/*`, `packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`)**:
  - Added `allowCommandSubstitution` support to policy rules (`yolo.toml`, `toml-loader.ts`, `policy-engine.ts`, `config.ts`, `docs/reference/policy-engine.md`).
  - Propagated `confirmedByUser` / `isUserConfirmed` through `resolveConfirmation`, `Scheduler`, and `ToolExecutor` strictly when a user interactively approves a confirmation prompt (resetting across `ModifyWithEditor` edits).
  - Updated `ShellToolInvocation` so commands with command substitution are permitted only when explicitly confirmed by the user or explicitly allowed by policy (`allowCommandSubstitution = true`), while unconfirmed or untrusted/tainted substitutions continue to be denied.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29738

## How to Validate

1. Run unit and policy safety test suites:
   ```bash
   npx vitest run \
     packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/tools/shell.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/policy/shell-safety.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/policy/policy-updater.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/scheduler/confirmation.test.ts
   ```
2. Verify PowerShell false positives from #29738 are no longer flagged as command substitution while real substitutions remain detected:
   - Allowed (`false`): `node -e "console.log(\"hello (world)\")"`, `git log --grep="\"(feat|fix)\""`, `$str.Trim()`, `[System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath('foo')`, `Get-ChildItem | Where-Object { $_.Name.EndsWith('.ts') }`, `dir C:\Program Files (x86)\Git`, `if (($a -eq 1) -and ($b -eq 2)) { Write-Host ok }`
   - Flagged (`true`): `echo $(whoami)`, `echo "$(whoami)"`, `echo @(whoami)`, `echo (whoami)`, `{ whoami }.Invoke()`
3. Verify policy enforcement with the bundled CLI:
   - With `allowCommandSubstitution` omitted (`false`), `run_shell_command` with `echo $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)` prompts (`ASK_USER`) in interactive mode and is denied in non-interactive `--approval-mode default`.
   - With `--yolo` or a policy rule setting `allowCommandSubstitution = true` for all inner and outer commands, `echo $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)` executes as configured.

prs.title: fix(core): preserve explicit gemini-2.5-flash model in dynamic model resolution
prs.body:
When `gemini-2.5-flash` is explicitly specified (e.g. via `--model gemini-2.5-flash` or `/model`) with dynamic model configuration enabled and `useLatestFlash` active (such as on Vertex AI or Gemini API key authentication where `hasLatestFlashGAAccess()` returns `true`), `DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS.modelIdResolutions['gemini-2.5-flash']` (`packages/core/src/config/defaultModelConfigs.ts`) previously rewrote `'gemini-2.5-flash'` to `LATEST_GEMINI_FLASH_MODEL`.

This caused explicit requests for `gemini-2.5-flash` in dynamic configuration mode to resolve to the latest Gemini 3 Flash model instead of preserving `gemini-2.5-flash`, diverging from the static resolution behavior in `models.ts` (`isPromotableFlashModel`) and deduplicating `gemini-2.5-flash` out of `ModelConfigService.getAvailableModelOptions()`.

This change removes the `useLatestFlash` promotion rule from `DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS.modelIdResolutions['gemini-2.5-flash']` so that explicit `gemini-2.5-flash` selections are preserved consistently across both static and dynamic model configurations, while keeping generic `'flash'` alias and base Flash tier promotions intact.

## Details

- **`DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS.modelIdResolutions['gemini-2.5-flash']` (`packages/core/src/config/defaultModelConfigs.ts`)**:
  - Removes the `contexts` entry that mapped `'gemini-2.5-flash'` to `LATEST_GEMINI_FLASH_MODEL` when `useLatestFlash: true`, preserving `'gemini-2.5-flash'` as its concrete model ID.
- **Generated Settings Schema & Documentation (`schemas/settings.schema.json`, `docs/reference/configuration.md`)**:
  - Regenerates the settings JSON schema and reference documentation (`npm run schema:settings` and `npm run docs:settings`) to stay in sync with `DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS`.
- **Unit Test Coverage**:
  - `packages/core/src/config/models.test.ts`: Verifies that explicit versioned models (`gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`, `gemini-3.6-flash`, etc.) are preserved when `useLatestFlash` / `useGemini3_5Flash` is `true` in both static and dynamic configuration modes, and includes `gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` in dynamic configuration parity checks.
  - `packages/core/src/services/modelConfigService.test.ts`: Verifies `ModelConfigService.resolveModelId('gemini-2.5-flash', ...)` and `ModelConfigService.getAvailableModelOptions({ useLatestFlash: true })` preserve `gemini-2.5-flash` in `DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS`.
  - `packages/core/src/availability/policyHelpers.test.ts`: Verifies `resolvePolicyChain` parity between static and dynamic configurations for `gemini-2.5-flash` with and without `useLatestFlash` enabled.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29213

## How to Validate

1. **Automated Unit Tests**:

prs.title: feat(cli): support standalone theme.json configuration for custom themes
prs.body:
Decouples custom color theme definitions from behavioral preferences in `settings.json` by automatically discovering standalone `theme.json` files from `~/.gemini/theme.json` and XDG fallback paths (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gemini/theme.json` and `~/.config/gemini/theme.json`). This allows dynamic palette generators (such as `wallust`, `pywal`, and `matugen`) to regenerate color palettes independently without overwriting user preferences like `vimMode`, model configuration, or authentication settings in `settings.json`.

## Details

- **Standalone `theme.json` Discovery (`packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme-manager.ts`)**:
  - Added `getUserThemePaths()` and `loadUserThemes()` to `ThemeManager` to discover standalone theme definitions from `~/.gemini/theme.json` (respecting `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` via `homedir()`) with fallback to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gemini/theme.json` and `~/.config/gemini/theme.json`.
  - Supports single theme objects, named theme catalog maps (`Record<string, CustomTheme>`), and `customThemes`-wrapped objects, with JSON comment support via `stripJsonComments`.
  - Enforces directory boundary checks on resolved canonical paths (`realpathSync`) so symlinks resolving outside trusted user configuration directories are skipped with a warning.
  - Gives `~/.gemini/theme.json` precedence over XDG paths and inline `settings.json` `customThemes`, deduplicating entries in `getAvailableThemes()` while keeping `settings.json` persistence completely untouched when behavioral settings or `ui.theme` are saved.
- **Startup & Interactive Refresh (`packages/cli/src/utils/terminalTheme.ts`, `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useThemeCommand.ts`)**:
  - Calls `themeManager.loadUserThemes()` during `setupTerminalAndTheme` and refreshes standalone user themes when opening `/theme` or selecting a theme so external palette updates can be picked up during an active session.
- **Storage & macOS Seatbelt Configuration (`packages/core/src/config/storage.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/sandboxBuiltinProfiles.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox-macos-*.sb`)**:
  - Added `Storage.getUserThemePath()` alongside `Storage.getUserKeybindingsPath()`.
  - Permitted read-only access to `~/.gemini/theme.json` in restrictive and strict macOS Seatbelt profiles (matching `settings.json` and `keybindings.json`).
- **Documentation & Tests**:
  - Documented standalone `theme.json` usage and XDG fallback paths in `docs/cli/themes.md`.
  - Added unit tests in `packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme-manager.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox-macos-profiles.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/sandboxUtils.test.ts`, and `packages/cli/src/utils/terminalTheme.test.ts`.

## Related Issues

## How to Validate

### Automated Tests

1. Run targeted unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/themes/theme-manager.test.ts src/utils/terminalTheme.test.ts src/utils/sandbox-macos-profiles.test.ts src/utils/sandboxUtils.test.ts
   ```
2. Run full preflight checks:

   ```json
       "name": "custom-wallust",
       "type": "custom",
       "background": {
         "primary": "#1d2021"
       },
   ```

prs.title: fix(core,cli): prevent $-pattern expansion in custom command and prompt substitutions
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes an issue where custom command `{{args}}` and system prompt substitutions (`${AgentSkills}`, `${SubAgents}`, `${AvailableTools}`) expand JavaScript `$` replacement patterns (such as `$$`, `$&`, `$'`, `$` `, and `$1`), corrupting user arguments and template text.

Fixes #30105

## Details
In `packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.ts` and `packages/core/src/prompts/utils.ts`, user input and dynamic system prompt variables were passed as replacement strings directly into `String.prototype.replaceAll` and `String.prototype.replace`. In JavaScript, string-based replacements treat `$` sequences as special patterns (e.g. `$$` collapses to `$`, and `$&` inserts the placeholder itself).

This fix:
- Replaces direct replacement strings with replacer callbacks (`() => value`) across `shellProcessor.ts` and `applySubstitutions` in `utils.ts`, ensuring literal string interpolation without pattern interpretation.
- Adds comprehensive unit tests in `shellProcessor.test.ts` (verifying `$` patterns in both raw `{{args}}` and inside/outside `!{}` shell injection blocks).
- Adds unit tests in `utils.test.ts` (verifying `$` patterns in `${AgentSkills}` and `${AvailableTools}`).

## Related Issues
Fixes #30105

## How to Validate
Run the test suites in `packages/cli` and `packages/core`:
```bash
npx vitest run src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.test.ts --coverage false
npx vitest run src/prompts/utils.test.ts --coverage false
```
Expected: All tests pass, including the new tests asserting literal preservation of `$$`, `$&`, `$'`, and `$1`.

prs.title: fix(cli): handle stream failures during extension release downloads
prs.body:
## Summary

Handle stream failures, partial-file cleanup, SSRF/redirect hardening, and socket timeouts during extension release downloads in `downloadFile` (`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.ts`).

Previously, `downloadFile` piped the HTTP response stream via `res.pipe(file)` without error listeners on either `res` or `file`, wrote directly to `dest`, and only resolved on `file.on('finish')`. As a result, disk/permission errors (`EACCES`/`ENOSPC`) crashed the CLI with an unhandled `'error'` event, truncated connections (`aborted`/premature `close`) hung the download promise indefinitely, and mid-transfer failures left corrupt partial archives on disk.

## Details

- **Stream pipeline & atomic staging:** Stream `200 OK` responses with `pipeline(res, file)` (`node:stream/promises`) to a temporary staging file (`${dest}.${crypto.randomUUID()}.tmp`), reject truncated transfers (`res.complete === false`), atomically move completed archives into place via `fs.promises.rename`, and await stream teardown before `fs.promises.unlink` cleanup on failure.
- **Single-settlement error handling:** Settle the download promise once with the first error across `req`, `res`, `file`, and `pipeline`, while absorbing secondary teardown errors and draining non-`200` / redirect responses (`res.resume()`).
- **SSRF & DNS-rebinding protection:** Validate initial and redirected URLs with `validateUrlDestination` from `@google/gemini-cli-core` and pass `lookupPublicAddress` (`safeLookup`) to `https.get` (shared with `github_fetch.ts`).
- **Token scoping & redirect parity:** Scope `GITHUB_TOKEN` (and strip `Authorization` headers) strictly to HTTPS `github.com` and `*.github.com` hosts (`isTrustedGitHubUrl`) so tokens are never leaked on redirects to external asset hosts (e.g., S3 / `objects.githubusercontent.com`). Support `301`, `302`, `303`, `307`, and `308` redirects and resolve relative `Location` headers against the request URL.
- **Socket inactivity timeout:** Configure a `30000`ms request timeout (`REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`) and handle `'timeout'` events by rejecting with `'Request timed out after 30000ms'`, tearing down streams, cleaning up partial `.tmp` files, and releasing sockets.

## Related Issues

Fixes #28645

## How to Validate

1. Run unit tests for extension GitHub fetching and downloads:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extensions/github.test.ts src/config/extensions/github_fetch.test.ts
   ```
2. Run lint and build checks:
   ```bash
   npm run lint
   npm run build -w @google/gemini-cli
   ```

prs.title: fix(core): cap grep_search output size and tell the model to narrow broad searches
prs.body:
## Summary

A broad `grep_search` can still send the model far more text than it can use. The match cap limits how many lines come back, not how big they are: with the default 100 matches over long log or minified lines, the tool builds about 150K characters today. The executor's generic 64KB cap then cuts that mid-line and tells the model to read the full output from a file, which is the opposite of what you want after a search that's too broad. This PR bounds grep output by size inside the tool and tells the model to narrow the search instead.

## Details

- `formatGrepResults` stops adding lines once the output would pass `MAX_GREP_OUTPUT_CHARS` (40,000 characters). It always cuts on a whole line and closes the file block, so the result stays well formed.
- When it cuts, it adds a short notice saying how many matches (or files, for `names_only`) were shown out of how many, and suggests a more specific pattern, `include_pattern`, `dir_path`, or `names_only`.
- If context lines are what doesn't fit, it drops them first and keeps the matches. That matters for the 1 to 3 match auto-context case on files with long lines, where 50 context lines can push the match itself out.
- 40,000 is the default `tools.truncateToolOutputThreshold` and the distillation threshold (10,000 tokens x 4), and it's under `MAX_STORED_TOOL_OUTPUT_BYTES`, so for normal text the generic truncation no longer fires on grep.
- Results under the budget are byte-for-byte the same as before, and the existing grep and ripgrep tests pass unchanged. The `(limited)` summary also shows when output was cut for size.

This complements #29822, which caps `total_max_matches` and rewords the overflow message. They don't overlap: 5000 matches of 120-character lines is still about 640K characters, and this is what bounds that.

## Related Issues

Related to #17448

The core of that report (one search sending ~41M tokens) can't happen on main anymore. The default match cap (#17146), per-line truncation (#21147) and the 64KB tool output cap (#29451) bound it, and the pre-send check has blocked oversized requests since #10459. This PR covers the "agent should refine its search" part; the UI wording is in #29822, which should be the one that closes the issue.

## How to Validate

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/tools/grep-utils.test.ts src/tools/grep.test.ts src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts`
2. On main, the new tests fail. The two end-to-end ones report 151,330 and 152,905 characters for a default search over long lines.
3. Manual: in a folder with a few files of long lines that share a word, ask the agent to search for it. The result ends with "Output truncated: showing N of 100 matches..." and stays under 40,000 characters.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any): none, output under the budget is unchanged
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods (unit tests ran on macOS; no manual CLI run yet)

prs.title: fix(core): drop tool calls streamed by failed attempts on retry
prs.body:
## Summary

On a mid-stream retry, `GeminiChat` has already yielded the failed attempt's chunks, while only the successful attempt's model turn is written to history. Every front end collected `ToolCallRequest` events from both attempts, executed both calls and answered both. A side-effecting command therefore ran twice, and the extra `functionResponse` no longer matched the model turn, so the next request failed with `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` and every later request in the session was rejected too.

This implements the existing `RETRY` contract ("The UI should discard any partial content from the attempt that just failed") for tool calls in every consumer.

## Details

- `core/Turn`: reset `pendingToolCalls` when a retry is signalled, so calls that never entered history are not reported as pending.
- ACP (`acpSession`), interactive UI (`useGeminiStream`, including `pendingToolCallRequestsRef`), headless (`nonInteractiveCli`), a2a-server (`executor`) and the subagent `LocalAgentExecutor`: drop the collected tool call requests on `Retry`.
- No behavior change when a turn is not retried; clearing only happens when the backend signals a retry.
- Out of scope (unchanged): partial text from a failed attempt is still displayed, and headless stream-json may still emit a `tool_use` event for a call that is dropped.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30014

## How to Validate

Each new test streams a tool call, then `Retry`, then a second call, and asserts that exactly one call is executed and answered. All of them fail without the source change.

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/turn.test.ts src/agents/local-executor.test.ts
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp/acpSession.test.ts src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx
cd packages/a2a-server && npx vitest run src/agent/executor.test.ts
```

Additional checks:

- `tsc --noEmit` (core/cli/a2a), `eslint --max-warnings 0` and `prettier --check` pass.
- Full `@google/gemini-cli-core` suite: 8555 passed. The single failure is the pre-existing macOS-only `/dev/ttys001` test from #30008.
- Full a2a-server suite: 183 passed.
- Affected suites also pass in a Linux Docker container (`node:22-bookworm`, linux/arm64) after a clean `npm ci` + `npm run build`.

## 中文说明

修复 #30014。流式中途重试时，失败 attempt 的 tool call 已经发给前端但不会进入 history，导致同一命令被执行两次，且多余的 functionResponse 与 history 不匹配，后续请求持续 400。现在各前端在收到 `Retry` 时丢弃失败 attempt 收集到的调用，并清空 `Turn.pendingToolCalls`；无重试时行为不变。

issues.title: Support opening reports and plans when there are multiple in a session

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

The ctrl+y key binding opens the plan, or the most recent report only if there is no plan. There is no way to reference or open other reports that have been generated previously, or any reports after a plan has been generated.

### Proposed solution

An `/open` command to provide a pick-list of the reports and plans that have been generated during the conversation, shown in chronological order. Picking one of them opens that markdown file using the normal viewer.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. Run a `/research` command on a topic, and see that it generates a markdown report
2. Run another `/research` command on a different topic, and see that it genrates a markdown report.The Ctrl+y opens only the most recent report markdown.
3. Use the (proposed) `/open` slash-command, and pick the older research report to view. Exit viewing when done.
4. Run a `/plan` command, and see it generates a markdown plan and that Ctrl+y can only open it.
5. Run a `/research` command to ask probing questions about something in the plan. See that it creates a research markdown report, but ctrl+y is can still only open the plan.
6. Use the (proposed) `/open` slash-command, and pick the first, second, or most recent research report to view.

### Additional context

There's currently only a `ctrl+y` key binding to show a markdown file that generated by the session. If a plan has been generated, that markdown file is always used instead of any research reports. There is no way to select which markdown file when there are multiple present.  

The current solution is to locate the full report file name listed in the history, and copy the path from the history output. Then open that file manually using some other tool. 

This is particularly annoying if you ran any `/research` commands after having generated a plan, because all new research reports are effectively inaccessible.
