issues.title: "Connected Connectors could not be loaded" on every interactive session, but succeeds in headless -p mode; underlying error only logged at debug level

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Summary

Every **interactive** CLI session prints:

```
[WARNING] Connected Connectors could not be loaded; existing local and self-hosted MCP servers remain available.
```

The same CLI version, same account and same working directory load Connectors **successfully** in non-interactive (`-p`) mode. So this appears to be specific to the interactive session-startup path, not to the account's Connectors configuration.

### Version

`1.0.105` (linux-x64, Node v24.22.1). `CONNECTORS` feature flag resolves to `true` for this account, so Connectors are enabled and failing rather than disabled.

### Observed behaviour

The warning appears on every interactive startup in all five of my retained session logs (2026-10-29, 2026-10-30 x2, 2026-11-02, 2026-11-03) — 100% reproduction rate, going back as far as log retention allows.

The emitting code is byte-identical between 1.0.103 and 1.0.105 (`reportManagedConnectorFailure` in `cli-main.js`), so this is not a recent regression — it just looks like a long-standing failure.

### Not reproducible headlessly

I ran, with debug logging enabled:

```
copilot --log-level debug --log-dir <dir> --allow-all-tools -p "reply with OK only"
```

twice — once in an empty `/tmp` directory, once in the large git repo where the interactive sessions fail. **Neither run produced the warning.** Both emitted `connector_client_operation` telemetry and completed Connector loading cleanly.

### Why that matters for diagnosis

Looking at `beginManagedConnectorLoad` in `cli-main.js`, interactive sessions appear to take a different branch from headless ones:

```js
let r = t.authInfo === void 0
  ? { apply: s => n.currentAndApplyToSession(t.nativeSessionId, s),
      current: s => n.currentForSession(t.nativeSessionId, s) }
  : void 0;
```

When `r` is set, the code applies session credentials and races them against an `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`, with failure paths that throw `"The active GitHub account changed while loading Connectors"`. Headless `-p` runs supply `authInfo` and skip that path entirely. That session-credential/timeout branch looks like the likely culprit.

### Main request: the failure cause is unobservable

The underlying exception is only logged on the failure path:

```js
T.warning(r);
T.debug(`Copilot Connectors session integration failed: ${k(n)}`);
```

Since the failure reproduces *only* interactively, and `--log-level debug` is most naturally exercised via `-p`, there is effectively no way for a user to capture the real error. I could not obtain it despite the failure occurring 100% of the time interactively.

Concretely, it would help a lot if:

1. The underlying cause were logged at `warning` level alongside the user-facing message (or at least included in it), rather than only at `debug`.
2. The user-facing warning distinguished "timed out", "account changed", and "server error", since the remediation differs wildly.

### Possibly related

I am simultaneously seeing `GET /copilot_internal/managed_settings` return `422 Validation Failed` on this account (filed separately). Connectors sit on the same managed/enterprise settings surface, so these may share a root cause — though the Connectors failure clearly predates the 422 by at least a week.

### Impact

Local and self-hosted MCP servers continue to work, so impact is limited to Connectors being unavailable plus a startup warning on every session.

issues.title: Managed settings endpoint returns 422 Validation Failed since 2026-11-03 (was working 2026-11-02, same CLI version)

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

issues.body:
### Summary

As of 2026-11-03, every managed-settings poll fails with HTTP 422. The same request succeeded on 2026-11-02 for the same account on the same CLI version, so this looks like a server-side regression rather than a client change.

The CLI logs this warning roughly every 30 seconds for the lifetime of the session:

```
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::storage::managed_settings] [managedSettings] server policy fetch failed ([fetchManagedSettings] Server returned 422) — preserving the current in-memory policy
```

### Version

`1.0.105` (linux-x64, Node v24.22.1). Note 1.0.105 was already in use on 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-02 without this error, so the CLI version is not the trigger.

### Before / after

Working, 2026-11-02:

```
[managedSettings] self-fetch starting for account https://github.com/<redacted>
[managedSettings] server policy received from https://github.com: bypassDisabled=false, keys=[telemetry]
[managedSettings] self-fetch complete for https://github.com/<redacted>: bypassDisabled=false, serverFetchFailed=false, serverResolution=Live, serverRetryableFailure=false, deviceLoadFailed=false
```

Failing, 2026-11-03:

```
[managedSettings] device MDM: no policy present on this device
[managedSettings] server policy fetch failed ([fetchManagedSettings] Server returned 422) — preserving the current in-memory policy
[managedSettings] effective policy resolved: source=server, bypassDisabled=false, serverFetchFailed=false, ...
[managedSettings] self-fetch complete for https://github.com/<redacted>: ... serverResolution=FallbackCache, ...
```

Occurrence counts across my five retained session logs:

| Session date | `Server returned 422` count |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-10-29 | 0 |
| 2026-10-30 (x2) | 0 |
| 2026-11-02 | 0 |
| 2026-11-03 | 45 and climbing (one per ~30s poll) |

### Direct reproduction

Reproducible outside the CLI with the CLI's own stored OAuth token:

```
GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/managed_settings
→ 422
{"message":"Validation Failed","documentation_url":"https://docs.github.com/rest","status":"422"}
```

Same 422 with every variant I tried:

- plain request
- `Editor-Version` / `Editor-Plugin-Version` headers
- `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28`
- `?client=cli`
- `?integration_id=copilot-developer-cli`

The token itself is valid — `GET https://api.github.com/user` returns `200` with the same credentials.

Account context: no device MDM policy present, `policyHelperConfigured=false`, personal account on github.com.

### Impact

Mostly cosmetic but noisy:

- A `[WARNING]` is written to the session log every ~30 seconds.
- The CLI correctly falls back to the cached policy, so no permission restrictions are wrongly applied (`bypassDisabled=false` throughout).

### Possible secondary issues

1. `422 Validation Failed` suggests the server is rejecting the request shape. If a newly-required parameter was added server-side, older clients will fail closed-ish forever with no actionable message.
2. The log message says `serverFetchFailed=false` on the very same line that reports the fetch failing, which seems inconsistent and made this harder to diagnose.
3. There is no apparent way to suppress or rate-limit the repeated warning once the endpoint is failing persistently.

issues.title: read_agent returns nothing of a background agent's work when it failed, or after --resume

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When a background agent fails, `read_agent` returns only the error. None of the agent's messages, commands or file edits come back, even when it did a lot before failing. After the session is resumed in a new process, it's worse: `read_agent` answers "Agent not found" for any agent started before the restart.

Either way, the main agent can't tell what the subagent did, so it goes through the files on disk and guesses, or redoes the work. The last time this happened to me, a subagent had worked for almost three hours (215 shell commands, 3 files written) when a network blip failed its model call 5 times. Then the session restarted, and the main agent got "Agent not found".

The work is all still in the parent session's `events.jsonl`: every event of the subagent is there, with `parentToolCallId` set to the id of the `task` call that started it. `read_agent` just doesn't look there once the agent is gone from memory or failed.

Maybe related: #2595 (completed agents purged quickly) and #2137 (results lost after compaction). This one is about failed agents and resumed sessions.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

I used a clean container (`node:22-bookworm`), `npm i -g @github/copilot@1.0.105`, an empty working directory and Claude Haiku 4.5.

**Agent forgotten after a resume**

1. `copilot -p "<prompt>" --model claude-haiku-4.5 --allow-all-tools`, where the prompt asks the main agent to launch one background agent with the `task` tool (a small job that ends with a known reply) and read it with `read_agent`.
2. This works: `read_agent` returns the agent's reply.
3. `copilot --resume=<id> -p "Use read_agent on the agent you launched earlier and give me its reply." --model claude-haiku-4.5 --allow-all-tools`
4. `read_agent` answers "Agent not found".

**Failed agent returns only the error**

1. In one `copilot -p` run, the main agent launches a background agent whose job includes `sleep 20`, then runs `sleep 150` itself so the process stays up.
2. While the agent is in its `sleep`, block outbound 443 (`iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j REJECT`), so its next model call fails.
3. Unblock, and let the main agent call `read_agent`. It gets:

```text
Agent failed ... total_turns: 0
Error: Failed to get response from the AI model; retried 5 times ... ECONNREFUSED
```

and nothing else, while the parent's `events.jsonl` has 7 events for that agent under its `parentToolCallId`.

### Expected behavior

`read_agent` on a failed agent returns what it did up to the failure, along with the error: at least its last messages and the files it touched. After `--resume`, agents from the earlier process can still be read, from the session's events if they're no longer in memory.

### Additional context

- Linux x86_64 (Docker), bash. I see it in my normal sessions on Linux too.
- For now I work around it with a small script that reads the agent's events from `events.jsonl` by `parentToolCallId`, and an instruction telling the agent to run it when `read_agent` fails. Sonnet 4.6 follows it; Haiku 4.5 still guessed from the files instead.

issues.title: BYOK: providers.json is ignored without COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL — no file-based activation; --model silently substitutes a subscription model

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

labels.name: area:configuration
labels.description: Config files, instruction files, settings, and environment variables

issues.body:
I'm trying to use my own model provider (an OpenAI-compatible endpoint) together with plugins that make their own `copilot -p` calls from hook processes, and I keep running into what looks like a gap in how BYOK mode gets activated.

`copilot help providers` says BYOK is activated by the `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` env var. I was hoping `providers.json` would work as the file-based equivalent, since it already accepts a static `apiKey`/`bearerToken` (what #4936 and #5287 are about). Mine looks like this:

```json
{
  "providers": [
    { "name": "myprov", "type": "openai", "wireApi": "responses",
      "baseUrl": "https://api.example.com/v1", "apiKey": "<redacted>" }
  ],
  "models": [
    { "provider": "myprov", "id": "mymodel", "modelId": "mymodel", "wireModel": "mymodel" }
  ]
}
```

But with that in place and **no** `COPILOT_PROVIDER_*` env vars, this:

```
copilot -p "Reply with exactly: OK" --model mymodel --output-format json
```

gives me:

```
session.info {"infoType": "model_unavailable", "message": "Model \"mymodel\" is no longer available. Using \"claude-sonnet-5.5\" instead."}
model.call_final_result {"model": "claude-sonnet-5.5", "isByok": false, "result": "success"}
```

So the `--model` I asked for quietly gets dropped and the request runs on my Copilot subscription instead. If I delete `providers.json` the same command fails loudly ("Model \"mymodel\" from --model flag is not available"), so the file *is* being read and the model is recognized — it's just unusable unless the env var flips BYOK on.

When I do set `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` (plus `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE` / `_WIRE_API`), the request finally goes to my provider (`"isByok": true`) — but the `apiKey` sitting in `providers.json` still isn't used. The request goes out unauthenticated and I get `session.error: "Authentication failed with provider at … (HTTP 401)"`. Only `COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `_BEARER_TOKEN` from the environment authenticate.

This matters for me beyond interactive use: plugins that call `copilot -p` from hook processes (I use microsoft/TokenEconomizer, whose loop guard and fact proposer work exactly this way) can't reach BYOK at all, because hooks don't inherit the session's `COPILOT_PROVIDER_*`. Before I figured out what was going on I got "not signed in" errors; after "fixing" it with `providers.json` my calls silently started billing my Copilot subscription instead of my own provider, which honestly feels worse.

What I'd love to see:

- `providers.json` alone activates BYOK (env vars keep working as an override)
- or hooks get the `COPILOT_PROVIDER_*` variables, or `providers.json` grows `apiKeyCommand` as #4936 asks
- and either way, an explicit `--model` that can't be honored should error out rather than swap in a subscription model

Tested on 1.0.105 (saw the same on 1.0.92), macOS arm64. Related: #4936, #5287, #4001.

issues.title: [Windows] PowerShell tool guidance: prefer -LiteralPath for file paths (brackets are wildcards with -Path)

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

On Windows, the agent often passes file names containing [ ] to cmdlets via -Path (the default), so PowerShell treats them as wildcards: commands fail, Test-Path returns a false negative, and Remove-Item can delete a different file.

### Proposed solution

Add a line to the built-in PowerShell tool guidance, alongside the existing Windows tips (`&&` vs `;`, no heredoc), for example:

> For concrete filesystem paths, prefer `-LiteralPath` where supported; quoting `-Path` does not disable wildcard expansion (`[ ] * ?`). Use `-Path` only when wildcard matching is intentional. (This applies to source paths such as `Get-Content`, `Set-Content`, `Test-Path`, `Remove-Item`, `Copy-Item`, `Move-Item`, `Rename-Item`, `Get-ChildItem`; not to destination parameters.)

Benefit: fewer failed tool calls and retries, and it reduces the risk of acting on the wrong file (data loss with `Remove-Item` / `Move-Item` / `Set-Content`).

### Example prompts or workflows

1. "Rename the scans in this folder to yyyy-MM-dd format": files like `scan[2].jpg` fail with `-Path`; the agent then retries with `-LiteralPath`.
2. "Delete del[2].jpg": `Remove-Item -Path 'del[2].jpg'` deletes `del2.jpg` if it exists, and the requested file stays.
3. "Edit notes [draft].md": `Set-Content -Path` fails with "An object at the specified path ... does not exist".

### Additional context

Repro (pwsh 7.6.9, Copilot CLI 1.0.105, Windows):
```powershell
Set-Content -LiteralPath 'a[1].txt' x
Test-Path -Path 'a[1].txt'      # False (file exists)
Get-Content -Path 'a[1].txt'    # error: An object at the specified path a[1].txt does not exist...
Set-Content a1.txt y
Remove-Item -Path 'a[1].txt'    # deletes a1.txt, keeps a[1].txt
```
Docs: [about_Wildcards](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_wildcards) and [Supporting Wildcard Characters in Cmdlet Parameters / -LiteralPath](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/developer/cmdlet/supporting-wildcard-characters-in-cmdlet-parameters).

Filed as a feature request rather than a bug: PowerShell behaves as designed; the ask is guidance for the model. No existing issue found for "LiteralPath".

issues.title: Explicit slash skill is redundantly reloaded through model registry and fails with “Skill not found”

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

An explicitly invoked interactive slash skill is successfully resolved and expanded into the conversation, but the assistant then attempts to load the same skill through the model-facing `skill()` tool. For skills excluded from model invocation, that redundant call fails with `Skill not found`, and the requested workflow does not start.

This differs from #4438: the interactive `/skill` resolver succeeds and provides the skill context. The failure happens afterward because the assistant routes the already-resolved explicit invocation back through the model-only registry.


### Affected version

 GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.79

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create a personal skill at `%USERPROFILE%\.agents\skills\implement`.
2. Configure `agents\openai.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   interface:
     display_name: "Implement"
     short_description: "Build work from a spec or tickets"
   policy:
     allow_implicit_invocation: false
   ```

3. Start an interactive Copilot CLI session using GPT-5.6 Sol.
4. Invoke the skill directly:

   ```text
   /implement 5514365
   ```

5. The CLI successfully injects an explicit invocation message and `<skill-context name="implement">` containing the skill's base directory and instructions.
6. Instead of following that supplied context, the assistant calls the model-facing tool:

   ```text
   skill: "implement"
   ```

7. The tool returns:

   ```text
   Skill not found: implement
   ```

The same session shows that skills with `allow_implicit_invocation: false` are absent from the model-facing registry, while skills without that policy are present. Skills under `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\skills` without this policy are also present.

### Expected behavior

Once an interactive slash command has resolved a skill and supplied its `<skill-context>`, the assistant should execute those instructions directly. It should not call the model-facing `skill()` tool again.

`allow_implicit_invocation: false` should prevent automatic model selection without breaking a direct `/skill` invocation that the CLI has already resolved.


### Additional context

- OS: Microsoft Windows 10.0.26200, x64
- PowerShell: 7.6.4
- Model: GPT-5.6 Sol
- Related registry/filtering issue: #4438

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When an MCP server returns an image content block in a tool result (per the MCP specification: content array item {type:"image", mimeType:"image/png", data:<base64>}), the image never reaches the model. Only the text blocks and structuredContent of the same tool result are delivered.

Verified from the agent side (Copilot CLI 1.0.80, Windows):
1. The MCP server's wire format is spec-compliant. Capturing the raw stdio JSON-RPC response for a screenshot tool shows content[0] = text block and content[1] = a valid image block (mimeType image/png, correct base64 PNG payload).
2. 2. Across multiple calls (window screenshot, region screenshot), the image data never appeared in the model context; only the text metadata block arrived.
3. 3. Static inspection of app.js (1.0.80) shows image handling only in two paths: user-attachment sanitization (file_data / image_url / input_image) and the mcp-sampling converter for user-role messages. No conversion path exists for MCP tool-result image blocks, and tool results are assembled through the native session layer (session.mcp.apps.callTool).
User-attached images (paste / drag-drop / @file) work fine, so the model and plan support vision. The gap is specific to images returned by MCP tools.

### Affected version

1.0.80 (Windows 10.0.26200, PowerShell)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure any MCP server whose tool returns an image content block (e.g. a UI-automation server with a screenshot tool; any tool returning {type:"image", mimeType:"image/png", data:<base64>} reproduces it).
2. 2. In an interactive Copilot CLI session, ask the agent to call that tool and then describe what it sees in the image.
3. 3. Observe: the agent only receives the text blocks / structuredContent of the tool result. It reports the image metadata but cannot see the actual pixels, and often states the image content is unavailable.

### Expected behavior

When the selected model supports vision, image content blocks inside MCP tool results should be passed to the model (like user-attached images), so agents can act on screenshots and other tool-generated images.

### Additional context

This blocks a whole class of computer-use / UI-automation workflows: MCP servers that follow the spec and return screenshots as image blocks work in other agent CLIs that surface tool-result images, but not in Copilot CLI. Current workaround: agents must rely on structured reads only, or the user must manually attach the image.

issues.title: ACP: session/prompt unconditionally aborts the session, cancelling all running background sub-agents (interactive TUI does not)

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp --stdio`), the `session/prompt` handler calls `session.abort()` unconditionally as its **first action**, before doing anything else with the request. When the session has background sub-agents running (launched via the `task` tool with `mode=background`), that abort tears all of them down.

This happens even when:

- **no prompt turn is in flight** — the previous turn already returned `stopReason: "end_turn"`, and the client waited before sending the next prompt; and
- **the client never sent `session/cancel`**.

The abort is issued with no reason argument, so it defaults to the *user-abort* constant. The event log therefore records `abort {"reason":"user_initiated"}` although no user initiated anything, and it is written **~140 ms before** the `user.message` that appears to have caused it.

The interactive TUI does not do this. Sending follow-up messages while background agents are running is safe there. This makes the behaviour a property of the ACP transport specifically, not of the session or the agent runtime.

### Impact

Any ACP client is unable to send a follow-up message to a session that has background sub-agents out without silently destroying that work. Because the agent had already reported `end_turn`, the session looks idle, so this is exactly the moment a client would reasonably prompt. There is no client-side workaround (see below).

---

## Affected version

```
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.81-6
```

Also present in every version I have on disk to compare against: **1.0.80, 1.0.81-0, 1.0.81-3, 1.0.81-5, 1.0.81-6**. Not a recent regression.

---

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

Save the script below as `acp-abort-repro.py` and run it (requires a logged-in CLI):

```bash
python3 acp-abort-repro.py --agents
```

<details>
<summary>acp-abort-repro.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal reproduction: GitHub Copilot CLI ACP mode aborts the session on every
session/prompt, even when no turn is in flight and the client never sent
session/cancel.

Usage:  python3 acp-abort-repro.py [--agents]

Requires a logged-in CLI (`copilot login`).

Without --agents: shows the spurious abort event (mechanism).
With --agents:    also shows background sub-agents being cancelled (impact).
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path

WITH_AGENTS = "--agents" in sys.argv
workdir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="acp-repro-")
copilot_home = Path(os.environ.get("COPILOT_HOME", Path.home() / ".copilot"))

proc = subprocess.Popen(
    ["copilot", "--acp", "--stdio", "--no-color", "--allow-all-tools"],
    stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    text=True,
    bufsize=1,
    cwd=workdir,
)

_id = 0


def send(method, params):
    global _id
    _id += 1
    proc.stdin.write(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": _id, "method": method, "params": params}) + "\n")
    proc.stdin.flush()
    return _id


def wait_for(req_id):
    """Read until the response to req_id; auto-approve any permission request."""
    while True:
        line = proc.stdout.readline()
        if not line:
            raise SystemExit("agent exited unexpectedly")
        try:
            msg = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if msg.get("method") == "session/request_permission":
            opts = msg["params"]["options"]
            pick = next((o for o in opts if "allow" in o["optionId"]), opts[0])
            proc.stdin.write(json.dumps({
                "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": msg["id"],
                "result": {"outcome": {"outcome": "selected", "optionId": pick["optionId"]}},
            }) + "\n")
            proc.stdin.flush()
        elif msg.get("id") == req_id:
            return msg


wait_for(send("initialize", {
    "protocolVersion": 1,
    "clientCapabilities": {"fs": {"readTextFile": False, "writeTextFile": False}, "terminal": False},
}))

res = wait_for(send("session/new", {"cwd": workdir, "mcpServers": []}))
session_id = res["result"]["sessionId"]
print(f"session: {session_id}")

if WITH_AGENTS:
    p1 = ("Use the task tool to launch 2 background agents (mode=background). "
          "Each agent must run the shell command `sleep 600`. "
          "Do NOT wait for them to finish. Reply with just: LAUNCHED")
else:
    p1 = "Reply with exactly: FIRST"

r = wait_for(send("session/prompt", {"sessionId": session_id,
                                     "prompt": [{"type": "text", "text": p1}]}))
print(f"prompt #1 stopReason: {r['result']['stopReason']}")

print("waiting 15s (no turn is in flight; client sends NO session/cancel)...")
time.sleep(15)

r = wait_for(send("session/prompt", {"sessionId": session_id,
                                     "prompt": [{"type": "text", "text": "Reply with exactly: SECOND"}]}))
print(f"prompt #2 stopReason: {r['result']['stopReason']}")

time.sleep(3)
proc.terminate()

print("\n--- event log ---")
log = copilot_home / "session-state" / session_id / "events.jsonl"

if log and log.exists():
    for line in log.read_text().splitlines():
        try:
            e = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        t = e.get("type", "")
        if t in ("user.message", "abort", "subagent.completed", "assistant.turn_end",
                 "tool.execution_start"):
            extra = ""
            if t == "abort":
                extra = f"  reason={e.get('reason') or e.get('data', {}).get('reason')}"
            if t == "subagent.completed":
                extra = f"  cancelled={e.get('cancelled', e.get('data', {}).get('cancelled'))}"
            print(f"{e.get('timestamp', '')[-13:]}  {t}{extra}")
else:
    print(f"log not found: {log}")

print(f"\nworkdir: {workdir}")
```

</details>

It performs a plain ACP exchange with no cancellation of any kind:

1. `initialize` (`protocolVersion: 1`)
2. `session/new`
3. `session/prompt` #1 — asks the agent to launch 2 background agents that each run `sleep 600`, and to not wait for them
4. Waits for `stopReason: "end_turn"`, then **sleeps 15 s** so no turn is in flight
5. `session/prompt` #2 — "Reply with exactly: SECOND"
6. Prints the relevant lines of `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`

### Actual output

```
prompt #1 stopReason: end_turn
waiting 15s (no turn is in flight; client sends NO session/cancel)...
prompt #2 stopReason: end_turn

--- event log ---
13:50:31.797Z  user.message
13:50:37.239Z  tool.execution_start
13:50:37.242Z  tool.execution_start
13:50:37.278Z  assistant.turn_end
13:50:38.955Z  assistant.turn_end
13:50:39.097Z  user.message
13:50:39.143Z  user.message
13:50:42.129Z  tool.execution_start
13:50:42.228Z  tool.execution_start
13:50:53.979Z  abort  reason=user_initiated      <-- nobody cancelled anything
13:50:53.992Z  subagent.completed  cancelled=True
13:50:53.986Z  subagent.completed  cancelled=True
13:50:54.118Z  user.message                      <-- prompt #2 lands 139 ms LATER
13:50:55.979Z  assistant.turn_end
```

Both background agents are cancelled 8 minutes into a 10-minute sleep.

### Control: the same scenario in the interactive TUI

Driving `copilot` (TUI) through a pty with the same prompts — 2 background agents out, then 3 consecutive follow-up messages — produces **zero** `abort` events and all agents survive and complete normally.

| driver | agents launched | follow-up prompts | `abort` events | agents surviving |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `copilot --acp --stdio` | 2 | 1 | **1** | **0** |
| `copilot` (interactive TUI) | 2 | 3 | 0 | 2 |

### Note on reproducing without background agents

If you run the script *without* `--agents`, no `abort` event is logged. The call still happens, but with no abortable work it is a no-op and nothing is recorded. The bug is only observable — and only harmful — when background work is outstanding.

---

## Expected behavior

Sending a `session/prompt` to a session whose previous turn has already completed should not cancel background sub-agents. Following up should be non-destructive, matching the interactive TUI.

Concretely, one of:

1. **Guard the abort** on there actually being an active turn (the adjacent `cancel` handler already does exactly this, via its `pendingPrompt` check); or
2. **Use `interruptMainTurn()` instead of `abort()`**. That method already exists and is precisely the narrower primitive — it stops the main turn and leaves background agents alone. The TUI keeps these two operations distinct, and the changelog for **1.0.69** documents that distinction as intentional user-facing behaviour:

   > "Double-press Esc now interrupts the running main turn (flushing queued messages), **or stops background agents when the main agent is idle**"

   The ACP path currently performs the second of those on every prompt.

At minimum, if the abort must stay, it should not pass the *user-initiated* reason when no user initiated it, since that misattributes the cancellation in the event log and in telemetry.

---

## Additional context

### Where it is

The bundled application in the runtime cache (`~/.cache/copilot/pkg/<platform>/<version>/app.js`) contains the ACP `session/prompt` handler:

```js
async prompt(t){
  let n = this.sessions.get(t.sessionId);
  if (!n) throw new _o(-32602, `Session ${t.sessionId} not found`);
  await n.session.abort(),        // <-- unconditional, first statement, no guard
  n.pendingPrompt = !0;
  ...
  await n.session.send(d)         // <-- the actual delivery
}
```

`n.session.send(d)` is the same call the TUI uses to deliver a message. **The extra `abort()` is the only difference between the two paths.**

The `cancel` handler a few lines below *is* guarded:

```js
async cancel(t){
  let n = this.sessions.get(t.sessionId);
  n?.pendingPrompt && (n.pendingPrompt = !1, await n.session.abort())
}
```

### Why it reaches background agents

`abort()` → `abortInProcessAndNative(t)` → `cancelProcessing(...)`, which dispatches `cancelSidekicks` (`sidekickManagerCancelAllNative`) and `cancelActiveAgents`. Because `prompt()` calls `abort()` with no argument, the reason falls back to `oAt = sessionConstantsAbortReasonUserAbort()`, which is where the `"user_initiated"` in the log comes from.

### Why there is no client-side workaround

- `session/prompt` is the only method that delivers user input; `session/fork`, `session/resume` and `session/load` do not.
- The abort precedes any use of the request parameters other than `sessionId`, so no field, `_meta`, capability or session config option can influence it.
- Sending `session/cancel` first does not help: `cancel` is a no-op when `pendingPrompt` is false (i.e. when idle), and `prompt` then aborts unconditionally regardless.
- ACP v2, whose prompt lifecycle explicitly supports background activity continuing while the agent reports idle, is not implemented here — `initialize` returns a hardcoded `protocolVersion: 1`.

The only way for a client to protect background agents today is to refuse to send the prompt until they finish, which defeats the purpose of background agents.

### Relation to the ACP spec

The spec does not require this behaviour. ACP v1 states:

> "Once a prompt turn completes, the Client **may** send another `session/prompt` to continue the conversation"

and scopes cancellation to in-flight turns:

> "Clients **MAY** cancel an **ongoing** prompt turn at any time by sending a `session/cancel` notification"

Zed's ACP client — the reference client — behaves the same way this repro does: in `acp_thread.rs`, `cancel_inner` returns immediately when there is no `running_turn`, so a follow-up prompt after `end_turn` is sent with no preceding cancellation.

The ACP v2 RFD names this exact scenario as a v1 gap:

> "if an agent finishes its turn, wants to wait for the next user action, but has a background subagent or task running, can it only submit updates about that status after the user prompts again?"

So v1 is silent on background work rather than mandating that it be cancelled, and the CLI's own TUI demonstrates the intended non-destructive behaviour.

### Environment

- OS: Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm), Linux 6.12.96 aarch64
- CPU architecture: ARM (aarch64)
- Shell: bash
- Installed via the platform binary package; version 1.0.81-6

labels.description: Display and rendering: flickering, scrolling, line wrapping, output formatting

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In the main session timeline, collapsed timeline entries such as `$ Shell ... 2 lines…` and `> Thought for 1s` can be expanded either by clicking on them with the mouse or via keyboard shortcuts (`Ctrl+O` to toggle all timeline entries, `Ctrl+T` to toggle reasoning).

When viewing a sub-agent's transcript via `/tasks` (selecting a sub-agent to open its fullscreen detail view), the exact same collapsed entries (`$ Shell ... 2 lines…`, `> Thought for Ns`, etc.) are rendered with the trailing `…` indicator, but clicking on them does nothing and `Ctrl+O` does not expand tool call outputs. As a result, there is no way to inspect the output of `Shell` or other tool calls executed by a sub-agent in `/tasks`.

### Affected version

1.0.103

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start an interactive `copilot` session in a terminal with mouse support (e.g. Windows Terminal).
2. Ask Copilot to run a shell command in the main session and then run a sub-agent that executes a shell command:
   - Main session command: `echo "Hello from the main session" && uname -a`
   - Sub-agent (`task`) command: `echo "Hello from the sub-agent" && uname -a`
3. In the main session timeline, click on `$ Shell ... 2 lines…` or `> Thought for 1s` — both expand to show full details.
4. Open `/tasks` and select the sub-agent to open its fullscreen transcript view.
5. Click on `$ Shell ... 2 lines…` (or press `Ctrl+O`).
6. Observe that `$ Shell ... 2 lines…` cannot be expanded by clicking or via `Ctrl+O`, and individual `> Thought for Ns` items cannot be clicked to expand.

### Expected behavior

Timeline entries in the `/tasks` sub-agent detail view (`$ Shell ... 2 lines…`, `> Thought for Ns`, and other expandable tool calls) should be interactive and expandable via mouse click and `Ctrl+O`, matching the main session timeline behavior (and fulfilling the intent of #1322 to inspect sub-agent tool call details).

### Additional context

**Environment:**
- Copilot CLI version: `1.0.103`
- OS: Linux `6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2` (x86_64)
- Terminal: Windows Terminal `1.24.12741.0`

**Root cause from inspecting `cli-main.js`:**
The sub-agent fullscreen detail view reuses the same timeline rendering hook and `FullscreenScrollView` component as the main session, and even computes and rebases `lineOwners` for `FullscreenScrollView`. However, per-entry expansion and click handling are not wired up in the sub-agent detail component:

1. `isTimelineEntryExpanded` is hardcoded to a no-op returning `false` (`useCallback(() => false, [])`) instead of tracking expanded entry IDs.
2. `isTimelineEntryClickable` and `expansionFingerprint` are omitted when calling the timeline rendering hook. Because `isTimelineEntryClickable` is `undefined`, `lineOwners` only records markdown code blocks (for `copyOnCodeBlockClick`) and skips all tool call and reasoning entries.
3. `onEntryClick` is omitted when rendering `FullscreenScrollView`, so mouse clicks on non-code-block rows return early.
4. While `Ctrl+T` happens to toggle all sub-agent reasoning blocks at once (because `showReasoningSummaries` is passed down from the root component into the sub-agent view as `reasoningExpanded`), `Ctrl+O` (`expand all timeline`) state is not passed down or handled in the sub-agent view.

issues.title: MCP OAuth: authorize request sends resource with a trailing slash that differs from the resource
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

For a remote HTTP MCP server configured with a bare-origin URL, the OAuth authorize request carries `resource=https://mcp.example.com/` (trailing slash). The server's protected-resource metadata advertises `"resource": "https://mcp.example.com"` (no slash). The authorization server compares resource indicators exactly, so it rejects the request and the browser lands on its error page. The sign-in never starts.

The CLI seems to re-serialize the configured URL, where an empty path becomes `/`, instead of using the PRM `resource` value as published. I haven't confirmed the cause in the source.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105 and 1.0.106-2 (prerelease), macOS arm64

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "example": {
         "type": "http",
         "url": "https://mcp.example.com",
         "oauthClientId": "<public-client-id>",
         "oauthPublicClient": true
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Run `copilot`, then `/mcp` and authenticate `example`.

### Observed

- `GET https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` returns:
  ```json
  {"resource":"https://mcp.example.com","authorization_servers":["https://auth.example.com"],"scopes_supported":["example:invoke","offline_access"],"bearer_methods_supported":["header"]}
  ```
- The authorize URL opened by the CLI:
  ```
  https://auth.example.com/connect/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<public-client-id>&state=...&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A<port>%2F&scope=example%3Ainvoke+offline_access&resource=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.example.com%2F&prompt=consent+select_account
  ```
- The authorization server rejects it with: `Invalid resource identifier "https://mcp.example.com/". It is either not found, not enabled, or does not support any of the requested scopes.` The `redirect_uri`, scope and client all validate. Only the trailing slash differs.
- The CLI reports only `MCP OAuth authorization failed`.

### Expected behavior

The `resource` parameter should be the PRM `resource` value exactly as published (RFC 9728 §3, RFC 8707 §2). Resource identifiers are absolute URIs compared as-is, so the CLI should not alter them. Other MCP clients, such as VS Code, send the PRM value without the slash and work against the same server.

### Workaround

None in config. The per-server OAuth fields (`oauthClientId`, `oauthPublicClient`, `oauthGrantType`, `oauthScopes`) don't control `resource`.

### Additional context

The CLI log shows a 401 challenge with `resource_metadata` and then `MCP OAuth authorization failed`. It does not log the authorize URL.

issues.title: ACP: session/prompt response is held until an async bash shell exits, so clients appear stuck

labels.name: area:non-interactive

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp`), when the agent starts a shell with the `bash` tool in `mode: "async"`, the `session/prompt` response is withheld until that shell exits, even though the agent's foreground work finished long before. If the async shell is a dev server or another long-running process, the prompt never completes. ACP clients have no other end-of-turn signal on protocol v1, so they show the session as busy indefinitely.

The same prompt with `detach: true` (bash args `{"mode":"async","detach":true}`) behaves as expected: `session/prompt` returns `end_turn` as soon as the foreground work ends, and the later shell-completion wake (`system.notification` → `read_bash` → new turn) still happens.

This makes ACP clients look stuck. It was reported downstream in T3 Code: https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/27301

### Affected version

1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start `copilot --acp` and send `initialize` (protocolVersion 1; optionally subscribe to raw events with `clientCapabilities._meta["github.com/copilot"].events = ["assistant.turn_end", "session.usage_checkpoint", "system.notification"]`).
2. `session/new`, then `session/prompt` with: *Use the bash tool with mode "async" (NOT detached) to run `sleep 25`, do not wait or read its output, then immediately reply with just the word ok. Do nothing else.* Allow the permission request.
3. Note when the `session/prompt` response arrives.
4. Repeat asking for `detach: true` for comparison, and check the bash arguments in `~/.copilot/session-state/<sessionId>/events.jsonl`: the bug needs `{"mode":"async","detach":false}` or no `detach` field.

Observed (seconds from start):

```
async, not detached ({"mode":"async"}):
  3.22  tool_call bash "sleep 25"
  3.94  sessionEvent assistant.turn_end
  3.94  sessionEvent session.usage_checkpoint    <- foreground work done, "ok" already sent
 28.27  sessionEvent system.notification         <- shell completed
 28.27  tool_call read_bash
 29.41  sessionEvent assistant.turn_end
 29.42  session/prompt response {"stopReason":"end_turn"}    <- held ~25 s

async + detach ({"mode":"async","detach":true}):
  4.18  tool_call bash "sleep 25"
  5.17  sessionEvent assistant.turn_end
  5.18  sessionEvent session.usage_checkpoint
  5.18  session/prompt response {"stopReason":"end_turn"}    <- immediate
 29.87  sessionEvent system.notification         <- wake still delivered
```

In a real session the agent started a local dev server with `mode: "async"`. The client showed the session as busy for about 10 minutes after the agent finished. The response to the next prompt came 0.5 s after I killed the dev server. Sending `session/cancel` also releases the held prompt without killing the async shell.

### Expected behavior

`session/prompt` should resolve with `end_turn` when the agent's foreground work ends, as it does for detached shells, even if an async shell started in that prompt is still running. If async shells must keep the prompt open by design, please provide a documented signal that foreground work has ended, such as ACP `state_update` idle (protocol v2) or a documented `sessionEvent`, so clients can show the session as idle with background work running.

### Additional context

- macOS 27.0.1, arm64
- Client: ACP over stdio (T3 Code; also reproduced with a minimal standalone JSON-RPC client)
- Models: claude-sonnet-5.5 (repro), gpt-6.1-sol (original session)

Also reproduced inside T3 Code with `{"command":"sleep 90","mode":"async","detach":false}`: the agent replied "ok" and emitted `session.usage_checkpoint` 4.3 s after the prompt, but the `session/prompt` response arrived 100 s after the prompt, only after the shell exited and the agent ran a second internal turn.

issues.title: [ACP] toolCall.title contains high-level summary instead of executable command, hiding shell command in client approval modals

labels.name: area:non-interactive

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When running the GitHub Copilot CLI in Agent Context Protocol (ACP) mode (e.g., connected to host editors like Zed), `toolCall.title` is populated with a high-level natural language summary (e.g., `"Search whole monorepo for double-entry"`) while the actual shell execution string is nested deep inside `toolCall.rawInput.command`.

Because ACP host clients rely on standard fields like `title` or top-level arguments to render command preview cards in their permission dialogs, users are asked to approve tool execution without being able to see the underlying shell command, flags, or parameters.

During a tool approval request, Copilot CLI ACP emits a JSON-RPC payload structured as follows:

```
{
  "sessionId": "d32e979a-eaa8-4e53-a31a-f9a1dba6bc09",
  "toolCall": {
    "toolCallId": "call-9480410f-3f47-441c-bcc3-decf647077aa-15",
    "title": "Search whole monorepo for double-entry",
    "kind": "execute",
    "status": "pending",
    "rawInput": {
      "command": "grep -rn -i 'double.entry\\|double_entry\\|DoubleEntry' ./ --include='*.ts' 2>/dev/null | head -50; ls ./",
      "commands": [
        "grep -rn -i 'double.entry\\|double_entry\\|DoubleEntry' ./ --include='*.ts' 2>/dev/null | head -50; ls ./"
      ]
    }
  },
  "options": [
    {
      "optionId": "allow_once",
      "kind": "allow_once",
      "name": "Allow once"
    },
    {
      "optionId": "allow_always",
      "kind": "allow_always",
      "name": "Always allow"
    },
    {
      "optionId": "reject_once",
      "kind": "reject_once",
      "name": "Deny"
    }
  ]
}
```

`toolCall.title` contains the high-level intent: `"Search whole monorepo for double-entry"`.

The actual raw command string is only present inside `rawInput.command` / `rawInput.commands`.

In ACP host clients (such as Zed), the UI permission modal displays `toolCall.title` as the title/code snippet preview, causing the actual executable string to remain completely hidden from the user during authorization

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

### **Steps to Reproduce**

1. Configure GitHub Copilot CLI as an ACP server in Zed (via the ACP Registry or in `settings.json`):
```json
{
  "agent_servers": {
    "Copilot": {
      "type": "custom",
      "command": "copilot",
      "args": ["--acp"]
    }
  }
}

```


2. Open any workspace or codebase in Zed.
3. Open the Agent Panel (`Cmd+?` on macOS / `Ctrl+?` on Linux/Windows) and start a new thread using the **Copilot** ACP agent.
4. Enter a prompt that triggers a shell tool call requiring client approval (e.g., *"Search the whole monorepo for double-entry pattern"*).
5. When Zed displays the tool execution approval dialog, observe the command preview card.

### **Observed Result**

The approval card displays the natural-language intent string (`"Search whole monorepo for double-entry"`) in place of the executable command. The actual shell command (`grep -rn -i ...`) remains hidden inside `toolCall.rawInput.command`.

### **Expected Result**

The approval dialog should render the actual raw shell command string (or include it within `toolCall.title` / standard tool arguments), allowing the user to inspect the exact flags, paths, and commands before granting execution authorization.

### Expected behavior

`toolCall.title` should explicitly contain or start with the raw command string being executed (e.g., `grep -rn -i ...`),

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

# Copilot CLI sandbox enforcement preflight fails with `CreateProcessW` error 2 on supported Windows host

## Describe the bug

On a managed Windows 11 device whose enterprise policy requires local sandboxing (`sandbox.enabled: true`, `failIfUnavailable: true`, `allowBypass: false`), every session is blocked at the sandbox enforcement preflight:

```text
This session is blocked because your organization's sandbox policy requires enforcement, but the sandbox is unavailable: backend_error: CreateProcessW failed with error code 2 (0x00000002). (CreateProcessW(PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_SECURITY_ENVIRONMENT) failed: WIN32_ERROR(2) (working directory: C:\Users\<user>\sandboxes\test (from process.cwd))). Start a new session after resolving the sandbox problem.
```

The host supports the sandbox. Outside Copilot, `@microsoft/mxc-sdk` 1.0.0 (the version bundled in Copilot 1.0.105) and 1.0.1 both successfully launch `cmd.exe`, Windows PowerShell 5.1, and PowerShell 7.6.9 on the same machine.

The standalone MXC tests use the same working directory and the same filesystem/network policy reported by `/sandbox policy`.

The failure has only been reproduced through Copilot's sandbox enforcement preflight. Because Copilot does not log the preflight image path or command line, I cannot determine which path is producing `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`.

**Important**: Local sandboxing works successfully on the same device when the enterprise-managed sandbox settings are not applied. The failure occurs when the enterprise-managed sandbox configuration is present and Copilot performs its managed sandbox enforcement/revalidation preflight.
## Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105, installed via WinGet (`GitHub.Copilot`).

WinGet reports:

```text
Name: GitHub Copilot CLI
Id: GitHub.Copilot
Version: 1.0.105
Installer Type: wix
Dependency: Microsoft.PowerShell >= 7.0.0
```

The standalone installation is located under:

```text
%LOCALAPPDATA%\GitHubCopilotCLI
```

and contains:

```text
copilot.exe
copilot-taskbar-activator.exe
GitHubCopilotCLI.sparse.msix
```

The same failure occurs through the VS Code Copilot shim and when invoking the standalone `copilot.exe` directly.

The 1.0.105-1 prerelease bundles the same `mxc-sdk` 1.0.0.



### Affected version

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use Windows 11 Enterprise 25H2, OS build 26200.9711.
2. Apply these managed settings from a GHE.com tenant:
   - `sandbox.enabled=true`
   - `sandbox.failIfUnavailable=true`
   - `sandbox.allowBypass=false`
3. Change to an empty local folder.
4. Run Copilot CLI and send any message.
5. Observe that the session is blocked by the sandbox enforcement preflight.

This occurs:

- on every new session;
- after restarting Windows;
- from different working directories;
- through the VS Code Copilot shim; and
- when invoking the standalone executable directly:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\GitHubCopilotCLI\copilot.exe"
```

## Expected behavior

The sandboxed session starts.

If the enforcement preflight cannot launch its process, the error or debug log should identify the image path and command line passed to the process creation operation.

## Additional diagnostics

### MXC platform support

Using `@microsoft/mxc-sdk/v1`:

```text
getPlatformSupport():
  isSupported: true
  isolationTier: "base-container"
```

`probe()` returns `base-container` with no warnings.

The following capabilities are reported as available:

```text
baseContainerApiPresent
baseContainerSupportsDenyPaths
baseContainerSupportsEnumeratePaths
baseContainerSupportsIngressHostLoopbackAllow
baseContainerSupportsIdentitylessLoopbackProxy
```

### Standalone MXC using Copilot's sandbox policy

A standalone MXC test uses:

- all 21 paths reported by `/sandbox policy`;
- egress allow;
- host loopback allow; and
- the same working directory that fails from Copilot.

Results:

| Program | mxc-sdk 1.0.0 | mxc-sdk 1.0.1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `cmd.exe` | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| Windows PowerShell 5.1 | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| PowerShell 7.6.9 | exit 0 | exit 0 |

This is significant because `mxc-sdk` 1.0.0 is also the version bundled with the affected Copilot CLI release.

### PowerShell resolution checked

PowerShell 7.6.9 is installed per-user without relying on the WindowsApps alias:

```text
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe
```

`Get-Command pwsh.exe -All` returns this executable before:

```text
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe
```

and:

```powershell
pwsh.exe --version
```

returns:

```text
PowerShell 7.6.9
```

The executable reports product/file version `7.6.9.500`.

The standalone MXC test successfully launches this unpackaged PowerShell executable.

### VS Code shim eliminated as cause

Both Copilot installations are visible on PATH:

```text
C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\bin\copilot-shim\copilot.exe
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\GitHubCopilotCLI\copilot.exe
```

The VS Code shim is normally resolved first.

However, explicitly bypassing the shim and running:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\GitHubCopilotCLI\copilot.exe"
```

produces the same sandbox enforcement failure.

Therefore, the failure is not specific to invoking Copilot through the VS Code shim.

### Other troubleshooting already performed

None of the following changed the error:

- Installed PowerShell 7.6.9.
- Put an unpackaged PowerShell 7 executable ahead of the WindowsApps alias on PATH.
- Verified that the real `pwsh.exe` is selected by `Get-Command` and `where.exe`.
- Added `C:\` and the PowerShell directory to `sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.readonlyPaths`.
- Set `sandbox.auth.git=false`.
- Set `sandbox.auth.gh=false`.
- Set `allowLocalNetwork=false`.
- Confirmed those settings through `/sandbox policy`.
- Used different working directories.
- Restarted Windows and started fresh sessions.
- Bypassed the VS Code shim and invoked the standalone CLI directly.
- Reproduced equivalent MXC launches successfully using both mxc-sdk 1.0.0 and 1.0.1.

## Logs

With `--log-level all`, the relevant output is:

```text
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::services::sandbox_service] managed sandbox enforcement revalidation refused the session {"error":"...CreateProcessW failed with error code 2..."}

[ERROR] [sandbox] enforcement preflight failed: Error: ...same message...

[WARNING] Failed to process event type 'session.sandbox_enforcement_blocked' for timeline reconstruction: Error: Unhandled event type in timeline: session.sandbox_enforcement_blocked
```

No image path or command line for the failed preflight process appears in the log.

## Current findings

The tests appear to rule out a general lack of MXC/base-container support on the host:

- MXC reports the platform as supported.
- MXC `probe()` succeeds.
- mxc-sdk 1.0.0 successfully creates sandboxed processes.
- mxc-sdk 1.0.1 successfully creates sandboxed processes.
- The Copilot-reported sandbox policy works in the standalone MXC test.
- The working directory works in the standalone MXC test.
- `cmd.exe`, Windows PowerShell, and PowerShell 7.6.9 all launch successfully through MXC.
- PowerShell 7 resolves to the real executable rather than the WindowsApps alias.
- Bypassing the VS Code shim does not change the result.

The remaining difference I have been unable to inspect is **the exact image, command line, and process creation configuration used by Copilot's managed sandbox enforcement preflight**.


### Expected behavior

Sandbox works without error

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: Add a way to un-archive a session that was marked as Done

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Marking a session as Done archives it, and there is no way to reverse that from the UI. An accidental click permanently removes an active, in-progress session from the sessions list — even though none of the session's data is actually gone.

This is especially easy to trigger by mis-click: when a session is waiting on a tool permission prompt, the **Allow** button pops up very close to the **Done** checkbox in the sessions view on the left-hand side. Reaching for Allow and hitting Done instead archives the session you were actively working in. The two controls being adjacent means the mistake happens precisely in the moment you are trying to move a session *forward*.

### Proposed solution

1. An **un-archive** / "mark as not done" action on archived sessions.
2. A visible way to list/filter archived sessions in the UI so a mis-archived session can be found again.
3. Ideally, more spacing (or a confirmation) between the **Allow** button and the **Done** checkbox, since that adjacency is what makes the mis-click likely in the first place.

Since the underlying data is fully preserved, un-archiving should be a cheap, purely-presentational change — the information needed to restore the session is all still there.

### Example prompts or workflows

- "I accidentally marked an agent as done. Can I recover it?" — the case that prompted this request.
- Reaching for **Allow** on a permission prompt, hitting **Done**, and needing to put the session straight back.
- Marking a session Done, then discovering the PR needs follow-up work and wanting to resume the original session with its full context rather than starting fresh.
- Reviewing archived sessions to find one worth reopening.

### Additional context

Observed while recovering an accidentally-archived session (Copilot CLI runtime in VS Code):

- **No data is lost on archive.** The transcript turns in `session-store.db`, the `events.jsonl` event log, the git worktree, the branch, and uncommitted changes were all fully intact.
- `list_sessions` reports the session as `status: "idle,archived"`, so the state is clearly tracked and reversible in principle.
- **Sending a new message to the session does not clear the archived flag** — the session stays archived even once it becomes active again.
- The archived flag does not appear in `session-store.db` or the session-state folder, so there is no supported way to undo it outside the UI.
- A session can be archived **while mid-turn and blocked on a pending permission prompt**. In that state the turn is still unfinished, which makes the accidental archive both easy to do and easy to miss.
