issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Hello! First let me thank you for your hard work. Here is below my described issue. I used copilot a bit to help on having a proper reproducer command and a potential hint. Thanks a lot guys!

---

I created a custom agent in `~/.copilot/agents/test.agent.md`
```
---
name: test
description: A minimal test custom agent
tools: []
---
You are the test custom agent. Always respond by saying: "Hello from test custom agent!"
```

When I launch copilot in "human mode" with `copilot --agent test` it works.
```
● Selected custom agent: test
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄
 ❯ hello                                                                                                                                            
▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀
● Hello from test custom agent!
```

However when I try to use use ACP, with `copilot --acp --agent test`. It ALWAYS use the default Copilot agent. I can only use my custom agent as subagent, for example by saying "use test agent for <...>".

It seems like when using `--acp`, the `--agent` option is totally ignored.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.65

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

## How to reproduce

#### 1. Create a minimal custom agent file in ~/.copilot/agents/test.agent.md:
```
---
name: test
description: A minimal test custom agent
tools: []
---
You are the test custom agent. Always respond by saying: "Hello from test custom agent!"
```

#### 2. Run this single command in your terminal to initialize a session and print the active agent configuration:
```
(echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":1,"clientCapabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test"}}}'; echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"session/new","params":{"cwd":"'"$(pwd)"'","mcpServers":[]}}'; sleep 6) | copilot --acp --agent test --yolo | grep -o '"id":"agent"[^}]*"currentValue":"[^"]*"'
```

## Expected behaviour
The active agent configuration option should reflect the command-line override ("test"):
```
"id":"agent","name":"Agent","currentValue":"test"
```

## Actual behaviour
The active agent configuration is empty, falling back to standard Copilot:
```
"id":"agent","name":"Agent","currentValue":""
```

### Expected behavior

Copilot should be launched in ACP with my custom agent as main agent. I want my session to have only the tools and context I have defined in my subagent, not with the general copilot gent. I don't want my custom agent to be available just as a tool.

## Expected behaviour
The active agent configuration option should reflect the command-line override ("test"):
```
"id":"agent","name":"Agent","currentValue":"test"
```

### Additional context

- Operating System: Linux (Kernel v24.16.0 or similar)
- CPU Architecture: x86_64 / x64 (installed as @github/copilot-linux-x64)
- Terminal Emulator: Ghostty (term/ghostty)
- Shell: Bash (v5.x)
- Copilot Version: v1.0.65
[copilot-acp-agent-bug.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29375552/copilot-acp-agent-bug.log)

---

## Analysis by Copilot himself

- When starting in `--acp` server mode, the CLI action handler calls `startServerMode({...}, authManager)`. However, the parsed value of `--agent` (`t.agent` / `agentName`) is completely omitted from the configuration object passed to `startServerMode`.
- There is no way for the ACP client to specify the agent in the `session/new` params, and the ACP server does not implement the `session/set_config_option` method, making it impossible to change the active agent after session creation.

An analysis of the bundled index.js reveals exactly where the flow breaks:

#### 1. CLI Flag Parser:
The parser registers the --agent option correctly:
.option("--agent <agent>", "Specify a custom agent to use")

#### 2. Server Mode Activation Block:
When `--acp` is supplied, the CLI invokes `startServerMode` like so:
```js
let { startServerMode: ee } = await Promise.resolve().then(() => (tIn(), Sto));
await ee({
  port: de,
  stdio: $,
  logDir: G,
  logLevel: b,
  settings: p,
  shutdownService: d,
  featureFlags: r
}, a)
```
Notice that `t.agent` (the custom agent command-line argument) is completely omitted here! The starting server is never supplied with the `--agent` option context.

#### 3. ACP Protocol Limitations:
- The JSON-RPC request for `session/new` (`Ny.SESSION_CREATE`) does not include any parameter to define or activate an agent dynamically.
- While the ACP protocol schema defines a `session/set_config_option` method, the `registerMethods` routing mechanism on the server lacks an implementation of `setSessionConfigOption` (it is defined in the type definitions/client adapter `OSe` but is completely absent from the actual server class router).

### Suggestion for fix:
Pass the command-line override into `startServerMode` configuration parameters and use it to define the initial/default `currentValue` of the `"agent"` configuration option during session setup.

issues.title: disable-model-invocation: true makes a skill unreachable, not manual-only (Skill not found on explicit invocation)

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Summary

A project skill whose `SKILL.md` frontmatter carries `disable-model-invocation: true` is not reachable from the CLI at all. `copilot skill list` shows it under **Project skills**, but the model's `skill()` tool returns `Skill not found: <name>`, so an explicit user request for the skill fails too.

In Claude Code (where the field originated) and in Cursor, `disable-model-invocation: true` means "the model may not select this skill on its own; the user can still invoke it by name". The CLI appears to treat it as "do not expose this skill at all", which leaves no way to run the skill.

### Version / environment

- `GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.79`
- Linux (Fedora, kernel 7.0.13)
- Skill directory: `<repo>/.github/skills/socratic-method/`, inside a git repository

### Reproduction

Using a published skill that ships the field ([socratic-method](https://github.com/grammy-jiang/socratic-method)):

```bash
pipx install socratic-method
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && git init -q .
socratic-method setup copilot --copy   # writes .github/skills/socratic-method/
```

1. The CLI discovers it:

```console
$ copilot skill list
Project skills:
  socratic-method - Interrogates the user's idea with disciplined Socratic questioning until hidden assumptions, ...
```

2. The model cannot reach it, even when named explicitly:

```console
$ copilot -p 'Use the /socratic-method skill. Before asking me anything, reply with exactly
  one line of JSON: {"loaded": true|false, "path": "<SKILL.md path>"}' --allow-all-tools --no-color

✗ skill(socratic-method) Skill not found: socratic-method

{"loaded": false, "path": ""}
```

3. Delete the `disable-model-invocation: true` line from `.github/skills/socratic-method/SKILL.md` and re-run the same prompt — the skill loads normally:

```console
● skill(socratic-method)

{"loaded": true, "path": "/tmp/tmp.XXXX/.github/skills/socratic-method/SKILL.md"}
```

### Isolation

Same sandbox, same prompt, only the frontmatter differs:

| Frontmatter | Result |
|---|---|
| `disable-model-invocation: true` + `user-invocable: true` | `Skill not found` |
| `disable-model-invocation: true` only | `Skill not found` |
| neither key | loads normally |

`disable-model-invocation` alone reproduces it; `user-invocable` is not involved. YAML comments elsewhere in the frontmatter are present in all three cases and are not a factor.

### Expected

`disable-model-invocation: true` should keep the skill out of automatic selection while leaving it invocable when the user names it — matching the semantics of the agent that introduced the field, and matching what the field is for: skills with side effects, or long interactive workflows, that should only run on request.

If the CLI intends different semantics, that is worth documenting. [Adding agent skills for GitHub Copilot CLI](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-skills) documents only `name`, `description`, `license` and `allowed-tools`, so today the behavior is silent: the skill installs fine, lists fine, and only fails at the moment of use.

### Impact

Portable skills written against the shared `SKILL.md` format and published for several agents carry this field to get manual-only behavior wherever it is supported. On the CLI those skills are silently dead — nothing in `skill list`, in install tooling, or in the docs signals a problem until a user tries to run one.

Related but distinct: #3095 (adding capability declaration fields to frontmatter).

issues.title: ACP: /rename reports success but doesn't rename the session

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp --stdio`), `/rename <name>` reports success but doesn't rename the session. Copilot advertises the command in `available_commands_update`, and sending it as a `session/prompt` ends `end_turn` in about 1 ms, with no model call, with the reply `Session renamed to: <name>`. But nothing is saved: the session's `workspace.yaml` keeps its old `name` and `user_named: false`, and `session/list` keeps returning the old `title`, from the same process and from a new one. `/session rename <name>` behaves the same.

ACP has no client method to set a session's title (titles are agent-owned and reported with `session_info_update`), so `/rename` is the only way for an ACP client to rename a Copilot session.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.95

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start `copilot --acp --stdio` and `initialize`.
2. `session/new` with a `cwd`, and send one ordinary prompt, so the session is saved and listed (its title is the first message).
3. Send a `session/prompt` with the text `/rename My new name`.
4. The reply is `Session renamed to: My new name`, with `stopReason: end_turn`.
5. Call `session/list` with that `cwd`, in the same process or a new one: the session's `title` is still the first message.
6. Open `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/workspace.yaml`: still the old `name`, and `user_named: false`. No `session_info_update` is sent with the new title.

### Expected behavior

`/rename <name>` over ACP renames the session as it does in the interactive CLI: it saves the name (`name`, `user_named: true`), `session/list` returns it, and Copilot sends a `session_info_update` with the new `title`, so the client can update its view.

### Additional context

- Windows 11, x86_64. Driven from a Node ACP client (`@agentclientprotocol/sdk`).
- Writing `name` and `user_named: true` into `workspace.yaml` by hand does change the title in `session/list`, so the listing side works. Only the command doesn't save.
- In the 1.0.95 bundle, one session implementation's `renameSession()` calls the native `session.name.set`, and another's is an empty stub (`async renameSession(t){}`, next to `getWorkspace(){return null}`). The ACP session seems to get the stub. The success message is printed either way.
- Related: #4244 (`/rename` in VS Code agent sessions), #2622 (a manual name overwritten by an automatic one).

issues.title: macOS sandbox blocks Gradle daemon connection despite local networking being allowed

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Gradle cannot execute even an offline `help` task inside the Copilot CLI macOS sandbox when outbound and local networking are configured as allowed.

The Gradle daemon starts successfully and listens on localhost, but the Gradle client cannot connect to it:

```text
java.net.SocketException: Operation not permitted
```

The identical command succeeds with the Copilot sandbox disabled. Restarting Copilot with the sandbox enabled does not resolve the failure.

### Affected version

Copilot CLI `1.0.95`; also observed on `1.0.93`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On macOS, enable the Copilot CLI sandbox and allow both outbound and local networking. The configured network settings are:

   ```json
   {
     "allowOutbound": true,
     "allowLocalNetwork": true,
     "allowedHosts": [],
     "blockedHosts": []
   }
   ```

   `/sandbox policy` reports outbound and local networking as allowed.

2. In a Gradle 9.1.0 wrapper project with Java 21 selected, ask Copilot to execute:

   ```bash
   ./gradlew --offline --no-daemon --console=plain --stacktrace help
   ```

3. Gradle launches a single-use daemon to honor the project's JVM settings. The daemon binds a localhost port, but the client connection fails with `Operation not permitted`, before any task executes.

4. Disable the Copilot sandbox and repeat the identical command. It succeeds, executing only `help`.

### Expected behavior

When local networking is explicitly allowed, Gradle should be able to connect to its localhost daemon.

If that setting intentionally excludes host-loopback connections, the policy display should make this distinction clear and document a supported way to permit the required connection without disabling the entire sandbox.

### Additional context

**Environment:** macOS `26.6.2`, ARM64; Gradle wrapper `9.1.0`; Java Amazon Corretto `21.0.6.7.1`.

The command uses offline mode, so dependency downloads are not involved. `--no-daemon` still launches a single-use daemon in this project.

**Kernel-confirmed denial**

In one sandbox-enabled run, the daemon listened on `127.0.0.1:53774`. The macOS kernel log recorded:

```text
Sandbox: java(5913) deny(1) network-outbound remote:*:53774
```

**Effective policy from a separate failing run**

Copilot's debug log identified the generated policy used for the command. Its network section was:

```json
{
  "network": {
    "egress": {
      "default": "deny"
    },
    "ingress": {
      "default": "allow",
      "hostLoopback": "deny"
    },
    "runtimeConfig": {
      "networkProxy": "http://127.0.0.1:55437"
    }
  }
}
```

In that run, the Gradle daemon listened on `127.0.0.1:55438`, not the proxy port `55437`.

This appears consistent with the client being denied a direct host-loopback connection despite `allowLocalNetwork: true`. Gradle's daemon protocol uses raw TCP, so the HTTP proxy cannot carry that connection.

Please investigate whether `allowLocalNetwork` is being mapped correctly to the effective macOS policy, or whether a separate supported host-loopback permission is required.

**Related reports**

- [github/copilot-cli#4854](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4854): a Windows `/sandbox policy` display issue. Unlike that report, the display here says networking is allowed, while the generated policy and kernel denial demonstrate an actual blocked connection.
- [github/copilot-cli#4516](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4516): JVM filesystem-grant failures on macOS, with a recent comment also describing remote-repository/proxy problems. This report concerns the local Gradle daemon connection, without dependency downloads.

Only sanitized excerpts are included here; no project source, credentials, or full conversation/debug logs are attached.

issues.title: Display-only hook for assistant messages (show real values to the user while the model sees redacted tokens)

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

A hook that changes what the **user sees** for an assistant message without changing what the **model sees**. Today a `postToolUse` hook can redact sensitive values in a tool result (`modifiedResult.textResultForLlm`) so the model only sees tokens like `<EMAIL_1>`. But nothing can turn those tokens back into the real values on screen, so the user is stuck reading `<EMAIL_1>` too.

### Proposed solution

Add a display-only hook event for assistant output, for example `messageDisplay` / `MessageDisplay`:

- **Input:** the assistant text as it streams (or the whole message when it's done), plus `sessionId` and a message id.
- **Output:** `displayContent`, the text to render in place of the original. Leaving it out shows the original.
- **Display only:** the session history, the model's context and `--output-format json` keep the original text, so the model never sees the replacement.
- **Fail-open:** on error or timeout, show the original text.

This is the reverse of `userPromptTransformed`, which today changes what the model gets while "the prompt displayed in the timeline is unaffected".

Claude Code ships this as the `MessageDisplay` hook (`hookSpecificOutput.displayContent`). It would also help plugins that target both CLIs, since Copilot CLI already accepts Claude-style PascalCase hooks.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. **Keep PII away from the model.** An MCP server returns customer records. A `postToolUse` hook replaces emails and phone numbers with `<EMAIL_1>`, `<PHONE_1>` and keeps the mapping locally. The model answers "Contact `<EMAIL_1>` about the refund", and the display hook shows the real email to the user.
2. **Internal identifiers.** Swap internal hostnames or account IDs for tokens before the model sees them, and show the real values on screen.
3. **Shown differently, not hidden.** Turn ticket IDs into clickable links, or mark up text on screen, without changing what the model sees or what's stored in the history.

### Additional context

- Tested on Copilot CLI 1.0.94: redacting with `postToolUse` → `modifiedResult` works (the model only sees the token), but the user also sees only the token.
- `--secret-env-vars` and streamer mode only hide values. They can't put the real value back for the user.
- Claude Code reference: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (MessageDisplay).

issues.title: Explicit-approval requests silently denied in resumed sessions: 'could not request permission from user' / orchestrator 'permission request denied: unusable session working directory'

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

In interactive sessions that have been **resumed**, any tool action requiring explicit approval is silently denied instead of prompting the user, even though allow-all ("yolo") elevation is active for the session. Two records appear for each denial:

1. Tool result: `Permission denied and could not request permission from user. Copilot needed the user's approval and no one could answer. This is not an OS or sandbox error.` (error code `denied`)
2. CLI log: `[rust:permissions_engine::orchestrator] permission request denied: unusable session working directory`

Auto-approval of judge-clean actions still works, so the failure masquerades as a targeted block on specific commands (e.g. `sudo pacman …`). `sudo` itself is not special: in one affected resumed session `/usr/bin/sudo -n true && echo sudo-ok` and `sudo -n git --version` were auto-approved and ran, while other escalated commands in the same time window were denied.

Denied actions all involve destructive/privileged operations or file effects **outside the session working directory**; read-only / in-cwd / trivially safe commands in the same turns auto-approve:

| Denied (exact events) | Auto-approved in the same session/turn |
|---|---|
| `mkdir -p ~/Workspace/pkgcache && sudo pacman -Sw --cachedir ~/Workspace/pkgcache …` | `/usr/bin/sudo -n true && echo sudo-ok` |
| `systemd-inhibit --what=idle --mode=block --who=… sleep 3 & INH=$!; loginctl show-session …` | `v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video0 --info …` |
| `rm -rf /tmp/… && mkdir -p /tmp/… && cd /tmp/… && git init …` | `sed -n '411,500p' crates/…/index.rs` |
| `cp -a /run/media/…/build/… /tmp/… && cd /tmp/…` | `echo ok && ls /tmp \| head -3` |
| `cd /tmp && GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0 git clone -q … && cd …` | `grep -n … …` |

All observed denials occurred in **resumed** sessions (one session resumed several times across 4 days; another resumed after a pause). Fresh sessions approve the same class of actions.

Onset: **2026-10-16 on 1.0.99-2** (prerelease channel, auto-update). No occurrences under 1.0.99-0 despite the same usage pattern. Still reproduces on 1.0.100-1 and 1.0.101-0. 24 denial events across `~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log` since 10-16.

## Affected version

`GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.101-0` (first seen on 1.0.99-2; also reproduced on 1.0.100-1)

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use an interactive session with `defaultPermissionMode: "allow-all"` active (session events show `allowAllPermissions: true`), do some ordinary work in a project subdirectory, then end the session.
2. `/resume` (or relaunch the CLI and resume) that session later.
3. In the resumed session, run a command with privileged components or file effects outside the session cwd, e.g. `mkdir -p ~/Workspace/pkgcache && sudo pacman -Sw --cachedir ~/Workspace/pkgcache <pkg>` or `systemd-inhibit --what=idle --mode=block --who=test sleep 3`.
4. Observe the denial above; the orchestrator warning `permission request denied: unusable session working directory` appears in the process log at the same timestamp.
5. Control: the same command in a **fresh** session succeeds; a simple `sudo -n true` in the same resumed session also succeeds.

## Expected behavior

Escalated actions in an interactive session should present an approval prompt the user can answer, or the allow-all elevation (which the session state still reports as active) should cover them. At minimum, the denial should say why the request could not be raised — `unusable session working directory` is currently visible only in the log file, and it is unclear what makes the working directory unusable.

## Additional context

- `~/.copilot/settings.json`: `"defaultPermissionMode": "allow-all"`, `"sandbox": {"enabled": false}`. No managed policy: logs report `[managedSettings] effective policy resolved: source=none, bypassDisabled=false`.
- OS: Linux x86_64 (CachyOS), shell fish (CLI processes run with /bin/bash), terminal Ghostty.
- `copilot help config` says of `defaultPermissionMode`: *"Any value is ignored on resumed sessions, outside interactive runs, and when `--allow-all`/`--yolo` already elevated the session."* The runtime also contains the string `the session-claim bypass requires force=true (omitting the flag is treated as a refusal to escalate)`. If resume intentionally drops the bypass, the session state is misleading: `session.permissions_changed` events still show `allowAllPermissionMode: "on"` and `/yolo on` appears effective.
- Possibly related recent changes (bundled changelog): 1.0.98 *"Resuming a session now respects abandoned pending-permission work and continues only active permission requests."*; 1.0.99-0 / 1.0.100 assisted-permission judge routing for bash commands; 1.0.96 timeline attribution of "unattended fallback" permission decisions.
- Ruled out:
  - **Command concurrency**: ~61% of 4,550 successful tool calls in the most-affected session overlapped another in-flight call; only 5 of 18 denials had an overlapping sibling.
  - **OS/sudo policy**: `sudo whoami` / `sudo -n whoami` run fine in fresh sessions (and simple sudo probes auto-approve even in affected sessions).
  - **Sandbox**: disabled in settings and in effect.
- Evidence is available in `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl` (tool.execution_start/_complete pairs with exact commands and error payloads) and `~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`; happy to attach sanitized extracts on request.

Questions: what condition produces `unusable session working directory` for a session whose cwd exists and is writable? And can the approval path recover (surface the prompt) instead of falling through to the unattended deny?

issues.title: LSP Java (jdtls) on Windows: position-based ops return "No language server available" while workspaceSymbol works

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
Environment:

 - Copilot CLI: 1.0.64
 - OS: Windows 11
 - Java: OpenJDK Temurin 21.0.9
 - LSP server: Eclipse JDT LS (jdtls), launcher org.eclipse.equinox.launcher_1.7.100.v20251111-0406.jar
 - Project: Spring Boot 3 / Java 17 Maven (medium size)

Config (~/.copilot/lsp-config.json):

 {
   "lspServers": {
     "java": {
       "command": "java",
       "args": [
         "-Declipse.application=org.eclipse.jdt.ls.core.id1",
         "-Dosgi.bundles.defaultStartLevel=4",
         "-Declipse.product=org.eclipse.jdt.ls.core.product",
         "-Dlog.level=ALL",
         "-Xmx1G",
         "-jar", "C:\\tools\\jdtls\\plugins\\org.eclipse.equinox.launcher_1.7.100.v20251111-0406.jar",
         "-configuration", "C:\\tools\\jdtls\\config_win",
         "-data", "C:\\tools\\jdtls\\workspace"
       ],
       "fileExtensions": { "java": "java" },
       "initializationTimeoutMs": 300000,
       "warmupTimeoutMs": 300000,
       "requestTimeoutMs": 120000,
       "spawnTimeoutMs": 60000
     }
   }
 }

What works:

 - /lsp test java succeeds; jdtls process spawns and stays alive (~1 GB RSS).
 - lsp workspaceSymbol returns correct results with package/line/column after initial indexing (~3 min on first call).

What fails:
All position-based and file-based LSP operations return "No language server available for file" even though the server is healthy and workspaceSymbol works in the same session:

 - lsp documentSymbol on a .java file in the project → "No language server available"
 - lsp goToDefinition (line/character on a known symbol) → "No language server available"
 - lsp findReferences → same
 - lsp hover → same
 - lsp goToImplementation → same

Tried both Windows paths (C:\...\File.java) and POSIX-style (C:/.../File.java) — same result. The file definitely exists and is inside the project root.

Logs (relevant excerpts from ~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log):

 [ERROR] LSP java server for C:\...\gpron-service: workspaceSymbols failed: Request 'workspace/symbol' timed out after 90000ms.

(Resolved after increasing requestTimeoutMs; workspaceSymbol then succeeded.)

Subsequent file-based operations log no jdtls error — the bridge seems to reject the request before it reaches the server.

Suspected cause:

 - Possible URI canonicalization mismatch on Windows (file:///c:/... vs file:///C:/...)
 - Possible missing textDocument/didOpen notification before position-based requests (jdtls requires the document to be opened first)

Expected: Position-based LSP ops should work consistently with workspaceSymbol once jdtls is initialized.

Workaround: Currently relying on workspaceSymbol + grep for code navigation in Java projects on Windows.

prs.title: [Feature] Add read-only agent monitor TUI (Graph + Timeline)
prs.body:
## Summary

Add an independent, read-only terminal viewer under `tools/agent-monitor` for one explicitly selected local Copilot CLI session, styled with Copilot CLI's own interface language. It answers the questions in the feature request: which agent launched which, who waited on whom and for how long, and what each finished execution produced.

Related: #1783

This is a **standalone sidecar TUI**, not a change to the Copilot CLI runtime or its built-in `/tasks` interface.

## Screenshots

From a fictional demo session (synthetic events, no real transcript).

**Graph** (default view): spawn tree with launch modes and recorded wait durations; the dialog shows the selected agent's task, result and relationships.

![Graph view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ychu-msft/copilot-cli/e0217921faa029277feb5c31e862ace4ec4b8008/tools/agent-monitor/docs/graph.png)

**Graph**, selecting an agent that is blocked on the sync agent it launched:

![Graph view with a waiting agent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ychu-msft/copilot-cli/e0217921faa029277feb5c31e862ace4ec4b8008/tools/agent-monitor/docs/graph-waiting.png)

**Timeline**: one swimlane per execution plus the main session's turns, waiting segments (`╍`), wait connectors (`▾`), a later turn of a reused agent, and the `now` cursor.

![Timeline view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ychu-msft/copilot-cli/e0217921faa029277feb5c31e862ace4ec4b8008/tools/agent-monitor/docs/timeline.png)

## Open it from Copilot CLI

`tools/agent-monitor/extension` is an experimental [Copilot CLI extension](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/tutorials/create-an-extension) that adds `/agent-monitor [graph|timeline|text]` to the session you are working in. It prints the session's agent tree in the conversation, then opens the interactive Graph or Timeline beside the CLI as a Windows Terminal (or tmux) split pane:

```text
● Agents · 7 executions: 1 running, 1 waiting, 3 done, 1 replied, 1 failed
  ○ main session · idle · 2m 41s
  ├─ ✓ api-consumers · explore · 9.0s · done
  │  └─ ↩ api-consumers · explore · turn · 6.7s · replied
  ├─ ✓ paging-scout · explore · 6.3s · done
  ├─ ✓ plan-critic · rubber-duck · 17.1s · done
  ├─ ◌ paging-impl · general-purpose · waiting on unit-tests 42.8s
  │  └─ ◐ unit-tests · task · 42.7s · running
  └─ ✗ web-build · task · 53.5s · failed
```

## Proposal: a built-in Agents tab

The extension API has no way to add a tab to Copilot CLI's own tab bar, so the views open beside it. Built into the CLI, they could be one more tab next to Current and Sessions, with Graph and Timeline as sub-views:

![Mockup: Agents tab with the Graph view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ychu-msft/copilot-cli/987994a30fe54ae47237671cbb1519ffd65375e6/tools/agent-monitor/docs/mockup-agents-tab-graph.png)

![Mockup: Agents tab with the Timeline view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ychu-msft/copilot-cli/987994a30fe54ae47237671cbb1519ffd65375e6/tools/agent-monitor/docs/mockup-agents-tab-timeline.png)

## What changed

- **Copilot CLI look:** tab bar, blue query chips, `·`-separated key hints, bordered detail dialog, and Primer semantic colors for the `/theme` modes (`--theme default|light|dim|high-contrast|colorblind`).
- **Graph (default view):** spawn tree with automatic layout. Edges show `bg` / `sync` plus recorded wait durations, naming the waiter when it is not the edge's parent. A reused agent's later turns sit side by side under its first turn. Cards narrow to fit a wide fan-out; beyond that the graph scrolls with the selection.
- **Timeline view:** swimlanes for every execution plus the main session's turns, waiting segments and connectors, a `now` cursor, and zoom/pan. The default window focuses on agent activity.
- **Detail dialog:** task prompt, final message or error (latest message while running), and recorded relationships. Tool calls stay hidden until `t` is pressed. Below 100 columns the dialog uses one column.
- **Statuses:** `done`, `failed`, `cancelled` (recorded `cancelled: true`, not a failure), `replied` (final answer and turn end recorded without a lifecycle event), and last-observed `running` / `waiting`.
- Replay and live follow remain read-only; partial records, source resets, session shutdown/resume, unsupported agent data, and source errors stay explicit.
- **Copilot CLI extension (experimental):** `/agent-monitor [graph|timeline|text]` prints the agent tree in the conversation and opens the interactive view beside the CLI; the viewer also takes `--view graph|timeline`.

## Review

Reviewed adversarially by two opposing agent groups, each with a separate production-code and test-code reviewer: one group argued for defects, the other challenged each claim against the event schema, synthetic reproductions, and aggregate counts from local logs. Confirmed findings were fixed in e40bc24. All 13 findings from the automated Copilot review on this PR were confirmed and fixed in f1b635c (control-sequence cleaning for every drawn string, read-failure reporting, shutdown/resume and superseded-turn lifecycle cases, early waits, multi-day timeline ticks, and tree-build cost).

<details>
<summary>Findings and resolutions</summary>

| Area | Finding | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lifecycle | `session.resume` after `session.shutdown` left the session `ended` with a frozen clock | Resume makes the session live again (+test) |
| Lifecycle | A completion or cancellation for a reused agent rewrote its first execution; `cancelled: true` was shown as done | Settles the agent's open execution, never overwrites a recorded outcome, new `cancelled` status (+test) |
| Lifecycle | Progress (`phase: commentary`) messages became results; stale `replied` state and end time | Only phase-less or `final_answer` replies count; `replied` needs a final answer in the current turn (+test) |
| Lifecycle | Rejected/blocked `session.task_complete` would show as done | Only accepted completions complete an agent (+test) |
| Robustness | Tool arguments of unexpected types stopped the viewer | Ignored; only `read_agent` targets are read (+test) |
| Layout | Each follow-up nested one level deeper, so long conversations overflowed the Timeline labels | Later turns grouped under the first turn; Timeline indentation capped (+test) |
| Layout | Five parallel agents overflowed 120 columns; 80-column header overlap; a tick label glued to `now`; a wide character at the right edge widened a row | Adaptive card width, progressive header, label gap, wide-character fix (+tests) |
| Performance | Off-screen graph drawing and re-wrapping long results on every frame; unused retained strings | Viewport clipping, wrap cache, unused fields removed |
| Accuracy | Main tool count capped at the 200-entry buffer; silent relationship truncation; text cache ignored log generation; clock kept moving after the source stopped | Total count, `+N more` line, generation-aware key, frozen clock |
| Tests | Assertions that could not fail (sanitization, legend-matched Timeline checks, duplicate events) | Rewritten as lane-specific and visible-text checks |
| Tests | Gaps: reader offsets past 64 KB and across polls, lazy-load race, reset, display names vs. agent IDs, graph scrolling | Added; guard tests mutation-checked |
| Decision | Defense objected to labelling waits from non-parents on a spawn edge, and to adaptive card widths | Kept: the label names the waiter explicitly (as later-turn edges already did), and common 4–5-way fan-outs now fit without hiding cards |

</details>

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck` and the strict unused-code check (`--noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters`) pass.
- `npm test`: **37/37** pass. The 10 tests for the review fixes fail on the previous commit; each of the 5 new guard tests fails when its guard is removed; the 8 tests added for the automated review findings fail without f1b635c.
- `npm run build` passes; built `--help` verified.
- Replay of 219 local session logs (aggregate counts only, no content committed): 5,040 Graph/Timeline frames at 80×24, 120×36 and 160×48 rendered with 0 errors and 0 mis-sized rows; maximum tree depth is now 6. Of 9 recorded cancellations, 1 cancels a follow-up turn (now `cancelled`); 8 arrive after the agent had already completed with no follow-up turn and now keep `completed` instead of moving its end time to the cancellation. One CLI 1.0.21 log is rejected with an explicit diagnostic.
- Windows ConPTY end-to-end run of the built CLI on this branch: Graph/Timeline switching, resizing through a too-small terminal and back, live follow of `session.shutdown` (`ended`) and `session.resume` (`following` again), quit with exit code 0 and alternate-screen restore, the source log left byte-for-byte unchanged, and a malformed record stopping the source with exit code 1. The run also found that keys arriving in one input chunk (a held key during a slow render) were dropped; fixed in e021792 with a test.
- Extension, in a real Copilot CLI 1.0.105 session started with `--experimental` under ConPTY: `/extensions manage` lists `agent-monitor` as running, and `/agent-monitor text` prints the tree in the conversation. The split-pane launch was checked in Windows Terminal: the pane's process received the viewer arguments intact, including a Node.js path containing spaces.
- Only synthetic fixtures and fictional screenshots are committed; private session logs are not.

## Local preview

Requires Node.js 22+ and a truecolor terminal (Windows Terminal works). In a separate terminal tab:

```powershell
Set-Location "<checkout>\tools\agent-monitor"
npm ci
npm run build
node .\dist\cli.js --session "<absolute-session-directory>"
```

Keys: `j`/`k` select, Tab or `v` switches Graph/Timeline, `f` filters, `t` toggles tool calls, Page Up/Down scrolls the result, `+`/`-` and `←`/`→` zoom and pan the Timeline, `q` quits. To use it from inside Copilot CLI, see the extension section of the README.

## Limitations

- The verified on-disk format is Copilot CLI **1.0.104** and **1.0.105** and is version-sensitive.
- Copilot CLI extensions are experimental, and the extension API cannot add tabs to the CLI's own tab bar.
- Spawn edges and recorded waits are not a complete prerequisite DAG. Unrecorded dependencies are labeled `not recorded` rather than inferred.
- Ephemeral events, such as live shell output, and unrecorded results, cancellation, or liveness cannot be reconstructed.
- Building this package does **not** rebuild or replace the `copilot` executable.

releases.body:
**Improved**
- Windows local model downloads install llama.cpp automatically and show engine installation progress.
- /memory show indicates when repository memory scope is unavailable

**Fixed**
- Warn on stderr when the agent selected with `-p --agent` has frontmatter keys Copilot ignores, and log every agent file's warnings
- Auto mode falls back to a valid default when a saved Efficiency preference is unavailable.
- `/fork` no longer fails with "Failed to copy fork session database" when the session's session.db cannot be read; the fork is created without the todo list, and a fork that does fail no longer leaves a half-created session directory behind.
- Hook config files saved with a UTF-8 byte-order mark, as Windows PowerShell 5 and older Notepad versions write them, are now loaded instead of being skipped with only a log entry.
- /share html exports now keep a numbered list's first number and the checkbox and state of task-list items, and both these exports and rich-text copies keep the text inside a raw HTML block such as <details> instead of dropping it.
- /ide draws IDE and folder names as plain text, one row each, and keeps its title, highlighted row and key hints on screen with a long workspace list or on a short terminal.
- A warning about an invalid entry in an LSP config file now names the server it belongs to, so a file with several servers can be fixed without bisecting it.
- A tool call to an HTTP MCP server that fails with a server error or a dropped connection no longer shows an internal Rust type name in front of the reason.
- An image or file path pasted into a message that starts with an absolute path, such as /var/log/app.log, is now attached instead of being sent as plain text.
- `copilot plugin uninstall` now removes a plugin that `copilot plugin list` still shows after its installed files went missing, instead of reporting that it is not installed
- Question forms show control characters in a prefilled default answer instead of sending its escape sequences to the terminal.
- Pasting two images or documents that share a file name from different folders now attaches both instead of silently sending only the second.
- The /tasks dialog draws each task on one row, so a line break in a task description no longer adds a row that looks like another task, and escape sequences no longer restyle it.
- A ~/ entry in the skillDirectories setting now loads skills from your home directory instead of a folder named ~ in the current directory.
- Model loading now fails faster on unreachable network endpoints and shows connectivity guidance.
- ACP sessions now appear in session history, /chronicle, and session_store_sql results.
- PowerShell approval prompts now explain when full-script review is required for valid commands.

issues.title: plugin: local plugin stuck on stale failed load after rebuild (concurrent reloads across locations)
issues.body:
**Bug**

A local plugin built with `tsc` gets stuck in "failed to load" after a rebuild, with an error about code that no longer exists on disk:

```
failed to load plugin target=~/.config/opencode/plugins/kimaki
SyntaxError: Export named 'registerMainmastCompaction' not found in module '.../dist/plugin/mainmast.js'
```

No file on disk imports that name anymore. Only `opencode service restart` fixes it. opencode v2.1.4, macOS, no symlinks (so not #52240).

**What happens (from the log)**

| time | event |
| --- | --- |
| 15:47:05.54 | tsc writes new `mainmast.js`, old `index.js` still on disk. 7 locations reload, all fail. Expected. |
| 15:47:05.69 | tsc writes new `index.js`. 7 locations reload again, **all fail again**, though the files are now consistent |
| later | every reload returns the cached failure until a service restart |

**Cause**

- every location has its own `createPluginSources` (supervisor is a location node: [supervisor.ts#L131](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4617210822bdbb31e5749751afbfb4584ccedac8/packages/core/src/plugin/supervisor.ts#L131), [L268](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4617210822bdbb31e5749751afbfb4584ccedac8/packages/core/src/plugin/supervisor.ts#L268), [module.ts#L40](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4617210822bdbb31e5749751afbfb4584ccedac8/packages/core/src/plugin/module.ts#L40)), but Bun's module registry is per process
- each location deletes `require.cache` and calls `import()` with no coordination with the others ([source.bun.ts#L22](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4617210822bdbb31e5749751afbfb4584ccedac8/packages/plugin/src/source.bun.ts#L22), [L70](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4617210822bdbb31e5749751afbfb4584ccedac8/packages/plugin/src/source.bun.ts#L70))
- when an import starts while another location's import of the half-written graph is in flight, Bun gives it the old `index.js` module record, so it fails even though disk is fine
- that failure is cached with the **new** file digests ([source.ts#L35-L38](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4617210822bdbb31e5749751afbfb4584ccedac8/packages/plugin/src/source.ts#L35-L38)), so the digest check returns it forever ([source.ts#L16-L17](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4617210822bdbb31e5749751afbfb4584ccedac8/packages/plugin/src/source.ts#L16-L17))
- reload debounce is only 100ms ([supervisor.ts#L236](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4617210822bdbb31e5749751afbfb4584ccedac8/packages/core/src/plugin/supervisor.ts#L236)), so a multi-file build triggers several reloads in the middle of the write

**Repro** (Bun 1.4.1, no opencode needed)

```ts
import { writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
const dir = `${import.meta.dir}/repro`
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })
const a = `${dir}/a.js`, b = `${dir}/b.js`
const filler = Array.from({ length: 200 }, (_, i) => `${dir}/f${i}.js`)
for (const f of filler) writeFileSync(f, 'export const v = 1')
const imports = filler.map((_, i) => `import './f${i}.js';`).join('\n')
const load = async (label: string) => {
  for (const f of [a, b, ...filler]) delete require.cache[f]
  try { await import(a); return `${label} ok` } catch { return `${label} FAIL` }
}
writeFileSync(a, `${imports}\nimport { x } from './b.js'; export default x`)
writeFileSync(b, 'export const x = 1')
await load('init')
writeFileSync(b, 'export const y = 2') // half-written build
const first = load('A')
await Bun.sleep(0.5)
writeFileSync(a, `${imports}\nimport { y } from './b.js'; export default y`) // build done
console.log(await Promise.all([first, load('B')]), await load('C'))
// [ "A FAIL", "B FAIL" ] C ok   <- B started after the build finished but still fails
```

**Proposal**

- **debounce reloads longer** (trailing, ~500ms to 1s, reset on every watcher event) so a whole `tsc` / bundler emit lands before any import runs. 100ms is shorter than the gap between files of a normal build
- run local plugin imports through **one process-wide queue** (module-level promise chain in `source.bun.ts`), since the registry they mutate is process-wide
- optionally: if a load fails and any tracked digest changed while it ran, do not cache the failure

issues.title: Desktop: fatal "Location plugins did not finish activating" when the OpenAI login refresh at startup takes over 5 seconds
issues.body:
### Description

When OpenCode Desktop starts and the saved ChatGPT/OpenAI login has expired, the built-in OpenAI plugins refresh it while plugins activate. If that refresh takes longer than 5 seconds, `/api/provider` and `/api/model` return 503 and the window shows a fatal error:

```
ServiceUnavailableError: Location plugins did not finish activating
```

Activation finishes about 2 seconds later in the background (`credential updated integrationID=openai`, then `provider.updated` / `model.updated`), but the window stays on the error until Desktop is restarted. The next start works because the token is fresh.

From the 2.2.5 build it looks like:
- each plugin-dependent request waits at most 5 seconds for Location plugin activation, then fails with 503;
- `ChatGPTPlugin`, `OpenAIPlugin` and `OpenAIContextCapsPlugin` await `integration.connection.resolve(...)` during activation, which refreshes the expired token;
- plugins activate one after another, so every later plugin waits behind the refresh.

Possible fixes: the window could wait or retry instead of treating this 503 as fatal, or the OpenAI plugins could refresh the token after activation or on first use.

Related: #57204 (same error on ACP `session/resume`).

Logs from the failing start (Desktop main/renderer and server, trimmed):

```
14:58:13.752 v2 CLI background service ready
14:58:19.058 GET /api/provider 503 (5060 ms)
14:58:19.060 GET /api/model 503 (5062 ms)
14:58:19.088 fatal renderer error: ServiceUnavailableError: Location plugins did not finish activating
14:58:20.730 credential updated integrationID=openai
14:58:20.858 provider.updated / model.updated
```

### Plugins

opencode-quota (local build). Its setup takes about 5 ms and runs after the built-in OpenAI plugins; the error is the same with a slow token refresh and no slow plugin work.

### OpenCode version

Desktop 2.2.5 (bundled CLI 2.2.5)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to OpenAI with ChatGPT in OpenCode Desktop.
2. Quit Desktop and wait until the access token has expired.
3. Make the token refresh slow. I held the reply to `POST https://auth.openai.com/api/accounts/oauth/token` for 8 seconds in a test harness; a slow network does the same.
4. Start Desktop.
5. The window shows "Location plugins did not finish activating". With no delay it starts normally.

### Screenshot and/or share link

```
ServiceUnavailableError: Location plugins did not finish activating
    at GSt (oc://renderer/assets/main-DH32_HOX.js:54:33442)
    at i (oc://renderer/assets/main-DH32_HOX.js:43:62924)

```

issues.title: mcp: dynamic client registration omits logo_uri
issues.body:
### Description

When an MCP server uses dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) instead of CIMD, the client metadata we send has no `logo_uri`, so authorization servers that would show a logo during consent have nothing to show.

We already declare the logo in the client metadata document we publish:

```json
// https://opencode.ai/oauth/opencode/client.json
"logo_uri": "https://opencode.ai/web-app-manifest-512x512.png"
```

But that document is only used when a server advertises `client_id_metadata_document_supported`. For servers that fall back to DCR (`registration=dcr`), `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth.ts` sets `client_name` and `client_uri` and stops there.

RFC 7591 §2 defines `logo_uri` and says the authorization server SHOULD display it to the end user during approval, so this is the field that makes consent screens look like us instead of a bare client name.

### OpenCode version

2.1.4

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a remote MCP server whose authorization server does not support CIMD.
2. Start the OAuth flow.
3. Inspect the `POST /register` body: `client_name` and `client_uri` are present, `logo_uri` is absent.

issues.title: migrate-v1: non-git sessions in "global" project hidden after V1→V2 upgrade
issues.body:
## Summary

After upgrading from V1.18.31 to V2.0.8, sessions that V1 stored in the `global` project (sessions created in non-git directories) become invisible in the TUI session picker, because V2 creates a per-directory project and the picker filters to the current project. The history is still in the database, so users perceive all recent conversations as lost.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.8 (upgraded from 1.18.31)
- OS: Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (WSL2), x86_64
- Terminal: xterm-256color
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest (curl installer replaced the V1 binary)
- Active plugins: `@wallbreakerno4/opencode-commandcode`

## Reproduction

1. On V1.18.31, run `opencode` in a non-git directory (e.g. `/home/wjf`) and create several sessions. They are stored with `project_id = 'global'`.
2. Upgrade to V2.0.8 so the installer replaces the V1 binary.
3. Start V2 in the same directory (`/home/wjf`).
4. V2 creates a new project keyed to `/home/wjf`. The session picker defaults to filtering by the current project and directory, so only sessions created after the upgrade are listed; all prior sessions are hidden.

## Expected Behavior

Sessions created for the same working directory should remain visible after upgrading. V1's `global` sessions in a non-git directory should be migrated to that directory's V2 project (or otherwise kept visible), per the migration guide's statement that supported non-API V1 behavior stays compatible.

## Actual Behavior

The sessions remain in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` but are not shown in the default session list. `GET /api/session` returns them (they carry `projectID: "global"`), while the TUI picker filters client-side to `projectID === current project.id && location.directory === current directory`. The `Ctrl+O` dialog reports `No matches · search all sessions with <leader>l`.

## Additional Context

- Database: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, table `session_v2`. Before repair: 104 sessions total, 93 with `project_id = 'global'` (81 in `/home/wjf`, 8 in `/tmp/opencode`, 3 in `/home/wjf/novel`, 1 in `/home/wjf/videos`).
- Sessions in a git repository were unaffected: `/home/wjf/fadebreak` kept a stable project id across the upgrade and stayed visible.
- Relevant log timing: migrations ran at `2026-09-18T17:52:20Z`; the new `/home/wjf` project row was created at `2026-09-18T17:52:21Z`.
- Workaround: `Ctrl+X` then `L` ("List all sessions") shows everything, including the `global` project. Inside `Ctrl+O`, pressing `<leader>l` switches to searching all sessions.
- Repair performed locally: `POST /api/session/{sessionID}/move` with `{"directory": "<the session's directory>"}` re-bound each of the 93 `global` sessions to its directory project, after which they appear normally. This worked, but required knowing the sessions were hidden.
- Likely cause: V1 used a single `global` project for non-git directories, while V2 derives a per-directory project id (SHA-1 of the path). No data migration re-keys V1 `global` sessions.

issues.title: tui: plan/build mode state desyncs between UI and agent, causing unauthorized or refused work
issues.body:
# opencode: Plan/Build mode state desyncs between UI and agent

## Summary

The system-reminder blocks injected into the conversation toggle between "You are in Plan
mode" and "You are NO LONGER in Plan mode" at points that do not match the user's actual
mode selection in the UI. This causes the agent to refuse modifications when the user
believes they are in Build mode, or to execute modifications when the user believes they
are in Plan mode. The confusion is recurring across sessions.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.5
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-42-generic (Ubuntu, x64)
- Terminal: Guake (TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor)
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest (release)
- Active plugins: None found in config
- Default agent: `"default_agent": "plan"` (set in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json)

## Reproduction

1. Start a session. The default agent is `plan`, so the session begins in Plan mode.
2. Switch to Build mode in the UI (or via agent switch).
3. Continue working. At various points, system-reminder blocks are injected stating
   "You are in Plan mode" even though the user selected Build mode.
4. Conversely, after the user switches back to Plan mode, reminders may say
   "You are NO LONGER in Plan mode."
5. The agent follows the reminder, not the user's stated mode, leading to either
   refused work or unauthorized modifications.

## Expected Behavior

The agent's mode should always match the user's current selection in the UI. Mode
transitions should be unambiguous and not fire spuriously mid-conversation.

## Actual Behavior

- System-reminder blocks toggle between Plan and Build mode independently of user
  actions, sometimes mid-conversation and sometimes after a single user message.
- The agent cannot verify the true mode state beyond these blocks.
- In this session alone, the mode flipped at least 6 times, including:
  - Plan mode active while user said "we're in build mode here, please continue"
  - Plan mode active immediately after a user message asking to commit changes
  - Build-mode actions (file writes, git commits, docker restarts) executed while
    the reminder said Plan mode, because the user explicitly requested them

## Additional Context

- The config has `"default_agent": "plan"`, which means every new session starts in
  Plan mode. This default may contribute to confusion — a new user or a user who
  expects Build mode on startup will immediately be in Plan mode without realizing it.
- **Session database investigation (privacy-safe):** Each session in
  `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` has an `agent` column (values: `plan`,
  `build`, `explore`). The mode is stored per-session, not per-message. When the
  user "switches agents" in the UI, it likely creates a new session or updates the
  `agent` field. The system-reminder blocks reference the mode of the *current*
  session, but the reminder text can lag behind the user's actual selection,
  especially when multiple sessions are open or the user switches mid-conversation.
- **Database evidence (this session, `ses_e6cefdd06ffe7nncEAts4aJCIa`):** The session's
  `agent` field in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` is `"plan"` and never changes.
  However, the synthetic system-reminder messages within the session toggle between
  "You are in Plan mode" and "You are NO LONGER in Plan mode" **13 times** in a
  single session. The timestamps of these toggles do not correlate with any user
  agent-switch action — they appear to fire on their own schedule.
- **Observed in this session:** The mode reminder toggled at least 13 times during
  a single long session, including:
  - "You are in Plan mode" appearing immediately after the user said "we're in
    build mode here, please continue" and asked me to commit changes.

issues.title: A bug where a session is automatically executed without permission.
issues.body:
## Description

I was building a desktop app (`translate-desktop`) in one project. The build was still running when I rebooted my computer.

After the reboot, I started `opencode --yolo` in a different project directory. OpenCode automatically resumed the unfinished session from the other project and continued running it. It repeatedly launched `translate-desktop` windows and interrupted my work.

I did not approve this. I also could not find a clear setting or command to disable it.

## OpenCode version(opencode TUI)

`2.2.1` (`latest` channel)

### Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), kernel `6.12.113+deb13-amd64`, x86_64.

### Terminal

GNOME Terminal on Wayland, `TERM=xterm-256color`, shell `/bin/bash`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a long-running build in a session. The build opens a desktop app window.
2. While it is still running, reboot the computer.
3. After reboot, start `opencode --yolo` from a different project directory.
4. Do not resume anything manually.
5. The old unfinished session starts by itself and keeps launching the app.

## Expected behavior

- After a reboot, unfinished sessions should stay paused.
- OpenCode should ask before resuming, or provide a clear setting/command to disable auto-resume.

## Actual behavior

The old session resumes automatically, runs tools without my consent, and opens app windows.

## Additional context

- The issue is not the app itself. The problem is that OpenCode resumes the old session without asking.
- The background service is global, so a session from another project can be resumed even when I start OpenCode in a different directory.
- Workaround: press `Esc` to interrupt the turn before rebooting, or run `opencode service set disabled true` to use a standalone server. There is no obvious setting for this.

issues.title: Opencode GO DeepSeek cache hit rate collapses with parallel subagents
issues.body:
### Description

# Go: DeepSeek cache hit rate collapses with parallel subagents

I normally get 97–99% cache hits with `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`. On two days, running more than one or two subagents at once caused repeated full-context rereads in both the parent and children. I've used subagents heavily before without this happening.

The clearest example: after launching nine children together, the parent's cache hit rate went from **97.4% to 7.0%** over five-minute windows. Billing exports also show the increase in uncached input, so this isn't just the TUI reporting it wrong.

## Setup

- OpenCode **2.2.0**, latest channel, `--standalone`
- Linux container, zsh
- Parent and children all using `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`
- Two local plugins: one allows model to call native compaction and one types continue if a model stops. Neither change anything cache related.

I used the same plugins and configuration throughout the run, on both good and bad days. The system prompts and tool definitions are static. The plugins trigger native compaction or print chat text; they don't rewrite the cacheable prefix. The cache losses below aren't compaction events.


## Related

In 2.2.0, [children share the parent's affinity ID](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.2.0/packages/core/src/session/affinity.ts). [That ID is used for both routing headers and the prompt cache key](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.2.0/packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts), so all nine children and the parent share it.

#61318 describes the same symptom, but I'm on **2.2.0**, not 2.2.4 or later.


### Plugins

two custom tools. No effect on cache.

### OpenCode version

2.2.0

### Steps to reproduce

## Steps

1. Work in a parent session until its cache is warm.
2. Launch several same-model subagents in parallel; nine in this example.
3. Let the parent and children keep working.

Already-warm sessions repeatedly drop to zero cache reads, recover, then drop again. I'd expect launching children not to destroy the parent's warm cache, or each other's.

## Numbers from the session database

These are ordinary parent requests, excluding compaction calls:

| Window around child launch | Requests | Cache hit rate | Zero-cache-read requests |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 minutes before | 26 | 97.43% | 1 |
| 5 minutes after | 14 | 6.95% | 13 |
| 15 minutes before | 123 | 97.90% | 2 |
| 15 minutes after | 54 | 49.65% | 26 |

The parent had compacted earlier, but cache reads had already recovered to **69,504 tokens** before the launch. Its next three requests read **zero** cached tokens, with **91,037 / 95,920 / 96,724** uncached input tokens. No compaction record falls between those requests.

It happens in the children too. One child's consecutive cache-read counts were **299,392 → 0 → 290,176 → 314,624**. The cold request started just 4.46 seconds after the warm one.

Across the capture there were **227 warm-to-zero transitions**, including 144 in children: a request with >95% hits and >50k cached tokens, followed within two minutes by zero cache reads, without an intervening compaction record.

Hit rates here are `cache_read / (uncached_input + cache_read)`.


### Screenshot

_No response_

### Operating System

Fedora 44 KDE

### Terminal

Kitty

issues.title: session: all history images are re-sent on every request, permanently breaking sessions on image-capped backends
issues.body:
## Summary

OpenCode re-sends every image that was ever pasted or returned by `Read` in a session on every model request, with no pruning. On backends that enforce a per-prompt image limit (e.g. vLLM with `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":4}'`), the session becomes permanently unusable once the history accumulates more images than the cap: every subsequent request fails instantly with a 400, and since the offending images are in history, re-prompting can never recover the session.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.0
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic (Ubuntu, x86_64)
- Terminal: TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest (opencode v2.2.0 via ~/.opencode/bin)
- Active plugins: none at time of failure (a local `image-budget` plugin was added afterwards as a workaround)

## Reproduction

1. Point OpenCode at an OpenAI-compatible server that caps images per request, e.g. vLLM started with `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":4}'`.
2. In one session, paste 2 screenshots and let the agent `Read` 3 PNG files across later turns (5 images total in history).
3. Ask anything, or ask the agent to check one more rendered image.

## Expected Behavior

The request still succeeds: stale images (tool-result screenshots the model already described in text, superseded screenshots) are pruned from the *outgoing request* — e.g. replaced by a short text placeholder like Claude Code does — keeping only the newest N images, where N matches the provider's supported per-prompt image count (configurable per model/provider).

## Actual Behavior

Every request carries all 5 history images and is rejected at ~46 ms:

```
Error: At most 4 image(s) may be provided in one prompt. (parameter=image)
```

The failure is sticky forever: the images live in persisted history and are re-sent on every turn, including new user messages, so the session can never continue. The only current recovery is manual (undo across image turns, or editing the session database).

## Additional Context

- Reproduced consistently; any session that iterates on rendered screenshots (a very common agent loop: render → Read PNG → adjust) inevitably crosses the cap.
- Anthropic-compatible clients such as Claude Code avoid this by stripping old image payloads from the request history after the model has consumed them, leaving a text placeholder; persisted history is unaffected. OpenCode sending history verbatim is the difference, not the server cap.
- The V2 plugin system can half-fix it (`ctx.session.hook("context")` mutating `event.messages`), which I'm using now, but a built-in policy is better: it needs no per-user plugin, and only OpenCode knows which images are stale vs. freshly attached in the current turn.
- Suggested design: a per-model/provider setting (e.g. `limit.imagesPerPrompt` or reuse `attachment`/modalities metadata) plus default pruning of image parts older than the current turn (or last-N), with the trimmed placeholder text explaining the image was pruned.

issues.title: agent: degenerate meta-planning loop - turn produces zero output, reasoning leaks into reply
issues.body:
## Summary

A large language-model session can end in a degenerate meta-planning loop: the model repeatedly announces imminent execution ("Execute now. FINAL. Go.") with increasing compression, never emits tool calls or a final answer, and the turn produces zero output. In observed cases, internal reasoning text also leaked into the visible reply instead of staying hidden.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.1.4
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26300 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Unavailable: terminal environment variables are not set (OpenCode desktop app)
- Shell: cmd.exe (harness); session tooling runs PowerShell
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: @dietrichgebert/ponytail (5.3.2, supply-chain audited — no network/eval/processes), opencode-spend-tracker (local file plugin, code-read: ledger reader only)

## Reproduction

Reproduction is not deterministic; it occurred in 2–3 sessions under these conditions:

1. A previous assistant turn fails or produces an incoherent/partial response.
2. The next turn carries a large multi-step task (recover from the failure + design + implement + run + report).
3. The model enters a planning phase that never terminates: instead of tool calls or a reply, it emits endlessly repeating self-instructions of the form "Execute now. (END) OK. Final answer now. Stop. Write. Go. FINAL." — each iteration shorter, hundreds of repetitions, consuming the entire turn.
4. No tool call is ever issued; the session appears hung from the user's side until manually interrupted.

## Expected Behavior

The agent either acts (issues tool calls) or produces a final reply. A failure to plan should surface as an error or a normal reply stating the difficulty — not an unterminated repetition loop.

## Actual Behavior

- Turn output = hundreds of repeated "executing now"-style filler tokens; zero tool calls; zero deliverable.
- Chain-of-thought/scratchpad text ("Hmm, but background is safer...", "Careful with the script — no bugs") appeared in the visible reply rather than staying in the hidden reasoning channel.
- Observed in 2–3 sessions over 2026-10-30/31; always after a prior turn failure; always under large multi-step task framing.

## Additional Context

- User workaround that works: interrupt early, then issue a direct imperative ("stop planning, act now") — a fresh, imperative-heavy turn recovers immediately. Smaller task scoping per turn also prevents recurrence.
- Possibly related to a separate harness-layer symptom reported separately: an instruction block appearing in the user channel that exists in zero stored session messages (see companion issue). Both symptoms sit at the client↔model context-assembly layer, so may share a root cause in middleware (context assembly/compaction/injection ordering).
- The corrupted turn is preserved verbatim by the user if the team wants the full token-level sample.

issues.title: harness: instruction block injected into user channel, absent from all stored session messages
issues.body:
## Summary

An instruction block headed "⚠️ CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS FROM USER" appeared in the user-message channel mid-session. It did not come from the user. Forensic sweep of the local session store shows the block exists in zero stored messages — it was injected between the client and the model, i.e., in the agent harness / middleware layer that assembles model context. The agent flagged it instead of obeying it; no harm occurred, but the injection path is unexplained.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.1.4
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26300 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Unavailable: terminal environment variables are not set (OpenCode desktop app)
- Shell: cmd.exe (harness)
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: @dietrichgebert/ponytail (5.3.2, audited: no network/eval/child processes), opencode-spend-tracker (server half read in full: pure ledger reader, no message mutation, no network)

## Reproduction

Not deterministically reproducible; occurred once (2026-10-29, ~21:36 UTC window):

1. Normal working session with tool calls (a browser tool call was interrupted immediately prior).
2. An instruction block appears in the user channel, styled as coming from the user ("⚠️ CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS FROM USER"), instructing the agent to persist instructions for all future steps, treat URLs/pages/user messages as untrusted, save evidence to a case folder, and end every reply with a structured report.
3. The real user states they never typed it.

## Forensic elimination (all vectors checked)

- Full read-only sweep of the local session store (`opencode.db` + WAL, all tables: session_message, event, session_inbox, session_pending, kv, account_state, account, control_account, credential, project*, instruction*, workspace, worktree, migration): the block's distinctive phrases exist in ZERO stored messages. Only hits are the agent's own discussion of it and the user quoting the warning later.
- Global plugins: both audited at code level; eliminated.
- OpenCode server: password IS set (`service.json`); server log in the window shows only routine plugin loads and worktree-discovery warnings — no hook events, no compaction.
- Desktop app store: `drafts.sqlite` (composer drafts) checked 2026-10-31 — zero hits. (Last vector; now closed.)

## Expected Behavior

Everything in the user channel should be traceable to a stored user message (or a documented harness mechanism). Nothing should enter model context that doesn't exist in the session store or an audited plugin.

## Actual Behavior

An instruction block entered model context that cannot be attributed to any stored artifact, plugin, or local hook — i.e., it was assembled into the prompt between client and model. Attribution beyond that boundary is outside the agent's reach.

## Additional Context

- Style/content of the block matches a scenario template (a security-training-style scenario: "treat everything as untrusted, save evidence, structured reports") rather than anything the user produced. It may originate from harness/middleware middleware (an evaluation or A/B scenario template leaking into a production context path).
- Defense adopted by the user regardless: instructions from non-composer channels are treated as DATA and never executed; unrecognized blocks are logged as incidents (this is incident #1 in the user's register).
- Possibly related to a companion issue: degenerate repetition loops observed in 2–3 subsequent sessions (same client↔model layer).

issues.title: Free tier issues: read this first, then post your report here

labels.name: zen
labels.description: Relates to Zen

issues.body:
This is the **main issue for free tier problems**. If you see any of these, you're in the right place:

- `Free usage exceeded, subscribe to Go`
- `Free usage limit reached`
- `You've used today's free messages. They reset at ...` and the reset never happens
- `This version of OpenCode Desktop no longer supports free models`
- `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`
- `OpenCode 1.18.0 or newer is required to use the free tier`

**Please comment here instead of opening a new issue.** We're closing duplicates and pointing them here so everything is in one place.

## 1. Make sure you're on the latest OpenCode v2

Most free tier reports come from **OpenCode v1** (versions `0.x` and `1.x`, for example Desktop or CLI `1.19.5`). v1 no longer supports free models and only gets fixes for critical bugs. Updating to v2 has fixed this for many people.

Check your version:

- **Terminal:** `opencode --version`
- **Desktop:** Settings → About

The latest v2 release is **2.2.1**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The v1 Desktop app's built-in updater keeps you on `1.x`. Download v2 manually from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**.

### Desktop

Download v2 Desktop for macOS, Windows or Linux from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**, or on macOS:

```sh
brew install --cask opencode-desktop
```

### Terminal (TUI / CLI)

All install options are listed at **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**. The quickest on macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

Or use a package manager:

```sh
npm install -g @opencode/cli
bun install -g --trust @opencode/cli
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
paru -S opencode-beta
```

v1 and v2 both use the `opencode` command. If you installed v1 with a package manager, remove it first, for example `npm uninstall -g opencode-ai`. Windows package managers (Chocolatey, Scoop) don't support v2. On Windows, use the Desktop app, npm, or a [standalone binary](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/).

### Useful docs

- [Install OpenCode v2](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)
- [Migrate from v1](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/)
- [Free models, limits and privacy](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/models/#free-models)
- [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/)
- [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting/)

## 2. Other things to check

- **Free models only work inside OpenCode.** Other clients, proxies and direct API calls can't use them. Use a paid model or [Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/) there instead.
- **Subscribed to Go but still seeing free limits?** Run `/connect`, sign in with **OpenCode Console** in your browser (make sure you authorize the workspace with your Go subscription, or choose **OpenCode Go** if you use a Go API key), then pick a Go model (`opencode-go/...`) with `/models` rather than a free model (`opencode/...-free`).
- **Hit the real daily limit?** Wait for the reset time shown, subscribe to [Go](https://opencode.ai/go), or connect another provider with `/connect`.

## 3. Still broken on the latest v2? Comment with:

- OpenCode version, and whether you use Desktop, TUI, CLI or web
- Operating system
- The free model you used
- The exact error message (a screenshot is fine)
- When it started and the reset time you were shown
- Whether you have Go or Console credits

> [!WARNING]
> Don't post email addresses, payment details or other account information here. This issue is public.

## 4. Still don't know what's going on?

If you're on the latest v2 and none of the above helps, or the problem is about your account, billing or Go subscription, email **help@anoma.ly** with the details from step 3. Billing and account issues can't be fixed in GitHub issues.

issues.title: MCP HTTP handlers read an empty registry on cold locations
issues.body:
### Description

MCP HTTP handlers can read the registry before config plugins register servers for a cold directory. On macOS, the first `opencode mcp list` says `No MCP servers configured`; the same command then lists the configured servers. This is a cold-location race, distinct from the persistent warm-service symptoms in #50710.

Source regression tests also reproduce cold `connect`, `disconnect`, and `remove` returning 404 for a configured server. Waiting for plugin activation makes those requests succeed. Proposed fix: #54191.

### Plugins

The source reproduction uses built-in config plugins only.

### OpenCode version

Installed 2.0.21; reproduced with current v2 source using Bun 1.4.2.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an MCP server in the global config.
2. Create a new directory and change into it.
3. Run `opencode mcp list`: it may report no configured servers.
4. Repeat from the same directory after initialization: the server appears.

Expected: the first request waits for config registration and lists the configured server.

The regression in #54191 uses an in-memory server and a disabled local MCP server, so it needs no remote authentication. Without the readiness wait, the first `/api/mcp` response is HTTP 200 with `data: []`.

### Screenshot and/or share link

Reproduction and regression tests: #54191.

### Operating System

macOS 26.5, Apple Silicon.

issues.title: app: sidebar does not show a forked session until returning to Home
issues.body:
## Summary

Forking a session from a message works on the server, but the desktop sidebar session list does not show the new forked session until the user returns to Home (full list refetch).

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.5 (OpenCode Desktop)
- OS: Windows 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Shell: cmd.exe
- Install/channel: release (`latest`)
- Active plugins: none

## Reproduction

1. Open any session in OpenCode Desktop 2.2.5.
2. Fork it from a message: message actions → "Fork from here", or the command palette → "Fork from message".
3. Look at the left sidebar session list.
4. The fork is missing. Navigate to Home and back, and it appears.

## Expected Behavior

The forked session appears in the sidebar immediately, the same way a newly created session does.

## Actual Behavior

The fork is created successfully server-side (`POST /api/session/{sessionID}/fork` returns 200, and `GET /api/session` includes it), but the sidebar list does not update.

## Additional Context

The desktop event handler handles `session.created` by invalidating and syncing the session, which is what inserts the sidebar row:

```js
case `session.created`:
  me(n.data.sessionID), C.delete(n.data.sessionID),
  Te.session.invalidate(n.data.sessionID),
  r(() => Te.session.sync(n.data.sessionID)),
  ...
```

There is no `case` for `session.forked` in that switch (49 `session.*` cases, no fork one). The fork endpoint emits `session.forked` only, not `session.created`, so the list never learns about the new session.

`session.viewed` cannot rescue it either, because it early-returns when the session is not already in the local store:

```js
case `session.viewed`:
  if (!o.session.info[n.data.sessionID] && !p.has(`session:${n.data.sessionID}`)) return
  Te.session.invalidate(n.data.sessionID), r(() => Te.session.sync(n.data.sessionID))
```

Suggested fix: handle `session.forked` like `session.created` (invalidate/sync and insert the forked session into the sidebar list)
