issues.title: acp: manual /compact turn completes with no output — ACP clients see an empty response and auto-retry (zhipu/glm-5.3-flash)
issues.body:
## Summary

Triggering context compaction over ACP reliably produces a turn with **no output at all**: the prompt completes without error, but nothing reaches the client, so the hosting app renders an empty-response error ("AI returned no content") and auto-continues the turn. Happens both when the user sends the `/compact` slash command and when the client's compaction action sends it.

The compaction itself appears to take effect (context usage drops sharply afterwards), but from the client's point of view the turn is completely silent.

## Environment

- opencode version: **v2.2.5** (`opencode acp`)
- Host app: ClawBench 0.131.0 (also reproduced on 0.130.0), driving the opencode agent over ACP stdio
- Model: `zhipu` / `glm-5.3-flash`
- OS: Linux x64

## Reproduction

1. Use a session with a large context (e.g. a few hundred k tokens) on `zhipu/glm-5.3-flash` via an ACP client.
2. Send `/compact` as a prompt (via slash command or a compaction button that sends the same text).
3. The turn runs for about a minute, then ends **without any content updates**. The client shows an empty-response error; the app's auto-continue then resumes the turn, consuming extra tokens.

Observed every time on both trigger paths.

## Host-side log evidence (ClawBench, abridged)

- `conn.Prompt done ... elapsed=1m4.8s error=<nil>` — the ACP prompt finished successfully
- `ai stream run done ... blocks=1 cancel_reason=""`
- `auto-continue: resuming abnormally terminated turn ... reason=empty max_retries=3` — the client classified the turn as empty
- `acp: compaction detected source=usage_drop used_before=364627 used_after=66327` — compaction did happen (usage collapsed), but the client could only infer it from the usage drop, never received the summary/completion itself

## Expected Behavior

A manual compaction turn should surface something to the client — the summary text and/or a completion notification — or fail with a visible error. Ending the turn successfully with zero output makes every ACP client that doesn't track compaction internally look broken (empty response + unintended retries).

## Actual Behavior

The turn ends cleanly with no content delivered; the client shows "AI returned no content" and auto-retries.

## Related

- #59518 — empty responses (`content=[]`, `finish=stop`) on GLM-family models
- #50295 / #40494 — earlier ACP compaction-summary handling changes

![screenshot: /compact sent, turn ends with "AI returned no content" and retry button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hechuancy/opencode-61232-screenshot/main/compact-empty.png)

issues.title: Settled assistant messages regress to running when session.step.started is re-delivered in the solid client reducer
issues.body:
Parent: #61401 (at-least-once SSE delivery confirmed; "hardening the reducer is correct under any duplication origin")

`session.step.started` (`packages/client/src/solid/data.ts`, case at ~line 972) unconditionally resets an existing assistant message when the same `assistantMessageID` is seen again:

```ts
existing.error = undefined
existing.finish = undefined
existing.rawFinish = undefined
existing.time.completed = undefined
existing.time.streamed = undefined
```

`session.tool.success` / `session.tool.failed` guard their terminal states (`if (tool.state.status !== "running") return`), and #61399 added the same guard for `tool.called` (#61401). `step.started` is the remaining unguarded handler.

### When this fires

A re-delivered `session.step.started` landing after `session.step.ended` / `session.step.failed` regresses a settled assistant message: `finish`, the completion time and any error banner vanish, and `message.activeAssistant` re-classifies it as an in-flight message until the next full message sync.

The legitimate retry path cannot produce this sequence: `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts` reuses the same assistant message id only inside the `Retry` outcome, which returns before any settlement — so a settled message receiving `Step.Started` again is necessarily a duplicate delivery.

### Repro (same harness as #61399's `packages/client/test/solid-data.test.ts`)

1. publish `session.step.started` (msg A)
2. publish `session.step.ended` (msg A, finish `"stop"`)
3. re-publish step 1

→ msg A: `time.completed === undefined`, `finish === undefined` — the completed message regressed to running.

### Fix direction

Mirror #61399 — in the reset branch: `if (existing.time.completed !== undefined) return` (the Retry path never settles before re-starting, so legitimate flows are unaffected).

Happy to follow up with a fix PR once triaged.

issues.title: Historical forks replay instruction updates that contradict their inherited baseline
issues.body:
### Description

A historical fork inherits the parent's latest instruction values, but also replays older instruction updates from the copied history. Those system messages can contradict the new baseline. API context entries explicitly say the old value supersedes the previous one.

### OpenCode version

`dev` at `fe046564650854594c4c5aa22270f46d9de6cace` (2.2.5).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a session with an instruction source whose value changes from A to B to C across requests.
2. Fork at a historical point that includes the B update but precedes C.
3. Continue the fork and inspect the next model request.

The initial instructions contain C, while a later system message still applies B. The inherited instruction state already equals C, so no corrective update is generated.

Expected: the fork uses its inherited current baseline without replaying superseded updates. New instruction changes made after the fork should still be delivered.

Reproduced with the real SessionRunner and database using a local test LLM. The existing `seeds a fork with the parent's newest instruction values` test currently asserts that the stale update remains; changing that expectation exposes the conflict. No live model behavior is claimed.

[Regression test and proposed fix](https://github.com/yyytttwww888-beep/opencode/commit/451a317230a129b8093489a9e6c223ed94196ba3).

prs.title: fix(plugin): serialize local module reloads across locations
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60312

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Overlapping location reloads can reuse an in-flight Bun import and cache its old module or failure under the new source digests. Later reads then keep returning that result even after the files are fixed.

Root `bun run check` passed all 35 tasks and plugin `typecheck:tsc` passed. In 610 repeated TUI source tests, an existing watcher test missed a filesystem event once; it then passed 10 standalone runs. The separate seven-cache rebuild probe also recovers after the files are consistent.

I haven't verified the compiled-binary case in #61525 or an interactive TUI session. Codex assisted with implementation and verification.

prs.title: perf(ui): run the spinner and the text shimmer on the compositor
prs.body:
While a session runs, its spinner and its "Working" shimmer animated on the main thread: every frame restyled and repainted the spinner's 24 dots and the shimmering text, for as long as the agent worked. Both now animate on the compositor, so a running session at rest costs the page's main thread nothing per frame. They look the same.

### Discovery (strobe)

The new case `wait on a running session` (below) watches five seconds of a running session with nothing streaming: the tab's spinner and the Working shimmer animate, and nothing else changes.

Recorded on an M4 MacBook Air (macOS 27) under `taskpolicy -b` while its owner used it. Single attribution recordings: noisy discovery evidence, not results.

```sh
strobe record --bench "packages/app/perf/stream.bench.ts#wait on a running session" --head fe04656465   # rec_d58880: dev
strobe record --bench "packages/app/perf/stream.bench.ts#wait on a running session" --head .            # rec_d08d12: this branch
strobe query rec_d58880 summary
strobe query rec_d58880 sql "select ... from slice where name in ('ProxyMain::BeginMainFrame', 'UpdateLayoutTree', ...)"   # per measured run
```

Per 5-second run (14 measured runs each):

| | dev (`rec_d58880`) | this branch (`rec_d08d12`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main-thread frames (`ProxyMain::BeginMainFrame`) | 25.9, 862 ms | 12.3, 21.5 ms |
| Style recalculation (`UpdateLayoutTree`) | 49.4, 302 ms | 23.2, 9.7 ms |
| Pre-paint | 140 ms | 2.2 ms |
| Main thread busy (summary) | 3.20% | 0.53% |

At background priority the Mac's renderer produced only a few main-thread frames a second on dev, so these are far fewer frames than a display at full speed would ask for; the timed run below measures the cost per run.

How it was found: `strobe record --bench "packages/app/perf/stream.bench.ts#stream a reply"` on dev (exp_c54492) failed its attribution block in setup with "the page never went idle": a running session kept producing frames long enough to count as busy. A headless trace of five idle seconds on a running session (`devtools.timeline.invalidationTracking`, not strobe) showed why: every frame restyled 24 SVG `rect`s (the spinner's dots) and one `span` (the shimmer), for 637 style recalculations, 1,272 paints and 331 ms of main-thread rendering work in 5 s. A CSS animation of a shape inside an SVG, or of `background-position`, runs on the main thread.

### The change

- **Spinner** (`Spinner`, so `ActivityRing` and `SessionProgressIndicatorV2` too): each dot is its own SVG over the whole box, holding one `rect` exactly where it sat in the single SVG, and the dot's opacity animation moves to that SVG element. The compositor runs opacity animations of SVG elements, not of shapes inside one. The root is a `span` sized by the same `width` and `height` props (as variables, so classes still size it over them), with the keyframes, phase pinning, off-screen pause and reduced motion unchanged.
- **Text shimmer** (`TextShimmer`): the sweep is the text again in the peak colour, seen through a soft window (a `mask-image` gradient) that crosses it. The window and the text inside it move by `translate` in opposite directions, so the text stays put while the window travels; the compositor runs both. The base text, the swap fade, the stagger, the timing and reduced motion are unchanged. The shimmer clips to its own box, where the old background painted, so the window's travel adds no overflow.

Headless result for the same five idle seconds: 26 style recalculations (only as the animations start) and 27 paints, 14 ms of main-thread rendering work instead of 331 ms.

**Looks the same.** Screenshots of base and head at 2x, light and dark, with every animation paused at 0, 300, 700, 1,100 and 1,500 ms: the spinner's dots match to within 33 of 255 on any channel (mean under 1); the shimmer's column-by-column brightness matches, and only antialiased glyph edges inside the moving highlight differ, by up to 63 of 255 in dark mode, because the highlight now draws the glyphs once more over the base text instead of filling them with one gradient.

### Results

Timed A/B on the M4 MacBook Air (macOS 27): queued, as

```sh
strobe bench packages/app/perf/stream.bench.ts --filter "wait on a running session" --base fe04656465 --head .
```

On macOS, strobe reads frames from Chromium's trace (no OS present events) and cannot pin CPUs, and the run shares the machine with its owner's work at background priority. This section takes the `report experiment <exp> --format pr` output verbatim when the run finishes.

### The bench

`packages/app/perf/stream.bench.ts`, case `wait on a running session`:

```ts
// Five seconds of a running session between deltas: the tab's spinner and the Working shimmer animate, and nothing
// else changes. Animation the compositor runs costs the page's main thread nothing.
"wait on a running session": {
  primary: "main.work",
  metrics: ["main.style", "cpu.renderer", "cpu.gpu", "frames.presented.count"],
  run: ({ page }) => page.wait(5000),
},
```

Its setup waits two seconds instead of `page.idle()`: on dev the page's animations never stop, and with the attribution probes on a slow machine their frames can run long enough that it never counts as idle.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none">
  <rect x="0.5" y="0.5" width="239" height="71" rx="8" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity="0.2"/>
  <g fill="currentColor">
    <rect x="24" y="24" width="6" height="6" rx="1.5" opacity="0.2"><animate attributeName="opacity" values="1;0.2;0.2;0.2" dur="1.2s" repeatCount="indefinite"/></rect>
    <rect x="33" y="24" width="6" height="6" rx="1.5" opacity="0.2"><animate attributeName="opacity" values="0.2;1;0.2;0.2" dur="1.2s" repeatCount="indefinite"/></rect>
    <rect x="33" y="33" width="6" height="6" rx="1.5" opacity="0.2"><animate attributeName="opacity" values="0.2;0.2;1;0.2" dur="1.2s" repeatCount="indefinite"/></rect>
    <rect x="24" y="33" width="6" height="6" rx="1.5" opacity="0.2"><animate attributeName="opacity" values="0.2;0.2;0.2;1" dur="1.2s" repeatCount="indefinite"/></rect>
  </g>
  <text x="54" y="38" font-size="15" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.45" font-family="sans-serif">Working</text>

    <linearGradient id="g" x1="0" x2="1"><stop offset="0" stop-color="#fff" stop-opacity="0"/><stop offset="0.5" stop-color="#fff"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="#fff" stop-opacity="0"/></linearGradient>
```

prs.title: perf(app): stop restyling the side panel on every move of a resize drag
prs.body:
Dragging the divider between the session and the review restyled every element in the side panel, the review's file tree and diffs included, on every pointer move. The side panel's content width was an inherited custom property set on an ancestor; it now goes to the one element that reads it.

### Discovery (strobe)

The new case `drag the review's edge` (below) holds the divider for five seconds and drags it the way a hand does: a pointer move every display frame, a slow stretch toward the session, jiggles, a fast throw toward the review, and a slow pull back.

Recorded on an M4 MacBook Air (macOS 27) under `taskpolicy -b` while its owner used it. Single attribution recordings: noisy discovery evidence, not results.

```sh
strobe record --bench "packages/app/perf/timeline.bench.ts#drag the review's edge" --head fe04656465   # rec_1d4e88: dev
strobe record --bench "packages/app/perf/timeline.bench.ts#drag the review's edge" --head .            # rec_c47811: this branch
strobe query rec_1d4e88 layout
strobe query rec_1d4e88 sql "select ... from slice where name = 'UpdateLayoutTree' ..."   # elementCount per measured run
```

On dev (`rec_1d4e88`), each 5-second drag spent 2,252 ms of the main thread recalculating style, in 163 recalculations that restyled 96,456 elements, and 83% of vsyncs showed no new frame. `query layout` put 1,819 ms of that style inside frames and 408 ms forced, mostly by the diff viewer's virtualizer reading `scrollHeight` in its frame callback.

strobe does not say which change invalidated style, so a headless trace with `devtools.timeline.invalidationTracking` named it: on every move `screen.tsx` set `--session-side-content-width` on `session-side-panel-content`, and `side-region.tsx` read it four levels down, on `session-review-content`. An unregistered custom property inherits, so each change marked the whole side panel for a style recalculation. In that headless drag, dev restyled 329,461 elements and this branch 89,647.

With this branch (`rec_c47811`), the same drag restyled 19,380 elements per run instead of 96,456.

### The change

- `SideRegion` takes `contentWidth` and writes `width: var(--panel-hold-width, <width>)` on `session-review-content`, the only element that reads it.
- `screen.tsx` no longer sets `--session-side-content-width`. Nothing else read it.

The width, the panel motion's `--panel-hold-width` hold during open and close flights, and every layout stay the same.

### Results

Timed A/B on an M4 MacBook Air (macOS 27), its owner's machine in use, run at background priority (`taskpolicy -b`):

```sh
strobe bench packages/app/perf/timeline.bench.ts --filter "drag the review's edge" --primary main.work --base fe04656465 --head .
```

What that means for these numbers: on macOS strobe reads frames from Chromium's trace (no OS present events), and it cannot pin CPUs, so other work on the machine widens the intervals (the Background warning below). At background priority Chromium runs on the efficiency cores and drops about 91% of frames on both builds, so this run decided `main.work` instead of the case's declared `frames.dropped.pct`, which says `same` here; the frame metrics need a run at normal priority (on Windows, with OS present events) to show what this does to frame pacing. The bottom command in strobe's output omits the `--filter` and `--primary` flags this run used; the command above is the one that produced the table.

**drag the review's edge · web**, 8 pairs of fresh launches:

| Metric | base | head | Change [interval] | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main.work` (primary) | 1834 ms | 1290 ms | −30% [−35% … −23%] | less |
| `main.work` | 1834 ms | 1290 ms | −30% [−34% … −24%] | — |
| `main.layout` | 116 ms | 126 ms | +8.6% [+4.1% … +14%] | — |
| `main.style` | 1224 ms | 710 ms | −42% [−44% … −37%] | — |
| `main.script` | 66.8 ms | 70.4 ms | +6.6% [+1.9% … +11%] | — |

prs.title: fix(cli): stop opencode run from leaving a background service running
prs.body:
### Problem

When no background service is running, `opencode run` starts one detached and leaves it running after it exits. In CI and Docker that leaves a stray `serve --service` behind, along with any work still running on it (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/55908).

### Change

`run` uses the background service if one is already up. If not, it starts a private server that exits with the run, the same one `--standalone` uses.

```diff
  opencode run "..."
    ├─ --server <url>   → that server
    ├─ --standalone     → private server
    ├─ service running  → the service
-   └─ none running     → start the service, leave it running
+   └─ none running     → private server, exits with the run
```

`--server`, `--standalone`, the TUI and every other command behave as before. The V1 `run` command already used a private server when not given `--server`.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" font-family="ui-monospace,monospace" font-size="9">
  <style>
    .srv{animation:srv 4s ease-in-out infinite}
    @keyframes srv{0%,15%{opacity:0}25%,70%{opacity:1}85%,100%{opacity:0}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.srv{animation:none;opacity:1}}
  </style>
  <rect x="10" y="22" width="70" height="26" rx="4"/>
  <text x="18" y="38" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">opencode run</text>
  <path d="M84 35h50" stroke-dasharray="3 3" class="srv"/>
  <rect class="srv" x="138" y="22" width="92" height="26" rx="4"/>
  <text class="srv" x="146" y="38" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">private server</text>
  <text x="10" y="64" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" opacity=".6">server exits with the run</text>
</svg>
```

### Out of scope

- A service that starts while a private `run` is going can resume that run's session, since both share the database (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/55076). That already happens with `--standalone` today and will be fixed separately.

### Verification

- `bun test test/server-connection.test.ts` in `packages/cli`: 4 pass, including a new check that `run` connects to a running service
- `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/cli`; `oxlint` and `prettier --check` on the changed files
- Ran `bun run src/index.ts run "hi"` with an empty HOME and XDG dirs and no service running: the prompt reached the model, no `service.json` was written, and no `opencode` process was left running afterwards

prs.title: fix(core): count-based image cap via media.image.max_images
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #59794

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Backends enforce a per-request image **count** (vLLM's `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":4}'`, for example), and once a session accumulates more images than that cap, every subsequent request is rejected — the session becomes permanently unusable. The existing image budget in `boundImages` only bounds **bytes** (`IMAGE_BYTES_TRIGGER`/`TARGET`), which small images can sail under forever.

This adds `media.image.max_images` to the config. When set, `boundImages` also drops the oldest images beyond the cap, replacing each with the same placeholder text the byte budget uses — so a tool can still read the original back by path. Unset keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte, which keeps the change zero-risk for existing sessions. The byte cut and the count cut run together and the tighter one wins, so the count cap can also catch images the byte budget kept.

This is a different slice from #59303: that PR proposes a fixed 30-image cap plus compaction on count errors, which still fails on a 4-image backend (as noted in the issue). A user-configured cap matches what the backend actually enforces.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Three new regression tests in `test/session-model-request.test.ts`: the count-only cut drops the oldest first, 40 small images stay untouched without a cap, and the tighter of the byte/count cuts wins.
- `bun test test/session-model-request.test.ts test/session-compaction.test.ts test/config/` is 324/324 passing.
- `bun typecheck` clean (1,884 files across 2 projects).

N/A, not a UI change.

prs.title: fix(core): move sessions to the remote-derived project id when a remote is added later
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #57985

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When a repo gains a git remote, its project id changes from the root-commit-derived one to a remote-derived one. The first resolution after `git remote add` upserts a second project row for the same directory, and every session created under the old id stops showing up in the project's session list (nothing is deleted, but the sessions are stranded).

The session projector already re-points sessions when a directory adopts a different identity (`Worktree.Event.Resolved` with `adopted`), but adoption only covered markerless projects being absorbed by a repo. This PR adds git projects that previously claimed the same directory row to the adoption candidates, so sessions created before the remote existed follow the directory to its new id. The global project stays excluded — its unborn-git directory rows are already handled through the `previous`/global candidates.

Stranded sessions from before this fix migrate on the next resolution of the directory (for example when the background service re-resolves it).

### How did you verify your code works?

- New regression test in `packages/core/test/session-create.test.ts`: create a session in a repo without a remote, add a remote, resolve — the session moves to the remote-derived project id and shows up in that project's session list. Fails without the fix (session stays under the root-commit id).
- `packages/core`: test/session-create, test/project, test/session-projector, test/session-move all green; full core suite run with only the pre-existing environment failures (ShellTool/Git trees/Worktree).

prs.title: perf(ui): hold the pointer on a resize handle while it drags
prs.body:
While a resize handle is dragged, hover no longer follows the pointer across the panels it resizes. The pointer runs ahead of the divider, so every move crossed into the timeline or the review and back, and each crossing restyled both panels' ancestor chains and the file tree's whole subtree. The handle now captures the pointer for the drag, as a native splitter does.

### Discovery (strobe)

With #61560 (which adds the `drag the review's edge` case and stops the side panel's inherited width from restyling the review), what was left of a drag's style work came from `:hover` changes.

Recorded on an M4 MacBook Air (macOS 27) under `taskpolicy -b` while its owner used it. Single attribution recordings: noisy discovery evidence, not results.

```sh
# Run from a checkout of #61560 alone (rec_c47811), then of #61560 with this change (branch resize-both, rec_e8aae9).
strobe record --bench "packages/app/perf/timeline.bench.ts#drag the review's edge" --head .
strobe query rec_e8aae9 layout
```

Per 5-second drag, from the measured runs of each recording:

| | dev (`rec_1d4e88`) | #61560 (`rec_c47811`) | #61560 and this change (`rec_e8aae9`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Style recalculation | 2,252 ms | 2,156 ms | 454 ms |
| Elements restyled | 96,456 | 19,380 | 3,199 |
| Events dispatched | 1,577 | 763 | 80 |

strobe does not say why style was invalidated, so a headless trace with `devtools.timeline.invalidationTracking` named the cause: `PseudoClass` (hover) invalidations up the chains of the timeline, the review and the file tree on every crossing, with the file tree's hover rules invalidating its subtree. In that headless drag, #61560 restyled 89,647 elements and spent 978 ms on style; with this change, 6,211 elements and 144 ms.

On its own, without #61560, this change saves little on this drag: the side panel's inherited width restyles the whole review on every move either way.

### The change

`ResizeHandle` calls `setPointerCapture` on a primary-button mouse `pointerdown`. The browser releases the capture when the button comes up. Every resize handle gets it: the session divider, the bottom pane, the side pane's split, the review's sidebar and the left sidebar.

What stays the same: the mouse-driven drag code, its limits and collapse thresholds, and the handle's pill, which `[data-dragging]` already shows for the whole drag. What changes: rows and buttons under the pointer no longer show hover states during a drag, as with a native splitter. Mouse events still reach the document listeners, so a release outside the window still ends the drag.

### Results

Timed A/B on the M4 MacBook Air (macOS 27): queued, to run after #61560's. The base is #61560, so the run measures this change:

```sh
# From a checkout of #61560, which adds the bench case.
strobe bench packages/app/perf/timeline.bench.ts --filter "drag the review's edge" --primary main.work --base side-panel-width --head resize-both
```

The case decides `frames.dropped.pct`; this run decides `main.work` instead, because under `taskpolicy -b` Chromium runs on the efficiency cores and drops most frames on both builds. On macOS, strobe reads frames from Chromium's trace (no OS present events) and cannot pin CPUs. This section takes the `report experiment <exp> --format pr` output verbatim when the run finishes.

### The bench

`drag the review's edge` in `packages/app/perf/timeline.bench.ts`, added by #61560.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #61554

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

```ts
OpenCodeWorkerd.layer({ ..., config: { experimental: { console_poll: false } } })
```

prs.title: fix(core): report true exit codes from PowerShell shell commands
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #61529

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

On Windows, the shell tool runs commands through PowerShell (Windows PowerShell 5.1 when pwsh is not installed) via `-Command`. The PS 5.1 console host never propagates a native command's exit code: the process exits 1 only when the *last statement* leaves `$?` false, otherwise 0. Two consequences:

- A failing native command is clamped to 1 — the true code is lost (`cmd /c "exit 3"` reports 1).
- A successful native command whose stderr is merged with `2>&1` reports 1, because each merged stderr line becomes an `ErrorRecord` that marks the statement failed — turning `git push` progress output, `docker build` logs, and `npm` deprecation warnings into apparent failures.

`ShellSelect.args()` (shared by the shell tool, the session shell endpoint, command interpolation, and scheduled checks) now wraps the command body for PowerShell shells:

```powershell
<command>
if ($?) { exit 0 } elseif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne $null -and @($error | Where-Object { $_.FullyQualifiedErrorId -notlike "NativeCommandError*" }).Count -eq 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE } else { exit 1 }
```

Why the suffix works:

- `$LASTEXITCODE` is stale once a successful native command is followed by a failing PowerShell statement (e.g. `npm ci; Copy-Item a b` with a failed copy), so the suffix only takes over when the last statement was native. On PS 5.1, merged native stderr appends `$error` records whose `FullyQualifiedErrorId` starts with `NativeCommandError` (the first line `NativeCommandError`, later lines `NativeCommandErrorMessage`), a failing cmdlet appends records with its own ID (`PathNotFound`, …), and a failing native without stderr appends nothing.
- The wrapper always launches a fresh `-NoProfile` process, so `$error` holds only the body's records when the suffix runs — no before/after counting is needed, and the 256-record `$error` limit is moot. All records match the `NativeCommandError*` pattern (or none exist) with `$LASTEXITCODE` set → `exit $LASTEXITCODE`; any real PowerShell failure → `exit 1`. `$LASTEXITCODE` is `$null` until a native command runs, so pure PowerShell failures also keep 1.
- Every branch exits explicitly because a bare trailing statement would reset `$?` and force exit 0. On pwsh 7.2+ merged stderr leaves `$?` true and appends no `$error` records, so the first branch handles it there.

| Last statement of the body | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| native command fails with code 3 | 1 | **3** |
| native command succeeds, stderr merged with `2>&1` | 1 | **0** |
| native command succeeds, multiple stderr lines merged with `2>&1` | 1 | **0** |
| native command succeeds, then a failing PowerShell statement | 1 | 1 |
| pure PowerShell success / failure | 0 / 1 | 0 / 1 |
| explicit `exit N` in the body | N | N (the body's `exit` runs first) |

Command output is unchanged: every branch of the suffix is a silent `exit` call.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Empirical probe matrices on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (this machine) and pwsh 7.6.9 (installed locally; the same engine family the CI runners resolve to) covering every suffix branch — the original suffix, the prefix-based suffix, the count-guarded alternative, and the final suffix — including the cases where each alternative still misreports (the prefix-based suffix exits 1 on a success with two merged stderr lines; the count-guarded alternative exits 1 on a failing native without stderr). On pwsh 7.6, merged stderr leaves `$?` true and appends no `$error` records, confirming the 7.2+ behavior.
- The exit-code `it.live` tests in `packages/core/test/tool-shell.test.ts` run the production `Shell.Service` against a real `powershell.exe`, one per branch: failing native (3), failing native + merged stderr (3), successful native + single-line merged stderr (0), successful native + multi-line merged stderr (0), failing statement after successful native (1), failure with no native command (1), successful statement after failing native (0); the pre-existing explicit-`exit 7` test covers the remaining path. On Windows they pin `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1) through a new optional `shell` parameter on the `withSession` harness, because production shell resolution on the CI runners picks the pre-installed `pwsh` first and 5.1 is where the clamping behavior lives.
- Negative check: with the prefix-based suffix, the new multi-line regression test fails (reports 1 instead of 0); with the final suffix everything passes.
- `bun test` on both files with `--rerun-each 10`: 530 pass / 330 platform-conditional skips / 0 fail (860 runs).
- `bun run check` from the repository root (via the pre-push hook): 35/35 tasks green.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" role="img" aria-label="Terminal: git push with merged stderr now reports exit 0 instead of exit 1">
  <rect x="1.5" y="1.5" width="237" height="69" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="3" opacity="0.35"/>
  <circle cx="14" cy="12" r="3" fill="currentColor" opacity="0.5"/>
```

prs.title: perf(core): write each assistant part as its own row instead of rewriting the message
prs.body:
**Stops rewriting a whole assistant message for every streamed part: each part becomes its own `session_part` row.**
On a 10-step tool-heavy session with screenshots, SQLite WAL writes drop by 84.4% (`47.89 MB -> 7.46 MB`, or 87.8% `47.89 MB -> 5.83 MB` with `experimental.media_blob`) and `fsync`s drop from 22 to 2. [#58915](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58915) (the table and the readers) has shipped in v2.2.2 through v2.2.5, so this write change can go out as the second release. Old rows stay readable and nothing is backfilled.

❌ **Before**
1. Every durable text, reasoning or tool event re-encodes the assistant message and rewrites its full `session_message` JSON, including every earlier part and tool output.
2. Updating `session_message` also sets `time_created` on every write, dirtying both `time_created` secondary indexes 21 times per step. ❌

✅ **After**
1. The message row keeps an envelope with `content: []`, updated only on step start/end, retry, or failure (without re-setting `time_created` on updates).
2. Each part is a `session_part` row: a new part is one insert, and an update rewrites only that part row.
3. Tool media still moves to blob storage per part (`externalizePart` and offline `SessionBlob.split`), and rewriting content releases media the new parts no longer use.
4. Older messages with inline content are split into part rows only right before one of their parts is written. If a downgrade left a message with both part rows and newer inline content, the inline parts are appended after the existing rows instead of replacing them. Envelope updates and reads (like starting a new step after a settled message) leave them as they are, and unchanged history is never migrated.
5. Forks copy a split parent's part rows and record blob refs for each forked message. An unsplit parent is copied inline as is, so old rows are never decoded during a fork. Imports write parts as rows, and with `media_blob` on, forks and imports move part media into blobs too.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Event["Durable step event"] --> Projector
  Projector -->|step start / end| Envelope["session_message (envelope, content: [])"]
  Projector -->|text / reasoning / tool| Part["session_part (message_id, ordinal)"]
  Legacy["Inline data.content"] -->|first part write| Split["delete + insert part rows, clear inline content"]
  style Part fill:#dcf5dc,stroke:#2f855a
  style Split fill:#dcf5dc,stroke:#2f855a
```

```diff
  on a part event:
-   message = decode(row);  edit message.content;  write the whole row (and re-index time_created)
+   split the message first if it still has inline content   (prepareAssistantParts, the only split path)
+   append:  insert one part row at the next ordinal
+   update:  find the latest matching part (type, call ID), apply the change, write that row only
+   replace: delete the message's parts, insert the new ones, release media they no longer name
```

📊 **Numbers**: scripted 10-step, 2-turn session (40 tool calls, 5 PNG screenshots at 380 KB each, 6 spilled 81 KB outputs) and 1-step 20-tool text session (`8 KB` output/tool)

| Measure | Before (`dev`) | After ([#58916](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58916)) | After + `media_blob` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10-step SQLite WAL written | 47.89 MB (11,623 pages) | 7.46 MB (1,811 pages, −84.4%) | 5.83 MB (1,415 pages, −87.8%) |
| Per-step SQLite WAL written | 4,788.7 KB / step | 746.1 KB / step | 583.0 KB / step |
| 10-step `session_message` (+ idx) WAL | 45.67 MB | 832.2 KB (−98.2%) | 309.0 KB (−99.3%) |

| 1-step 20-tool text WAL / JSON | 8.82 MB / 9.20 MB | 2.47 MB (−72.0%) / 208 KB (−97.7%) | — |

The new projector, fork blob-ref, downgrade-merge, and offline `SessionBlob.split` part tests fail without the change (366 pass across the seven core session test files; 2 pass in `packages/server/test/media.test.ts`). The numbers above are from before the rebase and were not re-measured.

↩️ **Undo:** revert this PR and keep the readers from #58915. Writes go back to inline content, and reads keep showing parts already written to `session_part`. Downgrading to a build older than v2.2.2 would hide the assistant content of messages written while this was live, which is why the readers went out first. Going back to a v2.2.x build and then forward again keeps every part.

👀 **Read:** `projector.ts`. Check `prepareAssistantParts`, the one place a legacy row is split, which appends inline parts after any existing part rows (the downgrade case), so a message never gets duplicate ordinals or loses parts. Then check that `updateMessage` keeps the row's existing `content` through `json_set`, so envelope updates never move or drop it. Then check the blob ref handling in the three part methods, in `SessionBlob.split` (`blob.ts`), and in fork: forked messages copy empty envelopes, so their refs come from the parts. `message-updater.ts` now talks to the projector through the part methods instead of editing the whole message. The rest is test updates.

### Review fixes

- Session stats now batch compaction usage queries under 100 bound parameters, so projects with 98 or more sessions stay within Durable Object SQLite's parameter limit.
- The Durable Object SQLite test fixture now turns on `foreign_keys` at open and rejects `PRAGMA foreign_keys`, so cascade deletes run under `--conditions=workerd` the same way they do in production.
- Hydrating part rows checks that inline `content` is an array before merging, so malformed message JSON fails cleanly with a decode error instead of throwing a `TypeError`, and removes the unused `hasInlineContent` export.

<sub>🔍 Found while profiling database writes during long tool-heavy turns · no user reports · measured with a scripted 10-step file-DB harness against SQLite WAL + `dbstat` · depends on [#58915](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58915)</sub>

prs.title: fix(core): price Copilot long-context tiers and cache writes
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52089

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

GitHub Copilot costs were undercounted badly on long sessions. In my case (#59671): a 25h session on Copilot / Claude Haiku 5.5, 348 requests, ~344K average context, OpenCode showed $1.56 when the real bill is roughly $9.34 (between $2.03 and $10.15, since Copilot picks the price tier per request by prompt size).

Two causes, both in the Copilot provider code:

1. Copilot's `/models` payload ships two price tiers (`default` and `long_context`, the latter starting above `default.max_prompt_tokens`). The builder only read the default tier.
2. The builder hardcoded cache writes to $0 (`cache_write_price` is in the payload, unread), and both usage adapters dropped `cache_write_tokens`, so cache writes weren't counted at all.

Pricing that session's totals at the ≤100K rates with free writes gives $1.5557 — cent-exact with the displayed $1.56, which is how I know exactly which rates the old code applied.

The builder now emits the write price and a context-tier cost entry, which `SessionUsage.calculateCost` already applies per request, so no calculator change was needed. The adapters map `cache_write_tokens` into `cacheWrite`. While there I replaced their hand-rolled `noCache` arithmetic with `ProviderShared.subtractTokens`/`sumTokens` like the shared protocols use: both streaming adapters left `noCache` undefined on responses without cache details, which downstream prices the entire prompt at $0, and neither clamped against broken breakdowns.

Deliberately not addressed: Copilot's own reported billed amount (#35765) and the richer `pricing` shape from #59460.

### How did you verify your code works?

New unit tests: the builder prices cache writes and emits the long-context tier entry (boundary taken from `default.max_prompt_tokens`), and keeps a model whose `long_context` object is malformed instead of dropping it from the catalog. Both streaming adapters map cache-write tokens into `cacheWrite` and keep the breakdown consistent (`nonCached + cacheRead + cacheWrite = total`). `bun run check` passes, and the `packages/core` suite has the same 4 failures as a clean `dev` checkout (all environment-related).

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" role="img" aria-label="Copilot session cost: displayed $1.56, actual about $9.34">
  <style>
    .bar { animation: grow 2.8s ease-in-out infinite; }
    .tag { animation: fade 2.8s ease-in-out infinite; }
    @keyframes grow { 0%, 15% { width: 26px } 55%, 100% { width: 142px } }
    @keyframes fade { 0%, 30% { opacity: 0 } 65%, 100% { opacity: .9 } }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .bar, .tag { animation: none } }
  </style>
  <g fill="currentColor" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,monospace" font-size="11">
    <text class="tag" x="12" y="11" font-size="9" opacity="0">6x undercount: tier + cache writes</text>
    <text x="12" y="27" opacity=".5">billed</text>
    <rect x="62" y="18" width="26" height="9" rx="2" opacity=".5"/>
    <text x="94" y="27" opacity=".5">$1.56</text>
    <text x="12" y="53">actual</text>
    <rect class="bar" x="62" y="44" width="142" height="9" rx="2" opacity=".9"/>
    <text x="206" y="53">$9.34</text>
  </g>
</svg>
```

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change, so none attached.

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(tui): add proper cold-start recovery for slow locations that return 503 on agent/model/provider metadata endpoints
prs.body:
Closes #61359

## Type of change
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

## Summary
This PR resolves a silent dead-state bug in the TUI (and web client) that occurs when opening a slow-initializing workspace location, most notably Windows UNC/SMB paths, or any project with slow plugin setup on first load.

During location cold initialization, the server returns `503 Service Unavailable` for `/api/agent`, `/api/model`, and `/api/provider` while plugins, worktree discovery, and location environment setup are still in progress. The original implementation limited this initial sync to only 3 retry attempts. Once those retries exhausted, the client permanently stopped fetching the metadata lists, with **no visible error shown to the user**.

The resulting user experience:
- Chat input accepts text, but prompts cannot be submitted
- `Shift+Tab` agent switching has no effect
- User has no indication what went wrong
- The only workaround is closing and restarting OpenCode after the location finishes warming up on the server

The server itself remains healthy during this window (the `/api/info` endpoint continues responding normally); only these three metadata routes are temporarily unavailable until location initialization completes. Once ready, the same API calls succeed quickly — the only missing piece was client-side logic to keep retrying and recover automatically.

## Root Cause Analysis
1. Cold location initialization can take an extended amount of time for UNC/SMB shares or projects with heavy startup plugins.
2. While initialization is ongoing, agent/model/provider metadata endpoints return 503.
3. Old sync logic used a fixed retry count of 3 attempts, ~5s apart.
4. After 3 failures, the sync process abandons the load entirely. No further polling, no event subscription, no error surface.
5. Even after the server finishes initializing and the endpoints become healthy, the client never re-attempts the sync, leaving the UI permanently broken until restart.
6. The same limitation applies to the web client, which inherited the same retry behaviour.

## Changes introduced
1. **Replace fixed 3-retries with bounded exponential backoff**
   - Starting delay: 1 second
   - Maximum per-retry delay cap: 5 seconds
   - Hard absolute budget: 5 minutes total for this initial cold sync sequence
   - Prevents infinite request storms while giving slow locations enough time to finish startup.

2. **Event-driven immediate refresh**
   - Subscribe to server-sent events: `agent.updated`, `model.updated`, `provider.updated`
   - When any of these events are emitted, trigger an immediate refresh of the corresponding list, bypassing the backoff timer.
   - This lets the UI recover instantly the moment the server signals metadata is ready, instead of waiting for the next scheduled retry.
   - Event listeners are scoped to the cold initialization lifecycle and cleaned up when the sync succeeds / times out to avoid stale event handlers and memory leaks.

3. **Add user visible failure state on timeout**
   - If the full 5-minute budget is exhausted and endpoints still return 503, render a descriptive error message inside the TUI.
   - The error explains that agent/model metadata failed to load, and suggests checking workspace permissions, network connectivity for remote paths, or restarting OpenCode.
   - No more silent broken input state; users understand the failure and available remediation steps.

4. **Align web client behaviour**
   - Port the identical retry, backoff, event subscription and timeout error logic to the web frontend.
   - Web and TUI clients now behave consistently for slow workspace locations.

## Out of scope / explicitly not fixed
This change only addresses **client-side retry and recovery flow**. It does **not** attempt to fix separate underlying issues noted in the issue report:
- Windows CMD limitation preventing local MCP servers from launching with a UNC working directory
- Git worktree discovery failures over SMB / UNC paths
- Third-party plugin compatibility issues with the V2 plugin API
- Transient MCP upstream authentication failures that happen during location startup
These are independent problems and remain tracked separately.

## Verification steps
I validated the fix using the delayed plugin simulation method described in the issue comment, which reliably reproduces the original 503 sequence without needing a real SMB/UNC share.

Test cases executed:
1. **Original failure reproduction**: Confirmed baseline behaviour: 3 retries then permanent silent failure, prompt unsubmittable, agent switching dead.
2. **Slow location happy recovery**: After applying the patch, TUI continues retrying past the old 3-attempt limit. Metadata loads automatically once server initialization completes; prompt submit and `Shift+Tab` agent switching function normally after recovery.
3. **Event trigger path**: Verified lists populate immediately when `*.updated` events fire, independent of the backoff schedule.
4. **Timeout failure path**: Simulated permanent 503 responses for longer than 5 minutes. Confirmed TUI shows a clear, human-readable error banner instead of silent failure.
5. **Fast workspace baseline**: Normal fast-loading projects start with zero extra delays; no unnecessary retry overhead added for ready locations.
6. **Web client parity**: Repeated the slow-start simulation on web UI and confirmed matching recovery and timeout behaviour.
7. **Cleanup check**: Confirmed event listeners unsubscribe correctly on success or timeout, no dangling subscriptions.

## Regression Risk Assessment
Risk level: Low
- Changes are isolated to the initial metadata sync for `/api/agent`, `/api/model`, `/api/provider`.
- Backoff has a hard maximum total budget and per-attempt cap, eliminating runaway request risks.
- The happy path (location already ready on first load) runs unchanged, no performance impact.
- Event subscriptions are strictly lifecycle-bound and cleaned up.
- This is purely a client behaviour adjustment; no server-side API or schema changes.

## Screenshots / recordings
No core UI redesign. The only new UI element is the timeout error banner. I can add a screenshot or screen recording of the error state after initial review feedback if maintainers request it.

## Checklist
- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR
- [x] This change is scoped only to the silent cold-start recovery bug described in #61359
- [x] No unrelated refactors, formatting churn, or side-effect changes included


---

Public API: adds an optional `timeout` option to `retry()` in @opencode/util (backwards compatible)

prs.title: fix(core): capture snapshots for a Location opened through a symlink
prs.body:
Snapshots stop working for a project opened through a symlinked path, such as macOS `/tmp`, `/var/folders`, or a symlinked `~/code`. `Snapshot.capture` returns `undefined` and logs "Location is outside the project", so undo and session diffs have nothing to work with.

- **Cause:** `Snapshot` resolves the Git worktree to its real path but compares it with `location.directory` as given. Through a symlink or a Windows junction the two paths differ, so the Location looks outside the project. A Location opened in another letter case on Windows had a quieter failure: the scope became a pathspec such as `SCOPE` that matches nothing, so every capture was empty.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60847

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Fixes two issues causing worktree cross-registration and bare repository spam when repositories have sibling worktrees:

1. `Git.worktree.list` parsed porcelain output by simply splitting on newlines matching `worktree `, ignoring attribute lines. In bare-backed worktree setups, the bare repository entry was parsed as `kind: "main"`. This led `Project.resolve` to treat the bare directory as the canonical project root, and subsequent discovery passes logged `Worktree.DirectoryUnavailableError` when probing the bare repo.
   - Fixed by parsing each porcelain record block and skipping entries flagged with `bare`.
2. `Worktree.refresh` enumerates worktrees via registered strategies (including `git worktree list`). In setups where sibling checkouts of the same repository belong to different projects, each project's refresh pass discovered sibling checkout roots and added them into the current project's `worktree` table. This cross-registered directories, mixed session lists, and caused sessions opened across project boundaries to render title-only.
   - Fixed by checking `ProjectTable.worktree` and `WorktreeTable` to exclude foreign project roots from discovery and prune any foreign roots previously recorded under the current project. Also preserves the current project root as unowned (`strategy: null`).

- Added `omits the bare repository entry when listing worktrees` in `packages/core/test/git.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(core): list sessions across every project row of the same worktree
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #59371

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`session list` resolves one project for the current directory and lists sessions for that project id. A worktree can own more than one `project` row — the row's identity includes the worktree's git fingerprint, so re-creating a remote, or opening the folder before and after that, leaves a second row behind (the report and #57985 both arrive this way). When that happens, sessions recorded under the other row are invisible: the caller is in the same folder, but the query only asks about one of the folder's rows.

`packages/core/src/session/store.ts` changes the project-scoped branch of `list` to cover every `project` row that shares the worktree, instead of only the row it was handed. The worktree is what a caller means by "this project"; the rows are an implementation detail of how that worktree was recorded.

Sessions therefore reappear for anyone already in this state, not only for worktrees created after the fix. Rows on a different worktree stay out of the result, and the exact-`directory` filter, the cursor and the returned session rows are unchanged.

A second commit keeps the `global` project row out of the match. That row's `worktree` is whichever commitless repository resolved to it first rather than the folder its sessions belong to, so a folder that had just gained its first commit listed sessions from unrelated commitless folders; a `global` caller has no folder identity to expand either, so it stays scoped to its own row. Its test fails without the fix and passes with it.

Part B of the report — `/api/location` returning the service's start directory rather than the caller's cwd — is a separate defect in a different layer and is deliberately not part of this change.

prs.title: fix(cli): wait for background jobs in opencode run
prs.body:
### Problem

`opencode run` exits as soon as the model's first reply ends. The `shell` tool tells the model to start long work with `background: true` and end its reply because it will be woken when the command finishes. In `run` there is nobody left to wake: training runs, test suites and evals get cut off before the model sees their results.


### Change

After each reply, `run` checks the whole session tree with `GET /api/experimental/job?sessionID=...&descendants=true`: the main session, its subagents, their subagents, and every background shell or image any of them started.

```text
a reply finishes anywhere in the tree
  ├─ nothing running, no wake queued → exit
  └─ any job in the tree still running → keep waiting
       └─ it finishes → its session is woken, replies → check again
```

- A job that finished but hasn't woken its session yet still holds the run. Its row is removed only after the wake is queued, so the check also looks at queued inbox items and active sessions in the tree.
- Ctrl-C while waiting now exits with code 130. Before, it hung when the session was already idle.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" font-family="ui-monospace,monospace" font-size="9">
  <style>
    .job{animation:job 4s linear infinite}
    .wake{opacity:.25;animation:wake 4s linear infinite}
    @keyframes job{0%{width:0}60%,100%{width:120px}}
    @keyframes wake{0%,60%{opacity:.25}70%,100%{opacity:1}}
```

prs.title: feat(app): let GUI plugins render and add actions to code blocks
prs.body:
Closes #61187. Unblocks #3366 and #40508 for plugins: Mermaid, LaTeX, CSV or any fenced language can now render as a plugin's own UI. - **`CodeBlock` registry**: a plugin renders the fenced blocks of the languages it lists as its own Solid UI, in place of the highlighted code. - **`CodeBlockAction` registry**: a plugin adds a button next to Copy for the languages it lists, for example "Run in terminal" for `sh`. No DOM hacks. - **Same model as the TUI**: `ctx.markdown.registerCodeBlockRenderer(language, render)` in the TUI, `ctx.add(CodeBlock, { languages, render })` in the GUI. In both, returning `undefined` keeps the default code block. ```tsx import { CodeBlock, CodeBlockAction } from "@opencode/plugin/gui" ctx.add(CodeBlock, { languages: ["csv"], render: (props) => (props.code.includes(",") ? : undefined), }) ctx.add(CodeBlockAction, { id: "run", languages: ["sh", "bash", "shell"], icon: "terminal", get title() { return ctx.t("run") }, run: (input) => runInTerminal(input.code, input.session), }) ``` | Before | After (demo plugin: `csv` renderer and a `sh` action) | | --- | --- | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1c4b692-e868-4875-bc31-907a11e7322c) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8eb5fce8-184e-421f-87c5-746ed515e516) | ### How a block renders ```mermaid flowchart LR A[fenced block in Markdown] --> B{language listed by a plugin?} B -- no --> C[highlighted code + Copy
one Set lookup, no subscription] B -- yes --> D{closing fence arrived?} D -- no, still streaming --> C D -- yes --> E[host placeholder div
Copy and actions stay] E --> F[plugin render, own Solid root
inside Contribution error boundary] F -- throws --> G[record plugin failure
show code again] F -- returns undefined --> H[show code again] F -- JSX --> I[plugin UI in place of the code] ``` - **Seam**: `MarkdownProvider` gets a `codeBlocks` field (`packages/session-ui/src/context/markdown.tsx`). `PluginLinks` (`packages/app/src/runtime/plugin/render.tsx`) fills it from the two registries, next to the link handlers it already wires. Session-ui knows no plugin; the host never touches markdown DOM. - **Streaming**: content mounts only once the block's closing fence arrives, in a streamed or completed message. Until then the user sees the highlighted code. Actions also wait, so "Run" never runs half a command. - **Fallback**: a render that throws records a `render` failure for that plugin (the plugin keeps running) and the block shows its code. `undefined` or `null` declines the block silently. A plugin that claims `mermaid` replaces the built-in diagram; when it declines or fails, the built-in diagram returns. - **Security**: plugin UI mounts with Solid `render` into a host-created `div[data-slot="markdown-code-content"]` inside the code wrapper. No plugin HTML strings enter the sanitized markdown pipeline. - **Late plugins**: a plugin that joins or leaves after a message rendered takes over or releases its blocks. The host memo changes only when a language's renderer or the action list changes, and only then does each Markdown re-decorate its code blocks. - **Recursion guard**: `ctx.ui.Code` and Markdown inside a `CodeBlock` render always show plain code, so a renderer can show its own source. ### Where it applies | Surface | Code block content | | --- | --- | | Timeline: assistant text, tool output | Yes | | Session side panels (file viewer Markdown and Mermaid preview) | Yes, inherited through `MarkdownProvider` | | `ctx.ui.Markdown` on the session screen | Yes | | `ctx.ui.Code`, Markdown inside a `CodeBlock` render | No | | Settings pages, dialogs, Home | No (no session screen) | ### Performance - **No plugin, or no matching language**: one `Set.has` per code block decoration. No per-block computation, subscription or DOM node. Each Markdown reads one memo inside its existing render effect. - **Matching block**: one Solid root per block, created only when the virtualized row renders. Rows already measure with a `ResizeObserver`, so content that grows later reflows like the built-in Mermaid diagram. The docs ask plugins to reserve a minimum height. Production `Markdown` bundle (Vite build of `session-ui`, real worker, sanitizer and highlighter), 30 completed messages with 90 fences, and one streamed message with 18 fences. Renderer task time per run (CDP `TaskDuration`), median of 30 interleaved runs per variant, Chromium headless: | Variant | Mount 30 messages | Stream 1 message | | --- | --- | --- | | `dev` (baseline) | 137 ms | 153 ms | | PR, no plugin | 129 ms | 162 ms | | PR, a plugin claims other languages (worst case for unmatched blocks) | 131 ms | 159 ms | - The differences are inside run-to-run noise: single runs of each variant spread from about 100 to 270 ms. - The machine had 99% background CPU load during the run, so strobe refused an A/B experiment. These numbers bound the cost; they do not resolve a difference of a few milliseconds. ### Visual ```svg ``` --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Related: #60875, #60145 Public API: adds the CodeBlock and CodeBlockAction GUI plugin registries and the CodeBlockProps type (backwards compatible)

prs.title: feat(core): tell the agent where a message came from (experimental)
prs.body:
**The agent can now tell when a message came from another session, a schedule, a slash command or another app rather than the person typing it.**
A message can say where it came from in its metadata, and the agent reads that as one line before the text. What was typed, what is stored and what the API returns stay exactly as sent.

💡 **Why**
Sessions message each other: a subagent gets its task from its parent, a schedule wakes a session, a slash command expands into a long template, and scripts report back. Today every one of these looks to the agent like the person typed it, so senders write "From X:" into the text by hand, a continued subagent gets no hint at all, and after compaction they are all labeled `[User]`.

🆕 **Now you can**
- Send a prompt with `metadata["opencode.origin"]` set to one of:
  - `{ from: "session:ses_…" }`: a machine sent it (another session, `schedule:sch_…`, `tool:release-bot`).
  - `{ via: "voice:phone" }`: the person, through another surface (a voice call, `command:review`, another app).
  - Either with `actor: "…"` when someone other than the session's owner sent it.
- Values are `scheme:id` strings, so any tool can pick its own scheme without a server change. `from` and `via` can't appear together; each value is one trimmed line of at most 200 characters. A prompt with an invalid origin is rejected.
- The agent reads `<message-origin from="session:ses_…"/>` (or `via="…"`, plus `actor="…"`) before the text.
- These are tagged by the server: the subagent tool and subagent commands (`from: session:<parent>`), scheduled prompts (`from: schedule:<id>`), and the slash commands it expands, including `/init`, `/review`, `/goal`, config commands and MCP prompts (`via: command:<name>`).
- Compaction's kept recent text labels a message `[User]` only when the person sent it; anything with a `from` or an `actor` is `[Message]`, followed by its origin line.

🚦 **How it ships**
Off by default, behind `experimental.message_context`. With it off, requests to the model are byte-for-byte what they are today. The origin is always stored, so turning it on later applies to earlier messages too.

```diff
- metadata["opencode.origin"] = { kind: "session", sessionID, title }   // title looked up from the sender at admission
+ metadata["opencode.origin"] = { from: "session:ses_…" } | { via: "voice:phone" }, + optional actor
+ admission: no lookup, stored as sent; the HTTP route validates it against the MessageOrigin schema
  history (model reads only): flag off, drop the origin in memory; flag on, keep it
  prompt builder: "<message-origin from|via=… [actor=…]/>\n" + text
+ compaction recent text: "[Message]:" instead of "[User]:" unless the person sent it
```

**No titles.** The earlier version of this PR stored the sender session's title when the message arrived. It's gone: the line holds IDs only. The agent doesn't need the title to act. A subagent's prompt already says it was spawned by another session, and the ID is what it needs to address the sender. Dropping it removes a database read on every prompt and the rules for untitled, renamed and deleted senders. Since IDs never change, the line a message produces never changes either, so the prompt cache holds. Clients can show a live title from the ID.

📊 **Proof**

| Case | What the agent reads |
|---|---|
| Flag off | the text alone, same request as a message without the key ✅ |
| `from` / `via` / `actor` | `<message-origin from="…"/>`, `via="…"`, `… actor="…"` ✅ |
| Both `from` and `via` | rejected by the API; a stored one renders nothing ✅ |
| Value with a line break, padding, or over 200 characters | rejected; a stored one renders nothing ✅ |
| `"`, `<`, `>`, `&` in a value | escaped in the attribute ✅ |
| Sender renamed or deleted after sending | the same line as before ✅ |
| Old `{ kind, sessionID }` shape | the text alone ✅ |
| Scheduled prompt | stored with `from: "schedule:<id>"` next to the existing `schedule` metadata ✅ |
| `/init`, `/review`, config command | stored with `via: "command:<name>"` ✅ |
| Continued subagent | origin on both the first and the follow-up prompt ✅ |
| Compaction's recent text | `[User]` for typed and `via` messages; `[Message]` for `from` and `actor` ✅ |
| `sessions.context` (HTTP, SDK, plugins) | metadata exactly as stored, whatever the flag ✅ |

New schema tests for the origin shape, exclusivity, value limits and metadata pass-through; the message-context tests rewritten for the new shape; origin checks added to the schedule, command, subagent and prompt admission tests.

👀 **Read:** `packages/schema/src/message-origin.ts` (the contract; exclusivity is an optional `never` key on each side) and `session/history.ts`, `loadForModel`, where the flag is read only for model requests. One known edge: turning the flag on and later off doesn't rewrite a provider-native compaction checkpoint made while it was on, so its replayed window keeps the lines it had. The rest is routine.

<sub>The generated SDK gains the optional `experimental.message_context` boolean and a typed `opencode.origin` key on prompt metadata; other metadata keys pass through unchanged.</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun test test/message-origin.test.ts` in packages/schema: 4 pass
- `bun test` in packages/core over every session, compaction, history, runner, schedule and command test file: 810 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test` over the changed test files after the review fix: 151 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck` in packages/schema, protocol, client, core, server: no errors
- `bun run check:generated` in packages/client and packages/protocol: clean
- `oxlint` on the changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): stop the /goal reviewer from looping after the work is done
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related: #61364 (Goal Mode cost), and reports that `/goal` with weaker models often isn't marked finished.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

With weaker models as the reviewer, `/goal` kept going after the work was done. The reviewer answered `continue` with general doubt ("the evidence doesn't prove every edge case") instead of naming a missing requirement. Stall detection doesn't catch this, because each reason is worded differently and the worker keeps calling tools. In one GPT-5.4-nano run the spec already passed every hidden check at the first review, and the goal still ran 33 more rounds.

Changes:

- **Reviewer prompt** (`goal/judge.txt`):
  - `done` when every requirement the objective states has evidence; don't hold back for edge cases, hidden tests or polish the objective doesn't ask for.
  - `continue` must name a specific unmet requirement; general doubt isn't a reason.
  - An assistant that stops to ask whether to keep going isn't `blocked`.
- **Looser verdict parsing:** reviewers sometimes escape characters JSON doesn't allow, most often a backtick quoting a command, which paused the goal with "gave no usable verdict". The parser now drops those invalid escapes and tries again.
- **Retry with the bad answer:** when the answer is still unusable, the retry shows the reviewer its previous reply (`goal/retry.txt`) instead of resending the same request.

### How did you verify your code works?

`goal.test.ts` covers the escaped verdict and the retry prompt. Goal tests and `bun typecheck` in core pass.

I also ran evals against local dev servers with real models:

- **End-to-end runs.** About 230 `/goal` sessions across 9 models (DeepSeek native and Zen, GLM, Qwen, MiniMax, GPT-5.4-nano, Haiku, Sonnet), on tasks from a test kata to a 12-command spec (also with `AGENTS.md` rules like "wait for plan approval"), plus an impossible publish task that should come back blocked. Hidden checkers scored the results.
- **Reviewer replay.** 70 frozen review points where ground truth comes from replaying the session's file edits and running the hidden checks, including near misses where tests fail or a few commands are broken.

Results:

- **Reviewer accuracy:** on points where the work was already done, GPT-5.4-nano answered `done` 3/36 times before and 24/36 after; native DeepSeek went from 21/36 to 26/36. Points that weren't done still got `continue`, and the blocked one still got `blocked`.
- **End to end with the fix:** 132 of 132 runs ended correctly, with no goal marked done while hidden checks failed. GPT-5.4-nano on the spec task finished in 0–2 extra rounds, down from 1–33.
- **Retry:** showing the reviewer its unusable answer fixed 22/22 such answers in replay, versus about 10/12 for resending the same request.

I also tested these, and didn't include them:

- Asking the reviewer a second time before every continuation: slightly better at recognizing done work, but about 70% more reviewer calls and one near miss wrongly marked done.
- `tool_choice: none` for the reviewer: no accuracy gain and a lower cache hit rate.
- Telling the worker not to stop and ask: no measurable effect.

prs.title: fix(core): continue after an empty model response
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55378

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

**An empty successful model reply gets one chance to continue instead of silently stopping the session.** Seen with a Gemini model after compaction, but the recovery applies to every provider.

❌ **Before**
1. The model returns a successful stop with no text or tool calls.
2. OpenCode goes idle even though the task is unfinished.

✅ **After**
1. OpenCode adds a short continuation prompt and reloads the conversation.
2. If the next response is also empty, it reports an error. Reasoning-only and whitespace-only responses count as empty. Text or tool output resets the allowance, including during output-limit or interrupted-stream recovery.

```diff
- successful stop -> session goes idle
+ empty successful stop -> one continuation prompt
+ another empty response -> visible error
```

👀 **Read:** `runner/step.ts` checks for an empty response only after cancellation and errors have been handled. `runner/llm.ts` bounds recovery without resetting the agent's step allowance.

prs.title: fix(core): publish terminal updates when programs change their titles
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When a program in a persistent terminal changes the terminal title (OSC 0/2, e.g. `printf '\033]2;vim\007'`), the daemon updates the terminal's title, but the server only published `persistent-pty.updated` after a rename. So tab labels in the desktop app and the TUI stayed stale until something listed the terminals again (a reload or a reconnect).

The fix is only in core, so no client or daemon changes are needed. `PersistentPty` now remembers each terminal's `title` and `userTitle` from the last listing. Every listing compares against that and publishes `persistent-pty.updated` once for each terminal whose title changed. Listings happen often, since every write, resize, input and snapshot looks the terminal up. To make updates prompt, a `title_changed` event on any attached subscription also starts a listing, unless an earlier listing already recorded that title. That means:

- the update goes out once, however many clients are attached. Comparing and recording happen together, so a second listing finds nothing new.
- when a user title hides the program's title, nothing is published, because the title the user sees did not change.
- rename no longer publishes on its own. The listing after the rename publishes it, so a rename and the subscription event it causes don't produce two updates.

Why not a daemon change: the daemon only sends title events on subscriptions, and only while a client is attached. A core-held observer subscription isn't safe. It would receive all of the terminal's output, observers are dropped when their queue fills, and an observer can be promoted to controller. A daemon-wide watch stream would need a new `features` entry and a new `@opencode/pty` release before it did anything. If a terminal changes its title while no client is attached, the update is published at the next listing (any terminal input, a snapshot, an agent read, a client refresh) rather than right away. A follow-up could add a `watch` feature to the daemon to cover that.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New core test (fake daemon): a program title change publishes one update even with repeated listings; a change hidden by a user title publishes nothing; clearing the user title shows the program's title. It fails (times out) without the fix.
- New server test (real `opencode-pty`, two attachments): an OSC title change sent through `cat` publishes exactly one `persistent-pty.updated`; a hidden change publishes none. It fails (times out) without the fix. I ran it 3 more times and it passed each time.
- Existing rename tests still pass.

prs.title: fix(mcp): show agents the instructions of client-attached MCP servers
prs.body:
**Agents now see the instructions of MCP servers that an app attaches over a client MCP socket.**
An app can attach its own tools to OpenCode over the experimental client MCP socket and send server instructions in its `initialize` reply. Until now only servers from OpenCode's config made it into the system prompt's `<mcp_instructions>` block, so agents got the tools but never the instructions. Configured servers behave as before.

❌ **Before**
1. An app attaches over the client MCP socket and sends instructions.
2. Its tools show up for the agent.
3. ❌ Its instructions are dropped; `<mcp_instructions>` lists configured servers only.

✅ **After**
1. An app attaches over the client MCP socket and sends instructions.
2. Its tools show up for the agent.
3. Its instructions appear under its server name in `<mcp_instructions>`, and the usual "only send what changed" updates fire when it attaches, detaches or a newer connection takes over the name.

```diff
  instructions = configured servers' instructions
+ instructions += attached client's instructions (newest connection serving the name)
+ same name configured and attached -> both, joined by a blank line
```

📊 **Proof**

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Attached client with instructions | ❌ not listed | ✅ listed under its name |
| Second connection under the same name | ❌ not listed | ✅ newest one's instructions |
| Newest connection closes | ❌ not listed | ✅ falls back to the previous one's |
| Last connection closes | – | ✅ entry removed |

The new test in `mcp-attach.test.ts` fails without the change; 19 pass across the attach and instructions tests.

👀 **Read:** `Mcp.instructions` in `packages/core/src/mcp/index.ts`. When a configured server and an attached client share a name, both sets of instructions are kept, since the configured server's other tools stay reachable. Visibility filtering and the change diffing are unchanged and already keyed by server name. The rest is routine.

prs.title: feat(plugin): add settings rows, selects and menu rows to ctx.ui
prs.body:
Third-party GUI plugins cannot import `@opencode/ui`, and `ctx.ui` had no settings rows, select, or menu rows. Community plugins hand-copy the app's private settings markup (`data-component="settings-row"`, `settings-tab-header`, …) or put a `ui.Button` inside the project menu, which does not navigate with the keyboard or close the menu.

This adds the missing pieces to `ctx.ui`, in the same thin-wrapper style as the existing members.

```tsx
const ui = ctx.ui

ctx.add(SettingsPage, {
  id: "usage",
  get title() {
    return ctx.t("title")
  },
  get entries() {
    return [{ id: "usage-period", title: ctx.t("period") }]
  },
  render: () => (
    <ui.SettingsLayout title={ctx.t("title")} description={ctx.t("description")}>
      <ui.SettingsSection title={ctx.t("tracking")}>
        <ui.SettingsRow id="usage-period" title={ctx.t("period")} description={ctx.t("period.description")}>
          <ui.Select label={ctx.t("period")} options={periods()} value={period()} onChange={setPeriod} />
        </ui.SettingsRow>
      </ui.SettingsSection>
    </ui.SettingsLayout>
  ),
})

ctx.add(Slot, {
  at: "session.location.menu",
  render: (input) => (
    <>
      <ui.MenuItem label={ctx.t("usage")} icon="status" onSelect={() => open(input.session)} />
      <ui.MenuSub label={ctx.t("openIn")} icon="outline-share">
        <For each={apps()}>{(app) => <ui.MenuItem label={app.name} onSelect={() => launch(app)} />}</For>
      </ui.MenuSub>
    </>
  ),
})
```

| Before: `ctx.ui` only | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9e19bea-49e9-4d57-9c6d-1d4848f1592b) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/283ec230-5f2d-4ecf-a4ec-03f5ebf223ba) |

### Why these

Audit of `@opencode/ui/*` and `@opencode/session-ui/*` imports in `packages/gui-plugins/src` against what `ctx.ui` already offers:

- **Settings markup**: `pairing/page.tsx`, `updater/section.tsx`, `review/settings.tsx` and `updater/beta-page.tsx` each copy the host's settings row, section and page header markup. no-phux/phux and slkiser/opencode-quota copy the same markup.
- **Select**: `review/parts.tsx` uses `@opencode/ui/select`; the app's settings rows use it for every dropdown. opencode-quota falls back to a native `<select>`.
- **Menu rows**: `details/location-menu.tsx`, `location-workspace.tsx` and `workspace-menu.tsx` render `Menu.Item`, `Menu.Group`, `Menu.Sub` straight into the project menu. `session.location.menu` is a public slot, but a third party could only put a `Button` there (opencode-quota does).
- Everything else built-ins import (`Tabs`, `ProgressCircle`, `DiffChanges`, file and review views, motion, theme internals) is feature-specific or already covered.

### What changed

- `Ui.MenuItem(props: UiMenuItem)`: same fields as a `Ui.Menu` item (`label`, `icon`, `keys`, `disabled`, `onSelect`).
- `Ui.MenuSeparator()`, `Ui.MenuGroup({ label, children })`, `Ui.MenuSub({ label, icon?, disabled?, onOpenChange?, children })`.
- `Ui.Select<T extends string>({ options: { value, label }[], value, onChange, label, placeholder?, disabled?, invalid?, placement?, class? })`.
- `Ui.SettingsLayout({ title, description?, actions?, children })`: page header plus sectioned body; search that reveals the page highlights the header.
- `Ui.SettingsSection({ title?, children, footer? })`: heading over the bordered list.
- `Ui.SettingsRow({ title, description?, id?, children? })`: `id` is the `SettingEntry.id` that search scrolls to and highlights.
- `packages/app/src/runtime/plugin/ui.tsx` implements them. Settings components reuse the settings screen's stylesheet, so the startup chunk does not grow.
- Pairing, updates and review now use `ctx.ui` instead of their copied rows. The pairing page renders pixel-identical.
- SDK TSDoc, `SlotMap["session.location.menu"]`, `SettingsPage.render`, the GUI plugin guide and `packages/gui-plugins/README.md` describe the new members.
- `plugin-host.spec.ts`: the `ctx.ui` case also renders the settings components and a select, and puts menu rows in a host menu (the fixture now holds `session.location.menu` in a menu).
