issues.title: Two extensions overriding the same built-in tool make pi exit 1 before the TUI starts

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

I installed two packages that each override a built-in tool and pi won't start at all — exit code 1, no TUI:

```
Error: Failed to load extension "/tmp/piconf/ext/b.ts": Tool "read" conflicts with "/tmp/piconf/ext/a.ts"
Hint: Start without extensions using "pi -ne".
```

`pi -ne` starts, and removing either package starts, so it's the pair. What makes it worse is that the second extension can't choose to yield: while extensions are loading, `pi.getAllTools()` throws `Extension runtime not initialized. Action methods cannot be called during extension loading.`, and the `replaceable: true` escape hatch in the SDK only applies to inline factories. So precedence comes down to load order in settings, and whichever package is listed second dies — taking the whole process with it.

### Steps to reproduce

Two five-line extensions, no third-party packages. Both register `read`:

```ts
// a.ts; b.ts is the same file with a different string in it
export default (pi: any) => pi.registerTool({ name: "read", label: "read", description: "a",
  parameters: { type: "object", properties: {} },
  execute: async () => ({ content: [{ type: "text", text: "a" }] }) });
```

```json
// settings.json
{ "extensions": ["/tmp/piconf/ext/a.ts", "/tmp/piconf/ext/b.ts"] }
```

```
PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/tmp/piconf pi -p "hi" --no-session   # exit 1
```

Swap the two entries and the error flips to the other file.

Real case, if it helps triage: pi-ssh-remote replaces the operations of `read`/`write`/`edit`/`bash` to route them over SSH, and pi-tool-display replaces the same four names to render diffs. Neither is doing anything undocumented; together pi won't start and one of them has to go.

### Expected behavior

Either of these would have kept my setup working: a tool-name conflict warns and picks a winner instead of killing the process, or an extension can find out who already owns a name while it's loading so the second one can skip its override.

Previous reports: #9649, #7696, #5316.

### Version

1.0.0

issues.title: 0.99.x: terminal color query replies leak into the prompt and BEL opens the external editor (mintty on Windows, ConPTY)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
### What happened?

On startup pi opens the external editor. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
The query runs regardless of theme.

**Versions:** 0.99.x are affected. 0.87.1 is fine. Windows Terminal is fine.
**Terminal:** mintty on Windows, native node.exe, `TERM=xterm`, `EDITOR=vim` (I am using GitBash for Windows environment)

## Cause

0.87.1 sent a single `ESC]11;?BEL` query. 0.99.x sends OSC 10, OSC 11, OSC 4 for indices 0–15, and DA1 (`ESC[c`) as the end marker (`TERMINAL_COLOR_QUERY` in `packages/tui/src/tui.ts`). In this terminal:

1. The DA1 reply arrives first, before any color reply. `consumeTerminalColorResponse` then drops the pending query, so later replies are no longer consumed.
2. The OSC replies arrive without their `ESC]4` prefix, in fragments (`;0`, `;rgb:0000/0000/0000`, `BEL`, `;1`, …). The reply regex cannot match them anyway.
3. `StdinBuffer` splits non-escape input into single characters, so they land in the editor as text. Each stray BEL is Ctrl+G and opens the external editor.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi under GitBash (Windows).
2. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
3. External editor opens, containing the prompt.

### Expected behavior

Prompt is empty and external editor is not opened at the startup. Worked in 0.87.1.

### Version

0.99.0, 0.99.1, 0.99.2,
1.0.0 (tui-mode regular; see my comment below)

issues.title: Windows: Ctrl+V is silently unbound in the editor (paste default is Alt+V only)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**What happened?**

On Windows, pressing Ctrl+V in the editor inserts nothing and shows no feedback, so pasting text looks broken. The only default paste binding is Alt+V.

This is not terminal-specific — on `win32` a `ctrl+v` binding does not exist at all. From `packages/coding-agent/src/core/keybindings.js`:

```js
"app.clipboard.pasteImage": {
    defaultKeys: windowsKeybindings ? "alt+v" : "ctrl+v",
    description: "Paste files on macOS, images, or text from clipboard"
}
```

`useWindowsKeybindings()` returns true for `win32` and for WSL, so both get `alt+v` only (`docs/keybindings.md` says `ctrl+v` (`alt+v` on Windows and WSL)). No other action binds `ctrl+v`, so the key falls through to the editor and is dropped silently.

I hit this running `pi` inside Tern 0.9.10's embedded terminal (ConPTY): that terminal does not do Ctrl+V paste itself either, so the only way to paste is knowing about Alt+V. Combined with #9509 (Alt+letter shortcuts not reaching the app in some terminals and layouts), Windows users can end up with no working paste key at all.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. On Windows (native or WSL), run `pi`.
2. Copy text in another app.
3. Press Ctrl+V in the editor: nothing is inserted, no message.

**Expected behavior**

Ctrl+V pastes on Windows too, or the editor says which key pastes. Terminals that implement Ctrl+V themselves are unaffected, since they send a bracketed paste instead of a `0x16` keypress.

**Workaround**

`<agent-dir>/keybindings.json`, then `/reload`:

```json
{ "app.clipboard.pasteImage": ["ctrl+v", "alt+v"] }
```

**Version**

1.5.0 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), Windows 11 26200, Tern 0.9.10 embedded terminal

issues.title: coding-agent: preserve Request cancellation when fetchWithRetry adds timeout signals

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Preserve a Request input’s abort signal in fetchWithRetry when init.signal is omitted. Explicit init.signal values, including null, should retain native fetch’s override behavior.

### Why?

Reproduced on main 676af1d777ef6f04b6bc8daf4cf3b9b1799cff4d, Node 24.22.1, with a localhost HTTP server and no extensions or provider calls:

1. Create a Request with an already-aborted signal.
2. Native fetch(request) rejects with the cancellation reason.
3. fetchWithRetry(request, undefined, { timeoutMs: 1000 }) instead sends the request and returns HTTP 200.

The helper reads only init?.signal. Adding its own timeout overrides the signal carried by the Request. attemptTimeoutMs has the same problem.

This is a helper-level contract bug; the current in-repo callers I checked pass URLs, so I am not claiming a demonstrated CLI failure.

### How? (optional)

Use Request.signal only when init.signal === undefined, then combine it with the existing timeout signals. The local fix passes all nine management-http.test.ts cases, including four added cases covering pre-aborted input, in-flight cancellation, and explicit signal/null overrides. The localhost reproduction and npm run check also pass. The full test.sh suite has not been run yet.

I would like to contribute the focused fix and tests. Could a maintainer review this proposal and grant lgtm approval before I open a PR?

This proposal and fix were prepared by Codex at the account owner’s request. An AI-labeled reproduction comment follows.

issues.title: Nix build fails on 9c9ce85: TS2322 in github-copilot.ts (empty classifier catalog group)

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

Building `9c9ce8547e5a88cbe834a53e9a6d83a789d08e47` from a Nix flake fails in `pi-workspace-packages`:

```text
src/providers/github-copilot.ts:33:3 - error TS2322: Type 'unknown[]' is not assignable to type 'readonly ProviderModel<GitHubCopilotApi>[]'.
```

Line 33 is

```ts
models: [...Object.values(GITHUB_COPILOT_MODELS), ...Object.values(GITHUB_COPILOT_CLASSIFIER_MODELS)],
```

The catalog hydrated from the pinned revision does not contain any `classifier` entry for `github-copilot`, so the key set of `ClassifierModelCatalog<TGroups, "github-copilot">` is empty and `Object.values(...)` is `unknown[]`.

This looks like the same class of problem as #10985 (stale Nix catalog pin vs. provider source): `update-model-catalog-pin.mjs --if-stale` compares hydration validity and model *groups*, not whether a provider has zero models of a type that the source code references unconditionally.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone `9c9ce8547e5a88cbe834a53e9a6d83a789d08e47`, `npm ci`.
2. Fetch the pinned catalog `sha256-f4dbabe79cda4b38aee4a761b23fd5eaf526ac2e28fed3c9ee86e37ca0e5d71e` and hydrate:
   `node packages/ai/scripts/hydrate-model-catalog.ts <catalog.json>`
3. `npx tsc -p packages/ai/tsconfig.build.json --noEmit`

TypeScript 7.0.2 (also `tsgo` 7.0.2 from nixpkgs) reports the error above; `npm run check:model-data` passes ("Generated model data is valid."). Only this one error is produced.

Notes from the investigation:

- The hydrated `github-copilot` data has three api groups (`anthropic-messages`, `openai-completions`, `openai-responses`) and **only `chat` entries** — no `classifier` of any type.
- The live catalog (`sha256-c2cce837…`) behaves the same; the only difference against the pinned revision is one extra chat model (`gpt-6.1-terra`).
- Pulling `data-json.d.ts` (`declare module "*.json"`) into the program via a looser `exclude` does not change the error, so the JSON import already resolves to `unknown` regardless of that declaration.
- Reproducible outside Nix on Arch/NixOS with the plain npm toolchain, i.e. it is not a packaging artifact.

### Expected behavior

Either the catalog should carry at least one `github-copilot` classifier entry, or `github-copilot.ts` should not spread `GITHUB_COPILOT_CLASSIFIER_MODELS` unconditionally (the constant it reads is derived from the hydrated JSON, which may legitimately be empty).

### Version

1.5.0, revision `9c9ce8547e5a88cbe834a53e9a6d83a789d08e47`, `nix/model-catalog.json` pin `sha256-f4dbabe79cda4b38aee4a761b23fd5eaf526ac2e28fed3c9ee86e37ca0e5d71e`.

The `nix.yml` run for this commit (2026-11-02T23:57:35Z) is reported green, so the CI environment must resolve the JSON type differently — please check whether the workflow still hydrates the catalog, or runs `tsc` from the JS TypeScript 7.0.2 package rather than `tsgo`.

AI-assisted diagnosis; the reproduction commands above are mine, run on Arch Linux and on NixOS.

issues.title: MCP SSE parser rejects valid CR-only line endings

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

MCP Streamable HTTP fails to parse SSE events whose lines end with a lone carriage return (`\r`). The SSE standard permits CRLF, LF, and lone CR line endings, but `consumeSseStream()` only splits on LF:

```ts
let newline = buffered.indexOf("\n");
```

The subsequent removal of a trailing CR handles CRLF; it does not recognize lone CR as a line boundary. With an `id` line followed by a `data` line using CR-only separators, a valid tool result is not dispatched and the call fails with:

```text
MCP response stream failed: stream ended without a response
```

This is a narrow protocol-compatibility issue. I have not identified a third-party MCP server using CR-only events; the common LF and CRLF paths work.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect the real `McpClient` and `StreamableHttpTransport` to a controlled local HTTP server and complete initialization.
2. Set `openGetStream: false` and `reconnect: { maxRetries: 0 }` to isolate response parsing.
3. For a tool call, respond with `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and a complete event constructed as:

   ```js
   [
     "id: result",
     "data: " + JSON.stringify({
       jsonrpc: "2.0",
       id: request.id,
       result: { content: [{ type: "text", text: "hello" }] },
     }),
     "",
     "",
   ].join("\r")
   ```

4. End the response. Repeat with `"\n"` and `"\r\n"` as controls.

LF and CRLF deliver the tool result; CR fails with the error above. A subsequent `ping` succeeds in all three cases. A parser-level check with one character per chunk gives the same distinction, including CRLF split across chunks.

A temporary parser copy recognizing CR/LF/CRLF made all three parser and local HTTP cases succeed. This was a cause-checking experiment, not a production-ready patch or a run of the full existing suite. No model API, external MCP server, or full Pi TUI was involved.

### Expected behavior

Recognize all three SSE line endings, as specified in [the SSE standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/dev/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream).

I propose a small incremental line parser: terminate a line on CR or LF, and remember to ignore one LF immediately following CR, including across chunks. Simply replacing every CR with LF would incorrectly turn CRLF into two line endings and could dispatch events prematurely. CR-terminated events should be delivered promptly without waiting for another chunk or EOF.

The change should preserve event boundaries, empty-data priming events, multiline data, streaming Unicode decoding, size limits, and error cleanup. Regression tests would cover all three line endings, mixed endings, split CRLF, trailing CR, and delivery while the stream remains open.

I am confident I can complete this focused fix and its regression tests. Would you be willing to give this work an `lgtm` so I can submit the PR?

### Version

Source commit `58c0b02ce552adab76014e7ed712ab7981359aa8`; Node.js 24.20.0; macOS. Dynamic tests used that local revision. Upstream commit `676af1d777ef6f04b6bc8daf4cf3b9b1799cff4d` retains the same LF-only splitting logic (source inspection only).

issues.title: MCP HTTP resumes response streams after tool calls are cancelled or time out

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

MCP Streamable HTTP continues resuming a tool's response stream after the tool call has been cancelled or timed out. The caller has already received `AbortError` or `McpTimeoutError`, and the server has received `notifications/cancelled`, but Pi still starts new resumption GETs. A late result then produces:

```text
Received response for unknown MCP request 2
```

Each test made only one `tools/call` POST. This is unnecessary response-stream recovery, not repeated tool execution.

### Steps to reproduce

Using the real `McpClient` and `StreamableHttpTransport` with a local HTTP fixture:

1. Complete MCP initialization. Set `openGetStream: false` to isolate response resumption from the independent notification stream.
2. Start `client.callTool()`.
3. Return a complete SSE priming event, then end the response normally:

   ```text
   id: initial
   retry: 100
   data:

   ```

4. Abort the call before its first resumption, or set `timeoutMs: 40`.
5. Record call settlement, cancellation notifications, and subsequent GETs. Have the fixture return further priming events on the first two GETs and the original result on the third.

Three runs against the unmodified implementation gave the same results:

| Scenario | Call outcome | New resumption GETs after settlement | Late error |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Abort | `AbortError` | 3 | Unknown request |
| Timeout | `McpTimeoutError` | 3 | Unknown request |
| No cancellation | Success after resumption | 0 | None |
| Close the whole connection | `McpConnectionClosedError` | 0 | None |

The three GETs reflect the fixture's response sequence, not a universal retry count. A subsequent `ping` succeeds after both abort and timeout. Cancellation is best-effort on the server; the problem here is that the client initiates new recovery requests after local cancellation has completed.

These are local HTTP integration tests without model APIs or external services, not full Pi TUI or third-party-server tests.

### Expected behavior

Stop recovery for an abandoned request without closing the shared transport or disrupting other calls and the independent notification stream.

In `client.ts`, removing the pending request aborts its send controller. However, `streamable-http.ts` starts `consumeResponseStream()` without that signal; its recovery loop checks whether the result arrived or the transport closed, not whether the request ended.

I plan to propagate request cancellation through the response stream's lifecycle:

- End the reconnect wait and prevent later resumption GETs.
- Stop the request's active response reader or resumption GET and release its resources.
- Avoid dispatching late results or synthetic errors for the removed request.
- Preserve other concurrent requests and the notification stream.

A temporary copy with cancellation checks before resumption reduced subsequent GETs from 3 to 0 for abort and timeout, removed the late errors, and preserved successful normal resumption. This validates the cause, but is not a complete fix: cancellation during an active read or an already-started GET still needs coverage.

I will add regression tests for normal resumption, cancellation during backoff and active reads, timeout, concurrent-request isolation, and full transport close. Assertions will use request traces and resource completion rather than precise timing thresholds.

I am confident I can complete this focused implementation and its regression tests. Would you be willing to give this work an `lgtm` so I can submit the PR?

### Version

Source commit `58c0b02ce552adab76014e7ed712ab7981359aa8`; Node.js 24.20.0; macOS. Dynamic tests used that local revision. Upstream commit `676af1d777ef6f04b6bc8daf4cf3b9b1799cff4d` still has the same missing signal propagation (source inspection only).

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Avoid repeatedly copying and rescanning incomplete large JSON-RPC messages in the MCP stdio transport.

`packages/mcp/src/transports/stdio.ts` currently handles each stdout chunk by copying the entire accumulated prefix and searching it from the beginning:

```ts
this.stdoutBuffer = Buffer.concat([
  this.stdoutBuffer,
  Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk : Buffer.from(chunk),
]);
const newline = this.stdoutBuffer.indexOf(0x0a);
```

When a large valid tool result arrives in fixed-size chunks, the same prefix is repeatedly copied and scanned until the terminating newline arrives. With the default 16 MiB message limit, a valid 12 MiB text result delivered through a real subprocess pipe arrived in about 200 chunks and produced approximately 1.23 GB of cumulative `Buffer.concat` output. This is cumulative copy volume, not peak memory usage or a memory leak.

A temporary chunk-queue comparison reduced the cumulative copy volume for the 12 MiB / 64 KiB case from about 1.23 GB to 12.6 MB. Parser-level median time changed from 51.36 ms to 5.54 ms; for 4 MiB it changed from 6.05 ms to 1.52 ms. A real subprocess-pipe comparison changed from approximately 96.5–97.4 ms to 55.2–56.2 ms, including subprocess serialization and pipe transfer. Processing 20,000 small complete JSON messages showed no additional overhead in the comparison.

These are transport-level measurements, not end-to-end Pi latency.

### Why?

The current approach makes buffering work grow quadratically for a long line delivered in many chunks, even though the newline delimiter is one byte and already received chunks do not need to be rescanned. Large but valid MCP tool results can therefore spend unnecessary time and allocation bandwidth in transport buffering before JSON parsing begins.

### How?

Use a small chunk queue and a pending byte count:

1. Search only newly received data for a newline.
2. When no newline is present, retain the chunks without concatenating the whole prefix.
3. When a newline arrives, concatenate the chunks for that complete line once, then reuse the existing UTF-8 decoding, JSON parsing, and dispatch logic.
4. Use a direct slice when a complete line is already within one chunk, and continue processing additional lines in the same chunk.

The change would remain limited to stdout buffering and newline scanning. It would preserve the existing message-size limit, CRLF and blank-line handling, invalid-message errors, oversized-message handling, incomplete-message checks on close, and process-shutdown behavior.

I have locally compared the temporary implementation across UTF-8 and CRLF splits, multiple messages in one chunk, blank and invalid lines, and oversized-message recovery; the results matched the current implementation. The existing MCP stdio tests also pass. A proper implementation should turn these checks into regression tests and verify cumulative copy/scanned-byte counts rather than timing thresholds.

I identified the initial code-level concern and the repeated-copying path through my own review of Pi's MCP stdio implementation. I then used AI assistance to help reproduce the behavior, build the temporary comparison, check edge cases, and organize the report.

I am confident I can complete the focused implementation, regression tests, and reproducible performance comparison. Would you be willing to give this work an `lgtm` so I can submit the PR?

### Version

Source commit `58c0b02ce552adab76014e7ed712ab7981359aa8`; Node.js 24.20.0; macOS.

issues.title: MCP SSE responses remain open after a request fails the message-size limit
issues.body:
### What happened?

When an MCP SSE message exceeds the size limit, Pi correctly rejects it, but does not cancel the HTTP response stream. If the server keeps the response open and sends heartbeats, the failed request continues holding connection resources.

`consumeSseStream()` in `packages/mcp/src/transports/streamable-http.ts` only releases the reader lock on exit:

```ts
finally {
  reader.releaseLock();
}
```

Releasing the lock does not cancel the response body. The request has failed, but its stream can remain open until the server ends it or the whole MCP client closes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect a real `McpClient` through `StreamableHttpTransport` to a local HTTP fixture, with `maxMessageBytes: 128` and `openGetStream: false` to exclude the separate notification stream.
2. After initialization, have a test request return SSE with a JSON-RPC result containing 512 `x` characters. Keep that response open and send SSE heartbeats every 20ms.
3. Make three such requests. Each fails with an error containing `MCP SSE event exceeds 128 bytes`.
4. Wait 140ms and check whether those HTTP responses have closed.

All three responses remained active. Across three repeated rounds, the server made 18 further heartbeat writes during the observation period. Closing the whole client released the responses. A temporary comparison that explicitly cancelled the reader left zero active responses and zero subsequent heartbeat writes; a follow-up `ping` succeeded in both versions.

This was a bounded loopback test using the real MCP client and transport, without extensions, model APIs, or external services. All test connections were cleaned up. No OOM, crash, or complete Pi TUI behavior was demonstrated.

### Expected behavior

Cancel an unused SSE response when parsing exits early on a size-limit error, then release the reader lock. Cleanup should not require closing the whole client.

My proposed fix is to distinguish normal completion from an error exit and cancel the response on the error path, without allowing a cancellation failure to replace the original error. I would add regression tests for prompt response cleanup and successful subsequent requests on the same client.

I'm interested in Pi and would like to contribute. Would you be open to a fix along these lines? If so, I'd be happy to submit a minimal patch with regression tests.

Related: #11335 concerns JSON responses bypassing the limit. Here SSE enforces the limit, but the error path does not cancel its response.

### Version

Reproduced on source commit `58c0b02ce552adab76014e7ed712ab7981359aa8`; Node.js 24.20.0; macOS. Upstream commit `90b42bca6ed161b8e7ee40ceda9755205c2882ec` still has only `reader.releaseLock()` in this finally block (source inspection only, not a repeated integration test).

issues.title: pi -p hangs indefinitely on Windows: no sockets, no child processes, no output, no timeout

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## `pi -p` (non-interactive) process hangs indefinitely with no sockets, no child processes, no output (Windows)

### Environment
- `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.4.0, Node v24.14.0, Windows 11
- Launched via a local wrapper proxy (`pxpipe-proxy` 0.15.1): proxy node → `pwsh -NoProfile -File …` → `node …/pi-coding-agent/dist/bundle/cli.js`
- Models: `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol:medium` and `openai-codex/gpt-6-luna:high`
- Prompt passed with `-p` (one-shot, output redirected to a file)

### What happened
Two independent `pi -p` runs, started 6 minutes apart in different git worktrees, both stopped producing output early. One stopped at 3924 bytes and the other at 2416 bytes. Each output only echoed the prompt. Neither process ever exited. Both had been stuck for about 16 hours when I checked. Other `pi -p` runs launched the same way on the same machine that day finished normally.

### State of the stuck `pi` processes (about 16 h after they started)
| | run A | run B |
|---|---|---|
| started | 16:18:32 | 16:24:05 |
| total CPU time | 1.1 s | 0.9 s |
| working set | 3 MB (paged out) | 6 MB |
| threads / handles | 13 / 205 | 13 / 205 |
| TCP sockets (`netstat -ano`) | **none** | **none** |
| child processes | **none** | **none** |

The wrapper proxy processes were still listening on loopback (`127.0.0.1:1113` and `:2478`) but had no established connections.

So the agent is not blocked on the network, a tool subprocess, or the CPU. It looks like it is waiting on a promise or event that never settles. There is no timeout and no error, so `-p` hangs forever and blocks whatever is waiting on it.

### Memory dump
I took a full minidump of run A (`procdump -ma`, 218 MB) while it was hung. I searched its strings for error text: `other side closed`, `terminated`, `premature close`, `stream_error`, `"type":"error"`. Every match was library source code (undici, retry-pattern lists). I found no runtime error message, which suggests the request never failed visibly; it just never settled. The dump contains private prompt content, so I am not attaching it, but I can run specific commands against it (`llnode`/WinDbg) if that helps.

### Expected
In `-p` mode, a stalled request or turn should time out, or at least exit non-zero with an error, instead of idling forever.

### Possibly related
#4945 (openai-codex connection reliability) and #8857 (no tool-call execution timeout). In this case no tool child process exists, though.

### Repro
Not deterministic. Happened on 2 of a few dozen `-p` runs in one day.

issues.title: pi-ai: Anthropic server-tool blocks dropped on decode break the next request (400 thinking blocks cannot be modified)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

We give a pi agent Anthropic's hosted web search by adding `{ "type": "web_search_20250305", "name": "web_search", "max_uses": 5 }` to `params.tools` in `onPayload`. Searching works. With extended thinking on, the response comes back as `thinking`, `server_tool_use`, `web_search_tool_result`, text with citations, `thinking` again, and finally a client `tool_use`.

The Anthropic adapter keeps only `text`, `thinking`, `redacted_thinking` and `tool_use` (`content_block_start` in `anthropic-messages.js`); `server_tool_use`, `web_search_tool_result` and `citations_delta` are thrown away, and `AssistantMessage` has no place for them. When the agent loop sends the tool result, the latest assistant message goes back to Anthropic with those blocks missing, so its thinking blocks no longer sit where they did, and Anthropic refuses:

```
400 invalid_request_error: messages.3.content.33: `thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be modified. These blocks must remain as they were in the original response.
```

Seen twice on a production deployment on 2026-11-03 (claude-opus-5-5, 15 successful tool-loop calls, then this on the first call where one response both searched and called a client tool). Plain multi-turn search without a client tool does not fail, it only loses the search results and citations on later turns.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `stream()` from `@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/anthropic-messages`, model `claude-opus-5-5`, thinking enabled, one ordinary client tool (e.g. `get_time`).
2. In `onPayload`, push `{ "type": "web_search_20250305", "name": "web_search", "max_uses": 5 }` onto `params.tools` and return the params.
3. Prompt: "Search the web for today's top headline, then call get_time."
4. Feed the tool result back and run the next step. The second request fails with the 400 above.

I can attach the SSE of the first response and the failing second request body if useful.

### Expected behavior

A content block the adapter does not understand should be kept as it came and sent back unchanged, in its original position, when the message is replayed to the same provider. An opaque raw-JSON content block on `AssistantMessage` would be enough; other providers' encoders would skip it. This is not a request for a server-tool abstraction (#1740, #6365), only for not losing what Anthropic returned. #11138 described the same gap without having hit the 400.

Happy to implement this if approved.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-ai` 1.3.0; the same code is in 1.4.0 and 1.5.0.

_Drafted with an AI assistant from my own debugging notes and reviewed by me._

issues.title: Add Modular as a built-in provider
issues.body: ### What do you want to change? I'm on the team at Modular that runs Modular Cloud, our hosted inference for open models, with an OpenAI-compatible API at `https://api.modular.com/v1`. I'd like to add Modular as a built-in provider, so a user only needs `MODULAR_API_KEY` to pick one of our models in `/model`. Our entry is now on models.dev (anomalyco/models.dev#11645), with the four models on our pay-as-you-go API (price per 1M input / output tokens): - MiniMax M3.1 Flash (`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`): 1M context, $0.15 / $0.60 - MiniMax M3 (`minimax/minimax-m3`): 1M context, $0.30 / $1.20 - DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`): 1M context, $0.17 / $1.20 - Gemma 4 31B (`google/gemma-4-31b-it`): 256K context, $0.25 / $0.65 The full list of models we serve is at https://docs.modular.com/models. ### Why? Today a Pi user who wants to try us has to write a custom provider by hand and look up model IDs, context limits and prices themselves. On speed: Artificial Analysis benchmarks every host serving the same model. For [MiniMax M3.1 Flash](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/minimax-m3-1-flash/providers), the newest model we serve, we're currently **third of 14 providers** on both output speed and time to first answer token. For [Gemma 4 31B](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/gemma-4-31b/providers), we're **first of 11** on time to first answer token and **second** on output speed. Pi goes back to the model after every tool call, so faster responses make a whole session feel more responsive. We'll also take care of keeping things up to date on our end. Since Pi pulls its models from models.dev, we're keeping our models.dev entry in sync upstream: price changes and retired models sync over automatically (anomalyco/models.dev#11887), and we'll send PRs there whenever we add new models. So there shouldn't be any extra maintenance on the Pi side. ### How? (optional) Same shape as Fireworks and Together with the new provider definitions: a `catalog/providers/modular.ts` that pulls our models.dev entry with `modelsDevModels()` on `openai-completions` (base URL `https://api.modular.com/v1`), `MODULAR_API_KEY` auth, a default model, and the docs rows. The one Modular-specific part is the reasoning controls, which differ per model: MiniMax M3.1 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash take an effort level (`reasoning.effort`), while MiniMax M3 and Gemma 4 31B switch reasoning on and off (`reasoning.enabled`). So each model gets its own `thinkingFormat` and `thinkingLevelMap`, which is the setup I tested with. I've run all four models end to end in Pi 1.4.0 using this as a custom provider, including tool calls, and I'm happy to open the PR. Thanks for building Pi and for taking a look at this!

issues.title: fix(tools): byte count in write, false limit warning in find, surrogate split in truncateLine
The grep tool with context lines can cause OOM

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

We use pi-coding-agent as headless SDK.  When the process died with `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`.

We pulled the core dump and found the heap was full of log files. When the grep gets context more than '0' it reads each matched file and splits into an array, just to print the surrounding two lines.

In our case, the agent grepped a directory of server logs, 100 MB to a few GB each, with context 2 and 12 files got loaded before the 4 GB default heap ran out. This has killed our process 10 times in the last 2 months and got auto-restarted before we noticed.

The file is core/tools/grep.ts in 'getFileLines' and 'formatBlock'.

We only use 'pi-mcp-adapter' extension, but its not the reason of this bug.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run below in bash to make 8 files of about 95 MB:
```
mkdir logs
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do seq 1 6000000 | sed 's/^/log line /' > logs/server$i.log; done
```

2. Below script will call grep tool with context. Save as grep-oom.mjs in the same directory (npm i @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent first):
```
import { createGrepTool } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
const tool = createGrepTool(process.cwd());
const r = await tool.execute("t", { pattern: "line 5999999", path: "logs", context: 2 });
console.log(r.content[0].text.split("\n").slice(0, 4).join("\n"));
```

3. Run with this:
```
node --max-old-space-size=1024 grep-oom.mjs
```

Result:
Dies in about 13 s with "FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit ... JavaScript heap out of memory". One match per file, but every file is read and split whole because of context: 2.

### Expected behavior

grep with context should never be able to run the process out of memory: its memory should follow the size of the output, not the size of the files it searches. ripgrep already handles context, so grep should pass the --context N flag through and format the 'context' events from rg --json. I have a small fix, and I'd like to send it as a PR.

### Version

0.85.0

TUI Markdown prints HTML comments as visible text
issues.body:
## What happened?

The pi-tui `Markdown` component prints `<!-- ... -->` comments verbatim. I hit it in the new "Extension Updates" notice: my release tooling keeps `<!-- USER-EDITABLE SECTION START -->` / `<!-- USER-EDITABLE SECTION END -->` markers in `CHANGELOG.md`, and both lines show up around every release entry. The markers come from my [semver-calver-release](https://github.com/cad0p/semver-calver-release/blob/b57af46335825afcbf8173a9fa0a32dbee8d1a01/release/action.yml#L279-L281) action; [pi-napkin's CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/cad0p/pi-napkin/blob/13adac98bf6137f5698841bc0442b1f986d793f0/CHANGELOG.md#L5-L13) is a real example. This is pi's own renderer on Markdown the package author wrote, not model output, so it is separate from #6454.

marked lexes comments as `html` tokens, and both the [block `html` case](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/10cf3264fbbb42d02f7dee45a8b19adcf9085e4e/packages/tui/src/components/markdown.ts#L717-L722) and the [inline `html` case](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/10cf3264fbbb42d02f7dee45a8b19adcf9085e4e/packages/tui/src/components/markdown.ts#L826-L831) push `token.raw` as plain text. Comments are meant to be invisible in rendered Markdown, so every surface using `Markdown` leaks them: the "Extension Updates" notice, "What's New", `/changelog` and assistant messages. An extension can't work around it for the notices: the [Extension Updates call site](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/10cf3264fbbb42d02f7dee45a8b19adcf9085e4e/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts#L897) passes no transform, so `registerMarkdownTransformer` never sees that text.

## Steps to reproduce

On 1.5.0, from the `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` install directory:

```js
import { Markdown } from "@earendil-works/pi-tui";
const theme = new Proxy({}, { get: () => (s) => s });
const md = new Markdown("## [1.0.0]\n\n<!-- release-notes:start -->\nFixed a bug.\n\nSee <!-- todo: link --> the docs.", 0, 0, theme);
console.log(md.render(60).map((l) => l.trimEnd()).join("\n"));
```

Output:

```
[1.0.0]

<!-- release-notes:start -->
Fixed a bug.

See <!-- todo: link --> the docs.
```

In the app: give an installed extension package a `CHANGELOG.md` entry containing an HTML comment and bump its version; the comment line appears under "Extension Updates".

## Expected behavior

Comments are not shown, without leaving extra blank lines or double spaces where they were. Other inline HTML keeps rendering as text (`with <tag> markers` should still show).

I'm happy to send this with a test if you want it.

## Version

1.5.0 (code unchanged on `main` @ `10cf3264f`)

issues.title: Extension changelog repeats on every launch when the package version is a prerelease
issues.body:
## What happened?

The new "Extension Updates" notice shows the same entries again on every fresh launch when the installed package version has a prerelease suffix and a patch number above 0.

[`getNewEntries()`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/642e30b68930a644050794011555a04ed9027eb4/packages/coding-agent/src/utils/changelog.ts#L182-L193) splits the saved version on `.`, so `0.1.5-20261020.7` becomes `["0", "1", "5-20261020", "7"]`. `Number("5-20261020")` is `NaN`, the `|| 0` turns it into 0, and the saved version is read as `0.1.0`. [`getExtensionChangelogUpdates()`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/642e30b68930a644050794011555a04ed9027eb4/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts#L1384-L1429) then finds `[0.1.1]` to `[0.1.5]` newer, shows them and saves `pkg.version` again, which reads back as `0.1.0` on the next launch.

This matters for packages published on a prerelease dist-tag. Mine publish `X.Y.Z-YYYYMMDD.N` builds to `@next`, so anyone on `@next` of a package at `0.1.5` would get the same notes on every new session.

## Steps to reproduce

On 1.5.0, from a directory where the package is installed:

```js
import { getNewEntries } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/utils/changelog.js";
const entries = [{ major: 0, minor: 1, patch: 5, content: "0.1.5" }, { major: 0, minor: 1, patch: 4, content: "0.1.4" }];
getNewEntries(entries, "0.1.5");            // []
getNewEntries(entries, "0.1.5-20261020.7"); // ["0.1.5", "0.1.4"] entries, every time
```

In the app: install a package with an extension, `version: "0.1.5-20261020.7"` and a `CHANGELOG.md` with `## [0.1.5]`, launch once to record it, then start a few fresh sessions. Launches 2 and 3 both showed the 0.1.5 and 0.1.4 notes, and the saved version stayed `0.1.5-20261020.7`.

## Expected behavior

Compare only the `major.minor.patch` part of the saved version, as already happens for the changelog headings, for example `lastVersion.split(/[-+]/)[0].split(".")`. Then `0.1.5-20261020.7` counts as `0.1.5` and nothing repeats.

I'm happy to send the one-line fix with a test if you want it.

## Version

1.5.0 (code unchanged on `main` @ `642e30b68`)

issues.title: /restart: resume the current session on the installed release

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add `/restart`: end the process and resume the same session on the release `install/current-version` names, in the same terminal. Model, thinking level and session id carry over, like `pi --session <file>`.

### Why?

After `pi update`, every open session keeps running the old release until it is restarted by hand: `/exit`, then `pi -c`, or `pi -r` in a directory with several sessions. `/reload` looks like the fix but is not one. It reloads extensions and settings; the core stays the release the process started on.

That gap is real. A day after updating to 1.5.0 I still had 15 sessions on 1.4.0. One of my long-running sessions ran 19 days on a release older than the #10267 fix and kept paying for the bug it fixed.

### How? (optional)

The managed launcher already `exec`s `install/releases/<current-version>`. It could loop instead: when pi exits with a reserved status and writes the session file path somewhere the launcher can read, the launcher runs `pi --session <file>` with the original environment. `/restart` then is `ctx.shutdown()` plus that status, and an extension API (`ctx.restart()`) could reuse it.

I run a local version of this today as an extension. A detached watcher waits for the pid to exit and types `pi --session <file>` into the tmux pane or terminal block. It works, but only inside a multiplexer, and it has to carry inline env (`FOO=1 pi ...`) by name. Launcher support would remove both limits.

issues.title: Installer script weaknesses

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

The following is an automatic review of the current installer script.  It is open to review but does seem to suggest certain weaknesses that may be easily resolvable.  The report follows.
---
# Security Analysis of the Pi Installer Script

## Overview

This is a production-quality installer for the `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` CLI tool. It supports both a "managed" (self-contained) install path and a legacy npm-global path, with interactive TTY prompts, a Node.js bootstrap installer, and animated progress. Below is a structured security review, ordered from most to least concerning.

---

## 🔴 High-Severity Findings

### 1. No Cryptographic Signature on Managed-Install Artifacts
`download_managed_install_artifacts` fetches `metadata.json`, `package.json`, and `package-lock.json` from `PI_INSTALLER_API_BASE` (default `https://pi.dev/api/installer/releases`). Validation in `validate_managed_install_artifacts` is **structural only** (version match, lockfileVersion, package entry existence). There is **no GPG, minisign, or TLS-pinned signature check**.

**Impact:** A compromised or spoofed `pi.dev` origin (or a successful MITM, see finding #2) can serve a structurally-valid but malicious `package-lock.json`. An attacker who controls the lock file can pin a transitive dependency to a malicious version. `--ignore-scripts` mitigates postinstall payload delivery, but a malicious *runtime* dependency (e.g. a trojaned `left-pad`) would still execute.

**Recommendation:** Sign the release artifacts (minisign / Sigstore / GPG) and verify the signature in the installer before `npm ci`.

### 2. `curl -L` Allows Protocol-Downgrade via Redirect
Two download paths use `curl -L`:

```sh
# download_installer_artifact
curl -L -sS -w '%{http_code}' -o "$output" "$url"

# install_node_standalone
curl -fsSL "$node_dist_base/SHASUMS256.txt" ...
curl -fsSL "$node_dist_base/$node_file" ...
```

By default, curl **follows HTTPS → HTTP redirects**. There is no `--proto-redir https` restriction and no `--max-redirs` cap.

**Impact:** An on-path attacker (or a compromised CDN edge) can issue a `302 Location: http://attacker.example/…` response. The client then downloads the "checksum file" or the Node.js tarball over plaintext HTTP, defeating both TLS integrity and the SHA-256 check (because the checksum file itself comes from the same attacker).

**Recommendation:**
```sh
curl -L --proto-redir https --max-redirs 5 --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 300 …
```

### 3. SHA-256 Verification Is Silently Skipped When No Tool Exists
```sh
verify_node_standalone_download() {
  …
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    …
  elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    …
  fi
  # ← no else / return 1
}
```

If neither `sha256sum` nor `shasum` is on `$PATH` (e.g. a minimal container), the function returns **0 (success)** and the unverified tarball is extracted and symlinked onto the user's `PATH`.

**Impact:** Silent execution of an unverified Node.js binary. Combined with finding #2, this is a full supply-chain compromise vector.

**Recommendation:**
```sh
  else
    printf 'error: no SHA-256 tool available; cannot verify download.\n' >&2
    return 1
  fi
```

---

## 🟠 Medium-Severity Findings

### 4. `--min-release-age=0` Bypasses npm's Fresh-Package Safety Gate
```sh
PI_NPM_INSTALL_MIN_AGE_ARG="--min-release-age=0"
```
This is applied to every `npm install -g` / `npm ci` call. The script's comment explains the rationale (published `npm-shrinkwrap.json`), but it also means a **just-pushed, potentially-typo-squatted or compromised** package version can be installed immediately. `--ignore-scripts` narrows the attack surface but does not eliminate it (a malicious *dependency* doesn't need a script).

**Recommendation:** Keep the flag for the managed path (where the lock file is pre-validated) but consider a short minimum age (e.g. 24 h) for the legacy `npm install -g` path, or add a registry-level allowlist.

### 5. No Timeout on Network Requests
Neither `curl` invocation sets `--connect-timeout` or `--max-time`. A hanging endpoint (or a slowloris-style attack) will block the installer indefinitely with the terminal cursor hidden (`\033[?25l`).

**Recommendation:** Add `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 600` to every `curl` call.

### 6. `PI_INSTALLER_API_BASE` Is Environment-Overrideable
```sh
PI_INSTALLER_API_BASE="${PI_INSTALLER_API_BASE:-https://pi.dev/api/installer/releases}"
```
Any process in the same environment (a `.bashrc` hook, a CI variable, a parent shell) can redirect all artifact downloads to an arbitrary URL. The script never warns the user that this variable is set, and the structural validation in `validate_managed_install_artifacts` would happily pass for a self-consistent fake.

**Recommendation:** If this override is intentional (air-gapped installs), print a prominent warning when it differs from the default. Alternatively, require a second confirmation or a `PI_TRUST_ALT_API=1` opt-in.

### 7. TOCTOU Window on Temp-File Creation
Several patterns:
```sh
rm -f "$log_file"
: >"$log_file"          # or  cat > "$log_file"
```
Between `rm` and `>` an attacker with local access could place a symlink at the PID-suffixed path. The PID in the filename makes this hard to predict, but it is not impossible (e.g. a forking attacker can scan `/tmp`).

**Recommendation:** Use `mktemp` or open with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`.

### 8. Tar Extraction Without Explicit Path-Traversal Guard
```sh
tar -xf "$node_tmp_dir/$node_file" -C "$node_base_dir"
```
Modern `tar` implementations (GNU, bsdtar) reject `..` and absolute paths by default, but the script does not pass `--no-absolute-files --no-absolute-names` (GNU) or `-P` avoidance (bsdtar). On a minimal system with an older `tar`, a crafted archive could write outside `node_base_dir`.

**Recommendation:** Add explicit flags:
```sh
tar --no-absolute-files --no-absolute-names -xf … -C …
```
or verify the archive entries before extraction.

---

### Why?

Apparent weaknesses in the current installer

### How? (optional)

Via the weaknesses and vulnerabilities shown in the report

issues.title: Compaction summaries ignore the transport setting (always WebSocket-first on openai-codex)
issues.body:
### What happened?

The `transport` setting is not applied to compaction summary requests. With `"transport": "sse"`, ordinary openai-codex requests use SSE, but automatic and manual (`/compact`) summaries still go out over WebSocket.

In 1.1.0 (installed dist):

- `core/compaction/compaction.js` `createSummarizationOptions()` builds `{ maxTokens, signal, apiKey, headers, env, sessionId }` (plus reasoning). There is no `transport`.
- `core/agent-session.js` calls the default compactor with `this.agent.streamFunction` and passes no transport; `core/sdk.js` adds timeout/retry/header policy to the summary options but does not fill in the settings transport.
- `openai-codex-responses.js` then defaults the missing transport to `auto`, which is WebSocket-first. Because summaries use `cacheRetention: "none"`, there is no cache session id, so a summary also does not see the session's sticky SSE fallback after an earlier WebSocket failure.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `"transport": "sse"` in settings and use an `openai-codex` model.
2. Lower `compaction.reserveTokens` so compaction triggers early, and run until an automatic compaction happens (or run `/compact`).
3. Observe the transport per request (for example with a custom `fetch` in the SDK): ordinary requests make one HTTP call; the summary request makes none, so it used WebSocket.

Observed in our test: `ordinary request: transport=sse, HTTP calls=1` / `summary request: transport=undefined, HTTP calls=0`. Passing `transport: "sse"` explicitly to the summary request made it use SSE and it succeeded.

### Expected behavior

Summary requests use the same transport as ordinary requests (or there is a documented setting for them). This matters when users switch to SSE to avoid WebSocket errors: we saw a Sol session near 255k tokens where auto-compaction failed with "Auto-compaction cancelled / This operation was aborted / WebSocket error", and switching the setting to SSE would not have changed the path that failed.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.1.0, Node 22, Linux.

(Drafted with an AI coding agent from a bounded test against the installed source, reviewed by me.)

prs.title: Feat/tencent token plan provider
prs.body:
## feat(ai): add Tencent Hy providers (TokenHub and Token Plan)

Adds Tencent Hunyuan (Hy) as two builtin providers: `tencent-tokenhub` (pay-as-you-go) and `tencent-token-plan` (prepaid plan). Both serve the same Hy models over Chat Completions, differing only in base URL and API key — matching how models.dev lists them.

The catalog definitions are thin on purpose: `tencentHyModels()` just forwards to `modelsDevModels()`, so model ids, context windows, effort ladders, and modalities are all derived from models.dev rather than hand-maintained. Token Plan reuses TokenHub's compat object and model factory outright.

### Changes

**Catalog (`packages/ai/catalog/`)**

- `providers/tencent-tokenhub.ts` — new. Exports `TOKENHUB_BASE_URL`, the shared `TENCENT_HY_COMPLETIONS_COMPAT` (`supportsDeveloperRole: false`, `supportsStore: false`, `maxTokensField: "max_tokens"`), and `tencentHyModels()`.
- `providers/tencent-token-plan.ts` — new. Reuses TokenHub's compat and model factory against `https://api.lkeap.cloud.tencent.com/plan/v3`.
- `providers/index.ts` — both registered in `PROVIDERS`.

**Runtime (`packages/ai/src/`)**

- `providers/tencent-tokenhub.ts`, `providers/tencent-token-plan.ts` — new provider factories.
- `providers/all.ts` — both added to `builtinProviders()`.
- `types.ts` — `"tencent-tokenhub"` / `"tencent-token-plan"` added to `KnownProvider`.
- `env-api-keys.ts` — `TENCENT_TOKENHUB_API_KEY` / `TENCENT_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY`.
- `providers/*.models.ts`, `models.generated.ts` — regenerated.

**Coding agent**

- `core/model-resolver.ts` — `defaultModelPerProvider` entries (both `hy3`).
- `docs/providers.md` — both API-key rows.

**Tests**

- `test/tencent-hy-models.test.ts` — new. Registration + name/baseUrl/model-list per provider; `hy3` served over Chat Completions on both endpoints with the expected context window, reasoning flag, and compat fields; `hy3-preview`'s TokenHub-only `low`/`medium`/`high` ladder (vs. `hy3`'s off/high, since it reports `["none","high"]`); API-key resolution from each provider's own env var.

### Notes

- **Effort ladders are derived, not hardcoded.** `hy3` reports `effort: ["none","high"]` in models.dev → `{off: "none", high: "high"}`; `hy3-preview` reports `["low","medium","high"]` with no `none` → `off: null`. The test pins both so a future models.dev change surfaces here instead of silently shifting behavior.
- **Model lists differ per endpoint.** TokenHub serves `hy3` / `hy3-preview` / `hy4-preview`; Token Plan serves `hy3` / `hy4-preview`. This follows models.dev — no local filtering.
- **Anthropic-compatible paths exist but aren't wired.** Both endpoints document one alongside Chat Completions; this PR uses Chat Completions only.

### Validation

~~~bash
node_modules/.bin/vitest run packages/ai/test/tencent-hy-models.test.ts
# 4 passed
~~~

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep model selector selection when the catalog refresh lands
prs.body:
## Problem

Opening the model selector shows cached models and refreshes the catalogs in the background. When the refresh finishes, `refreshModels()` rebuilds the list and resets the selection, so anything done in the meantime is lost.

Example: the current model is `slow-a`. Open the selector, press Down twice to reach `slow-c`, and wait:

```
→   slow-c [slow]      Refreshing model catalogs…
→ ✓ slow-a [slow]      Model catalogs refreshed.
```

Pressing Enter just after the refresh lands selects the wrong model. With a search query, the selection jumps to the top row instead.

## Fix

Remember the selected model before reloading and restore it by provider and ID afterwards. This is what `ScopedModelsSelectorComponent.updateModels()` already does.

If the selected model is no longer in the list, the existing fallback applies: the current model, or the top row with a query. Typing a query still moves the selection to the top row (#7209), because only the refresh path changes.

## Testing

- Added tests to `test/model-selector.test.ts` that hold the refresh open, browse, then let it land: plain browsing, an active query, new rows shifting the selected model, and the selected model being removed. The first three fail without the fix. The fourth pins the existing fallback.
- Ran the real TUI in tmux with an extension provider whose refresh takes 6 seconds. The selection jumps back to `slow-a` on `main` and stays on `slow-c` with the fix.
- `npm run check` passes, and the `packages/coding-agent` suite passes under `./test.sh`.

closes #9109

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): edit preserves untouched bytes (line endings, encodings)
prs.body:
The edit tool rewrote bytes outside the text it was asked to replace. This PR fixes four cases.

## A. Line endings (#8544)

**Problem.** The edit tool found the first line ending in the file, normalized the whole file to LF for matching, and wrote the whole file back with that one ending.

```
a\nb\r\nX = 1\r\n   edit X = 1 -> X = 2   =>  a\nb\nX = 2\n      (both CRLF became LF)
a\rb\nX = 1\n       edit X = 1 -> X = 2   =>  a\nb\nX = 2\n      (untouched lone CR became LF)
```

**Solution.** Matching still runs on the LF-normalized text, so matching behaves as before (exact, fuzzy, multi-edit, duplicates, overlaps). Each match is then mapped back to an offset range in the original text. Normalizing only shortens CRLF, so the mapping adds the number of CRLFs before an offset, and a range that covers a normalized LF covers the whole CRLF. Only those ranges are spliced into the original text. Everything else keeps its original bytes.

Line breaks in the new text use the ending of the line where the replaced range starts: its own LF or CRLF, or the previous line's ending if the range is in an unterminated last line. A lone CR counts as a line ending only in files with no LF at all (classic Mac files). Elsewhere a lone CR is more likely a control character inside a line, so it is not used for new line breaks. Pure LF and pure CRLF files get exactly the same output as before. Fuzzy matches still rewrite the whole lines they touch, as before, and those lines get the ending of the first line in the match.

## B. Files that are not valid UTF-8 (#10349, #5797)

**Problem.** The edit tool decoded every file as UTF-8. Each invalid byte became U+FFFD and was written back as `ef bf bd`. For example, `caf\xe9\nTIMEOUT = 30\n` with the edit `TIMEOUT = 30 -> 60` turned the untouched `e9` into `ef bf bd`, and the tool still reported success. GBK, Shift-JIS and similar files broke the same way.

**Solution.** When `isUtf8` rejects the bytes, the file is decoded as Latin-1. That is one character per byte, so the decoding is lossless. Edits are applied to that text, and the result is encoded back as Latin-1, so every byte outside the replaced ranges stays the same. The original encoding is unknown, so these edits are only accepted when the tool can splice exact bytes:

- `oldText` and `newText` must be ASCII. Non-ASCII text has no known byte form in this file, so the edit is refused. The error says the file is not valid UTF-8 and that only ASCII edits are applied byte-exactly. It suggests anchoring on ASCII-only text, using bash (`iconv`, or a script that reads and writes the file in its encoding), or `write` if converting the file to UTF-8 is acceptable.
- Only exact matches are accepted. Fuzzy matching rewrites the touched lines from NFKC/whitespace-normalized text. That would change non-ASCII bytes in those lines: `trimEnd` drops 0x85 (`…` in CP-1252), and NFKC turns 0xA0 into a space, although 0xA0 can be a GBK trail byte.
- An edit may not change the byte right after a non-ASCII byte. In GBK, Shift-JIS, Big5 and GB18030, the second byte of a character can be ASCII. For example, Shift-JIS `表` is `95 5C`, and `read` shows it as `\uFFFD\`. If the edit changes that byte, it changes the preceding character. Edits that keep their first character (`\abc -> \abd`) still work.

Alternatives I considered:
- **Refuse all non-UTF-8 files** (the patch proposed in #10349). This is safe, but the most common case, an ASCII change in a Windows-1252 or GBK source file, would then always need bash.
- **Guess the encoding (chardet-style) and transcode.** Guessing is unreliable on short files, as noted in #5797. A wrong guess silently corrupts the whole file, and `read` would still show the model U+FFFD.

Splicing bytes needs no guess. It can only fail by refusing the edit, never by corrupting the file.

## C. UTF-16 with BOM

**Problem.** UTF-16 files were also decoded as UTF-8. A normal `oldText` did not match, so nothing changed. But an `oldText` copied from garbled output, including its NUL characters, did match. The tool then wrote the file as UTF-8 with the BOM turned into U+FFFD: `fffe 6800...` became `efbfbd efbfbd 6800...`.

**Solution.** A small new `tools/file-encoding.ts` checks for a BOM first. `FF FE` means UTF-16LE and `FE FF` means UTF-16BE, if the length is even. The file is decoded with `Buffer` `utf16le` (byte-swapped for BE), which keeps lone surrogates and round-trips exactly. It is written back in the same encoding with the same BOM. UTF-8 handling, with or without BOM, is unchanged: the same `toString("utf-8")` and `splitBom`, and the same `writeFile(string)` call. `read.ts` is not touched. A separate PR makes `read` decode UTF-16 by BOM.

`EditOperations.writeFile` takes a string, so it cannot write these bytes. The interface gains an optional `writeFileBytes(absolutePath, content: Buffer)`, and the default operations implement it. Custom operations without it (for example the SSH and Gondolin examples) keep working for UTF-8 files. For UTF-16 and non-UTF-8 files they now get `Could not edit file: <path>. The file is UTF-16LE|not valid UTF-8, and the configured edit operations can only write UTF-8 text. The file was left unchanged.` Before, such files were corrupted (B) or did not match (C).

## D. Out of memory after writing

**Problem.** `execute` wrote the file first and then ran `generateDiffString` and `generateUnifiedPatch`. Each of them diffs the whole file with `diffLines`. The TUI preview (`computeEditsDiff`) read, applied and diffed the whole file again. A one-line edit of a 50 MB file under `--max-old-space-size=256` crashed with `FATAL ERROR: ... JavaScript heap out of memory` after `TARGET = 2` was already on disk.

**Solution.** The diff is now built only from windows around the changes. The replacement offsets are known, so each change is widened to its lines plus a 32-line margin, and overlapping windows are merged. `structuredPatch` runs on each window, and its hunks are shifted to file line numbers. The display diff is rendered from those hunks. The patch is `formatPatch` of the hunks. The rest of the file is only scanned to count lines. The diff is computed before the file is written, so a failure leaves the file unchanged. `computeEditsDiff` uses the same code.

`generateDiffString` (public) now renders through the same hunk formatter: `structuredPatch` on the whole input. Its output is unchanged. The margin is 32 lines, not just the 4 context lines, because in runs of repeated lines `diffLines` can place a change several lines away. With only 4 lines, 1356 of about 11k random edits on files with an 8-word vocabulary produced a different but valid diff. With 32 lines there were 0 differences, even with a 3-word vocabulary.

**What the model sees:** only `Successfully replaced N block(s) in <path>.` The `diff` and `patch` in `details` go to the TUI, the session file and extensions. They are not sent to the model, so the model-visible output does not change, even for huge files.

## Behavior differences

- Mixed or lone-CR line endings, non-UTF-8 files and UTF-16 files behave as described above. Classic Mac (CR-only) files now keep CR, and new line breaks in them use CR. Before, the whole file was converted to LF.
- Files that are not valid UTF-8: whitespace-insensitive matching is off, and non-ASCII edits are refused.
- Custom `EditOperations` without `writeFileBytes` get an error for non-UTF-8 and UTF-16 files.
- In long runs of repeated lines, the display diff and patch could in theory align a change differently from a whole-file diff. Both are valid diffs of the same change, and the random comparisons below found no case.
- UTF-16 without a BOM is not detected. It is usually valid UTF-8 (ASCII plus NULs) and is handled as before.
- Not changed: matching itself still normalizes the whole file for fuzzy duplicate counting (`countOccurrences`). Large files still cost several file-sized strings before the write. A failure there leaves the file unchanged.
- `packages/durable/src/tools/edit-diff.ts` is a separate copy with the same line-ending and encoding behavior. It is not changed here.

## Testing

- `npm run check`: clean.
- `test/tools.test.ts`, `test/edit-tool-legacy-input.test.ts`, `test/edit-tool-no-full-redraw.test.ts`, `test/file-mutation-queue.test.ts`, `test/suite/regressions/8337-utf8-bom-parsing.test.ts`, `test/tool-system-prompt-contributions.test.ts`: 137 passed.
- New tests in `test/tools.test.ts` with byte-level `Buffer.equals` assertions: mixed EOL (both examples from #8544), new line breaks in a mixed file, lone CR, CR-only file, fuzzy match in a mixed file, pure CRLF with a multi-line insert, UTF-8 BOM bytes, Latin-1 and GBK ASCII edits, non-ASCII edit refused (message checked, file unchanged), fuzzy match refused, Shift-JIS trail-byte guard, custom operations with and without `writeFileBytes`, UTF-16LE (with a non-BMP character) and UTF-16BE round trips, a NUL-garbled `oldText` on UTF-16 not matching, and the preview for both encodings. Windowed diffs and patches are checked to be identical to whole-file `generateDiffString`/`generateUnifiedPatch`, including merged and separate hunks (gaps 1, 7, 8, 9, 40, 80 lines), edits at file start and end, a file without a final newline, and an edit that joins lines.
- Run against the original `edit.ts`/`edit-diff.ts`: 17 of the new tests fail. The pure CRLF and UTF-8 BOM tests pass there too, as they should, since that behavior is unchanged.
- Ad-hoc reproduction (direct `execute` calls, bytes before -> after):
  - mixed: `610a620d0a58203d20310d0a` -> before `610a620a58203d20320a`, after `610a620d0a58203d20320d0a`
  - lone CR: `610d620a58203d20310a` -> before `610a620a58203d20320a`, after `610d620a58203d20320a`
  - Latin-1: `636166e90a54494d454f5554203d2033300a` -> before `636166efbfbd0a54494d454f5554203d2036300a`, after `636166e90a54494d454f5554203d2036300a`
  - UTF-16LE NUL `oldText`: before `efbfbdefbfbd680069000a0059000a00`, after not found, file unchanged
- Ad-hoc random comparison against the original implementation: 60k random edits on generated files and on slices of real source files, with LF and CRLF, exact and fuzzy matches, 1-3 edits each. The written file, the error messages, the display diff, `firstChangedLine` and the patch were identical in every case. Every patch applies. prs.title: fix(coding-agent): stream the read tool instead of loading whole files
prs.body:
## Problem

`read` loads the whole file before it applies `offset`/`limit`: `ops.readFile` -> `toString("utf-8")` -> `split("\n")`. Asking for one line still holds the file as a Buffer, as a string and as an array of lines.

Measured on main with a 200 MB log (2.36M lines):

- `offset: 1, limit: 1`: 640 MB RSS; with `--max-old-space-size=256` it crashes in `Runtime_StringSplit` (OOM).
- 800 MB file: `Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters`.
- 2.2 GB file: `File size (2306867200) is greater than 2 GiB`.
- Aborting only rejects the promise. The read keeps going in the background (on an 800 MB file it used 506 ms more CPU after the rejection and held 923 MB).

## Solution

- New optional `ReadOperations.createReadStream(absolutePath, { signal })` that returns an `AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>`. A Node `Readable` works. The default local operations implement it with `fs.createReadStream`. No existing member changed.
- The text path decodes chunk by chunk and counts lines as it goes. It passes only the selected lines (`offset .. offset+limit`) to a new `HeadTruncator` in `truncate.ts`. `HeadTruncator` is a streaming form of `truncateHead`: it keeps only lines that can still be shown (at most 50KB) and counts the bytes and lines of the rest without storing them. So `totalLines`, `totalBytes`, `truncatedBy`, the `[Showing lines ...]`, `[N more lines ...]` and offset-beyond-end notices, and the first-line-too-long notice all come out as before. Details keep their key order. Line counts still follow `text.split("\n")`.
- Abort: the signal goes to the stream, and the loop also checks it between chunks. Leaving the loop closes the stream.
- Two cases keep today's whole-file path, now only as a fallback: custom operations without `createReadStream`, and non-integer `offset`/`limit` or a negative `limit`. Today's array slicing defines what those ranges select; for example, `limit: -1` means "all lines but the last", which would need the line count before selecting. `truncateHead` itself is unchanged, so ls/grep/find are not affected.
- Images are unchanged (`readFile`).

## Intended behavior changes

1. **UTF-16**: a file starting with `FF FE` is decoded as UTF-16LE, and one starting with `FE FF` as UTF-16BE. The byte order mark is dropped. Before, such a file showed as `��h\0e\0l\0...`; ripgrep and the grep tool already decode it. Big endian is decoded by swapping the bytes into the UTF-16LE decoder, so it does not depend on ICU's `utf-16be`. Files without a byte order mark are UTF-8 as before. A UTF-8 byte order mark stays in the text as U+FEFF, as `Buffer.toString` keeps it (`TextDecoder` with `ignoreBOM: true`). Both the streaming path and the `readFile` path use this decoding.
2. **Fractional offset with a line over 50KB**: before, `Buffer.byteLength(allLines[1.5])` threw a TypeError. Now the notice reports the size of the first selected line.

Out of scope: #7329, the trailing-newline off-by-one in line counts (`"a\n"` counts as 2 lines). This PR keeps today's counts so that notices do not change.

## Testing

- `test/read-streaming.test.ts` (new) has a copy of the old text algorithm as the reference. For each case it compares the reference with the streaming path (chunks of 1, 3, 7 and 4096 bytes) and with the `readFile` fallback: text, details and error message. The cases: empty file, no trailing newline, trailing newline, only newlines, CRLF, lone CR, multi-byte characters, UTF-8 BOM, 2000/2001 lines with and without a trailing newline, first line at 50KB and at 50KB + 1 (ASCII and multi-byte), exactly 50KB, 50KB + a trailing newline (truncated, but `truncatedBy: "lines"`), 50KB + an empty line, long lines after short ones, over 50KB in lines. Each case runs with offsets and limits around 0, 1, 2, the line count and 2000. The test also covers characters split at every chunk boundary, invalid UTF-8 against `Buffer.toString`, fractional and negative ranges, UTF-16LE/BE with split surrogate pairs and a dangling odd byte, abort (the stream is closed and no more chunks are pulled), `HeadTruncator` against `truncateHead` for every split point and for 2000 random contents, and local files through the default stream, including EISDIR. With the original `read.ts`, 8 of the 13 tests fail. Mutating `HeadTruncator` or the line selection makes the matrix fail.
- `test/tools.test.ts`, `read-line-range-display`, `tool-execution-component`, `block-images`, `image-resize-callers` and `tool-system-prompt-contributions` pass. `npm run check` is clean.

Before/after, measured with ad-hoc scripts. The process baseline after loading modules is about 119 MB RSS.

| Case | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 MB, offset 1, limit 1 | 934 ms, 640 MB RSS | 537 ms, 130 MB RSS |
| 200 MB, offset 2000000, limit 10 | 1042 ms, 639 MB RSS | 510 ms, 131 MB RSS |
| 200 MB, no offset/limit (count all lines) | 1401 ms, 1007 MB RSS | 539 ms, 131 MB RSS |
| 200 MB, offset 1 limit 1, 256 MB heap | OOM crash | 129 MB RSS |
| 800 MB, offset 1, limit 1 | string length error | 1.7 s, 130 MB RSS |
| 2.2 GB (one line), offset 1, limit 1 | ERR_FS_FILE_TOO_LARGE | 4.9 s, 129 MB RSS, line size notice |
| abort after 100 ms, CPU in the next 3 s | 506 ms | 1 ms |

A 1 MB `highWaterMark` was about 12% faster but doubled the memory, so the stream keeps the default 64 KB chunks.

Remaining difference: custom operations that only implement `readFile` keep the whole-file memory use, and their reads continue after an abort, as before.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): do not split surrogate pairs when truncating text
prs.body:
Several places truncate text by UTF-16 code units with `slice()`. When the cut lands between the two halves of a surrogate pair (an emoji or other character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane), the result keeps a lone high or low surrogate. That is invalid UTF-16.

Example: a grep match line with 499 ASCII characters followed by `😀` is cut at 500 units, so the output ends in `\uD83D... [truncated]`.

The bundled providers strip lone surrogates before sending (`sanitizeSurrogates` in pi-ai), so the usual effect is a dropped character. But the broken text still reaches the session file, RPC and JSON clients (strict UTF-8 encoders such as Rust's serde_json reject lone surrogates), extensions, and custom providers.

This adds `sliceHead(text, n)` and `sliceTail(text, n)` to `core/tools/truncate.ts`. They behave like `slice(0, n)` and `slice(-n)` but return one unit fewer when the cut would split a pair, and are used where truncated text reaches the model:
- `truncateLine` (grep match lines), the case reported in #7121
- codemode `truncateOutput` head and tail, and its argument and error previews
- compaction `truncateForSummary` (tool results sent to the summarizer)
- MCP server summaries in the system prompt and stderr tails in connection errors

The cost is two `charCodeAt` checks per truncation, and nothing on the untruncated path.

The surrogate check follows the fix in #7122 by @IKEASven69, which @cristinaponcela reviewed in a follow-up branch. That PR was closed before merging.

Not changed: TUI-only previews (renderers, visual truncation) and line-based slicing. pi-private's pi-durable codemode `output.ts` has the same head/tail slicing and needs a separate change there.

**Testing**
- New `test/truncate-surrogates.test.ts`: an emoji at the cut in `truncateLine` is dropped whole, an emoji ending exactly at the limit is kept, `sliceHead`/`sliceTail` never leave a lone surrogate for any length, and they match `slice` on text without surrogates.
- `test/tools.test.ts`, compaction, MCP extension, and codemode tests pass.
- `npm run check` passes.

fixes #7121

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): find and ls limit edge cases
prs.body:
Three limit problems in the find and ls tools.

**1. `limit: 0` and other values below 1.** find passed `limit` to fd unchanged. fd treats `--max-results 0` as no limit, so `find({ pattern: "*", limit: 0 })` returned every match, followed by `[0 results limit reached. Use limit=0 for more, or refine pattern]`. ls with `limit: 0` listed nothing and printed `(empty directory)`. A fractional limit such as `1.5` printed `1.5 results limit reached. Use limit=3`.

Fix: both tools use `Math.max(1, Math.floor(limit ?? DEFAULT_LIMIT))`. grep already clamps to at least 1. The fd path and the custom `glob` path share this value.

**2. Notice at exactly N results (#7121).** With 3 matching files and `limit: 3`, fd returned 3 results. find checked `results >= limit` and printed `[3 results limit reached. Use limit=6 for more, or refine pattern]`, even though there were no more files.

Fix: find asks fd for `limit + 1` results, shows the first `limit`, and prints the notice only when the extra result exists. ls already worked this way. Custom `FindOperations.glob` now also gets `limit + 1`. The tool shows at most `limit` of the returned results and prints the notice only when more were returned. The interface is unchanged. This follows closed PR #7122 without its unrelated changes.

**3. Results past the 50KB cap.** find kept every fd line in memory. `truncateHead` then dropped everything past 50KB. find now handles each line as it arrives. It keeps lines up to the first one past the cap and only counts the rest, as grep does in #11705. Because that first line past the cap is kept, `truncateHead` makes the same truncation decision as before. `details.truncation.totalLines` and `totalBytes` come from the counts, so the notices and `details` are unchanged.

Behavior differences:
- A custom `glob` that ignores `options.limit` and returns more results used to have all of them shown. Now the tool shows the first `limit` results with the limit notice.
- Custom `glob` implementations get `limit + 1` instead of `limit`.
- In the fd path, output made only of blank lines with exit code 0 now gives `No files found matching pattern` instead of empty text. fd does not produce such output.

**Testing**
- New tests in `test/tools.test.ts`:
  - find: exactly N matches gives no notice, and N+1 matches give the notice with N lines (#7121). Fails on main.
  - find: `limit` 0, -5, 0.5 and 1.9 each show 1 result with the `1 results` notice. Fails on main.
  - find with custom `glob`: the operation gets `limit + 1`, and exact and over-limit results give the right output. Fails on main.
  - find past the byte cap: 300 names of 200 bytes each. `details.truncation` equals `truncateHead` of the full output, except for `content`. Passes on main too; it guards the counting. It fails if the `totalLines` override is removed.
  - ls: `limit` 0, -5, 0.5 and 1.9 each list 1 entry with the notice. Fails on main.
  - ls: exactly N entries gives no notice. Passes on main too; it guards the existing behavior.
- `test/tools.test.ts` and the find regression suites 3302, 3303 and 6104 pass (110 tests). `npm run check` passes.

fixes #7121
