releases.name: Release v0.26.7
releases.body:
<!-- qwen-release-notes:v1 -->

## Highlights

_See the complete change list below._

## Breaking Changes

No known breaking changes.

## Complete Change List

### Features

- Adds an operator-scoped model.catalogRefresh setting and lets privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled: false stop background catalog refreshes while local metadata remains available. ([#16066](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16066)) by @yiliang114
- feat(managed-agent): support full model configuration at session creation ([#16153](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16153)) by @doudouOUC
- When experimental.unifiedAgentLoop is enabled, ACP Goal turns run on the shared agent loop with shared rounds, tool batches, and stop points. ([#16131](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16131)) by @qqqys
- Adds a Channel events page to Web Shell with a filterable, auto-refreshing timeline of Channel activity, skip reasons, replies, task transitions, and poll results. ([#16106](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16106)) by @wenshao
- Adds a local /verify-pr Docker recipe that runs untrusted PR code in a container while keeping model credentials on the host through a chat-completion proxy. ([#16077](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16077)) by @wenshao
- Runs Mods prompt.submit hooks in the Ink terminal before typed prompts are processed, allowing hooks to see composer text with pasted content expanded. ([#16180](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16180)) by @qqqys
- Adds a managed Web Shell host entry, improves managed empty-state layout, and consolidates session-failure and unconfirmed-submission notices above the composer. ([#15928](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15928)) by @yiliang114
- Adds Settings → Connections → Allow remote connections to qwen serve, enabling remote access, token use, and client disconnects without restarting. ([#15887](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15887)) by @yiliang114
- With experimental.unifiedAgentLoop enabled, ACP cron and background-notification turns now use the shared agent loop for consistent rounds, tool batching, and stopping. ([#16190](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16190)) by @qqqys
- Workspace uploads can now proceed concurrently while still rejecting occupied destinations and preserving directory occupancy protections. ([#16212](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16212)) by @doudouOUC
- GitHub events for bound PRs now go to the associated session as untrusted prompts, and replies stay private unless published. ([#16117](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16117)) by @wenshao
- Web Shell channel editor can now edit GitHub repository access, mention behavior, and notification polling settings instead of requiring manual settings changes. ([#16149](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16149)) by @wenshao

### Bug Fixes

- Pins the RHEL 10 EPEL bootstrap RPM and makes desktop smoke teardown treat Linux zombie processes as stopped while still reporting live daemon failures. ([#16154](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16154)) by @yiliang114
- Compacts live ACP tool-result displays for session replay, so large file edit results show a saved-session preview instead of full old and new contents. ([#16172](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16172)) by @wenshao
- Fixes PR review endpoint routing by selecting the cohort before the model and reports the final bucket, cohort, model, and endpoint hostname. ([#16151](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16151)) by @yiliang114
- fix(serve): keep record_artifact guidance out of Managed Runtime worker results ([#16148](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16148)) by @wenshao
- Binds web-shell config synchronization to the current attachment so config writes made by the first prompt are no longer silently discarded. ([#16170](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16170)) by @wenshao
- Fixes tool-choice failures on Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1, and Mythos 5.1 by avoiding unsupported forced tool selection. ([#15558](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15558)) by @Adkid-Zephyr
- Fixes Web Shell pasting so a single copied image with an HTTP(S) URL attaches the image, while unavailable file pastes show a warning. ([#16179](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16179)) by @ytahdn
- Requires explicit folder trust before repository-supplied hooks, permission grants, and project language servers can run, improving safety for untrusted projects. ([#16182](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16182)) by @yiliang114
- Anthropic-compatible requests now honor the configured transport timeout and dispatcher, preventing premature request aborts when a longer API timeout is set. ([#16193](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16193)) by @yiliang114

issues.title: main does not compile: PersistRequest::ClearCheckpoint is now dead, and every PR's required checks fail on it
issues.body:
### What happened

`main` does not compile under the workspace's own lint policy. Every pull request's **required** checks now fail on the same error, so no external contribution can merge:

```
error: variant `ClearCheckpoint` is never constructed
  --> crates/tui/src/tui/persistence_actor.rs:80:5
```

Affected required checks on codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7147: `Lint` (→ `Run clippy`), `Test (windows-latest)`, `npm wrapper smoke (ubuntu-latest)`. `Test (ubuntu-latest)` fails at `Build canonical executable for acceptance tests` and `MSRV check (1.89)` at `cargo +1.89 check`, same error.

The cause is a dead variant, not anything in the PRs: `PersistRequest::ClearCheckpoint` lost its last non-test constructor, every remaining construction sits inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (line 843 onwards), and `[workspace.lints.rust] warnings = "deny"` plus `RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` turn that into a hard error.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
git fetch origin main
git checkout 6a08f0312      # current origin/main
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked
# error: variant `ClearCheckpoint` is never constructed

git checkout c4a4f42e9      # its parent
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked
# Finished — compiles
```

So the breakage is exactly one commit wide.

### Which commit

`6a08f0312 fix(session): retain recovery when reset snapshot fails [skip ci]`

It rewrote `persist_full_reset_snapshot` in `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/session_state.rs`; the replaced branch was the only production call site:

```diff
-    if let Some(session_id) = app.current_session_id.clone() {
-        persistence_actor::persist(PersistRequest::ClearCheckpoint { session_id });
-    }
+    let session = match session {
+        Ok(session) => session,
+        Err(err) => { /* ...add_message(Error)... */ return; }
+    };
```

That removal is intentional by the commit's own description ("retain recovery when reset snapshot fails" — the old branch cleared the checkpoint precisely when the replacement could not be built). What was missed is that the variant, its `PersistRequest` dispatch arms (lines 430/572/648), and its queue-coalescing paths are now unreachable from production code, and only the test module still names it.

### Why CI did not catch it

`ci.yml` triggers on `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` only — a push to `main` runs no build or test workflow at all (that is by design; CONTRIBUTING says the exhaustive gate runs once at release time via `gh workflow run ci.yml --expected_sha=…`). The commit also carries `[skip ci]`, which CONTRIBUTING explicitly forbids — but on a `main` push it is not what let this through, since nothing was scheduled either way.

The net effect is a window where `main` was red for its own lint gate and nobody could see it: the mirror/harvest workflows ran, the next PR did not.

### Suggested fix

One of:

1. **Delete the now-unused variant** — `ClearCheckpoint`, its `PersistRequest` match arms, its `PendingQueue`/`pending` handling, and its tests. Cleanest if the reset path genuinely never needs it again.
2. **Keep it with a stated reason** — `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]` on the variant plus a comment saying which future caller owns it. Cheap, but leaves a variant nobody constructs.
3. **Keep it and give it back its caller** — if clearing a stale checkpoint on a failed reset is still wanted (the removed comment argued it was: "Never let an older in-flight checkpoint resurrect the session the user just discarded"), reinstate the call instead of deleting the variant, which would also restore that behaviour.

I lean to (1) or (3) depending on which behaviour is correct; (2) only as a stop-gap to unblock the queue.

### For the process question

Two separate gaps, worth deciding on together:

* **The required checks are right, the invariant is not enforced where it broke.** `protect-main` already requires `Lint`, `Test (windows-latest)` and `npm wrapper smoke (ubuntu-latest)`, and the ruleset's `bypass_actors` is empty — yet `6a08f0312` and its four siblings landed as direct pushes with no PR and no CI. Whatever grants that (repository-admin role, or an org-level setting the ruleset does not expose) is what needs to change if direct pushes are meant to stay verified.
* **Nothing verifies** `main` **between releases.** With no `push` trigger, the only whole-workspace check is the manual pre-release dispatch. A cheap guard would be a `push: branches: [main]` job running just `cargo check`/`clippy` on the touched crates, or a scheduled run of the existing `Lint` job — minutes, and it would have caught this within the hour.

Cheap and durable: run the `Lint` job (or a `cargo check --workspace`) on every push to `main`, and require it alongside the PR checks. The release gate can stay as the exhaustive one.

### Environment

`main` at `6a08f0312`, macOS 26 (arm64), Rust per `rust-toolchain`. Reported while preparing codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7147.

Source verification for GitHub #7148. Commit 7198de9003 removed the dead persistence request and test-only route wrappers. Aboysky independently checked b92540d88 with RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo check -p codewhale-tui --lib and reported a clean result on the issue. Separate dependency PRs still show required checks for their own revisions. Keep release closure distinct from this verified source repair.

issues.title: auth chatgpt: 'ChatGPT token signature or identity claims failed verification' after successful browser sign-in (0.10.2, Windows)

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
## Summary
`codewhale auth chatgpt` completes the browser sign-in, but then fails with:

```
error: ChatGPT token signature or identity claims failed verification
```

`codewhale auth status --provider openai-codex` afterwards still reports `active source: missing`.

## Environment
- CodeWhale 0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf), installed via `npm i -g codewhale` (latest on npm)
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, Git Bash, Node via nvm4w
- No proxy / custom CA env vars

## Steps
1. `codewhale auth chatgpt`
2. Sign in on auth.openai.com in the browser (callback to `http://127.0.0.1:1455/auth/callback`)
3. Terminal prints the error above; no grant is stored.

## Checks already done
- Clock skew vs auth.openai.com is ~15 s
- `https://auth.openai.com/.well-known/jwks.json` and `openid-configuration` are reachable (HTTP 200)
- The error string appears to cover several failure paths in the binary (unknown/invalid verification key, audience mismatch with the registration, missing `chatgpt_account_id`/subject), so it is unclear which one is hit.

## Request
Please make the error say which check failed (signature / audience / identity claim), or document the account/plan requirements for `auth chatgpt`.

## Developer fast loop

The whole point of this decomposition: once a sub-EPIC's crate exists (EPIC-006 Feature 3 and later), day-to-day development happens **entirely outside the TUI monolith** (\~700k lines). The TUI is only compiled when you explicitly need it — TUI integration tests, `cargo test --workspace`, or the final pre-PR validation.

```bash
cargo check -p codewhale-commands          # production change check — seconds, not minutes
cargo test -p codewhale-commands           # test loop — compiles only the commands crate + thin test binaries, never the TUI
cargo watch -x "check -p codewhale-commands"  # continuous check while editing (cargo-watch)
cargo nextest run -p codewhale-commands    # optional: parallel test runner, faster startup
```

Why this stays fast:

* `cargo build` / `cargo check` never compiles `#[cfg(test)]` code, so production iteration is bounded to the small crate.
* `cargo test` compiles each `tests/` file as its **own small binary crate** depending only on the public API — a production change recompiles/relinks only those thin binaries, in parallel.
* The Gherkin acceptance harnesses live in separate test binaries (or a dedicated acceptance crate), so thousands of acceptance-test lines are **never part of the production crate compile**.
* Small white-box unit tests that need private access stay inline — they are cheap and cannot live outside the crate.

**Acceptance criterion for every extracted crate:** `cargo test -p <crate>` must compile only that crate and its test binaries — if it pulls in `codewhale-tui`, the boundary was cut wrong.

The numbers and impact motivating this are documented in [#4991](<https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4991>) (Discussion: Compilation times and the TUI crate monolith): 476k lines / 82% of the workspace in one crate, 8–16 min release builds, 30+ min test suite, 2–3 iterations per hour.

issues.title: [Feature-Req] opt-in incremental, cache-stable context fold for long sessions.

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body: > This feature request article is manually drafted by me and rewritten by Deepseek for more-organized content textflow and more-authentic English. ### Before you start - [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. Related work I found: #6540 / #6544 (compaction summary cache miss), #6541 (cost-based compaction trigger, closed as not planned), #6969 (prompt-cache economics), #6721 (emergency compaction), #6504 (sub-agent compaction). None proposes the incremental fold layout; #6541 is the closest, but it changes when compaction fires, not how the replacement history is laid out. ### What problem does this solve? Long coding sessions on 1M-token routes hit a late, one-shot compaction: at ~80% of the window, Codewhale summarizes the older span (including previous checkpoints) and rewrites the prefix. That is a good overflow guardrail, but it has three structural costs: - the model runs at a very large context before anything happens; - replacing the prefix invalidates provider prefix-cache reuse for the next request; - re-summarizing prior checkpoints makes early detail decay, and tool-heavy history is reduced to one summary plus a short tail. #6540 / #6544 fixed a specific summary-cache bug (reasoning tier), and #6541 proposed an earlier cost-based trigger; #6541 was closed as not planned. The replacement layout itself is unchanged, so the cache/retention problem remains for long sessions. ### What should Codewhale do? Add an **opt-in** `fold` strategy inspired by [billion-context](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context): - trigger at ~45% of the effective window **and** after ~50K tokens of new growth; keep the existing 80% path as the emergency fallback; - keep a stable prefix (system/tools + existing summary blocks), append one new summary block for the consumed increment, and keep a recent verbatim workspace (~50K, all message types); compress only the consumed increment and never rewrite earlier blocks; - reuse the existing summarizer, archive, and survival contract in the first slice; add block IDs/provenance and reuse `context_archive_search` / `context_archive_get`; - add `[compaction] strategy = "legacy" | "fold"` (default `legacy`), with `fold_trigger_percent`, `fold_growth_tokens`, `recent_workspace_tokens`, and `summary_block_budget`; - add the matching audit fields and a 100+ turn long-session fixture; compare billed input, cache hit, p95 latency, recall probes, and survival-contract tests. Non-goals: no default behavior change; no proxy; no provider API change; no new required dependency; no wholesale port of billion-context; no weakening of the survival contract. Acceptance: fold is opt-in and legacy stays untouched; survival-contract, tool-pair, anchor, and current-user-instruction tests pass; measurable reduction in billed input and cache-miss tokens with no recall regression; failed folds preserve history; docs explain the knobs. This is a safety-critical engine change. I'd rather you or a core contributor own the Rust implementation than review a drive-by PR from someone unfamiliar with the engine. I can provide the detailed spec, fixture matrix, benchmark harness, and long-session testing. Detailed background, current behavior, prior art, and open questions are in the first comment below. ### Where? TUI (terminal interface); CLI command (codewhale exec, ...); Providers and models. ### Workarounds or other tools (optional) Today I can lower `auto_compact_threshold_percent` (more frequent one-shot rewrites, worse cache), raise `retained_user_message_tokens` (more verbatim user text, less compression), or run `/compact ` manually. An external billion-context proxy is possible but adds a process and cannot change Codewhale's engine-side checkpoint/archive semantics. #6541 proposed an earlier cost-based trigger; it was closed as not planned, and it does not address the fold layout. ### Contributing - [ ] I would like to open a pull request for this. I'd rather the maintainers own the engine change; I can help with the spec, fixture matrix, benchmark harness, and long-session testing.

prs.title: feat(bridges): accept media and voice messages on the WeCom bridge
prs.body:
## Problem

The bridge rejects every non-text frame with `目前仅支持文本消息`. For a phone user that is the most natural interaction being unavailable: send the photo/video/file you want the agent to work on. Voice messages (which WeCom transcribes) are equally dropped.

Two extra defects while wiring this up:

- Media frames carry **no text**, and `stripGroupPrefix` returns `accepted: false` for empty text — media would be dropped **silently** if routed through it.
- Download links in media frames are valid for **~5 minutes**, so the download must start immediately and failures must tell the user to re-send.

## Change

- `video` / `file` / `image` frames: reply "downloading…", fetch via `client.downloadFile(url, aeskey)`, save under a configurable directory (`WECOM_MEDIA_DIR`, default `<workspace>/media`) with a sanitized filename, reply with the saved name, size and path. Failures name the 5-minute expiry.
- `voice` frames: the transcribed `voice.content` is used as the prompt text.
- Other message types get an explicit polite answer instead of the blanket refusal.
- `sanitizeFilename()` in `src/lib.mjs` with unit tests (path separators, control chars, leading dots, length cap, fallback).

Verified live: a 100 MB-class video and photos sent from the phone land in the media directory and the follow-up instruction can reference them. WeCom media caps (video 10 MB for sending back, links expire ~5 min) are documented in the PR for reviewers.

No-Issue: live defects found while running the WeCom bridge against a real bot; each fix carries its error evidence and tests

prs.title: feat(bridges): steer a running WeCom turn instead of dropping the message
prs.body:
## Problem

While a turn is running, `runPrompt` answers with the busy notice and **discards the message content**. On a phone this is the worst possible moment to lose input: the user watches a long turn, remembers something ("also skip the intro", "switch camera B"), sends it — and it is gone.

## Change

When `activeTurnBlock` reports a running turn, forward the text to the Runtime's documented steer endpoint (`POST /v1/threads/{id}/turns/{turn_id}/steer`, body `{prompt}`), reply `[running] forwarded to the active turn: …`, and keep the busy notice as fallback when the steer is rejected (turn already moved on, etc.).

## Notes

- The steer endpoint and its delivery semantics (queued / delivered / dropped verdicts) are documented in `docs/RUNTIME_API.md`.
- Verified live: mid-turn phone messages now reach the model and steer the run; the fallback path still answers the busy notice when steering fails.

No-Issue: live defects found while running the WeCom bridge against a real bot; each fix carries its error evidence and tests

prs.title: fix(bridges): rotate WeCom stream replies before the 10-minute expiry
prs.body:
## Problem

WeCom stream messages stop accepting updates after ~10 minutes:

```
{ errcode: 846608, errmsg: 'stream message update expired (>10 minutes), cannot update' }
```

`streamTurnEvents` keeps one `streamId` for the whole turn. A turn that runs longer (a report pipeline, a multi-step agent task) fails its next `replyStream`, the error surfaces as `Failed to handle WeCom message`, and the user never receives the final result even though the turn completed.

## Change

- `createStreamReply(client, frame, {rotateMs, now, genId})` in `wecom-bridge/src/lib.mjs`: finalizes the current stream ("…(continued)") and opens a fresh one when it is older than `rotateMs` (default 8 min), and reopens once when an update is rejected. Clock and id generation are injectable for tests.
- `streamTurnEvents` routes its three `replyStream` call sites through the helper.
- Unit tests for rotation and for the reopen-on-rejection path.

Verified live: a 12-minute turn now delivers its result as two messages instead of failing after minute 10.

No-Issue: live defects found while running the WeCom bridge against a real bot; each fix carries its error evidence and tests

prs.title: fix(bridges): cap WeCom reply chunks by UTF-8 bytes
prs.body:
## Problem

WeCom caps a single message at **4096 UTF-8 bytes**. `splitMessage` counts characters, so a Chinese reply of 3500 chars (~10.5 KB) was sent as one chunk and WeCom delivered it **silently truncated** — no error to the bridge, no log, the user just receives cut-off text. Observed live with a 10 KB Chinese report rendered in three different ways on the phone vs. on disk.

## Change

- `bridge-core` `splitMessage(text, maxChars, maxBytes = 0)`: when `maxBytes > 0`, any chunk whose UTF-8 size exceeds it is re-split on code-point boundaries (never mid-character). Opt-in; all existing callers keep current behavior.
- `wecom-bridge` `replyText` passes `config.maxReplyBytes` (default 3800, ~8% headroom; env `WECOM_MAX_REPLY_BYTES`).
- Tests: CJK text over the byte cap splits into byte-bounded chunks that reassemble to the original; short/mixed stays single; cap stays opt-in.

Verified live: a ~10 KB report now arrives complete in multiple messages.

No-Issue: live defects found while running the WeCom bridge against a real bot; each fix carries its error evidence and tests

prs.title: fix(bridges): surface WeCom API error details in bridge replies
prs.body:
## Problem

When the WeCom SDK rejects a call it throws a plain object, e.g.

```
{ errcode: 846608, errmsg: 'stream message update expired (>10 minutes), cannot update' }
```

The bridge's error formatter did `String(error?.message || error)`, which renders an object as `[object Object]`. Phone users get a reply like `Failed to handle WeCom message: [object Object]` with no actionable reason, and the log line loses the errcode too.

## Change

- Add a pure `formatPublicError()` in `wecom-bridge/src/lib.mjs`: renders `{errcode, errmsg}` objects as `errcode=<n>: <msg>`, falls back to `error.message`, then to a bounded `JSON.stringify`.
- `publicBridgeError()` in `src/index.mjs` now uses it (token redaction unchanged).
- Unit tests for the object, Error, string and undefined shapes.

Verified against a live rejection (errcode 846608) during a long-running turn.

No-Issue: live defects found while running the WeCom bridge against a real bot; each fix carries its error evidence and tests

prs.title: fix(engine): report file_search results from the workspace root
prs.body:
## What and why

`file_search` with a `path` returns matches relative to that path, while `read` and the other tools resolve from the workspace. So a search that's scoped correctly hands back a path that means a different file. In a repo with `package.json` at the root and in `packages/app`, `{"query":"package.json","path":"packages/app"}`:

Before:

```
[{"path":"package.json","name":"package.json","score":1.0}]
```

Reading that path gives `{"name":"root"}`, with no error. The file it found holds `{"name":"app"}`.

After:

```
[{"path":"packages/app/package.json","name":"package.json","score":1.0}]
```

The other shapes went wrong too: a `path` naming one file returned `""`, and `{"query":"**/*.json","path":"packages"}` returned `app/package.json`, which doesn't exist. They now return `packages/app/package.json`.

The reported path is now built the way `grep_files` builds its own: strip the workspace or its canonical form, and leave anything outside it absolute. Ranking and exclusions still use the path relative to the search root, so what matches doesn't change. A search with no `path` returns what it did. I didn't run a search outside the workspace; going by the code, that returns absolute paths where it used to return ones relative to the search root.

## Issue

No-Issue: file_search paths are relative to its path argument, so reading a result can open a different file; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at f4978e8fa in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server that scripts the tool calls, and read the tool results it received; the results above come from those runs. The cases were `packages/app`, `./packages/../packages/app`, the absolute path, a single file, a glob under `packages`, and no `path`. The server scripted the `read` too, so a real model picking that path is my inference.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-engine --lib`, twice with this change and once on f4978e8fa: 91 tests fail on `main`, all of them here too, and 41 `file_search` and `tools::search` tests pass. One more fails here both times, `auto_review_force_prompt_is_denied_without_opening_a_modal`: run alone with this change it failed 2 of 5, and it's in the failures on #7205, which only touches the TUI. In the second round `lifecycle_bulk_followup_preserves_mappings_and_retries_without_duplicate_workers` hung and I ended it after 69 minutes; it passed in 2.6 s in the first round.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-engine`: clean. `cargo clippy --no-deps -p codewhale-engine` with CI's flags on 1.99 reports errors in 13 files, none of them `file_search.rs`.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on f4978e8fa; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(workspace): stop a home workspace from refusing its own junctioned state directory
prs.body:
## What and why

A session started in the user's home directory treats that directory as its
workspace, and four call sites then hold it to workspace confinement. That is
wrong on its own 鈥?home is not a repository 鈥?but it breaks outright for the
supported layout where `~/.codewhale` is a directory junction onto another
volume (on Windows, `mklink /J C:\Users\<user>\.codewhale D:\CodeWhaleData`).
The junction reads as a link escaping the workspace, so the state directory is
refused as a whole:

- **skills**: 60 of 90 skills silently disappeared, leaving only `~/.agents`,
  with one warning (`Refusing symlinked path C:\Users\<user>\.codewhale`).
- **fleet roster**: every profile under `~/.codewhale/agents` was skipped.
- **subagent coordination**: the shared ledger never appended
  (`state path must not traverse symlinks`).
- **workflow journal**: `workflow-runs.jsonl` could be neither read nor written.

This follows the same class of failure as #6947, #6949 and #7098 鈥?a
user-owned relocated root treated as if it were untrusted repository content.
Those three already fixed the session, artifact and sub-agent state paths; the
four entry points here were never converted.

`workspace_is_user_home` and `workspace_state_path` put that decision in one
place. The root a link walk starts from is the whole question, because
`reject_linked_path` never examines the root itself:

- A **home** workspace resolves its own `~/.codewhale` once and uses the target
  as the root. The junction is where the user chose to keep state, and
  everything below it is still walked.
- **Every other** workspace keeps itself as the root with `.codewhale` still
  inside the walked path, so a repository-supplied link is refused exactly as
  it was before. Lowering the root instead would have made
  `<repo>/.codewhale` transparent 鈥?readable profiles with their `trust` and
  `permissions` fields, a journal writing outside the repository, and a lock
  creating directories through the link.

A state directory that exists but cannot be resolved falls back to the strict
root, so an unreachable junction fails closed rather than starting a second
state tree beside the one that cannot be reached.

The skills exemption is per directory rather than per workspace: only the home
state directory skips confinement, so links under any other home directory are
still refused and still warn.

## Issue

No-Issue: repairs state-path resolution for a home workspace; related junction reports are already closed.

## How I tested it

Reported honestly as it stands. CI owns fmt, clippy, the Linux suite and the
Windows build on the final base; the runs below were made on this branch before
it was carried onto current `main`, so the counts are what they were there, not
a claim about the merge commit.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` 鈫?passed.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-util` 鈫?**41 passed; 0 failed**.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-skills` 鈫?**174 passed; 0 failed**.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib -- tools::workflow::journal fleet::profile`
  鈫?**41 passed; 0 failed**, including
  `journal_never_writes_through_a_linked_codewhale_dir`, which is the test that
  pins the non-home refusal.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib -- subagent::tests::` 鈫?**590 passed;
  6 failed**. Those six fail identically on the base commit with this change
  stashed: four leak the real home skills into a tempdir workspace, and
  `agent_claim_expands_the_callers_write_scope` overflows the default Windows
  test stack. Not addressed here.
- Behaviour probe on Windows with junctions on both sides, through
  `reject_linked_path`:

  ```text
  non-home workspace: root=...\repo          refused=true  (Refusing symlinked path ...\repo\.codewhale)
  home workspace:     root=\\?\...\outside   refused=false
  ```

  A release build of the skills discovery probe with `C:\Users\asus` as the
  workspace reported **90 skills** where the same probe reported **30** and
  logged `Refusing symlinked path C:\Users\asus\.codewhale` before the change.

This was reviewed against its first version, which had the root lowering
described above and was rejected for it; the commit messages record what was
wrong and what replaced it.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

On the second box: the existing tests cover the non-home path this keeps
(`journal_never_writes_through_a_linked_codewhale_dir` and the skills workspace
link tests both still pass). The home branch 鈥?resolve `~/.codewhale`, use the
target as the root 鈥?has no test yet, because it needs a home override and a
link that a tempdir test can only build on Unix. Say the word and I will add
one on this branch.

No new user-facing command, flag, provider or feature: this repairs how
existing state paths resolve, so no `docs/features.toml` row applies.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep the draft when the command palette inserts a command
prs.body:
## What and why

Picking a command that takes an argument from the palette, such as `/rename`, replaces the composer with `/rename `, and whatever you'd typed is gone. History search can't find it either, because nothing stashed it. With `my draft` typed, then Ctrl+K, `rename`, Enter, Alt+R and `my`:

Before:

```
╭History search ──────
│my
│  No matches
```

After:

```
╭History search ──────
│my
│ ▸ my draft
```

The hotbar does the same insert in `prefill_composer` and calls `clear_input_recoverable` first. The palette's `InsertText` arm now does too.

Stashing goes through `clear_input`, which releases the command claim, so the insert now claims the line when its text starts with `/`. Without that, a typed `/xyz` replaced by `/rename` and then pasted past 16,000 characters goes to the model as prose instead of being held. An empty composer already did that on `main`; it holds now too. Palette entries that insert a bare name stay unclaimed.

## Issue

No-Issue: inserting a command from the palette loses the composer draft; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at b157e004b in a pseudo-terminal at 100x34 with an empty HOME and the steps above; the rows above come from those runs. The composer shows `/rename ` on both. The hold above came from pasting 17,600 characters after the insert and pressing Enter: over a typed `/xyz`, `main` holds it, and over an empty composer `main` sends it, while this change holds both and the mock server gets no chat request. I didn't run the bare-name entries.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 5903 of 5913 passed, with the 339 tests whose names match `palette`, `composer`, `hotbar` or `draft` among them. The same ten tests fail on `main` at b157e004b without this change: `golden_turn_events_match`, `model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens`, `continue_recovers_legacy_checkpoint_without_removing_it`, `auto_dispatch_keeps_last_and_pending_receipts_aligned`, `composer_send_anchors_new_message_at_tail`, `dispatch_user_message_surfaces_continued_message_submit_stderr`, `dispatch_user_message_surfaces_continued_message_submit_timeout`, `renamed_title_survives_next_in_memory_automatic_snapshot`, `reserved_dispatch_normal_engine_counts_requests_and_accepts_next_turn` and `fleet_row_repaints_resolved_model_and_each_distinct_usage_total`.

prs.title: fix(runtime): remove the isolated test state root at process exit
prs.body:
## What and why

Every test run leaves thousands of directories in the system temp dir. `isolated_test_state_root` keeps its directory in a static `OnceLock`, so `Drop` never runs, and nextest gives every test its own process, so each process that touches the root leaves one behind. On a machine that runs the suite often this adds up: I found about 286,000 of them after six days.

The whole workspace, once, on macOS, counting what's new in the temp dir afterwards:

```
                                  main     this change
new entries                       4404     362
codewhale-tui-test-state-*        4017     3
codewhale-test-audit-*            28       0
```

The root now registers an `atexit` hook when it's created. libtest reports a failed test by calling `exit`, so the hook runs on failures too. Staged plugin trees are non-writable on unix, so a failed removal makes the directories writable and tries again. The unsealed audit log moves into the root so it goes with it.

Two existing tests had to change. The engine's `unguarded_state_writes_use_isolated_test_root` checked for its files after the child process had exited; the child checks them now, and the parent checks that the root is gone. `unsealed_state_resolvers_stay_inside_the_isolated_root` and the audit test compared the log's path with `temp_dir()`, which fails on macOS now that it's under the canonicalized root (`/private/var` against `/var`), so they check for the root instead.

What this doesn't fix:

- Tests that call `temp_dir()` themselves still leave their directories. That's most of the 362.
- An abort or a kill skips the hook.
- Three roots survived the run above, each from one process. They hold `snapshots`, `sessions` and similar, so my guess is a background thread wrote after the hook ran, but I didn't trace them.
- I haven't run this on Windows. `atexit` is declared directly because `libc` is only a unix dependency of this crate.

I also looked at setting `TMPDIR` in `scripts/with-hermetic-test-home.sh`, which would catch everything in one place. That script wraps cargo too, and a sccache server started under it would outlive the directory. I didn't test that, so it may be worth a second look.

## Issue

No-Issue: test runs leave thousands of directories in the system temp dir; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- `cargo nextest run --workspace` through `scripts/with-hermetic-test-home.sh`, on this change and on `main` at c2d78581b, with the default `TMPDIR`; the counts above come from those runs. 18987 of 19025 passed here and 18988 on `main`. No test failed only on `main`.
- One test failed only here: `child_work_cancellation_wins_once` (`Running` where it expects `Cancelled`). It also fails without this change on 7ec9fdddb and 8225f75b1, and passed on c2d78581b, so it flips on its own. `session_close_withdraws_old_children_requests` flips too: it failed here in a lib-only run and passed on `main` in another, and run alone 40 times it fails 40 times on both.
- A throwaway test, not included, re-executed the test binary with a read-only directory in the root, once exiting cleanly and once through a failed assertion. Nothing was left either way.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `cargo clippy -p codewhale-runtime -p codewhale-engine --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags (also on 1.99): clean. `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-runtime -p codewhale-engine`: clean. `scripts/check-blocking-calls-budget.py` fails on `main` too, on `crates/app-server-protocol/src/bin/export.rs`.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on c2d78581b; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): keep escaped characters and named delimiters in math
prs.body:
## What and why

Math in a reply loses characters. The escape arm in `render_latex_to_string` consumes `\{`, `\}`, `\$`, `\%`, `\#`, `\&` and `\_` and prints nothing, so a percentage or a set comes out wrong with nothing to show for it. And `\left`, `\right` and `\big` take the next character as the delimiter even when it's a backslash. This reply, at 90 columns:

```
Set: $\{x \mid x > 0\}$ and $A = \{1, 2, 3\}$.

Percent: $50\%$ and $x = 3\%$.

Money: $\$5 + \$10$ and hash $\#1$.

Name: $a\_b$ and $x \& y$.

Spaced: $\left \langle x \right \rangle$ and $\left ( x \right )$.

Unspaced: $\left\langle x \right\rangle$ and $\left\{ x \right\}$ and $\left( x \right)$.

Big: $\bigl \langle x \bigr \rangle$ and $\bigl\{ x \bigr\}$ and $\big( x \big)$.
```

Before:

```
● Set: x | x > 0 and A = 1, 2, 3.
▏ Percent: 50 and x = 3.
▏ Money: 5 + 10 and hash 1.
▏ Name: ab and x y.
▏ Spaced: \langle x \rangle and ( x ).
▏ Unspaced: \langle x \rangle and \ x \ and ( x ).
▏ Big: \langle x \rangle and \ x \ and ( x ).
```

After:

```
● Set: {x | x > 0} and A = {1, 2, 3}.
▏ Percent: 50% and x = 3%.
▏ Money: $5 + $10 and hash #1.
▏ Name: a_b and x & y.
▏ Spaced: ⟨ x ⟩ and ( x ).
▏ Unspaced: ⟨ x ⟩ and { x } and ( x ).
▏ Big: ⟨ x ⟩ and { x } and ( x ).
```

The escape arm now prints the character. The delimiter arms leave a backslash for the main loop, which already knows `\langle` and `\{`.

The `Spaced` row with `\langle` is a regression from #7198, which Codex pointed out there: fixing the offset made the arm eat only the backslash, so the bracket that used to show as `\⟨` was lost. It's fixed here along with the unspaced form, which never worked.

`\lfloor` and `\lceil` aren't in the symbol table, so they still print as written, and `\left\|` still prints one bar rather than `‖`. Neither is touched here.

## Issue

No-Issue: math in replies drops escaped characters and named delimiters; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at acc47fbca in a pseudo-terminal at 90x30 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above; the rows above come from those runs, split across two replies. Before #7196 landed, on 1290995ac, 50x30 wrapped the same text with the same difference. The same replies also covered `\ `, `\text{}`, `\sum`, `\frac`, `\left.`, `\left|` and `\left[`, which render the same on both.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 6579 of 6587 passed, with 574 tests whose names match `latex`, `math`, `markdown`, `transcript`, `message` or `history` among them. The same eight tests fail on `main` at c2d78581b without this change: `golden_turn_events_match`, `model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens`, `session_save_without_an_id_keeps_the_conversation_that_owns_the_snapshots`, `continue_recovers_legacy_checkpoint_without_removing_it`, `dispatch_user_message_surfaces_continued_message_submit_stderr`, `dispatch_user_message_surfaces_continued_message_submit_timeout`, `offline_queue_lifecycle_preserves_edits_and_explicit_reset` and `renamed_title_survives_next_in_memory_automatic_snapshot`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` here: clean. `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` on 1290995ac, before I rebased over #7196: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on acc47fbca; it merges cleanly into current `main`

prs.title: feat: source navigation echoes and guarded fork-prefix inheritance
prs.body:
Index-free source-navigation echoes, bounded source reads and guarded fork-prefix inheritance on the existing Engine. Original contributor commits and credit are preserved; there is no replacement turn loop or indexing daemon.

**Current head:** [`7a491a9f`](https://github.com/AdityaVG13/CodeWhale/commit/7a491a9f17474af5239eb6fb47addad4b2aa794f), incorporating upstream main [`acc47fbca`](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/acc47fbcab3ea5906614aef77d15e95b7c7ddfff). The previous PR head remains an ancestor: this is a history-preserving update, not a force-push. The generated guide was rebuilt from the merged documentation rather than choosing a stale generated side.

## Implemented slice

- Revision-qualified Rust function/method references carry a path, source window and revision. Stale references are refused; guarded paging requires forward progress and retains snapshot identity.
- Focused Rust grep results can supply bounded enclosing-function references and small complete bodies. Broad/truncated searches retain their ordinary output. This is syntax evidence, not macro expansion or name/type resolution.
- Native `grep_files` is eager beside file-name search. Child/scout/workflow fixtures follow the current catalog; root goal mutation remains unavailable to children while goal inspection stays discoverable.
- Source echoes remain append-only tool/history evidence, not volatile additions to the pinned system/tool prefix. Host observations, current access authority and evidence actually delivered to a model remain separate.
- Fork-prefix inheritance remains gated by matching route/model/opaque receipt and supported dialect; unsupported or changed identities take the cold path.
- The skill index keeps eligible names enumerable without exposing mutable native skill paths. Workflow events retain task/workspace ownership.
- The native read budget now survives the final Chat Completions projection for execution-matched canonical reads. Ordinary unbudgeted, mismatched and oversized results retain the wire backstop; a source-looking footer is not authority. See [`3c31b672a`](https://github.com/AdityaVG13/CodeWhale/commit/3c31b672a).
- Finite headless turns receive a logged working-deadline notice while tools remain available. An exhausted ordinary turn can deliver its final text report without falsely becoming successful; cancellation and the distinct goal-pause contract remain intact. The existing feature row and configuration documentation are updated.

## Current verification

On the final merged source, **55 selected `codewhale-engine` library tests passed: 0 failed, 0 ignored**, using remote RCH. This is a one-package diagnostic, not a DSR repository-level gate. Selection covers native-read wire projection, stream decoding, deadline/admission/report-only fences, catalog deferral and the goal-pause contract.

The **four original subagent regressions also passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**, replayed directly from that same compiled engine test executable: BM25/regex delegation discovery, independent bounded activation caches, depth-cap catalog preservation, and child goal-control discovery. These are separate from the 55-test selection, not four additional compilations. The fixtures retain cache-budget and root-goal mutation boundaries rather than restoring forbidden child tools.

The selected Cargo payload was:

```sh
RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test --locked -p codewhale-engine --lib -- \
  admission_gates:: client::chat::stream_decoder_tests:: \
  model_tool_catalog_applies_native_and_mcp_deferral \
  capability_compact_surface_defers_nonessential_core_tools \
  capability_full_surface_preserves_small_default_head \
  goal_turn_uses_goal_step_allowance_and_pauses_budget_limit_after_final_report \
  --test-threads=1
```

`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, the staged diff whitespace check, and the website facts check pass. Nine owned source/documentation paths were read back from the worker after testing and matched local bytes. This does not claim a pristine pre-compile transfer of every repository file.

The earlier TUI-checkpoint receipts are historical, not substituted for current engine verification. Full web documentation validation remains blocked locally by missing `marked`; it is not recorded as passing. No full workspace suite, full web build, native macOS/Windows acceptance or packaged-release qualification is claimed.

## Still draft: task qualification remains blocked

This stays draft in accordance with [the contributor's scope decision](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6207193232). Earlier failed and incomplete comparisons remain in [the maintained progress record](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6185897898) and [the previous findings](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6524708140); they are not replaced or pooled into a success claim.

The latest paid follow-up repaired the task but remained unqualified after an incomplete final provider stream. No treatment followed that failed control. A fresh integrated screen was then blocked **offline, before paid forwarding**: current native startup creates v3 coordinator state outside the frozen fixture's v1 startup boundary. The source-bound Linux executable exercised at the preceding integration checkpoint is not claimed as a packaged build of this final merged head.

The frozen write-boundary rule remains unchanged. A compatible, explicitly versioned startup fixture must be approved and re-admitted before fresh controls; both controls must qualify before treatment. No current-PR speedup, cost reduction, task-quality improvement, live-provider cache saving or independent quality review is claimed. Wider composition/impact-navigation work and release acceptance are not implied.

issues.title: [Bug]: Empty tool result is sent as "(no output)" live but replayed as "[empty content omitted]", so history changes between turns

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

    When a tool returns an empty string (for example, `read` on an empty file), the same tool result reaches the model with **different text in different requests**:

    - **Live request (same turn, tool continuation):** the tool result is sent as `(no output)`.
    - **Next turn (history rebuilt from the transcript):** the same tool result is sent as `[empty content omitted]`.

    Two different code paths each fill in their own placeholder for empty content. So a message the model has already seen gets rewritten after it is stored. This has two effects:

    1. **Prompt cache break.** The bytes of an already-cached history message change. Provider prefix caching (Anthropic `cache_control`, OpenAI prompt caching, local prefix caches)
    misses from that message onward. Every empty tool result in a session causes at least one extra full cache write.
    2. **Inconsistent model-visible history.** The model reasoned about `(no output)` when it made its decision. On later turns its own history shows something else (`[empty content
    omitted]`), and that wording reads like the framework hid or dropped something rather than "the tool returned nothing".

### Steps to reproduce

    1. Create an empty file in the agent workspace: `echo ' ' > the_file.txt` (file with one space)
    2. Ask the agent: "Read the_file.txt and tell me what it says."
    3. The agent calls `read({"path": "the_file.txt"})`, which returns an empty string (one space).
    4. Send any follow-up message in the same session so the history is rebuilt from the transcript.
    5. Compare the model request input of the tool-continuation call in step 3 with the request in step 4 (for example, via request/cacheTrace diagnostics).

### Expected behavior

The model should get exactly the same content for a given tool result on every request, whether it is the live tool continuation or a later replay of the transcript. Empty tool output should use one consistent, honest placeholder, and it should not change after the message has been seen and cached.

### Actual behavior

changed from`(no output)` to `[empty content omitted]`

issues.title: [Bug]: 2026.10.10 accepts session-targeted agent-turn automations that can never run when the session uses a CLI-login runtime
issues.body:
**Version:** 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), Linux x64, npm install.

## Summary
Since 2026.10.10, a new agent-turn automation records a stored inference account when it's created. If the job targets an existing session (`sessionTarget: "current"` or `"session:<key>"`) whose runtime is a CLI login (here `claude-cli`), creation succeeds, but every run fails within a second:

> Automation candidate is incompatible with its recorded inference account and route. The selected runtime uses a CLI login, which cannot replace this job's stored account. Select a model compatible with the recorded account, or explicitly select a stored account with openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model <provider/model>@<profileId> using a host-managed runtime.

One-shot jobs are then disabled. The only feedback is a scheduler repair request, so a reminder the user relied on silently never happens.

## Setup
- The agent's default model is `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`. The only stored auth profile is an OpenAI OAuth profile.
- The target session has a model override of `claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5`, a CLI login with no stored profile.
- `agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow` includes `anthropic/*` and `openai/*`, not `claude-cli/*`.

## Reproduction (all on 2026.10.10)
1. From the claude-cli session, call `automations add` with `sessionTarget: "session:agent:main:main"` and `payload: {kind: "agentTurn", message: "Reply NO_REPLY"}`, with no model. It is accepted.
2. `automations run <id> --force` fails with the error above. Same result with `sessionTarget: "current"`.
3. Creating with `payload.model: "claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5"` is rejected: "Automation requires a stored inference account or a key in provider config."
4. Updating the job to `claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5` afterwards is accepted, but the run fails: rejected by `agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow`.
5. Updating it to `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` afterwards fails with the same "incompatible" error. The anthropic provider resolves to the CLI runtime, and the recorded OpenAI account is kept.
6. Control: `sessionTarget: "isolated"` with `payload.model: "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5"` at creation works. Isolated with no model works on OpenAI.
7. Jobs created before the upgrade (no recorded account) still run in the same session.

## Expected
One of the following:
- At creation, a session-targeted job takes on the target session's runtime authority. The docs say "an explicit update from an authorized native creator can adopt its runtime authority", but the creator here is the native claude-cli session, and neither creating nor updating the job adopts it.
- Or creation fails with a clear error, rather than accepting a job that can never run.

## Impact
Every reminder or follow-up that an agent on a CLI-login runtime schedules for its own conversation fails. The workaround is isolated jobs, which lose the conversation context.

## Related
#178811 (run automations as children of the creating conversation), #192009 (cross-provider cron fallback accounts).

issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators pass an explicit vocabulary to Scribe v2 through the bundled ElevenLabs batch transcription provider using the existing `providerOptions.elevenlabs` configuration.

### Problem to solve

When transcribing recordings containing product names or specialized terms, an operator may want to supply a specific list of recognition hints. A [LiveKit developer requested this integration control](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408) on February 27, 2026, and supplied an implementation for that product. This is an external demand signal; applying the task to OpenClaw's recorded-audio workflow is an inference, not a report that this person uses OpenClaw.

OpenClaw already transcribes audio through Scribe v2. Its [current ElevenLabs implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts) reads only `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from provider options. A configured `keyterms` array reaches the provider request context but never enters the multipart request. The [provider documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/docs/providers/elevenlabs.md#provider-options) explicitly limits support to those three fields.

The missing capability is selecting the terms used by Scribe's recognition-bias mechanism within this native transcription path. This does not promise correct spelling for every recording or a general improvement in accuracy.

### Proposed solution

Support one additional, opt-in provider option, `keyterms: string[]`, for `scribe_v2` batch transcription. Reuse current provider-scoped configuration and merge precedence; no new top-level configuration or tool is needed. For example:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "media": {
      "models": [{
        "provider": "elevenlabs",
        "model": "scribe_v2",
        "capabilities": ["audio"]
      }],
      "audio": {
        "enabled": true,
        "providerOptions": {
          "elevenlabs": {
            "keyterms": ["OpenClaw", "Acme Research", "PostgreSQL"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Serialize the list as repeated multipart `keyterms` fields, following the provider's array contract and [official SDK request construction](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/f5d53e09e35717523435cee238ac5cc7f51966fb/src/elevenlabs/speech_to_text/raw_client.py#L177). Preserve each term's spelling and Unicode content; do not comma-join the list or encode it as one JSON string. Keep all option fields before the original file, preserving its filename, MIME type, and bytes; the shared multipart builder documents this ordering for streaming parsers. Keep array assembly provider-local rather than widening the shared scalar helper. A model-entry list replaces the audio-default list, as existing options already do. An empty list clears inherited terms; an absent or empty effective list sends no keyterms.

Keep this an explicit allowlisted addition. Preserve dedicated fields, existing scalar options, authentication, guarded HTTP transport, cancellation, and the synchronous transcript-text result. Reject an incompatible option shape or unsupported model rather than silently applying a different control. Surface provider validation errors through the existing error/fallback handling without truncating terms silently.

Document the option and its extra provider charge before users choose it. The [current API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert) currently permits up to 1,000 terms, requires each term to have fewer than 50 characters and at most five normalized words, and specifies disallowed characters. It adds a 20% surcharge; more than 100 terms also impose a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds per request. The provider remains authoritative for validation and future billing changes. No vocabulary is inferred from conversation history or sent by default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Explicit transcription prompt:** OpenClaw already forwards a configured prompt as context. It may help some tasks, but the current ElevenLabs API reference does not specify it as equivalent to structured `keyterms`. Preserve existing prompt behavior; this proposal does not claim it is useless.
- **Deepgram:** OpenClaw supports repeatable Deepgram keyterms after [#176781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176781). Switching providers is valid. This proposal retains the selected ElevenLabs account and model.
- **Official ElevenLabs skill or SDK, a CLI transcription model, or a custom provider plugin:** These can perform vocabulary-guided transcription outside the bundled adapter. The [official skill reference](https://github.com/elevenlabs/skills/blob/9a1a4b7fbb6ca02fbdc7f44f2271e6c829d0f421/speech-to-text/references/transcription-options.md) includes keyterms. These are real alternatives; native support avoids maintaining a separate transcription script or provider registration for one additional input.
- **Correct text afterward:** This can repair known spelling errors but does not give the recognizer a selected term list. An uncertain correction can also change meaning.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Operators using bundled ElevenLabs transcription for recorded audio with specialized vocabulary. The affected OpenClaw population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: The requested recognition control is unavailable in that adapter; ordinary transcription remains usable. No production outage or measured urgency is established.
- Frequency: A configured list would apply to matching transcription requests. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: Operators must accept transcription without that control, correct text, switch providers, or maintain another integration. Time savings and accuracy gains have not been measured. Enabling keyterms can increase provider charges.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original integration request and follow-up](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408); [LiveKit implementation #4967](https://github.com/livekit/agents/pull/4967). These concern the same author and task, not two independent users.
- [Official keyterm guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/speech-to-text/batch/keyterm-prompting) describes vocabulary biasing and distinguishes batch and realtime inputs.
- [Current options schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/config/zod-schema.core.ts#L627), [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts#L86), and [registered provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts#L22) establish the input path and missing mapping.
- [#177975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177975) already implemented three scalar options. This request adds a vocabulary input; it does not reopen that repaired bug or propose unrestricted forwarding.

Verification was static against the pinned main revision. No installed Gateway, live ElevenLabs transcription, or recognition-quality comparison was run for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The implementation owner is `extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts`; its former standalone media-understanding module was consolidated into registration. Suggested work is provider-local array serialization and validation, focused registered-provider coverage, and documentation. Public `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` already accepts string arrays. A new SDK contract, provider manager, dictionary store, or model-facing tool is unnecessary.

Preserve the existing media authorization, HTTP guards, and cancellation behavior applicable to the caller at dispatch; this option does not introduce a new universal execution context. A vocabulary does not authorize a transcription request. Keep terms out of diagnostic logs; they may contain names absent from the audio. No retention or permission change is requested.

Non-goals: Realtime/Voice Call/Google Meet transcription, TTS pronunciation dictionaries, vocabulary management, speaker-label output, asynchronous webhooks, redaction, multichannel results, unrestricted form overrides, or guaranteed accuracy. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- With an isolated configuration selecting `elevenlabs/scribe_v2`, native recorded-audio transcription sends two configured terms as separate multipart fields alongside one unchanged audio file, and returns the transcript through the existing path.
- Capture the actual HTTP body from the shipped transcription entry point, not only a helper call. Verify model-entry replacement of defaults, an empty list clearing defaults, and unchanged requests without a list.
- Existing scalar `false` values and dedicated model/language/prompt fields retain their behavior. Other providers do not receive the ElevenLabs vocabulary; unsupported response-changing keys remain excluded.
- An incompatible scalar value or unsupported model does not silently send an unconditioned Scribe request. Provider-side term rejection surfaces without truncation. With an actual cancellation-capable execution context, cancellation before dispatch prevents a request.
- In an authorized live check, submit a synthetic name-bearing recording with a valid small vocabulary and confirm provider acceptance and native transcript return. Recognition output is observational evidence, not a promise that every supplied term appears.
