issues.body:
## Summary

Show Z.AI / GLM account balance (pay-as-you-go) and Coding Plan quota windows in `openclaw status --usage`, `/status`, and the Control UI Usage page.

## Problem to solve

Prepaid Z.AI accounts fail closed with no advance signal. When the cash balance reaches zero, chat completion requests start returning HTTP 429 with business code 1113 ("account in arrears, please top up"), and the agent stops mid-task. OpenClaw currently gives the operator no way to see the remaining balance before that happens.

The generic provider-usage framework already exists (#100494), but the Z.AI provider does not contribute any usage or billing snapshot:

- `openclaw status --usage` prints a balance line for DeepSeek and a plan-status line for MiniMax, and prints nothing at all for the configured `zai` provider.
- `/status` and the Control UI Usage page therefore show only transcript-derived token and cost estimates. An estimate of what OpenClaw billed is not the same as the provider-reported prepaid balance, and cannot answer "how much money is left".
- `extensions/zai` contains no usage/billing module, so there is no provider-owned fetcher for either the pay-as-you-go balance or the Coding Plan quota.

Z.AI exposes two different billing surfaces, and users need both distinguished:

- Pay-as-you-go API keys on the general endpoints (`https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4`, `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4`) are billed against a prepaid cash balance, with resource packs and granted credit consumed first.
- Coding Plan keys on the coding endpoints (`https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`, `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/coding/paas/v4`) are billed against plan quota windows (5-hour and weekly), and exhausting plan quota does not fall back to the cash balance.

Reporting one as the other would be actively misleading.

## Proposed solution

Add a provider-owned usage hook to `extensions/zai` that returns a structured snapshot, following the existing provider-usage contract:

- **Pay-as-you-go:** cash balance, granted/credit balance, currency, and any active resource-pack totals, each labeled with the source endpoint region.
- **Coding Plan:** plan name, per-window quota with normalized `X% left`, and reset times.
- **Unsupported or unknown key type:** return an explicit unavailable state for that surface rather than guessing a number or failing the whole usage read.
- Keep credential selection, endpoint choice, and response parsing inside the Z.AI plugin, and reuse the existing 60-second provider-usage cache.
- If a surface cannot be determined for a given key, render the provider summary text instead of a fabricated percentage, consistent with current behavior for providers without resettable quota windows.

Secondary, only if it falls out of the same data cheaply: surface a low-balance state (for example, balance below a configured threshold) so the operator sees it in the usage footer instead of discovering exhaustion through a failed request.

## Alternatives considered

- Compute remaining balance locally as "top-up minus OpenClaw estimated cost". This drifts immediately on shared accounts, granted credit, discounts, resource packs, and other applications using the same key, and produces confident wrong numbers. It should not be presented as an account balance.
- Scrape the BigModel/Z.ai console with browser cookies. This needs a logged-in desktop session, breaks on UI changes, and cannot follow the approved credential contract for provider usage. Out of scope.
- Show only provider text summaries without structured fields. Workable as a fallback, but it prevents consistent balance and quota rendering across providers and cannot support a low-balance state.
- Ask users to check the vendor console manually. That is the status quo, and it is exactly what fails when a task is already running.

## Impact

- Affected: operators using Z.AI / GLM through the bundled `zai` provider, especially prepaid pay-as-you-go accounts with modest balances.
- Severity: blocks workflow. Balance exhaustion interrupts an in-progress agent run and every subsequent request until the operator tops up.
- Frequency: every time the balance runs out; with small top-ups this recurs regularly.
- Consequence: failed turns, lost work in progress, manual console checks, and an unexplained "provider suddenly stopped working" failure that looks like a model or network fault rather than a billing state.

## Evidence/examples

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.10.7, Windows, `zai` provider configured with a general (pay-as-you-go) endpoint.

`openclaw status --usage` output from that host, with unrelated session details omitted:

```
Usage:
  DeepSeek
    Balance ¥24.77
    Balance: ¥24.77
  MiniMax: no active token plan subscription
```

The Z.AI provider is active in this install but contributes no line. DeepSeek shows a balance; Z.AI shows nothing. This is a coverage gap in the Z.AI provider hook, not a missing framework.

Repository state confirming the gap:

- `extensions/zai/` has no usage or billing module.
- The Z.AI provider docs describe endpoint selection and rate-limit behavior (codes 1302, 1305) but no balance or quota surface.
- Failure mode is `429` with business code `1113`; Coding Plan expiry is `1309`.

Prior art in the same framework: #100494 (closed as completed) established provider-owned usage fetchers and structured billing normalization.

## Additional information

Constraint: only ship this against a documented, stable vendor endpoint. If Z.AI has no public balance API for pay-as-you-go accounts, please say so in this issue so the request can be closed as vendor-blocked rather than left open as an assumed capability. A provider-specific "unsupported" result is preferable to deriving a number from local estimates.

Related but different surfaces: #91575 and #181246 cover pre-request budget guards and balance alerting. This issue is limited to exposing provider-reported balance and quota, which those features would need as an input.

No credentials, account identifiers, or balances from the reporting installation are included above.

issues.title: [Feature]: Search and send native Zalo stickers through the existing zalouser channel

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
### Summary

Support native sticker search and sending in the official Zalo Personal plugin using the existing `sticker-search` and `sticker` message actions.

### Problem to solve

An OpenClaw extension author built a [patch for `@openclaw/zalouser`](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/README.md) so group replies could include a native Zalo sticker selected by an emotion keyword. The [implementation](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/mentions.js) locates and rewrites the installed plugin's generated JavaScript, then calls `getStickers`, `getStickersDetail`, and `sendSticker` on its existing client. This is a concrete use case for sending a platform sticker object from an OpenClaw group conversation; an image attachment or emoji is a different output.

At [OpenClaw main `82c8ad576b31`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/channel.ts), the plugin exposes only `react` as an additional shared message action. Its separate [`zalouser` tool](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/tool.ts) accepts text, image, link, directory, profile, and status operations, with no sticker operation. Users of the official channel cannot perform this task through its supported actions.

The patch is historical, with its latest commit dated June 8, 2026. The same author's current [Setup project](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-setup/blob/0f12991d9787c1d3cf331b8b9ba1a256df2d559f/README.md) says the old integration and Sticker add-on were retired in favor of a maintained alternative channel. That is a valid solution. This request concerns supporting the same native object in the existing official channel, without maintaining a private patch or adopting another channel runtime. Current demand to migrate back to the official channel is unknown.

### Proposed solution

Extend the existing `zalouser` channel action adapter; add no new core action, tool, SDK surface, credential store, or channel.

- `sticker-search`: for the selected account and an authorized group conversation, accept a bounded keyword query and return a bounded set of native sticker choices. Each choice must include a send-compatible selector carrying the native sticker ID, category ID, and type. Reuse the existing `query`, `limit`, and `stickerId`/`fileId` fields where appropriate. Exact selector encoding is a plugin implementation decision.
- `sticker`: send exactly one selected native sticker to that group using the same account/profile and existing target resolution and action authorization. Return the platform message ID and normal channel delivery result. Reject malformed selectors and unsupported targets before sending.
- Reuse the current plugin's API/session owner and cancellation/effect-boundary handling. Include the native `/api/group/sticker` POST in its dispatch tracking. Stop before submission if the admitted operation is canceled or no longer current. An ambiguous network outcome must not trigger a blind resend or a claim of confirmed delivery.

Initial scope is explicit group sticker search and send. Suggested search budget: default 5, maximum 10 choices; these are proposed resource bounds, not Zalo API limits. No automatic interpretation of `[Sticker: ...]` in ordinary text, automatic emotional replies, mention changes, sticker uploads, whole-catalog collection, or DM support is requested.

### Alternatives considered

- **Alternative channel:** [OpenClaw Zalo Connect](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-zalo-connect/blob/0e5908c6ccc00cde6f539a82fd82086fc90285de/README.md) already advertises native stickers and many other actions. It is a valid option. The remaining proposed benefit is for installations retaining the official `zalouser` channel and its current account/session owner; no claim is made that all OpenClaw users are blocked.
- **Patch the generated plugin:** the cited implementation targets generated `zalo-js-*.js` files. It expresses the exact missing behavior, but does not establish compatibility with current main. We have not executed it.
- **Skill or separate tool:** a skill can call supported tools, but cannot obtain this missing behavior from the official tool's closed action enum. A separate code plugin could own another Zalo connection or use an alternative channel's bridge; the official channel's client implementation is private. This does not establish a missing generic SDK contract.
- **Send an image, emoji, or reaction:** these remain useful existing outputs but do not send a native sticker object.

### Impact

- Affected: users who retain the official Zalo Personal channel and want native sticker replies in groups. A historical plugin patch demonstrates the task; the current affected population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: this particular output is unavailable through the official channel; text, media, and reactions remain usable. No urgent incident or quantitative severity has been established.
- Frequency: unknown. Keyword-based group replies are described by the source; no usage frequency has been measured.
- Practical consequences: the documented approaches are patching generated plugin code or using a different channel. No time savings, user counts, or account-migration failure rates are claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original task and patch](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/README.md), plus [native lookup/send implementation](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/mentions.js), commit `6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2`. This is implementation evidence, not an independently observed live send.
- [Current channel action adapter](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/channel.ts) and [optional tool schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/tool.ts). A pinned scan of the plugin's non-test TypeScript, JSON, and Markdown found no sticker implementation.
- The plugin already pins [`zca-js` 2.2.0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/package.json). That package's published Git revision `dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9` contains [`getStickers`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/getStickers.ts), [`getStickersDetail`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/getStickersDetail.ts), and [`sendSticker`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/sendSticker.ts). The last accepts `id`, `cateId`, and `type`, supports group targets, and returns `msgId`.
- [Shared action vocabulary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts) and [schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/src/agents/tools/message-tool-schema.ts) already contain sticker search/send concepts. This is an adapter gap, not a new common contract.
- PRs [#27905](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/27905) and [#29075](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/29075) concern `zalo` Bot API inbound handling and emoji replies; neither supplies `zalouser` native sticker sending. Both are closed and unmerged at the research time.

Research is static. No dependency installation, external patch execution, paid service, account login, or authenticated Zalo delivery was performed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Implementation entry points are the plugin's `channel.ts` action descriptor/handler, its lazy `channel.runtime.ts` exports, the private `zca-client.ts` API typing, and the existing `zalo-js.ts` API/session owner. The existing [`send-context.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/send-context.ts) checks cancellation and current effect authority; its message dispatch path matcher currently excludes `/sticker`. Reuse that owner and [`send-receipt.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/send-receipt.ts) rather than introducing a second sender. These are implementation suggestions, not a claim that the change has been built.

Preserve plugin lazy loading, existing account isolation, target and access policies, credential ownership, and current delivery outcome semantics. No configuration migration, new persistent catalog, new authorization scope, or dependency upgrade is proposed. Search can return fewer choices when detail lookup is partial; it must not claim catalog completeness. The existing unofficial Zalo integration and its account/platform limitations continue to apply. No implementer has committed. Selector encoding and the exact bounded search defaults remain owner decisions.

Acceptance criteria:

1. In an authorized group conversation on a configured `zalouser` account, search a keyword, choose one returned selector, and send it through the shared message tool. Zalo displays one native sticker in that group and the tool reports its platform message ID.
2. The selected account/profile is used for lookup and send. Another configured account is not silently selected; malformed selectors and unsupported non-group targets do not issue a sticker POST.
3. Cancellation or retirement during lookup/session preparation prevents a later send. A recorded accepted send retains its ID; an uncertain outcome is not reported as confirmed or blindly retried.
4. Empty/partially unavailable search results are bounded and explicit. Existing text/media/react paths continue to work, and ordinary text containing `[Sticker: ...]` does not acquire a new side effect.

An implementer should run focused action, routing, send-context, and receipt tests, then the affected plugin checks and startup profiler. A real authorized Zalo group is needed to verify native rendering and actual transport outcomes; mocked API responses alone cannot establish that acceptance criterion.

issues.body:
Stopping a scheduled turn through its session controller can leave the cron caller signal live. The session-event owner flattens the controller cancellation to an error string; cron then records an ordinary failure, increments its failure streak, and can launch an unwanted repair or failure alert.

Carry the canonical terminal outcome from the actual turn/controller owner through the session-event receipt. Classify cancellation, restart, and supersession with the existing cron interruption policy while preserving genuine watchdog stalls and deadline timeouts. Verify Stop through normal sessions.abort RPC and real scheduler settlement, with only inference synthetic.

The associated restart guidance should also explain retained child sessions: children are not independently resumed, and a stopped execution is not a yielded pause. Existing workspace and publication ownership must remain intact.

issues.body:
## Summary

When the Control UI is opened at a name under `.localhost` (for example `http://openclaw.localhost:18789`, which major
browsers resolve to this machine), the Portals page shows **Remote portal ingress required** for a direct portal on
`127.0.0.1`, although the browser is on the Gateway host and the portal opens from **Open in new tab**.

## Version

2026.10.10-beta.5; unchanged on `release/2026.10.10` (134ba9c7) and on main (dce5fd66).

## Problem

`isLoopbackHostname` (ui/src/lib/gateway-locality.ts:1-7, identical in 2026.10.10-beta.5, on `release/2026.10.10` and on
main) accepts `localhost`, `::1`, `[::1]` and `127.0.0.0/8`, but no name under `.localhost`. RFC 6761, section 6.3,
reserves `localhost` and every name under it for loopback, and browsers treat such origins as secure contexts. The
runtime's own server-side check already agrees: `isExplicitLoopbackHostname` counts `hostname.endsWith(".localhost")`
(src/infra/net/ssrf.ts:395-402 on main).

The Portals page reads the Gateway at `ws://openclaw.localhost:18789` as remote and a loopback portal as unreachable
from this browser:

- on main, `ensurePortalProbe` in ui/src/pages/portals/portals-state.ts:362-367 sets `status: "ingress-required"`;
- in 2026.10.10-beta.5, `portalNeedsRemoteIngress` (ui/src/pages/portals/portal-url.ts:16-21), called from
  ui/src/pages/portals/portals-controller.ts:314; built as `vp` in dist/control-ui/assets/control-ui-core-P4iKKKP0.js and
  `Se` in dist/control-ui/assets/portals-page-335hxqpm.js.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run a gateway bound to loopback and open the Control UI at `http://openclaw.localhost:18789/portals`.
2. Ask an agent to open a portal for a dev server on this machine.
3. The page shows "Remote portal ingress required" instead of offering the portal in a new tab.

## Expected

The page offers the portal in a new tab (its `new-tab-required` state), as it does when the Control UI is opened at
`127.0.0.1` or `localhost`.

## Proposed fix

One function; its other readers (ui/src/api/gateway-connect-errors.ts:48 and
ui/src/components/board/board-widget-frame.tsx:53 on main) move toward the same truth:

```ts
export function isLoopbackHostname(hostname: string): boolean {
  const host = hostname.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/\.$/, "");
  return (
    host === "localhost" ||
    host.endsWith(".localhost") ||
    ["::1", "[::1]"].includes(host) ||
    (/^127(?:\.\d{1,3}){3}$/.test(host) && host.split(".").every((octet) => Number(octet) <= 255))
  );
}
```

with cases beside the existing ones: `isLoopbackHostname("openclaw.localhost")` and `isLoopbackHostname("a.b.localhost")`
are true; `isLoopbackHostname("localhost.example.com")` stays false.

## Why it matters

A `.localhost` name is the usual way to give a local Control UI its own origin (a local reverse proxy, a desktop shell, a
second gateway on the same machine). On such an origin every loopback portal is reported as needing remote ingress, and
the page's advice (Tailscale Serve, a wildcard HTTPS proxy) sends the operator to configure infrastructure that is not
needed.

Happy to open a PR with the change and its test if that helps.

issues.body:
## Problem

The Gateway can become ready under a 1 GiB memory limit and then run out of memory before its first real model response.

The current ARM64 Linux reproduction uses Node 24.22.1, one CPU, no swap, a 1 GiB outer cgroup, a 768 MiB service cgroup, and V8 limits of 256 MiB old space / 4 MiB semi-space. The service reached its 768 MiB limit after readiness; the cgroup recorded an OOM kill before the model response or soak completed.

## Acceptance

- Preserve normal model discovery and credential authority.
- Pass the unchanged 1 GiB profile: readiness, a real OpenAI response with the expected marker, 60 seconds of soak, peak memory at most 928 MiB, and no OOM events.
- Only after that passes, evaluate the separate 512 MiB profile.

Related: #160501, #191272, #192363.

Cold catalog preparation currently retains the full configuration validation import graph. A proposed follow-up removes those imports while preserving public constructor identity and default configuration capture. A matched local prototype reduced retained worker heap by 5.45 MiB (6.58%); this is not a Linux peak-memory or 1 GiB acceptance result.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

issues.body:
## Summary

After an involuntary Gateway process death, background agent preparation failed with `SQLite session reclamation commit checkpoint expired`. The affected agent then permanently refused `chat.history`, `chat.metadata`, `models.list` and progress-card requests with `UNAVAILABLE`, instructing an offline Doctor repair. The interrupted modeling request could not continue.

This report concerns recovery/admission after a refused reclamation commit, not a request to change history retention or bypass current-authority checks.

## Environment and actual observation

- Linux x64, Node 24.21.0, managed user systemd Gateway.
- Installed full-package source candidate: 2026.9.8 / `190042328f3e7d88570a388163820e4b67836c5e` (includes the separate indexed-media producer repair in #166568).
- 2026-10-07 14:44:23 UTC: systemd-oomd killed the Gateway cgroup after system memory and swap exceeded its 90% threshold. This was not a manual restart or printer operation.
- 14:44:29: systemd restarted the Gateway automatically.
- 14:45:54: HTTP listener bound; agent preparation continued in the background.
- By 14:52:29: affected-agent RPCs consistently returned the checkpoint-expired error and `Sessions remain unavailable. Stop the Gateway, run "openclaw doctor --fix" to inspect and repair this agent database, and restart.`
- Supported read-only `doctor --session-sqlite inspect --session-sqlite-agent <affected-agent> --json` completed successfully: one target, 97 SQLite session entries, zero reported issues, no import or archival mutations. This inventory is not a full integrity certification.
- The host was heavily CPU/I/O constrained during recovery. Exact data has not been reproduced in a synthetic fixture yet.

## Source lead, not a proven complete root cause

`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-commit.ts` uses a five-second worker decision wait. A host authorization callback that observes a cell no longer in REQUESTED throws the generic checkpoint-expired error; the worker has a distinct refused-request error and settlement/rollback protocol. Current main `9bdad160d80686de5d080e4f6f128736f4831aef` still has this same commit-decision code.

Please distinguish confirmed native rollback/refusal from uncertain mutation or failed close, and investigate how a late authorization/refused request is propagated into permanent agent readiness failure. Keep live-authority, database identity, integrity and write-settlement gates intact. Raising the timeout, clearing admission state by hand, deleting sessions or changing retention would not establish the producer repair.

## Expected / actual

Expected: crash recovery either completes through the supported owner or reports a specific durable-data risk; a safely refused and rolled-back cleanup request should not misdiagnose a healthy store as irrecoverably unavailable.

Actual: the affected agent remains unavailable after startup with the checkpoint error. No conversation rows, indexes, compaction summaries or history have been edited manually; no provider/model change or guard weakening was used.

Related: #162319 contains an earlier checkpoint-expired observation during cold archival, but its main request is a retention-policy decision. This incident is startup recovery becoming a persistent agent lockout.

issues.body:
### Summary
Continue a Beam in the same live logical conversation when moving between a source client and a Team Gateway. A provider-specific runtime session ID may change.

### Problem to solve
PR #192513 admits an authorized publisher to the existing transcript-copy flow. The first send creates a new Team session and imports the uploaded snapshot; later source uploads do not update that conversation. Reopening a Beam can therefore lead to another independent continuation. This fixes the blocked publisher composer, but does not satisfy logical conversation continuity.

Model handoff also has an inherited gap: the copy owner normalizes provider/model text, then requires exact provider/ID equality against available destination catalog rows. Destination aliases or provider-declared equivalent versions can unnecessarily fall back.

### Proposed solution and acceptance criteria
- Continue, retry and reopen resolve one durable logical conversation. Define the handoff and identity owner independently of provider runtime IDs.
- Keep one execution owner after handoff. Late source snapshots must not overwrite destination turns or revive an independent writable branch; preserve ordered history and deduplication.
- Normalize requested model identifiers through existing destination selection and provider-owned catalog equivalence contracts. Exact IDs, configured aliases and equivalent versions select an available, permitted destination model.
- When the requested model is unavailable, omit the source override and use the destination's configured default through normal resolution. Preserve normal authorization, account admission and setup errors.
- Demonstrate an authorized destination turn, retry and reopen in that same logical conversation, plus revocation, unavailable-model and equivalent-alias cases.
- Keep credentials and access policy owned by each destination. This request grants no credential sharing, source-machine access, policy bypass or automatic provider-session-ID reuse.

### Alternatives considered
The existing independent snapshot copy is a bounded improvement tracked by #192513, but does not meet the requested continuity. Requiring an identical provider runtime session ID is unnecessarily restrictive. Existing ACP adoption and ordinary model-selection seams should be investigated before introducing a new continuation mechanism; this issue does not prescribe an ACP backend.

### Impact
Publishers expect to keep working in the conversation opened by the returned Beam link. Independent copies split subsequent work and history. Exact-only model matching can silently select a different model despite a permitted equivalent at the destination.

### Evidence
- [Current copy owner creates a new Gateway session and imports history](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/53179a7943db55e20abb82bd2920c3ddf308e12d/src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog-gateway-copy.ts#L228).
- [Existing model assessment uses exact availability matching](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/53179a7943db55e20abb82bd2920c3ddf308e12d/src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog-gateway-copy.ts#L39).
- [Documented current snapshot-copy semantics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/53179a7943db55e20abb82bd2920c3ddf308e12d/docs/plugins/beam.md).
- [Destination model alias resolution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/53179a7943db55e20abb82bd2920c3ddf308e12d/src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts#L543) and [provider-owned catalog identity matching](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/53179a7943db55e20abb82bd2920c3ddf308e12d/src/agents/model-catalog-lookup.ts#L167).


**Open architecture finding:** the receiver binding does not yet establish a source-client ownership transfer. Source clients currently keep publishing without a handoff acknowledgment, allowing source and Team histories to diverge. The source-side one-way handoff/retirement or reroute must be implemented and validated before #192520 is complete or this PR is landable under the expanded direction.

### Implementation status
Vincent explicitly authorized implementation and landing of this continuity requirement together with the publisher repair in [PR #192513](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192513). Transcript-copy semantics alone do not complete this issue.

Candidate `a114bab949ed4c549c52056e8b336566babc7b61` adds a receiver-owned durable Beam continuation binding, import-once history, read-only resolution on reopen, normal destination model/version/alias selection, and configured-default fallback when unavailable. Normal source ownership, destination authorization, account admission and revocation remain enforced; no credentials or provider runtime session IDs are transferred. The candidate currently deduplicates receiver-side continuation only. It does not yet transfer source-client execution ownership: the original source and Team histories can still diverge. An acknowledged source-side one-way handoff/retirement or reroute remains required; bidirectional synchronization is not required.

Independent structured source reviews completed without P0-P2 findings. [Native exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41773103646), execution proof and required landing gates remain pending. This issue stays open until the implementation is validated and landed. No deployment or live provider proof is claimed.

issues.body:
## Summary

When a user manually switches the active model (e.g., `/model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`), OpenClaw disables the fallback chain entirely. If that model becomes unavailable (provider 503, timeout, 5xx), the session deadlocks — the Gateway retries the same model in a loop with no recovery path.

## Root Cause

`resolveEffectiveModelFallbacks()` in `src/agents/agent-scope.ts` returns `[]` when `modelOverrideSource === "user"`. The function treats any non-auto override as a signal to disable fallbacks, on the assumption that the user explicitly chose their model and no substitution should be made.

The downstream effect: `persistFallbackCandidateSelection()` in the agent runner also returns early for user-switched models, preventing fallback persistence. Between empty fallbacks and blocked persistence, the session has zero recovery options.

## Real Incident Data (2026-05-21, 14:00–14:14 CST)

### Timeline

| Time (CST) | Event |
|------------|-------|
| 13:43 | User switches to `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` |
| 13:46–14:00 | Normal conversation with 42 tool calls |
| 14:00:23 | DeepSeek v4-pro model call hangs (120s idle timeout) |
| 14:02:28 | Gateway logs: `stalled session`, `LLM idle timeout (120s): no response from model` |
| 14:07 | User sends follow-up message — system cannot process (v4-pro still hung) |
| 14:08:06 | Context compaction fails: v4-pro timeout (61s), v4-flash `file_lock_stale` |
| 14:10:15 | Another deepseek-v4-pro call times out (120s) |
| 14:10:36 | User force-restarts Gateway (SIGTERM) |
| 14:12:09 | After restart, compaction fails on v4-pro (timeout) |
| 14:12:12 | Compaction on v4-flash fails: `provider_error_5xx` |
| 14:13:12 | Another compaction fails on v4-flash: `provider_error_5xx` |
| 14:13:58 | Session finally aborted after ~14 minutes of stall |

### Provider error evidence

Confirmed DeepSeek outage at the time:
```
503 Service is too busy. We advise users to temporarily switch to alternative LLM API service providers.
```

### Gateway diagnostic logs

```
13:59:25 [diagnostic] long-running session: age=577s queueDepth=1 reason=queued_behind_active_work
14:02:25 [diagnostic] stalled session: age=757s reason=active_work_without_progress
14:02:28 [agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: decision=surface_error reason=timeout
  rawError="LLM idle timeout (120s): no response from model" fallbackConfigured=false
```

The `fallbackConfigured=false` flag confirms the session had no fallback path for the user-switched model.

## Proposed Fix

In `resolveEffectiveModelFallbacks()`: when `modelOverrideSource === "user"`, return the agent's configured fallbacks instead of an empty array. This gives user-switched models a per-call recovery path. The existing `persistFallbackCandidateSelection` guard ensures the fallback selection is NOT persisted to session state, so the user's model preference is preserved for the next message.

## Related

- PR: #TBD (to be linked)

## Problem

Replace Blacksmith with Boat for Linux CI and Crabbox-backed remote proof while preserving the current validation, resource, cleanup, and contributor-trust contracts.

## Narrow migration slices

- Keep Boat measurements out of existing GitHub-hosted and Blacksmith timing profiles until native Boat resources and timing behavior are qualified.
- Add native Boat sizing and clean-environment support in Crabbox, then prove bounded allocation, exact source synchronization, command status/output, artifact retrieval, reuse, and cleanup.
- Qualify native Boat GitHub Actions runners, cache/artifact behavior, fork admission, and resource limits.
- Update remote-proof bootstrap and reusable/release workflows; retain explicit coverage for ARM and Windows.
- Switch defaults and remove superseded Blacksmith configuration after the replacement paths pass their required proof.

The cutover covers active OpenClaw execution routes. Crabbox retains its public Blacksmith provider for other consumers; OpenClaw will not silently fall back to it. Subscription cancellation, account deletion, and unrelated fleet sessions are outside this work.

Each change should remain independently reviewable. This issue tracks the complete cutover; prerequisite PRs do not complete it by themselves.

## Pull requests

Eighteen prerequisite PRs are merged. Six drafts remain open: the native Boat CI pilot, two portable image builders, the wrapper lifecycle, release-source preparation, and unpublished-source seeding. issues.body:
## Summary

Since 2026.10.10, a scheduled `agentTurn` job that has no recorded inference account is refused whenever a candidate model is served by a provider configured with `auth: "aws-sdk"` (for example `amazon-bedrock` using an EC2 instance role or another credential from the default AWS chain). The run fails with:

```
Automation has no recorded inference account. Explicitly select its account with a model@profile update before running it.
```

The suggested fix cannot be applied: an `aws-sdk` provider has no auth profile, so `model@profile` has nothing to bind. On current `main` the Doctor inference-binding migration (from #192195) also explicitly skips these jobs with "The current route uses an ambient credential, not a durable stored account." As a result, a job routed through Bedrock with `aws-sdk` auth has no supported path to run again.

This is a different gap from #192195 (stored-profile jobs, now migrated by Doctor on `main`) and #192009 (authorizing a second provider account for fallbacks). The provider here has no stored account to adopt or authorize.

## Source evidence

**v2026.10.10 (`7dc3350`), `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-plan.ts`:**

- A cron run with no `authProfileBinding` and no `scheduledRuntimeAuthority` is refused when any prepared attempt has `credentialSource.kind === "profile"`, or `kind === "direct"` and `!isConfiguredKeyAuthSource(source)`.
- `isConfiguredKeyAuthSource` only accepts the evidence values `synthetic`, `environment` and `provider-config`.
- `model-auth-availability` classifies a provider with `auth: "aws-sdk"` as `evidence: "aws-sdk"`. That source is therefore treated like an unrecorded stored account and refused.

**Current `main`:**

- `auth-plan.ts` keeps the same `unrecorded` check.
- `src/commands/doctor/cron/inference-binding-migration.ts` throws "The current route uses an ambient credential, not a durable stored account." for `firstSource.kind === "direct"` when the source is not a configured key. Doctor reports the job but cannot migrate it.
- `runtimeAuthority` is only captured when a job is created or updated, so jobs created before 10.10 never get one.

## Impact (one installation, assessed before upgrading from 2026.9.36)

Our setup has 55 enabled isolated `agentTurn` jobs across 11 agents. The model chains mix two providers:

- `amazon-bedrock` (`auth: "aws-sdk"`, EC2 instance role)
- an OpenAI-compatible Bedrock endpoint configured with `apiKey` (`provider-config`)

Expected effect on 10.10:

- Jobs whose effective primary is the `aws-sdk` provider are refused on every run.
- Jobs whose primary uses the `provider-config` key run normally. Whenever the primary fails, the first `aws-sdk` fallback is refused, and because the refusal calls `recordModelFallbackStop`, the rest of the chain never runs.
- Interactive turns, heartbeats and script jobs are not affected (the guard is gated on `trigger === "cron"`).

We have not upgraded production. This is based on reading the released 10.10 dist and current `main` source, not on a live run.

## Expected

An `aws-sdk` (ambient AWS chain) provider should be treated like the configured-key sources. It is declared in provider config, it is the only credential that provider can use, and there is no stored account that could be adopted later. So either:

1. `isConfiguredKeyAuthSource` (or the `unrecorded` check) should accept `evidence: "aws-sdk"` when the provider config declares `auth: "aws-sdk"`, or
2. there should be a supported way to record an ambient/aws-sdk binding for an existing job (via Doctor migration, or `automations edit`), and the refusal message should name it instead of `model@profile`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure `models.providers.amazon-bedrock` with `auth: "aws-sdk"` and no auth profiles, using credentials from the default AWS chain (instance role or env).
2. On 2026.9.x or 2026.10.9, create an isolated `agentTurn` cron job whose model (or agent default) is an `amazon-bedrock/...` model.
3. Upgrade to 2026.10.10 and trigger the job.
4. Observed: refused with "Automation has no recorded inference account…". `automations edit --model amazon-bedrock/<model>@<profile>` has no valid profile id to use, and `openclaw doctor --fix` on `main` cannot migrate the job.

## Related

- #192195: legacy stored-profile jobs; migration landed on `main`, but it does not cover ambient credentials.
- #192009 / #192463: cross-provider fallback authorization.
- #141983: ambient AWS credentials and execution-owner fingerprints in another path.

### Bug type
Regression / cloud workers

### Summary
On 2026.10.10, a Crabbox (AWS) cloud worker allocates, completes setup, enrolls and goes live, but every OpenClaw turn on it fails immediately:

```
Cloud worker process failed before completing the turn: node worker failed with exit code 1: Runtime config is not prepared. Await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()() first.
```

### Setup
- Gateway 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), Linux, bind loopback, public ingress via Cloudflare Tunnel; `plugins.entries.device-pair.config.publicUrl` = the public HTTPS origin; `gateway.trustedProxies` = loopback.
- `cloudWorkers.profiles.aws`: provider crabbox, install bundle, settings provider aws / class small / target linux / warmImage true / desktop true; no setupSecrets (no tailnet join).
- Test: `sessions.dispatch` of a fresh session (no repo) to the aws profile.

### Observed
1. Lease allocated, setup finished (~3 min), node paired and connected from the worker's public IP through the public origin, runtime bundle installed, session went live on the worker.
2. The first turn fails with the error above. Every model fallback (GPT-6.1-sol, Grok 4.7, GPT-6-astra) fails identically, so it is not provider-specific.
3. The failure also caused OpenClaw to start a replacement lease automatically.

### Expected
The `openclaw worker` process prepares runtime config (awaits the async reader) before the turn starts, as the Gateway does.

### Notes
Looks like the same class as #170715 (runtime config read before it is published), but on the worker entry path. Possibly related to #182647 (worker-preparation failures before inference). Tailnet-delivery background: #192175.

### Bug type

Crash / run failure

### Summary

On 2026.10.10, a native `/status` command sent in the same Telegram forum topic while an ordinary agent turn is starting kills that turn with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` ("SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session-id>"). The turn is not retried; the user gets the host notice "OpenClaw couldn't finish this request" and the original request is silently dropped (nothing applied, no reply).

This is the same error family as #184909, #176235, #174994, #145551, but a different concurrent writer: the `/status` command reply appended to the transcript. #186619 (withdrawn steers → followups) and the closed-unmerged #185939 (recover rewrites from concurrent appends) do not cover it.

### Observed sequence (2026.10.10 7dc3350, Telegram forum topic, embedded agent, anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, queue mode default)

All times UTC, 2026-11-04, from the gateway log:

1. 03:01:34.886 — inbound user message (213 chars) in `telegram:group:<chat>:topic:1`.
2. 03:01:38.857 — inbound `/status` (18 chars) in the same topic, ~4 s later.
3. ~03:01:40.04 — agent turn `runId=099eb8e3…` starts on lane `session:agent:main:telegram:group:<chat>:topic:1` (durationMs=9203 ending at 03:01:49.24).
4. 03:01:42.76 — `/status` reply delivered (`telegram outbound send ok … operation=sendRichMessage`) and appended to the session transcript (it appears in session history at 03:01:42).
5. 03:01:49.241 — `lane task error: … errorName=SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError … error="SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session-id>"` (logged for both `lane=main` and `lane=session:…`).
6. 03:01:49.257 — `Embedded agent failed before reply: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite …`
7. 03:01:49.737 — `message-tool-outcome outcome=mute runStatus=errored`; transcript gets a custom entry "Your request couldn't be completed: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite …"; user sees "⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this request…".

No pending inputs remain afterwards (`pendingInputs.total=0`), so the user message is not re-queued.

### Expected

A command reply (`/status`, and likely other native commands answered outside the agent turn) appended while a turn is preparing must not fail that turn. Either the prepare/rewrite path should rebase onto concurrent appends (as for other concurrent writers), or command replies should be serialized behind the session lane / excluded from the rewrite fence. At minimum the conflict should trigger a retry of the turn instead of dropping the user request.

### Actual

Turn fails before any model output; request lost unless the user notices and resends.

### Frequency / scope

- First occurrence in this install's logs: 2 log lines on 2026-11-04 (one failure), 0 on 2026-11-03. Gateway was updated 2026.10.9 → 2026.10.10 on 2026-11-03 ~21:10 UTC; not checked whether 2026.10.9 shows the same.
- Observed once, not yet deterministically reproduced in isolation. Ordering is from logs; the `/status` reply is the only other write to that transcript in the window, so it is the likely conflicting writer, but the throwing call site was not instrumented.

### Suggested reproduction

1. Telegram forum topic (or any channel) bound to an embedded-agent session with SQLite transcript storage.
2. Send a normal request that makes the agent do real work.
3. Within ~1–5 s, before the agent's first model request, send `/status` in the same chat/topic.
4. Observe `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` and "couldn't finish this request".

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), Linux x64, Node 26.12.1
- Channel: Telegram (forum topic), embedded agent runtime
- Model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
- Error class appears in shipped `dist/state/openclaw-state-read-sqlite-snapshot-staging-owner-*.mjs` and `dist/managed-handoff-runtime.mjs`

### Related

#184909, #176235, #174994, #145551, #148280, #185939, #186619

issues.body:
### Summary

Session-level model pins/overrides (set via the Control UI model picker, `/model <id>`, or `sessions.patch`) replace the agent's entire candidate list with that single model. When the pinned model's provider fails (rate limit, usage limit, outage), the run surfaces the error instead of consulting the agent's configured fallback chain.

Proposal: **pinned models should inherit the agent's fallback chain** (pinned model first, then the configured fallbacks), with an opt-out for deliberate "this model only" pins.

### Current behavior

Agent config carries a real chain:

```json5
agents.entries.toolbuilder.model = { primary: "kimicode/k3", fallbacks: ["zai/glm-5.3", "kimicode/k3"] }
```

But a session pinned to `openai/gpt-6-astra` (subscription OAuth) fails hard when the subscription hits its usage window:

```
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed
  requested=openai/gpt-6-astra candidate=openai/gpt-6-astra reason=rate_limit next=none
  detail=Codex error: The usage limit has been reached
[agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: ... decision=surface_error reason=rate_limit
  attempt=1 retry=0 rotations=0 from=openai/gpt-6-astra
```

`next=none` is the tell: the candidate list contains only the pinned model. The user sees "The agent run failed before producing a reply." Meanwhile sibling sessions on the same agent (unpinned) fail over astra → sol → glm correctly, so the chain itself works — pins just don't carry it.

Reproduced on 2026.9.4 across two incidents (2026-09-15 and 2026-09-18) during a multi-day ChatGPT-subscription usage-limit window: every pinned-to-astra session failed with `next=none` while unpinned sessions on the same agents kept working via fallback.

### Expected behavior

When a session is pinned to model M, build the candidate list as `[M, ...agents.<agent>.model.fallbacks]` (deduped), so provider failures on the pin fall through to the configured chain instead of terminating the turn.

Possible shapes (any would resolve the incidents):

1. **Always inherit** — pins always append the agent's configured fallbacks.
2. **Opt-out flag** — inherit by default; `--no-fallback` / UI toggle for deliberate single-model pins.
3. **Config default** — e.g. `agents.defaults.modelPins.inheritFallbacks: true | false | "explicit-only"`.

Related: `agents.defaults.subagents.model` accepts a bare string (no fallbacks) or `{primary, fallbacks}` — task/spawn sessions created before this field was set in object form had the same single-candidate failure mode. Making string-form model refs everywhere resolve as `{primary: <string>, fallbacks: <agent chain>}` would close the remaining gap.

### Why this matters operationally

Subscription usage windows (ChatGPT 5h/weekly caps) and prepaid-credit exhaustion can last hours or days. During those windows, any session pinned to the capped model becomes unusable and requires manual intervention (re-pin to a healthy model, or `/model default`), even though healthy fallbacks are configured on the agent. Pins silently downgrade resilience to zero.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)
- macOS 26.3.1 (arm64), node 24.20.0
- Agents: 16 configured agents, all with `{primary, fallbacks}` chains; pins set via Control UI model picker

### Related issues

- #116315 — session overrides silently bypass the fallback chain (observed as one symptom of a larger incident; this FR proposes the design fix for that aspect)
- #141115 — 429 from primary terminates session instead of consulting fallback chain
- #149785 — usage-limit error surfaces without mid-run fallback on first occurrence

issues.body:
## Summary

After upgrading a multi-agent macOS Gateway from OpenClaw 2026.9.2 to 2026.9.6 (`eb377ac`), fresh non-delivering Codex-backed agent turns intermittently fail before producing a reply. Two observed failure classes are:

```text
prepared model runtime publication was superseded for <agent-dir>
codex app-server request timed out | codex app-server initialize timed out | CODEX_APP_SERVER_STARTUP_CANCELLED
```

The Gateway and auxiliary services remain reachable, so transport health checks alone do not catch the lost inference. The issue affects multiple agents rather than a single model alias or meeting job.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (`eb377ac`), upgraded from 2026.9.2
- macOS Apple Silicon, Node v24.16.0
- npm installation; Gateway runs under an existing macOS LaunchAgent with a nonstandard NVM Node path
- Codex runtime with named OpenAI Sol, Terra, and Luna model routes
- Approximately 100 enabled cron jobs across multiple agents

The service and Node path were checked against the existing LaunchAgent; no Node or package ambiguity was found.

## Observations

1. The 2026.9.6 package/config validated and model-status checks for sampled agents showed usable OpenAI profiles, zero missing providers, and zero route issues.
2. After one fresh Gateway start, coding-sysadmin (Sol) returned the publication-superseded error; coding-sysadmin and code-op-nuclear (Terra) also returned Codex app-server request timeouts.
3. A second operator-approved guarded restart, with no package or model-routing change, brought the same existing Gateway label back. Fresh non-delivering simple turns then yielded:
   - main / Sol: success (`OK`)
   - science-writer / Sol: publication-superseded error
   - worker / Luna: app-server initialize/request timeout with `CODEX_APP_SERVER_STARTUP_CANCELLED`
   - coding-sysadmin / Sol: publication-superseded error
   - code-op-nuclear / Terra: app-server initialize/request timeout
4. The live config hash and mtime did not change during these tests. No automatic config rewrite or hot reload trigger was observed. The Gateway process remained the sole listener on its port. Gateway HTTP/RPC, the report endpoint, and the A2A agent card responded successfully; Telegram probe also reported running/OK.
5. Before the second restart, multiple isolated jobs across agents ended in prepared reply-dispatch/runtime-owner errors. Only one scheduled heartbeat had run after the second restart at the time of this report, and it succeeded; no claim is made that the pre-restart job failure count measures post-restart reliability.
6. There are frequent `models.list` calls from existing control UI clients, and provider catalog refreshes sometimes coincide with app-server timeouts. This is a correlation only. `status --deep --json` sampled after the second restart showed modelCatalog worker `activeTasks:0`, `pendingTasks:0`; the perpetual catalog rebuild described in #157107 was not observed in that sample.

A narrow termination of one verified idle app-server child before the restarts did not fix the affected agent; it was not repeated. No Doctor, onboarding, model-policy change, broad process kill, or SentinelOne change was used.

## Investigation status (October 1, 2026)

Following the [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/158127#issuecomment-5833021330), this report tracks two separate failure boundaries:

- **Runtime publication admission:** `prepared model runtime publication was superseded` can reject a turn before model execution. Subsequent operator reports include non-Codex routes, so this path is not Codex-specific. OAuth adoption, catalog refresh, and scheduling overlap remain candidate triggers rather than an established shared cause.
- **Codex startup/acquisition:** initialize/request timeouts and startup cancellation occur before native turn execution. Our previously posted matched probes and native-log observations narrow this boundary; they do not prove a publication race causes it.

The [new per-agent auth-reload report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/158127#issuecomment-5875956290) provides a useful cold-start hypothesis for the second path. In our retained September 25 macOS observations, however, repeated auth-reload and remote-control preference messages appeared for both the failing auxiliary agent and the successful main-agent control. Those messages alone therefore do not distinguish our failure; their timing relative to initialization, auth application, catalog requests, and app-server generation needs correlation.

No deterministic reproduction against current main or recovery on a newer release has been established by the reporter. This update reviews retained evidence only; it includes no fresh production probe, restart, or configuration/auth change. The next evidence needed is a separately attributable admission trace for publication supersession and a startup trace for Codex acquisition. A blanket cron retry or copying auth files would not establish either cause.

## Expected

A fresh agent turn should acquire the current published runtime and complete or report a specific provider/auth error. A timed-out app-server initialization should be isolated and recoverable without repeated Gateway restarts or loss of unrelated agents' turns.

## Impact

Scheduled work and agent replies are at risk while the Gateway appears healthy. Two meeting-report inputs remain missing, and consolidation was held to avoid treating partial output as complete. The operator is keeping the partly functional Gateway running rather than taking down reports, A2A, and Telegram while investigating.

## Related reports

- #156975 has the exact `prepared model runtime publication was superseded` error on 2026.9.6, but focuses on fallback/error presentation on another platform.
- #139830 and #139710 report the related but different `plugin generation was superseded` error.
- #84567 and #80618 describe older Codex initialization/concurrency hangs.
- #157107 describes a 2026.9.6 catalog-worker loop; the sampled worker state here does not establish that loop.

Sanitized evidence is available; this is an observed production failure, not a deterministic minimal reproduction. AI-assisted investigation and report prepared with Codex.

issues.body:
## Summary

Binary requirement checks reuse a successful relative-PATH lookup after the process changes working directories. A tool found under the first workspace is then reported available in another workspace where it cannot be resolved.

## Reproduction

Reproduced on source `d64730851269b8ca5e82d9778810aa0669eb2e3e`, macOS arm64, Node 26.5.0, using the production functions in `src/shared/config-eval.ts`:

1. Create two temporary directories. Put an executable `fixture-tool` under `first/bin`; leave `second/bin` absent.
2. Set `PATH=./bin` and change cwd to `first`.
3. Call `hasBinary('fixture-tool')`: it returns `true`.
4. Change cwd to `second` without changing PATH.
5. Call `hasBinary('fixture-tool')` again and call `prepareBinaryAvailability(['fixture-tool'])`.

Actual: both APIs report `true`; the prepared result also reports `isCurrent() === true`.
Expected: both report `false` because `./bin/fixture-tool` does not exist in the second directory. Returning to the first directory should discover the tool again.

## Cause and impact

The successful-probe cache is keyed by PATH and PATHEXT only. The asynchronous preparation checks cwd freshness during its operation, but its initial cache-hit branch can reuse a hit from a previous cwd. Skill binary requirements can consequently advertise a tool that is unavailable in the current working directory.

Including cwd in the existing cache identity repairs both callers. Two focused regressions fail on the original code; the repaired 22-test suite and a real `process.chdir` fixture pass. The existing executable-path resolver already uses cwd as part of its own cache identity.

This is separate from #146188, which validates executable file types and explicitly leaves the caches unchanged.

issues.body:
## Summary

On a Gateway whose parent session runs on a CLI-backed agent runtime (`claude-cli`), a child subagent's completion can be lost twice:

1. The completion wake is replayed through the delivery queue and dead-lettered on `SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE` even though the model turn had not started. The session store lease was simply not ready yet; a later attempt would have succeeded (verified on v2026.10.9: the state clears within minutes). The replay path treated every adopted event as non-retryable.
2. When delivery is blocked, the parent receives (on v2026.10.9) only a short `systemEvent` text "Subagent completion delivery is blocked: …" with `internal_system` provenance. Clients render that as a system notice, the child's result text is not carried, and a CLI-backed parent never runs a turn on it. On current `main` the blocked-notice queueing was removed entirely (#185388) and the sentinel session-event replay path was deleted (#185730), so the parent gets nothing automatic; `transcript_commit_wait_unsupported` still applies to CLI-backed parents, so the symptom persists there in a different shape.

## What we changed on a fork of v2026.10.9 (reference only, not a PR)

Fork branch: https://github.com/jmoradian/openclaw/tree/fix/subagent-completion-notice-20261103 (tip caca94757d9a89cad0856343585869f4e190b4b8, base v2026.10.9 8b18b55)

- Replay of a queued `agentTurn`/`systemEvent` classifies failures by `errorCode` and `failurePhase` (added to `SessionEventOutcome`). `SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE` before execution becomes a safe retry (attempt ownership released); execution-phase failures and `SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_REVOKED` stay dead-letter. This changes dead-letter semantics for every sentinel replay source, not only subagent completions.
- `enqueueSessionEventForHost` accepts an explicit `inputProvenance`, and the sentinel replay passes the queued entry's provenance through (including policy re-admission).
- A blocked *successful* completion queues a visible `agentTurn` with `inter_session` provenance (`sourceTool: "subagent_completion_blocked"`, `sourceSessionKey: <child>`), carrying a header with the reason code, the retained final result (UTF-16-safe cap) and the child session key, with `expectedSessionId` set so a `/reset` between block and replay takes the session-changed branch. Idempotency key is per run, generation and attempt.
- Characterisation tests pin which `GenerationUnavailable` branch fires for a CLI-backed parent and that provenance survives persistence through the claude-cli history path.

## Why this is an issue and not a PR

The patched code paths no longer exist on `main` (see the two PRs above), and #179675 states the policy that failed recovery does not queue another model turn. A port would be a new design, so we are asking instead:

- How should a successful child's result reach a CLI-backed parent on `main` when the automatic wake fails? Today the result is retained on the run record but nothing visible or actionable reaches the parent.
- Is a provenance-labelled, visible inter-session turn (never framed as the user or as system text) acceptable as the delivery of last resort, or should this be exposed another way (e.g. a durable "unread completion" surfaced by `subagents list`)?

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55), macOS arm64, Node 24, parent on `claude-cli`.

issues.body:
### Summary

`openclaw doctor` reports `show_widget` as an unavailable allowlist entry on any install/surface that does not advertise the `inline-widgets` client capability, and because `show_widget` is a member of `group:openclaw`, the warning cannot be silenced by config without dropping that entire group. Request: a supported way to resolve this — either exclude capability-gated-only core tools from `group:openclaw`, or classify/suppress the warning the way gated core tools in built-in profiles already are (see #53702).

### Problem to solve

`show_widget` is a shipped core tool that is **conditionally available**: it declares `requiredClientCaps: ["inline-widgets"]` (`src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts`), so it is only registered/usable on surfaces whose client advertises that capability (Control UI, iOS, Android, macOS, Discord Activities, Linux Quick Chat). On a plain messaging surface such as Telegram it is unavailable.

It is nevertheless a static member of `group:openclaw`, because its catalog entry sets `includeInOpenClawGroup: true`:

```ts
// src/agents/tool-catalog.ts:344
{
  id: "show_widget",
  description: "Show an interactive widget on chat or an auto-fitting dashboard",
  sectionId: "ui",
  profiles: [],
  includeInOpenClawGroup: true,
},
```

Any operator whose allowlist references `group:openclaw` therefore gets, on every `doctor` run and gateway start, a warning that is structural and unavoidable on that surface:

```
[tools] tools.profile (messaging) allowlist contains unknown entries (show_widget). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.
[tools] agents.main.tools.allow allowlist contains unknown entries (show_widget). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.
```

This is unlike #146392 (where the message named a plugin that did not exist and was simply wrong): here the wording is *accurate* — the tool really is unavailable on this surface. The problem is that it is **noise with no resolution path**, and it is triggered by a group grant rather than by an explicit operator mistake:

- Removing `group:openclaw` silences it but drops ~51 unrelated core tools.
- Adding `show_widget` to `tools.deny` does not help (the warning is derived from allowlist analysis, not the deny list).
- `doctor --skip` / `--severity-min` do not help (`doctor --lint --all --json` returns `findings: []`; this line is advisory text, not a lint finding).
- No config key exists to alter group membership.

Note that `show_widget` is reachable via `group:openclaw`, `group:ui`, and the shipped `canvas` alias expansion (`SHIPPED_PLUGIN_POLICY_FAMILY_CORE_TOOLS = Map([["canvas", ["show_widget"]]])`), and `profiles: []` means no built-in profile grants it. So `group:openclaw` is the common path that drags it into an allowlist where it can never match on a messaging surface.

### Proposed solution

Two acceptable outcomes; maintainers should pick, since they have opposite tradeoffs:

1. **Exclude capability-gated-only tools from `group:openclaw`** (i.e. drop `includeInOpenClawGroup` from the `show_widget` catalog entry). This removes the warning at the source. Downside: operators who intentionally rely on `group:openclaw` and use a widget-capable surface (Control UI, Discord, iOS, Android, macOS) silently lose widget access, and must re-add `show_widget` literally (which then re-triggers the same warning on messaging-only surfaces). This is why we did **not** open a PR for the one-line change: it is a product decision, not a bug fix.

2. **Treat group-derived, capability-gated core tools as non-warnable** — extend the gating-aware suppression from #53702 so that an entry contributed by a shipped group, and unavailable solely because of a client-capability gate, is not reported as an operator misconfiguration in the doctor/CLI path. The runtime already suppresses this class of warning on the conversation path (`suppressUnavailableCoreToolWarning: true`); only the doctor/CLI path is affected.

We would prefer (2): it preserves the tool for capable surfaces while removing the unavoidable noise for messaging-only installs.

### Alternatives considered

- **`tools.deny: ["show_widget"]`** — does not silence it; the allowlist analysis that emits the warning ignores deny entries.
- **`doctor --skip <id>` / `--severity-min`** — no check id exists for this line (`findings: []`), so severity/skip filters do not apply.
- **Drop `group:openclaw` and re-state its members explicitly, minus `show_widget`** — works today, but it is a large manual rewrite of the allowlist purely to avoid a diagnostic, and it silently freezes the group membership (future additions to `group:openclaw` are lost).
- **Local patch of the `dist` bundle** — overwritten by the next update; not a real fix.

### Impact

- **Affected:** any operator with `group:openclaw` (or `canvas`) in an allowlist on a surface without `inline-widgets` — i.e. plain messaging channels (Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, ...) and CLI runs.
- **Severity:** low/cosmetic — nothing is broken; the tool simply does not exist on that surface.
- **Frequency:** always — every `doctor` run and gateway start, for as long as the group grant is present.
- **Consequence:** sustained warning noise in the same list that carries genuine plugin/config warnings, which trains operators to ignore the list. It also invites a harmful "fix": deleting a working group grant (or the widget tool) to make the message go away, silently losing widget access on surfaces where it works.

### Evidence/examples

Environment: OpenClaw `2026.9.6` (build `eb377ac`), npm global install, Ubuntu 24.04 / Linux 6.8, `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, Telegram direct channel.

Config shape (redacted): `agents.entries.main.tools.alsoAllow` includes `group:openclaw` and `canvas`; `tools.profile: messaging`.

Relevant source on `origin/main`:

- `src/agents/tool-catalog.ts:344` — `show_widget` catalog entry with `includeInOpenClawGroup: true`; `group:openclaw` is built by filtering `CORE_TOOL_DEFINITIONS` on that flag (`buildCoreToolGroupMap`).
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` — `SHOW_WIDGET_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPS = ["inline-widgets"]`, applied as `requiredClientCaps` unless a current-channel presenter or pinned-only surface is present.

`doctor --lint --all --json` on the same host: `{"ok":true,"checksRun":133,"checksSkipped":0,"findings":[]}` — confirming this line is not a lint finding and cannot be filtered via `--skip`/`--severity-min`.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance — we can open the one-line `includeInOpenClawGroup` change if option (1) is preferred, or a suppression patch if option (2) is preferred.

### Additional information

Related prior work on this same warning surface, different root causes: #146392 (closed; `pdf` absent from the catalog), #53702 (merged; suppressed gated core tool warnings for built-in profiles), #46071 / #45269 / #42726 (closed; the `apply_patch` / `memory_*` instances). This case is distinct: the tool is in the catalog and correctly classified as unavailable, but it is gated by a *client capability* (per-surface), which the doctor/CLI path cannot satisfy, so the warning is permanently present for messaging-only installs.

issues.body:
## Summary

On 2026.10.9 (gateway in Kubernetes), stdio MCP server child processes accumulate over time: the gateway keeps spawning fresh instances of the same configured stdio server while the previous instances stay alive indefinitely. Each orphan holds its full RSS, contributing to container memory pressure until the kernel OOM-kills the pod.

## Evidence

Agent with Google's `analytics-mcp` configured as a stdio MCP server (python, launched via uv). Within ~1h45m of a fresh container start, six instances were alive simultaneously:

```
USER   PID %CPU %MEM    VSZ    RSS START COMMAND
node 14606  0.0  0.4 320864 141936 21:55 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
node 10778  0.0  0.4 320860 137164 21:44 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
node 17477  0.0  0.4 320860 141832 22:08 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
node 30894  0.9  0.4 320860 141924 23:00 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
node 31201  2.1  0.4 320860 142004 23:02 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
node 31419  5.8  0.4 320860 141924 23:02 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
```

(Container started 21:18; only the newest instance appears to serve traffic. The rest never exit and are never killed.)

That is ~850MB of leaked RSS in under 2 hours, growing roughly linearly with session/cron activity (~1GB/day on this agent). The pod was OOM-killed at its 18Gi limit the same evening (the leak was a contributor alongside page-cache pressure from a large agent DB).

## Expected

When a session/run that spawned a stdio MCP server ends — or when a replacement instance is launched — the old child process (and its descendants, for npm/uv wrapper chains) should be killed and reaped.

## Notes

- Looks like the same class of bug reported against other MCP hosts (host kills only the wrapper, not the process tree; stdio servers do not exit on stdin close).
- 2026.10.10's notes mention child-process *metrics* ("identify more launch owners") but no reaping fix.
- Workaround we are deploying: a periodic reaper that kills all but the newest instance of each stdio server binary.

Happy to provide more diagnostics (gateway logs around spawn times, MCP config shape) if useful.

issues.body:
Environment: OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Windows 11 x64; class observed repeatedly 2026-08 through 09 across several releases.

Problem: a one-shot scheduled job using announce delivery with no explicit resolved target fails closed at fire time: announce falls back to the creation-bound conversation, and if that has no outbound route the delivery fails. Because deleteAfterRun only fires on success, the job then strands in the store as an error/disabled entry that still looks alive - it appears in listings with no next run, nothing distinguishes "dead" from "will fire later", and failed announce deliveries in multi-agent configs can also surface as a "no explicit owner" configuration error (see related reports). We have repeatedly found stranded one-shots days or weeks later (oldest about 7 days) and now run a dedicated audit check to hunt them.

Request: (a) warn (or refuse) at creation when an announce-delivery job has no explicit channel/to target in a multi-agent install, since the fallback target is not resolvable there; (b) support deleteAfterRun semantics that also clean up errored one-shots (for example deleteAfterRun: "always" | "on-error"), or auto-retire one-shots whose delivery failed N consecutive times; (c) surface "one-shot - no next run - last delivery failed" prominently in job listings.

Related: #124679, #124926 (announce owner requirements in multi-agent configs).

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Deferred context-engine maintenance can inherit a released caller admission root, rejecting a coalesced rerun with `Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted` even when global admission is open.

### Steps to reproduce
Deterministic isolated scheduler regression, based on the existing `context-engine-maintenance.preparation.test.ts` fixture:
1. Block the fixture's first maintenance execution.
2. Schedule maintenance three times under separately admitted roots, releasing each caller immediately after scheduling:
```ts
for (let turn = 0; turn < 3; turn += 1) {
  const parent = tryBeginGatewayRootWorkAdmission(`maintenance-turn-${turn}`)!;
  try { await parent.run(f.schedule); }
  finally { parent.release(); }
}
f.workRelease.resolve();
await f.disposeEntered.promise;
expect(f.maintain).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
expect(f.failure).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
```
3. Baseline produced one run instead of the expected initial run plus coalesced rerun. The isolated candidate retained the relevant admission roots through settlement/disposal and passed.

A separate minimal mechanism probe captured an admitted root's AsyncLocalStorage context, released the root, then enqueued in that captured context. Global admission was open while inherited subordinate admission was closed, yielding the same draining error.

### Expected behavior
Already accepted deferred work and its coalesced rerun retain valid work ownership through actual settlement. Real restart/suspend fences continue to reject new work. Ownership is released after cleanup.

### Actual behavior
The isolated released-root probe returned:
```text
{"globalAdmissionClosed":false,"inheritedChildAdmissionClosed":true}
Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted
```
On the inspected deployment, three post-restart failures followed maintenance queue logs without an intervening global admission-close/restart log. This supports the same mechanism, but the exact production caller-release site was not instrumented or proven.

### OpenClaw version
Observed deployment: 2026.9.6. Deterministic regression based on upstream `a410b4d0fb5316735ebb1f8e90ed55a6e6336923`. Scheduler source rechecked at main `e5441c22d8966ee2cc73dca5681f4e56dccdf1b4`; tests were not rerun at that newer revision.

### Operating system
macOS 26.5.1, Apple silicon

### Install method
Global OpenClaw installation; isolated upstream source checkout for tests.

### Model
No provider/model required for the deterministic scheduler regression.

### Provider / routing chain
Host-only regression: admitted caller -> background context-engine scheduler -> command lane / inherited admission context.

### Logs
```text
failed to schedule deferred context engine maintenance: Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
- [Scheduler global fence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e5441c22d8966ee2cc73dca5681f4e56dccdf1b4/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.ts#L285).
- [Captured async context](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e5441c22d8966ee2cc73dca5681f4e56dccdf1b4/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.ts#L556).
- [Command-lane enqueue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e5441c22d8966ee2cc73dca5681f4e56dccdf1b4/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.ts#L463).
- Isolated repair retained each relevant caller root through deferred settlement, including superseded/coalesced callers and asynchronous disposal. Focused controls covered released callers, restart/suspend refusal, task callback settlement and preparation failure cleanup.
- Combined candidate validation (this ownership repair plus a separate budget-propagation repair): 267 tests across 9 files and three selected typechecks passed. This is not 267 ownership-specific tests or a deployed fix.

### Impact and severity
Affected: deferred context-engine maintenance with caller release before later scheduling/rerun. Deterministic edge-case regression; three production warnings observed in the inspected interval. Maintenance can be skipped and the diagnostic misleading. No claim of proven history loss or fleet-wide incidence.

### Additional information
Related but distinct: #156766 and merged #151936 address the missing durable-turn maintenance handoff; merged #151106 addresses reentrant task callbacks/duplicate scheduling. This report concerns admission lifetime after maintenance has been offered/queued. Do not suppress admission guards or resurrect already released roots. A candidate is preserved but no live code/config/database was modified. AI-assisted investigation; private identifiers, transcripts, credentials and local paths omitted.
