### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Every inbound iMessage in a direct conversation includes a `reply_to_id` field pointing at the immediately preceding message — even when the user did not use iMessage's native reply/swipe gesture and simply typed and sent a normal message. This makes `reply_to_id` indistinguishable from "previous message in the conversation," rather than reflecting a genuine user-initiated reply relationship.

A related effect: because the agent's own internal reasoning/tool-use narration is sometimes delivered as a separate message from its actual final answer, the "reply target" resolved for the user's next message can end up being that internal-dialog message — not the message that actually contains the content the user is responding to. The two are sometimes bundled together and sometimes not, so the reply target is inconsistent even from the same conversation flow, reproduces on 2026.7.1-2 and 2026.9.4.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In an active iMessage DM with the agent, send a normal message (no swipe-to-reply, no tapback-reply — just type and hit send)
2. Inspect the internal context passed to the model
3. Observe `reply_to_id` is populated, pointing at the prior message, along with a fully resolved "Reply target of current user message" block
4. Note that the resolved reply target is often a long internal-narration message (agent reasoning/tool commentary) rather than the specific content the user meant to respond to

### Expected behavior

`reply_to_id` should only be populated when the user actually performs a native reply action (e.g., swipe-to-reply in Messages.app), and should be absent/null for ordinary sequential messages. When it is populated, it should point at a coherent, user-facing message — not an arbitrary internal-narration fragment that happened to be the most recent bubble.

### Actual behavior

`reply_to_id` is populated on effectively every message regardless of any reply gesture, and resolves to whatever the most recent message happens to be — including agent internal-dialog/narration content that isn't the actual reply target the user intended.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4

### Operating system

macOS 15.7

### Install method

npm global

### Model

anthropic/claud-sonnet-5

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> opencode zen -> anthropic

### Additional provider/model setup details

iMessage channel connected to agent dedicated apple id conversing with another apple id.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Example payload from a message that was just typed normally, not replied to anything:

{"chat_id":"chat_id:2","message_id":"2137","reply_to_id":"4D503960-ADED-410C-A9D8-5D34E4DF2C50","was_mentioned":true}
A later example in the same conversation resolved `reply_to_id` to an entire prior multi-paragraph agent message (reasoning + a full draft bug report embedded in it) — again with no reply gesture performed by the user.


### Impact and severity

Affected: iMessage channels from 2026.7.1-2 and 2026.9.4; signal channel on same installs seems to not be affected.
Severity: Low-to-moderate- any consumer relying on `reply_to_id` to detect genuine reply intent (vs. plain sequential chat) will get false positives on every message, and the resolved "reply target" content can be misleading (internal narration rather than the intended answer).

### Additional information

Seems to be new behavior since upgrading in 2026.7.x; remains in 2026.9.x

• Reproduced across 2 independent sessions, multiple consecutive normal (non-reply) messages, consistent every time

issues.body:
## Summary

Isolated automation (cron) runs are capped at a fixed **8 concurrent runs per gateway** (`DEFAULT_CRON_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS = 8`, `src/cron/service/run-admission-capacity.ts` `resolveRunConcurrency()` returns the constant), and the former knob `cron.maxConcurrentRuns` is now dead config (`src/config/dead-config-keys.test.ts`). #87174 was closed in May as "default 8 + documented supported knob"; the knob no longer exists.

## Version

OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (upstream main `359a8a35`), Linux x64, Node v24.21.0, 5 gateways on one host.

## Why 8 fixed does not fit a business workload

One gateway serves a whole company: ~20 recurring jobs (triage, hygiene, watchers, support checks) plus **work-loop jobs whose agent turn legitimately runs 1–2 h** (implementer + reviewer subagents, tests, deploy verification). We run 15 such queues (instance × kind of work).

- Every long work-loop run holds one of the 8 slots for its full duration. With 6 running, the remaining automations of *all* agents on the gateway compete for 2 slots; hourly jobs queue behind them.
- A trigger (`trigger.script`) evaluation also occupies a slot while it runs (measured: `runningAtMs` is set for the evaluation, ~2–3 s), so a 60 s gate on 16 jobs adds steady slot pressure.
- There is no per-agent or per-job concurrency class, so there is no way to say "work loops: at most N, never starve the watchers".

## Workaround we use (works, but it is orchestration we had to invent)

The trigger does not fire the cron run. It admits under a host lock and dispatches the work into an ordinary named session with its own code-mode tools: `sessions` patch (creates `agent:executor:lane:<queue>:<card>`, thinking) + `sessions_send` `mode: "followup"`, `timeoutSeconds: 0`. The turn runs in lane `nested:<key>`, outside the cron pool, and our gate enforces its own cap (8 work turns + 3 urgent). Side benefits: per-card persistent session (continuable later), subagent completions delivered reliably (vs. #44925). Costs: no per-run timeout on this route, a non-`NO_REPLY` final wakes a delivery turn in the trigger session, and admission/counting logic lives in our trigger script.

## Ask

1. Make run concurrency configurable again (global and ideally per agent/job class), or
2. document that long agent work should not run as cron runs and provide a first-class "dispatch a turn into a named session" action for triggers (with timeout and concurrency class), so this does not need custom admission code.

issues.body: ## Summary Links in dashboard HTML widgets (``) work in the browser Control UI but silently do nothing in native apps (confirmed: macOS app; likely iOS/Android Quick Chat webviews too). No error, no feedback — the tap is swallowed. ## Confirmed behavior - Same widget, same HTML: links open a new tab correctly in desktop Safari Control UI. - Same widget in the native macOS app: taps do nothing. - Likely same root family as #131406 (attachment `target="_blank"` links unresponsive in the macOS app). ## Architecture (traced through 2026.9.2 build + docs) The sandbox is not the bug — by design it never grants popup permission: 1. Widget HTML (whether via `show_widget` or `board.widget.put` → `buildWidgetDocument`) is wrapped in the canonical wrapper (`wrap.ts`), which intercepts primary-click on `target="_blank"` http(s) anchors (plus middle-click) and issues `request("host.open", {url})`. Script-initiated `window.open` is hard-locked to `undefined`. (`docs/tools/show-widget.md`: link forwarding "needs no grant and **never grants iframe popup permissions**".) 2. The Control UI host handles `host.open` (`board-view` bridge controller: validates `^https?://`, calls `this.openUrl(url)`, default `Ee` from the shared boot bundle). 3. There is **no `window.open` call anywhere** in the Control UI bundles — the final tab-open primitive lives in shared/native code, and evidently fails closed (returns null/falsy → `throw Error("widget link could not be opened")`, which the wrapper swallows: `then(()=>{},()=>{})`). So on surfaces where the open-URL primitive is unavailable (native webviews that block new tabs / lack external-open handling), every widget link silently dies. The failure is invisible by construction: the wrapper drops rejections silently and there is no fallback (no error toast, no copy-URL, nothing). ## Why not just `allow-popups` Per `docs/web/dashboard-architecture.md`, widget code is "arbitrary agent-authored HTML/JS in a hard sandbox… Capabilities over trust." Granting popup permission would bypass the user-gesture-gated, ticket-bound `host.open` path and enable scripted popups, phishing tabs, and URL-based exfiltration outside granted-`connect-src` containment. The fix should stay on the host side, not relax the sandbox. ## Suggested fix (host-side, no sandbox change) - Implement the open-URL primitive in native clients: route `host.open` to the system browser (or an in-app browser tab) instead of failing closed. - Alternatively/additionally: surface the failure — if `openUrl` returns falsy, show a toast / copy the URL to clipboard so the tap isn't a silent no-op. - Bonus: `sendPrompt`-style user-activation-gated fallback (e.g. long-press to copy link) for webviews that can't open tabs at all. ## Config consideration No config knob exists today for the sandbox attribute, `allow-popups`, or per-widget network (sandbox strings are hardcoded; only `mcp.apps.sandboxOrigin/sandboxPort` are configurable). This issue deliberately proposes **no new knob**: `host.open` already "needs no grant", so native clients just need to honor the contract the browser Control UI already honors. If maintainers want a kill-switch (e.g. `controlUi.widgetLinks: open|copy|disabled`), that's a product call — but the default should be working links everywhere. ## Repro 1. Push any HTML widget with `x` to a session dashboard (via `show_widget pin:true` or `board.widget.put`). 2. Open the dashboard in browser Control UI → link works. 3. Open the same dashboard in the macOS native app → tap does nothing. ## Labels suggestion `bug`, `bug:behavior`, `impact:ux-friction` (mirroring #131406); CC dashboard/widget maintainers.

| 10:15:06–10:16:09 | guard-triggered Gateway restart (clean boot) |
| **10:17:26–10:22:42** | **6/6 tool-call turns fail** with the 400 above, identical `rawErrorFingerprint`, including brand-new sessions |
| 10:38 | (workaround attempt) model `api` changed to `openai-completions` |
| 10:39:37 | Gateway crashed (watchdog `Crash #1`), restarted 10:40:15 |
| 10:44 | tool calls OK on `openai-completions` |
| 11:01–11:05 | restored the **original** `openai-responses` via config hot reload (no restart): **3/3 tool-call probes OK** (default thinking, `--thinking medium`, and a second tool turn in the same session) |

## Actual error

```json
{"subsystem":"openai-transport","message":"[responses] error provider=deepseek api=openai-responses model=deepseek-flash status=400 code=invalid_request_error type=invalid_request_error message=400 The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. (request_id: 1de2a758-...) requestNumber=2"}
```

- The failing request is always the follow-up request that carries the tool result (`requestNumber=2`).
- Independent of thinking level (`--thinking off` also failed) and of model (`deepseek-v4-pro` failed identically).
- All 6 failures landed on the Gateway that booted at 10:14/10:16; after the 10:40 restart the same config works.

## Hypothesis

The first boot after the upgrade ran while the bundled `deepseek` plugin's data/settings migration was still pending ("Package convergence must wait until the updating parent releases its install records"). If the provider's model metadata is incomplete in that state, the `openai-responses` adapter may not attach/replay the assistant's reasoning item on the post-tool request, which DeepSeek's thinking mode rejects.

Questions:

1. Is this known? Is there a supported way to make the upgrade/doctor **wait for plugin convergence before starting the Gateway** (or to detect "served with half-converged provider" and restart automatically)?
2. Any log/flag that would show the provider metadata state at first boot, so we can confirm rather than guess?

## Notes

- We could not reproduce it afterwards: a plain Gateway restart with `openai-responses` was not possible during the session without dropping the running Gateway, and the embedded (`--local`) probe refuses to run while a Gateway owns the state directory.
- Reporting anyway because the upgraded install was unusable for ~25 minutes, and the initial workaround (`openai-completions`) masked the actual trigger (first-boot state, not the transport).

Happy to run any specific diagnostic (e.g. dump the provider/model metadata at first boot, or test a pre-convergence boot) if you tell me where to look.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Once a subagent's task record is pruned by task retention, its delivery pointer in `subagent_runs` survives — and no supported command can clear it any more. `openclaw tasks dismiss` resolves the *task* first, fails with `Task not found`, and therefore never reaches the pointer that keeps injecting the completion into the requester's context on every single turn.

The result is a permanent, unremovable "Child results awaiting delivery" block: on this host three runs from 2026-08-22 and 2026-08-28 (`delivery=failed`) have been re-injected into every agent turn for 24 and 30 days respectively.

This is adjacent to #151769 but not the same defect. #151769 is about entries whose delivery state is *closed* still rendering. Here the delivery state is legitimately `failed` and the entry is genuinely outstanding — the defect is that the operator has no way to retire it once retention has removed the task record the tooling keys on.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On 2026.9.5, let a spawned subagent run terminate with `delivery=failed` (here: one `outcome=timeout`, two `outcome=error`; the requester was an ordinary WhatsApp DM session).
2. Do not clear it. Wait until the task-record retention window has passed, so the run disappears from `openclaw tasks list`.
3. Try to retire the completion by any supported route.

### Expected behavior

Either the delivery pointer is pruned together with the task record it depends on, or `openclaw tasks dismiss` can still retire a pointer whose task record is gone (the run id and session key are both still present in `subagent_runs`).

### Actual behavior

Every supported route fails, while the context block keeps rendering:

| attempt | result |
|---|---|
| `openclaw tasks dismiss <runId>` | `Task not found: <runId>. Run 'openclaw tasks list' to see recent task ids.` |
| `openclaw tasks dismiss <sessionKey>` | same `Task not found` |
| `openclaw tasks list --json` | 1808 tasks, **zero** matches on any of the three run ids or child session keys — the task records are gone |
| `openclaw tasks maintenance` (preview) | `tasks.pruned: 0`, `taskFlows.pruned: 0`, `sessions.pruned: 0` across all four agents — it does not consider these |
| `openclaw tasks audit --json` | reports `lost: 1` and `delivery_failed: 1` — **2 warnings for 3 stuck entries**, so audit does not see everything the context injects |
| session lifecycle delete on the child session | `Session lifecycle action requires a durable session identity` — the child sessions no longer exist |

### Where the state actually lives

From an official snapshot (`openclaw backup sqlite create --global`, `PRAGMA quick_check` = `ok`, inspected read-only on a private copy — live state untouched), all three are still present in the global `subagent_runs` table, with the requester session as `requester_session_key`:

```
5c7dd043-…  agent:main:subagent:cccd…  2026-08-28 14:05:52
d3d9d804-…  agent:main:subagent:aa91…  2026-08-28 14:21:32
ddb1fe94-…  agent:main:subagent:d9d7…  2026-08-22 07:17:45
```

Scale on this host: 485 rows in `subagent_runs`, 426 for this one requester session, 330 older than 14 days. Only these three still carry an open delivery — so the table is clearly not pruned in step with task retention, and the three stuck ones are simply the entries that never settled.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | `2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)` |
| OS | Linux x64, Node `v24.20.0` |
| Gateway | systemd **user** unit, long-running |
| Requester | ordinary WhatsApp DM session |
| Duration | 24 and 30 days of continuous re-injection at the time of writing |

### Suggested direction

Two options, in order of preference:

1. Make `tasks dismiss` (and `tasks retry`) resolve against the delivery pointer rather than the task record, so a run id from `subagent_runs` is enough. That also fixes the audit blind spot, since the same lookup can enumerate them.
2. Prune `subagent_runs` pointers in `tasks maintenance` when their task record has been pruned and the delivery state is terminal-but-unsettled, under the same retention policy.

Either way `tasks audit` should count all outstanding pointers, not a subset — the 2-of-3 discrepancy above is what made this hard to see in the first place.

I deliberately did **not** hand-edit the live state database, so the three entries are still there and this stays reproducible. Happy to run any read-only query on this host.

issues.body:
## Summary

On a long-lived (13-day, ~310k token) WeChat-bridge session, the agent repeatedly received **user prompts that the user never sent**. Those prompts exist in `trajectory_runtime_events.data.prompt` but have **no corresponding `transcript_events` user row** — so the user (looking at Control UI) and the agent (looking at its own context) disagree about what was said. This is not the same as #143632 (no serialized context envelope in the body) nor #148338 (prompts are not empty).

The same session also shows **system-internal strings being submitted as user prompts** and one **runtime event persisted as a `role: "user"` transcript row**, which points at prompt assembly / inbound dispatch rather than at the model.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.1** (gitSha `ad6fe23`), npm install, gateway local (`gateway --port 18789`)
- Windows 10.0.19045 (x64), Node **v24.15.0**
- Channel: `openclaw-weixin` (community WeChat bridge), single DM conversation, single account
- Model: `deepseek/deepseek-flash` (1M ctx), `thinking: high`
- Session: created 2026-09-05 during a `session-sqlite` migration (jsonl → sqlite), still running today (~2,930 transcript events)
- Config relevant bits: `contextPruning: {mode: "cache-ttl", ttl: "5m"}`, `compaction: {mode: "safeguard", keepRecentTokens: 50000}`, `heartbeat: {every: "60m", isolatedSession: true, lightContext: true}`
- Heavy use of **background exec** during the affected window (long downloads, benchmarks) → many `async command completion` events

## Observed behaviour

1. **Phantom user messages.** Three prompts were submitted to the model that the user confirms he never sent. For each of them:
   - `transcript_events`: **no** `role:"user"` row
   - `trajectory_runtime_events.prompt` (the input actually submitted): present
   - `trajectory_runtime_events.messages` (the history array shipped with the run): **absent** → rules out "history replay"
   - Later they appear in `assistantTexts` (the agent quoting them) and then again in later prompts after the user copy-pastes the agent's reply back (the bridge has no quote/reply feature, so the user must paste).

2. **System-internal strings submitted as user prompts.** In the same window, `prompt.submitted` events include prompts that are clearly not user text:

```
[Queued user message from a previous active turn; preserved as context only. Continue with the active prompt below.]
[OpenClaw heartbeat poll] An async command completion event was triggered, but user delivery is disabled ...
```

```
The previous assistant turn recorded reasoning but did not produce a user-visible answer.
Continue from that partial turn and produce the visible answer now. Do not restate the reasoning or restart from scratch.
```
(observed 6×)

```
[System] Your previous turn was interrupted by a gateway restart while OpenClaw was waiting on tool/model work. ...
```

```
[Malformed diagnostic JSON redacted]
```

3. **A runtime event persisted as a user message.** The event text below was written into `transcript_events` with `role: "user"`:

```
Continue the OpenClaw runtime event.
```

4. **Message splitting.** One inbound user message of **245 characters** was submitted as **two separate prompts** (first half, then second half as its own prompt).

5. **Duplicate submission.** The same 245-character message was submitted twice, verbatim, ~4 minutes apart (two distinct runIds).

6. **Timeline skew.** The same content appears as a `prompt.submitted` at `15:22:43Z` and as a `transcript_events` user row at `15:36:24Z` (~14 min apart).

## Impact

- The agent answers questions nobody asked, and quotes "user statements" that do not exist → it makes decisions on non-existent instructions.
- User and agent end up with **two different versions of the conversation**; the user reasonably concludes the agent is hallucinating, and the agent reasonably concludes the user forgot what he said.
- It is self-reinforcing: the agent quotes the phantom text → the quote appears in `assistantTexts` → it re-enters later prompts.

## Hypothesis

Prompt assembly appears to **merge** three things into one prompt when they coincide:

- a **queued user message** ("preserved as context only")
- a **heartbeat poll** event
- an **async command completion** event

If the "preserved as context only" queued item (or the internal string itself) is promoted to the *active* prompt, the agent will answer old/internal content as if it were a fresh user request. The three coincide exactly in the window where the phantom messages appear — and in this session they coincided because of heavy background-command usage.

## Notes / limits

- `trace.metadata` for the affected runs is redacted (`config: {redacted, runtime}`, `metadata: "[Truncated]"`), so the run's trigger source could not be inspected further from the client side.
- `standing_intents`, `session_pending_inputs` and `context_engine_turn_outbox` were all **empty** at inspection time.
- Persistence gap is separate: even the legitimately-injected prompts were **not** written to `transcript_events`, so a DB-only audit cannot see them.

## Related issues

- #143632 — inbound messages re-delivered with serialized internal context envelope (iMessage)
- #148338 — empty inbound envelopes trigger phantom turn scheduling (closed)
- #100368 — withheld finals stay in agent context, desynchronizing memory
- #143334 — queued user messages starved / settle-yield interaction

issues.body:
## Summary

On 2026.9.4 the Control UI WebChat rendered a **final assistant reply** (the turn's closing answer, not mid-turn commentary) **twice in the same session view** — two identical full copies stacked vertically. The gateway's transcript store holds exactly **one** copy of that message with a clean block structure, so this is a client-side rendering/reconciliation defect, not a persistence duplicate.

A companion symptom observed repeatedly over the past weeks on the same build family: portions of **final conversation content intermittently appear inside the collapsible "process" area** (the folded lane that normally hosts tool calls / thinking / commentary), visible only after expanding. Both symptoms point at the same suspicion: stream-segment → lane reconciliation assigning final-reply content to the wrong render lane (or duplicating it across lanes).

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.4 (`3a9d69d`), npm global install, launchd
- OS: macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Node v26.8.2
- Channel: WebChat (Control UI Dashboard, direct 1:1 session, single `main` agent)
- Model: kimi/k3 (cloud provider, thinking enabled)

## Observed behavior

1. ~20:53 local (12:53:24Z): a multi-section assistant final reply completes and renders once, normally.
2. Minutes later, scrolling the session shows the **entire reply duplicated** — two full identical copies, each with its own copy/branch affordances. (Sanitized screenshots available on request.)
3. No reload, no gateway restart, no new turn in between. The duplicate persisted until at least ~20 min later.
4. The turn's completion footer reports a single run (~1 min 22 s, ~2 k output tokens) matching one copy, and the two rendered copies are byte-identical (including tables and section order). A second model call or an in-generation self-repetition would have produced either two completion footers or a doubled token count — so this is one generation rendered twice.
5. Separately and repeatedly (many times over past weeks): normal conversation text is found **inside the collapsed process fold** rather than in the highlighted main lane; expanding the fold reveals content that should have been rendered as regular conversation.

## Storage-layer verification (store is clean)

Method: copied the agent SQLite (`openclaw-agent.sqlite` + WAL) aside and inspected `transcript_events` for the affected session.

- The duplicated reply exists **exactly once** (`seq=39`, one event, unique message id).
- Its content blocks are: `thinking` (`thinkingSignature: "reasoning_content"`) + `text` (**no** `textSignature`) — i.e., correctly stored as a final answer, **not** tagged `phase:"commentary"`.
- For contrast, genuine mid-turn narration in the same session carries `textSignature: {"v":1,"id":"commentary-0-<hash>","phase":"commentary"}` as expected — so the lane-tagging mechanism itself is present and working at write time.

- Independent corroboration from the projection side: a sanitized session-history readback of the same message returns it exactly once, with clean `thinking` + `text` content blocks and no stream-segment/fallback marker on the text part.

Conclusion: the second on-screen copy has no storage counterpart; duplication happens entirely in the WebChat render/reconciliation path.

## Why this looks like a new variant of the commentary-reconciliation family

Three fixed issues addressed commentary-lane duplication with the same "storage clean, screen duplicated" signature:

- #134276 — commentary rendered 3× (fixed 2026-08-31)
- #134971 — constant `itemId: "commentary-0"` breaking stream-segment reconciliation (fixed 2026-09-01)
- #144471 — completed commentary item overtaking its final text delta (fixed 2026-09-10)

This report differs in one important way: **the duplicated unit is the final reply itself, which carries no commentary signature**. The earlier fixes targeted commentary-lane reconciliation; on 2026.9.4 a final-lane message can still be duplicated (and final content can still land in the collapsible process lane). Whatever ownership/dedup rule distinguishes "streamed preview" from "persisted final" appears to still have an uncovered branch.

Cross-linking the umbrella tracker #69208 (this instance has a provably clean store, so it is a render-layer sibling rather than a transcript-duplication instance) and #130141 (projection-layer sibling where live messages vanish and reappear — different symptom, possibly shared invalidation path).

## Repro notes

Intermittent; no deterministic trigger identified yet. The duplicate-render instance reported here and the earlier vanish-then-reappear instance on the same build family (documented in #130141) both occurred on long turns with tool calls interleaved (multiple exec/read calls before the final reply). Happy to capture gateway logs, a HAR/WS frame dump, or run a patched build with extra reconciliation logging if a maintainer points at the right surface.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Tapping an automation's reply notification on Android opens the correct conversation but renders the app's empty state, so the report the notification just displayed is not reachable from it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pair the Android app as a node (app `2026.8.2`, `versionCode=2026080201`) against a `2026.9.3` Gateway.
2. Background the app.
3. Run an automation whose payload is an agent turn in an isolated session with `delivery.mode: announce` to a chat channel — here a daily `apt`/`fwupdmgr` report:
   ```
   openclaw automations run <jobId>
   ```
4. A notification arrives on the `openclaw.chat.replies` channel containing the full report text.
5. Tap the notification body.

### Expected behavior

Tapping opens the conversation showing the report that the notification displayed.

### Actual behavior

The app opens (`ai.openclaw.app/.MainActivity`) and the conversation picker resolves to the correct automation conversation — it reads `klawlikula` / `ubuntu Security U…` — but the message area shows the onboarding empty state:

```
Ready when you are
Start with a prompt, or use voice.
  1 Catch me up      Summarize recent threads and next steps.
  2 Plan the work    Turn a goal into an actionable checklist.
  3 Use this phone   Ask OpenClaw to use Android capabilities.
```

That is the explicit empty state, not an unscrolled transcript. The notification content is not reachable from the conversation it links to; the delivered copy has to be found manually in the chat-channel conversation instead.

The content exists Gateway-side. The run that produced the notification is session `068ab4a6…`, 12 transcript events, whose final assistant message is exactly the notification text:

```
16:17:43 [user]       [cron:<jobId> ubuntu-security-upgrades] Ubuntu Package Security check …
16:17:47 [assistant]  toolCall exec
16:17:48 [toolResult] …
16:17:52 [assistant]  toolCall exec
16:17:53 [toolResult] …
16:17:57 [assistant]  🖥️  Ubuntu Security Report — 2026-09-10 … Gateway 📊 0 upgradable · 0 security …
```

So the Gateway holds the transcript, the notification renders its text, and the app shows the conversation as empty.

### OpenClaw version

Gateway 2026.9.3; Android app 2026.8.2 (`versionCode=2026080201`, sideloaded `thirdParty` flavor from the v2026.8.2 release asset)

### Operating system

Gateway: Ubuntu (Linux 6.8.0-139-generic, x64). Device: Android, OnePlus 8T (KB2005).

### Install method

Gateway: npm global, systemd user service. App: `adb install` of `OpenClaw-Android.apk` from the v2026.8.2 GitHub release.

### Model

`llama-cpp/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat` — incidental; the defect is in notification-to-conversation routing, not model output.

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> llama-cpp (local llama-server). Not involved in the reported behavior.

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

Notification post, from `adb logcat` (device clock 16:17:57, matching the assistant reply above to the second):

```shell
09-10 16:17:57  NotificationRecord(pkg=ai.openclaw.app tag=openclaw.chat.<digest>
  channel=openclaw.chat.replies importance=4 category=msg groupKey=openclaw.chat
  shortcut=openclaw-chat-<digest> actions=1 locusId=LocusId[38_chars])
```

Tap, from `adb logcat`:

```shell
09-10 16:12:46  OplusNotificationLogger--> NOTIFICATION_CLICK --> onNotificationClicked
  isActivityIntent: true  key: 0|ai.openclaw.app|1|openclaw.chat.<digest>|10319
  reason = jump to app
```

Foreground activity after the tap:

```shell
topResumedActivity=ActivityRecord{… ai.openclaw.app/.MainActivity …}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Captured but not attached (local `gh` 2.45.0 predates `--attach`); happy to add them on request:

1. Notification in the shade showing the full report and a `Reply` action.
2. Post-tap screen showing the correct conversation selected in the picker with the onboarding empty state in the message area.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Android app users receiving notifications for automation output.
Severity: Medium — no data loss, and the content remains reachable elsewhere, but the notification's primary action leads to a dead end and the user must search for the delivered copy manually.
Frequency: 2/2 observed taps, on two separate automation runs.
Consequence: A notification advertises content and links to an empty conversation, so the fastest path to the report is the one that fails.

### Additional information

One inference is explicitly flagged rather than asserted: I could not decode the notification tag digest (`openclaw.chat.<sha>`, built from `stableDigest(gatewayStableId, agentId, sessionKey)`) back to a session key, so the identification of *which* conversation the notification targeted rests on two corroborating signals — the notification post time matching the cron session's final assistant reply exactly (16:17:57), and the conversation label shown in the app's picker after the tap. That is correlation, not the identifier itself; whoever owns this code can read the target directly.

Worth noting the delivered result is also mirrored into the chat-channel conversation (entries observed at 16:06:33 and 16:12:22 in the Discord channel session), which is where the content is actually readable in the app. Whether the notification should target that conversation instead, or the automation conversation should render its own transcript, looks like a product decision rather than an obvious one-line fix.

Filed alongside #144306, which concerns addressing a node as an automation delivery target; this report is about the app-side link from an existing notification.

issues.body:
# Heartbeat NO_REPLY re-commits and re-delivers the last final reply (2026.9.3)

## Summary

After a heartbeat poll that correctly returns `NO_REPLY`, the session's **last final assistant reply is re-committed to history and re-delivered to the channel** ~3 seconds later. Reproduced 3× in a row on 2026.9.3 (stable), always with the same timing pattern.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.3** (1391f7c), installed via npm (stable)
- Node v24.21.0, Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 kernel 6.8)
- Channel: Telegram (direct chat)
- Heartbeat config: `agents.defaults.heartbeat.every: "30m"`, model `ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4-flash:0731`
- No custom heartbeat prompt; default HEARTBEAT.md behavior

## Reproduction pattern (3× observed)

All timestamps UTC, 2026-09-10:

| # | Time | Event |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | 04:59:34 | Heartbeat poll → `NO_REPLY` (correct, silent) |
|   | 04:59:40 | **Duplicate** of the final reply from 04:40 re-committed + re-delivered to Telegram |
| 2 | 05:29:34 | Heartbeat poll → `NO_REPLY` (correct, silent) |
|   | 05:29:40 | **Duplicate** of the final reply from 05:08 re-committed + re-delivered |
| 3 | 05:59:34 | Heartbeat poll → `NO_REPLY` (correct, silent) |
|   | 05:59:42 | **Duplicate** of the final reply from 05:30 re-committed + re-delivered |

Control case: heartbeat polls that return a normal reply (e.g. `HEARTBEAT_OK`) do **not** produce duplicates.

## Expected behavior

A `NO_REPLY` heartbeat turn must not touch the last committed final reply — no re-commit, no re-delivery.

## Actual behavior

~3–8 s after a silent heartbeat, the previous final assistant message is committed again and sent again to the channel, producing user-visible duplicate messages.

## Suspected area

Session history commit / reply dispatch after silent (`NO_REPLY`) heartbeat turns — likely a regression in the 2026.9.x session-history or reply-dispatcher changes (persistent sessions / history commit rework).

## Workaround (confirmed effective)

Set `agents.defaults.heartbeat.isolatedSession: true` — heartbeat runs in an isolated session and can no longer re-commit the main session. Hot-reloads without restart.

## Impact

User-visible duplicate messages in chat after every silent heartbeat; noisy and confusing in DMs and groups. High annoyance, low data-integrity risk.

issues.body:
## Summary

When the memory index lives in the same agent database as sessions and transcripts, the final
publish step of a memory index rebuild runs as **one `IMMEDIATE` transaction** that rewrites every
index table. On this host that transaction takes **≥ 5 s**, which is exactly the `busy_timeout` of
the shared agent-DB write path. Any write that arrives inside that window fails at `step=begin`.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | 2026.9.2 (3928bad), npm global install |
| OS | Windows 11 (10.0.26200) x64 |
| Node | v22.23.2 |
| Memory backend | builtin `memory-core` |
| Embedding provider | ollama `bge-m3:latest`, 1024 dims |
| Agents | 1 (`main`) |
| Index size | 14,098 chunks, 1,881 sources, 14,372 embedding-cache rows |
| Agent DB | `openclaw-agent.sqlite` 851 MiB — memory index, sessions and transcripts in **one** DB |
| Sessions | 65, cron sessions firing at :00/:30 |

## Symptom

18 occurrences overnight (00:02:20 → 08:30:30, spaced roughly 30–45 min), every one with the same
shape:

```
Failed to write agent database
  operation = agent.write
  step      = begin
  totalMs   = 5402   (attempts = 2)
  SQLiteError: database is locked
```

`step = begin` means the writer never got the write lock (as opposed to failing mid-transaction),
and `totalMs ≈ 5400` matches the busy wait being exhausted plus retry overhead.

## Where the two sides meet

- Writer: `runSqliteImmediateTransaction` uses `busyTimeoutMs ?? 5e3` (`dist/node-sqlite-*.js`).
- Holder: `publishMemoryDatabaseTables` (`dist/manager-vector-warning-*.js:425`) performs
  `DELETE` + `INSERT ... SELECT` across `memory_index_sources`, `memory_index_chunks`, the FTS and
  `vec0` tables, plus the embedding-cache prune, inside a **single** `IMMEDIATE` transaction.
- Because index, sessions and transcripts share one database file, publishing and `agent.write`
  contend for the same write lock, and a rebuild's last step is a multi-second exclusive window.

## Measurement (on a copy of the DB, `PRAGMA quick_check` = ok)

| Case | Content | Publish total | Concurrent writer (`busy_timeout = 5000`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | chunks + sources (~300 MB) | 2.68 s (write 1.89, commit 0.79) | started at +0.5 s, waited 1.86 s → ok |
| E2 | chunks + sources + cache (~650 MB) | **5.41 s** (write 3.88, commit 1.53) | started at +0.5 s, waited **4.38 s** → ok by 0.6 s |

On an idle disk the publish already sits at the writer's budget. With a live WAL, checkpoints and
the FTS/`vec0` tables inside the same transaction it goes past it — which is what the overnight
signature looks like.

## Expected behavior / possible directions

- Publish in bounded batches (per table, or chunked `INSERT ... SELECT`) so the exclusive write
  window stays well under 5 s.
- Or give the agent write path a budget that is independent of the publish path, since the two are
  unrelated workloads sharing one lock.
- Separately: because the driver here is synchronous and runs on the Gateway event loop, the same
  window is also a window in which the process cannot service other work (the failed-shutdown side
  of this is tracked in #142701).

## Honest limits

The mechanism above is reproduced on a DB copy; per-event attribution of all 18 overnight failures
is inference, because the Gateway's temp log rolls over (approximately 1 MB) and the earlier window
was gone by the time we looked. Recorded here so a maintainer can weigh the evidence accordingly.

issues.body:
## Summary

`memory-wiki` bridge operations can fail with a false `not-found` / `ENOENT` on a vault stored on a WSL Windows mount (`/mnt/c/...`), even though the same target exists and is readable from the same runtime. Moving the vault to native WSL storage avoids the failure.

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.9.3` (the behaviour began after a recent 2026.9 update)
- WSL2, Linux runtime user
- `memory-wiki` in `bridge` mode, Obsidian render mode
- Vault located below `/mnt/c/...` (WSL DrvFS/9p mount)

## Reproduction

1. Configure a bridge-mode memory-wiki vault below `/mnt/c/...`.
2. Run `openclaw wiki bridge import` (or a command that triggers bridge import).
3. The bridge sometimes rejects an expected generated source page with an error like:

   ```text
   Refusing to write imported source page (not-found):
   sources/bridge-...-memory-YYYY-MM-DD-....md:
   file not found | not-found | ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '/mnt/c/.../sources/bridge-...md'
   ```

## Observed behaviour

At failure time, the exact target passed all of the following in the same runtime user/environment:

- `ls -l`, `stat`, `realpath -e`, and `test -e`
- Node `fs.existsSync` and `lstatSync`
- Python `os.path.exists` and `lstat`

The bridge resolver produced the expected relative target under the configured vault root; provenance pointed to the normal workspace memory source. There were no symlinks, traversal components, permission failures, or root-boundary violations.

The failure appears to occur in the guarded fs-safe `stat`/write path only. A subsequent guarded fs-safe stat can succeed for the same target.

## Workaround / confirmation

The vault was relocated unchanged to a native WSL filesystem path. A controlled `bridge import` → `compile` → `lint` cycle then completed successfully with no transient retry and no missing-source error.

## Expected behaviour

Bridge import should not reject an existing expected vault target merely because a transient guarded filesystem lookup on DrvFS/9p returns `ENOENT`. If maintaining the strict boundary checks, bounded retry limited to expected in-root targets and only `not-found` errors would preserve the safety model while handling this filesystem behaviour.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.10.8 with #186081 applied, two successful Discord `message(final:true)` replies produced native interruption records instead of normal completion and lacked persisted assistant answers, leaving misleading interruption context, repeated requests in later inputs, and missing request/answer pairs in conversation capture.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed sequence in one persistent Codex app-server thread:

1. Start a fresh session in an always-on Discord guild text channel with recent-history recovery enabled.
2. Send `reply only "60"`. In this run, the agent answered using:
   ```js
   await tools.message({ action: "send", message: "60", final: true });
   ```
3. After settlement, send `reply only "61"`. The agent again used `message(final:true)` to send the answer to the current source.
4. Send `reply only "62"`. The agent answered with ordinary assistant final text.
5. Ask how many copies of the original `reply only "60"` request are in context, then send `reply only "63"` and `reply only "64"`, allowing each turn to settle. These received ordinary finals.
6. Inspect the native rollout's user-role inputs, OpenClaw's canonical transcript and runtime trajectory, and the conversation-capture output.

The agent selected the reply routes itself; the numeric prompts do not guarantee that selection. To exercise the affected branch, the agent must actually issue the final message-tool send shown above.

### Expected behavior

The ordinary-final controls in the same session record assistant text, complete normally, appear in conversation capture, and are omitted from subsequent recent-history injection.

Confirmed final message-tool replies should likewise be recorded as completed assistant answers, with the delivered content available to transcript readers and accepted-turn capture. #186081 explicitly supports terminal message-tool source-reply mirrors as completion evidence: [transcript projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/495d9c3dfa55f5d486ab4a11211c54cbd106a59b/src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-text.ts#L121).

Successful final-tool completion should also complete the native turn normally, without `turn_aborted`, an `aborted by user` tool result, or an interruption warning inserted into the continuing thread. The successful delivery and completed answer should agree across native history, OpenClaw's transcript, and downstream capture, as they do for the ordinary-final controls.

The false-interruption mechanism was previously reported in #111019. It is included deliberately here because the same successful-final path exhibits both problems, and the requested outcome requires both to be fixed: recording the answer alone would leave false interruption context, while changing the stop mechanism alone would not establish that the delivered answer reaches persistence and capture. This does not assert that the interruption flag itself causes the missing transcript row.

### Actual behavior

For both tool-delivered answers, the Discord send succeeded and the canonical transcript retained a successful tool receipt, but its only rows for the turn were:

```text
user request
assistant toolCall: message(... final:true)
toolResult: successful Discord delivery
```

There was no assistant-answer text row or terminal source-reply mirror.

The native rollout recorded `turn_aborted` with reason `interrupted`, and the outer code-mode call received `aborted by user`. However, OpenClaw's own runtime trajectory recorded **`aborted:false`, `promptError:null`, and `status:"success"`** for both runs. No user cancellation occurred.

Both native turns also persisted a developer-role `<turn_aborted>` message saying that the previous turn was interrupted on purpose and that tools may have partially executed (quoted below). This is not merely a status label in a UI: misleading interruption guidance is recorded inside the continuing native thread. The underlying message-tool delivery receipt says the send settled successfully, while the outer code-mode result says it was aborted. No resulting model-behavior change was measured.

The later inputs repeatedly included the original `60` and `61` requests under `Recent chat history:`. The ordinary-final controls did not recur. This is old text injected into new requests, not duplicate standalone Discord event delivery.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.8, source/build commit `495d9c3dfa55f5d486ab4a11211c54cbd106a59b`.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04; Gateway running Node.js 26.12.1.

### Install method

Source checkout with a built distribution, launched using Node.js and `dist/index.js gateway`.

### Model

openai/gpt-6-luna

### Provider / routing chain

Discord -> OpenClaw Gateway -> bundled native Codex app-server harness -> OpenAI.

### Additional provider/model setup details

- One persistent native thread throughout the observed sequence.
- Native rollout reports Codex CLI version `0.164.0`.
- Guild text channel with always-on activation and recent-history recovery enabled.
- Affected capture consumer: third-party `openclaw-universal-capture` v0.7.1, using the context-engine `commitTurn` interface.
- The missing answer rows and continued history injection were inspected independently of the capture plugin's output.

### Logs

Selected fields from stored events, October 28, 2026, UTC. Private identifiers and unrelated payload fields omitted; this is a condensed evidence transcription, not a raw full log export.

```text
Answer 60:
09:02:40.845  native tool call: message({action:"send", message:"60", final:true})
09:02:41.913  Gateway: codex app-server turn released after terminal dynamic tool result
09:02:41.922  native outer tool output: aborted by user after 1.1s
09:02:41.977  OpenClaw model.completed: aborted=false, promptError=null, assistantTexts=[]
09:02:41.978  OpenClaw session.ended: status=success, promptError=null
09:02:41.979  native turn_aborted: reason=interrupted

Answer 61:
09:03:00.563  native tool call: message({action:"send", message:"61", final:true})
09:03:02.585  Gateway: codex app-server turn released after terminal dynamic tool result
09:03:02.617  native outer tool output: aborted by user after 2.0s
09:03:02.723  native turn_aborted: reason=interrupted
09:03:02.743  OpenClaw model.completed: aborted=false, promptError=null, assistantTexts=[]
09:03:02.750  OpenClaw session.ended: status=success, promptError=null

Ordinary-final controls:
09:03:22.300  native task_complete: last_agent_message="62"
09:28:26.657  native task_complete: last_agent_message="63"
09:44:47.251  native task_complete: last_agent_message="64"
```

For both affected turns, the underlying message-tool result retained these fields:

```text
isError: false
details.deliveryStatus: sent
details.sourceReplyRoute: current-source
details.messageDelivery.status: settled
details.messageDelivery.partialDelivery: false
details.messageDelivery.sourceReplyDelivered: true
```

Each result also contained a Discord platform message ID.

The native rollout contains this exact developer-role message after each affected send, at `09:02:41.955` and `09:03:02.693` UTC:

```text
<turn_aborted>
The previous turn was interrupted on purpose. Any running unified exec processes may still be running in the background. If any tools/commands were aborted, they may have partially executed.
</turn_aborted>
```

This current wording differs from the older user-interruption marker quoted in #111019; the current outer tool result still explicitly says `aborted by user`.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Evidence inspected: native JSONL rollout, canonical SQLite transcript, stored runtime trajectory, Gateway log, and Markdown conversation capture. Private raw transcripts are not attached.

A read-only replay through the installed capture selector, using actual persisted transcript ranges and configured options, returned:

- Tool-only `60`: zero capture entries.
- Tool-only `61`: zero capture entries.
- Ordinary final `62`: the expected request/answer entry.

The selector requires terminal assistant text, not an abort flag. Enabling commentary in the replay did not recover the affected answers because their text exists only inside tool-call arguments. Exact historical `commitTurn` invocation receipts were not retained after outbox acknowledgment; this replay verifies selection behavior, not a separately logged historical callback payload.


### Impact and severity

- **Affected:** the observed Discord channel using the bundled Codex app-server harness; its recent-history inputs and Universal Capture output.
- **Frequency:** both observed final message-tool replies exhibited the defect; the four ordinary-final control turns did not.
- **Severity:** completion-state consistency, conversation-record completeness, and context-quality defect. Delivered replies are represented as interrupted native work and are not retained as completed conversational answers.
- **Consequence:** native history retains false interruption guidance and aborted tool results; request/answer pairs are omitted from capture; answered requests are repeatedly inserted into later native inputs. No billing increase, resulting model-behavior change, or broader channel prevalence was measured.

### Additional information

Related issues and fix:

- #185844: original recent-history reinjection report.
- #186081: merged reconciliation fix, present in this build.
- #111019: earlier open report of clean final-tool completion producing false native interruption markers. This report intentionally overlaps that symptom, provides current-build evidence, and asks that native completion and answer persistence be addressed together rather than closing the problem after repairing only one side.

Source inspection at the tested commit:

1. [Terminal-tool lifecycle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/495d9c3dfa55f5d486ab4a11211c54cbd106a59b/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-lifecycle-controller.ts#L175) calls `interruptTurn(..., {locallyCompleted:true})`; [finalization](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/495d9c3dfa55f5d486ab4a11211c54cbd106a59b/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-finalize.ts#L287) accepts that local completion as success.
2. Discord [send actions run locally](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/495d9c3dfa55f5d486ab4a11211c54cbd106a59b/extensions/discord/src/channel-actions.ts#L22). [Destination-history recording](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/495d9c3dfa55f5d486ab4a11211c54cbd106a59b/src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts#L79) skips the producing conversation on the assumption it already recorded the turn.
3. The dedicated source-reply mirror is invoked through [Gateway RPC result handling](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/495d9c3dfa55f5d486ab4a11211c54cbd106a59b/src/gateway/server-methods/message-operation-result.ts#L131), rather than that local path.
4. [Recent-history reconciliation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/495d9c3dfa55f5d486ab4a11211c54cbd106a59b/src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.ts#L83) requests terminal message-tool reply evidence, but the observed turns have no such answer record.

These inspected paths explain a transcript-ownership gap consistent with the stored evidence. No instrumented replay of the complete delivery/persistence path or candidate fix was performed.

A complete repair should be verified through the composed final-tool path:

- The confirmed final send completes without a native aborted/interrupted outcome or a false interruption message in the continuing thread.
- The delivered answer is persisted exactly once with terminal source-turn evidence and is included in accepted-turn capture.
- Subsequent recent-history selection omits the unchanged answered request.

Relabeling OpenClaw's top-level result is insufficient: it already says success in these examples. Merely hiding an interruption message from display would not establish correct native completion. Conversely, suppressing the interruption does not by itself prove answer persistence.

A regression test should cover real final-tool delivery, native completion, canonical persistence, subsequent history selection, and accepted-turn capture. Manually seeding a correct terminal mirror would bypass the missing producer step. Preserve the distinction from progress-only replies, failed or partial sends, dry runs, other destinations, and genuine cancellation. The report specifies the required outcome, not an unverified choice of native protocol or stopping strategy.

No last-known-good version for this specific missing-answer defect was established. No code, configuration or runtime changes were made during diagnosis.

issues.body:
A scheduled job `openclaw backup create --to extssd --no-include-workspace …` fails daily with "Backup output must not be written inside a source path: ~/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-backup-owned-XXXX/archive.tar.gz is inside ~/.openclaw".

`backupRemote` creates scratch with `createBackupScratchDirectory(os.tmpdir())`, and under the Gateway TMPDIR resolves to `~/.openclaw/tmp`. Unlike local `backup create` (which uses `chooseBackupTempRoot` with a fallback), the offsite path never checks for overlap with the sources.

Workaround: set TMPDIR outside the state dir or pass `--output`.

Version: OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (59cb447), macOS.

## Problem

Cloud worker lifecycle and workspace settlement improvements are mixed across two large, dependent commits. They need independently reviewable fixes and coherent retained-disk changes before adoption in OpenClaw.

## Published first wave

All four first-wave PRs are merged into main: #188802, #188805, #188807 and #188817. They retain existing configuration and Gateway checkpoint durability; no deployment was performed. The production counts and initial proof below describe the original extraction candidates; final landing evidence is recorded in each PR.

|---|---|---:|
| #188802 | Linux platform certificate registration before fresh/cached enrollment | +20/−1 |

| #188817 | Deferred GitHub publication with frozen turn/session snapshots and queued-request reuse | +111/−74 |

Net production growth: **212 lines**. Each has focused regression proof and clean independent full-candidate review. Parent verification matched every published tree to its reviewed implementation and checked contributor credit and work-session links. The checkpoint fixture imports 263,529 bytes, then 1,580 bytes, then zero for an unchanged follow-up; this is work-count evidence, not a live latency benchmark.

Original implementation CI: #188817 passed its then-current exact-head aggregate gate. The original heads of the first three failed the test-line ratchet on unchanged inherited debt: exact main-parent excesses are 1,025, 1,025, and 1,013 lines respectively. Each PR adds exactly matching allocation for its own regression tests. Detailed attribution is in each PR; the shared baseline was not raised.

## Published second wave

[PR #188914](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188914) rejects new worker-turn and remote-exec input before claiming it when the exact attached provider lease cannot be qualified. Unavailable observations preserve ownership for retry; dormant devices retain reconnect behavior; confirmed loss uses the existing cleanup owner. It does not allocate a replacement or replay input.

- **Merged later at source7ed59f9b; see current landing evidence below.** Historical intermediate published head: `da87c635972f1cf8aada5fdd4410defc0012388d`. Original implementation proof below applies to head `8ac83252f073102fadf7dae6ee08a41835c7c808`, tree `7752a51579578515de57cd14993f061b31397951`; the later same-PR repair updates its direct consumers and fixtures.
- Six production files: **+199/−42 (net +157)**. Tests/support: +232/−3 with exactly 229 allocated regression lines; no shared baseline increase. All five implementation PRs total **+590/−221 (net +369) production lines**.
- Production-path baseline reproduction: 1 input claim / 0 inspections. Fixed: 0 claims / 1 exact-lease inspection. Real SQLite/service/launcher and recovery coverage qualifies 73 cases through separate receipts: 71 passed in the combined run, followed by both repaired fixture cases passing. No claim of a single 73-case final pass.
- Targeted type checks, type-aware lint, formatting, pre-commit, diff and documentation-link checks passed. Fresh independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P3 findings. Provider I/O is fixture-backed; no live provider allocation or model-driven Gateway run was performed.
- Published tree, contributor trailers, and both exact Work sessions links verified. Exact-head aggregate CI for `da87c635972f1cf8aada5fdd4410defc0012388d` is **successful**, rechecked October 31 at 05:02 UTC: [ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41160199574/job/124420827764). Production and test type checks also succeeded on that head.
- No schema, configuration, public provider API, same-node restart, retained-disk behavior, merge or deployment is included.

## Final delivery — November 4, 2026

**All 13 original implementation PRs are merged, plus provisioning repair #191006.** Final restart [#188981](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188981) merged at03:00UTC as `c1739437a5b7fcaa68291c47b7110f4d1cce26f7`, from reviewed `9195ba46`. Native outcome52630618 is complete; owner verified PR-worktree/preparation-branch cleanup. [Completion receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188981#issuecomment-6621337841).

Crabbox v0.81.0 (including #3001) is adopted in source. Released-runtime local SSH/Gateway/node proof covers74.1s reconnect,70.2s same-PID retry and cancellation/revocation retirement; original installation/remote-rehash/oracle limits remain. Repaired installed attempt7 passed activation, worker write, durable settlement, public Move and cleanup;125 files retained/rehashed. R5 upgrade/Doctor/cold-reopen scope and interrupted-wrapper limits are preserved. Source comparisons justify bounded reuse, not one final-main integrated suite. No deployment, live-profile activation, new release or paid Azure/model allocation.

**CI remains failed:** primary41744955659/1 retains112 inherited test lines of debt unchanged by828 new lines/credits; optional scaffold41744955439/2 timed out downloading the npm archive before validation completed. Protected inherited-failure admission completed with enforced security/review/live-writer checks; no baseline, credential, grant or rule changed, no third scaffold retry, no green-CI claim.

Production sums against actual landing parents: thirteen original PRs **+5,767/-1,316 (net+4,451)**; including #191006 **+5,805/-1,321 (net+4,484)**. Restart alone:16files,+414/-29. These are summed deltas, not unique final footprint. Separate Crabbox#3001:+201/-18.

Delivery order: certificates/Stop/checkpoints/frozen publication and exact-lease admission → immutable receipts → original-disk authority/recovery → current-disk I/O/frozen capture → Move/lifecycle/paused consumers → opt-in activation; restart is the parallel recovery slice. Mirrored mode remains default. Opt-in disk authority removes per-turn Gateway file backups: missing/mismatched disks hold recovery, confirmed disk loss can lose private work, and snapshots do not back up subsequent writes. Source-only reconstruction remains rejected.

### Historical acceptance checkpoints

The following retain original observations and failures; the final status above supersedes earlier pending/unqualified statements.

**Source closeout complete through S9:** all three native lifecycle/S8/S9 outcomes are complete, with exact-head CI, main containment, landed-tree composition, Galin credit and cleanup verified. The donor rule is **not non-lossy**: equality of the accepted file manifest and pinned source does not prove equality of Git history or publication membership.

[Investigation and proof session](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/06ccfc21-23e4-4a52-b337-0c6cfa8b4966)

## Accepted feature contracts — historical specification

Exact-lease turn admission is implemented in #188914 without changing public-provider or storage contracts. Source-only reconstruction is not currently a safe minimal extraction; it needs the positive evidence described above. Galin accepted the same-node restart and retained lifecycle proposal, then explicitly requested disk-authoritative Azure Sandbox workspaces in smaller PRs. Implementation remains subject to the new public-provider and persistence contracts under [the storage review checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes).

### 1. Same enrolled-node restart

Add one optional `WorkerProvider.resumeNode` capability to the existing provider contract, with exact lease ID, enrolled device ID, saved runtime identity, cancellation signal and live-authority callback. The runtime-refresh owner calls it only for an exclusively attached dedicated machine with no live enrolled-node process. Crabbox verifies retained runtime/config/device identity and process death before restarting that same node. It never allocates, pairs, changes repository contents or replays a turn. Providers without the capability retain today's reconnect behavior. A generic setup-command replay is not equivalent because it can rerun provisioning and grants.

### 2. Retained disk lifecycle while preserving Gateway backups

Opt-in `retention: { mode: "session-disk", computeWindowSeconds: <positive finite duration> }`, limited initially to a capable Linux Azure Sandbox Crabbox profile. Non-opted profiles remain unchanged. Reuse the environment store, writer, lock, maintenance sweep and teardown owner; no separate queue, timer or state file.

Persist a nullable session-retention record on each environment before allocation. It binds the exact session/agent, environment, original operation, policy, provider resource identity, current provider receipt and pending pause/resume intent. An existing shared/reserve allocation cannot silently become a session-private disk. Add a forward state-schema migration using the current upstream version rather than the donor's obsolete v32. Preserve existing rows; older binaries must refuse the new schema because their teardown code does not understand retained disks. PostgreSQL parity and generated schemas are part of the same PR.

Persist each lifecycle operation ID before the provider effect; after restart retry that exact operation. Validate receipts at the provider boundary and preserve unknown ownership. Only an active finite compute window admits execution; its deadline does not promise an exact provider billing cutoff. Idle suspension keeps the disk but stops compute; explicit Stop/Delete still final-saves and deletes through confirmed provider teardown. Failed or ambiguous deletion remains visibly pending. Routine turn settlement continues to create Gateway checkpoints in this first retention PR.

Rollback means disabling new retention admissions, safely settling/deleting or explicitly migrating every retained environment, then restoring the matching pre-migration backup with its binary. A package-only downgrade cannot safely forget retained resources. Suspended disks may continue to incur provider storage costs; this PR creates no live allocations during review.

Proof must cover fresh/old-state migration, PostgreSQL parity, same-session resume, interrupted operation/restart, expired compute admission, changed owner/resource refusal, offline observation, cancellation, final-save/Stop and confirmed deletion. The real provider CLI/controller must advertise `session-disk-retention-v1` and `pause-resume`; deterministic protocol tests alone are not live provider proof.

### 3. Classified provider-outage containment

Separate follow-up on the retention owner: hold only environments whose provider observation is specifically unavailable, allowing unrelated startup recovery to proceed. Storage corruption, cancellation and authority failures remain failures. No blanket catch-and-continue.

### 4. Disk-authoritative repositories — accepted target

Only after retained lifecycle is complete, optionally let the retained disk replace automatic per-turn Gateway file checkpoints for repository-only sessions. This can eliminate ordinary capture/upload/mirror scans but means confirmed disk loss can lose unpushed/private files. Keeping Gateway backups is a supported alternative and avoids this changed guarantee.

Activation must include the repository store's authority identity and downgrade fence, migration of existing pending results, refusal to restore stale Gateway mirrors, on-demand attachment/download/file access, and fresh explicit publication capture. These are required consumers, not optional follow-ups. Default behavior remains mirrored. Galin has authorized implementing opt-in activation in the PR series. Galin's later ready-PR merge instruction supersedes the original no-merge scope. It does not authorize migration of the live Team server, deployment, paid allocations, or lossy recovery.

### Other separable work

- Explicit lost-worker recovery from the recorded repository ref is a separate lossy opt-in. Reuse the existing loss-confirmation owner; never default to an arbitrary branch or confuse it with exact checkpoint reconstruction.
- Provisioning/settlement diagnostics can follow the finished owners using current loggers. No dedicated timing subsystem.

### Design acceptance and implementation boundary — 2026-10-31

Galin approved the restart and retained lifecycle proposal and subsequently requested: “the benefits of Azure Sandboxes and snapshot are Disk-authoritative workspace — let's implement it in smaller prs.” This accepts disk-authoritative workspaces as the target of the implementation series, including the previously explained removal of automatic per-turn Gateway file checkpoints. Source: [original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1c21e0ea-e918-4f4d-a25f-a46256a029bd).

The backup-preserving retention stage is an intermediate prerequisite, not a substitute for the requested final feature. Keep migration, exact resource ownership, old pending-result recovery, on-demand file/attachment reads, frozen publication capture, and refusal of stale mirror restoration complete before enabling disk authority. Snapshots do not imply continuous backup of every subsequent write.

Plugin boundary: extend the existing Crabbox worker integration and its Azure backend for vendor-specific allocation, snapshots and retained-resource operations. Core owns only generic capability/receipt contracts and workspace/recovery semantics; do not copy the donor's hard-coded Crabbox/Azure eligibility checks into core. A direct-Azure plugin independent of Crabbox is not part of this extraction.

PR boundaries are behavior-based: same-enrolled-node process restart; retained-resource lifecycle; durable repository/result authority and recovery prerequisites; explicit file/publication consumers; final opt-in activation. Foundation PRs must be labeled as prerequisites, compile with current consumers, and keep existing behavior until activation. Do not publish a design-only PR as implementation.

The original #188914 CI failures were repaired in the same PR; its exact-head aggregate gate is now successful as recorded above. Earlier focused receipts alone were not treated as broad CI qualification.

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows with 20 registered agents, the gateway child process sustains ~100-170% of one CPU core while completely idle on **2026.10.10**, after the watch-target refresh machinery named in #191612 was removed by PR #170341. The reported symptom persists in the replacement code path.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.10** (7dc3350), npm global install
- Windows 10.0.26200 x64, 20 logical CPUs, Node v24.22.1
- 20 agents under `agents.entries`, shared skills dir via `skills.load.extraDirs`
- Gateway launched by Windows Scheduled Task -> gateway.cmd -> `node dist/index.js gateway --port 18789 --task-supervisor`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Register 19-20 agents on Windows with a shared skills directory.
2. Start the gateway and leave it idle: no chat, no commands, no channel traffic.
3. Observe the `--task-supervisor-child` node process: sustained ~100-170% of one core indefinitely.
4. Kill it, upgrade 2026.10.7 -> 2026.10.10, rerun `openclaw doctor --fix` to completion, restart, wait past startup.
5. Observe: identical CPU consumption on the new release.

Scale dependence on one host (agent count is the only variable changed):

```
 0 agents ->   3.0% of one core
 2 agents ->  30.5%
 6 agents ->  79.7% average, decaying to 18-38%
17 agents -> 143.4%
19 agents -> 150-226%, never settles
```

## Expected behavior

An idle gateway consumes near-zero CPU.

## Actual behavior

Measured **after** upgrading to 2026.10.10, with `doctor --fix` completed at exit 0 and the gateway restarted on the new code:

```
run 1: 1,433 CPU-seconds in 14 minutes  (~170% of one core)
run 2:   518 CPU-seconds in  6 minutes  (~143% of one core)
4-second instantaneous sample: 168.6%
```

No errors, no warnings, no crash; the process stays functional. Per-second CPU deltas show no idle gaps.

## Confirmation that PR #170341 landed in this install

Grepped the installed `dist`:

```
refresh-watch-targets               -> 0 files
nativeWatchCapacityFailed           -> 0 files
addTrustedSymlinkSkillWatchTargets  -> 0 files
scanDirtySources (replacement)      -> present (refresh-epILD946.mjs)
```

So the owning refresh boundary and its sticky capacity machinery are genuinely gone, and the coalesced discovery replacement is present. The idle scan still re-enters.

## Where the remaining hot path may be

`ensureSkillsWatcher` survives in 2026.10.10 and is still referenced from the session-snapshot, workspace-worker, and server-startup-post-attach surfaces (5 dist files). It is called on every session snapshot when `watch !== false`, which would explain continuous re-entry independent of the removed watch-target resolver.

## Prior evidence

#191612 (closed as already-implemented) carries the original 2026.10.7 profile, the syscall-counting harness results, and the post-upgrade measurements:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191612#issuecomment-6620744886

Filed separately because the author cannot reopen an issue closed by a maintainer/bot, and a comment on a closed issue is not re-triaged.

## Impact

One of 20 cores permanently unavailable (~5% of machine capacity) on an idle gateway, with continuous heat and added latency when preparing sessions. No data risk.
