issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With `channels.feishu.streaming` set to `{ mode: "partial", block: { enabled: true } }`, a reply that reaches Feishu as two or more blocks closes its streaming card with the last block repeated, reproduced on main `56122102ae68` with a test against the Feishu reply dispatcher.

### Steps to reproduce

The setting that triggers this is `channels.feishu.streaming` set to `{ mode: "partial", block: { enabled: true } }`. This is the shape in `docs/channels/feishu/advanced-configuration.md`, where `block.enabled` is opt-in and off by default.

1. Check out main at `56122102ae68` and run `pnpm install`.
2. Add the case below to `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` just before "keeps an over-limit block in its active streaming card".
3. Run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --project extension-feishu extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts -t "does not repeat a completed"`.

```ts
  it.each([
    { name: "table", text: "Here is the table.\n\n| a | b |\n| - | - |\n| 1 | 2 |\n\nThat is all." },
    { name: "prose", text: "Here is the answer.\n\nThat is all." },
  ])("does not repeat a completed $name block that the preview already shows", async ({ text }) => {
    useStreamingBlockAccount();
    const { result, options } = createDispatcherHarness();
    await options.onReplyStart?.();
    result.replyOptions.onPartialReply?.({ text });
    await options.block({ text: "\n\nThat is all." });
    await options.onIdle?.();
    expectClosed(text);
  });
```

Both rows fail. In each, `closeWithResult` receives the expected text followed by a second `\n\nThat is all.`. A control where the block equals the whole preview closes correctly.

### Expected behavior

The card closes with the reply text once. That is what happens when a reply reaches Feishu as one block, because that block equals the whole preview and the dispatcher skips it, and it is what the control row closes with.

### Actual behavior

On main `56122102ae68`, this reply closed like this:

```
Here is the table.

| a | b |
| - | - |
| 1 | 2 |

That is all.

That is all.
```

The table plays no part. A reply made only of prose paragraphs doubles the same way. A reply that reaches Feishu as one block comes out right, because that block equals the whole preview and the dispatcher skips it.

Which replies arrive as several blocks depends on chunking and coalescing. In an in-process run with default coalescing, an 85 character reply arrived as one block and a reply of about 1700 characters arrived as sixteen, the last one a 14 character tail after a preview that already ended with it.

The repeat stays on the card unless a final payload replaces the card text before the idle close. From reading `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.ts:193-196`, core drops final payloads once block streaming has succeeded. I read that code and did not run it.

### OpenClaw version

Source checkout of main at `56122102ae68`

### Operating system

macOS 27.2

### Install method

Source checkout with `pnpm install`

### Model

None. The tests used the repo's own mocks and a fake model stream, with no real model.

### Provider / routing chain

None. No provider was called. The same mocks and fake model stream stood in for the whole model path.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Does not apply. There is no provider or model setup. The only config involved is `channels.feishu.streaming` from the steps above.

### Logs

```shell
# repro command on main 56122102ae68, prose row. The table row fails the same way.
 FAIL  |extension-feishu| extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts > createFeishuReplyDispatcher streaming behavior > does not repeat a completed prose block that the preview already shows
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ …(2) ]

Received:

  1st vi.fn() call:

  [
    "Here is the answer.

+ That is all.
+
  That is all.",
    {
      "note": "Agent: agent",
    },
  ]

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 80 skipped (82)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshots or recordings. The evidence is the failing test in the Logs field, where the Feishu session is the suite's stub and card text means the text passed to `closeWithResult`, plus the pipeline-order run below.

To check the order core really sends, I ran a fake model stream through a real agent session, the real embedded subscriber with `blockReplyBreak: "text_end"` and paragraph chunking, the presentation layer, the block pipeline with its coalescer, the dispatch wrappers with `preserveProgressCallbackStartOrder`, and the reply dispatcher queue, and recorded what arrives at the channel edge. In every run the preview that covers a block arrived before the block. With tight coalescing, or with a long reply, the last block arrived after a preview that already ended with it.

That run does not include the real Feishu dispatcher, a live Feishu tenant or a full gateway turn. The glue that builds the pipeline in `runReplyAgent` was rebuilt in the test from the same functions.

### Impact and severity

Affected are Feishu channel users with `channels.feishu.streaming` set to `mode: "partial"` and `block.enabled: true`. The block setting is opt-in and off by default.

Severity is a wrong closed card. The last block of each message stays on the card twice. No crash was observed, and the card keeps the full reply text and adds the repeat.

Frequency depends on how many blocks reach Feishu. Every shape I ran that arrived as two or more blocks doubled, and every one-block shape closed correctly. Which replies split depends on chunking and coalescing, see Actual behavior.

The consequence is a closed card that shows the last block twice. It stays that way unless a final payload replaces the card text before the idle close, as described above.

### Additional information

**Why it happens.** Core flushes the pending preview before it emits each block. `emitBlockReply` calls `flushAssistantStream()` first, in `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.reply-delivery.ts:439-440`. So the Feishu dispatcher receives the cumulative preview, which already ends with the block, and then the block itself.

The dispatcher stores the preview as a snapshot and appends the block as a delta at `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:1234`. `queueStreamingUpdate` skips a block only when it equals the whole last preview, at line 330. Otherwise line 335 appends it. After the first block of a message, a block is a suffix of the preview rather than the whole preview, so it lands twice. The next preview replaces the text again, which is why only the last block of each message stays doubled.

The comment above line 1234 says the delta path is for runtimes that emit blocks without partial or final callbacks. With both settings on, Feishu gets partials and blocks for the same text.

**What the existing test covers.** The `delta blocks` row asserts that a preview `hello` followed by a block `lo world` closes as `hellolo world`. There the block extends the preview, and #182438 removed overlap guessing on purpose. No row covers a block that the preview already ends with, which is the shape core sends when both streams are on.

**Related.**

- #74143 reported duplicated card text from block deltas after partial snapshots and closed as stale.
- #77685 closed on 10-24 asking for a new focused issue if lasting duplication shows up. This duplication lasts into the closed card.
- #179505 tried overlap merging on the delta path and closed unmerged. Its bot review showed that merging against all of `streamText` can drop text, for example block `ban`, preview `a`, block `ana` closing as `bana`. So a plain overlap rule is risky.

**Two cautions from a prototype.** Skipping every block once any preview has arrived for the message breaks the `delta blocks` row, which then closes as `hello` and loses `lo world`. Skipping a block only when the card text already ends with it passed the whole `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` file and closed the repro rows correctly, but it would also drop a genuine block that repeats the end of the existing text.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a Gateway without `gateway.roles`, sessions owned by an ordinary user profile never resume after a graceful restart. The same authority check also rejects their restart-captured queued messages and session-principal system turns. The error is `Session principal has no current run authority.` A single person connecting to their own Gateway over Tailscale, which is a typical setup, hits this on every restart.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Gateway with Tailscale (or trusted-proxy) sign-in and **no** `gateway.roles`. Sign in to the Control UI as yourself. Your connection maps to an ordinary user profile, not the reserved `gateway-owner` profile.
2. Start a long agent turn in a dashboard session.
3. Restart the Gateway gracefully (`openclaw gateway restart`, update, config restart).
4. After startup, open the session.

### Expected behavior

The session gets the standard "The Gateway restarted while you were working…" input and continues under the person's current authority, as it does for `gateway-owner` sessions and for profiles with a role.

### Actual behavior

The session shows "The Gateway restarted, but this run could not resume. Error: Session principal has no current run authority." The startup summary reports `resumed: 0` with `admission-failed`:

```
Skipped restart resume for agent:main:dashboard:<id>: Error: Session principal has no current run authority. {"sessionId":"…","runId":"…","admissionStage":"principal"}
startup restart resume: [{"agentId":"main","resumed":0,"skipped":11,"reasons":{…,"admission-failed":4}}]
```

On the reporting host, every restart on 2026-11-03 resumed 0 sessions, and 5 marked sessions were refused. A system turn in another session failed the same way (`message dispatch completed … outcome=error … Session principal has no current run authority.`).

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10 (1b23272). Still present on `main` at eee9925e84f.

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8)

### Install method

Source checkout, systemd user service

### Model

Not model-specific

### Provider / routing chain

Not provider-specific

### Additional provider/model setup details

`gateway.auth.mode: token`, `gateway.auth.allowTailscale: true`, no `gateway.roles`, no `gateway.auth.identityScopes`. Two profiles: the person's profile (owner and creator of the affected sessions) and the reserved `gateway-owner`.

### Logs

See Actual behavior.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

## Cause

#185730 (`refactor: resume running sessions after graceful restarts`, 9344233e7a6) replaced restart reconstruction with a single resume input admitted under the session principal's **current** authority. It added `prepareSessionPrincipalRunAccess`, which derives that authority from the profile alone:

- [`session-sharing-authorization-async.ts` L113–L132](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eee9925e84f32ab8378ccf64cc86bde13b85c4be/src/gateway/session-sharing-authorization-async.ts#L113-L132): the reserved `gateway-owner` profile gets `operator.admin`. Any other profile gets the scopes of its effective `gateway.roles` role, and gets `no current run authority` when that is missing.
- [`operator-role-policy.ts` L133](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eee9925e84f32ab8378ccf64cc86bde13b85c4be/src/gateway/operator-role-policy.ts#L133): `resolveOperatorRolePolicyForAssignment` returns `undefined` when roles are unset. Elsewhere this means "no role ceiling; use the connection's scopes". This path reads it as a denial.

On a Gateway without roles, a profile carries no authority of its own. A connection's scopes come from its paired device plus any `gateway.auth.identityScopes` grant ([`resolveEffectiveConnectionScopes`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eee9925e84f32ab8378ccf64cc86bde13b85c4be/src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-admission.ts#L140)). After a restart there is no connection, so there is nothing to derive from, and every ordinary profile is denied. Decision 1 in #185730 covered the owner profile and role-bearing profiles only.

Affected paths, all through `prepareSessionPrincipalRunAuthority`:

- restart resume, through `prepareSessionSystemTurnAuthority` ([`session-restart-resume.ts` L612–L622](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eee9925e84f32ab8378ccf64cc86bde13b85c4be/src/gateway/session-restart-resume.ts#L612-L622))
- restart-captured queued inputs ([`queued-chat-inputs.ts` L73](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eee9925e84f32ab8378ccf64cc86bde13b85c4be/src/gateway/queued-chat-inputs.ts#L73))
- unattributed host inputs / system turns that fall back to the session principal (`reply-source-admission.ts`, `operator-run-cancellation.ts`)

Test gap: the acceptance e2e ([`gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eee9925e84f32ab8378ccf64cc86bde13b85c4be/test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts#L583)) covers a `gateway-owner` session that resumes and a reader-role profile that is denied. It never covers an ordinary profile on a Gateway without roles. #191105 later reorganized the same function without changing behavior.

## Rejected fix: "no roles ⇒ admin"

Scheduled work treats any current profile as owner on an untiered Gateway ([`execution-context-admission.ts` L115–L123](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eee9925e84f32ab8378ccf64cc86bde13b85c4be/src/cron/execution-context-admission.ts#L115-L123)). Copying that rule here would be a privilege escalation. A Gateway without roles can still restrict people through `gateway.auth.identityScopes` or limited device pairing, and queued inputs run as their **sender**, so an admin grant would also bypass session membership. Cron itself prefers the creator's recorded authenticated source over that profile-only fallback: [`captureScheduledOperatorSource`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eee9925e84f32ab8378ccf64cc86bde13b85c4be/src/gateway/server-methods/cron-input-validation.ts#L350) records it, and [`restoreGatewayOperatorSource`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eee9925e84f32ab8378ccf64cc86bde13b85c4be/src/gateway/operator-run-recovery.ts#L348) rechecks it on every use.

## Intended fix

Reuse the existing, revalidating operator-source recovery that scheduled work already uses. This is not a saved grant that is trusted as-is.

1. **Record.** When a person's run is admitted from an authenticated connection in a session where they are the principal, store that run's bounded `recoverySnapshot` on the session entry, writing only when it changes. The snapshot holds the device ID and key, scopes, auth method, shared-secret generation and profile facts.
2. **Fallback.** Keep `prepareSessionPrincipalRunAuthority` as the first route for the owner and for role-bearing profiles. When it refuses, restore authority from the recorded source through `restoreGatewayOperatorSource`, but only if that source belongs to the same profile and session. Before each use, the restore checks:
   - the device is still paired, with the same key and scopes
   - the auth method is still allowed and the shared secret has not been rotated
   - the profile identity, role and access grant are unchanged
   - the session lifetime is unchanged

   It never grants more than the original connection had, and it revokes on any change. Restart resume, queued inputs and system turns all inherit this through the one shared entry point.
3. **Not covered.** A principal who never ran a turn from an authenticated connection in that session keeps today's visible "could not resume" notice.

Acceptance:
- On a Gateway without roles, an ordinary profile's session resumes after a graceful restart, its captured queued input runs, and its system turns are admitted.
- A device limited to `operator.write` resumes with `operator.write`, not admin.
- Unpairing the device or reducing its scopes before restart produces the visible refusal.
- The existing owner and reader-role cases are unchanged.
- Real-behavior proof is a restarted Gateway on a separate host.

### Impact and severity

High for affected setups. Any interrupted work is silently abandoned on every restart or update on single-user Gateways that sign in through Tailscale or trusted-proxy, and on multi-user Gateways without roles. The user must notice the interruption and send a new message to continue.

### Additional information

Regression introduced by #185730.

issues.body:
## Summary
On 2026.10.10 (7dc3350) a Crabbox cloud-worker profile that used `settings.setupEnv` cannot be migrated to `setupSecrets`, and the setupSecrets design cannot deliver a Tailscale auth key at all, so cloud workers that must join a tailnet to reach a Tailscale-Serve-only Gateway have no supported path.

## Details
- Profile `aws` had `setupEnv: ["OPENCLAW_CW_TS_AUTHKEY"]`; its setup script runs `tailscale up --authkey=$OPENCLAW_CW_TS_AUTHKEY` so the worker can reach `gateway.publicOrigin` (a ts.net Tailscale Serve URL).
- Health check: "Crabbox profile aws uses retired plaintext setupEnv and needs repair (OPENCLAW_CW_TS_AUTHKEY: missing)". Docs say `doctor --fix` migrates to **same-name** protected store entries, but the crabbox provider rejects any setupSecrets name starting with `OPENCLAW_` ("setupSecrets name ... is reserved"). So the documented migration can never succeed for an `OPENCLAW_*` name; the doctor hint does not mention renaming.
- Even after renaming, setupSecrets only gives the command a placeholder that the egress proxy substitutes in HTTPS URLs/headers/bodies at bound hosts. `tailscaled` sends the auth key to the control plane inside the Noise (ts2021) protocol, so substitution cannot work; the worker joins with a placeholder and fails.
- Meanwhile `gateway/worker-environments` logs "Worker provider maintenance failed (crabbox)" every ~30 s with no reason in the log line (~1,650/day), and warm-image refresh stops.

## Expected
1. Doctor/health hint should say the name must be renamed (and which names are reserved) instead of implying same-name migration.
2. A supported way for cloud workers to join a tailnet when the Gateway is only reachable over Tailscale (e.g. first-class Tailscale join using an OAuth client held by the Gateway, or a documented pattern minting an ephemeral key via api.tailscale.com through the egress proxy).
3. The maintenance failure log should include the reason.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Mattermost ignores `textChunkLimit` when a reply carries a file: the whole reply text is posted as the file's caption in one post, however long it is.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Mattermost with a small chunk limit, for example `channels.mattermost.textChunkLimit: 350` (optionally `streaming.chunkMode: "newline"`).
2. Have the agent send a reply of a few thousand characters that also attaches one file (a `MEDIA:` line in the reply, or `openclaw message send --channel mattermost --media <file> --message <long text>`).
3. Look at the resulting posts in the channel or thread.

### Expected behavior

The reply is split like a text-only reply: the first chunk is posted with the file and the remaining chunks follow as plain posts in the same channel/thread, in order, each within `textChunkLimit`.

### Actual behavior

Text-only replies are chunked correctly (every post within 350 chars), but each reply that carries a file arrives as one post with the full text, for example 3,000 to 4,600 characters, and mobile clients collapse it behind "Show more".

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10 (also present on current `main`)

### Operating system

Linux (Gateway); Mattermost 11.x server

### Install method

npm global

### Model

Any (not model-specific)

### Provider / routing chain

Not relevant (channel delivery)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

_No response_ (no error is logged; the post is accepted as sent)

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Root cause in code: text chunking runs only on text-only paths. When a reply has media, the caption is passed whole to the media send:

- Inbound replies: `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/reply-delivery.ts` calls `deliverTextOrMediaReply`, which sends the full text as the caption of the first file and uses `chunkText` only when there is no media.
- Outbound sends (message tool, `openclaw message send`): core plans one media unit with the whole text as caption, and `sendTextMediaPayload` does the same for payload sends; `chunker` / `textChunkLimit` apply to text-only payloads.
- `sendMessageMattermost` then creates one post with the whole message and the file.

Other channels already split long captions in their own send function (Slack, Discord, Matrix, SMS, Synology Chat).

### Impact and severity

Affected: Mattermost users with a `textChunkLimit` below the server post size, and any long reply that carries a file.
Severity: low to medium (readability; no data loss).
Frequency: every long reply that carries a file.
Consequence: very long single posts that the operator explicitly configured to avoid.

### Additional information

I have a fix ready and will open a PR that splits long captions inside `sendMessageMattermost`, so every Mattermost send path gets the same behavior.

### Summary
`openclaw gateway restart` validates its flag combinations (--skip-deferral needs --safe; --safe excludes --force, --wait and --preserve-definition; --force excludes --wait), but in human output the reason is swallowed and the root renderer prints only the generic failure. The `--json` envelope contains the specific message, so the validation runs; it just reaches the root CLI as a plain Error.

### Steps to reproduce (Linux, built CLI, no gateway needed)
1. pnpm install && pnpm build on main (cee08525d18), Node 24.22.1
2. OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) node openclaw.mjs gateway restart --skip-deferral
3. Repeat with: --safe --force · --safe --wait 5s · --force --wait 5s · --safe --preserve-definition

### Expected behavior
The specific reason, e.g. `--skip-deferral requires --safe`, exit 1 — same as other CLI validations after #189993 / #190366.

### Actual behavior
$ openclaw gateway restart --skip-deferral
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
[exit 1]
(identical for all five combinations)

$ openclaw gateway restart --skip-deferral --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "--skip-deferral requires --safe" } }
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.

### Suspected root cause
src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.ts runDaemonRestart throws `new Error("--preserve-definition requires a native restart without --safe")` and `new Error("--skip-deferral requires --safe")`; src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle-safe-restart.ts throws plain Errors for "--force cannot be combined with --wait", "--safe cannot be combined with --force…", "--safe cannot be combined with --wait…". Only ExpectedCliError keeps its message in the root renderer (src/entry.ts), so these are reported as the generic failure. Same class as #189993 and #190366.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.10 (cee0852) · Linux · Node 24.22.1

## Summary

Consolidate updater version ordering in its existing registry/version owner.

## Problem to solve

Core update checks and npm channel selection each implement the same monthly-release, correction-release, legacy dot-beta, and SemVer comparison policy. The CLI test helper also substitutes a numeric-only comparator that misses those distinctions. This duplicates policy across updater entry points and lets tests model different ordering from production.

## Proposed solution

Move the existing comparator unchanged into `src/infra/npm-registry-spec.ts`, reuse it in channel selection, migrate internal callers, and remove the inaccurate CLI substitute. Preserve current ordering, null handling, beta ties, and selected metadata identity. No config, storage, SDK, or operator-facing behavior changes.

## Alternatives considered

Importing the update-check module from channel selection creates a cycle and pulls probing code into a pure selector. The existing package-update and config comparators have different contracts and should remain separate.

## Impact

Internal maintenance improvement requested as part of the updater duplication audit. Existing runtime behavior must remain unchanged.

## Evidence/examples

The duplicate expressions are in `src/infra/update-check.ts` and `src/infra/update-channels.ts`; correction ordering is covered by the registry comparator and plugin channel-selection suites.

## Implementation intent

A narrow implementation PR will close this issue.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With `gateway.tailscale.mode: "serve"`, a restart of tailscaled (here: a Tailscale.app update to 1.102.4 on macOS) silently drops the Gateway's foreground `tailscale serve --bg=false` claim; the Gateway keeps running and reports healthy, but never re-claims the route, so `wss://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net` stays dead until a manual Gateway restart.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.3 as the macOS LaunchAgent (`ai.openclaw.gateway`) with `gateway.bind: "loopback"`, `gateway.tailscale.mode: "serve"`, `gateway.auth.mode: "token"`, `gateway.auth.allowTailscale: true`. Confirm `[tailscale] serve enabled: https://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net/` in the gateway log and that `tailscale serve status --json` shows the `Foreground` claim on 443.
2. Restart tailscaled without touching the Gateway. Observed trigger: the Tailscale.app in-place update (1.102.4). `ps` shows Tailscale and its network extension restarted at 09:56; the Gateway pid is unchanged.
3. Connect any remote client via `wss://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net`.

### Expected behavior

Per `docs/gateway/tailscale.md` ("OpenClaw holds Serve/Funnel as a foreground Tailscale claim... stopping or losing the Gateway releases it automatically") the claim is tied to the Gateway's lifetime. The reverse direction should also be handled: when the route-owner child exits while the Gateway is still running, the Gateway should re-run `claimTailscaleRoute` with backoff (or fail loudly / mark health degraded) rather than continue serving only on loopback. Prior observed behavior: before the tailscaled restart, remote clients connected normally.

### Actual behavior

- At the moment tailscaled restarts, every remote webchat connection drops with code 1006 (gateway.log below). No `[tailscale]` log line is emitted then or later.
- `tailscale serve status --json` afterwards has no `Foreground` entry; the 443 route is gone. A background route on another port (canvas host, `:18790`) survives, which confirms only the foreground claim was lost.
- `openclaw gateway status` reports `Runtime: running`, `Connectivity probe: ok`, `Listening: 127.0.0.1:18789`. The health monitor never flags anything. The Gateway ran in this state for 12+ minutes until I intervened (it would have stayed that way indefinitely).
- `startTailscaleRouteOwner` (`dist/tailscale-*.mjs`) sets `active = false` on worker `exit` and resolves `exited`, but nothing in `server-start` re-claims or surfaces it.

Workaround that restored service without a Gateway restart: add a background route to the managed ingress listener, i.e. `tailscale serve --bg --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral managed-ingress port>`. That port is only discoverable by probing the Gateway's loopback listeners for the one answering `proxy_attribution_required` (it is not logged). Pointing at the main port 18789 instead yields HTTP 403 `proxy_attribution_required`. The workaround has a sharp edge: on the next Gateway restart the leftover background route triggers `TailscaleRouteOwnershipConflictError` and the Gateway fails to start (KeepAlive crash-loop, cf. #125390), unless `tailscale serve --https=443 off` is run first.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.3 (1391f7c)

### Operating system

macOS 26.5.1 (arm64), Tailscale.app 1.102.4 (updated in place during the incident)

### Install method

npm global (`/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw`), launched via `openclaw gateway install` LaunchAgent `ai.openclaw.gateway` (KeepAlive)

### Model

n/a (ingress issue, model-independent)

### Provider / routing chain

Remote client -> Tailscale Serve (tailnet only, HTTPS 443) -> Gateway managed ingress listener 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral> ; local clients -> 127.0.0.1:18789

### Additional provider/model setup details

n/a

### Logs

`~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log` (local time, redacted):

```
2026-09-13T22:44:37.944-04:00 [tailscale] serve enabled: https://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net/ (WS via wss://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net)
...
2026-09-14T09:55:32.839-04:00 [ws] webchat disconnected code=1006 reason=n/a conn=b4253d85-...
2026-09-14T09:56:54.320-04:00 [ws] webchat disconnected code=1006 reason=n/a conn=891eccc9-...
2026-09-14T09:56:54.321-04:00 [ws] authenticated user disconnected code=1006 reason=n/a conn=891eccc9-... user=<redacted>
2026-09-14T09:56:54.329-04:00 [ws] webchat disconnected code=1006 reason=n/a conn=804ec07b-...
2026-09-14T09:56:55.361-04:00 [ws] webchat connected conn=1f17c5a1-... remote=127.0.0.1 client=openclaw-control-ui webchat v2026.9.3
(no [tailscale] lines after this point)
```

`ps` on the host (tailscaled restarted, gateway did not):

```
66350 10:44PM /opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port 18789
85500  9:56AM .../io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.network-extension.systemextension/Contents/MacOS/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.network-extension
84202  9:56AM /Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale
```

`tailscale serve status --json` after the restart (443 gone, `Foreground` absent):

```
{ "TCP": { "18790": { "HTTPS": true } },
  "Web": { "<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net:18790": { "Handlers": { "/": { "Proxy": "http://127.0.0.1:18790" } } } } }
```

`openclaw gateway status` in the broken state:

```
Gateway: bind=loopback (127.0.0.1), port=18789 (service args)
Runtime: running (pid 66350, state active)
Connectivity probe: ok
Listening: 127.0.0.1:18789
```

Gateway `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-09-14.log` when the wrong-port workaround was tried (403 from the plain listener):

```
{"subsystem":"gateway"} "gateway: observed unattributable proxy-shaped traffic from 127.0.0.1; Gateway-authenticated routes reject it, while plugin-authenticated routes ignore forwarded claims. Configure gateway.trustedProxies narrowly and make the proxy overwrite or safely rebuild forwarded client headers."
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Evidence is in the Logs section; no screenshots.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: every remote operator/node using the managed Tailscale Serve route (macOS app, Control UI, paired nodes). Local loopback clients unaffected.
- Severity: blocks workflow. Remote access is lost while the Gateway reports healthy, so there is nothing to alert on.
- Frequency: always, on every tailscaled restart (Tailscale updates happen regularly).
- Consequence: silent outage until someone notices and restarts the Gateway, which also drains any in-flight agent runs.

### Additional information

Related but distinct: #144845 and #139097 cover the serve claim failing at Gateway startup (Tailscale stopped / not ready). This report is about a claim that succeeded and was then lost while the Gateway kept running. #125390 (closed) covers the stale-:443-route crash-loop that the manual workaround above can trigger on the next restart.

Suggested fix: in `startTailscaleRouteOwner`/`server-tailscale`, treat the route-owner worker's `exit` (after `ready`) as a recoverable event: retry `claimTailscaleRoute` with bounded backoff, log `[tailscale] serve claim lost; re-claiming`, and mark gateway health degraded while unclaimed. Logging the managed ingress listener's ephemeral port at startup would also make manual recovery possible without probing.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add an opt-in Google Chat setting, `threadSessions` (default `false`), that keys each space thread to its own session when replies are threaded (`replyToMode: "first" | "all" | "batched"`). Existing configs keep today's one-session-per-space behavior.

### Problem to solve

With `replyToMode: "all"`, OpenClaw already replies inside the inbound thread, so a Google Chat space reads as one thread per question. But every thread in the space still resolves to the same session, `agent:<agentId>:googlechat:group:<spaceId>`. Here `<spaceId>` is the full resource name, for example `spaces/AAAA`.

When a bot is added to a shared space and several people ask unrelated questions in separate threads, this causes:

- **Context bleed:** an answer in thread B can draw on a different person's question and answer from thread A.
- **Serialization:** concurrent questions in different threads queue behind one session.
- **Disclosure risk for support-style bots:** one asker's thread content enters the context used to answer another asker.

**My use case.** We run OpenClaw as an internal consulting bot for our engineering team. The bot sits in one shared Google Chat space with `requireMention: true` and `replyToMode: "all"`, and answers from our service docs through memory search.

- Engineers from different teams @mention it to ask about a service: endpoints, deployment environments, alerting.
- Each question starts its own thread, follow-ups stay in that thread, and several threads are often active at the same time.
- We expect each thread to behave like its own conversation. Today it doesn't: every thread shares one session, so a follow-up such as "which of those is the health check?" can resolve against a different person's thread, and one asker's question becomes context for everyone else's answers.

The thread UI suggests isolation, but the session does not provide it. Mattermost, Microsoft Teams (`extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/thread-session.ts`) and Slack already key sessions by thread. Google Chat has no way to do this today.

### Proposed solution

Add `channels.googlechat.threadSessions` (boolean, default `false`; also per account under `accounts.<id>`).

- **Unset or `false`:** no change. One session per space, even with threaded replies.
- **`true`:** when the message is from a space (not a DM), `replyToMode` is set and not `"off"`, and the message carries `thread.name`, derive the session key with the existing `resolveThreadSessionKeys` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/routing`:

  ```
  agent:<agentId>:googlechat:group:<spaceId>:thread:<threadId>
  ```

- **`replyToMode` keeps its meaning.** It still decides only where replies go. `threadSessions` adds nothing when replies are top-level, because there is no thread to key on.

Details:

- **One decision point.** The monitor already computes the effective reply thread (space message and `replyToMode` not `"off"`). The session key reuses it, so reply placement and session keying cannot drift apart.
- **Use the thread key everywhere.** It goes to access-policy context binding, `buildContext` (as `dispatchSessionKey`; `routeSessionKey` stays the space key) and `resolveTurn`.
- **Thread sessions start fresh: no `parentSessionKey` is passed.** This differs on purpose from Microsoft Teams and Mattermost room threads, which fork their base session.
  - In those channels the top-level post lands in the base session, and the thread inherits it to see the post it replies to.
  - In Google Chat, every space message, including the first one, already carries `thread.name`, so it goes straight into its thread session.
  - Forking would therefore add no thread context. It would only copy space history from other askers into each thread, which is the leak this setting removes.
  - This matches Slack's default `inheritParent: false`.
- **Thread ids use the default lowercase normalization.** Google Chat thread ids are mixed case. With a case-preserving `normalizeThreadId`, the dispatch key differed from the stored session key, and every reply failed with `Reply execution target differs from its captured source`.
- **Docs:** `docs/channels/googlechat.md` documents the setting, its dependency on threaded replies, and the fresh start.

**New config option:** following "ask before adding config options", I'd like maintainer approval for `threadSessions`. It is a separate option, not an extension of `replyToMode`, because reply placement and session scope are different concerns. Tying them together would silently change session behavior for every existing config that threads replies.

### Alternatives considered

- **Fork the space session into each thread** (`parentSessionKey`). This keeps prior space context but copies it into every thread, which is the leak this setting removes.
- **Use `replyToMode: "off"`.** This keeps one shared session but gives up threaded replies, so concurrent questions interleave at the top level.
- **`session.threadBindings` / thread-bound subagent sessions.** These solve a different problem (binding a spawned session to a thread), not per-thread routing of inbound channel messages.

### Impact

- **Affected:** Google Chat spaces with threaded replies, especially shared spaces where several people ask the bot questions at the same time.
- **Severity:** blocks workflow for shared or support-style spaces. It is a data-exposure risk there, because one person's question content can surface in another person's answer.
- **Frequency:** always, for every thread after the first in a space with threaded replies.
- **Consequence:**
  - Answers are wrong or confused because of unrelated context from other threads.
  - Concurrent askers wait on each other.
  - Operators must use one space per asker, or turn threading off, to keep conversations apart.
- **Behavior change for existing users:** none. The setting defaults to `false`. Turning it on starts every thread in a space with a fresh session.

### Evidence/examples

Prior art in this repo:

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-context.ts`
- `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/thread-session.ts`
- `extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare-routing.ts`

Validation on a local build of `main` (`c8f87b2e516`) with the patch, running the Gateway in Docker against a real Google Chat app (Workspace add-on, webhook auth with `audienceType: "app-url"` and `appPrincipal`), `replyToMode: "all"`, `threadSessions: true` and `requireMention: true`:

1. @mention in a space: the reply posts in the inbound thread, and the session key is `agent:main:googlechat:group:spaces/<space>:thread:<threadId>`.
2. A follow-up @mention in the same thread uses that thread's earlier exchange.
3. A question in another thread cannot see the first thread's content.
4. `openclaw sessions` / the Control UI list one session per thread.
5. A message without an @mention gets no reply.

I repeated the same five checks with the patch applied to the `v2026.10.9` release tag, using the same setup and four concurrent threads. They gave the same results: four threads mapped to four thread sessions, and no shared space session.

Tests:

- New monitor cases cover `threadSessions` on/off with `replyToMode` `all`/`off`. The `threadSessions: true` + `replyToMode: "all"` case fails on `main` and passes with the patch; the unset case guards the default.
- `pnpm test:extension googlechat`, `pnpm test:contracts:channels`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `config:channels:check` and `config:docs:check` pass, and `oxfmt` is clean.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

- I have a branch ready: about 20 lines of source, one schema line plus regenerated config metadata, tests and docs ([compare](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/main...maxence2997:openclaw:feat/googlechat-thread-sessions)). I'll open the PR against this issue if the direction is acceptable.
- While testing I found that Workspace Add-on apps need `botUser`: their mention annotations name the app by numeric `users/<id>`, so `requireMention` drops every message without it. The docs call `botUser` optional; the branch adds a one-line docs note. I can split that into its own PR if preferred.
- Related but distinct: #184592 (referenced-message context for thread replies). That issue notes that per-thread isolation and referenced-message content are separate requirements. This proposal covers only isolation and routing.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With 19 registered agents on Windows, the gateway child process sustains ~100% of one CPU core
indefinitely while idle; a V8 CPU profile attributes ~78% of self time to filesystem syscalls in
skill watch-target resolution, with 0% idle.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, install OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (npm global) and register 19 agents under
   agents.entries, with skills.load.extraDirs pointing at a shared skills directory
   (config: skills.load.extraDirs=["C:/OpenClawLocal/shared-skills"]).
2. Start the gateway: node dist/index.js gateway --port 18789 --task-supervisor
3. Leave it completely idle (no chat, no commands, no channels receiving traffic).
4. Observe the gateway child process: sustained ~100% of one core. Measured 60,960 CPU-seconds
   over ~16.9 hours of wall clock (1.00-1.07 cores continuously).
5. Capture a CPU profile of the steady state; observe ~78% filesystem syscalls, 0% idle.

Scale dependence, same state, same host (agent count is the only variable that changes it):
  0 agents -> 3.0% of one core
  2 agents -> 30.5% steady
  6 agents -> 79.7% average, decaying to 18-38%
 17 agents -> 143.4%
 19 agents -> 150-226%, never settles

### Expected behavior

An idle gateway should consume near-zero CPU. Skill file changes should be detected via watch
subscriptions without continuously re-resolving the same watch target paths.

### Actual behavior

The gateway child sustains ~100% of one core while idle. Per-second sampling shows 0.58-0.98
CPU-seconds consumed in every 0.9 s window, with no idle gaps. The profile's hot chains are:
  safeRealpathSync <- resolveContainedSkillPath (10.4%)
  resolvePathViaExistingAncestorSync (8.6%)
  readBudgetedDirEntries <- addTrustedSymlinkSkillWatchTargets <- addSkillSourceWatchTargets
    <- resolveSkillsWatchTargets (6.6% + 2.6%)
No error, warning, or crash is produced; the process remains functional.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.7 (157d8c2)

### Operating system

Windows 10.0.26200 x64 (20 logical CPUs, 63.3 GB RAM), Node v24.22.1

### Install method

npm global (AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\openclaw); gateway launched by Windows Scheduled Task "OpenClaw Gateway" -> gateway.vbs -> gateway.cmd -> node dist/index.js gateway --port 18789 --task-supervisor

### Model

deepseek/deepseek-flash

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> deepseek (direct provider; no proxy or model router in the request path)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not implicated. memory.search uses a separate local Ollama process
(qwen3-embedding:0.6b-gpu, localhost:11434) measured at 8.3% CPU and 14 MB RSS; the spin is
unchanged with the embedding route idle. Only 2 node gateway processes exist (supervisor + child);
the child is the CPU consumer.

### Logs

```shell
No warnings or errors accompany the condition. The gateway service log ends at startup and
contains only bootstrap phases, e.g.:
  [gateway] startup phase: cli.bootstrap.admission.database-readiness ... agentCount=19
Per-second CPU deltas of the gateway child (seconds consumed per 0.9 s window):
  0.78 0.62 0.70 0.77 0.58 0.80 0.72 0.86 0.98 0.95
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Attaching: OpenClaw-gateway-cpu-report-2026-11-02.md (full investigation: environment, V8 profile
self-time and call chains, scaling matrix, ruled-out hypotheses, source-level analysis with line
numbers) and harness.mjs (standalone reproduction harness that drives the exported
ensureSkillsWatcher and counts fs syscalls).

### Impact and severity

Affected: single Windows host running 19 agents.
Severity: Moderate. No crash, no data loss, no incorrect output; one of 20 cores (5% of total
  machine capacity) is permanently unavailable, with sustained heat and some added latency when
  preparing sessions (the same worker performs the scans).
Frequency: Always, continuously, while idle.
Consequence: continuous CPU and power waste, plus reduced headroom for other work.

### Additional information

Not confirmed as a regression: no last-known-good version was established on this host.

Harness measurements driving the exported ensureSkillsWatcher (dist/refresh-BKbsZtV1.mjs):
  one cold pass, single workspace: 1,379.8 ms / 3,839 fs syscalls
  identical params repeated:        0.4 ms / 0 fs syscalls (signature cache works)
  19 agents, cold sweep:            5,729.4 ms / 29,754 fs syscalls
  intra-pass redundancy:            lstatSync 11,324 calls for 411 unique paths (x27.6)
                                    realpathSync 7,068 calls for 335 unique paths (x21.1)

Ruled out by measurement on this host:
  - plugin discovery walk: 73 plugins, full stat+realpath = 14 ms
  - skills.load.extraDirs removal: 172.7% (no change)
  - skills.load.watch=false: no effect. This key feeds the per-agent-command watcher
    (agent-command L3772 `watch: params.watchSkills`), not the gateway refresh path.
  - workspace size: removing two large workspaces 226% -> 143.4%
  - CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=1 + CHOKIDAR_INTERVAL=2000: verified loaded (gateway.cmd executed, log
    mtime advanced); CPU unchanged at ~107%. So the native-watch-capacity branch at L513 is not
    the only trigger.

Related reports: #73088 ("cold registry cache appears to be computed but never used"), #167466
(Windows, sustained single-core CPU and filesystem activity at startup).

Suggested direction: memoise path resolution per pass; single-flight the refresh pass; check the
signature cache before resolveSkillsWatchSourceRoots (L283) so cache hits cost nothing; key the
watch-target cache on stable inputs only.

issues.body:
## Summary

**At least 28** failures on stable **2026.10.5**; child effects unproved; no fix.

```text
service child cleanup identity lost: Error: Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission
```

## Environment

- Ubuntu **24.04.5 LTS**, Linux x64 **6.8.0-147-generic**.
- Node.js **24.21.0**.
- Stock npm OpenClaw **2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)**, managed user Gateway service.
- Official `v2026.10.5` tag resolves to commit
  `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8`.
- No locally patched core files were carried into this stable update.
- No deliberate concurrent schema mutation, forced workflow, restart,
  database repair, integrity bypass or child replay was used to reproduce it.
  The triggering operation was an already occurring ordinary scheduled turn.

## Actual Evidence And Timing

Original native event clocks, UTC:

| Evidence | Observed value |
| --- | --- |
| Host-exec request event | 2026-10-19T19:05:14.174Z |
| Native error result event | 2026-10-19T19:05:15.134Z; `isError:true` |
| Event-clock difference | 960 ms; not measured child runtime |
| Admitted helper stdout | None returned |
| Child start/exit/reap/cleanup receipt | None returned; lifecycle unknown |
| Repetition count | At least twenty-eight unique ordinary native-exec failures, including intervening successful ordinary turns |

Opaque SHA-256 digests of the retained canonical events (no event payloads
or identifiers are published):

```text
request event:

error result event:

```

### Subsequent Ordinary Observation: Did Not Recur

The next untouched normal turn exercised the same pure preparation path:

- Native request: 2026-10-19T19:34:48.783Z, event digest
  `71b87546c13fb672d52fa4a8351e939a5e38e7e59056a77b6f57ded597e6d488`.
- Admitted result: 2026-10-19T19:34:49.693Z, `isError:false`, `ok:true`,
  event digest
  `5f6fb687db628e2c9d9ccb80141195c0c5226716dd392155740503c9a63275b6`.
- The owning turn then genuinely persisted its question and source attempts,
  validated the written plan successfully, completed normal delivery/release
  and reached native terminal at 19:36:16.953Z. At 19:36:43Z the read-only
  handoff check found no matching runtime processes or active OAuth leases.

Intervening independent success required no core patch or restart; it neither repaired nor replayed the earlier unknown child outcome.

### Recurrence On A Different Local Read

A subsequent untouched ordinary turn returned the same full error on a
different local Python command that reads retained JSON research context:

- Request event: 2026-10-19T20:03:25.112Z, digest
  `e9b1da906778bf797fd8fc53bf117112a83053f26dc9aa253eb84005504cfa61`.
- Error result: 2026-10-19T20:03:25.751Z, `isError:true`, digest
  `70720e276fc1c900f1d3a01c94001c691ad8b1d89f045bde0c6b012965916bd5`.
- Event-clock difference: 639ms, not measured child runtime. Again, no helper
  stdout or child start/terminal receipt was admitted; actual child outcome
  remains unknown.

The turn continued using independent retained facts and fresh provider observations, without a same-reference retry, deliberate invalidation, core change, restart or forced workflow. That continuation does not prove the rejected child's outcome.

The local helper is a pure structural preparation operation: its relevant
branch imports no SQLite/OpenClaw state, Node runtime, claim or database
reader. A separate direct local structural invocation succeeds. That control
does **not** exercise native service-child admission and is not a repaired
native-exec result.

The owning workflow retained the failed preparation/persistence disposition;
it did not obtain completed question registration or attempt persistence
through this rejected call. The turn later completed its mandatory reporting
and bookkeeping. Those later technical flags do not prove the rejected exec
operation healthy, its persistence completed or any financial action cleared.

## Installed Source Boundary, Not A Captured Stack

Package-relative locations in this exact installed build:

- `dist/openclaw-state-db-read-connection-BVtgeFmS.mjs:97`:
  `prepareOpenClawStateDirectReader` rejects if the integrity revision differs
  from its epoch, or an existing-schema context lacks integrity/proof.
- `dist/exec-approvals-store-B7WwLRrI.mjs:218`:
  `prepareExecApprovalsCurrentRead(context)` prepares this direct reader;
  its returned guard independently rechecks admission and reads current policy.
- `dist/plugin-node-host-YOtba4hi.mjs:102`:
  plugin-exec authorization captures the worker context and prepares that
  current-policy reader. The approvals store has another authorization
  settlement caller; this error alone does not select between them.
- `dist/child-DMrKblk4.mjs:702`:
  service-child `loseIdentity` wraps its message as
  `service child cleanup identity lost: ...`.

The retained tool error is **not a JavaScript stack**. It does not reveal the
exact caller branch, concurrent writer, integrity epoch/revision/proof values,
schema operation, or ordering relative to process spawn. The source matches
identify a boundary to investigate, not a proven root cause or proof that
Python itself accessed shared state.

Exact installed artifact SHA-256s:

```text

44ec8e0167df30d308818637a70de85436604f8404a6bcd9b86b127135d84664

8065787d49ea90be0af69e2f45deaf003e11db127fbe6c8d3769a06bb246228e
```

## ClawSweeper Follow-Up

The [review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6275795871)
requests an isolated failing native stable case, payload-free admission and
child-lifecycle diagnostics, and the same case on pinned main. **These behavioral
proof requests remain unfulfilled.** No repair PR or incident-matched fix is claimed.

Source inspection confirms that merged [PR #169584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169584),
commit `d502f1aac87aee6c99c92a8a667810a2fefa4d88`, replaces the
[stable direct-reader policy preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8/src/infra/exec-approvals-store.ts#L148)
with a [worker-prepared current-policy owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d502f1aac87aee6c99c92a8a667810a2fefa4d88/src/infra/exec-approvals-store.ts#L286).
The changed path is a relevant candidate, not proof it resolves this incident.
Its separately reported synthetic allow/revocation evidence is not this case.

Inspected suites, an inconclusive bounded attempt and successful native controls
are recorded below, not a failure repro or suite verdict. Consumer/invalidator,
integrity values and child outcome remain unknown. Keep open; do not duplicate
existing repairs, manufacture revocation, patch/restart core or replay unknown work.

## Existing Repair And Duplicate Check

[PR #167486](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167486) already fixes
redundant schema initialization invalidating prepared exec integrity proof.
Its merge `5a0baa04e5bbe68767a9691497324c47c1ba3f96` is an ancestor of this
installed stable commit; GitHub compare reports behind=0. Its existing
real-worker/native-printf proof is useful prior work. This observation does
**not** establish that the same schema producer ran or regressed, nor justify
reimplementing that repair.

Distinct related boundaries, not duplicate evidence:

- [#176353](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176353), fixed by
  [#176413](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176413), concerns
  `Exec approval policy is unavailable or changing before execution`
  during Allow Once approval bookkeeping. This report has a different exact
  integrity error and no observed Allow Once trigger.
- [#161171](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/161171) concerns
  session-accessor prepared-admission tests, not this observed exec guard.
- [#161439](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/161439) tracks
  shared-state responsiveness. No event-loop/SQL-wait attribution was captured
  for the 960-ms event interval here; this is not evidence of its historical
  ordinary-workload stall.
- [#139887](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/139887) concerns a
  macOS EPERM process-group cleanup observation, not Linux integrity admission.

Read-only repository searches for the exact full error, `Direct shared-state
reader`, `prepareExecApprovalsCurrentRead`, and related integrity/exec-approval
terms found the merged repair above but no issue tracking this exact new
stable-release observation. Search results are not proof that no duplicate
exists; please consolidate under an existing exact owner if appropriate.

## Reproduction Status And Proposed Minimal Isolation

**No deterministic failing stable/main case or before/after repair proof exists.**
Use a credential-free Linux/Node24 scratch fixture and actual native consumer:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-approvals-schema-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Existing #167486 first-read/profile/provenance/bound-approval/audit and reopen
cases are starting points; the older-checkout attempt below timed out without
a verdict. A harmless native request may use
`python3 -c 'import json; print(json.dumps({"ok": True}))'`; direct Python is
not equivalent. Expand only from an observed failure.

Capture payload-free consumer, captured/current revision+epoch/proof, generation,
invalidating writer/committed outcome and ordered launch/exit/reap/cleanup.
Authorized execution must settle once; genuine authority changes must deny.
Unknown outcomes, blind replay and integrity bypass are not repair evidence.

## Evidence Ledger / Remaining Gaps

Supplied: pinned stable environment, canonical timings/digests, artifacts and repair/duplicate checks. At least28 distinct failures are retained. Positive controls and later ordinary success are not failing reproductions or fixes. The failing consumer, admission invalidator, child lifecycle, matched-main regression and repaired exactly-once/real-revocation behavior remain unproved.

## Further Ordinary Recurrence (2026-10-19)

An untouched later ordinary turn returned the identical full native exec error
twice more, bringing the retained total at that observation to four unique native errors:

| Local operation | Request UTC / SHA-256 | Error UTC / SHA-256 | Event-clock gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Read retained JSON context | `23:03:56.178Z` / `46c2b8ec08da558a09fd3ac7a438e4cf6f3aed7d52198670ec35241bc8716311` | `23:03:56.772Z` / `e9bedb11159fbb0bca1ba35381f05870205dd9e496142e34f50dfd7b5bc9d1e2` | 594 ms |
| Local finalization wrapper | `23:04:58.141Z` / `5ab1aabe66e4fa3547a9a1da9fad21d6af70bed2bbcdcdb72ec38925d0bb2ef6` | `23:04:58.660Z` / `0b33c2bce5dd057ab1e15ab6dd5d9b69e37bcb63d764ec7b7122ad1885e19b25` | 519 ms |

Both matched canonical results are `isError:true` with the quoted wrapped error. Intervals are event-clock spacing, not child runtimes. Neither admitted stdout/terminal proof; child effects remain unknown. Wrapper echoes are excluded and neither uncertain command was replayed.

The owning turn later reached a separate real finalizer result: exit 1 for a
missing new-candidate row. Canonical save, delivery, status and release completed,
while three technical verification checks were false. This establishes degraded
workflow completion, but does not establish that either native integrity failure
caused the independent candidate-registration failure. No Python decimal error,
broker failure, trade execution or financial clearance is inferred.

At this dated follow-up, latest stable was still `2026.10.5`; no core patch/update, Gateway restart or production/approval-data edit was used.

### Isolated Investigation Status

Exact installed boundaries were rechecked; consumer/invalidator and child outcome
remain unknown. Successful controls do not fulfill the failing-case requests above.

### Executed Stable Native Positive Controls

**Real environment tested:** the unmodified installed `2026.10.5` artifacts on
Linux / Node `v24.21.0`. A fresh process inherited only an explicit small `env -i`
environment: executable search path and scratch `HOME`, `TMPDIR`,
`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. No production configuration,
state, provider credentials, Gateway connection or listening port was used.

**Exact behavior exercised:** stock database bootstrap seeded a synthetic

ordinary feature schema; stock asynchronous database close completed. Two
scenarios then reopened that scratch database and used stock
`captureOpenClawStateWorkerContext` + `prepareExecApprovalsCurrentRead`:

1. Baseline after reopen.
2. An ordinary `listAgentProvenance()` worker read after reader preparation and
   before native launch.

Each scenario invoked the installed process supervisor's native
`anchored-shell` owner with the harmless command
`printf 'isolated-native-ok\n'` and its `required-all` cleanup owner. A fixture
guard called the actual prepared policy reader at every stock supervisor guard
callback and asserted the synthetic policy remained `full` / `off`. The fixture
did not invoke the full model/tool transport, plugin-exec policy consumer or
approval-settlement consumer; it exercises their implicated reader boundary with
a real native service child, not their complete authorization flow.

**Observed result, without a patch:** both real native calls returned exit 0
with exactly the expected stdout; each made six current-policy reader checks,
and both native scope cleanup joins completed. Captured epoch and current
revision were both `0` throughout; actual proof was present and unchanged.
The captured context's `existingSchemaPath` was absent. No diagnostic fields
were modified, no schema was dropped and no revocation was manufactured.

```text

provenance-after-preparation: checks=6, exitCode=0, expectedStdout=true, scope-cleanup-joined
```

Both scenarios and the enclosing process were joined; no control child was left
running. These hashes identify retained controls, not an attached reproducible
failing fixture.

Successful isolated stock-native controls only: no failing repro, production child-outcome proof, incident-matched main comparison or main deployment/test.

### Fifth Ordinary Occurrence: First Cycle Command

The next untouched scheduled turn failed on its first cycle-admission command,
before any broker/provider call. At that observation the retained total was
five unique native errors with the same exact message.

- Request event: `2026-10-19T23:32:13.679Z`, SHA-256
  `8f83952c1f5cd2d13a57e3d2e55be9a87578ae1cfdd720942244b25b0fc5346c`.
- Error event: `2026-10-19T23:32:14.761Z`, `isError:true`, SHA-256

  orchestration mirror is excluded from the unique count.
- Native turn terminal: `2026-10-19T23:32:28.472Z`. No admitted child stdout or
  child terminal receipt, no completion receipt and no broker/provider call
  were observed. The rejected command's actual child outcome remains unknown.
- Independent read-only checks found no claim for this exact turn and no
  matching runtime process; OAuth leases were zero. These observations do not
  substitute for the missing rejected-child terminal receipt. No command was
  replayed, no claim forcibly released, and no completion was manufactured.

This occurrence independently blocks admission before the earlier candidate-registration defect. Caller, invalidator and spawn order remain unknown. First-feature scratch exploration produced no result and is excluded; subsequent inspection found no scratch/native-control processes. Outstanding proof requests remain open.

### Sixth Unique Canonical Recurrence: Local Contract Read

Additional ordinary recurrence on unmodified stable2026.10.5, 2026-10-20; not a fix.

The directly recorded native `exec` request was a read-only local file operation:

A plain local workflow-contract file read, not a database operation.

The working directory was the configured agent workspace. No host override was supplied. This command did not request any broker action, network operation, credential change, or state repair.

The owning scheduled turn later reached native terminal at `2026-10-20T00:07:11.044Z`. ## Seventh Ordinary Recurrence: 2026-10-20T01:04Z

Sanitized evidence for the existing issue #177656. This is an observation of an ordinary scheduled cycle, not an injected reproduction or a claim that the issue has been fixed.

### Environment And Pinned Code

- Installed package version, read directly from package.json: **OpenClaw 2026.10.5 stable**.
- package.json SHA-256: `44c4e2ed880440392d10224f0fec7c4f5ad59d93008827586e2acb038a5a21ee`.
- Installed compiled shared-state reader `dist/openclaw-state-db-read-connection-BVtgeFmS.mjs` SHA-256: `591be6e4250c8d18e3a788b98a578b0488ea6415e44df2dc549b7098c4e5aad7`.
- Installed compiled child lifecycle owner `dist/child-DMrKblk4.mjs` SHA-256: `8065787d49ea90be0af69e2f45deaf003e11db127fbe6c8d3769a06bb246228e`.

### Observed Chronology

1. Ordinary scheduled native turn began at **2026-10-20T01:02:13.461Z**, using the existing native OpenAI/Codex path and unchanged auth/runtime owner.
2. At **01:04:49.411Z**, a native `exec` tool call requested a bounded read-only Python helper that indexes retained local venue proposals. Shape only: `{command: <fixed Python helper plus symbol argument>, workdir: <existing workflow directory>, title: <source lookup description>}`. Command payload, symbol, private paths and identifiers are intentionally omitted.
3. At **01:04:50.391Z**, the corresponding native runtime `tool.result` recorded `success: false`. Exact error:

   Same exact wrapped error quoted in Summary.

4. Another retained-source read was admitted at **01:04:50.538Z** and completed at **01:04:51.890Z**. The turn continued through later source projections and normal finalization.
5. A matching workflow completion receipt recorded save, report, status publication and release success at **01:07:24.267100Z**. Native runtime recorded `session.ended` with `status: success` at **01:07:26.676Z**; the native session window recorded **DONE** at **01:07:26.884Z**.

### What This Proves / Does Not Prove

- Real pinned-stable native exec failure, not an inferred timeout or optional remote failure; child spawn remains unknown.
- Reader line97 and child owner line702 are source correlations, not root cause or a minimal repro.
- Technical completion retained **execution untested** and an unresolved dated venue/calendar gate; no financial clearance follows from DONE.
- Observer used bounded read-only inspection only, without forced workflow, provider/order probe, claim/auth change, restart or core patch. Private proof retains exact sequences/hashes; Privacy below applies.

## October 20: Two Further Ordinary Native-Exec Failures

Two more distinct failed call/result pairs brought the retained count at that observation to **at least nine**. Orchestration echoes are excluded.

## Pinned Environment

Actual installed stable package remains OpenClaw **2026.10.5**, with no core patch or main/beta change for this observation.

- package.json SHA-256: `44c4e2ed880440392d10224f0fec7c4f5ad59d93008827586e2acb038a5a21ee`.
- Installed `dist/openclaw-state-db-read-connection-BVtgeFmS.mjs` SHA-256: `591be6e4250c8d18e3a788b98a578b0488ea6415e44df2dc549b7098c4e5aad7`.

## Native Boundaries

Both occurred during one ordinary scheduled native workflow; no reproduction or provider probe was forced.

1. **02:03:21.114Z → 02:03:21.326Z**: native `exec` call requesting a bounded read-only whole-account local projection; recorded `tool.result success=false`. The underlying canonical assistant tool call/result were timestamped 02:03:21.158Z / 02:03:21.297Z. Shape only: `{command: <fixed local projection plus owned run stamp>, workdir: <existing workflow directory>, title: <projection description>}`. No command payload, account data or identifiers are included.
2. **02:08:33.633Z → 02:08:35.182Z**: another native `exec` call/result, again `success=false`. The retained title describes preparing final source-binding stdin assembly before a final native refresh. The actual command is retained only as `[Malformed diagnostic JSON redacted]`; its exact command/effects are therefore **unknown**, not asserted read-only. The corresponding canonical failed result was timestamped 02:08:34.952Z.

Exact error in both failed native results:

```text
Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission
```

Both are the bare admission-error variant, not the cleanup wrapper. Child spawn/exit/effects remain unknown; failed tools do not prove no spawn or authorize replay.

## Continuation And Impact

- The first failure interrupted a financial-data projection, rather than an irrelevant optional lookup. A later owned projection returned `ok=true` at **02:03:34.652Z**, and further final native projection work completed. This does not erase the initial real failure or prove the core bug fixed.

issues.body:
### Summary

On 2026.10.9 (Linux, single host), `[sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold` lines are dominated by `operation=state.admission.fast-path`: **239 of ~400** slow holds in 24h, with `sqlMs` 1000–2700 ms while `beginMs`, `hostAdmissionWaitMs` and `commitMs` are ~0.

Because this runs inside a deferred **write** transaction and SQLite allows a single writer, other state writes (spawn / delivery / audit) queue behind it. With a long read in flight it can amplify into multi-second stalls and watchdog aborts (symptom reported in #191242).

### What the check does

`isOpenClawStateSchemaFastPathEligible()` opens a deferred transaction labelled `state.admission.fast-path` and, on each call, checks:

- supported schema version + content version (must be 20)
- schema cookie
- runtime integrity attestation
- table-contract shape (113 tables)
- legacy repair guard

### Evidence

- 239 occurrences / 24h; `phases={"beginMs":0,"sqlMs":1000-2700,"hostAdmissionWaitMs":0,"commitMs":0}`
- state DB ~142 MB, 113 tables, 243 indexes, WAL, `synchronous=2`
- no schema changes in the window; no long-running migration
- samples are `isMainThread=true` (unlike #188274, which covers misleading `async=false` labels)

### Expected

Compute eligibility once per process, keyed by schema cookie / content version, and reuse it; or perform the check outside the write transaction so admission cannot block other writers.

### Related

- #191242 slow commits block interactive history reads (same symptom family, different phase)
- #192378 forward-ports admission/lease fixes (open/lease ordering, not this check)
- #188274 diagnostics labeling

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.9
- single-node Linux gateway, state DB on local disk

issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.10.5, a WhatsApp group session repeatedly rejected new work with `DispatchSessionRefreshRequiredError` / `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` after a Codex turn ended with a terminal dynamic tool result and settled-turn context capture failed with `reason=invalid_content`.

The incident investigation observed this sequence twice on 2026-10-26 UTC. Both times a queued inbound arrived within about two seconds of finalization failure. Four earlier capture failures on 2026-10-25 had no inbound waiting and did not produce the persistent stall. This is an observed correlation; we have not built a deterministic reproduction of the initial race.

## Observed impact and retained ownership

The first stall persisted from approximately 00:42 to 05:25 UTC; another began at 05:59. Every later turn start on that session failed. The investigation found the ended run still named by `activeWriterRunId`, `lifecycleRunId`, and `restartRecoveryRuns` in its session entry. The unchanged session history remained available.

Re-read gateway logs for the second incident contain ten start-conflict records from 05:59:13 to 06:06:35 UTC, including both error names. Sanitized representative output:

```text
2026-10-26T05:59:13.183+00:00 [whatsapp] Failed handling inbound web message: DispatchSessionRefreshRequiredError: Session "agent:main:whatsapp:group:<redacted>" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-10-26T06:00:34.794+00:00 [ws] agent errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Session "agent:main:whatsapp:group:<redacted>" changed while starting work. Retry. | SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED
```

## Supported recovery

`sessions.abort` with `clearQueued` did not release the stale state. The original operator investigation called `sessions.recover {key, agentId:"main"}` at 06:09:33 UTC. It returned `ok`, retained the key and session ID, and launched a continuation. The session completed work at 06:13:58 with no subsequent start conflicts observed in that window. A later read-only `sessions.describe` confirmed the same session ID, `status:"done"`, `hasActiveRun:false`, and `activeRunIds:[]`.

No direct database writes or session reset are needed for this recovery. Restart recovery also cleared an earlier instance, but restarting is disruptive to unrelated live turns.

## Requested prevention and acceptance

Reconcile provably dead lifecycle/recovery ownership through the existing recovery owner after failed settled-turn capture, or before a queued inbound is admitted. Preserve foreground work, pending delivery and unfinished input custody. A regression should exercise finalization capture failure plus a waiting inbound and show that the same session admits work without reset or gateway restart.

We chose a bounded host-timer fallback using the supported recovery RPC rather than clearing markers in a local bundle patch. The evidence does not establish that every retained claim is safe to drop.

Related, but not established as the same cause: #181770 / #181801 and #181952 discuss killed-session recovery residue; #127195 explains why identical work-start errors do not identify the rejecting guard. #164191 concerns a different finalization-capture failure reason, `field_limit`.

Environment: Docker gateway `openclaw-runtime:2026.10.5-local`, OpenClaw 2026.10.5, Node v24.21.0, native Codex runtime, per-agent SQLite session storage, WhatsApp group inbound. Private chat identifiers and transcripts are omitted.
