issues.body:
Release-tooling pull requests with the `release-fast-lane` label can add unallocated test lines while all required CI gates pass. The full baseline bundle is deliberately omitted on this route, but no retained job runs the test-line budget guard.

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192297 added 65 test lines without an allocation. In https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41730525051, baseline ratchets were skipped, security-fast passed, and the aggregate gate passed. Main subsequently reported a 47-line inherited deficit after intervening test deletions: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41739237906/job/126276272288.

Keep the narrow release route and its existing required jobs. Run the existing dependency-free test-line checker in security-fast against the checked-out merge’s verified first parent, before landing. Do not add a runner, enable the full baseline bundle, or relax the budget.

prs.title: fix(codex): avoid Gateway freezes during app-server launch
prs.body:
**Landing status:** resource tradeoff accepted; rebased onto main `52da7f61d3aaefbdbee2f637efa1c5a924f0b920`. Final UI failure investigation and exact-head verification are in progress.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the whole Gateway freezing when the OS stalls while launching a local Codex app-server executable.

## User Impact

Other Gateway requests remain responsive while Codex process creation waits. App-server startup still waits for the executable, and the existing shared-client reuse, idle retirement, process registration, and descendant cleanup contracts remain intact. No configuration or database migration is required.

The tradeoff is one stdio worker per retained app-server, including its heap and stream-forwarding CPU cost. The measurements below expose that cost; this is an availability repair, not a throughput optimization.

## Why This Change Was Made

`child_process.spawn` synchronously waits on the native exec-status pipe. Moving native creation and bounded stdio forwarding into a worker preserves the Gateway as the OS parent. The existing Linux spawn broker changes the native parent and can fall back to direct spawning, so using it here would require a broader process-owner migration.

A late catalog launch does not imply repeated Gateway prewarm. The service captures its async task context; later catalog work retains that label. Ordinary reads use resident/persisted rows. A demand-gated safety refresh can launch a replacement after the shared client has retired for inactivity or exited. There is no demonstrated per-read spawn to remove, and the safety refresh is needed for silent older metadata/membership changes.

The upstream contract was personally checked at [Codex d84c872](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/d84c872464aca4821dc5cb548a651651aefd84fa): [single-client stdio startup](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d84c872464aca4821dc5cb548a651651aefd84fa/codex-rs/app-server/src/lib.rs#L817), [initialize admission](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d84c872464aca4821dc5cb548a651651aefd84fa/codex-rs/app-server/src/message_processor.rs#L1003), and [newline transport/closure](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d84c872464aca4821dc5cb548a651651aefd84fa/codex-rs/app-server-transport/src/transport/stdio.rs#L63).

Runtime TypeScript grows by 176 lines (+1 package worker-entry line; generated artifacts net zero). That is the stdio/event bridge needed to preserve direct-parent ownership. No cache, new config, public SDK export, or schema change was introduced.

## Evidence

The blocked-spawn regression fails with the original transport: a 350 ms injected native-spawn wait produces a **369.416 ms** host timer gap against the <150 ms requirement. The candidate passes, preserving exact payload, trailing stderr, native exit facts, and close. Focused consumer tests cover startup refusal/retry, durable registration, native config, node execution, upgrade, orphan recovery, and containment. Final transport suite: **22 passed**. Final build passed in **2m45.5s**; Node and Bun native worker stdio probes passed. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2 after fixing a reproduced worker-stdin retirement leak.

The committed isolated Gateway proof exercises public `sessions.catalog.list` with the pinned native app-server. During its **356 ms** injected spawn hold, **15 health RPCs completed**, maximum overlapping latency **39 ms**; all **32 synthetic sessions** were returned. Gateway shutdown completed cleanly in 5.641 s and Codex exited 0. A separate source-loader stall occurred before the spawn interval; this does not claim the entire source-loaded cold flow is stall-free.

### Transport measurements

Median (p95), five samples per arm; with five samples p95 is the observed maximum. Source-loaded transport on Apple M3 Ultra / macOS 27.0.1 / Node v26.12.1.

| Metric | Native baseline | Worker candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Host timer gap during 350 ms wait (ms) | 362.996 (365.373) | 12.098 (12.103) |
| Cold startup, no injected wait (ms) | 95.967 (97.273) | 114.721 (118.419) |
| Cold startup with 350 ms wait (ms) | 465.928 (467.983) | 481.681 (483.346) |
| Cold main-thread CPU, no wait (ms) | 1.542 (1.608) | 1.382 (1.616) |
| Cold total CPU, no wait (ms) | 1.965 (2.044) | 24.076 (25.000) |
| Warm 17.5 MiB stream time (ms) | 18.176 (19.757) | 23.675 (26.160) |
| Warm main-thread CPU (ms) | 13.918 (15.663) | 14.456 (17.285) |
| Warm total CPU (ms) | 15.343 (29.648) | 32.117 (51.392) |
| Main sampled allocation (MiB) | 0.501 (0.856) | 0.730 (0.871) |
| Worker peak heap (MiB) | 0.000 (0.000) | 9.331 (9.354) |
| Worker sampled allocation (MiB) | 0.000 (0.000) | 5.075 (5.279) |

A/A no-wait cold startup medians were 95.752 / 96.454 ms (ranges 93.892–97.391 / 95.250–97.091); warm stream medians 17.495 / 17.628 ms (ranges 17.151–17.596 / 17.364–17.865). The blocked-spawn A/A timer gaps were 362.331 / 357.946 ms. Allocation A/A medians were 0.564 / 0.563 MiB. All 80 samples preserved byte hashes, stderr, native exit, and exactly one spawn.

The worker removes the injected main-thread pause, but no-wait cold startup is 19.5% slower, warm transfer time is 30.3% higher, and warm total CPU is 109.3% higher. It adds about 9.33 MiB worker heap in this source-loaded workload. These adverse changes exceed A/A variation; the performance lead explicitly accepted them below. Production packaged-worker absolute costs were not benchmarked. CPU totals cover the host process (main thread plus workers), excluding the native child. Allocation figures are sampled JavaScript heap allocations; worker memory is peak JavaScript heap, not total process RSS or external buffer allocation.

Commands:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/codex-stdio-spawn-measure.ts --root <fixture-root> --prepare
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/codex-stdio-spawn-measure.ts --root <fixture-root> --output <results.json>
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/codex-catalog-gateway-proof.ts --state-dir <new-isolated-directory>
```

Acceptance fixed in the committed runner: one real spawn; byte-identical stdio, drained stderr and natural exit; candidate host timer gap <150 ms during the 350 ms forced native-spawn wait. Five interleaved A/A and A/B pairs per mode/delay, separate timing/allocation passes, main/total/worker CPU and worker heap, with host load recorded. Resource regressions are exposed rather than automatically accepted.

The transport fixture contains 62,000 actual workspace files/1.1 GB and 6,000 synthetic metadata rows, streaming 17.5 MiB. The workspace is launch cwd context, not scanned. Its explicitly inert sparse 35 GiB placeholder is not a database or workload proof. These macOS/source-loaded measurements do not reproduce a btrfs kernel stall or a full 35 GiB catalog workload; no real user data or inference credentials are used.

### Check results and inherited failures

`pnpm check:changed --staged` was run. All patch-caused failures were fixed; source/extension types, scripts/root test types, changed-code lint/format, import cycles, SDK boundaries/budgets, and ratchets pass. The broad command remains red for 20 pre-existing `max-lines` violations exposed because the worker package manifest edit disables untouched-file advisory overrides. All 20 reproduce with identical counts from exact base `0c0875810a6ced55235a855a7e10499ecf5a8a87`; each introduction and its actual parent were replayed under the unchanged lint rule (20 passing parents, 20 failing introductions). These remain unresolved main regressions, not noise.

<details>
<summary>Exact-base inherited line-cap attribution</summary>

| File | Cap | Exact base | Parent → introduction | Introducing commit / PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts` | 700 | 710 | 695 → 710 | [`f964859d9f2b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f964859d9f2bd045420271b95f6523df70285bd4) / [#176154](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176154) |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts` | 700 | 701 | 695 → 701 | [`96583dd4e435`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/96583dd4e435e01783f9a041c030f0d6e7ec6431) / [#154125](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154125) |
| `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts` | 1000 | 1062 | 937 → 1010 | [`dbcbb79c5c96`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/dbcbb79c5c96e37b053bd4ac4971ae60e53d30c1) / [#188802](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188802) |
| `extensions/oc-path/src/cli.test.ts` | 1000 | 1004 | 990 → 1004 | [`29447408ffeb`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/29447408ffeb449455d0e577592111bc0eba05ee) / [#178692](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178692) |

An adjacent cleanup-test fix restricts its process observation to the known descendant PID. Its old full macOS census reproduced EPERM against unrelated user processes on the exact base; that regression was introduced by #174284 and retained by #175368. Native containment itself still uses its existing full lineage checks. Both affected cleanup scenarios now pass.

The first exact-head security scan failed on the unchanged Git-environment clearing fixture. OpenGrep 1.32.0 reproduced the finding on exact base 0c0875810a6c and introduction 9284c76dea58 / #167443; the actual introduction parent is clean. A documented exact-rule exception on that removal-list fixture preserves the rule, inputs, assertions, and runtime behavior. The actual scanner wrapper now passes locally, and a fresh Codex review is scoped-clean. The final hosted security gate must pass; it is not bypassed.

Test cost accounting: the dedicated allocation grants exactly the 166 net test lines in this change, covering blocked native-spawn responsiveness, revoked launch authority after worker startup, and native kill with caller stdin still open. These exercise distinct lifecycle failures; the shared scalar is unchanged. The final transport run passed 22 tests in 32.80s wall time (30.22s Vitest duration, dominated by source compilation; test execution below 1s). The documented transport-spawn mock retires exactly one existing baseline entry; it is pruned with no new mock exception added to the baseline. CI caught both missing accounting updates, reproduced locally and repaired together; no runtime behavior changed.

The previous CI head also exposed a new main regression in the Draft capability-menu E2E tests. On exact CI parent `32f7f7fb14eabce0b2c204ce7809b694ccd7617f`, all three unchanged tests fail for the removed Draft checkbox; all three pass on `befd729208b6db1780d59cf4b29c5b70679bf7ad`. Introducing commit `2efd33452f2dae07bbad86a78600147fa2011e99` removes that menu item without migrating this test file. No UI source was changed here. A separate cron-inventory CI assertion did not reproduce: the exact-parent file passed 5/5. Its cause remains unresolved; this passing replay is not a fix and is not an inherited-failure waiver.

### Final exact-head result

Final head `f5378538a4050c70bf3b9c915309e5f48534cbf3` completed [CI run 41776377594](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41776377594) with one failing UI E2E lane plus its aggregate gate; all other jobs, including security, test accounting and cron UI, passed. Tested main parent was `8b9e240149fb8c3c871f92a653a0423fcc8b320d`. Draft failures again reproduced 3/3 on this exact parent, retaining the 2efd3345 attribution. The saved-widget case (`Ready` versus `Updated`) and stale-sidebar-rename case (missing page error) passed unchanged on the exact parent: 1/1 and 3/3 respectively. They remain unresolved and unproven inherited; no admin exception or CI rerun was used. The earlier cron replay/current-CI pass is not claimed as a fix.

Not merged. No merge or auto-merge request has been submitted.


## Resource acceptance

**ACCEPTED — performance lead decision, 2026-11-04, under Peter’s standing unattended decision authority.** Accepted costs: **~9.33 MiB worker heap, +19 ms cold launch, +5.5 ms elapsed / +17 ms CPU per 17.5 MiB streamed**. Production on **2026-11-04 03:51Z** showed a **67.5 s whole-Gateway freeze** from a main-thread spawn during a filesystem stall. Worker creation has a bounded, one-time cost per worker; forwarding has the measured per-stream cost. The avoided risk is a full outage-class freeze.

### Final simplification pass

Removed the caller’s redundant `stdio` option: the worker is the sole owner of native pipe creation and already selects `stdio: "pipe"`. Runtime growth is now **176 TypeScript lines + 1 package worker-entry line**, one line below the previous revision. The remaining bridge preserves native PID, exit facts, bounded streams, startup authority, process registration, and cleanup while isolating the blocking spawn. No cache, configuration, or schema was added.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): reserve capacity on PostgreSQL
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PostgreSQL-backed worktree creation fails when reserving capacity because its upsert references an ambiguous `owner` column.

## User Impact

Managed Git worktrees can be created and registered on PostgreSQL. Reservation renewal still requires the same owner; a replacement owner remains protected. SQLite behavior and persisted schemas are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Qualify the target table's existing owner predicate. Allocation, leases, worker dispatch, and error propagation remain with their native owners. The new PostgreSQL suite is now included in the existing conformance runner's default targets and CI shards.

## Executed behavior evidence

The committed `capacity.postgres.test.ts` now calls **`ManagedWorktreeService.create`**, creates a real local Git repository, uses the real allocation/lease/capacity worker transport against **PostgreSQL 17.11**, reads the created checkout's `README.md`, and checks the persisted worktree registry. This case does not mock dispatch, database admission, SQL, Git, or filesystem effects. The suite owns teardown of its isolated database schemas, workers, state, and checkout.

The same final suite was executed twice, changing only the production conflict predicate for the negative control:

```text
Original predicate: .where("owner", "=", key)
FAIL creates and registers a real Git checkout through PostgreSQL-backed allocation
error: column reference "owner" is ambiguous (PostgreSQL 42702)
FAIL admits and renews only the current owner capacity reservation
error: column reference "owner" is ambiguous (PostgreSQL 42702)

Fixed predicate: .where("state_leases.owner", "=", key)
PASS creates and registers a real Git checkout through PostgreSQL-backed allocation — 1195 ms
PASS admits and renews only the current owner capacity reservation — 42 ms
Test Files 1 passed; Tests 2 passed
```

The second case separately proves renewal and refusal after reservation-owner replacement with real PostgreSQL; only that case substitutes the transport grant callback. Both cases failed for the intended SQL error on the control. Fixed source bytes were restored and verified afterward.

Reproduce with a disposable PostgreSQL database:

```sh
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --list
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TEST_POSTGRES_URL" -- src/agents/worktrees/capacity.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

## Validation and limits

- Default conformance selection now includes this file. Existing target-inventory, disjoint-shard, listing, and argument-validation tests: **8 passed**. Their temporary fixture now declares its actual ESM package type instead of triggering an unexpected Node warning.
- Real PostgreSQL green run: **37.08 seconds wall**, including **29.7 seconds** of compiled-worker preparation; test bodies total about **1.24 seconds**. Negative control: **141.45 seconds wall**, including cold worker preparation. CI duration remains available on the current head's checks.
- Existing PostgreSQL/SQLite capacity sibling proof: **21 passed** on the original production fix; the production predicate is unchanged by this follow-up.
- Targeted agents-other and tooling test-type checks, typed lint (3 files), formatting, diff checks and staged test-line ratchet passed.
- Fresh installed independent P0–P2 autoreview of this complete candidate: **scoped-clean**, no findings.
- Full runtime/plugin/declaration build already passed with the original seven independent production fixes composed; this correction changes only regression selection, tests and allocation metadata. Current-head PR CI supplies broad proof.
- The **+85 test-line allocation** covers the two distinct PostgreSQL contracts and the one-line ESM fixture setup. The shared baseline is unchanged. No production API, schema, cache, or test-only seam is added.
- This is real production-owner/database/Git evidence, not a live cloud/model run. It makes no claim about worktree retirement: an exploratory `service.remove` call outside the CLI one-shot scope exposed a separate main-thread PostgreSQL admission refusal and was not included in the allocation claim.

## Summary

Address remaining startup risks under storage contention without increasing timeouts, concurrency, or pack-size limits:

- Retry classified native SQLite busy/locked lease-renewal failures asynchronously within the existing retry budget and confirmed expiry. Preserve cancellation, owner replacement, and loss handling; add bounded, sanitized diagnostics.
- Request opportunistic independent file clones through the existing safe-copy boundary, preserving ordinary-copy fallback, metadata, authority, cancellation, and symlink/hardlink policies.
- Include committed indexed `loose-*` Git packs in bounded consolidation while continuing to exclude dot-temporary, kept, and cruft packs.
- Record accepted handoff, dispatch admission, workspace/prompt readiness, and pre-copy wait versus active-copy timing through existing diagnostic owners, without logging message contents.

The native heartbeat scheduler and pack regression are extracted into focused sibling modules to respect existing file-size limits. No new configuration, schema, dependency, or concurrency increase.

## Validation

Prepared commit: `d457f4f5fbcbc855cabdfcd697f7f0d2c82f4b14`.

- Lease contention and loose-pack regressions fail on the base and pass with the fixes; startup timing regressions likewise fail on the base and pass with the fix.
- Isolated full-development dependency snapshot, with no shared release dependency mutation.
- Lease suite: 97 tests passed after extraction; the 8 native renewal cases were rerun after the final callback-binding adjustment.
- Maintenance: 22 tests passed. Copy/host boundary: 8 passed; provisioning service: 15 passed; selection/timing: 3 passed. Changed pack/copy fixtures were rerun after lint cleanup: 5 passed.
- Startup diagnostics/admission/readiness: 33 passed. Prompt stability: 14 passed.
- Core and affected test-owner typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet, documentation links, and whitespace checks passed.

This boundary was not bypassed. Focused tests are not presented as actual-agent runtime proof.

Main already contains the principal Git-maintenance/ref-queue separation repair; this preserves rather than duplicates it. Pack-size/resource limits remain unchanged. Functional copy tests do not establish a throughput improvement.

No live Gateway restart, repack, storage reconfiguration, shared dependency mutation, or deletion was performed. Repository include rules and ClawHub nested-dependency semantics remain unchanged. Deployment and disk-space recovery remain separately coordinated host operations.

prs.title: fix(cron): stopped session turns trigger failure alerts
prs.body:
Fixes #192549

## What Problem This Solves

Stopping a scheduled turn through its session can count as a failure and trigger an unwanted repair or failure alert.

## User Impact

Stopped, restarted, and superseded scheduled turns use the existing interruption policy. Genuine deadline timeouts and stalled executions retain failure semantics. Restart guidance tells the parent how to inspect and continue retained child work without mistaking a stopped execution for a yielded pause or transferring workspace ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-event owner recorded cancellation as a string while cron examined a different, still-live caller signal. Preserve the canonical terminal outcome before asynchronous settlement and cleanup, then pass its classification to cron. Scheduler policy and access rules stay with their current owners; no schema or configuration change is required.

## Evidence

Independent Codex P0-P2 source review passed; bounded independent review verified restart/retained-child guidance against current owners. Syntax, formatting and diff checks pass. New real-controller cases cover user cancellation, restart, supersession, deadline timeout and stall; a normal sessions.abort RPC case joins scheduled settlement and checks that no failure incident or alert is produced. These tests have not executed yet: local dependencies are unavailable, so exact-head hosted proof is pending.

No Team deployment, restart, or live-account proof is claimed. This fixes a proven classification defect; it does not establish that every historical thread failure had this cause.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attached runtime already owns a restricted attach-only worker profile. Use that same private config source for executable tool definition and action handling, including nested snapshot/screenshot reads. Ordinary local Browser calls retain the strict runtime reader and existing host/node authority refusals. The strict-reader import was introduced in #169714; the fix belongs at the attached Browser owner rather than global config bootstrap.

Reported by @davidcittadini. Existing tab-ownership work in #158558 and remote-profile work in #157837/#160516 remain separate.

## Evidence

- RED on pinned main `32f7f7fb14eabce0b2c204ce7809b694ccd7617f` (product tree verified with only the regression overlaid): real durable capability preparation and read/browser policy admission complete, then the real public executable Browser factory fails at `createBrowserToolDefinition` through the strict runtime reader.

Host/node targets remain refused; the cold global reader still throws. Snapshot reaches the intentionally failing synthetic launcher instead of a config read failure.
- The new regression passed on signed head `beb797ebe9f2dcd127673a30e04e60466d15b734` (29.621s test time; 75.40s Vitest wall time including cold build; 80.86s wrapper). Five named Browser/prompt-prefix sibling files passed 118 tests in 103.74s wrapper time. All runtime proof uses secretless AWS Crabbox, Node 24.22.1/pnpm 12.15.0, synthetic state and no inference. Successful browser capture and full worker/provider dispatch remain untested.

- Complete-body Codex autoreview: final local candidate against `aa57331785f4d0b6a4c5a7ccb9ee96b79a46cf99`, P0-P2, scoped-clean with no actionable findings. The subsequent signed rebase onto `32f7f7fb` is patch-identical. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; the hosted review fallback follows when ready.

The 151-line allocation is exactly this one regression's net growth; the shared scalar is unchanged. Mocked factory tests cannot cross the original failure boundary. prs.title: fix(auto-reply): internal reasoning ending in NO_REPLY is delivered when the closing line is padded
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent's internal reasoning is sent to the user as a visible chat message when the reasoning block ends in `NO_REPLY` but its closing line isn't an exact recognized silence phrase, or the token carries trailing punctuation (`NO_REPLY.`).

Closes #165025

## User Impact

Agents using reasoning models that close deliberation with `NO_REPLY` no longer leak the internal monologue (including internal message IDs and turn-taking notes) to end users when the closing line wraps the silence intent in extra prose — e.g. "The user already has my response. Adding more text would be noise." — or when the final token is punctuation-attached. Substantive answers that end with the token stay delivered: the substantive-answer cue guard now covers the whole remaining payload, including the closing line, so an answer containing cues like "answer", "please", or "use" is never suppressed even when its last line also carries a silence clause.

## Why This Change Was Made

`hasReasoningFinalSilentToken` required the final line to match `silentIntentTextRe` exactly (anchored `^...$`), and `stripFinalSilentToken` rejected a token followed by punctuation, so real-world padded closings fell through and the whole reasoning block was delivered. The change:

- tolerates punctuation-only tails after the final token (mirroring the existing punctuation-wrapped token-only matching),
- adds an unanchored closing-line clause check (`silentIntentClauseRe`): subject-bearing predicates keep the original whitelist shape; the new subject-less clauses ("no need to reply", "nothing more to add", "adding more ... noise") are inherently first-person silence intents,
- applies the substantive-answer cue guard to the entire remaining payload (previously only the lines before the closing one, and only when they were non-empty), which both protects the new containment match and closes a gap where a cue inside the closing line itself was ignored,
- leaves closed `<think>...</think>` payloads on their stricter exact-phrase behavior, where an existing test pins an instructional line ("You should not reply to that email.") as deliverable.

Unprefixed replies are untouched: text without a reasoning prefix still never enters this path, preserving the #19537 protection for ordinary answers ending in the token.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on current `main` before the fix: the issue's production payload (prefixed as `thinking:`) returned `false` from `isSilentReplyPayloadText`; with the fix it returns `true`, and a padded "I will stay silent." closing line is now suppressed too.
- Red→green regression tests: the three new suppression tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix; all 70 pre-existing tests pass unchanged, including every #19537 substantive-answer guard and the closed-`<think>` pin.
- `pnpm vitest run src/auto-reply/tokens.test.ts`: 73 tests, ~0.6 s wall locally (single small shard in CI).
- Caller suites green after the fix: `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts`, `replay-history.test.ts`.
- `pnpm check:changed` on this exact head: green except the pre-existing `dead export scan` red, whose findings (e.g. `src/agents/channel-tools.ts`, `ui/src/components/board/*`) are all in files this PR does not touch and include no auto-reply entries — this change adds no new exports.

## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter web search cannot consume the frozen model-less DeepSeek search operation even when a deployment advertises a qualified offer.

## User Impact

The actual `web_search` consumer can select the advertised DeepSeek native or manifest endpoint using only the configured ClawRouter key. It sends explicit `query`, `count` (1–10, default 5), and `need_content:false`, preserves native result metadata, and rejects stale or incompatible offers, unsupported inputs, partial responses and unsafe results without replay or result-URL fetches.

This is conditional client support. Router compiler/dispatch qualification and actual client-plus-Worker proof remain pending; this PR does not activate an offer, infer search fees from Chat pricing, or claim deployed parity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct DeepSeek plugin and proxy consumer share the existing native request/result formatter through `nativeWebSearchCodecs`. Direct-provider credentials, cache ownership and behavior stay unchanged. The existing scoped catalog resolver applies the fresh proxy-key requirement to the selected DeepSeek operation; other search-format eligibility stays unchanged.

Source contract: https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/721 at `e9002974ceb58fdee5537b3053afb21d89ab2d16`, extending the original frozen search codec from https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/491. The Gradium parent https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192052 landed as `d65390bcf36b818b5018029cc00951799bebf0ed`. Published candidate `b8fcbbd0ab0f3a916d1a8fb47f3283ca4c4ff4ba` integrates its five concrete parent repairs through native preparation. Eight of nine DeepSeek-owned blobs are unchanged; the ninth only gains the landed `Number.NaN` correction. Existing xAI and other client routes are preserved.

## Evidence

- Published candidate: `82dd065e23b678e61ad497f9d57fbb4c3da10eae`. [Exact-head native CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41774498964) has passed production/test types, owned extension lint, and all31 actual registered-host cases in Node plus31 in Bun (job126392167684). The invalid-count and redirect corrections now pass. SDK and package/build qualification remain pending; shared speech/catalog failures remain separately investigated.
- Previous candidate `59839dab554f585724780cb15a46bcd40a4d67f3` passed production/test types and extension lint. [Actual registered-host job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41770604440/job/126379763513) passed 28 cases in Node and 28 in Bun, including native 302 and manifest 307 denial with exactly discovery plus the original POST, no redirect or replay. Three invalid-count cases per runtime failed because their assertions expected a raw count message; the real host deliberately sanitizes it into `provider_error` / HTTP 400.
- The current correction changes only those assertions to the actual structured error and the matching allocation (392 to 393). Zero-egress assertions are preserved. Production and SDK code are unchanged from `59839dab`.
- The earlier redirect defect was fixed through the existing guarded-fetch API with `maxRedirects:0`, the original dispatcher/policy/deadline, and before-request grant/caller-abort validation. Other search formats retain their transport. The original timeout wrapper did not forward `maxRedirects`.
- Formatting, syntax, whitespace/privacy and normal commit hooks passed. Actual `createWebSearchTool` and direct-provider fixtures cover native/manifest requests, explicit count, Unicode bounds, native metadata, proxy-key isolation, stale/foreign offers, unsupported inputs, full response validation and cancellation.
- Shared speech explicit-key timeout and other native CI failures remain separate. Prior SDK cancellation produced no report artifact; no pass or failure attribution is inferred from cancellation.

Release-note context: support catalog-scoped DeepSeek web search with the actual native formatter, explicit request limits and proxy-only credentials. The release-owned changelog is unchanged.

At exact `82dd065e23b678e61ad497f9d57fbb4c3da10eae`, [job126392167901](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41774498964/job/126392167901) completed both API renders (832887ms base,827141ms tested head) before the30-minute outer job limit. Decoded added/removed entrypoints and exports are empty. Tested merge `cdd3b759f0c1af43523f3e142b1a6895029006ac` has ordered parents `7ca7ecb804ef50c487831053ca9349a92d3a52b8`, `82dd065e23b678e61ad497f9d57fbb4c3da10eae`; tree `3e737c9c7059596fbdf7b7b37b120ee2bbe94746`. ---

## What Problem This Solves

Native children could not inherit work held only on a parent's retained repository disk. Review also exposed successful file-only fallback after private-history failures and source reassignment reaching child checkpoint publication.

## User Impact

Children receive independent checkpoints with current private Git history and working files. The parent retains its disk, active turn and staging index; the child starts from HEAD plus working files, not a shared disk or copied index. Incomplete or unauthorized exports fail and roll back the unexposed child. No schema, configuration, receipt or permission migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stacked on [#190843](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190843). The non-rewriting integration commit `b782b5d4ff4dee05e6e153206705df7124d19377` preserves both the disk repair `ca21621d5d4fc049ba63041cbf501184d949d196` and checkpoint prerequisite `b081d9ace588fec30b1c23d81a17bd8b0a81a07f` as parents.

The existing mutation queue and snapshot owner capture the exact attached disk under quiescence. Prepared caller/parent authority remains live through Git and node effects; the asynchronous `diskExport.verifyCurrent()` check remains before accepting the child. The common checkpoint owner requires complete private history during export, extraction and child copying. Ordinary recovery/publication keep their file-only fallback. Allocation remains in the shared dependency leaf, and existing rollback owns failed preparation and scope cleanup.

The combined owner exceeded its file-size gate. Unchanged payload/history types moved into a type-only module, preserving the existing exported payload import path; no runtime policy or implementation was moved or weakened.

## Evidence

Source-reassignment probes also observed copying/publication before late binding refusal. The retained-authority repairs reject those effects.
- **Combined runtime qualification:** 2/2 public-handler cases and **50/50 owner cases across three suites** passed. Coverage includes allowed and revoked/reassigned creation, strict history failures, ordinary checkpoint recovery, fresh snapshot custody, parent index/disk/turn preservation and failed-resume cleanup. Timing controls call real implementations and negative cases require production refusals.
- Proof uses real Git, a local node runtime, HTTP transfer, and durable repository/session/placement stores. External provisioning and GitHub identity are fixtures. **No live cloud provisioning or real agent/model product turn was executed.**
- Runtime proof completed before the final type-only extraction. The runtime implementation is unchanged by that extraction; final core, gateway-server and gateway-other test typechecks, 12-file type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Both architecture cycle checks pass. No baseline or ignore exceptions were added.
- **Complete committed-range canonical autoreview:** `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914` → `b782b5d4ff4dee05e6e153206705df7124d19377`, P0–P2, 28 complete frozen context files: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. - Simplification retains existing allocation, source-authority, capture and checkpoint owners. The type-only split preserves the public contract without another runtime owner. The existing regression allocations and shared scalar remain unchanged by integration.
- Current-head hosted CI and overall review readiness remain required; neither is inferred from local review quality.

The three capability CLI failures in [run 41385139959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41385139959/job/125084729643) match a source-level test/owner contract mismatch already present in the actual tested main parent eb488191: PR [#189993](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189993) changed invalid numeric options to propagate ExpectedCliError, while these tests still expected the mocked runtime to throw “exit 1.” Upstream commit [2426aa9288](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2426aa9288a524c9cb912dca3da500f2f09fc83a) repairs exactly those three assertions and is present in main 2777468d26 (observed November 2, 2026). Requested by @galiniliev; adapted from the release-branch work with native OpenClaw owners. All commits retain Galin’s co-author credit.

## Follow-up: integrate the prerequisite consumer repair

The failed `check-test-types-core-4` job at `b782b5d4ff4dee05e6e153206705df7124d19377` is now attributed from its actual diagnostics: `session-create-preparation.test.ts(28,10)` reported TS2724 because the prerequisite had moved `prepareSessionRepositoryWorkspace` without migrating this test import. Integration commit `f79e5ae757f912311cf046cb441927dc4021b1a7` includes prerequisite repair `4d40d62ffd0e81f872ecf82ed813d50c5077598c` while preserving both published heads and all prior ancestry. Independent P0–P2 review of the complete corrected test, allocator leaf, and former owner found no actionable issues. All three reviewed contexts are byte-identical in the integrated disk candidate. The earlier complete stack review and 2 public-handler / 50 production-owner cases remain applicable to unchanged production bytes; the 50-case passing receipt is `stack-owner-proof.log`, not the earlier failed `pr190845-final-disk.log`.

This closes the diagnosed test/type cutover defect, not the current-head CI or overall-rating gates. Existing real Git/local-node/HTTP/durable-store owner proof is not a real Gateway/native-agent turn or live cloud provisioning proof. No such new execution is claimed in this addendum.

A source-pinned, network-isolated Gateway qualification was attempted on `b782b5d4ff4dee05e6e153206705df7124d19377` plus one staged test-only fixture. The repaired disk head `f79e5ae757f912311cf046cb441927dc4021b1a7` differs only in the allocator test import; production bytes are unchanged. prs.title: fix(cli): gateway restart flag conflicts print only "The CLI command failed."
prs.body:
Fixes #192477

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw gateway restart` prints only "The CLI command failed." when you pass a conflicting flag combination (`--skip-deferral` without `--safe`, `--safe` with `--force`, `--wait` or `--preserve-definition`, or `--force` with `--wait`).

## User Impact

User impact: operators see the specific reason, e.g. `Error: --skip-deferral requires --safe`, instead of a generic failure. Message text, exit code 1 and the `--json` envelope are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The five checks threw plain `Error`s, and the root renderer only keeps the message for `ExpectedCliError`. They now throw `ExpectedCliError` (human `Error: <msg>`, machine output = the same message), matching #190366 / #189993. The two native-restart checks move into a small `assertNativeRestartFlags` helper next to the existing safe-restart checks; order is unchanged (the service-mutation guard for `--preserve-definition` still runs first).

## Evidence

- Red/green: `src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.test.ts` now covers all five combinations, asserting `ExpectedCliError` with the original message and no gateway/service calls. On main: 5 failed / 43 passed. With the fix: 48/48.
- Scoped tests: `lifecycle.test.ts`, `lifecycle-core.test.ts`, `register-service-commands.test.ts`: 106/106 passed.
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` (touched files) and `pnpm tsgo:core` clean.

## Proof

Built CLI (`pnpm build`) on main `cee08525d18` vs this branch `a263687138e`, Linux, Node 24, no gateway running, fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (the `--preserve-definition` case uses the default state dir because the service-mutation guard refuses a temp one; it fails before any action). With `--json`, stdout stays a single valid envelope on both; only the stderr line changes.

prs.title: fix: stop retaining configurations after model catalog refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated live model-catalog refreshes retain old serialized configurations indefinitely in the process-wide readiness cache.

## User Impact

Live refreshes stop adding unused readiness entries. Cached callers retain at most 128 compact keys, and an in-place runtime update discards obsolete full-string keys. No configuration, database-schema change or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publication owner always bypassed readiness hits when reporting live discovery outcomes, but still fingerprinted and stored every generation. The fix skips that unused work and bounds the existing cache for callers that can reuse it.

The shared Map and serialized write queue keep their identities across runtime reloads. Alternating configurations remain reusable, file/auth/config fingerprints still invalidate readiness, and price invalidation and SQLite publication remain unchanged. Capacity eviction can cause extra serialized planning; it does not cancel publication.

## Evidence

Base: `7ca7ecb804ef50c487831053ca9349a92d3a52b8`. Final head: `c63dbdccf664b947537227c69046dff5e3472f3d`; tested/reviewed source tree: `68cae1ca2fdac3cfa916e889e5e3b51e90eab084`.

- Original production failed the new live regression: three published generations left three readiness entries instead of zero. All 11 other tests passed.
- Review found that pre-update full-string keys also survive in the shared Map. A seeded legacy key reproduced that failure against the first candidate: one retained entry instead of zero. The final cleanup fixes it.
- Final candidate: **40/40 tests passed across four files**, covering live retention, compact bounded history, alternating configuration reuse, external-file replacement, publication/pruning, write serialization, price invalidation, configuration environment and runtime-source snapshots. The tests use the existing synthetic planner with the real queue, file writer and SQLite publication owner.
- Native Blacksmith Testbox run: [41775377005](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41775377005). Focused test wrapper: 56.36 s; native command: 76.218 s. These are validation durations, not performance comparisons.
- Fresh Autoreview of the complete local change against the base: **scoped-clean through P2**, zero findings. The accepted upgrade finding from the first review was reproduced and fixed before this review. Effective reviewer: GPT-6.1 Sol, medium. This is source review; runtime execution is the separate evidence above.
- Exact-head CI: [run 41777262579](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41777262579). Preflight confirms checkout `c63dbdccf664b947537227c69046dff5e3472f3d`; the required build is in progress.
- Targeted checks printed passing core/dependent-test typechecks, format and lint results, then the combined Testbox invocation lost transport during the full build: native exit 255, workload exit unconfirmed, artifacts withheld. This is not qualified build proof. The PR remains draft; an exact-head CI build is required before ready/landing. The previously completed 40-test invocation exited 0 with settled state and its required JSON artifact.

Removed work: full serialized keys and all readiness fingerprint/admission work for live outcome-bearing refreshes. Production delta **+35 net lines**, justified by the resource bound, compact identity, upgrade cleanup and asynchronous ownership checks. Regression tests **+62 net lines**; the per-change allocation covers exactly those 62 lines.

This establishes removal of demonstrated retained state. It does **not** measure Gateway RSS or catalog-worker memory; the worker uses a different non-persisting path. No latency or RSS improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Acceptance declared before execution</summary>

Acceptance declared before execution:

- Run the committed `src/agents/models-config.write-serialization.test.ts` through the production queue, file writer and SQLite publication owner, using the existing synthetic planner fixture.
- Three distinct live-refresh configurations must publish all three expected catalogs and leave zero readiness entries after settlement. Planning must still run three times.
- Alternating configurations A → B → A with unchanged artifacts must plan only twice; an external artifact replacement must trigger a third plan and restore the expected bytes and private file mode.
- Cached callers must retain compact keys and at most 128 readiness entries. Capacity eviction may cause extra serialized planning; it must not change publication correctness.
- The new retention regression must fail on unchanged production code and pass with the repair. Preserve existing publication/pruning, write serialization and price-invalidation tests.
- Record test wall time and resource/work counts separately. This proof does not measure Gateway RSS, provider latency or the catalog worker, which uses a different non-persisting path. No RSS or timing improvement is claimed.


</details>

prs.title: fix(trajectory): keep quoted tool arguments parseable in exports
prs.body:
Related: #113709.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes malformed trajectory JSON/JSONL exports when quoted tool arguments contain token-like text, even though the export command reports success.

## User Impact

Diagnostic exports remain parseable while retaining default, configured-pattern and registered-secret masking, along with benign values. No configuration migration is required. Thanks to @nimarosa for isolating the escaped-quote case and @alfred429 for the installed-exporter report.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final support-file safety pass uses the existing JSON scalar editor for JSON and JSONL; plaintext keeps its existing path. Configured patterns retain their capture context and bounded scanning. The native-value serializer stays with the JSON token owner.

This maintenance normally merges official main `7ca7ecb804ef50c487831053ca9349a92d3a52b8` to address named CI budget and identity-fixture failures. Upstream history and contributor attribution are preserved. The original ten author files, including all six production owners and the private-browser clipboard fix, remain byte-identical to published `c79c878f`. One existing mention-alignment test now measures the font cap-height target already specified by its CSS and historical implementation.

The author regression allocation remains exactly **44 physical lines**: **42** for consolidated exporter contracts and **2** for the existing clipboard fixture's private-browser option and ownership comment. The mention-measurement correction has **zero net LF growth**. The tracked record is `config/test-lines-allocations/trajectory-export-json-redaction-187082.txt`; the shared scalar and other PR grants are unchanged relative to official main. The retained contracts cover JSON parsing, escaped secrets, default/custom/registered masking, >32 KiB context, root-array/nested output, benign duplicate controls and real clipboard isolation.

## Evidence

Current head `60ab35c07f9109262da3be737ff7819f6c72e05c`, reviewed tree `b17ffd5756ffc8a11561db37c6b361039f127f42`; normal merge parents are `c79c878f` and `7ca7ecb8`.

### Current local validation

Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0 were verified in the actual integration checkout; package/lock pins match the previously qualified install.

- **Exporter and logging:** all **43 exporter cases** and **75 logging cases** pass on the integrated support tree. The combined wrapper completed in **143.19 s**. The later mention-test-only edit leaves their determining source and inputs unchanged.
- **Browser flows:** initial focused selection in eight files produced **19 PASS / 1 FAIL / 39 unselected**, retaining the original failure below. After the measurement correction, both mention viewports pass (**2 cases; 43.43 s wrapper**). The other 18 successful cases retain identical determining production/test inputs: the complete pasted-text file's 11 cases, its GitHub device-copy caller, phone recovery, Memory/sidebar controls, long profile name/email, and the saved widget case. This is scoped proof with valid reuse, not a fresh replay of all UI shards.
- **Types and static gates:** production, backend test-consumer and UI test-consumer types pass; the UI leaf was rerun with both owned UI test files after the measurement edit. Scoped typed lint/format and native staged mock-export, file-cap, test-line and whitespace checks pass. Test lines are **6,452,808 / 6,452,843**, leaving **35**; own LF growth and own credit are both 44.
- **Independent review:** fresh independent local autoreview of all 11 selected files against pinned official main, at P0–P2, is scoped-clean. The reviewed tree matches this commit. Static reviewers did not independently execute the tests.

### Identity-fixture and measurement failures

Official [f1afbff3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f1afbff3a6dad36a2b020cbefd2a949f393b16d6) is now integrated. Its explicit long name/email and missing-avatar 404 fixtures match the canonical profile and avatar contracts. These change the old test premises: the previous null-name/email fallback and all-avatar-URLs-succeed assumptions are not asserted as product requirements. The modified mocked-Gateway scenarios were exercised; this does not include the separate real-Gateway profile case in that upstream commit.

The first integrated run passed the absent-avatar fallback/request/bounds checks, then failed the 390 px alignment assertion for both mentions. The test compared avatar centers with `Range.getClientRects()` text rectangles, whose vertical bounds use [font ascent and descent](https://www.w3.org/TR/cssom-view-1/#dom-range-getclientrects). The existing CSS deliberately centers avatars on capital letters. In the real Georgia 21 px browser case, the old reference differed by **1.296875 px**, while an independent zero-width cap-height/baseline reference differed by **0.0078125 px**. Before/during/after reference and avatar bounds were identical, confirming the measurement probe did not move this layout.

The fixture now measures that cap-height reference immediately after the avatar. The **1 px threshold**, both viewports and all image-state, request, size, line-fit, border, hidden-prefix, text and before/after-bounds assertions remain. Production CSS, permissions, waits and retries are unchanged. With only an evidence-only production-CSS substitution to the historical `vertical-align: middle`, the corrected 390 px test fails at the same alignment check (**1 intended FAIL; 34.54 s wrapper**). This verifies that the new reference still detects a real centering regression. The diagnostic and deliberate-mutation overlays are evidence-only and are not committed.

### Retained causal proof

- **Clipboard:** the earlier [CI run 41718859947](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41718859947) failed when native paste received a code actually copied by the GitHub authorization flow in another context of the shared browser. A two-file replay passed 12 cases without reproducing that schedule. A separate real-UI/Clipboard API control failed before the two-line private-browser selection and passed after it (**57.29 s / 42.75 s suite times**). The original CI ordering is not claimed reproduced. The complete pasted-text file also subsequently passed all 11 cases in CI; that owner fix remains unchanged.
- **Compiled CLI:** at `391ffec1`, normal `pnpm openclaw sessions export-trajectory` on private synthetic SQLite data returns 0 but emits two invalid files under a six-production-file revert control; the candidate parses four JSON documents and five JSONL rows while preserving masks, benign values, 0600 modes and manifest bytes. Those six production blobs remain unchanged. This keeps its named support-tree scope; the current integrated exporter API suite is the freshly executed boundary here.

prs.title: fix(perplexity): preserve synthesized search after Sonar shutdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: direct Perplexity `web_search` model/base-URL overrides would stop producing synthesized answers when Sonar Chat Completions reaches end of support on September 27, 2026.

## User Impact

User impact: existing direct Sonar overrides keep returning one synthesized, cited answer through Agent API. Native Perplexity Search API users and OpenRouter/custom chat-completions users keep their current transports and response shapes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Perplexity now maps the legacy Sonar models to Agent API presets. This change adds a direct-Perplexity `agent_api` transport, applies the official `sonar` → `fast`, `sonar-pro` → `low`, `sonar-reasoning-pro` → `medium`, and `sonar-deep-research` → `high` mappings, moves freshness into the Agent API web-search tool filters, and parses typed Agent API output. Non-Sonar direct model IDs are passed through with web search enabled.

The default Search API path remains `POST /search`. OpenRouter and non-Perplexity base URLs remain on `/chat/completions`; this PR does not force Agent API semantics onto those compatible endpoints.

prs.title: fix(agents): derive the legacy model allowlist from the authored config
prs.body:
Closes #191215

## What Problem This Solves

On a config with no `meta.migrations.modelPolicyAllowlist` marker and no `agents.defaults.modelPolicy`, `computeModelPolicyAllowlist` read the keys of `agents.defaults.models` as a legacy model allowlist. The Anthropic extension injects entries into that map at runtime to set `cacheRetention: "short"`, so an operator who never authored any model settings ends up with an accidental allowlist, and every explicit override outside it fails with `model not allowed`.

## User Impact

Runtime-injected model metadata no longer counts as an authored allowlist, so an explicit override such as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` is admitted. An operator-authored `agents.defaults.models` map keeps its exact legacy restriction; the injected keys are excluded from it and no other ref changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's next step on the issue: "Fix policy derivation at the authored-to-runtime boundary." The legacy refs are now resolved from the authored config source instead of the runtime config, through the existing `projectConfigOntoRuntimeSourceSnapshot` owner.

`computeAuthoredModelPolicyAllowlist` lives beside the legacy-allowlist detection it wraps (`src/config/model-policy-allowlist-migration.ts`, well under its line cap), so `src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts` — a grandfathered over-cap file where any growth fails `check:line-cap-ratchet` — ends up one line shorter than main. `resolveConfiguredModelPolicyAllow` calls the helper in a single line.

## Evidence

### Resolver-level red/green

![A/B proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191215/proof-191215.png)

The harness performs the production Gateway publication — `readConfigFileSnapshot()` then `setRuntimeConfigSnapshot(runtimeConfig, sourceConfig)`, exactly what `src/cli/program/config-guard.ts` does — for an isolated config, then asks the real `resolveConfiguredModelPolicyAllow` what it resolves. One variable differs between runs (this change).

| authored config | authored `agents.defaults.models` | runtime keys | main resolved policy | this branch resolved policy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no model map authored (the report) | `[]` | 4 (3 injected) | 4 refs — accidental allowlist | `[]` — unrestricted |
| authored legacy model map | 2 | 5 (3 injected) | 5 refs — authored + injected | the 2 authored refs |

### Shipped Gateway end-to-end (live A/B)

![Live Gateway A/B and v2026.10.9 upgrade](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191434/live-gateway-proof.png)

Every row below is one real turn through the shipped entry point: isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `openclaw gateway run`, then `openclaw agent --model … --json`. A deterministic local provider records each model POST, so **0 POSTs** means the override stopped before provider I/O. Anthropic runtime defaults were active in every row (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set), injecting three keys into `agents.defaults.models`.

`branch` is head `62ed4f4c887`. `main` is the same tree with only the two changed source files reverted (`git apply -R`) and rebuilt; `grep -c computeAuthoredModelPolicyAllowlist dist/*.mjs` returns 0 for that build and 1 for the branch build.

| authored config | requested override | branch | main (PR reverted) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no model map (reported case) | `proof/proof-model` | allowed, 1 POST | denied, 0 POSTs |
| no model map (control: injected provider still works) | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` | allowed, 1 POST | allowed, 1 POST |
| legacy map `{anthropic/claude-opus-4-8}` | `proof/proof-model` | denied, 0 POSTs | denied, 0 POSTs |
| legacy map `{anthropic/claude-opus-4-8}` | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` (injected, not authored) | denied, 0 POSTs | allowed, 1 POST |
| per-agent `agents.entries.ops.modelPolicy.allow=[anthropic/claude-opus-4-8]` | `proof/proof-model` | denied, 0 POSTs | denied, 0 POSTs |
| map removed again, same session after hot reload | `proof/proof-model` | allowed, 1 POST | denied, 0 POSTs |

What this covers:

- **Admission for a model outside the injected set:** with no authored map, the override reaches provider dispatch on this branch and is refused on main.
- **Authored default restriction still enforced before provider I/O:** with the authored legacy map, `proof/proof-model` is denied on both sides and the provider log stays empty.
- **Per-agent restriction still enforced before provider I/O:** agent `ops` with an explicit `modelPolicy.allow` is denied with 0 provider POSTs.
- **Injected keys no longer widen an authored restriction:** `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` is a runtime-injected key, not an authored one; this branch denies it, main admits it and dispatches.
- **Policy tightening across reload for a retained consumer:** the same session `proof-a` is allowed before the map is authored and denied after the hot reload; removing the map again admits it on this branch. Reloads are the Gateway's own config watcher (`config change detected` → `config hot reload applied`).

Raw Gateway lines:

```
res ✗ agent ... Model override "proof/proof-model" is not allowed for agent "main" by agents.defaults.models. Add "proof/proof-model" or "proof/*" to agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow...
res ✗ agent ... Model override "proof/proof-model" is not allowed for agent "ops" by agents.entries.*.modelPolicy.allow...
res ✓ agent 1854ms runId=ede478aa... payload "PROOF-PROVIDER-RESPONSE"
```

### v2026.10.9 upgrade with existing data

The released `openclaw@2026.10.9` CLI (build `8b18b55`) authored three configs; the released Gateway answered the turns first, then the copied state directory was loaded by this branch.

| config authored by v2026.10.9 | stable: proof | stable: injected anthropic | branch: proof | branch: injected anthropic |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| marked legacy map (written by `config set agents.defaults.models`) | allowed, 1 | allowed, 1 | allowed, 1 | allowed, 1 |
| explicit `agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow=[anthropic/claude-opus-4-8]` | denied, 0 | denied, 0 | denied, 0 | denied, 0 |
| pre-marker legacy map, hand-authored old install | denied, 0 | allowed, 1 | denied, 0 | denied, 0 |

- Marked and explicit configs behave identically before and after the branch loads them; their policy fields are unchanged.
- The pre-marker legacy config keeps its authored restriction (proof model denied). The injected Anthropic key is the only behavior change: admitted by 2026.10.9, denied by this branch.
- Existing stored data loads: the released state used agent DB **schema 25**, current main requires **39**. The documented `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` upgraded the copied state on all three configs (exit 0). For the pre-marker legacy config, doctor materialized `modelPolicy.allow=["anthropic/claude-opus-4-8"]` with `marker=true` — the authored ref only, no injected keys.

Local harness (not committed; temporary directory): `run-cases.sh branch|main` drives section 1, `run-upgrade.sh` drives section 2. Both start isolated Gateways, call `openclaw agent`, and count provider POSTs from the local endpoint's request log.

### Gates

Red/green unit coverage in `src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` ("derives the legacy allowlist from the authored config"): both cases fail against main's `model-selection-shared.ts` and pass with this change. Full suite: 55 passed. `src/config/io.meta.test.ts`: 10 passed. Local gates against `upstream/main`: oxfmt, oxlint, `run-tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (slack 2748). CI, `ci-gate`, and security review are green on `62ed4f4c887`.

## What was not tested

- No real Anthropic/OpenAI account or model key is available on this machine. The proof provider is a deterministic local endpoint speaking OpenAI Completions and Anthropic Messages; policy admission, dispatch, hot reload, and the upgrade path are the real shipped code paths, but model output quality is not under test.
- Only the Anthropic `cacheRetention` injection path is exercised; another provider's runtime-injected `agents.defaults.models` keys would take the same authored-source route but were not separately measured.

## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter file transcription previously uploaded to a fixed OpenAI route without checking the current catalog, and could not use the frozen SenseAudio native offer.

## User Impact

The real audio consumer now requires a fresh, eligible, model-bound native offer before upload. Qualified SenseAudio requests preserve their original AAC filenames and bytes. Stale, revoked, foreign, and unknown-format offers fail before recording upload; no upstream provider key is borrowed.

This is a draft source candidate, not live Worker activation. SenseAudio dispatch/catalog prerequisites and composed actual-consumer Worker proof remain separate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing credential-scoped resolver joins the selected model to its declared multipart request and response formats. Discovery and upload share the deadline, cancellation, proxy and network policy. SenseAudio uses the same actual SDK multipart implementation as its direct native provider, with an explicit AAC-preservation option; OpenAI's direct behavior is unchanged.

Scope: OpenAI gpt-4o-transcribe and SenseAudio senseaudio-asr-pro-1.5-260319 only. Raw Deepgram and JSON OpenRouter remain separate continuations. No manifest, Worker, pricing or deployment edits.

Originally stacked on [Gradium client PR192052](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192052). Its landed d65390bcf36b818b5018029cc00951799bebf0ed corrections are now integrated through the supported native baseline route at exact qualified `a29b8d3b84df9bca10c4e09172bad4660b2716f8`, including the existing landed SDK outer-deadline fix. This PR targets main; no new workflow or baseline-ceiling edit is introduced.

## Evidence

- Actual `transcribeAudioFile` tests cover catalog scope, revocation/key rotation, cancellation, model/route/format denials, SenseAudio multipart fields, unchanged WAV/AAC bytes and input limits. Direct SenseAudio AAC regression uses the actual provider/SDK implementation. Existing OpenAI AAC behavior is preserved.
- New catalog file: 22 cases; direct SenseAudio regression: 1 case. Existing transcription fixtures now serve the catalog and check bound-profile credentials. These cases are authored; semantic execution remains pending.
- Native formatter, SDK export synchronization, syntax/whitespace/privacy checks and normal commit hooks pass.
- Prior +290 test allocation; prior ratchet passes 6,437,743 / 6,438,181 (438 slack) against the frozen stack parent.
- Local dependencies are unqualified: the managed worktree wrapper rejects a nested workspace link. No install, dependency mutation, live/paid request or new remote lease was performed. Exact-head hosted build, types, SDK boundary/API and focused runtime evidence are required before ready/landing.
- Source contract: [ClawRouter PR455](https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/455) at 6fe3d95c2a9f8591099504aa7325a70812467439. Native multipart dispatch/activation remains the runtime owner's prerequisite; unknown billing qualifications do not become zero-cost requests.

Release-note context: ClawRouter transcription honors current native catalog grants and supports qualified SenseAudio multipart/AAC uploads. The repository's release-owned changelog is unchanged.

## Current Qualification

Current head: `ac585b75c5498b4c7e4f12ca956f4b5de8c8ea51` (native prepared publication; tree `40523e8e98e4c587b05d724fc66fcca769720f20`). The six native conflict resolutions preserve five exact landed Gradium blobs plus both Vercel and multipart documentation. The candidate has only ten multipart files relative to the qualified baseline;309 actual test LF equals allocation309. Changed TypeScript syntax, whitespace and privacy checks pass. Hosted proof remains pending; no READY claim.

prs.title: fix(ios): app reconnects forever with a revoked device token after setup-code pairing
prs.body:
Closes #190145

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an iPhone or Mac paired with a setup code keeps reconnecting forever with the same rejected token after the device is revoked (`openclaw devices revoke`) or the Gateway state is reset, until the Gateway's auth rate limiter trips. The app shows "Gateway token is out of date", which names a shared token the device doesn't have.

## User Impact

User impact: after a revoke or a Gateway reset, the app drops the dead stored device token and the next reconnect goes to the normal pairing path instead of looping. Clients that have an explicit Gateway token are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

When no explicit token is configured, `GatewayChannel` sends the stored device token as `auth.token`. The Gateway can't tell that apart from a shared token, so it answers `AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH` (or `AUTH_DEVICE_TOKEN_MISMATCH`). The existing clear-stale-token branch only ran on the explicit device-token retry path, so this case kept the token. The fix clears the stored token in that case only: no explicit token, the stored token was the credential sent, and the Gateway rejected it with one of those two codes. It uses the same `DeviceAuthStore.clearToken(observedToken:)` call as the existing branch, so a token rotated in the meantime is not wiped.

## Evidence

Tested on macOS 27.2 (arm64), Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Swift 6.4.2. Branch base: e8f91361ab.

Before the fix (`GatewayChannel.swift` from the parent commit; `swift test --filter GatewayChannelDeviceTokenRetryTests` in `apps/macos`): the 2 existing tests pass. The new test fails in both cases (`.authTokenMismatch`, `.authDeviceTokenMismatch`):

```
GatewayChannelDeviceTokenRetryTests.swift:322: Expectation failed: DeviceAuthStore.loadToken(...) == nil
GatewayChannelDeviceTokenRetryTests.swift:332: Expectation failed: recorder.auth(at: 1)?["token"] == nil
✘ Test run with 3 tests in 1 suite failed with 4 issues.
```

After the fix:
- `apps/macos`: `swift test --filter GatewayChannel`: 54 tests in 6 suites passed, including both cases of the new test.
- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`: `swift test --filter 'GatewayNodeSessionTests|GatewayErrorsTests'`: 120 tests in 3 suites passed.

### Real Gateway trace

A local Gateway built from this branch (`gateway --dev`, loopback, token auth, isolated state), and the `openclaw-mac` CLI from `apps/macos` built twice: from the PR base and from this branch. `openclaw-mac connect` runs the same `GatewayChannel` and SQLite credential store as the iOS and macOS apps, without the app UI.

`openclaw-mac` has no setup-code option, so each client pairs by connecting once with the Gateway token, and that token is then removed from its config. That leaves the same state as a setup-code-paired device: a stored device token is the only credential, and no explicit Gateway token is configured. Then the device's operator token is revoked with `openclaw devices revoke`, and the client reconnects three times. The "gateway:" lines are the Gateway's log for each attempt, and "stored device tokens" counts the rows in the client's credential store.

Without the fix, every reconnect resends the revoked token and the token is never cleared:

```
### openclaw-mac built from: base (the PR base, without the fix)

1. Pair: configure the client with the Gateway token and connect once, so the Gateway issues a device token
   result: ok - connected
   gateway: client connected, auth=token
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 1

2. Remove the Gateway token from the client config. The stored device token is now its only credential,
   which is the state a setup-code-paired phone or Mac is in
   result: ok - connected
   gateway: client connected, auth=device-token

3. Revoke the device's operator token on the Gateway: openclaw devices revoke --device 54cf1febccb0… --role operator
   revoked

4.1 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token mismatch (provide gateway auth token)
   gateway: unauthorized, auth=token device=yes
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 1
4.2 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token mismatch (provide gateway auth token)
   gateway: unauthorized, auth=token device=yes
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 1
4.3 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token mismatch (provide gateway auth token)
   gateway: unauthorized, auth=token device=yes
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 1
```

With the fix, the first reconnect after the revoke is rejected and the stored token is cleared, and later reconnects no longer send it (`auth=none`):

```
### openclaw-mac built from: fixed (focus/190145, with the fix)

1. Pair: configure the client with the Gateway token and connect once, so the Gateway issues a device token
   result: ok - connected
   gateway: client connected, auth=token
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 1

2. Remove the Gateway token from the client config. The stored device token is now its only credential,
   which is the state a setup-code-paired phone or Mac is in
   result: ok - connected
   gateway: client connected, auth=device-token

3. Revoke the device's operator token on the Gateway: openclaw devices revoke --device 67a8eff968dd… --role operator
   revoked

4.1 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token mismatch (provide gateway auth token)
   gateway: unauthorized, auth=token device=yes
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 0
4.2 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token missing (provide gateway auth token)
   gateway: unauthorized, auth=none device=yes
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 0
4.3 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token missing (provide gateway auth token)
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 0
```

Gateway log for the run with the fix, from the revoke on (peer ports and instance ids removed). The Gateway writes the `unauthorized` detail line once for back-to-back identical rejections, so the third attempt only shows its `res ✗ connect` line:

```

2026-11-03T02:26:01.147 [ws] unauthorized conn=3d2d412e-bc69-4fb8-9f9f-d289c0dd7ecd remote=127.0.0.1 client=proof-client-fixed ui vdev role=operator scopes=6 auth=token device=yes platform=macOS 27.2.0 host=127

2026-11-03T02:26:02.718 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ connect 1ms bytes=332 failurePhase=auth failureCause=unauthorized conn=7b5860d1…b487 id=B361D2E3…83B2
```

prs.title: chore: investigate Windows node exec pending in Code Mode (#176315)
prs.body:
Related: #176315

> **Investigation placeholder — intentionally draft, not ready for review or merge.** No implementation patch exists yet. The root cause and current-main reproduction remain unproven; no native Windows before/after result or passing regression is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

A Windows-node command submitted through Code Mode can remain pending without returning native output, an exit status, or an actionable failure, even when discovery and native Codex session listing succeed.

## User Impact

The intended outcome is for remote Windows commands to return their actual output and exit status, or a truthful denial, timeout, cancellation, or unknown-outcome result. There is no delivered behavior change yet. Authorization and unknown-outcome safeguards must remain intact; uncertain requests must not be replayed automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

Issue #176315 reports this failure with a Linux Gateway and native Windows node running OpenClaw 2026.10.4. The failing owner has not been identified, so this draft deliberately does not propose a speculative repair.

The next step is one bounded, harmless absolute-path `codex.exe --version` probe in an isolated paired environment, using normal supported approvals. Correlate the Code Mode bridge request with exec entry, preparation, approval disposition, node invocation, native process completion, terminal-result acceptance, and Code Mode continuation. Only then select the smallest fix at the responsible boundary.

## Evidence

**Completed investigation — source analysis, not native execution:**

- Read the report and complete comments, traced the execution and result-return owners, and compared release `383c124cc32f` with inspected main `76985e4c31c4`.
- The release sets `bridgeDispatchStarted` before `runBridgeRequest`; it does not establish that exec or a Windows process started. [Release source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af/src/agents/code-mode-state.ts#L570-L573).
- Last confirmed incident boundary: an outstanding Code Mode `bridge:callValue`. First unconfirmed boundary: entry into the nested exec implementation and node-target resolution. Later execution and return stages remain unconfirmed for that request.
- Compared #168523 (headless approval delivery), #104798 (bare-name allowlist precheck), PR #166140 (open at the October 29 inspection) (Windows shell-wrapper policy), and merged PRs #175949 and #128440 (Code Mode lifecycle repairs). Similar symptoms do not establish a shared cause or prove that this report is fixed.

**Required before this can become an implementation PR:**

- [ ] Verify actual Gateway/node builds, Node versions, transport, capabilities, and effective approval policy in the isolated test environment.
- [ ] Capture the bounded native Windows failure and its first stalled boundary; reconcile the request before any control or retry.
- [ ] Compare the equivalent supported direct node-exec path with Code Mode, keeping policy and command equivalent.
- [ ] Add a regression that fails on the base and passes with the owner-correct repair.
- [ ] Capture native Windows before/after stdout and exit delivery; verify relevant denial, error, cancellation, and disconnect cases.
- [ ] Complete targeted tests, typecheck, lint/format, and independent review; replace this draft's pending statements with exact results.

Native Windows access and an isolated paired Gateway were unavailable in the investigating session. No implementation tests were run, and no production service, approval policy, or unrelated session was changed.

Reported by @ceo633 in [#176315](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176315).

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6ba2f796-3a2a-4e83-976b-0e817bd5b51a)
- Implementation and verification: pending; no implementation session or patch exists yet.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

## Worked on by

- @DonnieFi
