prs.title: fix(plugins): defer channel admission imports in catalog workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider-only model catalogs import Gateway method validators and host channel-admission code while constructing the shared plugin registry. Those modules remain resident even when that catalog never creates an inbound channel runtime.

## User Impact

**Performance hold.** The historical comparison against `f75bd97` (including the scope-import fix now landed separately) used five paired runs that reduce cold post-GC worker heap from **89.596 to 86.372 MiB (−3.598%)**. Warm median latency improves 2.183%, but warm p95 increases 3.923%, CPU increases 0.955%, and the fifth pair regresses 61.981% in warm median / 64.952% in warm p95. These results do not meet the predeclared acceptance rule; no adverse tradeoff has been accepted.

This is a small import-footprint reduction, not a demonstrated Gateway RSS saving or a fixed memory leak. The historical measured worker still loads 3,096 scripts; no script-count or memory result is qualified for the current head. No configuration, migration, operator action, or public runtime API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Import ADMIN_SCOPE from its canonical lightweight owner instead of Gateway method policy.
- Keep channel trust, record identity, and revocation in the registry owner; obtain host inbound composition through the existing lazy native runtime owner only when a channel needs it.
- Preserve synchronous access, supplemental-media completion, inactive prepared loads, and exact-instance retirement. Remove eager host-admission construction from provider-only registry imports.
- Compose the same private factory in the unpublished source-test SDK facade. Its CI naming repair uses `createPluginTestRegistry` and migrates all 19 callers. Independent scoped review, exact mechanical-diff verification, formatting, and whitespace/privacy checks passed.

Current source delta versus frozen `f75bd97`: **production +93/−54, net +39; tests/test helpers +194/−90, net +104; test-budget metadata +3/−0**. Test-only SDK facades, test helpers, and test-support modules are counted with tests. Production growth supplies the private runtime ownership boundary; it adds no cache. The test ratchet counts +98; a scoped +98 allocation covers the new lifecycle assertions.

## Evidence

Current published PR head: `af67b3e07c15da6133d92cf51012c330d3f8a3f6`, tree `ffb90926046204e8b09540bf920959f29ab902e1`. After the historical measured head, `058e617` renamed the unpublished test-facade factory, migrated its 19 consumers, and allocated the test budget. The new `af67b3e` additionally changes the startup matcher import from `config-contracts.ts` to its existing `config-contract-matches.ts` owner (+1/−1 production line). The historical `b8420c5` table remains preserved evidence for that older source, not a performance result for af67.

[CI attached to af67](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41765145335) is complete. The only failed selected surface is the baseline ratchet; the aggregate CI gate consequently failed. The exact-head security review passed. The native informational classifier calls the ratchet “new” because a scheduled main job passed, explicitly noting that selected scope was not compared; the exact tested-parent arithmetic below establishes the inherited deficit without changing the failed CI outcome. The failed test-line ratchet is inherited: tested merge `1bc9c1e3d9e51f74513a987ad1a1766ed767083e` has ordered parents `f38495f7d044b35810ae1e03792bf9f80a571bf1` and af67. Its 6,452,269 test lines exceed a 6,452,249 ceiling by 20; the exact first-parent reconstruction is 6,452,171 versus 6,452,151, also 20 over. The PR adds 98 counted lines and a matching 98-line allocation. This is source/CI arithmetic, not a baseline rerun; the job remains failed.

The [latest ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191939#issuecomment-6605715158) now covers exact af67: no actionable correctness findings, but merge remains blocked by the performance hold. It explicitly records missing qualified af67 comparative/cold/post-load proof and red-on-base execution of the new admission assertions. Its rank-up move is completion of the already-declared comparison without discarding historical failures. No additional review request is needed while the head is unchanged.

[Historical CI for 058e617](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41678071453) passed the naming-collision guard and test-line budget. Its remaining failed test job was UI E2E: Brave and Firecrawl credential-save cases timed out waiting for `config.set` (`plugins-settings-admin.e2e.test.ts:305/426`). This mocked-Gateway path does not activate native plugins; its source/behavior boundary is outside the changed registry factories. That result is not current-head CI.

The Codex consumer edits only rename the test factory. Direct upstream contract inspection used `openai/codex` commit `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs:174–203` and `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs:857–930`. No RPC payload or behavior changes.

Measured source: `b8420c5e132945f10619b83b3896997850074576`, tree `e75e5611fb7f441d01af0d948469f4c4128e18ae`; compiled carrier: `453268180b7017c493a9215074cd79bd32ccaf8c`. Baseline: `f75bd97cda9f6d330cb2967a5816aa5af31e1f9c`, tree `50322a9265e3110258f4197119ad0179f0f5cc13`.

[Completed Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41660095779), Node 24.22.1, Linux x64, CPU affinity 0–3, no CPU/RAM cgroup limit, MemTotal 16,168,148 kB. Both arms have frozen dependency-input digest `20bebc43a6d6f0388e154e06d7fc79a9c9e47be5fcef2ef0ca694e7143c8c8c7`.

- Both full production builds, core typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, and all **46 focused tests in 3 files** passed: registry-runtime.channel-ingress, registry-runtime.twitch-ingress, loader.capability-factory.
- Compiled production-SDK admission checks passed for synchronous/asynchronous context, ordinary unbound context, retirement, and retirement while async context is pending.
- Isolated Twitch entrypoint import qualified, including cleanup; this is candidate-only cold-import coverage, not comparative performance evidence.
- Candidate production dist was frozen before tests: **26,252 files**, SHA-256 `d23b62424b74f291c3ba52b6a8f4ce6fc4d25df6cbe4b9bc26ae1274728859d0`. Source, output, dependency/runtime inventories were verified before timing, after timing, and after captures. Private QA entrypoints were absent.
- All **240 request outputs** match catalog/runtime hashes and counts: 1,200 catalog rows, 1,000 configured rows, 1,200 runtime models. Five timing pairs alternate BC/CB/BC/CB/BC; the separate CPU-profile pair follows. No windows overlap.
- Independent source review and autoreview found no actionable code defect. Independent receipt/metric audit reproduced the performance hold.
- Proof archive SHA-256: `06b61ac0405b2c28ec1caadbe7711352eceb3b6ac7c15f43ccefb25241246d9b`. Raw heap snapshots were not exported.
- [CI for the measured head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41665390569) is red. The source-contract failure was the test-facade export-name collision subsequently repaired in `058e617`. The test-line failure combines this PR's +98 with a 155-line inherited deficit at the synthetic merge base. UI lint fails on an unchanged navigator spread; browser-mock UI E2E has two credential-blur timeouts outside this changed native runtime path, without matching baseline execution proof. These are not reported as passing.

### Predeclared workload and acceptance

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/catalog-worker-retention-measure.ts \
  --built-worker <arm> --output <fresh-fixture> \
  --workspaces 1 --models 1000 --configured-models 1000 \
  --providers 2 --discovery-models 100 --runtime-plugin \
  --task-rounds 20 --measure-tasks
```

Five serial timing pairs; one separate pair with `OPENCLAW_BENCH_SAMPLE_CPU=1`. No allocation sampling or forced GC inside warm timing windows. Primary win: lower median cold post-GC worker heap, corroborated by compiled retained-code attribution. Every worse metric requires explicit owner acceptance; any ≥20% adverse cell holds landing. No unchanged rerun to seek favorable results.

Candidate `af67b3e07c15da6133d92cf51012c330d3f8a3f6`, control `82ce07207f64e4a1e1b220fbcf69be2db53b791b`, workload and acceptance remain unchanged. Install policy is also aligned at its producer: the candidate uses the selected source's install already performed by the native receiver; the baseline invokes that same canonical installer with the same frozen-install flags. No measurement existed at predeclaration, and the stopped attempt above produced none. Four further independent in-memory checks verify complete aggregate accounting for 13,995 additions, bounded path samples, root-group overflow and mixed add/remove/kind changes; they do not replace integrated proof.

The requested red-on-base admission-behavior proof is not applicable to this extraction. At the control, `src/plugins/registry-runtime-channel.ts:31` already constructs the wrapper only for a live trusted registered channel, caches its exact record, and revokes retired owners. The optimization counterfactual remains required: the baseline's eager registry-to-host import path versus the compiled prepared-catalog worker under the same cold/post-load workload. A source-edge cut alone cannot prove exclusion from shared emitted chunks or a memory improvement. This rationale addresses the review's behavioral red-on-base request without waiving the compiled import/performance gate, historical adverse results or HOLD.

Source audit at `af67b3e` confirms that `AuthStorage.inMemory` imports the standalone directory/config-loading path through `agents/config.ts`. A complete follow-up must isolate standalone/persistent factories from prepared-session construction while retaining one instance/backend/OAuth implementation and the public factory and request-auth contracts. prs.title: fix(slack): stop replies after their parent is deleted
prs.body:
Related: #96692; complements #119737. Compared with merged backport #180878, this draft retains observed-deletion lifecycle and per-physical-write/retry coverage; neither check and publication are atomic.

## What Problem This Solves

A threaded reply can outlive its parent. An observed parent deletion currently becomes only an informational event, so queued output, native buffered output, and files can continue publishing to a destination that no longer exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retire the exact active publishing address after an authorized deletion, without cancelling the underlying agent work. Carry that publication-only signal through deferred replies, previews, native streaming, and ordinary delivery. At the ordinary sender boundary, verify the live parent before each physical text/card send and file completion, including known-safe transport retries. Native retries and preview/final edit retries honor observed parent retirement too. Managed writers and deletion signals reach partial updates, both finalization paths, explicit rate-limit retries, and invalid-block replacement; ambiguous final-edit readback keeps the original reader. Keep earlier accepted parts and do not turn a later failure into permission to replay them.

This complements the confirmed-placement receipt work in #119737. It does not replace that PR or claim to repair every existing receipt/reconciliation inference. A parent read and Slack write are not atomic. Native streams without an observed deletion remain a separate limitation.

## User Impact

After OpenClaw observes deletion of an active reply parent, it stops publishing further output to that parent, including buffered native output. Child deletions and another workspace's matching timestamp leave unrelated publishers intact; explicit top-level sends remain supported. Ordinary threaded sends now require a readable live parent, adding bounded read requests and failing without publication when that evidence is unavailable. Workspace/listener and direct-handoff authority stay scoped to the existing delivery owner.

## Evidence

- Independent review found a native HTTP429 replay gap, and hosted review found a preview/final edit replay gap. Both are corrected in this candidate. A fresh frozen review of the complete staged candidate reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Its confidence is limited by unavailable surrounding source and unrun tests, types, lint and formatting; live behavior remains unverified.
- Candidate base: `7dcc40f7addb9e45ce3e36768c505ff9cb005209`.
- Regression cases cover deletion before pending final text/file output, deferred delivery, native buffered append/stop, workspace/child isolation, queued sender release, multipart acceptance, upload completion, and identity/transport retry boundaries.
- All 23 original changed TypeScript files and the seven follow-up files passed Node syntax parsing, and `git diff --check` passed. These do not establish type or runtime correctness.
- Local dependency setup is blocked: Corepack's fetch of the repository-pinned pnpm version received HTTP 403 from the managed package registry before installation. No alternate registry, package-manager version, or credentials were used.
- The focused repository test wrapper exits before collection because `node_modules` is unavailable. Tests, typecheck, lint, formatting and CI are pending; syntax-only checks and source review are not substitutes.
- No live Slack test messages, service changes, deployment or release performed. The incident's original raw Slack response is unavailable, so this is boundary repair rather than proof of the provider's exact fallback behavior.

Draft: validation and independent review must be resolved before readiness.

Production growth is needed to propagate exact-parent retirement across existing ordinary, preview, deferred and native publishing owners and to verify queued writes at the transport boundary. No configuration, schema, dependency or persistent-state changes.

Known readiness blocker from the #180878 comparison: the published head can drop the configured account reader when a monitor supplies its writer, and Enterprise parent reads can inherit the listener lookup policy. A six-file correction with credential-isolation and transport-deadline regressions is staged locally. Syntax and whitespace checks pass; fresh frozen review of the complete staged candidate reported no actionable P0–P2 findings, with unavailable unchanged source context and unrun checks as limits. The configured signing agent refused the normal commit signature, so the correction is not yet committed or pushed. No signing configuration or security hooks were bypassed. Runtime/type/lint/format validation remains pending.

prs.title: fix(onboarding): "No AI access" hides a running Ollama or LM Studio with no loaded model
prs.body:
Closes #191414

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: onboarding says no AI access was found and recommends installing Ollama while Ollama is running with no model loaded.

## User Impact

User impact: guided setup shows that the server is running, says no eligible model is loaded, and gives two ways forward. The running provider is dropped from the recommended installs. No model is loaded automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

Providers already expose a read-only availability probe that only the classic wizard used. Guided detection calls it when a provider returns no usable model, and reports the result through the existing `unavailableCandidates` field, which the wizard and macOS onboarding already render.

Without this change:

Closes #190741.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Portals incorrectly demanding remote ingress when the Control UI connects to its local Gateway through a `.localhost` hostname.

## User Impact

Local `.localhost` users see the normal HTTP new-tab notice rather than a misleading remote-ingress warning. Actual remote Gateways still require ingress for their loopback portals; ordinary 127.0.0.1 previews remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a separate portal-delivery locality predicate for the two hostname checks in Portals. This is not a broader stored-credential trust change:

- `isLoopbackHostname` executable body is unchanged.
- `isTrustedRetryEndpoint` and both credential-retry callers are unchanged, including the existing same-host exception.
- Portal publishing/URL producers are unchanged; the UI consumes the original published URL without rewriting it.

Retains both yy19971996 commits. Consolidates strict/delivery hostname expectations rather than duplicating matrices: tests net0, no allocation; production net+6 (12 gross changed lines). Existing docs explain the delivery-only distinction.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway + Chromium before/after proof and inspected screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191895#issuecomment-6621205386), exact candidate `c8a5f9f4b8be458e27ec178f12e10bdf180dff84`, secretless Node24.22.1 Docker:

- Real `portal.open` publication and normal `/portals` flow: `.localhost` **main twice** shows remote-ingress-required; **candidate twice** shows the normal new-tab notice. Browser origin, actual WebSocket hostname and served commit are asserted.
- Clicking the native launch link requests the exact service-published URL and renders the target application. No portal summaries, reachability responses or Gateway state are mocked.
- A Gateway on a separate container/network namespace still shows ingress-required on both builds. 127.0.0.1 still renders the app in its iframe and new tab. Malicious suffix controls remain remote.
- **36/36 focused tests pass**, formatter/linter pass. Supplemental retry-boundary execution on main/candidate agrees: another `.localhost` origin is not newly trusted; existing same-host and loopback behavior remains intact.

Before on `.localhost`:

![Before: incorrect remote-ingress warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0a69fe8-213c-431a-bee8-c264acb75aa8)

After on `.localhost`:

![After: normal HTTP new-tab notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/114cbcce-d378-42ee-b1ff-2dc6c16f0f15)

prs.title: refactor(skills): move Skill Workshop into its bundled plugin
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill Workshop (learned skills each agent saves from its own work) lived in core: about 20 core modules imported it, core special-cased its tool, prompt section, `/learn`, CLI, Gateway methods and Doctor check, and nothing else could build the same thing on supported contracts. This moves it into the bundled plugin `extensions/skill-workshop` on generic SDK seams that already landed (forked turns, completed-turn anchor, `run_stopped`, session notices, skill authoring, tool availability, skill usage, `/learn` contributions, personal-library split).

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Workshop keeps working the same way: the `skill_workshop` tool, background reviews and notices with Undo, daily maintenance, `/learn` (drafts, undo), `openclaw skills workshop ...`, the 8 `skills.workshop.*` Gateway methods (same names, payloads and scopes), and the Doctor tool-policy check. Workshop is enabled by default as before.

Accepted differences, each small and documented:
- Sandboxed runs no longer get `skill_workshop` (the plugin tool refuses sandboxed runs). Before, a sandboxed single-admin personal-library turn could still write Workshop skills.
- With the plugin disabled, the `skills.workshop.*` methods answer "unknown method"; the tool and the Workshop prompt section are absent; other skills load normally.
- The Doctor check id is `skill-workshop/tool-policy` (plugins cannot use `core/doctor/` ids).
- `skill_changed.source` is `"plugin"` for Workshop writes.
- `group:plugins` and plugin-id tool policies now apply to `skill_workshop` (it also stays in `group:agents` and the `coding` profile).
- Doctor auto-enable writes `plugins.entries.skill-workshop.enabled: true` when Workshop config exists.
- The once-per-agent-per-day maintenance memory resets when the plugin reloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Plugin layout: `index.ts` registers the v2 `skill_workshop` tool (manifest `contracts.tools`, `promptGuidance`), the review service (`agent_end` with `ctx.completedTurn`, `run_stopped`, forked review via `api.runtime.subagent.runForkedTurn`, notices via `api.runtime.system`, maintenance on the service scheduler), the `/learn` contribution, CLI under `skills`, the 8 Gateway methods and the Doctor health artifact. All former core Workshop modules and tests moved into `extensions/skill-workshop/src` and use only `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` and `api.runtime`.
- Change history stays in the core `skill_workshop_changes` table behind a narrow bundled-only SDK accessor (`skill-workshop-host-runtime`), as the approved plan says. No schema or data change.
- Deleted from core: the Workshop modules, the core tool, factory and schema, the prompt special case, the attempt catalog and tool construction special cases, review scheduling in agent-end, the direct `run_stopped` call, the core `/learn` injection, the CLI subcommands, the 8 core method descriptors and handlers, and the core Doctor check. A boundary rule now fails on core imports of Workshop code.
- Small generic core changes the move needed:
  - Personal-library grant (`applySkillLibraryGrant`): in a personal-default library turn, tools of plugins that declare a manifest `agentSkillsDir` are withheld; in a workspace-default turn their writes recheck current admin authority. This keeps today's shared-Gateway rule without naming the tool. Third-party plugins without `agentSkillsDir` are unaffected (tested).
  - Plugin tool calls capture the caller's authority when the call starts, and v2 `assertInvocationCurrent` rechecks it before a write.
  - Worker turns now give plugin tools invocation authority (before, every v2 plugin tool write was refused there).
  - Plugin forks default to the source session's stored auth profile on the session's own provider, so a review uses the profile the turn ran with.
  - Forks accept a catalog tool id the calling plugin declares in `contracts.tools`; `/learn` contribution handles are bound to the plugin's call scope.
  - `skill-authoring-runtime` gains `beforeDispatch` and caller `assertCurrent` on writes.
  - The deprecated public `buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection` stays as a byte-identical frozen copy until its removal date.
- Test harness (test-only): under Vitest the real loader gave plugin code a second copy of core. Pins and e2es share one module graph through `src/plugins/test-helpers/vitest-plugin-host-graph.ts`, which seeds the plugin's SDK imports with the test's modules and stages a source copy of the plugin in a temporary bundled root selected by the existing `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR` (a Gateway prefers built bundled artifacts; this root has none, so the Gateway runs the checkout source). Production plugin loading is unchanged. The shared-state admission keeps the first host binding (identical in a single-copy production Gateway).
- Doctor: the Workshop health artifact is optional in the bundled bridge, so a package without the plugin still runs `openclaw doctor`. The sandbox finding now names the paths that work: a non-sandboxed session or `openclaw skills workshop`.

## Evidence

- Behavior pins (`*.workshop-contract*`), setup-only changes (load the plugin, start its service, read history through the accessor); the only assertion change is T2/T3 comparing the library-turn skill tools as a set (plugin tools follow core tools; providers sort tools by name, so model-visible order is unchanged; approved):
  - unit: tool 15/15, commands, server-methods, CLI, system-prompt, maintenance 8/8, schema, validation, state migrations, workspace-skill-loader: 10 files pass.
  - e2e: review, learning 2/2, notice history 1/1.
- Seam e2es on the real plugin: forked turn (incl. source-session auth profile case), skill authoring, session notice. Pins and seam e2es: 6 e2e files, 36/36.
- Caller authority, through the real loader, the real `createOpenClawTools` and a Gateway caller identity (`src/agents/openclaw-tools.workshop-authority.test.ts`, `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-plugin-tool-authority.test.ts`). Executed traces:
  - authorized: `authority:captured → prepare:check:ok ×4 → awaited:check:ok ×7 → written → SKILL.md exists: true`
  - revoked during awaited preparation: `authority:captured → prepare:check:ok ×4 → awaited:check:ok → caller:revoked → awaited:check:revoked → refused (tool invocation authority is no longer active) → SKILL.md exists: false`
  - retained worker-turn tool: `turn:live → call:ok → turn:closed → late call refused (Aborted); effects: 1`
  - Negative controls: without the caller recheck in v2 `assertInvocationCurrent`, the revoked write lands; without the worker `assertInvocationCurrent`, even the live worker call is refused.
- Prompt cache (mock provider, `prefix-stability.mts`): `skill_workshop` provider tool definition byte-identical to base (name, description, schema) and name-ordered; Workshop system-prompt section byte-identical; review fork leaves the parent prefix unchanged and shares parent history bytes up to the anchor; skill refresh timing unchanged.
- Plugin disabled: core starts with no loader warnings, no Workshop tool or prompt section, workspace skills load, `skills.workshop.list` answers unknown method.
- Plugin tests 16 files, 135 tests. Prompt consumers (Codex, Copilot, Agents API, `system-prompt.test.ts`) load the plugin guidance and keep their Workshop assertions. Doctor isolation, bundled health bridge, skills CLI and SDK guardrail suites pass.
- Published upgrade lane (Docker, scenario `base`, candidate packed from `b16fffa513ff`, the current head): `openclaw@2026.10.9` → candidate 49/49 phases, `openclaw@2026.10.10` → candidate 49/49 phases (install, seed and assert baseline, update-candidate, Doctor, post-Doctor config validation, survival assertions, Gateway start, probes and status).
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, oxfmt, type-aware oxlint, `check:import-cycles`, `check:baseline-ratchets`, line-cap ratchet, `lint:plugins:no-extension-test-core-imports`, `plugin-sdk:check-exports`, `plugins:inventory:check`, `config:docs:check`, eager-import closure (`check-cli-bootstrap-imports` on a fresh build), Core tsgo graph boundary, extension SDK boundary, CI-mode oxlint (all five core stripes and extensions), `test/vitest-cli-ownership.test.ts`, the SDK package guardrails and the packaged Doctor JSON e2e (`test/cli-json-stdout.e2e.test.ts`, bundled dir without the plugin): pass. `plugin-sdk:surface:check` fails identically on base (3860 public exports vs budget 3859; pre-existing).
- Not run: `pnpm test:live:cache` (needs a provider key in a child environment; it checks core provider caching against stored baselines, independent of Workshop), `plugin-sdk:api:diff` (creates its own worktrees).

prs.title: feat(clawrouter): support OpenRouter MP3 speech
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter TTS and Talk cannot currently select OpenRouter speech offers. Buffered TTS also drops caller cancellation and can fall back to another paid provider after an uncertain synthesis attempt.

## User Impact

Qualified OpenRouter MP3 offers can serve the actual TTS tool and Talk handler using the selected ClawRouter proxy key. Caller abort reaches discovery, POST and body reads. A possibly-paid attempt cannot automatically replay through another provider; proven pre-egress failures retain normal fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ClawRouter speech registration adds the three finite catalog models: `openrouter/hexgrad/kokoro-82m`, `openrouter/elevenlabs/eleven-turbo-v2`, and `openrouter/mistralai/voxtral-mini-tts-2603`. Kokoro with `af_alloy` is the default for this upstream. The existing OpenAI-style body serializer is reused with explicit MP3 and qualified voice/speed/data-policy fields; the direct OpenRouter credential resolver is never invoked.

The exact offer contract is provider `openrouter`, POST, model capability `audio.speech`, request `openai.audio_speech`, response `audio.binary`, path `/v1/audio/speech`. Native dispatch is `/v1/native/openrouter/v1/audio/speech`; manifest dispatch uses `/v1/proxy/openrouter/<catalog-endpoint>` with `{ body }`. Catalog model ID and upstream must match the finite selected model. Fresh proxy scope, origin/profile/key and format boundaries remain enforced. No unified speech alias, Gemini PCM, Opus or telephony PCM is added.

Optional `SpeechSynthesisRequest.signal` is threaded through the existing buffered host and actual TTS tool. The existing `recordModelFallbackStop` marker is exposed through the existing speech-provider barrel; host fallback honors it. It controls replay only, not billing or refund authority. Complete HTTP200 audio/mpeg bytes are bounded to16MiB and the configured media cap, within one original operation deadline.

Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192234 at `53df502bee57f9a06b349a2f5741d3653eb600b1`; parent landing/retargeting remain required. Router runtime https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/793 landed at `0dd0b749d83c2b9e8c536199bb67c4faf4d84ce5`. Schema/catalog publication and actual composed Worker proof retain their owners; this draft does not activate an offer.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(macos): WIP — Launch at Login reports success after launchctl fails
prs.body:
Related: #127613

**WIP — the native API compatibility correction is published; fresh native CI is pending. Browser visual proof is available, but native execution, actual settings/upgrade proof, and full SourceKit-backed lint remain incomplete. Not ready for review or merge.**

## What Problem This Solves

Launch at Login could report success after launchctl failed; waiting for that operation inside the settings queue also prevented a newer Off choice from superseding an unfinished enable.

## User Impact

Failed changes reconcile the toggle and surface recovery guidance. A later login choice can reach the existing launch-agent owner before older work activates the app. Loaded-job refresh and disabling future autostart still leave the running app alone.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launch-agent owner checks required command statuses, stops on failure, restores the previous plist when activation fails, and publishes only its current intent's outcome.

The continuation at `ef351f748081480fe9981bef2680eb88637cf984` separates validated FIFO admission from reply completion. AppState reserves the login intent synchronously, before returning its completion task; the existing request queue retains and cancels deferred replies without blocking later admissions. Ordinary requests retain their previous serialization and consent behavior. Errors are associated with their own intent rather than read from a later request's shared error state.

The follow-up at `511d29078844175382e98b7fa3701b96e10ad75f` names the deferred entry point `enqueueAdmission`, rather than overloading `enqueue`. This removes an observed iOS compile ambiguity while preserving existing `enqueue { … } onCancel: { … }` callers and their FIFO behavior. The shared cancellation fixture now exercises that legacy call shape and immediate reply retirement.

This preserves [#145451](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145451)'s synchronous intent reservation, serialized launch-agent writes, and stale-hydration protection. No bridge wire keys, stored-data schema, configuration, dependencies, or upstream CI were changed.

## Evidence

- **Current source:** `511d29078844175382e98b7fa3701b96e10ad75f`, published as roboclaw-bot. Its complete tree matches the reviewed candidate. Independent automatic review of the complete 11-file candidate found no actionable P0–P2 issues. This is static review, not Swift compilation or runtime proof.

However, [the iOS build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41538222303/job/125595924843) was RED at unchanged `PermissionRequestBridgeTests.swift:141` (`ambiguous use of enqueue`). Current head `511d2907…` corrects the producer API name; fresh Mac/iOS compilation remains pending and that old iOS failure is not relabeled GREEN. Native test execution and the separate shared-queue package tests remain unproven. Added coverage for later admission while a reply is held, cancellation of an admitted completion, and queue → AppState → LaunchAgentManager supersession while the initial print is held. The last case requires Off admission before release and no bootstrap/kickstart afterward. Existing persistence-failure and direct-owner ordering assertions remain intact. These fixtures do not establish real WebKit GUI behavior, and no observed RED/GREEN is claimed for the new regression.
- **Focused source checks:** pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 passes all seven touched Swift files; native localization verification and whitespace checks pass. SwiftLint 0.65.1 reports zero violations in five production files, but its Linux static binary skips `custom_rules`, `literal_expression_end_indentation`, and `statement_position`: **partial lint only**, not full SourceKit-backed lint.
- **Compatibility inspection only:** the plist writer is source-identical to released [v2026.10.9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.9) (released file blob `7f32910f9f02a7438c397228fd935f4ebf33d697`). This does not substitute for a fresh-install or actual upgrade run with an existing login plist.

[Intermediate RED #12](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40427207955) exposed the persistence-failure invariant; its original assertions were preserved and passed in #13. None of these runs validates this substantive queue repair.

That assessment/rating is not a review of this head. No Diamond Lobster or completed new-head hosted review is claimed; a further hosted review is held until the required validation is complete.

prs.title: fix(cli): host runs out of memory when several Claude CLI conversations start at once
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway using the Claude CLI runtime can push its host into memory exhaustion when several conversations start new Claude processes close together.

On an 8 GB Linux VM without swap, several Slack/Teams turns arrived within about 3 minutes. The Gateway went from 3 to 7 warm Claude CLI processes, available memory fell from ~3.8 GB to ~250 MB and stayed there, and the VM thrashed (no OOM kill, CPU ~5%) until a reboot about 2 hours later. The only limit on warm processes was a fixed count of 16; idle warm processes were kept even while the host ran out of memory.

## User Impact

User impact: when host memory is low, a new Claude CLI conversation first closes idle warm processes (least recently used first). If memory is still low and every warm process is busy, that turn fails over with "Host memory is too low for another CLI live session." instead of starting another process. Hosts with enough free memory behave as before; turns that reuse their own warm process are unaffected; busy turns are never closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before a turn starts a new warm process, the live-session registry reads host free memory through the existing `readHostFreeMemoryBytes()` helper (`os.freemem()`, which is `MemAvailable` on Linux; `process.availableMemory()` on macOS). While it is below 1 GiB, it closes the least recently used idle process and waits for it to exit, then reads again. If no idle process is left, the turn fails over through the same `rate_limit` failover the 16-session cap already uses. The registry map is now kept in least-recently-used order, so both the memory path and the existing count cap close the conversation that has waited longest.

The 1 GiB floor comes from measurements of one warm session:

| Measurement | RSS |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code 2.1.314, Linux arm64 container, stream-json, idle after start | ~180 MiB |
| Same, after one Haiku turn / three concurrent Sonnet turns | ~195–198 MiB each |
| Full warm session under a Gateway (macOS): Claude Code + two Node supervisor helpers | ~490 MiB (264 + 138 + 87) |

1 GiB leaves room for about two more warm sessions before the kernel has to reclaim. The 16-session cap stays as the upper bound. No config key is added.

## Evidence

- Focused registry test (fails on `main`: `ensureCliLiveSessionMemory` is absent and nothing closes): under simulated low memory, a new session closes exactly the least recently used idle process and the live count does not grow; with enough memory nothing closes; a turn reusing its own process closes nothing; when memory stays low, every idle process closes, the busy one is untouched, and the turn fails over. Removing the LRU reorder makes the test fail (`recent.close` not called).
- `src/agents/cli-runner/`, `extensions/anthropic`, and the CLI attempt-execution tests: 1479 passed on the candidate; the registry and `execute-plugin` tests pass on the exact head (108). One failure, `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts` ("reports the discovery frontier…"), also fails alone on this host and does not touch the changed files.
- Real path on the exact head: isolated Gateway (own state, config and Claude config dir, test API key from env only), `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` with `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`, turns sent with `openclaw agent`. Memory pressure was simulated at the same seam the code reads (`os.freemem` / `process.availableMemory`), with each live Claude process under the Gateway counted as 700 MiB, so closing a process really raises the reading.
  - Real memory: 4 concurrent sessions start (`activeSessions=1…4`), no closures.
  - Low memory, new 5th session: `free-memory read: live claude processes=4 reported=424MiB` → `memory pressure: closing idle session activeSessions=4` → `processes=3 reported=1124MiB` → `cli live session start … activeSessions=4`; the turn replied.
  - Low memory, existing session: reused its warm process, no memory read, no closure; replied.
  - Low memory, all four warm sessions busy with long turns, new session: failed over in 54 ms with the message above; all four busy turns completed.

## Limits

- Admission only. A warm process that grows during a long turn after it started is not limited here.
- `readHostFreeMemoryBytes()` reads host memory on Linux, not a container cgroup limit; that helper is shared and unchanged.
- Turns that start at the same instant can each read the same free-memory value before any process exists; the floor's headroom covers a small burst, and the 16-session cap still holds.
- The failover reason reuses `rate_limit`, as the existing count cap does.
- The live check ran on macOS with a simulated reading; the Linux numbers come from an isolated Claude Code container run.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the previous behavior. No config, schema, stored state or published contract changes.

Blast radius: Gateways using a CLI runtime with warm live sessions (today Claude CLI). If the floor is wrong for a host, the effect is more closed idle sessions (a cold start on the next turn) or a failover when memory is below 1 GiB and every warm session is busy. Other runtimes and channels are not affected.

prs.title: fix(gateway): paired-node Claude continuations retain Gateway context
prs.body:
Closes #145636

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI continuation on a healthy paired node can fail with a Gateway-runtime or capability error after its originating request ends. Detached work retains a live Gateway resolver but deliberately does not retain the direct request context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two paired-node readers now use the existing resolver-first `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext` in the current request-scope owner. This integrates with main's `PluginRuntimeExecutionFrame` storage instead of reintroducing the former AsyncLocalStorage owner or a second accessor. A resolver returning `undefined` remains authoritative: stale direct context cannot revive a retired owner.

The command policy, expected connection and pairing generation, dispatch-time authority, and skill/run/placement lifecycle checks remain intact. There are no configuration, protocol, database-schema, or public SDK changes.

## User Impact

A detached Claude continuation can use its still-live Gateway and connected paired node. A retired owner fails before any node lookup, policy check, or dispatch.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh onto main `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`; current head `eb7a861ea7c06c277806dd2c6d0dba6b0f9c0443` also checks the captured Gateway remains current at dispatch and skill authority use. [Remote focused tests](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40626335729) passed 18 tests across both affected Gateway suites on a temporary child of this head. Full CI and refreshed real-node proof remain pending; earlier evidence below refers to the revisions identified there.

Reconciled against main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d`. The production diff is two reader substitutions, plus focused regression coverage.

### Actual Gateway and signed-node boundary

The same temporary source-runtime fixture starts the actual Gateway with an isolated home, config and state, loads a startup plugin through the normal loader, and captures its real context in an authenticated RPC. A separately signed WebSocket node completes normal local device pairing and command approval, verified in the persisted pairing records. After the capture RPC finishes, the fixture invokes the production `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun` in a resolver-only scope and repeats with a retired resolver plus deliberately stale direct context.

Main before the fix, observed with clean shutdown:

```json
{"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":0,"ok":false,"error":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":1,"ok":true}}
```

Exact candidate after the fix:

```json
{"head":"2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d","expectedFixed":true,"actualGateway":true,"signedNode":true,"devicePaired":true,"commandApproved":true,"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":1,"result":{"ok":true,"payload":{"exitCode":0,"stderrTail":"","truncated":false},"payloadJSON":null,"error":null}},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":0,"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"}}}}
```

The fixture exited 0, and the Gateway reported a clean shutdown.

This exercises real Gateway startup, plugin loading, authenticated RPC, signed WebSocket transport, persisted device/command pairing, NodeRegistry and the changed production invocation owner. The node returns a synthetic successful Claude-command payload. It does not establish live Claude model inference or a full terminal-close/Web-composer UI walkthrough.

The fixture uses synthetic data only. Update checks, telemetry and hosted catalog refresh are disabled with the documented config/environment opt-outs. Proof code and generated logs are temporary and are not committed.

### Regression coverage and checks

- Before the two reader substitutions: 13 failures / 3 passes across the invocation and paired-node skill suites. Detached dispatch failed unavailable; stale-context retirement incorrectly dispatched; skill preparation failed its Gateway/capability boundary.
- After, on the identical candidate tree: 27/27 tests across node invocation (5), paired-node skills (11), request-scope owner (7), and native Bash execution policy (4). Existing coverage for command denial, pairing-await authority retirement, capability requirements, skill delivery/authoring and publication retirement remains active under the resolver-only scope.
- Combined focused command: `pnpm test src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 85.02s wall time including the first compiled-subprocess generation.
- Per-file exact-head cost using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts` 5/5, 34.08s wall (21ms test bodies); `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts` 11/11, 65.68s wall (23901ms test bodies). The existing skill suite exercises real node-command subprocess/SQLite lifecycle boundaries; no new per-test Gateway boots, timers, or serial configuration were added. Hosted [changed-node CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276/job/111133298553) passed both files separately: invocation 5/5 in 22.88s (15ms test bodies), skills 11/11 in 19.83s (9.768s test bodies).
- Independent `autoreview --engine codex --mode local --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --max-priority P2`: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Four-file type-aware lint (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed files>`) passed in 22.70s. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The aggregate check passed conflict, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, database-worker, timeout-race, dependency, config, plugin-boundary and other prerequisite guards, plus the core graph boundary and full production-core typecheck.
- Hosted [CI run 37098465276](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276) passed on this exact head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, production types, all selected test-type stripes, lint, selected tests and guards. The [fresh review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145741#issuecomment-5644398815) resolves the previous integration concern and finds no actionable introduced issues: overall Platinum, proof Diamond.
- Full repository build/check/test is not claimed as locally passed. The bounded `check:changed --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --head HEAD` attempt ran 605.19s and stopped at its 600s budget during the broad 27-graph test-typecheck lane: `agents-root` passed, `agents-other` was interrupted (143). Remaining test graphs and later aggregate checks were not completed locally. The separate changed-file type-aware lint passed; the subsequent hosted CI run completed successfully and covers the selected global verification gates.

### Historical CI failure

[The old head's native-Bash policy job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34680714684/job/103518938237) reported `allowlist/on-miss`: expected `allow`, received `deny`, after 7.764s with a 5s fixture run budget. That is consistent with timeout-sensitive authority rejection, but the historical assertion omitted the denial message and run outcome, so the exact denial reason cannot be established from that log.

The integrated main already contains [the Date-based watchdog change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/62a8182e40d955ddcd509ba977badb37ea691d2a) and the independent [native-Bash fixture stabilization in #115184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ce11e2e25c3b0ad6360b8c4e5bd7f17357f81c42), which freezes the policy matrix's Date clock and asserts a non-timeout exit. The local native-Bash matrix passes 4/4 on this candidate. No native-Bash production policy, test fixture, or CI configuration is changed by this PR; a passing replay is not being presented as proof of the old run's exact cause.

prs.title: fix(team-reports): bound API response reads before parsing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every GitHub and Discord page a Team Reports run fetches was read with `response.text()`, which buffers the whole body before any budget applies — so whoever answers the request decides how much memory the run costs, and nothing in the plugin capped it.

- `extensions/team-reports/src/sources/http.ts:31` on `main` is `const body = await response.text()`, parsed at `:34`; that helper is the only place either source turns a response into bytes (`github/client.ts:84`, `discord/index.ts:70`).
- The plugin does have a budget — `MAX_REPORT_BYTES = 2 MiB` — but it applies to the rendered report after collection, so an oversized response was materialized before any limit could reject it. Reachable without a compromise: `github.apiBaseUrl` is a documented user-settable option (`src/config.ts:38`) for GitHub Enterprise Server, and an intermediary can inflate any response.

Solution: read through the shared bounded owner `readResponseWithLimit` with a per-response budget above the largest page these APIs can legitimately return, and report an oversized response as a size failure that names the cutoff and a next step.

What changed: `src/sources/http.ts` reads through `readResponseWithLimit` with `MAX_API_RESPONSE_BYTES` and maps overflow to a `too-large` read failure; `src/limits.ts` keeps `MAX_API_RESPONSE_BYTES = 32 MiB` with its derivation and derives the operator-facing label from it; `github/client.ts:24` maps each kind to a message, so an oversized page says `API response exceeded the 32 MiB limit; check the API base URL or proxy for oversized output, then regenerate the affected days`; `discord/index.ts:91` escapes the retry loop on `too-large` and says `Discord response exceeded the 32 MiB limit; check for oversized API output, then regenerate the affected days.`; the troubleshooting section of `docs/plugins/team-reports.md` documents the fixed budget, that it is not a configuration option, and the failure boundary and recovery.

Unchanged: SSRF guard options, `finally { release?.() }`, pagination and page size, retry for other failure classes, sub-budget parsing, report rendering, the 2 MiB report cap.

## User Impact

A page over the budget now fails with a size-specific warning that states the 32 MiB cutoff and what to do. The collection that needed it stops there (remaining pages for that repository, team, or channel are not fetched), other scopes keep collecting, and a failed day is not published over the last accepted report (`run.ts:110`).

Measured on the real source clients (below): `origin/main` accepted the 200 MiB roster page silently after the origin delivered 209,715,214 bytes, RSS +1053 MiB; here the origin delivered 38,797,323 bytes and saw the client close the stream, RSS +84 MiB. Discord: 209,715,246 → 39,845,910 bytes, RSS +844 → +85 MiB, one request instead of three. 100 items with 65,536-character bodies is under 26 MiB even when every character is multibyte, so no legitimate page reaches the budget.

Accepted rather than coded around: the budget is per response, so a hostile host that answers page after page still controls total work through pagination (`github/client.ts:167` `pages()` has no page or run-byte cap); this fix does not regress that.

Decision for the reviewer: 32 MiB stays a fixed collection bound with no config option — no new setting, nothing to migrate, so a fresh install and an upgrade pick it up on restart — and recovery is "regenerate the affected days".

## Evidence

Proof harness: a real `https.Server` on `93.184.215.10`, a public-range address the SSRF guard allows (no bypass), with a private CA in `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, so TLS is genuinely verified. The trace calls the shipped `createGithubSource(...).loadRoster` and `createDiscordSource(...).collect`: production guard, bounded reader, release path, retry loop and warning path. GitHub uses its documented `apiBaseUrl`; Discord's base is fixed in production, so that case points the same client at equivalent endpoints. Each case runs in its own process; the origin logs requests, bytes and how each stream ended.

```
case                     origin/main (parent of 66125f4b773)            this branch (c975f082d97)
github roster 200 MiB    accepted, no warning, 209,715,214 B, +1053 MiB  32 MiB warning, 38,797,323 B, client closed, +84 MiB
github roster small      ok, 2 people, +9 MiB                            ok, 2 people, +12 MiB
discord msgs 200 MiB     accepted, no warning, 209,715,246 B, +844 MiB   32 MiB warning, 39,845,910 B, client closed, +85 MiB
discord msgs small       ok, 1 channel, +18 MiB                          ok, 1 channel, +15 MiB
discord msgs HTTP 500    3 requests, 3.4 s, retry warning                3 requests, 3.4 s, retry warning (unchanged)
```

`client closed` is the origin observing the cancellation; under-budget rows are the no-regression half (same outcome, same bytes, same status).

Upgrade from the latest stable release (`v2026.10.10`): the released source created the store from scratch and wrote one accepted day; this branch read that report back intact (1315 bytes, both logins), wrote a second day, and reopened it (2 periods, no migration). The published artifact's own worker module (`@openclaw/team-reports@2026.10.10`) reproduces the same round trip, and a fresh install of this branch creates and reads its own store. Configuration parity: the released schema and this branch's parse a configuration with every documented option to identical JSON (735 bytes, `sha256:81fcc7c1…`) and both reject an unknown `maxApiResponseBytes` option, so nothing migrates and nothing is silently dropped; credentials and the private endpoint appear only as `<redacted-*>`. The transport matrix uses `main` as its baseline because the released plugin's HTTP layer predates this refactor and cannot run the same trace unmodified.

```
release-write      present true, 1315 bytes      v2026.10.10 source creates and writes
candidate-reopen   periods 2                     this branch reads it back and extends it, no migration
published-reopen   periods 1, then 2             same round trip through the published artifact
fresh-reopen       periods 1                     fresh install of this branch
config             735 bytes, sha256 81fcc7c1…   identical in v2026.10.10 and this branch
```

Regression tests, both updated to pin the new text:

- `github/transport.test.ts` — `releases guarded responses after consuming oversized JSON`: an over-budget roster must warn `API response exceeded the 32 MiB limit`, must not be parsed, and must still release the guarded response (`release` asserts `response.bodyUsed`).
- `discord/index.test.ts` — `reports an oversized message page once instead of retrying it`: one `/messages` request for the whole collection and a warning naming the channel, the limit and the recovery step, through the real retry loop and SSRF guard.

Mutation proof: swapping the bounded read back to `Buffer.from(await response.text())` in `src/sources/http.ts` fails exactly those two tests and leaves the other 38 green; restoring returns 40/40.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/team-reports --run   ->  Test Files 20 passed | 1 skipped (21)   Tests 207 passed | 5 skipped (212)
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts                   ->  Test lines 6446987 vs ceiling 6446844; net delta -2: this change does not add test lines.
format:check (6 changed files)                              ->  All matched files use the correct format
oxlint (3 changed sources, 259 rules)                       ->  Found 0 warnings and 0 errors
```

`tsc`/`tsgo` cannot run in this worktree (the shared install resolves `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` through a symlinked `node_modules`), so type checking rests on CI's `check-prod-types` / `check-test-types`; the bounded read call matches the shape already compiling on `main` at `extensions/discord/src/internal/rest.ts:66`.

prs.title: fix(openai): let fast voice answers skip acknowledgments
prs.body:
Related: #175603.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway-controlled OpenAI Talk acknowledges every delegated request immediately, even when the answer is ready fast enough to speak directly. Repeated acknowledgments make short conversations feel repetitive and add unnecessary speech before the result.

## User Impact

Work starts immediately. An answer or failure arriving within 1.5 seconds skips filler. Slower requests receive at most one short acknowledgment using the existing caller-language, naturally varied wording from #175603. Wording variation remains model-directed, not guaranteed.

Spoken updates, follow-ups, controls, and call shutdown cancel an unsent acknowledgment. Status, cancellation, final results, and failure delivery retain their existing ownership. No new configuration or client changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Race the existing consult against a short acknowledgment timer in its existing controller. This avoids a separate predictive model call or delaying the actual work. The timer is canceled when the consult settles or its presentation becomes obsolete, and uses the original socket's delivery checks.

The 1.5-second window is an initial UX choice, not a measured latency improvement. An answer arriving just after that window can still follow an acknowledgment already submitted to the provider.

## Evidence

- Baseline regression: 12 failures / 20 passes against the unmodified controller, including the new fast-answer, slow-answer, and cancellation cases failing on its immediate append.
- All 89 focused tests pass across delegation (32), public delegation (8), Gateway bridge and browser session (36 combined), and agent-tool prompt stability (13). Two old consumer expectations of immediate filler were updated and their 40-test subset rerun successfully.
- Changed delegation/public-delegation suites: 25.43 seconds including compilation; 28.19 seconds including runner cleanup. Earlier four-suite voice run: 6.52 seconds with cached compilation. Hosted CI timing pending.
- OpenAI package typecheck, type-aware lint of all four touched TypeScript files, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.
- Independent autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the diff. Review was limited to supplied changes; focused execution provides the runtime proof above.
- Graphify AST-only refresh completed for the OpenAI package. Generated graph files are not part of this PR.

No live provider/audio or physical-device acceptance test was run. The running Gateway and native app were not changed.

The simplification pass retains one timer in the existing controller and no new policy owner, queue, config surface, or predictive classifier. Production delta: +30/-2 lines; tests: +113/-17; docs: +5/-2.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): Windows Claude turns fail with large tool allowlists
prs.body:
Supersedes #156057, thanks @blazingphoenix7.
Related: #144792

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bundled Claude CLI turns on Windows fail to start when the admitted MCP tool list exceeds the Windows command-line limit.

## User Impact

Windows agents using OpenClaw-generated settings can retry startup with the same exact admitted tools, denials, permission mode, and restrictions. Commands that already fit retain their invocation without acquiring a temporary-file dependency. **Merge is blocked on native Claude validation described below.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Try the original invocation first. Only after Windows reports `ENAMETOOLONG`, place the admitted tool names and OpenClaw's path-independent restrictions in a private settings file owned by that child. The existing process owner rechecks live authority after the write; cleanup covers startup failures and child exit, including warm turns.

Only empty settings or the exact OpenClaw-generated restricted projection can relocate. Custom inline settings and settings paths keep their original error, because [moving caller-owned permission or sandbox paths can change their anchors](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#where-a-pattern-anchors). Tool, permission, sandbox, and execution boundaries are preserved.

## Evidence

- **Exact regression red on main:** [native Windows baseline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41767148011), test-only commit `29fb561553c889b90e775667a4d91090f53bd9e2` on main `fa997337ede78046bc0e3e790ba452d06e34627b`. Both oversized settings forms fail in the real launcher with `ENAMETOOLONG` (`-4064`).

prs.title: fix: relay coexistence checks fail after profile configuration drift
prs.body:
Related: #191614

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the relay-coexistence integration suite fails on profile port/name drift because it expects a passive availability probe to reject after cleanup.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change. The test now verifies refusal through explicit browser use while preserving the passive-status behavior introduced in #191614.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isTransportAvailable` observes existing relay state and correctly returns false when cleanup removed the relay. The drift scenario should exercise `ensureBrowserAvailable`, which owns active profile/relay reconciliation and must reject the superseded profile. The fixture now also proves its starting relay is borrowed and available; existing assertions still require retiring that exact access without stopping the daemon or breaking its external client.

No new helpers, retries, timeouts, mocks, or runtime fencing. Simplification retained the existing parameterized scenarios. Production delta: zero. Test delta: +3 net lines, allocated for setup proof and the active-use contract.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on base `34007820fa2c` through the real relay daemon and browser control service: **2 failed / 10 passed**, both drift cases resolving false instead of rejecting at the passive probe.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay/relay-coexistence.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **12 passed**, 51.79s wall time including cold compilation; CI timing pending. This is real local relay/control-service integration with a synthetic extension WebSocket peer, not a real Chrome UI or end-to-end model session.
- Format and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Extension test typecheck fails in unchanged MCP metadata/materialization files (`McpCatalogTool` missing export and optional-field type mismatches); targeted lint stops at declaration preparation on the same errors. No passing broad typecheck/build is claimed.
- Independent local ClawSweeper review of `34007820fa2c..00938234fda1`: complete; no actionable correctness or security findings. Source-only review; execution evidence is the test run above.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41742415327) attached after ready-for-review and is in progress; the initial draft-open run was skipped.

prs.title: fix(imessage): classify voice notes whose MIME is imsg's unknown sentinel
prs.body:
Closes #191335

## What Problem This Solves

In remote iMessage mode, Apple voice notes never reach the configured audio transcription pipeline. `imsg rpc` reports the literal string `"unknown"` (and, per the reporter's follow-up, sometimes `""`) for `mime_type`, because Apple leaves `attachment.mime_type` NULL for voice memos (UTI `com.apple.coreaudio-format`). The plugin passed that sentinel through as `contentType`, and because `"unknown"` is itself a valid media kind, classification stopped at it and never fell back to filename sniffing. The attachment stayed `kind: "unknown"`, so no audio capability was selected and the agent received `[Unsupported document format: unknown]` instead of a transcript.

## User Impact

A `.caf` voice note from an iPhone is now classified as audio and reaches the configured transcription pipeline, the same as any other inbound audio attachment. A real MIME type is left untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sentinel is a producer-side artifact of `imsg`, so it is normalized at the iMessage ingress rather than by relaxing global MIME precedence:

- `normalizeIMessageMimeType` treats the `"unknown"`/empty spellings as a missing MIME.
- `resolveIMessageAttachmentMimeType` then falls back to the attachment filename (`original_path`, then `transfer_name`), so `Audio Message.caf` resolves to `audio/x-caf`, which the existing `kindFromMime` maps to `audio`.
- Both ingress sites use it: `createTypeOnlyIMessageAttachment` (staging path) and the `mediaFacts` map in `monitor-provider.ts` (remote path, where staging is skipped).

Leaving the fact with only an absent `contentType` was not enough: the fact keeps its explicit `kind: "unknown"`, which downstream consumers (`resolveMediaFactKind`, `resolveAttachmentKind`) respect, so no audio transcription is selected.

## Evidence

### Live Gateway run (remote mode)

![Live Gateway A/B: parent commit vs this branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191405/proof-191405-live-gateway.png)

The shipped Gateway (`openclaw gateway run`, built from this tree with `scripts/build-all.mts gatewayWatch`) runs the real iMessage plugin in remote (`remoteHost`) mode. A test double for the macOS-only `imsg` answers the RPC surface and emits the captured imsg 0.20.0 `watch` event for one `Audio Message.caf`: `mime_type: "unknown"`, `transfer_name: "Audio Message.caf"`, `uti: "com.apple.coreaudio-format"`, `original_path` under `/Users/proof/Library/Messages/Attachments/…`. The Gateway does the rest itself: media facts → core `stageSandboxMedia` SCP staging into `media/remote-cache` → `tools.media` audio selection → the configured CLI transcription command → the agent turn → the outbound `send` RPC.

The same event, config and machine were run against the parent commit and against this branch; the only difference between the two builds on the iMessage/media path is the three files in this PR.

| stage | parent commit | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| media fact at ingress (resolver output) | `contentType: "unknown"`, `kind: "unknown"` | `contentType: "audio/x-caf"`, `kind: "audio"` |
| remote SCP staging | ran (file landed in `media/remote-cache`) | ran |
| audio selected | **no** | **yes** |
| configured CAF transcription CLI | **never invoked** (0 log lines) | invoked; validated `caff`, 16000 Hz, 16-bit, 32068 B |
| agent prompt | `[media attached: … (unknown)]` + `[Unsupported document format: audio/x-caf…]` | `[Audio]` / `Transcript: Quarterly report voice memo: revenue grew 12 percent…` |
| reply sent over `send` RPC | `AGENT-SAW-NO-TRANSCRIPT: …` | `AGENT-SAW-TRANSCRIPT: Quarterly report voice memo: …` |

Selected lines from the two runs (full excerpts in the image above):

```
# parent commit
19:53:49.046 emit message guid=proof-voice-note-0001 attachment=/Users/proof/…/Audio Message.caf mime_type="unknown"
19:53:51.547 scp -o BatchMode=yes -- proof-mac:/Users/proof/…/Audio Message.caf C:\…\stage-sandbox-media-fYmYlj\download
STT CLI: no invocation
19:53:54.545 model request hasAudioTranscript=false hasUnsupportedPlaceholder=true
19:53:54.881 send chat_id=42 text="AGENT-SAW-NO-TRANSCRIPT: …"

# this branch
19:49:01.793 emit message guid=proof-voice-note-0001 attachment=/Users/proof/…/Audio Message.caf mime_type="unknown"
19:49:04.251 scp -o BatchMode=yes -- proof-mac:/Users/proof/…/Audio Message.caf C:\…\stage-sandbox-media-xvZkTy\download
19:49:04.834 stt invoked path=…\remote-cache\…\input-Audio Message.caf exists=true
19:49:04.835 validated caff=true sampleRate=16000 channels=1 bits=16 bytes=32068
19:49:04.837 transcript="Quarterly report voice memo: revenue grew 12 percent and the team should review the pipeline before Friday. (decoded from a 16000 Hz 16-bit 1-channel CAF, 32068 bytes)"
19:49:07.551 model request hasAudioTranscript=true hasUnsupportedPlaceholder=false
19:49:07.869 send chat_id=42 text="AGENT-SAW-TRANSCRIPT: Quarterly report voice memo: …"
```

What is real: the Gateway process, the plugin's remote ingress and media facts, core SCP staging, media selection, the CLI invocation, the agent turn and the outbound send. What is doubled, and why: `imsg` is macOS-only, `scp` has no macOS host to reach from this box, and there is no STT provider or model key here, so those three are local test doubles. The event payload is the one captured in #191335, and the transcription command validates the staged CAF bytes before returning a fixed transcript.

### In-process resolver → selection A/B

![A/B proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191335/proof-191335.png)

A harness drives the real ingress resolver into the real audio-selection gate: it builds the same fact shape `monitor-provider.ts` produces for the remote path (`{ path, contentType, kind }`), converts it with the real `normalizeAttachments` (`src/media-understanding/attachments.normalize.ts`), and runs the real `selectAttachments({ capability: "audio" })` (`src/media-understanding/attachments.select.ts`). `MODE=baseline` reproduces main's verbatim ingress expression (`attachment.mime_type?.trim() || undefined`); `MODE=fix` uses `resolveIMessageAttachmentMimeType`. One variable differs.

| case | main `contentType` | main `kind` | main selected for audio | this branch `contentType` | this branch `kind` | selected for audio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.caf` + imsg `"unknown"` | `unknown` | `unknown` | **0** | `audio/x-caf` | `audio` | **1** |
| `.m4a` + imsg `"unknown"` | `unknown` | `unknown` | **0** | `audio/x-m4a` | `audio` | **1** |
| `.caf` + imsg `""` | absent | `unknown` | 1 (path fallback) | `audio/x-caf` | `audio` | 1 |

The live `watch` event path carries the literal `"unknown"`, which is the case that deterministically loses audio selection on main. The `""` spelling already reached selection through the downstream path fallback, and this change makes it consistent rather than dependent on that later stage.

Raw harness output (Windows 11 / Node 26.12.1, from the built tree):

```
$ MODE=baseline node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs probe.mts
{"mode":"baseline","case":"caf + imsg 'unknown'","contentType":"unknown","factKind":"unknown","selectedForAudio":0}
{"mode":"baseline","case":"caf + imsg ''","contentType":null,"factKind":"unknown","selectedForAudio":1}
{"mode":"baseline","case":"m4a + imsg 'unknown'","contentType":"unknown","factKind":"unknown","selectedForAudio":0}

$ MODE=fix node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs probe.mts
{"mode":"fix","case":"caf + imsg 'unknown'","contentType":"audio/x-caf","factKind":"audio","selectedForAudio":1}
{"mode":"fix","case":"caf + imsg ''","contentType":"audio/x-caf","factKind":"audio","selectedForAudio":1}
{"mode":"fix","case":"m4a + imsg 'unknown'","contentType":"audio/x-m4a","factKind":"audio","selectedForAudio":1}
```

Regression coverage in `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/media-staging.test-utils.ts` ("resolves the %s sentinel for %s from the filename", plus a real-MIME passthrough case): all 4 sentinel cases fail on main's `media-staging.ts` and pass with the change.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/imessage/src/monitor.behavior.test.ts -t "sentinel"
```

Gates run locally against `upstream/main`: oxfmt, oxlint, `run-tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (slack 3231).

## What was not tested

- No real Mac, `imsg` binary, iPhone voice note, STT provider, or model key is available on this box. The live run above substitutes a local `imsg`/`scp`/STT/model double, so the transport from an actual Mac and the real transcription output are still untested; the Gateway-side path that classifies the fact, stages the file, selects audio, and invokes the configured transcription command is exercised live.
- The `suggestion 2` alternative from the report (honoring `imsg`'s `converted_path`/`convert_attachments`) is not implemented; this change fixes the classification that blocks the configured pipeline first, without adding conversion settings.

prs.title: feat(clawrouter): route qualified Bedrock Converse streams
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter models using Bedrock ConverseStream cannot currently reach the native Bedrock SDK: catalog discovery rejects the API, and a base URL alone does not supply proxy authentication.

## User Impact

The exact `aws-bedrock/amazon.nova-lite-v1:0` model can use a fresh, eligible native or manifest ConverseStream offer with only its selected ClawRouter key. No AWS credentials, regional/profile aliases, new models, prices or live entitlement are inferred. Router runtime support and an explicit model declaration are required before the offer is usable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing Bedrock message/tool/image serializer, replay conversion, EventStream decoder, usage and delivery quarantine. A lazy factory on the existing stream-family SDK barrel supplies an explicit proxy transport after final AWS serialization. It rechecks current catalog scope and selected credential authority, bounds request and complete response bytes, honors abort and disables SDK retries. Direct Bedrock authentication and region/profile policy remain in their existing branch, extracted into a sibling to satisfy the native file-growth guard.

Manifest dispatch wraps the actual serialized JSON with the exact selected `pathParams.model`. Native dispatch uses the opaque model segment on the qualified ConverseStream path. Unsupported, stale, foreign, ambiguous and changed offers fail before POST.

prs.title: fix(android): start a new chat while a response is still running
prs.body:
Closes #191339

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android New does nothing while the open chat is still responding, and a later attempt can fail with "Parent session is still active."

## User Impact

User impact: New on Android starts another chat without waiting for the current response, keeps the previous chat's model, thinking, and Fast Mode, and leaves that response running.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar New button was refused in the app whenever a local run was pending, and the gateway treated that same create as a parent reset while the parent still had active work. Ordinary New now stays a parallel child: it still names the open chat as its parent so settings are inherited, and it does not run the parent reset hooks or stop the original response. An explicit worktree start still waits. Forks of an active parent stay refused.

## Evidence

Regressions failed on the pre-fix tree, then passed after the repair.

- Gateway, before: `sessions.create` with `succeedsParent: false` while the parent response was running returned `UNAVAILABLE` / `Parent session main is still active; try again in a moment.`
- Android, before: `startNewChatSucceedsWhileRunPending` failed because New returned false and never called `sessions.create`. The worktree wait still held.
- After: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.create.lifecycle.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.forks.test.ts` — 39 passed. The lifecycle test checks inherited provider, model, thinking, and Fast Mode, an unchanged parent session id, the parent run still in phase `running`, and no parent reset hooks.
- After: Android `ChatControllerCommandControlsTest`, `ChatControllerReconnectRestoreTest`, and `ChatControllerOutboxTest` passed. `:app:ktlintCheck` passed. Line-cap ratchet OK.

Fold proof on this head, after the proof gateway was rebuilt from `b8211519e3b14a91fbd1223b5393328fc2bee538`. The installed debug APK matches that build (`80f1d3f315ba148eb48169b643de714e3ce59ac7e9a3f9558fbfdfa2509ab093`). An earlier install was overwritten by a different debug APK and still showed the wait banner; the shots below are from the reinstalled matching APK. The gateway address in the sidebar is covered.

1. Stop is showing, 2 seconds into "List twenty harbor birds slowly one name per line." Model chip is Gemini 3.8 Flash.

![Stop visible during the original reply](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/saariuslystoned/9ef714b6a4cde33c6b287080430603dc/raw/93ee65f997bb973d0e00e200a2a63f56b38ddd91/08-birds-running.png)

2. Sidebar New, tapped while that Stop control was up. A separate "New chat" opens on the same model. The banner is the existing "Could not refresh models" notice, not "Wait for the current response to finish."

![New chat opened during the run](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/saariuslystoned/9ef714b6a4cde33c6b287080430603dc/raw/93ee65f997bb973d0e00e200a2a63f56b38ddd91/09-new-while-stop.png)

3. Back on the original thread, the bird list is complete and readable. The composer is idle again, still on Gemini 3.8 Flash. An earlier New in the same session was also used: that chat answered "docked" to "Reply with the single word docked."

![Original reply completed after New](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/saariuslystoned/9ef714b6a4cde33c6b287080430603dc/raw/93ee65f997bb973d0e00e200a2a63f56b38ddd91/10-original-after.png)

The shot is the local-pending case: New while Stop is on screen, against the patched gateway, with the original model run finishing afterward. A separate moment where the phone had already dropped its pending indicator while the gateway run was still active was not staged on its own.

Head `b8211519e3b14a91fbd1223b5393328fc2bee538`.

prs.title: feat: adjust answer length and wording without changing chat history
prs.body:
Related: #191342

## What Problem This Solves

A useful answer can still be too long or too technical. Asking for another rewrite adds conversation turns instead of letting the reader adjust the answer in place.

## User Impact

Readers can adjust completed prose with independent **Full / Shorter / Gist** and **Technical / Clearer / Simple** controls. Rewrites stream into view; **Original** restores the exact answer. The last explicit levels carry into new sessions and survive refreshes in the same browser. Copy/read-aloud follow the visible text.

Requires a configured utility model; rewrites use normal model calls. Canonical history stays unchanged. Code/media answers and configurable defaults are outside this slice.

**Maintainer decision pending:** whether this presentation feature, remembered automatic rewrites and streaming RPC belong in core or need a plugin-oriented extension design. This PR does not claim that decision is approved. Exact-head security-sensitive approval is also required before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway resolves the authorized original message and uses the existing tool-free utility runtime. Only the requesting connection receives provisional text. The UI owns cancellation, stale-result rejection and bounded completed-variant caching; only level choices persist locally. Original resets the preference.

The review repair retains the private actor's read guard through provider dispatch and every output chunk. Existing incognito permissions and the broadcaster are unchanged. Settings types now live in the preference leaf, and latest-answer identity follows the existing immutable-history memo rather than rescanning on text deltas. Native labeled menus replace bespoke dot-selector CSS, with **zero added stylesheet bytes**. No new dependency, service or database migration; rollback is a revert.

## Evidence

### Current repair: `08d302fc15df7b5c3c6f49b407054411d5a263f0`
