prs.title: improve(ios): reuse built test specification for screenshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release screenshot capture reopens the Xcode project and resolves its package graph for each iOS device after the lane has already built its test products.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. iPhone and iPad capture reuse the fresh build’s test specification, removing repeated package resolution. Hosted comparisons show lower capture time; overall job time still varies substantially with simulator startup and Watch runtime recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the single `.xctestrun` produced by the clean `build-for-testing` step directly to both device captures. Reject a missing or ambiguous specification before admitting a simulator. Keep the four exact tests, independent launches, credential/route assertions, sequential fresh simulators, cleanup, and Watch recovery unchanged.

Retain existing raw build/capture logs in main CI’s screenshot diagnostics artifact, including successful runs, to make future comparisons inspectable. No additional sampler is added.

## Evidence

Pinned baseline `c1739437a5b7fcaa68291c47b7110f4d1cce26f7`; candidate `b8736bc55449b60e7ab958ff1c49e90c3da5210c`. Both pairs used the unchanged screenshot-only workflow with the existing resource timeline enabled and startup probe disabled.

| Pair | Baseline combined iOS capture | Candidate combined iOS capture | Observed reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | [296.70s](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41764416106) | [233.40s](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41764818674) | 21.3% |
| 2 | [310.95s](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41767573343) | [265.17s](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41767582311) | 14.7% |

The mean combined capture duration was 303.83→249.29 seconds. Subtracting measured XCTest bodies leaves 126.18→89.66 seconds in pair 1 and 145.80→82.63 seconds in pair 2; these residuals include startup and other work, not just package resolution. Baseline capture logs resolve packages once per device; candidate logs resolve none.

All four runs passed on the first attempt. Independent canonical verification confirms all four exact tests passed once per device; logs confirm four launches/terminations per device. All nine PNGs were decoded and visually checked. Seven are byte-identical within each pair; differences are confined to a runtime identifier and minor rendering pixels. One simulator was active at a time, and each family’s shutdown/deletion returned to zero.

All runs matched runner class/image, Xcode 27.1, macOS, five CPUs/14 GiB, Watch RTC cache hit, and package-cache miss. Full-job durations were 818→897 seconds and 1062→824 seconds. Candidate 1 and baseline 2 needed approximately 60-second Watch runtime downloads. Two runs per version on CPU-saturated hosted machines support the observed capture improvement, not a general end-to-end speedup guarantee.

Focused Fastlane tests: 16 passed (0.937s test time; 2.38s wrapper). Targeted typecheck/lint/format, Ruby syntax, workflow checks, test-line budget, and whitespace checks passed. The existing workflow artifact contract test also passed (141ms test time; 2.54s wrapper). Fresh independent review of the production change found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Final head `1ed2dc8954cf7104f6836851ea5b3352558c33a3` adds only the artifact-path expectation to the benchmarked candidate. [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41772778161) passed, including screenshot capture and evidence verification; all required security statuses are successful. A successful main CI diagnostics artifact was independently downloaded and confirmed to contain build, iPhone, and iPad raw logs. No upload or release was performed.

prs.title: fix(zalouser): sanitize outbound tool traces
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

- **Problem / value:** Zalo Personal's custom monitor callback bypasses its standard adapter, so a `message_sending` hook can reintroduce internal tool traces immediately before transport. This patch keeps recipient text and captions clean while preserving configured Markdown-table rendering.
- **Relevance:** Independent P1/security report #90684 tracks this leakage class. Merged #112621 sanitizes the standard adapter only; current `main` still leaves this distinct callback seam open.
- **Smallest complete fix / review map:** Keep configured table conversion in `delivery.preparePayload`, where durable final delivery sees it, and sanitize only the effective post-hook payload in the custom callback. Scope is 4 files, `+76/-20`: two small helpers, two focused regressions, and the boundary wiring.
- **Risk / proof:** Risk is limited to ordering between two existing transforms. Exact head `b012137ca6889eab50e9474c9d34497b2e4752e3`; full Zalouser `221/221`; changed-file format/lint, extension production/test types, branch ratchets, and all 36 non-skipped hosted checks pass. The exact deterministic wrapper has only untouched frozen-base Codex/dead-export debt.
- **External proof limit:** Authenticated recipient-visible transport is `blocked_external` because no safe configured account/recipient route exists. Exact-head tests reach both lifecycle boundaries; no live send is claimed.
- **Non-goals:** Standard adapter, sanitizer parser dialects, Zalo Bot, authentication, configuration schema, and protocol changes.
- **Maintainer ask:** Please apply `no-stale` while authenticated recipient proof is coordinated; the assigned-PR age clock otherwise ignores substantive updates.

## What Problem This Solves

Zalo Personal's custom inbound-reply path in `monitor.ts` can deliver a post-hook payload without passing through the standard outbound adapter. That leaves one route for compact tool-failure lines or tool XML to reach recipients. The repair must also preserve `channels.zalouser.markdown.tables` for final replies handled by durable delivery. Related: #90684.

## User Impact

Recipients get intended assistant text and media without internal tool-trace scaffolding, while existing table preferences such as `markdown.tables: "bullets"` continue to apply to durable final replies. Ordinary prose, captions, chunking, and media delivery remain unchanged; users have no migration step.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `delivery.preparePayload` owns configured table conversion before the lifecycle can return through durable delivery.
- The private custom callback owns sanitization after `message_sending`, so a supported hook cannot reintroduce internal traces.
- Merged #112621 covers the standard adapter only; this remains a narrow, distinct callback repair.

## Evidence

- Exact signed candidate head: `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9` on frozen maintenance base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/zalouser`: `33` files and `317/317` tests passing, including configured bullet-table preparation before durable delivery and post-hook trace sanitization at custom delivery.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passing.
- Changed Zalouser scope passes type-aware Oxlint, Oxfmt, and `git diff --check`. Repository-wide extension lint's only failure is unchanged frozen-base debt in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` (`max-lines`).
- Deterministic `openclaw-pre-pr.sh` gate: passed for frozen base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`, exact head `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9`, and merge tree `1d2e0ad6dc09fd07dfa21423c38602b80e92ae9d`.
- Current-`main` negative control: the custom monitor callback still resolves and delivers the post-hook payload directly. This head restores pre-durable table preparation and sanitizes immediately before custom text/caption resolution.
- Remaining proof state is `blocked_external`, not a claimed live pass: authenticated recipient-visible proof still requires a safe Zalo Personal account and recipient route.

AI-assisted change, manually reviewed and validated.
## Exact-head refresh (2026-10-26)

<!-- clawsean-head-refresh-2026-10-26 -->
The current signed PR head is `b012137ca6889eab50e9474c9d34497b2e4752e3`, rebuilt on frozen base `f4a0d4875912103be54dd672e32db17064d003db` with a four-file patch and clean merge tree `f44ddf096cf52e14aadcf50b892f2ea4b8765eee`.

- Disposable Linux/arm64 proof used Node 24.22.1 and a fresh frozen-lockfile install; the full Zalouser suite passed `221/221` across 30 files.
- Changed-file format/lint, production and test extension typechecks, conflict/line-cap/assertion/SQLite/plugin-boundary ratchets, doctor-contract tests, media/runtime guards, and import-cycle checks passed.
- Independent exact-diff review found no P0-P2 findings. GitHub and the fork ref read back this exact head, and all 36 non-skipped hosted checks pass with none pending or failed.
- Authenticated recipient-visible Zalo proof remains externally blocked: no consented safe recipient route is available, so no private recipient was used and no live-send claim is made. The deterministic negative path, exact-head full suite, and hosted execution are the strongest contributor-safe evidence currently possible.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): preserve untouched frontmatter on metadata updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a wiki metadata update re-formats every frontmatter key it was never asked to touch, and can corrupt or break pages that use YAML anchors and aliases.

`renderWikiMarkdown` (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts:151`) rendered the frontmatter by stringifying the parsed JavaScript values it was handed, and `writeWikiPage` (`apply.ts:177`) fed it exactly those values. Anything the YAML parser could not round-trip was lost on the next write, and *any* metadata mutation rewrites the whole block — including the ones that only change `status` or `updatedAt`.

Reproduced end to end through the shipped CLI on the latest published stable (`OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350)`, installed with `npm install -g` into an isolated prefix): `openclaw wiki apply metadata <lookup>` (`cli.ts:737`) runs the same `applyMemoryWikiMutation` owner behind the `wiki_apply` tool (`tool.ts:256`) and the `wiki.apply` Gateway method (`gateway.ts:296`), against a temp vault page `entities/alpha.md`. Each row is the real page text after a mutation that names one key:

| page source | after a metadata update on stable v2026.10.10 | after this change |
|---|---|---|
| `version: 1.10` | `version: 1.1` | `version: 1.10` |
| `build: 007` | `build: 7` | `build: 007` |
| `big: 12345678901234567890` | `big: 12345678901234567000` | `big: 12345678901234567890` |
| `# provenance: imported from the OKF export` | (dropped) | kept |
| `  - alpha   # team tag` | `  - alpha` (comment dropped) | `  - alpha # team tag` |
| `description: >-` + two folded lines | one long `description: folded text …` line | block scalar kept, lines re-wrapped |
| `status: &s active` + `customStatus: *s` | anchor and alias flattened into two literals | `status: &s review` + `customStatus: active` — the alias is detached first, so it cannot follow the rewrite |
| `confidence: &c 0.3` + `customConfidence: *c`, then clear `confidence` | both keys flattened, structure gone | `confidence` removed, `customConfidence: 0.3` kept |
| `keyName: &k confidence` + `? *k` / `: 0.3`, then clear `confidence` | `keyName: confidence`, `&k` dropped, pair gone | `keyName: &k confidence` kept with its anchor; only the addressed pair is removed |
| `keyName: &s status` + `? *s` / `: active`, then set `status: review` | `keyName: status` + `status: review`, `&s` dropped | `keyName: &s status` + `status: review`, still one pair for `status` |
| `questions: &q` / `  - *q` / `  - kept`, then replace `questions` | whole page re-rendered from values, anchor structure gone | the key is patched in place; the rest of the page keeps its source |

So a comment written by a human, and numeric spellings that carry meaning (`007` asset tags, `1.10` version pins, snowflake-style ids), silently changed as a side effect of an unrelated field update; and the anchor/alias structure that shares one value between two keys was flattened away so the page no longer means what its author wrote. The page is the user's file: the mutation asked for `status` and got a parse/re-render of everything.

What changed: `renderWikiMarkdown` takes the page it is about to replace (`original`, `markdown.ts:158`) and, when that page has mapping frontmatter, patches that YAML document instead of stringifying values — keys the caller dropped are removed, keys whose value actually changed are set, untouched keys keep their source. The frontmatter half moved to its own module, `extensions/memory-wiki/src/frontmatter-source.ts` (entry point `renderWikiFrontmatter`, `frontmatter-source.ts:15`), because `markdown.ts` was already at the repository's `max-lines` ceiling. Because `*ref` reads through the node carrying `&ref`, the node the patch is about to change or delete is first resolved, in the two directions review found:

- every *value* alias of that node is replaced with a copy holding the value it had before the write (`detachKeyAliases`, `frontmatter-source.ts:132`), and that copy is rebuilt node by node so it neither repeats the source's anchors nor loses the numeric tokens `clone()` drops (`restoreFrontmatterCopy`, `frontmatter-source.ts:189`);
- every *key* the mutation addresses that the page spells as `? *ref` is first rewritten to a plain copy of the name it reads (`resolveAliasedKeys`, `frontmatter-source.ts:73`), because `Document.set`/`delete` address pairs by key name and would otherwise append a second pair next to the aliased one; when one name is spelled on more than one pair, every pair of that name is dropped before the single write (`dropDuplicateKeyPairs`, `frontmatter-source.ts:107`).

An alias that sits *inside* the node being detached leaves with that node, so it needs no copy (`containsFrontmatterNode`, `frontmatter-source.ts:317`) — without that skip, a list whose own item aliases the list (`questions: &q` / `- *q`) makes `clone()` recurse until the stack overflows. If a detached copy still could not be finite — the anchored node reads back into itself through some other reader — the page declines to the previous value-rendering path rather than hanging (`frontmatterAnchorLoops`, `frontmatter-source.ts:292`), and the same is true for a page whose top-level key is not a plain string (`frontmatter-source.ts:45`). The patched document is serialized as-is, and only yaml's own document terminator is trimmed (`frontmatter-source.ts:64`), so a block scalar's chomped trailing newlines stay part of the value. `writeWikiPage` now reads the page before rendering and passes it (`apply.ts:192`); without `original` (new pages, report generation) rendering is byte-for-byte what it was before.

What did NOT change: mutation semantics, the `status`/`updatedAt` writes, human `## Notes` block handling, the managed related-pages block, page ordering, compile/index side effects, the malformed-frontmatter refusal path, and the on-disk text for every page whose frontmatter is already canonical. No new config, no new file format, no migration.

## User Impact

User impact: a metadata update now leaves the rest of the page's frontmatter exactly as written, instead of quietly rewriting numbers, dropping comments, flattening block scalars or erasing the anchor/alias structure that ties two keys to one value.

Anyone who keeps a wiki vault of hand-written or imported Markdown — which is the documented use of this plugin (`docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md`) — stops losing frontmatter detail on unrelated metadata edits. Agents that call `wiki_apply` and operators who run `openclaw wiki apply metadata` get the same behavior; no action is required from them. Pages written by this branch are still read by the published stable CLI, and pages written by the published stable CLI are still read and patched by this branch (items 5 and 6 in Evidence).

Accepted, visible limits, called out rather than coded around:

- Block scalars keep their style and content but the emitter may re-wrap the folded lines, and spacing before an inline comment normalizes to one space (`- alpha   # team tag` → `- alpha # team tag`). Values are identical; only whitespace inside the block and before `#` moves.
- Non-numeric scalars are still emitted from their parsed value, so an unusual quote style (`'x'` vs `"x"`) can normalize. Only the value-bearing numeric spellings above are byte-preserved.
- An alias is detached into a literal copy only for the key the mutation actually touches; aliases whose anchor is untouched keep reading through `&anchor`.
- A `? *ref` key is only rewritten when the anchor it reads resolves to a plain string. A page whose addressed key reads to anything else — a mapping, a number — is not patched at all and takes the previous value-rendering path (`frontmatter-source.ts:86`).
- A recursive anchor whose detached copy would not be finite (the anchored node reads back into itself through a reader outside it) is not patched either; that page takes the same value-rendering path, which is what stable does today, so nothing regresses (`frontmatter-source.ts:167-172`).
- A merge key (`<<: *d`) is preserved when the caller hands back what it read, which is what the shipped metadata path does (item 10). A caller that instead hands over values where the merge was already expanded gets that one host written from those values, without its `<<` — the same bytes stable writes for that page today.
- A page whose frontmatter has a top-level key that is not a plain string (`1: alpha`, a complex `? {…}` key) is not patched at all — `Document.set`/`delete` address pairs by strict key equality and would append a second pair for the same key — so those pages take the previous value-rendering path.
- Only yaml's own document terminator is trimmed from the serialized document, never a keep-chomped (`|+`) value's blank lines. That class is pinned by the renderer test `keeps a keep-chomped block scalar's trailing newlines when a sibling key is removed`; it is not a shipped-CLI claim, because the metadata mutation appends `updatedAt` after any block scalar, so a keep-chomped value cannot be the last key on that path.
- `writeWikiPage` is the only caller that patches a page it just read, so this is the only path that preserves a user's source frontmatter. The other `renderWikiMarkdown` callers serialize frontmatter they own (`compile.ts:692` and `compile.ts:723` dashboard reports, `lint.ts:364` lint report, `okf.ts:516`, `chatgpt-import.ts:418` and `chatgpt-import.ts:486`, `source-page-shared.ts:31`) and pass no `original`, so their bytes are unchanged; the report refresh that carries parsed values forward (`compile.ts:725` spreads `...parsed.frontmatter`) is a separate cutover.

## Why This Change Was Made

Because "the mutation rewrote a field I never named" is a data-loss bug in the file that is the product's source of truth, and the repository already solved this exact problem twice.

- `renderWikiMarkdown` is the single owner of wiki page serialization — the metadata writer (`apply.ts:192`), the dashboard/report refresh (`compile.ts:692` and `compile.ts:723`), the lint report (`lint.ts:364`), the OKF and ChatGPT importers (`okf.ts:516`, `chatgpt-import.ts:418` and `chatgpt-import.ts:486`) and the shared source-page renderer (`source-page-shared.ts:31`) all call it. Fixing the owner keeps one place that decides what a page looks like, and the fidelity rule is available to every caller that has a page to patch.
- The raw-text pattern is already the house style in this module: `writeLintReport` (`lint.ts:355`) keeps the report's bytes and only replaces its managed block, precisely so a writer cannot reformat what it did not author. `extensions/oc-path/src/oc-path/yaml/edit.ts:151` does the same for an in-place YAML editor, and its `tests/edit.test.ts:22` pins that `1.10` and `0123` survive an edit — the `customTags`/`stringify` technique that keeps numeric tokens is reused here for the same reason.
- Document patching is the cheap mechanism here. The alternative — teaching every caller to only pass changed keys — leaves the lossy renderer in place for the next caller, and `writeWikiPage` cannot know which keys a mutation "meant" to change once the frontmatter has been merged into one object.
- The alias resolution belongs in the same owner because yaml makes the two inseparable: `YAMLMap` overwrite keeps the anchor and `delete` drops it, so patching the document without resolving alias *readers* would trade a formatting bug for a page that no longer parses; and patching without resolving an alias *key* would append a second pair for a name the page already spells. Both are addressed at the point where the pair is about to be touched (`frontmatter-source.ts:45-61`), not in a second pass over the document.
- The change is deliberately additive at the API: `original` is optional, so the report/new-page paths keep their current output and no caller has to adopt it to stay correct.
- Risk is bounded to serialization of pages that really do have non-canonical frontmatter. If the original frontmatter cannot be read as a mapping (no frontmatter, parse errors, sequence root, malformed page), or a touched pair is not addressable, the code takes the old `YAML.stringify` path — which is also what the existing malformed-write-target tests (`apply.test.ts`, `#96125`) exercise.

prs.title: feat(ci): freeze prospective graph selection decisions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adaptive CI needs a selection proposal recorded before test outcomes, based only on earlier published observations.

## User Impact

Sampled CI runs record a graph proposal against their complete native test inventory. Every scheduled test still executes; automatic skipping remains disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consumes the bounded prior bundle from [PR #192514](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192514) at the native inventory callback. Exact runtime/configuration identities and local source ancestry must match. The record retains prior artifact provenance, bundle hash, prior-to-current changed paths, candidate selection, full scheduled inventory and fallback reasons.

The manifest marks eligible jobs before compression, so direct, packed and pooled descriptors preserve the same download decision. Missing history, dirty checkouts or incompatible evidence retain full execution without fetching history or calling a model. Shallow history and differing shard identities remain explicit coverage gaps.

Built on merged https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192514. This second layer records prospective graph decisions.

## Evidence

- At `b4bd75815e279fb21ddd04a1c8c4b7186a3542c5`, 17 graph/observation tests passed (3.54s Vitest; 5.35s routed wall) and eight targeted matrix cases passed (17.88s Vitest; 19.24s routed wall). The 672 other matrix cases were intentionally outside the selected scope. The packed-matrix regression fails against the original planner.
- At `b4bd75815e279fb21ddd04a1c8c4b7186a3542c5`, scripts and tooling-test typechecks, scoped typed lint, formatting, generated-owner checks, workflow validation and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent review verified the context contract and packed-job repair. Local ClawSweeper found the original eligibility defect, then cleared the repair; the final follow-up only uses equivalent nonmutating sorting and required braces.
- Exact justified allocation: 221 added test lines. The shared baseline is unchanged.
- No omission savings or CI model tokens are claimed. Restoration/download/comparison overhead remains part of later net-benefit measurement.

The three-commit change was rebased onto the actual lower-layer squash with a patch-identical range-diff. Dependency inputs are unchanged. [Exact-head CI 41772709647, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41772709647) passed: 53 successful jobs, 22 skips, zero failures. Run time was 10m48s (04:21:30–04:32:18 UTC). Extension-lint shards took 6m18s, 6m16s and 7m09s; this is one-run bottleneck evidence, not a measured saving.

prs.title: fix(agents): transcode provider-unsupported images within limits
prs.body:
Fixes #192426

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a GIF that is within the size and dimension limits (for example from `view_image` or a prompt image) is sent to xAI as `image/gif`. xAI rejects the turn with a 400, and because the GIF is replayed from the transcript, every later turn in that session fails too.

## User Impact

User impact: on xAI, GIFs and other images that aren't JPEG, PNG or WebP are now sent as JPEG, so the turn succeeds. Existing xAI sessions that already hold a GIF recover on their next turn without being deleted. Other providers are unchanged and still receive the original GIF.

## Why This Change Was Made

xAI only accepts JPG, PNG, WebP and ICO, even for images within the size limits; other providers accept GIF. So format policy belongs to the provider, not to the shared sanitizer. The shared `sanitizeContentBlocksImages()` path is left exactly as on `main`.

The xAI stream wrapper (`extensions/xai/stream.ts`) now gets a `createXaiImageFormatWrapper` step. On each request it checks every message's image blocks: user content and tool results, so both the fresh turn and replayed history are covered. It converts any block whose format xAI rejects to JPEG with the existing `resizeToJpeg` helper (no enlargement; GIF first frame). Successful conversions are cached by source bytes (bounded at 64 entries), so replay doesn't re-encode on every request. Failed conversions are not cached, so a transient encoder failure (worker exit, timeout) is retried on the next request instead of sticking for the session. When nothing needs converting, the wrapper calls straight through, so no async step is added. If conversion fails, that block becomes omission text for xAI only: `[omitted image: could not convert image/gif to a format xAI accepts; ask the user to resend it as PNG or JPEG]`, so the model can tell the user what to do. The transcript is not rewritten.

Kept provider-specific format policy as recommended; other providers keep GIF pass-through.

Out of scope: the format-400 recovery / replay drop guard from the issue is intentionally not part of this PR.

## Evidence

- Regression test in `extensions/xai/stream.test.ts`: "converts within-limit GIFs to JPEG for xAI fresh and replayed turns only". If the encoder fails once, that request gets the actionable omission text, and the next request with the same image converts it (failures aren't cached). A tool-result GIF (replay) and a user GIF (fresh) must reach the underlying stream as `image/jpeg` for provider `xai`, and must stay as the original GIF for a non-xAI provider. It fails on `origin/main` and on the previous head (0d79e58), and passes on this branch.
- The round-1 global changes and their test edits (`tool-images.ts`, `tool-images.test.ts`, `images.test.ts`) were reverted to `main`, so the existing shared-sanitizer tests again assert GIF pass-through.
- Built CLI before/after against a local mock `/v1/responses` endpoint that returns xAI's 400 text for `data:image/gif`. I ran it with an `xai` provider pointed at the mock and with a non-xAI `openai-responses` provider (`mockother`). No live xAI request was made (no account); the mock stands in for xAI.

Mock `/v1/responses` request log, built CLI (`openclaw agent --local`, a 1×1 GIF in turn 1, then a text-only turn 2 in the same session):

```
# before (origin/main build), provider xai
POST /v1/responses images=[data:image/gif;base64,] -> 400
POST /v1/responses images=[data:image/gif;base64,] -> 400   # text-only turn still replays the GIF
# after (this branch build), provider xai
POST /v1/responses images=[data:image/jpeg;base64,] -> 200
POST /v1/responses images=[data:image/jpeg;base64,] -> 200
# after (this branch build), non-xAI provider: GIF pass-through unchanged
POST /v1/responses images=[data:image/gif;base64,] -> 400   # the mock emulates xAI; a real GIF-accepting provider would return 200
POST /v1/responses images=[data:image/gif;base64,] -> 400
```

<details><summary>Regression test, ratchets and checks</summary>

```
0d79e58 (previous head): × converts within-limit GIFs to JPEG for xAI fresh and replayed turns only
                         Tests  1 failed | 14 passed (15)
this branch:  pnpm test extensions/xai/stream.test.ts --maxWorkers=1   Tests 15 passed (15)  Duration 9.7s (wall 13s)
              tool-images / run/images / agent-tools.prefix-stability  all passed
pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet: Test lines OK: 6452522; ceiling: 6452526; slack: 4.
pnpm check:assertion-safety: OK;  check:test-mock-exports: OK
oxlint (run-oxlint-shards, changed files), oxfmt --check, tsgo:extensions:test, git diff --check: clean
test-lines allocation: config/test-lines-allocations/xai-gif-within-limits-192426.txt = 36 (exact net added test lines)
```
</details>

Terminal recordings (asciinema → agg), each showing an xai run then a non-xAI run:

Before (base): ![base](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerome-queck/openclaw/proof-192426/r2-base.gif)

After (head): ![head](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerome-queck/openclaw/proof-192426/r2-head.gif)

prs.title: fix(storage): forward-port SQLite admission and lease cleanup fixes
prs.body:
## Problem

Cold SQLite opens can deadlock behind the shared open queue, and an offline maintenance collision can leave a released lease blocking later acquirers.

## Solution

Take the database admission turn before the per-carrier open queue; retain cleanup ownership and retry maintenance contention until lease expiry. No schema or stored-data format changes.

Independent split of #191830, directly against `main`; no sibling PR is required. Original release provenance is preserved in commit bodies. Scope excludes every other forward-port group.

Local review found two additional cleanup defects: a synchronous filesystem admission failure left an outstanding reservation, and cleanup used the original acquisition expiry after automatic renewal. Both were reproduced before repair. The admission owner now settles its reservation in `finally`; lease cleanup uses the existing heartbeat's committed expiry observation. The shared heartbeat-state module owns buffer construction and expiry reading; no second lifecycle owner or new queue was added. Final review also caught a native startup regression in the repair: preallocating an observation changed who published startup renewals. The native lease now retains the heartbeat's own observation after construction, leaving its startup publication intact. A real delayed-worker startup regression reproduces the original-expiry failure before this correction.

The exact scoped allocation is **152 net regression-test lines**, covering cold admission ordering, physical-owner reuse, failed admission drainage, offline-maintenance release, and cleanup after renewal. Production delta is +95/-38 lines against the base; tests are +162/-10. Necessary growth retains bounded cleanup under the existing owner.

## Evidence

- Fresh six-suite validation passed **74/74 tests**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.capacity.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-async.maintenance.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-async.timer.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-contention.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-native-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Includes broker capacity/drainage, lease lifecycle, and real cross-process offline-maintenance contention.
- Red proofs: `settles cold admission filesystem failures before draining the broker` failed on the unrepaired source; `retries contended cleanup through the committed automatic renewal expiry` failed because release was called once instead of twice. Both pass after repair.
- Final helper-extraction replay passed **14/14** (6 timer tests and 8 real contention tests). Native startup/heartbeat plus startup, async timer, and maintenance validation passed **33/33** after the native-startup correction; the typed maintenance fixture was replayed afterward (**8/8**).
- Native-startup red proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-state-lease-heartbeat.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'preserves native startup renewals'` failed at the original ~1-second startup expiry. The same real lease / delayed real worker path passes after repair, without changing the existing startup cap.
- `git diff --check`, targeted oxfmt, and commit-hook line-cap checks passed.
- Targeted TypeScript validation is blocked by unchanged base MCP errors: `src/agents/mcp-metadata.ts` imports a missing `McpCatalogTool` export, with consequent optional-property errors in `agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts`. These source files are unchanged by this split. Broad CI remains separate; this is not a green-CI claim.
- Final local ClawSweeper reviewed the committed range `34007820fa2c..8405968e8578`: no actionable correctness or security findings; all previous findings resolved.
- Original combined-branch evidence: SQLite worker 384 tests and lease 26 files passed; deadlock regression failed on the original base. This is retained evidence, not a new split-head run.

Reviewed candidate: `8405968e8578`; base `34007820fa2c`. No live production or authenticated Gateway verification is claimed.

## Related CI repairs

Follow-up commit `ce08ea219f28` fixes both split-introduced CI failures from head `8405968e8578`:

- Use `throw` in the async admission function, retaining rejected-Promise behavior while satisfying `unicorn/no-useless-promise-resolve-reject`.
- Supply the heartbeat-owned shared expiry observation in the existing failed-startup mock using `createLeaseHeartbeatState()`. The scoped allocation grows by exactly two fixture lines, to 152.
- Fresh `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/gateway-owner-lease.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.capacity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **67/67 passed**, including failed heartbeat startup custody and broker admission/capacity/drainage.
- Targeted `run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on both changed TypeScript files, targeted format check, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.infra.json --noEmit`: the introduced missing-expiryObservation error is gone; only unchanged base MCP export/optional-property errors remain.
- Test-line checker: net +152 matches the allocation; inherited deficit remains 47 lines (6,445,063 versus 6,445,016). No baseline relaxation.

These are mechanical lint/fixture corrections following the prior clean local review; new-head CI is separate and not claimed green.

prs.title: fix(android): make sidebar session parentage explicit
prs.body:
Related: #150054 — Android-specific context: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150054#issuecomment-5848447065

## What Problem This Solves

Android needs an unambiguous choice between starting a new root chat and creating a child of the selected chat. Previously, implicit Gateway parentage could make a supposedly independent chat a child, while explicit children and grandchildren could appear at root in Threads.

## User Impact

- The sidebar header **+** starts an independent root session. There is no second, competing independent-session button.
- The selected eligible session's overflow menu offers **New child session**. Children and grandchildren retain their hierarchy in Threads.
- Existing sessions are not migrated or reparented. Connection, busy-state, write-access, and selected-parent guards remain.
- These creation actions require a Gateway supporting the new intent fields. An older Gateway gets an update-required error; the app does not silently fall back to different parentage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair carries explicit child intent through creation, persisted session metadata, reset preservation, list/describe/event projection, and Android rendering. Ordinary New sends `independent: true`; child creation sends `explicitChild: true` with the selected parent. Existing upstream standalone/direct-chat behavior and visibility admission remain intact.

The public API rejects conflicting independent/parent intent and adoption of existing keys. A review-discovered edge case is also fixed: explicit child creation without a key cannot take the main-session reset shortcut and reset its parent.

This is an Android proposal, not a web Control UI `/new` change. **Maintainer acceptance of the public `sessions.create` fields and Android product behavior remains separate from this repair.** No upstream merge is requested by this update.

## Evidence

### Final conflict refresh — October 31

Latest head: `83a24f9b7ac18ea4c62e5b94a2404c22023a5c87`, integrating upstream `20cdaea4bb5fc2035949a39643ae2df413ed9f3b` with published `edd05d65883acfcadf20f7b7ba8ecadf9563a321` as first parent. Normal fast-forward publication, no force push.

Upstream advanced during the preceding validation. The only new conflict was the generated Gateway predicate output: canonical regeneration preserves upstream's optional publication-review URL field alongside this PR's session intent fields. Main inspected the incremental generated diff; no handwritten repair was needed. **36 affected schema/compiled-validator tests passed**, canonical freshness and native merge hooks passed, and the exact tree/parents were verified. Prior session lifecycle, inheritance, projection, catalog, lint/types/format and Android evidence remains scoped evidence for unchanged PR-owned inputs. Earlier UI build proof is not exact-current-head clearance because upstream also changed unrelated UI files. Hosted CI remains separate.

### Preceding repair and integration — October 31

Preceding repair head: `edd05d65883acfcadf20f7b7ba8ecadf9563a321`, integrating upstream `bf56514c98ecb628b406889e6d573d0485bfd53e` while preserving published `7e886928692e6897289bf66af707fb86646b0609` as its first parent. No force push.

The earlier Build dist failure was caused by a stale Control UI history-state validator after the session-row schema gained `explicitChild`. prs.title: fix(telegram): drop native commands from DM senders dmPolicy does not admit
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a stranger's ordinary DM is dropped silently, but their builtin native command (`/think`, `/login`, ...) gets the reply `You are not authorized to use this command.` — confirming to an unknown sender that a bot is listening. Scoped direct-chat allowlists could still reach an earlier refusal even after the first repair.

## User Impact
Unadmitted DM senders, including senders excluded by a scoped direct-chat allowlist, are now ignored for native commands exactly as they are for ordinary messages. Senders admitted by dmPolicy but denied by `commands.allowFrom` keep the deliberate refusal; explicit command grants, owners, and group-command behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Native dispatch has more than one visible authorization-refusal boundary. A scoped direct `allowFrom` rejection happens during base-access evaluation, before final command authorization, so a final-only silence check left that path visible. The shared refusal path now applies the same DM-admission decision at every visible boundary. The final gate uses the latest owner result, while earlier boundaries preserve their existing explicit-grant and scoped-restriction semantics.

## Evidence
- Registered Bot pipeline with an owned loopback Bot API fixture: on the previous head, scoped-direct `/think` still produced the refusal (base-red). After the repair, account-level and scoped excluded senders produce no outbound reply and start no turn. An admitted command-denied sender still receives the refusal, an explicitly authorized sender retains the `/think` argument menu, and the existing group refusal regression stays green.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` against `bot-native-command-dispatch.routing.test.ts`, `.delivery.test.ts`, and `.concurrency.test.ts`: 38/38 passed. `bot-native-commands.registry.test.ts`: 8/8 passed, including `requireAuth:false` plugin commands. Node 24.22.1.
- Both extension production and extension-test tsgo lanes passed. Targeted extension lint completed with 0 warnings/errors across 292 rules, oxfmt passed, the SQLite worker ratchet passed against the PR merge base, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Broader local coverage is not claimed green: `pnpm test:extension telegram` timed out after 30 minutes with the first 11 files passing and no observed test failure; it did not finish. The full changed-check also reports existing dead-export findings outside this diff.
- Live Telegram Test Server proof was not run: the standalone doctor found no authenticated Convex launcher or broker environment pair, so no live trace or live cleanup is claimed. Independent `autoreview` produced no verdict because Codex returned HTTP 403.

prs.title: fix(telegram): ignore native commands from senders the DM policy rejects
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves

With `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a normal message from a sender who is not on the list is dropped. The same sender's native command (`/status` and the rest of the menu) got the reply "You are not authorized to use this command." That tells a stranger a bot is listening.

## User Impact

Senders the DM policy does not admit get no reply to native commands, the same as for ordinary messages. A sender who is admitted but is not allowed to run the command still gets the refusal. Pairing still replies, so a first contact can finish the challenge. `commands.allowFrom` denials are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#131408 made the refusal text deliberate for a channel-admitted sender who lacks command permission. This path was also used when `dmPolicy` itself rejected the sender. The command authorization result now carries that distinction, and the native-command dispatch returns without sending when the denial is `dm_policy_not_allowlisted` or `dm_policy_disabled`.

## Evidence

Regression in `src/channels/message-access/telegram-native-owner.test.ts`: a native command as sender 300 with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and `allowFrom: ["999999"]` must not call the handler and must not send a message. The existing owner-admission cases still expect the refusal text.

I could not run the OpenClaw suite on this machine. CI is the run that counts.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

prs.title: fix(ui): show website identity in dashboard gallery (#178467)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Dashboards whose primary content is a session:website widget appear as empty boards in the Dashboards gallery with the message 'A clear board, ready for work'. This occurs because session:website is registered with previewSafe: false to prevent passive code execution, causing board-document.tsx to filter out the widget and leaving BoardView with zero active rectangles (view().empty === true).

## Solution
Rather than changing previewSafe: true (which would allow unisolated iframes in gallery thumbnails), this change computes a safe websiteIdentity from authorized snapshot metadata during passive rendering. When BoardView detects an empty layout rectangle set, it inspects websiteIdentity and renders a recognizable website preview card featuring the built-in globe icon, saved title, and localized Website badge.

## Invariants & Security
- previewSafe: false is strictly retained in CORE_BOARD_WIDGET_ELEMENTS.
- Exactly 0 iframes or executable website widgets are mounted in passive mode.
- 0 network requests are initiated.
- Truly empty boards continue to display the standard empty-board prompt.
- Other unsafe widgets (agent:node-browser, mcp-app) remain isolated and do not display a website card.
- Mixed boards with preview-safe widgets (HTML) continue to render normal widget previews.

## Evidence
- Focused unit & integration regression tests: 27/27 pass.
  - ui/src/components/board/board-document.test.ts (14/14 pass).
  - ui/src/pages/dashboards/dashboards-page.test.tsx (6/6 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/website.test.ts (5/5 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/index.test.ts (2/2 pass).
- TypeScript check: pnpm tsgo:ui (0 errors).
- Linter checks: pnpm lint:ui:styles and pnpm lint:ui:no-raw-window-open (0 errors, 0 warnings across 6091 files).
- Build check: pnpm --dir ui build (clean build of 6325 modules in 1m 19s).
- Visual evidence: Playwright browser verification with system Chrome confirming recognizable card rendering with globe icon and widget title, and 0 iframes mounted.

Fixes #178467

prs.title: fix: bound Codex catalog startup and client cleanup
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/152886

## What Problem This Solves

Codex catalog startup can load the agent runtime prematurely and retain client work after its owner closes, while competing health refreshes can consume catalog admission during Gateway startup.

## User Impact

Catalog and client work keeps its existing owner, cancellation and cleanup boundaries. A canonically bundled Codex plugin can use the host's state APIs without mislabeling a locally patched archive as an official npm installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the catalog factory available when the harness loads while deferring heavyweight authentication code and actual client/catalog requests. Close owned transport work, fence native catalog walks, and align the bundled harness with native Codex 0.159.3.

This branch also includes its inherited Gateway health ownership, catalog admission, fleet metadata and serialized build fixes. It contains six commits and 39 changed files relative to the release branch's common ancestor; the final Codex commit changes 24 files. It preserves installed-plugin provenance and the existing local-archive trust refusal. Host bundling uses the canonical package composer.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep chat history retry windows on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI chat history retry still measures its 60s window with `Date.now()`. A suspended tab, laptop sleep, or wall-clock jump can close that window early (or keep it open too long) while `performance.now()` has barely advanced. TUI already moved these deadlines to monotonic time in #183635; session branch PR cache windows moved in #191576. Chat history reads and the message-subscription recovery loop were left on wall time.

## User Impact

After sleep or a clock adjustment, opening a conversation can drop a still-valid transient retry and surface a timeout (or keep retrying past the intended window). Fixing this keeps history load and subscription recovery on elapsed time so recovery behavior matches the rest of the UI stack.

## Why This Change Was Made

Complete the monotonic cutover for the remaining Control UI write/compare sites that still use `Date.now()` for the shared `CHAT_HISTORY_RETRY_WINDOW_MS` deadline:

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-history-retry.ts` — `retryChatHistoryRead` deadline + `shouldRetry`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-history-subscription.ts` — subscription recovery deadline before/after sleep

Both now use `monotonicDeadlineAfter` / `remainingMonotonicMs` from `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts`, the same helper `ui/src/lib/gateway-retry.ts` already uses.

## Evidence

Red/green unit tests (wall clock jumps +120s while monotonic time does not):

- `retries chat.history when the wall clock jumps forward` — red on base (no second request / load not committed), green with fix
- `retries the message subscription when the wall clock jumps forward` — red on base (`pending` stays `false`), green with fix

Full related suites green under `LANG=en_US.UTF-8` on a merge of this branch into current `main`:

- `chat-history-retry.test.ts` + `chat-history-subscription-errors.test.ts` → **36/36 passed**
- Merge of branch into `openclaw/main` is clean (4 files only)

No real-Gateway e2e; PR CI does not run `run_ui_real_gateway`.

## Merge Danger

Low. Narrow deadline clock swap in two chat modules plus tests; no protocol, schema, or config changes. Adjacent TUI/gateway monotonic cutovers (#183635, #191576) already landed on the same helper.

prs.title: fix(tools): accept an explicit optional: false in read arguments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`read` declares `optional` as `Type.Literal(true)` (`src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-schemas.ts:95`), so a model that spells the flag out as `false` gets its call rejected before the tool runs:

```
Validation failed for tool "read":
  - optional: must be equal to constant
```

That is what #189440 reports: `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` via OpenRouter emits `{"path": "...", "optional": false}` on roughly one in three cron turns. The model then re-sends the same `read` without the field, so the cost is a wasted round trip per occurrence — and any caller that keeps sending `false` never gets the file.

The flag is a switch, not an enum. `read.ts:499` only branches on `optional !== true`, so `false` and an omitted field already mean the same thing (a missing path throws). The schema was the only thing rejecting the value; the tool's behavior never needed to change.

This widens the input schema to `Type.Boolean()` and leaves the runtime path untouched:

- `optional: true` → missing paths still return the structured `not_found` result (`read.ts:504-512`).
- `optional: false` or omitted → a missing path still throws.
- `readToolOutputSchema` keeps `optional: Type.Literal(true)`, since the `not_found` output only ever carries `true`.

Advertised schemas change shape for providers that canonicalize literals: Gemini compatibility used to publish `enum: ["true"]` for this property (`agent-tools-parameter-schema.ts:102-103` turns `const` into a single-value enum) and now publishes `type: "boolean"`. `src/agents/tool-search-runtime.test.ts:261` pinned the old shape and is updated with it.

Closes #189440

## Evidence

Red, on the unchanged implementation — `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts`:

```
 ×  agents-support  src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts > read tool > accepts an explicit optional: false as a required read 9ms
   → Validation failed for tool "read":
  - optional: must be equal to constant
```

The new case runs the real `readToolInputSchema` through `validateToolArguments` (the same validator the agent loop uses), then executes the returned arguments against a temp file:

```ts
const args = validateToolArguments(
  { name: "read", description: "", parameters: readToolInputSchema },
  { type: "toolCall", id: "read-optional-false", name: "read", arguments: { path: "notes.txt", optional: false } },
);
expect(args.optional).toBe(false);
expect(textContent(await executeRead(tool, args))).toBe("present");
await expect(executeRead(tool, { path: "missing.txt", optional: false })).rejects.toThrow();
```

Green, after the change — same command:

```
 ×  agents-support  src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts > read tool > keeps terminal modules cold until rendering in a headless session 195ms
      Tests  1 failed | 31 passed | 1 skipped (33)
```

The remaining failure is not related to this change: that case spawns a subprocess that imports an absolute Windows path as an ESM URL, which the Node loader rejects before any of this code runs:

```
Error [ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME]: Only URLs with a scheme in: file, data, and node are supported by the default ESM loader.
On Windows, absolute paths must be valid file:// URLs. Received protocol 'd:'
```

Validation on the pushed head:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts     → 31 passed, 1 pre-existing Windows ESM failure
node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/tool-search-runtime.test.ts     → 46 passed (46)
./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <changed files>                               → 0 warnings, 0 errors
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                          → 6 pre-existing errors, none in the changed files (stale @openclaw/fs-safe in this checkout)
node scripts/run-format.mts --check                                      → all files formatted
```

`scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` aborts in this checkout at its extension-package boundary preparation step (`Boundary preparation failed (1). If deps changed, run pnpm install.`), a local dependency-state failure unrelated to these files, so the vendored `oxlint` binary was used directly.

Test-line allocation for the 19 added test lines is in `config/test-lines-allocations/read-explicit-optional-false.txt`.

prs.title: feat(beam): preserve live logical conversation handoff
prs.body:
An authorized Beam publisher could open the returned Team link but could not compose. The existing adoption flow also created independent transcript copies. This change lets the publisher send through ordinary destination creation and binds each Beam publication lifetime to one durable logical Team conversation.

Fixes #192520.

- First send imports the bounded, untrusted source history once. Continue, retry and reopen reuse the same destination and bound agent. Later source uploads preserve the binding and cannot replace Team turns; expiry/deletion starts a new publication lifetime.
- Reopen uses read-only resolution with normal source and destination read permissions. It verifies finalized origin before returning the key and never invokes sibling catalog continuation or upstream-link mutations. Connection, hello, phase and cancellation fences reject stale route results.
- Destination model selection uses existing configured aliases and provider-owned version/catalog equivalence. An unavailable preference leaves the override unset for normal configured-default resolution. Source credentials and account selections do not transfer; ordinary authorization and account admission remain enforced.
- The existing Beam SQLite row owns the binding and creation claim. Only an affirmative storage rejection or exact pending-row rollback permits retry. Unknown, missing or mismatched destinations fail visibly and retain reconciliation custody. No schema or protocol version bump; the additive read method reuses existing locator/result shapes.

### Validation

Candidate: `a114bab949ed4c549c52056e8b336566babc7b61`. Published for proof only; **not ready to merge**.

- Independent Codex structured review of the complete branch through `436a6fad9b5b468f8d943bedc1c073f306e70289`: complete, no P0-P2 findings. Independent structured review of the reconnect correction at the candidate: complete, no P0-P2 findings. Bounded independent storage and UI reviews also completed after their findings were repaired.
- Oxfmt, Node syntax checks for changed TypeScript files, diff checks and commit signature verification passed. New tests cover one-winner creation, restart/reopen identity, late uploads, source lifetime replacement, storage rollback, unavailable and equivalent models, destination ACLs, read-only navigation and stale connection results. These tests are not yet execution proof.
- [Native exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41773103646) is running on the candidate branch. Build, focused tests, mock-Gateway behavior, chat boot performance and required CI checks remain pending. Manual dispatch 41772777847 selected an incompatible validation tier and failed preflight before tests; it is not validation proof. Optional screenshot capture from that failed dispatch produced no evidence.
- [Original-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41767408295) built successfully but is red. It measured chat boot gzip at +80 bytes against +64 allowed; the corrected candidate must pass that existing budget. Locale catalogs/checkers/baselines are identical to the parent, as are the identified stale CSS, Knip and UI-selector inputs. Additional real-Gateway, identity, timing and cleanup failures remain under investigation; they are not assumed unrelated or waived.
- Dependency contract checked directly in [Codex model selection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6/codex-rs/models-manager/src/manager.rs#L145) and its [account-filtered model catalog](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6/codex-rs/app-server/src/models.rs). Provider runtime session identity is not the logical handoff identity.


**Open architecture finding:** the receiver binding does not yet establish a source-client ownership transfer. Source clients currently keep publishing without a handoff acknowledgment, allowing source and Team histories to diverge. The source-side one-way handoff/retirement or reroute must be implemented and validated before #192520 is complete or this PR is landable under the expanded direction.

### Scope and proof boundaries

This replaces repeat-copy behavior for receiver-owned handoffs while retaining native catalog adoption owners. It does not synchronize Team turns back to a source harness or grant source-machine access. No deployment or live-provider success is claimed. The separately denied privacy runtime qualification remains blocked; this PR does not bypass that denial.

Production growth is required for durable handoff ownership, creation-outcome proof and a read-only resolution seam; tests are counted separately. The implementation reuses the existing SQLite store, model-selection owner and ordinary Gateway creation/finalization path, without a broad resolver refactor. Against the original merge base, the current candidate changes production by +1,324/-335 (net +989) and tests by +1,049/-17 (net +1,032); docs are +10/-8. Release notes follow the repository release-owned workflow; user behavior is documented in `docs/plugins/beam.md`.

## What Problem This Solves

A synchronous database write scope could return a structural thenable after writing. If an outer transaction discarded that result, its Promise guard never saw it and could commit the write.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Promise-like classifier in both write-scope paths and remove the actor's redundant native-Promise check. Extend the existing repository guard to cover actor/write-scope callbacks and commit hooks at known transaction option positions, while retaining asynchronous preparation.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix(discord): keep guild-icon and wake-name cache windows on elapsed time
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

Maintainer edits to this branch are welcome and will not be overwritten; the author will not force-push over them.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- **Land-ready:** one owner (`extensions/discord`), behavior-preserving clock-domain substitution at all four private timestamp sites, deterministic red/green on base. No config, API, schema, or state change.
- **Alternatives:** keep the wall clock (accepts the defect); import the core `monotonicNow()` owner (extensions cannot depend on core internals — the established extension shape is inline `performance.now()`, e.g. #190894, #191533); change TTL durations (out of scope — durations unchanged).
- **Scope:** the guild-icon cache and the realtime wake-name follow-up window only. Wall-clock epochs that are part of an existing contract are deliberately untouched (e.g. `receive-recovery.ts` message timestamps).

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

A host wall-clock correction while the Gateway runs makes two Discord process-local cache windows jump with it: the guild-icon cache (`message-avatar.ts`) and the realtime wake-name follow-up window (`realtime-turns.ts`). A forward step expires a fresh entry and reissues a `fetchGuild` / invalidates a pending follow-up early; a backward step keeps entries alive far past their intended elapsed windows.

Precedent: #190894 (same shape — wall-clock cache windows → `performance.now()` in extensions; this PR covers the Discord sites that sweep left behind). Sibling: #191911, #191916, #191210, #192122, #192144 (same-class clock-domain fixes across Feishu / GitHub / Anthropic extensions).

## Why This Change Was Made

`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-avatar.ts` keeps `guildIcons` as a process-local map whose timestamps never leave the module; `extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-turns.ts` keeps `pendingWakeNameFollowup` the same way — grep-verified: no persistence, serialization, or cross-process exchange. The read and write sites now share the elapsed-time domain (`performance.now()`), the only domain a wall-clock step cannot shift; switching one side alone would mix clock domains, so all four sites move together. Known trade-off, identical to the core stale-while-revalidate cache owner: monotonic windows measure awake time, so system suspend pauses them. Fix classification: behavior-preserving (clock domain only; no TTL, owner, config, or API change).

## User Impact

On a long-running Gateway whose clock is corrected (NTP step, manual change, VM resume), Discord message attribution either loses the cached guild icon and spends Discord API quota on duplicate `fetchGuild` calls, or the realtime wake-name follow-up window is dropped or over-extended. TTL values and cooldown durations are unchanged.

## Evidence

Base `be881a7f8b1ff5af7ff7783340c98ed9047ea450` → candidate `3602d9e8573b1853d6b2f087e4c29e4a6be107b1`, same commands. The wall step is a process-local `Date.now` offset (the #190894/#188293 preload method), never an OS clock jump.

Deterministic regression in the existing suite (remote Node 24.22.1 container, `vitest.extension-discord.config.ts`):

| `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-avatar.test.ts` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Base | **1 failed / 4 passed** — exactly the new wall-clock case fails (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times`: the forward step makes the cache look expired and reissues `fetchGuild`) |
| Candidate | **5 passed** |

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-avatar.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The new test seeds a guild icon through the real resolver (real `fetchGuild` + real media download, network and storage mocked), then steps `Date.now()` forward 10 minutes — past the 5-minute `DISCORD_GUILD_ICON_TTL_MS` window — and asserts the cached icon is still reused without a second `fetchGuild`. On base (wall-clock window) the step expires the entry; on candidate (monotonic window) it stays fresh.

### Real-transport proof (shipped REST stack)

The discriminant also runs through the extension's real transport client — the shipped `RequestClient` (SSRF-guarded, `DISCORD_API_URL`-routed) driving the real resolver's `fetchGuild` against a local HTTP stub that counts `GET /guilds/{id}` requests (remote Node 24.22.1 container, `avatar-proof.test.ts`):

| `extensions/discord/src/avatar-proof.test.ts` | stub `GET /guilds/{id}` hits |
| --- | --- |
| Base (`Date.now`) | **2** — after the +6 min wall step the icon cache looks expired and reissues `fetchGuild` |
| Candidate (`performance.now`) | **1** — the cached icon is served; no second `fetchGuild` |

```
[stub] HTTP hit #1 GET /api/v10/guilds/123456789012345678
[result] guild hits before step=1 after step=1   # candidate
```

The wall step is again a process-local `Date.now` offset (the #190894 preload method). No mocks on the transport: the resolver's `fetchGuild` path is the real `RequestClient` over real HTTP to the stub.

### Real voice proof (wake-name follow-up)

The `realtime-turns.ts` change also runs through the real voice harness — a real `DiscordVoiceManager` joins the real `DiscordRealtimeTurns` instance; only the realtime bridge transport is mocked at the harness boundary, exactly as the existing suite drives it. The new case arms the wake-name follow-up, steps `Date.now()` forward past the 10 s window, then emits the follow-up transcript (remote Node 24.22.1 container, `vitest.extension-discord.config.ts`):

| `extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-turns.wake-name-followup.test.ts` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Base (`Date.now`) | **1 failed / 1 passed** — the new wall-clock case fails (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times`: the +11 s step expires the armed follow-up, so the follow-up transcript never reaches the agent command) |
| Candidate (`performance.now`) | **2 passed** |

```sh
vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-turns.wake-name-followup.test.ts
```

On base the wall-clock window treats the armed follow-up as expired after the step; on candidate the monotonic window keeps it fresh and the non-owner command fires once. The `libopus-wasm` / `@discordjs/voice` dependency closure is present in the remote container, so the voice harness loads end to end.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+4/−4` (4 sites, 2 files)
- Test LOC: `+61` (avatar cache `+28`, wake-name follow-up `+27`, existing suite `+6/−1`)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the established extension clock-domain shape (`performance.now()`) from #190894/#191533; no new helper or abstraction.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none.

prs.title: fix(gateway): carry run liveness on cron-binding session pushes
prs.body:
## Summary

After a cron wake into a session (`sessionTarget: session:<key>`, `delivery: none`), the `sessions.changed` push that announces the idle (`reason: "cron-binding"`) carried **no top-level `hasActiveRun`/`activeRunIds`** — only its nested `session` row said `false`. Clients that apply pushes as deltas (omitted field means no change, as `docs/gateway/clients.md` describes for session events) stay at `hasActiveRun: true` from the wake's `phase: "end"` push indefinitely.

Repro from #192398:

```
2026.10.10
t+16.91 phase=end            top-level={"status":"running","hasActiveRun":true,...}
t+16.97 reason=cron-binding  top-level={"status":"done","endedAt":"set"}  (no hasActiveRun)
                             nested session={"status":"done","hasActiveRun":false,"activeRunIds":[],...}
2026.10.8
t+15.57 phase=end            top-level={"status":"done","hasActiveRun":false,"activeRunIds":[],...}
```

## Root cause

`createGatewayCronPublisher` was the **only** `sessions.changed` producer broadcasting a key-only payload. Every other runtime producer (lifecycle events in `server-session-lifecycle-events.ts`, chat publications in `server-methods/session-change-event.ts`) resolves `resolveVisibleActiveSessionRunState` and passes it to `buildGatewaySessionSnapshot` as `activeRunState` — which is the only way top-level `hasActiveRun`/`activeRunIds` get emitted (`session-event-payload.ts` attaches them only when `activeRunState != null`). Without a row in the payload, the per-connection projection rebuilds one *without* run liveness, which is exactly the observed "nested row says false, top level says nothing" shape.

## Fix

Mirror the lifecycle publisher inside the cron publisher, after the existing projection materialization settle:

- resolve the agent scope (`resolveSessionEventAgentScope`);
- prepare the row (`withPreparedEventRow`);
- build the snapshot with `activeRunState` from `resolveVisibleActiveSessionRunState`;
- broadcast with `prepareSessionProjection` so recipients get their per-audience row with the producer's liveness facts attached (`reuseEnvelope: true`, like the lifecycle path).

Publishers without a bound projection (existing unit harnesses) keep the previous key-only broadcast. The publication settles outside the producer's async-work scope, matching the lifecycle publisher's "committed publications settle with the Gateway" rule.

## Regression test

`server-cron.publication.test-support.ts`: "carries run liveness facts on cron-binding session pushes" — binds a real projection + gateway context, adds a bound job, and asserts the `cron-binding` payload carries top-level `hasActiveRun: false`, `activeRunIds: []`, and a nested row that agrees.

Fixes #192398
