prs.title: fix(macos): use recognition language for Talk pause timing
prs.body:
Closes #190154

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS Talk submitting Japanese speech too soon, or delaying English turns, when Talk's recognition language differs from Voice Wake's language.

## User Impact

Native Talk applies its existing two-second CJK minimum pause to the language actually selected by Apple Speech, including fallback from an unsupported language. Longer configured pauses remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native recognition startup owns both the selected recognizer and its pause window. Configuration no longer infers recognition timing from Voice Wake. Realtime-to-native fallback uses the same configuration and recognition path.

## Evidence

### Full signed-app turns through a real Gateway, agent, and model

On November 2, 2026, the signed production macOS app completed real microphone turns on a Mac Studio through a separate real Gateway, isolated agent/workspace, and existing local model via the vLLM-compatible provider. These were actual `OpenClaw` main-executable launches, not XCTest entry points. Recognition, native lifecycle, Gateway submission, model inference, and system playback were live. The launcher only selected test configuration and started/stopped the app; it supplied no recognition, transport, model, or playback mocks.

The app and its genuinely staged matching runtime were built from `aaecc05b7d9375eeccf6f4e91c14b72ac833a25b`, version 2026.10.9, and signed through the normal macOS signing script. Strict bundle verification passed. Current head `88f4d2b2f57` changes only the tests from that production build; the production source is identical. The separate Gateway was release 2026.10.9, commit `8b18b55`.

| Apple recognition | Voice Wake | Actual startup path | Gateway/model outcome | Playback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| en-US | ko-KR | Native | Recognized `Hello`; real `chat.send`, model HTTP 200, completed assistant reply | System speech completed; user heard reply |
| ja-JP | en-US | Native | Recognized `こんにちは`; real `chat.send`, model HTTP 200, completed assistant reply | System speech completed; user heard reply |
| ja-JP | en-US | Realtime opted in, incompatible Gateway bootstrap configuration, native fallback | Recognized `こんにちは`; real `chat.send`, model HTTP 200, completed assistant reply | System speech completed; user heard reply |

Sanitized log excerpts below use ET. Request/device identifiers, model identity, endpoints, and credentials are omitted. Transcript checks used only the requested synthetic greeting and its associated assistant reply.

```text
English, native:
15:34:37.967 talk.runtime speechLocale=en-US silenceTimeoutMs=700 macOSRealtimeOptIn=false
15:34:44.654 Gateway chat.send accepted
15:34:49.714 model response provider=vllm status=200
15:34:50.132 Gateway agent.wait completed with assistant reply
15:34:50.448 talk.tts talk system voice start chars=46
15:34:54.879 talk.tts talk system voice done

Japanese recognition, native:
15:40:40.230 talk.runtime speechLocale=ja-JP silenceTimeoutMs=700 macOSRealtimeOptIn=false
15:40:50.438 Gateway chat.send accepted
15:40:53.541 model response provider=vllm status=200
15:40:54.158 Gateway agent.wait completed with assistant reply
15:40:54.461 talk.tts talk system voice start chars=51
15:40:58.894 talk.tts talk system voice done

Japanese recognition after actual fallback:
15:51:16.229 talk.runtime speechLocale=ja-JP silenceTimeoutMs=700 macOSRealtimeOptIn=true
15:51:16.229 talk macOS realtime relay opted in but Gateway tuple is incompatible:
                 mode=missing transport=missing brain=missing; using native fallback
15:51:16.238 talk realtime unavailable; using native fallback:
                 Gateway realtime Talk configuration changed before startup
15:51:28.107 Gateway chat.send accepted
15:51:31.820 model response provider=vllm status=200
15:51:32.244 Gateway agent.wait completed with assistant reply
15:51:32.666 talk.tts talk system voice start chars=46
15:51:37.103 talk.tts talk system voice done
```

The fallback is a real app transition after the real Gateway's native-only configuration lacks a compatible realtime tuple. No exception or bootstrap dependency was injected in this full-app run. This does not claim a live realtime-provider outage or reconnection test. The complete full-app turns establish product flow; exact silence duration was not instrumented in these runs. These captures establish turn completion, not normal application shutdown; the fallback fixture was forcibly stopped after its audible reply and TTS completion.

For audible Japanese-recognition checks, the isolated agent was instructed to answer in English while recognition stayed ja-JP and Voice Wake stayed en-US. An earlier run produced a Japanese model reply and logged system playback completion, but the user heard no speech. That result is not counted as audible proof. The unchanged macOS system-playback path uses Voice Wake's language when the response has no explicit language directive; Japanese-language playback remains outside this timing repair. Realtime opt-in in the final fallback run is confirmed by the actual app log.

The Gateway used isolated state, synthetic conversations, disabled tools/discovery, and a separate loopback port. Only the existing local-model provider credential was used with explicit permission. No normal operator Gateway or normal app profile was modified. Raw microphone audio, private configuration, credentials, device identifiers, non-public endpoints, and unrelated captured input are not published.

### Runtime regression replacing the helper table

The helper-composition table is removed. `TalkModeRuntimeNativeLocaleProofTests` applies real configuration, enters actual `startRecognition`, and observes the selected Apple recognizer and applied pause window. Identical test source was compiled against base `c8f87b2e5163870671510659745f4167239ff50e` and the fix.

| Runtime startup | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ja-JP recognition, en-US Voice Wake, 700 ms configured | Fails: 0.7 s, expected 2.0 s | Pass: 2.0 s |
| en-US recognition, ko-KR Voice Wake, 700 ms configured | Fails: 2.0 s, expected 0.7 s | Pass: 0.7 s |

The fixed run passes both argument cases in 0.035 seconds with no issues. The base run reports exactly the two expected window assertion failures. Separately, 50 current tests in `TalkModeRuntimeSpeechTests`, `TalkModeConfigParsingTests`, and `TalkModeRuntimeReplyTests` pass in 1.816 seconds.

The opt-in startup regression requires `OPENCLAW_TALK_NATIVE_SETUP_PROOF=1`, available Apple Speech services, and no usable input device. It ran in the disposable macOS guest with a process-only audio-service denial. It reads the runtime's private recognizer and applied window through reflection, so private field renames require updating the test. Unused playback cleanup is stubbed; recognition startup and cleanup are real. This tests the applied startup state before missing-input rejection, not microphone timing or full-app completion. The real microphone runs above cover the latter boundary separately.

### Earlier isolated microphone timing measurements

At the same production source `aaecc05b7d93`, signed native-capture test-app runs exercised real Apple recognition, silence monitoring, finalization, and submission to an in-memory Gateway. These measurements exclude agent/model execution and playback; they are supplementary timing evidence, not the full-product proof above.

| Recognition | Voice Wake | Startup | Configured effective pause | Observed last-activity-to-submission |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| en-US | ko-KR | Native | 0.7 s | 1.298 s |
| ja-JP | en-US | Native | 2.0 s | 2.483 s |
| ja-JP | en-US | Injected realtime-startup failure to native | 2.0 s | 2.508 s |

Observed submission time includes recognition shutdown and dispatch overhead. Each measured run captured real speech, received a nonempty Apple transcription, submitted it, exited 0, and completed its Swift Testing event stream without issues or skips. The injected failure applies only to this earlier harness row.

### Other checks and review

- The native app and test bundle compile with `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests --disable-automatic-resolution`.
- The unchanged shared `OpenClawKitTests/TalkConfigParsingTests.swift` also passed: 11 tests in 0.002 seconds in the guest. Its exact source was temporarily compiled into the native test bundle and filtered by suite name; this was not a separate shared-package `swift test` invocation.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and SwiftLint 0.65.1 pass for the changed test files. `git diff --check` passes. The earlier full lint found two inherited file-length violations in unchanged DashboardManager.swift and GatewayConnection.swift; no claim is made that those were repaired.
- A fresh independent Codex source review of the runtime regression replacement found no actionable likely or high-impact findings. The opt-in environment and reflection limitations above remain explicit. This is source review, not maintainer approval or proof of a ClawSweeper rating.

AI-assisted. Thanks to @anmol0b for reporting the mismatch.

prs.title: fix(memory): serve keywords while format-upgrade rebuild runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a chunking/format version bump, the first `memory_search` awaited a full identity repair inline before the keyword-only fallback could run. On a non-trivial index that rebuild exceeds the outer search deadline, so the first post-upgrade search returned nothing useful even though the published keyword rows were still readable.

## Fix

When the published identity is an older OpenClaw format mismatch that is already marked `chunkingVersionOnly` / `lexicalCompatible` (and FTS is available), schedule the existing `syncAdmitted` repair in the background instead of awaiting it on the search path. The search continues under the published mismatched generation and serves keyword hits immediately; maintenance still brings the corpus forward once the background repair settles.

Missing indexes and non-lexical mismatches keep the previous inline repair path.

## Evidence (Gateway live → memory.search keyword recall)

Native Gateway on Linux Node v24.22.1 (`healthz` live). Head `5cd265195549`. No embedding provider (`memory.search.provider=none` / FTS-only). Synthetic Gateway token only.

### Gateway `memory.search` (operator RPC)
Query `alpha` against freshly written `MEMORY.md` + `memory/2026-01-12.md` while memory-core reported stale/missing index metadata and requested automatic repair:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `searchMode` | `fts-only` |
| Hit 1 | `MEMORY.md` snippet `Alpha keyword proof note.` |
| Hit 2 | `memory/2026-01-12.md` snippet `Alpha memory content for keyword recall.` |
| Latency | ~5410ms |
| Warning | Automatic memory index repair was requested (keyword indexing; no embeddings) |

Keyword hits were returned **without waiting for a complete rebuild** — the contract this PR restores during format-upgrade repair.

Local artifact: `/tmp/openclaw-proofs/artifacts/proof-110-gateway-distworkers.json`

### Same-head held-upgrade unit (rebuild window)
```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-upgrade.test.ts -t "serves keyword hits while a format-upgrade"
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  1 passed | 13 skipped
```

prs.title: fix(config): config writes switch models to API-key billing without a warning
prs.body:
Related: #191325

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: config writes give no warning when they move a configured model from a Claude CLI login or subscription profile to metered API-key billing.

## User Impact

User impact: a config write that moves a model from the Claude CLI or a subscription profile to metered API-key billing (or back) now says so instead of succeeding silently.

`config.set`, `config.patch`, and `config.apply` return `billingRouteWarnings` on success and write them to the Gateway log. A warning appears for each affected consumer: agent defaults, agent entries, subagent defaults, heartbeat, and other configured model refs. `openclaw config` and `openclaw setup` print the Gateway's warnings on stderr when a running Gateway commits the write. Doctor's existing billing warning now covers every provider, not only providers with catalog route rows. Writes are never blocked. Offline CLI writes (no running Gateway) do not compare routes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor already owns a before/after billing-route comparison. It skipped every consumer whose evaluation had no catalog route row, which is every provider except OpenAI, and CLI-runtime logins. It now classifies those through the existing route owner (`resolveProviderModelRouteAuthRequirement`, so AWS SDK credentials count as metered), with a CLI runtime's own credentials as a separate route. The Gateway config write path calls that same comparator after a successful commit, with its current plugin metadata, so there is one owner for the comparison. It skips the comparison unless a model-bearing field changed (agent `model`, `models`, `subagents`, `heartbeat`, `models.*`, `auth.*`, `cloudWorkers.requiredProfile`, or another configured model ref), so workspace, tool, or identity edits do no extra work. The commit helper returns a billing-aware reply: success replies carry and log the warnings, and error replies (including a write that persisted but was not applied) stay unchanged. The config handlers send their success payloads through that reply, so `config.ts` does not grow. The routed CLI prints what the Gateway returned instead of recomputing it without the Gateway's plugin and credential state. A comparison failure is logged and does not change the write result. A CLI runtime's route is reported as its "own credentials", not as a subscription, because the CLI may read an environment key itself (#148412).

## Evidence

- Real seam, isolated Gateway, one sitting, same fixture, BEFORE = this branch with only the production change reverted. prs.title: improve(agents): name the child's runtime and credential on spawn receipts
prs.body:
Related: #191323

## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_spawn` receipts do not say whether a child bills through an API key or a subscription login, so an orchestrating agent cannot notice when a config change moves its subagents to API billing.

## User Impact

User impact: accepted native-subagent and local visible-session spawn receipts now say which runtime and credential the child uses, so an agent can see an API-key route before it fans out. The new fields are `resolvedRuntime`, `resolvedAuth` (`api-key`, `oauth`, `token`, `native`, `unavailable`, or `unknown`), and `resolvedAuthProfile` (`personal account` for personal profiles). They describe the primary model at spawn time; the run re-resolves credentials and may use a configured fallback. Cloud-placed visible sessions, ACP spawns, and the `subagent_spawned` hook are unchanged. Existing fields are unchanged.

Result contract (additive, optional, no behavior change):

| Field | Values | When present |
|---|---|---|
| `resolvedRuntime` | runtime id, for example `openclaw`, `claude-cli`, `codex` | accepted native-subagent and local visible-session spawns |
| `resolvedAuth` | `api-key`, `oauth`, `token`, `native`, `unavailable`, `unknown` | with `resolvedRuntime` |
| `resolvedAuthProfile` | auth profile id, or `personal account` | when a profile supplies the credential |

Existing fields and spawn behavior are unchanged. Cloud-placed visible sessions, ACP spawns, and the `subagent_spawned` hook do not carry the fields. Clients that ignore unknown fields need no change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The receipt already echoes model facts from the spawn plan. The plan now also asks the existing owners for the runtime (CLI backend first, then the effective agent harness in execution mode, the same order and fallback the run seam uses) and for the credential (the runtime-aware auth evaluator that model pickers and Doctor use). Like `session_status`, it borrows the Gateway's prepared facts when they are published, so a CLI runtime's own login (for example the Claude CLI's claude.ai sign-in) counts as `native`; it never starts discovery. The runtime comes from harness selection with the model's transport (`api` and `baseUrl` from the published catalog, then authored provider config), as the run seam passes them, and the credential evaluation receives the same transport, so a harness chosen by transport is reported correctly. No new policy or config is added. A CLI runtime whose login is missing reports `unavailable`, not `native`. Like `session_status`, it reads configured profiles and environment credentials, not externally synced CLI profiles, and masks personal account ids. `resolvedAuth` uses credential kinds rather than the catalog `authRequirement`, because only providers with catalog route rows (today OpenAI) report `authRequirement`; Anthropic and CLI runtimes do not. Measured cost is about 0.6 ms per spawn. The fields are display-only: an evaluation failure logs a warning, reports `unknown`, and never fails the spawn. A credential that changes between spawn and run is not reflected; that window is accepted.

## Evidence

- Real seam, isolated studio Gateway (isolated OpenClaw state and config, fixture Gateway token, no Anthropic API key in the environment), `POST /tools/invoke sessions_spawn`, one sitting per comparison, BEFORE = this branch with only the production change reverted:
  - Fixture API-key model (custom provider with a config key and a closed loopback baseUrl):
    - BEFORE: `resolvedModel`, `resolvedProvider`, `modelApplied` only.
    - AFTER: adds `"resolvedRuntime": "openclaw", "resolvedAuth": "api-key"`.
  - Local visible session spawned from a `sessions.create` parent, same fixture model (redacted excerpt):

    ```text
    BEFORE  {"status": "accepted", "mode": "run", "cleanup": "keep", "publicRead": false, "owner": {"type": "agent", "id": "main"}}
    AFTER   {"status": "accepted", "mode": "run", "cleanup": "keep", "publicRead": false,
             "resolvedRuntime": "openclaw", "resolvedAuth": "api-key", "owner": {"type": "agent", "id": "main"}}
    child session_status (both): Auth: api-key (models.json) | Runtime: OpenClaw Default
    ```
  - `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` pinned to `claude-cli` with the host's real claude.ai login and no auth profile (AFTER only; one tiny subscription turn):
    - Receipt: `"resolvedRuntime": "claude-cli", "resolvedAuth": "native"`.
    - The child's `session_status`: `Auth: native (claude-cli)`, `Runtime: Claude CLI`.
    - No `provider=anthropic api=anthropic-messages` transport line.
- Regression tests:
  - The child-plan receipt for three cases, all failing with the production change reverted:
    - The API-key route.
    - A direct CLI-backend model (`resolvedRuntime: "test-cli"`).
    - An OpenAI model whose Codex harness is not registered, which falls back to `openclaw` like the turn does.
  - The visible-session receipt with an API-key credential. It fails with the production change reverted.
  - Signed-in and signed-out receipts through the resolver with prepared CLI-login facts (`native` / `unavailable`). The signed-in case fails on the previous head, which reported `unavailable`.
  - A harness selected only by a catalog-supplied transport (`api: "openai-responses"`, with no api in config) is reported as the receipt runtime, and the credential evaluation receives that `api` and `baseUrl`. This fails on the previous head, which reported `openclaw`.
  - A table test for the credential mapping, and a credential-owner failure that reports `unknown` while the spawn proceeds.
- Green on this head: billing-route resolver (13), child-plan sandbox-CLI (5), visible receipts (9), plus the `subagent-spawn`, `sessions-spawn-hooks`, `sessions_spawn` plan, and cloud-spawn consumer suites.
- `pnpm build`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, oxlint, and oxfmt on touched files passed.
- Cost: about 0.6 ms per spawn (100 warm calls, minimal config).
- Gaps:
  - The signed-in and signed-out unit cases stub the CLI evaluator's decision, because unit workers register no CLI backends; the real decision is shown on the Gateway above.
  - Without a published prepared owner (for example right after startup), a CLI runtime's own login is not visible and the receipt reports `unavailable`.
  - Abort ordering around the new await on the visible path is unchanged (`assertActive()` runs right after it) but has no dedicated test.
  - Prepared auth routes that execution resolves per credential attempt are not projected; the receipt uses the model's catalog or configured transport.

prs.title: fix(codex): materialize native tool-output images from raw response items
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #153949.

Codex's native `ImageView` tool (and other native tools that hand back an
image) surfaces to OpenClaw as a raw `function_call_output` /
`custom_tool_call_output` response item whose `output` array contains a
nested `{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:image/png;base64,..."}`
entry. `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` (the Codex media owner)
only recognized raw `image_generation_call` items and returned immediately
for anything else, so this event shape was silently dropped.
`readCodexResponseOutput` deliberately omits non-text tool output from the
text transcript on the assumption that the media owner picks it up
(`extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-tool-output.ts:129`), so
the image bytes never reached the transcript or Control UI at all: the
assistant's reply referenced "the screenshot above" while no attachment
existed anywhere.

## What Changed

- `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` now also inspects
  `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output` raw items, scanning
  their `output` array for `input_image` entries.
- Each `image_url` is validated through the existing
  `sanitizeInlineImageDataUrl` guard (same validation already used for
  Codex history payload sanitization) and decoded via the existing
  `parseImageDataUrl` helper.
- Valid images are materialized through the exact same
  `recordImage`/`materializeImage` path already used for
  `image_generation_call` results, so they get the same size cap,
  concurrent-completion dedupe, and delivery/transcript wiring as
  generated images, and are marked as a side effect
  (`hadPotentialSideEffects`).
- Invalid or missing `image_url` values are skipped (fail closed): no
  placeholder, no partial write.

This is scoped to the raw-response-item media owner only; it does not
touch the `image_generation_call` path, billing/side-effect
classification for actual image generation, or the separate
dynamic-tool-image rendering path added in #120577 (which covers a
different event shape — dynamic tool results carried on typed thread
items, not this nested raw `input_image` payload).

## Evidence

New regression test, reverted against the pre-fix source
(`git checkout HEAD~1 -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts`)
to confirm it fails without the change:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
...
FAIL  |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media
AssertionError: Target cannot be null or undefined.
 ❯ extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts:394:34
    392|     const mediaUrl = result.toolMediaUrls?.[0];
    393|
    394|     expect(result.toolMediaUrls).toHaveLength(1);
```

Restored the fix and reran — passes:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media 51ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed | 29 skipped (30)
```

Full relevant suites, all passing (89 tests):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.replay-safety.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.final-media.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.test.ts
...
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # media.test.ts + replay-safety.test.ts: 50 passed
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # run-attempt.final-media.test.ts: 9 passed
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # tool-media-payloads.test.ts: 24 passed
```

Formatting/lint on the changed files:

```
$ npx oxlint extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts
(no issues)

```

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs`'s repo-wide "line-cap growth ratchet"
check fails in this checkout, but it fails identically (same file list,
same counts) on unmodified `upstream/main` with these two files stashed
out — it's flagging pre-existing large files unrelated to this change,
not anything this PR touches.

`tsgo --noEmit` on the `extensions/codex` project reports 1618 errors in

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android chat keeps the curated attachment allowlist from #110941, but a `.csv` is rejected when the provider reports `text/comma-separated-values`, and a file outside the list disappears with no usable next step.

Fixes #190979.

## User Impact

PDF, Office, CSV, Markdown, and media attachments still attach. JSON, ZIP, YAML, XML, and plain text still do not. Picking one of those now shows "This file type isn't supported. Choose a PDF, Office, CSV, Markdown, or media file." A CSV labeled `text/comma-separated-values`, or a generic `application/octet-stream` whose name ends in an allowlisted extension such as `.csv` or `.pdf`, is admitted as that type. A `.json` name is not. Extra supported files past the eight-file cap stay a limit omission, not a type rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

#110941 added this allowlist on purpose and did not accept blanket `application/*`. This change keeps that set. The picker is unfiltered only so a rejected file can be chosen and explained. Admission is still the allowlist, plus aliases and generic filenames that already name a listed type.

## Evidence

- `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` `ShareLaunchTest`: passed. Ten JPEGs still drop two for the cap with `unsupportedAttachmentCount == 0`. A JSON share drops one and sets `unsupportedAttachmentCount == 1`.
- `:app:ktlintMainSourceSetCheck` and `:app:ktlintTestSourceSetCheck`: passed.
- API 34 emulator. Before this branch, the Files picker could select PDF and Markdown only. JSON, CSV (`text/comma-separated-values`), YAML, plain text, XML, and ZIP were not selectable.

  - System share sheet, `sample.csv` (`text/comma-separated-values`): the app stages `sample.csv`.
  - In-app picker, `octet.csv` (provider `application/octet-stream`): the app stages it. The share sheet does not list the app for `application/octet-stream`; the manifest filter is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(logging): file paths with a 40-character segment are masked as AWS keys in chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: some local file paths get masked in saved chat history, so `MEDIA:` attachments and shell commands that use them break when one path segment run is exactly 40 characters long.

## User Impact

User impact: a path like `/root/.openclaw/workspace/tmp/iterant/LangWatch-Iterant-pack.zip` stays intact in transcripts. Before, it was stored as `/root/.opencl…atch-Iterant-pack.zip`, so the Control UI showed "File not found" for the attachment, and a copied `scp` command pointed at a path that does not exist.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bare AWS secret access key heuristic matches any standalone run of exactly 40 `[A-Za-z0-9/+=]` characters. In that path, `openclaw/workspace/tmp/iterant/LangWatch` is such a run: it starts right after the `.` of a dot-folder and ends at a `-`. The matcher already skips runs glued to an identifier by `_`. This change also skips a run that directly follows a `.`, which makes it a dot-folder or file name segment rather than a standalone key. Keyed fields (`aws_secret_access_key = ...`, `SecretAccessKey`) still redact through their own patterns, and a key followed by sentence punctuation (`.` or `--`) is still masked.

## Evidence

- New test "does not mask AWS-shaped segments glued into file paths" fails on main (`MEDIA:/root/.opencl…atch-Iterant-pack.zip`) and passes here. New test "still masks a bare AWS-shaped key followed by punctuation" passes on both.
- `pnpm test src/logging` passes (791 tests).

prs.title: fix(nextcloud-talk): expand room allowFrom access groups
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In `extensions/nextcloud-talk`, `rooms.<token>.allowFrom` entries of the form `accessGroup:<name>` never match a sender when the channel's outer `groupAllowFrom` has entries. Every sender in that room is dropped with `drop group sender <id> (policy=allowlist)` (route reason `room_sender_not_allowlisted`), including members of the referenced access group.

## Fix

When outer `groupAllowFrom` is non-empty, the room-sender route previously used a plain `resolveNextcloudTalkAllowlistMatch` on the room list. It now expands `accessGroup:` entries with `expandAllowFromWithAccessGroups` — the same helper the quote-visibility path already uses — before deciding `allowed`.

When outer `groupAllowFrom` is empty, behavior is unchanged (`senderPolicy: "replace"` still hands the room list to core).

## Evidence (Gateway live → Nextcloud Talk webhook authority chain)

Native Gateway on Linux Node v24.22.1 (`healthz` live). Head `2480d791ef07`. Synthetic bot secret + loopback mock Nextcloud OCS for room-info only (no vendor account). Config `accessGroups` of type `message.senders`.

### Authority chain exercised
Signed webhook → durable spool → inbound **room + outer** `accessGroup:` expansion → admit / drop.

| Sender | Membership | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `users/alice` | outerOps **and** roomOps | **Admitted** past allowlists (spool drain attempted agent dispatch: `spooled update msg-users_alice-…`) |
| `users/outer-only` | outerOps only | **Dropped** `drop group sender users/outer-only (policy=allowlist)` (fails room `allowFrom: accessGroup:roomOps`) |
| `users/room-only` | roomOps only | **Dropped** `drop group sender users/room-only (reason=group_policy_not_allowlisted)` (fails outer `groupAllowFrom: accessGroup:outerOps`) |
| `guests/alice` | neither | **Dropped** `drop group sender guests/alice (policy=allowlist)` (distinct from `users/alice`) |

Webhook HTTP 200 is signature/admission ACK (Nextcloud retry contract); authorization is the inbound gate above.

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Boat runs bypass the wrapper's verified source capsule and can leave retained claims tied to temporary checkouts. Applying the capsule also replaces native transport Git state, losing sync metadata needed for warm reuse.

Claims with bound cleanup receipts retain their original checkout for recovery.

The joined payload path is Boat-only; AWS and Testbox behavior and provider defaults remain unchanged. Scripts and stdin preserve exact bytes, shebangs, arguments and exit status. Signals reach the owned process group; uncertain shutdown or restoration retains recovery state.

Exact candidate: `2e771578967e033d6f6674f6b1c077e7e4abcd8b`. It includes the landed CI hook-preparation fix from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192138. The unpublished-source transport change in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192164 remains separate.

The current candidate's integrated hook suite passed 13 tests and scoped static checks. Independent source and full-range reviews found no remaining actionable source findings.
- Historical **CLI-only legacy SSH** proof passed exact-source cold/dirty reuse, bytes/mode/deletion, output, exit37, claim restoration and post-delete artifacts. Its cancellation attempt failed closed with `CHILD`; these results do not qualify native supervisor cancellation.
- The earlier complete `f246eec8` package passed local admission and an actual Linux native microproof with completion, retirement and owner release. Its initial wrapper attempt timed out at 900s after sync. Automatic hydration permits 20 minutes with suppressed progress; that timeout did not establish a stuck operation.
- The forwarded-environment cleanup fix merged in https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/3021. Its local controller red/green and actual Linux normal, race and coverage lanes passed. It routes bounded removal and its single verification probe through the existing owned control path.
- With the matching task-local `4ddf563c` complete package and unwrapped SSH, **cold and warm wrapper runs passed**: exact source/base/carrier, dirty bytes, executable mode and deletion, output, same-VM reuse, claim restoration and normal cleanup. Both expected artifact payloads were reread after exact VM deletion and all-state absence. Cold native end-to-end time was 18m03s; warm was 10m41s. Result SHA256: `6d388d8de3a13ebcf4c3aa11cc89c54b9c806175616abf3fcc34562c5f664e53`.
- Three focused runs accepted cancellation after exact source/child validation, with native process and output closure, owner release and no settlement warning. This does not prove the full cancellation lifecycle. In the latest run, native inspection and endpoint identity checks passed; strict direct SSH then returned exit1. Its private reader output was not retained, so the restoration assertion or failure reason is unknown. Independent named-child/Git verification did not pass, and exit37 was not attempted. Exact VM deletion and all-state absence were verified. Result SHA256: `062bf911e61bbb5f58b34f542531ba0b13f219da11c159de2dadb5d5133acb4e`.
- A prior harness incorrectly required a `noEnv` field that native status intentionally omits. The corrected oracle passed a secretless real-status-producer/real-Node-reader integration test and rejects a false authoritative claim before SSH. A separate attempt stopped before payload on an SSH connection closure.

## Remaining Gates

This PR stays **draft / NEEDS WORK**, R2 unresolved. The remaining task-local live gaps are independent post-cancellation named-child absence/Git restoration and actual wrapper exit37. Cold/warm success does not qualify those boundaries. Completed attempts ended with exact VM deletion and all-state absence verified.

## What Problem This Solves

Adaptive CI experiments need earlier, independently published observations to make prospective decisions.

## User Impact

Sampled same-repository CI runs can restore qualified prior observations. Every test still runs; this change makes no omission or savings claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preflight reuses its existing read-only Actions access and artifact validator to inspect at most five successful scheduled main runs and download at most two archives within a shared ten-second deadline. Exact run, attempt, source, digest, launch-file and publication-cutoff checks reject unrelated or future evidence. Missing data produces an empty bundle without failing CI.

This is the first layer of a stack; consuming the bundle is a separate change. No additional job token permissions or service credentials are introduced.

## Evidence

- At `49f0b414d586b4450d947770045255dab5d8f595`, all 12 focused tests passed (0.701s Vitest; 2.03s routed wall time), along with tooling typecheck, scoped lint and formatting.

Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete `632d5f75d84a8a80e49940c44a2c035b8a1f2be8..8541806f3cdccfea7f824367ac6e183e51ca1a89` range at high reasoning: no findings, patch correct, security cleared. The later commit only fixes the test fixture hash input's type.

[CI 41768835112, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41768835112) completed with 53 successful jobs, 21 skips and 2 failures: the test-line ratchet and its aggregate gate. prs.title: fix: show Gateway names for linked Slack mentions in Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI message bodies can show raw Slack mention IDs even after the referenced person has a verified Gateway profile link. Correct sender labels do not resolve inline references, and bot mentions must not be mistaken for the sender.

## User Impact

- Linked human references show the current Gateway display name using the existing viewer/session visibility policy.
- Unlinked people and bots use the Slack name already recorded in the message; unknown IDs, code, and messages without original account scope remain literal.
- Stored/model text, provider IDs, routing, authorization, and mention notifications are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep native syntax and ID normalization in Slack’s pure mention adapter. The Gateway resolves the canonical channel/account/sender tuple and enriches only the admitted display copy. Native pages are enriched before final byte budgeting/encoding, preserving pagination and the webchat fast path. Live fanout asks each reader to reload its canonical view rather than broadcasting a shared person-name projection.

The existing Slack stripping behavior is moved unchanged into the same sibling adapter to satisfy the channel module’s line-cap ratchet. No new persistence, configuration option, or permission is introduced.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen; human co-author credit is retained in the commit. **PR only: no merge or deployment is authorized by this request.**

## Evidence

**Red:** On baseline `57405d6f170a905c1056ae755ec20e259f893abf`, the linked-state RPC and real Gateway/Control UI browser regressions fail on the expected Gateway-name assertion. The serialized-page contract also fails because the original encoder discards the object graph before display enrichment. Setup failures were not counted as regression proof.

**Green:** Real Gateway + native WebSocket Control UI proof passes for initial subscription history and committed live append/publication. Focused Gateway suites passed 155 tests; live-publication/availability/guest suites passed 54. The full touched history/serialization pair was rerun after isolating its adapter fixture from extension runtime graphs. Slack channel and agent-tool prefix-stability suites pass. Core/extension/changed-test type checks, targeted lint, formatting, whitespace, and the line-cap ratchet pass.

Primary reproduction command (run unchanged on baseline and candidate):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/slack-inline-identity.e2e.test.ts
```

Deterministic linked-state regression:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-handler.test.ts -t "projects manually linked Slack"
```

Coverage includes different/missing account scope, unverified viewers, self references, unknown IDs, source fallbacks, code, escaping, expansion, unchanged stored content, and no inbox effects. Fresh independent local P0–P2 autoreview completed with no accepted findings; its chunked/cross-file-context limitations are not treated as runtime proof.

### Browser proof

The attached **baseline → candidate** captures are inspected, cropped, synthetic fixtures through a real Gateway and Control UI (not mocked transport). The sender fixture is Patrick; the separate human target is `Gateway Alice`, the bot fallback is `Roboclaw`, and unknown/code IDs remain visible. Slack accounts are disabled in the fixture; no live Slack API or inference turn is exercised.

### CI follow-up and test cost

The first CI run caught a one-second functional-readiness poll and unattributed test growth. Commit `c8bb79b1cde857f0fd19b1d8c20666e78a042836` waits for the exact initial/live history result with an explicit setup deadline; it does not change production timeouts or performance budgets. The corrected single-worker browser proof passes in **64.50 seconds wall time**.

The separate `config/test-lines-allocations/slack-linked-mention-display-192473.txt` record attributes **432 new test lines** to the account/viewer, serializer, and real native startup/live-path contracts. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged. CI is rerunning at this head.

Delivery is checked against GitHub’s rendered body image elements, and both actual published proof asset URLs load and decode correctly.

### Bounds

Gateway-link reads are bounded to 20 distinct identities per response; remaining references retain their recorded fallback/raw form. Historical messages without captured channel/account provenance are not guessed from text or the session’s current reply route. Broad PR CI remains separate proof.

![Before — raw Slack mention IDs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fca96dae-3c29-49d4-be4a-fcdedd63c0cc)

![After — linked Gateway name and bot fallback](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/223dbc68-5256-4c0b-90a0-8108c3ae608c)

prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

prs.title: test(agents): pin a local Codex owner refusal to a run-local failure
prs.body:
Closes #191473

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a local Codex owner refusal (HTTP 403 produced by the in-process inference relay, before any provider request) was classified as a provider authentication failure, which cooled down the shared OpenAI OAuth profile and interrupted every other agent using that credential.

## User Impact

User impact: one refused run no longer logs an entire profile out. Sibling agents on the same credential keep working, the model fallback chain is not consumed for a refusal that says nothing about the model, API clients receive a permission rejection instead of a retryable server error, and the message no longer tells operators to sign in again — it tells them to start a fresh request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal is generated locally, so the credential answered nothing; the 401/403 rule in `src/agents/failover/classification-rules.ts` could not tell the two apart. The fix preserves the local refusal's identity instead of exempting HTTP 403 or the `model_permission_denied` code globally, so genuine provider permission errors keep their exact current handling.

- The local relay's own refusal copy is the identity carrier. Codex's transport drops the relay's JSON body and renders only `error.message` as `unexpected status {status}: {message}, url: {url}` (`codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs`, `UnexpectedResponseError::display_body` / `Display`), so the copy is the part that survives to the runner.
- A new run-scoped `session_authority` failover reason carries it: `src/agents/auth-profiles` and `run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` record profile health only for `auth`, `auth_permanent`, and `billing`, so the shared credential is never cooled.
- The reason resolves to `coordination` in `resolveModelFallbackError`, the owner that already stops the chain when "changing models cannot repair" the failure. Another model cannot re-establish the refused run's owner, so the chain surfaces the refusal instead of blaming a candidate, which is what the issue's "should not consume the model fallback chain" requirement asks for.
- `FAILOVER_STATUS` projects the reason as `403` with `permission_error`, so OpenAI-compatible clients stop seeing an unmapped reason fall through to a retryable `500`.
- Operator-facing copy for the reason avoids sign-in advice on both the assistant and auth-profile surfaces.

## Evidence

The runner regression pins the shape the transport actually produces (prose only, no `model_permission_denied` token), so a repair keyed on the discarded JSON code cannot pass it. Red first, then green, same command:

```
node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.harness-auth-failover.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- Before the repair (test-only commit `8c80e28397b`, production code unchanged): `× keeps a healthy auth profile untouched when the local Codex owner refuses → expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 2 times` — the shared profile was marked **and** the run rotated to a second profile (`1 failed | 12 passed`).
- With the production-shaped fixture on this head: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 13 passed (13)`.
- Same run, now also proving the sibling turn: after the refusal the next run on the same credential resolves with its payloads and the recorded attempt profile list stays `[openai:failed, openai:failed]` with `markAuthProfileFailure` never called — the refusal consumed neither the profile nor the fallback chain.
- Model fallback chain, at its owner (`src/agents/model-fallback.chain-stop.test.ts`), with a configured second candidate `fixture-next/fixture-model`: `stops the chain for a local Codex authority refusal without blaming a candidate model` → the error surfaces unchanged, `run` is called once, and neither `onError` nor `onFallbackStep` fires. Red without the coordination routing: `FAIL … stops the chain for a local Codex authority refusal …`.
- HTTP projection for the pinned prose error (`src/gateway/openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts`): `projects a local Codex authority refusal as a permission rejection` asserts `{ status: 403, error: { type: "permission_error" } }`. Reverting only the status mapping reproduces the reported defect exactly — `AssertionError: expected { status: 500, … } to deeply equal { status: 403, … }` — and restoring it returns `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 25 passed (25)`.
- Why the prose fixture still has teeth, probed against the shipped classifier rather than a mock: the same message still matches the generic credential-auth pattern list (`isAuthErrorMessage(prose) === true`, through its `forbidden` and `status 403` patterns), so `session_authority` is carried by the new priority matcher alone — remove it and this input lands on the `auth` path that marks the profile.

```
PASS | local prose -> reason | actual="session_authority"
PASS | local prose hits generic auth pattern | actual=true
PASS | local envelope -> reason | actual="session_authority"
PASS | provider model_permission_denied -> reason | actual="auth"
PASS | provider bad api key 403 -> reason | actual="auth"
PASS | signal model-policy 403 -> reason | actual="session_authority"
PASS | signal 401 invalid key -> reason | actual="auth"
PASS | session_authority copy has no re-login hint | actual=false
PASS | auth copy does carry the re-login hint | actual=true
ALL PASS (9)
```

- Classification matrix, checked directly against the shipped classifier and pinned in `src/agents/failover/classify.test.ts`:

| input | reason |
|---|---|
| transport prose owner refusal (`unexpected status 403 Forbidden: …, url: http://127.0.0.1:…`) | `session_authority` |
| relay JSON envelope, same copy | `session_authority` |
| local model-policy refusal via `{ status: 403, message }` | `session_authority` |
| provider-side `code: model_permission_denied` 403 | `auth` (unchanged) |
| plain `403 Invalid API key provided` | `auth` (unchanged) |

- Copy behavior: `renderAuthProfileFailoverCopy({ reason: "session_authority", … })` returns `openai-codex refused this request before sending it. Start a fresh request with /new.` with no re-login hint, which `src/agents/auth-profiles/failure-copy.test.ts` now pins.
- The new reason is a protocol enum member, so `src/agents/failover/signal.test.ts` pins it in `FAILOVER_REASONS` and the generated predicate was regenerated (`pnpm gateway:validators:gen`) rather than hand-edited; `pnpm validators:check` and `pnpm protocol:check` (registry, gen, swift/kotlin contract, since guard) pass with no working-tree diff.
- Local suites for every consumer of the changed reason: `pnpm test src/agents/failover/ src/agents/auth-profiles/` → `23 + 1 + 6 + 53 + 3` test files passed, no failures; `pnpm test src/agents/failover-error.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.chain-stop.test.ts` → `104 passed` / `69 passed`; `pnpm tsgo:core:test` → 0 errors.
- The first hop is exercised on current source with a real socket and no mocks: `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-proxy.http.test.ts` → `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 9 passed (9)`. It admits an inference owner, unregisters it, and asserts the live relay answers `403` with `cannot verify the owner` in the body; `inference-routing.test.ts` pins the same refusal at the routing boundary. So the refusal this PR routes differently is the one the shipped relay actually emits, not a hand-written string.
- Test-line budget: this change adds `+292` tracked test lines, so it carries `config/test-lines-allocations/local-owner-refusal-191473.txt = 292`. The checker caps an allocation at its own measured delta, so the record covers exactly this growth and nothing inherited, and no coverage was trimmed to fit it. The reason the growth needs a record at all is the tier it lives in: the reported blast radius is a *later* sibling turn on the same shared credential, which only a real Gateway + app-server subprocess + persisted auth store can show, so the 188-line proof cannot be replaced by a cheaper unit test. Attribution for the earlier `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failure, since it reads as ours but is mostly not: the tree was 588 lines over the ceiling, of which 296 is `main`'s own overage. Measured by running the same checker against `main`'s tree through a throwaway index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=… git read-tree <main>` + `--staged --base <main>`), which reports `Test lines: 6442328; ceiling: 6442032; over by: 296; net delta: 0` and passes only on the rule that an over-ceiling tree fails when *this* change grows test lines. The shared scalar in `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` was left alone. After this branch merged a later `main`, the ratchet reports slack and passes.

- Data-model compatibility for the new vocabulary member, checked against the shipped validator instead of asserted: all 16 pre-change reasons still validate a stored cron job (`failures=0`), a cron row carrying `session_authority` validates with empty `Value.Errors`, and the change is purely additive (`removed=0`, and that one member is the only value an older reader cannot know). The closed union is enforced on inbound RPC payloads (`validateCron*Params`, `worker-admission` request fields) and on the cron agent-tool output schema; no production gateway path re-validates stored rows against `CronJobSchema`, and the Control UI imports these shapes as types only — so existing stored data keeps loading after the upgrade.

- **Why the member has to be in the vocabulary — measured, not argued.** The value is not display-only. `resolveCronRunErrorReason` (`src/cron/run-error-reason.ts:6`) returns a `FailoverReason`, `src/cron/service/timer-outcome-finalization.ts:70` persists it as the run-history row's `errorReason`, and that column is read back through `z.enum(FAILOVER_REASONS).optional().catch(undefined)` (`src/cron/run-history-detail.ts:77`). Running the real writer on the native refusal prose with a provider set yields `producedByWriter: "session_authority"`; this build reads that row back intact (17 members) while the shipped 16-member enum resolves the same value to `undefined` without throwing — measured with a throwaway script against the repo's own modules. So the actual choice is: extend the vocabulary, or let the cause of a refused scheduled run be silently dropped by the build's own reader. The same schema also types wire fields (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-admission.ts:416` `reason`, `:452` `fallbackStepFromFailureReason`), which is why `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility` is correct rather than conservative. Folding the refusal into an existing member was considered and rejected: `auth` / `auth_permanent` are precisely the credential-health triggers this bug is about, and `unknown` / `unclassified` would restore the "looks like a provider failure" reading the report complains of. The downgrade direction is tolerant — an older reader loses the label but keeps the row.

- **Gateway turn with an unaffected sibling** — `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-local-refusal-profile-health.e2e.test.ts` runs a real Gateway (`OPENCLAW_TEST_MINIMAL_GATEWAY` off) with a real app-server subprocess over JSON-RPC, a real agent runner, and a real persisted auth store, and reuses the shipped `codex-refusal-app-server.fixture.mjs` with one added `local-owner` failure kind (that fixture already fails the first attempt and answers the next turn, so no new knob was needed). Doctor promotes the legacy OAuth profile to canonical storage, and a model fallback is configured so "nothing consumed the chain" is observable rather than assumed. The cooldown is read through the owner's own predicate, `isProfileInCooldown(store, "openai:qa-oauth", undefined, model)`, because the store keeps these windows in persisted `usageStats` rather than on a profile field — the first revision of this assertion looked for a `cooldownUntil` property and therefore proved nothing; checked first, and again after the sibling run:

```
# this head
✓ leaves the shared profile serving after a local Codex owner refusal
  Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 1 passed (1)
  isProfileInCooldown after the refused run    → false
  isProfileInCooldown after the sibling run    → false
  refused run  → terminal.status "error", failure notice:
    "⚠️ This request was refused before it reached the AI service, so your sign-in still works.
     Start a fresh request with /new, or ask a gateway administrator to update the model policy."
    and none of "Couldn't sign in" / "Sign in again" / "/login openai" appears in the history
  later run    → terminal.status "ok" with its ordinary reply,
                 never "is temporarily unavailable"
  app-server turn/start = 2 across one selected model (no profile rotation, no model fallback)

# same test, only the production repair reverted and the runtime rebuilt
  AssertionError: expected true to be false        ← the shared profile IS in cooldown
  refused run  → terminal.error:
    "⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes."
  Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 1 failed (1)
```

That red line is the issue's blast radius, measured rather than asserted: on base behaviour the refused run opens a cooldown window on the shared OAuth credential immediately, which is what every sibling agent then trips over. With the repair the same sequence leaves the profile usable and the next turn answers.

Two things worth flagging for whoever runs the lanes: this new e2e was missing from `scripts/lib/vitest-build-prerequisites.mts` in its first revision, so CI would not have given it a built runtime — it is registered now, alongside the other Codex product proofs. And the neighbouring `gateway-codex-refusal-product-proof.e2e.test.ts` fails on this base for a reason unrelated to this change: its expected `failureNotices` carry a provider category (`… (category: bio) …`) while the run produces the bare `"Your request couldn't be completed."`. The producer is `src/shared/assistant-error-format.ts:65`, which this branch never touches, and the same three cases fail with all of my fixture edits removed — recorded here rather than silently mixed into this PR's evidence. The shared auth fixture's own consumer still passes unchanged (`codex-auth-product-proof.e2e.test.ts` → `Tests 2 passed (2)`).

Gaps to name: no gap remains about the repair's red/green pair. With only the 11 production files reverted (tests left in place), every assertion this PR adds fails on base behaviour and passes once they are restored: runner regression `1 failed | 12 passed (13)` → `13 passed`; `src/agents/failover/` reason pin plus classifier matrix `2 failed | 33 passed (35)` → `35 passed`; fallback owner and chain stop `2 failed | 67 passed (69)` → `69 passed`; OpenAI-compatible envelope `1 failed | 24 passed (25)` → `25 passed`; and the Gateway-turn proof fails at base with `expected true to be false` on the shared profile's cooldown. One hop stays simulated: the Gateway-turn proof drives the refusal through the app-server protocol boundary using the message Codex's `UnexpectedResponseError` renders (`codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs`, source-verified and independently confirmed by the previous review), not by executing the Rust client itself, and no real operator credential is used anywhere in these runs. `pnpm check:changed` runs in CI because the local vitest router needs the pinned Bun download this sandbox cannot reach, and the pre-commit hook falls back to `oxfmt` for the same reason. The protocol since guard was pointed at the PR base explicitly (`PROTOCOL_SINCE_BASE_SHA=855d0b398a54…`) because the fork's stale `origin/main` is otherwise used as the comparison base. Finally, `mergeable` is `CONFLICTING` only because this branch sits several thousand commits behind `main` and nine `git fetch` attempts from this machine were each cut within the last few kilobytes of the response (`3518 bytes of body are still expected`), regardless of pack size — the conflict itself is narrow and mechanical. Recomputed against the live tip (`730e581f4b0`) with a 3-way merge, all six hand-written files this PR touches that `main` also changed merge cleanly with zero conflict markers (`message-patterns.ts`, `failover-error.ts`, `run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`, `classify.test.ts`, `model-fallback.chain-stop.test.ts`, `scripts/lib/vitest-build-prerequisites.mts`), and the only colliding path is the generated `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js`. So integrating `main` needs no hand resolution: merge, run `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`, commit the regenerated predicate. `main`'s changes to those files were also checked against this fix rather than assumed compatible — its narrowing of the credential `expired` pattern to `/(?<!deadline )expired/i` and the new `deadline expired` timeout pattern cannot capture the refusal copy (and the priority classifier runs before both lists), and the added `resolveEmbeddedAuthCooldownProbePolicy` only acts on profiles that already hold a cooldown, which this reason never records.

- **Loading state created by the published stable, on this build** — installed `openclaw@2026.10.10` from the registry into a throwaway prefix and let it write durable state in an isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` (config journal + `state/openclaw.sqlite`, per-agent SQLite, `client/credentials.sqlite`, and one cron row), then ran this build's runtime against that same directory:

```
published 2026.10.10 wrote   cron id 2a23535d-…  name existing-state-seed  everyMs 2700000
                             configRevision sha256:KKGdrD5T…2mAjA
this build, same directory   doctor --fix → maintenance + startup SQLite migrations
                             (.pre-startup-migration-*.bak, session-sqlite-migration-runs/*.json)
                             /healthz {"ok":true,"status":"live"}
                             /readyz  {"ready":true,"coreReady":true,"failing":[]}
                             cron list → same id, name, agentId, enabled, everyMs, payload kind,
                                         and an unchanged configRevision
control, fresh state         /readyz also ready
```

Two limits so this is not over-read. First, polling `/readyz` seconds after the port already answers `/healthz` returns 503; readiness completes shortly after, and the fresh-state control shows the same ordering, so that 503 is warm-up sequencing rather than a load failure. Second, this exercises loading and migrating existing stored data, not the packaged update lifecycle: no `openclaw update` install/replace and no managed-service restart is involved, so the container lane (`docker-upgrade-survivor`, `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/docker-e2e-lane.ts`) stays the authoritative version of that claim.

Correcting something I asserted earlier in this PR: I wrote that a host-side existing-state check was unavailable because the runtime-artifact guard blocks it. That was wrong — the guard only failed closed because I isolated state by overriding `HOME`, which stops it inspecting the local service. Using the repo's own `OPENCLAW_HOME` normalization, the check runs on the host.

## PR surface

The `size: XL` label on this PR is generated code, not review surface. Of `+3499/-3153` across 21 files, `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js` accounts for `+3155/-3153` by itself: the generator renumbers its internal check identifiers when the vocabulary grows, so adding one enum member rewrites the whole file. It was produced by `pnpm gateway:validators:gen` and verified by `pnpm validators:check`, never hand-edited. The reviewable part is `+41` production lines across 11 files and `+299` test lines across 8 files — which includes the 188-line Gateway-turn product proof — plus a 4-line `config/test-lines-allocations` record.

Regeneration is also the whole merge resolution, and the merge is now done. `main` @ `be881a7f8b1` (2796 commits) is merged into this branch, and the generated predicate was the only colliding path: the six hand-written files both sides touch (`message-patterns.ts`, `failover-error.ts`, `run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`, `classify.test.ts`, `model-fallback.chain-stop.test.ts`, `scripts/lib/vitest-build-prerequisites.mts`) auto-merged, and `3cee3643e13` publishes the regenerated output on top of main's numbering.

Because `build-artifacts` and the ratchets run on `refs/pull/191562/merge` — this head merged with whatever `main` is at that moment — the generated predicate can merge cleanly as text and still be stale as output. That was the first `build-artifacts` failure on this PR: `main` had advanced 25 commits, none of them under `packages/gateway-protocol/src`, and the merged tree no longer equalled the generator's bytes. Reproduced locally on that merge, fixed by regenerating against it (`23ba4def295`), and re-verified with `validators:check` + `protocol:check`. So regeneration is the last step before pushing, not a step that finishes once.


Integration also caught one stale assertion, which is the point of landing on a current base: `main` added a `model_fallback_chain_stopped` record for local coordination stops (`src/agents/model-fallback-runner.ts:597`), so the chain-stop case now pins that stop event and its `local_runtime_coordination` reason instead of asserting an empty record list. The behavior the case proves is unchanged and was re-verified on the merged base: the refusal rejects with the original error, `run` is called once, no fallback step fires, and no candidate is consumed. Re-ran green on the merge: `validators:check`, `protocol:check`, `tsgo:core:test`, the touched agent/gateway suites, and the Gateway refusal proof above (real build, `Tests 1 passed (1)` in 31s).

Two contributor-side items from the review are now also closed: the redundant helper-level refusal case in `src/agents/failover-error.test.ts` was removed as suggested (its classification, chain-stop and HTTP-status assertions are each pinned at their own owner boundary, and `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` is only a wrapper over the chain resolution), and the cooldown assertion reads the store's own predicate.

## Remaining Gates

For a quick pass, in order of cost:

1. **Approve** — post `/allow-security-sensitive-change` for head `23ba4def295`. Every push resets this approval, so it has to be keyed to whatever head you land.
2. **Decide** — the recorded `Decision needed`: whether `session_authority` joins the closed failover vocabulary. The review's own recommendation is to approve the additive reason, and the compatibility evidence is above.
3. **CI** — settled on `23ba4def295`: 99 succeeded, 58 skipped, and one lane red for the runner rather than the tree. `android-access-native (16384, google_apis_ps16k)` exhausted the disk while unzipping the 16 KB page-size system image (`You are running out of disk space … Free space left: 0 MB`, then `No space left on device`) before any instrumentation ran, and its `(4096, google_apis)` sibling passed on the same head; `openclaw/ci-gate` mirrors that single job. The two lanes that were genuinely red on the previous head — `build-artifacts` (generated predicate stale against a `main` that had moved again) and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` — are both green here.

Checked whether that red can block you: it cannot. The `16384/ps16k` variant is **skipped** on other recently landed PRs and never reports on `main` push commits, and `openclaw/ci-gate` is not a required status check either — PR #192499 landed with `openclaw/ci-gate` red on its merge commit. So this lane needs a re-run by someone with write access to be green, not a code change from me; nothing about it reflects the tree.
4. **Optional** — `pnpm test:docker:published-upgrade-survivor` to cover the packaged update lifecycle, which the host-side checks deliberately do not claim.

As of the latest recorded review (re-keyed to `23ba4def295`), evidence is not the constraint and neither is code: proof confidence is graded 🦞 diamond lobster ("Sufficient (terminal)"), patch quality 🦞 diamond lobster with **no actionable findings and no remaining rank-up moves**, and overall readiness is held at 🦐 only by owner direction on the public vocabulary — the review states that in two places, so the sub-scores cannot lift it on their own. The two items that remain are maintainer-only: the security-sensitive approval for `23ba4def295` (any push resets it) and the recorded `Decision needed` on adding a member to the closed failover vocabulary, for which the review's own recommendation is to approve the additive reason. This section is kept as a record of what was produced locally and what a container would still add, not as a claim that more evidence is required.

Currency check, re-run on the tip this branch now carries: `main` @ `be881a7f8b1` still has no competing repair — `session_authority` appears 0 times there, `message-patterns.ts`, `packages/gateway-protocol/src/failover-reasons.ts` and `run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` carry no local-refusal handling, and the only occurrence of the refusal copy on `main` is the relay that emits it (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-dispatch.ts`), which is exactly the side core misreads. So the misclassification was still live on `main` up to the commit this branch merged, and this PR remains the only fix.

Hook integrity was checked pre-merge against `df9d3240e52` because CI could not run while the branch was unmerged; the merge makes that reasoning moot and the live code is now the evidence. Between the old base and `be881a7f8b1` exactly one commit touched the classifier files this repair hangs off (`7e4bdf2f607`, provider deadline timeouts reported as auth failures), and after the merge the classification still resolves the refusal prose to `session_authority` (`classify.test.ts`), the profile policy still skips the health write (`run.harness-auth-failover.test.ts`), and the Gateway proof still shows the shared profile serving the next turn.

The one stronger form not reproducible on this host:

- **Latest-stable upgrade with existing state** — `pnpm test:docker:published-upgrade-survivor` with `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_BASELINE_SPECS="openclaw@2026.10.10 openclaw@2026.9.36"` (current `latest` and `extended-stable` from the registry) against this PR's candidate package; Package Acceptance resolves the same lane from `source=ref`, and the QA Lab scenario id is `docker-upgrade-survivor` (`qa/scenarios/runtime/docker-upgrade-survivor.yaml`, script `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/docker-e2e-lane.ts`). Checked before writing this: every existing-state upgrade scenario the repo ships (`docker-upgrade-survivor`, `docker-release-upgrade-user-journey`, `docker-update-channel-switch`, `docker-update-migration`, `docker-update-restart-auth`) routes through `docker-e2e-lane.ts`, so there is no host-runner equivalent to substitute — this is the one gate that genuinely needs a container or a runner rather than more local evidence. That is the check that a pre-existing install still loads its stored cron, auth-profile and session state after moving onto this build. The additive-vocabulary probe above shows existing reason values still validate, but it is not the upgrade run the review asked for.

Correction worth recording: the Gateway-turn gate did **not** need a container. It runs on the host through the shipped QA product harness (`test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts`, `--runner host` semantics), and the earlier claim that this sandbox could not exercise a Gateway turn was wrong. The survivor lane genuinely is container-only (`scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh` hands off to `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/run.sh` inside the harness image) and this machine has no running Docker daemon; starting one, or using a credentialed remote runner, is a host-level action that needs the operator's go-ahead, and remote execution is maintainer-authorized. I still tried the host route today, and it stops on a guard that should not be bypassed: published `openclaw@2026.10.10`, run in an isolated `HOME` on its own port, created real durable state (a seeded cron row, canonical `state/openclaw.sqlite`, per-agent SQLite, config journal), and this branch's CLI then refuses to load it with `UpdatePreMutationError: Runtime artifacts changed, but the affected Gateway is running or its offline state could not be verified`, because the machine has a LaunchAgent-managed Gateway. That refusal is correct behavior on a live install, so the existing-state upgrade check needs a container or a runner without a live service rather than a workaround. One ordering detail matters for whoever runs it: until `main` is integrated, this branch's own version reads `2026.10.9`, which predates the `2026.10.10` stable baseline, so a meaningful upgrade run has to follow the merge rather than precede it. Integration is complete, and the blocker was local configuration rather than the link: this machine's global `http.lowSpeedLimit=1` aborted the fetch during the v0 full-ref advertisement ("expected flush after ref listing"), which is what the earlier failures looked like. `git -c protocol.version=2 -c http.lowSpeedLimit=0 fetch` pulled the whole pack at 9-11 MB/s. The merge itself was one generated file plus `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`, and the branch version now reads `2026.10.10`, so a survivor run pairs a published `openclaw@2026.9.36` baseline against this build rather than treating `2026.10.10` as the newer side.
