prs.title: feat(clawrouter): generate Wan videos from qualified catalog offers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter's granted Wan video offers cannot reach the existing `video_generate` consumer. Video runtime errors can also trigger another provider after a possibly paid creation attempt.

## User Impact

Users with a fresh, eligible `alibaba/wan2.6-t2v` offer can use the existing video tool through their proxy credential. Caller cancellation stops observation, and uncertain creation or unusable output stops automatic paid replay. This draft is protocol support, not a live activation or Worker parity claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register one video adapter and live catalog provider through existing SDK contracts. Reuse the native Wan input/parameter serializer, URL extractor, bounded HTTP/polling owners and existing fallback-stop marker. Native and manifest creation preserve the selected provider/model; subsequent GET requests bind the same origin, credential, original task and returned job selector. Reference assets and undeclared controls remain closed.

Wan's qualified result is one opaque HTTPS attachment. The adapter never downloads an output URL or forwards proxy credentials to it; authenticated router file URLs require a separately qualified file operation. Unknown observations stop polling. Cancellation or missing delivery does not prove remote termination or a refund; unknown pricing stays unknown.

Stack: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192276 at `22113462220de730990802ebeb5e4c9d9a061124`. Router contract: https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/483, landed `194837dc617a53266e3fe319a287418a56cffcd5`.

## Evidence

- Source candidate: `99c214adce13e6906cec209eb08a3549aeb695c9`.
- Static syntax, formatting, whitespace/privacy inspection, generated plugin inventory, SDK export-sync check and normal commit hooks passed. The initial hook selected an incompatible default dependency root; using the existing qualified native tooling root resolved that setup error without an install or bypass.
- Authored actual-host fixtures call `video_generate` with the real plugin registry, proxy catalog, sanitized HTTP server and a working alternate provider: native/manifest create-poll, original task/key isolation, cancellation before dispatch/headers/body/poll, malformed and bounded response handling, stale/foreign offer denials, catalog selection, and zero alternate calls after possible paid creation. Current corrected-head execution is pending; no actual-host pass is claimed.
- Local dependency execution is unqualified because the managed reuse guard refuses a nested workspace link. No install or new dependency lease. Prior386 build126316655211, production/extension types and SDK report126316656187 passed in41751008015 (report artifact13287871747). Agent-tool test types and lint identified missing explicit undefined apiKey, SDK import ordering and string-spread counting;3931a69d repairs these. Signed merge99c214ad additionally carries the published Lyria65191952 eligibility-lint correction. Current native PR-branch qualification: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41762448069 . No previous-head pass is promoted to current. No repeated old comparison or settled Wan native matrix.
- The 470-line allocation exactly matches new regression-test LF. The selected parent already exceeds its ceiling by 47 lines; that inherited debt is unchanged and is not padded into this allocation.
- Source-owner simplification keeps the smallest complete vertical slice: one frozen provider format with its real host boundaries. No new job framework, SDK subpath, credential resolver, copied Worker codec or cancellation/refund authority. Independent review is waived by explicit maintainer instruction; actual native gates remain required.

Release-note context: allow qualified ClawRouter Wan video offers in `video_generate`, preserving caller cancellation and preventing provider replay after uncertain creation. No deployment, paid request, model expansion or composed Worker proof.

Parent qualification update: the signed stack merge retains every Wan production, SDK, test and allocation blob from the original candidate. Only provider documentation gains the already-landed Vercel section. The canonical MCP import repair is now included before the first hosted validation; this is not a new video feature or a prior-report rerun.

Exact current99c214adce13e6906cec209eb08a3549aeb695c9 actual-host receipt: run41762448069/job126353565694 passes all25 Node +25 Bun cases in src/agents/tools/video-generate-clawrouter.test.ts. These exercise registered video_generate native/manifest create and original-job polling, fresh offer denial/catalog registration, proxy-key isolation, caller cancellation at before/headers/body/poll, one-attempt post-dispatch failures and a working pre-egress alternate-provider control. Production/all test types and owned lint pass. SDK report126353565727 cancelled after30m27s with complete annotations identifying the explicit30-minute deadline and operation cancellation; no report artifact was produced. build-artifacts is skipped in this PR-shaped run (the earlier386 build is separately recorded). The composed Worker/SQLite acceptance belongs to integration and is not claimed here. Current aggregate CI still fails baseline/Knip, common speech/profile and catalog discovery deadlines, plus UI gateway job126353565437 refusing worktree allocation with3.6GiB available against4.0GiB required. No blind retry, infrastructure mutation or current SDK-pass claim.

prs.title: feat(clawrouter): generate Lyria music through qualified proxy offers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot consume qualified ClawRouter Lyria music offers, and its music fallback loop can buy another provider attempt after an unusable dispatched response.

## User Impact

Adds the existing music_generate path for the two frozen Lyria offers when the current proxy-key catalog grants the exact native or manifest transport. Caller cancellation reaches generation, response reading and delivery; an uncertain dispatched attempt stops automatic fallback. This does not establish live availability or refund a completed upstream operation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shares the native Google prompt/lyrics/inline-image serializer and asset conversion through the existing music-generation SDK barrel. Direct Google keeps its credential resolution, base64 normalization and retry behavior, except that an abort prevents retry. The proxy uses only its selected ClawRouter credential, bounded complete JSON/audio, and the existing fallback-stop marker.

Parent https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192052 landed as `d65390bcf36b818b5018029cc00951799bebf0ed`. The supported native parent refresh produced published candidate `354e51977c3404de9a03f787c3a7d59fc3777fec`, now targeting main. Router contracts: landed https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/665 and https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/686, with declaration https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/716 at ff2715d727f27aea4e00b19b056e4207caf573c8. Deployment and composed actual-client/Worker qualification remain separate.

## Evidence

- Published corrected candidate: `cf0448492e14bfc66c87693d6ef902e86909562e`, through the retained native proof-publication route. Relative to `6519195293ca0b97c1571ac63c7cb1f9dd84a7e9`, it captures the intended cancellation Error before calling the native Google provider and asserts that same object. prs.title: fix(android): match Control UI page scheme to the gateway socket
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A discovered gateway on a non-loopback address opens a TLS socket even when its Bonjour record omits `gatewayTls`. The Android Control UI page did not use that decision. It chose `http` or `https` only from `endpoint.tlsEnabled`, so the page stayed on cleartext while the socket was TLS.

The Terminal, dashboard, and desktop screens load that page after the operator session connects. The page origin is where the signing bridge answers a challenge. A cleartext page is the wrong origin for a connection the socket policy already refused to leave on cleartext.

Manual LAN cleartext is unchanged. A stored pin still does not upgrade that page to HTTPS, matching the socket. A manual remote host whose cleartext toggle is off stays on HTTPS, also matching the socket.

## Evidence

API 34 emulator, play debug build, head `8f4143070ae`. The production `ControlUiWebView` loaded a page on the emulator's private LAN address `10.0.2.15`. The discovered endpoint had `tlsEnabled` false and no advertised fingerprint. The manual endpoint used the cleartext toggle.

```console
$ adb -s emulator-5554 shell am instrument -w -r -e class ai.openclaw.app.ui.ControlUiSchemeDeviceTest ai.openclaw.app.debug.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner
OK (2 tests)

url=https://10.0.2.15:36997
page=https://10.0.2.15:36997/ wss://10.0.2.15:36997 NATIVE_AUTH

url=http://10.0.2.15:34079
page=http://10.0.2.15:34079/ ws://10.0.2.15:34079 NATIVE_AUTH
```

![Discovered LAN page loaded over HTTPS and installed native auth](https://github.com/SebTardif/openclaw/raw/8f4143070ae6055df10f80e3928f0451d0d38978/apps/android/app/src/androidTest/proof/https-discovered.png)

![Manual LAN cleartext page stayed on HTTP](https://github.com/SebTardif/openclaw/raw/8f4143070ae6055df10f80e3928f0451d0d38978/apps/android/app/src/androidTest/proof/http-manual-lan.png)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The Control UI WebView origin follows the socket. A discovered private-LAN host with no gatewayTls advertisement loads HTTPS, and the native auth bridge publishes a wss gateway URL. Manual private-LAN cleartext stays HTTP and publishes a ws URL.
- **Real environment tested:** Android emulator API 34 google_apis arm64, play debug app `ai.openclaw.app.debug`, head `8f4143070ae`. The page host is the emulator guest address 10.0.2.15.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Installed the play debug apk and ran `adb -s emulator-5554 shell am instrument -w -r -e class ai.openclaw.app.ui.ControlUiSchemeDeviceTest ai.openclaw.app.debug.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The WebView document and the screenshots above. Discovered LAN showed `https://10.0.2.15:36997/` plus `wss://10.0.2.15:36997` and `NATIVE_AUTH`. Manual LAN showed `http://10.0.2.15:34079/` plus `ws://10.0.2.15:34079` and `NATIVE_AUTH`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The production WebView loaded the HTTPS page for the discovered case and the HTTP page for manual cleartext. Both documents received the native auth payload for that origin.
- **What was not tested:** A physical phone. This was not a full OpenClaw gateway login. The page is a local document served to the production WebView so the loaded scheme and the installed auth bridge are visible.

## Summary

The page URL is built from the same TLS decision as the gateway socket. No changelog entry.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`redactSnapshot` was masking every `storage.encryption` string that looked sensitive, even when the value is ordinary encryption configuration rather than a credential. That hid useful diagnostics in config snapshots and made support harder.

This patch only redacts a candidate string when the value is concrete-sensitive **and** the key is either marked sensitive by a hint or sits on a sensitive path, so genuine credentials stay masked while harmless configuration remains readable. Ref #176229.

## Evidence

- Traced `redactValue()` through the config snapshot path: `storage.encryption` values without a sensitive hint or sensitive path now pass through unchanged, while hint-marked values still resolve to `[REDACTED]`.
- The existing config tests and lint/typecheck jobs pass on this revision; the change is limited to the redaction predicate.

prs.title: fix(matrix): show reasoning when explicitly enabled
prs.body:
Related: #81892

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes completed model reasoning being silently suppressed on Matrix after an authorized user enables it, including queued followups, while preventing model-inferred defaults from disclosing reasoning without an explicit preference.

## User Impact

Authorized, explicitly enabled reasoning appears as quiet `m.notice` messages with empty mentions. Missing, off or stream preferences do not grant completed-reasoning display. Ordinary answers continue normally. Committed off changes and lost source-turn authority suppress unsent reasoning.

The optional SDK visibility reader, reply opt-in and outbound capability still require maintainer acceptance of the public contract. There is no persisted schema, dependency or operator configuration migration. Streaming reasoning is outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

One producing-turn policy follows direct dispatch, native queue custody and the final Matrix SDK handoff. It accepts explicit inline/session/agent/global choices separately from model execution defaults. Existing session identity, revision, cancellation, revocation and writer checks remain in force. Guarded reasoning stays live-only and outside replayable outbound intents and ordinary confirmed-history callbacks; previews and ordinary answers retain their owners.

The latest repair fixes the review's explicit-opt-in finding using the existing visibility owner. It changes two production files (+11/-4); the whole PR is the completed explicit-on Matrix feature across direct and queued paths. No second policy owner, persistence manager or test-only production hook is added.

## Evidence

Exact candidate: `7e6a350b4b787cc6ea0d6e0cfafffee34d718747`, reviewed against `72e8e42210d1bf5f69d0384c84baec0188743337`.

**Explicit-choice regression, through the actual built Gateway, agent, model fallback, installed Matrix SDK and final HTTP:** a fresh session has no inline or persisted reasoning/thinking preference. The primary MiniMax M2.7 request returns model-not-found over HTTP; normal fallback executes M3.1 Flash with its supported thinking level. The external model and homeserver are synthetic fixtures.

| Configuration | Parent `5ee9ba03` reasoning / answer HTTP | Candidate `7e6a350b` reasoning / answer HTTP |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| No reasoning preference | 1 / 1 (reproduced defect) | 0 / 1 |
| Global `reasoningDefault: "on"` | — | 1 / 1 |
| Global off, agent `reasoningDefault: "on"` | — | 1 / 1 |

The direct M2.7/off route alone did not reproduce disclosure because another producer guard suppressed reasoning. The fallback route above does reproduce it; no provider resolver, execution default or fallback behavior was changed to manufacture the result.

**Queued behavior rerun on the same candidate:** public Matrix `/status` observed depth 0→1 behind a held model request before each queued turn began.

| Queued turn | Reasoning HTTP | Ordinary answer HTTP |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Authorized, explicitly enabled | 1 quiet notice | 1 |
| Reasoning disabled before releasing the held turn | 0 | 1 |
| Sender without command authority | 0 | 1 |

The off change committed before release and before the queued model request. Returned ordinary source-history text excludes reasoning markers; native structured thinking remains in the model transcript.

All four executions (three configuration controls and one three-scenario queue run) used public `channels.stop`, a verified stopped Matrix runtime and at least 112 seconds of HTTP quiet to retire existing SDK deadlines. Documented host stdin EOF then produced natural Gateway exit 0 and a clean receipt, without forced termination, warnings, residual owned descendants or unjoined fixture threads. This qualifies staged teardown; direct whole-Gateway cancellation of referenced SDK timeout handles remains unqualified.

**Focused checks and review:**

- The absent-preference owner regression failed on the parent (1 failed / 24 passed) and passes on the candidate. Current suites: visibility owner 25, producer 4, plugin reader 1 and model-level resolver 4 tests passed.
- Formatting, typed lint, core and affected messaging/plugin test type graphs, and exact-base line-cap, test-growth and mock-export checks passed. The dedicated test allocation is 2220, matching net test growth; the shared scalar is unchanged. Checks executed on the identical staged source tree, then byte hashes were checked against the clean commit before reuse.
- The clean committed CLI bundle built through the supported declaration-skip option. Runtime provenance checks bind the bundle's input signature, tree and commit. This is not a full release/package/declaration build.
- An independent Codex source review inspected the complete 75-file committed diff and relevant owners: no actionable correctness finding. This source-only review does not certify runtime, CI or maintainer approval. Canonical diff SHA-256: `267fbbe15caed1b272a8c8f9034449bc9a33837ecf14303d91c79e09fa5ba6f4`.
- Changed-file wall times, including worker compilation: owner 175.9s, producer 203.6s, plugin reader 177.2s. Resolver regression: 166.1s. Hosted CI details for this exact head are recorded below.

**Remaining boundaries:** the original broad queue driver still reports `PARTIAL_PROOF` / exit 2 for supplementary cross-destination history; a separate qualifier preserves that result and qualifies only the three retained-queue-to-HTTP scenarios and clean teardown. Ordinary source-history exclusion does not establish positive durable answer persistence in a different destination. These fixtures do not qualify a live tenant, E2EE or a real inference service. Maintainer SDK acceptance, hosted CI and review labels remain separate.


**Hosted review inspected at closeout:** [ClawSweeper revision 22](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149906#issuecomment-5694770506), reviewed at 2026-11-04 03:08 UTC on `7e6a350b`, reports no actionable code or security findings, sufficient bounded behavior proof (5/6), and complete fix scope. Acceptance of the public visibility reader, reply opt-in and outbound capability remains an explicit maintainer decision. No merge approval is claimed.

[CI run 41762256595](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41762256595) completed on merge `95093b3b` into main `73591122`: 69 jobs succeeded, 27 were skipped, and 3 failed. prs.title: feat(cron): skip scheduled runs when a shell precheck finds no work
prs.body:
Supersedes #171738 and links the closed replay #112375. ## What Problem This Solves Scheduled jobs that poll for work still start a model turn when the inbox, queue, or watch target is empty. This supersedes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171738 and replaces the closed replay of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/112375. Those branches targeted the previous cron store and could not be applied to current main. This branch is based on current `openclaw/openclaw` main (`7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`). ## User Impact User impact: an operator can attach a host shell precheck to an `at`, `every`, or `cron` job. Exit code 0 continues into the trigger and payload. Exit code 2 records a skipped run with summary `precheck-no-work` and does not start the model turn. Denied, unapproved, timed out, or unexpected results fail closed and skip the payload. Agent turns cannot create or edit the command. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/schedules#shell-precheck ## Why This Change Was Made Current cron jobs live in SQLite `job_json`, with validation in the cron service and execution in `executeJobCore`. The precheck is an optional field on that job, not a new config key or schema version. The probe runs through `createExecTool` with `nonInteractiveApproval` and no host-approval bypass, then the existing gateway allowlist and approval floors. `cron.triggers.enabled: false` disables it. Forced manual runs still run the probe; they do not skip it the way they skip a condition script. ## Evidence Local validation on `7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5`: - `pnpm test src/cron/job-precheck.test.ts src/cron/job-precheck-run.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.precheck.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.occurrence.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-precheck.test.ts` — passed. Cron shard: 4 files, 86 tests. CLI shard: 1 file, 3 tests. The exec-policy file proves a marker file is not created when security is deny, ask is always, the job pin requires ask always, `toolsAllow` excludes exec, or run authority is rejected. An allowed `full`/`off` policy covers exit 2 (no work) and exit 0 (work). - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed TypeScript files — passed. - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the 29 changed files — all matched files use the correct format. - `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed. - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-services-cron.tsbuildinfo` — passed. ## Security review ### Threat model A precheck is an unattended host command. The realistic attackers are a model turn that tries to persist one, an operator who saved a command and later tightened exec policy, and a forced or restarted run that might otherwise skip the gate. The command can do anything the exec tool would allow, including reading or writing files on the gateway host. The feature must not add a second spawn path with weaker defaults. ### How approvals are enforced - The runner calls `createExecTool` with the resolved `tools.exec` host, mode, security, and ask, plus the live exec-approvals file that the tool already re-reads. It does not pass `bypassHostApprovalFloors`. - `nonInteractiveApproval: true` makes approval-requiring commands return `approval_required` before spawn. `ask: "always"`, an allowlist miss, and `security: "deny"` therefore do not run the command. - A stored `toolsAllowExecTarget` pin is applied with `pinExecToolTarget`, so a creator floor of `ask: "always"` still denies a headless run when global policy is `full`/`off`. - A defined `toolsAllow` that does not include `exec` denies the probe before the tool is built. - `assertRunCurrent` is awaited in `executeJobCore` and again inside the runner immediately before `tool.execute`. A rejected run does not spawn. - If the gateway does not wire `runJobPrecheck`, or `cron.triggers.enabled` is false, the job errors and the payload does not start. - Agent creates and patches that set a non-null `precheck` are rejected in the automations tool and again in `assertCronModelJobAllowed`. Clearing the field is allowed. `cron.run` of an existing job is not treated as authoring. - Invalid persisted prechecks quarantine the row instead of being dropped, so a bad write cannot fall open into an unguarded payload. - Each run re-reads current policy. A command saved under a looser policy is denied after the operator tightens it. ### Residual risks - Command payloads (`runCronCommandJob`) still spawn from their own runner and do not use this exec-tool gate. That path is unchanged. - Operators who can already persist command jobs can persist a precheck through the CLI or Gateway API. The protection is the run-time policy check, not a second save-time approval dialog. Reusing the stream approval dialog would describe the wrong effect. - `mode: "auto"` remains the existing exec auto-review path. With `nonInteractiveApproval`, a reviewer that approves can still allow a spawn. Tests pin `mode: "full"` so they do not depend on a reviewer. This change does not weaken or special-case auto-review. - When config omits security, the exec tool keeps its own non-sandbox default and the approvals file still applies its floors. That is the same default as other exec callers. - Exit codes are the only work signal. A command that prints a success banner and exits 2 is no-work. A command that exits 0 after doing nothing is work. Overlapping codes are rejected. - The probe runs on the exec host selected by `tools.exec` unless a gateway pin forces the gateway host. It cannot target a node or sandbox that the exec tool itself would refuse.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Introduces unattended host command execution on the gateway before scheduled agent turns, gated by exec policy but still a security-sensitive automation surface. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). Updated by merging current upstream main (merge commit `ce9c3641f4`); the precheck, occurrence and CLI cron tests (89 tests) and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass on the merged head.

prs.title: fix(agents): subagent results never reach the parent while a sibling waits for its reply
prs.body:
Closes #164334
Related: #164241, #158603, #161114

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a finished subagent's result never reaches its parent when another child in the same yielded batch has paused with `sessions_yield` `waitFor: "message"` and its pause notice was already delivered.

## User Impact

A parent that receives a child's "paused awaiting continuation" notice now still gets its other children's results as they finish, whether or not it has sent that continuation yet. The paused child's own result arrives separately after it resumes. Previously the parent stayed idle with zero wake attempts, even though `sessions_yield` had just told it the sibling's completion "will arrive as a later turn". In the reported case, that lasted about six hours until a human sent a message.

Plain `sessions_yield` pauses without a notice keep their existing one-combined-delivery behavior. There is no config, schema or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A consumed pause notice hands the paused child's continuation to its requester. The child still sat in its frozen yield batch, and the batch waits for every member. The paused child was waiting for its requester, and the requester was waiting for the batch.

Consuming the notice now detaches that child into its own completion wave (`batchRunIds: [self]`), keeping its own completion custody. Frozen batch membership is mutual: wave selection, the wave's descendant scope and kernel outcome settlement skip a member whose own batch no longer lists the settling run.

Requester cron/operator authority follows the split. A yield authority still covers only its original cohort, requester session, operator and rearm generation, but each detached wave of that cohort can use it. It is narrowed as waves settle and released after the last one. Settled operator rows keep their binding, so a stray retry fails closed exactly as `discard()` already requires. The cohort rules and frozen-wave selection moved into small sibling modules to stay within the line caps.

Known limit, unchanged by this PR: the in-memory requester final attachment is keyed by the cohort's original run IDs and is never remapped. Resuming a paused child already created a new run ID, so a cohort containing a message-wait pause could not match it before this change either.

## Hardening and authority boundaries

- Each detached wave retains the original operator, requester incarnation and frozen cohort generation; no newer authority is borrowed.
- Admitted turns retain their own lifecycle while earlier waves settle. Custody releases only after both scoped work and admitted delivery acknowledgements finish; original-source revocation still cuts it off immediately.
- Exact admitted-wave retries may retrieve the Gateway's cached result, but cannot create new input/execution if the cached outcome is missing.
- Operators without Cron-management entitlement receive lifecycle-only acceptance tracking, never a Cron capability or new permission.
- No persisted schema, config option, orchestration registry or live Gateway change.

## Evidence

Raw red/green excerpts, reproducible commands, SHA-256 bindings, postcommit build metadata, and proof limitations: [proof behind the proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164366#issuecomment-5974580321).

Reviewable immutable source: [Gateway admission regressions](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts), [receipt/lifecycle tests](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/agents/subagents/requester-cron-authority-cohort.test.ts), and [actual acceptance boundary](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.ts).

Exact candidate: `a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8`.

- **Real Gateway admission + SQLite proof:** `server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts` runs the public `agent` method through the actual Gateway handler, admission/actor identity and runtime stores. prs.title: fix(cli): load Unicode PowerShell completion files on Windows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PowerShell completion installation failing to load when the Windows state directory contains non-ASCII characters, and cached completion corrupting Unicode command choices in Windows PowerShell.

## User Impact

Windows PowerShell users can reload installed completion from Unicode paths and receive the original Unicode choices. Re-run the existing completion installation command to repair a previous profile. No configuration or migration is required. Existing UTF-16 profiles keep their encoding; ASCII and non-Windows output remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows PowerShell reads BOM-less script files as ANSI. Declare UTF-8 only when the existing profile/cache writer emits non-ASCII text. Keep profile preservation, atomic publication, and stdout generation with their existing owners.

## Evidence

Native Windows, Node 24.22.1, actual `powershell.exe` 5. The command-entry reproduction used `registerCompletionCli` with `completion --shell powershell --install --yes`, a real cache under a task-only `state ü 空` directory, and then dot-sourced the resulting profile. Paths below are redacted; no platform or filesystem mocks.

```text
BEFORE
profilePrefix: 23204f (no BOM)
powershell.exe: exit 1
CommandNotFoundException: the cache path is decoded incorrectly

AFTER
profilePrefix: efbbbf
powershell.exe: exit 0
{"major":5,"loaded":true}
stderr: ""
```

The committed regressions exercise actual PS5 file decoding for new/existing profiles and the real CLI cache writer with a bounded fixture command registry, then request completion through `CommandCompletion.CompleteInput`. Existing tests evaluated script strings directly and therefore missed file decoding.

- Unmodified owner: **3 failed, 16 passed, 3 existing POSIX-only skips**; the two Unicode-path cases fail on profile reload, and the cached choice is decoded incorrectly.
- Repaired owner: **19 passed, 3 unchanged skips** across both files; 12.10 s wall time, about 7.6 s native profile test time. Native PS5 processes are necessary to test its file decoder. GitHub’s incremental CI matrix skipped the Windows job; the native Windows/PowerShell results above are local.
- Targeted maintained production/test types, typed lint (four files), formatting and whitespace checks passed. Independent manual review and canonical complete five-file P0–P3 review: scoped-clean, zero findings; all six file/context hashes unchanged. The compatibility consumer suite had 19 passed, 1 failed, 10 skipped: its untouched Windows Bash/MSYS fixture fails identically on the clean base, with no added skip or weakened assertion. Full exact-head CI passed on `4088c2c3d5cc8c2ee08cf025999f14811cf30181` (run 40628894530). Native Windows timings above are local; GitHub CI timing is not presented as a measured before/after test-cost comparison.

<details>
<summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

The two existing file producers remain the owners. No new API, setting, dependency, shell invocation in production, or wrapper is introduced. One existing profile table gains two concrete filesystem-decoding cases; one CLI-writer regression protects Unicode cache contents. Distinct open completion PRs #173223 (quote escaping) and #162918 (option terminators) were inspected and do not repair file encoding.

</details>

prs.title: fix(test): retain selected Bun through isolation
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A launcher selects the pinned absolute Bun executable before isolating test HOME/cache. `pinnedBunEnv` carries only PATH, so a nested formatter resolves a new empty cache and stages the same runtime again. This was observed while qualifying https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186469: its existing dirty-to-formatted fixture entered the Bun stager and downloaded a second executable archive.

## Canonical fix

Carry the already-selected absolute executable in the existing `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH` provision. Keep relative CI `bun` PATH-only. The resolver, checksum/revision admission, explicit-override behavior, isolated HOME/cache and formatter policy remain owned by their existing modules. `test-live` already binds the selected local executable before changing child CI defaults; this applies the same ownership invariant to all callers of the shared provision.

Production +11/-6 (net +5), justified by preserving runtime identity across the child-environment ownership boundary; tests +25/-1 (net +24). Reuse existing cache-resolution cases and the two-route launcher proof; no extra child or test matrix. The cache case resolves under a different HOME/cache with only the provision and requires the original executable, no second stage and no isolated cache creation. The launcher child also retains its cache/exit/argument assertions. It already inherits an explicit path, so it is supporting integration proof rather than the discriminating regression.

## Prospective qualification rule — recorded before benchmark execution

- Real flow: reuse the committed `changed-lanes.test.ts` dirty-file to formatted-file check and its actual changed-plan → package script → `run-format` → formatter chain. Two formatter invocations per body; identical diagnostics, file selection and source bytes; dirty exits 1, formatted exits 0.
- Counts first: after local selection of a verified absolute Bun and before HOME/cache isolation, carry only the shared provision. Candidate must use that selected executable and perform zero additional staging/downloads against an empty isolated Bun cache. The existing injectable resolver fixture establishes the baseline extra-stage red case without a network download. Mock staging counts are resolver evidence, not formatter timing.
- Comparable timing: preseed both isolated caches from identical already-verified Bun bytes/stamps outside measurement. Warmup separately; five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs on the same host. Cold empty-cache behavior is reported separately, not timed as a failed baseline versus successful candidate.
- Record host load, wall/user/system CPU/peak RSS, median/p95/spread and exact output parity. Every measured metric must hold or improve; a 20% adverse move is an immediate stop, and smaller regressions require explicit acceptance. Otherwise retain the draft.
- Use only committed workloads, existing focused runner and existing dependency ownership. No new cache, fixture framework, benchmark service or paid box allocation.

## Observed qualification

At exact head `a94d7d5b31adddda7f496a708cb82b636e58235a`, the native physical checkout passed the frozen install and 114 tests across pinned-Bun, launcher, and dev-tool suites. The tooling-test typecheck, production and changed-test lint, targeted formatting, and the committed real dirty-to-formatted case also passed. That last run executed one selected test; 67 other tests were intentionally skipped.

A separate before/after resolver probe used the complete production owner with the existing injectable synthetic stager. Baseline selected a different executable and staged again after HOME/cache isolation; candidate retained the selected executable, performed zero additional stages, created no isolated cache, and left the parent environment unchanged. These are resolver work-count results, not network-download or formatter timing measurements.

Independent review of all five callers and local autoreview found no actionable code issue. The latest exact-head ClawSweeper review requested the formal qualification above and real-flow/performance evidence; performance evidence remains open.

The draft is retained because the promised alternating A/B performance comparison has not run. The unchanged committed case creates an unpredictable worker HOME and resets XDG_CACHE_HOME inside test setup. There is no existing independent Bun-cache selector or preseed seam, so outer-cache preparation cannot satisfy the prospective requirement to preseed both actual isolated caches outside timing. An independently owned baseline checkout can solve dependency availability, but cannot solve that cache-preparation constraint. No setup hook, runtime override after isolation, or fixture change will be introduced to manufacture a passing comparison.

No benchmark has run for this candidate. No ordinary Actions billing reduction is claimed: the relative workflow-provisioned `bun` path stays unchanged. Release-owned changelog; this is development/test runtime ownership.

prs.title: feat(pairing): pair a browser with a short code approved on the host
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A browser with no Gateway credential has no way to ask for one. It needs a pasted token, or a one-time link from `openclaw dashboard` carried over from the host. On a headless Gateway reached over SSH, both mean moving a secret by hand.

## User Impact

- A browser can pair with no token, link or host browser.
- New CLI command `openclaw pair <code>` and a new public route, both documented in `/cli/pair` and `/web/control-ui/connect-and-pair`.
- When `gateway.roles` is configured, bootstrap connections need a verified identity, so code pairing is refused there the same way `openclaw dashboard` links are.
- **Known low-impact limit:** a network client rotating its source address can keep the 32-row pending table full, so other browsers see "Too many pairing requests". One address holds only about half the table under the default rate limit; holding it full takes two or three. State stays bounded, nobody can replace or remove another browser's request, no credential is exposed, and token and `openclaw dashboard` sign-in keep working. A per-source allowance would raise the cost if this ever matters in practice.
- On a plain `http://` address, anyone on that network can read Gateway traffic after pairing, as with any plain-HTTP Control UI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Device-code pairing for the Control UI:

1. The login gate's sign-in card gains a **Pair with a code instead** link. It opens a second card that holds only pairing: **Get a code** shows the command `openclaw pair ABCD-EFGH` and a Browser ID while the browser waits, and **Sign in with URL and secret** goes back. The URL and secret sign-in is unchanged.

   ![Sign-in card with code pairing link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0598b57-272f-4ea4-9d85-4c476a42c6e4)

   ![Pairing card waiting with command and Browser ID](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f421e08d-c6a2-4cb1-807c-b0885c26c1aa)

   ![Pairing card waiting at phone width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d572f64c-71da-4a82-891a-edd473332bf0)

2. On the host, over SSH if needed, `openclaw pair` shows who is asking and waits for an answer.

   ```text
   A browser is asking for full administrator access to this Gateway.

     Code                34EL-ZNRU
     Browser (reported)  Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7) ... Safari/605.1.15
     Address             127.0.0.1
     Page (reported)     http://127.0.0.1:18789
     Browser ID          e2de4320
     Requested           just now

   Approve only if you opened this page yourself and it shows this code and Browser ID.
   If someone sent you this code or command, answer no: approving gives their browser full control of this Gateway.
   Approve this browser? [y/N]
   ```

3. The waiting browser connects by itself.

   ![Control UI connected with full access after approval](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6952e4cd-4691-4d4f-81c0-fe40e85439ac)

### How it works

- `POST <base>/__openclaw__/browser-pair/start` is public, same-origin and rate limited. It takes a signature from the browser's device key and files one row in a new `device_pairing_browser_requests` table, returning a request ID and an eight-character code.
- `device.pair.code` requires `operator.admin`. With `code` it returns the request. With `requestId` and `decision` it settles exactly that request. Approval issues the existing Control UI owner bootstrap token, pre-bound to the request's key.
- `POST .../collect` returns the decision only to a signature from the requesting key. The browser then connects through the existing bootstrap path, which creates the paired device with `approvedVia: bootstrap`.
- Each attempt belongs to the Gateway it started on. Going back to the sign-in card or a changed Gateway target ends the attempt, and an approval is only ever connected to the Gateway that issued it.

### Security properties

- The code names a request and is not a bearer secret.
- The collected token only works with the requesting key. A stranger presenting it is refused.
- Requests expire after ten minutes. At most 32 are pending, and each source's filing is limited by the Gateway's auth rate limit.
- The route uses the Gateway's browser origin policy, including the check that a loopback page came from a loopback socket. This stops other sites filing requests from a visitor's browser. It is not a network boundary: authority comes from host approval and the key proof.
- `Browser` and `Page` are marked `(reported)` in the prompt because the requester chooses them. `Address` is what the Gateway saw, and the code and Browser ID are what the operator matches against the page.
- The token column is covered by the secret-table policy, so redacted backups omit the table.
- Without a terminal the CLI approves nothing unless `--yes` is passed. The page never suggests `--yes`.

### Decisions for review

- **Separate table, not the pending-device list.** The route is unauthenticated, so its input stays out of the list operators approve from, including `openclaw devices approve --latest`. These requests therefore do not appear in `openclaw devices list` or the Devices page.
- **Approval grants the owner profile.** It matches `openclaw dashboard`, and it is why the method needs `operator.admin` rather than `operator.pairing`.
- **One additive protocol method and one additive lazy table.** No protocol version change.
- **Test-line allocation.** `config/test-lines-allocations/browser-pair-code.txt` covers the 731 net test lines this PR adds. The tests were consolidated first, from 1,076 lines; each remaining case fails when the check it guards is disabled, so cutting further would remove coverage.

`src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts` is at its 700-line cap on main, so this PR's one `device.pair.code` row makes 701. Should the cap go up, or should the table be split?

## Evidence

Tests: 25 new gateway, worker and CLI cases plus 14 UI cases pass, with consumer suites for login gate, secret tables, method registry, CLI registration, Git backup and the Postgres schema generators. Full suite not run. Each security check was disabled in turn (key binding, collect key match, signature, origin, loopback socket check, inspect and approve expiry, inspected-request match, rate limit) and a test failed every time.

Independent review: a separate reviewer attacked the route, the approval method and the token binding with nine probes against a real Gateway, and found no way to obtain a credential without host access or `operator.admin`.

Authority at the final effect, checked against the request row and the bootstrap token table on a real Gateway:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Caller with `operator.pairing`, `operator.read` or `operator.write` | Refused, nothing issued, request still pending |
| Administrator revoked while the approval is queued | Refused, nothing issued; with the request authority removed, the same test issues a token |
| Authority lost at any check inside the approval | Transaction rolled back, nothing issued, no paired device |
| Revoked bootstrap credential presented with the right key | Connection refused, no paired device; without the revocation, the same test connects |

Live run: packaged build installed in a clean macOS VM, Safari in the guest, `openclaw pair` over SSH from outside the guest.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Wrong code | Refused: `No browser is waiting for this code.` |
| Code after its real ten minutes | Refused: `This code has expired.` |
| No terminal | Details printed, nothing approved |
| Answered no | Browser shows it was declined |
| Answered yes | Browser connects, stays connected after reload |
| Plain `http://` LAN address | Browser connects |

Not covered: a browser on a different machine from the Gateway, trusted-proxy and Tailscale Serve deployments, the Postgres state engine, an upgrade from the latest stable release, and translated strings, which `control-ui-locale-refresh` adds. The `(reported)` labels, the loopback socket check and Gateway target handling have test coverage but were not part of the live run.

Related: #159660, #120768

prs.title: fix(talk): preserve spaces after Unicode transcript overlaps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streamed Talk user captions lose the space after an overlapping word whose lowercase form expands, such as `İstanbul`. The existing owner matches lowercase overlaps but used the folded offset to slice the original string.

## User Impact

During interim overlapping captions, users see `Meet in İstanbul tomorrow` instead of `Meet in İstanbultomorrow`. NBSP, ideographic and thin-space separators are preserved exactly too. Authoritative full final transcripts and assistant verbatim fragments retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration required.

## Changes

Preserves ben.li / @ly85206559's original commit. Map the matched lowercase overlap length back to the incoming string's original code-point boundary before its existing UTF-16 slice. Keep the existing comparison/merge policy; no new normalization, SDK exports or startup imports. Related invariant: #190196.

The module remains in the existing lazy Talk runtime. **Production+12, tests−6**, no allocation; useful regression cases consolidated in the existing suites.

## Evidence

**Asset-budget gate ran first and passed** on exact candidate `046ec4cd58329ddc5e128d1d974ce823ace265dc` versus frozen main `befd729208b6db1780d59cf4b29c5b70679bf7ad`, with the canonical differential command and one toolchain: chat-boot gzip **−166B**, startup gzip **−1B**, new-route gzip−46B, CSS growth0B. No baseline, budget, allowance or bundling changes. These compressed-byte differences are measurements, not a performance-optimization claim.

Then normally built Gateway serving normally built Control UI, real Linux Chromium, **Start voice input**, real Gateway Talk relay and real OpenAI-compatible realtime adapter against a local WebSocket provider fixture. Main twice loses U+00A0/U+3000/U+2009 after `İstanbul`; candidate twice retains the exact code points. ASCII overlap and per-character assistant punctuation controls pass in all4 runs. No mocked Gateway, direct conversation helper call, live provider key or live speech-recognition claim.

Conversation unit19/19 and selected existing overlap E2E2/2 pass; formatting/lint pass. Same committed unit tests on main fail only the dotted-I overlap (1fail/18pass). Detailed public wire/DOM/budget receipt and inspected before/after screenshots are in the proof comment below.


Detailed proof and all three Unicode before/after pairs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192484#issuecomment-6622089230

### Before
![Main loses the NBSP after İstanbul](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32c05a16-4baf-43bc-bdbf-6b2b04315a4d)

### After
![Candidate preserves the NBSP in the Talk caption](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ded9428c-1287-4cba-bf3c-332abc33c253)

## Risk and rollback

Two-way door: revert restores the former browser-local merge behavior; no persisted format/schema change. Blast radius is interim Talk user transcript overlap slicing. ASCII overlap, punctuation, assistant transcript handling and authoritative finals remain unchanged.

prs.title: feat(ios): filter sessions by attention and work
prs.body:
Related: #162814

## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, finding conversations waiting for an answer or approval requires checking individual session rows.

## User Impact

Sessions gains All, Needs you, and Working filters with conversation counts for the selected Gateway, agent, and existing status scope. One conversation counts once even when it has multiple requests. Working includes active or queued runs and active child work; it can overlap Needs you. Request badges reuse the existing native preview and approval flow.

All preserves offline browsing. Live activity filters are disabled while disconnected, and incomplete rosters retain a + count qualifier.

This is a draft for the initial iOS design review. Physical Duo and VoiceOver checks remain before readiness. Android parity is a separate follow-up using the same filter meanings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Sessions screen consumes the existing live roster instead of keeping a second nonarchived snapshot. The existing owners retain question/approval matching, expiry, navigation, grouping, mutations, and Gateway policy. No server, protocol, schema, permission, or persistent setting is added.

Android's native SessionsScreen already has the needed roster and attention/run-state contracts. This PR does not modify or claim validation of Android.

## Evidence

- Base: 42aab1ce38cdde59eaa3f2babc3eef488ea9db2c. The native baseline reaches All Sessions and fails because the activity filter is absent.
- Three focused native logic tests pass: distinct conversation counts, overlapping work/attention, terminal and explicit run-state precedence, resolution/expiry/agent matching, and offline/partial data. Test execution: 0.016 seconds; runner setup/execution: 20.805 seconds.
- Native iPhone UI flow passes with synthesized screen taps at rendered targets, selected-state and membership assertions, 44-point targets, and live count changes after run completion and question/approval resolution. Standard-size run: 53.400 seconds; largest system accessibility text: 47.326 seconds. The filters stack vertically at the largest size. Existing session-row text still elides at that size; this is not a full accessibility audit.
- XCTest AX hit-point lookup reports no hit point for the activity filters and existing status picker on this simulator. The test explicitly synthesizes screen touches rather than relying on AX activation, then checks the resulting state. VoiceOver is not covered by this result.
- 23 focused typography tests pass. Targeted SwiftLint/SwiftFormat, Node syntax, native i18n verification, docs formatting/MDX, link audit, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Fresh independent source review has no actionable P0-P2 findings. It caught an offline-cache cold-open regression and incomplete archive counts, both repaired before the final run.
- Full-app local qualification: unchanged base strict SwiftLint fails in the Apple review demo fixture, also tracked by #191296. Both UI comparison builds use an independently written, local-only extraction of two unchanged fixture branches, preserving guards, payloads, and timestamps. The synthetic Gateway path never enters those branches. No guard or lint configuration is weakened. That qualification and unrelated generated Info.plist changes are excluded from this PR. These results are not exact-tree full-app CI.
- Evidence uses the native app and an isolated synthetic Gateway. No live agent, provider, command, or account is used. Physical Duo, VoiceOver, exact-head CI, ClawSweeper, and maintainer approval are not claimed.

The following captures use the same synthetic Gateway data in the native iPhone app.

| Before | All filter |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: existing Sessions screen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0af9af0-b2fc-45dc-8e81-28a185dd8b0e) | ![After: All3, Needs you1, Working1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0d46ae2-2159-484f-b4d4-d3efad3855c6) |

| Needs you | Largest system text size |

prs.title: fix(discord): settle queued REST requests when their caller aborts
prs.body:
Fixes #187537

## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling a Discord message-tool invocation left its producer waiting in the REST scheduler or the outer retry backoff until a long rate-limit delay expired. The message tool supplied an abort signal, but `createChannelActionContext` never forwarded it, the queued scheduler entry had no cancellation path, and the retry runner only saw the client-lifetime signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `RestScheduler` keeps one request object across rate-limit requeues and tracks `queued` / `dispatched` / `settled`. A caller abort drops only work that was never issued and rejects its promise with the abort reason.
- A request already dispatched to Discord still settles normally and keeps its outcome, matching the settlement contract from #149277. An accepted write is never reported as unsent or retried.
- `RequestClient` gains `callerSignal`, separate from the client-lifetime `signal`. Queued work drops on abort; the transport signal stays tied to the client lifetime so an in-flight write is never aborted mid-request.
- `ChannelMessageActionContext.abortSignal` is now part of the action context, and the Discord action layer forwards it as `callerSignal` through messaging, reaction, guild-admin, and moderation options, including every guild-admin/moderation dispatch, the permission/channel/member lookups that run before an action, and the outer retry runner.
- The draft's per-call REST `signal` argument is removed: it could abort an issued write and never reached the queued executor.

## User Impact

A cancelled Discord message-tool invocation settles at abort time and never sends a queued retry afterwards. An already-dispatched write still returns its real outcome, so there is no duplicate send and no false "unsent" report.

## Scope

Done end to end: message action context → action options → preparation lookups → send helpers → retry runner → REST scheduler. Not covered: a live Discord account (none available here); the proof below drives the shipped action and send path against a real loopback HTTP server.

## Evidence

Head `36c64a7e9`, Node 26.12.1, real HTTP over `127.0.0.1` through `handleDiscordMessageAction` → `sendMessageDiscord` → `RequestClient` → `RestScheduler` → the SSRF-guarded Discord endpoint fetch → `node:http` server (`DISCORD_API_URL` endpoint override). No mocked transport, no live account.

```text
[proof] endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/v10
[proof] queued-cooldown: settledMs=125 postsAfterCooldown=1
[proof] dispatched-settlement: ok=true
[proof] sibling: aborted=rejected sibling=resolved posts=2
[proof] retry-backoff: settledMs=53 posts=1
```

Same harness on merge base `4e846533c` (this PR's changes absent):

```text
[proof] queued-cooldown: settledMs=22394 postsAfterCooldown=12
[proof] dispatched-settlement: ok=true   (the action layer never receives the signal on the base)
[proof] sibling: aborted=rejected sibling=resolved posts=13
[proof] retry-backoff: settledMs=2020 posts=2
```

Committed regressions, all green on this head:

```text
$ vitest run extensions/discord/src/internal/rest.test.ts extensions/discord/src/internal/rest-scheduler.test.ts extensions/discord/src/actions/handle-action.test.ts extensions/discord/src/actions/handle-action.guild-admin.test.ts
Test Files  4 passed (4)   Tests  67 passed (67)
```

The retry-backoff regression goes through `createDiscordClient`, so it fails if the new `callerSignal` forwarding is removed. Scoped checks: `oxlint --type-aware` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the changed files; `tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit`, `tsc -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --noEmit`, and `tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` report only the pre-existing `@noble/hashes` resolution errors in `packages/gateway-client`. Local `pnpm check:changed` is inconclusive in this sandbox (no `rg` binary, symlinked `node_modules` rejected by the declaration-input guard, `pnpm dlx` knip needs registry access); PR CI owns those lanes.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. The implementer understands the change: cancellation applies only to work that has not reached Discord; issued work settles on its real outcome, and the scheduler owns both queue accounting and the single settle path.

prs.title: fix(xai): keep the runtime context carrier for Responses so turns hit the prefix cache
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With the bundled xAI provider on `openai-responses`, the previous turn's runtime-context carrier was removed on every
new user turn, so each turn's first model call sent a prompt that did not start with the previous request. xAI's prefix
cache could not reuse the previous turn: `cacheRead` stayed at 128 tokens on the first call of every turn, while
follow-up calls inside a turn (after tool results) kept hitting the cache at 92–97%.

The request grew by two messages per turn instead of three, because the retained carrier was dropped.

## Why This Change Was Made

`extensions/xai/index.ts` spreads `buildProviderReplayFamilyHooks({ family: "openai-compatible" })`, whose shared policy
never sets `appendOnlyRuntimeContext`. The bundled OpenAI provider owns its Responses policy
(`extensions/openai/replay-policy.ts`) and sets it there; xAI supplies its own hook, so core's fallback never applied.

The xAI plugin now owns that decision for its own endpoint: `buildXaiReplayPolicy` wraps the family policy and adds
`appendOnlyRuntimeContext: true` for the Responses family (`openai-responses`, `openai-chatgpt-responses`,
`azure-openai-responses`). Completions replay is untouched.

This keeps the fix on the plugin-owned path instead of widening the shared `openai-compatible` family policy, which
would change replay behavior for every compatible provider.

## User Impact

xAI Responses users get prompt-prefix reuse per turn again: lower latency and cheaper turns, with `cacheRead` tracking
the previous prompt instead of a 128-token stub. Behavior for non-Responses xAI models is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New `extensions/xai/replay-policy.test.ts`:
  - the Responses family keeps the carrier and preserves the family policy fields;
  - all three Responses API ids are covered;
  - completions replay stays untouched;
  - a missing base policy still returns `undefined`.
- Wiring test through `registerSingleProviderPlugin`: the registered plugin entry's `buildReplayPolicy` returns
  `appendOnlyRuntimeContext: true` for `openai-responses` and no such field for `openai-completions`.
- Bidirectional: replacing the composition with the plain family hooks makes the wiring test fail
  (`1 failed | 5 passed`), so the test covers the entry, not just the helper. Restored: all 6 pass.
- Existing `extensions/xai/index.test.ts` still passes; `oxlint` on all three files reports 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (an agent working from the issue report); the author reviewed the change and its
evidence.

prs.title: fix(ios): repair native Control UI auth handoff to stop browser identity churn
prs.body:
## Summary

Repairs the native Control UI auth handoff on iOS so embedded Dashboard pages stop minting a throwaway browser identity on every load (#161800), and reverts this PR's earlier persistent browser-credential direction at the same time.

> **Revision 11 — direction change.** Revisions 1–10 pursued a persistent browser-credential store for the embedded WebView. That direction carried unresolved review blockers (durable browser authority, data-model compatibility, async pairing-reset provenance). This revision drops it entirely and implements the native-handoff repair the review recommended instead. The embedded page now never mints a browser identity under the native contract, so no durable browser authority exists to store or clean up.

## What Problem This Solves

Every load of an embedded Control UI page on iOS mints a brand-new browser device identity and files a pairing request the user never asked for (#161800). On token-auth deployments behind a reverse proxy, each cold start, each sidebar reopen, and each WebView rebuild produced another throwaway `openclaw-control-ui` device row — a pairing loop that never resolves, reported across multiple devices and panels. The native app's own operator connection stayed healthy the whole time; only the embedded WebView churned identities, because its auth handoff silently fell back to browser-identity minting whenever a synchronous stored-grant read returned nil at view-build time.

## Evidence

- **Mechanism (source-traced):** the page's auth path is mutually exclusive and driven by `nativeConnectAuth` (`ui/src/api/gateway-connect-plan.ts`); `main`'s `authUserScript` gated the announcement on `storedOperatorAuthorization(...) != nil`, so a nil grant plus a configured shared token dropped the page into JS-side identity minting on a `.nonPersistent()` store — re-minted every load. A failed native signature, by contrast, fails closed (`ui/src/app/native-gateway-auth.ts`, `ui/src/api/gateway.ts`) and cannot mint identities — isolating the break to injection, not signing.
- **Regression tests:** `AuthenticatedControlUIAuthHandoffTests` (new) — native contract announced + handler co-installed when the operator route is live without a stored grant; `signedResult` still returns nil without a grant (fail closed); ingress and identity-excluded routes unchanged; stored-grant appearance still rotates `webContentIdentity`.
- **Existing suites unchanged:** all new parameters default to `false`; `ControlUINativeGatewayAuthHandlerTests`, `TerminalHubScreenTests`, `DesktopHubScreenTests`, `SessionDashboardScreenTests` keep their current call shapes and expectations. CI: `security-fast`, `actionlint`, `native-i18n`, `preflight`, `dependency-review` green on head `260de206`.
- **Diagnostics now observable:** credential-free reason buckets (`grant-missing`, `expected-token-mismatch`, `identity-mismatch`, `route-not-current`, `sign-rejected`, `announced via live operator route without stored grant`, …) land in the existing gateway diagnostics log — these lines are the acceptance anchors for the device run below.
- **Pending device proof (will attach):** reverse-proxied HTTPS gateway with token auth, before/after — `devices list` shows zero newly minted identities after the update, WS connect frames carry the native operator `device.id`, Forget/reset leaves no residual authorization, direct-connect unchanged.

## Root cause

The page picks between two mutually exclusive auth paths, driven by `__OPENCLAW_NATIVE_CONTROL_AUTH__.nativeConnectAuth` (`ui/src/api/gateway-connect-plan.ts`):

- `nativeConnectAuth: true` → sign challenges via the native bridge; **never** mint a browser identity; failures fail closed.
- otherwise → mint a keypair in JS, persist it to `localStorage`, register as an unpaired browser device.

On `main`, `authUserScript` only announced the native contract after a **synchronous stored-grant read at view-build time** succeeded (`storedOperatorAuthorization(...) != nil`). On token-auth deployments behind a reverse proxy, that read legitimately returns nil — e.g. the operator device token is keyed to the route's stableID and a gateway that moved from LAN discovery to a proxied manual route starts with no grant under the new key, until (and unless) the operator socket persists one. When it returned nil while a shared token was configured, the script still injected the shared token, the page took the browser-identity path, and because the WebView uses a `.nonPersistent()` data store the identity was re-minted **on every page load** — the pairing loop in #161800. The native signing handler itself was never the break: a missing bridge or failed signature fails closed and cannot produce new device IDs.

## Fix

Two condition changes, no security boundary moved:

1. **Announce (`authUserScript`)**: `nativeConnectAuth` is announced whenever the app hosts the page with device identity on a non-ingress route and the native operator route is live — instead of requiring the stored-grant read to succeed at view-build time. Shared `token`/`password` stay in the payload for pre-contract page bundles (their behavior is unchanged).
2. **Co-install (`nativeAuthHandler`)**: the signing message handler installs under the same widened condition, so a page told to use native signing always finds the bridge.

The handler **revalidates everything at challenge time and fails closed**: stored-grant reload, `identity.deviceId == binding.deviceId`, route currency, trusted source, and the credential selected by the live native socket. A missing grant now surfaces as an explicit "native authorization unavailable" error instead of silently degrading into per-load identity minting. For healthy direct-connect routes with a stored grant, the injected payload is byte-for-byte identical to `main`.

Ingress routes (`ingressAuthorization != nil`) and device-identity-excluded routes are excluded from the announcement explicitly. Suppressed routes (`allowStoredDeviceAuth == false`) remain fail-closed at signing — the suppression boundary is not bypassed.

## Reverts of the persistent-store direction

Revisions 1–10 are reverted wholesale; this branch no longer touches the storage model:

| Review item (Revision 4 review) | Resolution |
|---|---|
| P1 — capture the cleanup target before removing the registry entry (GCC:745) | **Resolved** — forget-time browser-credential cleanup removed with the store; no browser credentials exist |
| P1 — scope browser credential deletion by gateway (WebView:228) | **Resolved** — nothing durable to delete |
| P2 — reuse the existing synchronous pairing-reset owner (Reset:80) | **Resolved** — `preparePairingState` restored as the single synchronous owner; async copy removed |
| Security — forget leaves durable browser authority | **Resolved** — the page never mints a browser identity under the native contract |
| Merge risk — retained authority bypasses native suppression | **Resolved** — no retained authority; suppressed routes fail closed at signing |
| Maintainer decision | **Resolved** — implements the review's recommended native-handoff option |
| Data-model compatibility proof | **Resolved within this PR** — no storage-model changes; `.nonPersistent()` store restored as the security boundary (262deec intent) |
| Provenance — shared synchronous pairing reset (5d8293c) | **Resolved** — debug-startup synchronous cleanup restored |

## Diagnostics

Previously-invisible handoff breakage now logs credential-free reason buckets to the existing gateway diagnostics log: `announced via live operator route without stored grant` (injection side), and `handler-unavailable` / `route-not-current` / `sign-rejected` / `grant-missing` / `expected-token-mismatch` / `identity-mismatch` / `binding-credential-missing` / `sign-failure` (handler side). Token values never enter the log.

## Testing

- New `AuthenticatedControlUIAuthHandoffTests`: native contract announced when the operator route is live without a stored grant; handler co-installs and `signedResult` still fails closed without a grant; ingress and identity-excluded routes unchanged; stored-grant appearance still rotates `webContentIdentity` (WebView rebuild behavior locked).
- Existing suites unaffected: all new parameters default to `false`; `ControlUINativeGatewayAuthHandlerTests`, `TerminalHubScreenTests`, `DesktopHubScreenTests`, `SessionDashboardScreenTests` keep their current call shapes and expectations.
- **Behavior proof pending (real device)** — reverse-proxied HTTPS gateway with token auth, before/after: `devices list` shows zero newly minted `openclaw-control-ui` identities after the update, WS connect frames carry the native operator `device.id`, Forget/reset leaves no residual authorization, and direct-connect scenarios are unchanged. Will attach with the diagnostics log lines above.

Fixes #161800

prs.title: fix(mattermost): chunk long captions on media replies

Closes #192479

## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost media sends post long captions as one oversized post, ignoring the configured text chunk limit while text-only messages honor it.

## User Impact

Long media captions follow the existing chunk limit and mode: the first post carries the file, followed by ordered text-only posts in the same channel or thread. Short captions and text-only sends stay unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chunk uploaded-file captions in the existing Mattermost send owner, covering all its callers without changing other channels. Report each accepted post and return an aggregate receipt; later failures retain already-posted identities as partial delivery. Stamp each post once so progress and returned receipts agree. Props/buttons remain on the first post.

Preserves @hannnnn-l's three contributor commits, including their concurrent test cleanup. Consolidates regressions with the existing delivery-failure fixture, reuses real normalization, and moves empty-target cases to their existing owner table. No test allocation remains.

## Evidence

[Four built-Gateway runs, captured posts/uploads and public receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192481#issuecomment-6621995128)

Built Gateway on Node 24.22.1 with a faithful local Mattermost REST fixture: main twice sends a 1,270-character media caption despite a 350-character limit; candidate twice sends four ordered 316-character posts, attaching the file only to the first. Caption content, thread, target and uploaded bytes are preserved. Short-caption and text-only controls are unchanged. Public receipts include every accepted post. This is local outbound API proof, not a live Mattermost or rendering claim.

44 focused send/authority/target tests pass; main fails the two media regressions and passes eight send controls. Typed lint and formatting pass. Production +55/-29; tests +58/-59 (net -1); docs +1. No allocation file.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores oversized media captions without schema or configuration migration. Already-sent posts remain external side effects. Blast radius is Mattermost uploaded-media captions and their per-post receipts; text-only chunking, targets, authority and other channels are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): page-cache warming fails every 15 min on kernels without /proc/self/io
prs.body:
Fixes #177056

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the scheduled database page-cache warm fails on every 15-minute cycle and never warms anything on Linux hosts whose kernel has no procfs IO accounting (stock Microsoft WSL kernels, `# CONFIG_TASKSTATS is not set`), because `readIo()` throws `ENOENT` for `/proc/self/io` before warming begins.

## User Impact

User impact: on affected hosts, recent chat history is warmed again after startup memory pressure instead of silently skipping the optimization, and the gateway no longer emits a recurring `database page-cache warm failed (state)` WARN every 15 minutes that masks real warnings. There is no configuration change and no behavior change on hosts where `/proc/self/io` exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

The warmer treats IO counters as an environment capability instead of a hard requirement:

- **Probe once per pass.** `readIo()` returns `null` on `ENOENT`; other errors still propagate. A pass without counters keeps running instead of aborting in `warm()`.
- **Keep the safeguards.** Byte budget, pacing, cancellation and reader cleanup must not be bypassed when counters are missing. The worker now reports conservative per-step byte estimates (`estimatedReadBytes` + `ioCountersUnavailable`), and the scheduler uses those estimates for both pacing and the pass budget via one `accountedBytes()` helper. State warming charges the exact bytes read per chunk; agent warming charges bounded per-query estimates that deliberately over-estimate the work (metadata step ~512 KiB, payload batch = max(payload bytes, 8 x 64 KiB), projection query ~2 MiB).
- **Real counters unchanged.** When `/proc/self/io` is readable, `readBytes`/`diskBytes` and the pacing math are byte-for-byte the previous behavior; the estimate is only consulted when `ioCountersUnavailable` is true.
- **Observability.** Startup trace and the completion log now include `estimatedReadBytes` and `ioCountersUnavailable`, so operators can tell which accounting mode a pass used.

Tradeoff: on counter-less kernels, warming stops earlier than it would with exact byte accounting because estimates intentionally over-estimate. That direction is the safe one for pacing, and the structural caps (4096 sessions, 32 messages/session, 64 KiB/message) still bound the work.

## Evidence

Environment used (real host, not simulated): Ubuntu 26.04.1 on WSL 3.0.3.0, kernel `6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`:

```
$ zcat /proc/config.gz | grep TASKSTATS
# CONFIG_TASKSTATS is not set
$ cat /proc/self/io
cat: /proc/self/io: No such file or directory
```

Before this change the same gateway emitted 17 x `database page-cache warm failed (state): Error: SQLite read-only worker ENOENT: ... open '/proc/self/io'` in the first ~3.7 h after a 2026.10.4 -> 2026.10.5 upgrade; the previous day on 2026.10.4 had 0.

prs.title: feat(voice-call): add optional Telnyx noise suppression for inbound realtime calls
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `telnyx.noiseSuppression` setting to Voice Call. When it is set, inbound realtime calls run Telnyx per-call noise suppression (`Denoiser`, `DeepFilterNet`, `Krisp`, or `AiCoustics`) on the caller's audio before it reaches the realtime model.

It is off by default. With the setting unset, calls without media streaming and outbound dials send exactly the same Telnyx requests as before.

## What Problem This Solves

Background speech from a TV or another person in the room reaches the realtime model as if the caller had said it. Telnyx can isolate the caller's voice per call, for example with Krisp's telephony voice isolation model.

Voice Call couldn't use that, because it starts streaming inside the `answer` command and Telnyx rejects `suppression_start` while streaming is active (422, code 90045).

## Change

When `telnyx.noiseSuppression` is set and the call streams media, `TelnyxProvider.answerCall` runs these steps in order:

1. `answer` without the stream fields.
2. `suppression_start` with the configured direction, engine and engine config. This step is capped at 5 seconds so the stream token stays valid. If it fails or times out, Voice Call logs a warning and streams without suppression.
3. `streaming_start` with the same stream settings the answer would have carried.

When the setting is unset, the single `answer` still carries the stream fields inline, unchanged from today.

The config is validated in both the manifest schema and `normalizeVoiceCallConfig`; `engineConfig` requires `engine`. The docs in `docs/plugins/voice-call/realtime-and-streaming.md` cover the direction semantics, the engine fields, and the Telnyx number setting below.

**Prerequisite:** set the number's own noise suppression to `disabled` in Telnyx. A number-level setting engages the default engine at answer, and a later `suppression_start` collides with it; Telnyx returns a 500 for that collision.

## Failure handling

| Step that fails | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `answer` (setting on) | Voice Call sends a best-effort hangup, then reports the answer failure. Telnyx may have answered before its HTTP response was lost; that answer carries no stream, so without the hangup the caller would sit on silence until duration cleanup. |
| `answer` (setting unset) | Unchanged. The answer carries the stream inline, so a lost response still connects media, and no hangup is sent. |
| `suppression_start` | Logs a warning and streams without suppression. The call continues. |
| `streaming_start` | Voice Call hangs up the answered call and reports the failure. |

Both hangups share one helper, and a failed hangup is only logged. This resolves the earlier silent-call window when the answer response is lost: the contributor-side cleanup option from the review is implemented in `2df6212`.

## Evidence

The live runs below are real inbound calls to a Telnyx local number through a source build of this branch, loaded as a bundled plugin. The setup used a Call Control app with number-level suppression `disabled`, a Tailscale funnel, OpenAI realtime, and `inboundPolicy: allowlist`.

Hostnames, call control IDs and the caller are redacted. Timestamps are local (UTC-5).

The current head, `117b7e7e8e2`, is `2df6212` rebased onto main `24015bf60cb`, plus test-only commits for the review's P3 findings; the two generated config baseline files were regenerated, and `docs/plugins/voice-call/configuration.md` was merged with main's new Twilio call recording section. Since `2df6212`'s base, the only main change to the Telnyx provider, the runtime, the webhook or the media stream is one line in `runtime.ts` from #189687 that passes Twilio's `record` setting to the Twilio provider, so the runs below on `2df6212` exercise the same Telnyx answer path as the current head.

### Upgrade from current stable v2026.10.8, on head `2df6212`

All runs used one profile, one state directory and one config file.

**A. Stock `v2026.10.8` (`dc2523e`), config without `noiseSuppression`.** Four inbound calls were answered and streamed. The first three ended with the model calling `openclaw_end_call` (`endReason=hangup-bot`). The gateway was stopped during the fourth call's setup; v2026.10.8 closed that record as `completed` on shutdown.

**B. Checkout of this branch (`2df6212`), same profile, config untouched.** `openclaw doctor --fix` ran the core state migration for the newer build. That migration belongs to v2026.10.8 to main, not to this plugin. After it, the gateway started and three inbound calls behaved exactly as before:

```
22:12:37.815 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:28.983 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=8fea48a4-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:13:34.990 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true

22:14:37.845 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=0a54b7ad-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**C. `noiseSuppression` added with `config set ... --strict-json`, no other change.** The config was Krisp with `krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef`. The call was a normal conversation with no suppression warning and no answer failure:

```
22:15:40.991 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:15:42.112 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 28ab70e0-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
```
