prs.title: feat(stepfun): default to Step 5 Preview with USD usage pricing
prs.body:
Related: #153525 (overlapping Step 5 Preview proposal). This is an independent implementation with official USD pricing and newly captured OpenClaw Web proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Step 5 Preview needs a default catalog entry with USD usage pricing; China endpoints also lost catalog capabilities and prices because their native URLs were not declared by the provider.

## User Impact

New Standard and Step Plan setups select Step 5 Preview by default. Repeating onboarding preserves an existing primary model, fallbacks, and ownership of the `StepFun` / `StepFun Plan` aliases; existing installations can explicitly select `stepfun/step-5-preview` or `stepfun-plan/step-5-preview`.

Standard usage estimates use the official USD rates per million tokens: **$1.00 input, $0.05 cached input, $2.70 output**. Step Plan remains zero in the token-cost catalog because it uses subscription credits. China accounts still receive their separate CNY bill; OpenClaw displays the documented USD estimate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider-owned manifest is the canonical catalog and price source. Add Step 5 Preview to both provider surfaces with 1,048,576 context, 65,536 maximum output, text/image input, and low/medium/high reasoning. Switch the shared default model identifier; reuse existing request shaping and cached-token accounting. Live validation caught a second owning-boundary gap: the implicit-catalog endpoint gate rejected `.com` URLs, suppressing both discovery and pricing. Declare all four native Standard/Plan endpoints in the plugin and mirror that metadata in the external-provider catalog. Custom proxies remain excluded. No new configuration option, migration, or core transport path is introduced.

The docs use the plugin catalog in merge-mode examples, keeping model capabilities and prices in one place. Runtime TypeScript is +9/-2 (seven net lines protect existing normalized alias ownership); catalog metadata is +102/-0 for model rows and endpoint ownership; tests are +222/-108; docs are +46/-68.

Sources: [model guide](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/guides/models/step-5-preview), [official USD price table](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/guides/pricing/details), [Step Plan](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/step-plan/overview).

## Evidence

**Live OpenClaw Web validation — candidate `ee6842c1f8dae16a98391115f4adf1b7ba9e0dfc`, isolated local Gateway, real China Standard API, no mocked provider.**

Computer Use drove the real Control UI, submitted a file-reading task, and captured these unedited browser screenshots. The final candidate called `step-5-preview` successfully (HTTP 200 streaming), read the workspace file, and returned marker `STEP5-WEB-20260923` and `137 + 256 + 89 = 482`. The new turn made two file reads and completed with 333 output tokens. The configured primary model is `stepfun/step-5-preview`; no custom model/cost rows were supplied (`models: []`).

![Step 5 Preview real OpenClaw Web conversation and tool execution](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a798a4d5-e312-41ea-ac8a-d8506688cb33)

The Usage page now attributes 86,830 tokens and about **$0.04** to Step 5 Preview, with 50.7K cached tokens, three total tool calls, and zero errors across both turns. The Control UI JSON export reports 35,455 uncached input, 687 output, and 50,688 cache-read tokens: **$0.0398443**, verified against `(input × 1 + output × 2.7 + cacheRead × 0.05) / 1e6`, with zero missing-cost entries.

![Step 5 Preview USD usage after real calls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3ec796d-4c51-4a3b-8cf5-f81e9e78aaac)

![Step 5 Preview model costs and cache accounting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3147a6bf-0502-4239-8f87-5a88330449c3)

<details>
<summary>Controlled before/after: the same original real conversation</summary>

Before declaring native endpoint ownership, the first candidate produced a correct response but the Usage page showed $0.00 and two missing-cost entries. After the fix, without another model call, the same 32,929 tokens were repriced to **$0.0184524** and **zero missing-cost entries**. The `sessions.usage` Gateway receipt reports 16,703 uncached input, 354 output, and 15,872 cache-read tokens:

`(16703 × 1 + 354 × 2.7 + 15872 × 0.05) / 1e6 = $0.0184524`

Before:

![Before endpoint repair: real usage incorrectly unpriced](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d19c2686-eef0-4c20-bb42-8c8fba4819d1)

After (same original conversation):

![After endpoint repair: the same usage priced in USD](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fc4d92a-82b2-4b20-9b27-b233100062c0)

</details>

### Review follow-up

The default change is intentional and explicitly requested for this PR. Fresh Standard and Step Plan setups use Step 5 Preview; existing explicit selections and aliases must retain their previous meaning. The maintainer can still decide whether to accept that default policy before merging.

The P1 alias finding is addressed at the StepFun onboarding owner: add the default alias only when no existing entry owns its trimmed, case-insensitive name. Twelve region/surface/normalization cases failed before the repair by resolving the old alias to Step 5, then passed after the repair through the actual SDK alias resolver. The new-model default tests remain green. The requested after-repair Web/price evidence is now included above, and all five inline images were confirmed to load anonymously in a browser.

Real CLI validation on final head `eb8beb5bbae`: fresh China Standard onboarding saved primary `stepfun/step-5-preview` and alias `StepFun`. Re-running both China Standard and Step Plan onboarding against a previous-setup configuration retained primary `StepFun`, fallback `StepFun Plan`, and the old whitespace/case-varied Step 3.5 aliases. `openclaw models status --json` then reported `resolvedDefault: stepfun/step-3.5-flash`. These runs used isolated state/workspace directories and skipped service installation. The follow-up changes onboarding alias ownership only; model/request/price code is unchanged from the live Web proof commit above.

### Automated checks

- 54 focused tests passed across provider catalog/request shaping and four onboarding auth choices, including new default selection and preservation of existing primary/fallbacks. The manifest → endpoint owner gate → effective catalog regression failed for both CN endpoints before the fix and passes for all four native URLs, while custom proxies remain excluded. Before implementation, the new-model expectations failed; before changing the default, 18 of 23 default-selection checks failed.
- The live-proof commit runtime, all external plugins, SDK declarations and Control UI build: `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed. The final follow-up head `eb8beb5bbae91ea95fe5719da8ef15d359458264` passed the same build again. A full `pnpm build` also passed before the endpoint-metadata follow-up.
- Changed-scope checks: formatting, guards, all 25 core/UI typecheck shards, plugin production/test typechecks and the dead-export scans passed before the alias follow-up. The broad run was stopped during full-core lint after a separate plugin-boundary declaration preparation timed out at 300 seconds; it is **not** reported as a full gate pass. Final alias-focused syntax lint passed; the final alias-follow-up plugin production typecheck (`tsconfig.extensions.json`) also passed. Hosted CI is separate.
- Independent Claude diff-scope review through the repository autoreview helper: no accepted P0–P2 findings; live validation is reported separately above. A fresh alias-follow-up review was also scoped-clean. Codex reviewer exited before producing a report; its result is not counted as approval.

### Hosted CI follow-up

The ready-for-review run on head `eb8beb5` is still running. [`check-dependencies`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35849554342/job/107144324148) failed in Knip with `scripts/run-swiftlint.mts: swiftlint` (unlisted binary). That script and `config/knip.config.ts` have identical blob SHAs in the tested main parent `760dc1498db8` and CI merge `5510839fe613`; neither file is changed by this PR. This is recorded as a main-side tooling follow-up, not a green CI claim.

### Direct API contract checks

- Real `step-5-preview` streaming requests succeeded both with and without `stream_options`. The default stream delivered final usage.
- A repeated prompt reported 2,843 prompt tokens, 86 output tokens, and 2,560 cached prompt tokens in `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. At the published USD prices, the expected cost is `(283 × 1 + 86 × 2.7 + 2560 × 0.05) / 1e6 = $0.0006432`.
- The provided credential is China-region: China Standard inference was tested; the international endpoint rejected it with 401. Authenticated international and Step Plan inference are **not** claimed as live-tested; their catalog/default behavior is covered by the four-region/plan setup matrix. The maximum context/output limits and image capability follow official documentation, not a maximum-size live stress test.

Keys and browser authentication material are excluded from this PR and all captures.

prs.title: fix(onboarding): keep npx Gateway services running after cache cleanup
prs.body:
Fixes #192328

## What Problem This Solves

Quick start currently skips background-service setup for npx/dlx users, so closing the terminal stops the Gateway. A manually installed service can also depend on files that disappear when the runner cache is cleared.

This offers background operation on supported hosts and installs the same OpenClaw version under the profile's durable npm prefix before writing the service. The service uses that copy and its launcher directory, excludes disposable paths, and runs install lifecycle scripts with the current Node. Standalone runtimes skip npm promotion. Repair planning validates the durable copy's version and integrity and asks for an explicit reinstall when it is unsuitable.

## Evidence

On vesta, built and packed `7c54aca2d47` once using Node 24.22.1, then ran the exact candidate through npx in a throwaway Linux user with its own systemd manager. Selected Quick start and answered Yes to “Keep OpenClaw running in the background?”. Model verification used a local mock with no account sign-in; package installation and the service were real. No lifecycle workaround was needed.

- Closing the terminal ended the npx/CLI processes; Gateway PID `966185` stayed ready.
- Deleted that user's `_npx` cache and restarted the service. New PID `966522` was active/running with `ready:true` and the cache still absent.
- Before and after restart, the service ran `~/.openclaw-final9b3/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`. PATH included the durable `npm/bin` and no `_npx` entry.
- Regressions for standalone npm promotion, unchecked durable-copy reuse, and the missing durable launcher PATH failed against the previous implementation and passed with the fix. The green runs passed 253 targeted and consumer tests with `--maxWorkers=1` (766.02s aggregate runner wall time); `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` passed. CI time was not measured.
- Package integrity passed. The build reported UI size-budget violations. All test users, services, caches and scratch artifacts were cleaned up.

Standalone installation is not verified end to end; it has regression-test coverage only. No macOS/Windows, real-model inference, or latest-stable upgrade validation was performed in this final-head live run.

- Upgrade proof on Linux: created a fresh named profile through published `2026.10.10` npx Quick start, selected a custom mock provider/model and the non-default alias `upgrade-proof`, created a real stored session, and installed the existing Gateway service with `--runtime node`. The original service used `_npx`.
- The published `openclaw update --dry-run` classified the npx installation as unmanaged and directed a reinstall through the original method. Upgraded through npx using the exact packed `7c54aca2d47` candidate and `gateway install --force --runtime node`. This required stopping the old test service and running the candidate's prescribed `doctor --fix --non-interactive` for backed-up database/client-credential migration before reinstalling. Doctor completed, with a service-inspection warning; service state was verified independently with systemctl. This is npx reinstall/upgrade proof, not a successful `openclaw update` run or an uninterrupted upgrade.
- Selected settings were identical before and after: model, alias, agent runtime, provider model settings, workspace, agent directory, Gateway mode and port. The existing session ID, original user/assistant messages and OpenClaw agent runtime survived. Resuming that same session succeeded, and the mock received both the original conversation and the new follow-up.
- Deleted the test user's entire `_npx` cache (1.3 GiB), restarted its user systemd service, and confirmed new PID `1008243`, `ready:true`, `coreReady:true`, and the cache still absent. The service used Node 24.22.1 and `~/.openclaw-upg9b1/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`; its PATH included the durable `npm/bin` and no `_npx`. The history API still returned all four messages after restart, and settings remained unchanged. The installed build metadata matched `7c54aca2d47`.
- Model responses were mocked; installation, migration, session storage, Gateway requests and systemd were real. No account sign-in or real credentials were used. Standalone installation, macOS/Windows and real-model inference remain unverified. One candidate build and package integrity validation passed; the build reported UI size-budget violations. All test services, processes, user state, caches and scratch build artifacts were removed after verification.

prs.title: fix(plugins): allow registry refresh to recover stale discovery
prs.body:
Related: #124468

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw plugins registry --refresh` being blocked by the stale plugin metadata it is intended to rebuild after a plugin source changes.

## User Impact

Operators can rebuild the registry when stale discovery causes plugin-derived configuration errors, including a false duplicate-plugin error across configured agent workspaces. The refresh action rejects malformed JSON and invalid core configuration. The refresh itself preserves the config file and installation records and does not activate plugin code. Successful refresh means the persisted registry is fresh; genuine plugin configuration errors can still require separate repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exact parsed `plugins registry --refresh` action now uses the existing core-only startup validation path, then rereads the current config under the plugin lifecycle lease before calling the existing registry refresh owner. The lease reaches the writer's transactional ownership check, and the command retains its persisted-replacement freshness verification. Before rebuilding, the command uses the existing legacy installation-index migration owner under the same lease. This preserves legacy-only installation records and canonical conflict precedence; unresolved migration warnings stop the rebuild. Plain registry inspection and unrelated commands retain their existing validation behavior.

The registry action moves into a dedicated lazy command module, keeping metadata repair separate from unrelated plugin-management runtime imports. This fixes the recovery bootstrap cycle; it does not change registry invalidation policy or claim to resolve the broader issue linked above.

## Evidence

- **Real registered-action reproduction:** an isolated fixture retains a physically present, old config-selected plugin source in the persisted registry while an authoritative managed installation selects its replacement. With two configured workspaces and empty `plugins.load.paths`, full config validation reports a false duplicate-plugin error. The registered `plugins registry --refresh --json` command fails before replacement on the original code and succeeds after the fix.
- **Persistence and activation checks:** the repaired registry selects the managed package, keeps its install record, and permits normal full config validation afterward. Configuration bytes remain identical. Both synthetic plugin runtimes contain activation sentinels and remain unloaded.
- **Bootstrap regression:** the actual Commander pre-action hook failed on the original refresh path and now requests core-only validation. Plain inspection remains normally guarded. An option value spelling `--refresh`, a flag after `--`, and invalid flag forms do not obtain recovery admission.
- **Refusal and partial-repair controls:** malformed JSON and invalid core schema leave the persisted registry unchanged. Registry repair can finish with a genuinely invalid plugin setting, while subsequent full config validation still rejects that setting.
- **Tests:** The original change passed 235 unique tests across the affected CLI command, pre-action hook, config guard, registry inspection, lazy loading, and neighboring command-output suites. The legacy correction additionally passed all 17 tests in the registry recovery and existing state-directory migration suites, including canonical ownership precedence and byte-preserving legacy archival.
- **Repository gates:** production typecheck, all 25 core-test typecheck groups, all three dead-export scans, changed-file formatting, line/assertion ratchets, plugin boundaries, runtime import-cycle checks, and the remaining selected static owner guards passed. Type-aware lint passed for the eight changed CLI production/test files and the changed test-routing file. `git diff --check` passed.
- **Correction gates:** Production core and affected config/CLI test typechecks, type-aware lint of all three changed TypeScript files, four-file formatting, line/assertion/wrapper guards, runtime import-cycle checks, and `git diff --check` passed after the migration correction.
- **Build:** The final `pnpm build` passed in 5 min 28 s, including CLI bootstrap imports, plugin control-plane loads, declarations, and UI asset checks. The supported package builder passed tarball integrity and import-graph checks; the package embeds commit `3c383fe6894060ce3f59ff43b2d92875ec5bfa8a`.
- **Validation scope:** the broad `check:changed --timed` aggregate was intentionally stopped during full-core lint and replaced with lint of the exact touched files; its completed checks were retained. This is not a claim that the entire aggregate or full-repository lint completed.
- **Review:** The actionable legacy-migration review finding is addressed. The earlier candidate received P1 autoreview and independent source review. The CI follow-up received fresh P1 review against the updated main and fixed the lease-ownership issue described below. A subsequent finding about interactive Doctor recovery was examined and rejected as an introduced blocker: the unchanged bootstrap requires separate explicit consent before running Doctor; the refresh itself still requires valid core configuration. Generic interactive recovery behavior is preserved.

### Public CLI and installed update proof

The final package embeds commit `3c383fe6894060ce3f59ff43b2d92875ec5bfa8a` and has SHA-256 `2fe7e6b6ea152e310582363b687b55c66574929c00d540f44e0d101a87414749`. The installed checks ran in a credential-free Linux container with no host mounts, using actual public CLI subprocesses and synthetic plugin packages. Fixture setup used the existing registry owner; the command, updater, Doctor, and runtime checks were unmodified.

| Boundary | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Original parent public CLI, plugin schema error | `pnpm openclaw plugins registry --refresh --json` exited 1 at normal plugin validation, before recovery could run. |
| Original PR head, legacy-only installation records | The same public command exited 1 with a stale persisted replacement; the linked install record was missing. The focused legacy regression also failed before the correction. |
| Final installed CLI, stale old config source versus managed replacement | A config read reproduced the false duplicate-workspace error. `openclaw plugins registry --refresh --json` exited 0, returned `state: fresh`, selected the managed replacement, preserved installation ownership and config bytes, and left both plugin activation sentinels untouched. Subsequent full `config validate --json` exited 0. |
| Final installed CLI, legacy-only linked ownership | Refresh exited 0 and returned `state: fresh`; the canonical registry retained the linked install record and selected its runtime source. The legacy JSON was archived with identical bytes; config bytes and the runtime sentinel were unchanged. |
| Final installed CLI, genuine plugin config error | Refresh exited 0 with a fresh registry. Both `config validate --json` and plain `plugins registry --json` still exited 1 for the invalid plugin setting. |
| Final installed CLI, invalid core config | Refresh exited 1 before replacing the registry; persisted registry bytes and input config bytes remained unchanged. Fresh-state refresh also passed. |
| Published driver × final candidate | Integrity-pinned official npm `2026.9.5` (`ec9c1a13db89`) ran `openclaw update --tag /inputs/registry-candidate.tgz --yes --no-restart --json`, exited 0 in 65.56 s, and installed the exact commit above. The real migration, Doctor, plugin/config, and canary Gateway checks completed. Linked legacy ownership survived; subsequent installed registry refresh and full config validation both exited 0. |

The false-duplicate **before** failure is proved at the real registered-action/config boundary; the whole-process source-parent fixture could self-repair during startup and is not claimed as a public-process failure. The separate public-process failures above cover plugin-validation admission and the legacy upgrade regression. Installed success is separate from the production incident's operational repair, and no live channel behavior is claimed by these metadata tests.

Initial fixture-only attempts were retained and excluded from the passing results: a retired configuration field was rejected as designed, and disabling bundled discovery made Doctor's own metadata unavailable. The successful updater used configuration supported by the published driver and normal bundled discovery. CI timing is not yet available.

### CI follow-up

Current reviewed head: `d1cea32ce47847de47fcb7640d9f0092ead3e406`; incorporated main: `5a15cf46eba351142e02e73668b87e5a3727d368`. The merge adopts main's equivalent Session Share service-lifecycle fixture repair (`d7b45d7e7`) and removes this branch's superseded registration helper. All five registry-recovery production files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed `108bbce` head. The earlier before/after and updater proof below remains tied to its stated source; this merge does not claim a new provider or installed-runtime replay.

The prior head's exact [CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35861753774/job/107184405898) failed one Gateway lifecycle case: `server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts:290` timed out polling for a pending install's captured setup. The failing fixture and its pending-install/config-notification owners are unchanged between that CI merge and current main. A bounded local reproduction ran the entire three-case file in original in-file order on the merged candidate: all three passed unchanged, including the reported case (13.735 s). Command wall was 67.62 s / supported runner 66.96 s. This does not establish the CI failure's cause or prove it fixed; no timeout, assertion, production path or retry policy was changed. The original 39-file CI shard was not replayed locally.

Fresh full-PR autoreview against the incorporated main is scoped-clean through P1; whitespace validation passes. New CI is left to normal repository execution, without claiming all checks green. The previous Session Share correction at `108bbce` started the actual registered catalog services through the existing controlled transport and awaited shutdown before isolated state teardown; main now owns that same lifecycle behavior.

The same complete integration file reproduced **3 failures / 10 passes** before this fixture correction and passed **13/13** afterward. The root-test type graph, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, full-PR file-growth ratchet, and whitespace checks passed. Fresh P0/P1 AutoReview was scoped-clean. These checks establish the targeted repair; the new remote CI run remains authoritative for the whole suite. The installed package and updater evidence below remains tied to its explicitly recorded historical revision, not this later test-only head.

The original CI run tested merge `a9261fbe5b52ddbd3854022cbc9d8088fcbd33a4` against main `69977d1a07613d871c1ea26ff3c28a2ae8aa2ade`. It failed an unchanged memory responsiveness assertion and a Gateway lifecycle shard. The failures were investigated rather than treated as flakes.

Newer upstream repairs address the owning tests: [#155745](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155745) synchronizes the two memory lookups with their retrieval worker, [#155751](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155751) joins archive-placement fixtures before teardown, and [94b9c471](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/94b9c471535b4c6b088852ecf353f45e6cf63307) joins archive lifecycle requests and removes the intermediate polling race. The branch first incorporated main `843b9f60186c54de1b7c479936942403b509826e` with these repairs, then merged main `b2727e7663e21dcb612277be2aa529039fcce6d2` on September 23. No assertions or timeouts were relaxed in this PR.

After the initial merge and ownership-fence correction, all 18 registry recovery and state-directory migration tests passed, including the new revocation case. The affected config/CLI graph typecheck, type-aware lint of the two changed files, formatting, and staged diff checks passed. The actionable lease finding was fixed; the existing consent-gated Doctor behavior was retained after examining its owner and baseline. The September 23 merge is commit `a9856681fc9c4b4f8631a98f651602b9a61f5285` against main `b2727e7663e21dcb612277be2aa529039fcce6d2`. Its 18 focused tests, affected config/CLI type graph, type-aware lint of the migration owner and registry command/test, formatting, and staged diff checks all passed. Fresh P1 AutoReview completed scoped-clean with no actionable findings after the conflict resolution. The working tree was clean after committing with the normal repository hook.

The installed CLI and updater results above remain measurements of package commit `3c383fe6894060ce3f59ff43b2d92875ec5bfa8a`. After the main merge, fresh review identified a missing final ownership check: the outer lease cleanup could reject a cancelled operation only after the command had emitted success. The command now calls the existing lease assertion immediately after the asynchronous inspection. A regression using the registered CLI and a real lifecycle lease cancels during the real inspection; before the correction the command rejects but has already emitted `refreshed: true`, while the corrected path rejects without emitting output. The configuration file remains unchanged and the persisted registry is still readable. The later September 23 merge accepts upstream [#156285](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156285), which retired the unrelated pre-June plugin-state sidecar importer. Its adjacent import conflict was resolved by retaining this PR's `InstalledPluginIndex` type and removing upstream's retired DB/Kysely imports. The supported `plugins/installs.json` installation-index migration and this PR's transactional lease propagation remain intact. No retired sidecar compatibility was restored. In an interactive terminal, the existing bootstrap may separately offer `openclaw doctor --fix` for invalid configuration and runs it only after explicit consent; the refresh action itself does not perform that repair. The noninteractive invalid-core refusal above remains unchanged. The retained installed results are not represented as a new package test of this later revision.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost</summary>

The original ready-for-review candidate was measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. These local measurements ran while required compilation gates were active; startup and worker compilation dominate some wall times. Test-body times are the sum of the reported individual test durations, not a claim about CI duration.

| New or changed test file | Tests | Command wall | Test bodies |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `src/cli/plugins-cli.registry-recovery.test.ts` | 6 | 38.40 s | 3.163 s |
| `src/cli/program/preaction.test.ts` | 79 | 89.97 s | 0.531 s |
| `src/cli/plugins-cli.lazy.test.ts` | 12 | 9.27 s | 0.899 s |
| `src/cli/plugins-cli.list.test.ts` | 41 | 89.81 s | 4.625 s |

The new recovery fixture uses the real registry persistence and registered CLI action because a mocked command alone cannot prove that stale source selection is replaced without losing installation ownership. The two added cases cover legacy-only ownership through the actual pre-action hook and refusal of an unreadable legacy ledger. The two longer wall measurements spent 92–95% of their Vitest duration in transformation/worker preparation. No sleeps, timers, Gateway boots, or new worker configuration were added; the new database test joins the existing host-broker test lane. CI timing is not yet available.

The CI follow-up adds one revocation case to the recovery file (7 cases total). The new case took 0.682 s in the September 22 recovery/migration run; that run took 68.57 s in the supported runner, including 49.474 s of cold worker preparation (65.41 s Vitest). The September 23 merge reran the same 18 cases: all passed in 102.90 s runner wall (97.54 s Vitest, including 64.524 s of cold worker preparation). The seven registry cases totaled 5.506 s of reported test execution, including 0.634 s for the revocation case; the eleven migration cases totaled 1.577 s. This measures the actual lease and registry boundary; no extra Gateway boot or sleep was added.

At `108bbce`, the Session Share fixture correction added no test cases. Its complete 13-case file passed in 33.24 s command wall / 32.84 s supported-runner wall, with 2.860 s test execution and individual cases ranging from 2 to 737 ms. Cold worker preparation took 21.847 s. Its extracted support file contains registration plumbing only. The before run failed the same three cases seen remotely; no assertion, timeout, or worker placement was relaxed.

</details>

prs.title: fix(acp): tolerate owner-repair verdicts on discarding close with clearMeta (#151859)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses openclaw/openclaw#151859 (task-maintenance discard teardown), resolving the P1 review blocker identified on openclaw/openclaw#152131 while complementing the task-maintenance cleanup deduplication in openclaw/openclaw#152613.

When an ACP session record has an unmigrated or unverifiable backend locator (raising `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired` with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`), automated task maintenance cleanup (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser` in `src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts`) fails closed every minute even though it explicitly requests to destroy both persistent state and stored metadata (`discardPersistentState: true`, `clearMeta: true`, and `allowBackendUnavailable: true`). Because teardown was blocked by the record's own provenance verdict, residue records survived and triggered repeated maintenance failures indefinitely.

*(Note: Gateway CLI deletion in `src/gateway/session-reset-acp.ts` returns earlier from cancellation and omits `clearMeta`; this PR focuses strictly on the maintenance closer path where `clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` are supplied together).*

In #152131, an attempt was made to permit discard-close past owner-repair verdicts, but it inadvertently suppressed owner-repair errors even when `clearMeta` was false or omitted. That introduced a P1 state lifecycle violation (`[P1] Preserve ownership failures when the session metadata is retained`), because an unmigrated session metadata entry would be retained on disk after a reset without notifying the operator or prompting for offline migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

To satisfy the product owner's state lifecycle decisions (*Preventative Preservation & Action Observability*):
1. **Strictly gate owner-repair bypass on `clearMeta: true`**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.close-session.ts`:
     - Recovery branch allows `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` with `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(acpError)` **only** when `Boolean(input.discardPersistentState) && Boolean(input.clearMeta)` and `input.allowBackendUnavailable`.
     - In both the fast-reset branch and recovery branch, fresh-session preparation catches `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(freshError)` **only** when `input.clearMeta` is `true`.
2. **Preserve fail-closed semantics for retained resets**:
   - When `clearMeta` is `false` or omitted (undefined), owner-repair errors are **always preserved and rethrown**, whether `discardPersistentState` is `false` or `true`. Stored metadata in the session store and SQLite database remains byte-for-byte intact.
3. **Comprehensive Regression Coverage**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`:
     - Fast-reset path (`identityHasStableSessionId` false): verifies retained resets (`clearMeta: false` and `undefined`) across both `discardPersistentState` variants reject with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` and leave metadata intact; verifies discarding reset with `clearMeta: true` deletes metadata and bypasses runtime close.
     - Recovery path (`identityHasStableSessionId` true): verifies retained resets reject and leave metadata intact; verifies non-discarding close rejects; verifies discarding close with `clearMeta: true` succeeds, records `runtimeNotice`, and deletes metadata without invoking `runtime.close`.

## User Impact

- Task registry maintenance cleanly purges residue ACP sessions whose backend locators are unverifiable or unmigrated, stopping perpetual maintenance log spam without manual intervention.
- Sessions undergoing non-destructive resets or retaining metadata are strictly protected from silent provenance mutation and continue to fail closed with directions to run Doctor repair.

## Evidence

### Real Runtime Verification: ACPX Backend Wiring & Production Task Closer

Executed against real SQLite session storage (`openclaw.sqlite`) wired to the actual ACPX locator check (`assertAcpxSessionOwnerLocator`) and production maintenance closer (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser`):

```text
=== ACPX & TASK REGISTRY MAINTENANCE CLEANUP VERIFICATION ===
[Setup] Unmigrated ACPX session initialized in SQLite:
  • sessionKey: legacy-session-1
  • backend: acpx | mode: persistent
  • state database: openclaw.sqlite

[Backend] Verified authentic ACPX locator check:
  • Exception: AcpRuntimeError [ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED]
  • Detail code: SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
  • Message excerpt: ACP session "legacy-session-1" has an unqualified or unverifiable backend locator. Stop the Gat...

[Test 1] Retained reset attempt (clearMeta: false)...
  -> Rejected as expected: fail-closed against unmigrated state
  -> Error detail: ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED [SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED]
  -> Stored metadata in SQLite preserved byte-for-byte: true

[Test 2] Invoking actual loadTaskAcpSessionCloser() from src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts...
  • Task closer loaded successfully from production task registry
  -> Production maintenance cleanup completed successfully!
  -> Metadata purged from openclaw.sqlite (readAcpSessionEntry?.acp): undefined (deleted)

=== ALL PRODUCTION & BACKEND VERIFICATION CHECKS PASSED ===
```

### Data-Model & Migration Compatibility Proof

- **SQLite Schema Version**: Unchanged (native state schema remains `v17`, verified by `pnpm check:native-state-schema-version`).
- **Data Migration / Backfill**: None required. No table schema, column, or type definitions are modified.
- **Backward & Forward Compatibility**:
  - Pre-existing session entries in `openclaw.sqlite` remain byte-for-byte intact and fully backward-compatible across upgrades.
  - Normal operations and retained resets (`clearMeta: false` or omitted) continue to fail closed and preserve stored metadata byte-for-byte in SQLite without modification.
  - Only explicit destructive cleanup (`clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` with `allowBackendUnavailable: true`) removes the session record from SQLite.

### Automated Suites & Ratchets

- **Unit & Control-Plane Test Suites**:
  - `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`: 10/10 tests pass across unit and acp projects.
  - Full `src/acp/control-plane/`: 42 files, 329/329 tests pass.
- **Ratchet & Quality Audits**:
  - `pnpm oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`: 2 changed files; no growth/violations.
  - `pnpm check:assertion-safety`: OK, 0 new unannotated assertions.
  - `pnpm check:changed`: All 21 checks passed (typecheck core, typecheck core tests, format, ratchets, Knip deadcode, import cycles).

prs.title: fix(runway): use valid model-specific Veo video durations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selecting a Runway Veo model without a duration sends five seconds, which its native endpoint rejects.

## User Impact

The existing `veo3.1`, `veo3.1_fast` and `veo3` models default to four seconds. Explicit durations must be 4, 6 or 8 seconds and unsupported values fail before submission. Other Runway models keep their existing defaults and normalization; no models or generation modes are added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the correction inside the existing Runway request builder, before credentials and HTTP submission. Reuse the exact three-model allowlist for this duration rule. The frozen provider source is byte-identical at campaign base `31ad71a8addc1d42fbc5478f7e114860f5cbf6c7`, inspected client `d8bb939408aa4d2be7df0161748edb52ebf3b1fb`, and selected source base `dbecd558192e86d1492de16ca21fa7963bb208a1`.

## Evidence

- Candidate `b01d76f2480c8d6c5c6b918a6fb71acdf3cfe17a`. Formatting, syntax, whitespace/privacy checks and normal commit hooks pass.
- Fifteen new cases extend the actual registered native provider suite: frozen Veo defaults, unchanged native Runway defaults, accepted explicit durations and rejected durations with zero submission/poll/download calls. All 15 new regressions PASS in exact-head native job126350348865. This is registered native Runway provider proof; source6 actual Worker proof is separate.

prs.title: fix(ui): let expired OAuth profiles reconnect
prs.body:
Closes #148323.

Supersedes #148325. **Still Draft:** conflict repair, public-code review and synthetic browser validation are complete; real expired-xAI authorization and credential persistence have not been exercised.

## What Problem This Solves

An expired OpenClaw-managed OAuth account in Models has no profile-level action to restart its provider's advertised authorization flow.

## User Impact

Reconnect opens the existing Gateway-owned OAuth/device-code wizard for an eligible expired account, then refreshes its status after completion. It does not change the active model. The recorded test demonstrates that UI path with fictional data, not compatibility with the real xAI service.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing login runner already owns authorization, mutation admission, cancellation and stale-result handling. This change reuses that owner instead of adding a credential store or authentication RPC.

Reconnect requires an expired OAuth profile, a positive Gateway `reconnectSupported` ownership capability, exactly one advertised OAuth/device-code route, and existing write/busy admission. Config display provenance and logout eligibility are not ownership authority. External or inherited profiles, missing local-ownership metadata and ambiguous routes fail closed; the Gateway excludes external IDs even if they overlap the local set. Existing logout behavior is unchanged.

### Conflict repair — 2026-10-25

Conflict-repair head: `ac5c975754f91d342e1cbe6de6557954c49f01c6`.
Merged actual upstream main `9629838ec1aab5d0917828453335473bfa385847` into prior published head `a6519de67ed551eec6b3c16553f9d55043dd805a`, preserving both parents and the original PR.

Resolved the two conflicts in the login controller and its browser suite. Reconnect now lives in current main's inline `providerActions` getter; removed single-use helper wrappers were not restored. The current model-access scenarios and their exact request/no-activation assertions are retained. The contribution remains 11 files (+518/-44) against that main commit; this is not a new feature expansion.

## Evidence

### Latest review follow-up — 2026-10-27

Current head: `91c80e7d53ef01e63a01acb5110ddc07bbc39d92` (two test files, +4/-20; production behavior unchanged).

- Fresh canonical independent **P0–P2 review of this two-file delta completed scoped-clean**, 1/1 pass with complete usage reporting. It assessed the diff and public configuration-owner/harness context; runtime coverage comes from the separate executed tests.
- The prior 59-UI/51-Gateway integration proof and production review remain attributed to `f0104df14`, whose production bytes are unchanged. They are not claimed as additional new-head runs. New-head hosted CI and review are separate.

**Still Draft:** the latest advisory also asks the maintainer to decide whether Reconnect should apply to routine access-token expiry or only unusable-sign-in credential facts, preserving automatic-refresh messaging. That product decision and authorized real-Gateway expired-xAI recovery through persistence/readback remain unresolved. This test-only follow-up does not change the proposed eligibility rule or perform real account authorization. No private data, real logs or secrets were used or shared; maintainer edits/secrets access remain disabled.

### Current main integration — 2026-10-27

The latest hosted ClawSweeper review of `ac5c975754` found no actionable correctness defects, but still requires **maintainer product acceptance** of the added account-row action and **authorized real-Gateway expired-xAI recovery through persistence/readback**. Those requirements are not claimed resolved. Hosted Codex's separate attempt failed with an unknown service error, not a code verdict; the independent local workflow review above is a separate result. The following conflict-repair results were recorded at `ac5c975754f91d342e1cbe6de6557954c49f01c6`, using merged candidate tree `c3e55272164f394fd183f75aa5bc2b2ade713867` on task-only Node 24.22.1 with current main's frozen dependency lock, including Solid rc.18. prs.title: fix(gateway): keep operator Home private from restricted guests
prs.body:
Related: #191140 (held historical proposal; this is a narrow privacy-only PR).

## What Problem This Solves

Restricted session-only guests could discover or read shared operator Home and create an absent Home through its main alias.

## User Impact

Home stays private from restricted guests. Full operators and ordinary shared or guest-owned conversations retain their existing access. Operator Home startup, native restore, explicit deep links, drafts, and the existing Welcome setup and retry flow are preserved. No migration or configuration change is required.

This does not change the global startup default to New session, introduce guided onboarding, change Welcome titles, or close/update the held broad proposal.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway sharing policy now enforces the Home boundary across read, event and mutation consumers. The UI waits for current connection authority before mounting or hydrating Home and reuses existing Welcome status/retry presentation when Home is unavailable.

The accepted production delta remains 18 files (+295/−200, net +95). Follow-up changes on this head are test-only fixture adaptations for full-read positive cases, Home absence before held hello, and ordinary-session restricted file navigation. No production permissions, defaults, assertions or test timeouts were weakened to repair CI.

## Evidence

Reviewed head: `9d82bd1a180a3b78215f689c7b116d6b5d43bb74`.

prs.title: feat(feishu): adopt the shared progress-draft compositor on the streaming card
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu was the only preview-capable bundled channel that did not use the shared progress-draft compositor. It rendered a single replaceable tool status line that could only attach to an already-started answer card (when no streaming session existed, `renderMode !== "card"` dropped it), and it ignored `onItemEvent` / `onPlanUpdate` / `onApprovalEvent` / `onCommandOutput` / `onPatchSummary`. Mid-turn, a Feishu DM stayed visually silent until the final answer began streaming (#147895).

This adopts the same engine the Telegram/Discord/Slack/Mattermost/MS Teams progress drafts use (`createChannelProgressDraftCompositor`) and completes the alignment based on live-gateway validation:

- **Lazy draft creation**: the streaming card starts on the first work event (tool, plan, approval) or streamed text, replacing the eager `onReplyStart` placeholder card. Quick Q&A turns no longer flash an empty card.
- **Progress ownership declaration**: `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages: true` while the preview is active. Core only forwards the quiet progress callbacks (`onToolStart`, `onItemEvent`, `onPlanUpdate`, `onCommandOutput`, compaction) to channels that declare ownership of progress display when tool summaries are hidden — without this flag the draft receives no events at all (verified live: zero callbacks before the flag, rolling tool lines after).
- **Draft rendering**: rolling tool lines, the plan checklist, approval lines, command-output ends, and patch summaries render through the shared compact progress formatter into the card's status slot.
- **Finalization**: the finalized card keeps only the committed answer by default (`streaming.finalize: "overwrite"`), matching the other draft channels. `streaming.finalize: "append"` opts into retaining the rolling tool lines above the final answer behind a `· · ·` separator; the rotating status label ("Working" and friends) is dropped either way since it marks an in-flight turn.
- **Lifecycle guards**: a committed final stops the draft so late events cannot spawn a phantom card, while a mid-turn retraction (`deleteCurrent`) keeps the draft armed for continued work. Progress callbacks stay unregistered when preview streaming is suppressed (outbound bot mentions, `renderMode: "raw"`, modifying hooks) — unchanged.
- Includes the block-streaming policy fix from #147897 (an unset `channels.feishu.streaming.block` follows `agents.defaults.blockStreamingDefault` instead of being hard-disabled), since mid-turn visibility needs both paths. Supersedes #147897.

## Config

New key `channels.feishu.streaming.finalize`: `"overwrite"` (default) | `"append"`. Documented in `docs/channels/feishu/advanced-configuration.md`; schema in `extensions/feishu/src/config-schema.ts`. The key raises the channel config-surface budget from 3730 to 3732 (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`), raised consciously per the config-surface bar: it is the first Feishu-side control for retaining mid-turn progress on the finalized card and mirrors the retention question raised for the other draft channels.

## Evidence

- `vitest run -c test/vitest/vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts`: 2089 passed. The one failure in `setup-surface.test.ts` ("prompts over SecretRef appId/appSecret config objects") reproduces on the base commit without these changes.
- Delivery-level tests in `reply-dispatcher.test.ts`: the card starts on the first tool event and rolls progress text; plan checklist steps render; **no placeholder card is created on reply start**; **append finalize keeps the tool lines above the answer behind a separator**; final close carries the answer only and stops the draft (a late tool event spawns no phantom card); the no-visible-reply fallback still fires after an empty card close under the lazy model; modifying hooks keep all progress callbacks unregistered.
- **Visual evidence** (real Feishu DM screenshots from the validating deployment):

- Before (stock `2026.9.4`): eager placeholder card stays empty for the whole turn — [screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Decent9967/openclaw/pr-assets-148176/assets/148176/feishu-before-empty-card.png)
- After (this PR): multi-tool turn finalizing with rolling progress retained above the `· · ·` separator and the answer below — [screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Decent9967/openclaw/pr-assets-148176/assets/148176/feishu-after-final-card.png)
- Live-text contrast: the same model turn renders live in CLI consumers while channels historically stayed silent — tracked with diagnostics in #132615 (text-only reference; the earlier screenshot attachment was dropped for exposing operational details)

Live validation on a production gateway (2 users, real multi-minute tasks): lazy creation confirmed (card first appears at the first tool event, ~69s into one turn), tool lines stream during execution, append finalize retains progress, final answer lands in the card.

## Notes for reviewers

- The shard16 startup-error test was flaky-red on #147897 while passing locally and on unrelated PRs; control-ui-performance sits ~66B over its bundle budget with zero UI files in the diff. Both reproduce independently of this change.
- Known upstream limitation (not addressed here): on the embedded agent runtime with the zai provider, text partials never reach channel callbacks even with this PR — tool/plan/approval events stream fine, text lands at turn end. Filing separately with the diagnostic trail.



# Production acceptance-recovery drill (2026-09-15, live gateway + real DM turn)
# Timeline (operator-controlled DNS/egress outage via iptables REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset):
11:21:00  POST /cardkit/v1/cards -> card created (cardId=<card-1>)  [Started streaming]
11:21:13  OUTAGE START (all resolved open.feishu.cn addresses rejected, 32 addrs)

## Raw session log lines (redacted: host, trace ids, file paths)

## Evidence notes

The acceptance-recovery path is covered three ways: the wire-level golden `recovered-content-rejection.trace.jsonl` (real dispatcher wiring, replayed in CI), dispatcher/session regression tests (rejected-write retry, coalescing, observer ordering), and the production drill above (a genuine 30s egress outage against the live gateway; the card content writes were rejected mid-stream and the card still closed with the full answer).

# Live mid-turn block drill (2026-09-15, real DM turns per config state; restored after)

- **Inherited-on emits mid-turn messages.** `streaming.mode="off"` (preview off), channel block key unset, `agents.defaults.blockStreamingDefault="on"`: a plan-first narration turn (message tools forbidden in the prompt) delivered the model's pre-tool-call plan as its own mid-turn `🛠` message alongside the final — chat timestamps `16:26:25` (final) / `16:26:27` (block); on the deployed v2026.9.4 core the progress flush coalesces to turn end, so the block lands ~2s after the final while carrying text authored before the tool call.
- **Explicit-off kept emitting — real gap caught by this drill, fixed in 047513ebc.** With `streaming.block.enabled=false` the `🛠` mid-turn message still arrived (`16:30:40` for the `16:29:29` turn): with preview off, nothing declared ownership of mid-turn progress. `c4f0ed77` first targeted `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages`, but that flag only governs quiet progress-callback forwarding; verbose progress messages are gated by `suppressToolProgressMessages` (`dispatch-from-config.choose-route.ts:100-102`). `047513ebc` sets `suppressToolProgressMessages: !previewStreamingEnabled && !blockStreamingEnabled` with two regressions pinning the flag; extension suite 202/202.
- **Version-skew note:** the post-merge branch requires the matching core build — rebuilt against v2026.9.4 the Feishu WebSocket fails at connect (newer SDK runtime symbol), so the live drill ran on the pre-merge extension build that carries the same block-policy wiring this PR finalizes.
- **Matching-core drill (main @ `ed264cc3c` + this branch's extension build):** inherited-on with verbose progress emits the 💬 commentary message and 🛠️ tool line mid-turn, before the final card (chat timestamps 23:44:22 inbound → 💬 23:44:31 → 🛠️ 23:44:32 → final 23:44:40); with verbose off (the default) three real turns produced exactly one final message each — no upgrade-time message spray. Explicit-off did **not** suppress the verbose lane on the live gateway (💬+🛠️ still preceded the final under `block.enabled=false`) on either core generation: the lane delivering these messages in real turns is not gated by channel `replyOptions` — see the drill comment for the full matrix and what that means for the commentary owner decision.

prs.title: fix: preserve interrupted turns after shutdown overruns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes interrupted conversations losing their automatic resume when shutdown exhausts its preparation budget after writing only some restart markers.

## User Impact

Interrupted root conversations retain one ordinary resume input after a partial or forced shutdown. Older abandoned runs, user-stopped work, resets, archived sessions, cron, subagents, and external harnesses retain their existing recovery rules. No configuration, schema migration, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `session-abort` trace includes marker persistence. Marker stores were processed serially, subagent settlement preceded root cancellation, partial markers disabled recovery across all stores, and a forced-stop boot record disabled unfinished-run adoption. A restart cancellation could also clear the only remaining run identity without repairing a missing marker.

Write independent store batches in parallel, bound each preparation phase to ten seconds within the existing shutdown deadline, and signal captured work before joining subagent settlement. Keep actual finalizer custody joined. A terminal lifecycle write during committed Gateway shutdown now preserves the existing resume marker or supplies it if the initial marker write failed. The existing boot ledger bounds fallback to the immediately preceding crashed/forced-stop lifetime; partial markers no longer veto other unfinished roots.

Required received-connection persistence joins are unchanged. A genuinely stuck finalizer can still reach the process watchdog. The historical long-running writer/finalizer and GC contribution have not been identified; this change addresses reproduced ordering and recovery defects, not a claim to have reproduced every production stall.

## Evidence

Acceptance: all 60 captured roots retain markers; cancellation-dependent child settlement must release without consuming the shutdown deadline; partial shutdown must resume current predecessor work once while rejecting stale work; healthy marker work and CPU must not regress.

Synthetic owner workload: 35.13 GiB agent SQLite DB, 10,000 sessions, one million transcript events, 62,000 workspace files (1.116 GB), approximately 2.92 GB retained heap. APFS; btrfs and production GC churn remain unproven. Existing `scripts/perf/restart-resume-measure.ts` now supports `--mark --heap-mib 2600`, plus pinned shutdown sources and `--cancel-dependent --shutdown-budget-ms 1000`. A/A controls, counterbalanced A/B samples, and separate allocation/profile runs were used.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Healthy marker wall median / p95, 5 batches × 5 calls/arm | 52.695 / 56.932 ms | 53.409 / 54.734 ms |
| Healthy marker process CPU median | 76.400 ms | 74.760 ms |
| Healthy marker main-thread CPU median | 13.093 ms | 13.077 ms |
| Cancellation-cycle preparation median / p95, 5 samples/arm | 1000.83 / 1002.09 ms | 61.37 / 78.42 ms |
| Cancellation-cycle deadline failures | 5/5 | 0/5 |
| Marked roots per sample | 60/60 | 60/60 |
| Separate cycle sampled allocations | 6.03 MB | 5.85 MB |

Percentiles are empirical maxima with five observations; healthy observations are batch means, not per-call tail latency. Healthy wall ranges were 52.299–56.932 / 52.030–54.734 ms; cycle ranges were 999.399–1002.091 / 58.832–78.418 ms. Marker A/A medians were 53.93/54.76 ms; cancellation-cycle A/A was 1001.24/1001.12 ms with every baseline call exhausting the budget. Cold first marker preparation was 6.77 s, ruling out a five-second cap for this fixture. One cycle pass had higher process CPU (84.40→106.09 ms); the separate instrumented pass measured 101.91→89.25 ms and healthy A/B remained flat. No CPU speedup claim. The cancellation-cycle measurement is owner proof, not whole-Gateway exit time.

87 focused tests passed (65.20 s wrapper), including real worker persistence, queued-marker preservation, partial recovery, forced-stop boot eligibility, and bounded shutdown. Missing-marker, partial-recovery, and abort-order regressions failed pre-fix. The relocated shutdown test passed with all 44 sibling tests (18.05 s wrapper). Chromium history-settlement browser proof passed (1/1), and bundled chat lifecycle E2E passed (14/14; 93.74 s including UI build). The real Gateway partial-shutdown regression fails on the exact parent and passes on this candidate (38.4 s test), recovering marked and unmarked predecessor work while settling the stale orphan. The forced-stop boot regression also fails on the exact parent. The runtime build passed (89.7 s). The public Gateway 60-turn run on the 35.13 GiB fixture exited cleanly on SIGTERM, verified 60/60 durable markers, then completed exactly 60 unique resumptions and 12 cron jobs. This process run used real agent execution against a deterministic local HTTP model fixture; the retained-heap owner measurement is separate. The harness does not expose whole-process stop duration. `pnpm check:changed` and `git diff --check` passed. The first changed-check attempt found a test-file growth cap and a benchmark resolver typing error; both were fixed before the successful full pass. Exact-head PR CI is run `41763931721`; the inherited ratchet failure is detailed below. Other required gates remain enforced.

Codex autoreview of the local candidate against `852933492df9`, through P1, was scoped-clean with no accepted/actionable findings. Production growth is 39 lines: the terminal-write recovery fact, bounded ordering, forced-stop eligibility, and stage diagnostics; eligibility is shared and the global marker veto is removed. The separate 107-line test allocation covers missing-marker persistence and cancellation ordering; existing recovery/budget tests are extended rather than duplicated.

### Exact-head inherited CI failure

CI run [41763931721](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41763931721), head `ff842b0a69306d84378e605e88ff5791f78fd589`, tested merge `4aee1c1302c0fb245b4be88272b613d655e5bd0a` over main parent `6a4638c30ec168b3d52221159d86a1dfcc7ffa29`, fails the test-line ratchet by 23 lines. This PR adds 107 test lines and exactly 107 allocation; it does not increase the inherited deficit.

The native checker reproduces on that exact main parent: total 6,450,637, ceiling 6,450,614, over 23, exit 1, using `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 466da81cce53000d5320ff9a24568d73d112c8d4 --no-merge-base`. The comparison base is the actual immediately preceding good commit: it passes with 67 spare lines. [#192435](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192435), `92d2dfcbb6fb5c017d190df35312254a511ac8b7`, adds 100 unallocated lines in `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.details-motion.e2e.test.ts` and fails by 33; subsequent deletions of nine and one lines leave 23. Its commit recorded a per-PR budget bypass. This is an attributable main ratchet regression for its owner to resolve, not CI noise. The failing source, checker, and scalar baseline are unchanged by this PR.

Scoped landing authorization permits an admin merge at the pinned head only with this exact-parent reproduction, introducing commit attribution, passing local proof, and no other unexplained failures. The failed CI is retained as failed; required security and review gates remain enforced.

prs.title: improve(ui): mark Incognito with a dashed composer instead of a banner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Incognito chats have a two-line limits banner under the header and a labeled pill before the title, but no desktop composer marker. Replace that intrusive chrome with quieter, persistent visual cues.

## Solution

- Remove `ChatPaneIncognitoNotice`, its header/pending/mobile plumbing, and superseded CSS.
- Move the desktop header indicator into the trailing actions as an icon-only button. Its accessible name and clickable retention tooltip remain; the existing mobile indicator remains.
- Use one shared dashed-composer rule in all themes, including focus and dictation. Owners pass the same Incognito decision used by the header, including canonical-key fallback and pending creation.
- Add a neutral top shade: theme ink at 7% in light mode, black at 32% in dark mode, fading below the header to transparent by 240px. Match the transcript-edge blend to avoid a visible band.
- Scope shading to the **visible cached pane**, not the whole cache/cell. Hidden Incognito sessions must not tint regular replacements.
- Remove the obsolete sole-child header fragment left after deleting the banner, keeping the compiled boot path smaller.

No session-retention or permission behavior changes. The creation page's lifetime/limits copy stays; `/new` itself is unchanged.

## Final landing evidence

Final source: `0a7d1dab4a3188088212dd06121c3446fc3feb2f`, published as `95718932a317e34a0d432b8bec391f5e8077e78f`. The exact CI comparison base `1139abee8063e7f6447a0329cdac394090b47cc3` was integrated to reproduce the chat-boot growth failure; no conflict-driven or speculative refresh.

- Header plus style-browser regressions: **38/38 passing**, 8.55s wall time on the integrated base. Both retained-pane theme cases fail against pre-repair CSS and pass with visible-pane ownership; isolated style run 1.18s.
- Real Control UI with mocked Gateway: `new-session-page.instant-thread.e2e.test.ts`, **15/15 passing**, 36.90s wall time on the integrated base. Covers pending admission, confirmed chat, rollback and navigation, including the dashed composer before creation completes.
- Bundle comparison against `1139abee`: chat boot JS gzip **1,282,215 → 1,282,153 B (-62 B)**; CSS raw **1,665,936 → 1,665,930 B (-6 B)**; CSS gzip **322,908 → 322,921 B (+13 B)**. All budget gates pass under the existing 64-byte build-variance allowance; no budget was raised.
- Test-line allocation **59**: 10 net composition-regression lines plus the 49-line retained-pane style fixture. The shared scalar stays unchanged. Gate passes against the integrated base.
- UI typecheck, earlier applicable UI-test typechecks, CSS stylelint, formatting, commit-hook line-cap checks and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent source review found no actionable issues. Local ClawSweeper was killed by its memory bound. The documented autoreview fallback completed on the final `1139abee..0a7d1dab` range, P0–P2 scope: **no actionable findings**. The reviewer did not independently execute tests or verify images; the lead did. One hosted re-review was requested on the earlier repair and remains advisory.

Inspected light/dark desktop and phone screenshots are delivered in chat and embedded in the [final visual proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192240#issuecomment-6621111856), alongside the [original before/after comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192240#issuecomment-6614745824). These captures remain applicable: the final wrapper deletion preserves the same single header DOM element and changes no presentation rule.

## Simplification and accepted edges

The repair removes the multi-stop gradient machinery and obsolete header fragment, reuses the existing transcript blend, and keeps one visible-pane shading owner. It retains the requested look within both bundle budgets.

Inactive split-view cells hide their header actions, including the icon; their dashed composer remains. The shade covers chat panes, including pending creation, not `/new`. Screenshots use synthetic fixtures, not live user data.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(infra): hide qualified mainline refs from dev install badge
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` returns a **qualified ref** (`heads/main`, or `refs/heads/main` when other refs deepen the ambiguity) when the checked-out branch shares a name with a tag. `resolveDevInstallGitBranch` compares that output directly against `HIDDEN_BRANCHES` (`{"main", "master", "HEAD"}`), so a mainline checkout on branch `main` with a same-name tag `main` is **not hidden** — the Control UI sidebar shows a dev-gateway badge carrying a qualified ref (e.g. `refs/heads/main`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Review follow-up to the prefix-stripping approach (thanks @roboclaw-bot / ClawSweeper): stripping `heads/` from abbreviated output cannot distinguish a **mainline checkout with a colliding tag** from a **literal branch named `heads/main`** — both abbreviate identically. This revision reads the actual branch identity with `git branch --show-current` (the same owner `session-diff.runtime` already uses) and applies the existing hidden-name check unchanged. No prefix stripping, no normalization.

**Fix classification: `behavior-preserving`** — mainline/detached/feature handling is unchanged for all existing inputs; only the previously-misclassified qualified-mainline case now resolves to `null` as intended, and literal `heads/`-prefixed branch names keep rendering as-is.

## User Impact

- **Before:** a source checkout whose branch shares a name with a tag (e.g. branch `main` + tag `main`) shows a dev-gateway badge in the Control UI sidebar footer (e.g. `refs/heads/main`).
- **After:** mainline checkouts stay hidden; genuinely drifted checkouts (including a literal branch named `heads/main`) show their real branch name.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (vitest, real git)

`src/infra/dev-install-branch.test.ts` — 17/17 pass via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on this branch (node v24.22.1):

- Existing mocked contract cases (feature branch visible; `main`/`master`/`HEAD`/detached/empty hidden; failure/nested/no-root → null) — unchanged, all pass.
- **Real-git controls** (production resolver, real git in temp repos, only package-root discovery stubbed):
  - branch `main` + tag `main` → `null` (hidden) — the reported bug.
  - literal branch `heads/main`, no tag → `"heads/main"` (visible) — the regression the review flagged; identical `--abbrev-ref HEAD` output to the tagged-mainline case.
  - branch `feat/dev-branch-badge` + same-name tag → `"feat/dev-branch-badge"` (real name kept).
  - detached HEAD → `null`.

### Real behavior proof through the shipped Control UI

Real Gateway (`openclaw.mjs --dev gateway`, loopback only) booted from a source checkout with the colliding tag, driven with Playwright against the served Control UI; bootstrap cross-checked at `/control-ui-config.json` in the same page. Loopback-only, synthetic local token, default identity — no credentials or non-public endpoints in captures.

| State | Checkout | `/control-ui-config.json` `devGitBranch` | Sidebar badge |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Before** (base `8f9190485c6` code) | branch `main` + tag `main` | `"refs/heads/main"` | **shown: `refs/heads/main`** (wrong) |
| **After** (this branch) | branch `main` + tag `main` | `null` | **hidden** (correct) |
| **After** (this branch) | literal branch `heads/main` | `"heads/main"` | **shown: `heads/main`** (correct literal name) |

![Badge before/after comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/badge-before-after-compare.png)

- Before, branch `main` + tag `main`: [full capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/before-tagged-main-full.png) — badge `refs/heads/main`.
- After, same checkout: [full capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/after-tagged-main-full.png) — no badge.
- After, literal `heads/main` branch: [full capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/after-literal-heads-main-full.png) — badge `heads/main`.

### Review response

- **[P2] Preserve literal branch names** — fixed by replacing prefix stripping with `git branch --show-current`; the real-git control above (identical abbreviated output, divergent classification) passes.
- **[Needs proof]** — provided via the real Gateway + shipped Control UI captures above, including the visible literal `heads/main` control.

### Local checks

- `pnpm test src/infra/dev-install-branch.test.ts` — 17/17 (via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs`).
- Type-aware oxlint on both changed files — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Full `check:changed` could not run locally: this host's glibc (2.28) is below the tsgo native binary's requirement (2.32+), and the repo-wide dead-export scan reports pre-existing findings in untouched files (`src/agents/*`, `ui/src/components/config-form.*`).

### CI attribution

Current red checks are **inherited from main**, not this PR: the failing type errors are confined to `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts` and `src/agents/mcp-metadata.ts` (main's in-flight MCP catalog metadata refactor `#192302` / follow-up `dbecd558192`, landed after this PR's base `8f9190485c6`). Neither file is touched here; this PR's two files produce no type or lint findings.

## Not tested

- Windows/macOS git variants — `branch --show-current` has produced the actual branch name across platforms since git 2.22 (the same dependency `session-diff.runtime` already relies on).
- The footer badge element itself is already covered by the existing UI e2e (`ui/src/e2e/sidebar-dev-branch.e2e.test.ts`); this proof exercised the real Gateway→bootstrap→UI chain end to end.

## Cleanup

No state/config/session/token touched in the product. Proof ran in an isolated temp checkout (`/tmp/ocdevproof192034`) with its own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; the temp repo and state were removed after capture. Media for this body lives on the fork's `proof-192034-media` branch.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the old comparison. Blast radius is the dev-install badge classification in the Control UI sidebar. Production diff: `src/infra/dev-install-branch.ts` +8/-15; test +60/-9.

prs.title: fix(reply): carry the queued chat identity into follow-up tool context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #184730.

A message drained as a native `followup` rebuilt its turn template context from the queued run's routing facts, but never restored the chat identity the source turn was addressed at. `buildEmbeddedContextFromTemplate` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.ts:288-290`) derives the tool-run `chatId` from `NativeChannelId ?? ChatId`, and `buildEmbeddedAttemptToolRunContext` projects that field as `nativeChannelId` for V2 plugin tools. A queued turn supplied neither field, so V2 plugin tools saw requester / channel / account facts with an absent `nativeChannelId`, while the same message as an immediate turn carried it (and the CLI candidate path already passed `followupRun.originatingChatId` as `chatId`).

The queued run already carries the value: `get-reply-run-execute.ts:501` captures `originatingChatId` as `NativeChannelId ?? ChatId` at enqueue time, and the drain preserves it. Only the follow-up template projection dropped it.

- `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.ts`: `buildFollowupTemplateContext` now publishes `ChatId: queued.originatingChatId`. The shared embedded context keeps its existing preference for `NativeChannelId` and only falls back to `ChatId`, so the follow-up projects the same native conversation as an immediate turn.
- No inference from prompt text, session-key parsing, route relaxation or extra session lookups: a queued turn without an originating chat id still projects none, so an absent identity keeps failing closed.

## Evidence

Red first, on the real follow-up execution owner. Regression added in `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts`:

```text
FAIL  src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts > executeFollowupTurn > carries the queued chat identity into the follow-up turn's tool context
AssertionError: expected undefined to be '-1001234567890' // Object.is equality

- Expected:
"-1001234567890"

+ Received:
undefined

 Tests  1 failed | 32 passed (33)
```

The case drives `executeFollowupTurn` with a queued `originatingChatId` and asserts both hops the issue is about: the turn template's `ChatId`, and the `chatId` that `buildEmbeddedRunContext` feeds into the tool-run context (which `nativeChannelId` is projected from). It also asserts the requester stays separate (`SenderId` unchanged), and a second case fixes the fail-closed side: with no queued chat id, both hops stay `undefined`.

Green after the change:

```text
 Tests  33 passed (33)          # src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts
 Tests  37 passed (37)          # followup-runner.test.ts + agent-runner-utils.test.ts
```

Verification on this host (`node scripts/...`, portable Node 24.22.2):

- `scripts/test-projects.mts` for the three files above — all passing.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint` on both changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors (259 rules).
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` — all matched files use the correct format.
- `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.messaging.json` — no diagnostic in either changed file. This workspace's installed `@openclaw/fs-safe` is older than current main, so the run stops on four pre-existing errors in unrelated files (`src/agents/host-file-write.ts`, `src/config/io.audit.ts`, `src/infra/private-dir-mode.ts`, `src/infra/state-migrations.agent-dir-receipt.ts`).
- The e2e lane (`agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`) needs a full build, which this host cannot produce (`ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE: mode 'preserve'`), so end-to-end shipped coverage is left to CI.

Test-line growth is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/followup-tool-chat-identity.txt` (32 net new test lines, measured after formatting).
