prs.title: fix(logging): preserve stuck-session recovery classification in automation failures
prs.body:
Related: #138528

## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled run that the stuck-session watchdog stops reports no reason: automation history keeps the mechanical effect (`Reply operation stalled`) and the failure alert ends with "Check automation history for details". The cause the attention layer already computed for that stall is dropped one layer above every operator-facing surface, so a run killed behind a tool call that never progresses is indistinguishable from one killed by a provider outage or an attempt deadline.

Fixes: the stop's classification reaches automation history and the failure alert, with recovery guidance.

## User Impact

An operator reading a stopped scheduled run now sees *why* it was stopped — in `lastError` / `cron runs` and in the chat alert's `Cause:` line plus a one-line recovery step — instead of a cause-free line. A run stopped while the provider is rate-limiting still reports the provider's own recovery text: the mechanical watchdog label never replaces it. Cancellation, restart and rate-limit handling, scheduler merge re-admission, abort signatures and alert routing are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session controller owns the stop; cron owns the operator-facing projection. The object connecting them already exists: the controller-owned `ReplyOperation` that `finalizeCronRun` reads. `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` commits the attention classification onto that operation (`recoveryClassification`) before it drives `watchdog.tick()`, and a stop performed by the watchdog tick records its own decision reason there instead. One owner, no diagnostic-owned store, nothing to keep in sync.

Cron projects that one field twice: as the run-history error when the run failed without a descriptive message, and as a typed `agent-stall` `CronFailureNotificationDetail` that the alert renders as `Cause: <classification>` plus guidance. Rate-limit precedence lives in one helper (`resolveCronRecoveryClassification`): `abortForStall` records a stop during provider backoff as `rate_limited` and `describeStop()` keeps the provider text, so no classification is projected.

Accepted edge case, named instead of coded around: whichever owner performs the stop decides the label. The watchdog timer usually fires its own quiet-tool allowance first, so a hung tool call reports the mechanical `semantic_stall`; when the diagnostics recovery request lands the stop, it reports the precise `blocked_tool_call` (§1). Both labels are recorded facts, and both now reach the operator.

Scope: cause attribution only. #138528 also asks for immediate exec-denial classification and the blocking tool identity inside the alert; neither is here, so `Related:` rather than `Closes:`.

## Evidence

### 1. Shipped Gateway, real chat alert

Shipped `openclaw.mjs gateway --dev` (isolated state dir, loopback), the shipped plugin installer registering a plugin whose `hang_forever` tool never settles, a local OpenAI-compatible provider that answers the first turn with that tool call, and the shipped `cron` CLI creating a recurring isolated job with `--timeout-seconds 0` so no attempt deadline can mask the block. `cron.failureAlert` = `{"enabled":true,"mode":"announce","channel":"qa-channel","to":"dm:operator"}` against a local qa-lab bus. No stubbed runtime, no clock instrumentation.

The attention layer classifies the in-flight tool call every heartbeat; the run ends when the quiet-tool allowance (15 min) is exhausted:

```
08:51:40 [diagnostic] stalled session: … state=processing age=685s
         reason=blocked_tool_call classification=blocked_tool_call activeWorkKind=tool_call
         activeTool=hang_forever activeToolAge=684s cronJob="watchdog-chat" recovery=controller_owned
08:55:16 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested durationMs=909760
         error="Reply operation stalled" errorName=AbortError taskKind=cron
```

The alert as the bus recorded the outbound message (ids and ports removed):

```
Automation "watchdog-chat" failed 1 times
Cause: semantic_stall
The agent made no semantic progress before the stall deadline.
Review the run transcript and simplify the task, then rerun.
```

Same moment, persisted history: `"lastError": "semantic_stall"`, `"lastDiagnosticSummary": "Reply operation stalled"`, `"lastDurationMs": 917358`, `"consecutiveErrors": 1`. The announce adapter left `lastFailureNotificationDeliveryStatus: "unknown"` (`cron: failure alert announcement timed out`) even though the bus recorded the text — the qa-channel fixture does not ack the announce send.

The precise label, when the recovery request lands the stop (same stack, webhook alert): run record `"error":"blocked_tool_call"`, alert `Last error: blocked_tool_call`.

### 2. Regression: red on pre-patch main, green here

`src/cron/isolated-agent/run.watchdog-cause.test.ts` drives the real cron finalizer with a controller-owned operation:

| code state | persists the cause | rate-limited stop keeps provider text |
|---|---|---|
| pre-patch `main` (`f75bd97cda9`) | **fails** | passes |
| reviewed head (`639c0970838`) | passes | **fails** |
| this head (`62c8927d339`) | passes | passes |

### 3. Acceptance on this head

```
vitest run run.watchdog-cause / failure-notification-text / diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery-cause
                             → 2 shards passed · 16 tests passed
pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base cd63adb5d66… (main, post-#192448) → Test lines OK: 6447381; ceiling: 6447381; slack: 0
oxfmt --check, oxlint --type-aware (12 changed code files) → formatted · 0 warnings, 0 errors
git diff --check                                     → clean
```

Gap: local type checking cannot run in this worktree — the `run-tsgo` boundary guard rejects the shared install's symlinks, so `check-prod-types` and `check-test-types-*` in CI own that lane. The proof stack stays outside the repository (~16 min wall clock per run, over the test cost budget), so the unit suites above are the persisted guards.

prs.title: fix(release): stop publishing after candidate tag changes
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127001

## What Problem This Solves

Release publication can update notes or upload evidence after its candidate tag moves or is deleted during intervening work.

## User Impact

Publication stops before the next release write when the remote tag no longer identifies the pinned candidate or signed tag object.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing tag verifier immediately before the five affected GitHub release writes. Existing resume, public-page, and documentation ownership behavior is preserved. This extracts the candidate-tag repair from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127001; its Windows publication and recovery replacement landed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191798.

## Evidence

- The actual upload helpers reproduce four failures on the base (moved/deleted tags across both writers) with two valid-tag controls. All six regression cases pass with the fix; changed signed-tag objects also refuse both uploads.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m6e21bjr67qs5c5y3y1kmxbw`: 62 tests passed across `release-publish-draft.test.ts` and `release-publish-parent.test.ts`, using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ... --maxWorkers=1`. Touched-test lint, oxfmt/Bun format parity, and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental` completed in the same successful payload. [Allocation run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41441040837). Provider cleanup initially timed out; its cleanup-only reconciliation subsequently succeeded. The Actions cancellation records external lease cleanup.
- Bash syntax and diff whitespace checks passed. Tests exercise the production shell helpers with isolated Git/GitHub transport fixtures; no live release was changed.
- Local ClawSweeper completed the full committed range `71e516af03a11fb1e309ff4fd2a0b8dccee506da..985c5557e40c11a923b42c3add513416dce232fa` with no actionable findings. Independent source review also found no actionable defect.

**Review discussion before merge:** the [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191089#issuecomment-6577413988) found no code findings and requests real GitHub-client final-effect proof from an authorized isolated release. The local real-Git matrix below adds the previously missing notes-path and signed-object coverage. GitHub effects are recorded at the CLI boundary, so this is not a claim that the hosted proof request is satisfied. That request remains for owner disposition or an explicitly authorized disposable GitHub test repository. Exact-head CI is green.

<details>
<summary>Real-Git boundary matrix: 40/40 cases</summary>

Baseline `71e516af03a11fb1e309ff4fd2a0b8dccee506da`; candidate `985c5557e40c11a923b42c3add513416dce232fa`.

**40/40 cases passed.** Each of the five production write paths permits its valid-tag control. On the base, all 15 revoked-tag cases reach the recorded write. On the candidate, all 15 refuse before the recorded write.

| Production path | Base cases reached write | Candidate valid control | Candidate moved/deleted/replaced signed object |
|---|---|---|---|
| draft-create | 4/4 | 1/1 allowed | 3/3 refused |
| draft-edit | 4/4 | 1/1 allowed | 3/3 refused |
| immutable-upload | 4/4 | 1/1 allowed | 3/3 refused |
| replaceable-upload | 4/4 | 1/1 allowed | 3/3 refused |
| notes-append | 4/4 | 1/1 allowed | 3/3 refused |

Git and `git ls-remote` are real, against a disposable local bare origin. Both annotated tag objects were really SSH-signed and verified; the replacement object points to the same commit as the approved object. The moved-tag cases independently exercise commit binding without a signed-object pin. Tags are revoked during the intervening GitHub read for draft create/edit and immutable upload, during the final body read for notes append, and before replaceable upload. The production verifier is not replaced.

GitHub calls are a shell fixture that records the final CLI write. Note rendering and unrelated proof preparation use fixture values. This proves production-helper decisions against real Git identities; it does not constitute real GitHub client, hosted release, or authenticated final-effect proof. That requires a separately authorized disposable GitHub repository.

No production release, registry, repository, Gateway, or credentials were mutated. The fixture private signing key was removed after the run; only the public verifier and signed Git objects remain.

</details>

Production grows by five calls to the existing verifier. The 52 regression-test lines receive an exact 52-line allocation to protect both upload boundaries against moved or deleted candidate tags; the shared test ceiling is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(release): bind GitHub and Windows writers
prs.body:
Related: #126881

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a release-integrity gap where GitHub Release edits and Windows installer promotion could continue after the approving release-tooling ref moved or without an immutable handoff binding the exact parent attempt, tooling revision, candidate, source release, and installer digests.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every GitHub Release mutation now revalidates the live protected-tooling identity immediately before the write. Stable Windows promotion consumes an attested `windows-release-approval.v1` artifact, validates installers in a read-only job, and performs per-asset writes only in a separate `npm-release` environment job. Recovery must reuse the original attested tuple and cannot substitute current `main`.

## User Impact

Release operators get fail-closed GitHub and Windows publication: moving refs, stale recovery inputs, mismatched parent attempts, changed candidates, changed Windows source tags, or changed installer digests stop before privileged writes.

## Evidence

Historical branch evidence, not current-main integration qualification:

- Stacked exactly on protected-tooling head `ac8018edcf93489277cd7c0267956518653c07ed`.
- Signed head: `8a09e719535`.
- `actionlint -color .github/workflows/openclaw-release-publish.yml .github/workflows/windows-node-release.yml`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/validate-release-publish-approval.test.ts` - 33 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts -t "gates stable GitHub publication on the Windows Hub release asset contract|rejects unsafe direct Windows recovery before uploading assets|keeps release publish artifacts and release-note ordering wired|resolves broad release evidence and exact-binds every publish child"` - 4 passed.
- Focused `oxlint` passed for the changed script and tests.
- `git diff --check`

Production delta is net +411 lines, justified by the new immutable approval schema, the read-only/promote ownership split, and immediate privileged-writer revalidation. Tests are net +171 lines.

## Current Integration Status

Source-only re-audit on 2026-09-24 retained head `8a09e7195358d81738c4539fbf4d7c1c18732459` against main `fe846d3c9498b855ae0d8bd3c95c318b12a04047`. Keep open for a narrow current-main reconstruction, not a mechanical rebase or complete-supersession closure.

- Protected tooling has landed through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126881, and final activation now has its own owner through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146052. Both merge commits were verified in main's ancestry. Preserve the detached, post-publication Windows delivery established by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/136790. The open VCR work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127000 is not this PR's direct base or a merged replacement.
- The Windows attestation, read-only validation/separate writer and per-asset authorization still have a distinct residual. Port only that residual and the uncovered GitHub mutation guards into the current owners.
- [The existing P1 review finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127001#issuecomment-5365191254) remains source-confirmed: the tag-to-candidate check is in the earlier validation job, while the immediate upload assertion checks tooling, attestation and parent metadata but does not reread the target tag. Revalidate the live tag against the approved target before each asset write; prove tag movement during the environment wait is refused before the upload.
- Separately resolve recovery-attempt ownership: the writer reads an attempt-specific historical endpoint, so its equality check does not establish that the approved attempt is still the current run attempt. The release owner must explicitly preserve or reject recovery from a superseded attempt, with matching boundary coverage; no executed exploit or independent second P1 verdict is claimed here.

Historical test counts above remain attached to this old head. Current-main integration, remote boundary proof, source review and exact-head gates remain pending. No release was dispatched, published, provisioned or changed during this audit.

prs.title: fix(plugins): stop canceled or replaced runs after delayed model routing
prs.body:
Related: #152208

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an asynchronous model-routing hook can finish after its source run is canceled or replaced, allowing a stale result to continue into model preparation.

## User Impact

Canceled or superseded runs discard late routing results before preparing a model. Existing provider/model precedence, locked-session routing bypass, and fail-open handling of ordinary hook errors remain unchanged for current runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the optional source `AbortSignal` to `before_model_resolve`, then revalidate the existing source/lifecycle and admitted-owner authority immediately after the await. The assertion is outside the hook-error catch, so stale work cannot resume through the ordinary fallback. Valid incoming runs tolerate an unrelated previous same-ID owner remaining active, being canceled, or finishing while routing is pending. No second ownership registry is introduced.

This is independent of the thinking API in #136454. It does not add reasoning-effort selection, durable notices, Auto UI projection, or atomic hook-field composition.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway cancellation proof — September 25

[Reproducible driver, setup, and sanitized output](https://gist.github.com/jb510/0b13a02499d93d0264e607bd910c5f8a).

Ran a real built Gateway and its built-in OpenClaw agent harness on macOS/Node 24 with an installed public-API plugin. The plugin deliberately holds `before_model_resolve`, ignores cancellation while pending, then returns a successful model override. The driver uses actual Gateway `chat.send` and `chat.abort` RPCs and validates the aborted run ID. Its provider's public `resolveDynamicModel` callback records whether selected-model preparation is reached.

After releasing the canceled hook, a successful control turn runs through the same serialized global lane before the counters are assessed. This both verifies the observation works and prevents an early abort acknowledgment from being mistaken for completed runner cleanup.

```text
canceled: chat.abort acknowledged the exact held run
canceled: delayed hook returned with signal.aborted=true
canceled: selected-model preparation=0; provider requests=0
Gateway: lane task error: AbortError, "This operation was aborted"
Gateway: model fallback chain stopped: caller_signal_aborted
following control: selected-model preparation=1; provider requests=1; status=ok
```

The canceled terminal `error` is the propagated AbortError. The control used a synthetic loopback HTTP model endpoint, not a paid model. There were no Vitest mocks or patched production modules in this proof. HOME, state, config, workspace, token and ports were isolated; inherited credentials were excluded. The owned Gateway stopped and its temporary state was removed. No existing installation was touched.

Source head: `51a9edc3609eafff291080daf6e41ea279c77738`. The runtime was built at `082af1952f165af400786321bdf6526dd9bf1f71`; production code is identical because the new commit changes only two test fixtures. The linked driver can rebuild and rerun at the new head. This proves cancellation before selected-model preparation; replacement remains covered by the focused boundary regressions, not claimed as a live scenario.

### Regression and independent validation

- **35/35 tests across three files passed**, including the entire 10-case lifetime suite, all six thinking-route cases, and prepared-harness source delivery. Wall time: **221.59 seconds**, including worker preparation. No test-name filter.
- The lifetime suite covers cancellation, same-ID replacement without aborting the old signal, revoked authority, locked-session bypass, ordinary hook failure and valid previous-owner handoffs. The original production implementation failed the cancellation/replacement regressions.
- This update repairs two existing CI fixtures: runtime preparation now owns a real admission throughout preparation and cleanup; the hook-event expectation includes the source AbortSignal. Production guards were not weakened.
- Targeted formatting, Oxlint and diff checks passed. Independent autoreview of the complete candidate diff found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The previous production-core and owning test-type checks passed; no production code changed in this update.
- Clean merge preflight against main `2716e9aa73f98faaf0d2018d725550853ffe7026` passed.

```sh
OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=0 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-preparation.thinking.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.prepared-harness-source-delivery.integration.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/model-setup.run-lifetime.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Fresh CI is running for `51a9edc3609`. The previous run also hit the shared CI planner's fixed 191-second chunk-floor assertion. Upstream already corrected that assertion to scale with the chunk's file count in [15ab76c3b680](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/15ab76c3b680688031b0ec7e7189035bfdd6dd70); this PR does not duplicate that unrelated test repair. Full repository CI and maintainer acceptance are still required. No channel/UI behavior changes, so notice or Telegram delivery proof is outside this revision's scope.

prs.title: fix(cron): reject compact digit --at values misread as epoch ms
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: confusing cron rejection when a compact datetime is passed to `--at` / `schedule.at` — `--at 20250101120000` (meant as `yyyyMMddHHmmss`) was read as epoch milliseconds and rejected with `schedule.at is too far in the future: 2611-09-14...`, which shows no trace of the input the user actually typed.

## User Impact

User impact: mistyped or compact numeric `--at` values are now rejected with the original input echoed back — `Invalid schedule.at: expected ISO-8601 timestamp (got 20250101120000)` via Gateway/API, and `Invalid --at "20250101120000". Use an ISO timestamp or a duration like 20m.` via CLI — so users can see what was rejected and why.

Behavior change (single, focused):
- Pure-digit `--at` values whose numeric value is 10,000,000,000,000 ms or more can no longer be parsed. Previously they were misread as epoch ms and rejected with a derived date centuries in the future; now they are rejected directly with the raw input in the message. Realistic epoch-ms input (anything before year 2286, including zero-padded forms like `01798761600000` = 2027-01-01 UTC) is still accepted, exactly as before.

ISO timestamps, documented durations (`20m`, `+30m`, …), and all previously accepted epoch-ms values behave exactly as before. No config, API schema, or stored-data format changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pure-digit strings were parsed as epoch ms, and the original string was destroyed before validation: the CLI converted the misread value to an ISO string, and Gateway normalization rewrote `schedule.at` the same way, so the rejection message could only name the derived date. Two paths now stop the misread at the parse boundary instead. `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` rejects digit strings by comparing the **parsed numeric value** against the upper end of the epoch-ms range reachable within the far-future scheduling cap — a 14-digit `yyyyMMddHHmmss` compact datetime (≈2.0e13 ms) is the realistic input there, while zero-padded epochs for valid dates keep parsing because the bound is on the value, not the digit count (review feedback; earlier revision used a digit-count check that rejected valid leading-zero epochs). The CLI `parseAt` no longer falls back to its bare-number-as-milliseconds duration interpretation for pure-digit input, which had reabsorbed the rejected value as a ~642-year duration. The CLI error message now includes the raw input, and the Gateway validator's existing message already echoes `schedule.at`, which normalization now leaves untouched when parsing fails.

<details>
<summary>Root cause walkthrough</summary>

- `src/cron/parse.ts:11-17` parsed any pure-digit string as epoch ms; `20250101120000` → `2611-09-14T04:05:20.000Z`.
- The 10-year cap in `src/cron/validate-timestamp.ts` did catch it (no silently wrong scheduling), but the message showed only the derived ISO.
- Original input was destroyed pre-validation: CLI `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts` converted to ISO, and Gateway `src/cron/normalize.ts:72-74` rewrote `at` to the derived ISO when parsing succeeded.
- Second absorption path: `parseAt`'s duration fallback parses bare numbers as milliseconds (`src/cli/parse-duration.ts:48-52`), turning the rejected compact date into "now + 20250101120000 ms" ≈ year 2668.

</details>

## Evidence

Targeted tests (169/169 passed, incl. new zero-padded-epoch regression that fails on the previous revision): `src/cron/{parse,validate-timestamp,normalize,schedule}.test.ts`, `src/cli/cron-cli/{shared,trigger-options,schedule-options.positional,schedule-options.onexit}.test.ts`. Lint and format clean. Structured self-review after the value-bound revision: PASSED, no P0–P2 findings, best-fix verdict `best`.

Real-behavior proof (shipped CLI + Gateway request path), captured against a fresh isolated gateway state dir (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof-state`, loopback port 19008, token auth); the dir and test jobs were removed after capture.

### Proof A — shipped CLI rejects the compact input (exit 1)

```
$ pnpm openclaw cron add --name proof-at-digits --agent main --message hello --at 20250101120000
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Invalid --at \"20250101120000\". Use an ISO timestamp or a duration like 20m."
  }
}
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```

### Proof B — Gateway request path rejects with the raw input

```
$ pnpm openclaw gateway call cron.add --port 19018 --params \
    '{"name":"proof-at-digits","sessionTarget":"main","wakeMode":"now",
      "schedule":{"kind":"at","at":"20250101120000"},
      "payload":{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"proof-tick"}}' --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "gateway_request_error",
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "Invalid schedule.at: expected ISO-8601 timestamp (got 20250101120000)",
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

### Proof C — zero-padded epoch accepted (numeric-domain compatibility)

```
$ pnpm openclaw gateway call cron.add --port 19018 --params \
    '{"name":"proof-zero-padded-epoch","sessionTarget":"main","wakeMode":"now",
      "schedule":{"kind":"at","at":"01798761600000"},
      "payload":{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"proof-tick"}}' --json
{
  "id": "d1a594b7-a163-4ccf-9467-7a71a27808de",
  "schedule": { "kind": "at", "at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" },
  "state": { "nextRunAtMs": 1798761600000 },
  ...
}
```

### Proof D — persisted data still loads after a gateway restart

`cron.list` before and after a full gateway restart both return the persisted job with `schedule.at: "2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"` and `nextRunAtMs: 1798761600000` (stored `at` values are ISO after create-time normalization; the parser's accepted digit-string domain is unchanged for every value it accepted before this PR).

### Before/after parser probe (supplementary)

Temporary vitest probe (removed after capture) exercising the parser/validator directly:

Before fix (pre-PR code):
```
parseAbsoluteTimeMs => 20250101120000 2611-09-14T04:05:20.000Z
parseAt => 2611-09-14T04:05:20.000Z
validate => {"ok":false,"message":"schedule.at is too far in the future: 2611-09-14T04:05:20.000Z (584 years ahead). Maximum allowed: 10 years"}
```

After fix (this PR):
```
parseAbsoluteTimeMs => null
parseAt => null
validate => {"ok":false,"message":"Invalid schedule.at: expected ISO-8601 timestamp (got 20250101120000)"}
```

What was not tested: `tsgo` type gates could not run locally (host glibc 2.28 < 2.32 required by the native tsgo binary); covered by CI. The full `src/cron` suite (160 files) was not run locally — the 8 directly affected files were run in full; remaining cron coverage runs in PR CI.

prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,660 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Authenticated remote writes, interactive OAuth, private/Enterprise access, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption and stable-to-candidate upgrades remain unqualified.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes four Plugin SDK API diff integration failures when declaration rendering enforces checkout-local compiler inputs during release validation.

## User Impact

No runtime or public SDK behavior changes. Release validation can exercise real declaration rendering using self-contained synthetic revision installs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing native compiler fixture owner to materialize compiler API, default libraries, and the platform executable into each synthetic revision before its fake pnpm install completes. Keep declaration containment, installation/render ordering, cancellation, and unique-selector assertions intact.

This is the main-first adaptation of reviewed release repair `4e64bf37aff5835061047dfcd887b579b29d43a9`; current main already factors fixture setup through `writePnpm`, so only those call sites were adapted. Production delta: zero. Test delta: +28/-1 lines. The small helper shares install setup between the two affected test groups.

## Evidence

- Current main `d777e01d7e12bd0f69fdfb41925adb24f51b0de2`, nested workspace TMPDIR: 4 failed / 7 passed before repair; failures report declaration input escaping the synthetic revision.
- Post-fix CLI suite: all 11 tests pass through the real CLI with nested workspace TMPDIR.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, format, and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Fresh independent autoreview: P0–P2 scoped-clean; no findings.
- Native declaration boundary/subprocess siblings: 14 pass; 3 existing Windows-only skips on Linux.
- No containment or compiler-selection guard weakened; no timeout, expectation, or production change.
- Release-tooling-only scope uses `release-fast-lane`; selected CI/security/review gates remain required.

prs.title: feat(notifications): add opt-in answer and question previews
prs.body:
Closes #170854
Related: #162120, #144862, #143946.

## What Problem This Solves

People following background OpenClaw conversations must open the Control UI to see the content behind every generic completion or question notification.

## User Impact

Users can separately opt into final-answer excerpts and simple-question previews under **Detailed** notification settings. Both controls default to off. Existing Detailed account and browser preferences stay labels-only until explicit consent. Eligible questions display the exact prompt and choices; selecting the notification opens the authenticated question route.

Preview text can contain sensitive information and remain visible on lock screens or in browser/OS notification centers. Turning previews off affects future sends and cannot recall delivered notifications. Credential redaction is best effort.

**Owner decision remains open:** this proposes both answer and simple-question disclosure with independent consent. Notification owners must accept each privacy tradeoff, and the security-sensitive-change guard requires maintainer approval for the latest head before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consent belongs to the account or device layer selecting Detailed. Explicit device overrides cannot silently acquire account consent, and lowering detail clears consent at that layer.

Previews use the exact completed answer or canonical pending question. Original source identity and current recipient authority are checked before the encrypted send. Missing, retired, incognito or uncertified sources stay generic. Complex or secret questions, redaction-changing choices, and oversized envelopes also fall back to generic text. The payload-size check includes the displayed choices and preserves complete routing and metadata.

The live answer producer retains the completed projected text through transcript persistence using private publication metadata, so retiring the display tail does not remove the notification excerpt. That text is not added to the WebSocket payload.

The optional versioned question snapshot is display context, not permission to answer. The service worker retains authenticated click-through without reply actions. This feature adds no service, schema migration or protocol-version bump.

## Evidence

**Candidate:** `20a5e0a6932d24b776e796e93ff244e6b39e2b4e`, rebased onto upstream `main` at `46053391a1ad842d290563c38ca17b6aeb1d1a46`. Both independent preview opt-ins remain. Rebase conflicts preserve upstream question-access tests and use upstream's canonical session-sharing type; the redundant type file is removed. The content-test fixture now supplies the session-read preparation method added upstream. Browser proof remains pinned to its original tested revisions; current-base automated validation is listed below.

### Real-browser delivery and native click-through

An actual built Gateway and Control UI ran with synthetic isolated state. Chromium 153.0.8010.12 used a fresh temporary profile, normal dashboard/device pairing, and the shipped settings/subscription UI. Detailed initially left both preview consents off; each control was enabled separately and the preference response confirmed version 1 for each. The served UI bundle matched the tested build byte-for-byte.

A deterministic local OpenAI Responses fixture supplied the answer. Gateway HTTP/WebSocket ingress, browser push delivery, service-worker handling and notification creation were real, without transport interception or synthetic click events. The question was created through authenticated `question.request` and its production owner.

Both notification types were delivered on `fdebc827916`; answer delivery and native click-through were repeated on rebuilt `b31bb273b9e`. The subsequent review cleanups were test-only. This rebase incorporates newer upstream code; native-browser captures were not repeated, while both encrypted-delivery paths and notification UI tests passed on the rebased candidate. Browser notification readback:

```text
OpenClaw agent finished
The garden plan is ready.

OpenClaw needs an answer
Which plan should we use?
• Option A
• Option B
```

On October 13, both preview types were recorded after real external push delivery. The `b31bb273b9e` answer receipt was read at 13:50:26 UTC. Its native click-through was verified at 13:51:03 UTC. Readback came from the browser's actual service-worker notification registry, not a constructed payload.

| Route proof | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Question, native macOS click on prior head `90a9d20` | Operator screenshot showed the exact question and choices. Clicking it navigated to the matching ask route, produced a successful authenticated `question.get`, displayed both choices, and removed that notification. The repaired candidate also delivered the same question preview; a native click was not repeated on that head. |
| Answer, native macOS click on tested head `b31bb27` | From a recorded `/settings/notifications` baseline, the operator clicked the real native notification. The browser navigated to the exact chat route from its payload, established a new authenticated `connect`, and completed `chat.startup` for the matching session. The exact answer was visible and the notification registry was empty afterward. No direct route navigation or injected click event was used for this step. |
| Unauthenticated routes | A separate browser context showed the credential screen for the question, and “Conversation unavailable” / “Log in” for the answer; neither disclosed the content. |

**Native answer click proof is complete.** The operator supplied a screenshot showing the macOS notification and confirmed the click. After an initial capture was ambiguous because the chat was already open, a fresh delivered notification was clicked from Settings; the recorded baseline, exact target, new authenticated requests, visible answer and notification removal establish the complete path. Native desktop screenshots were inspected locally; only sanitized browser viewport captures are published. Temporary test-app notification settings were restored to Off, and the isolated browser, profile, Gateway and synthetic state were removed. Regular browser profiles were untouched.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized native answer click readback</summary>

Synthetic run/session identifiers are retained to show that the notification target, navigation and authenticated retrieval match. Origins, credentials and private filesystem paths are omitted.

```json
{
  "candidate": "b31bb273b9ee5d62335c7ff454a76aa9f34bd06e",
  "content": "synthetic local provider fixture",
  "notification_observed_at": "2026-10-13T13:50:26.137Z",
  "notification": {
    "title": "OpenClaw agent finished",
    "body": "The garden plan is ready.",
    "tag": "openclaw-agent-finished-82b174a3-7094-4283-9426-16cc8b193751",
    "data": {
      "url": "chat/main/dashboard/1284e8d1-9f95-4dae-82d2-20922fc96fa3",
      "explicitUrl": true
    }
  },
  "baseline_observed_at": "2026-10-13T13:50:26.433Z",
  "baseline_path": "/settings/notifications",
  "after_operator_native_click_observed_at": "2026-10-13T13:51:03.730Z",
  "operatorConfirmed": true,
  "from": "/settings/notifications",
  "to": "/chat/main/dashboard/1284e8d1-9f95-4dae-82d2-20922fc96fa3",
  "reads": [
    {
      "method": "connect",
      "ok": true
    },
    {
      "method": "chat.startup",
      "ok": true,
      "sessionKey": "agent:main:dashboard:1284e8d1-9f95-4dae-82d2-20922fc96fa3"
    }
  ],
  "answerVisible": true,
  "remainingNotifications": []
}
```

</details>

The first real-browser run uncovered a PR integration defect: persisted answers retire the live display tail, so the completed terminal event could contain an empty display override and incorrectly produce a generic push. The follow-up commit preserves the live producer's already-projected answer privately through the existing exact-publication authority. The real transcript-to-encrypted-delivery regression failed before this repair and passed afterward. Other producers retain their display override behavior; redaction, bounds, current-source checks and recipient authorization still apply.

The settings page has an inherited stale-snapshot rendering issue: normal navigation away and back was needed to display a settled subscription/preferences response. The relevant settings wiring is unchanged from the PR base; this workaround is disclosed, not claimed as repaired.

<details>
<summary>Inspected browser captures</summary>

Real subscription and both separately enabled preview consents.

![Real browser subscription with both preview consents](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65ef5ba4-62eb-465c-869a-2b2445bc7cbf)

Question after an operator native-notification click, captured on `90a9d20`.

![Question and exact choices after native notification click](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07c314d1-7055-4f5e-9aec-7ee2053e888b)

Answer after the operator's native notification click on `b31bb27`. The additional “Clicked.” chat message came from the operator during the first attempt and generated the fresh notification used for the final Settings-to-chat capture.

![Answer visible after native notification click](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa957347-3881-4b20-9177-fee251195d88)

</details>

### Automated verification

- **Rebase validation on `20a5e0a6932d24b776e796e93ff244e6b39e2b4e`:** 154 distinct focused cases pass across ten files: content projection and consent, answer authority, real encrypted delivery, question-session access, preference worker/upgrade compatibility, settings, and service-worker routing. The initial eight-file run took 90.09 seconds and exposed ten failures in the content fixture: upstream now calls `prepareRead()` before final authorization, which that mock lacked. Adding the same method supplied by upstream's sibling fixture fixed all eleven content cases; the content plus two UI files then passed in 14.34 seconds. Assertions and production authorization behavior are unchanged. Gateway-root and Gateway-methods test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and diff checks passed. Canonical P0–P2 autoreview of the integration follow-up completed scoped-clean. The repository's documented `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1` wrapper ran under Node 24.21.0 because the local `pnpm` launcher is unavailable. New-head CI is pending; CI duration is not yet available.
- **Prior-head CI failure:** [run 38428239528](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38428239528) on `29694793abd` completed with a failure in extension-package lint stripe 6: plugin-SDK boundary declaration generation timed out after 300 seconds. The failure classifier could not compare this scope with main, so attribution remains unknown. This rebase is not claimed to fix that timeout; new-head CI must establish its outcome.
- **Review follow-up on `29694793abd`:** removed the mocked answer/question retirement rows requested in ClawSweeper Revision 6 and simplified their remaining fixture branches. Real answer session-reset/lifecycle tests and encrypted question-retirement delivery retain the security contract. No production files changed; both preview types and their independent opt-ins remain.
- **Focused validation:** all 21 cases across content, answer authority, and encrypted delivery passed with Node 24.21.0 using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/event-web-push-content.test.ts src/gateway/event-web-push-answer-authority.test.ts src/gateway/event-web-push.delivery-proof.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (30.85 seconds wall time). The content suite passed all 13 cases before cleanup (24.63 seconds including cold compilation); its 11 remaining cases pass afterward. The documented direct wrapper was used because the local `pnpm` launcher could not locate its cached entrypoint. Gateway-root test typechecking, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. Canonical P0–P2 autoreview of the follow-up completed scoped-clean. That prior-head CI run later failed during plugin-SDK declaration preparation, as described above. Earlier successful runs are identified by SHA.
- **History CI failure diagnosed and repaired:** [the failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38398176206/job/115299287031) tested the merge of this PR with newer main. Main's [raw-history admission change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0cbcfbe8721360edcfbf9412e29bdbb9c1454255) caps a single raw record at 8 MiB, while the old fixture created a record above 12 MiB. The PR branch lacked that new guard, explaining the passing local replays. Applied Peter Steinberger's exact [upstream fixture repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a2509eddf05943feae7489f0619fc4b0755b20e8), preserving author credit: the record still exceeds the 6 MiB response budget but fits under the 8 MiB raw-admission cap, with every pagination assertion retained. The selected history case now passes locally (18.82-second wrapper). The [formerly failing compact job passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38406805395/job/115329157022), and the full [CI run 38406805395](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38406805395) completed successfully on `b31bb273b9e`. This successful run predates the test-only `29694793abd` follow-up and the current rebase.
- **Earlier review cleanup on `b31bb273b9e`:** removed the two redundant mocked pairing/visibility denial cases requested in review. The real encrypted-delivery tests still verify pairing revocation during preparation and denied session access. All 18 remaining content/delivery cases pass (22.16-second wrapper). Both affected test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, and canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed. The rebuilt candidate runtime passed in 88.1 seconds.
- **Answer repair on `fdebc827916`:** 90 focused cases across five files passed in 80.74 seconds, including real transcript persistence, answer authority, content/size guards and encrypted delivery. The delivery regression replaces the former hand-built success event with the production agent/transcript lifecycle; it failed before the repair.
- **Answer-repair types, build and review on `fdebc827916`:** Gateway-root and Gateway-server test typechecks passed. That runtime build passed in 48.1 seconds. Changed-file lint/format checks passed. Canonical autoreview at P0–P2 completed scoped-clean with no actionable findings, including the private-metadata/wire-serialization boundary.
- **Earlier repository check (before this rebase):** full `pnpm check` passed preflight guards and production/script/root-test typechecks, then stopped on the same 33 existing `max-lines` diagnostics. The diagnostics match the prior head exactly, and every failing file is unchanged. Later format/policy stages did not run after that lint failure.
- **Prior-head CI:** [CI run 38381201034](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38381201034) passed for `90a9d20893aa51d73211034a3560986b497a6939` with 68 successful and 21 skipped jobs. This older run is not claimed as candidate-head CI.
- **Earlier feature verification:** the question display regression, source-lifetime/service-worker cases, five encrypted-delivery cases and released-state upgrade lifecycle all passed in the preceding 91-case follow-up. Unchanged upgrade coverage was not rerun for the answer repair.

<details>
<summary>Encrypted delivery and released-state upgrade evidence</summary>

prs.title: fix(workers): recover cloud sessions after their node process exits
prs.body:
Related: #188796 ## What Problem This Solves An attached cloud session can wait for a reconnect that cannot happen after its enrolled node process exits, even though the dedicated worker and workspace still exist. Retained-worker wake can reach the same dead end before ordinary runtime recovery runs. ## User Impact Recover the same enrolled node on eligible dedicated Linux Crabbox workers without allocating a replacement, reinstalling the runtime, pairing again, rerunning repository setup or replaying interrupted input. Preserve the resource binding, identity, configuration and workspace. Unsupported providers, desktop workers and records without saved runtime identity retain reconnect-only behavior; older runtime packages without the private consumer need an update or manual recovery. Adopt released [Crabbox v0.81.0](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/releases/tag/v0.81.0) through the canonical managed-distribution owner. It contains the landed native command-lifetime repair in [Crabbox #3001](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/3001). Existing configured distributions are not overwritten. No new public timeout/configuration, schema, retention policy, paid allocation or live deployment. ## Why This Change Was Made - Add an optional provider recovery operation under the existing runtime-refresh owner. Current requester/attachment/owner authority, an active dedicated inspection and the exact persisted resource receipt must qualify launch. - Retained wake already holds the environment operation lock. It calls the same internal resumer before waiting for reconnect, without reacquiring that lock or creating a second lifecycle owner. Current main's retention, prepared-intent, lease-inspection and bootstrap owners remain intact. - Compose two ordinary existing Crabbox invocations: read-only saved identity/runtime inspection, fresh host authority assertion, then separately admitted launch. Launch repeats package/PID checks; the canonical runner verifies the saved device, configuration and paired credential. - Private launcher IPC prevents an uncommitted detached child from entering the node runtime after its owner disappears. Publish the PID receipt atomically before commitment and wait for actual child exit on precommit cancellation. Retain an uncertain committed process/receipt for a subsequent probe rather than blindly replaying it. - Use one measured private 120-second work budget across both phases, still bounded by caller admission. Forward the existing cleanup-grace option with 20 seconds for this operation so the controller can finish its existing 15-second cleanup and full 5-second native TERM grace. No new public Crabbox command protocol, identity reader or core manager. ## Evidence ### Source and focused regression coverage Qualified local commit 4a9976e91405f709f96c085ecb933efa8658ba15, tree ac40b5077f476fa38e29d8f561ac5252144dfc9e, integrated with pinned main b2ceef2b5a5fbd8c88ff8497b8a986c692204141 because the published branch conflicted. All 16 production modules match the source-bound released-runtime proof. - Exercised all 11 affected/helper test files across their six owning shards (261 cases in the initial cohort). Preserved failures rather than treating them as flakes: an obsolete offline-cache version, an invalid dormant inspection fixture, an incorrect seeded-credential assumption and unread stderr in the launcher disconnect fixture. - Final complete retained-lifecycle and managed-binary suites: **10 + 33 passed**. Both launcher commit/disconnect cases pass with normal stderr draining and unchanged timeout/assertions. Unmodified passing cases were reused; exact published-head CI is separate evidence. - **Owning-boundary RED control:** both new retained service regressions fail with the exact pre-fix retained owner from pinned main: no restart before reconnect wait, and a replacement resource is not rejected. The qualified owner was restored byte-for-byte; both cases pass with the fix. This is an exact owning-module control within the integration, not a claim that the entire base checkout was tested. - Targeted TypeScript, type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace and test-line gates pass. Allocation is exactly **828** net regression lines; the shared baseline is unchanged. - Fresh independent production and final regression reviews found no actionable P0–P3 issues. Committed-range autoreview is **scoped-clean**, with no findings. Its static-review limits do not replace executed runtime proof or CI. ### Actual released controller/native runtime Canonical installation and resolution selected the released distribution with normal adjacent-pack discovery, not a private artifact override: | Input | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | | Linux amd64 release archive | 1d25267b161c1ac6c12c15cd7c4cb96a49a8c1622d365fb932f3ef3bd3123d33 | | Controller | 20d0cb5b592f339a2928139909f1f95990f28f7a03558ee9f570bf9171f3876c | | Adjacent native manifest | f0a5abfc81ccbf1e8f9e8efd61a271dfb97c56110f271c225efeeb7a54985d16 | | Linux amd64 native runtime | 2fa8b9ac1250bdbbe6f291c2084bd1ae0f46a34337ba962de9c7474060f88c7b | An isolated Gateway, genuinely paired node and real OpenSSH ran inside task-owned rootless Debian. The full current generated enrollment/trust command ran real certificate registration before node launch, without modifying host trust. | Case | Observed result | | --- | --- | | Same-device reconnect | 74.1 seconds; existing device/runtime/workspace retained | | Retry | 70.2 seconds; reused the same committed PID and device | | Cancel held read-only identity inspection | Child exited; original dead-PID receipt unchanged; five exact retirements before return | | Revoke host authority during held inspection | Fresh host assertion rejects launch; no new connection; five exact retirements before return | | Cancel actual detached child before commit | Child exited; original receipt preserved; no later node effect; ten exact retirements before return | Recovery and retry each confirmed ten native completion/retirement records before provider return. Production 20-second cleanup and full 5-second native grace were not shortened. A delayed/unobservable remote wrapper remains explicitly uncertain: local exit or absent remote state is never remote quiescence and does not authorize automatic replay. ### Proof limits and retained failures - Two original cancellation harness runs exited 1 because the old oracle counted the canonical enrollment's initial connection. Their raw reports remain failed; an independent corrected oracle verifies no new connection, actual child exit, unchanged receipt and exact retirement. They are not relabeled as original-script exit-zero runs. - QA used the canonical npm-verification branch, not fresh bootstrap-archive installation. The released controller and adjacent native inputs were hashed and real native dispatch/receipts observed; an independent remote executable rehash was not captured before normal cleanup. - The earlier one-shot authority failure and v0.80 retirement defect remain historical evidence. The existing-API split addresses the reported held-probe case; a new public commit protocol was not necessary. Earlier maintenance CI was never proof that the one-shot implementation was safe to ship. - This is local Linux/static-SSH and service-boundary proof, not a new paid cloud allocation or a replay of separate R5/installed acceptance runs. No live Gateway/profile deployment or new Crabbox release occurred. All 15 owned proof containers and three task images were removed after verifying they were stopped; no proof Gateway/node/sshd remains. A temporary compiler-input scan conflict from the proof image filesystem was resolved by owned-resource cleanup, not a guard/ignore change. Original failure logs and source/artifact receipts are retained. Contributor credit: @galiniliev authored the S4 source commit `9501dfaa8de7426a02badffd918e8eddc75c9e27` that informed this bounded extraction, reimplemented against current upstream owners at his request. ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1c21e0ea-e918-4f4d-a25f-a46256a029bd) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/d50d6742-c669-438e-9779-276e1117ca73) - [Existing-command split review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/8769e9c5-906b-4f16-988d-626eac19a170) - [CI synthetic-merge compatibility repair](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4489e496-7aa8-43f3-a3fa-d3a5939bee9a) - [Final canonical-owner maintenance review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b1e047e9-2553-47d0-adb4-788ba261b590) - [Final cancellation and settlement review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/9fc975e2-8c3b-426a-a370-b55eaccbc29d)
Earlier verification sessions - [Exact-base Stop recovery attribution](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/fafc6631-200a-4324-9b09-b753b63b4048) - [Real transport cancellation investigation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f1c1f0fb-88a9-4f27-9a1d-8f1e187e824b) - [CI synchronization follow-up](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/390ea07d-039d-4083-9d51-32d016ee34c7) - [Local Crabbox controller preparation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/92b15a87-7505-4ee6-9fb5-625340e35cf8) - [Final bounded independent review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/2136e4a4-fa16-4804-8ee2-ac906264351f)

prs.title: fix(config): keep config set secrets redacted when a value option precedes the positionals
prs.body:
Fixes #190075

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set` records the new value in the clear in the local config-audit record when a value-taking option such as `--expect-current-json` appears before the config path and value, even when that path is secret-bearing.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator who runs the documented conditional write with the option first — `openclaw config set --expect-current-json <json> <secret-path> <secret>` — no longer gets that secret stored unredacted in `<state>/state/openclaw.sqlite` (`diagnostic_events`, scope `config-audit`, latest 50000 rows). The same command with the option after the positionals already redacted correctly; both orders do now. No config format, CLI surface, or default behavior changes, and no migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`findConfigPositionals` decides which `config set` arguments are the path and the value, so it must skip the value of every value-taking option; `CONFIG_SET_VALUE_OPTIONS` is that hand-maintained contract. `--expect-current-json` is registered on `config set` (`src/cli/config-cli.ts:375-378`) but was missing from the set, so its JSON payload was counted as the path · `src/config/io.audit.ts:71-79`. The sensitive-path check then evaluated the payload instead of the real path and skipped the value · `src/config/io.audit.ts:114-123`. Adding the missing entry restores the order-independent positional discovery the list exists to provide; it is the only `config set` value option absent from the list. Repair classification: behavior-completing.

## Evidence

Rebased head: base `fa0bc65a7d` (current `main`) → candidate `2cae560f02`. The live CLI before/after proof below was captured on the original pair `482631a7d880f41588fc33540ecd8b188033d2b3` → `32f7ef384bb722af723514268824a5ed8fbe1b06`; both built with `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts`, each run using its own isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, read back with a read-only `node:sqlite` query against the state DB.

BEFORE (base) — the record keeps the value:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE node openclaw.mjs config set models.providers.openai.apiKey SEED_VALUE_AAA
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE node openclaw.mjs config set --expect-current-json '"SEED_VALUE_AAA"' \
    models.providers.openai.apiKey PROOF_SECRET_9F3E2D

argv: [".../node",".../openclaw.mjs","config","set","--expect-current-json","\"SEED_VALUE_AAA\"","models.providers.openai.apiKey","PROOF_SECRET_9F3E2D"]
needlePresent: true
```

AFTER (candidate) — same command, same persisted config value, record redacted:

```text
argv: [".../node",".../openclaw.mjs","config","set","--expect-current-json","\"SEED_VALUE_AAA\"","models.providers.openai.apiKey","***"]
needlePresent: false
```

Controls:

| Control | Result |
|---|---|
| Documented order (option after the positionals, `channels.slack.token`) | redacted `***` before and after |
| Non-sensitive path (`--expect-current-json 19001 gateway.port 19002`) | `19002` still recorded in the clear after the fix (no over-redaction) |

Focused test at the rebased head — `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.config.ts src/config/io.audit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`:

| Head | Result | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| `fa0bc65a7d` with the unpatched `io.audit.ts` | 1 failed \| 18 passed — the new option-before case persists `secret-value` where `***` is expected | ~11s |
| candidate `2cae560f02` | 19 passed | 11.3s |

Added cases follow the existing `redacts %j in persisted audit process info` table: the option-before regression and an option-after order control. `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on both changed files.

Not tested: no live Gateway process was started; the audit record is written by the `openclaw` CLI process itself, which is the writer under test. Broad suites are left to CI.

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- **Land-ready why:** one-line production change inside the existing owner, plus a table case; the invariant is already documented by the sibling entries.
- **Alternatives considered:** deriving the set from Commander's option metadata (larger change, new coupling) and clearing the record's argv entirely (drops the diagnostic value this list exists to preserve while redacting).
- **Scope:** `config set` positional discovery and its audit redaction only; no other command, schema, or output path is touched.
- **Precedent:** the sibling entries (`--batch-json`, `--ref-*`, `--provider-*`) already encode order-independent positional discovery; the same rule was recently applied to option-order handling in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-export-common.ts`.
- Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Impact surface</summary>

| File:line | Risk |
|---|---|
| `src/config/io.audit.ts:28` | Adds one member to the value-option set; only affects argv scanning for `config set` audit records. |
| `src/config/io.audit.test.ts:189` | Two new table rows; no shared harness change. |

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): reject reserved __proto__ keys in provider-env and mcp env/header
prs.body:
Fixes #190074

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw config set ... --provider-env` and `openclaw mcp add --env/--header` accept `KEY=VALUE` entries and build them into a plain object with `entries[key] = value`. When the key is `__proto__`, that assignment hits `Object.prototype`'s legacy setter instead of creating an own property, so the entry is silently dropped — the command still exits 0 and writes the config, just without the requested key. No warning, no error, nothing in the written file.

This is the same failure mode the repository already guards against at the MCP server-name boundary (`src/config/zod-schema.root-support.ts`):

```ts
// Plain assignment treats "__proto__" as a setter, so one unhardened map builder
// can silently drop the server. Reject the name at the config boundary instead.
```

This change applies that same principle to the two CLI `KEY=VALUE` boundaries: instead of dropping a reserved key silently, reject it with a message that names the flag and the key.

## User Impact

- An operator who passes `--provider-env __proto__=…` (or `mcp add --env/--header __proto__=…`) now gets an actionable error instead of a silently incomplete config.
- No change for any other key: normal entries are parsed and written exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The silent drop happens at the point the CLI parses each entry, so the guard is added there — that is also where the message can name the offending flag (`--provider-env`, `--env`, `--header`), which a schema-level error cannot.

- `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts` — `parseProviderEnvEntries` rejects a `__proto__` key.
- `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts` — `parseKeyValueEntries` (used by both `--env` and `--header`) rejects a `__proto__` key.

Scope follows the existing precedent exactly: only `__proto__` is rejected (the key that is silently dropped). `constructor`/`prototype` are not touched — plain assignment to those keys creates ordinary own properties, so they are not affected by this bug.

## Evidence

### Control-red: same commands, base vs this change

Run through the real CLI entry (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …`) with an isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.

| Scenario | Base (`main`) | This change |
|---|---|---|
| `config set secrets.providers.runner --provider-source exec --provider-command <cmd> --provider-env __proto__=injected --provider-env NORMAL_KEY=control` | exit `0`, no error, written `env` keys = `["NORMAL_KEY"]` (`__proto__` dropped) | exit `1`, `--provider-env key "__proto__" is reserved; use a different key name.`, nothing written |
| `mcp add probe --command <cmd> --no-probe --env __proto__=injected --env NORMAL_KEY=control` | exit `0`, no error, written `env` keys = `["NORMAL_KEY"]` (`__proto__` dropped) | exit `1`, `--env key "__proto__" is reserved; use a different key name.`, nothing written |
| `mcp add probe --url https://mcp.example.test/mcp --no-probe --header __proto__=injected --header X-Normal=control` | exit `0`, no error, written `headers` keys = `["X-Normal"]` (`__proto__` dropped) | exit `1`, `--header key "__proto__" is reserved; use a different key name.`, nothing written |

Raw JSON from the proof (base):

```json
{
  "providerEnv": { "exitCode": 0, "stderrHasError": false, "writtenEnvKeys": ["NORMAL_KEY"] },
  "mcpEnv":     { "exitCode": 0, "stderrHasError": false, "writtenMsKeys": ["NORMAL_KEY"] },
  "mcpHeader":  { "exitCode": 0, "stderrHasError": false, "writtenHeaderKeys": ["X-Normal"] }
}
```

Raw JSON after the change:

```json
{
  "providerEnv": { "exitCode": 1, "stderrFirstLine": "--provider-env key \"__proto__\" is reserved; use a different key name.", "writtenEnvKeys": [] },
  "mcpEnv":     { "exitCode": 1, "stderrFirstLine": "--env key \"__proto__\" is reserved; use a different key name.", "writtenMsKeys": [] },
  "mcpHeader":  { "exitCode": 1, "stderrFirstLine": "--header key \"__proto__\" is reserved; use a different key name.", "writtenHeaderKeys": [] }
}
```

### Regression tests

Added cases assert the rejection and that no config is written, for both boundaries:

- `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — `rejects a reserved __proto__ provider env key before writing`
- `src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts` — `rejects a reserved __proto__ key in --env and --header before writing`

```
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  72 passed (72)
```

```
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.mcpcheck.config.ts
 Tests  33 passed | 1 failed (34)
```

(`src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts` is excluded from the default CLI project and needs the host-owned SQLite broker, so it was run through an isolated scoped config.)

The single failure is a pre-existing environment failure on this host — `requires initialize to finish within the configured probe timeout before saving` — which spawns a probe child process; it fails identically on the unmodified base and is unrelated to this change (the new test passes in isolation).

### Lint

```
$ oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json src/cli/config-cli-input.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

### Types

Scoped `tsgo` over the changed files reports no errors in `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts` or `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts`. The remaining errors in the run are pre-existing dependency gaps in unrelated files (`pg`, `@resvg/resvg-js`, `@openclaw/proc-safe`) and are identical on the base.

### Sibling check

`gh search prs` for `__proto__ env`, `reserved prototype`, and `parseKeyValueEntries` returns no open or closed PR touching these two sites. This is distinct from #171770, which preserves `__proto__` keys in plain runtime maps (`cron` command env / process-env merge); the sites here flow into config that is validated through `z.record`, where the key is dropped regardless, so rejection — not preservation — is the correct fix and matches the existing boundary precedent.

prs.title: fix(git): run branch-read retry deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Branch discovery can stay stuck on an unavailable or non-Git result after a backward wall-clock correction, even after the repository becomes usable.

## User Impact

A later branch-picker request can retry after the existing five-second elapsed-time window instead of waiting for the wall clock to catch up. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing monotonicNow owner for the private in-memory retry comparison and both deadline writes. Retry duration, watchers, invalidation, Git worker, refresh behavior, continuation authority and public types are unchanged. Epoch timestamps and persisted state are untouched.

Preserves @wangmiao0668000666's fix and original commit. Parameterizes the existing real owner-boundary regression for no step and rollback rather than adding a separate replay; test-source growth is zero and no allocation is added.

## Evidence

[Six public Gateway/real-Git timing traces](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191982#issuecomment-6607776706)

Built Gateway worktrees.branches RPC with real Git on Node 24.22.1: main twice remains stale after a process-local one-hour Date.now rollback and ancestor Git initialization; candidate twice retries after the normal elapsed window. Immediate post-init snapshots prove no watcher invalidation. No forced refresh; no-step controls are unchanged. The host/system clock is never changed.

34 focused tests, typed lint and formatting pass; the final regression fails on main only for rollback. Production +4/-3, tests +3/-3 (net zero), docs +2.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: revert restores the wall-clock retry behavior, with no state migration or stored-data changes. Blast radius is process-local negative/failed branch-discovery retry timing; normal branch results, authorization, duration and watcher invalidation remain unchanged.
