prs.title: fix(feishu): keep the sender-name cache on elapsed time
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

Maintainer edits to this branch are welcome and will not be overwritten; the author will not force-push over them.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- **Land-ready:** one owner (`extensions/feishu/src/bot-sender-name.ts`), behavior-preserving clock-domain substitution at all three private timestamp sites, deterministic red/green on base plus a real-transport decision table. No config, API, schema, or state change.
- **Alternatives:** keep the wall clock (accepts the defect); import the core `monotonicNow()` owner (extensions cannot depend on core internals — the established extension shape is inline `performance.now()`); change TTL durations (out of scope — durations unchanged).
- **Scope:** sender-name cache only (resolved entries and the 41050 account-scoped miss window). The sibling display-name cache ships separately.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

A host wall-clock correction while the Gateway runs makes the Feishu sender-name cache jump with it: a forward step expires a fresh 10-minute entry and reissues the `contact.user` lookup, while a backward step keeps resolved names and the 30-minute account-scoped miss window alive far past their intended elapsed windows.

## User Impact

On a long-running Gateway whose clock is corrected (NTP step, manual change, VM resume), message attribution either loses the cached sender name and spends Feishu API quota on duplicate `contact.user` lookups, or keeps serving stale names beyond their windows. This is the default-on path: `resolveSenderNames` defaults to `true` and resolves every human-sender message through this cache. TTL values are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`extensions/feishu/src/bot-sender-name.ts` keeps `senderNameCache` as a process-local map whose timestamps never leave the module — grep-verified: no persistence, serialization, or cross-process exchange. The read and write sites now share the elapsed-time domain (`performance.now()`), the only domain a wall-clock step cannot shift; switching one side alone would mix clock domains, so all three sites move together. Known trade-off, identical to the core stale-while-revalidate cache owner: monotonic windows measure awake time, so system suspend pauses them. Fix classification: behavior-preserving (clock domain only; no TTL, owner, config, or API change).

## Evidence

Base `29e5360e957886bf47810b72dfe25dca44250e96` → candidate `244f04e0188c3ee107222b228e7f5bd3bd4a96cd` (this branch), same commands. Evidence tiers: (1) the resolver `bot.ts` calls through a real Lark SDK client over loopback TLS with real timers, and (2) **the shipped Gateway entry point** (webhook POST → Gateway → handler → SDK) below. In both tiers the wall step is a process-local `Date.now` offset (the #190894/#188293 preload method), never an OS clock jump.

Deterministic regressions in the existing suite (remote Node 24.22.1 container, `vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts`):

| `extensions/feishu/src/bot-sender-name.test.ts` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Base | **2 failed / 5 passed** — exactly the 2 new wall-clock cases fail |
| Candidate | **7 passed** |

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/bot-sender-name.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Real-transport decision table (temporary probe, removed before commit): `resolveFeishuSenderName` driven through the real SDK; decision metric = server-side `contact/v3/users` request count at a local HTTPS fixture.

| Scenario | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No-step control, double resolve | 1 request (passes) | 1 request |
| +61 min wall step, elapsed time fresh | **2 requests — premature refetch** (`expected 2 to be 1`) | **1 request — retained** |

Candidate probe: **1/1 passed**. Candidate trace: `POST /open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal` + `GET /open-apis/contact/v3/users/ou_probe_ok?user_id_type=open_id`, then cache reuse with no second GET; after the +61 min step still a single `GET …ou_probe_fwd`.

**Controls:** no-step reuse passes on both refs (no over-blocking; ordinary freshness intact). The backward direction for this module's 10-minute window is covered by the deterministic fake-timer regression (`expires … after elapsed time even when the wall clock rewinds`, red on base) rather than a real 10-minute wait.

### Shipped Gateway entry (stronger tier, 2026-11-04)

The same decision metric at the real product entry — closing the gap the review named ("the strongest proof is an in-process resolver exercise rather than a shipped Gateway entry point"):

- Normally built Gateway from this exact base/candidate (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime` → `dist/entry.js`, reports `OpenClaw 2026.10.10`) in a secretless Node 24.22.1 container on Linux 3.10 (KVM guest), `gateway.mode:"local"` bound to loopback, `channels.feishu.connectionMode:"webhook"`.
- Signed `im.message.receive_v1` webhook POSTs to the Gateway's real `/feishu/events` route flow through the shipped ingress → `EventDispatcher` → `handleFeishuMessage` → the shipped Lark SDK client (custom `https://127.0.0.1` origin, real TLS, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`) into a counting mock of the Lark Open API. `counts.unknown` is empty in every cell: a p2p text DM makes zero API calls before name resolution (`bot.ts:253`), so the mock counts *are* the decision metric.
- Between the two events the **process-local `Date.now` steps +11 min** via an `--import` preload: no OS clock change; `performance.now` and timers untouched. +11 min clears the 10-minute TTL and stays inside the webhook's ±1-hour signature freshness; the negative-cache cells step +31 min (> the 30-minute miss window, < 1 hour).
- Synthetic credentials only, loopback only, no live Feishu tenant, no agent turn (default `dmPolicy:"pairing"` stops the synthetic senders after name resolution, where the metric lives).

| Cell (tree · mode) | step | sender lookups expected | observed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base · positive | +11 min | 2 — premature refetch | **2** |
| base · positive control | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| **candidate · positive** | +11 min | **1 — retained** | **1** |
| candidate · positive control | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| base · 41050 negative cache | +31 min | 2 — miss window spuriously expired | **2** |
| **candidate · 41050 negative cache** | +31 min | **1 — miss window holds** | **1** |
| candidate · cross-control: bot display-name probe (file untouched by this PR) | +11 min | stays at base behavior: 2 | **2** |

Cross-control: under the identical step the sibling probe still counts 2 on this candidate — the harness steps the clock for every process cache; only this PR's file flips. The injected miss answers HTTP 404 `{code: 41050}` exactly as the product's axios-style extraction expects (`comment-shared.ts` reads `error.response.data.code`), so the negative-entry write/read sites are exercised, not simulated. Repro: per tree the build above, then one container per cell running the orchestrator (loopback TLS mock + `openclaw.mjs gateway run` with the preload + signed webhook POSTs + `GET /__counts`); per-cell `gw.log`/`mock.log`/`counts.json` retained off-repo.

**Reachability (not a theoretical edge):** the proof host is a KVM guest (`kvm-clock`) and its `/var/log/messages` records the wall clock running 2026-11-02 → 2026-01-01 → 2026-11-03 across boots — a multi-month step of exactly this class; merged [#190894](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190894) fixed the same defect class at Gateway entry points with this preload method.

**Not tested:** no live Feishu account round-trip; an isolated leaf `tsc` cannot resolve unbuilt `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` declarations in an unbuilt tree (pre-existing environment gap affecting untouched files equally) — exact-head PR CI supplies broad typecheck.

**Cleanup:** the probe file, local HTTPS fixture, and the Gateway-matrix orchestrator (mock, event builder, preload) are never committed; synthetic `cli_probe` credentials only; no production Gateway, config, state, or credentials touched.

## Precedent

Sibling: #191911 (same motif, adjacent cache owner).

Same accepted shape: [#191606](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191606) (private cache TTLs on elapsed time), [#182180](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182180) (Feishu registration poll on the monotonic clock), [#191165](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191165) (directory cache on elapsed time).

prs.title: fix(cron): give managed backup schedules an archive-sized budget
prs.body:
Fixes: #170241

Sibling: #170450 gives the backup's Git content commands the same content-sized budget at the `git` layer.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw backup enable --to <location>` builds a managed cron job whose command payload carries no execution budget, so a scheduled offsite archive inherits cron's generic ten-minute command deadline. A whole-installation archive is sized by the data (tens of GB, hours), so every scheduled run past ten minutes was aborted and recorded as a timeout — the native schedule could never succeed on a real install, and the operator had to patch `payload.timeoutSeconds` by hand with `cron.update`.

Cron already honors an explicit per-job budget at both of its deadline layers; the managed-backup owner simply never declared one:

- the scheduler watchdog, `resolveCronJobTimeoutMs` (`src/cron/service/timeout-policy.ts:28`), reads `payload.timeoutSeconds` first and otherwise applies `DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS` = 600000;
- the command runner, `runCronCommandJob` (`src/cron/command-runner.ts:130`), reads the same field before falling back to `DEFAULT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` = 600000.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildBackupScheduleJob` (`src/cron/backup-command.ts:83`, payload at `:122`, constant at `:29`) now stamps `timeoutSeconds: SCHEDULED_BACKUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (24 hours) on the command payload the managed-backup owner writes, so the schedule is self-describing and rides the existing `payload.timeoutSeconds` contract at both layers.

No scheduler policy changes. `resolveCronJobTimeoutMs` and `runCronCommandJob` are byte-identical to `main`: the ten-minute cron default, which exists so one stuck job cannot wedge the cron lane, still applies to every job that does not declare its own budget, and cron gains no backup-specific branch. The 24-hour value stays a finite ceiling rather than an unbounded wait (`timeoutSeconds: 0`, the only unbounded form, is untouched).

An explicit `timeoutSeconds` on the job still wins while the schedule is left alone. No flag, configuration, schema, protocol, or persistence surface is added.

A schedule written by an earlier release keeps the generic deadline until it is enabled again. `backup enable` writes through `cron.add`, whose declarative converge path (`applyDeclarativeJobSpec`, `src/cron/service/jobs.ts:499`) replaces the entire command payload, so re-running it with the same mode and target re-stamps the budget **and** drops any override a later `cron edit` left on the job (`--timeout-seconds`, staging `payload.env`). `docs/cli/backup.md` states that, and the run under Evidence shows it.

Revision notes: this head corrects the earlier claim that an explicit timeout always survives a refresh. The previous head removed the fallback that made the cron timeout policy resolve a backup budget for stored schedules with no payload timeout; that fallback changed an existing owner-built default retroactively, which is why the review held the PR for a maintainer decision. The budget now lives only in the declaration the backup owner already owns.

Production LOC is `+12/-1` in one file (the constant and its comment, plus the payload field); tests `+5`; docs `+7`. Total `+24/-1` across three files.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

A newly enabled scheduled Git or offsite backup larger than the generic ten-minute command budget runs to completion instead of being killed and recorded as a timeout. An install that already carries such a schedule re-runs `openclaw backup enable` with the same mode and target once to pick the budget up. An operator override set with `cron edit` keeps winning until the schedule is enabled again, at which point it is replaced by the declared budget and has to be reapplied. Unrelated command jobs are untouched.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `043ff745105fa153557ba43a822a7af01130063c`. Relative to `1b32faa6a683`, the producer change is comment-only and the two fallback files are gone; relative to `96982b9ed0a`, only `docs/cli/backup.md` changed (the refresh contract). The emitted payload is unchanged across all three heads.
- Current-main RED baseline: branch point `e8b8942affd`. Every file this PR touches or reverts is byte-identical on `origin/main` `4b7cf5946b8` (per-path blob comparison), so both the defect and the reverted fallback sit on the current base.
- Production entry: the production builder `buildBackupScheduleJob`, the scheduler decision `resolveCronJobTimeoutMs`, and the real cron command runner `runCronCommandJob` (`src/cron/command-runner.ts:94`).
- Decision surface: `payload.timeoutSeconds` on a managed backup schedule, and the resolved wall-clock budget at both layers.
- Recorder/readback boundary: the resolved budget in milliseconds, the run outcome (`ok` / `command timed out`), the stamped payload read back from the Gateway, and wall-clock elapsed ms.
- Cleanup: every run used an isolated temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and a scratch Git-free probe; no production Gateway, session, channel, token, config, or backup repository was touched.

### RED -> GREEN: the persisted payload

RED (production file reverted to `main`, recorded at the base):

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/backup-schedule.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 FAIL  scheduled backups > adds one isolated command job with the selected Git backup argv
 FAIL  scheduled backups > round-trips offsite CLI options with explicit claim=false …
 FAIL  scheduled backups > round-trips offsite CLI options with explicit claim=true …
   (persisted payload lacks "timeoutSeconds": 86400)
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  3 failed | 19 passed (22)
```

GREEN (exact head `96982b9ed0a`):

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/backup-schedule.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  22 passed (22)
   Duration  41.00s

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cron/service/timeout-policy.test.ts src/cron/command-runner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
   Duration  37.00s   [test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 46.38s
```

The three-file run (`[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 177.60s`) is the wall time this PR adds to `checks-node-changed-*`.

### Shipped Gateway: a stamped schedule outlives the generic deadline

Recorded at `1b32faa`, whose builder emits the identical payload and whose two consumers are now the literal `main` files, so the path under test is unchanged: a dist built from that head ran a real out-of-process Gateway (`plugins.enabled=false`), and three managed backup schedules ran through the shipped cron scheduler. The scheduled command is a PATH stub whose body lasts 630 s — the *deadline* is what is under test; the alternative is tens of GB of real dumps.

```text
$ node dist/index.js cron list --json          # stored payloads
0e6b6a8b-30d2-48a2-be95-5952dde8882e openclaw-backup-offsite-scheduled | timeoutSeconds= 86400      # B, stamped by the head CLI

$ node dist/index.js cron runs --all --json    # after cron run <id> for B
0e6b6a8b… ok    | durationMs= 630096 | SCHEDULED_BACKUP_COMMAND_DONE      # B: 630 s > 600 s

$ node dist/index.js cron edit <B> --timeout-seconds 30
$ node dist/index.js cron runs --all --json
0e6b6a8b… error | durationMs= 30100  | command timed out                  # explicit 30 s still wins
```

The same run also confirmed `payload.env` handling is untouched and that the retained schedule loads and runs from the same stored state the head Gateway opened.

### Shipped upgrade from the released 2026.10.3 build, then the refresh (exact head)

The release was installed into an isolated prefix (`npm install openclaw@2026.10.3`) and used to create a real Gateway-owned managed backup schedule in an isolated state directory; both operator overrides were applied with the released CLI. This is installed-release state, not a hand-seeded shape.

```text
$ openclaw --version                      # the released build that wrote the state
OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (59cb447)

$ openclaw cron list --json               # released state, before any candidate interaction
RELEASE_STATE: {"declarationKey":"openclaw-backup-scheduled","id":"2a5457a6-…",
 "payload":{"argv":["openclaw","backup","git","create","--repository","/…/repo","--all"],
 "env":{"PROOF_STAGING":"1"},"kind":"command","timeoutSeconds":30}}
PRAGMA user_version = 20                  # state schema written by the release
```

The candidate head then opened the same state directory:

```text
$ node dist/index.js --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.2 (043ff74)
[state/db] state database schema migration pending; verifying integrity first
PRAGMA user_version = 21                  # migrated in place, 20 -> 21

$ node dist/index.js cron list --json     # stored operator settings survive the upgrade
BEFORE_REFRESH: {"declarationKey":"openclaw-backup-scheduled","id":"2a5457a6-…",
 "payload":{"argv":["openclaw","backup","git","create","--repository","/…/repo","--all"],
 "env":{"PROOF_STAGING":"1"},"kind":"command","timeoutSeconds":30}}

$ node dist/index.js cron run <id> --json
{"ok":true,"enqueued":true,"runId":"cron-request.9b573136-…"}     # stored schedule admitted and executed after the upgrade

$ node dist/index.js backup enable --repository <repo>            # the documented refresh, same mode and target
Scheduled Git backups updated: every 24h to $OPENCLAW_HOME/repo

$ node dist/index.js cron list --json     # same job id, payload re-stamped
AFTER_REFRESH: {"declarationKey":"openclaw-backup-scheduled","id":"2a5457a6-…",
 "payload":{"argv":["openclaw","backup","git","create","--repository","/…/repo","--all"],
 "kind":"command","timeoutSeconds":86400}}
```

Same job id (updated in place), the operator's `timeoutSeconds: 30` and `payload.env` replaced by the declaration, and the archive-sized budget stamped — exactly what `docs/cli/backup.md` now states.

The scheduled command's own nested `openclaw` resolves through the host's login-shell `PATH`, which on this proof host puts a stale global install first (`OpenClaw 2026.9.9`, schema 19); that older build refuses the migrated schema-21 state, so the nested invocation exits non-zero with a schema refusal. That is a property of this host (an older global CLI ahead of the candidate on `PATH`) and reproduces for any command job, not of this change; the deadline and payload contract under test are unaffected.

For completeness, the same payload assignment seen in isolation, driven directly against the real converge function at `043ff745105`:

```text
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof-170406-reenable.mts
{"step":"stored","payload":{"kind":"command","argv":["openclaw","backup","create","--to","proof","--namespace","proof"],"timeoutSeconds":30,"env":{"PROOF_STAGING":"1"}}}
{"step":"after-reenable","payload":{"kind":"command","argv":["openclaw","backup","create","--to","proof","--namespace","proof"],"timeoutSeconds":86400}}
{"step":"delta","explicitTimeoutPreserved":false,"envPreserved":false}
```

Cleanup: both Gateways used isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`HOME`, a fake token, and a scratch Git repository; no production Gateway, session, channel, token, config, or backup repository was touched.

### Not tested / scope

- A managed schedule with **no** payload budget (the shape earlier releases wrote, `git show v2026.10.2:src/cron/backup-command.ts` has `payload: { kind: "command", argv }`) keeps the generic ten-minute deadline until `backup enable` re-stamps it. That is the deliberate scope of this revision; it is no longer auto-covered. The earlier shipped run shows that stored shape still loads and executes (it ran to the generic 600-second deadline), so existing data keeps working; it simply keeps the old deadline until the operator re-enables the schedule.
- A real multi-gigabyte archive longer than ten minutes was not produced (tens of GB of dumps plus a configured storage location). The shipped runs exercise the scheduler with the production job shape and a stub command body, so the deadline is what is proven, not archive internals.
- The upgrade trace above runs the released 2026.10.3 package itself; the earlier revision of this body seeded that shape by hand, which the review correctly rejected as insufficient.
- The full repository suite and type-aware lint were not run locally; CI covers them.

<details>
<summary>Scope, blast radius, and alternatives considered</summary>

**Blast radius:** one field on the payload of the job `backup enable` creates or updates. Nothing else reads it beyond the two deadline layers that already read `payload.timeoutSeconds` for every job kind.

**Existing schedules:** handled by the producer, not by a new cron policy. `backup enable` upserts the managed declaration, so re-running it re-stamps the field; `docs/cli/backup.md` states this and that an explicit `timeoutSeconds` still wins.

**Alternative considered and rejected:** making the budget unbounded (`timeoutSeconds: 0`). The scheduler's ten-minute default is a safety net against one stuck job wedging the cron lane; the fix needs an archive-sized ceiling, not the removal of the ceiling.

**Alternative considered and rejected:** changing the generic cron command default. The reported class is managed backups only; raising the shared default would change every command job on every install.

**Alternative considered and rejected (earlier revision):** resolving a backup budget inside `resolveCronJobTimeoutMs` for schedules without a payload timeout. That substitutes a contributor-chosen value for an owner-built default, so it needs a maintainer decision rather than evidence; the budget belongs to the owner that declares the schedule.

</details>

prs.title: fix(anthropic): measure session catalog TTLs against monotonic time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Anthropic session catalog keys its hard-scan tree backstop, its Desktop overlay refresh TTL, and its CLI-scan cache deadline with `Date.now()`. A wall-clock correction (NTP step or manual change) can stretch or shorten those elapsed-time TTLs: rolling the clock back keeps a stale tree snapshot "fresh" past its five-minute deadline, so deleted sessions linger as ghost entries until the next forced refresh; rolling it forward forces needless full rescans.

Precedent: #191606 (same elapsed-TTL-vs-wall-clock shape; this PR is the same shape at the remaining Anthropic extension sites).

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog's owners (`readProjectsTreeSnapshot` in `session-catalog-scan.ts`, `readDesktopOverlay` in `session-catalog-desktop.ts`, `readCliScan` in `session-catalog-discovery.ts`) each write and compare an in-memory TTL deadline with `Date.now()`. All three are elapsed-time budgets and are switched to `performance.now()`, matching the clock-sweep already merged for sibling extensions in #191606. No validator, option, config, or persistence policy is added or changed.

Production LOC is `+7/-7, net 0`.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Wall-clock corrections no longer disturb the catalog's five-minute rescan backstop, Desktop overlay refresh, or CLI-scan cache deadline. Sessions removed from disk are cleaned up on schedule regardless of NTP/manual clock changes; nothing else changes.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `14b10161fff79d7ffc82d8e748e30c50fc611b7e`
- Current-main RED baseline: `0bb438485084d55ff7c760b4f5ad3f79b16346e2`
- Production entry: `listClaudeSessions` -> `readProjectsTreeSnapshot` (`extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-scan.ts`)
- Canonical owner exercised: `readProjectsTreeSnapshot` hard-expiry check in `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-scan.ts:292`
- Decision surface: `current.hardExpiresAt <= <now>` (tree backstop TTL)
- Recorder/readback boundary: catalog page `sessions` list reflects whether the tree was rescanned
- Acceptance RED: on current main the discriminating test `re-scans on TTL expiry by elapsed time even when the wall clock rolls back` FAILS (ghost session survives a wall-clock rollback), 40/41
- Acceptance GREEN: on this head the same test PASSES (ghost session evicted on elapsed TTL), 41/41
- Legal control: existing catalog TTL tests (`retries transient index I/O without a metadata change`, `retries transient transcript I/O without a metadata change`) still pass with forward-only clock steps
- Cleanup: test uses a temp `HOME` via `createHome()`; no production Gateway/session/token/config touched

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace

The test drives both clocks independently: `performance.now()` (elapsed, advanced past the 5-minute hard TTL) and `Date.now()` (wall clock, rolled back an hour), then deletes a transcript while the watch is armed so only a full rescan can evict the ghost entry.

```text
# RED on current main (Date.now()-keyed deadlines): the rollback hides the expired TTL,
# the full rescan never runs, and the deleted session stays in the page.
FAIL extension-providers extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts > Claude session catalog > re-scans on TTL expiry by elapsed time even when the wall clock rolls back
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 40 passed (41)
```

```text
# GREEN on this head (performance.now()): the elapsed TTL expires, the tree is rescanned,
# and the ghost entry is evicted.
✓ extension-providers extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts > Claude session catalog > re-scans on TTL expiry by elapsed time even when the wall clock rolls back
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  41 passed (41)
```

### Real catalog entry trace

The real production entry `listClaudeSessions` (the function behind `sessions.catalog.list`) runs against a real temporary Claude store: first read discovers the session, a second read within the 5-minute hard TTL is served from cache, deleting the transcript and rolling `Date.now()` back an hour while `performance.now()` advances past the hard TTL forces a real rescan that evicts the ghost.

```text
# HEAD (performance.now()-keyed TTLs): the hard TTL expires on elapsed time despite the wall-clock rollback.
✓ extensions/anthropic/real-catalog-probe.test.ts > re-scans on TTL expiry by elapsed time even when the wall clock rolls back (real listClaudeSessions) 141ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed (1)
```

### Running-Gateway `sessions.catalog.list` trace (shipped entry)

A real Gateway is started from the built tree (`node openclaw.mjs gateway run`) with `HOME` pointed at a temporary Claude store holding one session (`ttl-session`), `auth.mode = none`, and a process-local `Date.now()` preload that can step the wall clock without touching `performance.now()`. The Gateway loads the bundled `anthropic` extension (log: `plugins.gateway-load.plugin.anthropic ... loadFailedCount=0`) and serves `sessions.catalog.list` with the claude catalog provider; no Anthropic API credential is involved (the catalog scans the local Claude store only).

```text
$ node openclaw.mjs gateway call sessions.catalog.list --port 18999

# call 1 (initial real scan): claude catalog host "gateway:local" reports the seeded session
{
  "catalogs": [ { "id": "claude", "label": "Claude Code", ...,
      "hosts": [ { "hostId": "gateway:local", "connected": true, "sessions": [
          { "threadId": "ttl-session", "status": "stored", "cwd": "/work/ttl-session",
            "updatedAt": 1793751445414.5825, "recencyAt": 1793751445414.5825, "name": "alpha", ... } ] } ] },
    { "id": "pi", ... } ]
}

# process-local wall-clock rollback: Date.now() -= 1h (performance.now() untouched)
$ echo -3600000 > "$OPENCLAW_PROOF_OFFSET_FILE"

# call 2 (after the rollback, within the 5-minute TTL): served from the cache; the session is
# unchanged and the payload is byte-identical -- the rollback neither froze nor pre-expired the
# elapsed-time TTL (HEAD keys the deadline with performance.now(), so wall-clock corrections
# are inert for the cache-freshness decision).
{
  "catalogs": [ { "id": "claude", ..., "hosts": [ { "hostId": "gateway:local", "sessions": [
      { "threadId": "ttl-session", "status": "stored", "updatedAt": 1793751445414.5825,
        "recencyAt": 1793751445414.5825, ... } ] } ] },
    { "id": "pi", ... } ]
}
# comparison: session present both calls; updatedAt identical (1793751445414.5825);
# catalogs payload identical => cache served both calls, rollback did not disturb the TTL.
```

The elapsed-time expiry side (the rescan that evicts a ghost when the TTL lapses) is covered by the discriminating mock-clock test above (RED on current main 40/41, GREEN on this head 41/41) and by the real `listClaudeSessions` probe; the running-Gateway trace above proves the shipped `sessions.catalog.list` path reaches the changed TTL comparisons and that a wall-clock correction is inert for them.

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts` (Node 24.18, docker) — 41/41 passed on head
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- Real path: the trace above runs the real `listClaudeSessions` entry against a real temporary Claude store, and a real Gateway (`node openclaw.mjs gateway run` from the built tree) serves `sessions.catalog.list` with the claude catalog and a process-local wall-clock rollback. No Anthropic credential is required (the catalog scans the local Claude store); the discriminating mock-clock test covers the expiry side.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+7/-7`
- Test LOC: `+31/-5`
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the established `performance.now()` elapsed-time pattern from #191606; no new helper, validator, or API surface
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none
### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts` (Node 24.18, docker) — 41/41 passed on head
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- Real path: the trace above runs the real `listClaudeSessions` entry against a real temporary Claude store. A full `sessions.catalog.list` via a running Gateway needs an Anthropic provider credential and a live Claude store, which this environment lacks; the real-entry trace plus the discriminating mock-clock test cover the changed TTL comparisons.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+7/-7`
- Test LOC: `+31/-5`
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the established `performance.now()` elapsed-time pattern from #191606; no new helper, validator, or API surface
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes release qualification fixtures that fail in deeply nested workspaces or no longer match the native update module closure.

## User Impact

No production behavior change. Release qualification continues exercising real ingress and real socket inodes without depending on absolute Unix socket path length. No timeouts are increased and no tests are skipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main-first integration of the approved 2026.11.1 blocker repairs. The native update fixture follows current module owners; the config fixture asserts the exact 500-code-point diagnostic contract. Socket fixtures use short relative bind paths, with Telegram failure coverage running actual ingress in a child process.

Original patch mapping: `afcf197dcdc8e925f6e9cbcec621651f69c47e5c` supplies the two native-update fixture changes; `066592bc38c38a6a986477bc4c4fc5feac8d54f2` supplies the five socket-fixture changes. Adaptation preserves main’s refactored config/docker helpers, omits the retired standalone redact-form-body module (owned inline by redact.ts on main), and uses the existing Windows child-process option convention. The TypeSafe test is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Native restart module suite: **19 passed** using `node --import tsx --experimental-vm-modules --test scripts/tests/update-restart-module-outcome.mjs` (5.40s).
- Four affected script suites: **56 passed** (docker 18, archive 27, config 4, Telegram failures 7). Telegram failures were rerun after the Windows-option review fix: **7 passed**.

Annotation-only replies now show **1 annotation / 2 annotations** rather than a blank queue row or internal filenames. Prompt text retains precedence; ordinary attachment names and image fallbacks remain.

Pending-input projection reads canonical media facts directly, so labels survive even when the displayed message has no fetchable media URL. Local whitespace-only text no longer masks the attachment preview. Shared queue presentation keeps counts consistent before and after server admission.

## Validation

Current published head: `3cde11a4fbe96d54eb5abc4ac2c7e2209e36d929`.

- **8 browser tests and 34 focused unit tests passed**. Coverage includes local/server one-/two-annotation rows, whitespace-only text, label-only canonical metadata, pointer/keyboard editing, value/focus, locked-row protection, and double-click protection. Wall time: 4.98 s browser; 12.13 s unit.
- Owning UI-chat test types, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. All other selected CI jobs passed; the bundle check and its aggregate gate failed.
- Fresh independent review: no P1/P2 findings against diff SHA-256 `4baf7cf7b740178c28937fde9510484bd553e5d3deb40d75ffc2bab5d881e6a0`. Published source is identical to that reviewed source.
- Tests reuse existing style/mount lifecycle and native browser matchers. **Net test lines: −1**. The unchanged local ratchet and CI baseline/test-line ratchets passed. No new allocation or PR-specific budget increase.
- Integrated the existing upstream test-budget reconciliation. No budget files are changed relative to main.
- Canonical producer → pending-input projection → queue proof passes, including label-only media. **Full live-Gateway/model proof remains incomplete:** prior isolated setup never reached annotation admission. No real-model credentials were used; setup failures are not product-failure evidence.
- Sanitized screenshots were inspected in the actual PR and delivered in the originating chat.

## Bundle budget / landing — blocked

[Exact-head CI run 41762587519](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41762587519) completed. The [bundle check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41762587519/job/126353993405) reports **1,282,319 B → 1,282,721 B gzip (+402 B)**, beyond the allowed 64 B build variance. The base already exceeds the unchanged 1,281,063-byte cap. Requests remain 20 → 20. The aggregate gate attributes its failure to this check; all other selected jobs passed.

Vyctor explicitly instructed “Don’t raise budget, bypass it.” That authorization remains recorded, but **the PR is not merged**: the available managed merger has no admin-bypass option, and the native inherited-failure exception does not cover PR-caused growth. No cap was raised, no failed check was relabeled passing, and new growth was not misrepresented as inherited. Landing requires a supported way to apply the authorized exception.

![After: queue row reads 2 annotations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41dd34de-9d7f-4440-80b6-310837942a40)

prs.title: fix: plugin-created automations have no recorded inference account
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin service `ctx.getCron().add()` creates agent-turn automations without recording their inference account. Stored-account execution then refuses both isolated and custom-session tasks before model execution.

Closes #192327.

## User Impact

New service-created automations retain the selected account and runtime. Existing bound jobs retain ownership; existing unbound jobs still require explicit adoption.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share the Gateway's existing target/session capture composition and account authorization owner. The service pins the effective agent across asynchronous capture, retains authorization through store acceptance, and releases it after settlement. Service stop, scheduler replacement, credential replacement and personal-account authorization remain admission boundaries. Gateway creator attribution and optional session-lookup ownership are preserved.

Current public head: `0122a28d0203d01901346d58bb59530ef80700d1`. Product code is unchanged from `1b4e35b4a6af2553548f519fca03ebb205306f23`; this head replaces the mocked lookup-call test group with real session-owner/runtime assertions. In addition to preserving mock exports, this fixes an extraction regression by deferring default-agent selection until a non-main agentTurn actually captures inference. Main/systemEvent creation no longer performs an irrelevant ambiguous default selection.

## Evidence

### Current-head validation status

ClawSweeper reviewed `0122a28d0203d01901346d58bb59530ef80700d1` at **02:48:38 UTC on November 4**: proof sufficient, previous test recommendation addressed, Before merge None, Findings None, Security None. [Durable review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192376#issuecomment-6618383123).

The new-head runtime build passed (82 seconds). Formal combined `ocpr prove --phase post` passed at `0122a28d0203d01901346d58bb59530ef80700d1`: built CLI/Gateway state-upgrade proof and real-owner authorization boundary proof both completed, with every process joined. Final clean source-bound canonical review completed scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings, patch correct; complete current-head CI, ci-gate and both CodeQL workflows passed; current-head ClawSweeper review also reports proof sufficient, with Before merge and Findings None. Historical1b4e proof sufficiency is not reused to certify0122.

The refined persistence suite passed **49/49** on the final working tree (222.31 seconds), with canonical affected test types, lint and independent P0–P2 review passing. Both real runtime-selection cases fail under an intentional wrong-owner lookup control and pass after restoring product bytes exactly. The test allocation was reduced to the exact **277** net added LF. The initial broker-less file placement and an unnecessary legacy fixture field failed setup/types; the final cases live in the existing broker-backed persistence suite and retain the original typed fixture configuration.

### Named-base pre-fail

Formal `ocpr prove` on base `206d54934a3d0764cad0ea59a31d43f74bec0fa0` exercised the built CLI, Gateway, plugin service, durable jobs and both execution paths:

```text
service-run-0 exit 1
Automation has no recorded inference account
service-run-1 exit 1
Automation has no recorded inference account
Both actual service-created run paths refused before model; provider calls=0; cleanup joined.
```

An operator-created control completed with the same synthetic stored account.

### Exact-head implementation and state-upgrade proof

`pnpm build:runtime` passed at `0122a28d0203d01901346d58bb59530ef80700d1` (82 seconds). The following formal proof executed that exact head. A comprehensive formal `ocpr prove --phase post` first created a persistent bound control and unbound service jobs through the actual named-base entry. The current candidate then reopened that exact physical state owner and created both service targets through a minimal Gateway-hosted plugin.

Actual entry commands included `pnpm openclaw gateway run --port <isolated-loopback-port>`, operator `cron add --every 1h`, and `pnpm openclaw cron run <job-id> --wait --wait-timeout 60s --timeout 70000`.

```text
Named base created persistent bound control and unbound service jobs; base control completed.
Candidate reused the exact physical state owner; all existing job identity, payload, schedule and binding fields unchanged.
New isolated/session jobs succeeded; existing bound control succeeded; existing unbound service job still refused.
Base and candidate ownerless main/systemEvent RPC creation succeeded with multiple agents; no inference binding recorded.
Successful task runs=3; refused unbound task=1; actual chat-completion requests=3; all credentials matched; all processes joined.
```

Successful terminal records returned `PREFLIGHT_OK`; readonly inspection verified recorded profile/runtime bindings and unchanged existing job definitions. This repairs creation without implicitly adopting old jobs.

### Final-effect service authorization proof

Additional formal `ocpr prove 192327 --phase post` executed unchanged head `0122a28d0203d01901346d58bb59530ef80700d1` in response to the current-head authority-chain request. A private source-entry driver ran the actual `createPluginServiceCronGetter`, shared capture, canonical account writers, `CronService` and SQLite mutation owners. Execution used `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <private-proof-driver> <isolated-state>`; private paths and credentials are omitted.

The only timing fixture was a held **actual scheduler partition lock**. The service completed real capture and queued its real add behind that lock; `persistAuthProfileBatch` then replaced the selected credential through its real owner before the lock was released. Neither capture, authorization nor scheduler persistence was mocked. Disabled tasks and a listening synthetic provider counted any unexpected inference. A real personal account was separately created through its account owner; the service still had no authenticated human.

```text
Positive before: accepted, stored profile recorded.
Personal selection: rejected — current authorized connection required.
Durable jobs before/after personal denial: 1 / 1; provider requests: 0.
Real capture completed; actual scheduler add queued behind partition lock.
Canonical credential owner replaced credential before lock release.
Queued add rejected — authorization was disconnected or replaced.
Durable jobs before/after replacement denial: 1 / 1; provider requests: 0.
Positive after replacement: accepted with a new authorization identity.
Runner requests: 0; provider requests: 0; cleanup joined.
Independent read-only SQLite after shutdown: only the two positive jobs; neither forbidden job present.
```

The post-replacement positive control shows rejection is tied to the old captured authority rather than blanket scheduler failure. This is a production-owner source-entry race proof with a controlled queue, complementing the built CLI/Gateway success and upgrade proof above; it is not an external-provider or transport proof. No product code or public head changed.

### Checks

- Local focused coverage: account persistence/authorization **47 passed**, capture lifetime **7 passed**, session lookup **2 passed**, existing service lifecycle **5 passed**, runner account continuity **9 passed**.
- After the export-preserving fixture repair, the affected **9 tests**, official mock-export gate, targeted lint and core test types passed. Production-source checks and broader local coverage were retained because production code did not change.

prs.title: fix(models): a saved login stays invisible to the Gateway when its settings write is rejected
prs.body:
Closes #186949

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after `openclaw models auth login` saves credentials but the provider settings write is rejected (for example a read-only Nix-managed config), the running Gateway is never told about the new credentials. Turns keep failing with HTTP 401 until the Gateway is restarted.

## User Impact

User impact: credentials saved by a login reach the running Gateway even when the settings write fails. The settings failure is still reported exactly as before ("Credentials saved, but provider settings could not be applied: …"), and the Nix-managed config stays untouched. No config or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The login flow saves credentials, writes provider settings, then calls the existing `refreshProviderAuthAfterLogin`. A settings-write error left the `try` before the refresh. The fix runs a best-effort refresh for saved credentials before rethrowing the settings error. The recovery lives in `refreshSavedAuthAfterRejectedSettings` (`auth-refresh.ts`):

- It does nothing when the login was cancelled, and checks current login authority before it starts. A login that lost authority during the failed write reaches neither the `models.authRefresh` RPC nor the hosted `refreshAfterLogin` callback.
- It never throws. A recovery failure, including a hosted callback that aborts and rejects, cannot replace the original `ProviderAuthConfigApplyError` or its cause.
- It does not claim the rejected settings were applied. It only republishes the saved auth state.

Production: `auth.ts` +2/-2, `auth-refresh.ts` +16. Tests: +28/-19 in `auth.test.ts`, +5/-1 in `auth-authority.test-support.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests, red on the base or the previous head:**
  - `auth.test.ts` › "identifies a config failure after credentials are saved and preserves its cause (Gateway refresh)". Expects the `models.authRefresh` call after the rejected settings write. It fails on the base: there is no refresh call.
  - `auth.test.ts` › "… (hosted refresh)". A hosted `refreshAfterLogin` aborts the login and rejects, and the original `ProviderAuthConfigApplyError` and its cause must survive. It fails on the previous head (e742544): the error was replaced by `ProviderCredentialsSavedError`.
  - `auth-authority.test-support.ts` › "does not publish after authority ends at beforeCommit / writeAuthority". These now also assert that neither the hosted callback (beforeCommit) nor the Gateway RPC (writeAuthority) runs. Both fail on the previous head: the refresh ran.
  - All of these pass on this head, together with the other authority cases (8/8).
- **Checks:** type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check` and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass. `tsgo:core:test` passes for the changed graphs (29 shards, run one at a time; the first attempt was killed by host memory pressure).
- **Live run: does not separate base from fix.**
  - Setup: an isolated Gateway built from this checkout, `OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1`, a read-only config.
  - Steps: from a separate CLI process, run `openclaw models auth login --provider moonshot --method api-key`.
    - The CLI reports `Credentials saved, but provider settings could not be applied: Config is managed by Nix …`.
    - The config file's sha256 is unchanged.
    - Without a restart, passive `models.authStatus` (no `refresh`) already lists `moonshot:default`. A model turn through a local stub also uses the saved key.
  - Base and fix behave the same here.
  - The reason: while a Gateway owns the state root, the CLI does not persist locally. It routes the login to the owning Gateway (`models.authLogin`, `src/cli/local-state-owner.ts`), so the credential is written inside the Gateway process, and this path shows no difference. A separate-process write only happens when no Gateway owns the state.
- **Gap, the reported path:** I could not run the reported path (Codex device-code login, "no account" until restart). I have no ChatGPT account. The device-code and token endpoints are fixed to `https://auth.openai.com` in `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts` and cannot be pointed at a local stub through config or environment.
- **Ratchets:**
  - `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (test lines) is expected to fail: `main` is already over the test-line ceiling, and the three added cases are needed to cover the review findings (net +13 test lines). I did not delete unrelated tests to offset them.
  - `auth.ts` is already over the 700-line cap (929 counted lines). With this head it is 935.

prs.body:
## Problem

`2026.11.5-beta.1` publication fails before any registry mutation (publish runs 41757100833 and 41759831231). The plugin npm child repacks `@openclaw/openshell-sandbox` with the publisher (P = main) toolchain, and `scripts/plugin-npm-security-scan.mts` rejects it:

```
@openclaw/openshell-sandbox: unreviewed critical findings in exact npm artifact:
[{"contentSha256":"c5050d40…","line":127,"path":"dist/.setup/worker-cli-<hash>.mjs","ruleId":"dangerous-exec"}]
```

The reviewed content hash `799a34cf…` was recorded on 2026-10-29 (#188083). On 2026-10-30, #188576 bumped tsdown 0.23.1 → 0.23.2 and rolldown 1.2.14 → 1.2.15, which changes the emitted bytes of that file. Main's own openshell build hashes to `c5050d40…` too, so main's scanner rejects main's own package as well.

## Review of the new bytes

Diff between the reviewed (`799a34cf…`) and current (`c5050d40…`) `worker-cli` bundle is 11 lines, all bundler cosmetics:

- import chunk name `./config-BFHm9T4X.mjs` → `./config-xMr6yx5f.mjs`
- `//#region <path>` / `//#endregion` markers → `// <path>` comments

The reviewed `spawn(worker.nodeCommand, args, { env, stdio: "inherit" })` logic at line 127 and the rest of the file are byte-identical.

## Solution

Record the new reviewed content hash. The finding count limit is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `plugin-npm-security-scan.mts` with this change passes main's own openshell pack and the 2026.11.5-beta.1 pack (both built with main's toolchain): 6 critical findings, all reviewed.
- `test/scripts/plugin-npm-security-scan.test.ts`: 7 passed.
- Release blocker for 2026.11.5-beta.1 publication (P-only repair; candidate and FRV 41732921061 unchanged).

prs.title: fix(feishu): prevent duplicate tails with preview and block streaming
prs.body:
Fixes #192446

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Feishu's completed streaming card repeats its last block when cumulative previews and completed-block streaming are enabled together. Reported by @MarMarLabs.

## User Impact

User impact: the completed card retains the answer once instead of appending the already-previewed tail again. No configuration, public API, or persistence changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatcher now consumes completed blocks against the latest preview in source order, within the existing assistant-message boundary. It tries an exact match at the consumed offset first, then allows separator whitespace omitted by sentence chunking. Independent blocks still append, and a genuinely repeated block beyond the consumed preview remains visible. It never guesses from suffix overlap.

The retained preview and consumed offset survive CardKit closeout but reset at the assistant-message boundary. This removes delta-text equality suppression without adding a second assembler or a global normalizer. Production +17 lines; tests -1 line against the merge base, with no test-line allocation.

## Evidence

[Original paired transport receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192482#issuecomment-6620924723) · [current merged-head validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192482#issuecomment-6621122370).

- Built Gateway, normal Feishu account startup, signed webhook ingress, a deterministic streamed model response, and actual Feishu SDK/CardKit HTTP requests to a task-owned HTTPS fixture: main twice ended with 1,784 characters and two tail markers; the original candidate twice ended with the exact 1,730-character answer and one tail marker. After integrating current main's elapsed-time backoff change, the new exact head repeats that byte-exact, one-tail result in a fresh real-path turn.
- Non-streaming replies and single-block replies are unchanged, twice on each original ref. The repeated-paragraph control retains both complete copies, twice on each original ref; its canonical CardKit bytes are identical across those paired runs.
- Three focused Feishu suites: 122 tests passed again after integration. The covered-tail and sentence-gap regressions fail on main. Changed-file formatting and lint pass; the merged candidate build passes.
- Scope/gap: the fixture is not an authenticated Feishu tenant or client screenshot. It also exposes inherited CardKit close/reopen fanout and repeated-paragraph ordering on main; this patch does not claim to repair those behaviors. Both repeated copies remain present, but their inherited ordering is not a correctness claim of this PR.

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting fully restores prior behavior, with no migration or stored-state change. Blast radius is Feishu's streaming text assembly, especially the opt-in combination of partial previews and completed blocks.

prs.title: fix(discord): keep REST entity cache entries on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Discord entity data expiring too early or remaining stale too long when the wall clock is corrected while the Gateway stays connected.

## User Impact

Discord's existing 30-second REST entity-cache window follows elapsed time rather than clock corrections. This prevents unnecessary REST requests after a forward correction and stale user, member, guild, channel, or emoji reads after a backward correction. Normal no-step behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retains @wangmiao0668000666's original fix: sample `performance.now()` in the existing private cache owner. Lookup, expiry creation, and sweeping already use that single sample. No new owner, SDK export, setting, persistence, or public timestamp contract is introduced. The TTL, sweep interval, 5,000-entry cap, and event invalidation stay intact. The sweep origin remains zero; its first process-start sweep can therefore wait until the existing 30-second interval, while reads still check expiry on every access.

The clock regression now extends the existing emoji-cache contract, with explicit Date/performance fake clocks. The independent capacity, late-response sweep, and event-invalidation cases remain. Removed the redundant standalone regression and its test-line allocation. Against frozen main `68a413a67ab14a569c4a82ff96bf8627e5163f51`: source **+1/−1**, tests **+4/−5 (net −1)**, docs **+5**.

## Evidence

Built both artifacts in secretless Docker on **Node 24.22.1**, then exercised the **bundled built Gateway with the actual Discord plugin**, not a manually constructed Client or transport. An authenticated operator called HTTP `/tools/invoke` with the real `message` tool's `emoji-list` action; the native Discord clients used a task-trusted TLS CONNECT protocol fixture at their normal authorities. The Discord Gateway connection remained alive throughout each run.

**Main twice, candidate twice**, with fresh isolated profiles each time:

| Scenario | Main, both runs | Candidate, both runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No clock step | Reuses `clock_v1` while fresh; reads `clock_v2` after 31 real seconds | Same |
| Forward +60s wall step while fresh | Incorrect immediate refetch: 2 REST reads, `clock_v2` | Keeps fresh entry: 1 REST read, `clock_v1` |
| Backward −60s wall step, then 31 real seconds | Incorrect stale entry: 1 REST read, `clock_v1` | Correct expiry: 2 REST reads, `clock_v2` |
| Restore wall time | Refreshes the stale main result to `clock_v2` | Retains the already refreshed `clock_v2` |

The step changes **only the Gateway process's `Date.now()`**, as in #190894. The system clock, native timers, `performance.now()`, public tool path, cache implementation, and its 30-second TTL are not replaced or accelerated. The fixture supplies protocol responses, not production credentials or live Discord delivery; all tool responses and actual REST requests are captured.

The consolidated regression fails on main for the two intended clock-direction assertions (**2 failed / 5 passed**) and passes on the candidate (**7/7**). Focused formatting and changed-file lint passed. [Detailed native-wire and returned-value receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190997#issuecomment-6575589269).

**Merge danger:** two-way door; reverting fully restores the previous process-local timing behavior, with no stored-data migration. Blast radius is the Discord Client's existing REST entity cache and its consumers; incorrect behavior could increase REST calls or prolong stale cached entities.

## What Problem This Solves

Claude quota windows, scoped model limits, and extra-usage amounts disappear when the OAuth/web usage response encodes numeric fields as strings. For example, `five_hour.utilization: "18"` is dropped instead of becoming an 18%-used quota window.

## User Impact

The provider usage display recovers finite numeric-string values. Number-typed responses keep their existing behavior; malformed strings remain ignored without hiding valid sibling windows.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Claude response owner now reuses strict `parseFiniteNumber` for the five numeric field reads instead of number-only `asFiniteNumber`. Sibling usage fetchers already use that helper. Existing clamping, labels, resets, deduplication, malformed-response isolation, and billing conversion remain in place.

Original implementation by @wangmiao0668000666; commit `728b70518a9f50ededdf82da5f1ee63699106433` is retained. The maintainer revision shares the complete number/string fixture and removes duplicate setup and the unused test-line allocation.

No authentication, endpoint, proxy policy, storage/schema/config-shape, or public API/export change.

## Evidence

[Inspectable shipped-CLI quota output and HTTPS receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190449#issuecomment-6576018470) compare main `e571cd1495c1358ab453c4496a645dc23af1602b` with exact head `3f1f070222af866850cff5407f10cca4bd9cefc0` in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker:

- A synthetic managed token profile is saved and selected through shipped CLI auth commands. No real credentials, legacy auth JSON seeding, Doctor migration, direct SQLite edits, or injected fetch.
- The trusted-CA CONNECT pattern from #188069 intercepts only `api.anthropic.com:443` at loopback with certificate verification enabled. All eight status runs reach the actual production HTTPS `GET /api/oauth/usage` path using the synthetic profile.
- `openclaw models status`, string-valued response: main **2/2** shows only the numeric Opus control; candidate **2/2** shows `5h 82% left · Week 58% left`.
- Numeric control quota lines are identical on both builds. Malformed strings are ignored on both builds while the valid Opus window survives.
- Final owner regression: main **1 fail / 13 pass**; candidate **14/14 pass**, including number/string variants, scoped limits, billing, resets, clamping, deduplication, and malformed siblings. Targeted lint/format pass.
- Whole-PR net lines: production **0**, tests **0**, docs **+1**; no allocation remains.

The CLI summary displays two windows; scoped-limit and billing assertions are covered at the owner boundary rather than claimed from that short status line. No live Anthropic account acceptance is claimed.

## Merge Danger

**Two-way door:** reverting restores number-only response parsing; no data or config migration is introduced. Blast radius is Claude OAuth/web usage response normalization and its quota/billing displays, not inference or credential handling. prs.title: fix(sessions): keep the picked session-group folder literal
prs.body:
## Problem

Sessions → group menu → **New session defaults** → *Browse folders* → pick a folder and **Save** stores a directory name with its edge whitespace removed. With a folder named `proof-repo ` (trailing space) and a sibling `proof-repo`, the group silently saves the sibling, so the saved default and the dialog identify a different directory than the one picked, and sessions started from that group resolve to the sibling.

The identity was destroyed at three layers:

1. `PlaceBrowserState.usablePath()` returned `this.draft.trim()`, so "Use this folder" already handed the trimmed path to the dialog.
2. `session-group-defaults-dialog.tsx` trimmed again in `applyFolder`, in the repository probe, and in `submit` (`cwd: cwd().trim()`).
3. `updateSessionGroupDefaults` normalized the saved folder with `normalizeOptionalString` (trims, then rejects blank), so even a literal request was narrowed on the way into SQLite.

## Solution

Keep the picked folder's literal bytes at every hop and let whitespace decide only whether a folder is configured:

- `PlaceBrowserState.usablePath()` returns the absolute draft as typed/selected; blank stays `""`, relative stays `null` (typed drafts keep their absolute/relative classification).
- The dialog sends and probes `cwd()` literally; emptiness checks still use `trim()`.
- `updateSessionGroupDefaults` stores `defaults.cwd` when `hasNonEmptyString(defaults.cwd)`, otherwise `null`.

No new config, API, RPC, or storage shape. Existing stored values are unaffected: they were already trimmed.

## Evidence

### Real stack: shipped Gateway + shipped Control UI + real folders

Base `92e1a1bb115f`, head `db494ab9d7cc`. Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `gateway.auth.mode: "none"`, real Gateway from this checkout (`dist/index.js gateway run`), the shipped Control UI bundle served by that Gateway, Chromium driven through the actual product flow (group menu → New session defaults → Browse folders → click the `proof-repo ` entry → Use this folder → Save). Two real directories:

```
/tmp/lcwd-proof/state/ws/proof-repo    identity.txt = TRIMMED-FOLDER   (decoy)
/tmp/lcwd-proof/state/ws/proof-repo    identity.txt = LITERAL-FOLDER   (note trailing space)
```

Read back with the shipped CLI — `openclaw gateway call sessions.groups.defaults`:

**Head (this PR)** — literal folder saved (trailing space visible via `cat -A`):

```
      "cwd": "/tmp/lcwd-proof/state/ws/proof-repo ",$
```

**Red on base** — same Gateway build, only the three UI source files reverted (i.e. this PR's Gateway change alone), same clicks:

```
[proof] picker entries: ["proof-repo","proof-repo ",".git"]
[proof] picker path after click: "/tmp/lcwd-proof/state/ws/proof-repo "
      "cwd": "/tmp/lcwd-proof/state/ws/proof-repo",     <-- decoy sibling
```

The picker already saw the literal listing entry, so the remaining loss is exactly the UI trim this PR removes.

Gateway-side red check, `src/gateway/session-groups.test.ts` on base source (test kept):

```
× session groups catalog > stores a literal default folder instead of its trimmed sibling
  Tests  1 failed | 23 passed (24)
```

same file on this head: `Tests 24 passed (24)` (286s cold, `pnpm test src/gateway/session-groups.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`).

### Upgrade / stored-data compatibility (latest stable → this branch)

Ran the catalog written by the newest published release through this branch. The stable side is `openclaw@2026.10.9` (npm `latest`), installed in an isolated prefix with its own state directory:

1. On the stable build, created a session group and saved its working directory through the shipped CLI: `cwd = /tmp/lcwd-upgrade/ws/existing-repo`. On-disk state: state DB `user_version=20`, agent DB `user_version=25`, row `session_groups(name='Compat Group', cwd='/tmp/lcwd-upgrade/ws/existing-repo')`.
2. Started this branch's build on that state. It refused to serve sessions, exactly as a user upgrading would see:

```
Agent main (.../openclaw-agent.sqlite): OpenClaw agent database ... uses schema version 25;
stop active agents and run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to schema version 38 before using it.
```

3. Ran the documented repair (`openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`): state DB `20 → 36`, agent DB `25 → 38`, pre-migration backups written, and the existing group row came through unchanged:

```
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: .../openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-*.bak
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: .../openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-*.bak
state DB user_version=36   agent DB user_version=38
session_groups: name='Compat Group'  quote(cwd)='/tmp/lcwd-upgrade/ws/existing-repo'
```

4. After the upgrade the stored default still loads and works:
   - the shipped Control UI dialog opens on the pre-existing folder — `Working directory: existing-repo — /tmp/lcwd-upgrade/ws/existing-repo` (screenshot below);
   - `sessions.create` with that stored default succeeds and binds `sessionRoot = /tmp/lcwd-upgrade/ws/existing-repo`;
   - a new save of a literal folder persists its trailing space alongside the old row:

```
$ openclaw gateway call sessions.groups.update --params '{"name":"Compat Group","worktree":false,"cwd":"/tmp/lcwd-upgrade/ws/literal-repo "}'
      "cwd": "/tmp/lcwd-upgrade/ws/literal-repo ",$
$ sqlite row: session_groups ... quote(cwd) = '/tmp/lcwd-upgrade/ws/literal-repo '
```

Rows above were read through the Node SQLite API because the host `sqlite3` binary predates `STRICT` tables. Nothing here changes the schema, the read path, or the stored shape; the only difference is that a nonblank folder is no longer trimmed before the write, so old rows keep loading and literal rows can live next to them.

### Regression tests

- `ui/src/components/session-group-defaults-dialog.test.ts` — picks the literal listing entry, asserts the probe and `submit` receive `"/workspace/client-work "`. On base source the test fails at `expected last "vi.fn()" call to have been called with [ '/workspace/client-work ' ]`; on head `8 passed (8)` (11.4s).
- `src/gateway/session-groups.test.ts` — `updateSessionGroupDefaults` keeps `"/repos/client "` and still clears a whitespace-only value.

### Screenshots

Picker listing both folders, the literal selection, the saved state, and the upgraded-state dialog are captured during the runs (attached below).

## Remaining cutover (not in this PR)

Session creation still normalizes the requested folder, so a literal saved default does not by itself make a session start in the literal directory. The same trim exists in:

- `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-create-params.ts:38` — `normalizeOptionalString(draft.cwd)`
- `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-place-state.ts` — the page's own picker still sets `folderValue = folder.trim()` (that file also has five open PRs)
- `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-create.ts:310` — `requestedCwd = normalizeOptionalString(p.cwd)`
- `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts:557` — session root normalization, which also feeds sandbox containment

Observed on this build: `sessions.create` with `cwd: "/tmp/lcwd-upgrade/ws/literal-repo "` answers `ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '/tmp/lcwd-upgrade/ws/literal-repo'` — the trimmed sibling — while the trimmed default (`existing-repo`) creates a session normally. That is a separate change through the session-creation owner (its root normalization is containment-validated), so it is deliberately kept out of this save-path repair.

## Not tested

- Windows: Win32 file-name rules cannot create a trailing-space directory, so this scenario cannot be reproduced there.

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions: Keep Allow edits from maintainers enabled</summary>
</details>

| New session defaults dialog | Literal folder selected | Saved |
|---|---|---|
| ![dialog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/969e7735-80ab-4aea-90c6-b4a4a995c476) | ![selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a75d0b2f-fb43-47bd-bcb7-31096f5a68e5) | ![saved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5362e438-7b07-49d8-b810-ec73e3621087) |

Upgraded state (`openclaw@2026.10.9` → this branch): the pre-existing group default still opens in the shipped dialog.

![upgraded state](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1bbc5607-39e0-44db-9687-1586a042f3df)

prs.title: fix(mxc): resolve literal sandbox file paths without trimming
prs.body:
Fixes #190077

## What Problem This Solves

The mxc sandbox fs bridge trimmed the tool-supplied `filePath` before mapping it onto its mounts, so a literal file name like `" x.txt"` silently addressed its trimmed sibling `x.txt`. A sandboxed agent reading or writing `" x.txt"` touched the decoy file instead of the one the model chose.

Precedent: #187554 ("The configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity"). Sibling: #172869.

## Why This Change Was Made

`MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts` now resolves the caller's literal `filePath`; only the optional invocation base (`cwd`) keeps its blank-check via `trim()`, matching the shape accepted in #187554. The mount-containment guard is unchanged and still operates on the literal-resolved path.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the literal-path contract to the mxc bridge owner).

## User Impact

Agents working in the mxc sandbox backend now read and write the exact file the model named, including names with leading/trailing whitespace. Ordinary paths, absolute paths, and outside-root rejections behave identically.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `ed26a563f` (branch `fix/mxc-literal-file-path`)
- Current-main RED baseline: `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711`
- Production entry: real dispatch via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mxc/test/fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (Node 24.18, Linux x64, secretless Docker)
- Canonical owner exercised: `MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts:178`, through the public `readFile` with real filesystem files
- Decision surface: the `filePath` parameter of sandboxed agent file tools (`Type.String` schema, no pattern constraint; no upstream trim in the tool chain)
- Recorder/readback boundary: the file bytes returned by `readFile`, asserted byte-for-byte against distinct literal/decoy contents
- Acceptance RED: on current main, the new assertion failed — `readFile(" x.txt")` returned the decoy's contents (`"decoy-data"` instead of `"literal-data"`); the two pre-existing test variants passed (1 failed / 2 passed)
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, all 3 tests pass, with both `" x.txt"` → literal and `"x.txt"` → decoy observed through the real bridge over real files
- Legal controls: the trimmed sibling still resolves to itself; the pre-existing native-tool-paths matrix (workspaceOnly true/false) and its mutation denials are unchanged and green
- Cleanup: isolated temp workspaces only; no mxc runtime, Gateway, or production config touched (the bridge owner is host path math plus real fs access checks)

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mxc/test/fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3/3 (RED run on main: 1 failed / 2 passed at the new assertion)
- `oxfmt --check` on both changed files — clean
- Not tested: live mxc container end-to-end (the changed owner is pure host-side path resolution + fs, exercised with real files here); Windows container-path normalization

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+4/-1`
- Test LOC: `+29/-0` (existing test file only)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing mount-containment guard (`isPathInside`) and mount table; no new validator or export
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none
- Two-way door: reverting restores trimmed-path resolution

## Maintainer edits

<details>
<summary>land-ready notes</summary>

- Maintainer edits are allowed on this branch (small, single-owner change).
- Alternative considered: normalizing only in the containment check — rejected: the resolved host path itself must stay literal or the fs target is wrong.
- Scope declaration: this PR changes the mirror/local mapping only; the mxc spawn launcher and readiness owners are untouched.

</details>


## Shipped-run proof (2026-10-30)

Reviewer demand: terminal evidence of **shipped file tools selecting ` x.txt` rather than `x.txt`**, with the Windows-flow boundary disclosed (no shipped Windows MXC flow was captured).

**Entry point: compiled shipped module + real fs** — no vitest, no tsx, no mocks.

- Class: `MxcFsBridge` compiled from this PR's sources by the repo's own extension build (same tsdown build that emits `dist/extensions/mxc/index.js`).
- The mxc Linux registration path is intentionally dormant (`registerMxcPlugin` warns and returns early off-Windows before registering any backend), so the class was imported through a **scratch-only re-export entry** (`extensions/mxc/proof-entry.ts`, worktree-local, never committed) that the same build emitted as `dist/extensions/mxc/proof-entry.js`. It was instantiated with the **exact shipped construction expression** from `mxc-backend.ts`: `new MxcFsBridge(sandbox)` — the same call the backend's `createFsBridge` performs for agent file tools. The compiled class is the shipped build output.
- The mxc read/write path under test is pure Node path-mapping over the mount table plus a real fs-safe root: no MXC binary and no Windows host is required for the code this PR changes.

**Boundary disclosure:** no Windows host is available for this run. The changed owner (`MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget`) is OS-agnostic Node path-mapping; Windows-specific container-path normalization (drive-letter/case semantics) is out of scope for this change and untested. This run is the strongest Linux shipped evidence for the mxc bridge.

Exact commands (scratch worktree at `b17f25996` + this PR's disjoint `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts`; local-only, nothing pushed from it):

```
export PATH=/tmp/node24/node-v24.22.1-linux-x64/bin:$PATH
cd <scratch-worktree>
pnpm openclaw --version            # full build; emits dist/extensions/mxc/proof-entry.js
node proof/mxc-driver.mjs          # head run -> GREEN below
# red pairing: restore base bridge, rebuild, rerun
git show c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711:extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts > extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-external-plugin-local-dist.mts
node proof/mxc-driver.mjs          # base run -> RED below
# restore head and rebuild
git checkout ed26a563fd3c370651150800d588fa5273ee1737 -- extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-external-plugin-local-dist.mts
```

Seeds: ` x.txt` = `PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content`, `x.txt` = `PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content` (0o644) under the rw agent-workspace mount.

Base `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711` (pre-fix `.trim()`) — exit 1:

```
read ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"          <-- trimmed to the decoy
writeFile ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> ok
  on-disk ' x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"                   <-- literal untouched
  on-disk 'x.txt'   -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-WRITTEN-BY-SHIPPED-BRIDGE" <-- decoy received the write
FAIL  read selects literal (relative+cwd)
FAIL  relative write landed on literal file
FAIL  relative write left decoy untouched
OVERALL: RED
```

Head `ed26a563fd3c370651150800d588fa5273ee1737` (this PR) — exit 0, full output:

```

read '/sandbox/x.txt'   -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"
read ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"          <-- literal selected
read '/sandbox/plain.txt' (control) -> "PROOF_PLAIN_77AA00-roundtrip"
writeFile ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> ok
  on-disk ' x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-WRITTEN-BY-SHIPPED-BRIDGE"   <-- literal updated
  on-disk 'x.txt'   -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"                       <-- decoy untouched
resolvePath '/sandbox/ x.txt' -> hostPath=.../agent-workspace/ x.txt     <-- literal identity kept
resolvePath '/sandbox/x.txt'   -> hostPath=.../agent-workspace/x.txt
PASS  read selects literal (absolute)
PASS  read selects decoy for unpadded sibling
PASS  read selects literal (relative+cwd)
PASS  relative write landed on literal file
PASS  relative write left decoy untouched
PASS  resolvePath keeps literal identity
PASS  resolvePath keeps decoy identity
PASS  control plain round-trip read
PASS  control plain round-trip write
OVERALL: GREEN
```

Controls: absolute-path read/write with only an interior space (`/sandbox/ x.txt`) is not affected by the trim bug and behaves identically on base and head; plain unpadded `plain.txt` round-trips on both. The defect scope is exactly a tool-supplied **relative** name with leading whitespace — the scenario the added regression test pins.

Cleanup: proof temp workspaces under `/tmp` removed; the scratch worktree (including the local-only `proof-entry.ts` re-export and its package.json build-config tweak) was never pushed; the PR branch itself is unchanged — head stays `ed26a563fd3c370651150800d588fa5273ee1737`, no commit/push was needed.

Not tested: Windows container end-to-end (no MXC-capable Windows host available; see boundary disclosure above) and a live mxc runtime turn. The changed owner is host-side path resolution + real fs access, which this compiled-module run exercises directly.
