prs.title: fix(sandbox): resolve literal remote-shell and ssh identity paths without trimming
prs.body:
Fixes #190056

## What Problem This Solves

Two path-selected inputs still trimmed their value before use, and the SSH identity kept being trimmed again by the Gateway callers that feed the tunnel.

- The remote-shell sandbox file bridge (`sandbox.backend: "ssh"` / remote shell) resolved `" note.txt"` to the sibling `note.txt`. A read returned the wrong file; a write overwrote it.
- The SSH tunnel (`openclaw gateway status`, client `gateway.remote.sshIdentity`) passed `gateway.remote.sshIdentity.trim()` to `ssh -i`, so a configured identity file whose name ends in whitespace loaded a different key.
- After fixing the tunnel, three Gateway owners still trimmed the configured identity before it reached the tunnel: `gatewayStatusCommand` (`sanitizeSshTarget` on the configured value), `resolveGatewayDeviceAuthRoute` (`normalizeOptionalString`), and `resolveSshConfig` (`opts.identity.trim()`). A user configuring `gateway.remote.sshIdentity: "/keys/id test "` never got the trailing space to `ssh -i`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the selected path literal at every owner that holds the configured value; the trimming resolver still owns only CLI-typed invocation strings and the SSH host target. The mount-containment guard is unchanged.

- `startSshPortForward`/`resolveSshConfig` load the exact identity file they are given (`-i`).
- `gatewayStatusCommand` preserves the configured `gateway.remote.sshIdentity` verbatim; CLI `--ssh-identity` still normalizes.
- `resolveGatewayDeviceAuthRoute` preserves the configured identity verbatim.
- The remote-shell bridge keeps the caller's `filePath` literal; only the invocation base goes through the trimming resolver.

Precedent: #187777 (OpenShell mirror-mode renderer), #187554 (linked hook discovery paths). Original fix by @wangmiao0668000666.

## Evidence

All legs are proven against the **compiled production `dist/`** (no vitest, no test doubles), running a real agent turn / real ssh client against a real `sshd` on `127.0.0.1:2222`, on an isolated Linux box. The fixture drives the real entry points: Leg A and Leg C use the shipped `ssh-tunnel-*.mjs` / `gateway-status-*.mjs` bundles, and Leg B runs the shipped `dist/entry.js agent --local` with a mock OpenAI-compatible model that asks the `read` tool for `" note.txt"`.

Harness: `proof-188906.mjs` / `proof-matrix.mjs` (Leg A/B: dynamically imports the compiled `ssh-tunnel-*.mjs`, runs the real `startSshPortForward` against a disposable loopback `sshd`, and runs the real agent turn). Leg C invokes the compiled `gatewayStatusCommand` bundle with the configured trailing-space identity. Ref under test swaps `dist/`; everything else is identical.

### Leg A — ssh tunnel identity (gateway.remote.sshIdentity)

`startSshPortForward({ target: "root@127.0.0.1:2222", identity: "/proof/keys/key.pending " })`. The configured identity path ends in a trailing space. Two contradictory keys are installed: the LITERAL path `/proof/keys/key.pending ` (RSA `SHA256:XI06ezVZAi99pMBJo/uw62G4ZNXWsgbS5L9U+6uMuok`) and the trimmed sibling `/proof/keys/key.trim` (RSA `SHA256:o2b1l7QQtnCpRbbsioGAeDlZOVhxdUopbtHzfiqcEdQ`). The server logs exactly which public key was accepted during kex; the tunnelled HTTP request proves the tunnel carries the process.

| ref | identity | result | server sees |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| head `3e023096ccb` | `/proof/keys/key.pending ` | `tunnel started`, HTTP `200 OPENCLAW_PROOF_HTTP_OK` | `Accepted publickey ... RSA SHA256:XI06ezVZAi99pMBJo/uw62G4ZNXWsgbS5L9U+6uMuok` (the LITERAL key) |
| base `8034bb1fafb` | `/proof/keys/key.pending ` | `tunnel rejected` (ssh exit 255) | ssh stderr: `Warning: Identity file /proof/keys/key.pending not accessible: No such file or directory.` — the trailing space was trimmed, so ssh loaded the nonexistent `key.pending` path |

### Leg B — remote-shell sandbox file bridge

The ssh sandbox runtime (`sandbox.backend: "ssh"`, `ssh.workspaceRoot: /proof/mirror`) mirrors the agent's local workspace to `<workspaceRoot>/<runtimeId>/workspace`. The local workspace holds BOTH the literal `" note.txt"` (`PROOF_REMOTE_LITERAL_4C1D`) and the decoy `note.txt` (`PROOF_REMOTE_DECOY_9A2B`). The mock model asks `read(" note.txt")`; the shipped agent resolves the path through the real `resolveTarget`.

| ref | model observed | agent result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| head `3e023096ccb` | `READ RESULT literal=true decoy=false: PROOF_REMOTE_LITERAL_4C1D` | `PROOF_LITERAL` — read the literal `" note.txt"` |
| base `8034bb1fafb` | `READ RESULT literal=false decoy=true: PROOF_REMOTE_DECOY_9A2B` | `PROOF_DECOY` — trimmed `" note.txt"` → read the sibling `note.txt` |

### Leg C — configured gateway-status entry point (P2 caller fix)

The compiled `gateway-status-*.mjs` bundle (`gatewayStatusCommand`) is invoked with a real config whose `gateway.remote.sshIdentity` ends in a trailing space, against a real `sshd` on `127.0.0.1:2222`. Two contradictory identity files are installed: the LITERAL path `/proof-c/keys/key.pending ` (RSA `SHA256:XI06ezVZAi99pMBJo/uw62G4ZNXWsgbS5L9U+6uMuok`) and the trimmed sibling `/proof-c/keys/key.trim` (RSA `SHA256:o2b1l7QQtnCpRbbsioGAeDlZOVhxdUopbtHzfiqcEdQ`). The command runs the real chain `gatewayStatusCommand → resolveSshConfig → startSshPortForward → ssh -i`, and the server logs which key was accepted.

| ref | sshd sees | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| head `79c4156a3e2` (P2 fix) | `Accepted publickey ... RSA SHA256:XI06ezVZAi99pMBJo/uw62G4ZNXWsgbS5L9U+6uMuok` (the LITERAL key, twice) | the configured trailing-space identity reaches real `ssh -i` unchanged |
| base `8034bb1fafb` | `Connection closed by 127.0.0.1 ... [preauth]` | the identity was trimmed to `/proof-c/keys/key.pending`, no usable key → sshd rejects before authentication |

## Focused tests

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Node 24.22.1, Linux:

- `src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts`: 26 passed (whole file; new case `passes the configured identity to ssh without trimming its whitespace`). On base the new case fails with `expected [ '-i', '/keys/id test' ] to deeply equal [ '-i', '/keys/id test ' ]`.
- `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.test.ts`: 24 passed (whole file; new case `addresses literal whitespace-padded paths instead of their trimmed siblings`). On base it fails because `" note.txt"` returns the trimmed sibling's bytes.
- `src/infra/ssh-config.test.ts`: 7 passed (new assertion keeps `-i "/keys/id test "` literal instead of trimming).
- `src/gateway/client-bootstrap.test.ts`: 24 passed (new case `preserves trailing whitespace in the configured ssh identity path` asserts `resolveGatewayDeviceAuthRoute` returns `identity: "/keys/id test "`).
- `src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts`: 31 passed (new case `passes a configured ssh identity to the tunnel without trimming its whitespace` asserts `startSshPortForward` receives `identity: "/keys/id test "` for `gateway.remote.sshIdentity: "/keys/id test "`).

Existing directory, mount-root, symlink-escape and read-only protections keep their assertions.

Not tested: real SSH host, Windows, macOS, mounted gateway flows, live gateway, real remote gateway server (Leg C's remote probe fails after the tunnel is up; the key-acceptance evidence is the sshd auth log).

## Merge danger

Two-way door: revert restores the trimming. No stored format, migration or protocol change. Users who (unintentionally) relied on trailing whitespace being ignored in `gateway.remote.sshIdentity` or in remote-shell relative paths now address the literal value they supplied; that matches every file tool and the documented behavior of #187777.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes saved numeric overrides being removed when an unfinished number such as `1e` is blurred in Memory settings.

## User Impact

Unfinished numeric input restores the last admitted value without changing the saved override. Deliberately clearing a field still removes its override; valid edits and existing range/integer limits are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browsers sanitize unfinished number text to an empty native value while reporting `validity.badInput`. Reject that state before the existing deliberate-clear branch. The fix remains in the existing field change handler, with no new API, state or configuration behavior.

Retains wangmiao0668000666's original fix. Consolidates numeric regression coverage into the existing draft/refresh case, preserving its boundaries without duplicate setup: production +5 lines, tests net 0, no allocation file.

## Evidence

[Built Control UI + real Gateway proof and inspected screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191875#issuecomment-6606192799).

- Chromium, main twice versus exact candidate `f3f58517ea8395d8223de85403ba53e28cebc3ee` twice: actual keyboard `1e`, native `badInput=true`, then Tab. Main removes the saved override 7; candidate retains 7, restores the text and sends no config write. Both Gateway raw-config and on-disk own-key readback agree.
- All four runs pass valid integer/float persistence, negative/fractional/range rejection and deliberate-clear controls.
- Focused tests: candidate 6/6 pass; same regression on main fails at the intended admitted-value assertion. Existing unrelated/authoritative refresh and shared-owner persistence/defaults checks retained. Focused formatter/linter pass.
- Optional WebKit stalled and was stopped; no WebKit result claimed.

Before (native value is empty despite the browser painting `1e`; persisted override removed):

![Before: unfinished input removes saved override](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/347f1597-3cb5-4fad-8eb3-6825310a0e9b)

After (saved override and admitted value remain 7):

![After: saved override retained](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6c67cf1-73bd-4538-bdfa-1b74c5c4fc30)

Two-way door: revert restores the old field behavior; there is no migration or published-contract change. Blast radius is native bad-input handling in curated settings fields; intentional clearing and admitted edits remain on their existing paths.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report session-start conflicts in HTTP APIs
prs.body:
Closes #192465

## What Problem This Solves

Session-start conflicts currently reach OpenAI-compatible clients as an opaque HTTP 500 or streaming `api_error`, hiding the reason for the rejected turn.

## User Impact

Both Chat Completions and Responses now identify recognized session conflicts with `session_conflict_error`. Non-streaming requests return HTTP 409. An already-started stream keeps HTTP 200 and emits one failure followed by `[DONE]`, without exposing the session key.

Check the session state before retrying. This error does not guarantee that the request had no earlier effects; the Gateway does not automatically replay it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing guard for native changed/invalidated errors and their serialized codes in the shared error mapper. A distinct error type also survives the existing Responses projection into `error.code`, without changing unrelated provider error envelopes or admission behavior.

## Evidence

- On base `ca4cf041fc3b0f2d2bd6d39ecdfbe8899f9e5754`, all 16 new regressions failed for the expected mapping defect: HTTP 500 instead of 409, or the generic SSE error instead of the conflict.
- With the fix, all 214 tests in the following four files passed: `openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts`, `openai-http.test.ts`, `openresponses-http.test.ts`, and `openai-compatible-archived-session.server.test.ts`. Command: `pnpm test src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts src/gateway/openai-http.test.ts src/gateway/openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts src/gateway/openai-compatible-archived-session.server.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- The new cases cover both APIs, streaming and JSON responses, native and serialized conflicts, sanitized output, one agent invocation, one failure terminal and one `[DONE]`, and no success terminal.
- Core production typecheck and the `core-test-gateway-root` test typecheck passed. Targeted lint, formatting, test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent local review found no blocking issues. The change adds 11 production lines and 82 regression-test lines. The separate 82-line allocation covers the two transport regression tables.
- The four-file run took 271.52 seconds wall time (265.30 seconds Vitest), including cold graph preparation and existing real-Gateway suite setup. Hosted CI timing is not yet available.

These tests use isolated real Gateway HTTP servers with deterministic agent rejection fixtures. They establish the error-mapping defect and its repair, not the original low-frequency admission race or live model behavior. The full `check:changed` aggregate, full repository suite, and build were not run; targeted checks are recorded above.

The session branch-PR cache used wall-clock epochs for its90-second success TTL and failure/quota backoffs. This is the remaining branch-cache member after #191606.

- Preserve wangmiao0668000666's two original commits and use the existing core `monotonicDeadlineAfter`/`monotonicNow` owner at all five deadline write/comparison sites.
- Keep durations, branch/session/credential identity, cancellation, forced-refresh ordering, GitHub transport and persisted timestamps unchanged.
- Fold the clock regression into existing list-failure/retry coverage, and advance the retention fixture's elapsed clock alongside its Date step. **Tests net0; production+1; docs+1.** No allocation or baseline changes.

## Evidence

Built Gateway in secretless Node24.22.1 Docker, real Git checkout/branch/commit/remote, real WebSocket subscription RPC, and recorded local GitHub HTTP responses: **main twice prematurely refetches revision2 after a process-local forward Date.now step; candidate twice retains revision1 through the original90-second TTL.** Ordinary no-step reuse controls pass. The consolidated backward-clock regression fails on pre-fix main and passes on candidate. Both touched suites pass **11/11**; targeted formatting and lint pass. ## Risk and rollback

prs.title: fix(codex): keep plugin metadata cache on elapsed time
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>maintainer-edits</summary>

Maintainer edits are enabled on this branch: feel free to rebase, tweak comment wording, or land it directly without waiting for another round from me.

</details>

<details>
<summary>maintainer-options</summary>

**Land-ready rationale**

- **Owner:** `CodexPluginMetadataCache` (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/plugin-metadata-cache.ts`) owns both TTL writes (`load` :112) and the only expiry comparison (`read` :70) in one class; the entry is a module-private `Map` and is never persisted, serialized or exchanged. After this change the file contains zero `Date.now()` calls.
- **No contract change:** the TTL stays `60 * 60 * 1_000`; `performance.now()` is process-local by construction (the same clock source the sibling app-inventory cache and the elapsed-time shape use). Exact-boundary expiry, in-flight coalescing, invalidation, `clear()` and the `cacheable` fail-open guard are untouched.
- **Matches an already-approved shape:** the process-local elapsed-time cache window has landed in `usage-cache` (#190894), the Discord entity cache (#190997), the GitHub detail cache (#191210), the outbound directory cache (#191165) and the pending-binding approval deadline (#191198).
- **Proof is deterministic and cheap:** the two production swaps plus a real-import probe show the wall-clock step no longer collapses the window.

**Alternatives considered**

| Option | Effect | Cost if chosen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Accept (this PR)** | the 60-minute window is measured on elapsed time; a clock correction neither collapses nor extends it | none beyond the 2-token production change |
| Keep `Date.now()` and document it | no code change | a `+1h` wall-clock jump (laptop resume, NTP step, VM restore) evicts every settled plugin catalog at once and re-issues `plugin/list` against the upstream registry; a `−1h` jump serves a catalog past its real window |
| Use the `monotonicNow` core helper | same behavior | the codex extension cannot import `src/shared/` (core internals); sibling extensions use `performance.now()` directly |

**Scope statement:** 2 files, +19/−4; production change is two `Date.now()` → `performance.now()` swaps plus a 3-line comment. No new option, validator, config key, schema, persistence or shared API. No other cache or clock site is touched.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`CodexPluginMetadataCache` caches upstream `plugin/list` / `plugin/installed` responses in a process-local `Map` for 60 minutes. Both the expiry write and the expiry comparison use `Date.now()` (host wall clock):

- `+1h` wall-clock correction (laptop resume, NTP step, VM restore): every settled snapshot instantly reads as expired — the next plugin discovery re-issues the upstream registry request immediately, a stampede right when the host is also re-syncing.
- `−1h` correction: a snapshot that passed its 60-minute window keeps being served — stale plugin catalog stays visible past its designed refresh window for as long as the wall clock lags.

Precedent: [#190894](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190894) (merged 2026-11-02) moved cache windows and timings onto `performance.now()` / `monotonicNow()` including `usage-cache`; [#190997](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190997) (same day) applied it to the Discord entity cache; [#191210](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191210) and [#191165](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191165) did the same for the GitHub detail cache and the outbound directory cache. This PR switches the remaining process-local cache window in the codex extension.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both TTL sites now read `performance.now()` instead of `Date.now()`: the expiry write in `load` (`:112`) and the expiry comparison in `read` (`:70`). The two sites form one closed loop inside a single class — there is no third reader that could compare the stored value against wall time — so the swap cannot split the time base.

Nothing else changes: `CODEX_PLUGIN_METADATA_CACHE_TTL_MS` keeps its value, in-flight request coalescing, per-runtime key scoping, `invalidate()` / `clear()`, and the `cacheable` fail-open guard (a marketplace-load-error snapshot is never cached) are untouched, and no option/validator/config/persistence is added. The existing expiry test now spies `performance.now` instead of `Date.now`; a new case proves a forward wall-clock step no longer collapses the window.

Classification: `behavior-completing` — it completes the elapsed-time cutover the sibling cache owners already made.

## User Impact

A codex-backed turn no longer re-issues upstream `plugin/list` against the registry right after a host clock correction, and never serves a plugin catalog past its real 60-minute window. Under an uncorrected clock the read pattern is identical to before.

## Evidence

### Shipped-flow proof (shipped discovery entry → real codex app-server → real RPC trace)

The probe executes **OpenClaw's shipped discovery entry point**, `readCodexPluginInventory` (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/plugin-inventory.ts:105`, the function `plugin-thread-config.ts:153` calls to build each codex thread config). Its `request` callback is bound to a **real `@openai/codex` 0.164.0 app-server** spawned over stdio JSON-RPC: the probe sends `initialize` → `marketplace/add` (registers the real local marketplace `probe-mkt`) → then lets the shipped reader issue `plugin/installed`, `plugin/list` and `plugin/read`. The `metadataCache` parameter is the **real `CodexPluginMetadataCache`** (candidate uses `performance.now`, base uses `Date.now`); only that module differs between refs (base sha256 `02ce150fca105107cd73a33062329c9159b8f6045c338a17a13732d6cc5b809c`, head sha256 `c22de6a49ee712fb1b640b29c13104d1bdc2bf650d2f6b0e0d4eccbeef99c29b`). The probe itself is byte-identical on both sides and does not mock or stub the cache, the inventory reader, or the app-server; it runs under the repository vitest runtime, which resolves the real shipped `src/plugin-sdk/*` sources. Each scenario ran **twice per ref** in a secretless container, offsetting **only the process's `Date.now`** by `+61 min` while the catalog was fresh (a wall-clock step, not an OS clock jump or a timer change — the same method as #190894/#191165).

**Inspectable trace** (candidate, third discovery after the `+61 min` step):

```text
[trace] plugin/installed -> {"marketplaces":[],"marketplaceLoadErrors":[]}
[trace] plugin/list -> {"marketplaces":[{"name":"probe-mkt","path":"/data/mkt5/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json","interface":null,"plugins":[{"id":"hello@probe-mkt","remotePluginId":null,"version":null,"localVersion":null,"name":"hello","shareContext":null,"source":{"type":"local","path":"/data/mkt5/plugins/hello"},"installed":false,"installedAt":null,"enabled":false,"installPolicy":"AVAILABLE","installPolicySource":null,"mustShowInstallationInterstitial":null,"authPolicy":"ON_INSTALL","availability":"AVAILABLE","disabledReason":null,"eligiblePlanTypes":null,"interface":null,"keywords":[]}]}],"marketplaceLoadErrors":[],"featuredPluginIds":[]}
[trace] plugin/read -> {"plugin":{"marketplaceName":"probe-mkt","marketplacePath":"/data/mkt5/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json","summary":{"id":"hello@probe-mkt","name":"hello","source":{"type":"local","path":"/data/mkt5/plugins/hello"},"installed":false,"enabled":false,"installPolicy":"AVAILABLE","authPolicy":"ON_INSTALL","availability":"AVAILABLE","interface":null},"shareUrl":null,"description":"probe plugin","skills":[],"onboardingSkill":null,"hooks":[],"apps":[],"appTemplates":[],"mcpServers":[],"scheduledTasks":null}}
```

**The decision is the `plugin/list` call count across discovery runs.** The first discovery settles the catalog with exactly one `plugin/list` (trace above). A within-TTL control discovery and the discovery **after a `+61 min` wall step** must not issue a second `plugin/list`:

| Ref | `plugin/list` calls after `+61 min` step | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BASE (`Date.now`) | **2** — the wall step expires the settled catalog; discovery re-issues `plugin/list` | ❌ RED (2/2) |
| HEAD (`performance.now`) | **1** — the elapsed window survives the step; the settled catalog is served | ✅ GREEN (2/2) |

On BASE the assertion `expect(pluginListCalls).toBe(1)` fails (`expected 2 to be 1`); on HEAD it passes. `plugin/installed` and `plugin/read` still fire on both refs — they are not the TTL-covered catalog window — which is why the trace is required: only `plugin/list` must be held. The `+61 min` step exceeds the 60-minute TTL, so on `main` a catalog with ~59 real minutes of freshness left is evicted and re-fetched right when the host is re-syncing; a `−61 min` step likewise serves the catalog past its real window while the wall clock lags.

### Regression fixture fix (review finding P2)

The earlier revision's wall-clock case loaded the cache **before** mocking `Date.now`, then returned `3_610_000` — a raw 1970 epoch that moved the clock **backward** to January 1970 rather than forward one hour, so the unchanged `Date.now` implementation also served a cached entry and the regression could not detect the bug. The case now pins an **initial wall reading before `load`**, then advances **that same mock** by more than the 60-minute TTL. Verified on the pinned host (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/plugin-metadata-cache.test.ts`):

- BASE (main, `Date.now`): `keeps a settled snapshot across a forward wall-clock step` **FAILS** (`2 failed | 5 passed`; the expiry case also follows the production clock, as expected on base).
- HEAD (this PR): **7/7 passed**.

### Verification

- Shipped-flow probe RED/GREEN: BASE 2/2 re-issued `plugin/list` after the `+61 min` step, HEAD 2/2 held the settled catalog — both runs secretless, no credentials, loopback only (local marketplace source, real local codex app-server).
- The committed `plugin-metadata-cache.test.ts` keeps all existing cases (coalescing, partial-catalog isolation, expiry, failed-load sharing, invalidation, clear) and adds the corrected wall-clock case; CI runs the codex extension vitest shard.
- Production LOC `+3/−2`; test LOC `+25/−3`.
- Not tested: a bundled `dist` codex run (local builds are banned on this host) and live upstream registry (the proof drives the real cache class against the real local codex app-server with a local marketplace, not the network).

### Scope and risk

| Impact surface | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/plugin-metadata-cache.ts:70` | expiry comparison on `performance.now()` | same window, elapsed base; single closed loop |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/plugin-metadata-cache.ts:112` | TTL write on `performance.now()` | value never leaves the class (grep-verified) |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/plugin-metadata-cache.test.ts` | expiry case spies `performance.now`; new wall-clock case | test-only |

prs.title: fix(feishu): keep probe and streaming-backoff windows on elapsed time
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

Maintainer edits to this branch are welcome and will not be overwritten; the author will not force-push over them.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- **Land-ready:** one owner (`extensions/feishu`), behavior-preserving clock-domain substitution at four private timestamp sites, deterministic red/green on base. No config, API, schema, or state change.
- **Alternatives:** keep the wall clock (accepts the defect); import the core `monotonicNow()` owner (extensions cannot depend on core internals — the established extension shape is inline `performance.now()`, e.g. #190894, #191533); change TTL durations (out of scope — durations unchanged).
- **Scope:** the probe result cache (`probe.ts`, 10-min success / 60-s error TTL) and the streaming-start failure backoff (`reply-dispatcher.ts`, 60 s). The message-create epoch comparison in `reply-dispatcher.ts:190` (`Date.now() - messageCreateTimeMs`) is deliberately untouched — it is an epoch-vs-epoch elapsed check on a stored message timestamp, which the #190894 sweep keeps on the wall clock.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

A host wall-clock correction while the Gateway runs makes two Feishu process-local cache/backoff windows jump with it: the health-probe result cache (`probe.ts`) and the streaming-start failure backoff (`reply-dispatcher.ts`). A forward step expires a fresh 10-minute probe entry and reissues the `bot/v3/info` API call (burning Feishu's free-tier quota on duplicate health checks), and clears the 60-second streaming backoff early; a backward step keeps entries and backoff alive far past their intended elapsed windows.

Precedent: #190894 (same shape — wall-clock cache/backoff windows → `performance.now()` in extensions; this PR covers the Feishu sites that sweep left behind). Sibling: #191911, #191916 (same Feishu extension, bot-name/sender-name caches), #191210, #192122, #192144, #192293, #192296.

## Why This Change Was Made

`extensions/feishu/src/probe.ts` keeps `probeCache` as a process-local map whose timestamps never leave the module; `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts`'s `streamingStartBackoffUntilByAccount` (in `reply-dispatcher-state.ts`) is the same. The read and write sites now share the elapsed-time domain (`performance.now()`), the only domain a wall-clock step cannot shift; switching one side alone would mix clock domains, so each window's sites move together. Known trade-off, identical to the core stale-while-revalidate cache owner: monotonic windows measure awake time, so system suspend pauses them. Fix classification: behavior-preserving (clock domain only; no TTL, owner, config, or API change).

## User Impact

On a long-running Gateway whose clock is corrected (NTP step, manual change, VM resume), Feishu health checks either lose the cached probe result and spend free-tier API quota on duplicate `bot/v3/info` calls (or a failed probe is retried immediately instead of after its 60-second error window), or keep serving stale probe verdicts and suppressing streaming beyond their windows. TTL values and backoff durations are unchanged.

## Evidence

Base `be881a7f8b1ff5af7ff7783340c98ed9047ea450` → candidate `8773efbdc3a6f00d95fa4fbb40fb258db6c3c651`, same commands. The wall step is a process-local `Date.now` offset under fake timers (the #190894/#188293 preload method), never an OS clock jump.

Deterministic regression in the existing suite (remote Node 24.22.1 container, `vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts`):

| `extensions/feishu/src/probe.test.ts` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Base | **1 failed / 13 passed** — exactly the new wall-clock case fails (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times`: the forward step expires the 10-minute window and reissues the bot-info request) |
| Candidate | **14 passed** |

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/probe.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The new test seeds a successful probe through the real `probeFeishu` (real client factory, request mocked), then steps `Date.now()` forward 20 minutes — past the 10-minute `PROBE_SUCCESS_TTL_MS` window — and asserts the cached result is still returned without a second bot-info request. On base (wall-clock window) the step expires it; on candidate (monotonic window) it stays fresh.

### Real-transport proof (shipped Lark SDK over HTTPS proxy)

The discriminant also runs through the extension's real transport — the shipped `createFeishuClient` (Lark SDK on the extension's own HTTP transport) making a real HTTPS request through an ambient `HTTPS_PROXY` to a local CONNECT stub that counts tunnel connections, then forwarding to a TLS origin stub (remote Node 24.22.1 container, `proof.test.ts`):

| `extensions/feishu/src/proof.test.ts` | CONNECT tunnels |
| --- | --- |
| Base (`Date.now`) | **3** — after the +11 min wall step the 10-min success window looks expired and re-probes (tenant token + bot info) |
| Candidate (`performance.now`) | **2** — the cached probe is served; no re-probe |

```
[stub-proxy] CONNECT #1  [tenant_access_token]
[stub-proxy] CONNECT #2  [bot/v3/info]
[result] connects before step=2 after step=2   # candidate
```

The wall step is again a process-local `Date.now` offset (the #190894 preload method). No mocks on the transport: `probeFeishu` → real `createFeishuClient` → real TLS handshake through the proxy to the stub.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+4/−4` (4 sites, 2 files)
- Test LOC: `+22`
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the established extension clock-domain shape (`performance.now()`) from #190894/#191533; no new helper or abstraction.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none.
- Not tested: the streaming-start failure backoff change (`reply-dispatcher.ts`) has no remote-runnable suite here — its test pulls `mdast-util-from-markdown` (via `markdown.ts`) which the remote dependency closure lacks. The change is the same two-site clock-domain substitution as the proven `probe.ts` change (same read/write symmetry), and `streamingStartBackoffUntilByAccount` is a plain in-memory `Map<string, number>` (grep-verified, `reply-dispatcher-state.ts`). The existing `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` covers the backoff path under fake timers.

prs.title: fix(browser): keep relay capture TTL on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The browser extension-relay capture TTL used the wall clock. A host clock correction could retire a relay operation whose 5-minute elapsed window was still open.

## User Impact

A captured relay operation (CDP commands bridged from the browser extension to the Gateway) keeps its full TTL budget when the Gateway host's wall clock changes. Without this, a forward wall-clock step past the remaining budget made `captureFor` return undefined and the in-flight operation fail as "no longer current".

## Why This Change Was Made

The two private capture deadline checks in `attachRelayOwner` (`owner-server.ts`) compare `expires` against `Date.now()`. The capture's cleanup is already owned by a `setTimeout(RELAY_OPERATION_TTL_MS)` timer (elapsed-based); the `expires` field is a secondary check consulted by `resolve` and `cdp.open`. Using `performance.now()` for both the deadline and the check keeps them on the same monotonic clock as the timer, so a wall-clock step no longer shortens the window. Existing timers, authority, cancellation, settlement ordering and cleanup are unchanged.

This is the same elapsed-budget defect category as #190894 / #191606 / #191668; the browser extension was not covered by the #190894 sweep (its 32 files touched no `extensions/browser` paths), and the follow-up browser clock repairs (#191668 uploads/downloads, #191740 armed dialogs) did not touch the relay.

`Precedent: #190894` — keep private cache/probe windows on elapsed time.
`Related: #191668` — sibling elapsed-budget repair in the same browser extension.

## Evidence

Real WebSocket loopback: a `WebSocketServer` on 127.0.0.1, `attachRelayOwner` on the accepted socket, `captureOperationTarget` spied to return a live target. After registering a capture, the host wall clock is stepped forward 6 minutes (past the 5-minute TTL) with `vi.setSystemTime` while the cleanup timer never fires. The subsequent `resolve` of the captured ref:

| Case | Wall-clock step | `resolve` result |
|---|---|---|
| main (BASE) | +6min | `null` — operation retired early |
| candidate (HEAD) | +6min | `"target-id"` — operation retained |

New discriminating test `owner-server.clock.test.ts` (RED on base, GREEN on head). Existing `owner-server.test.ts` stays green on head.

Focused suite (extension-relay directory, remote Node 24.22.1 in secretless Docker):
- BASE (unmodified): 1 intended clock failure.
- HEAD: `owner-server.test.ts` + `owner-server.clock.test.ts` 2/2 pass.
- Full `extension-relay/` directory on HEAD: 19/20 files pass (239/241 tests). The 2 failing tests in `relay-coexistence.integration.test.ts` (profile port/name drift) fail identically on BASE — they are an existing defect being fixed separately by #192396, not a regression from this change.

Production +2/−2 (net 0); one new test file. No SDK export, baseline increase or new option.

## Risk and rollback

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous wall-clock comparisons with no migration. Blast radius is relay capture TTL timing only.

**Boundary (deliberately unchanged):** `auth-v2.ts` keeps `Date.now()` for its challenge TTL (10s) and replay-window checks — those are security semantics (replay protection / challenge expiry), a different clock domain from this operational capture TTL. `pw-tools-core.downloads.ts:516` also stays on `Date.now()` because that deadline is compared inside Chrome's `page.evaluate` where a cross-process monotonic origin cannot be exchanged (documented in #191668).

## Pre-existing CI failure (not from this change)

`checks-node-changed-extensions-config` runs `relay-coexistence.integration.test.ts` because this PR touches the `extension-relay` directory. Two tests there — "retires borrowed access on configured profile port/name drift" — fail on both BASE and HEAD with `promise resolved "false" instead of rejecting` at `relay-coexistence.integration.test.ts:348`. That is a pre-existing defect introduced with #191614 and being fixed separately by #192396; this PR does not modify that test file or the coexistence code it exercises.

`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (test-lines) also fails on this PR, but the clean `origin/main` at `b215829af28` already runs the same ratchet over by 145 with net delta 0 (`Test lines: 6446874; ceiling: 6446729`). The test-lines baseline is simply ahead of `ci-ratchet-base`; this PR's own +79 lines are covered by the added allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/browser-relay-capture-ttl.txt`, so the change neither adds nor widens the gap.

prs.title: fix(gateway): guests cannot see who is online in the Users sidebar
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Guests can use the Users sidebar but cannot see who is online or idle: hello presence, live presence events and `system-presence` required broad `operator.read`, while guests have only session scopes. Their own `presence.activity` reports were also rejected.

## User Impact

Guests receive online/idle presence and references to watched sessions they can already access. Operator readers retain the full presence view. Email, `onlineSince`, device/network details and connection identifiers are never included in the guest projection. `presence.query` remains operator-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createPresenceRecipientProjection` allowlists person fields for session-only readers: profile identity/name/avatar, `ts`, `lastActivityAt`, a disconnect marker, and permitted watched-session keys. Rows without resolved profiles carry no person. Detail level is included in view and audience cache keys.

`system-presence` and `presence.activity` declare `operator.sessions.read` directly in the Gateway's method descriptors. The presence event guard accepts session readers while retaining recipient-specific projection. No role configuration change is needed.

The final correction removes the earlier additions to the UI-imported shared method set. There is now no diff in `ui/` or `src/shared/` against the PR's base; presence permission declarations stay Gateway-owned. Earlier attribution of the bundle-size failure solely to main was insufficient because that shared set ships in the UI.

Accepted tradeoff, approved by code owner Json: retain one wire row per connection so source/delta keys stay aligned. The UI still groups people into one displayed row; guests can infer connection counts. A per-person wire protocol would need separate key handling, not simply collapsing this array.

The integration with #191978 preserves its demoted-guest denial of `users.list`, `presence.query` and other people's Activity timelines. Online presence is the separately approved exception; demoted session readers receive only the person-level view.

## Evidence

- Real-Gateway regression covers guest hello, `system-presence`, live presence events, private-field omission, watched-session filtering, denied `presence.query`, and accepted self activity. Original guest RPC assertion is red on base and green with the fix.
- Final Gateway-only declaration correction: **82 tests passed** across presence audience, own-session method scopes, shared session scopes, and presence activity. Gateway-server test typecheck, targeted lint, format and `git diff --check` passed.
- Earlier related presence/delta/broadcast suites passed; their evidence applies to the unchanged projection/delivery implementation, not new-head CI.
- Fresh local autoreview of the final candidate, through P2: no actionable findings. Reviewer noted limited unchanged-code context. Additional timed-out reviewer attempts are not counted as passing reviews.
- A scoped allocation covers all **59 net added test lines**. Earlier CI still reported an inherited total ceiling excess; this is not a passing CI claim. Current-head CI is authoritative.
- Remaining proof gaps: no live guest browser screenshot; dedicated guest delta/revocation scenarios were requested by advisory review. Existing delivery scope checks and delta path remain intact; no reachable disclosure defect was established by the review.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve(setup): simplify local AI menu language
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The local AI menu asks new users to understand service and GGUF terminology before they can choose how to set up a model.

## User Impact

Users see **Local AI**, a plain-language explanation of connecting an app versus letting OpenClaw download and run a model, and **Set up** as the shared fallback action.

This is a copy-only follow-up. It does not implement app detection, app installation, or Windows recovery; those remain separate focused changes. No merge is requested.

prs.title: fix(github): keep detail cache windows on elapsed time
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>maintainer-edits</summary>

Maintainer edits are enabled on this branch: feel free to rebase, tweak comment wording, adjust how the rewritten cases are grouped, or land it directly without waiting for another round from me.

</details>

<details>
<summary>maintainer-options</summary>

**Land-ready rationale**

- **Owner:** `detailCache` is a module-private `Map` in `extensions/github/src/detail.ts:66`; all three `entry.expiresAt` writes (:535, :542, :550) and both reads (:300, :322) live in the same `loadGitHubDetailWithIdentity` closure. The five `Date.now()` sites in the file are exactly these TTL sites — after this change the file contains zero `Date.now()` calls, so no mixed time base is possible inside the owner.
- **No contract change:** `grep -rn detailCache` across the repo hits only this file (12 sites); the entry type is never exported, serialized, written to disk or compared anywhere else, so the reading is process-local by construction — what `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts` documents for elapsed readings.
- **Completes the cutover already made next door:** #190894 (merged 2026-11-02) converted the *same shape* in this same extension's sibling store — `extensions/acpx/src/pi-session-store.ts` cache windows went to `performance.now()` — plus `src/gateway/server-methods/usage-cache.ts` and `extensions/github/src/preview.ts` (every timing in it is already `performance.now()`). `detail.ts` is the leftover point.
- **Proof is deterministic and cheap:** two regression cases fail at their intended assertions on current main and the full two-file suite passes at head (64/64, 5.78s), plus an 8-run standalone real-transport matrix and a 6-run shipped-Gateway RPC matrix over real HTTPS with control groups.

**Alternatives considered**

| Option | Effect | Cost if chosen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Accept (this PR)** | 5-minute/30-second detail windows are measured on elapsed time; clock corrections neither stampede GitHub reads nor serve stale details | none beyond the 5 one-token changes + comment |
| Keep `Date.now()` and document it | no code change | a `+5 min` jump drops every cached issue/PR detail at once (immediate re-read burst against GitHub rate limits right after a resume); a `−5 min` jump serves PR-head/check state past its 30-second partial window |
| Convert the 429 cooldown in `github-api.ts` too | — | **rejected:** that deadline must stay wall clock — it compares against GitHub's own epoch (`x-ratelimit-reset`, `retry-after`); mixing domains there would be wrong. Out of this PR's scope by design. |

**Scope statement:** 3 files, +61/−5; production change is 5 token swaps plus a 3-line comment. No new option, validator, config key, schema, persistence or shared API. No other extension or core clock site is touched.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

The Control-UI/tool GitHub detail reader (`controlUi.githubDetail`, `tools.github read`) caches issue/PR/commit documents in a process-local map whose windows are computed on the host wall clock:

- `+5 min` wall-clock correction (laptop resume, NTP step, VM restore): every cached detail instantly reads as expired — the next Control-UI render or agent tool read re-issues the repository + item reads immediately, a stampede against GitHub exactly when the host is also re-syncing.
- `−5 min` correction: an entry that passed its 30-second partial window (pull requests, whose heads and checks move independently of the body) keeps being served — stale PR-head/check state stays visible past its designed refresh window for as long as the wall clock lags.

Precedent: [#190894](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190894) (merged 2026-11-02) moved probe timings and cache windows onto `performance.now()` / `monotonicNow()` across ~20 sites **including the same-shape cache in `extensions/acpx/src/pi-session-store.ts` and every timing in the sibling `extensions/github/src/preview.ts`**; [#190997](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190997) (same day) applied it to the Discord entity cache. This PR switches the remaining cache window in `detail.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

All five TTL sites now read `performance.now()` instead of `Date.now()`: the two freshness reads (:300 hit check, :322 overview reuse) and the three entry writes (:535 success 5 min, :542/:550 partial 30 s). The five sites form one closed loop inside a single function — there is no sixth reader that could compare the stored value against wall time (grep-verified), so the swap cannot split the time base.

Nothing else changes: `SUCCESS_CACHE_MS`/`PARTIAL_CACHE_MS` keep their values, LRU pruning, `refresh` sweeps, the 409 head recheck, identity revalidation and the GitHub-driven 429 cooldown are untouched, and no option/validator/config/persistence is added. The existing `expires cached visibility failures` case now spies both clocks (`Date.now` and `performance.now`), the same adaptation #190894 made in `preview.test.ts`.

Production LOC is `+10/−5` (five swaps — one rewraps a long condition across three lines — plus a 3-line comment).

Classification: `behavior-completing` — it completes the elapsed-time cutover the sibling files already made.

## User Impact

Operators running a long-lived Gateway with the Control UI or GitHub tool reads no longer see detail-cache churn or stale PR state when the host clock is corrected: after a resume the reader keeps serving an entry until its real 5 minutes / 30 seconds pass instead of bursting fresh GitHub requests, and entries never outlive their real window. Under an uncorrected clock the read pattern is identical to before (control runs match request-for-request).

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `5339649b68b582043c926992356590efbd39eeb5`
- Current-main RED baseline: `d56403f0c3c25e5d579ba26d49db12b26ece6814` (production untouched; only the new/updated tests applied)
  - `extensions/github/src/detail.ts` md5 `0fb973689937b900df917a789709c51c` (base) → `305f2fd4397fba13fda9f510f4d0adec` (head)
  - `extensions/github/src/detail.test.ts` md5 `a5e9cf2f61fb68673b3092de4713ede1` (base) → `8e6855cf9a116efeee1406866f92cbaa` (base+new cases / head)
  - `extensions/github/src/detail-checks.test.ts` md5 `c879c38da7df4d44b8091518c6006c4c` (base) → `43fddc2ca40ee31879b600e9e1267669` (head; dual-clock spy added for the review's P2)
- Production entry: `loadSessionGitHubDetail` / `loadGitHubDetail` → `loadGitHubDetailWithIdentity` in `extensions/github/src/detail.ts:270-556`; shipped chains: `src/gateway/server-methods/control-ui.ts:438-441` (`controlUi.githubDetail`) and `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.ts:100` (agent tool read)
- Decision surface: `entry.expiresAt` (5 min success / 30 s partial window)
- Recorder/readback boundary: stub-side request counts (`PROOF_LOAD1` / `PROOF_LOAD2 delta`) and the vitest fetch-mock call counts
- Harness: frozen preload sha256 `b5036740d672d736703befc16087c9f9619a0d96ab54c5b17cdf65992d3e0991` (patches **only** `Date.now`, applied 200 ms after the probe's marker file, i.e. after the entry exists), probe sha256 `8c6cdccee3ce49fbfbdbcb68ae5747613ce7b4506f3309d9dd593c7ba80c18cf`, identical bytes on both sides; secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker on the pinned test host; **real HTTPS on loopback** (the shipped resolver only accepts `https` bases, so the stub terminates TLS with a probe-scoped self-signed certificate and only the probe process sets a probe-scoped Node TLS verification relaxation (env scoped to the probe process only); loopback only, no credentials, no external network)

### Inspectable RED → GREEN traces

RED — current main + only the new/updated tests (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/github/src/detail.test.ts extensions/github/src/detail-checks.test.ts`, both files of the extension together):

```text
× GitHub detail cache clock domain > keeps a settled detail cached across a forward wall-clock step
  → expected 2 to be 1 // Object.is equality
× GitHub detail cache clock domain > refreshes a stale detail after a backward wall-clock step once its window passes
  → expected 1 to be 2 // Object.is equality
 Test Files  1 failed (1) | 1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 62 passed (64)
```

(`2` = base re-read the item after only a wall step; `1` = base kept serving after its real window. The other 62 — including the rewritten visibility case and the review's P2 checks-expiry case — pass on the baseline.)

GREEN — exact head (md5s `305f2fd4…` / `8e6855cf…` / `43fddc2c…` verified in-tree before the run):

```text
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  64 passed (64)
  Duration  5.78s
```

Real-entry matrix — real HTTPS loopback stub, real exported session read, frozen harness, 8 runs, exit 0 each:

| Scenario | base | head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| reuse (no step, read again at ~1 s) | delta 0 | delta 0 |
| natural expiry (no step, read again at 31 s) | delta 3 | delta 3 |
| `+600 s` step after entry exists | **delta 3 (premature re-read)** | **delta 0 (window held)** |
| `−600 s` step, read again after 31 real seconds | **delta 0 (stale past window)** | **delta 3 (refreshed on schedule)** |

### Shipped Gateway RPC matrix — `controlUi.githubDetail` over the real WebSocket

The same discriminating matrix, now through the shipped Gateway entry (`src/index.ts gateway run`, source tree of the exact head, md5s `305f2fd4…` / `8e6855cf…` / `43fddc2c…` verified in-tree before the runs) on the pinned secretless Docker host (Node 24.22.1): a real Gateway process, a real WebSocket `connect` handshake (protocol 4, `operator.read`, token auth), the real `controlUi.githubDetail` handler, and a real HTTPS loopback GitHub stub (self-signed probe certificate; a docker extra-hosts loopback mapping for the GitHub API host; a probe-scoped Node TLS verification relaxation (env scoped to the probe process only) scoped to the Gateway child only; proxy env stripped). `delta` = stub requests the second read adds (0 = served from cache, 3 = full re-read).

Frozen harness: probe sha256 `8c3adac51d1072131335f423c819fd181be434619d33ff90eae924cbc371d4f1` (patches **only** `Date.now`, applied ≥200 ms after the marker so the entry exists first; per-pid `.applied` readback confirms the Gateway main thread took every step), client sha256 `5ba8a28e0970e37bde1df91fa51e5218f4957b6744892957af8570b108829cd6`. The client waits for the `http server listening` startup summary before the first read, so plugin/sidecar startup load cannot race the measurements.

| Scenario | base | head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| control (no step, re-read at ~2.5 s) | delta 0 | delta 0 |
| `+600 s` step after entry exists | **delta 3 (premature re-read)** | **delta 0 (window held)** |
| `−600 s` step, re-read after 31 real seconds | **delta 0 (stale past window)** | **delta 3 (refreshed on schedule)** |

6 runs, exit 0, one `RESULT` line each — the shipped RPC reproduces the standalone matrix exactly: the wall-clock step moves base's window in both directions while head's elapsed-time window holds. Environment repairs on the test host only (no PR file touched): the offline `node_modules` mirror is one lockfile generation stale (`@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.26.13 lacks `overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority`, which the model-runtime sidecar imports), so the 0.26.15 implementation of that one function was ported into the tree's copy to keep the Gateway alive for the full 31 s backward wait.

### Review item P2 — checks expiry regression (fixed)

`extensions/github/src/detail-checks.test.ts` drove the 30-second partial window with a `Date.now` spy only. After the deadline conversion that spy no longer moves the cache, so the final `not.toBe(fresh)` assertion failed in exact-head CI (the reviewer's finding at `detail-checks.test.ts:252`). The case now spies **both** clocks (`Date.now` and `performance.now`) with the same values, preserving its ordering, recovery and expiry assertions — the same adaptation #190894 made in `preview.test.ts`. RED on baseline showed only the two clock-domain cases; the whole two-file suite is green at head (64/64).

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/github/src/detail.test.ts` — RED `2 failed | 48 passed (50)` on baseline, GREEN `50 passed (50)` at head; 5.71s per run on the pinned host (this host forbids local test execution; CI re-runs the suite)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json extensions/github/src/detail.ts extensions/github/src/detail.test.ts extensions/github/src/detail-checks.test.ts` — 0 warnings / 0 errors, 259 rules
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on all three files — clean
- `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts` — `Test lines OK: 6395094; ceiling: 6404398; slack: 9304`
- `git diff --check` — clean
- Not tested: a bundled `dist` Gateway build (local builds are banned on this host and the remote bundler path is unavailable; the shipped-Gateway matrix above runs the exact-head source entry instead), enterprise-redirect/429-cooldown paths (unchanged by design), and live GitHub (the proof stubs the API on loopback)

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+10/−5` (five `Date.now()`→`performance.now()` swaps, one of which rewraps, plus a 3-line comment; all in `extensions/github/src/detail.ts`)
- Test LOC: `+51/−0` (three clock-domain cases + two spy lines in the visibility case + five dual-clock spy lines in the checks-expiry case)

| Impact surface | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/github/src/detail.ts:66-68` | 3-line comment naming the clock domain | none |
| `extensions/github/src/detail.ts:300` | hit check on `performance.now()` | same window, elapsed base; single closed loop |
| `extensions/github/src/detail.ts:322` | overview-seed reuse on `performance.now()` | same |
| `extensions/github/src/detail.ts:535,542,550` | three expiry writes on `performance.now()` | value never leaves the module (grep-verified) |

| `extensions/github/src/detail-checks.test.ts:213,251,255` | checks-expiry case now advances both clocks (review P2) | test-only; ordering/recovery/expiry assertions unchanged |
| `extensions/github/src/detail.test.ts:767-809` | three new clock-domain cases | test-only |

- Existing-solutions preflight: uses the platform monotonic clock directly, exactly as #190894 did inside extensions (which cannot import `src/shared`); no new helper, validator, option or config

prs.title: fix(ui): toast sidebar session action failures
prs.body:
## Summary

Session actions such as archive could render a large dismissible error inside the session sidebar, pushing the session list down. Route current-scope action failures through the shared **top-right toast** lane instead.

- Separate list-loading errors from action errors: failed lists still have their contextual sidebar error and dismissal.
- Preserve action error text for dialogs and reject late errors from retired mutation scopes.
- Keep sidebar rendering and snapshot settlement tied to list errors, not past actions.
- Preserve the server's session-identity/lifecycle checks. This fixes error presentation; it does not silently retry rejected archive operations against replacement sessions.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the old sidebar error through the browser archive-failure flow; inspected and attached [sanitized before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192462#issuecomment-6620416120). Production rendering is unchanged by the subsequent test-only CI repair.
- Owner regression fails on the base because no toast is published, and passes with the fix. Includes top-right placement and retired-scope suppression; consolidated into the existing list/action error matrix.
- Initial focused proof: 230 unit tests and 27 browser scenarios passed across session data, sidebar interactions, archive/undo, rename, delete, filtered list-error flows, and the Sessions page.
- CI follow-up `c9e37ac99774443ed3631582b1e387e2ec5bcde0`: 112 affected unit tests and 9 browser scenarios passed after repairing consumer assertions. Dialog preparation failures assert top-right toasts; rename assertions distinguish the dialog's inline callout from modal-hosted toast alerts and use the existing virtual clock for transient feedback.
- Test-line ratchet passes with a **net reduction of 7 lines** against base `40b3be0b302d885a880dee8435d479a093b23bad`. Existing batch setup and regressions were consolidated; no allocation, ceiling increase, or skipped coverage was added. This addresses the hosted P2 budget finding.
- UI typecheck, scoped formatting, targeted lint, and `git diff --check` passed after the CI repair. The initial broader targeted lint reported existing Solid reactivity warnings, with no errors.
- Independent local autoreview, P0–P2 coverage: scoped-clean with no actionable findings for the original production change (`40b3be0` → local snapshot committed as `fd3dddf`) and for the subsequent test-only repair (`aba344e` → local snapshot committed as `c9e37ac`).

Fresh remote CI remains the landing gate; the local results above are not a claim that remote CI has passed.

The archive incident's log confirms a session-state guard rejection but does not identify the changed field. No backend root-cause fix or live Gateway deployment is claimed.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): avoid slow snapshots of installed dependencies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Managed worktrees with provisioned `node_modules` can spend minutes snapshotting installed dependencies before removal, keeping session deletion pending and filling the shared-state database.

## User Impact

Ordinary removal skips ignored provisioned files inside `node_modules`, including nested package dependencies. Reinstall dependencies after restoring the worktree. Edited local configuration, tracked changes, and non-ignored untracked work remain recoverable. Explicit exact-state retirement and existing snapshots retain their previous recovery behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each provisioned file previously incurred filesystem inspection, three Git membership queries per batch, and one awaited SQLite transaction per at-most-1-MiB chunk. A 62,000-file synthetic dependency tree caused 62,001 chunk writes and 1,455 membership subprocesses. Excluding reinstallable dependency bytes at the snapshot entry point removes that work without changing schemas, adding a cache, or weakening removal ownership. Other ignored configuration can contain user edits, so its existing capture remains.

Production code grows by four lines to retain that distinction and the explicit exact-state contract. The 69-line test allocation covers real removal/restore, nested dependencies, force-tracked dependency-directory content, edited local configuration, and exact-state fallback recovery.

## Evidence

- Regression failed on the original snapshot owner because dependency chunks were persisted. Both affected service suites pass: 36 tests, 57.21 seconds test-runner duration.
- Codex autoreview: scoped clean through P2. Core/test/script typechecks and core lint pass. Two benchmark-only lint findings were corrected and focused script lint passes. `pnpm check:changed --staged` also reports four unrelated production dead exports in `node-plugin-tool-snapshot.ts`; the identical production scan fails on untouched main parent `1ca0669dbe3982369463b921397027f3727f51fd`. These exports lost their external production consumers in #191589 (`e0ac3370bbe37d73abc057bc8bd4dd32670c8e97`), a confirmed main regression. All remaining changed-file checks pass after the focused lint correction.
- Five serial interleaved native APFS pairs completed on Apple M3 Ultra (32 cores, 512 GiB RAM, Node 26.12.1) (2,388 tracked files; 62,000 provisioned files / 1.064 GiB, nested pnpm layout). Both A/A controls agree within 0.64%; every candidate preserves the identical Git user-work tree and edited configuration. Nearest-rank p95 is the maximum of five samples.

| Measured owner | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Snapshot wall time | 103.665s / 108.419s | 0.975s / 0.983s |
| Whole removal wall time | 106.163s / 111.699s | 3.530s / 3.553s |
| Snapshot process CPU | 223.219s / 232.464s | 0.850s / 0.855s |
| Snapshot main-thread allocation | 10.203GB / 10.220GB | 24.251MB / 25.091MB |
| Chunk writes / bytes, every run | 62,001 / 1,142,784,025 | 1 / 25 |

Snapshot latency improves 99.06%; whole removal improves 96.68%. The original five-pair finish sample shows **23.83% higher macOS physical footprint**, comparing ~3.5s candidate completion with ~106s baseline completion. This field is named RSS by Node but installed libuv uses [Darwin physical footprint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libuv/libuv/v1.53.0/src/unix/darwin.c). It was investigated rather than dismissed:

- A separate unmodified committed-workload pair under `/usr/bin/time -l` reduces native peak RSS **1,951.48 → 1,316.34 MiB (-32.55%)**, and peak physical footprint **1,941,799,344 → 1,401,428,192 bytes**.
- The original lifecycle diagnostic has similar initial footprints (958.82 / 934.49 MiB). At common removal ages ~5s / 30s / 60s, baseline footprint is **1,346.05 / 1,610.98 / 1,398.87 MiB**, versus candidate **1,203.39 / 922.50 / 899.11 MiB**. The fast return is sampled earlier in reclamation; both named worker sets retire normally.
- An additional candidate control at the baseline's exact 182.187s age records **498,144,800 vs 629,163,192 bytes**; after registered-worker drainage and main GC, **467,897,944 vs 595,410,064 bytes**, stable five seconds later. This extra candidate started lower (723.44 MiB), so it is a single diagnostic control, not proof of a repeatable retained-memory saving. No production GC or worker-lifetime change is made.

Separate 1,000-file worker profiles confirm BEGIN/COMMIT **1,009 → 9**, SELECT **9,068 → 68**, INSERT **1,005 → 5**, and maintenance `lstat` **30,052 → 52**. Native SQL subtotal is **100.98 → 1.44ms**, summed writer-held intervals **500.22 → 11.40ms**. Native main and worker CPU/allocation profiles are retained; main traces include setup, so only scoped counters are reported as removal CPU. prs.title: fix(slack-huddles): huddle links stall and in-call mic checks fail when Slack opens a separate call window
prs.body:
Related: #176115

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Slack huddles plugin stalls when joining from a huddle link, reports a false microphone problem once in the call, and collects no captions. Current Slack sends the link through a desktop-app page and a "Join a huddle?" prompt, then opens the call in a separate window that the plugin never looked at.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw slackhuddles join <huddle link>` now joins an active huddle muted with the camera off and reports `inCall: true` without a false `slack-microphone-required` action. It collects captions and leaves cleanly. An empty huddle reports `slack-huddle-not-active`. No config or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack opens the call in an unnamed `about:blank` window from the channel tab. Only the handle `window.open` returns can reach it, so the Slack status script now keeps that handle. It searches the window for the join preview, mute button, microphone picker, camera, and captions. The window is used only while its URL names the same workspace and channel as the verified channel tab. Membership is still proven only by the channel tab's huddle header: the status script reads that header from the tab itself, never from the call window, as the audio, leave and page-identity checks already do. Every click keeps its existing authority recheck.

The script also:

- continues past the desktop-app page only to the requested huddle;
- answers the link prompt only for an active huddle;
- reads the preview Join button's `aria-label`;
- treats a disabled preview microphone as off only when Chrome has not granted microphone access;
- accepts the `OpenClaw Meeting Audio (Preferred)` label.

**Maintainer decision:** `controlDocumentsSource` is a new optional field on the shared status-prelude options used by `MeetingPlatformAdapter.createPageScripts`. It defaults to the current page, and only Slack sets it. If you'd rather not widen that contract, the lookup can move into Slack-only helpers, at the cost of duplicating `firstRaw` and the microphone-device lookup.

Known limits:

- A call window opened by hand, or before a page reload, is not reachable.
- Leaving from the preview, before Join, can leave Slack's preview window open.
- Leave still uses the channel tab's Leave buttons, which exist in today's layout.

## Evidence

Versions: the head merges current `main` (`42aab1c`, 4 Nov). An earlier merge (`05a73c2`) brought in the change that folded Slack's in-call status file into `slack-huddles-page-scripts.ts` (the participant count now reads the call window there too). The live runs below used `ed23110` and the real-Chrome check used `620f9a0`, both on the earlier base; the head then adds only the tab-only membership read and its test. They were not rerun on the new base. The head was rechecked on an isolated Linux test machine (Node 26), targeted to the change; results below the test list.

### Live run

Live runs on a real Slack workspace with two members: a person in the huddle and the agent's account. Linux, Chrome 155, OpenClaw built from this branch (`ed23110`). IDs are placeholders.

| Scenario | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Join from link (`transcribe`) | stuck on the desktop-app page; prompt never answered | `inCall: true`, `micMuted: true`, `cameraOff: true`, no manual action; stayed in 2+ min |
| In-call microphone check | `slack-microphone-required` (false) | none |
| Captions | not collected | `captioning: true`; participant speech captured |
| Empty huddle | — | `slack-huddle-not-active` |
| Leave | — | `browserLeft: true`; tab and call window closed |
| Talk-back (`bidi`) | — | `inCall: true`, both audio directions routed, `speechReady: true`, realtime session ready |

```text
main:      join https://app.slack.com/huddle/T…/C…  -> stuck on slack.com/huddle/C… ("Launching … Open Slack"), inCall: false
           joined by hand -> inCall: true, manualAction.reason: "slack-microphone-required"
this PR:   join … --mode transcribe -> "inCall": true, "micMuted": true, "cameraOff": true (no manualAction)
           captions -> "captioning": true, "lastCaptionText": "You want or not that is the question."
           leave -> "browserLeft": true
```

Talk-back on this branch alone stops because of #173896 and #177633, which this PR does not fix. With #173898 applied and the lab DNS stall removed, a full two-way conversation worked in the huddle: 371 audio pulls over 2 minutes, no failures, and the participant heard the agent answer. Details are in the notes below.

### Real-Chrome authority check

A throwaway headless Chrome 155 ran this branch's production Slack status script against crafted `app.slack.com` pages served through CDP `Fetch`. No Slack login was used. The channel tab opens its call window with `window.open("about:blank")`, as Slack does. The window holds a mute button, the microphone label and a caption. Every case uses talk-back with Chrome's microphone granted and starts muted, so a trusted window gets exactly one Unmute click. Each case ran 3 times with identical results.

The status scripts that ran hash to `1fd7a710fce6b8fd` (channel-only link) and `75abf935718bc2b3` (workspace link), the scripts `620f9a0` built (before the merge of current `main` and the tab-only membership read).

| Case | Unmute clicks in window | Captions read | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Channel-only link, window on the bound workspace | 1 | 1 | `inCall: true`, input routed |
| Channel-only link, window on another workspace (`T9999…`) | 0 | 0 | window ignored; `slack-microphone-required` |
| Workspace link, session kept (control) | 1 | 1 | `inCall: true`, input routed |
| Workspace link, session replaced during the awaited permission check | 0 | 0 | `inCall: false`, `captioning: false` |

The remaining `slack-audio-choice-required` in the trusted cases comes from the crafted page, which has no speaker control.

Tests: new `slack-huddles-platform-adapter.window.test.ts` with 21 cases. On the earlier base, 14 of the first 20 failed on `main`; the rest are negative controls. The membership case added now passes on `main` too, which never reads the call window. The cases cover:

- the desktop-app page;
- the link prompt;
- a muted join from the call window;
- in-call controls;
- workspace isolation;
- a replaced session, before and during the status check;
- captions in both windows;
- membership: a call window showing the in-huddle header while the channel tab does not leaves the session out of the call. It fails with the earlier call-window read (`inCall` true) and passes with this head.

The earlier Teams test that checked which element the caption observer watched was removed: it asserted the mocked observer target, not caption text. The Slack window test above checks that the observer watches the call window and that its captions are collected.

Checks on `b2caea5` (on `main` `05a73c2`); the head adds only a clean merge of `main` `42aab1c`:
- Slack huddles tests (platform adapter, audio, window, URLs): 4 files, 104 passed. Shared meeting tests (`status-call-source`, `status-source-parity`, `platform-adapter.provenance`): 3 files, 30 passed.
- Teams and Zoom adapter and caption tests, which share the changed status code: 4 files, 91 passed.
- The new membership case against the head with the earlier membership read: 1 failed, 20 passed; on the head: 21 passed.
- Core test typecheck shards, core and extensions typecheck: clean. Oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files: clean.

Proof artifice: the real-Chrome authority check served crafted `app.slack.com` pages through CDP `Fetch` instead of Slack, and the unit tests use fixture pages. The live runs used a real Slack workspace, a real participant and the real browser with nothing scripted.

Test lines are net +400 against `main` (allocation record `config/test-lines-allocations/slack-huddle-call-window.txt`): one new window test file whose 21 cases cover each Slack page the join passes through (desktop-app page, link prompt, call-window preview), workspace isolation, a replaced session, captions in both windows and tab-only membership. It reuses the existing Slack adapter fixture (`slack-huddles-platform-adapter.test-helpers.ts`, extended with a microphone-permission option and an observer record); the existing Slack suites have no second window, so no smaller set covers these cases.

Test gap: talk-back works live only with #173898 applied and the DNS stall from #177633 removed.

<details>
<summary>Investigation notes</summary>

- **Window identity.** Chrome `Target.getTargets` shows the call window's `openerId` is the channel tab. Its controls (`segmented-mute-button-main`, `huddle-toolbar-mic-popover-button`) and captions (`.p-huddle_closed_caption_event__event_text`) render only there. The channel tab keeps `.p-huddle_channel_header_button--in_huddle`.
- **Talk-back failure.** Slack's `p-huddle_audio` element in the channel tab carries the live call stream once Slack has a microphone. The realtime bridge then closes with `Meeting browser audio capture failed: Gateway requester authority changed`, which is #173896.
- **Lab check with #173898.** Its three production files were applied on this branch and reverted afterward. Capture outlived the join response, and the model started output. About 6 s later, a capture pull failed with `browser request timed out` and the session closed. A second run timed out during the join. This remaining shared-runtime timeout is not addressed here. Stage timing traced it to the browser plugin's URL safety check, which resolves the page hostname on every audio pull; a lab DNS lookup that hangs for the 5 s resolver timeout exhausts the pull's 5 s budget. Pinning the hostname removed the failure. Tracked in #177633. Caption reads still failed with `Gateway requester authority changed` after the join, a path #173898 does not cover.
- **Host-only failures, not this change:**
  - Closing tabs mid-call left a stale Slack device, and later joins then failed. In three controlled trials with a clean start, joins held for 70 s; four later trials were blocked by a stale device the test harness left behind.
  - Chrome auto-blocked the microphone after repeated ignored prompts; permission grants do not override that block.
  - The container's WirePlumber had no default audio device. Without a microphone, Slack joins presence-only and opens no call audio.
- **Not reproducible live.** Channel ids are unique across workspaces, so the same-id case cannot be produced against live Slack. It is covered by the real-Chrome check above and the unit tests.

</details>

prs.title: fix: sessions of signed-in people never resume after restart on Gateways without roles
prs.body:
Closes #192416

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a Gateway without `gateway.roles`, sessions owned by an ordinary signed-in person (for example, a single user on Tailscale or trusted-proxy sign-in) never resume after a graceful restart. Their restart-captured queued messages are dropped, and host events in their sessions fail with `Session principal has no current run authority.` Affected host events include exec completion wakes, plugin runtime events and `system-event` wakes.

## User Impact

User impact: after a restart or update, interrupted work in these sessions continues automatically, captured messages are sent, and background notices reach the agent again. Each person runs with no more than the authority of the connection they last sent from: a write-only device stays write-only. Owner sessions and Gateways with roles behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

#185730 admits session-principal work under the principal's *current* authority, which it derives from the profile alone. Without roles, a profile has no authority of its own: a connection's scopes come from its paired device and `identityScopes`. Every non-owner profile was therefore denied. Granting admin whenever roles are unset would let limited devices and identity grants escalate. This change instead reuses the revalidating operator-source recovery that scheduled work already relies on:

- After a person's input is accepted, the admitted run's existing bounded `recoverySnapshot` is stored on the session entry under `operatorSources[profileId]`. It is written only when it changes, kept private, follows the logical session, and is not copied to forks.
- `prepareSessionPrincipalRunAuthority`, the single entry point for restart resume, captured queued inputs and principal system turns, restores that person's recorded source through `restoreGatewayQueuedOperatorRecovery` when roles are unset. That owner rechecks the following on every use and revokes running work when any of them change:
  - device pairing, token and scopes
  - auth method
  - shared-secret generation
  - profile identity and role policy
  - access grant
- The usual session-sharing authorization still applies.

Accepted limit: a person who never sent from an authenticated connection in a session still gets today's visible "could not resume" notice there.

## Evidence

- **Acceptance e2e, real Gateway processes** (`test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts`, new case "resumes a signed-in person's session and queued input on a Gateway without roles"). Setup: trusted-proxy sign-in, no roles, a person on a device paired for `operator.read`+`operator.write`, and a session created by their first `chat.send`. A second person queues input, then the Gateway receives SIGTERM and restarts. Results:
  - The resume input runs.
  - The queued input runs under its sender's source.
  - A later `system-event` wake runs in the person's session.
  - The recorded scopes stay `operator.read`/`operator.write`.
  - The log has no `no current run authority`.
- **Red on base:** the same test with the production change removed fails with exactly the production errors: `Skipped restart resume … Session principal has no current run authority` and `Queued input … was not sent after restart`.
- **Focused unit tests** (`src/gateway/session-operator-sources.test.ts`):
  - Admission works only after a source is recorded, with the original scopes and no admin substitute.
  - Unpairing the device denies admission.
  - The source survives transcript rotation.
  - Configured roles take precedence.
  - Incognito reset keeps the source and a new node drops it.
- **Hook payloads:** the reset/new and session patch hooks never expose `operatorSources`. The regression test uses the real hook emitters.
- **Mac Studio real-behavior proof (Crabbox):** the PR head passes 5/5. The base is red with the same two production errors. Details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192444#issuecomment-6620648966
- **Inherited CI flake:** `restart markers survive graceful shutdown (suspend/reopen and blocked store: false)` times out on unmodified `main` (2 of 2 local runs). It passes on this PR head (2 of 2 local runs, plus the Studio run). Its sessions use the shared-token owner, which this change skips.
