prs.title: fix(codex): pass /v1/responses client functions to the Codex runtime
prs.body:
Closes #113318

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on the Codex runtime, caller functions sent as `tools` to `/v1/responses` or `/v1/chat/completions` are never shown to the model. With a pinned or `required` `tool_choice` the request then fails with HTTP 502 (`tool_choice required a <name> tool call, but the agent did not produce one`); with an optional `tool_choice` the model can only answer in prose.

## User Impact

User impact: callers can pass their own functions, including a pinned `tool_choice`, to an agent on the Codex runtime and get the call back, the same as on the built-in runtime: a `function_call` output item on `/v1/responses`, or `choices[].message.tool_calls` on `/v1/chat/completions`. OpenClaw does not run these functions; the caller does. When a pinned or `required` `tool_choice` is still not satisfied, the request fails with the same 502 as before; optional-tool requests may still return prose.

## Why This Change Was Made

The HTTP endpoint already hands caller functions to the run as `clientTools`, and the built-in runtime turns them into delegated tools. The Codex runtime builds its own tool list and left them out, so the model only saw OpenClaw's tools and answered in prose.

This adds a harness adapter, `createAgentHarnessClientTools`, next to the built-in runtime's `toClientToolDefinitions`. The built-in runtime keeps using `toClientToolDefinitions`. The new adapter reuses the same delegated-tool contract and its supporting helpers:
- the shared delegated pending result;
- the attempt's `toolsAllow` cap;
- the existing name-conflict error, which the endpoint maps to HTTP 400;
- the same eligibility: no client functions when tools are disabled, for memory runs, or for a model without tool support;
- source order for parallel calls: Codex reserves each call's slot when it arrives, before hooks run.

Codex adds these tools to the thread's dynamic tools. The existing bridge wraps them with the usual hooks, and their terminal result uses the existing terminal-tool release to stop the native turn, so Codex makes no second model request. The recorded calls go back as the attempt's `clientToolCalls`, which the shared runner already turns into each endpoint's tool-call output.

Accepted edge cases:
- A Codex-supervised thread keeps its saved native tool declarations and cannot add caller functions; with a pinned or `required` `tool_choice` such a request still fails with the existing 502.
- Like `sessions_yield`, the stop is a native interrupt, so Codex may record an interruption marker after the call. Changing the function set between requests on one session is a dynamic-tool change and is handled like any other.

The reporter's fork PR (hddms-matt-bot/openclaw#1) took a similar direction on older source; this change was written against current `main` and reuses the existing delegated-tool and terminal-release owners instead of a Codex-only delegation path.

Maintainer decision: this adds `createAgentHarnessClientTools` to the private harness SDK subpath `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-tool-runtime` (documented in the harness attempt-runtime page). If the owner prefers another surface, the Codex side only needs the tools, the reserve call and the recorded calls.

## Evidence

- New regression tests, red on `main` and green with the fix:
  - `run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts`: a client function is declared to Codex, its call returns `clientToolCalls`, the turn is interrupted, and no OpenClaw tool runs. On `main`: fails ("expected [ 'managed_task' ] to include 'submit_probe_result'").
  - The same Codex file also checks that no client function is declared when tools are disabled or the model cannot call tools (a guard; it passes on `main` too).
  - `agent-tool-definition-adapter.test.ts`: the harness helper applies `toolsAllow`, keeps the model's order when a later call finishes first, and raises the shared conflict error. On `main`: fails (helper missing).
- Focused files pass with the fix (Codex dynamic tools 19, adapter 29, adapter fires-once, `openresponses-http.test.ts`).
- Core, core-test, extension and extension-test typechecks, lint and format pass on the changed files; `check:changed` and the baseline ratchets pass except checks that could not run offline on the test machine (listed below).
- Test lines are net +96 against `main`, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-responses-client-tools.txt`: one Codex boundary test and one two-case eligibility table that reuses the existing run-attempt harness (`startTool`, `createStartedThreadHarness`) and one short helper test in the existing conflict-check block.

### Real Gateway proof with a real model

Tested revisions: base `6c298cb69d8` (`main`) and fix `066157068b1`. The PR head merges current `main` (`baaa01091c5`, 4 Nov); besides the test-line allocation record, it differs from the tested fix only in the adapter's imports, because `main` moved `jsonResult`, `payloadTextResult` and `ToolInputError` into their own modules (#191905). Rechecked on the merged head on an isolated Linux test machine (Node 26): the four `agent-tool-definition-adapter` test files 40 passed, `openresponses-http.test.ts` 60 passed, Codex `run-attempt.dynamic-tools` 19 and `event-projector.dynamic-tools` 14 passed; core, core-test and extensions typechecks, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files clean.

An isolated Gateway built from the tree, the real Codex app-server (`@openai/codex` 0.164.0) and the real OpenAI model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` on the Codex runtime. The request is the reporter's: `/v1/responses`, `tools: [submit_probe_result]`, pinned `tool_choice`, `stream: false`; a new session per request.

| Tree | Requests | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base `6c298cb69d8` | 2 | 2 × HTTP 502 `tool_choice required a submit_probe_result tool call, but the agent did not produce one`, no output items |
| fix `066157068b1` | 3 | 3 × HTTP 200, one `function_call` `submit_probe_result` `{"greeting":"Hello"}`, status `completed` |

```
[6c298cb69d8] RUN1 status=502 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[] tokens in/out 140686/363
[6c298cb69d8] RUN2 status=502 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[] tokens in/out 161571/348
[066157068b1] RUN1 status=200 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[function_call submit_probe_result {"greeting":"Hello"}] tokens in/out 30180/41
[066157068b1] RUN2 status=200 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[function_call submit_probe_result {"greeting":"Hello"}] tokens in/out 30180/53
[066157068b1] RUN3 status=200 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[function_call submit_probe_result {"greeting":"Hello"}] tokens in/out 30180/48
```

On `main` the model spent several steps (about 140k input tokens) looking for a function it could not see, then the Gateway failed closed. With the fix the turn ends at the call: one model step, and the function is returned to the caller instead of being run.

### Gateway proof with a scripted model (more cases)

The same Gateway and Codex app-server with a local fake model that calls a function only if Codex lists it (otherwise it answers "Hello" in prose):

| Run | HTTP | Output | Model saw the function |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v2026.7.1-1` (reporter's release) | 502, same error | none | n/a (that release's mock does not record tools) |
| base `6c298cb69d8` | 502, same error | none | no |
| fix `066157068b1` | 200 | `function_call submit_probe_result` | yes |
| fix, same session, different function | 200 | `function_call submit_other_result` | only the new one |
| fix, same session, no functions | 200 | message "Hello" | none left over |

With the fix, the fake model received one request per call and no `function_call_output`, so OpenClaw did not run the function.

Proof artifice: the second table uses a scripted local model endpoint; the first table uses a real OpenAI model.

Proof gap: the streaming (`stream: true`) path and `/v1/chat/completions` were not run live; they share the same attempt result. `check:changed` checks that need network on the test machine (Bun format/lint comparison, `knip`) and the SQLite worker ratchet (no `rg` in the container) could not run there; CI runs them.

prs.title: fix(agents): sandbox policies reject sandboxed agent runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A plugin requiring `before_agent_run` context `sandboxed === true` rejects a builtin embedded run even after the host has prepared its sandbox. Setup supplies the prepared sandbox to tools, but downstream hook context reads the original attempt parameters.

## User Impact

Policy plugins receive the sandbox state actually prepared for the current attempt. A genuinely sandboxed run can satisfy the existing policy, while preparation returning no sandbox produces `sandboxed=false` and remains blocked by that policy before model dispatch.

The assignment also overwrites a stale caller sandbox on internal attempt input. That defensive case is covered by an in-process regression; no supported normal Gateway route injecting that stale value was identified, so this PR does not claim a reproduced externally reachable policy bypass.

## Why This Change Was Made

Publish the prepared sandbox in the existing local attempt snapshot before downstream hooks consume it. The change preserves the caller's sandbox field/object and the public hook contract; it adds no new policy state, API or fallback. This is not a claim of whole-input immutability: existing finalization separately clears `input.continuation`.

Production +3 lines, tests +36, allocation metadata +2 across three files. The two added full-attempt regressions cover prepared-sandbox admission and stale-caller rejection using mocked preparation/prompt execution. CLI filesystem binding remains separate work: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163238.

## Evidence on the Reviewed Main Candidate

[Candidate-specific terminal excerpts, six Gateway results, reproduction commands, complete standalone probe and supplementary test instrumentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191205#issuecomment-6596016240).

- Tested head: `c9b74a6e9a148207996054be8d8ce2cc06de59f1`.
- Head tree: `45782131d0f23e9ea2046e9a3eb7486deecf108e`.
- Unfixed control: exact parent `ed2def8f795223f8aa49490aeb800b03be2b01c0`.
- Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, official pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`, same workspace dependencies/lockfile on both sides.

These executions are specific to the main PR candidate, not the release backport. The latest moving main was not dynamically tested.

### Same full regression file on parent and head

The identical head test file was copied onto the parent without the production fix: **25 pass / 2 fail / 0 skip**, with the two expected opposite sandbox-value assertion failures (43.53s Vitest). On head: **27 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip** (24.23s).

Because the original red assertions stop before the prompt assertion, separate temporary soft-assert instrumentation recorded both hook values and prompt calls. For prepared=true/caller absent, parent reports false and makes 0 prompt calls; head reports true and makes 1. For prepared=false/stale caller present, parent reports true and makes 1 prompt call; head reports false and makes 0. Both consistent-state controls pass. These are internal mocked-preparation tests, not HTTP-provider observations. The instrumentation is included with the evidence and was removed after testing.

### Shipped Gateway + real Docker + local HTTP provider

Both exact revisions were separately built with official `qaRuntime`. The same standalone probe launches `node openclaw.mjs gateway run` and calls `gateway call agent --expect-final`, with isolated HOME/state/config, a real loaded policy plugin, a local HTTP Responses fixture, and the real builtin `exec` tool.

| Revision / sandbox / plugin policy | Hook sandboxed | HTTP requests | Observed result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Parent / on / observe | false | 2 | Real exec returns `DOCKER\n/workspace`; run completes |
| Parent / on / require true | false | 0 | Run blocked by the test plugin |
| Head / on / observe | true | 2 | Real exec returns `DOCKER\n/workspace`; run completes |
| Head / on / require true | true | 2 | Real exec returns `DOCKER\n/workspace`; run completes |
| Parent / off / require true | false | 0 | Run blocked before the first HTTP request |
| Head / off / require true | false | 0 | Run blocked before the first HTTP request |

The observe control establishes that the parent really runs the tool inside Docker while publishing false to the hook. The require-policy pair then demonstrates the user-visible false rejection and its repair. Blocked RPC results have `status: error` and `hook_block`; command exit code 0 is not counted as an admitted run.

**Boundary:** The strict policy is a test plugin, not a default OpenClaw policy. The real Gateway off/require test has no stale caller value. That stale-value combination is proven only at the internal attempt boundary above: public builtin entry parameters do not supply sandbox, and dispatch supplies it only to the transport-owning plugin-harness branch. No reachable Gateway stale-input bypass or private-data disclosure was reproduced. `sandboxed=true` describes prepared sandbox state, not confinement of every plugin tool, elevated exec or external CLI.

### Additional verification

- Official typed lint, oxfmt/Bun format parity and affected strict test type graph pass.
- Adjacent sandbox/hook-context/Knowledge regressions: **14/14**; existing CLI admission/reliability regressions: **150/150**.
- [Independent hosted verification](https://github.com/WangKangAandy/openclaw/actions/runs/41485974966) asserts the exact candidate SHA/tree/parent and passes official focused checks, full 27-case regression, test-line allocation and tracked-source cleanliness. Its separate workflow commit `2641c57bfdf490abe85d5c161a59531552f6e117` is not part of this PR.
- [Upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41487743941) succeeded on this head; inapplicable skipped jobs are not represented as executed tests.
- Local allocation-ratchet execution was blocked by an old Git lacking `git cat-file --batch -z`; only the separate hosted result is claimed for that check.

No production deployment, live platform delivery, real paid model, new real HTTP-503 fallback integration, or full release/UI build was performed for these main-candidate checks. Earlier release-backport integration remains separate historical evidence and is not used to establish this candidate's behavior.

prs.title: fix(meetings): one slow browser audio pull ends a talk-back call
prs.body:
Fixes #177633

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: one slow browser audio pull ends a meeting talk-back call. The browser audio transport closes the realtime bridge on the first failed pull, so a single browser request that misses its 5 s deadline drops the call, even though the page capture is still alive.

## User Impact

User impact: a talk-back (`bidi`) meeting call now survives one stalled audio pull. The participant loses at most the audio the page dropped while the pull was stuck. Two failed pulls in a row still end the call, and a capture the page reports as closed still ends it at once. No config or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createBrowserMeetingRealtimeAudioTransport` pulls captured audio from the page about three times a second. Any pull error called `fail()`, which stops capture and closes the bridge.

A failed pull does not mean the capture is gone. The node audio transport (`realtime-node-audio-transport.ts`) already tolerates transient input errors, counting `consecutiveInputErrors` up to 5. The browser transport now uses the same counter and warning, with a limit of 2: the page keeps only the newest audio (47 chunks) and closes a capture that goes 10 s without a pull, which two 5 s pulls reach. The count resets after the pull and any audio processing complete without an error, so unusable audio or a failed hand-off to the realtime engine still counts as a failure. Every browser safety and authority check still runs on every pull; nothing is skipped or cached.

## Evidence

### Live run

Live Slack huddle in a lab container: Linux, Chrome 155, OpenClaw built from #177357 (`83d04fa`) with #173898 applied, OpenAI realtime voice. Lab-only stage timing was added inside the browser plugin's `/act` route. IDs are placeholders.

Four talk-back runs failed 5–15 s after the join with `Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out`. In each run, successful pulls finished their page work in about 3 ms. The failing pull in the clearest run finished its page work, then waited in the response's URL check until the request was cancelled:

```text
02:07:12.426 guard assert-done
02:07:12.426 fffvt evaluate-start
02:07:12.428 fffvt evaluate-end
02:07:12.681 fffvt guard-exit
02:07:12.682 post json-ok-start      <- resolveTabUrl -> navigation URL check (hostname lookup)
02:07:17.411 post released           <- request cancelled; 4.7 s with no further stage
02:07:17.413 Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out
```

With the SSRF policy active, that check resolves the page hostname on every call. In the same container, 2 of 200 lookups of the Slack hostname took about 5006 ms, exceeding the audio pull's 5 s budget. In another run, the failing pull stalled before its page work started, at a step that run did not split further.

With the hostname pinned in the container's hosts file, a two-way conversation ran for 2 minutes: 371 audio pulls, no failures, and the participant heard the agent answer.

With this change (and #173898) and normal DNS, the same lab ran a two-way conversation for over 12 minutes. Four pulls stalled in the first 30 s; each was retried, participant audio resumed, and the agent kept answering the participant coherently for the rest of the call:

```text
03:07:16.375 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:24.193 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:33.775 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:41.694 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
```

Twelve minutes after the join, `slackhuddles status` still reported `inCall: true`, `audioInputRouted: true`, `providerConnected: true`, `bridgeClosed: false`, and the log had no `capture failed` or session-close entry. Before this change, every normal-DNS run ended at the first such stall. The live run used `8cc7ccc`; later commits only move the counter reset after audio processing and reword its comment; a stalled pull never reaches that point. The participant heard some agent replies cut short. The log shows four `audio output backpressured` warnings, which may explain them; that output path is not touched here and the cut-offs were not matched to log times.

Proof artifice: the live runs were built on #177357's branch and applied #173898's production files by hand (talk-back stops before this point without them) and one diagnostic run pinned the Slack hostname in the container's hosts file; the 12-minute run used normal DNS, a real Slack workspace, a real participant and a real voice model.

### Tests

`realtime-browser-audio-transport.test.ts` adds "keeps the call through one stalled pull and ends it on a second in a row". It fails on `main` (the first rejected pull ends the call) and passes here. "ends the call when pulled audio keeps failing to reach the model" covers unusable audio and a failed hand-off twice in a row. All 35 `src/meeting-bot` test files pass, and `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` are clean.

After merging current `main`, the two tests were rewritten to the test file's new layout; on `main` they fail and with this change all 4 tests in the file pass (5 repeat runs).

After merging current `main` again on 4 Nov (`baaa01091c5`; only the test-line record conflicted), the targeted checks were rerun on an isolated Linux test machine (Node 26): the four realtime meeting test files (browser, node audio transports, engine, shutdown) 51 passed; core test typecheck shards and core typecheck clean; oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files clean.

Test lines are net +47 against `main` (allocation record `config/test-lines-allocations/meeting-audio-pull-retry.txt`; the shared ceiling is no longer raised): one regression that fails on `main` and one consecutive-failure case, both in the existing transport test file and reusing its harness; no smaller set covers the single retry and the end on a second failure.

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

- **Why not change the URL check.** Skipping it for audio pulls, or remembering a tab's approval, could miss a tab that moved to another page or a hostname that started resolving to a private address. Reducing the repeated lookups while keeping those checks is for the browser owners; the timing above is the evidence.
- **Related, not fixed here:** #173896 (audio stops when the join's requester disconnects; still open) must be fixed first for talk-back to reach this point. Caption reads still fail with `Gateway requester authority changed` after the join.

</details>

## Summary
Fix a failing test on scheduled main CI: the PR-provisioning isolation observer still expected read-only SQLite snapshots directly under the private cache root. #192368 added an installation namespace (`sqlite-<24 hex characters>`) before the snapshot directory.

Update only the test observer to require that namespace and validate snapshot names below it. Repository containment, symlink/hardlink checks, admitted SQLite filenames, and negative live-store checks remain unchanged. No production change, budget change, snapshot-baseline update, or gate bypass.

## Failure and cause
- Scheduled main CI run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41753977574
- Failing job: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41753977574/job/126325771982
- `test/scripts/pr-worktree-state.test.ts` failed before its expected migration assertions with `Unexpected provisioning SQLite store` for the valid new namespace.
- The canonical layout is produced by `src/infra/sqlite-private-directory.ts` using `sha256(stateDir).slice(0, 24)`.

## Validation
- Reproduced the failure on current main using `pnpm test test/scripts/pr-worktree-state.test.ts` before editing.

- Independent fresh review: approved without blockers; local autoreview: no P0/P1 findings. Hosted ClawSweeper requested as fallback to unavailable local ClawSweeper.

## Scope
This fixes the provisioning-isolation failure, not a claim that all main CI is green. Other observed UI failures were separately addressed by `72217ea0860038f`; the unused node snapshot exports by `155ac6884808627`.

## What Problem This Solves

PR provisioning schema-migration tests reject their own private SQLite snapshots after installation-specific cache namespaces were introduced. This repairs the three failing cases in [main CI job 126308363460](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41748647188/job/126308363460).

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. The existing migration and provisioning-isolation assertions can execute against the current snapshot layout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commit `c16858baa256a33134f35970df04519f48d3d7ed` added `sqlite-<24 hex digits>` between the admitted cache root and snapshot tokens. The test observer still required every intermediate component to be a snapshot token. Require the installation namespace in its proper position while retaining the private fixture root, token/payload allowlist, repository identity, and file/directory alias checks.

The patch changes two fixture lines. Production delta: zero; test LF delta: zero. All test cases and assertions remain. Simplification review found no extra machinery to remove.

- Node syntax, single-file oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. - Independent canonical autoreview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2) reviewed the complete two-line candidate against `155ac6884808627c964743a9ab7bcd6c2e524f51`: scoped-clean, no findings. Explicit authorization/isolation review found the private-root and alias boundaries intact; full provisioning integration remains unverified.

Current proof update (2026-11-04): normal PR [CI41758178338](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41758178338) completed successfully at exact head `79955b0d3041225c22f4462688edc777ebbb3913`, including changed Node, compact-small-1, changed-boundary, baseline-ratchets, core lint/types, and the required CI gate. The security review and status gate are also successful. This supersedes the local lint/type setup gaps above.

prs.title: fix(ui): show the creating agent on agent-written session openings
prs.body:
## Problem

Agent-written opening messages from `sessions_create`/visible `sessions_spawn` show the opaque sender `agent:roboclaw` and a letter avatar, including in reply previews.

## Solution

Derive the creating agent from structured inter-session provenance, not from an opaque sender id. Message normalization uses the canonical session-key parser without adding the UI session-parser dependency to shared sender labels. Message groups and reply previews reuse agent names and avatar rendering.

Loaded reply sources pass the current agent explicitly to the sender-label owner, and their index cache includes current-agent identity and roster. This fixes the hosted review's P2 finding: a loaded opening could previously retain `main` instead of Roboclaw. The sender-label owner handles the default agent once; callers do not spread reactive props and accidentally invalidate the entire transcript on streamed text.

User-turn ownership, Gateway authority, stored transcripts, and `sessions_send` forwarding remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Original create/spawn normalization and opening reply-preview regressions failed on base and passed with the fix; the `sessions_send` negative control passed on both.
- Latest loaded-source regression runs the real `buildChatItems -> projectTranscriptChain -> projectTranscriptIndex` path. It reproduced `expected 'main' to be 'Roboclaw'` before the repair and now passes, including current-agent changes and roster renames on the same cached chain.
- Focused UI-harness checks pass create/spawn attribution, same/different-agent reply names and avatars, and raw-id, wrong-kind, wrong-tool and malformed-key negatives.
- All **100 existing tests** across transcript indexing, projection scale, forwarded attribution and session activity pass. Typecheck, lint, format and whitespace checks pass.
- Final same-toolchain comparison against `bf10667561bfdf36fed14c70a5f8ec97b4a01f09` passes: chat gzip **1281740 -> 1281736 B (-4 B)**; new-session gzip **796928 -> 796832 B (-96 B)**; request counts unchanged. No budgets or baselines were raised. This is local proof; remote exact-head CI is tracked separately.
- Fresh local autoreview, **P0–P3**, on the complete staged candidate against `bf106675` (the tree committed as `16133edb6274b02`): completed with no actionable findings. Unchanged helper implementations and other call sites were outside the reviewer context; focused consumer and integration proofs above cover those boundaries.
- Original signed-in Control UI e2e reproduced the letter-avatar/raw-id bug and passed with the fix. Inspected synthetic captures:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: letter avatar and agent:main sender](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7ed43fc-6e6f-4864-93a3-19b20906e1d1) | ![After: Roboclaw avatar and name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6ac07ab-7b04-4c7d-925b-5193700d278d) |

## Prior-head inherited CI failures

On `edb3d4e`, run `41750806506` tested merge `e0ac1f1470132af8b37624673c0d847167bf6a21` against main `b215829af2858d74b5d5e20f4c503c548374adff`. All 13 failures in UI jobs `126315769473` and `126315769567` were traced to baseline toast changes from `eee9925e84f32ab8378ccf64cc86bde13b85c4be` (#192015): split title/description, required error severity, and `role="alert"` instead of `status`. The affected tests, producers, renderer and copy are unchanged by this PR. This does not establish the outcome of any subsequent CI attempt. The owned bundle and loaded-reply defects were repaired separately.

## Test coverage gap

The new regression/e2e additions were removed earlier to keep net test-line growth at zero while main exceeded its ceiling. Local regression results above are proof, but those new regressions are not committed. Follow-up: restore coverage without expanding the ceiling. Existing tests are preserved; no allocation or CI-policy limit was raised.

## Accepted edge case

An agent without a display name falls back to its bare id, matching forwarded messages.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

## Proof reconciliation after the enrollment and socket prerequisites landed

The checkpoint head remains **4d40d62ffd0e81f872ecf82ed813d50c5077598c**. This reconciles existing evidence with now-public prerequisites; it is not a new runtime execution or a claim of exact-head Gateway proof.

**What actually ran.** The existing [runtime run 41571285323](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41571285323) used base HEAD b782b5d4ff4dee05e6e153206705df7124d19377 plus the enrollment prerequisite, socket repair and five qualification files. The real Linux Gateway/native-child run passed **2/2 tests**, covering the mirrored and retained-disk positive cases plus their negative control, private HEAD/ancestry and dirty/untracked-byte preservation, child completion, and parent preservation. The two reporter summaries represent the **same execution**, not four tests. The original combined driver outcome remains **exit 2**: the SUT exited 0, but two enabled console reporters rendered the same successful ledger twice and the post-test collector rejected the duplicate. The retained ledger objects compare identically. Do not relabel the driver exit as 0. Deterministic model/provider fixtures and task-local retained storage are not commercial provider or durable-volume qualification.

**Now-public prerequisite source.** The four enrollment implementation/test blobs and four socket implementation/test blobs below match the corresponding executed c4 blobs byte-for-byte. Both prerequisites are ancestors of the main snapshot inspected for this reconciliation.

- Enrollment commit [c8afcc453aacdce66c751729c83986378739f719](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c8afcc453aacdce66c751729c83986378739f719): [provider lifecycle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c8afcc453aacdce66c751729c83986378739f719/src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-lifecycle.ts), [node provisioning](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c8afcc453aacdce66c751729c83986378739f719/src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-node-provisioning.ts), [owner lifecycle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c8afcc453aacdce66c751729c83986378739f719/src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-owner-lifecycle.ts), and [regressions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c8afcc453aacdce66c751729c83986378739f719/src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-provisioning-node.test.ts).

Its extracted-wrapper helper registration also landed; this does not change the identity of the earlier runtime source.

**Checkpoint versus combined stack.** The executed candidate includes the disk extension. Checkpoint-only 4d40 therefore differs from that candidate in sessions-create.ts, session-project-source.ts, session-worktree-preparation.ts and session-repository-checkpoints.ts, plus docs and the compensation test. The checkpoint's session-repository-preparation.ts owner and its project-creation regression/support files match the executed blobs. The [b782→published disk f79 comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/b782b5d4ff4dee05e6e153206705df7124d19377...f79e5ae757f912311cf046cb441927dc4021b1a7) is only the compensation test's import cutover to the shared preparation owner; it introduces no production change. None of this makes the combined run an execution of checkpoint-only 4d40.

**Current-main limits.** The inspected main snapshot was 2dbd7f79bbf1fc49b38049429cb9e55b5437f0be. Its material overlaps are durable session-creation wrapping, attended-session defaults/response handling in sessions-create.ts, responsive Git-backed checkout probing in session-project-source.ts, and related preparation-test changes. The broker-host exit-cleanup registration also differs from the old runtime and was separately covered during socket integration. Read-only textual composition found no conflict markers, but it is **not** a prepared native merge tree, current-base CI result, or runtime-equivalence proof. Preserve the existing checkpoint/disk dependency order and validate the actual landing composition through the native owner.

The unchanged checkpoint's [CI 41434222984](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41434222984) passed for 4d40. The retained raw runtime/source-binding evidence remains local; landing the prerequisite code does not make local logs public or resolve the review environment's earlier raw-log redirect restriction. No upload retry or new runtime run was performed for this reconciliation. Hosted review, overall readiness and native landing gates remain independent; no Platinum outcome is asserted or guaranteed.


---

## Latest runtime qualification — November 3, 2026

Both native inheritance paths passed on a combined candidate containing this stack, the already-landed enrollment fix [#191006](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191006), and the then-unpublished socket-owner repair, now landed as [#191659](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191659). This closes the previously reported runtime-execution gap for that composition, **not** for an unchanged published head. This was the state at execution; the reconciliation above records the later prerequisite landings and exact-head CI. The requested overall review rating and native landing remain outstanding. Earlier attempts and their limits below are retained as historical evidence.

### Complete mirrored and retained runtime assertions passed

[Blacksmith run 41571285323](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41571285323), lease tbx_01m6fpj94dvws978szp6fg1fe1, executed the unchanged fixture through a real Gateway and authenticated native nodes on Linux/Node24.22.1.

Executed source tree: c4a401fe4d33312a427d8f7e1ee72fdff533bdd3. Actual remote source digest: d6560ace95d0e2292d6c8b5bb4c2ec46f95ae53d51a3d5c1bd3453e18529f669 (62,592 files). This is the combined candidate with the exact enrollment prerequisite and socket-owner repair, not a claim about an unchanged published PR head.

Actual output:

    Test Files  1 passed (1)
    Tests       2 passed (2)
    Duration    290.09s
    REVIEWED_DRIVER_EXIT=2

The two tests are configuration preflight and the complete runtime composition. Within that composition:

| Scenario | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Invalid placed schema | Rejected without child/provider allocation |
| Mirrored parent → native child | Completed; private history and current files preserved |
| Retained parent → native child | Completed; fresh disk-only history/files preserved; independently owned child resource |

Both children completed and their expected assistant replies were verified. The run observed four distinct authenticated native nodes and 13 deterministic streaming requests, including two child requests. Before/after parent identity, liveness, placement, repository workspace, disk authority and filesystem/index snapshots remained unchanged. Child workspaces, branches, directories and environments were independent; editing each child did not alter its parent.

Verified private HEADs:
- Mirrored: 38cfb78fb2e6c3dfec9e5b01a25332087fda7f35.
- Retained: 31ba6401a43e752e38a72028882e18b8d608cbda, including changes made after the parent’s completed baseline turn.

**Why driver exit2:** all runtime assertions passed, but its post-test collector expected one rendered ledger line. The maintained verbose and default reporters rendered the same console event twice. Both complete payloads are byte-identical: SHA256 e26a8cbc772108f4c5f9304b6b1b3dac4633571a325226ffd266256d0ff5c343. Raw receipts remain unchanged; a separately labeled ledger was recovered only after equality and completeness verification. No runtime retry or assertion relaxation occurred. The collector-only correction is proposed, not applied.

**Cleanup:** exact container, bridge and snapshot removal passed. Fourteen evidence files were downloaded/hash-verified before lease release and reverified afterward. Final lease settlement is complete; the Actions cancellation reflects lease teardown. One allocation and one driver, 16m38s including preparation, collection and cleanup.

**Limits:** real Gateway, enrollment, native processes, Git/files/stores; deterministic model and managed-provider fixtures. Retained resources are task-local directories/receipts, not commercial durable-volume provisioning. Internal bridge is not network-none or guaranteed host-unreachable. This is not current published-head CI, merge equivalence or an overall Platinum rating.


---

## What Problem This Solves

Native same-agent children of repository-only sessions incorrectly fall back to the configured Gateway workspace. Creation fails when that directory is not a Git checkout. Review also exposed a runtime import cycle and a late source check that could copy a parent's checkpoint after reassignment, before session binding finally refused it.

## User Impact

Children receive independent repository workspaces preserving the parent's requested ref, accepted base and checkpoint files. Setup-script permission remains the intersection of the parent's permission and the current caller's authority. Reassigned or revoked sources are refused before child copying and binding. Incompatible local selectors and initial local turns remain invalid. Disk-authoritative parents stay guarded here; #190845 adds fresh disk exports. No schema, configuration or resource-receipt migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing parent-source selector and checkpoint fork owner retain responsibility. Repository allocation moves unchanged into a dependency leaf shared by explicit creation and inherited preparation, removing the import cycle without another allocator or forwarding wrapper. The fork owner prepares and retains canonical parent predicates for Git effects, then releases them before returning. Existing rollback also covers source-scope cleanup failures.

## Evidence

The original public-handler regression failed on base `4221b02`:

```text
{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"agent workspace is not a git checkout"}: expected false to be true
```

A follow-up production-path probe on the pre-repair stack's checkpoint route exposed the late reassignment check:

```text
checkpoint source reassignment completed copies: 1
AssertionError: expected 1 to be +0
```

The maintained regression now checks real checkpoint bytes in an allowed child, refusal before preparation, caller revocation before copying and binding, and parent reassignment before copying. Timing observers delegate to the real implementations. Rejected operations leave no child session or repository owner, preserve the parent workspace, and complete zero copies when authority was lost before copying.

Final focused commands and actual sanitized output:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.create.projects.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'repository children inherit independent sources'
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/session-repository-checkpoints.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```
```text

Duration  302.73s (transform 89%, worker 6%, tests 3%, import 2%, setup 1%)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 322.06s

Tests  28 passed (28)
Duration  26.69s (tests 74%, transform 23%, import 2%, worker 1%)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 28.56s
```

Both architecture gates now pass; the reviewed predecessor reported a three-module cycle through project creation, lifecycle preparation and worktree preparation:

```sh
pnpm check:import-cycles
pnpm check:madge-import-cycles
```
```text
Import cycle check: 0 runtime value cycle(s).
Madge import cycle check: 0 cycle(s).
```

- Core and gateway-server test typechecks, seven-file type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Lint output: `✓ No problems in 7 files [4.17s]`.
- Fresh canonical **committed-range autoreview** covered `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914` → `b081d9ace588fec30b1c23d81a17bd8b0a81a07f` at P0–P2: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. It covers allocation ownership, cycle removal, current parent/caller authority, cleanup, caller contracts, setup intersection and intentional disk-export refusal. This supersedes the earlier local INDEX-only predecessor ambiguity. The reviewer assessed frozen code and supporting evidence; it did not execute tests.
- Simplification keeps one allocator and one checkpoint owner. The additional exact 102-line regression allocation covers the authority boundaries and shared fixture setup; the existing allocation and shared scalar are unchanged.
- Broader consumer evidence is bounded: all 18 project cases emitted passing results before a combined replay reached its 600-second outer deadline. A subsequent Node spawn replay reported **27/27 passed** in 575.39s, but its wrapper was terminated during compiler-output verification. Neither attempt is called a clean combined-suite run; completed focused proof above is retained separately. Owned runner extinction was verified after interruption.
- **Earlier CLI CI reconciled:** The three capability CLI failures in [run 41385139959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41385139959/job/125084729643) match a source-level test/owner contract mismatch already present in the actual tested main parent eb488191: PR [#189993](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189993) changed invalid numeric options to propagate ExpectedCliError, while these tests still expected the mocked runtime to throw “exit 1.” Upstream commit [2426aa9288](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2426aa9288a524c9cb912dca3da500f2f09fc83a) repairs exactly those three assertions and is present in main 2777468d26 (observed November 2, 2026). The earlier passing replay used 4221b02, which predates the parser change, so it was not an exact-tested-base comparison. This is source attribution and a verified upstream repair, not a newly executed-base failure or current-PR green-CI result; fresh current-PR CI remains required.

**Proof limits:** the harness invokes production session creation, authority, Git and durable-store owners. It is not hosted cloud provisioning or a real model turn, and neither is claimed. Current-head CI and overall hosted review readiness remain separate gates.

## Credits

Requested by @galiniliev; adapted from the release-branch work with native OpenClaw owners. All commits retain Galin’s co-author credit.

## Follow-up: complete the allocator consumer cutover

The failures at `b081d9ace588fec30b1c23d81a17bd8b0a81a07f` were introduced by this PR: `session-create-preparation.test.ts` still imported `prepareSessionRepositoryWorkspace` from the former project-preparation module. Commit `4d40d62ffd0e81f872ecf82ed813d50c5077598c` imports the canonical `session-repository-preparation.js` leaf directly. A tracked-symbol and former-module caller audit found no additional missed allocator consumers. No forwarding export, production change, assertion relaxation, or new test was added (test delta +1/−1).

### Executed red/green qualification

On the published predecessor:

```bash
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-root.json --incremental

  src/gateway/session-create-preparation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 \
  -t 'keeps repository creation compensation'
# Tests 2 failed | 24 skipped (26); exit 1
```

Commands and result excerpts below are local qualification, not current-head CI clearance.

```bash

  src/gateway/session-create-preparation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The first complete-file run on the correction recorded 24 passes and two failures: a 120-second timeout in the first Draft-copy case, followed by an unknown-parent result in the next case. Both repaired compensation cases passed in that run. The unchanged full-file replay above passed all 26 cases; no timeout, fixture, or expectation was changed. That replay does not establish the cause of the earlier timeout/next-case failure, and the failed receipt is retained. An initial concurrent lint invocation also hit its outer deadline; the serial invocation completed successfully.

Independent P0–P2 autoreview completed with no actionable findings, using the complete affected test plus the canonical allocator and former-owner modules. Existing checkpoint/source-authority production-path evidence remains applicable because this follow-up changes only a test import.

The older CLI numeric-error CI failure is a separate issue: its merge's main parent was `eb488191`, and upstream `2426aa9288a524c9cb912dca3da500f2f09fc83a` repairs those three stale assertions. Earlier passing replays on `4221b02` are pre-change-base evidence, not proof that the original failure was inherited. No unrelated CLI change or main integration was added here.

Current-head green CI and overall Platinum-or-higher remain separate landing requirements.

## Additional isolated runtime attempt: setup failure, not feature proof

A source-pinned, network-isolated Gateway qualification was attempted on `b782b5d4ff4dee05e6e153206705df7124d19377` plus one staged test-only fixture. The repaired disk head `f79e5ae757f912311cf046cb441927dc4021b1a7` differs only in the allocator test import; production bytes are unchanged. The native image was `sha256:847f71bbb3f17fc1032d50d75bf6fb3fdcf188b16dff81f24667fe9ae9409e01`, with Node 26.12.1 and native pnpm 12.15.0.

```text
Gateway startup exit: 78
Test Files 1 failed (1)
Tests 1 failed (1)
Vitest duration: 51.36s; runner exit: 1
```

This is our fixture setup error, not an inheritance failure or a permission refusal. No native spawn, parent/child state assertion, retained-disk export, or child completion was reached. The deterministic model and local Git/HTTP fixtures do not establish a successful model turn. The fixture did not yet contain the retained-disk case.

The retired setting was removed only after the run ended; the corrected fixture was formatted/restaged but **not rerun**. Executed fixture SHA-256: `98857ff7aaf88eb1dc1ec790aa35f68cdd78272d52a5095a39ee4e737d6594dc`. Corrected, unexecuted fixture SHA-256: `1b3c6fb979d6895e644722605cd78f47b521d59f89a6153e84aa1b3ff0c29954`. Both test containers were confirmed absent, and the runner cleaned its disposable build snapshot. No production change, shared-checkout mutation, live state, or cloud allocation was used.

The successful public-handler and production-owner evidence remains as previously reported. This additional attempt does **not** close the Gateway/native-agent or retained-disk runtime proof gap and does not support an overall Platinum claim.

prs.title: fix(sessions): title pasted paths and non-control leading-slash text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session title derivation treated any first message that starts with `/` as a slash command and skipped it. Pasted absolute paths (`/Users/…/handover.md read this`) therefore stayed untitled (`New conversation`) and worktree sessions fell back to random crustacean branch names.

## Fix

- In `resolveSessionTitleSource`, keep skill-command arg extraction. For other leading-slash text, accept only **path-like** forms (`//…` or a second `/` in the string) as title source. Unregistered `/command` tokens stay untitled so we do not need the heavy `command-detection` wrapper import.
- In `prepareDashboardSessionTitle`, prepare skill commands whenever the trimmed draft starts with `/` so registered skills stay skill-aware before the empty-command fast path.

## Evidence

### Live Gateway proof (Linux Node v24.22.1, synthetic model over loopback)

Built/started real `startGatewayServer` on loopback with a synthetic OpenAI-compatible title utility (API key `synthetic-key-not-real`, no vendor account). Health `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`.

```
chat.send sessionKey=agent:main:dashboard:path-title-proof
message='/tmp/openclaw-path-proof-notes.md read this handover'
→ sessions.displayName='Summarise the notes file'
builderPath='/tmp/openclaw-path-proof-notes.md read this handover'
resolveSessionTitleSource='/tmp/openclaw-path-proof-notes.md read this handover'
attachment-first /explain → 'Explain DNS resolution'
fakeModelRequests=1
```

Artifact: `/tmp/openclaw-proofs/artifacts/proof-043-113.json` (case pr=192043). Head `aee4a653f`.


## Notes

Does not add a post-reply title retry; this PR only corrects the leading-slash skip so the existing first-message path can name path-like sessions.

Closes #192031

prs.title: fix(copilot): discover models with usable saved sign-ins
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/1870

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GitHub Copilot model discovery returns no usable models when an inactive setup replacement or expired token is the first saved profile, even though a later saved sign-in works.

## User Impact

Users can discover Copilot models using an eligible saved sign-in without adding a manual auth order or repeating device login. Explicitly selected profiles, configured account order (including an empty order), and direct/environment credential priority are unchanged.

This is a partial repair related to the Store onboarding report. It does not establish or claim to fix its separate runtime SecretRef error, the rejected profile's HTTP 401, or Windows issue #1761's browser callback failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automatic discovery bypassed the shared credential eligibility owner and selected the first stored profile. The existing explicit-order path already used the canonical resolver. Both unpinned paths now use that resolver, removing the separate first-profile policy. Explicit profile requests remain pinned.

Simplification: production +7/-13 lines, tests +27, docs +3/-1. No new state, configuration, migration, retry, or credential fallback mechanism.

## Evidence

- Base-red registered-provider regression: both inactive and expired first-profile cases return an empty model list instead of the usable later account's model. Two failures, 39 skipped; 126.62s wrapper wall with cold compiled-worker setup.
- After repair: all 41 registered-provider tests and all 14 auth-resolution tests pass. Two shards, 65.40s wrapper wall; registered-provider file 45.84s including compilation (test execution about 10s), auth file 15.32s.
- The regression uses the registered provider catalog and real isolated auth-profile storage. Copilot token exchange and model HTTP responses are synthetic. It observes the model list exposed to the caller and ensures exactly one exchange, not a retry loop.
- Extension production and test TypeScript checks pass. Focused type-aware lint, formatting and git diff checks pass.
- Fresh shared Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Review scope was the three-file patch plus supplied owner/issue context; unchanged source was unavailable to the reviewer.
- Separate existing real-WebSocket first-signin integration passed (one scenario, 38.7s test / 345.3s wrapper including a cold runtime build). This exercises sign-in reuse, protected tokenRef activation, ownership and revocation with synthetic provider HTTP. It is not a reproduction of the reported Windows Current model verification failure.

Not verified: authenticated Microsoft Store/Windows UI flow, live provider account, update/reboot scenario. [Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40438130948) and its [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40439243860) passed for head `25042ab6d7fcb0d5454b4608644a323c49d9b958`. [Exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185328#issuecomment-6432400928) completed with no findings or before-merge requests. Shipped CLI/upgrade proof remains an optional improvement, not executed evidence. No merge requested.

prs.title: fix(gateway): record visible activity on chat setup failures
prs.body:
Related: #160003

## What Problem This Solves

When an accepted chat fails during setup or dispatch before its run starts, the terminal failure can be recorded without advancing session activity. A user who has already marked the session read can therefore miss that failure.

The restart-safe recovery path originally addressed by this PR was removed by #185730. This revision targets the remaining setup and dispatch failure paths in the current architecture. It does not claim that the removed mechanism still exists or that every symptom in #160003 is resolved.

## Change

Carry the existing run and RPC-source visibility into terminal lifecycle persistence. Visible failures advance activity; hidden work remains quiet. Lifecycle ownership and the unread predicate are unchanged.

Thanks @wangmiao0668000666 for the original investigation in #159285.

## Evidence

- On upstream main `4e472c7eda03fe91631ee666ca79e08b40206ae7`, the new isolated SQLite regressions fail for visible setup and unstarted dispatch failures because `lastActivityAt` does not advance. The hidden setup control passes.
- On the candidate, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-dispatch-errors.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 25/25 on Windows with Node 24.22.1 using isolated SQLite state. Targeted lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and the test-line ratchet against that upstream snapshot passed. The separate allocation covers 61 net regression-test lines for both terminal paths and hidden controls.
- Independent source review found no actionable defects. This exercises the lifecycle owner, not a browser-rendering or live Gateway flow.
- The updated head `278ccf6b9159efcdcb8d8c08e187cd82538857a8` has a successful `openclaw/ci-gate` status. Consult its checks for details.

The prior PR evidence and old-head CI concerned the removed recovery path and are not validation of this revision.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep commentary's tool call inside its activity group
prs.body:
## Problem

In chat, commentary followed by a tool group could leave its own tool call in a standalone row. `coalesceToolActivityMessages` merged the commentary into that call's invocation row; `chat-thread-grouping` then classified it as an assistant group to keep the text visible. Later calls formed a separate activity group.

## Solution

- Split prose/media and identified tool calls into separate rows in source order. Mixed `text, call, text, call` messages keep their order, including calls without merged results.
- Prepared activity belongs only to invocation rows, not their split prose. Raw calls still count correctly when the source has no prepared activity.
- When tools are hidden, remove call-only rows but retain handoffs, permission requests, and accompanying content on anonymous calls that cannot be split into identified rows.

User text accompanying `tool_result` blocks now also gets its own row rather than appearing inside the tool group. Reasoning stays in order beside calls rather than inside a nested raw-details log.

## Screenshots

Captured from a Control UI e2e scenario (`installMockGateway`, synthetic history: commentary + call, a second call, a reply).

| Before (main) | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before: standalone tool row beside commentary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87a8028f-77d8-4cc9-a22c-577acf4f2dab) | ![After: one activity group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b52d934-b05f-4f4c-8774-aa9e9d64c065) |
| Commentary, then standalone `Recheck ratchet` and `Ratchet numbers` rows | Commentary, then one `2 commands` activity group |

## Evidence

- The original split regression failed on main and passed with the fix. The committed coalescer test now covers text and thinking interleaved with calls, and verifies prepared activity appears only once. The hidden-tools regression verifies commentary survives an anonymous call.
- Final independent Codex autoreview (P0–P2) found two defects on `b4031469`: duplicated prepared activity on prose, and lost commentary beside hidden anonymous calls. Both were reproduced with failing tests and fixed. Follow-up autoreview of the repair relative to `b4031469` found no actionable P0–P2 defects; only whitespace changed afterward. The repair is committed in `4993df67`.
- Final code: **254/254 tests across 8 affected files pass**, including coalescing, sessions yield, reasoning, reply attribution, thread grouping, transcript indexing and feed. The nested-tool browser suite passes **2/2 tests**.
- UI and UI-test typechecks, focused oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and the test-lines ratchet pass. Net test-line delta remains **0**; test layout was compacted without removing further coverage.
- Earlier broader validation: 732/734 chat unit files passed. The mobile session menu and effort picker failed in that broad run and passed individually. Earlier chat e2e validation passed 8/8 files. These are prior-head results, not claims of a new full-suite run.
- The screenshot scenario failed on main and passed with the fix. That dedicated browser scenario is not committed; the committed regression coverage is described above. Screenshots use synthetic history, not a live model/Gateway conversation.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(sandbox): treat dash missing-parent cd errors as ENOENT
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`SandboxFsBridgeImpl.stat()` only treated GNU/BusyBox `No such file or directory` as a missing path. On Debian/Ubuntu sandbox containers where `/bin/sh` is dash, stating a path whose **parent directory does not exist** fails at `cd -- "$1"` with `can't cd to …`, and the bridge threw an uncategorized `stat failed …` error instead of returning `null` (`ENOENT`). That broke `optional: true` / path-variant fallbacks in sandboxed `read`.

## Fix

- Before `cd`, the container script now checks `[ -d "$1" ]` and emits a C-locale `No such file or directory` when the parent is missing.
- `isSandboxStatMissingPathError()` also accepts dash's `can't cd to ` wording so historical/edge failure shapes still map to `null`.
- Non-missing failures (e.g. `Permission denied`) still throw.

## Evidence

### Local dash (/bin/sh) behavior on head `4cac7473877e`

Host Linux with `/bin/sh -> dash`. Exercised the exact fs-bridge stat script and the shipped sandboxed read tool through the local remote-shell backend (argv `sh -c`, so dash).

Shell script comparison (missing parent / inaccessible parent / present file):

```text
Host: Linux 6.12.94+ x86_64
Shell: /usr/bin/dash
date (Asia/Taipei): 2026-11-04 09:15:44 CST
PR head: 4cac7473877e5fccb2a81b3e5f043ea2a697c78e
Note: /bin/sh -> dash on this Linux box; scripts match fs-bridge.ts head.

=== Historical dash cd on missing parent (pre-fix wording) ===
sh: 1: cd: can't cd to /tmp/tmp.KwUwfZAevB/workspace/missing_parent_xyz
exit:2

=== Head script: direct parent/basename stat on missing parent ===
stat: cannot statx '/tmp/tmp.KwUwfZAevB/workspace/missing_parent_xyz/file.txt': No such file or directory
exit:1

=== Head script: inaccessible parent remains permission error ===
stat: cannot statx '/tmp/tmp.KwUwfZAevB/noperm/file.txt': Permission denied
exit:1

=== Head script: present file succeeds ===
regular file|6|2026-11-04 09:15:44.919617924 +0800
exit:0
```

`SandboxFsBridge.stat` via dash:

```text
date 2026-11-04T01:16:26.054Z
sh resolves to /usr/bin/dash
stat missing parent => null
stat inaccessible throws: EACCES: permission denied, lstat '/tmp/openclaw-dash-proof-Sq8PrL/workspace/noperm/file.txt'
code: EACCES
stat present => { type: 'file', size: 5, mtimeMs: 1793754986074 }
```

Shipped `createSandboxedReadTool` via dash (matches ClawSweeper ask: optional missing-parent → not_found; ordinary missing → ENOENT; inaccessible parent → EACCES):

```text
date 2026-11-04T01:16:44.403Z
sh /usr/bin/dash
head 4cac7473877e5fccb2a81b3e5f043ea2a697c78e

=== optional missing-parent read ===
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "Optional file not found: no_such_dir_xyz/file.txt."
    }
  ],
  "details": {
    "kind": "not_found",
    "status": "not_found",
    "path": "no_such_dir_xyz/file.txt",
    "optional": true
  }
}

=== ordinary missing-parent read ===
throws: File not found: no_such_dir_xyz/file.txt.
code: ENOENT

=== inaccessible parent read ===
throws: EACCES: permission denied, lstat '/tmp/openclaw-dash-read-MmJAXd/workspace/noperm/file.txt'
code: EACCES

=== present file read ===
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "hello"
    }
  ],
  "details": {
    "kind": "text",
    "content": "hello"
  }
}
```

Focused Vitest on head:

```text
pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts -t "dash|missing|non-missing"
# 3 passed (C-locale missing, dash missing-parent wording absent, non-missing errors kept)
```

### Still needs maintainer

`/allow-security-sensitive-change` on head `4cac7473877e` (sandbox fs-bridge).


### Gateway agent/model turn (Docker dash sandbox)

Live `startGatewayServer` + `chat.send` on head `4cac7473877e`, Docker `27.5.1`, image `openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim` (`/bin/sh` → `/usr/bin/dash`), synthetic loopback model. Artifact: `proof-047-agent-turn.json` (all four cases `ok: true`).

| Case | Tool result / settle |
|------|----------------------|
| optional missing parent | `Optional file not found: missing_parent_xyz/child.txt.` |
| required missing parent | `File not found: …` then assistant `MARK_REQ` |
| present file | `hello-from-proof` then `MARK_PRESENT` |
| inaccessible parent | `EACCES: permission denied, lstat '…/locked_parent/secret.txt'` then `MARK_PERM` |

Gateway logs include `sandbox.backend.container_start` mid-turn. See latest Evidence comment for full transcript excerpts.

prs.title: fix: keep runtime catalog, relay and Feishu windows on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Host wall-clock corrections can prematurely expire process-local caches and relay references, or postpone their elapsed-time backstops. This sweep combines #192122, #192422 and #192308, preserving all original contributor commits from @wangmiao0668000666 through cherry-picks.

## Changes

Use `performance.now()` at the existing extension owners for:
- Anthropic CLI session scan, partial-discovery and Desktop overlay refresh deadlines.
- Browser extension-relay captured-operation lifetime.
- Feishu bot-info probe caching and streaming-start failure backoff.

No TTL values, model-facing text, persisted/native timestamps, SDK contracts, authentication, update, approval or voice-activation policy change. Excludes #192296, #192293 and #192144.

Remove both proposed test allocations and fold regressions into existing boundary scenarios: assembled catalog caching with a missing Desktop transcript and forward/backward corrections; an authenticated relay's real captured reference plus existing connection isolation/cleanup; and failed Feishu probe reuse. Keep partial-scan retry, watcher invalidation, Desktop backstop and streaming recovery coverage. **Production net0; tests net−1.** No new production abstraction or SDK exports. Documentation is intentionally unchanged: existing duration contracts are restored, not altered.

## Evidence

Normally built Gateway in secretless Linux Node24.22.1 Docker, task-only profiles/config/state/ports. **Only the Gateway process's Date.now is stepped**; performance and real timers are untouched. This is a process-local wall-clock step, never a system clock change.

| Member / shipped entry | Main twice | Candidate twice | Controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| #192122 `sessions.catalog.list`, task-owned native-format Claude transcript store | +61min step causes an extra filesystem tree scan (readdir4→5) before elapsed expiry | no extra scan (4→4) | no-step4→4; same real transcript returned; read-only filesystem observation, no fake reader/watch |
| #192422 built Gateway, real Chromium/unpacked extension, authenticated owner protocol capture | +6min step retires the valid captured reference immediately | same captured tab remains resolvable | no-step resolves on both; a fresh real capture becomes stale after301 real seconds on both; real DOM remains readable |
| #192308 `channels.status` probe and signed Feishu inbound webhook → real agent dispatch → Lark TLS transport | probe1→2 after +11min; natural HTTP400 streaming create retries prematurely after +2min (1→2) | probe remains1; streaming create remains suppressed at1 | no-step reuse on both; after61 real seconds streaming retries again (main3, candidate2); all4 turns deliver complete static fallback prose |

Run IDs:
- Catalog main `catalog-base-1-n1p63e`, `catalog-base-2-Sm4TpT`; candidate `catalog-candidate-1-A7jq56`, `catalog-candidate-2-2toxpJ`.
- Relay main `relay-base-1-9zb3y5`, `relay-base-2-Ac1ROM`; candidate `relay-candidate-1-aj7yhd`, `relay-candidate-2-zqDYyj`.
- Feishu main `stream-base-1-GO9v4x`, `stream-base-2-axD629`; candidate `stream-candidate-1-wSzUmn`, `stream-candidate-2-z4chwP`.

The Feishu fixture returns real HTTP400 for `/open-apis/cardkit/v1/cards`; the SDK and streaming owner are unmodified. Signed webhooks, real OpenClaw agent turns against a local Responses fixture, recorded outbound static-card content and subsequent successful retry prove the actual reply-dispatch boundary. Synthetic managed API-key profile only; no live tenant/provider credentials or live-delivery claim. Catalog proof uses the actual Gateway RPC and native-format store, not an exported catalog-helper replay. Relay proof loads the actual unpacked extension in Chromium and captures its real advertised tab, not a synthesized bridge acceptance.

Focused checks: **137/137 pass** across five touched test files (3 browser,93 Feishu,41 Anthropic). Formatting and lint pass on11 changed files. Identical consolidated regressions against baseline fail at the intended boundaries: catalog hard-scan backstop, relay resolve after wall step, and3 failed-probe cache cases. Baseline `1ca0669dbe3982369463b921397027f3727f51fd`; production bytes tested match this candidate (subsequent edits only consolidate tests). Raw JSON, HTTP/DOM/IO observations and sanitized logs are retained; public receipt follows below.

## Risk and rollback

Two-way door: reverting restores the former in-process timing; no schema/state migration. Blast radius is Claude catalog scan freshness, extension captured-operation expiry, and Feishu probe/streaming retry timing. Stored epochs, typing-age timestamps, connection authority, scopes, cancellation and cleanup remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(cli): do not re-publish a binding cleared mid-turn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`persistCliSessionBindingResult` rewrote the native CLI session binding on every non-`preserveBinding` settle. `agent_end` (and other writers) can clear that binding **before** settle. The settle path then resurrected the retired id, so the next turn resumed a process the clear had already retired (`useResume=true resumeSession=<old>`).

## Fix

- `withAdmittedCliCandidate` captures the in-lane resumed native session id.
- `persistCliSessionBindingResult` skips applying a settle result that would only re-publish that same resumed id when the store no longer names it.
- Explicit clears and newly minted native ids still publish.

## Evidence

```
pnpm test src/agents/cli-session-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  32 passed (32)
```

New coverage:
- `does not re-publish a resumed binding another writer cleared mid-turn`
- `still publishes a newly minted native id after a mid-turn clear`

Closes #186613

prs.title: fix(crabbox): explain reserved setup migration and preserve cleanup
prs.body:
Related: #192175

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor sends legacy Crabbox profiles with reserved setup environment names through an impossible same-name migration, and those profiles can block retained checkpoint cleanup while awaiting repair.

## User Impact

Doctor identifies reserved names before store lookup and explains the required manual environment-key and setup-command rename. Existing protected store IDs and destination bindings can stay unchanged. Lease cleanup, checkpoint deletion, and periodic checkpoint maintenance remain available while the profile awaits migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing profile parser owns reserved-name policy; Doctor now uses that policy before asking operators to repair store entries. Checkpoint housekeeping uses the existing cleanup parser, which retains legacy cleanup without allowing new provisioning or capture. Doctor preserves authored config and never rewrites setup commands.

Protected setup still requires a coordinator-owned Linux lease. The separate direct-provider egress capability request in #192175 remains open; this change does not restore plaintext forwarding.

## Evidence

- Prior corrected source head `1a39dad79a8119ed177cc8e465c7e3755ae2dc1a`: [build and artifact verification passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41746839536/job/126302768441), [production types passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41746839536/job/126302771115), and [test types passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41746839536/job/126302771707). The earlier introduced TS2345/TS2322 errors are repaired by sharing the validating parser’s raw-settings input contract; no cast or runtime relaxation.
- [Ordinary CI at production head `1a39`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41750063634/job/126313384348) passes all 23 Doctor, 28 checkpoint-retirement, and 19 profile-parser cases under the maintained Bun policy, without target skips. This covers preserved config/manual recovery before store lookup, legacy/healthy cleanup and maintenance, and strict provisioning refusal. The prior head `8b9894f214c5bf73c4bb7442d0b881051f859aef` consolidates the duplicate missing/ready cases into one fail-on-call store probe; [its refreshed focused job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41751823286/job/126319246073) passes Doctor22/22, retirement28/28 and profile19/19 (69/69, Bun policy, no target skips), including the single fail-on-call regression in4ms. Production source is unchanged by that simplification; prior-head build/types remain explicitly prior-head.
- `git diff --check` and docs inventory inspection pass. Canonical complete-candidate autoreview P0–P2 is scoped-clean, no findings (confidence 0.94); the test-only consolidation has fresh scoped-clean review (0.96).
