prs.title: fix(imessage): fail closed when pairing-store reads reject
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the iMessage pairing store cannot be read, a pairing-policy DM whose sender is not already on a configured allowlist was still treated as unpaired. Shared ingress turned the read failure into an empty allowlist, and iMessage issued a pairing challenge as if the sender had never paired.

## Fix

- Add `readIMessageInboundStoreAllowFrom` so the store is read only when admission still depends on stored approval (pairing-policy DM, not already admitted by configured allowFrom / access groups / group allowlist).
- Await that read before createResolver so failures propagate instead of becoming `[]` → pairing. The existing inbound dispatch catch logs `imessage: inbound dispatch failed` and abandons the durable claim for retry.
- Configured allowFrom / access-group matches continue without touching the store.

## Evidence

```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.context.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/pairing-store-admission.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
# Tests  14 passed (14)
```

- failed pairing-store read → rejects (fail closed), not `{ kind: "pairing" }`
- configured allowFrom skips the store
- unpaired pairing-policy DM still reads the store

Closes #191457

prs.title: fix(signal): bound monitor teardown when receive work stalls
prs.body:
Related #191401

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway stop and Signal channel restart waited forever when one inbound receive or reply never finished. `waitForIdle` looped on a non-empty `inFlight` set with no deadline, so teardown stayed stuck in `monitorSignalProvider`'s `finally`.

## User Impact

Stopping the Gateway or restarting Signal returns after a bounded idle window when receive/reply work makes no progress. Leftover reply work is logged and left running; delivery is retired so abandoned callbacks cannot send after the task drain gives up. Ingress stop still joins settlement-safe claim disposal before teardown reports complete, so same-process replacement recovery is not blocked by abandoned ownership. Accepted claims stay queued for recovery. Ingress-stop settlement failures propagate instead of being counted as successful progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extract the monitor task runner into `monitor/task-runner.ts` with a 30s progress-aware idle window for tracked receive/reply tasks. Teardown bounds that task drain first, then always awaits ingress `stop()` (joined disposal) and only afterward waits for daemon exit so a stuck `signal-cli` cannot report the channel complete while claim custody is unfinished. Wire `isDeliveryRetired` through the event-handler / send handoff so post-timeout sends fail closed. Prior repair #141305 closed unmerged for inactivity; this lands the same contract against current main.

## Evidence

```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/signal/src/signal-ingress.test.ts -t "pre-adoption" --maxWorkers=1
# Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Head `9636d38a6` sets `waitForDeliveryIdleOnStop: false` so a hung pre-adoption delivery callback cannot block ingress stop after the task idle window; settlements still join through dispose. Unresolved-callback stop regression retained on the real ingress owner.

Task-runner helper suite was dropped to keep test-lines net-delta ≤ 0 while the tree is over ceiling; production `waitForIdle` / `waitForSignalMonitorTeardown` behavior is unchanged.

Live Signal Gateway stop/restart traces still need a configured signal-cli account.

## Scope / Risk

Signal monitor teardown + delivery retirement only. No protocol/RPC changes. Daemon exit still unbounded by design.

prs.title: fix(imessage): keep probe and chat-list cache windows on elapsed time
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

Maintainer edits to this branch are welcome and will not be overwritten; the author will not force-push over them.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- **Land-ready:** one owner (`extensions/imessage`), behavior-preserving clock-domain substitution at all five private timestamp sites, deterministic red/green on base. No config, API, schema, or state change.
- **Alternatives:** keep the wall clock (accepts the defect); import the core `monotonicNow()` owner (extensions cannot depend on core internals — the established extension shape is inline `performance.now()`, e.g. #190894, #191533); change TTL durations (out of scope — durations unchanged).
- **Scope:** the chat-list cache, the rpc-support cache, and the private-API negative verdict cache only. The `expiresAt === 0` permanent-verdict sentinel (available bridge) is preserved unchanged.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

A host wall-clock correction while the Gateway runs makes three iMessage process-local cache windows jump with it: the chat-list cache (`chat-lookup.ts`, 30 s), the rpc-support cache (`probe.ts`, 5 min), and the private-API negative-verdict cache (`probe.ts` + `private-api-status.ts`, 10 s). A forward step expires a fresh entry and reissues a `chats.list` RPC / `imsg rpc --help` probe / `imsg status --json` probe; a backward step keeps entries alive far past their intended elapsed windows.

Precedent: #190894 (same shape — wall-clock cache windows → `performance.now()` in extensions; this PR covers the iMessage sites that sweep left behind). Sibling: #191911, #191916, #191210, #192122, #192144, #192293 (same-class clock-domain fixes across Feishu / GitHub / Anthropic / Discord extensions).

## Why This Change Was Made

`extensions/imessage/src/chat-lookup.ts` keeps `chatListCache`, and `extensions/imessage/src/probe.ts` keeps `rpcSupportCache`, as process-local maps whose timestamps never leave the module; `private-api-status.ts`'s `bridgeStatusCache` is the same. The read and write sites now share the elapsed-time domain (`performance.now()`), the only domain a wall-clock step cannot shift; switching one side alone would mix clock domains, so each window's sites move together. The permanent-verdict sentinel (`expiresAt === 0` for an available bridge) is unchanged — it is special-cased before the elapsed comparison, and `performance.now()` is never `0`. Known trade-off, identical to the core stale-while-revalidate cache owner: monotonic windows measure awake time, so system suspend pauses them. Fix classification: behavior-preserving (clock domain only; no TTL, owner, config, or API change).

## User Impact

On a long-running Gateway whose clock is corrected (NTP step, manual change, VM resume), iMessage lookups either lose the cached chat list / rpc-support verdict / negative probe verdict and re-issue `chats.list` RPCs or `imsg` probes, or keep serving stale data beyond their windows. TTL values and cooldown durations are unchanged.

## Evidence

Base `be881a7f8b1ff5af7ff7783340c98ed9047ea450` → candidate `7cda812cef75fc7024ffe47897a448d8faf233ba`, same commands. The wall step is a process-local `Date.now` offset (the #190894/#188293 preload method), never an OS clock jump.

Deterministic regression in the existing suite (remote Node 24.22.1 container, `vitest.extension-imessage.config.ts`):

| `extensions/imessage/src/probe.test.ts` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Base | **2 failed / 3 passed** — the re-anchored expiry test and the new wall-clock case both fail |
| Candidate | **5 passed** |

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/imessage/src/probe.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Consumer coverage on candidate: `chat.test.ts` + `client.test.ts` — **27 passed** (no over-blocking; ordinary chat-list and client paths intact).

The new test seeds a temporary negative verdict through the real `setCachedIMessagePrivateApiStatus`, then steps `Date.now()` forward 100 seconds — past the 10-second `PRIVATE_API_NEGATIVE_TTL_MS` window — and asserts the verdict is still returned. On base (wall-clock window) the step expires it; on candidate (monotonic window) it stays fresh. The existing "expires temporary verdicts" test was re-anchored from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()` so it exercises the same clock domain the cache now uses.

### Real-transport proof (real imsg CLI subprocess)

The discriminant also runs through the extension's real transport — the shipped `probeIMessage` invoking the real imsg CLI via `runCommandWithTimeout` (a real subprocess against a real executable stand-in that counts `rpc --help` invocations in a shared file; remote Node 24.22.1 container, `imsg-proof.test.ts`):

| `imsg-proof.test.ts` (`probeIMessage` rpc-support cache) | `rpc --help` invocations |
| --- | --- |
| Base (`Date.now`) | **2** — after the +6 min wall step the 5-min cache looks expired and re-invokes the CLI |
| Candidate (`performance.now`) | **1** — the cached fatal verdict is served; the CLI is not re-invoked |

```
[imsg-clock] rpc --help (call #1) -> unknown command "rpc" (fatal, cached)
[result] rpc --help calls before step=1 after step=1   # candidate
```

The wall step is again a process-local `Date.now` offset (the #190894 preload method). No mocks on the transport: `probeRpcSupport` → real `runCommandWithTimeout` → real executable process.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+3/−3` (5 sites, 3 files)
- Test LOC: `+15/−1`
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the established extension clock-domain shape (`performance.now()`) from #190894/#191533; no new helper or abstraction.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none.
- Not tested: no live iMessage bridge (macOS-only); the cache windows are exercised through the real probe/cache functions with the SDK RPC surface mocked, which is the boundary where the wall-clock defect manifests.

prs.title: fix: keep release tooling fixtures runnable in module worktrees
prs.body:

prs.title: fix(matrix): message bursts become separate turns despite messages.inbound debounce
prs.body:
Closes #165823 Related: #161505 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Matrix turns every line of a quick text burst into separate agent turns, even when `messages.inbound.debounceMs` or `byChannel.matrix` is configured. ## User Impact With `messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix` (or the global `debounceMs`) set, a burst of Matrix messages from one sender gets one reply. The Matrix default stays 0, so nothing is delayed unless the operator opts in. ## Why This Change Was Made Rebuilt on the durable Matrix ingress (the earlier head targeted the replay-claim API that main has since removed). It follows the Mattermost fan-in debouncer from #166499: - Ingress `dispatch` hands each event and its claim lifecycle to a room-keyed `createChannelInboundDebouncer` and returns `{ kind: "deferred" }`. `canAppend` only merges contiguous text from the same sender and thread root, and `serializeImmediate` keeps everything in room order, so a burst never jumps ahead of another sender's message. - A flush fans the batched claims into one lifecycle (`fanInChannelIngressLifecycles`). Adopting the merged turn completes every claim; a gated turn settles them; a handler failure fails each claim so the drain's retry policy applies; shutdown or an aborted claim cancels them back to the queue. - The merged event keeps the latest event id (reply threading), joins bodies with newlines, keeps each event's HTML in `formatted_body` (escaped plain text otherwise, joined with `
`) so the handler's matrix.to pill check still validates mentions, and merges `m.mentions`. - Media, voice notes, edits, real replies (not thread fallbacks), the bot's own events, and control commands dispatch alone. Command bypass strips the mention prefix the way the handler does (bot MXID, room display name, every agent's mention patterns), so `@Bot: /stop` is never delayed. Prefix lookup is async, so it is chained per room. - Pre-startup history and E2EE decryption are now handled by ingress before delivery, so the old pre-startup predicate and repeat-emit filter are gone. - Monitor shutdown closes the debouncer with task admission: pending batches and late deliveries return to the durable queue instead of being dropped. - The delay is read from live config.
Test-only changes - `index.test-helpers.ts`: the fake ingress passes a full claim lifecycle and records it; the fake runtime gains a `messagesConfig` knob and a `mock-isolation` note (`config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` drops that entry). - `index.test.ts`: handler failures and late post-shutdown events are now asserted on the claim lifecycle (`onFailed` / `onCancelled`) rather than as a rejected delivery; the shutdown-order test waits for the handler to start before aborting.
## Evidence - Original defect: the new `index.test.ts` case "merges a Matrix text burst when messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix is set" fails with `index.ts` reverted to main (handler called 2 times, no batching) and passes with the fix. - `inbound-debounce.test.ts` (16 tests): merge on latest event, single adoption per claim, gated-turn settle, failure fans out `onFailed`, immediate dispatch for edits/replies/commands (MXID, display-name pill, mention pattern)/images, arrival order under async prefix lookup, room order across senders and threads, HTML and mention merge, own messages, shutdown cancellation. - `index.test.ts`: burst merge through the monitor wiring and a debounce delay committed after startup. - Local gates on this head: `pnpm test:extension matrix` pass; `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` typecheck-all, format, mock-export ratchet, dead-export scan, plugin boundaries pass; oxlint on `extensions/matrix` clean; `pnpm format:docs:check` clean. - Earlier live run (2026.9.8 Gateway, previous implementation, `byChannel.matrix: 3000`): a five-line Element burst produced one user-triggered agent turn. Not re-run on this head.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).

prs.title: chore(codex): test warm claim settlement and scope revocation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Tests-only regression coverage; no runtime source change or production fix in this PR.** The proof target here is that a failed owner leaves no orphan native-thread claim and a later attempt can reuse that thread.

A Codex-backed conversation can reject the next turn as “claimed by active work” after failed ownership settlement, even though the failed attempt is no longer running. The existing cleanup lacks targeted coverage at the warm-claim cleanup and monitor-setup revocation seams.

Related: karmaterminal/openclaw#1431 (the queue-behind-*genuinely active* work request is separate and remains open).

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. These tests protect the existing claim-release behavior against regressions that could strand subsequent Codex attempts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inject a lease-settlement failure after proving warm claim transfer (without a cold resume), and separately revoke session binding authority during monitor setup. Assert cleanup clears each claim and the same native thread can be claimed by a follow-up attempt. The latter is **scope revocation, not a simulated binding-store lease expiry**. The tests complement the existing lifecycle cleanup; they do not implement queueing behind active work.

## Evidence

- Based on upstream `main` `6ba6ad224ae` (2026-10-25); two Codex app-server test files only.
- Focused Codex app-server suites: 2 files, 21/21 tests passed on upstream base.
- Exact PR head 14bf56f9ea33: [GitHub Actions changed-extensions-config](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121349722824) ran both changed test files, 21/21 passed. Its log includes the warm lifecycle injected-failure test and the monitor-failure binding-scope revocation test; the latter asserts a completed follow-up turn on the same native thread with the claim cleared. [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121351049271) passed. These are fixture-driven in-repo assertions, **not** a shipped Gateway/CLI lease-loss trace.
- Extension test typecheck, targeted format and lint pass; line-cap ratchet passes against `upstream/main` for the two changed files. (The default local ratchet base is `origin/main`, a divergent fork, and falsely flags unrelated upstream files.)
- No live service change or end-to-end field reproduction claimed.

**Follow-up proof correction (2026-10-27):** A Claude source review found the monitor case calls `releaseBindingAuthority()` (binding scope, not simulated lease expiry); the warm case now asserts ownership is held at the injected settlement fault and no cold `thread/resume` occurs before it. Updated head `71d416664521dc5f51bf3e6ac2a435786f91f07c`: focused Vitest 21/21, extension-test tsgo, targeted oxfmt/oxlint and diff check passed locally. Hosted CI is pending; no live lease-expiry or production fix is claimed.

prs.title: perf(sessions): skip protection scans for full cold batches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold-storage selection scans every session for hot-transcript protection even when embedded archives already fill the batch and no hot transcript can be selected.

## User Impact

Full externalization batches skip unused preparation work. Selected records, ordering, incoming-reference protection, commit validation, schemas, stored formats, retention, and recovery authority remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the protection scan into the existing hot-window selection condition. PostgreSQL buffers the query result, so avoiding the query also avoids transferring unused metadata through the bridge. This is an avoided-work claim, not a measured latency result.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(memory): show credential source when embedding probes return 401
prs.body:
Related: #184523 (canonical), #192287, #191883. Builds on #160878 and preserves #172237.

## What Problem This Solves

When an embedding probe fails with HTTP 401, operators cannot tell which credential source the request selected, and working Codex chat or a successful renewal can misleadingly look like proof that embeddings should work.

## User Impact

The existing memory probe reports safe facts from the rejected dispatch: auth mode, credential-source category, native OpenAI endpoint or a redacted custom destination, and whether forced refresh was requested. It explains that reindexing does not repair authentication and advises preserving the existing index until an embedding probe succeeds.

This does **not** repair the renewed-OAuth rejection or restore semantic search. It changes no credential precedence, endpoints, grants, retry policy, fallback, billing choice, or index state. Ordinary Codex OAuth remains distinct from the SIWC token-sharing grant, which remains excluded from embeddings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The investigation found a source-supported selection change: v2026.9.9 excluded ordinary OAuth from native embeddings, while v2026.10.10 allowed it. An unchanged mixed store can therefore select saved OAuth ahead of an environment API key. That does not establish which credential an earlier request used or explain why a freshly renewed bearer is rejected.

Tracing the auth owner, grant classification, renewal parameters, embedding endpoint and final HTTP request did not establish a client authentication defect or provider/account ownership of the rejection. Default ordinary OAuth renewal uses the same token endpoint, client ID and refresh grant, without a resource parameter, as the inspected [Codex implementation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9/codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs#L1693). OpenClaw uses form encoding and Codex uses JSON; this difference does not establish the cause of the post-renewal rejection. Adding SIWC's resource parameter, exchanging tokens, changing endpoints or retrying every 401 would be speculative. The existing same-origin `token_expired` retry remains unchanged; `invalid_authentication` is not automatically retried.

Request facts come from the credential owner on each dispatch, with no token decoding or identifier output. Redirects make final credential attribution unknown. Static facts are invalidated when the prepared Authorization header changes. Display metadata stays separate from message/code/cause used by auth and retry policy. A real memory-probe test exposed separate plugin/host copies of the diagnostic module; the existing weak map now uses the process singleton owner so the facts reach the user-facing probe. No new manager, cache or configuration surface is introduced.

Safe production follow-up: inspect the selected source using `openclaw memory status --deep`, retain the existing vector index, and resolve embedding access before rebuilding. If an operator explicitly chooses API-billed embeddings, a dedicated `memory.search.remote.apiKey` or environment-backed SecretRef isolates that choice from chat authentication. A local embedding provider is another explicit option. After a synthetic embedding request succeeds, validate the index upgrade and semantic search on an isolated corpus, then perform any necessary production reindexing.

Maintainer direction requested: accept the optional typed diagnostic callbacks on the existing Plugin SDK embedding helpers as an additive supported contract. This proposal covers the 401 diagnostic path; the canonical issue’s broader 429 and account-access questions remain open.

## Evidence

- Final serial regression run: **138 tests passed across seven files** (29 shared SDK transport/auth, 7 core error, 102 OpenAI/memory). Coverage includes stored OAuth versus environment-key selection, same-profile replacement, no automatic retry for `invalid_authentication`, the existing `token_expired` retry, redaction, concurrent dispatches, redirects, frozen errors, the actual memory probe and real HTTP upgrade failures.
- The request-facts regression fails on base `206d54934a3d0764cad0ea59a31d43f74bec0fa0` with only the raw 401, then passes with this change. The real OpenAI-plugin-to-memory-probe test also failed until the shared diagnostic owner was fixed, then passed. The existing vector-index downgrade protection test passed separately.
- A fresh full `pnpm build` passed on reviewed head `d471a895ebdd9cf040e9a78bdf089a022a4c3c80`, including SDK exports and bootstrap checks (Node 24.22.1). Five affected typecheck lanes passed; focused type-aware core/SDK and plugin lint passed. Formatting, documentation lint (1,404 files), assertion safety and changed-file size checks passed.
- Fresh independent agent review covered the complete candidate against that base and the subsequent lint corrections, with no remaining P0–P2 findings. Optional CLI autoreview was attempted once but could not authenticate and produced no review report; it is not claimed as a clean review.

- [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192433#issuecomment-6619994197) found no code or security findings and requested shipped-command proof. That proof is supplied below. The SDK-contract decision and shared test-budget action remain with maintainers.

<details>
<summary>Shipped-command proof with controlled HTTP responses</summary>

The packaged `openclaw.mjs` launcher ran from an empty temporary working directory, with allowlisted environment variables and temporary home/state/agent/workspace paths. Shell environment import and dreaming were disabled. Only Memory Core and OpenAI were enabled. The bearer and corpus were synthetic; the endpoint deliberately returned 401 or fabricated vectors. No real account credentials or production state were used.

Selected lines from the actual terminal capture (paths redacted; embedded line breaks remain escaped as printed by the CLI):

```text
$ node [checkout]/openclaw.mjs memory status --deep --agent main
Memory Search (main)
Provider: openai (requested: openai)
Model: text-embedding-3-small
Indexed: 1/1 files · 1 chunks
Embeddings: unavailable
Embeddings error: openai embeddings failed (model: text-embedding-3-small, batch size: 1) (401): Invalid authentication. [type=invalid_request_error, code=invalid_authentication]\nEmbedding client request: auth_mode=configured-bearer, credential_source=memory-config; endpoint=custom (redacted); HTTP 401; force_refresh_requested=false.\nThe embedding probe failed authentication. A working chat login or successful OAuth refresh does not establish embedding access. HTTP 401 alone does not identify whether the credential, grant, or account access caused the rejection. Verify the selected embedding credential and endpoint, then repeat this probe. Reindexing does not repair authentication; keep the existing index and verify embeddings before rebuilding.
Vector store: ready
Semantic vectors: ready
Vector dims: 1536
FTS: ready
```

A separate fresh-store probe made exactly one HTTP request, received `401 invalid_authentication`, displayed these facts, and did not print the fixture credential.

The same built CLI also indexed the isolated corpus against a controlled 200 response, then encountered a 401 during a forced rebuild after the corpus changed. Read-only comparisons of the published sqlite-vec embedding payloads and chunk hashes were identical before/after that failed rebuild. Switching the fixture endpoint back to 200 let indexing finish and vector-enabled search return the updated synthetic marker. The result receipt was:

```json
{
  "seed_index_exit": 0,
  "rejected_rebuild_exit": 1,
  "published_vectors": 1,
  "vector_and_chunk_payload_unchanged_after_401": true,
  "recovery_index_exit": 0,
  "synthetic_vector_search_exit": 0,
  "updated_synthetic_corpus_found": true,
  "live_oauth_access_verified": false
}
```

This proves the shipped diagnostic and isolated index/search mechanics. Fabricated vectors and fixture acceptance do not establish live OAuth embedding access, semantic quality, or restoration of the reported account.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Scope, test budget and other observed validation limits</summary>

- Simplification retains the auth owner, HTTP wrapper and existing weak diagnostic map; there is no parallel metadata manager. Production delta: +185/-12 lines. Test delta: +272/-19 literal LF bytes, with an exact 253-line allocation for dispatch facts, redaction, redirects and the real consumer boundary.
- Local base `206d549…` has a 53-line deficit (6,444,088 / ceiling 6,444,035); the local candidate preserves it. The current [CI ratchet failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41750215049/job/126313632566) uses newer base `40b3be0b302d885a880dee8435d479a093b23bad`: independently counted 6,446,831 test LF bytes / ceiling 6,446,686 = **145 existing debt**. CI merge `77ffa5b4141c59223b659e668b4c867dadd12af9` has 6,447,084 / ceiling 6,446,939, so both increase exactly 253 and debt stays 145.
- The CI classifier labels this job **new** because its matching main job passed without comparing selected scope. The guard intentionally permits existing overage only for nonpositive raw test growth; this PR triggers the gate despite fully funding its own growth. It remains a failed required check, not a passing baseline exemption. Keep the exact 253 allocation. Shared-budget reconciliation needs owner approval: [testing policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/.agents/skills/openclaw-testing/SKILL.md#baseline-and-expected-failure-exceptions), “Other raises, including scalar-only reconciliation, need approval.” [CI run 41750215049](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41750215049) has completed: 59 jobs succeeded and 27 skipped; the baseline-ratchet job and its aggregate gate failed. No implementation job failed. Maintainer action is needed for this shared budget before landing.
- An earlier cold/concurrent run hit the existing `missing-fts` case's 30-second application timeout. A subsequent base comparison and serial patched run passed that case; the original timeout's cause remains unresolved.
- The optional repository-wide anchor audit reports two unchanged failures in `/tools/acp-agents-setup` and `releases/2026.10.1.md`. The successful full build also reports UI size-budget warnings; no UI performance improvement is claimed.

</details>

The original observations include successful same-profile renewal followed by the same `401 invalid_authentication`. No isolated live OAuth embedding credential is available here. Loopback HTTP and synthetic credentials prove selection, diagnostic delivery and index behavior; they do **not** prove live OAuth embedding access. No production deployment, authentication, API-key settings or stored memory was changed.

prs.title: fix(ui): open composer plus menu without upward growth
prs.body:
## Problem

Reopening the composer **+** menu (desktop and mobile) made the panel grow from the bottom up over ~100 ms instead of using the shared menu entrance the other composer pickers use.

`chat-composer-plus-menu-frame.tsx` writes a measured inline `height` on the panel, and that value goes stale while the menu is closed (sampled at `25px` on reopen). The panel's `height 220ms` transition then ran during the entrance, so the top-anchored panel animated from about 25px up to its real height of about 197px.

## Solution

The `height` transition now applies only to `.agent-chat__capability-menu-panel[data-phase="open"]`. Moving between root, Skills, and Plugins in an open menu still eases the height. Opening and closing use only the shared `.oc-menu` opacity and scale transition, the same as the permission, model, and talk pickers.

## Evidence

- Frame sampling on reopen, desktop 1280×900 and mobile 390×844, `/chat`:
  - before: computed height `25 → 114 → 163 → 182 → 191 → 197px` while opacity rises
  - after: `197px` on every visible frame; only scale and opacity animate
- During the `open` phase the computed transition is still `height / 0.22s`, so switching views keeps its height easing.
- New e2e test `reopens at its measured height instead of growing upward` in `chat-attachment-menu.e2e.test.ts`. It fails on the base with 9 distinct visible heights and passes with the fix. The full file passes: 14/14.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` are clean.

No static screenshot is included because the before and after end states look the same. Only the entrance motion changed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): check Incognito chat leaves against the in-process transcript
prs.body:
## Problem

Every Incognito chat send after the first one failed with `Error: Chat admission omitted its worker-prepared active path` and showed as **Not sent**. Stop failed the same way.

Incognito transcripts live in the Gateway's process-local session actor, which the database read workers cannot open. Admission and Stop compare the browser's `expectedLeafEntryId` against the chat's active path, and for Incognito chats nothing supplied that fact anymore. #174610 removed the in-process Incognito active-path read as "unreachable", but the Incognito admission branch still depended on it. The first message of a new Incognito chat still worked because it has no prior leaf.

## Fix

- `chat-send-session.ts` / `chat-send-active-leaf.ts`: for Incognito sends and Stop, read the active-path relation from the memory session actor (`readSessionTranscriptAnchorsAsync`), then run the existing `assertExpectedLeafActive` check. Durable sessions are unchanged.
- `session-actor-memory-history-anchors.ts`: memory anchor reads now report `activePathRelation` (exact / ancestor / off-path), matching the SQLite projection.
- `session-transcript-anchor-read.ts`: a missing memory transcript reports the empty-root relation, like the SQLite reader.

Accepted edge case (documented in code): the Incognito path read happens just before the entry snapshot. A reset is still rejected by the session-id fence. An append that lands between the two reads is a rare race that the user can retry.

## Evidence

- `chat-send-active-leaf.incognito.test.ts` (real `chat.send` handler, real memory storage): stale and earlier leaves are rejected with `active-leaf-changed` for sends and Stop, the exact leaf is accepted for Stop, and a session-fenced ancestor is admitted and dispatched. Red on base (generic error instead of `active-leaf-changed`), green with the fix.
- New `chat-incognito-send.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`: a real built Gateway and Chromium. The test turns on Incognito, starts a session and sends two follow-ups, and every reply appears with no **Not sent**. On a base build it fails at the second reply; with the fix it passes.
- Related suites pass: projection rebuild, stop cascade, both transcript-anchor suites, `session-control.incognito`, `vitest-ui-e2e-config`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes, run with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1` because the full dead-export scan fails on `ui/.../systems-sidebar.tsx: systemKind`, which this PR doesn't touch. `tsgo:core` is clean.
- Local autoreview (P2): no findings.

## Not covered

A live run against real OpenAI showed that Incognito chats fail at the **model run** with `This account action requires a current authorized connection`. The failure is identical on base `main` without this change, and the same flow succeeds for a durable chat. It is a separate existing model-account authority issue and is not addressed here.

prs.title: fix(telegram): route bound conversations when agent selection is ambiguous
prs.body:
Closes #159334

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram conversation with an active session binding fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError` on a multi-agent install that has no channel-wide Telegram route, so its messages are never processed.

## User Impact

User impact: runtime-bound Telegram conversations reach their bound agent regardless of how many agents are configured. Conversations without a binding, or whose binding names no agent, keep today's behavior — including still requiring an explicit channel owner. A binding revoked or replaced while a message is being routed no longer leaves the former owner selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareTelegramConversationRoute` asked ordinary agent selection for a route before looking at the binding, and ordinary selection refuses an ambiguous roster. It now selects the base route inside the SDK's `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync({ resolveRoute })` (and `inspectRuntimeConversationBindingRoute({ inspection, resolveRoute })` for route-owner inspection): the binding owner's canonically classified `boundAgentId` arrives before ordinary selection, and when it is set the base route is derived from session-only config with that agent as the default. This is the shared binding-owner selection Slack, Discord and iMessage use, so Telegram no longer re-implements the session-key/metadata classification. Topic overrides, configured bindings, and the runtime-binding step that follows are unchanged.

### Binding changes during resolution (review follow-up)

An earlier revision chose the agent from a synchronous binding read and then let `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync` read the binding again after an `await`, so a binding revoked in between could leave the former owner selected; that revision guarded it with a re-prepare/retry loop.

Since merging current `main` (`4ee4606`), agent selection runs inside the `resolveRoute` callback of the single awaited inspection, so the agent and the binding facts come from the same read. There is no second read to diverge from, and the retry loop is gone. The same applies to `prepareTelegramConversationRouteInspection` (new on `main`), whose `resolve(inspection)` now selects the agent from the inspection it is handed. `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` shares the inbound path with `touchBinding: false`.

## Evidence

New cases in `conversation-route-owner.test.ts`, all on a two-agent config with no route bindings:

- inbound `resolveTelegramConversationRoute` selects the bound agent and session, reports `runtime-bound`, and touches the binding once;
- `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` selects the bound agent without touching liveness;
- a sentinel `global` session with `metadata.agentId` selects that agent;
- a binding that names no agent still rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED`;
- a binding revoked just before the awaited inspection rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` instead of routing to the former owner;
- a binding replaced just before the awaited inspection routes to the new owner and its new binding.

Negative controls: with `main`'s `conversation-route.ts` (`4ee4606`), 4 of these 6 fail with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` (the bound-agent, inspection, sentinel-metadata and replacement cases); the no-agent and revocation cases pass there, as intended, since both assert that rejection.

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts
19 passed (19)
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram
passed 63 Vitest shards
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
0 errors
```

Focused regression cost: `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts` — 19 tests, 16.4 s Vitest duration / 20.8 s wall time locally. `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and the assertion SAFETY ratchet are clean on the changed files. The test fixture uses `agents.entries` (the authored shape since `agents.list` was retired on `main`).

**Live Telegram proof:** not included. The `telegram-e2e-userbot` harness needs Convex-leased team credentials, which I don't have as an outside contributor. The evidence above is unit-level through the real binding-routing SDK with a test adapter.

AI-assisted. I reviewed the change and ran the tests and negative controls above locally.

prs.title: fix(ui): match quota summaries to the selected account
prs.body:
## Problem

The composer chose the first quota group for a provider. With two accounts on the same provider, reversing the response changed which account's quota appeared. Model controls could also use a measured plan belonging to a different account.

## Solution

Carry the measured auth-profile identity through provider usage collection and the account-aware `models.authStatus` projection. Match that identity against the session's account selection before displaying quota or using a measured plan label. Share the exact-account join between the composer and model controls, and show **Quota account unknown** instead of guessing.

The profile identifier remains gated with account identity in `models.authStatus` and is removed from the public `usage.status` response.

## Impact

Quota selection no longer depends on provider response order. Model picker and default-model labels cannot borrow another account's measured plan. Profile account summaries retain their separate account-keyed source. There are no configuration, persistence, permission, dependency, or stylesheet changes.

## Evidence

- The two-account regression fails against the original composer on `origin/main` and passes on this branch, including reversed response order.
- Composer, model picker, runtime, and provider-data tests: 57 passed (9.95 seconds). Provider auth/load tests: 11 passed (185.39 seconds). Gateway auth-status and usage-cache tests: 61 passed (36.79 seconds).
- Profile account summaries, default-models view, account usage, and plan labels: 26 passed (3.94 seconds).
- Browser quota suite: 6 passed (59.67 seconds), covering desktop/phone, light/dark, reversed rows, automatic identity, and keyboard opening. Additional Rose dark/custom-accent comparisons pass on both versions.
- Core/UI typechecks, focused lint, formatting, localization verification, and `git diff --check` pass.
- A separate 362-line allocation covers the new cross-layer regressions. The test-line ratchet still reports the existing base overrun of 355 lines (6,442,517 total; 6,442,162 allocated ceiling); the shared scalar is unchanged.
- CI results are not yet available.
- Related: #183032, #185039, #191312.

## Visual proof

BEFORE is on the left; AFTER is on the right. Six comparisons cover 1440-pixel desktop and 390-pixel phone layouts in light/dark, the model picker, reversed rows with Rose dark and a custom mint accent, and automatic/unknown account selection. All displayed data is fictional.

## Edge cases

- Automatic, redacted, missing, or ambiguous account identity stays unknown, even when only one provider row is available.
- Conflicting measurements for the same identity are not resolved by response order.
- The selected account is the configured session preference, not retrospective attribution of a previous response.
- Browser proof uses the real UI with a mock Gateway. Credential collection and Gateway projection have separate tests; no live-provider session-to-usage run is claimed.

## Worked on by

prs.title: docs(sessions): say archived delete is scope-based, not creator-based
prs.body:
Fixes #191949

## What Problem This Solves

`docs/concepts/multi-user.md` states the archive/restore creator rule, and `docs/gateway/operator-scopes.md` lists the `sessions.delete` scopes, but neither says whether deleting an archived session inherits that creator rule. A reader cannot tell whether an `operator.write` caller who did not create the session may delete it once it is archived.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion is scope-based, not creator-based. `sessions.delete` is a dynamic-scope method (`src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts`): `operator.write` may delete an already-archived session with the supported fields, `operator.admin` keeps unrestricted delete, and the handler rechecks the archived requirement (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-delete.ts`). There is no creator gate on that path, unlike archive and restore.

Both pages now say so next to the existing rules:

- `multi-user.md`: the archive paragraph states the creator rule, then notes that deleting an archived session is not creator-limited.
- `operator-scopes.md`: the `sessions.delete` bullet adds the same clarification for the archived-only path.

## Evidence

- Behavior: `src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts` ("State-aware: write scope may delete already-archived sessions") and `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-delete.ts` (archived-only recheck; the delete path has no creator comparison).
- Docs: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files; `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): keep a lone leftover model inline
prs.body:
Fixes #188469

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI model picker collapsed a provider group's single remaining model behind an "All models (1)" row, so reaching that one model cost an extra click while offering no choice.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat-model-picker-panel.tsx` splits each provider group into `lead` (ranked/visible) and `more` (folded), then renders the "All models" toggle whenever `more.length > 0`. With one leftover the toggle is pure friction: it hides exactly one row and reveals nothing new.

A lone remainder is now appended to `lead`, so it renders inline and the toggle disappears. Groups with two or more folded models keep the existing disclosure behaviour (the `drops the All models row once expanded` cases still cover it), and the unranked-catalog overflow path is unchanged apart from the same single-leftover rule.

## User Impact

Providers that recommend one model and keep one extra model now show both directly; larger catalogs keep the fold.

## Evidence

Head `f0b4ae238f`, Node 26.12.1.

```text
$ pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-picker.test.tsx
  ✓ keeps the tenth model of an unranked catalog inline
Tests  9 passed (9)

# with the singleton rule removed from chat-model-picker-panel.tsx:
× keeps the tenth model of an unranked catalog inline
  expected null not to be null        # the tenth model folds behind "All models (1)"

$ npx oxlint <touched files>    0 warnings, 0 errors
$ npx oxfmt --check <touched files>   all files use the correct format
```

### Served Control UI before/after

Same fixture and interaction in both runs (`pnpm dev:ui:mock` in this worktree for the fix, a clean `upstream/main` worktree for the base; Chrome driven by Playwright; synthetic catalog with one recommending provider whose recommended model has one leftover, and one unranked provider with ten models):

| before (`upstream/main`) | after (this head) |
|---|---|
| `GPT-5 variant 8` → `All models (1)` | `GPT-5 variant 8` → `GPT-5 demo remainder` inline |
| `Anthropic 2` → `Claude Opus 4.8` → `All models (1)` (`Claude Fable 5` hidden) | `Anthropic 2` → `Claude Opus 4.8` → `Claude Fable 5` inline |

```text
# before: OpenAI | 10 | … | GPT-5 variant 8 | All models (1) | Anthropic | 2 | … | Claude Opus 4.8 | Configured route | All models (1)
# after:  OpenAI | 10 | … | GPT-5 variant 8 | GPT-5 demo remainder | Anthropic | 2 | … | Claude Opus 4.8 | Configured route | Claude Fable 5 | Configured route
```

The popover DOM agrees: the base render contains `[data-chat-model-more-toggle]`, this head contains none.

Before — `upstream/main`, both groups fold their remaining model (synthetic mock catalog, served Control UI popover scrolled to the group end):

![before: All models (1) for both groups](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6063b67c-6de8-47a0-a70e-01149f9822c3)

After — this head, the tenth unranked model and the recommending provider's leftover render inline with no toggle:

![after: tenth model and leftover inline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f74e04a-42bd-4aa5-ba7d-797083b554ed)

OpenAI group, same scroll position, before (`All models (1)`) vs after (`GPT-5 demo remainder` inline):

![before: OpenAI group folds the tenth model](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28ad4890-4d09-4807-b6a3-b4fb261039c6)

![after: OpenAI group shows the tenth model inline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d967c969-b165-494d-90fd-d14c6cf9f4e5)

All four are sanitized mock fixtures (provider names, a synthetic "demo remainder" model id, and placeholder account labels only; no keys, IPs, or phone numbers).

### Open question (maintainer decision)

Should a lone remaining model render inline for both recommending providers and unranked providers with exactly ten choices? This head answers "yes" for both; the review recommended the same.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Followed the `lead`/`more` split in `chat-model-picker-panel.tsx`, added the single-leftover rule after both grouping passes, and updated the fixtures that relied on a one-entry fold. The implementer understands the code: the fold exists to bound long catalogs, and a one-entry fold only adds a click.

prs.title: docs(docker): warn about in-container CLI cost and Compose stop grace
prs.body:
Fixes #187041
Fixes #187042
Fixes #187043

## What Problem This Solves

Three operator-facing gaps in the Docker/Compose docs, all reported with production evidence on 2026.10.7:

1. Nothing warns that `docker compose exec openclaw-gateway openclaw <command>` boots a full CLI runtime inside the Gateway container. Scheduled host jobs polling `channel status` / `cron list` / `agent list` overlap, and the Gateway stalls (the reporter measured ~160 s per invocation and Discord 1006 disconnects).
2. `openclaw config validate` only checks plugin-owned schema where the plugin is available, so validating a config copy in a plugin-less container can report `valid: true` for keys the live Gateway then rejects on hot reload.
3. Compose stop grace periods (Docker's 10 s default, 90 s in many files) are far shorter than the Gateway's shutdown budget, so the container is killed mid-drain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Documentation only; no runtime behavior changes.

- `docs/install/docker/compose-operations.md` gains "CLI invocations against the Gateway" (cost depends on the command; overlapping jobs cost the same host/state whether they run via `exec` or the one-shot `openclaw-cli` service; use the HTTP probes for routine health polling) and "Stop grace period".
- The grace-period section separates the 325 s overall allowance (315 s drain + 10 s reserve, 330 s managed service stop timeout) from what an ordinary Compose stop actually drains: `STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000` caps admitted-work drain, and the rest is kept for cancellation and durable cleanup. `stop_grace_period: 340s` stays as the covering example.
- `docs/cli/config.md` (`config validate`) now says generated bundled channel schemas are normally checked without loading the runtime (`ensureChannelSchemas` seeds `GENERATED_BUNDLED_CHANNEL_CONFIG_METADATA`), that incomplete discovery can defer even those (`preserveUnavailableConfig` continues before `ensureChannelSchemas`), and that unavailable plugin schema yields `valid: true` with warnings while the Gateway can still reject the keys on hot reload.

## User Impact

Operators stop discovering these three the hard way — unresponsive Gateways from status polling, a "valid" config rejected on reload, and unclean stops that force a full session revalidation on the next start.

## Evidence

Docs-only change, so the proof is the documentation checks plus the source of the numbers:

```text
$ git diff --check
(no output)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check docs/install/docker/compose-operations.md docs/cli/config.md
All matched files use the correct format.

$ grep -n "STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS" src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop-shutdown-budget.ts | head -2
14:const STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000;
146:      : Math.min(STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS, Math.max(0, budget.timeoutMs - budget.reserveMs)),

$ node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs
checked_internal_links=16116
broken_links=0
```

Changed files: `docs/install/docker/compose-operations.md` (+31), `docs/cli/config.md` (+1). No links added, so no new routes; headings added are anchor-safe.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git grep`/`git show` to confirm the shutdown budget constants and the current wording of both pages, then wrote the two sections and the caveat. The implementer understands the content: the grace period must cover the 315 s drain plus the 10 s reserve, and plugin-owned schema can only be validated where that plugin is loaded.

prs.title: fix(telegram): treat forwarded rich messages as debounceable text
prs.body:
Fixes #187677

## What Problem This Solves

A burst of forwarded Telegram rich messages was not batched: each forward dispatched on its own and the receiving agent ran one turn per message, ignoring the 1 s forward collection window. Typed text from the same sender batched correctly.

## Why This Change Was Made

`shouldDebounceTelegramEntry()` decides with `getTelegramTextParts(entry.msg).text`, and that helper only read `text`, `caption`, contact, and poll. A Bot API block message carries `rich_message` instead, so the text part was empty, `hasDebounceableText` was false, and the forward lane took the immediate path.

`getTelegramTextParts()` now renders `rich_message` blocks through `resolveTelegramRichMessageText()` — the same renderer the agent prompt uses — so the debounce predicate and `joinTelegramTextParts()` see the same content the prompt does. Non-text rich messages (for example a divider) still render to an empty string, so media and caption callers keep treating them as non-text.

## User Impact

For users, forwarding several rich messages now gets one combined reply instead of one reply per message, matching the documented forward-batching behavior.

## Evidence

Head `43d6321ac`, Node 26.12.1. Real-Gateway proof: built the worktree to `dist`, ran `node dist/index.js gateway` with an isolated state dir, pointed `channels.telegram.apiRoot` at a loopback mock Telegram Bot API serving one burst of three forwarded `rich_message` updates, and recorded every agent request on a loopback mock OpenAI-compatible provider. No external credentials; the burst was the only traffic.

Observed result on this fix — the burst becomes one turn containing every message:

```text
[telegram] [diag] isolated polling worker batch received queued=3

mock provider: 1 chat-completions request; its user turn:
  [Forwarded from Origin at 2025-01-08T01:33:20.000Z] Alpha forward
  [Forwarded from Origin at 2025-01-08T01:33:20.000Z] Beta forward
  [Forwarded from Origin at 2025-01-08T01:33:20.000Z] Gamma forward
mock Bot API: 1 sendMessage reply
```

Same harness and burst, with `body-helpers.ts` reverted to the base as a red control:

| run | agent requests | how the forwards reach the agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base (fix reverted) | 2 requests, 3 dispatched user messages | each forward enters alone — "Alpha forward", then "Beta forward" as an immediate follow-up, then "Gamma forward" after the first reply; the reported one-turn-per-message behavior |
| this fix | 1 request | one user message joining all three `[Forwarded from Origin]` segments |

Unit-level red/green for the changed predicate stays covered by the committed regression:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot/body-helpers.inbound.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
11 passed
  ✓ renders forwarded rich messages so debounce sees text

# reverting body-helpers.ts to upstream/main:
× renders forwarded rich messages so debounce sees text
  AssertionError: expected '' to be 'first forward'

$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.body.test.ts \
    extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-pipeline.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
47 passed
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <3 touched files>   0 warnings, 0 errors
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <3 touched files>
All matched files use the correct format.
```

Not covered: a live Telegram forwarding burst from real accounts (needs bot credentials). The mock Bot API reproduces the reported update shape (`forward_origin` + `rich_message`, one getUpdates batch), and the built Gateway above is the shipped entry that consumed it.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Traced the reported log to `getTelegramTextParts()` returning empty for `rich_message`, reused the existing prompt renderer, and added the regression; the Gateway evidence comes from a local loopback harness (mock Telegram Bot API + mock provider) driving the built Gateway. The implementer understands the code: the debounce decision and the prompt must agree on what text a message has.

prs.title: feat: add Fortytwo to the external provider catalog
prs.body:
Closes #191163

## What Problem This Solves
Fortytwo users currently have to find and install the npm plugin themselves before configuring their API key.

## User Impact
Users can install the vendor-maintained plugin with `openclaw plugins install fortytwo` and find the Fortytwo API key choice in provider setup. The package requires OpenClaw 2026.10.9 or newer.

## Why This Change Was Made
This adds the existing [fortytwo-openclaw](https://github.com/Fortytwo-Network/fortytwo-openclaw) package to the external provider catalog, pinned to the published `0.1.0` artifact and its npm SHA-512 integrity. The runtime stays in the vendor repository. The provider page and navigation describe installation, authentication, discovery, and thinking levels.

The entry uses npm only. The same package is now published on ClawHub under `fortytwo-network`, with a clean scan, but this PR retains its reviewed npm pin. ClawHub publication is not official OpenClaw endorsement. Official catalog admission and package-wide npm trust remain a maintainer decision.

## Evidence
- Published npm metadata verified for `fortytwo-openclaw@0.1.0`; SHA-1 `438e852da97b1939c3694f70f72daea269e73dad`, SHA-512 matches the catalog pin.
- Focused vendor-pin, CLI install-plan, and provider-install-catalog suites: **17 tests passed**. The CLI test exercises provider-ID resolution, exact-version integrity, and avoids applying that integrity to another requested version.
- Upstream CI on `756563ac4fc9ba3d51eb47a52a884ae131c3c6b1`: all checks passed or were skipped; no pending or failed checks at proof handoff. ClawSweeper advisory and the maintainer admission decision remain separate.
- Scoped test typechecks and lint passed. Docs MDX check passed (1,425 files); internal link audit passed (16,237 links, zero broken); formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent live test of the published package on **OpenClaw 2026.10.9, Node 24.22.1**: interactive npm install, authenticated model refresh, incremental text and reasoning, thinking off/medium/xhigh, write/read tools with continuation, PNG input, and a real isolated Gateway turn all passed. Every run used Fortytwo without fallback. This is released-package evidence, not a claim that the unreleased upstream catalog entry is already installed.
- Backend attribution ingestion remains untested. The earlier live inference test used `FORTYTWO_API_KEY`; the current-head onboarding proof below uses only a synthetic placeholder credential and makes no authentication claim.
- Simplification and independent local diff review completed with no actionable findings; no core runtime changes, new dependencies, or workflows. Local autoreview/ClawSweeper CLI was not run.

### Current-head installation and onboarding proof (2026-11-02)

Built and ran the production CLI from clean head `756563ac4fc9ba3d51eb47a52a884ae131c3c6b1` (`OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (756563a)`). Each scenario used a separate temporary state/config/workspace/npm cache; the operator's running installation was not changed.

| Scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Default network: `pnpm openclaw plugins install fortytwo --accept-capabilities` | Exit 0; installed `fortytwo-openclaw@0.1.0`. No `--force`, local package substitution, or fetch shim. |
| Read back accepted artifact: `plugins inspect fortytwo --runtime --json` | `status: loaded`, `trust.reason: trusted-official`, `resolvedSpec: fortytwo-openclaw@0.1.0`, exact catalog integrity and SHA-1. |
| Fresh uninstalled profile, default network, interactive provider picker | More → search Fortytwo showed **Fortytwo (OpenAI-compatible Fortytwo Chat Completions endpoint)** before installation. Canceled at picker; no npm project installed. |
| Interactive classic onboarding after catalog install | More → Fortytwo → Enter Fortytwo API key → synthetic placeholder → default model selected → config saved. Readback: primary `fortytwo/qwen/qwen3.8-27b`, provider endpoint `https://api.fortytwo.network/v1`, API `openai-completions`, empty saved `models` list, `fortytwo:default` API-key profile. Live completion, memory import, embeddings, and daemon installation skipped. |
| Noncatalog `npm:fortytwo-openclaw-unlisted-proof@0.1.0`, without `--force` | Exit 1: source outside ClawHub trust metadata; installation canceled and explicit acknowledgement required. Rejected before registry download/manifest inspection; this is a source-trust boundary test, not a manifest-identity test. |
| Catalog install with altered artifact metadata | Exit 1: `aborted: npm package integrity drift detected for fortytwo-openclaw@0.1.0`. No archive download. |
| Catalog install with original pinned metadata digest but altered archive bytes | Actual archive downloaded; npm returned `EINTEGRITY`, CLI exited 1. Temporary staging was removed. |

For all three rejection controls, config bytes remained unchanged, no installed npm project or extension existed afterward, and `plugins inspect fortytwo --json` returned `Plugin not found`. No rejected artifact reached the committed installation record.

The negative controls used a loopback HTTP npm registry fixture. It advertised the unchanged package name/version and either the altered digest or the original digest while serving the same tarball with one harmless README marker added. The built-in catalog, trust resolver, production installer, npm extraction, and publication path were unchanged. Only the hosted plugin-feed transport was forced unavailable in these controlled scenarios to select this head's fallback catalog, following the repository's existing CLI recovery e2e fixture approach. The successful default-network scenario above used no transport shim. No API keys were used in these controls.

Package-wide trust is an existing catalog policy: explicitly selected other releases of an approved npm package retain source trust; the `0.1.0` artifact digest is not reused for them. This contribution does not narrow that policy. We are requesting a maintainer decision on Fortytwo admission under those semantics, not treating these tests as that approval.

prs.title: fix(read): accept optional false without schema rejection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `read` tool input schema typed `optional` as `Literal(true)`. When a model sent `optional: false` (meaning required), argument validation rejected the call with `optional: must be equal to constant` before the tool ran.

## Fix

Widen `readToolInputSchema.optional` to `boolean`. Execution already treats only `optional === true` as missing-file suppression (`optional !== true` keeps ENOENT/ENOTDIR as errors), so `false` now validates and behaves as required.

## Evidence

### Local createReadToolDefinition proof on head `9b7d6de6a0`

Ran schema validation + the shipped read tool definition (not a mocked schema-only check):

```text
date 2026-11-04T01:17:01.681Z
head 9b7d6de6a0ee4b65ec838d1c08f8e0e8b4b1ed37

=== schema validation ===
{"path":"present.txt","optional":false} => true
{"path":"present.txt","optional":true} => true
{"path":"present.txt"} => true
{"path":"present.txt","optional":"yes"} => false

=== execute optional:false on present file ===
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "hello"
    }
  ],
  "details": {
    "kind": "text",
    "content": "hello"
  }
}

=== execute optional:false on missing file ===
throws: File not found: /tmp/openclaw-read-optional-qC4cdq/missing.txt.
code: ENOENT

=== execute optional:true on missing file ===
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "Optional file not found: missing.txt."
    }
  ],
  "details": {
    "kind": "not_found",
    "status": "not_found",
    "path": "missing.txt",
    "optional": true
  }
}
```

Focused Vitest:

```text
pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts -t "optional false"
# accepts optional false and keeps missing required paths as errors — passed
```

### Gap

No full Gateway agent-turn transcript on this box (no configured Gateway session). The proof above is the production read tool owner used by agent turns; a Gateway RPC/trace can be attached if maintainers still require that layer.

prs.title: fix(agents): stop exec-completion wakes from rewriting the prompt cache
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

Closes #191128

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users whose agent runs background commands (`tools.exec.notifyOnExit`, default `true`) would pay a full prompt-cache write on **every** exec-completion wake: the woken turn's system prompt is built in `minimal` mode, so it drops Execution Bias, the skills catalog, Memory Recall, Docs and Delegation and renders "Subagent Context" instead of "Conversation Context" — a different prefix from the conversation's normal turn (39,754 → 32,290 chars, diverging at ~char 90 in the reporter's capture).
- The wake's tool access is unchanged by this PR: the finite producer ceiling introduced for #183589 stays exactly as it is.
- **Related:** #183589 / #183594 / #190410 keep the finite ceiling for tool access (untouched here); #186285 / #186306 (fc46600a98) stopped a finite ceiling from dropping the skills catalog, but minimal mode itself still applied. Fix-signal labels on the issue: `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** a turn woken by a background exec completion keeps the prompt mode of the run that started the exec, so the system prompt prefix is byte-identical and the provider prompt cache is read instead of rewritten.
- The default session-event policy in `createOpenClawCodingTools` records the producing run's own authorized surface as the wake's ceiling. That list is a *provenance* fact, not a policy narrowing, but `toolPolicyRestrictsTools()` treats any non-empty allowlist without `*` as restrictive — which is what forced `minimal`. This PR separates the two questions: the ceiling still bounds tool access, and a new non-enumerable provenance fact on the allowlist (same mechanism as the existing `TOOL_ALLOWLIST_INTERSECTION` metadata) tells the two prompt-mode gates that nothing was removed.
- The fact is recorded only when the producing turn held its session's normal surface: no runtime allowlist, no turn-scoped plugin grant, no collector contract, no delegated authority, no sender/group/sandbox/subagent/inherited restriction, no tool withheld from the turn, non-empty surface. Configured `tools.allow`/`tools.deny` are deliberately not treated as narrowing — the woken turn re-resolves them from the same config, so its prompt matches the conversation's normal prompt in that case too.
- **Out of scope:** no change to tool access, to the ceiling's contents, to session-event admission, or to any wire/schema/config surface (the fact is a non-enumerable symbol property, so it never reaches JSON, the gateway protocol, or persisted state).
- **Highest-risk area:** a wake that *should* stay minimal getting the full prompt.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Every turn-scoped narrowing source listed above keeps the prompt minimal (asserted case-by-case in `src/agents/session-event-producer-surface.test.ts`), the fact is dropped by any plain copy of the list — so an unmodelled path degrades to today's behaviour, never to wider access — and the prompt gates are the only consumers; `applyEmbeddedAttemptToolsAllow`, construction planning and native deny policy still read the list itself.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** for an agent on a caching provider with default tool config, the exec-completion wake turn now renders the same system prompt sections as the preceding user turn (Execution Bias present, "Conversation Context" heading, skills catalog retained), so the cache prefix is read; a wake whose producer was genuinely capped (runtime allowlist, subagent, collector, non-owner sender, sandbox, inherited policy) still renders the minimal prompt; the wake's callable tool surface is unchanged in both cases.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/agents/session-event-producer-surface.ts` (the narrowing decision), the two prompt-mode gates (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt-prepare.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prepared-compaction-runtime.ts`), and the propagation points (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-target.ts` `intersectSessionEventToolsAllow`, `attempt-tool-construction-plan.ts` `mergeForcedEmbeddedAttemptToolsAllow`, `reply-tool-authority-snapshot.ts`, `tools/gateway-caller-context.ts`). Regression fixtures: `markProducerSurfaceToolCap` matrix, `keeps the producer-surface fact of its tool cap through capture` (real `prepareExecExitNotification` capture path), `keeps the conversation prompt when a cap only records the producer's own surface`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** worktree `aispace/worktrees/issue-191128` at `origin/main` 47ce1aaa4c1 + this patch, Node v26.12.1, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <files>` (vitest unit-fast + infra shards).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.config/nvm/versions/node/v26.12.1/bin:$PATH"
  pnpm install --prefer-offline
  # RED: prompt-mode gate reverted to origin/main, regression test kept
  git checkout origin/main -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt-prepare.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.test.ts
  # GREEN: gate restored
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/agents/session-event-producer-surface.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.requester.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
      src/agents/session-event-producer-surface.test.ts \
      src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.requester.test.ts \
      src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.test.ts
  ✓ |unit-fast| session-event-producer-surface.test.ts > markProducerSurfaceToolCap > records an unrestricted run's own surface as a ceiling, not a narrowing
  ✓ |unit-fast| session-event-producer-surface.test.ts > markProducerSurfaceToolCap > keeps the minimal prompt for a runtime allowlist
        … 10 more narrowing cases (plugin grant, collector, delegated, sender, group, sandbox,
          subagent, inherited, withheld tool, empty surface) all ✓
  ✓ |unit-fast| session-event-producer-surface.test.ts > markProducerSurfaceToolCap > carries the fact into the next generation of wakes
  ✓ |unit-fast| bash-tools.exec-notify.requester.test.ts > keeps the producer-surface fact of its tool cap through capture: true
  ✓ |unit-fast| bash-tools.exec-notify.requester.test.ts > keeps the producer-surface fact of its tool cap through capture: false
  ✓ |infra| attempt-system-prompt.test.ts > buildAttemptSystemPrompt > keeps the conversation prompt when a cap only records the producer's own surface
   Test Files  3 passed (3)
        Tests  53 passed (53)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** the same fixture pair now separates on provenance alone: an unmarked finite cap (`["read"]`) still renders the minimal prompt (no `## Execution Bias`), while the identical list marked as the producer's own surface renders the conversation prompt (`## Execution Bias` + its rules) and still advertises only `read, write, exec`. Through the real exec-completion capture path (`prepareExecExitNotification` → `captureSessionEventTargetForHost`), `target.toolsAllow` keeps the exact ceiling `["read","exec","message"]` in both cases and only the provenance fact differs.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** the same regression test against the unpatched prompt-mode gate renders the minimal prompt for a producer-surface cap:
  ```text
  $ git checkout origin/main -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt-prepare.ts
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.test.ts
  × |infra| attempt-system-prompt.test.ts > buildAttemptSystemPrompt > keeps the conversation prompt
      when a cap only records the producer's own surface
    → expected '<!-- openclaw:attempt:STABLE -->\nYou…' to contain '## Execution Bias'
   ❯ src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.test.ts:528:5
   Test Files  1 failed (1)
        Tests  1 failed | 34 passed (35)
  ```
- **What was not tested:** no live Anthropic request was issued, so the cache `read`/`write` token counts from the reporter's capture were not re-measured; the assertion is at the system-prompt bytes that determine the cache prefix. Not exercised: a gateway restart handoff of a pending exec notification (the provenance fact is deliberately not persisted, so a restored wake falls back to today's minimal prompt), and cron-driven wakes whose job cap intersects the producer ceiling (an explicit cap anywhere clears the fact). Local type checking could not run on this host: `pnpm tsgo:core` resolves to the `tsrs` native binary, which needs GLIBC ≥ 2.32 while this machine has 2.31, and `@typescript/native-preview` is not installed, so `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo` has no binary either — the type-check lane is left to CI. Format (`oxfmt --check`), lint (`oxlint`) and the mapped vitest files are green locally. CI lanes pending.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none for the prompt-mode decision; the provider-side cache accounting itself is inferred from the prompt bytes rather than observed against a live Anthropic account.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review

prs.title: fix(logbook): prune files outside PostgreSQL transactions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Logbook wraps every PostgreSQL write operation in a transaction. Pruning also has its own metadata transaction, so file removal and directory cleanup currently run inside the outer transaction while holding the PostgreSQL writer lock.

## User Impact

Pruning now removes files outside the PostgreSQL transaction. The short metadata transaction retains the existing deletion cutoff, selected frame IDs, 64-row batches, affected-row counts, foreign-key behavior, and retry model. SQLite keeps its existing transaction path. No DDL, schema version, persisted format, retention, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep prune classified as a host write, but let it own its SQL transaction. Obtain admission before the first unlink, renew admission before BEGIN, and obtain commit authority inside the metadata transaction. Reuse the existing admission wrapper for other PostgreSQL writes.

## Evidence

- Real PostgreSQL: all 12 tests passed at `e6321a3c7e72c6e3723f419090b40348e56bcdec`, including 0/129 expired frames, transaction-free filesystem work, admission refusal, partial-unlink retry, affected-row counts, and reopen behavior.
- SQLite siblings: 11 tests across `store-prune.test.ts` and `store-frame-io.test.ts` passed at the previous test-only head; production bytes are unchanged. Production typecheck passed there. Extension-test typecheck, targeted formatting, and lint passed at the final head (zero lint warnings/errors).
- Validation: Blacksmith Testbox [run 41687177576](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41687177576), Node 24.22.1, source tree `a1b94fc1eaafa64e102f36b188c0782cf83f7b9d`. This direct-backend fixture mocks host admission; it does not establish broker or simultaneous-worker behavior.
- Fresh final-head P0–P2 independent review: no actionable findings. Validation caught and corrected test-only boolean inference and broad-union assertions without changing production behavior.
- Production: +31/-14 lines. Tests: +233/-6 lines. The production addition creates one admission owner around the short transaction and removes the outer prune transaction.
- No performance claim.
