prs.title: fix(ui): require explicit toast severity
prs.body:
## Problem
Failure producers frequently omitted toast severity. A denied clipboard operation reached the real toast renderer without its error class and looked like a successful copy.

## Solution
- Require `ToastOptions.severity`: explicit `success`, `error`, or `undefined` for neutral/unadorned notices.
- Classify all 156 production producers, including eight conditional clipboard outcomes, and update synthetic callers and consumer expectations in the same cutover.
- Keep the existing renderer, tokens, layout, stacking, actions, and message copy unchanged. Pending publication, intentional discard, operator-stopped work, and bounded partial imports are not mislabeled as completed successes or failures.

## Impact
Preferences, chat/dashboard actions, session management, clipboard feedback, browser/portal actions, templates, uploads/downloads, and background-session notices share the enforced contract. Future callers cannot silently omit an outcome.

Related open PRs: #192013, #192014, #192015. This is based on main, not their branches. It overlaps #192013 at the options contract and #192015 in producer files. Explicit `undefined` preserves #192013’s no-icon convention; no new neutral variant is introduced. The component/stack redesign and alert-role changes remain with #192013/#192014. #192015’s copy changes are deliberately not duplicated.

## Evidence
- Baseline clipboard E2E fails at the renderer boundary: expected the error class after the actual session-menu copy action, received false. Only external clipboard I/O is denied; the production menu, toast owner, and renderer remain mounted.
- Final-head E2E passes for success/error at 1440×900 and 390×844, in Claw light, Claw dark, and CRT dark. Fresh captures rebuilt all six comparisons byte-for-byte identically to the originals. All six were personally inspected for clipping, alignment, spacing, and theme consistency.
- 87 affected consumer test files / 1,579 tests pass. This includes all 12 toast browser tests, rich feedback at 1280/390/320px, oversized errors, and native-modal/anchored/bottom placement. The changed-file selection also passes: 26 files / 604 tests (overlapping coverage).
- UI typecheck, 121-file formatting, focused lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Lint retains eight warnings on unchanged Solid/reactivity statements, with no errors. A resource-stalled first test attempt was rerun in full and passed.
- AST check: every production call specifies severity. Normalizing away severity leaves identical ASTs in all 92 migrated production consumers; the remaining production change is the owner’s required type field.

prs.title: fix(exec): dollar amounts in agent messages are corrupted when exec text uses $<digit> in double quotes
prs.body:
Closes #179890

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dollar amounts in agent-sent messages are silently corrupted ("$900" becomes "00") when an `exec` command passes the text in double quotes.

## User Impact

User impact: exec commands that would deliver a corrupted dollar amount are refused before they run. The refusal shows the text as written next to what the shell would deliver, and how to fix it (single quotes, `\$`, or a quoted heredoc), so the agent retries correctly instead of sending the wrong amount to a customer. It can be disabled with `OPENCLAW_EXEC_DOLLAR_GUARD=off`.

**Open question for maintainers:** this is default-on and uses an environment switch. If you'd prefer it opt-in, or shipped as a plugin on the existing `before_tool_call` hook instead of in core, I'm happy to rework it that way. Tell me which shape you want.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBeforeToolCallHook` checks `exec` command text for a `$<digit>` that the shell would expand, before any plugin or approval policy runs. Codex-native shell commands reach the same policy through the PreToolUse native hook relay. Relay planning now counts the guard as a before-tool-call policy and keeps `exec` in the PreToolUse matcher, so native commands are covered even with no other policy installed.

The scanner is deliberately conservative. It only flags an expansion it can show would be empty:
- It honours single quotes, `\$`, `$'...'`, quoted heredoc delimiters, `${...}`, `$((...))` and comments.
- It recurses into `$(...)`, including substitutions inside unquoted heredoc bodies, with their own quoting.
- It ignores `$0` (the shell or script name) unless it reads as money (`$0.50`).
- It stays out of commands that define functions or set positional parameters (`set --`, `shift`, `getopts`), where `$1.00` may be intended.
- It fails open on anything it cannot parse.

Code-mode `exec` (JavaScript) is excluded.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/shell-dollar-expansion-guard.test.ts` (35 tests): the hazard shapes, every safe quoting form, `$0`, populated positional parameters, heredoc command substitution, `bash -lc` unwrapping, fail-open, and the `runBeforeToolCallHook` veto, allow and disable cases. The `$0`, positional-parameter and heredoc-substitution cases fail on the previous revision and pass now.
- `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.dollar-guard.test.ts` (6 tests): Codex `Bash` and `exec_command` are denied and single-quoted amounts pass. Relay planning enables PreToolUse for `exec` with no other policy and keeps it in a relay scoped to other tools; these planning cases fail without the relay change.
- The existing `agent-tools.before-tool-call*` and `native-hook-relay*` unit suites pass. `native-hook-relay.participants` and `native-hook-relay.remote-http` fail identically on `main` without this change in my environment.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Replayed against 391 unique `$`-bearing exec commands from a production deployment: 18 were flagged, all genuine expansion bugs, with no false positives.
- Still to add: a gateway trace of a real agent refusing and retrying. I'll attach it before asking for re-review.

prs.title: fix(agents): a quota-class failure should prefer the model chain over a same-profile auth rotation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a quota-class provider failure (HTTP 429 with a usage/plan-limit body), the embedded agent rotates the auth profile and re-runs the **same** model before the configured model-fallback chain is consulted. When the provider has exactly one usable profile - or when the rotation re-selects the profile that just failed - that rotation is a no-op: it spends a provider attempt against the same exhausted plan and delays the chain that could have recovered the run.

The `rate_limit` path already has a rotation cap that escalates to the model chain (`MAX_RATE_LIMIT_PROFILE_ROTATIONS`), and the `overloaded` path escalates through `overloadProfileRotationLimit`. What is missing is the rule that **a rotation which lands on the same profile is not a rotation at all**.

## User Impact

A quota-class failure now advances the model chain in the same failure instead of burning an attempt on the exhausted profile first. A run that has a working fallback chain configured recovers on the first quota error rather than the second.

## Why This Change Was Made

`advanceAuthProfileCandidate` advances by **index** over the prepared auth attempts. When two prepared attempts carry the same profile id (an OAuth attempt and an inline attempt for the same profile, or two routes for one profile), the "rotation" re-selects the profile that just failed and still reports success. The caller then retries the same model against the same exhausted plan.

The fix keeps profile rotation useful whenever it can actually change the credentials:

- The rotation is reported as a rotation only when the active profile changes.
- When the rotation re-selects the failed profile and a model chain is configured, the controller reports "no rotation", so the failover policy resolves to `fallback_model` and the chain advances immediately.
- Without a configured chain the existing same-profile retry is preserved, so a single-model deployment loses nothing.

Scope notes:

- The `overloaded` path is untouched.
- The session/request model-pin contract (#151980) is untouched; this change is about auth profiles, not model pins.
- The failed profile is still marked in cooldown exactly as before; only the decision to *retry* the same profile changes.

Related: #141115 (a 429 must consult the chain - this PR is the ordering half of that class), #151980 (session model pins stay strict; this change touches auth profiles, not model pins), #186418 (the request-level ladder half, carried by #186420).

## Evidence

Focused test run on this branch (rebased onto main at `fdeb8f7e`):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-embedded-agent-run.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts
    -> Test Files  1 passed (1), Tests  42 passed (42)

New coverage in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts`:

- a quota-class rotation that re-selects the failed profile reports no rotation, so the caller advances the model chain;
- a quota-class rotation that moves to a different profile still reports a rotation and still counts toward the rotation cap;
- without a configured model chain the same-profile rotation still retries, so single-model deployments keep their existing recovery.

One existing fixture was updated: "waits for the provider floor before exhausting recovery and rotating credentials" used an `advanceAttemptAuthProfile` stub that returned `true` without moving the active profile. A successful rotation moves the active profile, so the stub now does the same; the assertions are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ui): explain missing operator scopes in access errors
prs.body:
## Summary

F3: preserve the Gateway’s existing missing-scope reason in Control UI permission copy, with plain-language next steps rather than raw scope identifiers.

- Read `MISSING_SCOPE` / `missingScope` through the existing Gateway client parser. Authorization, required scopes, grants, retry behavior, and technical error details are unchanged.
- One UI copy formatter covers generic missing-scope failures and existing feature-specific read-access messages (logs, usage, agents, model providers, scheduled tasks, context breakdown, and session history).
- Following Vyctor’s approved wording, display `operator.read` as “read access.” After inspecting `src/gateway/operator-scopes.ts` and `src/gateway/method-scopes.ts`, display `operator.write` as “write access” and `operator.admin` as “admin access.” Other scopes use “the required access,” never a guessed read-access label. Technical scopes remain in the original Gateway error details.
- Preserve “session history,” the distinction between sessions and conversation content, “admin,” curly apostrophes, and “Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}.” Explicit `UserFacingError` messages and unrelated errors retain their handling.

## Before → after

- `permission denied` / `missing scope: {scope}` → `Couldn’t complete this request. Ask an admin to grant {access}.`
- `Couldn’t view {thing}. Ask an admin to grant operator.read.` → `Couldn’t view {thing}. Ask an admin to grant read access.`
- Generic requests: `operator.write` → “write access”; `operator.admin` → “admin access”; any other scope → “the required access.”
- The initial F3 change also replaced `existing chat history` with `session history`.

## Review and validation

- Fresh independent read-only review of the plain-language revision: **no actionable findings**. The reviewer inspected the scope owners, full changed formatter, and corresponding test diffs; no validation commands were run. Review run: `e66a07b4-c233-4fb2-aa2d-451af26ce776`.
- Normal pre-commit hook passed for copy revision `973dcb092dbfc25510def283507b63afe3f84701`; the exact Vyctor co-author trailer is present.
- Quoted assertions are updated. The existing table now describes read, write, admin, and unknown-scope wording.
- Historical evidence from the initial implementation only: six targeted files / 133 tests, two focused missing-scope cases, and i18n verification passed before this plain-language revision. These are not proof for the final wording revision.

## Gaps and follow-up

- **This revision intentionally has no test, E2E, browser, screenshot, CI, build, standalone typecheck/lint, or new i18n runs beyond the normal hook.** Updated assertions were inspected, not executed. Landing-phase validation is deferred to the parent’s landing lanes.
- Guest/role restrictions, admin-only settings without a missing-scope reason, approval-required policy, and disconnected-device failures remain follow-up work at their owning structured-error contracts. A generic `FORBIDDEN` is not guessed to mean one of these cases.
- Unmapped scopes retain accurate generic guidance rather than an invented permission label.
- No new “Show details” presentation; F1 owns that surface. Original error objects and technical details remain available to existing callers.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(browser): tab list fails when Chrome refuses to attach to a tab
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Chrome extension relay fails the whole tab list (`Target.getTargets` → "Target identities are unavailable") in **All tabs** access mode when Chrome permanently refuses to attach its debugger to an ordinary tab.

## User Impact

User impact: users with many open tabs in All tabs mode keep getting a tab list; tabs Chrome will not debug are skipped with a warning (as already happens for the Chrome Web Store and `chrome://` pages) instead of making every tab query fail.

## Why This Change Was Made

`enumerateTargetInfos` only treats three exact Chrome messages as permanent refusals (`The extensions gallery cannot be scripted.`, `Cannot access a chrome:// URL`, `Cannot access a chrome-extension:// URL of different extension`). For some regular tabs Chrome returns `Cannot attach to this target.` on every attempt. Those tabs were not skipped, never got an identity, and the later identity check failed the whole request. `docs/tools/chrome-extension.md` already says pages Chrome permanently refuses to debug are excluded while transient failures still fail the request; this adds the missing permanent refusal and extends the doc sentence accordingly. The match stays an exact message comparison, so other attach failures (conflicts, permissions, timeouts, retired generations) still fail the request.

Repro conditions: >100 open tabs, access mode All tabs, Chrome reports `Cannot attach to this target.` for a few tabs (relay log: `setAutoAttach attach failed: Error: Cannot attach to this target.`).

## Evidence

- New test in `relay-bridge.test.ts`: a tab whose attach fails with `Cannot attach to this target.` is skipped and the other tabs are returned. Red on base (`Target identities are unavailable`), green with the fix.
- `vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay`: 19 files / 241 tests passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on touched files clean; `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass.
- Observed on a real setup (OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.5, Windows, Chrome, >100 tabs, All tabs): 2/2 tab queries failed before; with the equivalent one-line skip, 2/2 succeeded.

## Verification & Proof (real browser, not mocked)

The fix lives in the Node-side relay bridge (`extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay/relay-bridge.ts`); the Chrome extension side is unchanged by this PR and already forwards Chrome's raw `chrome.debugger.attach` error text. The change was verified end-to-end against a **real Chromium browser** running the **real unpacked OpenClaw extension**, with the changed bridge built/bundled from the fixed source.

Build (all exit 0):

- `corepack pnpm tsgo:extensions` — typecheck of the changed source.
- `corepack pnpm build:runtime` — full bundle; the fix appears in `dist/relay-server-*.mjs` next to the existing refusal strings.
- `node extensions/browser/scripts/copy-chrome-extension.mjs` — unpacks the real MV3 extension to `dist/extensions/browser/chrome-extension/`.

Browser under test: **Chromium 156.0.8078.47** (Debian), launched headless with the unpacked extension via `--load-extension`. The same `debugger_api.cc` constant (`kRestrictedError = "Cannot attach to this target."`) governs Google Chrome, Chrome for Testing, and Chromium, and the exact string was confirmed present in the shipped binary.

How the real refusal tab was produced: a **security interstitial** tab. A tab navigated to a host serving a self-signed certificate (`https://self-signed.badssl.com/`) displays Chrome's SSL interstitial, and real `chrome.debugger.attach` on that tab returns exactly `Cannot attach to this target.` (the deterministic trigger for `kRestrictedError`, distinct from `Cannot access a chrome:// URL`, which `chrome://` tabs return). A healthy `https://example.com/` tab attaches normally.

Real terminal transcript (exit code 0; port, extension id and tab id redacted):

```
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs run-real-proof.mts
[real-proof] starting real extension relay server on 127.0.0.1:<port>
[real-proof] relay server up; bridge extensionConnected=false
[real-proof] extension id: <extension-id>
[real-proof] opening healthy tab
[real-proof] opening security-interstitial (self-signed cert) tab
[real-proof]   interstitial navigation (expected): page.goto: net::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID at https://self-s...
[real-proof] pairing extension with relay server (access mode: all)
[real-proof] pair result: {"ok":true}
[browser/extension-relay] extension authenticated and connected to relay
[real-proof] extension connected to bridge; waiting for tab snapshot
[browser/extension-relay] Skipping tab <tab-id> during target enumeration: Cannot attach to this target.
[real-proof] Target.getTargets returned 1 target(s): ["https://example.com/"]
[real-proof] REAL PROOF PASS: refused tab skipped, healthy tab returned
```

This shows the exact production code path under review: the real extension's `chrome.debugger.attach` fails with `Cannot attach to this target.` on the interstitial tab, the changed bridge skips that tab with the same warning as the existing permanent refusals, and the healthy tab is still returned in `Target.getTargets`. No mocked socket, scripted extension, or synthetic error was used.


## Additional built Gateway verification

[Built Gateway / browser-tabs CLI evidence, native Chrome refusal logs and inspected precondition screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191578#issuecomment-6620035095).

Chromium 156.0.8078.79 on Node 24.22.1, with the real bundled unpacked extension installed and automatically paired through the native host. A task-local self-signed TLS security interstitial naturally produces Chrome's exact refusal. Two main inventories fail; two candidate inventories return exactly the two healthy tabs, byte-identical to the candidate's normal inventory. Normal repeats and recovery are unchanged on both refs. A separate real Chrome host-policy restriction still fails inventory on both refs; removing it restores all targets. No mocked error or standalone bridge substitutes for this Gateway/CLI proof.

The existing refusal/recovery table now covers all four exact permanent refusals and a near-match that must still fail. Focused candidate file: 43 passed; identical cases on main: 1 intended failure / 42 passed. Formatting/lint and both runtime builds passed. Tests are net 0 (+11/−11); the 12-line allocation is removed. Production +3/−1; documentation +3/−2. Contributor commits are preserved.

Validation status: [Two unrelated profile-retirement assertions still fail at this head and with all production changes reverted](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191578#issuecomment-6620282485). Both resolve `false` where the existing tests expect rejection; other selected gates passed.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: revert fully restores the old classifier; no persisted state, schema, config, permission, dependency or SDK changes. Blast radius is Chrome extension-relay inventory when Chrome emits this exact refusal. Other errors continue failing the complete request, and omitted targets are retried on the next enumeration rather than cached as unavailable.

Fixes #192426

## What Problem This Solves

A valid GIF returned by view_image can make xAI reject the image turn and every later text-only turn that replays it.

## User Impact

xAI Responses requests can use retained inline GIF images without requiring users to delete their sessions. Animation is flattened to the first frame as JPEG (quality 85, maximum side 1200); if conversion fails, the model receives visible fallback text asking for PNG or JPEG. No configuration change or history migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize image bytes in the xAI-only request projection after asynchronous payload hooks settle. This covers native tool-output arrays and Grok OAuth image carriers while preserving stored history, frozen input objects, global GIF support, and other providers' behavior. The existing image processor performs the conversion; no dependency, lockfile, or test-budget settings change is included.

The final fixture adds animation, a preceding assistant tool call, synthetic disk reload, and additional controls.

The final new regression file separately passed **8 tests**, covering fresh images, synthetic disk reload before a later text-only turn, fully decoded/re-encoded JPEG output, failure text, unchanged request prefixes/history, supported formats, non-xAI behavior, and async replacement with frozen input.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI slash-command feedback uses inconsistent terms such as “active run,” title-case headings, and failure messages that lead with a diagnostic instead of a recovery action.

## User Impact

Commands use “reply,” “effort,” sentence-case headings, and actionable failure summaries. Diagnostics remain available in a separate paragraph. Slash tokens, command behavior, permissions, and redaction are unchanged.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Inject a message into the active run | Guide the agent’s current reply |
| Clear chat history | Clear this conversation |
| Available Commands | Available commands |
| Failed to get model info: … | Couldn’t load model details. Try again. + diagnostic paragraph |
| Prompt budget (last run) | Prompt budget (last reply) |
| Session capability is unavailable | Couldn’t access this session. Open another session and try again. |

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies the approved Control UI glossary to the slash-command catalogs and moves the executor’s connection-change text into the English catalog. Updates quoted command feedback in the Chat documentation and all affected assertions. Retains the existing result contract rather than introducing another error-rendering owner.

## Follow-up: effort glossary correction

Vyctor’s copy audit found five error strings still using “thinking level.” All eight strings in that command-result group now use “effort,” including the current value, reset confirmation, and set confirmation. The failure-matrix regression rejects the retired terms, and real-Gateway assertions quote the updated copy. The complete PR copy diff was re-read against the approved glossary; no additional glossary changes were needed. Internal translation keys and slash tokens remain unchanged.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Current thinking level: {level}. | Current effort: {level}. |
| Couldn’t load the thinking level. Try again. | Couldn’t load effort. Try again. |
| Thinking level reset to default. | Effort reset to default. |
| Couldn’t reset the thinking level. Try again. | Couldn’t reset effort. Try again. |
| Couldn’t change the thinking level to “{level}”. Choose {options}. | Couldn’t change effort to “{level}”. Choose {options}. |
| Couldn’t use thinking level “{level}” with this model. Choose {options}. | Couldn’t use effort “{level}” with this model. Choose {options}. |
| Thinking level set to {level}. | Effort set to {level}. |
| Couldn’t change the thinking level. Try again. | Couldn’t change effort. Try again. |

Existing diagnostic placeholders are unchanged. The final follow-up passed `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` with a three-minute timeout and the normal pre-commit hook.

### Follow-up Gaps

Per Vyctor’s revised instructions, no further browser, e2e, screenshot, full-test, or CI runs were started after the correction to the test plan. The final real-Gateway assertion updates were not rerun. An earlier follow-up e2e attempt exposed two stale “Current thinking level” assertions; both are corrected, but this is not a passing final-head e2e claim. Earlier unit and visual results below are historical evidence, not a substitute for landing-time validation. No CI watching or landing was performed.

## Evidence from the earlier PR revision

- 68 unit tests passed across the executor, failure matrix, command metadata, and root-copy loading.
- 5 browser/real-Gateway tests passed across inference setup and thinking metadata.
- Mocked Control UI visual harness: 2 before/after scenarios passed; synthetic data, light theme, same-frame crops. Screenshots below were inspected locally and again from their public attachment URLs.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` completed with no baseline diff; `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed.
- Touched-file oxfmt and oxlint, UI TypeScript check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local chat boot budget vs source base `1248bee4959bf403d1823fc0748d291354cee074`: JS gzip 1,280,959 → 1,280,944 bytes (−15); 20 → 20 requests. CSS gzip 130,910 → 130,910 bytes; 3 → 3 requests.
- Fresh independent review found two stale text assertions; both are fixed. Author simplification pass retained the existing executor/result/redaction owners.

### CI blocker from the earlier PR revision

The PR is **not ready to land**. [Control UI performance failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41679325228/job/126069775916) on the CI merge against base `2cf02a5d104a4dfccd62dc90ebd33e8f417b972c`: chat boot JS gzip 1,280,794 → 1,281,067 bytes (+273). That base already exceeds the cap; the allowed build variance is 64 bytes. The aggregate CI gate therefore fails.

Reproducing locally on that exact newer base also failed (+308 bytes). Shorter menu descriptions did not resolve it (+538 bytes); that experiment and the investigative rebase were reverted, leaving the reviewed source unchanged. No budget, baseline, or permission exception was added. Resolving this merge-base-sensitive boot-size regression remains required.

### Visual proof

| Surface | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Steer menu | ![Before: steer menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b7abab5-eb58-4b56-978a-bbc80d06e6a6) | ![After: steer menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d45add96-9545-4877-a024-48cb7bfe90c1) |

### Gaps and retained behavior

The shared F1 collapsed “Show details” contract is not on this base. Raw `{error}`/`{reason}` diagnostics remain in the existing result content, separated from the summary by a paragraph: compaction failed/skipped; model get/set; effort get/reset/set; verbose get/set; fast get/reset/set; usage; agents; steer and redirect requests. No new error component or competing result contract is added.

Visual failure proof invokes the real executor with a synthetic failing capability and delivers its result through the mocked transcript renderer; it is not a live provider failure. Compatible short labels and slash tokens are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(macos): keep attach-only save failures visible
prs.body:
Closes #190153

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the macOS Debug "Attach only" toggle silently failing when it cannot save the setting.

## User Impact

The toggle reports a failed save and returns to its saved value. A permission problem can be corrected and retried without the rollback erasing the error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The marker write now throws on failure. A user-action binding owns persistence, so updating the displayed value after a failed save cannot trigger another write that clears the error. There are no new settings or storage formats.

## Evidence

- On unchanged main `c8f87b2e516`, a non-root disposable macOS 27.0 guest exercised the real marker setter against a task-owned read-only directory. The new creation regression failed because the setter returned nil even though the marker did not exist. The complete owner suite finished with 24 tests and this one expected failure, 0.062 seconds.
- With the repair, all 111 tests in GatewayLaunchAgentManagerTests, GatewayProcessManagerTests, and GatewayAutostartPolicyTests pass in the guest, 17.267 seconds. The new table covers both write directions, unchanged saved state after failure, successful retry, and idempotency.
- The native app and test bundle compile with `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests --disable-automatic-resolution`, 101.86 seconds.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1, SwiftLint 0.65.1, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent source review found no actionable P1/P2 findings.

The full macOS formatting check passes. The full lint script reports two inherited file-length violations in unchanged DashboardManager.swift and GatewayConnection.swift; both files are byte-identical to the base. The local sandbox also prevented SwiftLint cache writes. Lint of every changed file passes without a cache.

Actual-app before/after proof was captured in the disposable guest on November 2. With the task-owned state directory at mode 0500, the baseline app's failed removal returned the toggle to on and erased the error. The fixed app kept the saved on state and displayed the permission error. Restoring mode 0700 and retrying turned the control off, removed the marker, and cleared the error. Failed creation likewise kept the control off and showed an error; a writable retry recreated the marker. The test directory is back at mode 0700. This was a new offline profile with no running Gateway, operator credentials, or live account data.

![Before: failed-removal rollback silently clears the save error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e1dabea-74b4-4fbd-ac50-8d2a48392281)

![After: failed removal retains the saved state and permission error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e917158-e598-4700-bfd2-df8d0d93211a)

![After: failed creation reports the save error and stays off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70a7209b-cdb0-4005-a941-2a93b63bc54f)

![After: restoring write access lets the retry succeed and clears the error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d38548c9-6e09-4350-9228-ed8fedbf563a)

The production change removes one net line; the regression adds 23 Swift test lines. Release-note context: macOS attach-only preference save failures remain visible and can be retried.

AI-assisted. Thanks to @anmol0b for reporting both failure paths.

prs.title: fix: hide operator Home from guests and start new sessions by default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restricted guests could see the rolling operator Home conversation even when its composer denied participation. Implicit startup also opened Home instead of New Session.

## User Impact

Operator Home rows and transcript reads are withheld from session-only restricted guests. General-read and full-session operators retain explicit Home access. Implicit startup uses New Session while valid explicit links, unsent drafts and non-Home/native restoration remain supported. No new configuration option or permission grant is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session-sharing policy owns Home admission. Discovery, exact readers, HTTP/media, mentions and remote-ingress adapters forward current main-key/scope facts; sharing-cache identity includes the main key. Full-read mention requesters and connect-less internal callers remain supported without exempting restricted session-only grants.

The UI checks Home authority before cached transcript hydration, including literal aliases. Bootstrap owns native restoration before routing. Not-found recovery preserves non-Home conversations while excluding cached Home using canonical identity bound to the navigation-selected owner, including ownerless global keys.

The latest update completes individually audited conversation-fixture entry/navigation cutover through the existing URL helper while preserving intentional New/default, query/hash/history and denial controls. CSP interception and navigation use the same exact session URL. API, service-worker and phone setup repairs preserve their security/recovery assertions.

Denied Home and New Session reuse the existing Welcome status renderer and app-owned handle, preserving pending/failure/retry presentation without a second owner, polling, redirects, permission or locale changes. This minimal integration changes three production files, +14 net LF. Identical menu-locator reuse removes the affected fixture's max-lines violation without an exception.

## Evidence

Latest published head: `88d20b5fb91ba0840495ddda6a1e7104199a73b6`. The direct-5f49 update is 215 paths, 264,481 bytes, SHA-256 `7179c96bdcc202399b2d2794e9b031aa77360700d2a530450ef942479b04dd50`. The lead personally read the entire patch and three production modules; all 215 published blobs, parent and Vincent credit were independently verified. Allocation: **811 net test LF = 481 previously published +330**; no shared baseline increase. Four original and fresh incremental independent narrative reviews cover the final files, including CSP, renderer lifecycle and locator repairs; these are not isolated CLI attestations.

prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

- Production Control UI build completed successfully in **18.94 seconds**.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation MDX/link checks, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety guards, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review identified missing route-loader result narrowing in the migrated test fixture. Explicit route and result guards address it; the final focused rerun and fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed without remaining actionable findings.

**Outstanding verification:** Physical iPhone QA and inspected before/after screenshots remain unavailable. The DOM tests provide synthetic bridge-contract evidence and do not establish native-device or visual behavior. Production UI typechecking, a reduced focused typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. prs.title: fix(agents): move active node presence to current-turn context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #192364. `active_node` and `active_node_identity` are on the Runtime line, and `openai-completions` routes relocate that line into the first user message. When a Mac app quits or comes back, the value changes, message 1 is rewritten, and everything after the system prompt falls out of an exact-prefix cache. The report measured 67-85 s replies instead of about 1 s on a ~90k-token session.

## User Impact

A node going away or returning no longer rewrites earlier messages, so the conversation stays cached. The model still sees the current active computer every turn, now in the newest message's runtime context.

Two visible changes:

- CLI backends now always get the fact in the turn context. It used to be skipped when the system prompt was sent, because the Runtime line carried it.
- **Known gap:** `settled-tool-finalization` and raw model runs carry no runtime facts by design, so those runs no longer see `active_node`. They previously saw it through the system prompt. The report also flags this. I kept their exact-prompt rule rather than adding text; a maintainer may want to weigh in if finalization needs it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direction comes from @dertbv's diagnosis and local test in the issue. The CLI and harness paths already deliver this as a per-turn fact, so this moves the embedded path onto the same model:

- Removes the two fields from `buildRuntimeLine`, the runtime info types, `buildSystemPromptParams` and the prompt-cache field labels.
- `prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptContext` runs `prepareActiveNodeContext` for the admitted run's operator profile and then adds `buildActiveNodeContextText` as a `conversation-data` fragment. The hint is read synchronously, so the keyed refresh has to come first or a revoked pairing could still show the retired node.
- `buildCliTurnAppendContext` appends it unconditionally, before media progress, which stays last.

## Evidence

![Prefix A/B](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/192364/proof-192364.png)

Real Gateway on Windows with real agent turns in one session. A stub `openai-completions` provider diffs each request's messages against the previous request. Presence is on for requests 1-2, gone for 3-4, and back for 5.

| Request | Presence | Before: earlier messages | After: earlier messages |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | `mac-node-1` | identical | identical |
| 3 | gone | **`msg[1]` rewritten** | identical |
| 4 | gone | identical | identical |
| 5 | back | **`msg[1]` rewritten** | identical |

Before, the value lives in `msg[1]` and changes there. After, each turn's value is in that turn's own message (`msg[2]`, `msg[5]`, `msg[8]`, ...) and later requests leave those bytes alone. In the before run, the rewritten requests kept 54162 of 56011 and 54162 of 57600 characters as an unchanged prefix; the small size is the stub session's, not a real session's.

**CLI backend.** I registered a stub executable with `api.registerCliBackend` (`systemPromptArg`, `systemPromptWhen: "first"`, `resumeArgs`), so the real CLI runner builds the arguments. The stub logs what it received:

| Turn | Before: value in system prompt / prompt | After: value in system prompt / prompt |
|---|---|---|
| First (new session) | `mac-node-1` / none | none / `mac-node-1` |
| Resumed, node gone | not passed / `unknown` | not passed / `unknown` |
| Resumed, node back | not passed / `mac-node-1` | not passed / `mac-node-1` |

Tests, with regressions in `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` that fail without the embedded fact and without the refresh before reading it:

| File | Result |
|---|---|
| `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` | 21 passed |
| `system-prompt-params.test.ts` | 23 passed |
| `runtime-facts-prompt.test.ts` | 10 passed |
| `runtime-prompt.test.ts` | 8 passed |
| `gateway/node-registry-pairing.test.ts` | 12 passed |
| `tool-result-truncation.test.ts` | 1 failed, 55 passed: a Windows path error (ENOENT on a drive-letter path joined under the temp dir) in a spill-pointer test this PR does not touch; I did not rerun it on base |
| `attempt-prompt-build.*`, `attempt-prompt-submit`, `attempt-context-advancement`, phase and media-hint tests | passed |
| `cli-runner/prepare.durable-context.test.ts` | 13 failed, 7 passed, same as base |
| `cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` | 13 failed, 100 passed, same as base |

Those two CLI files already fail on this Windows machine (for example `/bin/echo` not resolvable and `EBUSY`). I compared failing test names with and without the change and none are new, but this means CLI path coverage is weak locally, so please check them in CI.

Passed locally: oxfmt, oxlint, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (net 0 test lines), `agents-root` and `agents-other` test types (the project CI failed on before).

**Limits**

- Presence was changed with a preload calling `setActiveNodeContexts`, because this box has no paired Mac. The node connect and disconnect path was not exercised; the report did exercise it on a similar patch.
- The stub compares bytes. I did not measure real cache hits or latency on a caching server; the report's numbers are from its own patched build.
- The CLI proof uses a stub executable through the real runner, not Claude Code or another real CLI.
- Requester-scoped refresh is covered by unit tests and the default-profile live path; I did not run a non-owner profile with a revoked pairing end to end.

prs.title: fix(codex): stop background exec completions from replaying full history into a fresh thread
prs.body:
Related: #183286, #179363, #172026, #178982

## What Problem This Solves

When a background `exec` finishes in a Codex-backed WebChat session, the completion wake does not continue the session's bound native thread. It starts a fresh transient thread, replays the full session history into it uncached, and does it again for the follow-up turn. On a long session every completion wake costs a full uncached history read. In one observed session, four completion wakes each sent about 190k uncached input tokens.

This finishes, for event wakes, what #183286 started: tool declarations belong to the session, not to the turn. #183286 kept seven native Codex thread, plugin, and supervision declarations stable across owner and completion turns. A completion wake still differed from the user turn in three other ways, and each one alone forces a new thread:

1. **Tool-policy scope.** The default session-event source policy caps every follow-up at the producer's tool list. A wake with a cap runs as a turn-scoped restricted turn, which the Codex harness serves on a transient thread with native code mode off (48 eager dynamic tools instead of 10).
2. **`skill_workshop` schema.** The personal-library schema is published only on human turns that carry an authoring grant. A wake publishes a narrower schema, the dynamic tool catalog fingerprint changes, and the bound thread rotates. The Claude CLI runner already fixed this in #172026 (`resolveStableCliSkillAuthoring`); the embedded/harness path never used it.
3. **Conversation context.** An internal (WebChat) session stores no delivery route, so `buildSessionEventContext` never matched the wake's own WebChat route and dropped the session chat type. The wake's developer instructions then lacked the "You are in a WebChat direct conversation" line, the live thread config fingerprint changed, and Codex had to cold-resume the thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each layer is fixed where the difference starts, without widening authority:

- **Scope (A).** A cap from a conversation-scoped producer turn is the session's own policy, and the follow-up re-derives that policy itself. `createCodingToolsGatewayCaller` marks the caller identity session-scoped when the policy scope is `conversation` and no caller-supplied source policy exists, and `session-event-target` skips it only when the follow-up's destination is the same session. The mark is not set when group, per-DM, or sender policy narrowed the producer (`groupPolicy`/`senderPolicy`). Those come from the inbound request, the wake cannot rebuild them, and the cap keeps carrying them. The caller-inheritance merge keeps the mark only for an inherited owner of the same agent and session that has no narrower cap of its own. Cross-session follow-ups, sender-narrowed producers, and turn-scoped producers keep the cap exactly as before.
- **Policy lifetime stays host-owned.** No public SDK option is added. The host already computes the attempt's policy lifetime for Codex (`pluginHarnessToolPolicyScope`, `resolvePluginHarnessToolPolicies`). Host policy preparation now records that value in the attempt's host capability, and the host's tool construction (`createToolSurfaceAsync`, which is how Codex builds every dynamic tool) passes it to the internal tool options. A plugin cannot set it through tool options: a plugin-supplied `toolPolicyScope` is overwritten by the host value, and when the host has none the cap stays in place (fail-closed).
- **`skill_workshop` (B).** The #172026 helper moves from `cli-runner/` to `src/agents/stable-skill-authoring.ts` as a per-runtime factory and is also applied at the embedded attempt dispatch. Internal turns publish the session's last human shape with an expired grant: the declaration matches, personal-library calls fail with `AUTHORITY_EXPIRED`, and workspace calls keep the ordinary no-grant rule (unsandboxed runs only). Grants that are already expired (transcript follow-ups, stranded-reply recovery) now carry `expired: true` and no longer replace the remembered human shape.
- **Context (C).** For a session that stores no delivery route, an event on that session's own WebChat route (`channel: "webchat"`, `to: <sessionKey>`, the shape `chat.send` and subagent announce already use) keeps the session chat type. Events routed to any other session still get none.

Out of scope, noted for follow-up: when a thread's config does change (for example a model switch), Codex can take longer than OpenClaw's 2-second unload budget to close a code-mode thread after `thread/unsubscribe` (measured 0.7 s, 2.9 s, and 10.6 s in this harness). The cold resume then fails with "Codex did not confirm unloading its previous configuration". With this change, completion wakes no longer take that path.

AI-assisted: written with Claude Code. Every claim below was checked by running it.

## User Impact

- Background `exec` completion wakes in Codex-backed sessions continue the bound thread with native code mode on. The wake reads the session prefix from cache instead of replaying the full history uncached, and the next user turn stays on the same thread.
- No tool, personal-library, or workspace access is widened. Sessions narrowed by group, per-DM, or sender policy keep today's behavior, including the fresh-thread wake.
- On internal turns with a remembered personal default target, `skill_workshop` calls that rely on that default now return `AUTHORITY_EXPIRED` instead of running against the workspace. Explicit `target=workspace` calls keep the no-grant rule.

## Evidence

### November 1 upkeep (current head)

Rebased onto main `72cab24990b`; `git range-diff` confirms all four existing commits are patch-identical. Added only `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-exec-event-thread.txt` (282 lines): the authority final-effect matrix, host-owned policy scope, expired skill-authoring grant, and wake-context regressions protect distinct contracts. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

- Test-line ratchet passes: 6,366,399 lines / 6,385,147 effective ceiling. `git diff --check` passes.
- Local focused run is **not green**: wake-context 3/3 passed; permission suite 27 passed / 4 failed. The local install has `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.26.13 while current main requires 0.27.0; the installed `advanced` module lacks `overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority`, breaking actual writes (including the same-session regression). Other selected agent suites did not yield valid results in this wrapper run. Total wrapper time: 116.17 seconds. Fresh CI is required; the older passing evidence below is historical, not a claim about this head.
- Previous-head CI lint failed on an untouched `sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts` curly-brace violation. The old test-line budget failure is addressed by the rebase and dedicated allocation. No claim that new-head CI is green yet.
- Maintainer security-sensitive approval remains required; contributor changes cannot satisfy that gate.

Regression tests, each shown failing without its fix and passing with it:

| Test | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| `host-capability.tool-policy-scope.test.ts` (new): host-prepared scope reaches tool construction; a plugin-supplied `toolPolicyScope: "conversation"` does not | 2 failed, 1 passed (host value not injected) | 3 passed |
| `session-event-permissions.test.ts` "bounds a same-session background completion's final effects: same-session" | fails: `writeOffered: false`, expected `true` (the producer cap is kept) | passes |
| `agent-tools.session-event-cap.test.ts` "a sender narrowed by toolsBySender" (real `createOpenClawCodingTools`, real caller identity, no mock) | fails: `expected true to be undefined` when the sender check is removed | 3 passed |
| `stable-skill-authoring.test.ts` "keeps the human shape when a follow-up passes an expired grant" | 1 failed, 3 passed | 4 passed |
| `session-event-context.test.ts` "keeps the session chat type only for $route" | 1 failed, 2 passed | 3 passed |
| `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` "offers the human turn's skill_workshop definition on an internal turn" | asserts the surfaces differ without the helper | equal with it |

### Authority controls around the same-session exemption

`session-event-permissions.test.ts` "bounds a same-session background completion's final effects" runs the production path: a real `captureSessionEventTargetForHost` under a caller identity, the real `enqueueSessionEventForHost` admission, the real harness host capabilities and managed tool surface, and a real file write. Each row captures a producer whose ceiling lists only `read`:

| Row | Producer identity | Follow-up tool surface | File after the follow-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| `same-session` | same session, marked session-scoped | `write` offered | written |
| `restricted-sender` | same session, not marked (the caller leaves the mark off when `senderPolicy` or `groupPolicy` narrowed the turn; see the caller test above) | no `write` | unchanged |
| `cross-session` | other session, marked | no `write` | unchanged |
| `revoked-before-write` | same session, marked; the session permission mode is set to `read-only` after the tool surface is built | `write` offered, call refused (authority/permission error) | unchanged |

Result: 4 passed. With `session-event-target.ts` restored to its base version, the `same-session` row fails (`writeOffered: false`).

Expired personal-library calls: `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` builds the real coding tools for an internal turn and shows `skill_workshop` with `target: "personal"` rejected with "fresh message" (`AUTHORITY_EXPIRED`). `stable-skill-authoring.test.ts` shows an expired grant refuses personal-library calls and never replaces the remembered human shape; the sandboxed-run refusal for workspace calls is unchanged code from #172026 and is not re-tested here.

What this does not show: the embedded dispatch wiring (`resolveStableEmbeddedSkillAuthoring` at `run-attempt-dispatch.ts`) is a single call covered by the two tests above through the same factory, not by a dispatch-level test.

Touched suites: the files above plus `gateway-caller-context.test.ts` and `agent-tools.delegated-authority.test.ts` pass. The new production-boundary rows pass 4 of 4. `tsgo` core and the `src` test shards: clean. `oxfmt` on the repository: clean. `check:test-mock-exports` and `check:max-lines-ratchet` against the base commit: OK (the PR adds no mock factory and no line to `agent-tools.ts` or `cli-runner/prepare.ts`).

### Required test lanes that fail on this PR's CI

Three required lanes failed on the earlier heads. Each was checked against `main`:

- `src/gateway/mcp-http.exec-completion.test.ts` "an empty CLI final": fails the same way with every file this PR touches restored to `origin/main` (`1e89f5b3fe8`), and fails in CI on unrelated PRs (for example https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40290743775 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40292785214). It is inherited.
- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts` "drains a restored interrupted predecessor before later cohorts": fails the same way with the PR's files restored to `origin/main`, and fails in CI on an unrelated PR (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40292474849). It is inherited.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.operator-continuation.test.ts`: all 20 tests pass locally on this branch merged with `origin/main`. I could not reproduce the CI failure. By construction this PR cannot reach that path: the new session-scoped marking requires `toolPolicyScope: "conversation"`, which that test never sets, so its follow-up ceiling is unchanged. I did not find this failure on another PR, so I cannot call it inherited.

Live run against a real Codex app-server (codex 0.162.1, the version pinned on `main`), an isolated gateway, and `chat.send`. Script: user turn, a turn that starts `exec` with `background=true`, the completion wake, then a user turn. Wire capture of the app-server JSON-RPC, base `4fa442e3327`:

```
# stock (4fa442e3327)
in thread/start None dynTools=10
-> thread thread-A
# user turn
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20064 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# user turn that starts the background exec
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20204 cached= 20061
usage thread-A in= 21343 cached= 20201
usage thread-A in= 21589 cached= 21340
out turn/completed thread-A completed
in thread/start None dynTools=48
-> thread thread-B
# completion wake (turn 1 of 2)
in turn/start thread-B
usage thread-B in= 29269 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-B completed
in thread/start None dynTools=48
-> thread thread-C
# completion wake (turn 2 of 2)
in turn/start thread-C
usage thread-C in= 29183 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-C completed
```

```
# this branch
in thread/start None dynTools=10
-> thread thread-A
# user turn
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20064 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# user turn that starts the background exec
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20204 cached= 20061
usage thread-A in= 21336 cached= 20201
usage thread-A in= 21632 cached= 21333
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# completion wake (turn 1 of 2)
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 21761 cached= 21629
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# completion wake (turn 2 of 2)
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 21830 cached= 21758
out turn/completed thread-A completed

in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 22124 cached= 21827
out turn/completed thread-A completed
```

The live run used commit 591bd2b60aa on base `4fa442e3327`. The branch was then rebased onto `d4ae3a73118` without conflicts. Typecheck and the regression and affected suites were rerun after the rebase. Commit `80b8c1192d9` came later: it moves the marking decision into `createCodingToolsGatewayCaller` and adds the tests above, with no change to the runtime behavior traced here; the live trace was not repeated.

Stock: each wake turn starts a fresh thread with 48 dynamic tools and 0 cached tokens. Patched: one thread with 10 dynamic tools for the whole session. The wake turns are plain `turn/start` calls on the bound thread, reading 99% of their input from cache, with no `thread/resume` or `thread/unsubscribe` in the wire log. The next user turn stays on the same thread. (The stock run's next user turn did not reach the app-server before the harness stopped, so it is not shown.)

What this evidence does not show: the harness covers a WebChat direct session with no group, per-DM, or sender policy. Sessions with those policies are covered by the unit tests above, not by a live run.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes automation management disappearing when an owner's channel message waits in the follow-up queue.

## User Impact

The queued message receives the management capabilities it is still entitled to when execution starts. Expired ingress grants remain expired; revoked or unverified inputs remain restricted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backports [#172539](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172539) to `kimiyu_openclaw_2026-10-01-beta1-reviewed`, retaining this branch's private owner checks. The original ingress captures identity and eligibility; queued execution creates a new scope, and collected messages require every source's authority to remain current. No persistence, recovery replay or catalog guard changes.

## Evidence

- 274 relevant tests passed: 133 producer/queue cases (including 40 new cases), 55 shared ingress-authority cases, 56 follow-up/queue cases, 6 direct-caller cases, and 24 private-final cases. The latest 188-case producer/shared-fixture run passed in 84.13 seconds; unaffected earlier evidence is reused.
- [Six final-effect cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7c99e67918e53f9f4ed8b0ff239790c3919882cc/src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.queued-cron-final-effect.test-support.ts) exercise real ingress, producer, collection, queued scope, channel admission, embedded tool preparation, in-process Gateway dispatch, cron handlers and SQLite. The owner can list and update a foreign-session job exactly once. Member/unverified sources cannot see or mutate that job. Revocation, cancellation, and retirement of the first collected source after grant redemption prevent writes; the second collected source remains current in that last case.
- Negative control: restoring all six runtime files to `c772` while retaining the new tests makes the owner's real global-list assertion fail (foreign job absent). Restoring the candidate passes. This is a six-runtime-file counterfactual, not a full-tree baseline run. The earlier two-file management-schema counterfactual also reproduced the loss.
- Core and changed-test typechecks, native guards, lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Queue tests now await each input's existing lifecycle settlement; no queue-deletion polling or new completion API. The final-effect proof uses a synthetic model decision with real dispatch/handler/store, not a deployed Slack, real LLM, scheduled-agent or OAuth test.

CI also exposed an old `required + NO_REPLY` assertion that failed with all nine original PR files restored to the unchanged `c772` baseline. [#171437](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171437) already made a successful explicit `NO_REPLY` intentional silence. This PR corrects that test assertion only; genuine-empty reply failure coverage and all product completion behavior remain unchanged. The final head `7c99e679` passed [main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41737590105) and [scaffold validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41737589911) after a normal retry of the npm archive download timeout. Exact-head review has no open findings. Merged as `adca087e79d1e9a342b0f3c150bd182144b16274`; its full tree matches the tested head.

Post-merge real 30-minute staging B retest passed on `adca087e` / image `a8530e61`: both runtimes upgraded, the original tool was not replayed, and both original queued inputs executed and replied exactly once in the same Slack thread without `/new`. The old turn was interrupted and reported once; it was not recovered. All four captured ingress records completed. Ordinary A and installed-image R11 evidence is reused. Staging cleanup finished and production remains locked. [Full live evidence and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192329#issuecomment-6619986895).

prs.title: fix(ios): keep submitted text when chat switching interrupts delivery
prs.body:
Related: #165515, #190416. This is ordinary live-text delivery recovery; the local slash-command repairs remain separate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: submitted text can disappear when switching chats, agents, or Gateways interrupts native iOS message delivery.

## User Impact

Keep the original submission recoverable without overwriting newer drafts or automatically resending a message whose delivery is uncertain. If recovery storage is full or unavailable during a handoff, the original presentation stays in copy-only recovery: copy any needed text before choosing **Clear recovered text and continue**.

**Draft for the explicitly requested local Mac/iOS runner handoff—not ready for review or merge. Native behavior and the new recovery UI are not yet qualified.**

## Why This Change Was Made

- Recover against the captured conversation/composer key and revision, rather than whichever chat is currently displayed.
- Distinguish interrupted pre-live admission, successful durable capture, known-unsent failures, and ambiguous delivery. Ambiguous delivery retains its warning and manual-review path; reconnect does not blindly replay it.
- Revoke a replaced presentation's transport immediately, while the existing owner retains any text that could not enter the outbox. The fallback pane is copy-only; its explicit Clear action releases local recovery without sending or cancelling Gateway work.
- Retire only the matching captured draft after durable acceptance, including after detachment, and preserve newer original/destination drafts. Defer new-session actions while recovery owns the presentation.

No new manager, storage backend, schema, configuration option, dependency, or universal replay mechanism.

## Evidence

### Published source and source review

- Current head: `4c560af3b05d20e71eea605eede11c31bd7c5663`; tree: `db103d63470c32a62883ed992c4f1824e033a515`. The repair commit preserves parent `9513194e09737b9631d91a7aade2a33d670dcfc1` and adds only six files (+154/-133); the complete candidate versus audited baseline `70c99be459a77d474f19a7eed0e575449ef088e1` is 13 files (+652/-179). This is not current-main integration proof.

All 19 member lengths/hashes were verified; separate private indexes reconstructed the declared repaired tree from both tested base951 and published tree84f. Only the six source files were incorporated, not standalone proof projects, build inputs, launchers, caches, keys or dependency setup.
- Repairs include the explicit `expectedTexts: [String]` annotation addressing the review's compiler/GRDB overload ambiguity, with continuation/assertions unchanged; a byte-identical 1,317-byte retired-composer recovery block moved into the existing Sending extension without visibility/type/isolation changes; assertion/await-equivalent hydration helper extraction; existing demo fixture-body extraction; and formatting. No test assertions, attributes, skips or baselines were weakened.
- Source-equivalence checks, whitespace checks (including the committed repair), and `pnpm docs:list` passed. Simplification and fresh independent review of the complete 13-file diff were scoped-clean for P0–P2. This was static review, not execution; unchanged routing/branch implementations were outside its supplied context. The [earlier public source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191535#issuecomment-6591707574) applies to historical head951, not a completed review of the new head.

### Attributed native runner evidence

The [runner report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191535#issuecomment-6606248103) tested **head951 plus local repair patches**, whose recovered source now matches published tree db103. This is source-equivalent prior runner evidence, **not fresh execution of the new commit or a hosted-CI pass**. Raw logs, xcresult bundles and commands remain runner-local and were not independently replayed or media-inspected here. Captured generated inputs do not establish their historical byte identity at execution.

- Original `ChatViewModelOutboxTests` + `ChatViewModelTests`: **403 declarations / 478 parameterized executions, 0 failures, 0 skips**.
- Normal iOS app/Share/Watch graph and `ChatSendHydrationTests`: **3 XCTest methods / 9 transitions, 0 failures, 0 skips**. **Keep Draft/unqualified.** Fresh qualification of the fetchable repair head, measured behavioral base-red/fix-green, app-level interrupted-delivery recovery, crash/relaunch durability and inspected before/after recovery screenshots remain pending. ## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

**Draft — qualification incomplete:** the recovered repairs are now published at `7fb156ad5b16a98ec40f6c28e28a18eba349f24a`. ## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier Dashboard consolidation intentionally removed duplicate native settings. This restores only a small local-device projection, not native copies of Gateway work pages. Native controls and the authenticated WebKit adapter share IOSDeviceSettingsActions and the existing consent, permission, snapshot, and preference owners.

No configuration keys, schemas, durability policy, dependencies, or protocol versions change. The simplify pass removed the bridge-only forwarding wrapper and kept one setting-effect implementation. The subsequent fixture-array extraction satisfies the inherited function-length gate without changing message content or suppressing the gate.

## Evidence

### Published source and recovered-input identity

Current head `7fb156ad5b16a98ec40f6c28e28a18eba349f24a`, tree `98d5d0361e2e5b940bb41da3d01a687819162adf`, directly advances `a3e98bc461650d7f36eaa61fa41114a0857b287c`. History, attribution, existing cleanup, localization, and native/WebKit guards are preserved. No dependency, configuration, schema, protocol, or permission-policy change.

Archive SHA-256 `128c19c99ce2aa99f2674ac19685303d78306f917570dfde1a6f850c74320830` and all 13 inventoried member hashes were verified. Both `repair.patch` (SHA-256 `33fe0dc71e6e729cfa8a8b8c2aa2f6712d978755f727774330dce581e687b0b9`) and the saved tested patch independently produce declared source tree `84ec7f2e6f3a928fd27c1586d9ca3722a0f825d1` on declared base `a3e98bc…`. That base matched the then-public source exactly, so no prior public fix was reversed or reapplied.

**All seven Swift repair blobs are byte-identical to that tested source tree.** The only additional change is `test/scripts/ios-release-fastlane-gates.test.ts`: its static consumer now reads main, Chat, and Helpers files for the same XCTestCase. It failed on the exact recovered source with missing `captureReleaseScreenshot`, then passed with this migration. Positive and negative oracles are unchanged. The split retains one XCTestCase/app owner, all 60 entrypoints, and all 683 existing assertion-opening lines; one failure assertion was added for a missing notification-denial action. prs.title: fix(ios): discard stale wake commands after chat or Gateway changes
prs.body:
Related: #165515 (focused-chat routing; intentionally unchanged here).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: buffered Voice Wake recognition can survive a chat or Gateway change and create another command after the previous command was canceled.

## User Impact

Pending wake commands and buffered results from the old capture are discarded when the destination changes; fresh listening can resume through the existing admission gates.

**Draft for local Mac runner validation. This does not fix main-versus-focused-chat routing:** that separate change is already proposed in #165515. No configuration, dependency, protocol, or data migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route invalidation now reuses VoiceWakeManager’s existing recognition generation, capture teardown, and command cancellation instead of canceling only the pending send. Internal recognition start/teardown retain a cancellation-only helper to avoid recursive teardown.

On the pinned main baseline, Watch-started Talk can retain another chat’s key after Talk stops. Phone focus changing to that same key would otherwise skip invalidation because Talk already targets it. The focused-chat owner now invalidates wake on an actual phone-focus change independently of that Talk shortcut. This guard should be reevaluated if #165515’s different Watch-target behavior lands first.

## Evidence

### Published source and review

- Current head `21c5dc32043fdbba041354bcd8b5fbb1da2f53ce` has source tree `b5ff2ebea106c5ca8fde0318c00918a1a7887e3d`, the exact recovered runner-tested source tree. It appends to `0fb71abd0c385bdb3b132b0baa0c2004ee173ff6`; the follow-up is limited to two files (+94/−86), with the full PR at five files (+188/−85).
- The follow-up explicitly marks the test's `receive(_ command: String, generation: UInt64) throws` helper `@MainActor` and lifts `try` from the `#require` arguments to the enclosing callback call. The three throwing callers and all expectation/require expressions are preserved. This addresses the prior ClawSweeper P2 **source-isolation finding at old-head lines 232–234**, not microphone or Gateway final-effect qualification.
- The inherited demo-fixture function-length blocker is repaired only by extracting the two existing seed builders into private helpers. Fixture bodies, selectors/order, timestamp inputs, and the rest of the owner were checked unchanged; no lint rule or guard was weakened.
- Fresh whole-five-file Autoreview, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`, exit 0, no findings, bound to the `b5ff…` tree against audited baseline `70c99be459a77d474f19a7eed0e575449ef088e1`. Staged whitespace, fixture/assertion-preservation, and exact source-identity checks passed. This is static review, not a fresh native execution.
- All three parts and 13 file hashes in the [complete repair attachment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191521#issuecomment-6608862109) were verified. Both complete patch forms independently reconstruct the same repaired tree from their declared tested base. Generated Xcode inputs and proof documents remain supplemental and were not committed; their historical execution-time byte identity is not established.

### Runner-reported native results and limits

The [2026-11-03 requester report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191521#issuecomment-6606242554) ran `0fb71abd0c385bdb3b132b0baa0c2004ee173ff6` plus the recovered repairs: native `VoiceWakeManagerStateTests`, **six declarations / eight executions, zero failures and zero skips**, and the normal app/Share/Watch graph built on an iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.5 simulator. Focused strict SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, and diff checks were also reported passing. Those repairs are now published in the source-equivalent tree above. **These are attributed source-equivalent results—not a fresh Mac run of this commit or a hosted-CI pass.**

The [earlier qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191521#issuecomment-6591318088) remains historical evidence: normal build and correct hosted test selection exited 65 before execution at the inherited fixture lint gate, and an earlier Logic selection exited 0 with **zero tests—not a pass**. Later repaired-source success does not relabel those attempts. Previously skipped or permission-blocked hosted checks are not counted as passes.

Detailed native logs, commands, xcresult bundles, and executable receipts remain runner-local, not public downloadable attachments; they were not independently replayed or media-inspected here. The Linux preparation environment has no native Swift/Xcode tooling, and its Node 24.20 runtime is below the repository floor, so unsupported Node gates were not run or bypassed.

**Remaining / keep Draft:** obtain inspectable native receipts bound to the published source and close remaining affected-consumer coverage (including `VoiceWakeGatewaySyncTests`) and observed baseline-red/fix-green evidence. Microphone recognition, audio quality, real suppression/teardown/fresh listening, and physical-device Voice Wake remain unproven. Full Gateway final-effect/authority proof also remains open: show allowed fresh delivery while canceled pending work and buffered callbacks from a retired capture produce no replacement-Gateway event through `commandTask`, `sendVoiceTranscript`, and `GatewayNodeSession.sendEvent`. The actor-helper source repair and simulator state tests do not establish those physical or final-effect behaviors; no ready/merge qualification is claimed.

The change is nonvisual. The duplicate focused-routing callback/acceptance hunks, speculative send guards, and shared WebSocket-fixture additions were removed from this safety-only slice.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the iOS share sheet reporting **Sent** and dismissing its draft when the Gateway ignored an oversized message or rejected its attachments.

## User Impact

Rejected shares stay editable with an actionable error. **Sent** means the Gateway admitted the request for agent dispatch, not that the agent finished. Older Gateways cannot confirm admission: the sheet keeps the draft and asks users to check the destination session before retrying and update the Gateway. Retries are not deduplicated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `NodeEventResult` contract for explicit admission/rejection. Publish the decided receipt before an incognito session's existing accepted-work drain, without releasing actor custody or weakening connection checks. The share extension checks that receipt instead of treating RPC success as admission. No protocol/schema/config or dependency changes.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep background work visible while chat waits
prs.body:
Related: #182684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the missing work signal when a chat is waiting on subagents or still has task-owned background commands running.

## User Impact

The existing compact footer keeps its claw, elapsed time, and separate subagent/command counts visible, including in bubble mode. Counts open the existing Subagents and Processes panels. Detached services do not keep an idle conversation looking busy, and unavailable command observations are labeled rather than presented as zero.

## Why This Change Was Made

Implements the selected minimal-footer design without restoring the removed delegation tracker or per-worker narration. Command classification comes from the execution owner's retained request ownership, not command-name or output heuristics. The visible conversation shares the existing process observation with the panels.

Counts cover reconnectable background exec processes, not every foreground tool or OS process. Truncated inventories show a lower bound with "+". Older workers lacking ownership metadata remain inspectable in Processes but do not acquire an inferred busy signal. No execution, cancellation, retention, or permission behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Missing-claw regression fails on the original in flat and bubble modes and passes with the fix.
- Producer regression fails on the original and passes with task-owned, explicitly detached, unknown-owner, and terminal command cases.
- 60 focused UI tests and 7 producer tests pass. Production UI and affected chat-test typechecks pass; scoped lint, styles, controller guards, and formatting pass.
- Five browser flows pass, covering subagent waiting/resumption, one and 12 workers, command-only work, detached services, unavailable reads, reconnect, completion, and existing panel navigation. Deterministic Gateway fixtures exercise the actual running Control UI; the producer regression exercises real ownership with external process I/O fixed.
- [Inspected before/after screenshots and the command-only state](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185241#issuecomment-6430583591), embedded in the linked proof comment. The representative before/after pair was also delivered in the originating chat.

Focused UI proof took 15.45 seconds of Vitest time / 25.06 seconds wall; browser proof took 81.28 seconds including its production build. Producer proof took 71.97 seconds wall, mostly compiled-worker preparation; its new regression took 465 ms. CI timing is pending.

Initial broad ui/tsconfig.json validation also reported existing unrelated native-desktop and quota-diagnostics test errors; the proper production UI and scoped chat-test lanes pass. No claim of a passing broad test typecheck is made.

Independent review found a reconnect uncertainty bug in the first candidate; it was repaired and added to the browser regression. The final independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Prompt indexing and row-content dependency computation were moved intact to their existing owners to respect the projection module's line limit. No new process manager or polling loop is introduced. The publisher's metadata-only commit has the same source tree as the tested and reviewed candidate.

Worked on by: @steipete

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d56dcb22-4fa6-4e67-9e48-b268811190ee)
