prs.title: fix: restore iOS image shares on multi-agent gateways
prs.body:
Closes #186392.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iOS image shares fail with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` when a Gateway has explicit multi-agent ownership and a configured system agent.

## User Impact

Image requests with unscoped session keys can reach the resolved agent. Global sessions and explicitly selected agents retain their owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the owner already returned by session lookup for the image-capability check. Resolving the raw key again discarded that owner. This removes the redundant resolution without changing ownership policy or permissions.

## Evidence

- Before the fix on `ca305f7d9425`: the unscoped and global cases failed at the handler's resolver with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED`; the explicit-agent control passed. The regression was then moved to a dedicated file to respect the existing suite's line limit.
- After the fix: **70 tests passed across three files**, including all three image-owner cases, the existing node-event suite, and session-request ownership tests. Command:
  ```sh
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server-node-events.image-owner.test.ts src/gateway/server-node-events.test.ts src/gateway/session-request-agent.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  ```
- Gateway-server typecheck passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json --noEmit`.
- Formatting, targeted syntax lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable findings.
- Typed lint did not reach analysis: its plugin-SDK declaration preparation timed out after 300 seconds on this Windows host. The separate Gateway-server typecheck above passed. On current PR head `4ed31dc44b650354a56715051018ad3f049e1ba5`, [CI lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40615285034/job/122577645475), production types, test types, and the [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40615285034/job/122583839563) passed.
- Windows, Node 26.12.1. Local Vitest duration: 282.61 seconds, including 170.06 seconds preparing the shared worker bundle; the three new cases took 20–21 ms each.

The regression exercises the real handler and ownership resolution with image parsing, persistence, and agent dispatch mocked. A live iOS share-sheet/model-provider flow was not tested.

### Review follow-up (2026-10-28)

[ClawSweeper reviewed head `4ed31dc44b65`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186416#issuecomment-6458459704) and reported no code findings, but requested real iOS behavior proof. The current head has 123 reported check/status entries with none failing or pending; skipped native-app lanes do not provide that proof.

**Remaining evidence gap:** no iPhone or iPad test device is currently available to the contributor, so the requested demonstration remains unverified. It requires an iOS photo share through an isolated Gateway configured with explicit multi-agent ownership and a system agent, evidence of successful image receipt by the agent, and a text-only control. A recording or Gateway/model output must redact credentials, private endpoints, and personal data. The automated regression and green CI do not replace this live test. No re-review is being requested until the missing proof is available.

prs.title: fix(gateway): agent.run can carry a fallback ladder so a pinned model no longer dead-ends on a quota 429
prs.body:
Closes #186418
Related: #151980, #141115, #181981

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation caller that pins a model on the WebSocket agent.run request loses the agent's configured model-fallback ladder, so a quota-class 429 ends the run instead of advancing to the next candidate.

The request schema had no way to express a chain, so the only lever an automation caller had was to pin a model - which silently suppresses the configured ladder. Operators who configured a working fallback chain for the agent had no caller-side way to keep it alive.

## User Impact

User impact: automation callers can now send an explicit fallback ladder with their agent.run request, so a provider quota window on the pinned model no longer ends the run - the run advances to the next candidate the caller named.

This is opt-in and additive. A request that pins a model and sends no ladder behaves exactly as before: the pin stays strict and the configured chain stays suppressed, which is the contract #151980 asks to keep.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway already had the pieces to carry a run-scoped chain, but the wire protocol could not express one. Rather than relax the strict-pin contract, this change adds an explicit field so the caller states the chain it wants:

- agent.run accepts an optional fallbacks array of provider/model refs. Entries are trimmed, de-duplicated, and bounded to 16.
- The ladder is authorized exactly like a model override: a caller without the model-override scope is rejected with INVALID_REQUEST and a clear message.
- Every named model is checked against the agent's visible model set and the caller's operator authority before the run starts, so a caller cannot widen model access by naming extra chain entries.
- The chain travels with the run as a request-scoped override, so it is used for this run only and does not become session state.

The request-level pin remains the primary model; the ladder only adds candidates behind it.

## Evidence

Focused test runs, both green on this branch (rebased onto main at d2491817):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-request-preflight.test.ts
    -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 33 passed (33)

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts
    -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 44 passed (44)

Typecheck:

    pnpm tsgo:test:root -> exit 0 (all root shards)
    pnpm tsgo:test:packages -> exit 0

New coverage:

- src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-request-preflight.test.ts - a request that carries both a pinned model and a ladder keeps the ladder and reports it as request-scoped; a request with a ladder but no model-override scope is rejected; a request with no ladder leaves the override unset.
- src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts - a request-supplied ladder survives a pinned model during model selection, and a request-supplied chain that names a model the agent cannot use is rejected before the run starts.

Behavior with no fallbacks in the request is unchanged, so existing agent.run callers are unaffected.

prs.title: fix: preserve assistant answers when media delivery reuses response indexes
prs.body:
Closes #166536

## What Problem This Solves

Distinct assistant responses can be suppressed when retries reuse content indexes or repeat text and images. Streamed media and recovered answers can also end up attached to the wrong response during finalization.

## User Impact

Each physical response keeps its own delivery and transcript identity. Streamed images survive finalization, source images remain visible alongside TTS audio, and canonical provider content and signatures remain intact. This prevents further corruption; it does not repair previously altered history.

## Why This Change Was Made

Upstream #177049 (`0d7df3fc2cf6bc9c53b04f7857b7cbca61b3c927`) now owns `AgentAssistantSourceReceipt` and exact transcript-anchor enrichment. This correction reuses that owner and removes the competing receipt pipeline. The remaining changes scope delivery dedupe, aggregate coverage, streamed-media finalization and timeout-recovery custody to each physical response.

Published head: `8716154f8d06ff3609f62f583c7c48df2ff6ed3a`. A normal merge of main `cf2558f5639e273dc4fe1f19e9c5f7715dc8d0de` preserves the original PR history. No force-push, schema/configuration change, signing infrastructure or release publication is included. Maintainer edits remain enabled.

## Evidence

- Final complete affected Gateway suites: 149/149 passed, no skips, including committed/suppressed/indexed/unkeyed/owned source-media plus TTS cases.
- Commentary media: 18/18 passed. Focused unchanged agent/autoreply owners passed 43 unit-fast, 52 auto-reply, 36 lifecycle and 34 terminal tests; real subscription dispatch cases also passed.
- Main-production controls reproduced the occurrence and recovered-answer failures. Real transcript regressions reproduced TTS selection, append-key and owned-rewrite losses before their repairs.
- Type-aware lint on all 19 changed source files, production core typecheck, formatting and diff checks passed.
- The initial committed correction and the subsequent CI test repair each received fresh independent P2 review with no actionable findings.
- CI run [39902028749](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39902028749) exposed two test-type defects and a stale unkeyed fenced-stream lookup. All reproduced locally. The follow-up repairs only test callers: source-aware lookup with an unkeyed negative control, required assertion diagnostics, and the fixture return type tied to the real transcript writer.
- Repair proof: 185 focused tests passed (134 Gateway and 51 agents; 182.39 seconds wall time including fixture/compiler startup), both affected test-type configurations passed, and targeted lint, formatting, diff and staged line-cap checks passed. The final fixture adjustment is type-only; Gateway types were rechecked afterward. [Hosted CI on this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39909500750) completed successfully. GitHub reports 78 passing checks, 54 skipped and no failing or pending checks; the consolidated CI, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review statuses passed.

Mandatory exact-candidate Telegram Test Server proof remains unperformed. The checked authoring hosts lack the existing launcher/broker access; no live lease was allocated. Local tests and earlier real model/media/compaction observations do not replace the requested reused-index Telegram scenario. The [existing QA handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166568#issuecomment-6087119969) records that gap for upstream review. It does not prevent contributor submission; no local signing setup is requested.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep terminal tab navigation out of the PTY
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End select a terminal tab, but the asynchronous after-render callback steals focus into the PTY, breaking continued tab navigation. Conversely, Enter, Space and clicking the already-selected terminal tab can leave focus on the tab instead of entering the terminal.

## User Impact

Keyboard navigation stays in the tablist; explicit activation enters the selected real terminal without sending shell input. This applies to the standalone terminal and the chat's hosted terminal header. Selecting a different tab with the mouse and switching to other panel tabs retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing native selection event through the internal UI adapters. The terminal owner selects, refits and repaints without focusing for navigation keys; explicit activation uses the existing per-tab callback. Hosted-header expansion retains priority over terminal activation.

**No Gateway PTY permission, terminal protocol, request schema, input policy or configuration/default changes.** The event objects are local DOM callback arguments, not wire fields. Alix-007's original `d134bbaa6aebf279b78a6907a6162e6f8a1bed8f` commit is preserved.

## Evidence

[Fresh native proof and request/readback receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192096#issuecomment-6611938494) · [all sixteen inspected screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192096#issuecomment-6611789760)

Built main `22e063a9435f752547f380d074e6401c39e78614` versus exact head `df49134e63ac812fba7cf0bbcdd972e4e077afb3`, served by real built Gateways in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker, **Chromium 156.0.8078.4**, actual native `/bin/sh` PTYs:

| Observation, repeated twice per surface | Main | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Standalone and hosted header: ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End | Focus ends in Terminal input | Focus remains on selected tab |
| Both surfaces: Enter / Space / selected-tab click | Focus stays on tab | Focus enters Terminal input |
| Different-terminal pointer selection | PTY gets focus | Unchanged |
| Hosted Files-tab control | Files selected, no PTY focus | Unchanged |
| `terminal.input` during navigation/activation | 0 frames in every scene | 0 frames in every scene |

The hosted scene uses the real chat panel launcher and docking flow, then runs the assertions in the chat header—not a manually mounted component or standalone-only substitute. Public `terminal.list` confirms the two actual opened sessions remain attached; distinct startup PIDs identify their different contents. Client/Gateway build stamps and served entry hashes are checked. No model turn or shell command is typed.

| Hosted header | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| ArrowLeft: tab focus should remain | ![Main loses tab focus into the PTY](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c6e0069-b171-4c48-bffe-cfcdec474a44) | ![Candidate retains the selected tab focus ring](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f4e285f-a789-4346-adbd-bb962195b7e3) |
| Enter: explicit activation should enter the PTY | ![Main leaves Enter focus on the tab](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52e1507f-7bb7-419a-beac-1f18527b2163) | ![Candidate Enter focuses the actual Terminal input](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f6caae7-981c-4d85-9e5e-ca3936cac02f) |

### Explicit WebKit coverage limitation

[Main-baseline WebKit startup receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192096#issuecomment-6611903210). Available Linux WebKit 27.2 lanes authenticate and load the built assets but stall **on main itself, before the first terminal.open**, so the focus assertions cannot run. Ordinary ARM64 headless/headed and x64 lanes were tried; no WebKit/Safari pass is claimed. Maintainer scope excludes repairing that separate startup prerequisite in this PR and requests review of the bounded Chromium evidence with the gap stated plainly. If real WebKit terminal acceptance remains required by review, this PR stays parked rather than being called cross-browser validated.

### Regression coverage and simplification

Keep all **58** owner/shared-header test cases, including repaint/notifications, metadata, routing, close and expansion contracts. Consolidate duplicate fixture setup and reuse the existing shared strip's three-action activation coverage; retain the header forwarding assertion and the new real hosted-header proof. Remove the proposed allocation entirely.

- Candidate: **4 focused files, 58 passed**. Paired main run: **6 intended event/focus/activation failures, 52 passed**.
- Focused format: pass. Type-aware lint: **0 errors**, two existing warnings in unchanged header code. Normal root/UI builds: pass.
- Whole PR: **tests +26/−26 (net 0)**; production **+37/−14 (net +23)**. Direct key comparisons avoid a per-selection navigation-array allocation. No new grant, scalar, global helper or state owner.

Merge risk: **two-way door**; reverting restores the prior focus behavior without a migration or stored-data change. Blast radius is internal terminal-tab selection/activation in standalone and hosted headers; other panels retain their existing callbacks, and Gateway PTY authority/input handling is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(proxy): serialize IPv6 debug proxy listener URLs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw proxy start --host ::1` and `openclaw proxy run --host ::1` bind a native IPv6 listener, then serialize it as `http://::1:PORT`. Constructing the private capture endpoint with `new URL` throws `Invalid URL`, so the CLI cannot forward traffic or run its child.

## User Impact

The debug proxy works on IPv6 loopback as well as IPv4. Its public listener uses the required bracketed authority (`http://[::1]:PORT`); bind behavior, request checks, auth and private capture credentials are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `formatHostForUrl` from #190942 at the shared listener URL producer. Both CLI entry points already use this owner. No new URL helper, fallback, public API, configuration or persistence change is needed. Alix-007's original fix commit is preserved.

## Evidence

[Fresh native CLI reproduction, forwarding receipts and capture readback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192029#issuecomment-6609676418)

Official `node:24.22.1` secretless Linux Docker, separately built CLI/Gateway, real local IPv6/IPv4 origins, explicit isolated profiles and state. Main `215c89296cb6bbbf7dc376a9e2a6858a2cc21b2c` versus exact head `6ac7705bfad72157f7336468ddb486c231343127`:

| Public CLI path | Main, twice | Candidate, twice |
|---|---|---|
| `proxy start --host ::1 --port 0` | `Invalid URL`; no forward, 0 capture events | Complete HTTP 201, exact echoed body, 2 capture events |
| `proxy run --host ::1 --port 0 -- node <client>` | `Invalid URL`; child not run, 0 events | Child forwards successfully, complete HTTP 201, 2 events |
| Both IPv4 equivalents | Pass, 2 events each | Unchanged pass, 2 events each |

Main reached the real listener producer and failed at its `new URL`; watchdog SIGTERM cleanup of those failed processes is not claimed as successful startup or natural exit. Candidate IPv6 traffic actually traversed `::1` to origins that independently recorded that peer address. Every successful CLI and both Gateways exited 0; all successful sessions were ended with exactly two events through public `proxy sessions --json` readback.

Credential controls: public proxy URLs have no credentials; each `proxy run` child's private capture endpoint has credentials and the same origin. Origins receive neither Authorization nor Proxy-Authorization. Only presence booleans are recorded; no credentials are exposed. No model/provider, helper-import reproduction or protocol mock is involved.

The owner test reuses its existing UTF-8 body/capture regression for IPv4 and IPv6. Main: the intended IPv6 `Invalid URL` failure, 16 other cases pass. Candidate: **17 passed**. Focused lint/format and normal root builds pass. The proposed allocation is removed; whole-PR tests are **+4/−4 (net 0)**, production **+2/−1 (net +1)**. No ratchet or grant increase.

Merge risk: **two-way door**; reverting restores the previous URL spelling without any migration or stored-data change. Blast radius is the debug proxy's advertised listener/capture endpoint URL, used by `proxy start` and `proxy run`; native binding and upstream request/auth policy do not change.

prs.title: improve(ui): clarify provider accounts and model setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Models mixed provider, connection, credential, and profile terminology for saved access. Sign-out/removal copy also used inconsistent actions and “runs,” while setup failures exposed role scopes.

## User Impact

- Models calls saved access **accounts**, distinct from providers and externally managed API keys.
- Sign-out/removal dialogs use question titles and retain the consequences for shared accounts, other agents, and active replies.
- Successful sign-out is quiet when the account disappearance already confirms it; warnings remain visible.
- Selected agent-creation, model-setup, and device-setup errors use the approved nouns and actionable wording. Request/retry behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies the approved Control UI glossary to the most visible M1 surfaces without changing routes, protocol keys, foreign locales, authentication, or retry identities. Three docs distinguish saved accounts from external key sources. The catalog-only row label stays short because its layout truncates long metadata.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Save credentials for this agent | Add an account for this agent |
| Compare connection methods | Compare sign-in methods |
| Credentials / Provider profiles | Accounts |
| Log out / Logging out… | Sign out / Signing out… |
| Remove {provider} | Remove {provider}? |
| Active runs | Active replies |
| Couldn’t create a connection link. | Couldn’t create the device connection link. Try again. |
| operator.admin requirement | You need admin access to create an agent. |

## Evidence

- 13 touched unit-test files: 162 tests passed across bounded runs. Account ordering/sign-out and Start Chat were rerun after the final assertion changes. Coverage includes agent-creation recovery, account removal consequences, and preserving warnings without a redundant success toast.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed; no raw-copy baseline change was needed.
- Direct oxlint on touched TypeScript/TSX: no warnings or errors. Oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh review covered provider/account behavior and warning preservation. Addressed its findings by reverting device-only label changes and updating the quoted account-navigation labels.
- The touched browser component test passed (1 test). The touched model-setup E2E command exited with “No test files found” under the current E2E project selection; this is a discovery/proof gap, not a product pass.

### Visual proof

Inspected synthetic-data, light-theme Models capture:

![After: Models with saved accounts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe97d24a-9b56-4b0e-ac00-eda6b568a40b)

Before capture and a fresh narrow-width/dialog capture could not complete: the interrupted local harness retained a fail-closed `dist-artifacts.lock` ownership record. No media is committed.

### Scope and gaps

- Most remaining login/recovery/account-controls/runtime setup copy is deferred to keep M1 bounded.
- Raw `{error}` details remain in agent creation, its first-message failure, command-palette session-start failure, and setup cancellation failure because the shared collapsed-details contract is not available on this base.
- The retained short catalog-only row text is deliberate; its metadata uses ellipsis at narrow widths.
- Device-only labels and broader setup copy remain unchanged in this PR.

## Follow-up: device action wording

- Restored `newSession.connectMachine`: “Connect a machine” → “Connect a device”.
- Audited the PR’s added English UI strings; no other requested noun, “thinking level”, or straight-apostrophe fixes were needed.
- Added a palette-menu regression assertion. `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` and the touched palette-menu suite (4 tests) passed with five-minute command limits.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: retain safe causes when provider catalog discovery fails
prs.body:
Related: #165888

## What Problem This Solves

Provider catalog failures discard the safe cause needed to distinguish authentication, HTTP, timeout, and unexpected failures during model discovery.

## User Impact

Operators receive bounded diagnostic fields when discovery skips an unavailable catalog. Existing discovery outcomes, authentication handling, sibling discovery, and deadlines are preserved. This improves diagnosis; it does not claim to repair the underlying refresh failure or update the installed runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inner catalog boundary and outer discovery deadline share a fixed warning containing a validated provider identifier, phase, closed failure reason, elapsed milliseconds, and optional numeric HTTP status. Exception messages, stacks, URLs, response bodies, and credentials stay out of the warning. Adversarial thrown values cannot replace the existing graceful failure.

Current head is `b03de01539525e527ed38963758453b2e0b19997`. It integrates upstream main's timeout handling, flattened test layout and per-provider failure isolation (request-wide rethrow, unavailable outcomes) while retaining the five-file diagnostic repair, plus a test-line allocation for its +198 test lines. No dependency, scanner, or runtime deployment change is included.

## Evidence

- Prior-head CI on `05a58b8ab6e` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39186736715)) was successful; current-head CI fails only `test-lines` because of main's pre-existing 145-line unallocated debt ([details](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165915#issuecomment-6619830554)).
- The [October 19 integration report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165915#issuecomment-6257882153) records 26 passing focused tests on this candidate, preserving main's `timeoutMs` behavior. Earlier type/build/red-first evidence remains in the PR history; it is not represented as a fresh run on this head.
- **Review is still held:** [ClawSweeper's input-safety receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165915#issuecomment-6008077645) produced no verdict and did not disclose a rejected location. Passing dispatch or security-review checks do not release that hold.
- **Maintainer action:** qualify the intentional synthetic fault/leakage fixtures in `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-outcome.internal.test.ts` and release the hold, or identify the rejected source location so it can be corrected without weakening the leakage regression. The reserved `example.test` URL and synthetic placeholders are deliberate test inputs; no exact scanner-trigger claim is made.

The branch and fixture assertions remain intact. Fresh automated review can be requested after qualification; no approval, merge, or production rollout is claimed.

prs.title: feat(ui): auto-load older sidebar sessions on scroll
prs.body:
## Problem

To see older sessions in the sidebar you have to click **Load more sessions** at the bottom of the list. Reaching the end of the list should load the next page by itself, but only where the new rows show up at that end.

## Solution

- `RosterLoadMore` watches the existing button with the shared `createIntersectionObserver` helper. When the button comes into view, it calls the same owner action as a click (`loadMoreSidebarSessions`).
- It loads one page each time the button comes into view. If the new rows land off-screen, or a load fails, the button stays where it is, so nothing fires again until the user scrolls away and back. That prevents request loops without any retry or backoff state. The owner's existing `sessionsLoading` guard still drops overlapping loads.
- The observer callback only loads when the host's `effectiveSessionsGrouping() === "none"` and `effectiveSessionSortMode() !== "people"`. These owner methods are now part of `SidebarSessionListHost`, so no new prop is threaded through the list.
  - **Auto-loads:** flat list ("none"), sorted by created or updated time. Older rows mostly land at the end of the single ungrouped section, and the existing visible-limit bump shows them.
  - **Stays manual:** custom groups (`category`, which also adds the smart group/coding zones), `person`, `project`, and the People sort. In these views the new rows go into earlier sections or between existing rows, not at the bottom.
- The button stays as the manual fallback, the loading indicator and the keyboard/screen reader path.

Accepted edge cases:

- If the flat list is short enough that the button is already on screen when the sidebar opens, one page loads straight away. Nothing more loads after that.
- In flat view, a page can still land above the fold. Created order sorts by creation time while the server pages by update time, and session catalog sections sit below the native list. In those cases, auto-load still loads at most one page each time the button comes into view, the same as a click.
- If you switch to the flat view while the button is already on screen, nothing loads until it scrolls out of view and back.

## Evidence

- New `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-load-more.e2e.test.ts` cases with a 40-row first page and a 600px-tall viewport:
  - `none`: scrolling the button into view requests the sidebar's `offset: 40` page with no click, and the button goes away. **Fails on base** (the request never happens), **passes with the fix**.
  - `category`: scrolling the button into view sends no paged sidebar request. Clicking it still loads.
  - Request matches are scoped to `source: "sidebar"`, because the chat pane follows the mocked cursor too.
  - The existing hidden-only page tests still pass (4/4).
- `app-sidebar.session-feedback.test.ts` now installs its pending page before switching to the flat view, because the visible button may start that page itself. 10/10 pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `oxfmt` and `oxlint` on the touched files: clean. The only lint warning (`solid(reactivity)` in `renderSessionList`) was already on base.
- Test-line growth (+73) is allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/sidebar-auto-load-more.txt`.
- A fresh independent review returned "ready". Its one actionable item (the gate comment overstated the guarantee) is fixed.

## CI status

All checks pass except these two budget gates. `main` is already over the limit for both:

- **`control-ui-performance`:** `main`'s chat boot JS is 1281327 B, over the 1281063 B cap. The gate therefore allows at most 64 B of growth, and this PR adds +184 B. Reading the gate from the host instead of a new prop brought it down from +239 B.
- **`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (test-lines):** `main` is over its test-line ceiling, so any positive net delta fails, even when it is allocated.

No visual change. The button looks the same; only what triggers it changed.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): stop replaying answered group questions
prs.body:
Related: #192139

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: previously answered WhatsApp group questions are reinserted into "Chat history since last reply" after a confirmed `message` tool reply, causing agents to answer them again.

## User Impact

User impact: WhatsApp group turns retain genuinely pending messages while completed questions no longer reappear as unanswered context. Direct messages and other channels keep their existing history behavior.

This PR remains a draft pending human readiness review. Exact-head hosted build and test type checks passed on the fork, but the overall workflow was cancelled and is not a full CI pass.

## Why This Change Was Made

WhatsApp already clears its in-memory pending group buffer after dispatch. The shared transcript merge then adds earlier user rows back to that buffer because WhatsApp selected the pending-history mode. Selecting the existing recent-history mode for groups uses the transcript's confirmed terminal-delivery evidence to remove answered native rows and stops the legacy merge from reintroducing old questions. It leaves unconfirmed questions intact. The separate TUI symptom in #192139 is not addressed here.

## Evidence

- On the base behavior, the new WhatsApp admission test fails because group context has no `historyKind: "recent"`; the prior SQLite test showed a confirmed answer omitted from restored pending history. With this change, six focused test shards pass, 129 tests total, on Node 26.12.1: WhatsApp admission/process-message, SQLite transcript context, shared context, transcript reader, and prompt-prefix stability.
- The full WhatsApp extension lane ran twice. Its only failure was `send.delivery-recovery.test.ts` expecting four `sendMessage` arguments while current production sends a fifth `{ accountId: "default" }`; 1,042 other tests passed in the second run. The same failure reproduced with this PR's single production line removed, so it is present at the base behavior and unrelated to this change.
- Touched-file Oxlint and Oxfmt checks pass; `tsc --noEmit --declaration false` passes for `tsconfig.core.json` and `tsconfig.extensions.json`; `git diff --check` passes.
- `pnpm build` starts and completes native protocol/runtime script/plugin asset phases, then stops at `tsdown-ai`: declaration tooling rejects the checkout's borrowed `node_modules` symlink because dependencies reside in another worktree. The official `tsgo:core` route stops at the same physical-dependency guard. This is an environment gap, not a passing build. The checkout has no physical pnpm install and the host had 2.4 GiB free before this run.
- After fork CI found a missing `CommandAuthorized` field in the new test fixture, commit `4cef1c9d700` added it. The affected test, focused test types, touched-file lint/format, and diff check pass locally on that head.
- Fork [CI run 41736540902](https://github.com/1052326311/openclaw/actions/runs/41736540902) checked out exact head `4cef1c9d700`: `build-artifacts` passed, including `Build dist` and built-artifact checks, and `check-test-types-core-4` passed. The overall run was cancelled after other broad jobs failed or were pending. This is exact-head build/type evidence, not a full CI pass; the draft PR's automatic jobs are skipped.
- No live WhatsApp service or TUI session was exercised. The SQLite-to-rendered-context regression is local, not a live-channel claim.

## What Problem This Solves

People need to narrow shared Team conversations to those they own or are involved in without changing what the source publishes for everyone.

## User Impact

The existing **Owned by me** and **Involving me** sidebar filters also apply to supported shared catalogs, including pagination, transcript reads and imports. The source's optional global person selector can remain unset for personal request filtering. Existing publication restrictions and authorization remain in force; no migration or new persistent setting is required.

Request-scoped relationship selection reuses canonical session relations and verified numeric account mapping. It intersects source publication policy. Unlinked or ambiguous identities fail explicitly. Agent/query changes retire only that consumer's prior background poll; unsupported catalogs retain their existing behavior.

Catalog transcript execution and incremental pagination now load when needed. Admission and fresh-window reauthorization remain with their existing controllers; ownership and discovery visibility are checked after the import wait.

prs.title: fix(database): avoid writer stalls during initial host admission
prs.body:
Related: #169260, #169283

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: personal account, operator approval, and auth usage writes can block other SQLite writers while a busy Gateway host decides their initial admission.

## User Impact

Account connect/link/unlink, approval decisions, and credential usage recording no longer reserve the shared SQLite writer before their first host authorization. This reduces avoidable contention without changing credentials, permissions, schemas, retention, or timeout budgets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Seven initial admission calls ran after `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`: four account mutations in `src/state/user-model-accounts.ts:392`, two auth handlers in `src/agents/auth-profiles/store.worker.ts:108`, and the shared approval transaction helper in `src/gateway/operator-approval-store.worker.ts:47`. They now obtain that grant before beginning the transaction. Authoritative rows are still read inside the transaction; final host authorization, rollback, and committed receipt publication remain intact.

The tests pause at real worker admission and attempt a zero-timeout `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` from an independent SQLite connection. Initial admission must leave the writer free; final commit admission must retain it. This deterministically proves the lock boundary without sleeps, extra worker startup races, or altered production timeout settings. Enrollment now uses a populated shared auth row and verifies persisted authorization metadata.

## Evidence

Sanitized Gateway journal, 2026-10-22 around 23:30:29 UTC, line 9463: `pluginState.register` failed at `BEGIN` after 5,013 ms with SQLite busy/lock contention. This proves a competing state-DB writer exceeded its budget; it does **not** identify these account/approval/auth writers as that incident's holder.

Another visible state-DB writer nearby was `localWorkspace.mutate` (line 9382): 1,553 ms transaction hold, including 1,525 ms of host-admission wait. The `trajectory.runtime.append` and `sessions.transcript-maintenance` diagnostics at lines 9448 and 9453 refer to the separate agent database.

Local proof:

- A standalone Node 26.12.1 control called the four real account mutation APIs against an isolated SQLite database and probed the writer at each admission. With production modules from main `b4031b2954c7984754a2c375ab528162b795654b`, all four assertions failed: initial admission observed `transaction:held`. Restoring this candidate made all four pass with `transaction:free`, while final admission remained `commit:held` in both cases. No host timing or sleeps are involved.
- `pnpm test src/state/user-model-accounts-contention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 4 passed (Bun; about 1 second of tests).
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-personal.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 32 passed, including persisted authorization enrollment and existing revocation/receipt cases. Total wall time was 243.5 seconds on a loaded host, primarily transformation/worker setup; the new enrollment case took 1.653 seconds.
- Targeted `run-tsgo.mjs` check: passed for the nine changed TypeScript files using a temporary config extending `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.shard.json`.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on those nine files: passed. `oxfmt --check` on all ten changed files and `git diff --check`: passed.

Local limitation: the combined usage/account-connect/approval worker shard was stopped during Vite source-map transformation before reporting test results. A separate Vitest baseline attempt likewise spent 328 seconds preparing 16,820 worker inputs; the standalone real-owner control above supplied the negative proof. Exact-head CI run [39887110150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39887110150) passed, providing the remaining broad verification; these interrupted local runs are not claimed as passes.

Compared with current main: production +14/-10 (net +4), tests/support +227, docs +6. This removes 263 test lines from the contributor version, principally the repeated extra-worker/timed-stall scaffolding. The production fix is unchanged apart from merging current main's usage-receipt shape.

Original-head CI classification: CI run 39382949804 passed. The two red commit statuses, `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` and its aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`, came from Security Review run 39383995622 awaiting maintainer approval. They were not test failures or inherited-main failures. No changed path matches the restricted CODEOWNERS rules; the supported maintainer security clearance is still required.

Codex committed-branch autoreview: scoped-clean through P2; no accepted/actionable findings.

Accepted scope: final commit admission still holds transaction custody to preserve current authority. Other writer families are unchanged. No live Gateway was modified.

Contributor: @xialonglee; original commits retained, with maintainer conflict resolution and deterministic test simplification.

Verified head: `54f03650d71ad85b3106a5966d66935878aa4982`. Exact-head CI [39887110150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39887110150) is green, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. Maintainer security clearance passed in [39887297739](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39887297739). The exact-head watcher reports GREEN; older superseded check runs remain visible in the raw GitHub rollup. No inherited-failure exception or CI rerun was used.

prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson: their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**", "memory/.dreams/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.10.10 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, next to the existing `extraPaths` glob matcher in the memory host SDK, is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main: production +67/-8 in 15 files; tests +148/-3; docs +15/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2586 -> 2590 on main `bf10667`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on head `b607675` (on main `3c8129e`), starting from the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.10.10` from npm (npm 11.20 skipped the package's install scripts by default; the CLI ran without them). Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade from 2026.10.10 and existing data:** 2026.10.10 builds the index (10 files, 10 chunks). After this branch's `doctor --fix` (main's agent-database migrations since 2026.10.10, v27 -> v40), the existing index loads clean (`Dirty: no`) and returns the same results and scores as 2026.10.10, before any re-index. With `excludePaths` unset, `memory index` keeps the stored scope hash, the chunking version and every stored chunk row (same count and same fingerprint over `id`, `path`, `hash`). This PR adds no database schema or stored fields; the scope hash changes only when `excludePaths` is set. **Opting in:** setting `excludePaths` marks the index dirty with a scope change and pauses vector search until a rebuild, both shown in `memory status`. `memory index` then drops the 7 reports and keeps the 3 curated files; the curated note ranks first, and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.10.10 OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.331 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.323 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.316 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.309 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.302 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.10.10): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (2026.10.10): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (b607675) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.10.10 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v27 -> v40 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 10 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main # existing 2026.10.10 index, before any re-index 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.331 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.323 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.316 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.309 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.302 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (this branch, no excludePaths): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**","memory/.dreams/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher: a local chat-completions stub calls `memory_search` once, through `dispatch_action`, because current main keeps `memory_search` behind Tool Search for this model. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within about 2 s and never indexes the report.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback ... # throwaway Gateway [gateway] ready $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "When does the nightly backup run?" # stub model calls memory_search once via dispatch_action Done. tool call: dispatch_action {"id":"memory_search","args":{"query":"nightly backup"}} # memory_search result paths (from the stub log): memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~2s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```
**Regressions fail without the fix:** - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` "rebaselines shared exclusions when a differently scoped agent joins and leaves" fails with `excludePaths` removed from `selectionKeys` ("expected setScopes to be called once, but got 0 times"). - `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` "drops generated Dream reports once excluded and keeps curated edits fresh" fails when the config resolver drops `excludePaths` (the report is still found). **Changed test files** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `685db0c`, same test code as `8eb4b7b`, where they pass again; CI seconds to follow): | File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` | 29 passed | 48s | 41.65s | | `manager-reindex-state.test.ts` | 49 passed | 40s | 36.19s | | `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` | 11 passed | 71s | 64.91s | | `watch-policy.test.ts` | 6 passed | 47s | 41.51s | | `internal.test.ts` | 43 passed | 4s | 749ms | | `memory-search.test.ts` | 39 passed | 46s | 42.06s | Vitest time is mostly cold transform; the new manager case takes about 4 s and the other new cases take 1-24 ms. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` on `83eb31b` (main `200afde`, same code) passes typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports, plugin boundaries and the other changed-file guards. Three lanes fail outside this PR: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection`) and the public Plugin SDK surface budget (`agent-harness-runtime`) fail identically on clean main `200afde`, and the dead-export scan lists only auto-reply, gateway and UI exports this PR does not touch. The `pnpm check:docs` content checks pass. Test lines grow by a net +145, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/memory-search-exclude-paths-188294.txt`: default scope-hash compatibility, the shared-watcher rebaseline, discovery and glob matching, and the exclusion rebuild. **PR CI:** earlier runs had failures inherited from main: `read-file.test.ts` after the fs-safe 0.26.14 bump (#188352) and `archive-restore.postgres.test.ts` from #155538, both fixed on main (#188531, `34a4e118dc1`), then `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` while main was over its test-line ceiling (main's own scheduled job logged the same overage with net delta 0). #188780 restored the headroom. The branch now merges main `bf10667` at `1cc43f3`; earlier merges conflicted only on the generated config baseline, which was regenerated each time, and the PR diff is unchanged. The v2026.10.10 proof above ran on `b607675`; the merge after it brought in only main's changes and the regenerated baseline. Main's #191749 bounded the realpath deduplication at the end of `listMemoryFiles`; it merges cleanly because `excludePaths` filters files as they are collected, before that step. On `1cc43f3`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` fails because main is over its own test-line ceiling: main `bf10667` alone has 6,446,635 test lines against a ceiling of 6,446,498 (over by 137), and this PR adds +145 covered by its 145-line allocation, so CI reports "over by: 137; net delta: +145". Main's own scheduled CI run on `3400782` logged the same state ("over by: 47; net delta: 0. Tree is over the ceiling; this change does not add test lines") and passed only because that run added no test lines, so `ci-gate` classifies this failure as new and fails. Latest main `b215829` is still over by 145 on its own, so merging it would not clear the check; I will merge main once its count is back under the ceiling. `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `config:docs:check` pass, and the touched tests plus `memory-files-worker.test.ts`, `workspace-memory-client.test.ts` and `manager-search-orchestration.test.ts` (files main also changed) pass. `checks-node-changed` on `a63b2b5` failed in `plugin-sdk-package-contract-guardrails.test.ts` after main's #188833 referenced an untyped SDK entrypoint in a guide; main fixed it in #188937, and that test passes locally on `1cc43f3`. prs.title: fix(transcripts): auto-start shutdown stalls past its stop budget when the wall clock steps
prs.body:
Related: #185146, #186484

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway transcript auto-start shutdown waits far beyond its five-second pending-start budget when the wall clock moves backward during shutdown.

## User Impact

Operators retain the intended pending-start cleanup budget during shutdown/restart even after a system clock correction. This does not abandon in-flight cleanup: the original provider owner still joins and finishes when its transport settles. Stored transcript timestamps remain wall-clock timestamps.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts` clock for both the deadline and its rechecks, with no local clock helper. Existing failed-start custody coverage now exercises backward/forward wall-clock steps, and affected fixtures fake `performance` together with `Date`. Consolidated the separate added regression into that owner suite: test delta 0; production delta +2 against the merge base.

## Evidence

Both revisions fully built in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker. A normally registered public transcript-source plugin models a transport still starting while the built Gateway auto-start service shuts down. Only `Date.now` in that isolated process is stepped; the system clock is untouched. Native Gateway startup, configured capture admission, SIGTERM, provider abort and stop-budget warning are observed rather than invoking the service helper directly. Detailed captures are in the evidence comment.

Focused affected suites: 64 tests pass. Formatting and type-aware lint pass. The same backward-step regression on main remains pending after its five-second fake-timer advance and hits the external 120-second watchdog; the forward-step case completes. Its matching built-Gateway reproduction records the approximately 65-second wait.

Observed before/after captures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187156#issuecomment-6486158779

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting restores prior timeout behavior without a migration or persisted-contract change. Blast radius is pending transcript auto-start cleanup during shutdown or provider replacement; transcript content, source authorization and completed-capture cleanup remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(telegram): release account throttlers for retired bot tokens
prs.body:
Related: gap finding `gap-telegram-throttler-token-leak` (hot-update token rotation / repeated account add-remove, evidence level A — real Gateway process logs + unit/integration tests)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: rotating a Telegram bot token or removing a Telegram account leaks the old token's limiter — Bottleneck heartbeat timers and memory grow monotonically until the Gateway is restarted.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can now rotate bot tokens and remove Telegram accounts on a long-running Gateway without leaked Bottleneck heartbeat timers and cache entries accumulating for every retired token; the retirement runs inside the Gateway process on the config hot-reload stop, settling queued sends and not-yet-dispatched chat actions before disconnecting the old token's limiter while in-flight requests finish. A chat action sleeping in its 401 authorization backoff settles immediately at retirement — for group and DM dispatch alike — and never sends on the retired token. No config or behavior change for steady-state operation; the per-token shared throttling contract is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`getOrCreateAccountThrottler` caches one throttler per bot token in a process-global map with no eviction path, and grammY's `apiThrottler()` never exposes its Bottleneck instances, so each retired token left 3 perpetual `setInterval` timers (250 ms reservoir heartbeat + two group auto-cleanup loops) plus its object graph in memory forever. This change mirrors the upstream `apiThrottler()` defaults in an owned factory (`grammy-api-throttler.ts`) so the limiters can be disconnected, and retires the token's throttler in the process that owns the map:

- **Gateway-side retirement:** the CLI lifecycle hooks (`onAccountConfigChanged` / `onAccountRemoved`) never run inside the Gateway that holds the map. All three account lifecycle hooks (config change, removal, `gateway.stopAccount`) now release the throttler once the token is no longer configured for any account. Unchanged-token reloads and manual stops keep the limiter so flood penalty state survives restarts; a shared token used by another account is never released.
- **Settling queued work:** retirement stops admissions first (a `retired` gate rejects later calls on the captured transformer and prevents new group limiter creation), rejects queued group sends and not-yet-dispatched chat actions immediately, re-checks retirement after the action pacing sleep and again at the shared final dispatch boundary — including after the 401 authorization backoff, for DM and group actions alike — then `limiter.stop({ dropWaitingJobs: true })` — queued sends reject with a clear BottleneckError while running sends finish — and only then disconnects, clears the group auto-cleanup intervals, and drops the map entry. Disposal is idempotent. Backing-off group actions stay tracked for retirement settlement until their transport dispatch actually begins, so their callers settle right away instead of waiting out the backoff.
- **Thin channel hooks:** the rotated/removed/stopped release operations live in `account-throttler-lifecycle.ts`; `channel.ts` returns under its 700-line cap.

## Evidence

### Waiting requests settle during retirement (production client, real timers)

A production-client script (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-settlement-169536.mjs`) drives the shipped `account-throttler` module through the real production undici transport (`resolveTelegramTransport` + `createTelegramClientFetch`, the same stack the Gateway uses) against the loopback Bot API stub, with real timers and real Bottleneck. It parks one send in flight, queues a second send behind it, arms the 401 authorization backoff with a group action, parks a second action in that backoff, and retires the token:

```
PROOF live intervals after throttler create: 3
PROOF send A dispatched and held in flight by the stub (3s)
PROOF send B queued behind the in-flight send
PROOF action C failed with 401 (backoff armed)
PROOF action D sleeping in authorization backoff
PROOF releaseAccountThrottler -> true after 1428ms (waits for the in-flight send to finish)
PROOF in-flight send A: fulfilled
PROOF waiting send B:   rejected: This limiter has been stopped.
PROOF backing-off action D: rejected: Telegram throttler for this token has been released
PROOF intervals: after create=3 before release=3 after release=0 (created=3, cleared=3)
PROOF stub sendMessage requests total: 1 (expected 1)
PROOF stub sendChatAction requests total: 1 (expected 1)
PROOF OK: waiting sends and actions settled, in-flight send preserved, intervals reclaimed

=== STUB LOG ===
stub listening on http://127.0.0.1:19877
2026-10-13T02:44:50.265Z  sendMessage      111:proof-token  held=3000ms
2026-10-13T02:44:50.332Z  sendChatAction   111:proof-token  first-action=401
```

The waiting send settles with Bottleneck's "limiter has been stopped", the backing-off action settles immediately with the released error, the in-flight send completes through the real transport after its 3 s hold, all three live intervals are reclaimed, and the stub records exactly one sendMessage and one sendChatAction — no dispatch ever reaches the retired token after retirement. Tokens are synthetic (`111:proof-token`); no credentials appear.

### Real Gateway process (built from this branch, this revision)

A full build of this branch (rebased on current upstream main) was run and the Gateway launched from that build with an isolated state directory and port (`gateway run --port 19876 --auth none`), talking to a local loopback Bot API stub (`apiRoot: http://127.0.0.1:19877`). Tokens are synthetic (`111:...`/`222:...`); no credentials appear in the logs. Both retirement paths were driven through the real config hot-reload.

**Rotation with an in-flight reply.** An unpaired DM reached the Gateway; its pairing reply `sendMessage` was held in flight by the stub (3 s). The token was rotated while the reply was still held:

```
2026-10-13T04:21:26.XXXZ  (stub) sendMessage 111:proof-token  held=3000ms
2026-10-13T12:21:04.187+08:00 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (channels.telegram.accounts.default.botToken)
2026-10-13T12:21:04.286+08:00 [reload] config change requires channel reload (telegram) — deferring until 1 gateway request(s) complete
2026-10-13T12:21:27.926+08:00 [gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
2026-10-13T12:21:27.962+08:00 [telegram] [default] released retired Telegram account throttler
2026-10-13T12:21:27.966+08:00 [reload] config hot reload applied (channels.telegram.accounts.default.botToken)
2026-10-13T12:21:28.001+08:00 [telegram] [default] starting provider (@proof_bot_222)
2026-10-13T12:21:28.004+08:00 [telegram] Detected bot identity change for account "default" (was 111, now 222); discarding stale update offset 1 and starting fresh.
```

The hot reload deferred until the held `sendMessage` completed, the in-flight request succeeded (no failure logged), and only then did the retirement release the throttler — the "preserve already-running I/O" contract through the real transport client.

**Account removal.** Dropping the whole `channels.telegram` section produced the second release on the same Gateway run:

```
2026-10-13T12:21:30.596+08:00 [gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
2026-10-13T12:21:30.612+08:00 [telegram] [default] released retired Telegram account throttler
```

**Clean token cutover (stub log).** The stub recorded every authenticated request: exactly one `sendMessage` on the retired token (completed after the hold), none on the new token, and no retired-token request after the rotation:

```
2026-10-13T04:21:27.168Z  getUpdates   111:proof-token   <- last long poll by the retired token
2026-10-13T04:21:27.984Z  getMe        222:proof-token   <- restart one second later
```

After rotation no `111:proof-token` request appears again: the retired token stops polling entirely instead of leaking a live long poll — the same leak class this PR eliminates for the throttle limiter.

Full redacted logs in this checkout: `.openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-gateway-169536.log` and `.openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-stub-169536.log` (driver: `.openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-driver-169536.mjs`, stub: `.openclaw/.tmp/telegram-proof-stub.mjs`).

### Waiting actions settle and never dispatch after retirement (unit)

`account-throttler.test.ts` regressions for the action lane, covering the retirement windows:

- `settles a pacing action and never dispatches it when the account is retired` — the successor is sleeping out its one-second pacing window when the token is released; its caller settles immediately and the dispatch counter stays at 1.
- `settles actions queued behind a running predecessor when the account is retired` — retirement while the predecessor's dispatch is in flight settles the queued successor immediately; the in-flight I/O completes; the dispatch counter stays at 1.
- `settles a backing-off action immediately when the account is retired` (revised in this revision) — the successor parks in the 401 authorization backoff after pacing; releasing the token during that backoff settles its caller **at release time** (asserted before any further timer advancement), and advancing 10 minutes afterwards still produces no dispatch.
- `never dispatches a DM action whose authorization backoff outlives retirement` (new in this revision) — the DM successor parks in the 401 backoff; retiring during the backoff rejects it with the released error and the final dispatch never reaches the API.

Baseline: both new/revised regressions fail on the pre-fix source (previous commit `ba17964a2af`): the group regression reports `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times` (no immediate settlement) and the DM regression reports `promise resolved "true" instead of rejecting` (the retired token dispatched). The low-value `keeps releasing other tokens independent` test was removed per review.

### Queued sends settle on release (unit)

`account-throttler.test.ts` `stops timers and settles queued sends on release`: with the default owned limiter, a second DM send queued behind a running one rejects with `This limiter has been stopped` when the token is released, the live `setInterval` handle set returns to zero (all heartbeats/cleanup timers cleared), and a later call on the captured transformer rejects with `Telegram throttler for this token has been released` without creating new limiters.

### Retire gate blocks queued group sends and fresh work (unit)

`account-throttler.test.ts` `rejects queued group sends and new work once the account is retired`: retirement settles the group sends already queued on the group limiter, rejects a later group send with a clear `BottleneckError`, clears the group engine timers, and a subsequent call on the captured transformer is rejected by the retired gate without creating a new group limiter.

### Before/after timer probe

Probe counting `setInterval`/`clearInterval` against the real code path (`getOrCreateAccountThrottler` + `releaseAccountThrottler`):

```
baseline:                          created=0  cleared=0
after create (1 token entry):      created=3  cleared=2
after 2 rotations (3 entries):     created=9  cleared=6
after releasing all 3 entries:     created=9  cleared=15   (+9 real clears, net 0 leaked timers)
```

Before the fix the same rotation sequence left all 9 timers firing until process exit. The production-client trace above re-confirms the same balance with real timers (`after create=3 … after release=0`).

Behavior parity with upstream grammY defaults is anchored by the pre-existing reservoir tests (e.g. "preserves the group message budget while sending topic actions": 30/msg-min global + 20/msg-min per group chat).

### Local verification on this revision

- `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/account-throttler.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 23/23; `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/channel.gateway.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 27/27 (includes the restored removal-hook regression `releases the removed account's throttler`); `pnpm test test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 17/17
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: 0 errors; oxlint clean on the changed files; `pnpm format` clean on the changed files

The previous head's `checks-node-compact-small-6` failure was an inherited red-main window (duplicate `transcript-entry-anchor.ts` wrapper-inventory entry on main between 12:04–12:36 UTC, fixed upstream by `30b2ef35d02`); the rebase clears it, and the test passes locally (17/17).

- Live Telegram end-to-end (no real Bot API traffic): the change is transport-independent lifecycle plumbing; the Gateway-process proof above uses a loopback Bot API, the production-client trace uses the real undici transport, and existing HTTP-conformance suites cover the throttling contract.

- Accepted edge case: after retirement settles a backing-off action's caller, the bounded one-shot backoff timer (≤ 5 min) can still run to completion in the dead scheduler; it finishes into the final dispatch guard and can never send on the retired token. Reaching into the caller's AbortSignal to reclaim that timer would cross the grammY/undici signal-type boundary for a timer that is bounded and harmless.

prs.title: fix(telegram): album fetch failure warning always says "images"
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A partially downloaded Telegram album always produces a chat warning saying "images", even when the album contains videos or documents. For example, one downloaded member of a two-video album is reported as "Received 1 of 2 images".

## User Impact

The warning now names the album's actual native kind: images, videos, audio, files, or stickers. Mixed-kind albums use "attachments". The fetch-failure log likewise names the failed item's native kind rather than always saying "photo".

Counts, download limits, retry behavior, authorization, topic routing, and the structured attachment context sent to the agent are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing album owner already computes each message's native media kind. It now retains the set of kinds for the complete album, including unavailable members, and selects the warning noun from that set. No public API, SDK export, new setting, or parallel classification owner is introduced.

Contributor: @xialonglee. This repairs the album-warning gap described in this PR. Related earlier work: #82987 (warnings for failed photos in media groups).

## Evidence

[Real Telegram Test Server proof, native warning timelines, and captured agent input](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187497#issuecomment-6493372483).

Exact sources were built in isolated Linux ARM64 Node 24.22.1:

- Main: `c8a27378eecac4f7cb82110f682ca0284d0493a9`.
- Candidate: `ded9d0407e60ba7d81b1a4bf04c3c03f8d5c9abd`, contributor commit preserved unchanged.

A Convex-leased QA user sent real native video albums to fresh built Gateways. The existing inbound limit was lowered to 0.08 MiB, with one valid small video below the limit and one real valid video above it:

- **Twice on main:** "Received 1 of 2 images — 1 could not be fetched and was skipped."
- **Twice on candidate:** "Received 1 of 2 videos — 1 could not be fetched and was skipped."
- A mixed photo/video partial album changed from "1 of 2 images" to "1 of 2 attachments".
- Successful two-video and two-photo albums, plus a single successful video, produced no fetch warning on either ref.
- All six main agent requests per ref were captured. Partial albums retained one real attachment and `[media unavailable: 1 of 2 attachments could not be downloaded]`; successful albums retained two files and the single-video control retained one. This confirms that the agent context and counts were preserved, rather than implying that this PR changes the agent-side notice.

All sends and both recordings completed. Both run-owned forums were confirmed deleted. An interrupted harness attempt's forum was also recovered under a fresh active lease and deleted. Product processes were joined, private credential scratch and payload were removed, and the proof lease was explicitly released. Harness-only video sending and stream-cancellation extensions were identical on both refs and are explained in the linked evidence; no API data was fabricated.

The contributor's two existing regression cases cover homogeneous video and mixed-kind warnings. This repair pass added and ran zero tests; those fixture cases are supporting coverage, not the live proof above. Simplification retained the existing warning and native-kind owners. Whole-PR deltas are production +24/-2 and tests +104/-0 across two files; the growth is limited to the noun distinction and its two regression boundaries.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting fully restores the old warning strings, without a schema, state, configuration, or published API migration. Blast radius is the wording of Telegram partial-album warnings and the matching fetch-failure log; media delivery, counts, permissions, and retry policy are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(agents): a Claude 5-hour limit reply shows generic failure copy instead of the reset time
prs.body:
Related: #190750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a run that exhausts a subscription's usage window ends with `The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.` — even when the provider's own reply states when the window resets, and even when that reset is days away.

## User Impact

User impact: when a usage window is used up and no fallback model is left to run, the chat now carries the provider's bounded wording with its reset time (`You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm`) instead of advice to retry in a few minutes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reported symptom had two independent causes, and the second one is why the first alone is not enough.

**1. The window was not recognized.** `PERIODIC_USAGE_LIMIT_RE` accepted only calendar windows — `daily` / `weekly` / `monthly` — plus their Chinese equivalents. Rolling windows (`5-hour`, `hourly`) describe the same condition with the same reset hint but did not match, so `isPeriodicUsageLimitErrorMessage` answered false for the Claude CLI reply. `retry-evidence.ts` already ORs this predicate next to its own long-window check, so extending the one owner of this concept also makes hour-shaped windows count as long-window retry evidence.

The pattern stays narrow on purpose: the window token has to lead the word `limit` (`hourly limit`, `5-hour limit`, `24 hour limit`). Unrelated durations such as `request timeout after 2 hours` or `The limit is 2 hours` still do not match.

**2. The quota copy was unreachable from the terminal reply.** `buildExternalRunFailureReply` is the single renderer every channel uses for a failed run. It consults the quota copy path only after rate-limit retries are exhausted, and `resolveReplyFailoverFacts` — which supplies `requestFailureText` — never consulted it at all. So a quota that names its reset time fell through to `renderAssistantRequestFailureCopy`, whose `rate_limit` entry is the fixed "try again in a few minutes" sentence. That affected calendar windows too: on current `main`, a weekly quota with an explicit reset date renders as "try again in a few minutes" through the same function, which is wrong by days.

`resolveReplyFailoverFacts` now forwards the quota renderer's output when the failure text names a periodic usage window. That renderer already sanitizes and bounds the provider line, so no raw provider text is introduced here; a plain `429 slow down` still gets the existing generic copy.

## Evidence

### The shipped reply renderer, before and after

`buildExternalRunFailureReply` is the function that produces the text any channel sends. Same call, same input, `includeDetails: false`:

Before (current `main`):

```text
in : 429 You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm
out: ⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.

in : 429 You have reached your weekly limit; resets Monday 09:00 UTC
out: ⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.

in : 429 You are being rate limited, slow down
out: ⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.
```

After:

```text
in : 429 You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm
out: ⚠️ You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm

in : 429 You have reached your weekly limit; resets Monday 09:00 UTC
out: ⚠️ You have reached your weekly limit; resets Monday 09:00 UTC

in : 429 You are being rate limited, slow down
out: ⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.
```

The second row is a defect on current `main` that this change also fixes: a calendar-window quota whose reset is days away was telling the user to retry in a few minutes. The third row is the deliberate non-goal — a rate limit that names no window keeps its existing copy.

### The committed regressions fail without the fix

`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts`, with `request-error-facts.ts` reverted and the new tests kept:

```text
vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "subscription usage window"
  Tests  1 failed | 21 skipped (22)
  expected '⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.' to equal '⚠️ You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm'
```

With the fix in place:

```text
vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  22 passed (22)
```

### Classification before / after

Judged with the exported function on the same strings.

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm` | false | **true** |
| `5-hour limit reached ∙ resets 11pm` | false | **true** |
| `hourly limit reached` | false | **true** |
| `24 hour limit exceeded` | false | **true** |
| `You have reached your weekly limit` | true | true |
| `daily usage limit exceeded` | true | true |
| `402 Payment Required: Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted` | true | true |
| `已达到 Token Plan 用量上限` | true | true |
| `request timeout after 2 hours` | false | false |
| `The limit is 2 hours` | false | false |
| `rate limit 5 requests per hour` | false | false |

### Checks run

```text
vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts --maxWorkers=1                -> 22 passed
vitest run src/agents/failover/user-copy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1                                   -> 25 passed
vitest run src/agents/failover/classify.test.ts \
           src/agents/failover/retry-evidence.test.ts \
           src/agents/failover/failover-classification.corpus.test.ts --maxWorkers=1              -> 125 passed
oxfmt --check (all four touched files)                                                            -> clean
```

### Gaps

This is not a Discord replay. The proof runs the shipped reply renderer that every channel calls, with the same function and inputs a channel failure produces, and shows the rendered text changing; it does not stand up a Discord client. The sanitizer remains the second gate — copy without a reset time is still replaced with the generic message, which is existing intended behaviour and is why the new assertions pin the reset hint rather than the raw provider text.

`#172065` (open) changes failover behaviour when a fallback candidate exists. This PR covers the surface that remains when none does, so the two are complementary rather than overlapping.
