prs.title: fix(msteams): message search misses text in a different Unicode normalization form
prs.body:
Relates to gap finding: msteams-message-search-unicode-nfc (analysis, evidence level A)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: MS Teams message search misses messages whose text differs from the query only in Unicode normalization form (e.g. a message sent from a macOS/iOS Teams client cannot be found with the same accented text typed on Windows, and vice versa).

## User Impact

User impact: searching messages in an MS Teams chat or channel now matches text canonically — accents and other combining characters match regardless of whether the message or the query was composed in NFC or NFD form. No behavior change for exact matches.

## Why This Change Was Made

`searchMessagesMSTeams` lowercased both the query and the message text but never Unicode-normalized either side, and `String.prototype.includes` compares code points, so canonically-equivalent strings in different normalization forms never matched. Both sides are now normalized with `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(...).normalize("NFC")` before comparison, following the repo's existing NFC search convention (memory-core, memory-wiki, beam, x, discord plugins).

## Evidence

### Before fix

New regression tests fail on the base implementation (3 failed, 18 passed):

```
FAIL > searchMessagesMSTeams > matches message text across Unicode normalization forms
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'msg-nfd' ]
FAIL > searchMessagesMSTeams > matches NFC message text from an NFD query
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'msg-nfc' ]
FAIL > searchMessagesMSTeams > normalizes HTML-stripped content before matching
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'msg-html' ]
```

Runtime check of the comparison: `"café".normalize("NFD").toLowerCase().includes("café".toLowerCase())` → `false` in both directions; NFC-normalizing both sides → `true`.

### After fix

`pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/graph-messages.read.test.ts` — 21/21 passed (18 pre-existing + 3 new Unicode normalization cases covering NFD content × NFC query, NFC content × NFD query, and HTML-stripped NFD content × NFC query).

- `oxlint` on changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `format:check` on changed files: clean
- Full-project typecheck could not run on this host (pinned native tsgo requires glibc ≥ 2.32; classic-tsc fallback OOMs) — covered by CI.

## What was not tested

- Live Graph API round trip against a real Teams tenant (unit-level proof only; the comparison change is local string preprocessing around the existing mocked-Graph test harness).
- Sender display-name matching (`matchesSearchSender`) is a separate, narrower exact-equality comparison and is intentionally left unchanged.

prs.title: fix(msteams): channel directory search drops channels with NFD-normalized names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: MS Teams channel directory search silently drops channels whose displayName differs in Unicode normalization form (e.g. NFD-stored names from macOS clients vs NFC-typed queries, or NFD queries from macOS input methods vs NFC-stored names).

## User Impact

User impact: searching the Teams channel directory now matches channel names regardless of NFC/NFD normalization differences; previously matching channels were silently missing from results. Pure-ASCII names behave exactly as before, and returned entries keep their original spelling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel-name substring filter in `listMSTeamsDirectoryGroupsLive` compared trim+lowercased strings at the UTF-16 code-unit level without canonical-equivalence normalization, so canonically equal names failed `includes()` and were skipped. Both the query side and the displayName side now go through `.normalize("NFC")`, matching the existing directory-search idiom in `extensions/buzz/src/directory-query.ts` ("Canonical forms compare equal here; directory entries keep their original spelling"). Team-name search is unchanged (server-side Graph `$search`); the peers path is also server-side.

## Evidence

### Before fix

New regression tests on unpatched code fail (channels silently dropped):


prs.title: fix(agents): keep MCP startup backoff and failure cooldowns on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MCP startup backoff, catalog retries and repeated tool-failure cooldowns currently depend on wall time. A clock correction can reconnect a failing server early or keep a recovered server unavailable long after its intended cooldown.

## User Impact

Configured MCP servers retain their existing elapsed retry windows across forward and backward wall-clock steps. Human-facing retry messages remain ISO timestamps. Display/bookkeeping timestamps remain on the wall clock.

## Fix

Use the existing `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts` owner for core deadline reads and writes, converting remaining time to wall time only when rendering retry messages. No local helper, new retry policy, configuration, SDK or state format. The contributor's original commit is retained.

Clock regressions reuse the existing startup/catalog recovery cases rather than adding duplicate fixture/test scaffolding. Existing Date/performance fake-clock coverage and the performance-based catalog-expiry spy remain coherent.

Related monotonic deadline precedents: #185704, #184711, #184056, #183356. This does not alter the request-lifecycle fix in #184056.

## Evidence

[Captured built-Gateway traces through a real local MCP transport](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187198#issuecomment-6487397647).

- Baseline main: `61e0cf581df7cea360bb7670b136e59b8d8105aa`.
- Candidate: `9d2648c7fd8a3aef2677027110a78ca30519bcac`.
- Ordinary agent turns use Tool Search, tool_describe and dispatch_action against a real Streamable HTTP MCP server, driven by a credential-free local model fixture.
- Tool cooldown, twice per direction: main admits a fourth request early after +10m and still blocks after 61 real seconds with -10m; candidate blocks the early request and recovers after the real cooldown. No-step controls pass twice on both builds.
- Separate startup/catalog transport failures reproduce early and late retries twice each on main. Candidate retains the five-second first-owner/catalog window, with no-step controls twice for each failure kind.
- Only Date.now is stepped inside task Gateway processes; performance/timers and the system clock are unchanged.
- Both frozen installs/full builds and targeted formatting/lint passed. All 62 focused tests pass in Docker, including real stdio cases. Final regression on main: 2 failed, 9 passed.
- Whole PR delta: production +6 net lines (shared-helper imports), tests 0.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the original in-process clock arithmetic; no persisted-state migration. Blast radius is recovery scheduling for failing configured MCP servers. Retry durations, authorization-denial suppression, first-owner early retry, connection recycling, tool policies and catalog publication boundaries stay unchanged.

prs.title: fix(matrix): live directory search misses rooms with canonically equivalent Unicode names

## What Problem This Solves

Matrix live-directory group lookup omits joined rooms when the stored name and query have canonically equivalent NFC/NFD Unicode spellings.

## User Impact

The same joined room can be found with composed or decomposed text. Existing case-insensitivity and original returned names/handles remain intact. No configuration or migration is required.

## Fix

Apply NFC after lowercasing only to the local room comparison operands. Do not normalize stored values, direct room aliases or peer-directory HTTP search terms. Peers remain matched by the homeserver. This uses the existing local comparison owner without a shared SDK helper or another lookup path.

## Evidence

[Built CLI + real Synapse differential and exact HTTP terms](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187881#issuecomment-6508752525):
- Frozen main `1dca2e5bcb91d3d42895112f78a7a2d325b95e84`: both opposite-composition room queries return no rooms, twice each.
- Built candidate: both directions return the correct joined room, twice each, with original name/handle bytes preserved.
- Actual shipped `directory groups list --channel matrix --query ... --json`, bundled Matrix plugin, real Synapse users/rooms/aliases created through Matrix APIs. Secretless Node24.22.1 Docker, explicit isolated profiles/config/state/SQLite paths. No mocked directory responses, private helper imports, real personal account or UI claim.
- ASCII and same-form NFC/NFD controls pass on both refs.
- Actual alias GET URLs preserve their mixed case and NFD/NFC percent encoding on both refs. Actual peer POST `search_term` fields preserve exact raw casing/composition; evidence includes UTF-8 hex identities.
- All22 lookup CLI processes exited0; Synapse gracefully stopped with exit0.
- Focused regressions: **8 passed**. The retained bidirectional table fails on main in both forms. Consolidation replaces duplicated mock fixtures and the weaker mocked alias happy-path check with real Synapse alias controls; tests **+9/-11 (net−2)**.

Final head `8003b993e3f45ce9ef6cec1c0a9a1a2e6b7009a9` changes only tests after the proven contributor build; production remains **+3/-2**, unchanged. Contributor commit retained. No storage, schema, dependency, permission or SDK changes.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous local matching behavior; no data is rewritten or migrated. Blast radius is the Matrix joined-room name filter only. Direct alias lookup and delegated peer search retain their existing wire contracts, covered by real homeserver controls.

prs.title: fix(line,tlon): redact credentials reflected in remote API error bodies
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

LINE and Tlon can expose credentials in thrown errors when an API or proxy reflects request authentication in a rejected response. This follows the shared diagnostic-redaction pattern in #141317.

## Changes

Redact rejected response bodies before constructing LINE send errors and Tlon poke/subscription errors. Boundaries use the shared `redactToolPayloadText` SDK helper. Tlon additionally masks bare `urbauth-` cookie reflections through its credential-owning plugin helper. Shared core redaction policy is unchanged.

HTTP status, useful diagnostic text, authentication/signatures, response-size limits, and delivery semantics are unchanged. The shared owner uses its existing diagnostic masking convention. Arbitrary value-only reflections without recognizable credential syntax are not covered by this change.

## Evidence

Built baseline `b0c330d27df4a528f65185cc3e509284d1b218d9` and the updated candidate in isolated Docker, then ran the real `openclaw message send` CLI for both channels against local credential reflectors returning HTTP 503.

- LINE: the actual thrown `HTTPFetchError.body` contains the full synthetic token on base and a masked token on candidate. The observer records the completed Error object; transport, request authentication, and response parsing remain real. The CLI itself displays only the status on both revisions.
- Tlon: base CLI error exposes the reflected session cookie; candidate masks it. `Poke failed: 503`, `reflector unavailable`, and `retry later` remain.
- LINE uses its normal HTTPS URL, resolved to a container-local TLS reflector with a task CA. Tlon uses its supported ship URL pointed at a local HTTP reflector.
- `pnpm tsgo:prod` passed (core, UI, and extensions).
- Focused LINE send, Tlon outbound-loopback, and Tlon error-boundary tests passed. CLI reflector checks cover both the contributor design and its maintained revision.
- No live LINE/Tlon vendor delivery is claimed.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

Original fix and reflector regressions by @xialonglee; CLI proof and current-main integration added during maintenance.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores prior diagnostic handling; no state migration, configuration change, or authentication change. Blast radius is LINE/Tlon rejected-response diagnostics.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): keep emoji whole at free-text caps in cards, statements and excerpts
prs.body:
Related: #181741, #182776

## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge claim cards, related statements and evidence excerpts can end with a lone UTF-16 surrogate when an existing free-text cap lands inside an emoji. The streaming evidence path can also fill the unused unit with a later newline, producing text that is no longer a source prefix.

## User Impact

These bounded previews now preserve surrogate pairs and remain contiguous source prefixes. Existing caps and truncation flags remain; complete claim bodies and retained originals are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` already exports `truncateUtf16Safe`. The changed projections consume that supported helper directly; the duplicated `truncateWhole` implementation is removed. No SDK source or export is changed.

Once a streaming piece is shortened, a request-local flag stops further preview accumulation. Hashing, locator verification and full-source character counting continue normally. This avoids appending later lines into the one unused UTF-16 unit.

## Evidence

[Independent built-Gateway before/after trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186083#issuecomment-6450374246): ordinary Gateway agent turns execute the registered Knowledge tools through a deterministic local tool-calling provider. Sources are attached and claims/continuity links authored through public tools, not raw vault edits or private service calls. Actual tool results forwarded to the provider are captured.

- Main twice: claim cards, related statements and default evidence previews end with U+D83D at 4,000 units.
- Repaired candidate twice: those outputs are valid 3,999-unit prefixes; stored bodies remain unchanged.
- Buffered and over-17-MiB streaming sources exercise the real inspector threshold. At the larger 20,000-unit preview cap, the intermediate contributor implementation returns a later newline only on the streaming path. Repaired buffered/streamed excerpts are identical valid 19,999-unit prefixes.
- Full source hashes, sizes, a locator quote after the cut, and truncation flags remain verified.
- The multiline inspector regression fails before the latch repair. Four focused files pass **24/24** after it; touched lint and formatting pass.

Existing ASCII, complete-emoji, hash, locator, pagination, lifecycle and batching coverage remains. Regression cases share existing owner fixtures rather than adding duplicate suites: the complete change has **net zero test-line growth**. Production is net +8 lines; the existing Knowledge tool reference documents the preview behavior.

## Not Fixed Here

Short-field caps on titles, labels and diagnostic messages in other Knowledge owners are outside this repair. This preserves UTF-16 surrogate pairs; it does not introduce grapheme-cluster truncation or rewrite previously stored text.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: a revert restores the prior preview projections. No configuration, SDK API, stored-record format or schema migration changes. Blast radius is Knowledge card, related-statement and evidence-preview output.


### Source-worker dependency verification

The existing Knowledge worker SDK alias table now declares the reused text-utility facade. This fixes the Bun source-mode child import without changing any SDK export. On `b6c10e0e60080882e240bc534f94d063bf093dd7`, the two affected child-process test files pass 18/18 on Node and 18/18 on the pinned Bun fork, and the rebuilt shipped Knowledge flow passes twice again: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186083#issuecomment-6450715785.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report real token usage from the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/v1/embeddings` reports zero token usage even when the embedding provider returns actual token counts.

## User Impact

Clients receive provider-reported counts through native Ollama and OpenAI-compatible embedding transports. Providers that report zero keep zero; missing or incomplete counts remain zero without estimates. Existing embedding plugins retain their vector-only return values. No configuration, stored data, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Usage was discarded by response parsers, and the Gateway hard-coded both usage fields. The existing embedding call options now carry an optional `onUsage` observer. Parsers validate external counts, providers report each successful upstream response, and the Gateway sums complete reports. The same call path preserves model preload, service leases, cancellation, and deadlines; separate detailed-batch methods and their duplicate lifecycle wrappers are removed.

This preserves @xialonglee's original commits and contribution while merging current main and simplifying the implementation. Production: **+95/−84** (net +11, reduced from the original net +178); tests/support: **+123/−30**; docs: **+9/−0**; assertion baseline: **−1** for the removed Ollama cast. The remaining production growth supplies the optional typed observer and validates provider counts.

## Evidence

Baseline captured before repair: `ea6022cae60c509d8c0e8029ad8030557a917617`, real isolated Gateway on loopback port 19232. With `["alpha","beta"]`, direct Ollama reports 7 tokens for `bge-m3` and 6 for `nomic-embed-text`; both the native and `/v1` Gateway paths returned 0/0. LM Studio `text-embedding-nomic-embed-text-v1.5` reports upstream 0/0.

The existing Gateway regression failed on main production at its usage assertion (upstream 777/778, Gateway 0/0; wall 264.23s), then passed after the repair. All **116 tests across five files passed**, combined wrapper wall **226.87s**:

| File | Passing tests | Vitest duration |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Gateway embeddings HTTP | 32 | 93.87s |
| OpenAI-compatible provider | 9 | 31.59s |
| Native Ollama provider | 43 | 61.98s |
| Remote response parsing | 29 | 0.532s |
| Remote provider grouping | 3 | 2.75s |

The Gateway tests reuse the existing suite server. The changed HTTP usage assertion took 59ms; the new split-usage cases exercise complete totals and missing reports without additional Gateway boots. Provider tests cover singleton/batch reporting, zero, missing counts, and invalid counts.

Core and Ollama package typechecks, Gateway/plugins/packages test type graphs, scoped core/Ollama lint, SDK export checks, and all required baseline ratchets passed. Broad extension typechecking could not resolve QA Lab's `crabbox-provider` under the gateway-only dependency profile; the affected Ollama package was checked separately. An initial regression attempt overlapped setup and failed before test discovery on a generated-asset `ENOENT`; the settled run supplied the actual failing-before proof.

Live after proof on `b645ca800f3f17035796406f5f73cf9f14b5480e`, through the real isolated Gateway HTTP endpoint:

| Local provider/model | Before usage | After usage | Upstream count | Vector dimensions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Ollama native / bge-m3 | 0/0 | 7/7 | 7 | 1024 |
| Ollama native / nomic-embed-text | 0/0 | 6/6 | 6 | 768 |
| Ollama OpenAI-compatible / bge-m3 | 0/0 | 7/7 | 7/7 | 1024 |
| Ollama OpenAI-compatible / nomic-embed-text | 0/0 | 6/6 | 6/6 | 768 |
| LM Studio / nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 768 |

Every successful response contained two vectors. Example request (the `native` agent selects Ollama's native transport; `compat` selects its `/v1` transport):

```sh
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:19232/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GATEWAY_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-openclaw-model: bge-m3' \
  -d '{"model":"openclaw/native","input":["alpha","beta"]}'
```

The isolated Gateway was stopped after proof. Shared Ollama and LM Studio services were left running. Slash-containing overrides are handled separately in #161170.

Full `pnpm build` passed on the live-tested head `b645ca800f3f17035796406f5f73cf9f14b5480e` (wall **1694.45s**). The first full build reached final stamping but detected input changes while checks and maintenance were running; the successful retry was serialized with no concurrent writers. The earlier review preparation also refused changing artifacts, so the final independent review runs only after build and live proof settle.

Independent Codex branch autoreview was **scoped-clean** through P2 on the live-tested head, with final source verification passed.



### Final merge resolution

Main advanced while verification ran and introduced caller-owned HTTP deadlines in the generic embedding transport. Merged main `9c241fea9080083518a64a2b3278d3e7f391167e` without rewriting contributor history. The only conflict resolution preserves its `fetchWithCallerDeadline` dispatcher and reads the signal from `callOptions?.signal` instead of the removed `params.signal`. Merge-resolution head: `5c34c17e9d316bcb20981019ef5d5f5586f5eb18`.

On the resolved head, all **11 generic-provider tests** passed, including both new deadline cases (wall **287.61s**); core typechecking (41.23s), scoped type-aware core lint, and affected line-cap, max-lines, and assertion ratchets passed. The earlier lint invocation unnecessarily entered plugin declaration preparation and hit its timeout; the canonical core config completed without that unrelated preparation.

The real Gateway matrix and full build above belong to `b645ca8`; they were reused for unchanged usage mapping, and no live run is claimed for the mechanical merge resolution. ClawSweeper's first exact-head review found no code issues, accepted the live proof, and requested only this main-conflict repair.

Fresh independent Codex branch autoreview on `5c34c17e9d316bcb20981019ef5d5f5586f5eb18`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable P0–P2 findings; final source verification passed. The review explicitly checked the merged signal/deadline integration.



### Repair inherited CI fixture

CI run [38009841853](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38009841853/job/114087322212) on `5c34c17` exposed a deterministic 120 s timeout in `memory-runtime.owners.test.ts`'s `late-probe` case. Main commit `603f60a38cfe` (#167891) switched availability probes from `embedBatch` to `embed`, but the fixture still signaled its entry gate only from `embedBatch`. The real probe returned while the test waited forever for an unused stub. The exact new-main control also failed; older main passed.

Fixture-repair head `eb710ad903121ff3f0cea0b8406e4cb5a91b9d48` moves the existing gate and probe-call assertions to an `embed` mock returning a flat vector, while retaining a batch-shaped `embedBatch` fallback. This is a six-line test-only correction with no budget increase, retry, production seam, or weakened assertion. The ownership file passes 17/17 (wall 150.81s), and the original seven-file/two-worker CI selection passes 101/101 (wall 195.43s). Scoped test types, type-aware lint, and affected line-cap, timeout-race, and mock-export ratchets pass.

Fresh independent Codex branch autoreview on `eb710ad903121ff3f0cea0b8406e4cb5a91b9d48`: **scoped-clean** through P2; final source verification passed. The reviewer also checked the ownership-fixture correction.



### Preserve current response diagnostics

Main subsequently added contextual embedding errors in #168035. Final head `4f5fece0f60e1c1441bf80b0f0bbac5485d194b7` merges main `a0197f4921be56a09126b9b96f583c84423de342`, retaining its unknown-payload parsing, vector diagnostics, request/response logs, error mapping, and caller-abort behavior. Each adapter validates vectors before reporting usage. Usage assertions now use main's real HTTP Response fixture, including a valid JSON number that parses to infinity.

Both affected suites pass **43/43** (32 remote-response cases and 11 generic-provider cases), combined wall **266.85s**. Core typechecking (56.15s), canonical type-aware scoped lint, and affected line-cap/max-lines/assertion/mock-export ratchets pass. The proven ownership fixture remains intact. These integrations use focused proof; the full build and real local-model matrix remain explicitly attributed to `b645ca8`.

Fresh independent Codex branch autoreview on `4f5fece0f60e1c1441bf80b0f0bbac5485d194b7`: **scoped-clean** through P2; final source verification passed. Immediately before publication, a read-only merge against live main `e09f3ecd491db23f4fdc6e79b4349808d010f394` was clean.

Final-head `openclaw/ci-gate` passed in [run 38018085761](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38018085761/job/114114428272). [ClawSweeper’s exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154721#issuecomment-5759768702) found no code issues and accepted the live proof and focused integration checks. Its requested maintainer direction is recorded below. No merge has been requested.

### Maintainer direction

Use the additive, optional `EmbeddingProviderCallOptions.onUsage` callback as the supported public SDK contract for this repair. This is the requested design for propagating upstream embedding usage through the existing call contract. Preserve the vector return values of `embed` and `embedBatch`, compatibility with existing providers/callers, and zero usage when counts are unavailable. The callback adds no configuration, persistence, retention, or authority.


### Main conflict repair (current head)

Current head `d98e79d71fb13f7dbe0e0d4c6ca9c215034e5d22` merges main `2d6f7a3052a03867896f10d521969c78c4555d9a` into the contributor branch without rewriting history. The only manual conflict resolution combines the HTTP helper's optional model-override header with its upstream usage assertion. Both slash-containing model coverage and usage coverage remain; production code merged automatically.

Focused embeddings validation passed **123/123 tests across five files**, wall **590.51s**. After reconciling the worktree's stale dependencies with the merged frozen lockfile, core types passed (**160.66s**), Gateway test types passed (**55.32s**), and scoped type-aware lint passed (**84.11s**). Line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, database-worker, test-timeout-race, test-mock-exports, config-docs, and plugin-inventory checks all passed. Independent Codex review of the frozen merge candidate was **scoped-clean through P2**.

A supplemental HTTP rerun after dependency reconciliation failed during the existing `beforeAll` Gateway startup hook at its 180-second deadline; all 34 cases were skipped, and teardown then encountered the uncreated server. Its wall time was **766.67s**, including a cold compiled-worker rebuild. The setup/teardown path is unchanged by this PR and the conflict repair, but the local startup timeout remains unresolved; it is not represented as passing proof. No timeout increase or retry was used. Earlier live/build proof remains attached to its stated prior head. Current-head `openclaw/ci-gate` passed in [run 38024880303](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38024880303/job/114134860820); all 86 jobs completed successfully.

prs.title: fix(agents): record interrupted trajectory ending for restart-marked sessions
prs.body:
Closes #104950

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a gateway restart or crash could leave a main session marked `abortedLastRun: true` in its session state with no corresponding terminal event in its trajectory, making interrupted sessions silently disappear from audit, alerting, and retrospectives — no error count to alert on, and cron-triggered work products lose their durable record of why they stopped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The four producers that set `abortedLastRun: true` outside the normal attempt-settle path — the forced-restart marker, the startup-orphan marker, the force-cleared-run terminal state, and the admitted-recovery rollback — committed their state transition without recording a trajectory `session.ended` event. The normal attempt-settle path writes that event, but it never runs when the process dies.

This change:

- Adds an `afterWriteInTransaction` hook to `patchSessionEntryCore` and `applySessionEntryReplacements`. The hook runs synchronously inside the SQLite write transaction after the session entry is durable; throwing rolls the entire transaction back.
- Adds `src/trajectory/interrupted-end.ts` with `appendInterruptedSessionTrajectoryEndSync`, a synchronous helper that appends a canonical `session.ended` event with `status: "interrupted"` and `aborted: true`. Because it runs inside the caller's transaction, a failed append aborts the state change too.
- Resolves the trajectory SQLite target **before** opening the session write transaction in each producer, so filesystem and database-owner inspection no longer runs while the session write lock is held. The pre-resolved target is passed into the in-transaction append via `agentDatabasePath`/`agentDatabaseAgentId`.
- Wires the hook in all relevant producers: `createRestoreAdmittedRecoveryInterrupted` (records the terminal event only when the admitted-recovery transition is actually applied), the restart/startup orphaned-session marker (one event per marked session, atomically with the row write), and the force-cleared embedded run terminal state (records only when the row transition actually kills the run, so a stale force-clear against an already-killed row does not duplicate the event).
- Routes every post-admission pre-dispatch exit in the admission phase (user-turn preparation failure, admission revalidation failure, deferred outcome) through the same restore closure, which writes the interrupted terminal event atomically with the row rollback. Trajectory target resolution failure rejects the run **before** `admit_recovery` commits, while the row is still in its pre-admission state.
- Stamps the recovery state with the restored run identity so a second, independent restore closure for the same admitted attempt (Gateway execution vs. outer restart-dispatch failure path) stays a durable no-op and the interrupted terminal event records exactly once.
- Honors the shipped `OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY=0` capture opt-out with the same `parseBooleanValue` semantics as the normal runtime recorder (`src/trajectory/runtime.ts`): a capture-disabled process skips the terminal event but still commits its recovery-state transition.

The interrupted attempt's `lifecycleRunId` is preserved and stamped onto the terminal event, so trajectory export scopes its final-status cohort to that run ID and no longer filters out the interrupted ending.

The durable fixed-store owner (`storePath` + `agentId`) plumbing this PR originally carried through detection, recovery reads, recovery commits, and dispatch has since landed on `main` independently (`MainSessionRecoveryStoreTarget`, shared-store trajectory preservation in #138240, and the unified restart-recovery admission snapshots in #139233); this branch builds directly on that upstream plumbing instead of duplicating it.

The branch is rebased onto current `upstream/main` (`c8cb22a899a`) as a single commit (`e96e6e04bf2`).

## User Impact

Interrupted main sessions now leave a durable `session.ended` record in the trajectory, bound to the original run. Audit, alerting, and retrospective tools can see when and why a session was aborted, instead of the session vanishing silently after a restart or force-clear. A failed recovery admission no longer strands the session row: either the run is admitted and dispatched, or the row is restored with its interrupted terminal event.

## Evidence

### Regression test — trajectory append failure rolls back the state transition

`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-recovery-store.interrupted-trajectory-failure.test.ts` mocks `appendSqliteTrajectoryRuntimeEvents` to throw on the first call and verifies the admitted-recovery state transition is rolled back (`abortedLastRun: false`), no trajectory event is left behind, and a retry re-applies the transition and records the event atomically.

### Regression test — target resolution and post-admission preparation failures

`src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.restart-recovery.test.ts` covers:

- Trajectory target resolution failure rejects the run **before** `admit_recovery` commits; the row keeps `abortedLastRun: true` and no restore closure is needed.
- User-turn preparation failure **after** admission restores the row through the interrupted terminal-event path: `abortedLastRun: true`, cleared `lifecycleRunId`, one `session.ended` event with `status: "interrupted"` / `aborted: true`, and the pending recovery target re-scheduled.

### Regression test — accepted pre-start rollback through atomic owner-aware restore

`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` extends the default-owner accepted-then-fail test to assert the interrupted `session.ended` event is recorded, and adds an `ops`-owned fixed-store global session variant asserting the restore commits on the `ops` partition, the scheduled pending target carries `agentId: "ops"`, and exactly one trajectory event exists with `status: "interrupted"` / `aborted: true`.

### Regression test — cross-closure restore idempotency

`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-recovery-store.test.ts` builds two independent `createRestoreAdmittedRecoveryInterrupted` closures for one admitted run (as Gateway execution and the outer restart-dispatch failure path do) and asserts the first applies and records exactly one `session.ended` event while the second resolves `undefined` with no duplicate event. The test fails on the closure-local-only dedup, where the durable transition re-applies and double-counts the interruption.

### Regression test — capture opt-out

`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` sets `OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY=0` and asserts the restart marker still commits (`marked: 1`, `abortedLastRun: true`) while zero trajectory events are written. The test fails on the pre-fix writer, which appended unconditionally.

### Focused suites at the rebased head `e96e6e04bf2`

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/main-session-recovery
 Test Files  7 passed (7)
      Tests  284 passed (284)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.force-clear-terminal.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/trajectory/export.test.ts src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.restart-recovery.test.ts
 (all shards passed)
```

Lint (`run-oxlint.mjs`, 0 warnings / 0 errors) and `oxfmt --check` pass on all changed files at this head (`e96e6e04bf2`); core production typecheck (`run-tsgo.mts -p tsconfig.core.json`) reports no errors in any touched file.

### Real behavior proof — exact-head CI before/after on real SQLite (rebased head)

A secretless GitHub Actions workflow checked out the exact base and head SHAs independently and ran real SQLite-backed proof scripts against both, on the rebased head:

- Before (current `upstream/main`): `c8cb22a899a`
- After (PR head): `e96e6e04bf2`
- Proof run: https://github.com/xialonglee/openclaw/actions/runs/34243457114
- Artifact download: https://github.com/xialonglee/openclaw/actions/runs/34243457114/artifacts/10063021102

Proof markers from the run log — the before scene reproduces the gap on current `main`, the after scenes prove the fix on fresh stores, the existing-store scene proves pre-existing trajectory rows survive the interrupted append with correct reopen reads, and the opt-out scene proves `OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY=0` still commits the state transition while writing no event:

```text
[proof] scene=restart_marker_before status=pass marked=1 abortedLastRun=true events=0
[proof] scene=restart_marker_after status=pass marked=1 events=1
[proof] scene=admitted_recovery_rollback status=pass restored=true events=1
[proof] scene=existing_store_survives status=pass marked=1 priorEvents=2 newEvents=1
[proof] scene=capture_opt_out_skips_event status=pass marked=1 events=0
```

### Known tradeoff

During a graceful restart drain, a marked run that completes normally afterwards writes its own later terminal event (e.g. `success`), so the trajectory can contain `interrupted` followed by the true final status. Trajectory export already resolves the latest `session.ended` as authoritative (`findLast` in `src/trajectory/export.ts`), so consumers reading the final status see the truth; the interrupted record preserves the restart-marker fact.

### Durability contract (for maintainer acceptance)

Recovery-state commits are now coupled to the companion trajectory append: if the in-transaction `session.ended` append fails, the whole SQLite transaction — including the recovery-state change — rolls back. This is the intended contract (an interrupted state without its terminal record recreates the silent-gap bug), and it is the explicit design-acceptance point called out in review. The fresh/existing-store validation above was produced at the rebased head for this acceptance.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes HTTP 400 responses from `/v1/embeddings` when an explicitly configured model or `x-openclaw-model` override contains a slash, such as Ollama's `library/bge-m3` or `hf:org/model`.

## User Impact

Clients can use the complete embedding model ID with the agent's configured provider. A recognized prefix selecting a different provider still returns HTTP 400. The OpenAI `model` field remains an OpenClaw agent target.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway previously interpreted every slash as a provider separator. It now asks the existing embedding provider resolver whether the prefix names a provider; otherwise it forwards the full model ID. Redundant `auto` handling is removed from this consumer because memory configuration already owns that normalization.

Merged current main into the contributor branch and simplified the regressions into the existing HTTP fixture. Thanks @xialonglee for the original fix and regression; all contributor commits are preserved.

Compatibility: this changes request-time routing only. It does not write memory indexes or alter stored vectors, embedding metadata, schemas, migrations, configuration formats, or authentication. The after-proof reuses the isolated state/config created by main.

## Evidence

Baseline: main `ea6022cae60c509d8c0e8029ad8030557a917617`. Candidate: `80c9550d4ec6ca86db2283d8521fcde245d5974b`.

- Fail-on-main proof: both added HTTP cases fail with expected 200 / received 400; the ordinary model case passes. Wall time 267.83 s.
- Fixed full endpoint suite: 31/31 pass, wall time 252.05 s. The new cases take 28 ms and 29 ms using the existing suite-level Gateway. Whole-file wall time includes worker compilation, Gateway startup, and existing auth/lifecycle scenarios; no new Gateway boots or timers were added.
- Scoped oxlint, core and Gateway-root test typechecks pass. Required ratchets and plugin inventory pass. Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2.
- Full `pnpm build` passes (20m 44.4s on the shared host). The matching `ollama/bge-m3` override also returns 200 with 1024 dimensions.
- Exact-head [CI run 38000747791](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38000747791) and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. The `checks-node-changed` job took 254 s (whole-job duration, not isolated test-file timing); baseline ratchets took 94 s.
- Production LOC +9/-9; tests +39/-23; docs +2/-0. No changelog changes.

Live proof uses the real built Gateway on port 19232 and real local Ollama and LM Studio models, with input `["alpha","beta"]`:

| Route/model | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native Ollama `library/bge-m3` | 400 | 200, 1024 dimensions |
| Native Ollama `library/nomic-embed-text` | 400 | 200, 768 dimensions |
| Ollama `/v1`, `library/bge-m3` | 400 | 200, 1024 dimensions |
| Ollama `/v1`, `library/nomic-embed-text` | 400 | 200, 768 dimensions |
| LM Studio `text-embedding-nomic-embed-text-v1.5` | 200, 768 dimensions | 200, 768 dimensions |
| Native Ollama agent, different `openai` provider override | 400 | 400 |

The native/compatible agents use `memory.search.provider` values `ollama` and `openai-compatible`, with remote URLs `http://127.0.0.1:11434` and `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`; LM Studio uses port 1234. Representative request:

```sh
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:19232/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-openclaw-model: library/bge-m3' \
  -d '{"model":"openclaw/native","input":["alpha","beta"]}'
```

The Gateway was started through `pnpm openclaw --profile gateway-embeddings gateway run --port 19232 --bind loopback`, with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. Provider token usage is a separate PR; this routing change retains the existing usage response.

prs.title: fix(doctor): no workspace suggestions on an explicitly empty roster
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor` reports a misleading "No agents configured" error/warning from the workspace-suggestions check on installs whose agent roster is explicitly empty (`{ agents: { entries: {} } }`), even though the config is valid.

## User Impact

User impact: Doctor no longer emits a false workspace-suggestions error/warning on installs with zero configured agents. An explicitly empty roster owns no agent workspaces, so the check now returns nothing instead of throwing. This matches the semantic already established for the Memory Dreaming resolver in #169516.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveDoctorWorkspaceSuggestionScopes` fell back to `resolveDefaultAgentId(cfg)` whenever `listAgentIds(cfg)` returned nothing. `listAgentIds` returns an empty list only for an explicitly empty roster — raw pre-roster configs still get the legacy implicit `main` id, so the fallback branch is dead for them. In the empty-roster state `resolveDefaultAgentId` always throws ("No agents configured"). That fallback was left over when the runtime `main` fallbacks were removed, the same pattern #169516 removed from `resolveMemoryDreamingWorkspaces`: an empty roster has no agent workspaces, so the resolver now returns `[]`. The Doctor containment already turns a thrown detect into an error finding / warning; returning `[]` stops the misleading output at the source. Both callers (`doctor-core-checks.ts:759`, `doctor-health-contribution-runners.workspace.ts:166`) already treat an empty scope list as a no-op.

Maintainer decision (aligns with the #169516 semantic): the fix keeps the change **narrowed to a no-op** — no default agent is injected anywhere; raw empty/structured input is normalized at the existing choke points (`implicit-agent-roster.ts:10` injects `main` for non-explicit entries, applied at `validation-core.ts:477` and `io.load.ts:89/120`), and the roster bootstrap + config-admission validation that reject an explicit empty roster in config (`zod-schema.agents.ts:43-49`) are retained unchanged. The only delete is the unreachable fallback branch and its now-unused import.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-workspace-suggestions.test.ts src/flows/doctor-health.update-scope.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 2 files passed, 6 tests passed. The flipped test now asserts `[]` findings for `cfg: { agents: { entries: {} } }`.
- Lint (`run-oxlint.mjs`, oxlint.core): 0 warnings, 0 errors on both changed files. Format check: both changed files use the correct format. `tsgo:core` incremental: no type errors in the changed files (pre-existing `koffi` missing-module errors unrelated).
- CI: all checks green (61 passed / 0 failed on the push of `6066716da5b`). After rebasing onto the latest upstream `main` (`7ae60e40d6f`), CI is re-running on the new head `8acad23a3ef` with no failures so far (24 passed / 0 failed / 17 pending at last check).
- Mergeability: branch rebased onto the latest upstream `main` (`7ae60e40d6f`); GitHub reports `mergeable = MERGEABLE`.
- Real behavior (live `doctor` CLI run, three config states): each scenario ran the compiled product entry with isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` per scenario, all `exit 0`:

| Scenario | Config | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — empty roster, implicit mode | `{ "agents": { "entries": {} } }` | Clean exit 0; no throw; workspace-suggestion check returns nothing ("Prepared the agent roster for persistence"). |
| B — raw `{}` (pre-roster) | `{}` | Same as A; exit 0. |
| C — explicit empty roster | `{ "agents": { "ownership": "explicit", "entries": {} } }` | Exit 0; config admission/interception reports `Config invalid; doctor will run with best-effort config`; the workspace-suggestion check itself emits nothing. The two `doctor:auth-profile-migration run failed ... No agents configured` / `doctor:skill-workshop-tool-policy run failed ...` warnings come from a separate diagnostic in `agent-scope-config.ts:223` on an explicitly empty (invalid) roster — pre-existing behavior unrelated to this PR. |

Environment caveat: the `pnpm openclaw` wrapper is unusable in this container (its runtime-artifact sync is refused by the systemd-service inspection on a host with no systemd and a live Gateway), so the real-behavior runs used the compiled product entry `node dist/entry.js` (built from the same HEAD `6066716da5b`, build exit 0) — the same entry point the launcher imports. The PR branch was later rebased onto the latest upstream `main` (`7ae60e40d6f`); the new head `8acad23a3ef` keeps both changed files byte-identical to `6066716da5b` (`git diff` of the two file pairs is empty), so this real-behavior evidence and the CI proof below remain valid for the current head. Since the fix, `rg 'No agents configured' src/` finds the text only in `workspace-run.ts:37` (different context) and `agent-scope-config.ts:223` (the independent per-run diagnostic above); `doctor-workspace-suggestion-scopes.ts` no longer contains it. Three-scenario run logs retained at `.tmp/doctor-proof/logs/{scenario-a,b,c}.out`.


### CI proof: exact-head before/after + latest-stable upgrade

Review-endorsed proof path — direct empty-roster injection into `resolveDoctorWorkspaceSuggestionScopes` with `{ agents: { entries: {} } }` — run at exact immutable heads on a secretless GitHub Actions workflow (fork repo `xialonglee/openclaw`, `permissions: {}`):

Both changed files are byte-identical to the proven `6066716da5b` (`git diff` of the file pairs is empty), so this exact-head proof remains valid for the current head. The Before/After SHAs above are immutable evidence from that specific run and are kept unchanged.



### Artifact inspection — maintainer decision

Resolves the ClawSweeper "needs maintainer proof decision" blocker: the proof artifact ([run 38522961887](https://github.com/xialonglee/openclaw/actions/runs/38522961887), `proof-doctor-empty-roster`) was downloaded and inspected on a host with artifact access — the step the ClawSweeper review host could not perform. prs.title: fix(docker): honor OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT when healthcheck config load fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The official Docker healthcheck ignored an explicit `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` when configuration loading failed before port resolution. A healthy Gateway on a nondefault port could therefore be marked unhealthy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve a valid environment port before loading configuration, while retaining the live Gateway lock as the first authority. Invalid or absent environment values retain the existing configuration path. Thanks to @xialonglee for the fix.

## User Impact

A broken or unreadable config does not prevent probing the explicit environment port. Healthcheck output, HTTP liveness semantics, and lock > environment > configuration precedence remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Built main `008cf7bc06ab7e3c6fc118cf88e782cd159d752f` and the candidate with the actual official Dockerfile and its pinned Node 24.22.1 images. Inspected each built image's HEALTHCHECK and executed that exact command, `node dist/docker-healthcheck.js`, from its runtime image.

A genuine isolated OpenClaw Gateway listened on nondefault port 19565 with valid Gateway-owned state. Separate healthcheck containers shared only its network namespace and had their own state/config paths, no discoverable live lock, and truncated JSON config. A request-only observer on the real Gateway recorded `/healthz` traffic without replacing the server or response.

- Main twice: exit 1 after the config parse error; no HTTP request reached the Gateway.
- Candidate twice: exit 0; each probe reached the real Gateway's `/healthz` endpoint.
- No-listener, missing-env/malformed-config, valid-config, and environment-over-config controls preserved their expected results.
- The live Gateway lock still won over a conflicting environment port.
- Focused healthcheck suite: six tests passed; changed TypeScript formatting check passed.

### Latest stable upgrade

Resolved the current published stable as **2026.10.7** and used the official `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.10.7` image, not an older historical release. Started its real Gateway on a task-owned volume, created a disabled synthetic cron job through the shipped CLI, and retained a workspace sentinel. Stopped it, then started the candidate official image against the same volume.

The candidate preserved exact configuration and workspace-file bytes and the persisted job's id, disabled state, payload, and schedule. Both versions' actual image HEALTHCHECK commands passed. Both Gateways shut down with exit 0. The disabled job never ran; no provider or channel was used.

The fix reuses the existing environment parser and port owner, without a fallback listener, new config, or migration. Production +8/-1; tests +23/-4. The throwing-config regression uses scoped mock restoration without duplicate environment call-count assertions. Necessary production growth moves environment admission ahead of the fallible config load.

Two-way door: reverting fully restores prior healthcheck behavior. The check is read-only and changes no stored format. Blast radius is Docker liveness probing when no active lock is available and an explicit environment port is present.

prs.title: fix(discord): long CRLF replies split with a dangling carriage return
prs.body:
Relates to gap finding: c2-discord-crlf (free_text, evidence level A)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord length-mode chunking ends long CRLF text chunks with a bare `\r` and drops the following `\n`, splitting a CRLF grapheme cluster at every line-end chunk boundary.

## User Impact

User impact: long Discord replies containing Windows-style line endings now split at line boundaries exactly like LF text — no message ends with a stray carriage return, and the next message does not start with an empty line. Inline code that crosses a boundary still keeps its original CRLF content.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chunker's line loop already drops the single LF terminator at a chunk boundary, but `boundary()` had a CRLF special case that pushed the grapheme-safe cut from before `\r` to the `\n` index. The emitted chunk therefore kept the `\r`, and the next line started after the `\n`, silently losing it. The fix leaves the grapheme-safe cut before `\r` and lets `flush()` drop the whole CRLF pair as one separator. A cut inside an inline code span still keeps the pair so code content round-trips. `newline` mode is unaffected because `chunkByParagraph` normalizes CRLF before chunking.

## Evidence

### Before fix

`500 × "hello world\r\n"` with default limits:

```text
chunks=30
src \r=500 \n=500 | joined \r=500 \n=471 | roundtrip=false
chunks ending with bare "\r": 29
chunk0 tail="\r\nhello world\r"
```

### After fix

Same input:

```text
chunks=30
src \r=500 \n=500 | joined \r=471 \n=471
chunks ending with bare "\r": 0; chunks starting with "\n": 0
chunk0 tail="d\r\nhello world" chunk1 head="hello world\r\nh"
```

The 29 dropped CRLF pairs match the LF control, which likewise drops one terminator per message boundary. After normalizing each remaining `\r\n` to `\n`, the CRLF chunks equal the LF chunks chunk-for-chunk.

### Shipped Discord send entry point proof

The repo's Crabline Discord QA lane runs the real bundled Discord plugin inside an isolated QA Gateway and records the Discord REST message creates it sends (`POST /api/v10/channels/<id>/messages`). The model is the deterministic `mock-openai` provider, so the sender and chunker under test are the shipped code and the recorded bodies are the delivered message content. Lane: `channelDriver: "crabline"`, `channelId: "discord"`, `providerMode: "mock-openai"`. No public Discord traffic or bot credentials are involved.

A 60-line `hello world` reply is delivered with CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings, then again with an LF control:

```text
# this head (3a921f5): scenario passes
Discord CRLF chunk boundary delivery proof: pass
  delivers a long CRLF reply: pass
  delivers the LF control reply: pass
  compares delivered CRLF and LF message boundaries: pass

[CRLF] 4 delivered messages | dangling CR tails=0 | leading LF heads=0 | CR=56 LF=56
       boundary tails=["ld","ld","ld","ld"] heads=["he","he","he","he"]
[LF]   4 delivered messages | dangling CR tails=0 | leading LF heads=0 | CR=0 LF=56
CRLF-vs-LF chunk parity after CRLF normalization: true

# parent commit 2e6e86c, same lane
[CRLF] 4 delivered messages | dangling CR tails=3 | leading LF heads=0 | CR=59 LF=56
       boundary tails=["d\r","d\r","d\r","ld"]
CRLF-vs-LF chunk parity after CRLF normalization: false
```

Inline code crossing a boundary keeps its CRLF pair (`cutsSpan`): `chunk.test.ts` covers it with `preserves rendered inline content at 6 chars and 17 lines` (includes a `\r\n` code span) and `retains inline ownership after blockquote list prefixes` (CRLF variants). The mock provider directive cannot emit backticks, so the live lane does not exercise that branch.

### Checks

- New regression test `treats a CRLF line boundary like an LF boundary`: red on the base, green with the fix.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.inline-range-work.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/durable-line-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` → 68/68 passed.
- `oxlint` → 0 errors; format check and line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety ratchets pass.

### What was not tested

No message was delivered to the public Discord API: this host has no leased Discord bot credentials, so the shipped-entry-point run above uses the repo's local Crabline Discord provider. The pinned `tsgo` binary does not run on this host (missing GLIBC 2.29–2.34), so the same extension tsconfigs were checked with the same-version `tsc`; the only error is the pre-existing, unrelated `extensions/canvas/src/a2ui-jsonl.ts` missing `@a2ui/web_core/v0_9`.


## Independent verification

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184435#issuecomment-6439673685 — shipped-agent replies over 2000 characters: main has three dangling CR tails in each of two runs; candidate has none in either run. Actual Discord REST create bodies captured; LF/short controls unchanged. Mocked REST and deterministic-provider limits are disclosed.


## Current merged-head verification

Head `9668544ae9e26c05eecda2da0a3408b761519463` cleanly merges current main `cf5ac5266cde705b46330a6c91c394d499afbf3e`, preserving the contributor commit and main's chunker changes. No manual conflict resolution or additional product change was required. Both runtime builds passed in isolated containers. The focused Discord chunker suite passed **20 tests**, including CRLF, inline-code, fences, grapheme boundaries and hard-cap coverage.

The shipped-agent Discord REST-boundary scenario was rerun on both rebuilt refs. Each of two 2818-character long-CRLF runs still emitted **three dangling CR tails on main versus zero on the merged candidate**, with zero leading LF chunks. LF and short controls remained unchanged; inline-code and fenced controls completed with no malformed candidate boundary. Main chunk lengths were 798/798/390/784/45, candidate 797/797/390/783/45. Same deterministic-provider and mocked-REST limitations as the linked independent proof apply; no live Discord rendering or global LF/CRLF parity claim is added.

Simplification: the delta against merged main remains **+14/-9 production lines (net +5)** and **+12 regression-test lines**, selecting the existing source-range owner rather than adding another chunking path. Previous unchanged Telegram regression proof is retained below.

prs.title: fix(cli): reject invalid cron expressions at the CLI and fix the misleading "choose exactly one schedule" error
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw cron add "every day at 9am sharp"` fails with "Choose exactly one schedule" even though exactly one positional schedule was given. Also fixes: a positional or `--cron` schedule that is not a valid cron expression (e.g. `openclaw cron add "9am standup with the team today"`) is not validated by the CLI; it is forwarded to the Gateway, which rejects it at RPC admission with a cryptic parser-internal error such as `invalid cron.add params: CronPattern: configuration entry 0 (9am) contains illegal characters.` — an error that names neither what the user typed nor how to fix it.

## User Impact

User impact: `cron add`/`cron edit` now reject unparseable cron expressions locally, before any Gateway call, with an actionable message that quotes the input and shows valid 5- and 6-field examples; every-prefixed positional schedules such as "every day at 9am sharp" now fail with the correct "Invalid --every" guidance instead of the self-contradictory "choose exactly one schedule". Valid inputs (`every 10m`, `0 9 * * *`, ISO timestamps, durations) are unchanged, verified against a live Gateway below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The positional-schedule heuristic filled the `every` slot (prefix match) and the `cron` slot (word count of 5/6) independently, so one positional argument could double-fill and trip the mutual-exclusion check. The word-count path also never validated cron syntax. The positional fill is now mutually exclusive (an every-prefixed positional owns the `every` slot only — a valid cron expression starts with a minute field and can never begin with "every"), and the cron branch of `resolveDirectSchedule` now validates the expression with the same croner rules the scheduler uses (new `isValidCronExpression` export in `src/cron/schedule.ts`), so anything the CLI accepts, the scheduler parses. One chokepoint covers `cron add`/`cron edit` and the positional/`--cron` flag paths. Out of scope: 6-field expressions that are syntactically valid but semantically unintended (e.g. `0 9 * * * *` runs hourly at :09 instead of daily at 9:00) remain accepted, as before.

## Evidence

Real-behavior proof: built CLI (`openclaw.mjs` dist entry) against a live throwaway Gateway (isolated `cronproof` profile, loopback bind, token auth, port 29901). Base = pre-fix build; head = this PR's build.

### Base (pre-fix)

```

Choose exactly one schedule: --at, --every, --cron, --on-exit, or --stream-command

$ cron add "9am standup with the team today" --message proof --name base-b2   (exit 1)
invalid cron.add params: CronPattern: configuration entry 0 (9am) contains illegal characters.

$ cron add --cron "9am standup" --message proof --name base-b3            (exit 1)

$ cron add "0 9 * * *" --message proof --name base-b4-cron                (exit 0, job created)
$ cron add "every 10m" --message proof --name base-b5-every               (exit 0, everyMs 600000)
$ cron edit <b4-id> --cron "9am standup"                                  (exit 1)
invalid cron.update params: CronPattern: invalid configuration format ('9am standup'), exactly five, six, or seven space separated parts are required.
$ cron edit <b4-id> --cron "0 10 * * *"                                   (exit 0, expr updated)
```

### Head (this PR)

```
$ cron add "every day at 9am sharp" --message proof --name head-h1        (exit 1)
Invalid --every. Use a duration like 10m, 1h, or 1d.

$ cron add "9am standup with the team today" --message proof --name head-h2   (exit 1)
Invalid cron expression "9am standup with the team today". Use 5 fields like "0 9 * * *" or 6 fields like "0 0 9 * * *".

$ cron add --cron "9am standup" --message proof --name head-h3            (exit 1)
Invalid cron expression "9am standup". Use 5 fields like "0 9 * * *" or 6 fields like "0 0 9 * * *".

$ cron add "0 9 * * *" --message proof --name head-h4-cron                (exit 0, job created)
$ cron add "every 10m" --message proof --name head-h5-every               (exit 0, everyMs 600000)
$ cron edit <h4-id> --cron "9am standup"                                  (exit 1)
Invalid cron expression "9am standup". Use 5 fields like "0 9 * * *" or 6 fields like "0 0 9 * * *".
$ cron edit <h4-id> --cron "0 10 * * *"                                   (exit 0, expr updated)
```

Every malformed input is rejected locally in the head build — no Gateway round trip (the Commander-harness tests additionally assert zero gateway RPC calls); every valid control behaves identically in both builds.

- Focused tests: `pnpm test src/cli/cron-cli/schedule-options.positional.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-edit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — wall time ~70s locally (vitest startup/transform dominates; the new tests themselves run in <1s). 104 cron-cli tests pass; 63 `src/cron` tests pass. Helper-level cases duplicated by the Commander add/edit tests were removed per review; the Commander tests now assert the full rejection message.
- Typecheck: `tsgo` core (incremental) plus `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json` and `tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json` shards clean (the services-cron shard caught an `it.each` tuple-callback type error that is now fixed); oxlint 0 warnings/errors; oxfmt clean.
- Structured local review: PASSED, best-fix verdict, no P0-P2 findings.

### What was not tested
- 6-field semantic-misalignment detection (see Why This Change Was Made): a syntactically valid 6-field expression such as `0 9 * * * *` is accepted in both builds, unchanged by this PR.


## Maintainer follow-up

Removed the redundant valid positional-every helper case; Commander coverage retains that contract. Documented supported positional interval syntax and local cron validation.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the previous CLI diagnostics. No persisted schedule format, schema, or scheduling semantics change. Blast radius is CLI schedule input validation for cron add/edit.

### Additional compatibility proof

Built baseline `70eb60085510496f2af11366023b127a52ecba1d` and candidate `4f00c37ce0f75c67e2733c0309aaded4eb857966` in isolated Node 24 Docker environments. `pnpm openclaw cron add/edit` against each isolated Gateway reproduced the two old diagnostics and the corrected CLI errors. The natural-language positional is still rejected, correctly as an invalid interval; this does not introduce natural-language scheduling.

The returned creation schedules and persisted edited schedules match across baseline and candidate, excluding the expected per-operation interval anchor timestamps. Invalid timezone still takes precedence over invalid cron syntax.

prs.title: fix(cron): follow-up wait drops subagent results or overruns when the wall clock jumps
prs.body:
Related: #180554 (merged drain-side complement), #175040, #171097.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cron follow-up results can be dropped after a forward system-clock correction, or the descendant wait can exceed its budget after a backward correction.

## User Impact

Scheduled tasks keep waiting for descendant results for the intended duration across wall-clock changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Measure the existing in-process deadline with `performance.now()` throughout the follow-up owner. Pass the remaining duration to the shared drain, whose monotonic implementation landed in #180554. Persisted timestamps and the existing timeout policy stay unchanged.

Thanks @xialonglee for the original fix and isolated-Gateway investigation.

## Evidence

Final integrated head: `be862319a2e0e79ed5b098219c016d9b38f1695d` ([checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/be862319a2e0e79ed5b098219c016d9b38f1695d/checks)).

- Both clock-step regression cases fail on current-main base `0eb245aedb568f8579bb9c0c4f537051fb155c2a`: the forward step ends the wait early and the backward step extends it. With the fix, all 24 owner tests and six production-settlement consumer cases pass. The fake-clock regressions add no real waits.
- Independent review of the final production change found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The final integrated owner run passed 24/24 in 56.57 seconds including wrapper/worker preparation (the test body used fake timers); the final targeted consumer run passed 6/6 (with 60 unrelated cases excluded). These exercise the production follow-up/drain and delivery composition with synthetic external I/O.
- Targeted typed oxlint, oxfmt, and diff checks pass. Local native typechecking refused the shared compiler/dependency path before compilation; exact-head CI supplies broad integrated proof.
- Production delta: 0 lines (+9/-9); tests: +31 lines. The two regression directions share one table and abort cleanup, replacing the larger contributor test block.
- No fresh Gateway run was performed for this revision because recreating the provider/Gateway fixture exceeds the bounded live-proof budget. The contributor trace below exercises the same production change; it is attributed evidence, not a new run on the integrated head.

### Contributor-supplied isolated-Gateway evidence

The following trace was supplied by @xialonglee for contributor head `c4499684555` and its parent. The final repair retains that production behavior and simplifies comments/tests.


Built `dist` at this head (`c4499684555`) and at its parent `96938085d64` (base; already contains the merged drain fix `68b73bf9ca`). For each cell:

- A fresh isolated Gateway ran from that build (`node dist/index.js gateway run`, loopback, token auth, isolated HOME/state/config, scripted OpenAI-compatible model provider). Both builds run the same gateway code — the PR touches only `src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.ts` and its test.
- A real parent turn ran through the Gateway (`POST /v1/responses`), then a real `sessions_spawn` through the Gateway's tools-invoke API with the parent session as requester. The descendant is a real Gateway subagent run; its scripted model response is held so the descendant is genuinely running during the wait.
- The harness process then calls the unmodified production `waitForDescendantSubagentResult({sessionKey, runStartedAt, timeoutMs: 30000})` — the same owner the cron dispatcher calls (`delivery-dispatch.ts:128-135`). Its `bindAgentToolGatewayRequest` default client performs real WebSocket `chat.history` / `agent.wait` round-trips to the live Gateway, and descendant state is read from the Gateway's real SQLite `subagent_runs` registry (requester binding, settlement, terminal reply).
- At +800ms into the wait the harness offsets `Date.now` by ±60s — the same effect as an NTP step / VM resume for the process evaluating the owner. `performance.now()` is untouched.

Matrix, budget 30,000ms (timeoutMs is floored by the owner's 30s minimum wait):

| build | clock step | real elapsed | follow-up result | descendant |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| head | +60s @ 800ms | **4,856ms** | `"final report ready"` (visible) | settled with visible reply |
| head | −60s @ 800ms | **30,051ms** | undefined (budget honored) | still running when the budget expired |
| base | +60s @ 800ms | **1,509ms** | undefined — result dropped | still running when the wait was abandoned |
| base | −60s @ 800ms | **90,055ms** | undefined — 60,055ms overrun | still running when the wait finally returned |

Verbatim harness output (trimmed to the timing lines):

```
# head, +60s
[t=+32718ms] calling production waitForDescendantSubagentResult({sessionKey, runStartedAt, timeoutMs: 30000})
[t=+33518ms] wall clock jumped +60s (Date.now offset injected in owner process; same effect as an NTP step / VM resume)
[t=+37577ms] follow-up returned after 4856ms
follow-up result: {"reply":"final report ready","disposition":"visible"}
descendant settle facts from registry: outcome={"status":"ok","elapsedMs":3699}, terminalReply={"disposition":"visible","text":"final report ready"}, cleanupCompletedAt=set

# head, -60s
[t=+33663ms] wall clock jumped -60s
[t=+62917ms] follow-up returned after 30051ms
follow-up result: null
descendant settle facts from registry: endedAt=null (still running)

# base, +60s
[t=+34036ms] wall clock jumped +60s
[t=+34747ms] follow-up returned after 1509ms
follow-up result: null
descendant settle facts from registry: endedAt=null (still running when the wait was abandoned)

# base, -60s
[t=+33030ms] wall clock jumped -60s
[t=+122289ms] follow-up returned after 90055ms
follow-up result: null
```

Reading:

- Forward jump: the base abandoned the wait 1.5s in and dropped the descendant's visible result; the head kept observing real `agent.wait`/registry settlement and returned the descendant reply at 4.9s.
- Backward jump: the head expired at 30.05s against the 30s budget; the base stayed blocked for 90.06s (budget + the 60s rewind) because every loop re-derived its elapsed budget from the rewound wall clock.
- Both red rows reproduce the reported defects at the production boundary; both green rows show the fix holding with real transport and registry settlement.


Real VM suspend/resume, a live NTP change, and a live model provider were not tested. The clock offset and model responses were controlled; Gateway transport and registry settlement were real.

prs.title: fix(codex): prevent sandbox glob checks from stalling the Gateway
prs.body:
Related: #166684 (same defect class, fixed for browser URL globs in #166727)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Codex sandbox filesystem request can stall the Gateway event loop for seconds when the session's sandbox glob denies a requested path. The sandbox exec server compiles each fs sandbox glob into a backtracking regular expression and runs it synchronously on every fs read/write/metadata request; both the glob pattern (model-session sandbox context) and the requested path are model-controlled, and a short adversarial miss already stalls Node for seconds (14 adjacent `*a` quantifiers: ~6.7 s).

## User Impact

User impact: Codex sandboxed filesystem requests no longer stall the Gateway on the adversarial glob cases covered here. The matcher removes catastrophic regex backtracking and repeated full-literal comparisons while preserving access decisions; the sandbox exec server runs these checks synchronously in the Gateway process. Glob semantics are unchanged from the previous regex, including single `*` staying inside one segment, `**` crossing separators, `?` and character classes, `u`-flag code-point behavior, and — matching the old regex compiled without the dotAll flag — globstars stopping at line terminators (LF, CR, U+2028, U+2029).

## Why This Change Was Made

The glob compiler translated `*` to `[^/]*` and `**` to `.*` / `(?:.*/)?`, so adjacent quantifiers retry overlapping splits exponentially on a miss. The matcher now advances cursor ranges in one pass per token (the linear algorithm merged for browser URL globs in #166727, extended here for `?`, `[...]`, and `**/`, with cursor positions indexed by Unicode code point to preserve the old `u`-flag regex semantics). Character classes keep their exact regex semantics by testing a single code point against the same class source. Globstar reach stops before each line terminator, mirroring the old dot-without-dotAll behavior; globstar-slash merges precomputed separator-follow positions bounded by the next line terminator, emitting each follow once and collapsing adjacent `**/` tokens, so repeated globstar-slash stays linear as well.

Two sibling glob-to-regex compilers keep the old backtracking shape and are intentionally out of scope here: `src/infra/exec-allowlist-pattern.ts` (operator-authored patterns; overlaps with the open argPattern safety work in #82950 and the macOS Swift matcher parity) and `src/infra/package-dist-inventory.ts` (maintainer-authored patterns and targets). Follow-up material.

## Evidence

### Long-literal correction

Landing review found a second slowdown: comparing a long literal at every reachable cursor remained quadratic. Literal matching now uses Unicode code-point KMP prefix fallback, preserving overlapping matches and permission boundaries while removing the redundant UTF-16 lookup maps.

- The new regression failed on the original PR implementation after **28,514 ms**; the corrected regression test passes in **26 ms**.
- Matcher suite: **12/12 passed**, including overlapping-prefix, reachable-start, astral-character and unpaired-surrogate cases. Command: `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/fs-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; measured wall time **22.21 s**, including shared compiled-worker preparation.
- Filesystem RPC integration suite: **23/23 passed**. Command: `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.fs.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; measured wall time **46.45 s**, dominated by shared transform/import preparation. This existing integration suite exercises the real exec-server handlers and filesystem authorization boundaries.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38067182387) passed for `37cc502d81b3041fe51903246f1ba6ede45761e5`: 31 jobs succeeded and 29 were intentionally skipped. The 12 matcher cases reported **0.180 s** total test-case time, including **20 ms** for the long-literal regression; their containing `checks-node-changed-extensions-config` job took **129 s**, including setup and other tests.
- Fresh independent review of the complete corrected candidate found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The final follow-up only changes the equivalent zero-array initializer to satisfy lint; targeted lint reports no errors.
- Historical full pre-publication [Testbox attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37959885965): build and repository typechecks passed, but full lint found 12 pre-existing max-lines violations in untouched files. That attempt was stopped; its full test suite did not run. This is not a successful full-gate result. The current maintainer workflow permits correction publication with pending GitHub gates; exact-head CI, security, and review still govern merging.
- The focused regression and RPC proof ran in isolated AWS with no instance role, no credential hydration, and synthetic filesystem bridges. Both changed file hashes were checked against the correction. A live Codex app-server session was not tested.

- CI baseline recovery: the unrelated stale session-accessor allowance was fixed on `main` by [e9bbc78b9bbd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e9bbc78b9bbdcd887a2b3693ea4ee1ebc1805672). The repaired base is incorporated without changing this PR’s three-file matcher scope; fresh exact-head CI is required after the refresh.

### Original contributor evidence

The evidence below records the original PR-head validation before the additional long-literal correction.

### Before fix

The legacy regex compiler (extracted verbatim from `origin/main`) and the new matcher, same process, same adversarial miss — glob `*a` repeated 14, target 29 `a` characters plus `x`:

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/fs-redos-proof.mts
before matched=false ms=6729
after  matched=false ms=1
after16 matched=false (16-star cluster)
```

### After fix

Timing through the real sandbox exec-server fs RPC over WebSocket with a mocked fs bridge (the same request path production uses; bridge calls are logged):

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/fs-boundary-proof.mts
bridge-read /workspace/allowed/report.txt
allowed-status ok bytes=15
adversarial-denied-promptly true ms 2
line-terminator-denied-before-io true
bridge-read /workspace/work/a/b/secret.txt
nested-grant-status ok bytes=15
bridge-read-total 2
```

- An allowed path through a glob grant reaches bridge I/O and returns content.
- An adversarial `*a`×14 glob policy denies the crafted miss end-to-end in 2 ms (was ~6.7 s for the matcher alone on the old compiler).
- `file:///workspace/work/a%0Ab/secret.txt` (decoded `/workspace/work/a\nb/secret.txt`) against a `work/**` read grant is rejected before any bridge I/O — globstars stop at the line terminator exactly like the old dot-without-dotAll regex — and the bridge is never called for it.
- The positive control `/workspace/work/a/b/secret.txt` is authorized and does reach the bridge; total bridge reads: 2 (only the authorized paths).

Test and gate summary:

- New unit tests: 11/11 — semantics matrix, line-terminator parity matrix (LF/CR/U+2028/U+2029 across both globstar forms, plus stars/`?`/classes still matching them), adversarial timing guards (<250 ms), globstar-slash spam regression with nonempty path components, and a 3000-round deterministic differential fuzz against the legacy regex compiler through the public `resolveFsSandboxPolicy` / `assertResolvedFsSandboxAccess` path (fuzz targets include all four line terminators; the oracle applies the same posix-normalization contract production uses).
- Existing `sandbox-exec-server.fs.test.ts` integration: 23/23.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, changed-file oxlint (0 findings), knip dead-export scan (0), and format all pass.

Not tested: a live Codex app-server sandbox session; the timed calls above run through the real exec-server RPC handlers with a synthetic bridge, and the unit/integration suites cover the rest.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** catastrophic backtracking when a sandbox fs glob misses a model-requested path, and preservation of the exact authorization boundary (including line terminators) while removing it.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node v24.18.0, this branch, worktree `/home/0668000452/codes/OPENSOURCES/openclaw`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/fs-boundary-proof.mts` (starts the sandbox exec server, drives `fs/readFile` over its WebSocket JSON-RPC with a tracking fs bridge), plus `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/fs-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` and `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.fs.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output above; 11/11 and 23/23 test totals; line-terminator path denied before bridge I/O while authorized paths reach it.
- **What was not tested:** a gateway-routed live Codex sandbox session.

## Contributor credit

Original implementation by @xialonglee. Maintainer correction and squash landing requested by @Takhoffman; the requested co-author credit is retained.

## Work sessions

- [Landing discussion, correction and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/a0b6e66b-5fb6-421a-b4f0-29b3f6ecaf83)
