prs.title: fix(agents): break prepared catalog worker fingerprint import cycle
prs.body:
Related: unblocks PRs failing `check-guards-architecture` with an inherited madge import cycle (e.g. #167234, run 37869244019).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every PR whose merge ref includes current `main` fails `check-guards-architecture` on a madge import cycle it did not introduce, blocking CI through no fault of the PR author.

## User Impact

User impact: contributors' PRs stop inheriting a red `check-guards-architecture` / `ci-gate` from `main`, restoring merge readiness signals that were stuck failing for unrelated work.

## Why This Change Was Made

`811d442afa2` introduced `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-fingerprints.ts`, which type-imports `PreparedModelCatalogWorkerInput` / `PreparedModelWorkerRequest` from `prepared-model-catalog-worker.ts` while that worker value-imports fingerprint functions back — a two-node cycle. The madge gate runs only on PRs, so `main` stayed green while every PR merging this `main` went red. This extracts the shared worker types into a leaf contract (`src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.types.ts`); the worker imports and re-exports them so existing consumers keep working unchanged, and `fingerprints` imports them from the leaf, leaving the cycle with no return edge. Five imports left unused by the move were removed.

## Evidence

### Before fix

`check-guards-architecture` on PR #167234 (run 37869244019), failing on code its diff does not touch:

```text
Madge import cycle check: 1 cycle(s).
Madge circular dependencies:
# cycle 1
src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-fingerprints.ts
-> src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.ts
Break the cycle or extract a leaf contract instead of routing through a barrel.
```

Local reproduction against unpatched `main` fails identically.

### After fix

```text
$ pnpm check:madge-import-cycles
Madge import cycle check: 0 cycle(s).

$ pnpm check:import-cycles
Import cycle check: 0 runtime value cycle(s).

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.test.ts src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.directory.test.ts

      Tests  4 passed (4)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.secrets.test.ts

      Tests  7 passed (7)

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental ...
core-exit=0

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json --builders 1
```

- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.types.ts src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.ts src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-fingerprints.ts`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `oxfmt --check` on changed files: clean.
- The type move is semantics-preserving: both `ReturnType<typeof ...>` dependencies were carried over as type-level `typeof import(...)` aliases, and the worker re-exports the previously public names, so `prepared-model-catalog.worker.ts`, the heap/e2e tests, and the catalog test helpers needed no changes.
- What was not tested: no behavior change is expected or observable beyond the import graph; the gate that was failing (`check:madge-import-cycles` inside `check-guards-architecture`) now passes locally on the exact tree this PR ships.

prs.title: fix(buzz): directory search fails on Unicode-equivalent profile and room names
prs.body:
Relates to gap finding: gap-buzz-directory-unicode-nfc (pattern-copy, evidence level A)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Buzz (Nostr team rooms) channel directory search returns an empty result when the searched profile display name or room name uses a different Unicode normalization form than the typed query — e.g. names produced by macOS/iOS Nostr clients (NFD, `Cafe\u0301`) never match an NFC query (`Café`).

## User Impact

User impact: searching the Buzz directory for peers or groups now matches names regardless of Unicode normalization form; previously such profiles and rooms were unsearchable and the directory query silently returned nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The directory query filter compared raw code units after only `trim().toLowerCase()`, so canonically equivalent strings with different code points (NFC vs NFD) never matched. The fix normalizes both the query and the compared entry fields (`id`/`name`/`handle`) to NFC before matching, mirroring the contract the Matrix live directory lookup fix established: canonical forms compare equal, directory entries keep their original spelling. This is the same bug class fixed for Matrix in `129cfb57fa4`; Buzz's other `toLowerCase()` call sites operate on hex keys, hostnames, and protocol identifiers (pure ASCII) and are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Before fix

New reproduction test on the unmodified code fails exactly as reported:

```text
FAIL  extensions/buzz/src/directory.test.ts > Buzz directory state > matches directory queries across Unicode normalization forms
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'Café' ]
```

### After fix

- `pnpm vitest run extensions/buzz/src/directory.test.ts` → **13 passed (13)**, including the new regression test covering both directions: NFC-stored profile name matched by an NFD query, and NFD-stored room name matched by an NFC query.
- Full Buzz suite: 208 passed; the 7 failures in `buzz-bus.socket.test.ts` / `gateway.cold-start-recovery.test.ts` (gateway settle timeouts) also fail on the unmodified base — verified by rerunning just those files with the change stashed — pre-existing and unrelated.

prs.title: fix: restore error messages dropped by Bun bare-header stacks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: user-visible diagnostic messages (version resolution failures, help display errors, unhandled rejections, main-session recovery warnings) are printed without their error message when the CLI/Gateway runs on Bun.

Bun's GC can materialize `Error#stack` with a bare header (`"Error\n    at ..."`) that drops the message V8-style stacks carry. Diagnostic paths that read `error.stack ?? error.message` then render a stack with no message, hiding what actually failed.

## User Impact

User impact: failures on Bun report the actual error message again; stacks that already embed the message are unchanged. Node-only installs are unaffected (their stacks already carry the message).

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical fix already exists upstream as `formatErrorStackWithMessage` in `packages/normalization-core/src/error-coercion.ts` (upstream PR #172774, already merged into base, already used by `formatUncaughtError`). This PR routes the remaining `src/` production `stack ?? message` reads through that helper: on a bare-header stack it restores `"Name: message"` and keeps the rest verbatim; otherwise it returns the stack/message exactly as before, so every replacement is equivalent-or-strictly-better.

`node-runtime-recovery.mjs` mirrors the helper inline because the pre-compile bootstrap cannot import compiled packages; the inline copy is byte-for-byte consistent with the canonical implementation and the file header documents the dependency constraint.

The 5 extension call sites (reached via the plugin-sdk error seam) still use the old expression; fixing them requires widening a frozen plugin-sdk export surface, so they are tracked as a follow-up for the next stable cycle rather than included here.

## Evidence

- Helper unit tests (5 cases) cover: bare-header restore, V8-style stack unchanged, custom error name on a bare header, no-name-line prefix, and no-stack fallback — `packages/normalization-core/src/error-coercion.test.ts`.
- `unhandled-rejections.fatal-detection.test.ts` uses an independent bare-header fixture (`"Error\n    at handlerThatThrew (source.js:3)"`) and asserts the exact restored output instead of re-applying the production formatter (ClawSweeper Tests feedback); all 12 tests pass.
- Rebased onto current `upstream/main` (`11d0c854192`); branch head is `58f53d53c9c`.
- Red-on-base/green-on-head on the revised registry test: HEAD passes 12/12; with `src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts` reverted to base `11d0c854192`, the same test fails with the bare `Error` header (`1 failed | 11 passed`), exactly the regression this PR fixes.
- Shipped Gateway proof: the built `dist/index.js` (`OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (58f53d5)`) loads a standalone plugin through `plugins.load.paths`; the plugin registers a real `onDiagnosticEvent` listener that throws a bare-header-stack error, and the migrated `diagnostic-events` reporter prints `Error: plugin diagnostic listener failed: disk quota exceeded` with the frame preserved. Full output above.
- Type/lint/format on the 14 changed files: oxlint 0 warnings / 0 errors; `oxfmt --check` clean; fallback `tsc` reports no diagnostics in any changed file. The repo `tsgo` wrapper could not run in this checkout because the local install predates the `tsrs` dependency; CI's production and test type lanes cover that gap.
- CI on `58f53d53c9c`: all product checks pass except two unrelated failures. `checks-node-changed-compact-small-4` times out in the untouched `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.fallback-transcript.test.ts`; the same test fails locally with all 12 PR source files reverted to base, so it is pre-existing/environmental. `Intersect shared OpenClawKit dead code` fails before scanning with `Error: Missing or ambiguous ios Periphery producer`; this PR changes no iOS/Swift files.
- `security-sensitive-review` / `ci-gate` still require a maintainer approval for the security-sensitive path change (`/allow-security-sensitive-change`); that is an approval step, not an author code action.

### Real behavior proof (Bun, newly migrated reporter)

ClawSweeper's remaining ask was proof from a **newly migrated** reporter, not the pre-existing `formatUncaughtError`. This exercises the changed **handler-failure reporter** in `src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts` end to end: a real Bun process imports the real module, registers a handler that throws a bare-header-stack error (the exact shape Bun's GC materializes, per the `error-coercion.ts` docstring), installs the real `unhandledRejection` handler, and triggers a genuine rejection, so the changed `catch` block formats the thrown error through `formatErrorStackWithMessage`.

Runtime: Bun 1.4.3, Linux x64. Driver (uncommitted temp script): installs the real listener, registers a throwing handler, then runs `Promise.reject(new Error("orphaned background compaction rejected"))`. BASE = `upstream/main` `11d0c854192`, HEAD = this PR `58f53d53c9c`:

```text
## BASE — upstream/main reporter (`err.stack ?? err.message`)
[openclaw] Unhandled rejection handler failed: Error
    at compactionRunner (session-store.js:412:7)
[openclaw] Unhandled promise rejection: Error: orphaned background compaction rejected
    at <repo>/.tmp/unhandled-proof.ts:14:20

## HEAD — this PR reporter (`formatErrorStackWithMessage`)
[openclaw] Unhandled rejection handler failed: Error: disk quota exceeded while compacting session store
    at compactionRunner (session-store.js:412:7)
[openclaw] Unhandled promise rejection: Error: orphaned background compaction rejected
    at <repo>/.tmp/unhandled-proof.ts:14:20
```

The BASE reporter prints a bare `Error` header with the message dropped; the HEAD reporter restores `Error: disk quota exceeded while compacting session store` and keeps the stack frames verbatim. Both runs exit 1. This is the revised regression shown failing on the base and passing on the head.

### Real behavior proof (shipped Gateway entry point)

ClawSweeper's remaining ask was a newly migrated reporter reached through a shipped CLI/Gateway entry rather than a direct module import. This run uses the built Gateway from this PR (`dist/index.js`, `OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (58f53d5)`, Node v24.18.0) and a standalone plugin enabled through `plugins.load.paths`. The plugin registers a real `onDiagnosticEvent` listener that throws an error whose `stack` is the exact bare-header shape Bun materializes (`"Error\n    at ..."`), then emits a real `webhook.received` diagnostic event. The migrated `diagnostic-events` listener-error reporter formats the caught error:

```text
2026-10-20T09:59:39.991+08:00 [diagnostic-events] listener error type=webhook.received seq=79: Error: plugin diagnostic listener failed: disk quota exceeded
    at pluginDiagnosticListener (diagnostic-failure-plugin.cjs:10:13)
```

The same Gateway process loaded the plugin and shut down cleanly:

```text
2026-10-20T09:59:40.066+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (1 plugin: diagnostic-failure-plugin; 11.0s)
2026-10-20T09:59:42.179+08:00 [gateway] [shutdown] completed cleanly in 162ms
```

Command (isolated HOME/state/config; plugin file listed in `plugins.load.paths` and enabled through `plugins.entries`):

```bash
OPENCLAW_HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=... OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 \
  node dist/index.js gateway --port 19031 --bind loopback
```

### Red-on-base / green-on-head (revised registry test)

HEAD `58f53d53c9c`:

```text
$ pnpm test src/infra/unhandled-rejections.fatal-detection.test.ts

      Tests  12 passed (12)
```

Same test file with only `src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts` reverted to base `11d0c854192`:

```text
FAIL  src/infra/unhandled-rejections.fatal-detection.test.ts > process error handlers > continues past declining and throwing handlers, then stops at the first claim
- Expected: "Error: bare header message\n    at handlerThatThrew (source.js:3)"
+ Received: "Error\n    at handlerThatThrew (source.js:3)"
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)
```

### Real behavior proof (Bun, pre-existing formatter surface)

Bun-run real behavior on the pre-compile `src/infra/errors.ts` public `formatUncaughtError` surface (already migrated before this PR), feeding the exact bare-header stack shape and comparing against the old `err.stack ?? err.message` expression:

```text
runtime: bun 1.4.3
error.message: "version resolution failed"
error.stack: "Error\n    at <anonymous> (src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts:102:84)"

BEFORE — old expression `err.stack ?? err.message`:
  "Error\n    at <anonymous> (src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts:102:84)"

AFTER — production formatUncaughtError (formatUncaughtError -> formatErrorStackWithMessage):
  "Error: version resolution failed\n    at <anonymous> (src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts:102:84)"
```

prs.title: improve(worktrees): skip the default-branch fetch when origin has not moved
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: creating a managed worktree on the default branch (Control UI "Updating repository…", gateway phase `preparing_worktree_base`) always runs a network `git fetch` of the default branch, even when origin's default branch has not moved since the clone last fetched it.

## User Impact

User impact: default-branch worktree starts skip the fetch round trip (and its pack/ref write on the shared clone) whenever origin still advertises the commit the clone already tracks. Fetch, fallback, and warning behavior are unchanged when origin has moved or the advertisement is unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Part of the worktree base latency investigation 2026-11-02. Over 176 default-branch starts (Oct 30 – Nov 2) the base phase took p50 5.2s, p90 48s, p99 261s (max 302s); GitHub `ls-remote` is ~0.95s, and the slowest sample spent 234s in `baseRefresh` (ls-remote + fetch) on an IO-starved host with a 1,216-pack partial clone.

Root cause: `fetchRemoteDefault` in `src/agents/worktrees/base-ref.ts` (line 463 on `63c25f72`) runs `git fetch origin +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` unconditionally, although the immediately preceding `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` already reports the advertised tip.

Solution: parse the HEAD object id from that same advertisement (it follows the `ref:` line), read the local `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` with `for-each-ref`, and when they match treat the base as freshly confirmed (`fetchSucceeded: true`). Everything downstream is unchanged: the origin/HEAD symref update on a default-branch switch, the 30-second preparation reuse window, `estimateWorktreeGitBytes` hydration, and local default fast-forwarding. Any mismatch, missing id, or failed advertisement takes the existing fetch path. Docs (`docs/concepts/managed-worktrees.md`) note the skip.

Accepted edge cases:
- `for-each-ref` prefix-matches nested refs (`origin/main/*`); multiple lines never equal the advertised id, so this falls back to fetching.
- A failing local `for-each-ref` read throws like the other required local Git reads in this function.
- With an unchanged tip, the fetch (`--no-tags`, single explicit refspec) would update nothing, so skipping it loses no ref effect.

## Evidence

- Regression test `confirms an unchanged default from origin's advertisement without fetching` (`src/agents/worktrees/base-ref.test.ts`): red on base (`expected [ 'ls-remote', 'fetch', 'ls-remote', 'fetch' ] to deeply equal [ 'ls-remote', 'fetch', 'ls-remote' ]`, 1 failed), green with fix. It also covers a default-branch switch to an already-tracked commit (origin/HEAD still moves) and a moved remote (fetch still runs).
- Existing tests that used `fetch` as the discovery marker now count `ls-remote`; abort/revoke recovery matrices expect recovery to confirm an already-landed fetch without a second fetch.
- `base-ref.test.ts`: 51/51 passed (`--maxWorkers=1`).
- Consumers `capacity`, `git-fetch`, `git`, `service-branches`, `service.removal-budget`: 138 passed, 2 skipped. In the first combined run, one removal-budget case hit its 120s timeout under host IO load; it passed alone (9s) and in the rerun.
- `tsgo` (`tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json`), oxlint on touched files (including `max-lines`, now exactly at 700), oxfmt check, `git diff --check`: clean.
- Synthetic local `file://` bench of the command sequence (3,000 commits, 3,000 branches, blob:none clone; 15 runs): median 10 → 8 ms with 1 pack, 21 → 12 ms with 600 packs. This only measures local cost. The production saving is the GitHub fetch negotiation plus the ref-transaction/pack write on the shared clone.
- Local autoreview (Codex, branch mode against `origin/main`, P0–P2): scoped-clean, no findings.

Gaps: no live Gateway measurement. The benefit applies only when origin's default has not advanced since the clone's last fetch, and the busy `main` advances often, so the share of starts that skip is unmeasured. Hydration and `ls-remote` latency are unchanged, and other lanes of the investigation address them.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(worktrees): bound default-branch fetch by one refresh deadline
prs.body:
## Problem

"Updating repository…" (gateway phase `preparing_worktree_base`) can hold session startup for minutes. The default-branch refresh is supposed to be bounded by `ls-remote` (30s) plus `fetch` (60s). On the team gateway (worktree base latency investigation 2026-11-02), the slowest start took 270.7s with `baseRefresh=234126ms`, and its fetch **succeeded** without a warning. A borrower sharing that attempt waited `baseWait=120557ms`.

## Root cause

The gateway's diagnostics for that start show that the time was spent waiting in a queue, not in Git or on the network:

```
10:57:40.637 slow Git ref mutation  queueWaitMs=0       queuedOperationMs=807300   (another writer on the same clone)
10:57:44.425 slow Git ref mutation  queueWaitMs=229670  queuedOperationMs=3787     (the default-branch fetch)
```

`fetchRemoteDefault` runs `git fetch origin +refs/heads/<default>:refs/remotes/origin/<default>` with `{ ...options, timeoutMs: 60_000 }` (`src/agents/worktrees/base-ref.ts:473` on `main`). A fetch is a ref mutation, so `withGitRefAdmission` (`src/agents/worktrees/git.ts:198`) first enqueues it on the per-clone `enqueueGitRefMutation` queue (`git.ts:238`). The 60s timeout starts only after the queue admits the fetch and its process starts. While queued, the fetch is bounded only by the caller's signal, and that signal has no deadline here.

As a result, any long ref writer on the same clone (`worktree add`, hydration, pack maintenance, a fast-forward) stretches the "60s" fetch to the length of its own run. In the slow start above, the fetch queued for 229.7s and ran for 3.8s, which adds up to the 234s `baseRefresh`. On Nov 2, the same log also shows other holders running for 123–807s and queued waiters waiting 47–230s.

## Solution

Give the default-branch refresh one deadline. `fetchRemoteDefault` arms a 90s deadline (the existing 30s + 60s budgets) before `ls-remote`, combines it with the caller's signal, and passes the result to the fetch:

- If the deadline expires while the fetch is still queued, the ref queue drops the fetch before it starts.
- If the deadline expires while the fetch is running, the process is stopped like a timeout.

Both cases take the existing fetch-failure path: keep the cached `refs/remotes/origin/<default>`, report `fetchSucceeded: false`, and add a warning that names the 90s budget and the wait for other Git ref updates. This adds no fallback mode, option, or queue policy.

The caller's own signal still owns cancellation and attempt retirement. The deadline applies only to the fetch call, so an expired refresh is not treated as a cancelled owner.

## Impact

- A held ref queue now adds at most ~90s of refresh to a default-branch start, instead of the holder's full duration (230s observed, up to 807s possible). The start then proceeds on the cached default with a visible warning.
- Borrowers sharing the attempt get the same bounded result.
- As before, the fallback does not mark the base fresh, so the next start retries the fetch.

## Evidence

Regression test in `base-ref.test.ts`: "uses the cached default when the fetch outwaits the refresh deadline in the ref queue". It uses a real Git repo and remote, a real ref-queue holder on the same clone, and the real `resolveWorktreeBase`. Only the 90s timer is replaced by a test-controlled signal.

- Base (`63c25f72`): **red**. The test times out after Vitest's 120000ms because the fetch stays queued behind the holder.
- Fix: **green**. The whole `base-ref.test.ts` file passes (51 passed).

Wall-clock repro (a scratch test that is not committed; real timers, real Git, real ref queue, with another writer holding the clone's ref queue for 150s):

| | wall time of `resolveWorktreeBase` | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base | 151,482 ms | waited for the holder; `fetchSucceeded: true` |
| Fix | 91,698 ms | cached default, `fetchSucceeded: false`, deadline warning |

Other checks: `git-fetch.test.ts` and `git.test.ts` pass (43 passed). `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass. oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the touched files.

Review: local autoreview (Codex engine, branch mode, base `63c25f72` → head `4c0ad6c7`, max priority P2) was scoped-clean with no actionable findings. The reviewer noted limited surrounding context and that it did not run the tests.

## Accepted edge cases

- The local reads before and after the network refresh (`git remote`, `config`, `symbolic-ref`, the cached `rev-parse`) keep their standard 120s budgets. They do not queue, and they are needed to produce the cached fallback. They are slow only when the host itself is IO-starved.
- The `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` update after a successful fetch is also a ref mutation, so it can still queue. It runs only when the remote default branch changes.
- `baseHydration` (`estimateWorktreeGitBytes`) is not covered, because the checkout needs those objects. Its 120s and 240s tails on this host come from local Git reads reaching their 120s budget on a clone with 1,216 packs and no multi-pack-index, and those starts failed. That belongs to clone maintenance, not to this deadline.
- The 807s ref-queue holder on Nov 2 was not identified from the logs. This change bounds its effect on startup but does not shorten the holder.
- I did not measure a remote that hangs. In this sandbox, a synthetic hanging `upload-pack` made `ls-remote` end with a cleanup-uncertain error at its 30s timeout on base. That is a separate path from the queue wait.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(ui): cap the Subagents summary at two statuses
prs.body:
## Problem

The Details → Subagents summary shows every status at once (Working, Waiting on subagents, Queued, Done, Stopped). The counts wrap onto several rows and Done ends up mid-row, so the summary stops working as an at-a-glance signal.

## Solution

The summary now shows at most two statuses. `projectDetailsSubagents` decides which ones; the component and CSS only lay them out.

- **Anything working** (waiting parents count as working): Working beside the avatars, then **Queued** on the right if anything is queued, otherwise **Done**.
- **Nothing working but some queued:** Queued, then Done.
- **Only finished:** Done beside the avatars.
- **Failed and stopped runs count as Done.** Agents usually retry or spawn a replacement around them, so Stopped never gets a status of its own. The per-row list still shows each child's real outcome.

The second status is always pushed to the right. The first status uses the primary text color.

The per-row list and the collapsed "N subagents running" header are unchanged.

## Evidence

Same mocked-Gateway fixtures before and after, captured with the Control UI e2e harness (Chromium, 1728 px).

prs.body:
## Summary
- Export `ApprovalRequest`, `ApprovalResolved`, and `ChannelApprovalKind` from the approval handler runtime SDK surface.
- Reuse the exported approval event types in `plugin-sdk/approval-handler-runtime` instead of maintaining local unions.

## Reasoning
Channel-native approval runtimes already operate on generic OpenClaw approval events, not channel-specific request shapes. The internal runtime types define those shared unions, but the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/approval-handler-runtime` subpath did not expose them. That leaves downstream channel adapters unable to name the callback request/resolution types from the same SDK surface that provides `ChannelApprovalNativeRuntimeAdapter` and related helpers.

This showed up while implementing a RovoClaw native approval adapter: the adapter needed to type an approval request as exec-or-plugin, so it had to recreate a local `ExecApprovalRequest | PluginApprovalRequest` alias. Exporting the existing internal union avoids that duplication and keeps plugin authors on the supported SDK contract.

This is intentionally a type-surface change only. It does not change approval creation, delivery, resolution, fallback behavior, or any RovoClaw/ACP-specific logic.

prs.title: fix(plugins): honor subagent model-override opt-in in interactive sessions
prs.body:
Closes #102167

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a plugin calling `api.runtime.subagent.run(...)` with a `provider`/`model` override from an interactive session (webchat/Control UI, TUI, ACP, or any gateway-client-scoped turn) was rejected with "provider/model override is not authorized" even when the operator had explicitly trusted the plugin via `plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride: true`. The opt-in was only consulted for clientless background runs, so cost-tiered plugin workflows (e.g. cheap evidence-gathering subagent workers feeding a more capable main session) could not guarantee the worker model from chat sessions — and the documented config knob appeared broken because docs never said it was background-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin-requested subagent overrides are now authorized by exactly two things, in every execution context: genuine admin scope on the calling client, or the operator's per-plugin opt-in (`allowModelOverride` + `allowedModels`). A policy-authorized override rides the dispatched request's client as a copied internal flag so the downstream `agent` gate honors it without leaking authority to the caller's live connection — and that internal flag is deliberately **not** accepted back as caller authority, so an inherited flag on the request scope can never bypass the policy for nested spawns (`allowedModels` bounds the whole spawn tree; this also closes a pre-existing bypass on the background path, where nested spawns under a synthetic flagged client skipped the allowlist). This aligns the subagent surface with `api.runtime.llm.complete`, whose equivalent per-plugin trust config already applies in every context. Defaults are unchanged and fail closed: no config → deny, now with an actionable pointer to the config key.

## User Impact

Operators can trust a plugin to steer subagent model selection once, and it works the same in interactive and background contexts. Plugin authors can build guaranteed-model subagent workers reachable from chat sessions without granting the driving client admin scope.

**Compatibility note (intentional semantic widening of a shipped key):** on shipped releases (e.g. v2026.6.11) the help text scoped `subagent.allowModelOverride` to "background subagent runs" and the runtime enforced that. After this change, operators who already set the opt-in for background jobs also authorize overrides from interactive turns on upgrade, with no config change. The grant stays plugin-scoped (HTTP/webchat callers never gain model control themselves) and `allowedModels`-bounded; help text and docs were rewritten in this PR to state the widened scope. Flagging explicitly for release notes: config/default surface changed — 1 key widened, 0 added, 0 removed. Second intentional behavior change: nested plugin spawns under internally flagged clients (background synthetic runs, `openai-http`/voice-ingress-triggered runs) previously inherited blanket override authority; they now consult the per-plugin policy like any other plugin call.

## Evidence

- New tests in `src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts`: trusted plugin + non-admin client → override forwarded and the dispatched client carries `internal.allowModelOverride: true` on unchanged `operator.write` scopes (proves the downstream gate path); untrusted plugin + non-admin client → rejected with the config-pointer error; **inherited internal flag on the scope client + untrusted plugin → still rejected** (pins the non-transitivity of minted authority). Existing fallback-path and admin-client tests updated for the reworded messages and kept green.
- Focused suites: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-narrative.test.ts` → 178 tests passed post-hardening.
- Changed-files gate: `pnpm check:changed` on Blacksmith Testbox → exit 0 (lint, import cycles, repo guards): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28939856076 (first commit) and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28942275771 (hardening commit), both exit 0.
- Multi-agent review pass on this diff (8 finder angles, per-candidate adversarial verification): the privilege-transitivity finding was verified PLAUSIBLE (mechanism confirmed at every static link, reachability timing-dependent on lane drain context) and is fixed by the second commit; confirmed cleanup findings (merge-guard doubling, doc self-contradiction, comment budget, test fixture duplication) are applied.
- Named follow-up (out of scope here): consolidate the duplicated per-plugin model-override policy engines (`subagent.*` in `src/gateway/server-plugins.ts` vs `llm.*` in `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.runtime.ts`), including unifying allowlist canonicalization on `modelKey()` — the two copies already drift on double-prefix suppression.

prs.title: feat: add execution-scoped plugin turn yielding
prs.body:
Related: #109761

Alternative implementation to #101665.

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools cannot currently end the active agent turn after completing a durable handoff. Only the core `sessions_yield` tool can reach the host yield lifecycle, so plugin authors either cannot express this outcome or must rely on host-specific behavior that does not cover static tools, cached descriptors, and every agent harness consistently.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-yield-runtime` API backed by an execution-scoped host lease. Eligible plugin tools opt into the existing direct-only and sequential contracts, request a yield from inside their actual tool body, and share the same first-request controller as `sessions_yield`; the host commits the request only after the tool returns successfully.

The execution-time lease is the canonical owner boundary: it works for factory and static tools, does not capture per-run callbacks in memoized plugin wrappers or descriptor caches, revokes detached work, and avoids changing the generic tool-result protocol. Copilot now enforces the same sequential contract across direct tool handlers and awaits session-abort acknowledgement; Codex dynamic tools already serialize by upstream contract. Standalone plugin-tools MCP execution and remote node tools remain explicitly unsupported because they do not share the in-process turn lifecycle.

No configuration, storage, gateway protocol, or generic `AgentToolResult` shape changes are introduced. The stale duplicate `sessions_yield.onBeforeYield` path is removed.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can call `isTurnYieldAvailable()` and `requestTurnYield(message?)` from a direct-only, sequential tool to complete a handoff and end the current turn without another model round-trip. The first request wins, repeated requests are idempotent, detached async work is revoked, failed tool executions do not yield, and messages are bounded to 1,000 UTF-16-safe characters.

The supported embedded, Codex, and Copilot harnesses use the existing session-yield lifecycle. Unsupported runtimes return `false` from the availability check and reject a yield request with an actionable error.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/plugin-tool-yield.test.ts src/agents/turn-yield-controller.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/tool-yield-context.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.registration.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-yield-tool.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.test.ts src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts extensions/copilot/src/tool-bridge.test.ts` — 372 tests passed across 5 shards.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`, `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports`, and `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` — passed; public surface is 150 entrypoints / 4,824 exports / 2,901 callables.
- Full TypeScript project graph: [`pnpm tsgo:all`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30791477170) — passed on Testbox.
- Production package build: [`pnpm build`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30791997888) — passed on Testbox and verified all 150 public SDK subpaths and declarations.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Structured autoreview of the complete patch — clean, no accepted/actionable findings (0.93 confidence).
- Codex `rust-v0.146.0` contract checked directly: [`ToolExecutor` defaults dynamic tools to nonparallel](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/e363b08c9175ac1cbe5893615dd2cb9ddf95043b/codex-rs/tools/src/tool_executor.rs#L64-L66), [`DynamicToolHandler` does not override that default](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/e363b08c9175ac1cbe5893615dd2cb9ddf95043b/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs#L85-L110), and [nonparallel calls take the write lock](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/e363b08c9175ac1cbe5893615dd2cb9ddf95043b/codex-rs/core/src/tools/parallel.rs#L100-L137).
- Pinned `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.7 source checked directly: `session.abort()` awaits the `session.abort` RPC acknowledgement and propagates connection failures.

Production/package wiring is +307 net lines for the new public capability, execution-lifecycle safety boundary, and cross-harness sequential scheduler. Tests are +719 net lines and docs/generated API evidence are +84 net lines.

prs.title: fix(agents): always classify claude-cli pre-tool narration as commentary
prs.body:
Closes #121558

## What Problem This Solves

Cron and isolated runs on `claude-cli`-backed agents delivered the model's run narration fused onto the front of the announced message — "Connected. Let me pull the daily summaries…", inter-tool status lines, even self-corrections ("HEARTBEAT_OK / Wait — that's wrong…"). Root cause (full evidence in #121558): Claude Code's stream-json carries no phase metadata on assistant text, so OpenClaw classifies pre-tool narration as commentary heuristically — but only when a commentary consumer is wired. Cron wires none, so the classifier never engaged, narration accumulated into the assistant text, and `preferStreamedClaudeTextOverResult` then promoted the fused concatenation over the clean terminal result envelope.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commentary classification for the Claude stream-json dialect is now unconditional instead of consumer-keyed (`src/agents/cli-output-stream.ts`). Narration streams to the consumer when one exists (interactive progress lanes — behavior unchanged) and is dropped when none does (cron/quiet lanes). The result envelope becomes the authoritative final text, with streamed text still backfilling an empty result (the #90450 guarantee).

This matches how every clean lane already works — the codex harness honors the Responses API's protocol-native `phase: commentary` tag, and the embedded anthropic/openai transports stamp commentary phases in the transcript unconditionally, with delivery filtering by phase (see the cross-harness comparison on #121558). Classification-as-recorded-fact, consumer-independent, is the established architecture; claude-cli was the outlier.

With classification unconditional, the superseded-draft boundary machinery (`preferStreamedClaudeTextOverResult`, `missingMessageBoundarySeparator`, six boundary-tracking state variables) became dead on every live path and is removed in the same change. The live-session fallback reparse now also classifies identically to the streaming parser, closing its documented boundary-loss gap.

## User Impact

- Scheduled/cron announce deliveries from `claude-cli` agents carry only the final reply. No cron-executor changes were needed; the fix lands at the parser owner boundary.
- Interactive lanes with commentary/progress streaming enabled are byte-identical.
- Interactive lanes with commentary off no longer fuse narration into replies, aligning claude-cli with the embedded anthropic/openai lanes and the codex harness (also softens #25592 for this backend).
- Streaming granularity: with no consumer, assistant deltas now arrive merged at flush boundaries — the granularity commentary-enabled lanes already had.
- Known limitation (documented in #121558): narration the model writes inside its single final message when extended thinking does not engage is a model behavior, out of reach of the parser; mitigation is prompt-side.

Production LOC is net negative: 51 insertions / 163 deletions across the change; the production files alone drop ~80 lines.

## Evidence

- Root cause proven end-to-end in #121558: OTel/Phoenix trace comparison (clean runs = narration in reasoning blocks; leaky runs = narration in visible text), raw Claude CLI session transcripts showing narration as separate pre-tool text blocks, and three weeks of delivery mirrors from a production instance.
- Focused suites green post-change and post-rebase: parser suites (36), cli-runner + live-session + cron isolated-agent + subagent announce delivery (308), gateway agent-events (142), auto-reply CLI progress/dispatch (39). `pnpm tsgo` clean, oxlint clean, oxfmt applied.
- Rewritten tests pin the new invariant, including the exact cron shape: "classifies pre-tool text as commentary even when no consumer is wired" and "drops unconsumed pre-tool commentary and delivers only the result envelope". With-consumer commentary tests unchanged.
- Autoreview (codex, gpt-5.6-sol, high reasoning): clean, no P0 findings — "behavioral changes are deliberate and covered by updated tests."

prs.title: fix(ci): bound test-line growth on the release fast lane
prs.body:
Closes #192405

## What Problem This Solves

Release-tooling PRs carrying `release-fast-lane` could add test lines without a budget allocation while every required gate stayed green, because the lane skips the baseline-ratchet bundle and `security-fast` only ran the test-line guard on main pushes.

- Problem: `runBaselineRatchets` is disabled for the lane (`scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs:518`), and the `security-fast` ratchet step is gated to `push` on `main`, so no PR-time job checked the test-line budget.
- Solution: in `security-fast`, for labeled fast-lane PRs, run the existing dependency-free checker against the merge's verified first parent before landing.
- What changed: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and one regression test under `test/scripts/`.
- What did NOT change: the lane's required jobs, runner set, baseline bundle, and the budget itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

The narrowest retained guard is the existing checker on the comparison base CI already verifies, so no runner, dependency install, or wider bundle is needed.

- Best fix: reuse `scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts` — it imports only Node built-ins, so it runs under the job's existing Node 24.22.1 setup with no install step.
- Base: `security-fast` already verifies the merge commit's shape in "Resolve security diff base" (HEAD, first parent, second parent, no extras) and publishes that first parent; the step consumes the same `steps.diff_base.outputs.sha`.
- Alternative: enable the full baseline bundle for the lane — rejected by the issue; it also contradicts keeping the route narrow.
- Risk / non-goals: the ceiling is absolute, so a tree already over budget still fails an additive PR even when its growth is fully allocated — the ordinary ratchet job behaves the same way today. The guard never fails on inherited debt alone, because the checker returns success when net delta is not positive.

## User Impact

A `release-fast-lane` PR that adds test lines without a matching allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/` now fails in `security-fast` before landing, instead of silently leaving inherited debt on `main`.

## Evidence

Regression test — red on the base workflow, green with the change:

```console
$ node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts \
    test/scripts/ci-release-fast-lane-test-lines.test.ts

# base (step absent)
Error: expected Check release fast lane test-line budget to be defined
 Test Files  1 failed (1)

# this branch
 ✓ rejects unallocated growth against the merge's first parent
 ✓ passes when the checker accepts the tree
 ✓ fails closed when the merge has no verified first parent
 Tests  4 passed (4)
```

The test pins the label and verified-base gating, the exact checker invocation, propagation of a rejecting checker exit, and fail-closed behaviour without a verified base.

Checker runs against a real first parent, under the Node version the job sets up (24.22.2 locally, matching `REQUESTED_NODE_VERSION: "24.22.1"`):

```console
# no test changes in the PR
$ node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base <first-parent> --no-merge-base
Test lines: 6446620; ceiling: 6446483; over by: 137; net delta: 0.
Tree is over the ceiling; this change does not add test lines.
exit 0

# +63 staged test lines, no allocation (the #192297 shape)
Test lines: 6446683; ceiling: 6446483; over by: 200; net delta: +63.
exit 1
```

Workflow and shell validation: `yaml.safe_load` on `ci.yml` succeeds, and `bash -n` on the step's run block succeeds.

### What still needs a maintainer

The new step is skipped on this PR because it only runs for pull requests labeled `release-fast-lane`, and contributors cannot apply repository labels — GitHub rejects `AddLabelsToLabelable` for this account. Applying that label (here or on any labeled release-tooling PR) will make the step run and produce the requested Actions log; the regression above executes the same command and covers exit propagation.

Unrelated CI: `checks-ui` currently fails in three `ui/` tests (`app-sidebar.interactions`, `usage-page-export-interruption`, `widget-card`) that this workflow-only PR does not touch; they reproduce independently of this change.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `grep`, `gh` and local checker runs to trace why the lane skipped the budget guard, then pinned the new step with a regression that executes its shell. The implementer understands the code: the lane keeps its job set, and the only added gate is the existing checker bound to the first parent that `security-fast` already verifies. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope image capability discovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- scope attachment image-capability fallback to the selected provider instead of rebuilding every provider catalog
- keep runtime-only models by using the existing request-scoped live catalog path
- retry the complete Gateway projection when its published runtime owner is replaced during scoped discovery

## Root cause and owner

Attachment admission first reads the lifecycle-published catalog. When a selected runtime-only model is absent or has provisional text-only metadata, current main falls back to `readOnly: false`, which rebuilds the full cross-provider catalog inside the request. The provider-scoped catalog machinery exists, but this Gateway caller did not use it.

The canonical owner is the Gateway catalog projection. The second read now carries the selected provider into the existing prepared request-scoped live catalog. The projection checks the published owner before and after the asynchronous scoped read and reacquires the full owner on replacement, so catalog, config, agent identity, and auth projection never mix generations.

## ClawSweeper findings

- Early owner replacement: fixed by retrying at the Gateway projection boundary; the regression replaces the owner during scoped discovery and proves only the replacement catalog returns.
- Final provider I/O fence: the old branch tried to turn generation liveness into a public provider-auth revocation contract, but that was incomplete and added a large cross-plugin surface. This port removes that contract. Published-generation liveness governs whether results may publish; it does not retroactively revoke already-started provider requests. Results from a retired generation are discarded and the owner is reacquired.
- Runtime-only models: retained. An independent P1 review caught and rejected an intermediate static-only rewrite; the final branch uses the existing scoped live mode.
- Test-cost evidence: recorded below for the new image-capability file and the combined focused Gateway set.

## Scope

Seven Gateway files changed against integrated main: 222 insertions and 60 deletions. Reuses the existing scoped catalog owner; no provider/plugin implementation changes, new configuration, or cache.

## Validation

- Integrated main: `1f01f4944d45eb265081f8bfbf8d3e8e54ff4266`; resolved conflicts while retaining current static-capability and projection owners.
- Three focused Gateway suites: 86 tests passed (image capability, catalog projection, session utilities).
- Core production typecheck and targeted lint passed; `git diff --check` clean.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the seven-file candidate diff. Surrounding loader implementations were not included in the isolated reviewer bundle; integration assurance also relies on focused tests and source inspection.
- Previous validation counts and hosted evidence were for the old head and are not current-head proof.
- No new real-channel/live-provider proof was run.
- CI follow-up: the new catalog mock now accepts the loader's optional argument. The affected Gateway-server test-type leaf passed; 16 catalog tests passed. Current head: `8a7567d2df5d`. Replacement exact-head CI is pending, not claimed green.

Agent transcript omitted.

prs.title: docs(i18n): expand Russian glossary (250 entries) and add ru navigation (12 tabs / 55 groups)
prs.body:
## What

Russian docs localization is wired up but nearly empty: `docs/.i18n/glossary.ru.json` was 21 entries (1.2 KB) against 107 KB for `zh-CN`, and `ru-navigation.json` did not exist at all, so the Russian sidebar fell back to English while the pages themselves were already 75% translated.

This PR fills in the two files that drive the Russian locale:

- `glossary.ru.json`: **21 → 250 entries** (1.2 KB → 18.6 KB). Existing entries and their order are preserved; 6 target terms were corrected for consistency with the pages: Compaction → Сжатие контекста, Gateway → Шлюз, Node → Нода, Plugin → Плагин, Skills → Скиллы, Webhook → Вебхук. Deliberately kept in English: Active Memory, Cron, Dreaming, Heartbeat, Loopback, Markdown, Self-hosted.
- `ru-navigation.json`: **created from scratch — 12 tabs, 55 groups** (8.6 KB), mirroring the English navigation structure.

No page content, no build scripts, no English strings touched: two data files only.

## Verification

- Every path in `ru-navigation.json` was checked against the repository tree (1,385 `.md` files): 0 broken links, 55 unique anchors.
- Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`: 12/12 Russian tabs, 55/55 groups, pages resolve as `ru/index…`.
- `glossary.ru.json` parses as valid JSON and keeps the original key order (`json.load` round-trip diff on the untouched prefix).
- Note: `check-docs-i18n-glossary.mts` only validates `zh-CN` today, so this file is not CI-gated — I verified it manually as described above.

## Why

The Russian locale is the largest non-English audience for OpenClaw docs and currently has English headings over Russian text. These two files are the smallest, highest-leverage change: no translation work, but the sidebar and the inline glossary switch to Russian immediately.

## Visual proof

Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`, locale `ru`, same tree, only `docs/.i18n/ru-navigation.json` added.

| Before (`main` — no ru overlay) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamant064/openclaw/docs/ru-i18n-proof/proof/ru-sidebar-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamant064/openclaw/docs/ru-i18n-proof/proof/ru-sidebar-after.png) |

Behavioural comparison of the two composed configs:

```
before: tabs 12, groups 55, pages 308
after : tabs 12, groups 55, pages 308      # page inventory identical
before tabs: Get started | Install | Channels | Agents | Capabilities | Models |
             Platforms | Gateway & Ops | Reference | Releases | Contributing | Help
after  tabs: Начало работы | Установка | Каналы | Агенты | Возможности | Модели |
             Платформы | Шлюз и эксплуатация | Справочник | Релизы | Участие в разработке | Помощь
```

Only labels change; every route and its order is preserved, which is the guarantee the overlay functions (`applyLocaleNavLabelOverlay`) are supposed to give. Screenshots are generated from the composed `docs.json` (sidebar label tree), not from a live docs host, so nothing is redacted and no endpoint is involved.

prs.title: fix(ci): release fast lane can land unallocated test growth
prs.body:
Closes #192405

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes release-tooling PRs landing unallocated test growth because their narrow CI route skips the test-line budget check.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. CI checks the existing budget before landing while keeping the release fast lane and its smaller job inventory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run the unchanged, dependency-free checker inside the existing required security job, using its verified merge first parent. No new job, dependency setup, full baseline bundle, budget relaxation, or removed coverage.

The existing shallow-checkout regression now runs the actual workflow command: one unallocated line fails, one exact indexed allocation passes. A separate 43-line allocation funds exactly its 43 added regression lines; the shared baseline is unchanged.

## Evidence

- [The escaped release PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192297) added 65 unallocated test lines; [its CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41730525051) passed security-fast and the aggregate gate with baseline ratchets skipped.
- On head `69a89e67040236f82531ab975f3f5a4e3a568494`, the two focused workflow/checker files pass: 200 active tests, 8 existing skips. The added regression fails with the baseline workflow because its budget step is absent, then passes with this fix. It executes the real workflow command against a shallow synthetic PR merge: unallocated growth fails; exact allocation credit passes.
- Targeted tooling-test typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, workflow validation (including zizmor), and `git diff --check` pass. Full Git-index budget accounting passes with zero slack: 6,445,993 LF against a ceiling of 6,445,993.
- Fresh independent source review and local committed-range ClawSweeper review found no actionable issues. The subsequently incorporated main correction leaves all four reviewed patch files and their proof inputs unchanged.
- Main independently reconciled the historical 47-line debt in `d27139b2b220327d6f65b659c6fba0b0110fad97`; this branch includes that correction. This PR changes no shared scalar and allocates only its own 43 added test lines.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41747013862) completed with 48 successful jobs and four independently attributed inherited failures, plus the downstream aggregate. Security-fast passed. The failed budget job retains the exact main parent’s 137-line debt: this PR adds 43 LF and exactly 43 credit, preserving the same debt. The 137 unallocated LF came from the recent toast changes on main.
- The three UI shards report 19 failures inherited from [toast severity/copy changes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192015), [arrival placement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192016), and [toast lane fixture changes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192014). The complete UI tree and all 27 named failing test/helper/owner blobs are identical between tested merge `83422df6065e01f8b7a10ad1346a0a5ea73890c3` and its main parent `847080e81b2cb282165090424cd5a8de5cc45c37`. No separate baseline UI execution or successful broad CI is claimed.
- Landing uses the native attributed inherited-failure route under maintainer scope, retaining the failed CI and source evidence. This fix prevents an observed CI regression path; it does not claim a measured Blacksmith invoice reduction.

prs.title: ci(i18n): add non-publishing native locale refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where maintainers cannot refresh secret-backed native translations for review without also creating and arming an auto-merge generated PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit non-publishing dispatch mode that runs the existing bounded locale matrix and validation, then uploads an allowlisted binary patch artifact. The default publishing path remains unchanged.

Secret-backed non-publishing runs execute only from the trusted `main` workflow. The operator supplies an exact source SHA; that SHA must be the current head of one open, non-draft PR targeting `main` with GitHub's current review decision `APPROVED`. Each locale worker revalidates the exact PR head and current approval immediately before the translation-secret step. Branch-selected preflight support was removed: guards inside branch-controlled YAML cannot independently guarantee secret isolation. Manual runs use the trusted main workflow definition.

## User Impact

No direct user-facing change. Maintainers gain a review-only native translation refresh path that cannot push, open a PR, or enable auto-merge, while non-publishing source selection requires current exact-head review approval.

## Evidence

### November 2 review-readiness repair

- Removed the branch-selected preflight mode and restored the main-only dispatch contract, addressing the P1 workflow-boundary finding without adding another execution path.
- Focused workflow contract regression: fails on the previous head at the branch-admission condition; passes after the repair (1 test, 4.97s runner wall).
- Workflow validation passed, including pinned tooling fallback and zizmor.
- Changed-surface checks passed: formatting, root-test typechecks, dependency/coercion/dead-export guards, and script/test lint. `git diff --check` passed.
- Repair delta: 12 insertions / 37 deletions across workflow and guard test; removed the separate preflight input, scheduling branch, and branch-dispatch route.
- Local autoreview of this repair against `7bf16b8fd47f07612777b4957b1a14bbc66eba42`: scoped-clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings.
- Remaining integration proof: no new credentialed translation run was dispatched. The earlier hosted translation/artifact run predates the current approval checks, so it does not prove approved and revoked-source behavior for this head. That remains an explicit pre-merge validation gap.

### CI integration repair

- Integrated main `1f01f4944d45` to resolve a concrete CI failure: the new non-publishing upload step retained an old action pin while main's canonical workflow helper required the updated pin.
- Both upload steps now use main's existing upload-artifact v7.0.2 pin; the dispatch/security repair is unchanged.
- Focused workflow regression: 1 passed on the integrated candidate. Full workflow validation, including zizmor, passed. `git diff --check` passed.
- Current head: `ae494551c445`; replacement exact-head CI is pending. Prior failed run is not claimed passing.

### Earlier branch evidence (not current-head proof)

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/native-app-locale-refresh-workflow.test.ts` — 1 passed on exact head after rebase
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- .github/workflows/native-app-locale-refresh.yml test/scripts/native-app-locale-refresh-workflow.test.ts` — changed-surface format, type, lint, dependency, coercion, and dead-export gates passed
- `pnpm format:check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- .github/workflows/native-app-locale-refresh.yml test/scripts/native-app-locale-refresh-workflow.test.ts` — passed after rebase
- `git diff --check` — passed after rebase
- Autoreview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings (confidence 0.87)
- Security boundary: non-publishing translation requires `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`; `source_sha` is exact, PR-bound, currently approved, and revalidated directly before the secret-bearing step. The advertised branch-selected preflight mode has been removed; manual runs are main-only.
- Production LOC: 0. Workflow policy: +198/-12. Guard tests: +101.

prs.title: fix(agents): don't apply subagent default tool denies to visible spawned sessions
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Sessions created with `sessions_spawn` `visible: true` are interactive sessions that a person keeps chatting in from the sidebar. They are currently treated as subagent envelopes, so `resolveSubagentToolPolicyForSession` applies the built-in `SUBAGENT_TOOL_DENY_ALWAYS` list (only `message` was exempted) and, at leaf depth, `SUBAGENT_TOOL_DENY_LEAF`.

On the Codex harness this has an outsized effect. `sessions_send`, `conversations_*` and the leaf `sessions_*`/`subagents` denies are not in `CODEX_TOOL_POLICY_SAFE_DENY_NAMES`, so the turn becomes policy-restricted and the whole Codex native shell/file surface is disabled. Where the deployment also excludes the gateway-local fallback tools, a visible spawned session ends up with no shell or file tools at all, while ordinary dashboard sessions on the same agent keep `bash`/`apply_patch`.

Background exec exit notifications are also suppressed for these sessions, as they are for hidden workers.

## User impact

Visible spawned sessions behave like the interactive sessions they are:

- The built-in subagent default denies (always and leaf) no longer apply to them. On Codex, they keep the native shell/file surface when the parent is unrestricted.
- Background exec exit notifications are delivered to them again.

## What is preserved

- Visible spawns keep their subagent envelope. Inherited and delegated tool policy still apply, so a visible spawn from a restricted turn stays restricted.
- Operator-configured `tools.subagents.tools` allow/deny still applies to visible spawns.
- Spawn admission (depth cap and child limits) is unchanged. Visible spawns regain `sessions_spawn`/`subagents`, but admission still enforces the caps.
- Hidden subagents (`agent:*:subagent:*`) are unchanged: same default denies, same Codex restriction, same notification suppression.
- Classification uses the persisted entry (`createdVia: "spawn"` via `isVisibleSpawnedSession`), never key shape alone.

## Authority boundary

The only policy change is which built-in default list `resolveSubagentToolPolicyForSession` returns for a persisted visible spawn. Nothing that enforces policy at the point of effect changes:

- Inherited policy is resolved separately by `resolveInheritedToolPolicyForSession` and is untouched. The new restricted-parent case shows an inherited `exec` deny still marks the Codex turn restricted (native shell/file surface off), the same mechanism every restricted session uses.
- Delegated policy, including revocation, is enforced by the unchanged delegated-tool-policy and mediated-delegation owners (`src/agents/delegated-tool-policy.test.ts`, `src/agents/harness/mediated-delegation-effects.test.ts`).
- Operator-configured `tools.subagents.tools.deny` is still appended for visible spawns (`tools-effective-inventory.policy.test.ts`, "configured subagent deny" case).
- `sessions_spawn` admission still rejects a visible spawn's own child at the depth cap before any Gateway call (`sessions-spawn-tool.visible-depth.test-support.ts`).

No stored-data change: `createdVia`, `spawnDepth` and `spawnedBy` are existing session fields, and a dashboard session without `createdVia: "spawn"` keeps the previous behavior ("unstamped dashboard child" cases).

## Changes

- `src/agents/agent-tools.policy.ts`: skip `SUBAGENT_TOOL_DENY_ALWAYS`/`LEAF` for visible spawned sessions; configured denies still apply.
- `src/agents/bash-process-durable-notify.ts`, `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-request-preparation.ts`: only hidden subagent envelopes suppress exit notifications.
- `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-capabilities.ts`: `isVisibleSpawnedSession` accepts an already-read entry.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/visible-spawn-default-tool-denies.txt`: allocates the 94 net regression-test lines.
- Tests and docs (`docs/tools/subagents*.md`, `docs/tools/exec.md`, `docs/gateway/background-process.md`, `docs/plugins/codex-harness-reference/restricted-turns.md`).

## Evidence

Focused tests (all passed):

```
node scripts/test-projects.mts \
  src/agents/harness/codex-subagent-tool-policy.test.ts \
  src/agents/bash-process-durable-notify.test.ts \
  src/agents/bash-tools.visible-subagent-notify.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.policy.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-capabilities.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.policy.test.ts
```

Covered cases: (a) visible spawn with an unrestricted parent gets no default denies and Codex stays unrestricted; (b) visible spawn from a restricted parent stays restricted; (c) hidden subagent unchanged (denies and Codex restriction); (d) spawn depth limit still enforced from a visible spawn; (e) exit notification on for a visible spawn, off for a hidden subagent, including restart-adopted durable processes.

Test-line budget: the regression coverage adds 94 net test lines (the visible-spawn durable-notify case is folded into the existing eligibility table). They are allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/visible-spawn-default-tool-denies.txt`; the shared scalar is unchanged. The test-line ratchet still reports the tree over its ceiling by the amount `main` itself is over (its own check passes only because it adds no lines), so that residual is inherited from `main`.

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint of changed files and the other guards pass. The dead-export scan reports unused exports in `src/gateway/node-plugin-tool-snapshot.ts`, a file this PR does not touch; that failure is pre-existing on `main`.

## Not in scope

Hidden Codex subagents still lose the native surface because of the same session/conversation denies. That needs a separate change (disabling only Codex native delegation for those turns, or a harness-routed fallback) and is tracked separately.

prs.title: fix(codex): retain native thread reasoning effort
prs.body:
## Summary

- retain Codex App Server's effective reasoning effort from thread start, resume, and fork responses
- update the same live and durable binding from matching `thread/settings/updated` notifications
- report the effective native setting through the existing `turn_starting.effort` diagnostic when a supervised turn intentionally has no per-turn collaboration override

## Root cause and canonical fix

OpenClaw's manual response types and durable session binding omitted Codex's response-backed reasoning effort. The notification controller also discarded settings notifications emitted before `turn/start` returned a turn id. Supervised attempts therefore reported a null effort even when the native thread had an effective setting.

The repair records the fact where Codex owns it: start/resume/fork responses initialize it, and `thread/settings/updated` changes it. All binding writers carry the same nullable field. Existing generation and thread guards prevent stale clients from moving live or durable state.

This current-main rewrite does not add `thread_ready.reasoningEffort` or another event field. It fills the long-standing `turn_starting.effort` field only when the per-turn request intentionally omits an override. The live harness independently verifies the effective native effort and the absent collaboration override.

## Dependency contract

The integrated plugin pins `@openai/codex` 0.164.0. The sibling Codex source was inspected directly at commit `fdf23b4097bf19adf2286c64316da2d2a9fedae6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs` defines response-backed nullable `reasoning_effort` for thread start/resume and `ThreadSettings.effort` for settings updates. Native thread facts remain separate from per-turn overrides.

## Coverage and change shape

Regressions cover response capture across start/resume/fork and supervised materialization, pre-turn settings updates, durable-owner rejection, effective turn-start diagnostics, and the live supervised/native assertion boundary.

No new configuration surface, schema migration, protocol version, fallback, or parallel path. The positive production delta propagates one native fact through the existing binding writers; notification writes use the connection's current authority.

## Validation

- Current head: `ae1b83e6b0bd`; integrated main: `1f01f4944d45`.
- 89 tests passed across three affected files during conflict repair.
- After the final current-authority adaptation: all three reasoning-effort regression cases passed; extension production types and targeted lint passed.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the supplied candidate diff; unchanged surrounding source was unavailable to the isolated reviewer.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- No fresh credentialed live Codex run. Historical CI and hosted review are not current-head evidence.
- Exact-head CI pending after publication; not claimed green.

Agent transcript omitted.

prs.title: fix: exclude fenced dreaming ranges from memory indexing and recall signal
prs.body:
Closes #172547

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed dreaming output written into daily memory notes under `openclaw:dreaming` fences is embedded, returned by memory search, and staged into short-term recall, even though it is scratchwork that can never be promoted.

Scope confirmation: this branch implements the scope Peter Steinberger set on #172547 on 2026-10-27: "Managed inline dreaming fences should be excluded from default memory retrieval, before chunking." and "@CloudCorpRecords, please go ahead with your branch on that scope."

## User Impact

User impact: memory search and recall signals no longer surface fenced dreaming scratchwork, while ordinary note content keeps its exact citation line numbers and the note files themselves are never modified. Indexes built by earlier versions rebuild once through the existing chunking generation, so already-indexed fenced chunks are reconciled away, and already-staged fenced candidates stay unpromotable through the existing rehydration owner. No new config option.

## Why This Change Was Made

Index preparation now blanks managed fenced ranges (blank lines, never deletions, so line numbers stay exact) before chunking, for memory sources only. The fence policy lives in one new owner, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/dreaming-fences.ts`, exported through the host internals and the `memory-core-host-engine-indexing` plugin SDK surface. Promotion rehydration imports the same helpers and its private copy of the fence regexes and overlap logic is deleted, so indexing and promotion cannot drift on what a fence is. `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION` moves from 6 to 7 so the existing reindex owner rebuilds stored indexes instead of a parallel migration.

## Evidence

- New unit tests for the shared module: 12/12 pass (closed, unclosed, mixed, stray-marker, and CRLF cases).
- Index-preparation tests, including two new fence cases (mixed note excluded with original line numbers; fence-only note produces no chunks): 9/9 pass.
- Differential fuzz of the shared overlap helper against the pre-cutover rehydration implementation, transcribed verbatim: 72,871 cases, 0 mismatches (an earlier run of the same comparison covered 235,839 cases, also 0 mismatches).
- Acceptance scenario from the issue thread, exercised at the preparation and promotion-guard boundaries: a synthetic daily note with ordinary facts before and after a managed fence produces no chunk containing fenced text or markers, chunk texts and start/end lines are identical to a pre-blanked control (the after-fence fact still ends at its original line), the source string is unchanged, and the promotion guard refuses the fenced range and both marker lines while admitting the ordinary lines.
- Red/green check: the pre-change path (strip annotation carriers, then chunk) leaks the fenced text into chunks; the new path does not, and keeps the ordinary facts.
- `tsc --strict` on the new module: clean.

Honest limits: the local runs above used a vitest-shim harness because this sandbox cannot install the repo toolchain (pnpm self-install fails here), so the repo's own test suite, typecheck, and lint are CI's to confirm. The full end-to-end pass from the issue (real memory index, search, and promote paths with isolated state and a real local embedding model) was not run locally because no local embedding model is available in this environment; it is a reviewer or CI step, not something claimed here. The branch was brought current with main by a merge commit; conflicts were resolved by reapplying the branch changes at their current locations, and the resulting diff against main is exactly the 8 intended files.

prs.title: fix(qa): correct SIGKILL recovery expectation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a release-validation QA failure when an eligible active session resumes after its Gateway is killed with `SIGKILL`.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The QA test now checks the current crash-recovery contract instead of requiring eligible work to remain idle.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test retained the no-resume expectation from #185730. #190964 intentionally added recovery of persisted active runs after `SIGKILL`, and #190995 restricted unmarked recovery to the immediately preceding Gateway lifetime. The release failure and an unchanged local reproduction both contained the actual restart-resume input, not merely a late pre-kill request.

The test now observes requests after confirmed process death, distinguishes fresh user input from provider history, and requires exactly one resume input without replaying the original user input. It also verifies one original input and one resume in the transcript, a successful subsequent user reply, and terminal settlement in the same session. The existing Gateway recovery E2E retains the abandoned-session negative boundary; this PR does not change that boundary or production code.
