prs.title: fix: config unset prunes emptied parent objects
prs.body:
Closes #191889

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config unset <path>` leaves stale empty object parents (e.g. `"logging": {}`) in the config file instead of pruning them.

## User Impact

After `config unset`, config files no longer keep empty object sections (`logging: {}`, `plugins.entries.<id>: {}`); empty arrays like `tools.allow: []` are still preserved because an empty allowlist is meaningful. Agent roster entries are preserved: removing an agent's last override clears the field but keeps the keyed entry (`agents.entries.research: {}`), because only a whole-entry deletion may remove an agent. No config behavior changes, only tidier authored files.

## Why This Change Was Made

`config unset` deletes the leaf value from the in-memory config before the write path runs, so when the write path's `applyUnsetPathsForWrite` reaches the unset path the leaf is already gone and its `Object.hasOwn` guard returns early — the empty-parent pruning never runs. The fix prunes emptied plain-object parents with the same semantics as the write path, but consolidates the pruning in the existing config mutation owner so CLI and persistence share one policy:

- `src/config/config-path-mutation.ts` now owns the prune policy (`pruneEmptyConfigParents`, shared with the CLI) and the write-path `unsetPathForWriteAt` applies the same rule. This keeps the recursive empty-object removal, empty-object array splice, and empty-array retention from #148216 in one owner.
- `src/cli/config-cli-path.ts` `unsetAtPath` keeps its leaf deletion and the mutation receipt from #140326 (the array/object receipt that prevents repeated array removal) and delegates parent pruning to the shared owner.
- Keyed `agents.entries.<id>` entries are a meaningful boundary: an inner-field unset leaves the entry as `{}` so the roster-loss guard accepts the save; a whole-entry unset still removes it.

## Review responses

- **P1 (preserve agent entries when their last override is unset):** fixed. `pruneEmptyConfigParents` stops at `agents.entries.<id>`, so `config unset agents.entries.research.name` keeps `research: {}` and the write succeeds. Covered by a unit test, a roster integration test through persistence (including a reload-valid check), and an `applyUnsetPathsForWrite` owner test.
- **P2 (consolidate pruning in the existing config mutation owner):** done. The CLI's private `pruneEmptyObjectParents` is removed; the CLI now calls the shared `pruneEmptyConfigParents` in `config-path-mutation.ts`, and `unsetPathForWriteAt` shares the same roster-boundary predicate.
- **P2 (narrow the parent container before indexing it):** the pruning now lives in the shared owner using `isRecord` guards — no new type assertions (assertion-safety ratchet green).
- **P2 (test budget):** removed the three unit tests that duplicated the command-to-disk integration coverage; kept a distinct whole-entry roster unit test and added the meaningful empty-agent-entry regression. Allocation updated to the actual added test-line delta.
- **P2 (preserve roster entries only when pruning an ancestor):** fixed. The roster-boundary predicate now also requires the emptied child to be an ancestor of the requested leaf (`depth < pathSegments.length - 1`), so an explicit whole-entry unset (`agents.entries.research`) still removes the entry from the persisted payload while an inner-field unset keeps `research: {}`. Added the write-owner whole-entry deletion regression (`io.write-prepare.test.ts`) and dropped the duplicated inner-field unit case; the test-lines allocation now tracks the consolidated 128 added lines.

## Evidence

Tests (all green): unit tests in `src/cli/config-cli-path.test.ts`; command-to-disk integration tests in `src/cli/config-cli.unset-prunes.integration.test.ts`; roster-entry persistence test in `src/cli/config-cli.roster.integration.test.ts`; write-owner test in `src/config/io.write-prepare.test.ts`. Also green: `tsgo:core`, focused oxlint, assertion-safety ratchet, test-lines ratchet, test-mock-exports ratchet, max-lines ratchet, and the affected suites (`config-cli.reference-values`, `io.write-config` intent cases, `mutate`, `io.deferred-plugin-migrations`, `io.session-store-owner`).

### Real CLI output — normal shipped launcher

Each command ran through the normal CLI launcher (`node openclaw.mjs`, the dist-bundle entry built from this head, `2026.10.10 (3f28cc8)`) against an isolated `openclaw.json` in a temp directory with a fresh state dir, so nothing below touches a real user profile or credentials. `meta` is the auto-managed stamp every write adds; keys, IPs, phone numbers, and endpoints are all synthetic.

```
$ node openclaw.mjs --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (3f28cc8)

### Scenario: logging-prune
Before (openclaw.json):
{"logging":{"level":"debug"},"tools":{"allow":["a","b"]}}

$ node openclaw.mjs config unset logging.level
Removed logging.level. No gateway restart needed.
Exit code: 0
After (openclaw.json):
{
  "tools": { "allow": ["a", "b"] },
  "meta": { "migrations": { "modelPolicyAllowlist": true, "utilityModelSeparation": true, "skillWorkshopPlugin": true }, "lastTouchedVersion": "2026.10.10" }
}

### Scenario: array-splice
Before (openclaw.json):
{"plugins":{"entries":{"example":{"config":{"values":[{"value":"a"},{"value":"b"}]}}}}}

$ node openclaw.mjs config unset plugins.entries.example.config.values.0.value
Removed plugins.entries.example.config.values[0].value. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
Exit code: 0
After (openclaw.json):
{ "plugins": { "entries": { "example": { "config": { "values": [{ "value": "b" }] } } } }, "meta": { ... } }

### Scenario: empty-array
Before (openclaw.json):
{"tools":{"allow":["a"]}}

$ node openclaw.mjs config unset tools.allow.0
Removed tools.allow[0]. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
Exit code: 0
After (openclaw.json):
{ "tools": { "allow": [] }, "meta": { ... } }

### Scenario: roster-entry (inner-field unset keeps the keyed entry)
Before (openclaw.json):
{"agents":{"ownership":"explicit","entries":{"main":{},"research":{"name":"Research"}}}}

$ node openclaw.mjs config unset agents.entries.research.name
Removed agents.entries.research.name. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
Exit code: 0
After (openclaw.json):
{ "agents": { "ownership": "explicit", "entries": { "main": {}, "research": {} } }, "meta": { ... } }

### Scenario: whole-entry-roster (explicit removal still works)
Before (openclaw.json):
{"agents":{"ownership":"explicit","entries":{"main":{},"research":{"name":"Research"}}}}

$ node openclaw.mjs config unset agents.entries.research
Removed agents.entries.research. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
Exit code: 0
After (openclaw.json):
{ "agents": { "ownership": "explicit", "entries": { "main": {} } }, "meta": { ... } }
```

Every scenario exits 0. `logging.level` unset prunes the emptied `logging` section while `tools.allow` is untouched; the array element removal splices the array instead of emptying it; unsetting the last allowlist entry leaves `tools.allow: []`; the inner-field roster unset keeps `research: {}` (roster-loss guard passes), and the whole-entry unset still removes `research` outright.

### Data-model compatibility after upgrade

An `openclaw.json` authored by the latest stable release (it still contains an emptied `logging: {}` section) loads, validates, reads, and writes under this head:

```
$ node openclaw.mjs config validate
Config valid: .../upgrade-compat/openclaw.json
Exit code: 0

$ node openclaw.mjs config get logging.level
Config path is valid but unset: logging.level. The runtime default applies until you set an authored value with openclaw config set logging.level <value>.
Exit code: 1   (expected: key was unset)

$ node openclaw.mjs config set logging.level debug
Updated logging.level. No gateway restart needed.
Exit code: 0
After set (openclaw.json):
{
  "gateway": { "mode": "local" },
  "logging": { "level": "debug" },
  "tools": { "allow": ["a", "b"] },
  "agents": { "ownership": "explicit", "entries": { "main": {} } },
  "meta": { "migrations": { "modelPolicyAllowlist": true, "utilityModelSeparation": true, "skillWorkshopPlugin": true }, "lastTouchedVersion": "2026.10.10" }
}
```

Existing stored data (including empty sections this change would clean up on a later write) loads and validates unchanged, unset keys read as "valid but unset", and writes still work. The write-path change only affects unsets of a keyed agent entry's inner field when the leaf is still present (a path the CLI no longer produces because it prunes first); existing stored configs load and validate unchanged, and the roster-loss guard still rejects any unauthorized whole-entry removal.

## AI-assisted

This change was developed with AI assistance (CoMind). Root cause, fix, and tests were reviewed and verified locally by the author against the real CLI and write-path semantics.

## What Problem This Solves

Opening the @mention picker in an active chat showed globally online/alphabetical names before the humans who had actually posted there.

## User Impact

- Current-chat speakers appear first, newest message sender first.
- Members without a sent message follow speakers; other eligible people retain the stable online/name/profile-ID fallback.
- Search matching, self-exclusion, and recipient access checks are unchanged. Message recency from other chats is not used.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rank at the users.mentionable producer, before the 100-recipient limit, so UI-only sorting cannot lose a current-chat speaker outside the old global top 100. Reuse existing worker-read participant contribution timestamps, resolving retained sender IDs through the canonical profile owner and keeping their maximum timestamp; no transcript scan, schema, config, or permission changes. Preserve the target-cache preparation used by the legacy synchronous recipient validator. Document the ordering.

prs.title: fix(channels): text-only reply to a photo reports source_modality "image"
prs.body:
Closes #192253
Resubmits #192277, which the open-PR limit closed at 21:16Z. #192286 (opened at 21:22Z) targets the same issue by pinning `SourceModality` before the merge and adding a shared modality helper; this one is the 4-line finalizer change with the end-to-end check below. Happy to close either way.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: per-turn `Conversation info` says `"source_modality":"image"` when a user replies to a photo with text only.

## User Impact

User impact: a text-only reply to a photo is now described as `"source_modality":"text"`, so the model is no longer told the user sent an image. The replied photo is still attached for inspection, and replies that carry their own photo, voice note or file report that modality as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared channel finalizer appends quote media to the turn's media list so the model can see the replied photo. When a channel states no modality, the inbound metadata derives `source_modality` from the first media kind in that list, so a reply with no attachment picked up the quoted photo. The finalizer is the last place that knows which media belong to the current message: when quote media joins a turn that has none of its own, it now records the message as `text` unless the channel stated a modality (Telegram's `voice` still wins). Messages without quote media are unchanged, including plain text, where the field stays absent.

This covers every channel that hands quote media to the shared finalizer: Telegram (measured below) and Discord replies to other users' messages (same code path, not run end to end). No per-channel changes.

pr-simplify: the fix stays inside the finalizer that does the merge, and the renderer keeps the one media-to-modality mapping. I did not move that mapping into a shared helper for the finalizer: it would add an export and gives the same answer for every case measured here. Deltas vs merge base: production +4, tests +22, test-lines allocation +2.

## Evidence

- Unit test in `src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts` builds the context through `buildChannelInboundEventContext` and renders it through `buildInboundUserContextPrefix`. On base `f5f27c3ef6e` the text-reply row fails with `"source_modality":"image"`; with the fix all 19 pass. The other rows fail if the fix overrides a stated `voice`, pins `text` on a reply that has its own photo, or drops the quoted photo from a text reply (each checked by mutating the fix).
- End to end: the Gateway harness from #192254 (real Gateway, Telegram plugin, loopback Bot API, mock OpenAI) with two added `source_modality` assertions. Base: `expected 'image' to be 'text'` on the text-only reply. With the fix: text-only reply `source_modality=text` with the bot's photo still attached (1 `input_image`), reply with a new photo `source_modality=image` (2 `input_image`). I can add those assertions to #192254 once this lands.
- 17 affected suites (channel finalizer, inbound-meta, inbound-context, plugin-sdk channel-inbound, Telegram context/bot, Discord context, Feishu bot, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`): 329 passed, 0 failed.
- `tsgo:all`, oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race and max-lines ratchets pass. Test-lines: `config/test-lines-allocations/source-modality-current-message-192253.txt` allocates the 22 added lines; the ratchet still reports "over by: 10", which the bare base reports too.
- Cost: `context.test.ts` 4.5 s warm (`--maxWorkers=1`), up from 3.4 s, from importing the renderer.

Not covered: a real Telegram account or Discord server, Discord end to end, channels that turn quoted media into the message's own attachment before the finalizer (WhatsApp does this when the reply has no media, so it can still say `image`), and TTS `auto: "inbound"`, which reads the same merged list for audio.

prs.body:
fix(channels): keep quoted-message media from redefining source_modality

Closes #192253

## What Problem This Solves

A text-only Telegram reply to a photo reported `source_modality: "image"` in its per-turn Conversation info: quote media are merged into the turn's media list before the modality fallback derives from it, so the field described the quoted message instead of the current one.

## User Impact

Per-turn metadata that the prompt presents as reliable context now describes the actual message: a text-only reply no longer tells the model it came from an image. Channels that merge quote media without self-quote suppression (Telegram) stop mislabeling every such reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The derivation order made merged quote media win the fallback. This change pins SourceModality from the message's own media before quote media merge — defaulting to "text" for a text-only reply — and factors the media-to-modality mapping into a shared helper used by both the finalize path and the template fallback, so the rule exists in one place.

## Evidence

- Focused runs on latest main content: src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts and src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts, 49/49 passed, including new cases (text-only reply to a photo pins "text"; own media keeps its own modality).
- Red check: reverting only the pin fails exactly the two new pin cases (2 failed | 16 passed); restoring passes.
- Broader suites: src/auto-reply/reply and src/channels/inbound-event green (one pre-existing timing flake reproduced identically on pristine main without this change).

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and module tracing to analyze issue #192253, locate the quote-media merge in src/channels/inbound-event/context.ts and the modality fallback in src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts, and implement the pin with a shared media-to-modality helper. The implementer understands the code: quoted media merge into the same list the fallback derives from, so the pin must happen before the merge. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Inbound context reports `source_modality: "image"` when a user sends a text-only reply to a message containing a photo.

## User Impact

User impact: Text replies to photos now correctly identify their original text modality in runtime message context rather than misrepresenting text input as an image.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `finalizeChannelInboundContext`, when a message contains no attachments of its own (`initialMedia.length === 0`) but has supplemental quote media merged (`media.length > 0`), `SourceModality` is pinned to `"text"`. prs.title: fix(exec): fall back to params session key in approval runtime context
prs.body:
Fixes #151622

## Summary

- Problem: Running shell commands on a paired remote node (`exec host=node`) always failed approval matching with "approval id does not match request". The node's `system.run.prepare` response carries no `sessionKey`, so the approval runtime context resolved `sessionKey: null` while the stored approval binding did carry the session key — every remote-node exec was rejected.
- Solution: `resolveSystemRunApprovalRuntimeContext` in `src/infra/system-run-approval-context.ts` now falls back to `params.sessionKey` when the prepared plan has no `sessionKey` (the same fallback the binding-creation path already used), and normalizes the resolved session key into the forwarded plan so the Gateway context and the plan the node validates agree.
- What changed: `src/infra/system-run-approval-context.ts` (resolver fallback + forwarded-plan normalization), `src/infra/system-run-approval-context.test.ts` (regression coverage asserting both the context and the forwarded plan fields).
- What did NOT change: Approval creation, binding storage, decision handling, and local `host=gateway` execution are untouched. No other components were affected.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Approval-gated remote-node shell execution (`exec host=node`) failed every time with "approval id does not match request" because the prepared node plan has `sessionKey: null` while the stored binding carries the request session key.
- **Real environment tested:** Real OpenClaw dev Gateway (`node scripts/run-node.mjs --dev gateway`, the `pnpm gateway:dev` entry) on `ws://127.0.0.1:19001` with a real paired Linux node (`openclaw node run`, node id `b68bb2e5…5a375a`, approved commands `system.run`/`system.run.prepare`), running this branch at head `f783f696916c0c940356d6a0deb67678b64dbf34`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # terminal 1 (pnpm gateway:dev equivalent): start the dev Gateway
  node scripts/run-node.mjs --dev gateway
  # terminal 2: connect and pair a real local node
  node scripts/run-node.mjs --dev node run --host 127.0.0.1 --port 19001
  # terminal 3: drive the real approval chain through the Gateway client:
  #   node.invoke system.run.prepare  (no sessionKey -> plan.sessionKey=null, the issue condition)
  #   exec.approval.request           (host=node, systemRunPlan without sessionKey, sessionKey on params)
  #   exec.approval.resolve           (allow-once)
  #   node.invoke system.run          (approved replay through the patched sanitizer)
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof-e2e.mts
  # regression test
  npx vitest run src/infra/system-run-approval-context.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  runId=eb037138-5664-4607-a973-0c149bad50e7
  step1 prepare ok, plan.sessionKey=null
  step2 approval requested: {"status":"accepted","id":"eb037138-5664-4607-a973-0c149bad50e7","deliveryRoute":"none","createdAtMs":1789787446457,"expiresAtMs":1789787566457}
  step3 resolved: {"ok":true}
  step4 system.run result:
  {
    "ok": true,
    "nodeId": "b68bb2e585b9c6967e58f9b078470d6ec43e6cb2a885677b16a29bcdcb5a375a",
    "command": "system.run",
    "payload": {
      "exitCode": 0,
      "timedOut": false,
      "success": true,
      "stdout": "e2e-proof-ok",
      "stderr": "",
      "error": null
    }
  }
  ```
  Gateway log for the approved replay: `[ws] ⇄ res ✓ node.invoke 58ms` (no `APPROVAL_REQUEST_MISMATCH` / "approval id does not match request" error).
- **Observed result after fix:** With the prepared plan carrying `sessionKey: null` (the exact issue condition), the Gateway resolved the runtime session key from the request params, matched the stored approval binding, forwarded the plan with the normalized session key, the node validated it, and the command completed on the node with exit code 0 and the expected stdout.
- **What was not tested:** Non-Linux nodes (macOS/iOS/Android) and chat-channel approval delivery were not exercised; the patched resolver runs on the Gateway before forwarding, so the node platform does not change the resolved binding. No other known gaps.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `src/infra/system-run-approval-context.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: `resolveSystemRunApprovalRuntimeContext` falls back to `params.sessionKey` when the plan has no `sessionKey`, and the returned plan is normalized to the same resolved session key so the forwarded plan and runtime context stay consistent. Verified: 10/10 tests pass, including "falls back to params.sessionKey when the plan has no sessionKey".
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The bug was an asymmetric fallback between binding creation and runtime resolution inside this one function; pinning both output fields (context + plan) at the resolver level blocks any regression of the mismatch without touching the broader approval machinery.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: The approval binding-creation path derived the session key as `plan?.sessionKey ?? normalizeNonEmptyString(params.sessionKey)`, but the runtime-resolution path in `resolveSystemRunApprovalRuntimeContext` took `normalizedPlan.sessionKey` directly. Node `system.run.prepare` plans never carry a `sessionKey`, so replay resolution produced `sessionKey: null` and the exact stored-binding comparison failed with "approval id does not match request".
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test covered a plan with a null `sessionKey` against a request that carries one, and the forwarded plan was never normalized to the resolved session key; the new regression test now asserts both the resolved context and the forwarded plan.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): avoid cleanup delays when publishing dependency templates
prs.body:
Related: #191530, #191985

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes dependency-template preparation waiting for Podman's physical cleanup even after the builder and every descendant have stopped writing.

## User Impact

Native Linux Podman builders can publish their finished dependency template promptly while registry housekeeping completes container removal. Publication still fails closed if a captured cgroup remains populated or becomes unreadable. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Podman 5.7.0 `wait` and `inspect` serialize behind conmon cleanup's container lock. Capture the immutable container's engine-recorded systemd cgroup before installation, pin its `cgroup.events` descriptor, then prove extinction after killing that container ID. Recursive `populated 0`, or kernel `ENODEV` from removal of that previously admitted scope, establishes the stopped boundary without acquiring the cleanup lock. Unknown initial captures and process-restart recovery keep the existing engine proof; removal remains housekeeping-owned.

The production increase is 116 lines for the kernel reader and descriptor lifetime. The captured retirement path deletes its inspect/wait/inspect sequence; retaining the fallback is a safety requirement for builders without an exact local capture.

## Evidence

- 17 focused publication/lifecycle tests pass. The new publication regression fails against the original implementation when engine wait is held by cleanup.
- Native crash recovery passes through the actual registry and housekeeping owners: persist a real builder, SIGKILL the process holding its cgroup handle, then use a fresh process to run `runSandboxPrune`; both the registry row and immutable container ID are absent afterward. This proves builder recovery, not a full Gateway restart.
- Codex autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Real rootless Podman 5.7.0 / conmon 2.1.13 / systemd user scopes / cgroup v2 proof uses a synthetic 62,000-file, 1.1 GB btrfs workspace and a three-second poststop hook. Five counterbalanced pairs reduced retirement median/p95 from 3130.8/3132.7 ms to 65.4/67.3 ms; including startup capture, 97.1/102.6 ms. A/A controls were 3136.9 and 3138.2 ms. Every sample had zero surviving writers and stable bytes after proof. Capture + retirement CPU fell from 104.4 to 61.7 ms and sampled V8 allocation from 1,025,944 to 727,424 bytes (separate allocation run). A real populated-cgroup negative rejected at five seconds. An injected sibling writer briefly survived the actual kill; the poll waited until that descendant died before succeeding. The fixture qualifies workspace scale, not a large agent database; this owner never reads the agent database.
- `pnpm check:changed --base HEAD`: formatting, lint, core/test/script typechecks, and all other guards passed except the dead-export scan. The exact main parent independently reproduces four unused exports in `node-plugin-tool-snapshot.ts`, introduced by #191589 (`e0ac3370bbe37d73abc057bc8bd4dd32670c8e97`); that main regression is unrelated to this change.

Source contracts: [Podman inspect locking](https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/v5.7.0/libpod/container_inspect.go#L39-L50), [engine-recorded cgroup](https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/v5.7.0/libpod/container.go#L1130-L1220), [conmon placement](https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/v5.7.0/libpod/oci_conmon_linux.go#L162-L216), [conmon's parent placement handshake](https://github.com/containers/conmon/blob/v2.1.13/src/conmon.c#L64-L79), [recursive kernel population](https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html#un-populated-notification), [kernel removal restrictions](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.12/kernel/cgroup/cgroup.c#L5581-L5686), and [removed descriptor semantics](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.12/fs/kernfs/file.c#L105-L147).

Prior-head CI run [41745061319](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41745061319) completed: 34 jobs passed; only `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and its aggregate gate failed. The test-line ceiling is already 112 lines short on exact CI main parent `aa49c2b7a6a4aa30cda4a7e877ed214061c8f693`: canonical checker exits 1 with 6,446,460 lines / 6,446,348 ceiling. #192013 (`1be3b6d2a1a786a325724faf9126010b7195087f`) introduced 46 unallocated lines; #192014 (`98561a57a6e228465657c155902e24416527cbe8`) added 66. Their prior zero-slack commits pass. This PR adds 82 test lines and 82 allocation, preserving the inherited deficit. Native landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception; CI is not represented as green.

Conflict repair: main #192390 added a writable builder home and a new test import. Integrated main `a29b8d3b84df9bca10c4e09172bad4660b2716f8`, retaining both imports and both fixes. Reviewed head is now `393439d089f2fc8b5d568062829552f7f8ce2322`. Focused tests: 17 passed, one existing opt-in Docker fixture skipped; core typecheck/lint and fresh Codex autoreview passed. Kernel helper/harness are byte-identical to the native proof. Prior-head CI is retained only as historical evidence; final-head results are below.

Final reviewed head `393439d089f2fc8b5d568062829552f7f8ce2322`: [CI41747332822](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41747332822) completed with34 passing jobs and only the inherited test-line ratchet plus aggregate gate failing. Exact CI main parent `bf10667561bfdf36fed14c70a5f8ec97b4a01f09` independently reproduces137 lines of debt: the earlier112 plus17 from #192015 (`eee9925e84f32ab8378ccf64cc86bde13b85c4be`) and8 from #192016 (`847080e81b2cb282165090424cd5a8de5cc45c37`). Each introducer fails the canonical checker against its parent. Exact final main parent fails against prior main `aa49c2b7`, while its zero-growth comparison to `a29b8d3` correctly passes the existing allowance. This PR remains fully allocated (+82/+82). Native pinned-head inherited-failure admission preserves the failed CI result.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI slash-command feedback uses inconsistent terms such as “active run,” title-case headings, and failure messages that lead with a diagnostic instead of a recovery action.

## User Impact

Commands use “reply,” “effort,” sentence-case headings, and actionable failure summaries. Diagnostics remain available in a separate paragraph. Slash tokens, command behavior, permissions, and redaction are unchanged.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Inject a message into the active run | Guide the agent’s current reply |
| Clear chat history | Clear this conversation |
| Available Commands | Available commands |
| Failed to get model info: … | Couldn’t load model details. Try again. + diagnostic paragraph |
| Prompt budget (last run) | Prompt budget (last reply) |
| Session capability is unavailable | Couldn’t access this session. Open another session and try again. |

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies the approved Control UI glossary to the slash-command catalogs and moves the executor’s connection-change text into the English catalog. Updates quoted command feedback in the Chat documentation and all affected assertions. Retains the existing result contract rather than introducing another error-rendering owner.

## Follow-up: effort glossary correction

Vyctor’s copy audit found five error strings still using “thinking level.” All eight strings in that command-result group now use “effort,” including the current value, reset confirmation, and set confirmation. The failure-matrix regression rejects the retired terms, and real-Gateway assertions quote the updated copy. The complete PR copy diff was re-read against the approved glossary; no additional glossary changes were needed. Internal translation keys and slash tokens remain unchanged.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Current thinking level: {level}. | Current effort: {level}. |
| Couldn’t load the thinking level. Try again. | Couldn’t load effort. Try again. |
| Thinking level reset to default. | Effort reset to default. |
| Couldn’t reset the thinking level. Try again. | Couldn’t reset effort. Try again. |
| Couldn’t change the thinking level to “{level}”. Choose {options}. | Couldn’t change effort to “{level}”. Choose {options}. |
| Couldn’t use thinking level “{level}” with this model. Choose {options}. | Couldn’t use effort “{level}” with this model. Choose {options}. |
| Thinking level set to {level}. | Effort set to {level}. |
| Couldn’t change the thinking level. Try again. | Couldn’t change effort. Try again. |

Existing diagnostic placeholders are unchanged. The final follow-up passed `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` with a three-minute timeout and the normal pre-commit hook.

### Follow-up Gaps

Per Vyctor’s revised instructions, no further browser, e2e, screenshot, full-test, or CI runs were started after the correction to the test plan. The final real-Gateway assertion updates were not rerun. An earlier follow-up e2e attempt exposed two stale “Current thinking level” assertions; both are corrected, but this is not a passing final-head e2e claim. Earlier unit and visual results below are historical evidence, not a substitute for landing-time validation. No CI watching or landing was performed.

## Evidence from the earlier PR revision

- 68 unit tests passed across the executor, failure matrix, command metadata, and root-copy loading.
- 5 browser/real-Gateway tests passed across inference setup and thinking metadata.
- Mocked Control UI visual harness: 2 before/after scenarios passed; synthetic data, light theme, same-frame crops. Screenshots below were inspected locally and again from their public attachment URLs.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` completed with no baseline diff; `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed.
- Touched-file oxfmt and oxlint, UI TypeScript check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local chat boot budget vs source base `1248bee4959bf403d1823fc0748d291354cee074`: JS gzip 1,280,959 → 1,280,944 bytes (−15); 20 → 20 requests. CSS gzip 130,910 → 130,910 bytes; 3 → 3 requests.
- Fresh independent review found two stale text assertions; both are fixed. Author simplification pass retained the existing executor/result/redaction owners.

### CI blocker from the earlier PR revision

The PR is **not ready to land**. [Control UI performance failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41679325228/job/126069775916) on the CI merge against base `2cf02a5d104a4dfccd62dc90ebd33e8f417b972c`: chat boot JS gzip 1,280,794 → 1,281,067 bytes (+273). That base already exceeds the cap; the allowed build variance is 64 bytes. The aggregate CI gate therefore fails.

Reproducing locally on that exact newer base also failed (+308 bytes). Shorter menu descriptions did not resolve it (+538 bytes); that experiment and the investigative rebase were reverted, leaving the reviewed source unchanged. No budget, baseline, or permission exception was added. Resolving this merge-base-sensitive boot-size regression remains required.

### Visual proof

| Surface | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Steer menu | ![Before: steer menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b7abab5-eb58-4b56-978a-bbc80d06e6a6) | ![After: steer menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d45add96-9545-4877-a024-48cb7bfe90c1) |

### Gaps and retained behavior

The shared F1 collapsed “Show details” contract is not on this base. Raw `{error}`/`{reason}` diagnostics remain in the existing result content, separated from the summary by a paragraph: compaction failed/skipped; model get/set; effort get/reset/set; verbose get/set; fast get/reset/set; usage; agents; steer and redirect requests. No new error component or competing result contract is added.

Visual failure proof invokes the real executor with a synthetic failing capability and delivers its result through the mocked transcript renderer; it is not a live provider failure. Compatible short labels and slash tokens are unchanged.

Supersedes #192107 (publisher created a new branch)

### Effort fixes in this PR

- Current value, reset confirmation, and set confirmation use “effort.”
- Load, reset, unsupported-value, unsupported-model, and set failures use “effort.”
- Real-Gateway assertions quote “Current effort” and “Couldn’t use effort.”

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191191

## What Problem This Solves

The adaptive CI pilot records native inventory after Vitest loads, but lacks a record of the source, comparison diff and selection inputs available before launch.

## User Impact

Background evidence only. All existing tests and required checks still run; this adds no model calls or test omission.

## Why This Change Was Made

Write a bounded, sanitized launch record before each sampled Vitest child and bind its hash to the native observation snapshot. Upload both through the existing sampled artifact. Record dirty source, unavailable local history and absent prior evidence as explicit fallbacks. Keep the comparison base separate from any future prior-graph base. The optional base does not add a checkout fetch, and historical runner adapters retain their import closure.

prs.title: fix #188935: throw the typed schema-admission error at handle adoption
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When an agent-database open loses the schema-admission race at handle adoption, the site throws an untyped `Error` ("Agent schema admission changed before handle adoption; retry the operation") instead of `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError`, so no retry/replay path classifies it and a completed long turn ends with only "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply" (#188935).
- Solution: Throw the existing typed `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError` at the adoption site (keeping its exact message), so the transcript-commit replay classifier already in the tree treats the race as retryable.
- What changed: `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-schema.ts` (typed throw), `src/state/agent-database-admission-error.ts` (optional custom message, default unchanged), strengthened race assertions in `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: The typed error's identity, default message, and all publication-path behavior; the admission/adoption verdicts themselves; no retry logic was added — the fix only connects the existing throw to the existing classifier.

Fixes #188935

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A session-turn Worker's agent-database open lost the publication race at handle adoption and threw an untyped `Error`, which `isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError` could not classify, so the turn was terminated terminally instead of being retried.
- **Real environment tested:** This branch's worktree on Linux x64, Node v24.20.0, pnpm 12.15.0, driving the real `adoptOpenClawAgentDatabaseSchema` through the repo's concurrent-publication race fixture with a real SQLite agent database and the real replay classifier `isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  pnpm install
  OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts
  ```
  (`OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1` keeps test file logs under the repo on this host; see "What was not tested".)
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  before (production files restored to unmodified main, same assertions):
    × schema: expected Error: Agent schema admission changed bef… to be an instance of SchemaAdmissionChangedError
    (the adoption race surfaced as a bare Error; the replay classifier did not own it)
  after (this patch):
    ✓ same race now throws AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError with the unchanged message
    ✓ isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError(error) === true
    ✓ openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts: 51 passed (51)
  worker transport replay (real session Worker, src/worker/worker.transcript-failure.test.ts):
    ✓ replays transient transcript failures and completes the run without duplicate messages
      — drives an actual AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError through the real worker
      transcript-commit transport: replayed requests equal the original, the run completes,
      and no duplicate messages are persisted (3 passed, exit 0)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The adoption-race failure is now an instance of the typed error the transcript-commit replay path already classifies as retryable, so a raced open can be retried instead of discarding the turn; the same typed error is shown replaying through the real worker transcript transport to a clean completion without duplicate persisted messages (the pre-existing worker replay suite, re-run green on this head).
- **What was not tested:** The original 54-minute Feishu turn was not replayed (the race window requires a live long-running turn plus a concurrent memory-index publication; the repo's race fixture exercises the exact adoption path deterministically). The `core-runtime-infra-state` CI-like shard was attempted but this host's dist-fence guard refuses to run it (it cannot verify separation from managed Gateway artifacts; this is an environment restriction, not a test failure) — the affected validation-cache suite runs green standalone and CI lanes remain the shard guardrail. This host's `/` is world-writable without the sticky bit, so tests resolving the default rolling log path use the repo-supported `OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1` route, which CI does not need. tsgo could not run locally (GLIBC too old for the native binary); CI type lanes remain the guardrail.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: the "schema" race in `distinguishes raced publication from malformed receipts even after revocation` now asserts the adoption failure is an `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError` with the exact message and is classified replayable by the transcript-commit path.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it fails on unpatched main with the precise defect from the issue (bare Error, unclassifiable) and pins both the type contract and the replay classification without touching unrelated races.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the handle-adoption race site threw a bare `Error`, while the sibling publication-race site threw the typed `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError`; the replay classifier keys on the type, so the adoption race fell through every retry path despite its message saying "retry the operation".
- Missing detection / guardrail: the race fixture asserted only the message text, never the error type or its replay classification, so the untyped throw compiled and passed review.

prs.title: improve: render chat composer mentions inline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selecting a person in the chat composer adds a separate “Will notify” strip, while the draft itself still looks like plain text. That repeats recipient information and uses a different treatment from sent-message mentions.

## User Impact

- Selected people appear inline with the shared highlighted pill: a **full-size (1em) avatar**, a 2px gap, and the name.
- The extra notification strip is removed from both Chat and New Session. Notification/submission semantics are unchanged: the raw `@Name` text and mention offsets sent to the Gateway are identical.
- The name remains ordinary editable text; caret, selection, wrapping, clipboard, undo/redo and IME are handled by a real document-aware editor rather than a painted overlay.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requested by Patrick, with Vyctor Brzezowski cc’d. Earlier revisions painted the avatar over a textarea, which could only fit it inside the width of the `@` glyph (first overlapping the name, then shrunk to 0.7em). Patrick asked for a text-sized avatar with proper spacing, which needs real inline layout.

The composer now lazily mounts a shared CodeMirror view (existing dependency) once a person is selected, for both Chat and New Session. Only the raw `@` character is replaced by an avatar widget that reserves 1em + 2px; the whole `@Name` range gets the shared `markdown-person-reference` highlight. The original textarea stays as the hidden raw-value/event port for existing controllers, through an explicit bridge (focus, selection, replacement, caret coordinates); its geometry is never used. Explicit focus requests and boot selection restoration were routed through that bridge after local review. No new dependencies, injected wire-text spaces, or native metric overrides. The command-palette recipient strip is intentionally unchanged.

## Evidence

- Current head: `b2d87aec0f07a05778bdd25b0f8561b38f21d713`. [Matched before/after proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192242#issuecomment-6619285884): real Chromium on the actual Control UI source with a mocked Gateway and synthetic profile/avatar. Chat and New Session both measure **14px text, 14×14px avatar, 2px gap**; the previous head measured a 9.8px avatar.
- In the real app: typing around the mention, undo/redo, long-draft and compact-pane caret visibility, no mobile overflow, no page errors, and Send produced the exact 765-character raw message with mention offsets 26–44.
- **18/18** Chromium editor/caller tests, **37/37** controller tests, **23/23** chat-pane lifecycle tests. Formatting, focused oxlint (0 errors), Control UI controller guard and `pnpm --dir ui build` passed; the editor stays in a lazy chunk.
- Gaps: UI-wide `tsc --noEmit` reports generated DB/type diagnostics outside the changed files (none in changed files); the updated full-app E2E could not run locally because its runner failed to resolve `@openclaw/workboard-contract`. IME coverage is event-level, not an OS IME session; WebKit was not run. Keeping this draft until exact-head CI covers those gates.

prs.title: fix(matrix): expand access groups in DM and room allowlists
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix direct messages, room allowlists, room command authorization, and allowlist-scoped thread/reply context did not expand `accessGroup:<name>` entries, even though `docs/channels/access-groups.md` documents `accessGroup:` as supported anywhere a message channel takes sender allowlists. A person listed only through a group was refused (`dm_policy_not_allowlisted`) while the same entry was accepted on channels wired through the shared ingress helpers.

Six Matrix-side causes:

- `resolveMatrixMonitorLiveUserAllowlist` dropped every entry that was not `*` or a qualified `@user:server` id, so `accessGroup:admins` never reached ingress.
- `filterMatrixAllowlistEntries` dropped the same references during startup preparation, so the startup allowlists and the verification-notice router never saw them.
- `normalizeMatrixAllowList` lower-cased entries, turning `accessGroup:Admins` into `accessgroup:admins`; the shared parser requires the exact `accessGroup:` prefix and a case-sensitive group name.
- Startup and room-user canonicalization deduplicated entries with `normalizeMatrixUserId`, collapsing `accessGroup:Admins` and `accessGroup:admins` into one reference.
- Both `createResolver` calls — message ingress and `resolveMatrixMonitorCommandAccess` — were created without `cfg`, so even a preserved reference had no `accessGroups` to resolve against.
- Allowlist-scoped context visibility still matched room users with the literal Matrix matcher, so a thread root or quoted reply from a group-only member was dropped even though that member's message was admitted.
- Verification notices resolved authorization only before an asynchronous crypto lookup and retry, so a membership revocation or channel reload during that wait could still transmit the notice.
- The live verification authorization reader returned raw allowlist entries instead of the startup-prepared list, so an opted-in display name that startup had already resolved to a Matrix id would be rejected before the shared resolver saw it.

The fix keeps group references symbolic and case-sensitive through startup and live preparation, passes the live config to both resolvers, resolves context senders with the existing public `expandAllowFromWithAccessGroups` owner and the Matrix matcher, and lets the shared ingress perform `message.senders` membership matching. The docs' supported-channel list now includes Matrix.

## Evidence

All evidence comes from the shipped Gateway built at `630c6472514` (`node openclaw.mjs --version` → `2026.10.9 (630c647)`) on Windows 11 / Node 26.12.1 against a local Synapse 1.164.1 homeserver (server name `localhost`) and a local OpenAI-compatible stub model; no real model key is available on this machine, so model output quality is out of scope.

| What | How it is shown |
|---|---|
| Access-group DM/room admission, stranger rejection, removal re-evaluation | ![live allowlist proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191118/proof-191118-live3.png) — five-case table with provider-request counts |
| Helper-level before/after | ![helper proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191048/proof-191048-v5.png) — full production diff reverted, same shipped functions |
| Verification-notice authority re-check when the removal lands after the ingress check | ![in-flight proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191118/proof-191118-inflight.png) — A/B/C table and log excerpt below |

### Verification notice: removal that lands after the ingress authorization

Same DM, same synthetic `m.key.verification.start` from `@alice:localhost`, E2EE enabled (Rust crypto), `dm.allowFrom: ["accessGroup:admins"]` with Alice only authorized through the group:

| Run | Config change | Send-boundary check | Room result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A · control, no change | none | allowed | `m.notice "Matrix verification started with @alice:localhost."` at received+812 ms |
| B · channel reload in flight, membership kept | unrelated `accessGroups.proofreload` key (same reload path) | allowed | notice sent at received+814 ms |
| C · channel reload in flight, Alice removed | `accessGroups.admins.members.matrix = []` | **blocked** at received+773 ms | **0 notices** |

Run C Gateway log (UTC):

```
18:23:59.637  [MatrixClient] Incoming verification event $tXdu... type m.key.verification.start from @alice:localhost
18:23:59.666  config change detected; evaluating reload (accessGroups.admins.members.matrix)
18:23:59.677  restarting matrix channel
18:23:59.678  matrix: stopping client
18:24:00.410  matrix: blocked verification sender @alice:localhost (dmPolicy=allowlist)
18:24:00.439  config hot reload applied (accessGroups.admins.members.matrix)
18:24:00.546  matrix: blocked verification sender @alice:localhost (dmPolicy=allowlist)
```

The ingress authorization runs synchronously on receipt; run A shows it passing and the notice leaving ~812 ms later, after the crypto lookup and the 750 ms retry. In run C the removal is adopted 29 ms after receipt (after that first check) and the only denial is logged 773 ms after receipt at the pre-send re-check, with no notice transmitted; the later replayed event is denied as well. Run B keeps the membership and still sends through the same in-flight reload, so the removal, not the channel restart, is what blocks. The earlier repeat of run C (`18:22:54`) shows the same boundary denial at 778 ms. The mocked-client regression stays as CI coverage for the same window.

## Real behavior proof (shipped Gateway + Matrix homeserver)

![live proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191118/proof-191118-live3.png)

Fresh isolated Gateway on Windows 11 / Node 26.12.1, built from `c46963c686d` (later heads change verification authorization only, not the admission path shown here), against a local Synapse 1.164.1 homeserver (server name `localhost`) with a configured Matrix account. The model is a local OpenAI-compatible stub at `127.0.0.1:18009`; no real model key is available on this machine, so model quality is out of scope — the production Matrix authorization path and the before-provider-I/O boundary are what is exercised.

| Case | Ingress decision | Agent/provider I/O | Bot reply |
|---|---|---|---|
| DM · `allowFrom: ["accessGroup:admins"]` · member `@alice:localhost` | allow | 1 provider request | sent (`23:07:16`) |
| Room · `groupAllowFrom: ["accessGroup:admins"]` · member `@alice:localhost` | allow | 1 provider request | sent (`23:07:25`) |
| DM · same allowlist · stranger `@mallory:localhost` | block — `dm_policy_not_allowlisted` | **0 provider requests** | none |
| Remove Alice from `accessGroups.admins` · DM | block — `dm_policy_not_allowlisted` | **0 provider requests** | none |
| Remove Alice from `accessGroups.admins` · room message | block — `group_policy_not_allowlisted` | **0 provider requests** | none |

The removal cases use a live config edit; the Gateway logged `config hot reload applied (accessGroups.admins.members.matrix)` and the next message was re-evaluated against current membership before admission, so group authority retained by a session is not trusted after removal. Raw decision lines and the provider-request log are in the image; only loopback URLs and local test user ids appear, no keys or non-public endpoints.

Verification notices use the same live account authorization: each check re-reads `core.config.current()`, and the notice loop repeats the check immediately before `sendMessage`. The live list is built by `resolveMatrixMonitorLiveUserAllowlist` with the startup-resolved entries, preserving the opted-in display-name resolution from `93ff72a5` (a name such as `Bob` still resolves through `@bob:example.org`), and access-group references stay symbolic for the shared resolver. Live notice transport is also captured: after an `m.key.verification.start` from the group member, the Gateway sent `m.notice "Matrix verification started with @alice:localhost."` to the DM at `16:08:47`; after the live group removal, the next verification event was rejected at `16:09:29` (`blocked verification sender @alice:localhost`) and no notice followed. Regressions cover the name-resolution case and the narrower in-flight window where the first authorization passes and the second check sees the revoked group, asserting that no notice is sent. The shipped binary now also has the live end-to-end version of that window (see Evidence above). A full SAS emoji/device pairing is still not possible on this local account, so the transfer phase after the notice is not exercised.

No stored data model changes: the PR only affects authorization lists read from configuration. The existing-state check also ran: a stable npm `openclaw@2026.10.9` install (state schema 20 / agent 25) started on an isolated state directory and accepted this config, then the branch build started on the same directory, passed `state.schema-preflight`, connected the existing Matrix account, rejoined the proof rooms, and delivered a post-upgrade DM with a provider request and bot reply. No new account, room, or config was created for the upgrade step.

## Helper-level before / after

The production-diff reverse comparison is still useful for the individual helper decisions:

![before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191048/proof-191048-v5.png)

| Case (shipped functions) | Before: full production patch reverted | After: this branch |
|---|---|---|
| DM · `allowFrom: ["accessGroup:admins"]` · group member `@alice:example.org` | `block` | `allow` |
| DM · same allowlist · stranger `@mallory:example.org` | `block` | `block` |
| DM · `accessGroup:missing` · member sender | `block` | `block` |
| Room · `groupAllowFrom: ["accessGroup:admins"]` · member sender | `block` | `allow` |
| Room command `/status` · admitted member | `unauthorized` | `authorized` |
| Room thread root / quoted reply · group member sender | dropped | kept |
| Live allowlist keeps `accessGroup:Admins` + `accessGroup:admins` | only `@alice` kept | both kept |
| Startup DM/group allowlist + room users keep both refs | dropped (`[]`) | both kept |
| `normalizeMatrixAllowList` keeps reference case | `accessgroup:admins` | `accessGroup:Admins` |

Local run on Windows 11 / Node 26.12.1 through the extension test router: the monitor suites pass on this branch, and a reverse-diff run with the production changes removed failed the group decisions shown above (`git diff <base> -- '*.ts' ':(exclude)*.test.ts'`). `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` is clean on the changed files; `pnpm lint:docs` is 0 issues; the assertion-safety ratchet passes and no laundered casts were added. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` reports only the two pre-existing failures on this checkout (`extensions/muse/harness.ts` and `src/infra/secret-file.ts` from the installed `@openclaw/fs-safe` version); neither file is touched here.

## What was not tested

- End-to-end encryption: the local proof rooms were unencrypted; E2EE key/device paths are unchanged by this PR.
- A public or federated Matrix homeserver. The local Synapse was a fresh install with a fresh account. E2EE was not enabled, so a full pending SAS/device verification flow (emoji pairing) was not available; the crypto-pending revocation window is covered by the regression test.
- Real model output: the proof uses a local OpenAI-compatible stub, as no real model credentials are available on this machine.
- Full SAS/device verification: notice transport is live-proven for stage notices, and the pre-send decision is live-proven for a removal that lands during the crypto wait; the SAS emoji/decimal transfer itself is not exercised.

## Tests added

- DM decisions for an access-group member, a stranger, and a missing group.
- Room allowlist decision and room command authorization for an access-group member.
- `normalizeMatrixAllowList` keeps `accessGroup:` symbolic and case-sensitive and never matches it as a user.
- Live and startup DM/group allowlists and room users keep distinct group references instead of dropping or collapsing them.
- Handler regression: a thread root from a group-only member is kept under `contextVisibility: "allowlist"`.
- Verification regression: a revoked group between the first authorization and the send boundary drops the notice; an opted-in name entry keeps its startup-resolved id; access-group references stay symbolic.
- Context-sender helper: group member admitted, stranger/missing group rejected, literal allowlists and empty filters unchanged.

## Scope

This is the Matrix half of #191048. Slack's DM gate is untouched: it lower-cases the allowlist before matching, so `accessGroup:` entries still read as literals there. The issue offers documenting that limitation as the alternative; I left it out to keep this change a Matrix fix, and can take the Slack half separately.

prs.title: fix(telegram): inbound webhook updates dropped when webhook URL has a query string or trailing slash
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: all Telegram inbound updates are dropped (persistent 404, zero logs) when the webhook URL carries a query string or trailing slash, which reverse proxies commonly append.

## User Impact

User impact: Telegram bots hosted behind ngrok/Cloudflare-style proxies (which append `?token=...` to the webhook URL) or proxies that normalize URLs with a trailing slash now receive updates instead of silently losing every message after Telegram gives up retrying.

Behavior note: query-free configured routes now accept incoming variants (appended query parameters, trailing slashes), while configured `webhookPath` values that carry query text (e.g. `/healthz?token=known`) keep their exact raw-URL identity. Two accounts on `/hook?tenant=a` and `/hook?tenant=b` stay distinct buckets, and a proxy-appended variant can never merge them.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handleTelegramWebhook` mixed the raw `req.url` with normalized route keys: `normalizeWebhookPath` never strips the query, and `target.requestPath === req.url` compared raw bytes, so `POST /telegram-webhook?token=xyz` never matched the registered `/telegram-webhook` target and fell to a bare 404.

The handler now resolves targets in two steps: exact configured identity first (raw `requestPath === req.url`, preserving the raw callback-path contract from the Gateway-route refactor and legacy-callback preservation work), then — only for query-free configured routes — the normalized request pathname, so proxy-appended query strings and trailing slashes still reach the target. Failed-secret throttling keys on the resolved route identity in both the Gateway limiter and `createTelegramLegacyWebhookAuthLimiter`, so query variants of one route share the existing 120-attempt-per-minute budget instead of minting a fresh budget per raw URL.

## Evidence

### Shipped-Gateway real behavior (this branch, `qaRuntime` build)

Ran the real Gateway (`node openclaw.mjs gateway run`) on loopback with a stub Telegram Bot API (getMe/setWebhook only) and two configured accounts: query-free `/hook` and query-bearing `/hook2?tenant=a`. Redacted terminal output:

```
[telegram] webhook Gateway route /hook2?tenant=a (port 18765)
[telegram] webhook Gateway route /hook (port 18765)
[telegram] webhook advertised to telegram on http://127.0.0.1:18765/hook2?tenant=a
[telegram] webhook advertised to telegram on http://127.0.0.1:18765/hook

POST /hook?token=known        -> status=200 accepted=durable
POST /hook/ (trailing slash)  -> status=200 accepted=durable
POST /hook (exact)            -> status=200 accepted=durable
POST /hook?token=known (wrong secret) -> status=401 body=unauthorized
wrong-secret guesses via /hook?attempt=N: attempt 1 -> 401 ... attempt 120 -> 429
POST /hook (no query, wrong secret, same client) -> 429 (same budget)
POST /hook2?tenant=a (exact configured) -> status=200 accepted=durable
POST /hook2?tenant=b (other tenant)     -> status=404
POST /hook2 (bare pathname)             -> status=404
POST /hook correct secret (after throttling) -> status=200 accepted=durable
```

### Regression tests (red on the previous revision, green here)

- `webhook-route-identity.test.ts`: query-bearing configured identities per account — exact deliveries to `/hook?tenant=a` and `/hook?tenant=b` both 200 even with a shared secret (no merged bucket, no ambiguous 401); `/hook?tenant=c`, bare `/hook`, and `/hook/?tenant=a` 404. On the previous revision the identities merged into one pathname bucket.
- `webhook-route-identity.test.ts`: failed-auth budget sharing — 120 wrong-secret guesses across `/hook?attempt=N` variants return 401 and the next request returns 429, on both the Gateway limiter and the legacy-listener limiter; authenticated delivery still returns 200 durable afterwards.
- `webhook.test.ts` "preserves exact webhook target": restored `/healthz?token=known` + legacy listener (starts, exact delivery 200, appended query 404 — the previous revision threw at startup); per-case `extra` expectation documents that appended queries are rejected only for query-bearing configured identities.
- `webhook-routing.test.ts`: reserved-path assertions restored to main behavior (`/healthz?token=known` is a probe conflict without legacy, not a health conflict).

### Commands and results

- `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts`: 82 passed.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/webhook-route-identity.test.ts`: 4 passed.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/webhook-routing.test.ts`: 9 passed.
- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base origin/main`: OK (6474 grandfathered factories; new mocks carry `mock-isolation` annotations).
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`: OK.
- `oxlint` on all changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

### What was not tested

- Native `tsgo` typecheck could not run on this host (glibc 2.28 < 2.32 required by the tsgo binary); a full-program `tsc --noEmit` fallback is not viable on this monorepo size. Type gating relies on CI.
- The proof stubbed the Telegram Bot API (getMe/setWebhook contract) with fake tokens on loopback; no live Telegram-server e2e. Webhook ingress, spool admission, throttling, and route identity all ran through the shipped Gateway runtime.

prs.title: improve: hand off portal previews in private chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents without a Control UI side panel are directed to the Portals page even when the user explicitly requests a private app-preview link in chat.

Requested by @vincentkoc in the [original discussion](https://x.com/vincent_koc/status/2115408545948852444).

## User Impact

Agents are explicitly guided to return the existing portal's authenticated launch URL for a requested private handoff to the authorized recipient, while retaining the Control UI panel path for in-UI previews. They must not automatically post bearer links to group/public chats or present loopback-only routes as phone-accessible links.

This is an agent-guidance change, not a new transport, automatic message sender, permission grant, or network setup. The agent still needs existing portal tool access and the deployment still needs reachable private ingress. No authentication, tool policy, Gateway configuration, or tunnel behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

One small, static guidance source now supplies the system-prompt presentation advice, both portal tool descriptions, and open/list results. It distinguishes authenticated url from token-free publicUrl and keeps private sharing, link withdrawal, and reachability limitations consistent. Existing portal URL generation and proxying remain the single networking owner.

The focused regression extends existing prompt and portal-tool tests; no additional Gateway boot or test harness is introduced. The separate 13-line test allocation covers the exact net regression growth without changing the shared baseline.

## Evidence

- The new generated-prompt contract failed both screen/no-screen cases before the production change and passes afterward.
- Focused tests: **89 passed** across UI presentation, portal tool routing/results, full system-prompt assembly, and tool-prefix stability. The selected wrapper completed in 835.39 seconds including cold worker preparation. Modified-file timings: UI presentation 2.40 seconds; portal tool 33.98 seconds, dominated by transform/import work (test execution 28 milliseconds). CI seconds are not available yet.
- Targeted agents-tools and agents-root TypeScript projects passed; type-aware lint passed for all six changed TypeScript files; formatting and git diff checks passed.
- Documentation link audit: 16,232 internal links checked, zero broken.
- The repository-wide staged test-line ratchet did not complete within a 300-second execution budget. The staged diff has 13 net new test lines and its separate allocation is exactly 13; the CI ratchet remains pending.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) found no actionable findings in the complete candidate against base 63c25f72daff6906c011027195a3187c8d8b7f06. The only later adjustment reduced the test allocation from 14 to the measured 13 lines; reviewed guidance and code stayed unchanged.

An initial 300-second execution deadline interrupted cold worker/boundary preparation before the larger test and lint checks completed. After reconciling the stopped processes, the same scoped checks completed with sufficient build time; no test assertion was weakened.

**Remaining proof gap:** no live model-driven Telegram handoff or physical-phone/Safari run is claimed. Earlier local PoC checks exercised actual portal authentication, app assets/navigation/downloads/streaming, and link withdrawal, but the available deployment returned loopback-only exposure. These tests protect the model-facing guidance and existing tool contracts; they do not prove model compliance or remote phone reachability.

prs.title: fix(workboard): settle cards after delayed agent end
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Workboard cards remaining running when the worker session becomes inactive shortly after its `agent_end` hook.

## User Impact

Linked cards now reflect the completed attempt without waiting for stale-session recovery in this delayed-settlement case. Active runs remain running; failed or aborted attempts remain blocked. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adapt the Workboard portions of the 2026.10.10 release repairs to main: the active lifecycle service owns a bounded sequence of session re-reads (100ms through 1.6s delays, about 3.1s total). Prepared plugin hooks route to that shared service, and retirement cancels retries and discards in-flight reads. Later fallback attempts replace earlier pending outcomes only for the same session and effective run identity; delayed hooks from another run cannot cancel current work. Unrelated prepared-launch recovery changes are excluded.

Simplification removes the superseded reader-only service adapter and reader bookkeeping, and moves hook handling out of the registration generation. Net production growth is 104 lines for service routing, retry lifecycle, and retirement checks. Net regression growth is 82 lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/workboard-deferred-agent-end.txt` for registered-plugin success/failure, overlapping fallback outcomes, cross-run isolation, and stale-owner proof.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on base `34007820fa2c`: registered-plugin `agent_end` regression failed with `running` instead of `review`; seven existing tests passed. Cold run: 118.27s total; failing regression: 276ms.
- Local review identified overlapping fallback attempts retaining stale failure outcomes, then stale cross-run hooks cancelling current retries. Both findings were reproduced red through the registered plugin and repaired, including event-run precedence and context-run fallback cases.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/index.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/workboard/src/lifecycle-sync.test.ts test/plugins/workboard-automation-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 54 passed before integrating main; all 54 also passed after integration in 78.00s total.
- Targeted TypeScript and test-line allocation ratchet pass after integrating main `d27139b2b220` to resolve observed inherited MCP metadata and 47-line ceiling failures. No unrelated ceiling raise is included in this PR.
- Focused formatting and `git diff --check`: pass. Targeted lint: passed.
- Fresh independent source reviews found no remaining actionable findings. Final local ClawSweeper review of `d27139b2b220..2b249b1713b1`: complete, no findings. Subsequent fixture-only cleanup uses Vitest’s test-completion hook to restore timers; production code is unchanged. After that cleanup, the registered-plugin suite passed all 12 tests in 29.21s including worker preparation, and targeted lint passed.

The registered-plugin proof uses the real plugin/store and a Gateway metadata I/O fixture. The authority consumer tests exercise real plugin services, Gateway dispatch and Cron after caller closure. No live-model Gateway or browser proof was performed. CI duration is not yet available.

## CI follow-up

CI exposed a fixture-only callback type error: `onTestFinished` requires `void`, but the callback returned Vitest’s helper object. The exact extension-test typecheck reproduced TS2322 locally. Explicitly discarding that return value fixes it; the same extension-test typecheck, targeted lint, format, and registered-plugin suite (12 passed, 30.10s including preparation) all pass. No product code or test-line allocation changed. Earlier CI also reports the separately tracked inherited main test-budget debt; this is not a green-CI claim.
