prs.title: fix(ios): wrap chat markdown tables instead of clipping the last column
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #191076

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where iPhone users reading a markdown table in the native chat saw the last column cut off mid-word ("Sautéing, roasting, driz"), with no cue that the table could be scrolled and with table text visibly smaller than the paragraphs and bullet list in the same reply.
- The same shared renderer draws tables in the macOS chat, where columns likewise never wrapped and cells stayed at footnote size.
- **Related:** #191077 (companion report about card/block padding on small iPhones) is a separate, broader layout question and is intentionally not touched here; the ClawSweeper review on #191076 asks for "a focused repair in the existing shared table view … without a Markdown parser rewrite or the broader card-layout redesign".

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** table cells wrap to the width the reply actually has, table text renders at the reply's body size, and horizontal scrolling remains available — with a visible indicator — only for tables whose minimum column widths genuinely exceed that width.
- The horizontal `ScrollView` proposed an unbounded width to the `Grid`, so every column took its longest cell's ideal width and the viewport clipped the result; `showsIndicators: false` removed the only cue; cells were pinned to `OpenClawChatTypography.footnote` while surrounding prose uses `ChatMarkdownRenderer.Typography.proseFont` (`OpenClawChatTypography.body`), a fixed ratio that Dynamic Type cannot close.
- The table now measures the width its reply actually gives it (`onGeometryChange` on the card) and bounds every cell to a column width derived from that measurement: `sharedColumnWidth(cardWidth:columns:)` splits the card's content width (card width minus 2 × 10 pt padding minus 14 pt per inter-column gap) equally between the columns, and each cell is laid out at that width with `.frame(width:alignment:)` on top of the existing `.fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)`, so the text wraps and wrapped rows keep their height. GFM per-column alignment now rides on the cell frame's `Alignment` (`cellAlignment(_:)`) as well as the header's `gridColumnAlignment`, because every cell fills its column instead of reporting its own ideal width. Typography is passed down from the renderer exactly like `listView(_:)` already does, so thinking blocks keep their own profile.
- Scrolling is a decision taken **after** the columns are bounded, not a fit test on an unconstrained grid: `overflowsReplyWidth(cardWidth:columns:)` is true only when the equal share drops below `minimumColumnWidth` (120 pt), i.e. when the table cannot keep its columns readable at the reply's width. Then the grid keeps 120 pt columns, ends up wider than the card, and is hosted in a `ScrollView(.horizontal)` carrying `.scrollIndicators(.visible)`; otherwise there is no scroller at all and the grid simply wraps. Before the first measurement (`cardWidth == 0`) the cell width is `nil` and no overflow is reported, so the initial layout pass is exactly the unbounded layout the view had before. An earlier revision of this PR made that choice with `ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal)`; the review pointed out that a fit test compares ideal widths, and an unconstrained grid always reports its unwrapped width, so the measured decision replaced it.
- **Out of scope:** no parser changes, no stacked/card redesign, no new settings, and no change to code or math blocks (they keep their indicator-free scrollers).
- **Highest-risk area:** the table view is shared with macOS, where wide tables must stay fully reachable and column alignment must survive; the card width now also arrives from a layout-pass callback, so the view renders once before the measurement lands.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The scroll branch reuses the same grid and only adds the indicator, per-column GFM alignment is applied to every cell (not just the header), the pre-measurement pass keeps `columnWidth == nil` so nothing collapses to zero width, and two new suites cover the change: `ChatMarkdownTableColumnWidthTests` pins the decision arithmetic (the reported two-column table at a 366 pt card, a six-column table that must scroll, a 1200 pt reply, and the unmeasured case), while `ChatMarkdownTableCompactWidthTests` renders the reported table through `ChatMarkdownRenderer` into an `NSHostingView` bitmap at 390 pt and 1200 pt and compares the rendered cell line pitch against probes built from the prose and footnote fonts.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** a two-column reply table on an iPhone shows both columns in full — cells wrap instead of running off the screen — table text is the same size as the reply's body text, and a table too wide to fit still scrolls with a visible indicator.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatMarkdownBlockViews.swift` — `ChatMarkdownTableView`'s measured `cardWidth`, `sharedColumnWidth(cardWidth:columns:)` / `overflowsReplyWidth(cardWidth:columns:)`, `tableLayout`'s scroll decision, and `cell(_:isHeader:column:)`'s bounded frame; the one-line renderer wiring in `ChatMarkdownRenderer.swift`; and the two suites `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatMarkdownTableColumnWidthTests.swift` and `ChatMarkdownTableCompactWidthTests.swift` (fixture: the oil/uses table reported in #191076).

## Evidence
- **Real environment tested:** worktree `aispace/worktrees/issue-191076`, branch `feat/issue-191076-ios-table-readability`, base `origin/main` `f2884869274`, head `64ae46ce12b`. No Apple toolchain exists on this Linux host (`which swift swiftc xcodebuild` → all absent), so no Swift compilation, `swift test`, simulator run or device screenshot was performed by me. I did try to stop guessing at the pinned formatter: `scripts/install-swift-tools.sh` installs macOS-only release binaries, and building SwiftFormat 0.63.1 from source inside a `swift:6.2` Linux container hangs in the Swift driver (0 % CPU, `hrtimer_nanosleep`, no output after 20 minutes). The formatting fixes below were derived from the pinned rules' published behaviour plus the shapes this repository's already-linted sources use, and were then confirmed by CI.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # 1. repository pre-commit freshness gate (protocol models + native i18n inventory) — passed on every commit
  git commit --amend --no-edit

  # 2. arithmetic cross-check of the fit decision, re-derived from the Swift source because no Swift
  #    toolchain exists here; mirrors Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatMarkdownTableColumnWidthTests.swift
  node column-width-crosscheck.mjs        # exit 0

  # 3. the Swift suites that would execute this code — not runnable here, and not runnable in fork-PR CI
  swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatMarkdownTable
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  # node column-width-crosscheck.mjs — the four cases ChatMarkdownTableColumnWidthTests asserts,
  # recomputed from sharedColumnWidth / overflowsReplyWidth exactly as written in the patch
  PASS  reported table does not scroll                   [overflows=false]
  PASS  two bounded columns + gap == card content width   [width=166 content=332]
  PASS  column stays readable                            [width=166 >= 120]
  PASS  6 columns at phone width scroll                  [shared=46.00 < 120]
  PASS  equal share below readable minimum               [shared=46.00]
  PASS  scrolled content wider than the card             [790 > 366]
  PASS  6 columns at 1200 pt do not scroll               [width=185.00]
  PASS  wide columns above readable minimum              [width=185.00]
  PASS  unmeasured width never scrolls                   [cardWidth=0]
  {"checks":9,"failed":0}                                  exit 0
  ```
  That is a consistency check between the implementation's arithmetic and the expectations its unit test asserts. It is not Swift execution and it renders nothing.
- **CI on head `64ae46ce12b`:** the `CI` workflow is green — all of its checks pass, including `ios-screenshots` (builds the app and runs it in the simulator) and both `openclaw/ci-gate` checks. `Build iOS Periphery reports` / `Build macOS Periphery reports` compile `OpenClawChatUI` for both platforms and run the pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 + SwiftLint phases clean, and `Scan shared kit from iOS` / `Scan shared kit from macOS` — the dead-code scans that cover the changed file — pass. The only red check on the PR is `Scan iOS dead code` in the separate report workflow, detailed below.
  The single red check is `Scan iOS dead code` in the separate `macOS Periphery Dead Code [report]` workflow, whose only finding is
  ```text
  {"hints":["unused"],"name":"scan()","location":"Sources/Settings/ESPSetupSession.swift:76:10","modules":["OpenClaw"]}
  ```
  `apps/ios/Sources/Settings/ESPSetupSession.swift` exists in neither this head nor current `origin/main` (`git cat-file -e origin/main:apps/ios/Sources/Settings/ESPSetupSession.swift` → absent; `git grep ESPSetupSession origin/main` → no match), so that finding comes from the scan's restored index store, not from this diff — which touches three files under `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` and no iOS app-target code. `openclaw/ci-gate` is green, so this report workflow does not gate the PR; I am not chasing it here.
- **Why the fit decision went through three shapes (CI history):**
  1. head `d63058aac10` — `SwiftFormat (lint)` `indent` errors at `ChatMarkdownBlockViews.swift:198-202`: with `--xcodeindentation enabled` a comment between a chain head and its first modifier indents the rest of that chain one extra level (accepted in-repo shapes: `ChatMessageViews.swift:1031-1035`, `ControlUIHubScreen.swift:97-99`). Fixed by moving the comment above the statement (`8f39257913e`).
  2. heads `7e7a2063dbb` / `ece3d361f2a` — the review's P2 on the fitted `ViewThatFits` candidate: `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` reports the proposed width whatever the grid does, so the scroller was unreachable. That clamp was dropped.
  3. head `5f7dfdeb91c` — `ViewThatFits` replaced outright by the measured-width layout above, which is what the review asked for ("allocate constrained widths in the existing table layout before using scrolling as the overflow fallback"). CI then reported **both** `ChatMarkdownBlockViews.swift:194:1: error: (redundantStaticSelf)` and `(redundantSelf)` on that one line: with `--self insert` and `redundantStaticSelf` both enabled, a statement-initial `return Self.member …` inside a `static func` is claimed by the two rules at once — removing `Self.` makes the insert rule ask for `self.`, which cannot compile in a static context. Fixed in `64ae46ce12b` by binding the values first and returning an expression over locals, the shape this repository's linted sources already use (`apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/GatewayEndpointID.swift:18-23`; 78 further `let x = Self.staticMember` occurrences inside static funcs across `apps/ios/Sources`, `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources` and `apps/macos/Sources`):
  ```diff
       static func overflowsReplyWidth(cardWidth: CGFloat, columns: Int) -> Bool {
           guard cardWidth > 0 else { return false }
  -        return Self.sharedColumnWidth(cardWidth: cardWidth, columns: columns) < Self.minimumColumnWidth
  +        let width = Self.sharedColumnWidth(cardWidth: cardWidth, columns: columns)
  +        let readableMinimum = Self.minimumColumnWidth
  +        return width < readableMinimum
       }
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** no rendering was observed by me — see the tier below. What is observable in this environment: `OpenClawChatUI` compiles for iOS and macOS and passes the pinned SwiftFormat/SwiftLint phases, the iOS app builds and runs in the simulator, and the shared-kit dead-code scans are clean for the changed file. In the code, `ChatMarkdownTableView` measures its card width, bounds every cell to an equal share of that width, renders cells at the reply's prose font, keeps GFM alignment per cell, and only reaches for a `ScrollView(.horizontal)` with a visible indicator when the share would fall below the 120 pt readable minimum.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** the reporter's screenshots in #191076 show the clipped second column and the smaller table text. On `origin/main` the table grid only ever lives inside `ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false)`, so no cell is ever proposed a bounded width, nothing can wrap, and the hidden columns have no cue.
- **What was not tested:** no Swift compilation, `swift test`, simulator run or device screenshot was performed by me, and neither new suite has been executed anywhere — `scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs` gates both Apple test lanes on `!ordinaryPullRequest` (`runMacos` :365-371 → `runMacosSwift` :385-388, and `runIosBuild` :399), so on any `pull_request` event `macos-swift (tests|packages)` and `ios-build` report `skipping`, which is what this PR's check list shows; the `OpenClawKit tests` step (`swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:5347-5361`) only runs on a maintainer `workflow_dispatch`/`schedule` run or after merge. Real iPhone/iPad rendering, Dynamic Type sizes, and wide-table behaviour in the macOS chat are therefore unverified by me. One earlier `ios-screenshots` attempt (head `7e7a2063dbb`) failed in `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.testReleaseChatScreenshot` at `:145` on `iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)` only: that test drives the release chat fixture in `apps/ios/Sources/Chat/AppleReviewDemoChatTransport.swift`, which seeds one sentence plus a fenced mermaid block and no markdown table, so the table view is never instantiated on that path; the same job passed on `iPhone 18 Pro Max` in the same run and on every later head.
- **Proof tier:** L1

The deterministic local evidence is the arithmetic cross-check above plus the CI compile/lint/dead-code results on this head; the rendered-behaviour evidence (wrapping at 390 pt, cell line pitch matching the prose font, scrolling with a visible indicator only below the readable minimum) exists as executable tests but has not been executed by me.

prs.title: feat(cron): configurable default delivery and failure destinations
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Today every automation either names its own chat route or follows the conversation that created it. An operator who wants all results in one place (for example topic 1 of a Telegram forum) has to pin `channel`/`to`/`threadId` on every job, and agent-created jobs pin whatever chat they were made in. Failure alerts have a Gateway-wide route but no per-agent or per-person one.

This adds configurable default destinations at three layers, for both primary results and failure alerts:

- `cron.delivery` (and the existing `cron.failureAlert`): Gateway-wide defaults.
- `cron.agents.<agentId>.delivery` and `.failureAlert`: defaults for the agent that owns the job.
- `cron.creators.<profileId>.delivery` and `.failureAlert`: defaults for the human who created the job, keyed by Gateway profile id.

Defaults resolve at run time. Stored jobs are never rewritten, and a job that names its own route keeps it.

```json5
{
  cron: {
    delivery: { channel: "telegram", to: "-100123456789", threadId: 1 },
    failureAlert: { channel: "telegram", to: "-100123456789:topic:1" },
    agents: {
      ops: { delivery: { channel: "slack", to: "channel:C123" } },
    },
    creators: {
      "profile-id": {
        delivery: { channel: "telegram", to: "-100123456789", threadId: 2 },
        failureAlert: { channel: "telegram", to: "-100123456789:topic:2" },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

### Contract

- **Owner.** The job's `agentId`, else the agent in its session key, else the default agent.
- **Creator.** The trusted creation seam already stamps `createdActor` on every job it stores (`cron-creator-session.ts`, `cron-input-validation.ts`), and run-time execution context already reads its profile id. The creator layer reads the same stamp through the canonical `sessionCreatorProfileId` helper. It applies when the creator is a human with a Gateway profile, or a human profile that delegated creation to an agent (`delegatedBy`). Legacy jobs with no `createdActor`, and channel-only, unknown, agent-without-a-human, and system creators have no creator default. Profile keys match exactly; they are opaque ids, so they are not case-folded like agent ids.
- **One shared helper.** `resolveCronDeliveryDefaultsScope` derives both the owner and the creator for every path: preview, isolated run delivery, command/script completion, run-queue check, failure alerts, and create/update validation. `cron.add` passes the stamped creator into its validation and preview so the add result already shows the creator default.
- **Precedence.** The job's own route, then the creator-profile default, then the owner-agent default, then the Gateway-wide default, then today's behavior. "Own route" means a `channel` other than `last`, `to`, `threadId`, `accountId`, or `target: "owner"`.
- **Why this order.**
  - The job's own route is explicit intent for that one job, so nothing overrides it.
  - The creator is the person who set the job up, the most specific "who". Their chosen inbox should follow them across whichever agent they used.
  - An agent is a shared runtime that can serve several people, so its default is broader than one person's.
  - The Gateway default is the catch-all, and with nothing configured behavior is unchanged. "Routing fields" means a `channel` other than `last`, `to`, `threadId`, `accountId`, or `target: "owner"`.
- **Most specific default wins whole.** No field merging, because recipient, thread, and account belong to the channel that supplied them.
- **Eligibility.** Only a resolved `announce` mode with no routing field gets a default. This holds for every session target, including `current` and `main`, where the default replaces the creating-conversation route.
- **`mode: "none"` and `"webhook"` never gain a chat destination.** That includes `message`-tool context. Failure alerts for `none` jobs still use configured failure routes, as today.
- **Failure route.** `cron.creators.<profileId>.failureAlert` and `cron.agents.<id>.failureAlert` set `mode`, `channel`, `to`, and `accountId`, in the same creator-then-agent order, replacing the global route fields whole. `enabled`, `after`, `cooldownMs`, and `includeSkipped` stay Gateway-wide, so `cron.failureAlert.enabled: false` still disables inherited alerts. Like a `cron.failureAlert` object, a scoped route activates the alert policy. Precedence: per-job `failureAlert` route, then `delivery.failureDestination` layered over the creator route, else the agent route, else the global route, then the primary announce route. That last step now includes a primary default, and its `threadId` is kept.
- **Agent-created jobs.** When the cron tool creates a route-less job and a default applies to the job's agent or to the requesting human profile, it no longer pins the creating chat route. Otherwise the inferred route would become an explicit per-job route and hide the default. The tool reads the requester profile from the authenticated requester origin, the same source the Gateway uses to stamp `delegatedBy`.
- **Validation.** Config load rejects a default whose `channel` names no installed channel plugin (`cron.delivery` and the `cron.agents`/`cron.creators` `delivery` and `failureAlert` routes; built-in aliases such as `gchat` pass). An unknown `cron.failureAlert.channel` only warns, so existing configs keep loading. `cron.agents` keys that resolve to the same agent id (`ops` and `OPS`) are rejected with the same check `agents.entries` uses. `openclaw doctor`'s delivery-target advisory also lists defaults whose channel plugin is not active.
- **Compatibility.**
  - With no defaults configured, nothing changes.
  - Existing jobs that already store a route, including routes pinned at creation by earlier releases, keep it.
  - The new keys are optional and the `cron` block stays strict.

### Behavior matrix (tested)

| Config | Job delivery | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| global only | announce, no route | global default |
| agent only (owner matches) | announce, no route | agent default |
| global + agent | announce, no route, owner has entry | agent default, whole (no global field merge) |
| global + agent | announce, no route, other owner | global default |
| any | names channel / to / threadId / accountId / owner target | job's own route |
| any | `none` / `webhook` | unchanged |
| none configured, or only another agent's entry | announce, no route | unchanged (creating chat / remembered route) |
| creator + agent + global | announce, no route, human profile creator | creator default, whole |
| creator only | announce, no route, human profile creator | creator default |
| creator + agent + global | announce, no route, agent creator with delegating human profile | creator default |
| creator + agent + global | announce, no route; creator legacy (no `createdActor`), channel-only, unknown, agent, system, other profile, or case-different id | agent default (no creator default) |
| creator + agent + global | names a route, owner target, `none`, `webhook` | unchanged by the creator default |
| global failureAlert + agent failureAlert | any | agent route fields, global tuning |
| global + agent + creator failureAlert | human profile creator | creator route fields, global tuning |
| creator with only `delivery` | failure alert | agent failure route |
| global `enabled: false` + agent failureAlert | no job failureAlert | no alert |
| per-job failureAlert | any | per-job route |
| primary default, no failure route | announce | alert to primary default (thread kept) |
| primary default and agent failure route | announce | primary to default, failures to agent route, independently |
| owner only in session key | route-less | session-key agent's defaults in preview, completion, and alerts |

### Docs

- `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`: new "Default destinations" section with the precedence table, the `none` decision, the session-route decision, and failure-route layering.
- `docs/gateway/config-automation.md`: `cron.delivery`, `cron.agents`, and `cron.creators` reference, plus the updated failure precedence.
- Configuration reference index, schema help and labels, and the generated config baseline.

## Verification

- Typecheck:
  - `pnpm tsgo:core`: pass.
  - `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: all shards pass.
  - `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: pass.
- Lint and format: `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on touched files are clean.
- Schema and docs generation:
  - `pnpm check:base-config-schema`: ok.
  - `pnpm config:docs:check`: ok, after `config:docs:gen`.
  - `pnpm format:docs:check`: clean.
  - `pnpm docs:check-links`: 0 broken.
  - `docs:check-links:anchors`: 6 misses, all in pre-existing release notes and none in touched pages.
  - `git diff --check`: clean.
- Focused tests (`pnpm test <files>`), all passing. New tests:
  - `src/cron/delivery-defaults.test.ts`: the matrix above, including every non-creator actor shape, legacy jobs with no `createdActor`, the `none`/`webhook` interaction, and failure vs primary resolved independently.
  - `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`: no route pinning when a Gateway, agent, or creator default applies (requesting or delegating profile); still pins for another agent's default, another profile's default, or a requester without a profile.
  - `src/cron/delivery-preview.test.ts`: real `resolveDeliveryTarget`. A route-less `current` job previews to the default; an explicit `to` still wins; another agent's default is ignored; a human-profile creator's default beats the agent default.
  - `src/gateway/server-cron-completion.test.ts`: completion uses the session-key owner's default rather than the resolver fallback agent.
- Existing suites rerun, all passing:
  - delivery-plan, failure-alerts (account routing, outcome, persistence), service failure-alert and delivery-plan;
  - isolated delivery-target, session-run, server-cron-completion;
  - gateway cron validation, request-validation, webchat-delivery, caller-scope, ownership-matrix;
  - config schema, metadata, hints, control-ui contract, zod agents and core;
  - run-recovery, run-finalization and scheduler-actor workers;
  - after the creator layer: delivery-plan, failure-alerts (account routing, outcome, persistence), gateway cron validation, request-validation, webchat-delivery, caller-scope, ownership-matrix, delegated-creator and creator-transports integration, server-cron-completion, isolated delivery-target, and config schema, help quality, hints, field metadata, control-ui contract, zod core, base generated schema (22 files, all passing).
- Mutation checks:
  - The cron-tool tests fail against the base `cron-tool.ts`.
  - Creator mutants each killed by the new tests: dropping the creator from the scope, swapping creator and agent order, dropping the creator failure route, attributing any actor id as a creator, and case-folding creator keys.
  - The completion owner test fails when the session-key owner resolution is removed.
- Independent review: three structured review passes (P0 to P2). The first raised two findings:
  - Missing `defaultAgentId` on finalization and skip snapshots: verified false, the snapshots already carry it.
  - Completion owner taken from `job.agentId` only: valid, fixed by the shared scope helper.
  - The second pass on the agent/global diff was clean.
  - The third pass on the final diff, including the creator layer, was clean. Its one open doubt (whether worker-loaded jobs carry `createdActor`) checks out: failure-alert workers load jobs through the same row decoder (`loadedCronStoreFromRows`) whose `createdActor` the run-time execution context already reads.
- Validation follow-up (head after `7d661bba`):
  - Lint fix: the create-time default check no longer casts raw cron tool input to `CronDelivery`; `check:assertion-safety-ratchet` (`src/cron/delivery-context.ts: 2 > 1`) now passes.
  - `pnpm check:changed --base 5c410ef4eb5`: all lanes pass except the dead-export scan, whose entries are all in files this PR does not touch (same list on the base).
  - New `src/config/config.cron-default-destinations.test.ts`: unknown channel rejected at each of the five default paths, global `cron.failureAlert` only warns, known channels and built-in aliases pass, `last`/webhook routes skipped, `cron.agents` keys differing by case rejected.
  - `src/commands/doctor/cron/warnings.test.ts`: defaults on inactive channels are listed; active defaults stay quiet.
  - Mutation checks: dropping the load-time issue, the `cron.agents` duplicate check, or the doctor default scan each fails the new tests.
- Micro-benchmark of `resolveCronDeliveryPlan`. Node 24.22, 64-job mix, 20k-iteration warmup, 15 samples of 5k iterations, median ns per call, base (`5c410ef4`) vs head, three runs:
  - no defaults argument: about 24.5 → 30.5;
  - defaults scope with nothing configured: about 33;
  - defaults configured: about 178. That path resolves and normalizes the default route and scans agent keys.
  - Plan resolution happens a few times per run, so this is negligible next to run cost. I moved the default lookup before the eligibility normalization so unconfigured Gateways pay only the lookup.

### What was not tested

- No live channel send. Proof is through the real target resolution and completion paths with synthetic channel I/O.
- `openclaw doctor` does not flag an unknown agent id under `cron.agents`.
- Config-load validation checks that a default's channel plugin is installed, not that the channel is configured or the recipient exists; doctor covers inactive plugins, and a wrong recipient still surfaces at send time.
- No Control UI changes or checks beyond the generated schema metadata.

### Open questions

- **Opting a job back into creating-chat routing.** Once a default is configured, a route-less job cannot return to the creating conversation, because `channel: "last"` is also the stored CLI default. Should there be an explicit opt-out, such as `delivery.target: "source"`? Today such a job must name its `channel`/`to`.
- **Failure routes have no `threadId`.** Telegram topics use the `-100…:topic:N` form, matching the existing `cron.failureAlert` shape. Should failure routes get a `threadId` field for parity?

prs.title: feat(simlock): add owner-scoped mobile device tools
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Owners need agent-device UI automation on an existing Simlock gateway without exposing arbitrary commands or treating a shared fleet token as conversation-level device authority.

## User Impact

Adds an optional, independently installable Simlock tool package: read-only health/discovery, owned-lease status and observations; finite acquisition, explicit bounded renewal, UI actions, and explicit release that warns Simlock may wipe app data. Tools remain owner-only and subject to existing OpenClaw policy and live invocation authority. Endpoint and SecretRef examples are synthetic.

No host provisioning, rentals/billing, app installs, arbitrary shell/flags/reset, guest access system, hosting Gateway installation/restart, or npm release is included. Reopening retains the same owned lease/session rather than silently replacing a device.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses existing public plugin SDK contracts with version-2 tool factories; no core SDK expansion. Simlock remains the pool/TTL owner. Process-local receipts bind the host agent, session and incarnation to plugin-acquired scope. Cancelled/uncertain acquisitions are retained; proven undispatched failures retire safely. Explicit reconciliation of an unallocated receipt requires the pinned queue/TTL settlement bounds and fresh authoritative absence of both the lease and its pending requester. Release may wipe, so it is a separate explicitly destructive tool.

Contracts are source-pinned to Simlock `0aa6a58d0f84ed2f4409a669de5d54352f078b99` and minimum agent-device daemon `542fb77b324e522b121b18550307e457ba9be471` (RPC 2). Accessibility output is projected and infrastructure identifiers/credentials are withheld; screenshot bytes are not general app-content DLP. See the package README for setup, permission separation and lifecycle limits.

## Evidence

- 22 plugin tests passed across 3 files, including production HTTP transport against isolated synthetic fixtures and public SDK tool registration. Covers authority/revocation, ownership/incarnation isolation, read-only versus mutation grants, concurrency, cancellation, uncertain recovery, renewal failure/expiry, explicit release, redaction, screenshots and no reset/replacement requests.
- 412 package-manifest/runtime-dependency contract tests passed across 2 files.
- Package-local production typecheck and targeted test typecheck passed; canonical SDK declarations prepared by their owning scripts.
- Oxlint: zero warnings/errors; Oxfmt check and staged diff check passed. Both SDK-source and cross-package import boundary checks passed.
- `pnpm pack` produced the standalone archive; inspected contents contain only production entry/client/controller, manifest/package metadata, README and license. No tests, credentials or private configuration are packaged.
- Fresh native independent P0–P2 review found an acquisition-recovery defect; two regressions reproduced it before repair, then passed with the fix. Follow-up review reported no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The broad extension dispatcher attempt hit Bun worker aborts/timeouts and was not used as passing evidence; corrected focused test lanes above passed.

**Keep this PR draft.** No real endpoint/token/Mac/lease exists for this task. Live authentication, installed daemon compatibility, real device UI/screenshot behavior and app/cache retention across reconnect/relaunch remain unverified. Fixtures prove adapter behavior, not live mobile-device behavior. Plugin/Gateway restarts lose process-local ownership receipts and do not adopt or replace leases; Simlock TTL and operator reconciliation remain authoritative.

## Worked on by

- @TheAngryPit

prs.title: fix(ci): allow serial SDK API reports to finish
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The SDK API report can exhaust its 30-minute job deadline after rendering the base, before rendering the head.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Maintainers get a bounded opportunity for the existing report to complete on constrained runners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give only the SDK API report job 60 minutes. Its existing resource policy serializes base/head rendering below 8 CPUs or 24 GiB; one observed base render took 1,283,606 ms (21m23s). Two comparable renders plus setup fit within 60 minutes. Keep the renderer, API assertions, check selection, runner selection, runtimes, action pins, permissions and credentials unchanged.

## Evidence

- [Exact failed report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41690637714/job/126109868347): base `d8d80bf1e80722f76a346e0ca67254adeadd9a6d` rendered successfully; head `c471475a5185f14cba44ec80ddaf2fbead581a2a` started at 18:33:01 UTC and was canceled at 18:40:25 UTC. The job annotation reports the 30-minute maximum.
- The job used `ubuntu-24.04`. There is no additional timeout on the report step or its shell command. Renderer control flow is unchanged between the compared revisions.
- Local workflow formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Source-owner simplification leaves one deadline change and its explanation; SDK/API assertions and line budgets remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(macos): New Thread exhausts memory during session creation
prs.body:
Closes #186215

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native macOS New Thread hanging and allocating unbounded memory when creating a conversation.

## User Impact

Native Mac users can create a thread through the sidebar or keyboard shortcut without entering recursive session creation. A missing or retired Gateway connection is rejected rather than silently retargeted. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mac transport now routes ordinary creation through its existing captured new-session lease. This replaces the recursive default-dispatch path without introducing another request builder or changing generic transports and iOS.

## Evidence

Product head: `2b916adf3896eb18fb11d7702c9dd203fa1aaecf` (unchanged).

- **Native regression/build:** [baseline red 40568043055](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40568043055); [exact-head native build and 35/35 mapping tests 40577761227](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40577761227). SwiftFormat required changes in 0/416 source and 0/33 test files. Lint passed with one nonblocking `file_length` advisory in untouched `DashboardManager.swift:1642` (1505/1500), covered by `LIMIT_RULES`; not zero warnings.
- **Shared consumer validation: PASS.** Canonical [run 41741119844](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/41741119844) succeeded on the exact product checkout above, using fork workflow SHA `d8aaa1f4648d6a7375c20760baaa7bdd794f42e0`. Swift Testing executed **104 tests in 4 suites**, all passed after **1.000 seconds** (compilation: 1483.64 seconds). All three requested suites explicitly passed: `ChatViewModelSessionActionTests` (0.855s), `ChatGatewayTransportTests` (0.006s), and `ChatGatewayRequestTests` (0.111s); additional `ChatGatewayPayloadCodecTests` passed (0.024s). These are suite durations, not invented per-suite test counts. The XCTest bootstrap's zero-test message is not the selected Swift Testing result.
- **Inspectable shared artifact:** [13282253631](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/41741119844/artifacts/13282253631), GitHub SHA-256 `4e365458a53eef598c352ec68a930d9b3dc7d3243755a9a0eed018c19e1aeb8a`. @harjothkhara downloaded and read `source-and-toolchain.log` and `shared-consumer-tests.log`; public run success/workflow identity and artifact digest were verified here. Hosted `macos-26-intel`, Xcode 26.6 (17F113), Swift 6.3.3, Node 24.22.1; normal `setup-node-env` and `node scripts/prepare-apple-mermaid.mjs`, no source/test edits or full app build. Initial focused run 41739785982 was canceled before tests; 41740028156 failed missing generated Mermaid resources before tests. Those setup outcomes are not product defects; 41741119844 is the canonical executed result.
- **Actual native flow, full observer INCOMPLETE:** [run 41724743098](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/41724743098), [artifact 13279006255](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/41724743098/artifacts/13279006255), proof SHA `277557c120bea8530cfb2cb4b3ea6b2cbc9375cd`, targeted the same product head. Coordinator-inspected artifact records exactly one verified native New Thread AXPress and exactly one native `openclaw-macos` / `operator` `sessions.create`, succeeded for `agent:main:ios-2195ed8d-9dc4-4f7b-9243-95f0e69875a3`, followed by successful `sessions.messages.subscribe` and `chat.history` for that key. The main parent was initialized through the public Gateway first. RSS: 57 samples / 6.178 seconds; first 177428 KiB, last/peak 181316 KiB, no observed runaway, normal cleanup. The workflow nevertheless failed in phase `stability`: post-action `ax-copy-key` hit `TargetedMenu.deadline` at ~3032 ms. No after screenshot or post-inventory exists; this is **not a full harness pass**.
- **Relevant upstream workflows succeeded:** [CI 41738331438](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41738331438), [Security 41738331887](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41738331887), [OpenGrep 41738331471](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41738331471), and [Periphery 41738331200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41738331200), including macOS/iOS consumer reports. Ordinary-PR native Swift jobs were intentionally skipped; the standalone artifact above supplies the shared-suite execution, not ordinary PR CI.

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Native macOS New Thread must avoid recursive creation defaults and unbounded allocation and reach normal Gateway creation/error handling.
- **Real environment tested:** The exact-head native app plus isolated public Gateway on hosted Mac infrastructure; shared suites on the exact same product source with the toolchain above.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Connect the native app with an existing public-API-initialized main parent and invoke native Thread → New Thread once, recording RPCs/RSS. Shared validation: `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --scratch-path "$RUNNER_TEMP/session-test-build" --disable-index-store -Xswiftc -gline-tables-only --no-parallel --filter 'ChatViewModelSessionActionTests|ChatGatewayTransportTests|ChatGatewayRequestTests'`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Baseline regression red; exact-head native build and 35/35 mapping tests; successful actual native create → subscribe → history; standalone Swift Testing **104 tests in 4 suites passed**, with all three requested suites explicitly successful.
- **Observed result after fix:** The native action crossed the transport boundary once, created the new session and subscribed/loaded history for its key, without runaway allocation in the sampled interval. Shared consumer validation passed. The later copy-key observer timed out, so the full app-proof verdict remains incomplete.

The short RSS sample is not long-duration memory proof. A second complete baseline-app build is not supplied; parent-selection PR #189467 and other PRs remain separate scope.

The PR remains open and ready for maintainer review, not merged. The former shared-suite evidence gap is now supplied by the canonical standalone result; no additional tests, harness changes, or duplicate runs were made. Fresh review is requested against this updated evidence; its acceptance/completion must be read separately.

prs.body:
Related: #192116

## What Problem This Solves

Config form and device-binding browser tests spend real seconds waiting for Saved to offer Apply changes.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The same seven E2E cases run faster: summed file medians fall from **35.429s to 16.633s**, saving **18.796s (53.1%)**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the page-clock polling pattern from #192116. Advance one polling window at a time so config RPCs can settle between ticks; resume the defaults clock for later edits and reloads. Preserve every payload, reload, acknowledgement, request-count, Saved, cleared-notice, and inventory-recovery assertion. No negative absence window is shortened.

The two-second grace contract remains owned by `ui/src/lib/config/config-apply-prompt.test.ts`; Saved-to-Apply presentation remains covered by `ui/src/components/settings-save-indicator.test.ts`. These E2E files retain the composed browser flows.

prs.title: fix(codex): redact credentials in dynamic tool error content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Thrown and failed Codex dynamic-tool paths were putting raw `errorMessage` / failure `message` text into `contentItems` without running it through `sanitizeToolResult`. Successful and middleware-adjusted result paths already redacted credentials, so a thrown tool error that embedded a bearer token (or similar secret) could still surface the credential in the app-server tool-result content.

**Configuration-dependent gap:** `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → `redactSensitiveText` uses configured `logging.redactPatterns` **in place of** defaults. Model-visible `sanitizeToolResult` / `redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText` **combines** custom patterns with built-in tool payload patterns. So under a nonmatching custom `redactPatterns` config, diagnostic/error formatting alone still leaks an unregistered synthetic bearer, while catch-path `sanitizeToolResult` keeps built-in bearer protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared `sanitizeToolResult` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` on the two remaining failure content builders:

- `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` catch path in `dynamic-tools.ts` (thrown execution errors)
- `createFailedDynamicToolResponse` in `dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` (failed response factory)

Non-goals: no change to success-path redaction, budget truncation, or middleware ordering.

## User Impact

**Before:** A dynamic tool that threw (or failed via the shared failed-response helper) could return `contentItems` containing unsanitized credentials from the error text — especially when `logging.redactPatterns` replaced diagnostic defaults with patterns that do not cover bearer tokens.

**After:** Thrown/failed dynamic-tool error content is redacted with the same `sanitizeToolResult` used on successful result content (built-ins always apply for model-visible output).

## Evidence

- Production catch path: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` now sets `text: sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)`.
- Shared failed factory: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` sanitizes the failure `message` before building `contentItems`.
- Regression: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` spies `readLoggingConfig` with nonmatching `redactPatterns` `[String.raw`\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\b`]`, asserts `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` still contains the synthetic bearer (before), and asserts model-visible `contentItems` do not (after `sanitizeToolResult`). Mock restored in `finally`.
- Diagnostic harness: `scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts` prints the actual protocol response JSON.





### Custom-pattern regression (exact head `67505f4ca5c4`)

```text
Product head: 67505f4ca5c482f9eac9474cd0a6f25bf4afc2bd
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.thrown-error-redaction.test.ts --reporter=verbose
PASS redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items under custom logging patterns
```

Configures logging.redactPatterns=["never-match-custom-redact-pattern-141271"] via isolated OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH so formatToolExecutionErrorMessage still contains the synthetic bearer (defaults bypassed), then asserts the bridge response does not.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Thrown dynamic-tool error content could include unsanitized credentials when diagnostic redact patterns replace defaults.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` → tool `execute` throws → `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → catch builds `contentItems` with `sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)` → `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse`.
- **Boundary crossed:** Extension dynamic-tool error content → shared `sanitizeToolResult` from plugin-sdk agent-harness-runtime (model-visible policy merges built-ins).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused existing `sanitizeToolResult`; no new helper.
- **Real environment tested:** Local diagnostic harness against production `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` + `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse` under custom `logging.redactPatterns`. **Live Codex binary was NOT used** — this records the actual protocol response object returned toward Codex, not a full app-server binary round-trip.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts
# writes /workspace/codex-runtime-proof.txt
```

- **Evidence after fix (diagnostic transcript):**

```text
# Codex dynamic-tool thrown-error redaction diagnostic
# Generated: 2026-09-07T14:53:48.289Z (UTC)
# Proof surface: createCodexDynamicToolBridge → handleToolCall catch path
#               → toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse (JSON contentItems)
# Live Codex binary: NOT used (unavailable / not required for this harness)
# Synthetic credential only — non-usable fixture.

logging.redactPatterns = ["\\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\\b"]
(nonmatching custom patterns replace diagnostic defaults;
 model-visible sanitizeToolResult merges built-ins.)

## Before catch-path sanitizeToolResult
formatToolExecutionErrorMessage(...) under custom redactPatterns:
{
  "formatted": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer-model-visible-credential-1234567890"
}
contains synthetic credential: true

sanitizeToolResult(formatted) alone (model-visible built-ins):
{
  "sanitizedAlone": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
}
contains synthetic credential: false

## After fix: protocol response returned toward Codex app-server
toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse(createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall(...)):
{
  "contentItems": [
    {
      "type": "inputText",
      "text": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
    }
  ],
  "success": false
}

success: false
contentItems text contains synthetic credential: false
contentItems text contains "Authorization: Bearer": true

## Summary
- Under custom nonmatching redactPatterns, diagnostic formatting LEAKS the synthetic bearer.
- After sanitizeToolResult on the catch path, protocol contentItems do NOT contain it.
- This records the actual protocol response object, not Vitest expect() output.
```

- **Vitest (distinguishing regression):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts -t 'redacts credentials from thrown' --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items 38ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 172 skipped (173)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 25.56s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Under custom nonmatching `redactPatterns`, diagnostic formatting still contains the synthetic bearer; protocol `contentItems` after the catch-path sanitizer do not (`Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890`).
- **What was not tested:** Live Codex app-server / `@openai/codex` binary round-trip. Proof surface is the real bridge + protocol response object.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

prs.title: test(gateway): channel account routes keep serving after another plugin's config reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A channel account that serves inbound traffic over HTTP must keep its route when a different plugin's config is edited and the Gateway hot-reloads. Nothing tested that path end to end on a real Gateway. If it regresses, the account still reports as running, but its route returns 404 until a restart.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change; this adds a test only. It protects channels that register an HTTP route when an account starts, such as webhook-style inbound routes.

## Why This Change Was Made

On reload, a retained plugin's routes are projected into the new registry. Today only unit tests in `src/gateway/server/plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` cover that projection. The real-Gateway channel lifecycle tests reload the route's own plugin, not an unrelated one.

The new test follows the existing `server-plugins.lifecycle.*` fixtures and helpers. It starts a channel account that registers a prefix route at `startAccount`. It then hot-reloads another plugin's config three times with `config.patch`. After each reload it checks four things:
- the other plugin really re-registered, with a new instance and a new active registry;
- the account's route still answers 200 from the current registry;
- the route set is unchanged;
- the account was started only once.

Finally, stopping the account still removes the route (404).

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.channel-routes.test.ts` on current `main`: 1 passed (gateway-server project).
- **Mutation check.** The mutation removes the `target.httpRoutes.push(...)` line from `projectPluginHttpRoutes` in `src/plugins/http-route-owner.ts`.
  - The new test fails at the first reload: `status: 404`, expected 200.
  - Under the same mutation, `server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts` still passes 3/3 and `plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` fails 3/8.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the file: clean.
- `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json`: clean. A type error injected into the file makes it fail, so the file is in that project.
- `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:assertion-safety` and `check:database-worker-ratchet`, run against the parent commit: OK.

prs.title: fix(codex): settled-turn recovery rejects sessions containing a media-only user turn
prs.body:
Closes #185079

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex settled-turn finalization repeatedly fails with `invalid_content` when the session history contains a legitimate media-only user turn — a message persisted with empty text plus ordered `__openclaw.media` facts (for example, a JPEG-only Telegram message) and no upstream-text fallback. The projection validated every earlier message before trimming, so one such historical turn kept rejecting every later finalization context capture on that session.

## User Impact

User impact: a verified historical media-only message no longer invalidates settled-turn recovery. It projects as a bounded, deterministic marker naming the attachment types, and finalization context capture succeeds for sessions that contain one. Empty messages without any well-formed media fact are still rejected, upstream text keeps winning over the placeholder, and current-turn evidence and pairing checks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`projectUserMessage` required non-empty text and threw `CodexHistoryRejection("invalid_content")` for a blank user turn. The persisted representation for media-only turns is exactly that shape (empty `content`, media metadata under `message.__openclaw.media` — the documented "media-bearing user turns use ordered `message.__openclaw.media` facts" convention). The payloads themselves are not replayable through the text-oriented recovery projection, so the fix projects a deterministic `[User media attachment unavailable in this context: <types>]` marker — the same approach the projector already uses for image tool results (`[Image tool result: <mime>]`) — capped at the first eight entries with a `+N more` suffix, always inside the existing byte budgets.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.test.ts`: against unpatched `origin/main`, exactly the two placeholder-projecting cases fail (media-only turn rejected with `invalid_content`); with the fix all 26 cases pass, including the guards for empty turns without well-formed media facts (still `invalid_content`), upstream-text precedence, and the placeholder cap.
- `pnpm test:extension codex` passes except two `transport-startup.test.ts` cases that fail identically on unpatched `main` on this machine (macOS native process inspection returns a permission error in this environment); the projection suites themselves are fully green.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes typecheck extensions, typecheck extension tests, and lint extension changed files. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` unused-export scan flagging three exports in files this PR does not touch.


**Remaining proof:** No end-to-end Gateway/Codex recovery run with persisted media-only history has been performed. The regression tests cover the projection boundary; they do not establish the full recovery and finalization flow.

prs.title: fix: retry model listing when a remote catalog replaces its snapshot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `models.list` can return retryable `UNAVAILABLE` when a remote catalog publication replaces the snapshot between acquisition and projection, even though a replacement is ready and clients do not retry.

## User Impact

Model listing uses the current replacement without asking the client to retry. Account unlink and other authority changes retain their existing rejection behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The remote publication owner records the exact retired-to-replacement generation. Catalog acquisition rereads published facts once only while that replacement remains current, before capturing private account facts. It does not replay discovery or introduce a generic retry for supersession errors.

This is intentionally bounded to published-catalog acquisition. It does not retry later account-preparation failures or independently cached/preloaded chat-metadata failures. The acquisition operation lives in a focused sibling module to preserve the listing owner's enforced line cap.

## Evidence

- Real `models.list` handler plus remote publication owner regression: fails against base production code (the handler returns failure), passes with the fix and replacement rows.
- Remote publication followed by retirement of its replacement still rejects without rereading.
- Focused tests: 47 passed across `prepared-model-runtime.remote-publication.test.ts`, `models-list-result.plugin-runtime.test.ts`, `models-list-result.configured-static.test.ts`, and `model-account-catalog-authority.integration.test.ts`, including unlink during auth and DNS. All 47 also passed after extraction.
- Final extracted remote suite: 10 passed, 18.30 seconds suite duration. Other three suites: 37 passed, 118.34 seconds. The combined command completed in 184.03 seconds including worker preparation. These are local durations; hosted CI timing is pending. Fixtures isolate provider I/O; this is not a live-provider claim.
- Formatting, diff checks, and staged line-cap ratchet pass. Core typecheck and targeted lint bootstrap encounter inherited errors in unchanged `mcp-metadata.ts` / `agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts` (`McpCatalogTool` export and optional `uiVisibility`); lint cannot reach its changed-file pass because boundary declaration generation fails first.
- Independent review: no actionable P0–P3 findings; fresh extraction-only review also found no actionable issues. Local ClawSweeper review complete for `34007820fa2c..19c133d7d247`: no actionable correctness or security findings.
- Simplification retains every existing authority predicate and introduces no handler-wide retry. Net production growth is 47 lines; 38 net test lines cover successful replacement and revoked-replacement rejection, with a separate allocation record.

## CI follow-up

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41742931012/job/126289295861) fails in the existing Goal authority test: it expects a revoked Goal to remain `active`, but receives `paused`; zero continuation turns still matches. The test and lifecycle implementation are identical on the feature base, this PR head, and observed main `c16858baa256`. Ancestor `85f973601725` intentionally pauses active goals after Stop. [Separate PR #192387](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192387), split from #191830, already owns that exact expectation correction; it is not duplicated here.

The CI classifier returned unknown because a matching main job/log was unavailable. An independent Bun replay stopped before tests on inherited MCP declaration errors during required build preparation, so no fresh local reproduction is claimed. This PR’s CI remains failed, not green.

prs.title: fix(ui): follow the Activity page scroll owner on phones
prs.body:
## Problem
Activity changes scroll owners at its phone/short-landscape breakpoint, but live auto-follow still reads and writes the inner stream. On base `91d08c31`, the phone regression leaves a 395px bottom gap; explicit resume also misses the end. Related: #190393, #190409.

## Solution
- Select the outer content on phone/short-landscape layouts and the stream on desktop.
- After DOM insertion, own one capture listener on the containing page for the mounted Live view. Filter events to the active scroll owner; no reactive listener-rebinding effect is needed.
- Make shared auto-follow read its configured container instead of the event listener's currentTarget, so captured and element-bound callers agree on one owner.
- Cover follow, wheel-scroll pause, and resume at 390×844, 768×1024, 932×430, and 1440×844; reuse the existing shared-helper test for captured-scroll delivery.

## Impact
No CSS, theme-token, markup, or public API changes. Update-run retains its own inner scroll containers and is covered by its existing tests. Logs/transcripts are unchanged. Production delta against the merge base: +28/−5 lines; test delta: +121/−3 (net +118).

## Evidence
- Base browser reproduction: expected bottom gap <2px, observed 395px. Existing matched captures show 395px → 0px following and 3664px → 0px after resume.
- Final bundled Chromium regression: **4 passed**, 29.84s wall time, with synthetic Gateway events and fixed fixture time. Final source hashes were recorded with the run.
- Shared captured-scroll regression: **red before the helper fix** (expected scrollTop 0, got 1000), green afterward. Activity, shared auto-follow, and update-run unit suites: **47 passed**, 6.16s wall time.
- Final UI typecheck, targeted oxlint, format check, controller guard, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- CI on `6a1b82b6f2b7979bf6d2f30e2643229231de79f6` has settled; UI e2e and i18n passed. Production types and all six test-type jobs fail in untouched MCP modules. Their compiler diagnostics match #192368, #192383, and #192389; the package-boundary declaration errors match those PRs as well.
- The test-lines ratchet reports 47 inherited over-budget lines, also observed on #192368, #192383, and #192389. This PR adds 118 test lines and an exactly matching 118-line allocation. Local reproduction reports the same 355-line excess on both the original base (zero test delta) and this branch; the allocation does not absorb existing debt.
- The shared startup-JS budget check reports 90,688 B against 90,687 B. The same budget check fails on unrelated #192377 (90,696 B) and #192373 (90,701 B). The aggregate CI gate reflects these failed jobs.
- Prior light/dark visual scenarios: **4 passed**. No rendered change was made in this CI repair, so the six existing comparisons are retained rather than recaptured.

## Visual proof
Six labeled **BEFORE | AFTER** phone comparisons are attached below: light/dark × following/paused/resumed. The captions include the measured distance from the actual scroll owner to the bottom. Also inspected matching 1440px light/dark captures for all five checkpoints; desktop layout and behavior stay consistent. Fixture data is fictional.

## Accepted edge cases / follow-ups
- Verified in Chromium browser fixtures, not on physical phones or against a live Gateway. No color/markup changes, so custom-theme, loading/error, and translated-copy layouts are unaffected by this scroll-owner-only change.
- The responsive query intentionally matches the existing page-scrolling CSS, including short landscape phones; keep them in sync if that layout breakpoint changes.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve(ui): clarify chat command and composer errors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Chat command, composer, and session errors use inconsistent wording, expose implementation terms, and sometimes omit a useful next step. Model/setting failures also bypass the English catalog.

## User Impact
Errors now say what failed and how to recover. Session/reply terminology is consistent, and setting/model failures are localized. Sending, reconnect admission, queued retries, and draft retention are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
This is the scoped C8 copy pass: command results, composer/menu, questions, core session copy, and their error callers. It adds no error transport or runtime policy. An independent review caught a misleading “select another session” recovery; the final wording correctly describes a session-details load failure.

### Glossary follow-up
- Changed the added effort load/reset/change errors from “thinking level” to “effort”, including the session-setting error and exact test expectations.
- Re-read the full added-copy diff against the approved glossary. Remaining Chat references name the screen; node/host occurrences are code identifiers, not user-facing nouns.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` and the normal pre-commit hook passed. No behavior or control flow changed.

### Copy examples
| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Failed to set model: {error} | Couldn’t change the model. Try again. {error} |
| Failed to set thinking level: {error} | Couldn’t change effort. Try again. {error} |
| Unable to access the camera. | Couldn’t access the camera. Check this browser’s camera permission and try again. |
| Could not submit: {error} | Couldn’t submit your answer. Try again. {error} |
| Couldn’t load earlier messages | Couldn’t load earlier messages. Try again. |
| Admin access is required to manage MCP servers. | You need admin access to manage MCP servers. |
| Reconnect to change tools for this chat. | Reconnect to change tools for this session. |
| Prompt budget (last run) | Prompt budget (last reply) |
| Session capability is unavailable | Couldn’t load session details. Check your connection and try again. |

## Evidence
- Mocked Control UI browser tests: **2 files, 4 tests passed**. The new failed-command scenario verifies a newer draft is retained and no ordinary message is sent.
- Focused command, session/settings, send, and realtime tests: 9 files passed in the initial run; the final command/composer rerun passed **52 tests** after updating the /usage English assertion.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed. Baseline generation produced no tracked change.
- Oxfmt and oxlint passed on the 12 touched TypeScript files; `git diff --check` passed.
- UI typecheck passed with `pnpm exec tsrs --noEmit --declaration false -p ui/tsconfig.json`.
- Searched command/Chat docs for the changed output; no exact quotes needed updating.
- Before the instruction to stop additional testing arrived, the glossary follow-up’s focused command/send tests passed (138 tests), and its single mocked browser scenario passed. No further tests were started.

### Before
Cropped from the mocked Control UI in light theme, with synthetic error data.

### After
Same failed-command surface; the summary adds recovery guidance and retains the diagnostic. These published images document the original C8 pass, before the effort terminology follow-up.

![After: failed thinking command with recovery guidance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c08b8d0-e055-4c56-891a-593b34608eaf)

### Gaps and intentionally unchanged behavior
- The glossary follow-up did not run full suites, additional typechecking, or CI. No further browser runs, screenshot review, or screenshot publication were performed after the stop instruction. Existing screenshots predate this follow-up.
- F1’s shared collapsed error-details contract is not on this base. Raw details remain inline for `commandResults.compaction.failedWithReason`, `model.{get,set}Failed`, `thinking.{get,reset,set}Failed`, `verbose.{get,set}Failed`, `fast.{get,reset,set}Failed`, `usage.failed`, `steer.requestFailed`, `redirect.requestFailed`, `questions.submitFailed`, and `settingErrors.{model,thinking,speed,contextWindow,accessProgram}` (all under `chat`).

prs.title: fix: avoid Gateway stalls while archiving large worktrees
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway main-thread pauses when cleanup archives large managed sandbox worktrees. Archive preparation currently materializes, parses, and validates the full accepted manifest on the host, then constructs another full archive baseline.

## User Impact

Archive preparation keeps full-tree computation in the existing filesystem worker. Live file changes still block stale archive capture, active owners remain protected, and ignored files and empty directories retain their restore receipts. No configuration or database schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest owner already holds an admitted tree. The worker compares live files with those records and constructs receipt bytes only when Git omits accepted content. A complete Git archive returns only the no-overlay result. Legacy recovery keeps its existing serialization contract, and projection-root and deletion-authority checks remain in place.

Regular GC already skips ineligible/protected worktrees and the scheduler already yields every eight checkpointed records. A stored manifest revision cannot safely replace fresh filesystem observation: guest writes do not advance that revision. This change adds no cache.

## Evidence

- Real `service.gc()` regression: baseline removed the checkout but parsed the full manifest once on the main thread; candidate removes it with zero host parses. Active-owner cleanup retains it with zero parses. The same owner proof rejects guest edits, additions, deletions, and a symlinked projection root.
- Focused validation: 105 passed, two environment skips; after the archive extraction and legacy/root-guard preservation, all 10 affected archive/restore cases passed. The final consolidated regression passed in 13.25 seconds including runner setup (about two seconds of test work).
- `pnpm check:changed`: all checks passed except the benchmark promise-executor lint (fixed; targeted lint and script typecheck now pass) and four unused exports in untouched `src/gateway/node-plugin-tool-snapshot.ts`. Those four exports reproduce with no resolution errors on exact main parent `f3d7a450b3ff9a0de30ffbf596e49261eaa8661c` (production Knip exit 1). This is a main regression introduced by #191589 (`e0ac3370bbe37d73abc057bc8bd4dd32670c8e97`), which removed the production consumers while retaining their exports; it is not part of this patch. Timing and allocation campaigns are complete; the actual cleanup/restore comparison also passed.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2 on the local candidate against `f3d7a450b3ff9a0de30ffbf596e49261eaa8661c`; no accepted/actionable findings.

### Measurement acceptance rule

`scripts/perf/worktree-archive-maintenance-measure.ts` uses 60 registered managed Git worktrees with independent projections, each containing 10,000 synthetic source files of 16,384 bytes. Prepare outside measurement, run identical-code A/A controls, then at least five serial interleaved A/B pairs for timing and separate sampled-allocation pairs. Require identical archive decisions and accepted roots, zero main-thread manifest parses, lower main-thread CPU/allocation/blocking, and investigate any wall-time or total-process CPU regression over 20%. Run actual 60-tree cleanup on each revision and restore through the service between them to compare deletion decisions and snapshot trees.

These are APFS archive-owner measurements, not whole-Gateway, btrfs, or large-session-database latency measurements. Process CPU includes workers but excludes Git subprocess CPU; allocation and GC metrics describe the main thread.

That run began at host load 47.9 on 32 logical CPUs, and per-tree latency fell 62% within the run; it also overlapped a 5.3-second filename inventory. These observations establish disturbance, but do not identify the worker/kernel CPU cause. Every sample is retained. The claim is less main-thread work and allocation, not a reliable overall-process CPU improvement or reproduction of production stall duration.

The real cleanup comparison passed: baseline GC removed all 60 worktrees, service restore recreated all 60 at the original commit, and candidate GC removed the same 60 IDs. Both retained identical snapshot Git trees and durable removal metadata, with zero issues, failures, or deferrals. Main-thread parses were 60→0. Chat mixes three-dot ellipses, title-case headings, emphatic copy feedback, and inconsistent failure summaries.

prs.title: fix(cron): preserve runs and pacing through unrelated MCP reloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled session turns failing during preparation after an unrelated `mcp.servers.*` config patch, then losing their accepted `next_check` cadence until the next daily slot.

## User Impact

Scheduled turns on the OpenClaw runtime continue through unrelated MCP server edits. Failed paced checks retain their pending occurrence through normal error backoff and Gateway restart. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run admission was comparing MCP server configuration even when the selected runtime already delegates connection authority to the MCP owner. The policy now uses the runtime facts selected upstream: OpenClaw-owned connections retain exact-instance revocation, while CLI and other native runtimes that receive raw MCP config keep their existing checks. Potentially effectful work is never blindly replayed.

The cron owner now retains a due paced occurrence until it succeeds or is disabled. This removes the redundant expiry guard and its special-case plumbing. Production code grows by 26 lines to carry selected runtime facts and preserve failed occurrence ownership; no cache, new generation, or retry wrapper is added. The local type-import repair matches the fix subsequently landed on main in dbecd558192e.

## Evidence

- Clean parent `9038857e7327bafc88b6bc716784ffcc451eb38f`: all four new behavioral regressions fail. Candidate: full `pnpm build` passes; 217 focused tests pass, including MCP connection retirement, scheduled admission/readmission, prefix stability, paced failure/restart, and force-run ownership.
- Real isolated Gateway, two existing sessions, real cron scheduling and `automations.next_check`, loopback model, actual `config.patch` during native preparation: parent produces two authority errors and next checks about 86,372 seconds away; candidate completes both and keeps their 3-second next checks. Preparation counts prove no extra admission/replay.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2, including the final diff. `pnpm check:changed --base HEAD` completed. Its typecheck and proof-script lint findings were fixed; core, all core-test shards, script typechecks, and targeted script lint now pass. The only remaining failure is four untouched node-plugin snapshot exports, reproduced by the same production Knip scan on exact parent 9038857e7327 and introduced by e0ac3370bbe3 / #191589. This is an inherited main regression, not a waived PR defect.
- Reproducible synthetic proof scripts are included. No production data or credentials are used. Synthetic scale is 5,000 sessions / 35 GiB SQLite and 62,000 files / 1.116 GB; owner timing excludes fixture setup. Host filesystem is APFS, so this does not claim btrfs equivalence.

Successful-policy timing control: 38.752→39.649 µs wall and 38.425→39.263 µs thread CPU; the ~2.3% change is within ~4.9% A/A drift. Under the MCP patch, parent incorrectly rejects all 125,000 checks at 26.172 µs while candidate retains all at 41.763 µs; those different outcomes are not an optimization comparison.

Equal successful-check sampled allocation: 50,073→50,733 B/check (+1.32%); changed-MCP early-refusal versus completed validation: 32,899→53,848 B/check. Five A/B pairs plus two A/A pairs cover the changed publication; three A/B pairs cover equal successful work.

prs.title: fix(android): show retry instead of SHA-256 entry on TLS timeout
prs.body:
Closes #142528

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android asks for a SHA-256 certificate fingerprint when the first TLS probe to a Gateway times out, for example a Tailscale Serve endpoint whose handshake stalls.

## User Impact

A timed-out first connection now shows the connection recovery screen with Retry (and the Tailscale hint on tailnet hosts) instead of asking the user to fetch a fingerprint from the Gateway host.

## Why This Change Was Made

#142651 routed `ENDPOINT_UNREACHABLE` to the network recovery path; this does the same for `TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` in `decideGatewayTlsTrust` and reuses `gatewayNetworkConnectError(timedOut = true)` in `NodeRuntime`, keeping the existing timeout text. No UI or string changes.

This changes the fallback order from #110976 on purpose. A timeout with no captured fingerprint means the server never sent a certificate within the probe budget, so a pasted pin has nothing to match. Manual entry stays for `TLS_UNAVAILABLE`, which `connect_enforcesAcceptedManualFingerprintAfterTlsProbeFailure` still covers. iOS already treats `.tlsHandshakeTimeout` as a timeout rather than manual entry (`GatewayConnectionSupport.swift`). This follows the ClawSweeper recommendation on the issue, without the separate advanced pin action, because that action cannot help a stalled handshake.

Accepted edge case: the probe budget is 13s and the real connection timeout is 20s. A server whose handshake consistently takes 13–20s previously connected through a pasted pin; it now gets Retry.

## Evidence

Draft: tests and device proof not yet captured.

- [ ] Main RED: the `GatewayTlsTest` and `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest` timeout cases fail with the fix lines reverted.
- [ ] Fix GREEN: `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` for `GatewayTlsTest`, `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest`, `InitialOnboardingLayoutTest`, `FoldAwareDialogTest`; `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck`.
- [ ] Device: main vs fix APK against a TCP listener that never completes a handshake, no saved pin — prompt (main) vs recovery screen (fix).

Production delta +9/-4; test delta +26/-19.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the prior prompt with no state or config migration. Blast radius is first-time Android connections whose TLS probe times out.

prs.title: feat(clawrouter): consume native ElevenLabs speech offers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter TTS and Talk cannot consume a qualified native ElevenLabs speech offer.

## User Impact

Users can select `upstreamProvider: "elevenlabs"` when their proxy key's fresh catalog exposes the qualified model-less speech operation. Native and manifest transports preserve the voice path, native model input, bounded voice settings and query options. Only complete MP3 output is supported; streaming, voice notes, telephony and unsupported settings fail before dispatch. Direct ElevenLabs behavior is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit Talk/TTS voice overrides now apply after canonical configured speaker selection; case-insensitive Talk aliases still use the existing host resolver. The proxy consumer and direct ElevenLabs plugin share the existing native JSON payload through the speech-provider SDK. Catalog resolution accepts a validated voice path segment without allowing it to replace the catalog-owned model. The proxy key alone authorizes discovery and synthesis; explicit profiles remain terminal, stale or foreign offers fail closed, and uncertain synthesis is never replayed.
