prs.title: fix: reclaim abandoned read-only database snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: read-only database copies accumulate after a creator is killed, and plain `openclaw status` can unnecessarily copy the entire state database when reading update history.

## User Impact

New abandoned snapshots are reclaimed by Gateway maintenance after a 15-minute grace period, without deleting copies held by live creators, nested workers, or inspection workers. Plain status reads avoid an unnecessary snapshot. Existing flat shared-cache snapshots remain explicit offline cleanup because their installation cannot be identified safely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stage new copies under a private namespace derived from the installation's state directory. The existing delayed startup/hourly maintenance owner runs a streaming scan with bounded memory and the native worker deadline through the existing native SQLite worker, using the existing lifetime-token retirement protocol. Inspection workers retain their own read token through result publication, so killing their launcher cannot expose a live snapshot to reclamation. Explicit artifact-preserving update diagnostics retain their existing behavior.

No new configuration, SQLite schema, survivor process, or cleanup IPC. Production growth is 164 lines for the deferred reclamation owner and complete lifetime coverage; removing the redundant status scope is a net deletion. Related: #191639, #191782.

## Evidence

Focused regressions fail on exact parent `073498226768e62d6ee0232b4e196cb487fc56cc` and pass on this change: unnecessary update-history snapshot; inspection-worker lifetime after launcher release; Gateway maintenance leaving an aged abandoned copy. Real native byte-copy SIGSTOP/SIGKILL proof covers abandoned journal files, live parent ownership, live nested ownership, and subsequent reclamation. Relevant read-only, update, cancellation, cleanup, and Gateway maintenance tests pass. `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passes. Independent Codex autoreview: no actionable findings.

Synthetic btrfs workload: 35.03 GiB database, 4,000 sessions, 62,000 workspace files / 1.10 GB. A/A controls and five interleaved A/B pairs: all unchanged-owner samples retain the abandoned copy; all reclamation samples remove it; live owners remain. Median copied bytes at kill: 596 MiB. Reclamation median/p95: 45.47/59.14 ms wall, 10.76/11.47 ms owner CPU, 364/446 KB sampled allocation. This measures a byte copy; it does not assert a production-matched fragmentation ratio.

Rerunnable workloads: `scripts/perf/sqlite-staging-reclamation-measure.mts`, `scripts/perf/sqlite-staging-maintenance-measure.mts`, and `scripts/perf/gateway-status-read-measure.mts`. Acceptance: zero unnecessary status snapshots; dead copies reclaimed with live copies retained; five paired fresh-process measurements plus A/A controls; maintenance/rollback wall, CPU, allocation and tails must not materially regress (20% is a stop). Final status-owner results on a synthetic 12.03-GiB shared state database (five counterbalanced pairs):

| Median / p95 | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Staged directories | 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 |
| Wall | 34.448 / 55.121 s | 3.654 / 3.802 s |
| Owner CPU | 4.872 / 7.567 s | 3.064 / 3.169 s |
| Total process CPU | 12.90 / 15.24 s | 10.22 / 10.72 s |
| Instrumented allocation | 13.11 / 20.63 MB | 1.89 / 2.05 MB |
| Peak RSS | 756 / 760 MB | 679 / 687 MB |

A/A wall controls were 44.78/26.51 s. Allocation includes the staging observer, so longer copies incur more observer allocation. Endpoint RSS increased 467→677 MB at substantially different process ages; peak RSS is the one-shot process maximum and improved. This measures the update-history owner, not every possible diagnostic read.

Quiet fresh-maintenance/rollback qualification (A/A controls and five counterbalanced pairs):

| Median / p95 | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maintenance wall | 13.825 / 16.955 s | 14.076 / 15.186 s |
| Maintenance CPU | 627 / 855 ms | 630 / 674 ms |
| Maintenance allocation | 162.294 / 166.591 MB | 161.080 / 163.947 MB |
| Rollback wall | 8.202 / 10.705 s | 8.271 / 9.271 s |
| Rollback CPU | 1,373 / 1,595 ms | 1,398 / 1,555 ms |
| Rollback allocation | 14.259 / 15.370 MB | 14.191 / 14.631 MB |
| Total process CPU | 61.89 / 69.06 s | 62.63 / 69.94 s |

Median wall/CPU changes are at most +1.82%, below A/A variation (about 2–6%); allocations decrease slightly. Loads were 7.42–12.98. An earlier campaign overlapped builds/checks and regressed maintenance/rollback timing tails by 52.5%/73.5%; those raw results were retained and a serial repeat resolved the qualification gap. No speedup is claimed from baseline tail variation.

Commands: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/sqlite-staging-reclamation-measure.mts --root <synthetic-root>`; `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/sqlite-staging-maintenance-measure.mts --base <parent> --candidate <candidate> --out <new-output>`; and `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/gateway-status-read-measure.mts --subject src/infra/update-run-reader.ts --export getUpdateRunHistoryStatusAsync` with isolated synthetic state/cache environment.

Hosted review found fixed-prefix scan starvation; the corrected streaming scan is covered by 257 reclaimable copies mixed with 256 missing-token directories. The regression fails before that correction and passes afterward. Initial CI also caught the omitted wrapper inventory entry and a proof byte-count race before SIGSTOP delivery; both are repaired, with the exact byte-count assertion retained. Focused wrapper, Gateway maintenance, and real SIGKILL tests pass.

`pnpm check:changed` exposes a main regression: four unused exports in `src/gateway/node-plugin-tool-snapshot.ts`, reproduced on the exact parent and introduced by `e0ac3370bbe37d73abc057bc8bd4dd32670c8e97` (#191589). This PR does not modify that owner; the failure is retained for attribution rather than hidden with a baseline change.

The exact parent also exceeds the test-line ceiling by 53 (6,443,949 versus 6,443,896). Commit `073498226768` (#192297) added 65 lines with only 12 slack and no allocation. The exact-parent staged ratchet against its predecessor reproduces the failure. This is a second inherited main regression; this PR adds only its own 282-line justified allocation and does not alter the baseline.

Final CI checks out merge `f185cb0d5e7f34143c148f1b2b40f3bb22e1e7a7` of this head into main `70f04d86b7c52c5948d50c0593745d9fdd99c8b5`. That actual main parent has 47 lines of inherited budget debt: #192302 removed six lines from the original 53-line overrun.

A newly introduced main type regression also appears in final CI: `f32ee258e30983f699abbe4fd3c4d3ad0114f563` (#192302) moved `McpCatalogTool` to `agent-bundle-mcp-catalog.types.ts` without updating the import in `mcp-metadata.ts`. The repository core typecheck on exact main parent `70f04d86` exits 2 with all five diagnostics identical to CI. The owner sources, configuration, package manifest and lockfile are identical between that parent and the tested merge. SDK declaration emission fails on the same missing type; the later missing-full-receipt publication error is downstream. This is a main regression requiring repair, not noise or a PR-caused failure. Final CI run [41739591548](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41739591548), attempt 1, completed with exactly nine inherited root failures plus the aggregate: the budget ratchet, seven typecheck jobs, and SDK declaration/publication. All selected test jobs, including PostgreSQL conformance, passed; `security-fast` passed. Extension lint was selected but skipped because the failed SDK declaration job emitted no artifact, and its job condition requires that artifact. This downstream skip is included explicitly in the aggregate attribution. Native admission uses the explicitly authorized pinned-head inherited-failure route and retains failed CI rather than relabeling it green.

## Problem

Matrix fixes found during the 2026.10.10 stable release did not reach main: monitor readiness could be announced before startup maintenance completed, request deadline timers kept finished CLI commands alive, and late in-room verification failures could become unhandled rejections.

## Solution

This independently mergeable slice of #191830 targets `main` (not another split PR). It retains the Matrix startup/status fix, the SDK shutdown/error-handling patch, and the related E2EE QA scenarios aligned with offline state ownership and corrupt-snapshot refusal. No Codex, process, storage, scheduling, or unrelated fixes are included.

Forward-ports release commits `5fe32d9c57`, `4bbc5971ba`, `2a6a3bc041`, and `0f4dc59109`; original references and authorship are preserved in the commits. The original aggregate test-line allocation is replaced with 162 lines specific to these regressions.

## Evidence

- The 11 changed product/test/patch/scenario files are byte-identical to the corresponding files at the original #191830 head; the lockfile changes retain only this Matrix SDK patch hash.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-matrix.config.ts extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/index.test.ts extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/status.test.ts extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/matrix-js-sdk-patch.sdk.test.ts`: 3 files, 31 tests passed.

- Initial monitor/QA setup attempts failed because the new worktree lacked package-local dependency links for subprocess builds; after restoring links to the existing matching install, the suites above passed.
- Simplification pass: every retained hunk serves Matrix startup, shutdown, verification, or the matching QA contract; no new generic helper or owner was introduced. Delta versus main: 349 added / 42 removed lines across 13 files, including 162 regression lines and the two-line scoped allocation.

## Limitations / before landing

- The SDK patch extends `patches/matrix-js-sdk@43.0.0.patch`; explicit dependency-patch approval remains required before landing. These hunks were already shipped in 2026.10.10's SDK 42.4.0 patch, and the guarded 43.0.0 code is identical.

prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Toasts in the Control UI had no shared anatomy: errors tinted the whole card red, success and warning icons were blue, a long action label wrapped inside a 35% column, and the dismiss X sat in the row taking space from the message. ## User Impact Every toast now uses one component: - A leading slot (status icon or agent avatar), a title, an optional muted description, an action, and a dismiss X that appears on the top-right corner only on hover or focus. - Variants: neutral (no icon), success, info, warning, error and progress. The only signal is the icon color; the card stays neutral. Errors announce with `role="alert"`. - One button: a 28 px pill. Primary (terracotta fill) is opt-in through `actionPrimary`. - One line is a pill; two or more lines use a 28 px corner. Width hugs the content between 240 and 360 px. Themes with square corners keep them. - The action stays beside the text only while the text fits one line next to it; otherwise it moves to its own row, right aligned. Existing callers keep working; the three that passed an `icon` now pass the matching severity. ## Why This Change Was Made This is the approved toast design, split into four stacked PRs. This one is the component; placement and stacking follow in the next PR. ## Evidence Mock Control UI, Absolutely light, 1440 and 390, reached through real clicks (archive from the sidebar, an oversized upload, a background session finishing). Before and After, Session archived: Hover shows the dismiss X on the corner: Before and After, an error: the red card becomes a neutral card with a red icon: Before and After, a background session with an avatar; the action moves to its own row when the title does not fit beside it: After, 390: Checks run locally: oxfmt, oxlint, stylelint, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `toast.test.ts`, `toast-host.loading.test.ts` and `toast.browser.test.ts` (all pass). The attachment e2e helper that asserted the red card now asserts the icon color; e2e was not run. ## Problem
Phone Back and Escape did not agree on a settings subpage's parent. Plugin configuration exposed both problems: the shell's Escape path discarded the location, and the plugin page's capture handler bypassed the shell entirely, jumping straight to the installed list.

Related: #191206, #191222.

## Solution

- Let plugin settings Escape bubble to the shell instead of maintaining a second navigation implementation. Keep modal, menu, IME, skill-preview, and focused-field handling intact.
- Preserve plugin configuration → detail → list ordering and `from=plugins` origin navigation. Keep the intentional top-level behavior: Escape exits Settings; phone Back is absent there.

## Impact
All settings child routes use the same parent decision, including agent/model setup and appearance subpages. Plugin discovery keeps its own dismissal behavior. No CSS, colors, layout, configuration, or public contract changes.

Built on main; open #191395 also touches `app-shell-view-state.ts`. This change only renames its parent-target import/call and does not modify that PR or its branch.

prs.title: feat: run admitted MCP tools on the worker node that hosts them
prs.body:
Builds on the Gateway question flow merged in #191589. This PR targets `main` and adds same-node execution.

## What Problem This Solves

A dedicated worker can run the model turn on the same node that owns an MCP client. Sending that call through the Gateway serializes the projected result and loses the metadata Code Mode needs to expose it to the model.

## User Impact

A compatible worker calls its node's existing MCP client through its supervisor and projects the result in the model process. The MCP server can run on the node or at a remote HTTPS endpoint. In the Slack test, OCE handled OAuth and the worker used a bearer placeholder for Slack’s hosted MCP server. Known timeouts, authentication failures, and incompatible responses reach the model with a bounded, redacted diagnostic. Unexpected exceptions get a generic message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway applies the turn's tool policy and grants a handle only for eligible tools on the selected node. Older workers, tools on other nodes, and tools requiring Gateway hooks retain Gateway dispatch. The node captures permission when the launch arrives. Once the node processes a withdrawal or connection replacement, an old grant cannot start another MCP call. Restoring permission requires a fresh grant for a later turn. The model turn can continue.

When a local tool asks the user for input, the worker presents its Gateway-issued grant from this turn. Only the question and answer use the Gateway. A tool with execution permission alone receives a local decline. Workers using the earlier preview protocol fall back to Gateway dispatch.

## Evidence

**Question routing.** A real HTTP MCP server received `engineering` through either execution route. After the user answered, retiring the grant or replacing the pairing prevented delivery on both routes. Ending the originating turn also blocked delivery to a worker that was still waiting. With tool execution alone, the worker declined locally and sent zero Gateway requests. The test controls the paired transport and the answering user. [Server-side checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/79ea16e79fb130ba8aab7d4f1fcac2f7d4b572c5/src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.event.test.ts#L363-L396)

**Transport compatibility.** The direct node runner can receive the Gateway's local execution policy. The macOS app's private bridge keeps MCP calls on Gateway dispatch. The stdio regression test checks that a configured app worker offers the routed MCP command, omits local execution from its inventory and dispatches a routed invocation. The test uses a stub invocation handler. Older preview workers advertising `worker-local-mcp-v1` also use Gateway dispatch.

**Earlier live Console run on a dedicated worker.** With a real Slack account, the first turn of revision 1 returned the exact clickable thread permalink in Slack's MCP result, including its thread timestamp. The Gateway trace covered one worker launch and 17 worker control frames. It recorded one admitted search handle, zero worker-to-Gateway invocations for that handle, and zero Gateway-to-node MCP invocations. This run used the [OCE runtime backport at e38c4e63](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/commit/e38c4e6349ccd6e9e511b15b7ff25b334aca5a71) before the diagnostic and launch-race fixes below.

**What reaches the MCP server.** The integration test uses the production Gateway registry, worker supervisor and node MCP client, and sends requests to a real loopback HTTP MCP server. The Gateway socket, worker process, journal and turn descriptors are controlled test fixtures. The server counts incoming `tools/call` frames before it dispatches them. Each successful control also executes the tool.

| Request | Incoming `tools/call` |
| --- | ---: |
| Admitted handle | 1 |
| Ungranted handle | 0 |
| After withdrawal | 0 |
| Same grant after permission is restored | 0 |
| Previous turn's frame, or its handle sent by the current turn | 0 each |
| Current turn's admitted handle | 1 |
| Old connection after replacement | 0 |
| Newly admitted handle on the replacement connection | 1 |

Run `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/node-host/node-worker-mcp.authority.integration.test.ts` to reproduce the [server request counts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2a553f4d8ff292f2bbaeffb14275855422b0f174/src/node-host/node-worker-mcp.authority.integration.test.ts#L87-L158). Other tests exercise turn admission, remote or older workers, live pairing changes, Code Mode result projection, cancellation, and Linux supervisor process ownership.

**Launch race.** On the previously reviewed head `f04d03a9`, withdrawing and restoring permission while workspace admission was paused let a queued launch invoke the MCP client once, for both a fresh and a retained child. With this fix, both reject the old handle before invoking the client. Separate ingress coverage checks that the model turn's cancellation signal stays live.

The local upstream tests used an existing dependency installation because the registry's package-age rule deferred one dependency in a clean install.

The test allocation covers 1,019 net lines for worker admission, permission withdrawal on retained workers, server request counts, pending answers, result projection and transport fallback. The routed and same-node Gateway event suite passed all 28 tests.

## CI

On `5f93758e1fa`, all 28 Gateway event tests and all three worker-local MCP tests passed. The repository's test-line check passed after incorporating the baseline reconciliation from main (6,444,905 lines against a ceiling of 6,444,915). [Upstream correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/53a21b70627) · [CI for this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41731792912)

prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36`. The 2 November merge combines the published discovery-test follow-up `64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7` with main `c1b0fc1415a09138c48e3f81055aca0f8e4f12aa`. Evidence below is pinned to the revision actually checked; earlier runs are not current-head native execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41518373631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518373631) completed successfully at product `6fc1559`, including selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n and the CI gate. The [combined gate 41518985777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518985777) and security/dependency review statuses also passed. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. Periphery build and scan checks passed separately; neither is native test execution.
- **Published discovery regression:** [Commit `64bf55b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7) strengthens the existing selection test: it clears both selection keys, calls real discovery, asserts executable/version persistence before managed inspection, and removes the debug project-path shortcut before checking the resolver. The complete delta is one test file (+11/−1), with no production seam or weakened controls. Exact source-delta, patch-application and whitespace checks passed. Independent source review and scoped AutoReview (P0–P3, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, no findings) covered the prepared test change against `b3ee562`; native compilation/execution and baseline mutation proof were not run. Public source inspection confirms these assertions remain present at `6fc1559`.
- **Current-head review (2 November):** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) completed a review of exact head `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36` with no actionable code findings. Patch quality is 4/6; overall readiness and proof remain 2/6 because actual app-entry/install-update behavior, current native execution and released-state upgrade qualification are not established. [Review run 41547046623](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41547046623) completed; this is source review, not execution proof. The generic existing-data checklist does not identify a concrete schema or data-model defect; the bounded upgrade/preservation proof remains outstanding.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.
- **Fixture follow-up:** [Commit `4298606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af) changes exactly two positive Node fixture literals, preserving all assertions, old-runtime controls, and production source. Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. This covers inspection only at the earlier revision, not current signed-app install/update or upgrade behavior. Preceding failed QA attempts do not establish this result.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI and source qualification</summary>

[CI 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816), including native Swift, [macOS Periphery 37194001640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001640), and [shared OpenClawKit Periphery 37194001665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001665) passed at earlier head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. prs.body: Closes #141184 ## What Problem This Solves The iOS chat composer occupies a large fixed footer, preventing messages from flowing behind Liquid Glass. Connection and loading indicators compete with the conversation, and ordinary session actions look destructive. ## Why This Change Was Made Use a compact floating composer with measured trailing transcript space, native menus, and quieter navigation while preserving the existing red/gray palette, typography, attachments, and voice controls. The composer overlays the transcript instead of reducing its viewport. Upstream’s session-bound, one-shot scroll commands handle sending and jumping to the latest reply without retaining row-ID scroll constraints. Shared presentation helpers keep loading and connection chrome consistent. ## User Impact - Messages scroll behind the composer; multiline drafts grow naturally, and the latest reply remains reachable above the input. - Attachments come first in the options menu. Model, effort, context, and permission controls retain their capability restrictions and use catalog-compatible localized labels. - Selected model options remain visible to accessibility. The macOS model menu retains its sign-in action when no models are available. - Ordinary session actions use standard colors; Delete remains destructive. Unread indicators are neutral, and rows announce unread/pinned state. - Overview keeps its toolbar reachable, uses quieter counters, and opens Usage from Tokens. Small sidebar and onboarding controls meet 44-point touch targets. Reduce Motion is respected. - Upstream’s persistent iOS chat owner, gateway switcher, session attention controls, and desktop styling are preserved. ## Evidence October 12 update integrates upstream `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54`, retaining its live-reply deduplication, deferred menus, compact-width avatar treatment, session-bound scroll commands, and operator/node connection distinction. Removed the unused chat-layout parameter reported by shared dead-code CI. The previously blocked keyboard/history flow reproduced on the integrated candidate: after a multiline send, the app consumed a full CPU core in SwiftUI `LazySubviewPlacements`. Ungrouped transcript content now has one stable layout container per lazy-stack child, preserving row IDs and spacing. The unchanged keyboard/history test passes after this repair; assertions were not weakened. Local validation on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.2 with Xcode 27: - 106 iOS tests in six suites pass, including the latest upstream connection/reconnect regressions, sidebar, and typography. - 39 shared chat tests in five suites pass; shared macOS and iOS simulator builds pass. - The full keyboard/history test passes three times after the fix, covering keyboard opening, typing, sending, preserved history position, multiline anchored replies, and jumping back to the latest reply. - Composer/options sizing, restored session history, long-press actions, and Overview/Usage navigation UI tests pass. - Native lint/formatting, localization verification, and `git diff --check` pass (existing test-file length warnings remain). - Interaction proof used layout fix `5fc55fcc218`; the final `66f8e6bb317` integration adds only upstream’s connection-state changes to the native code, validated by the 106-test run. Shared transcript/composer code is identical. No new tests or CI jobs were added; the existing keyboard/history regression supplies the before/after proof. Independent reviews of the full integration and the focused layout repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Hosted CI on the pushed head remains separate from this local evidence. The baseline fixture’s model label was normalized for publication; its layout is unchanged. Physical-device, iPad, largest Dynamic Type, and macOS visual comparisons remain unverified. prs.title: feat(sessions): split deleted archive retention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` previously applied the same age cutoff to both reset and deleted transcript archives. This adds `session.maintenance.deletedArchiveRetention` as an independent duration-or-`false` control.

When omitted, `deletedArchiveRetention` inherits `resetArchiveRetention` for backward compatibility. An explicit duration or `false` overrides it independently. Both settings age archive artifacts; they do not age retained SQLite reset history or transcript rows.

## Implementation

- Resolves independent deleted/reset rules from configuration.
- Applies those rules through legacy file-backed maintenance, cron reaping, and ordinary SQLite maintenance.
- Ordinary SQLite maintenance runs archive cleanup even when no session rows are removed.
- Removes a derived archive file before deleting its published SQLite recovery row; failed file cleanup leaves the recovery row intact.
- Preserves inherited deleted retention for older resolved-maintenance callers while retaining explicit disablement.
- Fences archive-row pruning against maintenance-owner invalidation before and inside each SQLite writer callback.
- Updates schema help, examples, and session-management documentation.

## Evidence
- Exact pushed head: `5460eaf7b0ab2221938f1b7a4dbfc052e69d9588`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused runtime command:
  `pnpm exec vitest run src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-retention.integration.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-writer.test.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.archive-retention.test.ts src/config/sessions/cleanup-service.fix-missing.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
  Result: **4 test files passed, 22 tests passed**.
- The unmocked integration proof loads a real config file and exercises both paths:
  - a fresh configured store is initialized (`configuredFreshStore: true`);
  - an existing configured store is maintained with independent cutoffs (`configuredExistingStore: true`);
  - the expired deleted archive file and its SQLite recovery row are absent after cleanup (`deletedArchiveFile: false`, `deletedArchiveRow: false` — `false` here means absent);
  - the reset archive remains (`resetArchiveFile: true`).
- The focused tests additionally prove inherited retention for older resolved callers, explicit `false` disablement, ordinary SQLite archive cleanup with no session removals, maintenance-owner invalidation without reopening the store, file-before-row deletion ordering, and lifecycle-deletion failure recovery.
- This proof is on the exact pushed head above; no claim is made that it resolves the separate current-base merge conflict or pending maintainer acceptance.
## Known Gate

This change affects persistent retention and upgrade behavior. Maintainer acceptance of the independent retention contract, ordinary-maintenance deletion timing, and the accessor cleanup boundary remains required before merge.

- Jacqueline Henriksen (@jjjhenriksen)

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): queued turn re-compacts a small context when preflight accounting is refused
prs.body:
Related: #140819

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a busy chat session would compact its context again on the very next queued turn, even though the context was far below the compaction budget. Each spurious pass spent minutes summarizing, appended another summary on top of the previous one, blocked the queued message behind the session lane, failed that queued message with `Session changed before compaction maintenance could be recorded`, and surfaced another "Context compacted" card. On one Signal session this repeated four times in fourteen minutes; three of the four ran against a context of roughly 84k, 120k, and 91k tokens against a 252k budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Token-triggered preflight compaction committed the compaction to the transcript inside the queued compactor's session-lane task, but recorded the session-row accounting (count, `totalTokens`, byte latch) only after that task returned and the lane was released. A run waiting on the lane claims the session writer as its first lane write, so the accounting compare-and-swap was correctly refused, the row kept its pre-compaction fresh total, and the next preflight projected pressure from that stale total and compacted again. The queued compactor already exposes a host commit callback that runs while the lane and writer fence are still held; the Codex transcript-byte path used it and the token path did not. This change routes accounting through that callback for every runtime, and supplies the transcript-settled callback for byte-triggered compaction on every runtime so the byte latch keeps measuring the post-maintenance transcript. Nothing about the writer, lifecycle, or session guards changes: a writer that replaces the row before the host commit is still refused, and the after-return path remains only for compactors that emit no host commit.

Non-goals: no retry against a replacement writer, no schema or config change, no change to projection inputs or context limits.

## User Impact

After a preflight compaction, the session's recorded context and compaction count match the transcript, so the following queued turn no longer re-compacts a small context, the queued message is delivered instead of failing, and users stop seeing back-to-back "Context compacted" cards for a session that was not over budget.

## Evidence

- Regression test `lands before a run waiting on the session lane claims the writer` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts`) models the queued-execution contract against a real SQLite session store: successor acceptance and host commit inside the lane, then a replacement writer claim once the compactor returns. Red/green on this head: with the pre-change `agent-runner-memory.ts` from `upstream/main` swapped in, that test fails with `Session changed before compaction maintenance could be recorded` thrown from `recordCompactionAccounting` (1 failed, 125 passed); with the change it passes, the count and `totalTokens` land, the replacement writer's claim is intact, accounting runs exactly once, and the next preflight does not compact again.
- Guard test `does not account against a writer that replaced the row before the host commit` keeps the newer-writer protection on the in-lane path.
- The byte-latch test now runs for both the Codex and the embedded runtime and asserts the persisted latch right after the first compaction equals the settled (post-maintenance) transcript size. The embedded case would fail if the settled-latch callback were supplied only for Codex, because the in-lane host commit measures the pre-maintenance size.
- Focused suites on this head (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`, one invocation): `agent-runner-memory` (126), `session-updates.lifecycle` (17), `compact.queued-successor` (25), `agent-runner-memory.preflight-stale-tokens` (7), `agent-runner-execution-compaction` (14), `commands-compact.lifecycle` (8): 197 passed. `compact.queued-successor` already pins that `onHostCompactionCommitted` is awaited before the checkpoint and maintenance steps.
- Changed-path gate on this head (`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main`): all 29 checks pass, including `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and `oxfmt` on the changed files, the max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets, dead-export scan, and import-cycle check; `git diff --check` is clean. A second red check confirms the byte-latch asymmetry: with the settled-latch callback supplied only for Codex, the embedded case fails (`activeBytes` 314 persisted instead of the settled 186).
- Production correlation (sanitized, from the reporter's gateway): each refused accounting was preceded by `lane wait exceeded` on the same session lane 50 to 330 ms before the accounting error, and the one compaction with no lane waiter recorded its accounting normally. Effective harness was `openclaw`; the model route was an OpenAI subscription Responses route.
- Independent review: repository `autoreview` helper on the Claude engine (`claude-fable-5-1`, xhigh), branch mode against `upstream/main`, P2 threshold: `scoped-clean`, no findings. An earlier Codex-engine autoreview of the pre-amend commit (P1 threshold) and an adversarial read-only concurrency review of the diff and tests were also clean at P0/P1; that review's P2 notes (byte-latch timing on non-Codex byte triggers, comment precision, two test-fidelity cleanups) are addressed in this head.

Known gap: this is a source-only repair validated with focused tests; it has not been applied to a live Gateway. The branch includes a merge of current `upstream/main`; upstream did not touch the changed files.

prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The latest exact-head review found media pre-download omitted configured participant mentions. This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.
- Telegram command-gate and ingress-supersede tests: **26/26 passed**, including bare `/steer`, `/steer@bot`, other-bot addressing, DM, always-active group, and pre-adoption cancellation cases.
- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.
- Worker-backed Plugin SDK session read: the focused `session-store-runtime` read test passed. This replaces the new synchronous SQLite lookup flagged in the first PR review.
- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.
- An isolated exact-head `check:changed` run passed the branch-owned gates, including formatting, policy ratchets, Plugin SDK exports/surface budget, plugin boundaries, core typecheck, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, extension and extension-test typechecks, and script typecheck. The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. The third failure is the aggregate gate reflecting those two. No branch-caused hosted failure was found.
- Repository-supported Crabline Telegram integration proof passed on the exact PR tree: the real Telegram plugin and an ephemeral Gateway ran against a local Bot API transport with a mock provider. In a mention-gated group, bare `/status` and `/steer` produced no outbound reply, zero provider requests, and no session mutation; `/status@crabline_bot` was admitted; another-bot addressing stayed quiet. Bare DM `/status` and bare `/status` in an always-active group remained admitted. This is transport-emulated integration evidence, not Telegram Test Server/TDLib proof.
- Real Telegram Test Server behavior proof is still pending. The exact-head repository doctor was attempted, but no existing Convex launcher could authenticate and no QA broker environment pair was available, so it stopped before acquiring a credential or starting a Gateway. A maintainer/credential-owner run of the group-capable `telegram-e2e-userbot` route is required; the automatic DM-only Mantis plan cannot prove this group-policy change. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

## Review focus

Please confirm that making effective group/topic `mention` activation authoritative for commands is the desired compatibility contract, and review the one-function public Plugin SDK expansion required for the nonblocking session read. The patch keeps bare commands in DMs and `always` groups, and gates the early cancellation paths so an ignored command cannot still interrupt pending work.

prs.title: fix(android): keep realtime Talk alive through slow audio acknowledgments
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182602

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android realtime Talk over the Gateway relay ends with "Talk failed: request timeout" when the Gateway's answer to one audio append takes longer than 8 seconds, on the phone and through a paired Watch.

## User Impact

User impact: a short network stall or a busy Gateway no longer ends an Android realtime Talk call. Audio past about three seconds in flight is dropped, Talk says "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part", and "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" once the Gateway catches up. A paired Watch shows its own shorter text ("Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part.", "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part.") in place of the elapsed time; each notice stays until the next Talk state change, as on the phone. Talk still ends on an explicit Gateway error, a lost connection, or an append left unanswered for 30 seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser relay and the Apple apps already follow this contract (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155839, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572, `docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md`); https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 did not reach Android. Both Android relays sent every frame with an 8 second deadline, no limit on audio in flight, and ended Talk on the first timeout.

A small `RealtimeInputAudioBudget` owns the three-second budget and the two notices, and both relays use it: the phone's append loop in `TalkModeManager` and the Watch relay in `WearRealtimeTalkController`. To release audio from the budget when the Gateway answers, `GatewaySession.sendRequestFrameForEndpoint` gains an optional success callback, and the Watch relay's send callback now reports success as well as errors. The append deadline is the 30 second liveness limit from the same contract. The Watch shows the notices from its own strings: the relay's snapshot gains an optional `notice` field (older watches ignore it), and the Watch Talk screen shows it in place of "Listening · 0:00" while listening. The notices are registered for translation; the docs page now says Android follows the same budget.

Trade-off: a Gateway that keeps the socket open but stops answering is now noticed after 30 seconds instead of 8, as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 states for the Apple apps.

## Evidence

Tested at `170d5c59956` (base `upstream/main` `315fba74e12`). The Before/After runs below used a build of an earlier revision of this branch with the same phone-side code; the stall run was repeated on a build of this head (see "Re-run at this head").

Real app: the Android app (play debug build of each side) on an Android 16 emulator, paired with an isolated Gateway (empty state directory, loopback port, no outside traffic) whose realtime Talk provider is a local fake that only counts audio. The Gateway is an older source build (2026.9.6, `19afe35954`) on both sides; the bug and the fix are in the Android client. A local WebSocket proxy between the app and the Gateway sets the answer delay: while a stall is on, it holds each `talk.session.appendAudio` answer for a fixed time and logs every 50th held answer as `hold`. Same steps on both sides: open the chat, start realtime Talk, let audio flow, turn the stall on.

Proxy lines are UTC; logcat lines are the emulator's local time (UTC+9), whose clock runs about 1.06 s behind the proxy's. On the proxy clock, Talk closes 8.0 s after the stall starts on the base and 30.0 s after it in the 40 second run.

Before (base, 12 second stall per answer):

```text
11:58:35.244Z req   talk.session.create
12:00:20.447Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
12:00:25.441Z hold  held=51  stallMs=12000      (every frame still sent)
21:00:27.401 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:00:28.448Z req   talk.session.close
screen: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"
```

After (this PR, same stall):

```text
12:17:39.337Z req   talk.session.create
12:17:48.405Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" (held answers start coming back, about 12 s in)
(stall turned off by the operator at about 12.7 s, not logged)
12:18:03.915Z append appends=151
12:18:13.912Z append appends=251
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat, Talk stays on

40 second stall per answer:
12:19:02.948Z hold  held=1   stallMs=40000
21:19:31.897 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:19:32.953Z req   talk.session.close
```

![Before: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/before.png)
![After: "Realtime audio input fell behind" notice during the stall](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-fell-behind.png)
![After: "Microphone input recovered" notice, Talk still on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-recovered.png)

Re-run at this head (`170d5c59956`, same Gateway, fake provider and proxy, each held answer delayed 12 s; screenshot times are the host clock, which matches the proxy's):

```text
13:14:31.185Z req    talk.session.create
13:14:44.146Z hold   held=1   stallMs=12000
13:15:01.746Z append appends=301
13:15:08      screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
13:15:15.876Z append appends=351      (14.1 s for 50 appends instead of 5 s: frames past the budget were dropped, not sent)
13:15:16      screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part", Talk still on
13:15:20.854Z append appends=401
...
13:17:30.856Z append appends=1701
13:17:57.360Z close  who=client code=1006 appends=1952 held=31   (held: running count of held answers; the operator closed the app)
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat
```

Watch display (rendered by `WearVoiceLayoutTest` under Robolectric, round 192 dp, not on a watch): before this commit the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" while the relay reports the notice; now it shows each notice.

![Watch before: "Listening · 0:00" while input fell behind](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-before.png)
![Watch after: "Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-fell-behind.png)
![Watch after: "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-recovered.png)

Mixed versions with the latest stable (`v2026.10.9`, `8b18b5578f6`): the new `notice` field crosses the phone-Watch protocol in both directions while one side still runs the stable release. A throwaway JUnit test (not committed) ran in `:wear-shared` of each tree and passed the real encoded bytes between them: this head's `WearProtocolCodec.encode` of a Talk event with each notice, decoded by the stable `WearProtocolCodec.decode` and `WearRealtimeTalkCodec.decode`, and the stable encoding of a listening event decoded by this head.

```text
head wrote    {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"notice":"INPUT_FELL_BEHIND"}}
stable read   WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(attemptId=attempt-1, active=true, listening=true, speaking=false, status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[])
stable read   (same for INPUT_RECOVERED)
stable wrote  {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"conversation":[]}}
head read     WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(..., status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[], notice=null)
```

An updated phone with a stable Watch keeps Talk working and the Watch shows its usual status text; a stable phone with an updated Watch sends no notice and the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" as before. In the stable release both codecs already share `WearProtocolCodec.json`, which sets `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` and `explicitNulls = false`.

Upgrade from v2026.10.9 (same emulator, same isolated Gateway and proxy, no stall): the stable play debug build was installed on a wiped Android 16 emulator, paired with the Gateway (operator and node approved), and the Talk speaker set to "Muted" in Voice settings. This head's build was then installed over it with `adb install -r` (no uninstall; both builds are version code 2026080201, `firstInstallTime` unchanged, `lastUpdateTime` changed).

```text
14:57:11.572Z close  who=client code=1006   (the install stops the stable app)
14:57:14.909Z req    connect                (same device ID, no pairing request, no onboarding)
screen: Overview with Gateway "Online"; Voice settings still show "Enable speaker · Muted"
14:57:44.825Z req    talk.session.create
14:58:05.492Z append appends=201            (Talk "Listening")
```

After the upgrade the Overview's Nodes row shows "Review node access" instead of "1 online": `openclaw nodes list` on the same Gateway shows the node in `pending-reapproval` with the same 7 caps and 14 commands as approved and one changed permission, `microphone` false to true, because the microphone was granted after the node was approved and 14:57:14 was the first reconnect since; the stable build, installed back over this head, reconnects into the same `pending-reapproval` and shows the same row, so it does not come from this change.

Observed result: on the base, Talk ends 8 seconds into the stall; with this PR it drops audio past the budget with the notice, recovers when the answers arrive, and ends only after an append is unanswered for 30 seconds.

Regression tests: `TalkModeManagerTest.stalledAppendsDropInputPastThreeSecondsWithoutEndingTalk` feeds 31 frames while every append is unanswered, expects 30 appends, the fell-behind notice and Talk still on, then answers one append and expects the recovered notice and the next frame sent. It fails on the base (the 31st frame is sent) and passes with this PR. `WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest` has the same case for the Watch relay and also asserts the 30 second deadline on every append, which pins the deadline constant both relays share; it changes the relay's callback type, so it does not compile on the base. It also asserts the notice the relay sends to the Watch. `WearVoiceLayoutTest` has two new listening cases with each notice; they fail with the previous Watch screen code (the notice text is not on screen) and pass with this PR, and they check the text fits the round screen at font scale 1 and 1.3 in English and in the German locale (which shows the English text until the native locale refresh adds the translation).

Checks at this head: `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.wear.*' --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.gateway.*' :wear:testDebugUnitTest :wear-shared:testDebugUnitTest :wear:lintDebug` (848 tests, 0 failures); `:app`, `:benchmark`, `:wear` and `:wear-shared` `ktlintCheck`; `node scripts/check-native-state-schema-version.mjs`; `pnpm native:i18n:verify`; `git diff --check`. `TalkModeManagerTest` was run again on the base with the test file carried over: the new test times out at 31 appends there, and the other 111 tests pass on both sides. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

CI: the previous head failed `preflight` with "Native generated locale artifacts must be isolated from source changes", and `openclaw/ci-gate` failed because of it. That head carried English placeholders in 21 Watch `values-*/strings.xml` files. This head leaves those files unchanged, so the native locale refresh workflow fills them. `node scripts/ci-changed-scope.mjs --base 315fba74e12` exits 1 with that message on the previous head and exits 0 on this one.

CI at this head ([run 41094221772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772)): `preflight`, `android-test-play`, `android-test-third-party`, `android-test-wear`, `android-ktlint` and `android-access-native (16384, google_apis_ps16k)` passed. `android-access-native (4096, google_apis)` [failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772/job/124196671436) while installing the Android Emulator, before the emulator started or any test ran: `sdkmanager` reported "Error reading Zip content from a SeekableByteChannel" while preparing the Android Emulator package, and the job uploaded no test results. `openclaw/ci-gate` is red only because of that job. The same job passed on main in [run 41123124777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41123124777/job/124295092007) (that run is red for unrelated Node and UI jobs). That job has not passed on this head; it needs a rerun.

The CI seconds below come from the JUnit reports of `android-test-play` (phone files) and `android-test-wear` (Watch file). CI tests the PR merged into main, where `TalkModeManagerTest` has 113 tests.

| Test file | Local wall (Gradle, this head) | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManagerTest.kt` | 0.84 s for the new test (file 17.8 s, 112 tests, Gradle `--max-workers=4` with other modules running) | 0.77 s for the new test (file 14.8 s, 113 tests) |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/wear/WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest.kt` | 0.16 s for the new test (file 1.1 s, 26 tests) | 0.01 s for the new test (file 0.38 s, 26 tests) |
| `apps/android/wear/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/wear/WearVoiceLayoutTest.kt` | two more cases in the existing layout loop (file 7.9 s, 12 tests) | file 4.5 s, 12 tests |

Simplify pass: no change. One budget type serves both relays instead of two copies of the policy, and each new test covers a different relay. Against the merge base: production +147/−15 lines, tests +135/−6, docs +2, Watch English strings +2, translation source +4.

Not covered: no real phone and no real Watch. The phone runs used the Android 16 emulator. No Wear OS device is available, and no Wear OS emulator image is installed; pairing an emulator also needs the Play Store companion app and a Google sign-in. So there are no Watch screenshots or recordings with transport logs from a live call. The phone-side Watch relay is proven by its unit test, the Watch screen by Robolectric renders, and the phone-Watch payload against the latest stable by the codec run above. The device runs used an older Gateway build (see above); the change is client-only. Non-English locales show the English notices on both the phone and the Watch until the native locale refresh translates them.

Follow-up: the microphone transcription stream (`NodeRuntime` `appendTranscriptionAudio`, used by `MicCaptureManager`) also sends `talk.session.appendAudio` with an 8 second deadline. It is a separate feature outside the realtime Talk contract, so it is left for its own change.

prs.title: fix(matrix): stop treating unnamed two-member rooms as DMs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Before the Matrix `m.direct` cache has loaded, an unnamed room with exactly two members is classified as a direct message. Ingress no longer does that. A room is still a direct message when `is_direct` is set, when the room is stored in `m.direct`, when a recent invite was promoted, or when opted-in per-room recovery allows it.

## Evidence

On commit `567572f5adc51a` the direct-room tracker refuses an unnamed two-member room before the cache seeds, and it still accepts `is_direct` and `m.direct`. The QA harness sets the Matrix wildcard group to accept a reply without a mention, because those smoke rooms are groups now.

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/direct.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "does not treat an exact 2-member|still trusts is_direct|binds Matrix"
 ✓ createDirectRoomTracker > does not treat an exact 2-member room as a DM before the dm cache seeds 24ms
 ✓ createDirectRoomTracker > still trusts is_direct and m.direct before the dm cache seeds 1ms
 ✓ crabline transport > binds Matrix config and normalizes transport targets 3065ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 10.89s
```

QA smoke profile 6, which includes `matrix-restart-resume` and `matrix-restart-replay-dedupe`, passed on this head in CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41541733549/job/125608393398

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** An unnamed two-member Matrix room is not a direct message only because the direct-room cache has not seeded. Explicit direct signals still are.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin 27.0.0 arm64, Node v26.12.1, worktree at `567572f5adc51a` on `fix/matrix-dm-two-member-fallback`.

prs.title: fix(codex): forward-port 2026.10.10 thread ownership and cleanup fixes
prs.body:
## Problem

The 2026.10.10 stable release fixed Codex thread ownership and native follow-up failures that were missing from main. A freshly forked child could fail its first turn with an active-writer error; a resumed thread could race its previous owner; a later parent turn could no longer resolve a native child by task name. Short shutdown budgets also converted healthy loaded cleanup into failure.

## Solution

Keep this existing PR for the Codex portion of the original forward-port batch. All sibling splits target main independently; this is not a stack.

- Unload a canonical fork before its child turn connection resumes it.
- Wait for a live previous owner's unload before another client resumes the same thread.
- Preserve bounded loaded one-shot cleanup and match Codex's 10-second unload confirmation window.
- Retain canonical native child paths across parent registrations and name usable agent IDs for unidentified targets.

Preserves the six original Codex forward-port commits and release references. Fresh local review also caught a defect in the inherited one-shot change: shared retirement started shutdown before its longer grace options were applied. The repair now applies those options at the first close; the operation lives with the existing shared-client lifecycle owner. A deterministic fake-clock regression fails before this repair because containment starts before the delayed clean exit. The exact scoped test-line allocation is 295 lines for fork handoff, native targeting, previous-owner handoff, and shutdown-budget regressions. Simplification review kept these ownership fixes together; unrelated Matrix, process, storage, cron, config, startup, and file-transfer changes moved out.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` and targeted oxfmt checks passed.
- Red proof for shared cleanup: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-shutdown.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — the new grace regression failed as expected; 3 existing tests passed.
- Fresh targeted lint and extension typecheck were attempted after a successful isolated frozen install. Both are blocked by an unchanged main error: `src/agents/mcp-metadata.ts:5` imports `McpCatalogTool` from a module that does not export it, with consequent optional-property errors in `agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts`. All three source files are byte-identical to base 34007820fa2cc4b5a7a9b9bdc2047aafed41ab1c.
- Fresh cleanup validation: shared-client/client-shutdown 162/162 and one-shot cleanup 11/11 passed. Final local ClawSweeper reviewed `34007820fa2c..f00f4d2e7b58`: no actionable correctness or security findings; prior shutdown-grace finding resolved.
- Fresh focused validation: all 336 tests passed across 6 files / 3 Vitest shards (814.57s including worker compilation): native-subagent inventory, native thread handoff, thread binding, run-attempt, canonical-descendant integration, and Gateway Codex failure recovery.

Prior combined-PR evidence: canonical-descendant 65/65; native-subagent 141; binding 100/100; codex-failure-recovery 7/7; handoff.native 2/2. The original regressions were confirmed failing without the corresponding changes, except the one-shot cleanup budget (the delayed-exit fixture was flaky and nondiscriminating, so no such test is claimed).

Codex shutdown contract checked against sibling source commit 092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d; the per-thread unload-delay override was also verified against pinned rust-v0.164.0 (6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9): `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs` waits for shutdown and only emits `thread/closed` after cleanup, reporting shutdown as slow after 10 seconds.

Known limitation retained from the original PR: the retired native child-path index is not pruned. Broad CI and live authenticated Codex/MCP qualification are not claimed by local fixture tests.

prs.title: improve(ios): compare screenshot capture without Shortcuts indexing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Screenshot capture can compete with first-boot Shortcuts indexing on fresh iOS simulators. This experiment measures whether removing that unrelated work improves the existing complete screenshot job.

## User Impact

No default behavior changes. A temporary, opt-in `shortcuts_probe` input applies only to the screenshot-only job. Release uploads and qualification stay stock, and Watch capture stays unchanged. The probe has no upload or signing step.

## Why This Change Was Made

A fresh local iOS 27 simulator reproduced `BackgroundShortcutRunner` startup activity. Its launchd service lives in `siriactionsd`'s process domain; its sampled stacks resolve Shortcuts action metadata. Disabling and booting out only the simulator's `user/foreground/com.apple.siriactionsd` stopped its worker. Asset download, keyboard, accessibility, and web services remain enabled. The override disappears when the existing lane deletes its disposable simulator.

## Evidence

Local boundary probe: the service became disabled and unloaded, its worker exited, and the task-owned simulator was shut down and deleted. This establishes the control's scope, not a screenshot speedup or a repair for earlier intermittent screenshot failures.

### Measurement rule, recorded before hosted measurements

- Workload: the committed `pnpm ios:screenshots` entry point, all four iPhone tests, all four iPad tests, and Watch capture. Same pushed source SHA and `xcode-27-xlarge` runner label for both arms. `startup_probe=false`, resource diagnostics enabled, fresh simulators and fresh compilation; normal download-cache restoration remains enabled and its hits are recorded.
- A: `shortcuts_probe=false`. B: `shortcuts_probe=true`. Run serially in alternating A/B order, starting with one pilot pair. Stop on a behavioral regression or an unpromising candidate; otherwise collect five runs per arm before making any default recommendation.
- Primary metric: the complete screenshot job's elapsed time, including setup, native build, simulator preparation, all captures, cleanup, and evidence upload. Secondary metrics: capture-command elapsed time, per-device boot/preparation/capture durations, worker CPU observations and host load from the existing resource timeline. Report medians, nearest-rank p95, and min/max; retain failures separately rather than dropping them from reliability results.
- Acceptance: at least 5% lower median complete-job time, no increase in its p95, no regression in per-device capture medians/p95, and all nine screenshots visually correct. All eight XCTest cases must pass once without retries in each run; Watch must pass. A 20% regression in any user-facing metric stops acceptance and requires investigation. Incomplete process samples do not establish that background work disappeared.
- This PR remains experimental until those criteria are met. A passing replay does not prove the prior intermittent chat failure fixed. If the experiment has no measurable benefit, remove it instead of promoting it.

Local validation: Ruby syntax, workflow validation, formatting, focused lint and the tooling test typecheck passed. All 11 required macOS workflow/native contract files passed across the initial run and a focused rerun after completing this isolated checkout's workspace dependencies (1,187 unique passing tests, 10 existing platform skips). The changed Fastlane file's 16 tests took 0.91s; the production screenshot-lifecycle fixture took 0.55s. Hosted CI seconds remain pending.

The new 25 test lines extend that existing lifecycle fixture to cover default-off behavior, both disposable iOS devices, Watch exclusion, and cleanup on preparation failure; the separate allocation grants exactly 25 lines. The line ratchet still fails on inherited debt: base total/ceiling 6,444,088/6,444,035; candidate 6,444,113/6,444,060. Both are 53 lines over. The shared scalar and unrelated tests are unchanged.

An independent pre-commit P1 review found no high-priority defects. Local ClawSweeper completed its full committed-range review of `206d54934a3d0764cad0ea59a31d43f74bec0fa0..77c9abced3397ba06ff3299bbcc3289c67c9383b`: patch correct, no actionable correctness or security findings. It was a source-only review; hosted measurements remain pending.


### Hosted pilot results and decision

The pilot is complete. Closing this experiment without merging: the candidate did not show a useful complete-job improvement, so the predeclared stopping rule does not justify the larger five-per-arm campaign. Default screenshots, release uploads, and qualification remain unchanged.

Both runs used source `77c9abced3397ba06ff3299bbcc3289c67c9383b`, `xcode-27-xlarge`, Xcode 27.1 build 27A9275, the same iOS/watchOS 27.0 runtime selection, five reported CPUs, and 14 GiB reported memory. Both restored the identical Watch RTC cache, verified one native RTC hit, and missed the identical Swift package cache key. Resource diagnostics were enabled and the startup probe was off. Qualification and upload jobs were skipped in both runs.

| Metric | A1: stock | B1: Shortcuts disabled | B1 versus A1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Complete screenshot job | 963s (16m03s) | 1,013s (16m53s) | +5.19% |
| Build/capture workflow step | 830s | 884s | +6.51% |
| Native build | 186.66s | 207.53s | +11.18% |
| Shortcuts preparation, both devices | 0s | 53.33s | Added overhead |
| iPhone capture | 164.71s | 163.02s | -1.03% |
| iPad capture | 199.55s | 164.62s | -17.50% |
| Watch capture (unchanged implementation) | 31.91s | 27.59s | -13.54% |

- A1: [baseline run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41736619045). Artifact: `ios-screenshots-41736619045-1`.
- B1: [candidate run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41739002757). Artifact: `ios-screenshots-41739002757-1`.
- Both runs passed all eight XCTest cases exactly once, without capture retries; Watch capture passed. All nine screenshots from each run were visually inspected and show the expected content. All recorded shutdown/deletion phases passed.
- The service-control commands succeeded for both disposable iOS devices. They took 7.49s on iPhone and 45.84s on iPad. The iPad `disable` call alone took about 32s; `bootout` and command overhead account for the remainder. This preparation cost exceeds the combined observed iPhone/iPad capture saving of 36.62s.
- The CPU-idle median during both iPhone and iPad capture remained 0% in both arms. Memory pressure stayed normal and observed swap-outs stayed zero. Shortcuts suppression did not establish relief from the overall contention; other simulator work remained active.
- Candidate boot durations, before applying the control, increased 23.70% on iPhone and 21.04% on iPad. iPad status-bar setup increased from 9.68s to 18.20s. These exceed the predeclared 20% investigation threshold. The separate native build also increased 20.87s, and unchanged Watch capture improved. This demonstrates run-to-run variation: the pilot cannot attribute the complete 50s increase solely to the control.

This is **one run per arm**, not a reliable median/p95 comparison or proof that the control always slows capture. There is no measured end-to-end benefit supporting a default change. No earlier intermittent screenshot failure is claimed fixed.

The hosted review correctly identified a diagnostic limitation: `shortcuts-disable` was not registered in the resource collector's phase allowlist. Samples during preparation therefore appear as `other`. The separate Fastlane diagnostics retain the exact per-device preparation durations used above; complete-job timings are unaffected. The experiment is being retired rather than expanding its implementation. Process sampling was sparse and sometimes timed out, so missing worker names are not evidence that a worker exited on the hosted runner.

prs.title: fix(agents): stop retaining completed tool calls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained completed tool calls when a tool leaves an async resource or captured async scope alive after execution.

## User Impact

Completed tool-call context can be collected while background resources continue. This removes a confirmed retention edge in the Team heap regression window; it does not establish that this edge explains the entire observed production heap plateau.

## Why This Change Was Made

The skill-usage recorder added in #191661 closes over a callback that captures the executing call's context. Closing it only changed a boolean. Clear that callback on close instead, preserving active skill attribution and refusal of late attribution.

The existing plugin skill-usage integration test now drains queued diagnostics before tracker cleanup, retains an async snapshot, and checks that the completed call context is collected and late recording still returns false. Fixture reuse keeps regression-test growth at **0 lines**; production growth is **+1 line**. No configuration, schema, durable retention, or public API change.

## Evidence

A focused offline Node probe runs the real `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` path with `--expose-gc`: 16 completed calls, each with a synthetic 512 KiB call-context payload and an independently retained timer. After event-loop turns and forced GC:

| Source | Payloads retained | Retained heap delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Base | 16/16 | +8,695,488 bytes |
| Fix | 0/16 | +240,344 bytes |

The narrower production-recorder probe changes from 16/16 retained (+8,449,152 bytes) to 0/16 (+57,992 bytes). A separate 16-iteration GC-diagnostic subscription probe stays below 60 KiB growth. These synthetic measurements prove the ownership defect; they do not measure production savings.

Focused two-file lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and Codex-backed autoreview pass (no actionable P0–P2 findings). The final-head integration regression [passes on Bun in 421 ms](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41736512183/job/126267851700), including persistence, collection, and late-call refusal. The [final-head CI run completed successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41736512183), with 38 jobs passed and 30 plan skips; `build-artifacts` is skipped by the scope plan. Testbox queued and the task-owned request was stopped; no local broad-test fallback. No production Gateway RPC, profile, signal, state change, or deployment was performed.

Completed tool-call context can be collected while background resources continue. This removes a confirmed retention edge in the Team heap regression window; it does not establish that this edge explains the entire observed production heap plateau.

## Why This Change Was Made

The skill-usage recorder added in #191661 closes over a callback that captures the executing call's context. Closing it only changed a boolean. Clear that callback on close instead, preserving active skill attribution and refusal of late attribution.

The existing plugin skill-usage integration test now drains queued diagnostics before tracker cleanup, retains an async snapshot, and checks that the completed call context is collected and late recording still returns false. Fixture reuse keeps regression-test growth at **0 lines**; production growth is **+1 line**. No configuration, schema, durable retention, or public API change.

## Evidence

A focused offline Node probe runs the real `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` path with `--expose-gc`: 16 completed calls, each with a synthetic 512 KiB call-context payload and an independently retained timer. After event-loop turns and forced GC:

| Source | Payloads retained | Retained heap delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Base | 16/16 | +8,695,488 bytes |
| Fix | 0/16 | +240,344 bytes |

The narrower production-recorder probe changes from 16/16 retained (+8,449,152 bytes) to 0/16 (+57,992 bytes). A separate 16-iteration GC-diagnostic subscription probe stays below 60 KiB growth. These synthetic measurements prove the ownership defect; they do not measure production savings.

Focused two-file lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and Codex-backed autoreview pass (no actionable P0–P2 findings). The final-head integration regression [passes on Bun in 421 ms](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41736512183/job/126267851700), including persistence, collection, and late-call refusal. Remaining selected CI gates are pending; `build-artifacts` is skipped by the scope plan. Testbox queued and the task-owned request was stopped; no local broad-test fallback. No production Gateway RPC, profile, signal, state change, or deployment was performed.
