prs.title: fix(auth): remove provider credentials from their owning stores
prs.body:
Related: #127543

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `infer model auth logout --provider` reports saved credentials removed while shared credentials remain available to the selected agent.

## User Impact

User impact: provider logout removes the selected saved credential generations from their physical owners, including an inherited shared credential, and reports the actual removal inventory. Unrelated providers and independent replacement credentials retain the existing cleanup guarantees. No configuration or stored-format migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The infer command maintained a separate deletion loop over a merged runtime view but only updated the local store. It now uses the existing credential-removal owner, with persisted IDs as owner-discovery hints and provider-wide selection under the canonical cleanup path. Gateway logout also takes its receipt from that owner rather than an earlier profile read. The single-profile and API-key paths retain their existing requested-ID receipt semantics.

## Evidence

Base: `6b06549c3e0041eca6046c0e2568cc62cbf75dbf` → candidate: `be58ec9c42e4a93979235f1736a8e167d4715866`.

Real executable before/after runs used separately seeded temporary state, an explicit main/child agent roster, Node 24.22.2, synthetic credentials, and a secretless container with networking disabled. The base executable was built from clean base source before the production edits. The candidate executable was built from the final validated tree. It was built before the commit, so the embedded version still names the base commit. The repository's canonical build-input fingerprint was checked after committing and matches the actual artifact, tying these captures to the reviewed code:

```json
{"head":"be58ec9c42e4a93979235f1736a8e167d4715866","builtFromCommit":"6b06549c3e0041eca6046c0e2568cc62cbf75dbf","currentInputSignature":"3997fc4d492ba0628d7a96f3cf3dc217de97e616744f977f7a21cfcab9af1e8f","builtInputSignature":"3997fc4d492ba0628d7a96f3cf3dc217de97e616744f977f7a21cfcab9af1e8f","inputsMatch":true}
```
 Each persisted-state read below ran in a separate Node process through `loadAuthProfileStoreForRuntimeAsync(agentDir, { readOnly: true, allowKeychainPrompt: false })`, rather than trusting the logout receipt.


<details>
<summary>Fixture configuration and environment</summary>

Each run uses its own temporary directory. These are the actual environment selections, with the temporary directory name normalized:

```sh
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PROOF_STATE"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$PROOF_STATE/openclaw.json"
export OPENCLAW_HOME="$PROOF_STATE"
export NO_COLOR=1
```

The config below is written before seeding; `PROOF_STATE` represents that run's absolute temporary directory, and its `workspace` directory is created first:

```json
{
  "gateway": {
    "mode": "local"
  },
  "plugins": {
    "slots": {
      "memory": "none"
    }
  },
  "agents": {
    "ownership": "explicit",
    "entries": {
      "main": {},
      "child": {}
    },
    "defaults": {
      "workspace": "PROOF_STATE/workspace",
      "systemAgent": {
        "agentId": "main"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The SDK seeding and read processes import the freshly built `dist/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.js`. Reads print only profile IDs; no credential value is published.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Real CLI proof: a main agent with local and shared saved credentials</summary>

The SDK fixture seeds `openai:shared` and `anthropic:control` with `upsertAuthProfileAsync` through the main agent, then seeds `openai:local` in that agent's local store with `updateAuthProfileStoreWithLock`. Both versions begin with the following separate-read stdout:

```json
{"profileIds":["openai:local","openai:shared","anthropic:control"]}
```

Actual command on both versions:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs infer model auth logout --provider openai --agent main --json
```

Base logout stdout (exit 0):

```json
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "removedProfiles": [
    "openai:local",
    "openai:shared"
  ]
}
```

Base subsequent persisted/runtime read stdout (exit 0):

```json
{"profileIds":["openai:shared","anthropic:control"]}
```

Candidate logout stdout (exit 0):

```json
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "removedProfiles": [
    "openai:shared",
    "openai:local"
  ]
}
```

Candidate subsequent persisted/runtime read stdout (exit 0):

```json
{"profileIds":["anthropic:control"]}
```

The base runner exits 1 after explicitly confirming the false-success defect. The candidate runner exits 0 after asserting the exact removal receipt, absence of saved OpenAI profiles, and preservation of the unrelated Anthropic control.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Real CLI proof: a child agent with only an inherited shared credential</summary>

No child-local credential is seeded. Initial separate-read stdout:

```json
{"profileIds":["openai:shared","anthropic:control"]}
```

Actual command on both versions:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs infer model auth logout --provider openai --agent child --json
```

Base logout stdout (exit 0):

```json
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "removedProfiles": [
    "openai:shared"
  ]
}
```

Base subsequent persisted/runtime read stdout (exit 0):

```json
{"profileIds":["openai:shared","anthropic:control"]}
```

Candidate logout stdout (exit 0):

```json
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "removedProfiles": [
    "openai:shared"
  ]
}
```

Candidate subsequent persisted/runtime read stdout (exit 0):

```json
{"profileIds":["anthropic:control"]}
```

The base runner exits 1 on the reproduced defect; the candidate runner exits 0.

</details>

The new Gateway regression writes an additional real saved profile between the handler's pre-read and canonical removal. On the base it fails because the receipt omits `openai:concurrent` (8 existing cases pass); on the candidate it verifies both the fresh receipt and actual persisted cleanup. The full infer CLI concurrent-lock timing from #127543 was not reproduced on this base, so this PR uses `Related` rather than claiming that entire reported timing issue is proven fixed.

Validation: 215 tests passed across the five focused files (`auth-logout`, `auth-api-key`, capability CLI, Gateway auth status, and OAuth peer settlement), in four serial Vitest shards (785.07s including cold transforms). This covers existing targeted/API-key cleanup, authority and rollback behavior, peer replacement, and the touched consumers. Core types, all three changed test type graphs, touched-file lint/format, source/test line ratchets, `git diff --check`, fresh executable build, and both real CLI runtime checks passed. The +15 net test lines have an explicit allocation for the real persisted-owner regression and receipt/warning/error contracts; production code shrinks by 19 lines.

Local review: the final committed seven-file full diff was reviewed in one autoreview pass (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning, default P0 reporting scope), with no accepted/actionable findings. A separate owner-boundary review and lead inspection also found no remaining issues. This records the actual review scope; it does not claim review coverage of every lower-severity concern.

Proof boundary: these runs prove saved synthetic credential removal and persisted-state visibility. External provider revocation, live key validity, and refreshing an already-running live Gateway were not exercised. No SDK contract, stored format, schema, or migration changes are introduced.

prs.title: fix(models): skip JSONC scans for strict catalogs
prs.body:
## What problem does this PR solve?

Catalog loading normalizes comments and trailing commas with two full regex passes even when the producer emitted strict JSON. Both passes visit every quoted key and string, allocating temporary regex results before the native parser runs. This repeats when catalog workers refresh their registries.

## User impact

Generated catalogs and authored strict-JSON catalogs can use native parsing directly. Authored JSONC retains the existing normalization and final error diagnostic. No new cache, retained representation, setting, or catalog format is introduced.

## Why this approach?

The shared parser owns the redundant work, so its four callers keep their existing validation, malformed-generated-catalog isolation, and doctor behavior. Production delta: +9 lines; the two normalization passes remain only on the JSONC path.

The regression fixtures extend existing registry tests for JSON/JSONC string fidelity and forked metadata, plus authored-error provenance and generated-catalog isolation. The separate 40-line test allocation covers exactly that net growth; the shared budget is unchanged.

## Evidence

- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41442309126) passed for `db78a650b7b03543db1f834ba6f9c176e6270319`: production/test types, lint, baseline ratchets, changed Node suites, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. Logs confirm 95 passing tests across registry (36), invalid-cost handling (14), credential migration (18), plugin-catalog migration (26), and stale-reference JSONC repair (1). The changed registry file took 18.37s in Vitest and 21.18s for its CI command; these are file costs, not total CI billing.
- Independent autoreview covered P0–P2 on baseline `86dea7b503700634179e67028b97d2eeee801009` through this head: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper had unrelated checkout state, so the documented fallback was used. [Hosted ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191078#issuecomment-6577121661) reviewed the same head without actionable code findings; its requested paired comparison is now reported below.
- Dependency-free parser parity on Node 26.12.1: 11 strict JSON, JSONC, malformed, unsupported-syntax, duplicate-key, and primitive fixtures matched baseline values and diagnostics. JSONC timing was not measured.
- [Compiled comparison run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41564292091): Blacksmith Testbox; both full builds passed, all 22 launches succeeded, wrapper exit 0 with settled children. The task-owned Testbox was stopped and reported completed. Native lease cleanup can cancel the linked Actions job after successful payload completion.
- Linux Node 24.22.1, four observed CPUs, 15.419 GiB RAM; requested label was 16-class. Per-run one-minute host load was 1.73–2.25. Independent frozen installs used identical dependency-input hash `b354dcbaf10f65858635172b5615b132a4824d3c8f206df7e8398f9745852fae`.
- Baseline build commit `86dea7b503700634179e67028b97d2eeee801009`; candidate transport commit `3dba2a2cf5d130a25065332ac10b703352dcb8b8`, whose tree `b77fb81e801263683bcf33db2d4ff37045b4dffe` exactly matches the reviewed source head. Both build-info commits were verified. Proof bundle SHA-256: `8a4bcd47144cef419c23e7a563b690c76a8e47fc672098ca6b7d2ccf5a5c80f6`.
- All 440 request records match across arms: revisions 0–19, one workspace, 1,200 entries, 1,000 configured entries, 1,200 runtime models, and identical complete snapshot/runtime hashes. All measured windows are complete; stderr files are empty. Independent evidence audit reproduced the results and recommends holding under the declared rule.

### Performance acceptance rule (declared before measurement)

- Compare baseline `86dea7b503700634179e67028b97d2eeee801009` with this candidate using independent frozen installs and complete builds on one remote host, serially.
- Reuse committed `scripts/perf/catalog-worker-retention-measure.ts` with `--built-worker <arm-build> --output <fresh-fixture> --workspaces 1 --models 1000 --configured-models 1000 --providers 2 --discovery-models 100 --runtime-plugin --task-rounds 20 --measure-tasks`.
- Five alternating baseline/candidate pairs per mode, BC/CB/BC/CB/BC. Timing and allocation runs are separate; allocation adds `--sample-allocation`. A separate CPU-profile run attributes the hot path and does not supply timing gates.
- Request zero is cold; the remaining 19 requests are warm. Preserve matching complete output hashes and model counts, 20 successful records per run, completed measurements, and clean worker shutdown.
- Report cold latency and post-GC heap; warm median/p95, thread CPU, initial/peak/final heap, GC distributions and reclaimed bytes, aggregate process RSS, sampled allocations, and every loop histogram's sample count/p95/p99/max. Include host load, cohort medians/p95/ranges, and each paired delta.
- A win requires a repeatable reduction in allocation or work/latency with identical output. Every other measured metric must hold or improve; any worsening requires explicit owner acceptance. A 20% adverse paired cell stops landing rather than being dismissed as spread. Do not repeat an unchanged experiment to seek a passing median.
- RSS includes the source controller and compiled worker; it is not full Gateway RSS. Worker heap excludes TypeScript transform caches. The worker generates strict JSON, so JSONC compatibility is covered by real-registry/doctor tests; this workload does not establish authored-JSONC timing.

### Results and landing hold

**The repeatable allocation/CPU gain is established, but the declared landing rule does not pass without explicit owner acceptance of the adverse cells.** No merge has been requested.

Values below are medians of five independent launches per arm. Sampled allocation includes collected objects over 19 warm requests; it is not live heap or RSS.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Sampled allocation over 19 warm requests (MiB) | 1816.655 | 1742.151 | -4.101% |
| Warm request median (ms) | 104.348 | 101.148 | -3.067% |
| Warm request p95 (ms) | 156.607 | 154.087 | -1.609% |
| Worker CPU over warm window (ms) | 1888.035 | 1817.646 | -3.728% |

| Peak ordinary worker heap (MiB) | 148.117 | 149.273 | +0.781% |
| Worker-loop p95 (ms) | 9.314 | 9.355 | +0.440% |

Allocation falls in every pair (3.177%–4.763%), saving about 3.921 MiB per warm refresh. Worker CPU also falls in every timing pair. The worker still samples about 91.692 MiB of allocation per warm refresh, so most refresh work remains.

This does **not** demonstrate a large retained-memory repair: cold post-GC heap increases by 7,856 bytes and peak ordinary heap increases by 1,212,360 bytes. RSS includes the source controller and all process isolates; two timing pairs increase despite the lower cohort median. Final ordinary heap is not a post-GC retention measurement.

Four distinct timing diagnostics cross the 20% stop threshold:

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Worker-loop p95 | 2 | 7.618559 → 9.355263 ms | +22.796% |

| All-GC p99 | 4 | 3.351400 → 5.417260 ms | +61.642% |

The unchanged 1 ms event-loop histogram had 592 → 476 samples in timing pair 2. Its population changed, but 19 operations represent 3.21% → 3.99%, both below 5%; the prior campaign's threshold-crossing explanation does not directly explain this stop. Population effects are a possible limitation, not evidence that clears the regression.

Separate CPU profiles attribute 60.192 → 8.503 sampled inclusive milliseconds to `parseModelCatalogJson` and its children. prs.title: feat(google-meet): observe and reply in the Meet in-call chat
prs.body:
## Summary

Google Meet browser sessions now observe the in-call chat and can post chat messages through the existing native participation framework.

Before this change the Google Meet plugin registered a participation adapter that advertised no capabilities and answered every `participate` call with `unsupported`, so `participation_context` never listed chat sources and the agent had no way to reply in the Meet chat.

- `extensions/google-meet/src/transports/google-meet-chat-scripts.ts` (new): page scripts that read the Meet side-panel message log (`[jsname=xySENc]`, `[data-message-id]` rows), open the panel with Meet's `Ctrl+Alt+C` shortcut (works from a synthetic `keydown`, no trusted input needed), fill the composer (`textarea[jsname=YPqjbf]`) and click send (`button[jsname=SoqoBf]`). Includes a `MeetingBrowserParticipationAdapter` with capability `chat`, action validation (non-empty, <= 4000 chars, Meet's own limit), and mapping of observed messages to finalized `kind: "chat"` participation sources. Own messages are flagged `ownEcho` so they never become actionable sources.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/transports/chrome.ts`: `readChromeMeetChat` and `participateInChromeMeet` (local Chrome and chrome-node routes, same as transcript reads / leave).
- `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts`: advertises `chat` for tracked browser sessions, executes chat actions via `runMeetingParticipationWithBrowser`, and observes chat on every transcript capture tick (`#captureTranscript`), so chat sources appear in `participation_context` at the durable-transcript cadence (5s). Chat read failures are logged at debug level and never block the transcript snapshot. The chat epoch is `<sessionId>:<targetId>`, so a reassigned tab retires stale chat sources.
- `src/plugin-sdk/meeting-runtime.ts`: exports `evaluateMeetingBrowser`, `MeetingParticipationAction`, `MeetingParticipationEffectResult` for plugin use.

The action script performs the send synchronously before its first `await` (as `participation-browser.ts` requires), then only observes the message log to report `succeeded` + `observed.messageId`, `uncertain` (submitted but not observed), or a correctable `rejected` when the composer is closed / send disabled and no message was sent.

## Why

Agents joined through Chrome could hear and speak but were blind to the text chat, which is where participants drop links, questions for the bot, and "please post the summary" requests. The participation framework (sources, request ids, correction, authority rechecks) already existed; only the Meet implementation was missing.

## Not in scope

- No automatic chat-reply loop. The agent reads sources via `participation_context` and replies via `participate`; wiring chat sources into the realtime consult path is a follow-up.
- Selectors target the English UI (`hl=en`, which the plugin already forces).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm vitest run extensions/google-meet/src/transports/google-meet-chat-scripts.test.ts` (jsdom: read with sender/self attribution, panel closed, wrong meeting, Ctrl+Alt+C open, fill+send+observe, uncertain, rejected paths, validation, source mapping)
- [x] `pnpm vitest run extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.chat-participation.test.ts` (runtime advertises `chat`, observes chat on transcript capture, rejects empty text, executes chat action with the tracked tab, closes on leave)
- [x] `pnpm vitest run extensions/google-meet` (existing suite)
- [x] `pnpm tsgo` / lint on changed files
- [x] Manual: selectors and the Ctrl+Alt+C shortcut verified against a live Meet tab via CDP on a headless Chrome guest (message sent, appeared with `data-message-id`, other participants' messages attributed by display name).

prs.title: test(codex): observe lazy CLI module evaluation
prs.body:
## What problem does this PR solve?

The Codex CLI metadata test checks that the session registrar was not called during discovery. An eager import can evaluate the entire session CLI module while that assertion still passes.

## User impact

The existing test now catches eager session CLI loading during metadata discovery.

## Why this change?

Observe the mocked module factory before and after invoking the deferred CLI callback. Keep the existing case, descriptors, Commander forwarding and every original assertion. The five added test lines have exact separate allocation credit; production and the shared scalar are unchanged. Use the supported isolation annotation to avoid loading the real session CLI runtime, and retire only the changed factory's obsolete baseline entry.

## Evidence

- Untouched native main `073498226768e62d6ee0232b4e196cb487fc56cc`: the existing case passes; all three CLI source inputs match the task base.
- Actual metadata-owner eager-import control: the original passes; the repaired test fails at the pre-callback module-evaluation assertion. Owner and test restore byte for byte.
- Clean candidate: 1 pass. Session CLI and registration-import siblings: 19 passes across two suites, no skips.
- Focused typecheck, lint, formatting, MDX and whitespace checks pass. Test-line ratchet passes with exact +5/+5 credit and 10 lines of slack.
- Initial [CI41734710226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41734710226) failed mock-exports and test-lines. The mock fingerprint failure was caused by this PR and is repaired: the guard now passes with 6,400 retained grandfathered factories. Repeated eager-import controls and the clean case pass as described above.
- The initial CI base `206d54934a3d0764cad0ea59a31d43f74bec0fa0` has 53 lines of inherited budget debt; the tested merge retained the same debt. That attribution covers the initial attempt only.
- [Repaired-head CI, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41737007881) completed failed: 29 jobs passed, 28 skipped, and 2 failed. Only `test-lines` failed in `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`; the other nine subchecks, including `mock-exports`, passed. `openclaw/ci-gate` failed downstream. The single `security-fast` job and [exact-tuple Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41738002235) passed.
- Repaired-head CI base `65a13b12d9609d386dac41a53784d57b710f56aa` independently counts 6,444,296 test lines against a 6,444,243 ceiling. Actual CI merge `23937faabc11c4c0abbcc529f6f4cf2847001ace` counts 6,444,301 against 6,444,248. Both retain 53 lines of inherited debt; this PR's +5 test lines and +5 allocation leave it unchanged. Positive growth exposes the inherited deficit, while nonpositive growth may pass despite overage; this does not assert that the same job necessarily failed on main. CI remains failed. Unchanged policy paths do not imply equality of all counted test inputs.
- Final range `a12e3ae8d85d1f86263054bcd44687b082c710ba..e4cc1d3f3fb7225c5af66d599d87c71616ba3374`: fresh local ClawSweeper review completed with zero actionable correctness or security findings (full range, high reasoning). This independent read-only review did not rerun tests. Native review-tests on the published final head passes the existing case.

This is local metadata-loading proof. Gateway, native Codex execution and authorization behavior are outside this test.

prs.title: fix(security): respect channel bindings in exposure checks
prs.body:
Closes #175215

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes security audit warnings that attribute a private agent's tools to an open, messaging-only channel route, while preserving warnings for privileged route overrides.

## User Impact

Operators can audit isolated channel/account bindings without unrelated capability warnings. Peer, guild, team and wildcard overrides remain in scope. Telegram topic agent overrides retain all four exposure warnings when the topic can reach a privileged agent.

Channel-owned `agentId` overrides deliberately retain conservative all-agent analysis for the affected channel, including overrides on a closed sibling account. This can retain warnings for those configurations. Actual routing, tool permissions, configuration and state formats are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audit uses the canonical channel/account binding index and effective tool policies. Core bindings cannot exhaust plugin-owned routes, so configured channel-owned targets fall back to the existing all-agent analysis instead of silently excluding reachable tools. Private agents' explicitly configured full-exec posture warnings remain visible independently of open ingress.

## Evidence

Follow-up source: `0f60e7682bf5e636ad9bbaac8dc11ab958c62450` (tree `5e6c744ef2473c12c4ac8d78b304cf887b37908a`).

- Real built `openclaw security audit --json`, with isolated synthetic config/state and networking disabled: an open Telegram group bound to messaging-only `mailroom` reports none of the four exposure warnings; a direct binding to unrestricted `main` reports all four. Before this repair, a topic `agentId=main` overriding the mailroom binding incorrectly reported none; after repair it reports all four. All commands exit naturally with code 0. This proves the cold audit CLI diagnostic, not live Telegram transport.
- The supported source-runner build and replay ran on the precommit candidate with canonical build-input signature `1b46a0c0ceee5035115d0360357eacb0f462507cdd006d1a8a75735fe114ecbc`. The workflow verified that the commit contains the same candidate tree; no postcommit rebuild is asserted.
- The committed consumer regression is red before the production repair (topic case fails, ordinary-route control passes), then green. Fresh verification passes 61 tests across the exec surface, exposure matrix and audit summary suites. The wrapper takes 230.72 seconds including compiler preparation; the changed exec suite reports 175.86 seconds including transformation, and the other shard 39.41 seconds. Existing named-account isolation and narrower binding controls remain.
- Fresh source/test type graphs, typed lint, formatting, whitespace, line-cap and test-line ratchets pass. The separate test-line allocation grants exactly this PR's 89 net regression lines; the shared ceiling is unchanged.
- Original route-isolation CLI before/after evidence remains bound to base `6b06549c3e00` and earlier candidate `e047cf08f637`: six controls cover plain and named-account isolation, peer/guild/team overrides, and unresolved routing. These retained observations are historical, separate from the fresh topic replay above.

Local autoreview did not send a review: its helper rejected an unsupported `stream_max_retries` field in the configured provider. Independent host-agent source review of the complete nine-file base-to-head diff (`6b06549c3e00` → `0f60e7682bf5`) found no supported P0/P1/P2 findings and independently matched the captured source digests to the committed files. This is a source review, not a clean autoreview tool run; live channel transport and persisted runtime-binding enumeration remain outside this cold diagnostic proof.

The previous hosted review correctly identified the topic false negative and does not review this new head. Maintainer security approval is required for the current revision; no approval, Ready label or full CI pass is inferred from local validation.

### Current hosted checks

The current revision still requires maintainer security approval. Its integration CI also reports two failures inherited from main: the UI `no-misused-spread` error at `ui/src/pages/about/view.test.tsx:143` ([lint log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41662568915/job/126011321989)), whose file blob is identical in the CI base and merge tree, and a shared test-line debt of 17 lines ([ratchet log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41662568915/job/126010453719)). The test-line job reports this PR's +89 lines and its exact +89 allocation; removing both gives the same 17-line overage on the CI base. Other baseline ratchets passed. These are unresolved hosted gates, not a claim of all-green CI; no unrelated UI change or extra allocation is included.

prs.title: improve(plugins): explain the permission to modify prompts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The plugin consent dialog calls legitimate prompt/context contributions “Prompt injection,” while plugin settings say “Add context to prompts,” which understates the ability to change instructions.

## User Impact

The permission is consistently named **Modify prompts** in consent, plugin settings, and configuration hints. Its explanation says:

> Allows this plugin to add or change the context and instructions sent to the model, which can influence its responses. Only allow this for plugins you trust.

The configuration help also states that this capability is allowed by default and that denying it blocks prompt-modifying hooks, tool prompt guidance, next-turn contributions, and active-run steering. Conversation access remains a separate grant.

This is presentation-only: no capability/config/i18n identifiers, defaults, policy enforcement, stored grants, dependencies, or migrations change. No plugin-specific exception is introduced. No production Gateway changes, restarts, deployment, or merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inspected current main at `073498226768e62d6ee0232b4e196cb487fc56cc`, the hook-policy/registry owners, grant projection, and current Solid UI before editing. The label must describe prompt modification rather than an attack, without presenting the grant as harmless context-only access.

Related: #155227 and #182274 address missing-permission diagnostics; this does not duplicate those features or claim that all Lossless functionality requires this grant. The recorded Lossless denial in #155227 concerned conversation access, not a new prompt-modification default.

## Evidence

Reviewed head: `2ebc8a6ce7d933ec6fdcf340ccef7ddc109b9f6a`. Isolated checkout; 13 changed files. Simplification reuses the existing SettingsRow description slot, with no new state/helper/policy owner. Production +10 net lines; tests +39, allocated only to existing regression assertions and opt-in proof capture.

- Red/green: updated consent assertions failed on the original UI (2 failures for missing “Modify prompts”), then passed with the copy.
- 40 focused tests passed: consent dialog, settings lifecycle/read-only/default/reset/Ask behavior, plugin help, capability-summary grants, and config-schema tiers. Command: `pnpm test ui/src/pages/plugins/consent-dialog.test.tsx ui/src/pages/plugins/settings-lifecycle.test.tsx ui/src/pages/plugins/plugin-help.test.ts src/plugins/capability-summary.test.ts src/config/schema.tiers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Final shard durations: 0.10s, 0.65s, 2.06s.
- 18 built-Chromium scenarios passed: `pnpm test:ui:e2e` for `ui/src/pages/plugins/{plugins-runtime,plugin-overview}.e2e.test.ts` (6, 21.1s wall) and `ui/src/e2e/{plugins-settings-admin,plugins-settings-refresh}.e2e.test.ts` (12, 27.6s wall). Verifies consent acknowledgment, direct/refreshed settings, saving/resetting the same key, read-only behavior, and recovery. No real Gateway/provider/Lossless execution claimed; synthetic mock-Gateway fixtures exercise the production-built UI.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. UI lint retains one pre-existing warning at settings-lifecycle.test.tsx:108; no new warning. English only per source-owned i18n workflow; foreign catalogs remain release/bot-owned.
- Local ClawSweeper, full committed range `073498226768e62d6ee0232b4e196cb487fc56cc..2ebc8a6ce7d933ec6fdcf340ccef7ddc109b9f6a`, high reasoning: complete, no actionable correctness/security findings. The earlier stale-selector finding was repaired and both consumer suites passed. Runtime/screenshots were inspected separately by the author, not validated by the read-only reviewer. Hosted CI timing/results are not yet available.

### Known check limitations

- The test-line ratchet is red with inherited debt: untouched base has 6,443,949 lines against a 6,443,896 ceiling (53 over), verified using a separate index at the base. This change has 6,443,988 lines against a 6,443,935 ceiling, still 53 over after its exact +39 allocation. No shared baseline or unrelated tests were changed to hide the debt.

releases.body:
## 2026.11.5-beta.1

### Highlights

- **Knowledge Scribes:** add first-class knowledge capture and reusable scribe workflows across agents, sessions, and the Control UI. (#185583, #185637, #185974, #186270, #186455, #187659) Thanks @jalehman.
- **PostgreSQL data plane:** add PostgreSQL-backed state, migration tooling, and compatibility coverage for existing deployments. (#173968, #174080, #174085, #174183, #174242, #174374, #174387, #174399, #174623) Authored by @steipete.
- **Control UI:** overhaul mobile and desktop navigation, layouts, and interaction details. (#176356, #176466, #176505, #176540, #176557, #176653) Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski.
- **Pull requests from chat:** add end-to-end PR preparation, publication, review, and status workflows directly from conversations. (#176105, #176139, #178055, #178233, #178281, #178756) Thanks @shakkernerd.
- **Cross-device and cloud execution:** expand attached-device, cloud-placement, and cyber-access workflows, including safer capability handoffs. (#185230, #185477, #186560, #187408; related #186553) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @VACInc, @joshavant, @galiniliev, and @shakkernerd.
- **Decision and media models:** add specialized decision routing and media-capable model support, including ClawRouter integrations. (#177369, #178860, #178876, #178886, #178920, #179362; related #179360) Thanks @vincentkoc and @fuller-stack-dev.
- **Plugin experience:** improve plugin discovery, installation, authoring, and runtime integration. (#177869, #182419, #185315, #185544) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa and @jalehman.
- **Backup and upgrade safety:** harden backup, recovery, and upgrade paths with clearer state preservation and rollback behavior. (#186953, #187564, #187688, #187737; fixes #187519, #187678, #187657) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @art22s, @RomneyDa, @McgAtom, and @Yachiyo1680.

### Changes

- **Automations:** add persistent streams and richer execution context for durable scheduled work. (#177941, #177942, #179011, #179062, #179669, #182561) Thanks @joshavant, @eleqtrizit, and @jalehman.
- **Sharing and guests:** expand session sharing, guest access, and visitor lifecycle controls. (#181680, #182218, #182337, #182352) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @shakkernerd and @jalehman.
- **Learning and skills:** improve learned-skill capture, reuse, and guided authoring. (#181747, #181879, #186861) Thanks @obviyus and @jalehman.
- **Providers:** add and refine provider integrations, authentication, and model discovery. (#175509, #175729, #180788, #182248; related #175543) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @midhunvnadh, @obviyus, @lavicosa, and @hannesrudolph.

- **Session composition:** improve multi-session composition, routing, and coordinated execution. (#178842, #179609, #182742) Thanks @jalehman and @vyctorbrzezowski.
- **Credential compatibility:** improve credential migration and compatibility across legacy and current configuration formats. (#174294, #174599) Authored by @steipete.
- **Doctor compatibility:** broaden doctor checks and automated repair guidance for migrated installations. (#179387, #182328) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @jalehman.
- **Memory maintenance:** add safer memory cleanup and maintenance flows. (#182530; fixes #157280) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @islandpreneur007.
- **Model routing:** improve provider-aware model selection and routing behavior. (#180509, #183637) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @VACInc and @tommyjoseph.

### Fixes

- **Gateway startup:** fix startup recovery, dependency ordering, and service-state handling across upgrades. (#186920, #187724, #187819, #187870; fixes #186875, #187723) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @yousan, @bianyuxia-commits, @masatohoshino, @obviyus, @RomneyDa, @jalehman, @fuller-stack-dev, and @vincentkoc.

issues.title: Add Sprouts Data MCP preset (hosted Streamable HTTP, API key)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

Sprouts Data runs a hosted MCP server for B2B company and people data (search companies and people, find look-alike companies, look up records by domain / LinkedIn URL / ID, map relationships). Connecting it in nanobot today means building a custom MCP connection by hand. Similar services (Lusha, Hunter, Apollo.io, Clay) already have presets under Apps → MCP.


### Proposed Solution

Add an API-key preset in the crm category, following the existing Lusha preset:

```json
{
  "name": "sprouts_data",
  "display_name": "Sprouts Data",
  "category": "crm",
  "description": "Search companies and people, find look-alikes, and look up records.",
  "docs_url": "https://dashboard.sproutsdata.ai/docs",
  "transport": "streamableHttp",
  "install_supported": true,
  "brand_domain": "sproutsdata.ai",
  "server": {
    "type": "streamableHttp",
    "url": "https://dashboard.sproutsdata.ai/mcp",
    "tool_timeout": 60
  },
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "sprouts_api_key",
      "label": "Sprouts Data API key",
      "target": ["header", "X-API-Key"],
      "env_var": "SPROUTS_API_KEY",
      "placeholder": "Paste your token"
    }
  ],
  "requires": "Sprouts Data API key",
  "note": "Test keys (sk_dsp_test_) are charged 0 credits. Live keys use prepaid Sprouts credits."
}
```

Docs row for docs/mcp-presets.md (Hosted services):
| Sprouts Data | API key | [Official guide](https://dashboard.sproutsdata.ai/docs) |

brand_color is left out; happy to supply one if you need it.

### Alternatives Considered

Browser OAuth instead of an API key. The server also supports OAuth 2.1 with discovery and dynamic client registration (registration_endpoint in https://dashboard.sproutsdata.ai/authsvc/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server), so an "auth": "oauth" preset like Apollo.io's should also work. The API-key preset is the simpler option and matches Lusha.


### Related Component

Skills / Plugins

### Additional Context

- Transport: Streamable HTTP only, at https://dashboard.sproutsdata.ai/mcp. Nothing to install.
- Auth: API key in the X-API-Key header. The MCP server also accepts "Authorization: Bearer <key>".
- Keys are created in the Sprouts dashboard and carry scopes, so a key can be limited to the tools it needs.
- Free testing: test keys (sk_dsp_test_) search the same data and are charged 0 credits, and new workspaces get 1,000 free credits. A quick connection check is the free sprouts_coverage tool.
- 12 tools, including sprouts_search, sprouts_similar and sprouts_entity_lookup.

Disclosure: I work at Sprouts Inc. (doing business as Sprouts.ai), which runs Sprouts Data.

issues.title: Subagents ignore `tools.cliApps.enable: false` (run_cli_app still registered for subagents)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug Description

**Version:** nanobot-ai 0.4.0 (also present on `main` as of 2026-11-04, commit 8632940)

**What happens**
With `tools.cliApps.enable` set to `false`, the main agent correctly no longer offers `run_cli_app`, but subagents still get it.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Config:
   ```json
   { "tools": { "restrictToWorkspace": true, "exec": { "enable": false }, "web": { "enable": false },
                "cliApps": { "enable": false }, "my": { "enable": false } } }
   ```
2. `nanobot agent -m "Use a subagent to count the lines in inbox.md and report the number."`
3. Inspect the tool list sent to the model (e.g. via a logging proxy in front of the provider):
   - main agent requests: no `run_cli_app` ✓
   - subagent requests: `apply_patch, edit_file, find_files, grep, list_dir, read_file, run_cli_app, write_file` ✗

**Cause**
`nanobot/agent/subagent.py`, `SubagentManager._subagent_tools_config()` builds a fresh `ToolsConfig` copying only `exec`, `web`, `file` and `restrict_to_workspace` from the parent config. `cli_apps` falls back to its default (`enable: true`), and `RunCliAppTool` is in the `subagent` scope (`_scopes = {"core", "subagent"}`), so it gets registered for subagents.

### Expected Behavior

**Expected**
Subagents should not get tools the operator disabled for the main agent. Suggested fix: also pass `cli_apps=self.tools_config.cli_apps` in `_subagent_tools_config()` (or derive the subagent config from the parent with `model_copy`, so future tool settings are inherited by default).

issues.title: Proposal: evolve the current subagent system toward multi-agent collaboration

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

The current subagent system is closer to background task delegation than a true multi-agent system.

A subagent receives a task, executes it independently, and returns a final result to the main agent. However, subagents do not have persistent identities, shared task state, agent-to-agent communication, or the ability to coordinate and delegate work among themselves.

This limits more complex workflows that require multiple specialized agents to collaborate, share intermediate results, and coordinate dependent or parallel tasks.

### Proposed Solution

Consider evolving the current design toward an optional multi-agent system where multiple agents can:

- have distinct roles and responsibilities;
- communicate and collaborate with each other;
- share task status and intermediate results;
- coordinate dependent or parallel tasks;
- delegate bounded subtasks when necessary.

The existing subagent feature could remain as the lightweight option for simple background delegation, while multi-agent coordination could support more complex workflows.

### Alternatives Considered

Keep the current one-shot subagent model and rely on the main agent to manually coordinate all delegated tasks. This remains useful for simple background work, but it does not provide direct collaboration or shared coordination between agents.

### Related Component

Agent / Prompts

### Additional Context

This should follow nanobot's "core stays small; extend at the edges" principle. Ideally, multi-agent coordination could be introduced as an optional tool, plugin, or external service without adding significant complexity to AgentLoop or AgentRunner.

issues.title: WebUI: model button does not reflect the active primary or fallback model
issues.body:
### Bug Description

The WebUI composer model button can be mistaken for the model handling the current request, but it displays the configured/selected preset rather than following the gateway's `turn_model_updated` events. In particular, it does not update when a fallback handles the turn. This makes the interface misleading when the default preset, session selection, and actual response model differ.

In the reported case, the global default was `GPT 6.1 Sol Med`, the user selected `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` through OpenRouter for a chat, and the interface still appeared to identify GPT as primary during processing. Sanitized gateway logs established that Nemotron was actually attempted as primary. OpenRouter rejected it with HTTP 401, followed by Gemini fallback attempts; `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview` ultimately succeeded. The display discrepancy should not be interpreted as evidence that GPT actually processed that request.

The OpenRouter authentication failure and provider quota errors are separate configuration/service problems. This report concerns accurate model attribution in the WebUI, not bypassing those failures or changing fallback routing.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a default model preset and at least one different fallback preset.
2. Open a WebUI chat and select its intended preset.
3. Submit a request that causes the primary provider to fail and a configured fallback to be used. A mocked provider failure is sufficient; no external outage is required.
4. Observe the gateway's `turn_model_updated` events and the composer model button while processing and after completion.

For a deterministic frontend reproduction, render `ThreadShell` with a default OpenAI Codex preset, emit a chat-scoped `turn_model_updated` event identifying a different primary model, and then emit one with `model_name: "deepseek/deepseek-chat", fallback: true`. The button continues to show the configured preset instead of following the reported runtime model.

### Expected Behavior

The interface should clearly distinguish the preset selected for the next request from the model actually processing the current turn. The model button should reflect the gateway-reported primary/fallback model and provider while processing, with the last reported model visible after completion. Opening the picker should retain the user's selected preset for the next request; using a fallback must not silently change that selection.

Alternatively, if maintainers prefer the button to represent only the next-request selection, its presentation should make that distinction explicit and provide equally visible current-model attribution during processing.

### Actual Behavior / Code Evidence

At upstream revision `cc4dd1ceb`:

- `webui/src/components/thread/ThreadShell.tsx` derives `modelBadge` from `toModelBadgeInfo(modelName, settings, activeModelPreset)`. Non-fallback `turn_model_updated` events only clear the fallback notice; fallback events populate a separate notice without updating the composer model display.
- `webui/src/tests/thread-shell.test.tsx` explicitly covers the existing behavior in the test named “keeps the selected composer preset and attributes only the reply to its actual source”.
- `docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md` says the composer still shows the selected preset.

This is therefore a request to correct a confusing display contract, not a claim that the existing behavior is accidental or that backend model selection has been proven broken. Fallback notices and per-reply attribution already exist; they do not make the model button itself follow the active model.

### Environment

- nanobot: 0.4.0; source baseline `cc4dd1ceb` with local WhatsApp integration fixes
- Python: 3.13.2
- OS: macOS arm64
- Channel: WebUI / WebSocket
- Connection: local gateway, packaged WebUI
- Browser version: not recorded
- Providers involved in the report: OpenAI Codex default, OpenRouter-selected Nemotron, Gemini fallbacks

### Local Fix and Verification

A local patch now tracks the existing chat-scoped runtime model events for display separately from the selected preset. It updates the button label/provider without changing the picker selection or model-routing policy. No protocol changes are required; hosts without runtime-model events retain the existing configured-preset display.

Verification:

- Regression test reproduced the unchanged fallback label before the fix and passed afterward.
- 335 tests passed across `thread-shell.test.tsx`, `model-preset-badge.test.tsx`, `thread-composer.test.tsx`, and `model-fallback-notice.test.tsx`.
- The updated regression also verifies a reported Nemotron primary differing from the configured default, its OpenRouter branding, fallback display, and resetting to the reported primary on the next turn.
- A picker regression verifies that runtime display does not change the selected preset or its model details.
- Type checking, focused ESLint, client import-boundary checking, and the production WebUI build passed.
- The rebuilt WebUI was installed locally and its served bundle verified. No new live model request was sent to validate this display patch; runtime events were exercised deterministically in tests.

Related reports: #5198 concerns session model switching itself; #6031 concerns fallback notifications on non-WebUI chat channels. This report focuses on the WebUI composer button's runtime-model attribution.

issues.title: Required Codex compaction can fall through to generation during image retry
issues.body:
## Bug Description

If required Codex compaction fails on a request containing images, the image-removal retry clears native conversation state and rebuilds ProviderCallContext without compaction_input_budget. It then sends an ordinary generation request before compaction has succeeded.

I reproduced this through both public retry APIs, streaming and non-streaming, with a simulated HTTP 400 unsupported_value error. The reproduction uses mocked transport calls.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use an isolated checkout of source revision `384b7638307e5c9279286df78ace5759311ea603` with the repository's development dependencies.
2. Copy [the regression test file](https://github.com/KDB-Wind/nanobot/blob/5e04de932d9ea3ac209c2f1f7e967bc6ee27b695/tests/providers/test_openai_codex_provider.py) to `tests/providers/test_openai_codex_provider.py`, keeping `nanobot/providers/base.py` unchanged.
3. Run:

```text
python -m pytest tests/providers/test_openai_codex_provider.py -k image_retry_cannot_bypass_required_compaction -q
```

The fixture creates resumable Responses state with a pending image message and a compaction_input_budget. It rejects the first transport call and records the submission types. The required-budget cases cover both entry points.

On this upstream revision, the two required-budget cases fail and the two optional-budget controls pass. All four pass with the candidate fix.

## Expected Behavior

Return the compaction failure with its provider-state recovery signal. Image repair should respect the required budget and continue working for calls without that requirement.

## Relevant Logs

The test records:

```text
Required budget, current affected behavior: ["compaction", "generation"]
Required budget, expected behavior:         ["compaction"]
No required budget, compatibility control:  ["generation", "generation"]
```

## Environment

- nanobot version: source revision `384b7638307e5c9279286df78ace5759311ea603`.
- Python: 3.12.13.
- Operating system: Windows.
- Channel / platform: provider retry API; not channel-specific.
- LLM provider: openai_codex.
- Model: gpt-5.6-sol in the fixture; HTTP requests are mocked.
- Browser / connection: not applicable to this reproduction.

## Additional Context

The field is lost in LLMProvider._retry_without_images in `nanobot/providers/base.py`. A [candidate fix is available in my fork](https://github.com/KDB-Wind/nanobot/commit/5e04de932d9ea3ac209c2f1f7e967bc6ee27b695). It is one commit on the upstream revision above and changes two files. Related provider retry, Codex, and runner fallback tests passed: 200, including the four regression cases. Changed-file Ruff and BasedPyright checks passed.

issues.title: PermissionError [WinError 5] when rewriting the gateway client lease on Windows

labels.name: question
labels.description: Further information is requested

issues.body:
# `PermissionError: [WinError 5]` when the gateway client lease is rewritten on Windows

## Summary

On Windows, rewriting `~/.nanobot/run/gateway.clients.json` intermittently fails with
`PermissionError: [WinError 5] 拒绝访问 (Access is denied)`.

The file is the on-demand gateway client lease (`{"auto_stop": ..., "clients": {...}}`).
It is written with a temp-file + `os.replace()` pattern, and Windows refuses the rename
whenever any other handle has the target open without `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, or when a
real-time scanner is briefly holding the temp file.

Because Python's `Path.read_text()` (used by the same class to read the lease) does not
grant delete sharing, a reader on the other side of the race is enough to make the write
fail. The failure is not retried, so it escapes as an exception to the calling client.

Related: a failed write also means the client is *not* registered in the lease, which is
the data structure that decides whether an on-demand gateway may auto-stop.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Windows 11 (AMD64) |
| Python | 3.14.9 |
| nanobot | 0.4.0 |
| Commit | `4a14faa47e9af06a66968cb59f5b5d46754dc6fe` |
| Install | source checkout, `python -m nanobot gateway --foreground --port 18790` |
| Data home | `%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot` |
| File system | local NTFS, not a network drive, not OneDrive-synced |

## Actual behaviour

```
PermissionError: [WinError 5] 拒绝访问。:
  '%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot\run\gateway.clients.json.d8y0i3t6.tmp'
  -> '%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot\run\gateway.clients.json'
```

Observed while a single gateway service was running (one launcher process plus its
worker child, the worker owning ports 8765 and 18790). The run directory was writable —
`run/gateway.json` was being written successfully in the same time window — so this is
not a directory ACL problem, and the lease file was not marked read-only. No `.tmp`
leftovers remained, i.e. the `finally: temporary.unlink()` cleanup ran each time.

## Expected behaviour

The lease write should tolerate a transient sharing violation, since the file is
short-lived state that is read roughly once per second by
`monitor_gateway_clients()`.

## Root cause

`nanobot/gateway/runtime.py`:

- write path — `GatewayClientLease._write_state()` (lines 782–798):

  ```python
  fd, temporary_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
      prefix=f"{self.state_path.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=self.state_path.parent
  )
  temporary = Path(temporary_name)
  try:
      with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
          json.dump(state, handle, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
          ...
          os.fsync(handle.fileno())
      temporary.replace(self.state_path)      # <-- single attempt, no retry
  finally:
      temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
  ```

- read path — `GatewayClientLease._read_state()` (lines 766–773):

  ```python
  payload: object = json.loads(self.state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
  ```

- poller — `monitor_gateway_clients()` (lines 801–815) calls
  `lease.begin_orphan_shutdown()` every `poll_interval_s` (default `1.0`), and
  `begin_orphan_shutdown()` (lines 622–637) reads *and* writes the lease.

On POSIX, `os.replace()` over a file that another process has open simply succeeds.
On Windows it maps to `MoveFileExW(..., MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)`, which returns
`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (5) when the destination has an open handle that did not specify
`FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, or when the destination is read-only.

Python's `open()` / `Path.read_text()` on Windows requests read+write sharing but **not**
delete sharing, so any concurrent `_read_state()` — in the gateway process, in a second
client process, or in a status/UI reader — is enough to make the replace fail.

Note that `begin_orphan_shutdown()` does take `transition_lock` before touching the file,
so the *application-level* readers and writers it controls are serialised. The remaining
windows are:

1. external handles that do not participate in the app-level lock (real-time antivirus /
   Defender scanning the freshly written `.tmp`, Windows Search indexer, backup agents,
   an editor with the file open), and
2. any future/third-party reader of the lease that calls `_read_state()` outside the
   transition lock.

Either way the mitigation is the same: don't let a transient share lock turn into a
hard failure.

## Minimal reproduction of the underlying Windows behaviour

```python
import os
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

d = Path(os.environ["TEMP"]) / "share-lock"
d.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
target = d / "gateway.clients.json"
target.write_text('{"old": 1}', encoding="utf-8")

handle = open(target, "r", encoding="utf-8")   # same sharing as Path.read_text()
tmp = d / "new.tmp"
tmp.write_text('{"new": 2}', encoding="utf-8")


def replace():
    try:
        os.replace(tmp, target)                 # nanobot line 796
        print("ok")
    except PermissionError as exc:
        print("failed:", exc)                   # -> [WinError 5]


thread = threading.Thread(target=replace)
thread.start()
time.sleep(0.01)
handle.close()
thread.join()
```

A single `os.replace()` fails here; a short bounded retry succeeds as soon as the reader
closes.

## Proposed fix

Retry the replace with a bounded, short backoff. The whole function is state that is
rewritten immediately afterwards anyway, so a few milliseconds of patience is harmless,
and it keeps a scanner/reader blip from raising into the client.

```diff
--- a/nanobot/gateway/runtime.py
+++ b/nanobot/gateway/runtime.py
@@ -793,7 +793,7 @@ class GatewayClientLease:
                 handle.write("\n")
                 handle.flush()
                 os.fsync(handle.fileno())
-            temporary.replace(self.state_path)
+            _replace_with_sharing_retry(temporary, self.state_path)
         finally:
             temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
@@ -820,3 +820,20 @@ def _instance_suffix(*, workspace: str | None, config_path: str | None) -> str |
     if not raw:
         return None
     return hashlib.sha1(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
+
+
+def _replace_with_sharing_retry(source: Path, target: Path, *, attempts: int = 10) -> None:
+    """Atomically replace ``target`` with ``source``, retrying Windows share locks.
+
+    Windows reports a concurrent reader of ``target`` (or a scanner briefly
+    holding ``source``) as ``ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED``; the window is short, so a
+    bounded retry clears it where a single ``os.replace`` would fail.
+    """
+    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
+        try:
+            os.replace(source, target)
+            return
+        except PermissionError:
+            if attempt == attempts:
+                raise
+            time.sleep(0.005 * attempt)
```

`time` is already imported in this module. Worst case adds ~0.23 s before the original
`PermissionError` is re-raised, so a permanently locked file still fails loudly instead
of hanging.

Verified locally against both cases:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Reader holds the file briefly, then closes | replace succeeds, new content visible |
| Reader never closes the file | `PermissionError` still raised, after ~0.23 s |

## Possible follow-ups for maintainers

- If `_read_state()` should never block a writer, the read could be done through a
  handle opened with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` (ctypes `CreateFileW`) so `os.replace()`
  succeeds even while a read is in flight. The retry above makes that optional.
- Consider logging a warning plus retry-scheduling instead of propagating, so a client
  attach never fails because of lease bookkeeping.

## Workaround for users (no code change)

- Add `%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot` to antivirus exclusions.
- Make sure only one gateway service runs (`nanobot gateway status` / one `gateway start`).
- The error is transient: the next lease write succeeds, and the client can usually
  attach again.

issues.title: WhatsApp: missing native libmagic is reported as missing plugin dependencies
issues.body:
## Bug Description

`_load_neonize()` in [`nanobot/channels/whatsapp/runtime.py`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/main/nanobot/channels/whatsapp/runtime.py#L83-L101) groups `import magic`, Neonize imports, and magic API validation under a single `ImportError` handler. When the Python `magic` wrapper is installed but cannot load the native `libmagic` shared library, the resulting error is:

```
WhatsApp dependencies not installed. Run: nanobot plugins enable whatsapp
```

This is misleading because:
1. The WhatsApp plugin dependencies **are** installed — `python-magic` and `neonize` are both present.
2. The actual problem is a missing **native system library** (`libmagic.dylib` / `libmagic.so`), which `nanobot plugins enable whatsapp` does not install.
3. The user has no way to distinguish between missing Python packages, a missing native library, or an incompatible `magic` API from the error message alone.

### Root Cause

The `try/except ImportError` block at [runtime.py:88–101](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/main/nanobot/channels/whatsapp/runtime.py#L88-L101) catches all `ImportError` variants uniformly:

```python
def _load_neonize() -> _NeonizeAPI:
    global _NEONIZE_API
    if _NEONIZE_API is not None:
        return _NEONIZE_API

    try:
        import magic
        from neonize.aioze.client import NewAClient
        from neonize.aioze.events import ConnectedEv, DisconnectedEv, MessageEv, PairStatusEv
        from neonize.utils.jid import build_jid

        detect_mime = getattr(magic, "from_file", None)
        detect_buffer = getattr(magic, "from_buffer", None)
        if not callable(detect_mime) or not callable(detect_buffer):
            raise ImportError("python-magic does not expose from_file/from_buffer")
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "WhatsApp dependencies not installed. Run: nanobot plugins enable whatsapp"
        ) from exc
```

When `python-magic` is installed but `libmagic` (the native C library) is not available, `import magic` succeeds but the first call to `magic.from_file()` or `magic.from_buffer()` raises an `ImportError` or `OSError` depending on the `python-magic` version. In some versions, the native-library load happens at import time and raises `ImportError` directly — which is caught by the blanket handler and misreported as missing plugin dependencies.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install nanobot with WhatsApp plugin enabled: `nanobot plugins enable whatsapp`
2. Ensure `python-magic` and `neonize` are installed (`pip show python-magic neonize` both succeed)
3. Remove or make unavailable the native `libmagic` library (e.g., on macOS: `brew uninstall libmagic` or rename `/opt/homebrew/lib/libmagic.dylib`)
4. Start nanobot or trigger any WhatsApp media operation that invokes `_load_neonize()`
5. Observe the error message

## Expected Behavior

The error should distinguish between at least these failure modes with actionable guidance:

| Failure | Expected diagnostic |
|---|---|
| Neonize Python package missing | `"Neonize not installed. Run: nanobot plugins enable whatsapp"` |
| `python-magic` wrapper missing | `"python-magic not installed. Run: pip install python-magic"` |
| Wrapper present, native `libmagic` unavailable | `"Native libmagic library not found. Install it with your system package manager (e.g., brew install libmagic on macOS, apt install libmagic1 on Debian/Ubuntu)"` |
| Incompatible `magic` module (missing `from_file`/`from_buffer`) | `"Installed magic module does not expose the expected API. Ensure python-magic (not python-magic-bin or file-magic) is installed"` |

Each error should preserve the original exception cause via exception chaining (`raise ... from exc`).

## Relevant Logs

```shell
# Simulated reproduction — python-magic installed, libmagic native library absent
$ python -c "import magic; magic.from_file(__file__)"
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ImportError: failed to find libmagic.  Check your installation

# Actual nanobot error surfaced to user:
RuntimeError: WhatsApp dependencies not installed. Run: nanobot plugins enable whatsapp
```

## Environment

- **nanobot Version:** 0.4.0
- **Python Version:** 3.13.2
- **Operating System:** macOS arm64 (Apple Silicon)
- **Channel / Platform:** WhatsApp
- **LLM Provider:** (any — issue is in channel dependency initialization, not provider)
- **Model:** N/A

## Additional Context

- The original exception chain is preserved (`from exc`), but the user-facing message does not surface it — users see only the `RuntimeError` text.
- Lazy optional dependency loading should be preserved: importing non-WhatsApp code must not require `libmagic` or `neonize`.
- The fix should not replace byte-level MIME sniffing with `mimetypes` filename guessing, as that is not equivalent for buffers, extensionless files, or files with misleading extensions.
- Existing `_NEONIZE_API` caching behavior should remain intact.
- Setup/troubleshooting docs should be updated to distinguish Python package vs. native system library requirements with platform-specific installation guidance.

prs.title: fix(runner): insert user-attention hint before mid-turn user messages
prs.body:
## 问题

用户在 LLM 执行工具链期间发送消息时，LLM 可能忽略新消息继续调用工具。需要中断工具链让 LLM 优先响应用户。

## 核心目的
hint 和用户输入合并后作为一条独立的 user 消息发给 LLM，夹在 assistant(tool_calls) 和接下来的工具结果之间。LLM 看到这条 user 消息——没有其他 role 混在一起——它必须处理，不能跳过继续调工具。和之前内容前缀方案的区别是，这次不是拼在已有消息里，而是让它占据一个完整的 user 轮次。

## 方案
hint 作为第一条 injection 交给 `_append_injected_messages`，由其内部的 `_merge_message_content` 自动合并连续 user 消息，产生**一条独立 user 消息**（hint 为前缀），夹在 assistant(tool_calls) 和工具结果之间：

```
messages = [
  assistant_tool_calls,
  user: "⚠️ 用户打断了你...\n\n我想改个方向",  ← 合并后的单条 user 消息
  tool_result_1,                                  ← 工具结果完整保留
  tool_result_2,
]
```

**实现**：

```python
hint_msg = {"role": "user", "content": hint}
injections.insert(0, hint_msg)
# _append_injected_messages 检测连续 user → merge 为单条
self._append_injected_messages(messages, injections)
```

**优点**：
- 复用项目已有的 `_append_injected_messages` 角色交替保证，不绕过现有逻辑
- 单条 user 消息，对主流 provider 无连续 user 兼容性问题
- 避免 multimodal content（list）时 str + list crash
- 工具结果完整保留，LLM 回应用户后可继续

## 改动

`nanobot/agent/runner.py` `_try_drain_injections()` 中，`real_injection` 时在前插入 hint_msg。

## 影响

- 仅影响 mid-turn 注入的消息格式，不影响正常对话流
- 全 provider 兼容（user role，单条消息）
- 效果待实测定性：需确认 LLM 在 hint 后确实优先回应用户而非继续调工具

prs.title: feat(telegram): support custom Bot API base URL and extra headers
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements #4702 — lets the Telegram channel target a self-hosted Bot API server or an enterprise gateway instead of the hardcoded `https://api.telegram.org`.

Adds two optional fields to `TelegramConfig`:

- **`api_base`** — custom Bot API endpoint. Forwarded to both the send and polling `HTTPXRequest` pools as `base_url`. Leave unset to keep using the official API (default).
- **`extra_headers`** — extra HTTP headers appended to every Bot API request (e.g. an auth token for a corporate gateway). Mirrors the existing `extra_headers` field on the provider config for consistency.

### Why

Some users sit behind regional or enterprise network setups where `api.telegram.org` is unreachable or must be routed through a private gateway. The channel already supports a SOCKS/HTTP `proxy`, but that doesn't cover self-hosted [Telegram Bot API local servers](https://github.com/tdlib/telegram-bot-api) or gateways that require custom request headers. `python-telegram-bot`'s `HTTPXRequest` accepts both `base_url` and `extra_headers` natively, so this just wires the config through.

### Validation

- `api_base` is validated to be an HTTPS URL with a host (mirrors the existing `webhook_url` check); whitespace is stripped and an empty value normalizes to `None`.
- Both fields default to `None`, so existing configurations are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check` passes
- [x] New unit tests:
  - `test_telegram_config_api_base_defaults_none_and_accepts_https`
  - `test_telegram_config_api_base_rejects_non_https` (parametrized: http/ftp/no-scheme/no-host)
  - `test_start_injects_api_base_and_extra_headers` (both pools receive `base_url` + `extra_headers`)
  - `test_start_without_api_base_passes_none` (default behavior unchanged)
- [x] Full `tests/channels/test_telegram_channel.py` suite: 97 passed

## Notes

- Minimal change, scoped to the Telegram channel only — no core/loop changes.
- Naming (`api_base` / `extra_headers`) matches the provider config to keep the mental model consistent.
- Manual end-to-end verification against a real self-hosted Bot API server is left to whoever has such an environment; the wiring is covered by unit tests.

Closes #4702

prs.title: ci(release): share manual and opt-in daily candidate preparation
prs.body:
## Summary

Start a lighter release process without adding a second build system.

- Keep one Stable preparation path for feature releases and patches. Patches need generated change notes and affected documentation, not a full wiki and promotional refresh.
- Add opt-in daily Preview candidate preparation to the existing workflow. It stays disabled unless maintainers enable the repository variable. Require successful latest push CI for the exact source and skip an already accepted source/base pair.
- Generate draft change notes from the preceding release on the selected source line. Stable notes exclude Preview tags. Retain notes with candidate reports and explicitly requested installable handoffs.
- Preserve existing dispatch inputs, Preview numbering, five-platform acceptance and artifact-ID handoffs. Daily runs cannot replace pending manual runs.

## Boundary

This is the preparation step, not a complete automatic publisher. It creates no tags, GitHub Releases, PyPI uploads or catalogue updates. It does not change the signing workflow, client trust policy, repository variables or protection settings. Automatic Preview publication remains follow-up work. No release workflow was dispatched for this PR.

The existing five native runners, including macOS and Linux arm64, and temporary wheel transfers remain unchanged. Enabling daily preparation would incur those costs; it does not retain the optional large installable handoff. Daily preparation is disabled by default.

No application, configuration, session, package-layout or model-request behavior changes. Existing manual inputs remain supported. Website deployment and public channel announcements are outside this draft.

## Verification

- 48 focused tests passed: planning and workflow contracts, candidate preparation, manifests and installation-guide regressions.
- A clean planning environment with only Pydantic and packaging ran the CLI against real repository history. A read-only check of the current main CI also passed; no Actions run or publication was started.
- Actionlint 1.7.12 passed for the changed workflow (without ShellCheck). Ruff, focused BasedPyright and whitespace checks passed.
- Five-platform binary builds, native acceptance execution and public signed installation were not run locally for this source-only draft. PR CI is separate evidence and remains to be checked on the pushed head.

Contributes to NAN-392.

An active Goal now keeps one ReAct execution running beyond the ordinary `max_tool_iterations` limit. Normal text responses receive an internal continuation prompt while the committed goal remains active. A successful `update_goal(complete/cancel/block)` releases that continuation requirement; tool-based closure after the limit still gets a bounded final-answer request.

This replaces the earlier version of this PR, which isolated Goal policy but retained cross-turn continuation. Active Goals are no longer bounded by the former 12 continuation rounds. Stop, cancellation, terminal provider failures and refusals retain their termination semantics; stopping execution does not cancel the saved objective.

## Mechanisms removed or retained

- Remove Goal-specific next-turn requests, queued handoff objects, encoded continuation tickets, round accounting and rollback, and mutable continuation-pending state. The iteration counter remains monotonic within one runner invocation.
- Keep input draining separate from continuation guidance. Initial, injected and recovered unconsumed user input authorizes Goal creation/replacement only when actually consumed.
- Remove the uncalled sustained-turn predicate, constructor-time authorization path, unused goal-start metadata, redundant scope entry override, cross-turn start-time guards, obsolete interrupted-handoff completion variant and cross-turn usage accumulation. Authorization tests now exercise actual input consumption; explicit recovery and historical fork-field filtering remain live.
- Keep generic session queues, explicit interruption recovery, checkpoint/history commits, generation guards, provider state, context compaction, and independent automation behavior.
- Keep one cancellation-safe terminal publication owner. Failed old-generation checkpoints do not publish a completion that can recreate a deleted session.
- Retain the small Goal assembly/scope boundary for consistent Gateway, CLI and SDK registration and execution-local authorization; it no longer implements scheduling or budget-decision variants. Presentation formatting remains in the WebUI adapter.
- Update existing tests for long same-run execution, successful closure beyond the cap, real input priority, Stop/checkpoint settlement, generation replacement, provider-state continuity, and final replies. Real isolated Gateway/WebSocket scenarios use a local synthetic model and exceed the former per-turn and continuation-count limits.
- Consolidate redundant regression coverage: 16 fewer expanded test cases and 427 net test lines removed. Retained long-run and committed-checkpoint scenarios own the distinct lifecycle, usage, history, provider-state privacy and Stop/capacity assertions; real Gateway scenarios, authorization and generation boundaries remain covered.

## User-visible cautions

- Active Goals may consume more model tokens and time than before. Objectives should remain bounded; `/stop` interrupts work.
- The existing `/compact` FIFO barrier remains: it waits for the active execution to finish, and later inputs do not overtake it. With a continuous Goal this wait can last until goal closure. Stop cancels queued commands; users can resubmit `/compact` after stopping. This consequence is awaiting explicit user confirmation; automatic in-run context compaction is unchanged.
- Restart does not automatically resume a persisted active Goal; existing explicit recovery remains.

## Verification

[Full remote CI passed](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/41621109642) for final head `6eaa1b738`, including the dead-code cleanup and test simplification. GitHub tested merge checkout `bafefcb42` against target `354553912`; all 15 jobs succeeded.

- Python 3.11 and Linux Python 3.14: 11,286 main-suite tests and 256 serial CLI tests passed in each environment. Windows Python 3.14: 10,985 main-suite tests and 248 serial CLI tests passed, plus the selected Windows compatibility suites. Platform exclusions/skips remain those declared by CI.
- Ruff, strict BasedPyright and import boundaries passed. WebUI checks/build/browser, TUI Linux/Windows, Docker and Linux/Windows native installation/update/recovery acceptance passed; the aggregate CI required check is green.
- The Python suites retain both real isolated Gateway/WebSocket Goal scenarios with a synthetic local model: successful completion beyond the old limits, and Stop at a committed checkpoint followed by independent input. This is transport/runtime acceptance, not a manual Goal UI acceptance claim.
- The test-only follow-up leaves production code and CI configuration unchanged. Source/diff checks passed; no local tests, collection, lint, typechecking, builds or browser runs were performed after the user's remote-only instruction.

Resolves NAN-401

Long-running goals now keep the existing context meter and recent-round chart current before the whole task finishes. Existing run indicators and controls are reused; no separate model-status text is added. Individual tool results are published when each call settles, rather than waiting for slower siblings.

## Changes

- Emit typed logical model-call lifecycle snapshots at the provider invocation boundary, including failure/cancellation. Reuse reported usage and measured streaming telemetry; snapshots contain cumulative usage and at most eight runner-visible rounds. Recovery requests update the current round, matching terminal aggregation rather than changing the chart when the turn closes.
- Reuse existing routed delivery and durable display history. Update active-turn usage independently of answer streaming; final snapshots replace rather than duplicate live statistics. Fence duplicate/stale events and reject late usage snapshots after Stop/end.
- Publish per-call tool start/result events, including rejected calls and cancellation, without duplicate batch-end results. This does not change background shell-process observation semantics or absorb the closed, unmerged #6524.
- Preserve context-meter invalidation after successful compaction until a newer request reports context usage.
- Keep protocol v1 compatible: new clients opt into model-request history via `include_model_requests=1`; default history omits the optional event for older clients, with separate ETags. Older hosts still provide end-of-task statistics. Other channels do not receive model-request UI traffic.

## Verification

- Focused runner, hook, progress, WebSocket, transcript, and frontend regression suites cover live updates, bounded snapshots, cancellation/failure, fast tools with blocked siblings, deduplication, history replay, and compatibility.
- Latest UI-only verification: 247 focused frontend tests, TypeScript, targeted ESLint, and production build. Retired the extra status-label test along with its component, helper, unused projected phase, and ten locale strings; kept coverage for live usage, Stop, and stale-snapshot rejection.

prs.title: fix(webui): cache tool catalogs across settings navigation
prs.body:
## Why

Returning to the Tools page rebuilt its CLI Apps and MCP catalogs from empty settings-local state, so users repeatedly waited for lists they had just opened. The gateway's on-disk registry cache did not prevent these frontend requests or loading placeholders.

Resolves NAN-402

## What changed

- Retain the two catalogs in a bounded, in-memory cache scoped to the host client and current authentication token. Reentry within 30 seconds reuses them without another catalog GET; expired rows stay visible while refreshing.
- Update cached catalogs from action results, invalidate them after relevant configuration/OAuth changes and gateway readiness, and prevent superseded reads from replacing newer results.
- Preserve CLI registry-refresh and MCP connection polling across navigation, along with initial loading and retryable failures.

## Scope

Frontend Tools catalogs only. No API/protocol, gateway registry-cache, layout, or browser-storage changes. A full page reload still starts a new in-memory cache; this does not cache all settings requests.

## Tradeoffs

External changes without an existing notification may remain cached for up to the 30-second freshness window before the next page read. Background refresh keeps the last successful list visible rather than blanking it.

## Blast Radius

Apps/MCP settings reads and actions, related runtime settings invalidation, and the gateway-ready subscription. Cache identity and request generations keep other clients/credentials and older in-flight reads from replacing current catalog data.

prs.title: fix(agent): isolate inline command failures
prs.body:
## Problem

  `/status` runs inline in `AgentLoop.run()`, outside the session worker's exception handling. If session loading or runtime resolution raises an unhandled
  exception, it escapes the command handler and terminates the consumer.

  The loop then calls `aclose()`, cancelling active tasks in other sessions and closing shared resources. Under the standard gateway startup path, the runtime task
  failure also triggers gateway cleanup.

  ## Changes

  - Catch ordinary handler exceptions at the inline command execution boundary.
  - Log the failure while respecting the session's logging policy.
  - Reuse `TurnDelivery.fail()` to send a safe error response with the request's routing metadata.
  - Avoid publishing completion or idle events for an already active session.
  - Preserve existing session queue/conflict exception handling and `CancelledError` propagation.

  Successful command dispatch and response publication remain unchanged.
