## Summary

Prevent Dream from advancing its history cursor when the provider explicitly returns `refusal` or `content_filter`.

## Root cause

The runner treated a non-empty policy-blocked response as a completed turn and discarded the provider's terminal reason. Dream relied solely on that completion status, so it marked unprocessed history as consumed and reported success.

## Changes

- Preserve the provider's terminal reason in the runner result.
- Forward it through ephemeral response metadata.
- Reject policy-blocked Dream completion and report the specific reason.
- Add regression coverage for direct refusal, content filtering, refusal during empty-response finalization, and successful no-change completion.

Production changes are limited to `runner.py`, `loop.py`, and `memory.py`.

## Result

Policy-blocked Dream runs retain their cursor and pending history batch for a later attempt. Both manual and scheduled Dream use the shared completion check.

Successful no-change runs still advance the cursor. Existing turn completion semantics and policy restrictions remain unchanged.

## Test

- Before the fix: three blocked-response regression cases failed; the successful no-change control passed.
- After the fix: 224 related tests passed across Dream, runner, loop integration, command, and gateway suites.

prs.title: fix(providers): update compaction retries in place
prs.body:
## Why

Codex native-compaction retries currently create a new status row for every failed attempt. A compaction that eventually succeeds can therefore leave several failure notices above the success notice. Keep one logical compaction lifecycle across the provider request's retry attempts so clients update the existing row.

## What changed

- Share pending compaction state within one provider retry chain, emitting one start and one final success, failure, or cancellation event. Later independent compactions receive fresh IDs.
- Preserve direct provider calls, image-repair context handling, and cancellation-safe success delivery without changing retry policy or the wire format.
- Extend existing provider and browser coverage for retry success/exhaustion, cancellation during retry waits, optional compaction failure, and singular live/history rendering.

## Scope

This changes the provider-owned event lifecycle; WebUI and TUI continue consuming the existing event contract. Previously persisted duplicate notices are not rewritten. When optional compaction fails but generation continues, its notice remains pending until the retry chain settles, then reports failure rather than treating a successful answer as successful compaction.

## Verification

- Python regression tests: `pytest tests/providers/test_openai_codex_provider.py tests/providers/test_provider_retry.py tests/providers/test_strip_image_content.py -q` — 121 passed. The new retry regression failed before the fix because a failed terminal event was emitted before retrying.
- Focused WebUI tests: `vitest run src/tests/useNanobotStream.test.tsx src/tests/compaction-reasons.test.ts src/tests/thread-transcript.test.ts -t compaction` — 13 passed.
- Browser regression: `playwright test browser/history-hydration.spec.ts -g 'pre-request compaction stays in place' --workers=1` — passed, including retry waits, thread refresh, and full-page reload. Uses the existing synthetic WebSocket fixture, not a live model service.
- Focused Ruff, BasedPyright, and ESLint checks; browser TypeScript check; Python import-boundary check; `git diff --check` — passed.
- Full-project validation is left to remote CI.

- Upgrade existing archive tables to remove orphan flags and enforce references to persisted sessions. Clearing history retains archive state; deleting a session removes it.
- Earlier grouping/pane/UI expansions remain withdrawn. Frontend changes are limited to the newly requested draft archive eligibility and its tests. No separate archive page, read-only mode, compression, database, or new public interface.

## Performance

- Unchanged snapshots avoid database writes and global read barriers; actual mutations write only differences. Archive-only changes do not rewrite unchanged JSON preferences.
- Concurrent readers overlap while queued writes retain ordering. Failed/cancelled accepted writes drain their I/O before releasing admission. SQLite WAL and synchronous=FULL remain enabled.
- Prior full-path comparisons used identical synthetic workloads, five alternating rounds, dedicated data/source directories, localhost HTTP/WebSocket clients, concurrent storage, delete, heartbeat, import, and lock contention. Detailed measurements and remaining costs: [NAN-390 report](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nan-390归档-sqlite-性能实测与剩余开销-7510687ecfb2). Those measurements are bound to the preceding performance snapshot, not blanket final-head timing claims.

Per-round medians: baseline 1.32–1.40 ms; new persisted-reference enforcement 1.53–1.61 ms. Paired median increments 0.16–0.25 ms. Per-round p95 ranges 1.51–1.79 versus 1.78–1.95 ms; p99 ranges 1.62–3.65 versus 1.96–5.44 ms. These are backend store timings, not click-to-render latency or a zero-regression claim. Unchanged sidebar fast paths are retained.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): report libmagic dependency failures
prs.body:
## Why

When the `python-magic` wrapper is present but its native `libmagic` cannot be loaded, WhatsApp reports that its Python dependencies are missing. In the gateway status and WebUI QR flow, even that message is replaced by a generic failure, so the user cannot see how to fix the actual problem.

## What changed

- Distinguish missing Python modules, recognized native `libmagic` load failures, and an incompatible `magic` module. Preserve and log the original exception; unrelated import failures still propagate without being classified as missing `libmagic`.
- Surface the channel-owned actionable diagnostic in gateway status and the WebUI connection flow, with platform-appropriate guidance for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
- Add a short troubleshooting note and cover the reported failure paths. Credit @HackyRoot for the report.

## Scope

WhatsApp's lazy loading, cached SDK, and existing MIME detection behavior are unchanged. The native-library classification recognizes the `python-magic` loader's missing-library error and a `libmagic`-specific native load error; it does not guess the cause of arbitrary import errors.

## Verification

- Windows, Python 3.14: `python -m pytest nanobot/channels/whatsapp/tests -q` — 60 passed.
- Windows, Python 3.14: `python -m pytest nanobot/channels/websocket/tests/test_websocket_http_routes.py::test_whatsapp_connect_reports_libmagic_failure nanobot/channels/websocket/tests/test_websocket_http_routes.py::test_channel_connect_runtime_import_error_is_not_reported_as_unsupported -q` — 2 passed.
- Loaded the actual `python-magic 0.4.27` wheel with native library loading forced to fail in an isolated process. With a simulated macOS platform, the diagnostic suggested `brew install libmagic` and retained the original `ImportError` as its cause.
- The macOS environment and native Windows DLL failure were simulated, not tested on a real affected macOS installation. Full cross-platform checks are delegated to CI.

Resolves NAN-398

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): update Neonize for current clients
prs.body:
## Why

WhatsApp can reject the older client bundled with Neonize 0.4.3.post0 as outdated. The current `<0.5.0` constraint also causes gateway startup to replace a manually installed newer version with an older version. The reporter confirmed that 0.5.2 connected in their environment.

## What changed

- Require `neonize>=0.5.2,<1.0.0`, allowing the current 0.10.0 release as well as 0.5.2.
- Cover old-version upgrades and preservation of compatible versions, including 0.10.0, in the startup dependency check.
- Credit @edualbercas for the report and verified workaround.

## Tradeoffs

The broader range allows later 0.x releases without requiring a nanobot update, but future Neonize API changes could still require compatibility work. The 1.0 boundary remains excluded. Neonize 0.5.2 and 0.10.0 publish platform-specific wheels rather than a universal wheel.

## Blast Radius

Enabled WhatsApp channels with an older Neonize installation will install a supported newer dependency at startup. An already compatible installation is left unchanged; it is not automatically upgraded to the latest version. Other channels are unchanged.

## Verification

- Windows, Python 3.14, Neonize 0.10.0: `python -m pytest nanobot/channels/whatsapp/tests/test_whatsapp_channel.py::test_startup_preserves_compatible_neonize tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py::test_optional_dependency_metadata_for_enable tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py::test_manager_installs_manifest_dependencies_before_loading_enabled_channel tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py::test_manager_reports_dependency_install_failure_as_runtime_failure -q` — 6 passed. The 0.10.0 startup regression case failed against the earlier `<0.6.0` bound before this update.
- On an earlier PR snapshot, 54 focused tests passed with Neonize 0.10.0, including the SDK-internal callback test since removed. The actual SDK loaded, its call signatures accepted the adapter's usage, and synthetic QR and connected events reached the registered handlers. These were isolated compatibility checks, not a real WhatsApp login. `uv pip check` passed for the test environment.
- Earlier on the initial PR snapshot, the focused suite passed 53 cases with Neonize 0.5.2.
- An isolated, unauthenticated connection attempt with 0.5.2 could not reach `web.whatsapp.com` from this machine and timed out before a QR code. Real account pairing, existing-session reconnection, message/media delivery, and proxy behavior remain to be verified; the reporter's successful connection is not an independent test here.
- Full cross-platform verification is delegated to CI.

Fixes #6544
Contributes to NAN-397

issues.title: [Bug]: same stored session id can stay unended in two profile stores; Desktop/CLI resume races the shorter lineage into view
issues.body:
## Bug Description

The same **stored session id** can remain **unended in two profile `state.db` files** at once (default/root store + a named Bot Mode profile store), with **divergent transcripts**. After a gateway restart, re-host, or `hermes chat --resume`, Desktop/CLI resume is store-scoped and will happily continue whichever copy the active backend has. The operator sees a Bot Chat that has “rewound” days: the short default-store fork is what the renderer shows, while the named-profile store still holds the canonical forever-chat.

This is not fixed by Desktop `(profile, id)` row identity (#95895 / #92454). That stops twins collapsing in the sidebar. It does not stop `create_session` / `ensure_session` **upserting a naked id into the wrong store**, and it does not stop an `end_session` fence on the stale copy from being **reopened** the next time Desktop talks to the default backend under that id.

`hermes sessions repair-profiles` also misses it: it only walks `session_key LIKE 'agent:%'`. The default-store twin in the incident had `session_key` NULL, `source=desktop`, `profile_name=default`.

Related (same family, different layer):

- #54878 — stamping a live conversation `ended` makes the owner treat the route as stale and replace it. Lifecycle-aware end/adopt is required; raw UPDATEs are unsafe. Ending the stale twin is also **not durable** if the default store still receives RPCs for that id.
- #67709 — Desktop cold-start restore can resume a session into the wrong profile (closed; renderer still not a store fence).
- #92454 / #95895 — UI twins no longer collapse; backend dual-home remains.
- `tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py` documents the viewer-end → owner-replace path (#54878 / #140642).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Bot Mode with at least two local profiles (default + a named bot).
2. Build a long canonical `Bot Chat` in the named profile store (thousands of messages).
3. Restart or briefly lose the gateway. During the outage, run `hermes chat --resume <same-id>` and/or reopen Desktop so the **default** store also materializes that id (Desktop source, often `session_key` NULL).
4. Continue chatting from Desktop without confirming which store is scoped.
5. Inspect both `state.db` files read-only:

```sql
SELECT id, source, profile_name, session_key, ended_at, message_count
FROM sessions WHERE id = '<id>';
```

6. Optional: `end_session` the default-store row. Reopen the Bot tile in Desktop. The default-store row comes back live (`ended_at` NULL) and keeps accumulating the short lineage.

## Expected Behavior

- One stored session id has **one unended owner store**. Sibling stores must not insert or resume it.
- `create_session` / `ensure_session` / client-supplied resume **fail closed** if another store already has that id unended (`session_id_owned_elsewhere`), instead of minting a twin.
- `hermes sessions repair-profiles` reports `dual_home` by **stored id**, not only by `session_key`. It must not auto-move a live Bot Chat.
- Desktop restore/resume is `(connection, profile, id)` end to end; a remembered naked id must not be written into the active profile’s store when another profile already owns it.

## Actual Behavior

Observed on a live Bot Mode install (Linux, multiplexed profiles, Desktop + TUI):

| Store | `source` | `profile_name` | `session_key` | live? | `sessions.message_count` (approx) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default / root `state.db` | `desktop` | `default` | NULL | yes (reopened after an `end_session` fence) | ~180 |
| `profiles/<bot>/state.db` | `tui` | named bot | `agent:<bot>:local:dm:<id>` | yes | ~277 active / 15k+ total incl. compacted |

Desktop rendered the short default-store lineage after gateway restore (“rewound ~3 days”). Ending the default-store row with a dedicated `end_reason` did **not** hold: within minutes Desktop had `ended_at` NULL again and was still appending.

`hermes sessions repair-profiles --json` reported thousands of `routing_stray` rows and **zero** findings for this id.

## Affected Component

- Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)
- CLI (interactive chat)
- Other (Desktop Bot Mode + per-profile `state.db` + `tui_gateway` session lifecycle)

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

- N/A (CLI only)

(Local Desktop / TUI Bot Mode, not a hosted messenger.)

## Debug Report

Withheld. `hermes debug share` would upload Bot Mode transcripts and org logs. Reproduction is the dual `state.db` census above (read-only SQLite). Happy to share redacted schema/query shape privately.

## Operating System

Ubuntu Linux (x86_64), Hermes home with multiplexed named profiles.

## Python Version

Hermes runtime 3.14.9; host `python3` 3.12.3.

## Hermes Version

Install `Hermes Agent v0.22.7+98.ga66e74d (2026.9.24)` · checkout `a66e74dc67` on `main` (post-#95895). The defect is in session insert/resume, not a single release tag.

## Root Cause Analysis

`SessionDB.create_session` / `ensure_session` upsert **inside one store** (`hermes_state_sessions.py`). There is no sibling-store probe. Profile isolation is “new writes go to the scoped store” (#88734) plus renderer identity (#95895). Neither prevents a client-supplied id from being inserted into a second store, and `repair-profiles` never looks at keyless desktop twins.

Gateway routing for Bot Mode lives in the launch/default store and maps `agent:<profile>:local:dm:<id>` → `<id>`. After restart, whichever backend handles the next resume owns the visible transcript.

## Proposed Fix

Fail-closed insert fence (report-only repair finding; do **not** auto-apply a move of a live Bot Chat):

1. Before inserting a **new** row for id `S` into store `P`, read-only probe every other profile `state.db`. If any has `S` with `ended_at IS NULL`, raise `session_id_owned_elsewhere` instead of creating a twin. No-op if `P` already has the row (canonical owner continuing).
2. Add `dual_home` to `hermes sessions repair-profiles` keyed on stored id. Report-only.
3. Resume of a client-supplied id must resolve owner as `(profile, id)` and must not `ensure_session` a stub in the active profile when another profile already owns it.

A small isolated prototype of (1) is ready (sibling-store probe + tests). It should not be hot-patched onto a live gateway that currently owns the conversation.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Yes — fail-closed insert fence + `repair-profiles` report-only `dual_home` finding, with tests. Not a data-migration of existing poisoned installs.

issues.body:
Tracking issue for the staged fast-follow named in [#134889](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889)'s scope note: *"the browser dashboard and Desktop URL / Cloud / SSH modes still talk to standalone `hermes serve`."* [#106742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742) (merged Oct 14, `eb75627f`) gave every **local** surface one gateway-owned session authority per profile. This issue tracks moving the remaining entry points onto that same authority and then removing the old in-process session host.

Design: [One Gateway: Entry-Point and Session Ownership Plan](https://gist.github.com/unsupportedpastels/765f9d551ce88ee01630c18367763e75). Profile-multiplexing direction: [#109417](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/109417) (one `hermes gateway run` serves every profile).

**Status (Oct 26, after EP-1, first repros and EP-2 baseline):** EP-1 (caller map) is done, traced by code reading on `main` at `edfa1c2a`. It traced EP-8 to EP-11, split EP-11, and added EP-13 to EP-17 and D6. EP-13 and EP-15 are now reproduced in-process on `edfa1c2a` (no live gateway). 16 open rows, 2 verification rows, 6 open decisions. Nothing is in a package yet. EP-2 has a headless baseline (289 tests passed); `verify_parity2.sh` and the manual live checks need rebuilding. Other rows were checked against `main` at `d49e2ebb`; rows marked *needs repro* come from code reading only.

**Scope:** `hermes serve`, standalone `hermes dashboard`, Desktop remote modes (SSH / URL / Cloud), remaining direct agent constructors, and removal of the legacy host. **Out of scope:** the forced-migration campaign (soak, service-manager behavior, rollback window, `--force`), storage redesign, protocol unification, a replacement browser UI and a mobile client.

## Done on `main` (not tracked here)

- Local Desktop runs `gateway ensure` (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`); `5e783bde` removed code that only Desktop's own `serve` reached.
- `session.detach` is wired in `gateway/session_controls.py`.
- `SessionAuthorities` supports `add`/`remove` at runtime (`gateway/session_authorities.py`, `gateway/run_runtime.py`); see V1.
- [#141864](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/141864) serves the Desktop webapp (`apps/desktop/dist-webapp`, not `web/`) from the gateway's own listener.

## Contract under test

- Every supported entry point reaches the canonical profile authority; none starts its own session runtime.
- Closing a client removes a viewer. It never stops accepted work.
- Authorized clients can join and leave the same conversation and see the same queue, execution state and pending controls.
- Profile selection resolves an authority inside the multiplexer; `serve -p X` never launches an independent gateway for X.
- Documented callback URLs, profile-scoped auth, `--force` and standalone migration support are unchanged.
- No legacy execution fallback remains at completion.

## Legend

🔴 open, no fix · 🟡 fix PR open · 🟣 fix in review (member PR) · 🔵 waiting on a maintainer decision · ⚪ not reproduced · 🟢 fixed on `main`

## Open findings

### Stage 1: caller map and parity harness (start here)

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-1 | Caller map for `serve`. **Done at `edfa1c2a`.** One FastAPI app runs in two modes, chosen only by `app.state.gateway_runner` (`hermes_cli/web_server_app.py:234`). Only the gateway's own mount sets it (`gateway/run_api.py:96-97`), so every `hermes serve`, `hermes dashboard` and `serve --isolated` runs `standalone_lifespan` with no authority. `serve` never discovers or forwards to a running gateway, except single-session edits over `session.mutate` (`hermes_cli/web_server_sessions.py:188-234`). Results feed D1 to D6 below. | P1 | 🟢 |
| EP-2 | Parity rigs on the combined tree. **Headless baseline recorded on `edfa1c2a`** (scratch home, one pytest process per file): 31 files, 289 tests passed, about 8 min. Covers entrypoint parity and boot contract (`tests/e2e/core/parity/`), two-tenant gateway and Desktop backend (`tests/e2e/core/tenancy/`), live hot-serve (`tests/gateway/test_multiplex_hot_serve_live.py`, 7), gateway turn liveness (`tests/e2e/core/chaos/test_gateway_turn_liveness.py`, 12), and the profile-isolation, handoff, recovery and admission/replay unit tests. `tests/e2e/core/tenancy/test_routing_truth_table.py` could not run on this host (its guard refuses temp dirs under `~/.hermes`); use the CI `e2e` job result. **Missing:** `verify_parity2.sh` is not in the tree, git history or any linked issue; the #134889 "Verified working" live checks were manual and have no scripts. **Not run here:** Desktop `apps/desktop/e2e/core` (`remote-topology`, `remote-secondary`, `local-gateway-attach`) needs a GUI; CI lane `e2e-desktop-core` runs it. Next: rerun the same file set on every combined-tree candidate; rebuild network drop mid-turn, cron→compress→input and SSE approvals as scripted e2e tests. | P1 | 🔴 |

### Stages 2–3: `serve` uses the authority

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-3 | With no `gateway_runner`, `serve` selects `standalone_lifespan` and runs agents in-process (`hermes_cli/web_server_app.py:234`; comment at `hermes_cli/main.py:2598`). | P1 | 🔴 (blocked on D1, D2) |
| EP-4 | `/api/ws` sends every RPC to the legacy `server.dispatch` when no authority is present (`tui_gateway/ws.py:362-390`). With an authority, non-session verbs that the authority answers with -32601 still fall back to legacy handlers in-process (`tui_gateway/ws_legacy_fallback.py:53-64`): 100 methods go to the authority, 163 fall back, 16 are blocked. | P1 | 🔴 |
| EP-5 | New work can enter `serve` without going through the authority's admission: [#138750](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/138750). The issue's line numbers have drifted; on `edfa1c2a` the console executor is `hermes_cli/web_routers/chat_ws.py:278`, PTY spawn `:552`, action subprocesses `hermes_cli/web_server_gateway.py:475`. | P1 | 🔴 |
| EP-6 | Version skew: a new remote client's `prompt.submit` attachments are refused by an older `serve`: [#144186](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/144186). Traced: the retry strips only `submission_id`, then the legacy param model refuses `attachments` with `4000`. | P2 | 🔴 (blocked on D5) |
| EP-13 | Session-bound legacy fallback methods on authority sessions. **Reproduced in-process at `edfa1c2a`:** the authority answers -32601 for all 13, the fallback runs the legacy handler, and the handler can't find the session (authority sessions are never in `server._sessions`). 10 fail with `4001 session not found`; `tools.list` and `toolsets.list` silently ignore the session and return launch-profile data; `insights.get` isn't session-bound (it rejects `session_id` with 4000). Clients gate or translate 11 of the 13 before they reach the wire. Two still reach the server and fail silently: Desktop `image.detach` on chip removal (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/hooks/use-composer-actions.ts:922`, harmless) and ui-tui `input.detect_drop` for a dropped non-image path (`ui-tui/src/app/useComposerState.ts:339-379`), which pastes raw text instead of an attachment. `handoff.*` and `tools.configure` are refused by name client-side (feature gap). Defensive server fix: keep -32601 for these verbs in `tui_gateway/ws_legacy_fallback.py`, as already done for `session.`/`prompt.`. | P3 | 🔴 |
| EP-14 | `POST /api/cron/jobs/{id}/trigger` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py:762`) runs the job's agent inside the request thread (`cron/scheduler.py:3373`) outside admission, in both modes; the code marks the path deprecated. `POST /api/cron/fire` already forwards to the gateway. | P2 | 🔴 |
| EP-15 | `POST /api/health/retirement` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:160`) is live on the gateway listener and declares a busy gateway idle. **Reproduced in-process at `edfa1c2a`** (real dashboard app bound the way `gateway/run_api.py:75-108` binds it, a claimed admission and one running agent; runner and authority are stand-ins): `GET /api/health/idle` returns `idle: true`, `prepare` returns 200 with a token, `commit` returns 200. Afterwards dashboard JSON-RPC answers 5035 "backend is retiring", cron `tick()` dispatches nothing and the fence admits no new work until restart, while the gateway keeps running. Cause: the idle proof (`hermes_cli/web_server_idle_proof.py:39-58`, `hermes_cli/web_server_idle_exit.py:104-136`) reads only the legacy session table, delegation, cron and the fence; it never consults the gateway runner or authority, and nothing under `gateway/` takes the fence. Latent: no in-repo client calls the route, and it needs an owner or local token. Fix direction: refuse when `app.state.gateway_runner` is set, or base idleness on `gateway/run_idle_exit.py:busy_reason` and fail closed. | P1 | 🔴 |
| EP-17 | Bulk session REST (bulk delete, delete-empty, prune) writes `state.db` directly under a store-wide lock and returns 409 while a gateway owns the store, with no owner path. | P3 | 🔴 |

### Stage 4: remote Desktop and browser

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-7 | SSH mode starts `serve --isolated` and kills it on disconnect, so closing the client stops accepted work (`apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.ts:1142-1161`, `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:9486`). Every disconnect path (quit, connection switch or edit, profile delete, recycle) kills the remote process with no check for a running turn. | P1 | 🔴 (blocked on D4) |
| EP-8 | Desktop URL and Cloud modes reach whatever process the URL names; neither calls `gateway ensure`. The Docker image's dashboard service runs standalone `hermes dashboard` on 9119 (`docker/s6-rc.d/dashboard/run:52-54`). Desktop reads no `gateway_mode` or host role, so it can't tell which backend it reached. Hosted Cloud agents are inferred to match; Cloud infra isn't in this repo. | P1 | 🔴 |
| EP-9 | Standalone `hermes dashboard` chat (the sidebar's `/api/ws`, and the chat terminal when no profile is named) and its session REST use the legacy dispatcher, not the authority. A named profile attaches to the profile's gateway. *Reworded:* `ChatPage` can't reach `serve`, which is headless and doesn't serve `web/` (`hermes_cli/web_server_dashboard.py:126-149`). | P2 | 🔴 (D6) |
| EP-16 | SSH, URL and Cloud remotes send raw method names: the 13 rewrites to `session.mutate` with revision/generation checks in `canonical-protocol.ts` apply only to `native_dial` sockets. `handoff.*` is refused locally but still sent to remotes. **Fixed by #148219 (`7bc10408da`):** Desktop now selects the canonical adapter from `session_authority: true` in `gateway.ready`, so the rewrites and the `handoff.*` refusal apply to any remote that advertises it. SSH still reaches `serve --isolated`, which serves the legacy names (EP-7). | P2 | 🟢 |

### Stage 5: remaining producers

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-10 | The slash worker runs a second `HermesCLI` per session: [#141196](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/141196). Standalone backends only (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py:1070-1086`); the gateway serves `slash.exec` itself (`gateway/session_controls.py:390`). | P2 | 🔴 (D6) |
| EP-11a | `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` `_run_agent` builds a bare `AIAgent`, but it's dead code: its only caller `_run_and_exit_oneshot` is called only from tests, and `-z` goes through `launch_gateway_chat` (`hermes_cli/main.py:3020-3026`). Removal candidate. | P3 | ⚪ |
| EP-11b | `prompt.background` (`tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py:1184`) writes a separate `bg_*` session row and skips the gateway's queue check; `preview.restart` (`:1249`) builds `AIAgent` with no session store. Standalone backends only; gateway connections refuse `prompt.*` fallback. | P2 | 🔴 (D6) |

### Stage 6: remove the legacy host (after parity)

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-12 | The legacy session host still exists: `tui_gateway/server.py` (2,187 lines), `tui_gateway/agent_factory.py`, `ws_legacy_fallback`. Remove only after EP-3 to EP-17 are green and EP-2 passes. Modules named `tui_gateway` that don't host sessions stay. | P2 | 🔴 (blocked on stages 2–5) |

### Verification (believed done; needs evidence)

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V1 | Hot-added and removed profiles create and retire authorities. #134889 lists the served profile set as a start-time snapshot, but `main` now has `SessionAuthorities.add`/`remove`, driven by the `serve-profile`, `unserve-profile` and `rescan-profiles` control-socket verbs (`gateway/run_runtime.py:380`, `:459`). **Partly verified on `edfa1c2a`:** `test_multiplex_hot_serve_live.py` (7 passed) drives `rescan-profiles` against a real multiplexer, and unserve is covered at the function level (`test_run_runtime_hot_serve_cleanup.py`). No test sends `serve-profile` or `unserve-profile` by name; add one to the live test, then update #134889's "Deliberate limits". | P2 | 🔴 |
| V2 | [#109403](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109403), [#109405](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109405) and [#109412](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109412) closed unmerged. Check whether `main` covers each one's piece ([#109404](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109404)'s is covered by `session.detach`). | P3 | 🔴 |

## Decisions to settle

| ID | Decision | EP-1 input | Gates | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Which existing startup/discovery path does `serve` reuse, and when does it start the owner versus forward to it? | `gateway_runner` is in-process only, so forwarding means a proxy, and that needs identity forwarding (D2). The evidence favors remote clients attaching to the gateway listener directly (it mounts the same app and auth), with `serve` as a launcher that uses control-socket discovery (`identify`, `session-ticket`). Blockers: `/api/ws` accepts loopback only; no remote ticket path. | EP-3, EP-4, EP-7, EP-8 | 🔵 |
| D2 | Can owner-side authentication preserve current deployments without delegated identity forwarding? | Yes if the gateway authenticates clients itself; it already runs the same auth stack. No if `serve` forwards: tickets, the session token and cookies are process- or origin-bound, so a forwarder collapses every user into one identity. Missing on the gateway: the SSH `--isolated` token and owner nonce, the Desktop env token, the rendezvous-record token, and carrying `dashboard.public_url` to `webapp.public_url`. | EP-3, EP-8 | 🔵 |
| D3 | Which legacy capabilities need mappings before their callers can move? | Of 254 legacy methods: 75 mapped, 14 partial, 163 legacy fallback, 2 refused (`agents.list`, `session.activate`). Gaps: EP-13 (reproduced: 2 client-reachable, both silent); no authority verb tears a session down like `session.close`; host-wide services (pet, projects, MCP, vault, voice, billing, connectors, group replica/peer) run in the owner process outside admission. | stages 2–5 | 🔵 |
| D4 | Which web/SSH changes are inseparable from keeping those entry points supported? | SSH options: (a) run remote `gateway ensure --json` and tunnel to the gateway, with a capability probe and fallback to isolated `serve`; (b) interim: keep isolated `serve` but stop killing it on quit or window close, relying on its 900 s idle retirement and existing reattach. | EP-7, EP-9 | 🔵 |
| D5 | What explicit migration behavior covers version skew and unsupported legacy operations? | No version handshake exists; Desktop infers canonical vs legacy from `?native_dial`. `gateway.capabilities` exists in the contract but no client uses it. Hosted-room peers' `protocol_versions` plus per-capability flags is a working model. | EP-6 | 🔵 |
| D6 | Is authority-less `serve`/`dashboard` still a supported host? If not, fence that backend instead of fixing each producer. | — | EP-9, EP-10, EP-11b, EP-17 | 🔵 |

Open question: [#109417](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/109417) closed Sep 21 with no successor found for its forced-migration gates. This tracker doesn't own those gates; it needs to know whether they're met before EP-12.

## Not tracked here

These are separate operational work, not prerequisites for removing the alternate owner: extracting an execution-host interface from the messaging runner, independent adapter supervision, moving storage off the event loop, durable event retention and idle-session eviction.

## Working rules

- Work is grouped into package issues by stage; each package lists its rows, prerequisites, consumers and acceptance evidence.
- Reproduce on current `main` before fixing; no repro means no commit, plus a ⚪ note here.
- PRs use `Refs #<this issue> (EP-n)`, never `Fixes`.
- If an entry point already meets the contract on `main`, mark it 🟢 and leave the code alone.
- Stop and add a 🔵 row when a slice needs a new framework or an unplanned auth/lifecycle policy.

## Found a problem? Report here

Comment on this issue with: `main` SHA, Desktop version if involved, surface and mode (serve / dashboard / SSH / URL / Cloud / browser), OS and topology, steps, expected, actual, and the relevant lines from `gateway.log`, `errors.log` and `desktop.log`. Redact tokens, cookies, tickets and session URLs.

issues.title: kanban: stranded_running heartbeat-age rule + worktree-exclusivity guard for multi-agent fleets
issues.body:
## Context (fleet incident, 2026-11-03)

We run a multi-agent fleet (several `hermes` profiles dispatching kanban tasks) and hit a real collision that `hermes kanban diag` cannot currently see:

- A child task's session operated for **hours inside the parent task's assigned worktree** while the parent card sat in `running` — stashing the parent session's WIP, force-pushing the parent task's branch (mid-acceptance), and recreating scratch files that broke the parent's pre-push gate twice. Nothing in `kanban diag` detects any of this: the parent is `running`, so `stranded_in_ready` (correctly) excludes it, and no other rule covers "running with no liveness evidence".
- Reflog/stash forensics confirmed it: `reset: moving to HEAD` at 09:25, stash popped, foreign commits appearing inside the window.

## Proposal 1 — `stranded_running` heartbeat-age rule in `kanban_diagnostics.py`

Complement to the existing `_rule_stranded_in_ready` (same file, same shape: age-based, identity-agnostic, config-threshold):

- Fires when a task is `status == running` for >= a configurable heartbeat-age threshold **with no liveness evidence** — no recent `kanban heartbeat` stamp event (the stamp already exists as `hermes kanban heartbeat`), no claim/progress event in the window.
- The fleet already stamps heartbeats, so the liveness primitive exists; the rule just needs to consume its event age.
- Config alongside the existing key (see #140661 — the diagnostics section is undocumented; include docs in scope): e.g. `kanban.diagnostics.stranded_running_heartbeat_seconds`.

## Proposal 2 — worktree-exclusivity (assignment lock)

The incident above is a **worktree-exclusivity gap**: nothing prevents a session (especially a child task's) from committing, stashing, and force-pushing inside another task's assigned worktree. The dirty-tree refusal in external sweeps protects files from *deletion*, but nothing guards *concurrent mutation* — the parent's acceptance loop silently failed twice on corrupted state.

Minimum viable shape: `hermes kanban` worktree operations (claim/attach/commit helpers) validate that the operating profile matches the task's assignee (or hold an explicit lease), and warn/refuse otherwise. Related: #148002 (prune protection is directory-name-based and unlogged — same family: worktree identity is weakly enforced).

## Proposal 3 — cross-reference, not duplicate

External stack sweeps (devsecops tooling) already reclaim task-scoped Docker stacks two-phase (containers → volumes) and never read task status; the Hermes-side **teardown-notification hook** belongs with #148546, which we've commented on rather than re-filed.

## Evidence trail

- Tester incident report + forensics (stash/reflog timeline, third-session commits signed with the parent profile's stamp, child task `kanban:t_c2f81fa7`).
- Parent task stuck `running` through the entire window; two acceptance-loop runs silently failed on corrupted state before the humans noticed.

Happy to provide reflog excerpts, commit shas, or the fleet topology if useful.

issues.body:
## Summary

Hermes today lives in the terminal, the desktop app, the web dashboard, and 20+ messaging
platforms. What is missing is a **first-party mobile app (Android + iOS)** that makes the agent
a genuine always-with-you assistant rather than a bot you text.

A phone is the one device the user always carries, so it is where the agent's *senses*
(location, voice, camera, notifications) and its *approvals* naturally belong. This request
covers the app itself, an explicit **location consent model (allow / deny)**, and
**real-time speech-to-speech voice**, plus a set of improvements that fall out of putting
those three together.

## Motivation

Right now a Hermes assistant is effectively reachable but not *present*:

- **Notifications are one-way in practice.** The agent can send a message; getting a decision,
  an approval, or a quick correction back requires opening a chat client and typing.
- **Location is all-or-nothing.** The only practical paths are OS-level phone linking
  (e.g. Microsoft Phone Link on Windows) — which many users disable for privacy — or manually
  sharing a location in a chat. There is no documented, per-request consent model, and no clear
  behaviour for how a shared live location appears to the agent.
- **Voice is turn-based.** Voice notes and STT/TTS are supported, but there is no low-latency,
  interruptible, hands-free conversation like the real-time voice modes users now expect from
  Gemini / ChatGPT.
- **Long-running work is invisible.** Cron jobs, delegated subagents, and background runs
  complete somewhere else; the phone shows nothing until a message lands.

## Proposed feature

### 1. First-party mobile app (Android + iOS)

- Thin client over the existing gateway / API server — **execution stays server-side**, the phone
  is a control surface. No duplicated agent runtime on the device.
- **Device pairing by QR code** against an existing profile/gateway, with per-device scopes.
- Full session continuity: list sessions, switch profiles, resume a conversation started on the
  desktop, and stream replies live.
- Rich rendering: markdown, tables, code, files, images, charts; file upload/download.
- Deep linking (`hermes://session/...`), share-sheet target (send text/image/URL *into* Hermes).
- Platform niceties:
  - **iOS**: Share extension, App Intents + Siri Shortcuts, Live Activities / Dynamic Island for
    running tasks, Action Button / Control Center shortcuts, watchOS companion.
  - **Android**: share target, notification quick-reply, home-screen widgets, Quick Settings
    tile, Tasker / automation intents, Wear OS companion.
- Offline behaviour: queue outbound messages/approvals, reconnect cleanly, never silently drop an
  approval decision.

### 2. Location sharing with explicit allow / deny

- **Default: off.** Location is off until the user turns it on for a specific scope.
- Consent UI mirroring the OS model, but per-profile and per-purpose:
  `Allow once` · `Allow while using the app` · `Allow for this task` · `Deny` · `Revoke`
  — plus the ability to revoke at any time from a "what the agent can see" screen.
- **Approval-gated reads.** A location read triggered by the agent raises a request; the user
  approves or denies. A standing opt-in is allowed but must be visibly indicated in the session.
- **Coarse-by-default output.** Prefer derived, non-identifying values the user actually wants:
  `home / office / en route / away`, distance from a saved place, ETA — rather than raw
  coordinates. Raw coordinates only with an explicit higher tier of consent.
- **Geofence events instead of tracking.** For location-triggered automations ("arriving home",
  "left the office"), the app should emit an *event* (`arrived`, `departed`) computed on-device
  rather than exposing a coordinate stream.
- **Privacy defaults**: never persist coordinates; short TTL on any cached position (e.g. 5 min);
  treat coordinates as PII in redaction; clear entry in the audit log for every read; no silent
  or continuous background collection.
- When unavailable, deny, or stale: return **"unavailable"** and never substitute a guessed
  location.

### 3. Real-time voice conversation

- **Speech-to-speech** over a duplex transport (WebRTC or the provider's realtime API) with
  low latency, **barge-in/interruption**, and natural turn-taking — the Gemini / ChatGPT voice
  experience, but backed by the user's own Hermes profile (tools, memory, skills).
- **Push-to-talk as the default**, hands-free/continuous as an opt-in (driver mode).
- Tool use *during* voice: the agent can run a tool mid-conversation and speak the result
  ("what's on my calendar", "how much did I spend on that SMS batch").
- Voice as a full input channel, not a transcription side-channel: streaming partials,
  multilingual + code-switching (Korean/English at minimum), user-selectable voice and speed.
- Same session as text — a voice turn and a typed turn belong to one conversation.

### 4. Approvals and long-running work as first-class mobile UI

- Push notifications for: approval requests, cron job results, delegated task completions,
  failures — with **1-tap approve/deny** from the notification and a deep link into context.
- **Live task view**: cron/subagent/background run status, streaming output, cancel button.
- Audited action log: what the agent did, when, with what approval, and where the artifacts are.

## Additional improvements worth including

1. **Presence over position.** A single "what may the agent know about where I am" setting with
   three tiers (none / coarse / precise) is more usable and privacy-preserving than per-app
   toggles, and maps cleanly onto geofence events.
2. **Signed, replayable approvals.** Approval decisions should carry device identity and be
   recorded in the audit log, so "who approved this side effect" is answerable later.
3. **Quiet hours and urgency.** Notification routing should respect the calendar and the
   profile's working hours; failures and security events bypass quiet hours.
4. **Emergency card (offline).** Medical notes and emergency contacts stored locally, readable
   without network — high value for personal-assistant / caregiver use cases.
5. **Session handoff.** Continue on desktop, finish on phone, without forking the transcript.
6. **Camera / screen as opt-in senses.** "Look at this" (photo → agent) with per-use approval,
   same consent framework as location. Useful for forms, receipts, error screens.
7. **Multi-device, one profile.** Phone, watch, desktop, and chat platforms as views of the same
   session, with per-device scopes and remote device revoke.
8. **Accessibility first.** Large-type mode, one-handed operation, screen-reader labels — the
   users who need an always-on assistant most are often the ones least served by small UIs.
9. **Cost and rate visibility.** Show the profile's model, spend, and rate-limit state in-app so
   surprises are visible before they happen.
10. **Local-first option.** Allow a fully local backend (loopback/LAN gateway) so nothing leaves
    the user's network when they choose that mode.

## Relationship to existing work

Inbound location handling already appears partially supported on some platforms
(`fix(telegram): handle live locations in the background` #66280,
`docs(telegram): document inbound sticker/location-pin/album behaviors` #78740,
`feat(matrix): receive native location shares` #125901,
`fix(feishu): normalize share_location messages with coordinates` #82935).

**At minimum, documenting how a shared live location currently reaches the agent (shape, cadence,
availability) would close most of the gap for users who cannot install an app.** The mobile app
then makes that behaviour explicit and consent-driven instead of incidental.

Voice Mode already exists for CLI, Telegram, and Discord; the mobile app is where real-time
speech-to-speech becomes genuinely useful (backgrounded, hands-free, interruptible).

## Suggested implementation paths

- Reuse the existing **gateway + API server** as the only agent runtime; the app talks to it.
- Reuse the **desktop app's plugin/permission model** so mobile and desktop stay consistent.
- Push via **FCM / APNs**; a small "notification → approval action" endpoint on the gateway.
- Location and geofencing handled **on-device** (OS geofencing APIs), with only derived events
  leaving the phone.
- Realtime voice: provider-agnostic adapter (realtime WebSocket/WebRTC) so OpenAI/Gemini/local
  backends can all be plugged in, consistent with Hermes' provider-agnostic design.

## Scope / non-goals

- No silent tracking, no background coordinate collection, no location history by default.
- The phone does not become a second agent runtime with divergent memory — one profile, one
  source of truth.
- Not a replacement for the desktop app or the messaging gateway; a complement.

## Environment context

- Hermes on Windows 11, profile-based setup (personal-assistant bot on Telegram), multiple
  profiles for separate channels, cron jobs delivering reports, local STT/TTS in use.
- The users this would benefit most are non-developers running assistant/caregiver profiles who
  live on their phones, not in a terminal.

issues.body:
# Upstream Bug Report: hermes-agent MCP client silently drops tool-call arguments (SSE)

## Summary

The hermes-agent's MCP-over-SSE client **silently drops the arguments of tool calls**, causing the target server to execute tool functions with only their default parameter values. The server receives the call (executes and returns a normal response), but the arguments never arrive. The gateway sees no error — the failure is invisible to the caller. The defect manifests intermittently after a period of session uptime, and as of 2026-11-03, **persists even after full session re-registration and gateway restart**.

## Environment

- **hermes-agent**: commit `bf0203a794` (from `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/.git/HEAD`)
- **Gateway**: `hermes gateway` with api_server platform on `172.17.0.1:8642`
- **MCP server**: OfficeMCP v1.0.5 (`fastmcp==4.1.5`) on `http://127.0.0.1:8888/sse` (Windows host, WSL mirrored networking)
- **MCP config**: `~/.hermes/config.yaml` → `OfficeMCP: url: http://127.0.0.1:8888/sse, enabled: true` (14/14 tools enabled)
- **Transport**: SSE (FastMCP's `/sse` endpoint + `/messages/?session_id=...` POST)

## Reproduction

The defect is **intermittent** — hours between occurrences — but has been observed **five times in two days** with a clean isolation:

### The three-probe diagnosis (separates the layers)

| Probe | Method | Result (always) |
|-------|--------|-----------------|
| 1. Direct raw MCP call to the server | Raw JSON-RPC over SSE (initialize → tools/call with explicit `code` argument) | **Arguments always delivered** — the server executes the code correctly |
| 2. `hermes mcp test OfficeMCP` | The gateway's built-in connection test | **Tools enumerate correctly** — the config and connectivity are fine |
| 3. Lane-level task (a real tool call through the gateway agent) | `POST /v1/responses` → the agent calls the MCP tool | **Arguments dropped** — the server receives the call with empty/default arguments |

This isolation proves: the **server and transport are healthy**; the drop happens inside the **gateway's MCP client session**.

### Evidence from five occurrences (2026-11-02 → 2026-11-03)

**Occurrence 1** (2026-11-02, email compose):
- Agent report: *"the tool dropped my `code` argument on every invocation and ran only its default snippet"*
- The agent fell back to a PowerShell COM detour, which the gateway's consent gate blocked

**Occurrence 2** (2026-11-03, battery O1/O2):
- Agent report: *"the harness delivered my tool_call arguments as empty on 9 consecutive attempts"*
- PowerShell fallback: *"held for user consent and timed out"*

**Occurrence 3** (2026-11-03, user's email task):
- Same args-dropped pattern; the agent's PowerShell fallback executed the compose successfully

**Occurrence 4** (2026-11-03, during the officemcp-connection-error fix verification):
- The first W0 probe (a trivial RunningApps query) timed out at 300s with the sidecar down
- After recovery, the retry passed in 5s — intermittent

**Occurrence 5** (2026-11-03, during the `deploy all` battery):
- After a **full reset** (kill OfficeMCP process + fresh start + COM warm-up via direct call + `hermes mcp remove/add` + `hermes gateway restart`), the gateway's calls **still arrived with empty arguments** on most probes (only 1 of 10 office-lane probes succeeded)
- This is the critical finding: the defect **persists after full session re-registration**, which previously cleared it

### The recovery procedure (now insufficient)

The following used to clear the defect every time (3 recoveries verified on 2026-11-02 → 2026-11-03 morning):
```bash
hermes mcp remove OfficeMCP
yes | hermes mcp add OfficeMCP --url http://127.0.0.1:8888/sse
hermes gateway restart -y --detach
```

As of occurrence 5 (2026-11-03 afternoon), this procedure **no longer clears the defect** — the gateway's tool calls continue to arrive with empty arguments immediately after a clean re-registration + restart.

## The dropped data

The MCP server's `RunPython` tool signature:
```python
def RunPython(code: str = "\nprint(f'hello world from {data}')\noutput=data\n", data: str = "OfficeMCP") -> dict:
```

When the arguments are dropped, the server executes the **default** code (printing "hello world from OfficeMCP") and returns `{"success": true, "output": "Execution completed"}` — a **normal, successful response with wrong data**. The gateway never sees an error, which makes the failure invisible to both the agent and the caller.

## Suspected mechanism

The SSE POST to `/messages/?session_id=...` carries the tool-call arguments as a JSON-RPC request body. The server receives and processes the call (proven by the default-snippet execution), but the `arguments` field arrives empty. Possible causes inside the hermes-agent MCP client:

1. **Serialization**: the client's JSON serialization of tool-call arguments may fail silently (e.g., a type-coercion or encoding issue), sending the method name but emptying the params
2. **Session state**: the SSE session's message-routing table may lose the argument routing after the session state degrades
3. **Threading/async race**: the MCP client may have a race condition between argument construction and the SSE POST

The defect is **not** in:
- The MCP server (direct raw calls always deliver args)
- The SSE transport (byte-clean; the POST reaches the server)
- The mirrored networking (WSL loopback is stable)
- The Dify/sidecar layer (the directive construction is upstream and correct)

## Impact

Every Office-lane turn silently fails — the agent retries (observed: 4-9 consecutive empty deliveries), burns the 300-600s turn budget, or falls back to a PowerShell detour that the gateway's consent gate blocks. The user sees "no response" or a confusing partial failure. The agent cannot execute any real Office task while the session is degraded.

## Workaround

- **Detection**: the agent's instructions include a "SESSION-DEGRADATION RULE" (stop retrying after 2+ consecutive default-echo returns; report `TASK: FAILED — OfficeMCP session stale` with the recovery steps). A battery pre-flight (W0) detects a degraded session in <10s.
- **Recovery**: the re-registration + restart procedure (now only temporarily effective)
- **Bypass**: direct raw MCP calls to the server always work (verified in every occurrence)

## Request

Please investigate the MCP client's tool-call argument serialization and session state management. The three-probe isolation (raw call works → mcp test works → gateway agent call drops args) should pinpoint the layer. The defect is reproducible with any MCP server using the SSE transport — it is not OfficeMCP-specific.

At Hermes `58d146e961108e84f41bfed59f586121ecb3372c`, install a custom subdirectory plugin without `--ref`, for example `hermes plugins install briancaffey/hermes-otel/hermes_otel`. The sidecar correctly records the source and revision with `pinned: false`, but the installed subdirectory has no `.git`.

`hermes plugins check-updates` reports class `drift` and advises reinstalling. Reinstallation repeats the same condition. In contrast, `hermes plugins update hermes_otel` succeeds and reports already up to date. Both behaviors were exercised on the same install.

Source: `plugins_provenance.py` classifies row-only installs as DRIFT, and `plugins_updates.py:check_local_provenance` returns that warning before checking the recorded source. `plugins_cmd_update.py:_pull_plugin_update` explicitly handles this legitimate no-`.git` case by invoking `_reclone_plugin_update` with the sidecar source.

Expected: read-only check-updates recognizes installer-owned subdirectory installs and checks their approved recorded source, consistently with the actual update path, without requiring fabricated Git metadata. Preserve the existing provenance and update-URL trust checks.

issues.body:
## Summary

`hermes update` fails during dependency resolution when the same plugin is installed into more than one profile home. The updater builds a uv workspace from installed plugin sources, and uv rejects two members that share a package name.

```
Preparing the isolated Hermes runtime…
  ✓ Installing Python dependencies
  ✗ Resolving Python dependencies failed; last 1 lines of output:
      error: Two workspace members are both named `hermes-telemetry`:
        .../workspace/plugin-sources/hermes-telemetry-4860c944135caca8
        .../workspace/plugin-sources/hermes-telemetry-4f5b6ba2a2de0995
```

The update aborts before anything is installed, so the runtime stays on the old version with no partial state.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.5 (2026.8.19), install method: git, Python 3.11.16
- Linux, system-scoped gateway unit, two profile homes under `~/.hermes/profiles/`

## Reproduce

1. Install the same plugin into two profile homes, e.g. `HERMES_HOME=~/.hermes/profiles/<a> hermes plugins install <source>` and again for `<b>`. (A deployment script that installs its plugin set into every served profile produces this naturally.)
2. Run `hermes update`.
3. Dependency resolution fails with the duplicate workspace member error above.

## Observation

In our case the copies are not divergent versions — all installed copies are byte-identical (same content digest, same `version = "0.8.0"` in `pyproject.toml`). The hashed directory suffixes differ while the package name does not, so uv sees two distinct members with one name.

Per-profile plugin copies appear to be the intended layout: each profile home owns its own `plugins/<name>/` tree, and installing per profile is how profile-scoped enablement works. If that is correct, the updater's workspace assembly and the per-profile install layout are in conflict.

## Expected

`hermes update` succeeds when a plugin is installed in several profile homes. Some possibilities, in rough order of preference:

1. Scope the workspace to the profile being upgraded rather than every profile home.
2. Deduplicate identical plugin sources by content hash before adding workspace members.
3. Give each member a unique workspace name (e.g. qualify by profile) when several copies must participate.
4. Fail with an actionable message naming the owning profiles and the remediation, if duplicates genuinely cannot be supported.

## Workaround

None applied here. Deleting or relocating one of the copies would likely unblock resolution, but that mutates a profile's installed plugin set to work around a packaging-layer restriction, so we stopped and filed this instead.

## Note

Upgrading matters for us because plugin-registered slash commands get no bound session identity on v0.20.5 (`gateway/run.py`, the `get_plugin_command_handler` dispatch calls the handler without binding session context). That is already fixed in newer code — `gateway/run_inbound.py` wraps the same dispatch in `_session_env_scope(...)` — so this issue is only about the updater failure that blocks reaching that fix.

issues.title: [Bug] Hermes ships multiple split Python environments (Docker AND plain install) — shell / skill / pip all see different worlds; operators must hand-stitch HERMES_SITE
issues.body:
## Bug Description

The Docker image ships **three distinct Python environments** that are only usable when manually stitched together at process start, and every shell/terminal/skill entry point sees a *different, incomplete* world. This makes the container fundamentally hostile for operators, skill scripts, plugin development, and project development alike.

**UPDATE: this is NOT only a Docker problem.** The same split-Python-worlds defect exists on a plain (non-container) install — see issue #125040 (PATH resolves the PM tool-Python before the dependency venv, breaking `import yaml` in skill scripts; reported against a non-Docker install). On a home install we measured the same root cause: `python` in a Hermes terminal session resolves to the PM-managed private Python (3.14.x, `sys.prefix == sys.base_prefix`, no venv), while the user's system Python (e.g. Miniconda tools, 3.10) sits unused on the side; anything installed into the system Python is invisible to the Hermes terminal; anything Hermes needs lives in `~/.hermes/installs/*/environments/*/venv`, which no plain `python` sees without manually reading facts.json and constructing the path. Docker merely adds a third interpreter and makes it worse, but the root cause predates containers.

The three environments on `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.5`:

1. **System Python** — `/usr/bin/python` (bare, few packages).
2. **Image venv** — `/opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python` — at the **front** of PATH; this is what `python` in any shell resolves to.
3. **Dependency-generation venv** — `/opt/data/installs/<id>/environments/<generation>/venv` — where plugins and lazily-installed extras (lark_oapi, mem0, qrcode, …) actually land.

The gateway process is launched from the **image venv** and only becomes "complete" by reaching into a generation venv via `site.addsitedir(os.environ['HERMES_SITE'])`:

```
/opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python -P -c "import os, site, sys; ... site.addsitedir(os.environ['HERMES_SITE']); ..." gateway run --replace
```

## Steps to Reproduce (in the container)

1. `docker exec hermes python -c "import yaml"` → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'`, even though PyYAML/ruamel is installed in the active generation venv.
2. `python --version` resolves to the PM tool Python (`/opt/hermes/tools/python-3.14.9.../bin/python3.14`), not any venv.
3. `pip install <anything>` in the container installs into the image venv — which the docs declare **sealed/immutable** — so project dependencies are installed into a tree PM will never see and may refuse to write at all.
4. Skill scripts that shell out to `python3` get the half-environment and fail on `import yaml`, `import lark_oapi`, etc. — identical root cause as #125040 (PATH ordering + tool-Python shadowing), now amplified in the container where THERE ARE THREE environments, not two.
5. There is no single command an operator can run to know "which python has my dependencies" — you must read `facts.json` → `.packages.venv.environment` and construct `/opt/data/installs/*/environments/*/venv/bin/python` by hand.

## Expected Behavior

An operator (or skill script, or project dev flow) in the container should get **one** coherent Python environment on PATH:
- `python` should resolve to the active dependency generation's venv (the same one the gateway actually uses), and
- `pip install` should target an environment Hermes will actually load (or at least fail with a clear instruction), and
- shell/skill/terminal tool python must see the same site-packages as the gateway process.

## Actual Behavior

- `python` (image venv / tool Python) ≠ gateway interpreter (image venv + HERMES_SITE overlay) ≠ dependency venv. Three worlds, none of them complete alone.
- `import yaml` fails in shell but works in the gateway — an operator cannot reproduce/verify anything from the shell.
- Plugin dependency installs land in `/opt/data/installs/*/environments/*/venv`, invisible to any non-gateway python unless HERMES_SITE is manually exported.
- Reclaiming superseded generations requires a container restart (`collect_generations` runs from stage2 on boot); a long-running container accumulates multiple 2 GB generations with no in-process GC schedule.

## Environment

- Docker: image `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.5`, `docker compose up -d`, single data volume `/opt/data`, reproduction as `hermes` user (uid 10000)
- Plain install (non-Docker): home install, Hermes terminal session; same split-Python defect (see #125040)

This is a continuation of the same class of problem as #125040 (terminal tool PATH picks the PM tool-Python and breaks `import yaml` in skill scripts). The container makes it strictly worse: three environments instead of two, plus a sealed image venv that turns `pip install` into a trap. **The non-Docker installs are affected by the same root cause — this is architectural, not container-specific.**

Long-term, please consider: **one writable venv per install that IS the PATH python and IS the gateway interpreter**, rather than a sealed image venv + per-generation venvs + a manually exported HERMES_SITE overlay.

issues.title: [Bug]: Update check's downgrade guard lazy-fetches on git < 2.44: `hermes --version` takes 40 s and the status cache does not help
issues.body:
### Bug Description

On a blobless git install with git older than 2.44, `hermes --version` takes about 40 s when an update is offered
and the release commit is not in the local object store yet. macOS ships git 2.39, so a stock Mac is affected.

The passive update check runs the downgrade guard (`_hold_refused_release` → `_update_refuses` → `would_refuse`),
whose two git probes have a 20 s timeout each. `source_git_env()` sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, but git older than
2.44 ignores it, so both probes lazy-fetch from the promisor remote until they are killed.

The visible failure was Desktop's 15 s `--version` probe timing out, which showed first-run setup on a healthy
install. #148498 reports that symptom on macOS from a different cause (slow `git status` on a large repo), and
#79087 reports it on Windows. This cause does not depend on repo size or machine load:

- Skipping the update check in Desktop's probe (#148498, PR #139468) would stop the setup screen but leave
  `hermes --version` at 40 s.
- Moving the cache check earlier would not help, because `_hold_refused_release` also runs on a status-cache hit
  (`source_check.py:555-559`). This part comes from reading the code; I measured the 40 s, not a cache-hit run
  on its own.

#138404 reported the same class of problem for `_head_containing`; the downgrade guard is a separate call site.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. macOS with the system git 2.39.5 (or any git older than 2.44), installed with `scripts/install.sh` (blobless
   clone, `remote.origin.promisor=true`).
2. A release newer than the checkout is published, and its commit is not in the local object store yet.
3. `time ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/.hermes/bin/hermes --version` takes about 40 s and ends with
   `Update available — run 'hermes update'`.
4. With Desktop open, run `hermes gateway restart`. Desktop looks up its backend again, the probe times out, and
   the first-run setup screen appears.

### Expected Behavior

`hermes --version` answers quickly whatever the network or git state, and a read-only update check never downloads
from the promisor remote.

### Actual Behavior

`~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log`:

```
2026-11-02 18:40:49,570 [hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend
2026-11-02 18:40:49,652 [hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes runtime
2026-11-02 18:41:34,671 [hermes] [bootstrap] no usable Hermes install at ~/.hermes/hermes-agent and no published user-bin launcher
2026-11-02 18:41:34,672 [hermes] [boot] Waiting for first-run setup choice
```

The checkout was clean and unchanged throughout.

### Affected Component

CLI (update check), Desktop (backend lookup).

### Debug Report

```
version:  0.22.5+2610.g0e8d470 [0e8d4708] (2026-10-28)
os:       Darwin 27.0.0 arm64
python:   3.14.9
git:      2.39.5 (Apple Git-154)
install:  git, blobless clone (remote.origin.promisor=true, partialclonefilter=blob:none)
```

The `hermes debug share` logs are not attached because they include private chat text. I can share specific log
lines on request.

### Operating System

macOS 27.0 (Apple silicon)

### Python Version

3.14.9

### Hermes Version

`Hermes Agent v0.22.5+2610.g0e8d470 (2026.9.24) · stable · local 0e8d47084818`, install method git.

### Root Cause Analysis

Line numbers are from `main` at `aac7f1b696`, which has the same code.

- `hermes_cli/_startup_fast.py:187-228`: `print_fast_version_info(check_updates=True)` runs
  `check_for_updates(passive=True)` synchronously.
- `hermes_cli/source_check.py:555-559`: on a status-cache hit, `check_for_updates` still calls
  `_hold_refused_release`, as it does after a fresh check (`:577`).
- `hermes_cli/source_check.py:376-392`: `_update_refuses` gives `would_refuse` a git runner with `timeout=20`.
- `hermes_cli/update_downgrade_guard.py:58` runs `merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD <release>` and `:61` runs
  `rev-list --objects --no-walk --sparse --missing=error <release> -- <state modules>`.
- `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py:282-283`: `NO_LAZY_FETCH_ENV`, with the note that older git ignores it.
- `apps/desktop/electron/source-backend.ts:47` probes `--version`; the default timeout is 15 s
  (`backend-probes.ts:9`).

Running `git -C ~/.hermes/hermes-agent cat-file -t <release sha>` once fetched the commit. After that,
`hermes --version` returned in 0.51 s.

### Proposed Fix

1. When git cannot be stopped from lazy-fetching (older than 2.44), skip the guard's local git probes in the
   passive check. It could use the `remote` answer `would_refuse` already accepts, or treat the relation as unknown.
2. On the Desktop side, keep the update check out of the liveness probe, as #148498 and PR #139468 propose.

Workaround from #148498: `hermes config set updates.check false`. The gate at `source_check.py:537` returns before
any of this runs.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.body:
### Summary

A process-completion watch tied to one Discord thread is refused with `admission_conflict` **every 60 seconds, indefinitely** — 494 occurrences in a single gateway log, still firing after 6 hours. Two things that should stop it don't:

1. **The attempt cap never fires.** `_MAX_COMPLETION_INJECTION_ATTEMPTS = 8` (`gateway/run_notifications.py:68`) should produce one `"completion for … was refused 8 times; falling back to the notify_mode=… notice"` line per eight refusals. In the same log there are **3** such lines against **494** refusals — so the loop producing this pair is not running the capped path.
2. **`display.background_process_notifications: off` has no effect on it.** Set on disk and confirmed read by a fresh process (`False`), the loop continued at the same cadence. Restarting with the value already `off` at boot (so a fresh worker snapshots it) still continued.

The loop also survives gateway restarts and a live turn in the affected thread.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.22.4`, Python 3.14.7, Ubuntu (kernel 6.8.0), single profile, **not** multiplexed
- Platform: Discord (thread), `chat=1562977450600702004`, guild `1548996776000888852`
- Session: `20261022_235423_95462272`, `chat_type=thread`, `origin.user_name=selig` (not null), no `end_reason`, `expiry_finalized=0`

### Log signature

```
19:59:23,834 INFO  gateway.run: Watch pattern notification — injecting for discord chat=1562977450600702004 thread=1562977450600702004
19:59:23,840 WARNING gateway.run: Watch notification not admitted for discord chat=1562977450600702004: admission_conflict
20:00:24,203 INFO  gateway.run: Watch pattern notification — injecting for discord chat=1562977450600702004 thread=1562977450600702004
20:00:24,207 WARNING gateway.run: Watch notification not admitted for discord chat=1562977450600702004: admission_conflict
```

Inter-line gaps measured over 20 consecutive ticks: `60, 60, 61, 60, 60, 61, 60, 60, 61, 60, 61, 60, 60, 60, 61, 60, 61, 60, 60, 19` — flat 60s, the `_COMPLETION_INJECTION_RETRY_MAX_DELAY` value. The refusal lands **4 ms** after the inject line, so it is a deterministic state check, not a transient race.

Sequence from the start of the episode (backoff restarts on every boot):

- First refusal `2026-10-23 16:12`; the `gateway_routing` row for that session was rewritten at **16:08:15**, four minutes earlier, while the session's `runtime_generation` was 17.
- Restart #1 (18:15): pid 160 → 128391. Refusals resumed 25 s later, backoff restarting from 4 s: `4, 8, 16, 32, 60, 60, …`
- Live turn in the thread at 19:58:15 (`msg='hello'`): response delivered, session grew 126 → 129 messages, `runtime_generation` **17 → 18**, routing row re-stamped at 19:58:20. Next tick refused anyway.
- Restart #2 (20:03) with `display.background_process_notifications: off` already on disk: pid 128391 → 135018, 9 refusals in the first 5.7 minutes at the same 60s cadence.

### What I ruled out

- **Poisoned admission record.** No `RETIRED_PREFIX + session_id` rows, no `gateway.terminal_admission.v1.*` rows anywhere in `state_meta`. `session_admissions` has 18 rows for the session, all `status=terminal`, `outcome=completed`, newest at `generation=18`.
- **Stale route/generation mismatch alone.** Bumping the generation with a real turn (`17 → 18`, route re-stamped in the same second) did not change admission.
- **Pruning the session.** `hermes sessions prune --chat-id …` skips it (open session); and no storage-side change should matter, since the retry reads routing from the queued event (`"Routing comes from the queued event, never the active foreground message"`).
- **Config mode gate.** See above — off at boot, confirmed `False` by `load_user_config_effective`, made no difference. There is no `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS` env override and no `profiles/` directory.
- **Watcher attempt cap.** 494 refusals vs 3 `falling back to the notify_mode` lines.

### Suspected area

`gateway/run_notifications.py` — between `_drain_watch_notifications` (mode gate at `:733`, requeue via `_requeue_refused_watch_event`, no counter) and `_run_process_watcher` (`:1763`, capped at `_MAX_COMPLETION_INJECTION_ATTEMPTS`). The observed behaviour (60s flat, no cap, mode-independent, rearmed at boot) matches a requeue loop that has neither the cap nor the mode gate, with the event reconstructed at startup.

### Impact

Log churn only — nothing is delivered, no agent turn is produced, and the affected session works normally for real messages. At one line pair a minute it is ~2,900 log lines/day and it masks real watch notifications for that thread.

### Related

- #140189 — undeliverable process-completion notification retried forever, no backoff/cap (5s cadence, Feishu, multiplexed)
- #143447 — automation wakes refused `admission_conflict` forever when the lane's profile route postdates the session origin (matches the 16:08 route re-stamp here)
- #143306 — shared Discord thread speaker changes strand pinned completion wakes with `admission_conflict`
- #142402 — background-process completions refused when the stored origin's `user_name` is null (here it is `selig`, so not this one)
