issues.body:
## Bug Description

On a Windows Desktop install with one very large stored session, the Desktop repeatedly shows
`会话控制不可用: request timed out after 30s: session.control.read` ("session control unavailable").
The same 10-minute window also logged 30s client timeouts for `session.interrupt` (x5) and
`session.resume` (x2), and **every** WebSocket connection in that window was torn down with
`reason=send_failed_after_response`.

The failing RPC itself is *not* slow — `session.control.read` costs ~1.6 ms of DB work here. What
happens is that it is queued behind a genuinely slow handler on the same connection, because
`_dispatch_loop` dispatches **one request at a time per connection**, and the slow handler in this
environment is `session.context_breakdown` evaluated over a 9,501-message transcript.

Chain (all on `main`, commit `868b9f244f`):

1. `apps/desktop/src/api/client.ts:26` — `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`.
2. `apps/shared/src/json-rpc-channel.ts:295` — rejects with `request timed out after 30s: <method>`.
3. `apps/desktop/src/store/session-control.ts:736-800` — `refreshSessionControl()` polls
   `session.control.read`; `publishFailure()` turns the rejection into the UI message.
4. `tui_gateway/ws.py:94-98` + `406-429` — requests are dispatched **serially, in arrival order,
   one per connection** (only `gateway.ping` bypasses the queue, `ws.py:509`). Any slow handler
   therefore delays every later RPC on that socket.
5. `gateway/session_ancillary.py:192-215` — `read(kind='control')` runs on the loop thread, takes
   `live.event_stream.lock` (a `threading.RLock`) and then calls the synchronous
   `control_snapshot()` (`session_ancillary.py:387-415`, 3 x `db.get_meta`).
6. `gateway/session_tui_reads.py:133-170` — `context_breakdown` performs
   `db.get_messages_as_conversation(stored, include_ancestors=True)` and then
   `compute_session_context_breakdown()` (`agent/context_breakdown.py:143-181`), which calls
   `build_system_prompt_parts(agent)` and `estimate_messages_tokens_rough(messages)` over the
   **entire** transcript — while holding the connection's single dispatch slot.
7. The Desktop polls it whenever the session view is idle and retries on a ladder
   (`apps/desktop/src/app/shell/hooks/use-context-breakdown.ts:133-188`), so the slow request is
   re-issued after each reconnect.
8. When the server finally writes that reply, the client has already given up, so
   `tui_gateway/ws.py:88-92` (`_WS_SEND_DEADLINE_S = 30.0`) / the dead socket fails the write:
   `ws response send failed ... method=session.context_breakdown` → `ws closed
   reason=send_failed_after_response` → every other in-flight RPC on that socket is rejected
   (`Hermes gateway connection closed` / `connection changed; reopen the session`).

Note the two 30 s deadlines race each other: `_WS_SEND_DEADLINE_S = 30.0` is exactly the Desktop's
30 s RPC timeout, so a slow reply can never win, and the user gets a phantom "request timed out"
instead of an honest disconnect.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Windows 11 Desktop install, single local profile, latest `main`.
2. Have a session whose stored transcript is very large (here: 9,501 rows in `messages`,
   `state.db` = 215 MB / 54,882 pages, WAL 4.7 MB).
3. Open that session while idle so the context meter issues `session.context_breakdown`.
4. While that RPC is in flight, let any other RPC land on the same socket
   (`session.control.read` poll from the status stack, `session.interrupt`, `process.list`).
5. Observe: the later RPC hits the client's 30 s deadline; shortly after, the server logs the
   failed write for the *first* method and closes the connection.

## Expected Behavior

- One slow read-only RPC must not starve unrelated RPCs on the same connection.
- A read-only control snapshot must never make the event loop wait on a `threading.RLock` or a
  synchronous SQLite read.
- A timing-out RPC should surface as its own error, not silently cost the whole socket.

## Actual Behavior

- `session.control.read` (~1.6 ms of work) reports `request timed out after 30s`.
- `session.interrupt` / `session.resume` in the same window also time out at 30 s.
- Every WS connection ends with `send_failed_after_response`; the user sees the session-control
  card report "unavailable" and has to reopen the session.

## Affected Component

Other: Desktop ⇄ `tui_gateway` RPC transport (per-connection serial dispatch) + `Agent Core`
context-breakdown computation on long sessions.

## Debug Report

`hermes debug share` upload is deliberately not used by this reporter (it uploads config and
logs). Everything needed to reproduce is inline below: exact commit, OS/Python, the log lines, and
the measurements. Local log paths: `logs/agent.log`, `logs/errors.log`, `logs/desktop.log`.

## Operating System

Windows 11 (Desktop app, `win-unpacked`)

## Python Version

3.14.7

## Hermes Version

`868b9f244f` — `feat: add deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 to OpenRouter and Nous catalogs`,
2026-10-17 04:38 -0700. Working tree == `origin/main` (0 ahead / 0 behind).

## Additional Logs / Traceback

Measured, not inferred:

- 3 x `state_meta` primary-key reads (the whole of `control_snapshot`) on this `state.db`:
  **1.6 ms** — so the timing-out RPC is innocent.
- Raw `fetchall()` of the 9,501 rows of the largest session, fresh process, no lock contention:
  **1.91 s** — a *lower bound* for step 6, which additionally builds per-row dicts over 30 columns
  (several JSON blobs: `api_content`, `reasoning_details`, `display_metadata`,
  `codex_reasoning_items`, `tool_calls`), parses them, and rebuilds the system prompt per poll.
- Client-side 30 s timeouts in one 10-minute window (`desktop.log`):
  `session.interrupt` x5, `session.resume` x2.
- Connection teardowns in the same period — 8 of 8 with `reason=send_failed_after_response`, and
  the method whose reply failed to write: `session.context_breakdown` x6, `model.options` x1,
  `setup.status` x1 (the last two during a Desktop restart).
- `state.db`: `journal_mode=wal`, 54,882 pages, 17,848 messages total, largest session 9,501.

A second, independent squeeze on the same process is also present (see #133830): the post-turn
background review fork runs as a full turn sharing the gateway process —
`thread=bg-review:22008`, `origin=background_review`, `calls=4 in=13305 out=9768 cache_read=678272`.
It cannot explain a `session.context_breakdown` reply missing its write deadline, but it makes the
window tighter on this host.

## Root Cause Analysis

Two independent design choices compose badly:

1. **Per-connection serial dispatch** (`tui_gateway/ws.py:406-429`): correct for ordering, but it
   makes handler latency additive per socket. One expensive read-only handler is enough to push
   every later RPC past the client's deadline.
2. **Synchronous work on the loop thread inside a handler**
   (`gateway/session_ancillary.py:192-215` and `387-415`): `session.control.read` takes a
   `threading.RLock` and performs SQLite reads without `asyncio.to_thread`, so it also blocks the
   loop for every other connection while it waits.

`session.context_breakdown` amplifies both: its cost scales with transcript length
(O(messages) query + O(messages) token estimate + a full system-prompt rebuild), and the Desktop
re-issues it on every idle mount and after every reconnect.

## Proposed Fix

Ranked, each independently useful:

1. **Keep the loop free.** In `gateway/session_ancillary.py:192-215`, run the snapshot body via
   `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` and do not hold `live.event_stream.lock` across a DB read —
   `control_snapshot()` reads persisted `state_meta` only, so the stream lock is not needed for it.
2. **Do not let one handler own the socket.** Give `_dispatch_loop` bounded concurrency (e.g. a
   per-connection `asyncio.Semaphore(4)` around `_dispatch_request`), or route known-expensive
   read-only handlers (`session.context_breakdown`, `session.usage`, `tools.show`) through the
   LONG pool instead of awaiting them inline.
3. **Make `context_breakdown` cheap or off-path.** Cache the payload keyed by
   `(session_id, last message id / count)` and invalidate on append, or publish it as an event
   after the turn instead of serving it as a polling RPC.
4. **Add server-side duration telemetry.** There is currently no per-RPC handler timing anywhere,
   which is why this class is undiagnosable from logs alone. A `>2 s` warning with `(peer, id,
   method)` in `_dispatch_loop` would have identified this in one run.
5. **Make the two deadlines ordered.** `_WS_SEND_DEADLINE_S = 30.0` equals the Desktop's 30 s RPC
   timeout; a strictly smaller server deadline (e.g. 25 s) would surface an honest disconnect
   instead of a phantom timeout, and would keep the "which side gave up" question answerable.

## Not a duplicate of

- #132546 — LONG-handler *pool* has no per-task timeout. Different path: authority handlers are
  awaited inline in `_dispatch_loop`, they are not scheduled on `server._pool` (`server.py:200-201`).
- #133830 — background-review forks competing with live chats. Real on this host (proven above),
  but it cannot produce a `session.context_breakdown` reply that misses its own write deadline.
- #108154 — bounding the WS send backlog: that is the write side, not dispatch serialization.
- #121865 / #121904 — reconnect ladder and poll out-dialing: fixed, and already in this build.

issues.body:
# Bug Report: `computer_use` fails with `cua-driver session setup failed: fileno`

## Summary

`computer_use` tool fails immediately during backend session setup with:

```
RuntimeError: cua-driver session setup failed: fileno
Caused by: UnsupportedOperation: fileno
```

This occurs even though `cua-driver` is correctly installed, the daemon is running, and `cua-driver doctor` reports healthy. The failure is specific to the MCP stdio client spawning `cua-driver mcp` in environments where `sys.stderr` has been replaced with a non-fileno stream (e.g., `execute_code`, test harnesses, captured REPLs).

## Environment

- **Platform**: macOS (darwin)
- **Hermes**: installed at `~/.hermes`
- **cua-driver**: `0.28.2` (system), also `0.21.0` pinned by PM
- **Python**: `3.14.7` (Hermes runtime)
- **MCP SDK**: vendored in Hermes venv at:
  `~/.hermes/installs/.../venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/mcp/client/stdio.py`
- **Triggering condition**: any execution context that replaces `sys.stderr` with an `io.StringIO`-like object (no `fileno()`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open any Hermes session that uses `execute_code` or captures stderr.
2. Run `computer_use` with `action: capture` (or any action that triggers backend startup).
3. Observe:

```
computer_use backend unavailable: cua-driver session setup failed: fileno
```

### Minimal Reproduction

```python
import sys
import io
import asyncio

# Simulate execute_code-style stderr capture
sys.stderr = io.StringIO()

# Now start the backend
from tools.computer_use.cua_backend import CuaDriverBackend
backend = CuaDriverBackend(permission_mode="standard")
backend.start()
# -> RuntimeError: cua-driver session setup failed: fileno
```

### Verified Non-Reproduction

Running the same backend start from a normal shell where `sys.stderr` is a real `TextIOWrapper` succeeds through MCP session setup.

## Expected Behavior

`computer_use` should start the cua-driver MCP session successfully regardless of whether the host Python process has replaced `sys.stderr` with a non-fileno stream.

## Actual Behavior

Session setup crashes inside `mcp/client/stdio.py` because the default parameter `errlog: TextIO = sys.stderr` binds to a non-fileno stream. When `anyio.open_process` / `subprocess.Popen` tries to create the subprocess stderr pipe, it calls `stderr.fileno()` and raises `io.UnsupportedOperation`.

## Root Cause

In `mcp/client/stdio.py`, `stdio_client` uses a **mutable default argument bound at function-definition time**:

```python
async def stdio_client(
    server: StdioServerParameters, errlog: TextIO = sys.stderr
) -> AsyncGenerator[TransportStreams, None]:
```

When `sys.stderr` is later replaced with a non-fileno stream, the default argument still references that replaced object. The subprocess spawn path then fails because it requires a real file descriptor.

Traceback excerpt:

```
File ".../mcp/client/stdio.py", line 125, in stdio_client
    process = await _create_platform_compatible_process(...)
File ".../mcp/client/stdio.py", line 342, in _create_platform_compatible_process
    return await anyio.open_process(..., stderr=errlog, ...)
File ".../subprocess.py", line 1779, in _get_handles
    errwrite = stderr.fileno()
io.UnsupportedOperation: fileno
```

## Proposed Fix

Change the default to `None` and resolve the real stderr at call time:

```python
@asynccontextmanager
async def stdio_client(
    server: StdioServerParameters, errlog: TextIO | None = None
) -> AsyncGenerator[TransportStreams, None]:
    if errlog is None:
        errlog = sys.__stderr__
```

`sys.__stderr__` is the original interpreter stderr file descriptor and remains valid even when `sys.stderr` is monkeypatched.

### Why this fix

- Preserves existing behavior for normal callers (no `errlog` passed).
- Avoids binding to a mutable/modifiable global at definition time.
- `sys.__stderr__` is guaranteed to be the real file object; it is not replaced by `execute_code`-style capture.
- Minimal diff, no API breakage for callers that already pass `errlog` explicitly.

## Additional Notes

- `cua-driver doctor`, `manifest`, `status`, and `sessions` all pass because they use synchronous `subprocess.run` and do not rely on the MCP stdio transport.
- The failure is in the **MCP client stdio transport**, not in cua-driver itself.
- There is also a version mismatch: Hermes PM pins `cua-driver 0.21.0` under `~/.hermes/tools/`, while a newer `0.28.2` exists at `~/.local/bin/cua-driver`. The `fileno` failure reproduces with both versions, so this is orthogonal, but should ideally be reconciled.

## Suggested Upstream Actions

1. Patch `mcp/client/stdio.py` to resolve `errlog` lazily instead of binding `sys.stderr` at import time.
2. Consider whether `stdio_client` should accept `errlog=None` semantically and treat it as “no errlog” or “real stderr” consistently across POSIX/Windows.
3. Optionally add a regression test: replace `sys.stderr` with `io.StringIO()` and assert `stdio_client` can still spawn a trivial server subprocess.

issues.title: [Bug]: graceful restart wait ignores running async delegations; they are interrupted with most of the drain cap unused
issues.body:
### Bug

The graceful restart wait (#77184, `_await_active_work_before_restart` in `gateway/run_shutdown.py`) builds its wait set from chat turns, cron jobs, managed, API and deferred workers (`gateway/run_shutdown.py:1570-1605`). Running **async delegations** (`tools.async_delegation`) are not in that set. So the restart waits for the parent's chat turn to end, then proceeds, and the final cleanup interrupts every background delegation (`interrupt_all`, `gateway/run_shutdown.py:~1783`).

The idle check in the same file already counts them (`_delegations_active` → `async_delegation.active_count()`, `gateway/run_shutdown.py:332-334`), so the two disagree: delegations keep the gateway from scaling to zero, but don't delay a restart.

### Observed (v0.22.6-432-g2dbeda872f, macOS, multiplexed local gateway)

A scheduled `hermes update` restart:
```
05:04:53 Restart requested with 1 active work unit(s); deferring stop() until they finish (cap=1800s) ... (#77184)
05:06:11 Restart deferred wait complete — active work drained; proceeding to stop()
05:06:20 Shutdown (final-cleanup): interrupted 2 background delegation(s)
05:06:20 Subagent 0 raised KeyError after 3004.7s
```
A 50-minute builder delegation was lost with about 1,700 s of the 1,800 s cap still unused.

### Proposal

Add `("async_delegation", active_count())` units to the restart wait set, as awaitable work bounded by the same `restart_after_turn_timeout` cap. Delegations past the cap are interrupted as today.

issues.body:
Three things from daily use of the Android beta app (`ai.nousresearch.hermes.mobile`):

### 1. Voice messages (outbound audio bubbles)
The app can record voice input, but the agent can't send a voice bubble back — `hermes_mobile` has no outgoing audio path at all. Would love a proper voice bubble: TTS on the gateway side (the `tts` provider is already configurable) delivered as playable audio in the chat, ideally with an inline waveform/player and a way to turn it off per chat.

### 2. More expressive agent avatar in the chat header
The avatar in the chat header is small and static. It would be nice if it could be:
- **larger**, and
- **animated / stateful** — e.g. idle, thinking, speaking, working (the gateway already emits activity state, so the header could react to it), plus an occasional idle animation so the character feels alive instead of being a static icon.
Support for a custom avatar per agent/profile (image or short animated asset) would make this land for people who run multiple agents.

### 3. Cleaner chat screen
The chat screen feels visually busy: tool cards, thinking blocks, timestamps, folded turns and message bodies all compete at the same weight. Suggestions:
- tighter, lower-contrast treatment for tool/thinking rows, collapsed by default with a subtle summary line
- more breathing room around assistant text, consistent spacing
- fewer borders/outlines around the message area
- a "compact" density option alongside the current one

Happy to share screenshots and compare against what other chat UIs do if that helps scope it.

issues.title: [Bug] `providers.<name>.enabled` is honored, yet every load warns "unknown config keys ignored: enabled"

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

issues.body:
### Summary

`providers.<name>.enabled` **works correctly** but is reported as **ignored** on every config load:

```
WARNING hermes_cli.config: providers.<name>: unknown config keys ignored: enabled
```

The warning is technically about a real drop — `_normalize_custom_provider_entry()` does discard the key — but the key's **effect has already been applied one step earlier, from the original entry**, so nothing is actually lost. The log line says `ignored`, which reads as "this key does nothing", and that misreading has already produced a false bug report (see below).

### The two-step flow (this is why the warning is misleading)

`hermes_cli/config_providers.py`, `providers_dict_to_custom_providers()` (~line 303):

```python
for key, entry in providers_dict.items():
    if isinstance(entry, dict) and not is_provider_enabled(entry):
        continue                                   # ← decided HERE, on the ORIGINAL entry
    normalized = _normalize_custom_provider_entry(entry, provider_key=coerce_provider_id(key))
    if normalized is not None:                     # ← warning raised HERE, on the normalized copy
        custom_providers.append(normalized)
```

1. `is_provider_enabled(entry)` reads the original dict, so a disabled provider is correctly skipped.
2. Only *enabled* entries reach `_normalize_custom_provider_entry()`, where `enabled` is absent from `_KNOWN_PROVIDER_KEYS` and the warning fires.

So the key is honored; it is simply dropped from a normalized copy that no longer needs it. `is_provider_enabled()` is also consulted directly by the runtime resolver, `doctor`, and the model-picker post-pass — all on the original mapping.

### Where the warning comes from

`hermes_cli/config_providers.py`, `_KNOWN_PROVIDER_KEYS` (line 114):

```python
_KNOWN_PROVIDER_KEYS = {
    # ``provider`` duplicates the ``providers.<name>`` mapping key and is unused here, but Hermes'
    # own config writer has historically emitted it. Accept it so self-written configs don't warn.
    "provider",
    "name", "api", "url", "base_url", "api_key", "key_env", "api_key_env", "key_cmd",
    ...
}
```

`enabled` is absent, so the `unknown = set(entry.keys()) - _KNOWN_PROVIDER_KEYS - ...` check at line 207 flags it:

```python
unknown = set(entry.keys()) - _KNOWN_PROVIDER_KEYS - set(_CAMEL_ALIASES.keys())
if unknown:
    _warn_once_per_provider(
        provider_key, "unknown:" + ",".join(sorted(unknown)),
        "providers.%s: unknown config keys ignored: %s", ...)
```

Note the comment above `"provider"`: the set already accepts a key purely to keep self-written configs quiet. `enabled` has a stronger claim than that one — it is documented behavior with several consumer sites, not a legacy artifact.

### Why this matters (not just log noise)

**#104322** was filed as *"[Bug]: `providers.<name>.enabled: false` is silently ignored — key dropped by `_KNOWN_PROVIDER_KEYS` and flipped to true"* and was closed 11 minutes later by its own author after retesting showed the key works. That author read this warning, concluded the feature was broken, and spent a round-trip on a non-bug. The wording invites exactly that error: it names a real drop without mentioning that the effect was already applied a step earlier.

### Steps to reproduce

```yaml
# config.yaml
providers:
  my-provider:
    enabled: false
    base_url: https://example.invalid/v1
    api_key: ${MY_PROVIDER_KEY}
    models:
      - some-model
```

1. Start Hermes (or run any command that loads config).
2. Observe: `providers.my-provider: unknown config keys ignored: enabled`
3. Observe the opposite of what the warning implies — the provider is correctly hidden from `/models` and the runtime resolver.

### Suggested fix

Add `"enabled"` to `_KNOWN_PROVIDER_KEYS`, mirroring the existing `"provider"` entry:

```python
    # ``enabled`` is applied by is_provider_enabled() before normalization (see
    # providers_dict_to_custom_providers); the normalized copy intentionally drops it, so don't
    # warn about a key whose effect has already been honored.
    "enabled",
```

### Verification performed

Reproduced on `main` at commit `536802c00e` (`_KNOWN_PROVIDER_KEYS` still lacks `enabled`; the warning string is still emitted).

Direct calls against the real functions — this is what pins down the mechanism, since the key is not merely "tolerated", it is applied *before* the drop:

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `_normalize_custom_provider_entry({..., "enabled": False})` | emits `unknown config keys ignored: enabled`; returned dict has **no** `enabled` key |
| `is_provider_enabled({"enabled": False})` | `False` |
| `is_provider_enabled({"enabled": True})` | `True` |
| `is_provider_enabled({"enabled": "false"})` | `False` (quoted form handled) |
| `is_provider_enabled({})` | `True` (default) |

So the warning is accurate about the normalized copy and wrong about the feature — which is precisely the confusing part. A `debug`-level note would be fine here; a `WARNING` naming the key is not.

I'm happy to open the one-line PR if that's the preferred path.

issues.title: _strip_provider_prefix drops a configured provider name from "::"-style model IDs, so context-length lookup misses
issues.body:
With a provider named `tensorzero` in `config.yaml` (a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint), the model `tensorzero::function_name::mechanical` reaches the context-length lookup as `:function_name::mechanical`.

`_strip_provider_prefix` in `agent/model_metadata.py` splits on the first `:` and strips the prefix when `get_provider_profile(prefix)` returns a profile. Any name under `providers:` resolves to the generic custom profile, so `tensorzero` is treated as a provider and stripped. Every lookup then misses, and the context length falls back to 256,000 tokens.

Symptoms:
- `Could not determine context length for model ':function_name::mechanical' ... falling back to 256,000 tokens` on every gateway boot.
- The same warning for other TensorZero functions (`bigread`, `integration`) on turns that use them.

Suggested fix (untested): skip the strip when the suffix begins with `:`. `x::y` is never `provider:model`.

Related: #102425 (`custom:` prefix in capability lookup), #137991 and #94696 (256K fallback). None of them covers this case.

Environment: Hermes Agent v0.22.6 (f0d94882e89a), macOS.

issues.body:
## Summary
On the Android beta app (`ai.nousresearch.hermes.mobile`), long assistant messages render **truncated** (tail cut off) whenever reasoning / "thinking" panels are enabled. Switching the chat style between bubble and classic/plain does **not** fix it — as long as thinking rows are shown, message text gets eaten. With thinking display turned off, the exact same message renders in full.

## Environment
- App: Hermes Mobile Android beta, package `ai.nousresearch.hermes.mobile`
- Device: Android 16
- Gateway: self-hosted hermes-agent on Android/Termux, `hermes_mobile` adapter (local pairing), model `deepseek-v4.1-flash` via an OpenAI-compatible provider

## Steps to reproduce
1. Settings → Chat → Chat Visibility → enable **Thinking** (tool calls on or off both reproduce).
2. Ask the agent for a reply of ~400+ characters, with a unique sentinel at the very end (I used `【EOF-TEST-0007】` followed by `完`).
3. Open that conversation and scroll to the message.

## Expected
The whole message, including the sentinel, is displayed.

## Actual
The message is cut off mid-way; the last paragraphs and the sentinel are missing, with no "show more" affordance. Changing Settings → Chat → Bubbles between the two styles changes the visuals but not the truncation. Turning thinking display off makes the same message display completely.

## Server-side check
The message is stored **in full** in `state.db` (425 chars including the sentinel) and the history payload returned by the gateway is intact. So this looks like a client-side rendering / height-measurement problem in the message list when thinking rows are present (possibly the row height is measured before the thinking panels collapse or expand).

## Notes
Reproducible on every attempt on this device. Happy to provide logcat or a screen recording if useful.

prs.title: fix(groups): run cross-machine group chats without Desktop again
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

**The problem.** From v2026.8.31 to v0.22.0, a group chat could include bots from several computers, say a laptop and a home server, and keep running with Desktop closed. The gateway that owned the group chat sent each turn to the other computer's bot itself (#99007, #99099, #99244). Since v0.22.1 (#106742), the gateway refuses bots from other gateways, so this stopped working:

- creating a group chat with bots from two computers fails (#141178, #142248, #144634);
- existing cross-machine group chats wouldn't open after the update, and their history was hidden (#142926).

#148418 (on `main`, not yet in a stable release) brings these group chats back, but only while Desktop is open, because Desktop now passes every message between the two gateways. Quit Desktop or let the laptop sleep, and the group chat stops until Desktop is back.

**What changes.** The owning gateway can again seat a bot from another gateway. Each bot still answers from its own computer, but the owning gateway keeps the conversation and decides whose turn it is, so **the group chat keeps running with Desktop closed**, as it did before v0.22.1. When you come back, the replies are in the group chat.

The PR also covers the cases that break between computers:

- a reply lost between the two gateways doesn't make a bot answer twice;
- Stop reports only what the other gateway confirms;
- Disband works while the other computer is offline: its access is revoked once it can be reached again, or lapses when it expires;
- bots on the other computer show what they're doing, like local bots.

This is the gateway half. Desktop doesn't create these group chats yet. That comes in the Desktop half, a follow-up that offers this option under **New group chat** and keeps #148418's Desktop-driven group chat as the fallback. Until then, you set one up by hand with the JSON-RPC steps in the Bot Mode guide.

## Related Issue

Refs #142248
Refs #141178
Refs #142926
Refs #144634
Refs #97681

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

On `main` the canonical gateway always reports `room_link: {enabled: false, reason: 'canonical_driver_required'}` (`gateway/session_group_controls.py`). That was set in 3e896bc390, while the canonical gateway had no group driver yet (`driver: False`). The driver has since landed, but `room_link` stayed off, so seating a peer works only on the standalone `hermes serve` surface. This PR builds on #99244's room grants and peer transport, which are still on `main`, and wires them into the canonical gateway. It changes no picker code.

- **Seating** (`gateway/session_group_peers.py`, `gateway/session_group_controls.py`, `tui_gateway/contracts/canonical.py`): `groups.peer.invite` and `groups.peer.revoke` are operator-only on the member's gateway; `groups.peer.register` needs the group chat owner's control permission and binds the grant to the pinned member, catalog, profile and endpoint after a scoped live probe. Grants are never sent to another endpoint or echoed in errors. Invitation minting is shared with the existing HTTP route (`api_server_room_grants.py`).
- **Capabilities:** these owner/lender rules apply to the canonical gateway (`hermes gateway run`), including when `hermes serve` forwards Desktop's group calls to it. The home owns a peer group chat when `groups.capabilities` reports `driver: true`, `persistent_process: true` and `groups.peer.register` in `methods`; the home needs no `room_link.enabled` of its own. Lending a bot is advertised separately by `room_link.enabled: true` with its catalog/endpoint and `groups.peer.invite` in `methods` (default profile, API server, durable run storage, grant secret, supported execution policy, endpoint), with the reason when it can't. Standalone `hermes serve` answering for its own group chats derives `persistent_process` from its lending catalog and skips API-server and endpoint checks for `room_link`; clients should not use it as a home for gateway-owned group chats.
- **Renewal:** invitations take an optional `status_ttl_seconds` (up to 30 days, `peer_renewal_horizon` feature). Active routes renew at dispatch, and `hermes serve` accepts and forwards the field unchanged. Renewal compares, saves and publishes under the same lock as registration and Disband.
- **Lost replies and Retry** (`tui_gateway/hosted_room_driver.py`, `hosted_room_peer_http.py`): a lost or conflicting admission reply stays uncertain instead of being requeued; recovery and deferred Retry use the original generation (inside main's generation fence), each turn reads its own run, and re-registration keeps a route's trace and cancellation identity.
- **Stop** reports only what the member gateway confirms; an unconfirmed running Stop becomes deferred after the recovery window, so other group chat work can go on.
- **Disband while a member is offline:** the group chat ends locally. Its routes are dropped and the revokes it owes are recorded in the same transaction, then retried by a bounded worker (one per cycle, 3-second total deadline, at most four outstanding attempts, backoff to an hour) until the grant is revoked or expires. Registration and renewal get a retryable `room_disbanding_retry` while Disband runs. A Stop failure leaves the group chat undisbanded with its routes intact; if the later tombstone write fails after route retirement, the group chat remains undisbanded with routes dropped and revokes owed.
- **Live state:** peer bots report their current tool and last progress time through the existing run poll, like local bots under #148422's live member state; a recovered attempt shows while the member gateway confirms it is running, and a refused Retry keeps its progress.
- The admission, observation, Retry, Stop, renewal and revocation fixes also apply to RoomLink group chats on `hermes serve`.
- **Docs:** `website/docs/user-guide/bot-mode.md` and `apps/desktop/docs/canonical-groups.md`: gateway-owned cross-machine group chats vs Desktop-driven ones, and the JSON-RPC setup sequence.

This continues the cross-gateway text lifecycle from #100016 and the client-side lost-reply work from #99960, rebased on current `main` (`7b55a7c236`, 3 November, after #148418 and #148422). Main's generation-fenced Retry, stalled-preparation Retry, standalone-to-owner forwarding, committed Send acknowledgment, discussion budgets and pre-submit attachment refusals all stay in place.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_session_group_peers.py tests/gateway/test_hosted_room_disband_publication.py tests/tui_gateway/test_hosted_room_peer_recovery.py tests/tui_gateway/test_groups_renewable_forward.py`: seating, renewal, Disband windows and lost-reply recovery. `test_home_without_room_link_can_register_and_run_a_lent_member` proves that a home advertising `room_link.enabled: false` still registers a member from a lending gateway and publishes its reply; adding a home-side `room_link.enabled` gate makes it fail.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_hosted_room_two_gateway_scoped.py tests/gateway/test_session_group_peer_setup_daemons.py`: two real gateways in temporary `HERMES_HOME`s. A lost admission reply runs the peer's turn once (twice with the uncertainty fix reverted). An interrupted setup, an owner restart and a peer restart still end with one seated member, one reply, and the grants revoked on Disband.
3. By hand, two computers each running `hermes gateway run`: on the bot's computer enable the API server and set `gateway.room_link_url`, then follow the JSON-RPC sequence in the Bot Mode guide (create the group chat on the home, `groups.peer.invite` on the member, `groups.peer.register` on the home). With no Desktop running, `groups.send` an `@all` message to the home: both machines answer and the group chat settles.

Branch suite: 531 passed, 0 failed across 52 files. Each fix commit's regression test fails with its product change reverted, and the owner/lender test fails when registration is gated on the home's `room_link.enabled`.

## Limits

- Text-only peer turns to the member gateway's `default` profile; off-loopback endpoints need HTTPS. New group chat seating is the separate Desktop half.
- An invitation that never reached the home has no revoke debt; it lapses at its own dispatch expiry (at most 24 hours), and only the operator who minted it holds it.
- A `hermes serve` group chat disbanded while its member was offline keeps its revoke debt in that machine's standalone store, paid whenever `hermes serve` runs again; otherwise the grant lapses at its own expiry.
- A grant replaced by renewal stays valid until it expires (exact revocation is separate work); Disband still owes the scope revoke.
- The peer lifecycle test can hit open `main` bug #143302 (a message sent as the previous discussion settles gets no turn) until its fix lands.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (the branch's 52 targeted files and their neighbours, not the whole suite)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A

prs.title: TypeScript LSP starts 2 processes instead of 4, same diagnostics (port omo#11756)
prs.body:
TypeScript code checking used to start four background programs per project, two of which Hermes never talks to; one of them also quietly downloaded type packages from npm. Now it starts only the two it uses, with the same error reports.

**Outcome:** each TypeScript workspace's language server drops from 4 processes / ~520 MiB to 2 / ~210 MiB with identical diagnostics.

Port of code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent#11756 (shipped in their train #11766).

## Changes
- `agent/lsp/servers.py::_spawn_typescript` sends `tsserver.useSyntaxServer: "never"` and `disableAutomaticTypingAcquisition: true` in both trust modes; the untrusted-workspace SDK pin (`tsserver.path`) is unchanged.
- `lsp.servers.typescript.initialization_options` still overrides both keys (existing `_make_spec` merge), so the old behaviour is one config entry away. Documented in `website/docs/user-guide/features/lsp.md`.
- Tests: new `tests/agent/lsp/test_typescript_lean_defaults.py` (defaults sent; user keys win), red on base 1/2. `test_workspace_trust.py`'s trusted-workspace assertion now checks the actual invariant (no Hermes SDK pin when trusted) instead of `init == {}`.

## Live repro (real typescript-language-server 6.x from `~/.hermes/lsp`, Hermes `LSPClient`, a.ts with a type error)

| | init options | node children | child RSS | diagnostics |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, trusted | `{}` | 3 (semantic tsserver, syntax tsserver, typingsInstaller) | 536 MiB | `Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'.` + unused-var |
| main, untrusted | `{tsserver:{path}}` | 3 | 507 MiB | same |
| head, trusted | `useSyntaxServer:never`, `disableAutomaticTypingAcquisition` | 1 (semantic tsserver) | 211 MiB | same |
| head, untrusted | same + `path` | 1 | 209 MiB | same |

Root cause: typescript-language-server's defaults run a syntax-only tsserver for editor-latency features (folding, outline) and an automatic typings installer; Hermes only requests diagnostics.

## Ours vs theirs
- omo had to first fix their config merge so builtin `initialization` defaults reached `initialize` at all; Hermes' `_make_spec` already merges builtin base + user overrides, so the port is the defaults only.
- They also moved tsserver onto the host Bun runtime (#11758); not applicable (Hermes runs servers on its managed node).

Tests: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/lsp` 117 passed, 1 skipped. `scripts/check --only health` ok.

prs.title: fix(gateway): bind persisted supervisor commands to the install root
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes gateway restart` / `install` (and `gateway run`'s boot-time refresh) invoked through a dependency generation's venv console script runs with `PROJECT_ROOT` inside `installs/<key>/environments/<gen>/workspace` — so the unit/plist it persists pins that GC-able workspace launcher, whose install key has no committed environment. The supervised service then crash-loops with `no dependency environment is committed` (#131164) and dies for good once `collect_generations` reaps the tree. The same launcher contract exists in the launchd plist, so macOS is exposed too.

This fixes the class in both directions — it never poisons a definition again, and existing poisoned definitions get healed:

- **Canonicalize (primary)**: a root under `installs/<key>/environments/<gen>/` maps back to the owning checkout via the install state's `inputs/.project-root` stamp (validated against the install-key path hash, fail-closed), so a venv-invoked `gateway restart` transparently writes the correct checkout-rooted definition instead of bouncing. Applied at `generate_systemd_unit`, `_prepare_service_launcher`, and the launchd run-command wrapper.
- **Refuse (backstop)**: `_refuse_generation_launcher_service_write` guards every persisted write — systemd refresh + install, launchd refresh/install/start self-heal — mirroring `_refuse_temp_home_service_write`. Exec-line scan for units; a tighter launcher-binary scan for plists, whose PATH values may legitimately carry a generation's bin dir.
- **Heal (stock)**: `hermes pm repair` rewrites definitions still pointing into a generation tree and reports what stands after the rewrite (✓ healed / ⚠ still poisoned + the stable-launcher remedy) — repair previously couldn't touch the unit, which is why the loop survived `pm repair` in the wild.

Fixes #131164

- #131192 (closed) patched `get_python_path` detection; this keeps the contract at the generation-root level instead.

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: feat(gateway): per-channel fallback_providers in channel_overrides
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`channel_overrides` can pin a chat's model and provider, but the chat still falls back through the profile-wide `fallback_providers`. A chat moved onto a cheaper model then falls back to the expensive global chain.

This adds an optional `fallback_providers` list to a channel override. It takes the same shape and normalisation as the top-level key and replaces the profile chain for that chat. `[]` turns fallback off there. Chats without the key keep the profile chain.

```yaml
platforms:
  whatsapp:
    channel_overrides:
      "1203630000@g.us":
        model: claude-sonnet-4.6
        provider: anthropic
        fallback_providers:
          - provider: openrouter
            model: openai/gpt-5-mini
```

## Changes Made

- `gateway/config.py`: `ChannelOverride.fallback_providers`.
- `gateway/run_config_loaders.py`: `_fallback_chain_for(source)` refreshes the profile chain as before, then applies the chat's override through the existing `scoped_fallback_chain` helper (unpinned: absent inherits, `[]` disables, malformed entries dropped).
- `gateway/session_execution.py`, `gateway/run_turn.py`, `gateway/session_cold_review.py`: the agent builders and the per-turn refresh of a cached agent use it. The refresh now resolves per chat, so it no longer overwrites a channel's chain with the global one.
- Docs: the per-channel overrides section in `user-guide/messaging`.

## How to Test

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_fallback_chain_reload.py tests/gateway/test_channel_overrides.py`

The new tests fail on `main` and pass here. They check that a channel chain replaces the global one only for its own chat, that `[]` disables fallback, that a cached-agent refresh keeps the channel chain, and that the key round-trips through `PlatformConfig`.

prs.title: fix(pm): fold identical buildable workspace members across profiles
prs.body:
## Summary
A buildable plugin keeps its declared `[project].name` in the uv workspace because uv verifies it against backend metadata. Enabling identical copies across profiles therefore used to produce duplicate workspace names and prevent dependency rebuilds.

This PR folds buildable copies only when their build-relevant source bytes **and effective external path inputs** agree. Within an equal group it preserves the installed identity referenced by an exact editable package source in the seed lock, falling back to config order when none is referenced. Diverged copies remain separate so their conflicts are not silently hidden.

Fixes #125252

## Root Cause
Virtual members can be renamed to identity-keyed names, but buildable members cannot. Deduplication must happen at member collection, where all copies and their effective inputs are visible. Install-local provenance can prevent otherwise identical copies from matching; choosing the first copy unconditionally can also remove the editable path still referenced by the previous generation's lock.

## Changes
- `pm/workspace.py`: compare buildable source trees and effective external path inputs, retaining separate installed identities and staged sources for Mapping inputs.
- Exclude `.hermes-*`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, and `.ruff_cache` from **equality only**. Snapshot copying and generation stamps remain unchanged.
- Parse the seed lock as TOML and match exact package `source.editable` paths, not arbitrary substrings. Select each group's representative before copying its member.
- Read the explicit seed once and reuse its bytes for selection and lock copying; a missing explicit seed still raises rather than silently resolving fresh versions.
- `tests/pm/test_member_selection.py`, `test_member_relative_source_identity.py`, and `test_member_source_folding.py`: existing regressions for duplicate names, Mapping inputs, and distinct/shared/internal/absolute/array-shaped path sources. The contributed external-source regression retains its original authorship.
- `tests/pm/test_member_install_metadata.py`: catalog/catalog and catalog/git-style provenance differences, all three tool caches, list and staged Mapping inputs, unchanged snapshot/stamp behavior, and real source divergence.
- `tests/pm/test_member_seed_selection.py`: exact editable-path parsing, substring/comment/unrelated-field controls, config-order fallback, distinct source/external-input guards, and real offline uv metadata/lock resolution across four profile selections for both input shapes.

## Current Testing
At head `8a96c3f7832d08b1c94093c5a301844343ae616e`:

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /Users/liyuan/github/ai/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/pm/test_member_seed_selection.py tests/pm/test_member_install_metadata.py tests/pm/test_member_relative_source_identity.py tests/pm/test_member_source_folding.py tests/pm/test_member_selection.py tests/pm/test_workspace.py tests/pm/test_workspace_build_inputs.py tests/pm/test_workspace_output_encoding.py tests/pm/test_plugin_declarations.py tests/pm/test_plugin_inputs.py tests/pm/test_plugins_state.py -q -o addopts='' -p no:cacheprovider
```

**121 passed in 19.50s**, macOS/Python 3.14.5, uv 0.12.19. `git diff --check` passed.

Both latest reported defects were reproduced before their fixes: provenance prevented folding; a real seeded lock referencing the second clone failed with uv exit 2, `Distribution not found`.

The new integration regression exercises the real `lock_and_sync` generation/seed path with a lock-only consumer invoking real `uv lock --offline --no-config --python <test interpreter>`. Its dependency-free in-tree backend is executed and recorded. No package installation or live plugin deployment is performed. The missing-explicit-seed regression is included and passes.

The canonical whole-tree runner/full suite was not rerun under critical disk pressure. Validation used targeted pytest with `tests/conftest.py` home isolation and bytecode/cache output disabled. No PR CI checks were reported before the push.

## Historical Testing (earlier revisions)
- The original duplicate-member regression failed on the earlier pristine upstream baseline and passed with folding; `test_member_selection.py` then passed 5/5.
- The external-source follow-up at `091ca6962ed1ad4ee03fbfaad16577a74c01fc39` passed 44 tests across six workspace files, independently verified on Linux/Zorin with Python 3.14.7.
- Earlier broader testing returned 79 passed and two failures in `test_plugin_survival_contract.py` (`test_conflicting_candidate_refused_unenabled_and_unimported`, `test_update_sync_disables_later_plugin_of_unresolvable_union`). Both were previously reproduced on pristine upstream on this machine. Earlier `isolated_python` fixture errors in `test_environment_build.py` / `test_build_operations.py` also reproduced upstream. Those broader files were not rerun in the current targeted validation.

## Checklist

prs.title: fix(desktop): negotiate remote session authority before requests
prs.body:
Remote Desktop can complete a URL gateway connection but still send legacy session requests to an authority gateway. `HermesGateway` currently selects its canonical adapter only when the URL contains `native_dial`. The result is `invalid_params` when creating/submitting a session, rejected legacy model changes (`use_session_mutation_model`), and missing profile projection for incoming messages.

Wait for the remote gateway's ready event and select the adapter from its advertised `session_authority` capability before startup requests or replay. Keep `native_dial` separate as the sole desktop-local capability signal. A ready event without session authority retains the legacy adapter. Readiness is bounded; failed dials reject pending startup and cannot cancel a replacement dial started by a close handler.

Validation:

- Added real loopback WebSocket coverage for delayed readiness, session creation/submission/model mutation, message profile routing, close before ready, and immediate redial after failure.
- The new create/submit regression fails with `invalid_params` against unpatched upstream `6696c7b0a404a156d4e93f4fdc11bb0802b9c85c` and passes with this change.
- 107 canonical API tests pass in 24 files on the branch rebased onto that upstream commit.
- Renderer TypeScript and changed-file ESLint pass.

Checks use the existing local dependency installation; this draft is ready for upstream CI against the current lockfile. Native platform/packaging suites were not run for this contribution. The change contains only the four Desktop API/test files; private deployment tools and user configuration are excluded.

prs.title: fix(desktop): negotiate canonical protocol on public connections
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Negotiate the existing canonical desktop protocol for authenticated public remote WebSocket connections when `gateway.ready` explicitly advertises `session_authority: true`.

Previously, `HermesGateway` selected the canonical adapter only from the private `native_dial` URL marker. An ordinary public-ticket connection to the same canonical gateway therefore used legacy request handling. Resuming a named-profile Bot Chat and then submitting through the normal profileless caller could lose the learned profile and submission identity, resulting in `permission_denied` despite a valid login.

The fix uses the existing `CanonicalDesktopProtocol`, without changing ticket construction, server permissions, native adoption, or authentication. Native-dial provenance is separate from negotiated wire mode, so a public canonical connection does not advertise itself as desktop-local.

Public requests and retained replay wait for protocol readiness. Readiness failure invalidates only the owning connection generation and cleans up its timer/listeners. A new connection resets protocol selection, preserving legacy behavior unless the new peer advertises the explicit boolean capability.

## Related Issue

No dedicated issue is closed by this PR.

Searched open, closed and merged PRs before publication, including `native_dial`, `session_authority`, public connections, canonical desktop, protocol negotiation and `gateway.ready`.

- Related #73821 moves readiness handling into the shared transport. Its desktop change adds an auth-rejection message; it does not select the canonical adapter for public remote connections. This PR includes a desktop-local readiness barrier because current main resolves the shared transport at raw WebSocket open. If #73821 lands first, the barrier can be reconciled with that shared implementation while retaining the public protocol-selection and provenance fix.
- #64266 concerns the older profile-capability/backend create-resume contract, not this client's canonical adapter selection.
- #143188 is a separate legacy-history adoption prerequisite. This PR does not adopt history or relax its protections.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Tests

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/api/client.ts`: negotiate public canonical mode from readiness, keep native provenance separate, gate pre-ready requests/replay, reset on reconnect and invalidate the owning transport on handshake failure.
- `remote-canonical-negotiation.test.ts`: real WebSocket regressions for named-profile resume/profileless submit, submission identity, strict capability selection, canonical-to-legacy reconnect, pre-ready input, early disconnect and timeout followed by successful redial.
- `canonical-reconnect-replay-owner.test.ts`: exercise retained replay for native and delayed-ready public connections while preserving the existing profile/event assertions.
- `canonical-protocol-wire.test.ts`: two legacy fixtures now emit their normal empty `gateway.ready`; existing wire assertions are unchanged.

No dependency, lockfile, backend, listener or authentication changes.

## How to Test

From the repository root:

```bash
npm run test:ui --workspace apps/desktop -- src/api
npm run typecheck --workspace apps/desktop
npm run build --workspace apps/desktop
```

Run installed ESLint on the four changed API files and `git diff --check`.

Observed fail-before cases included an input request emitted before delayed public readiness, and a readiness timeout leaving the socket open instead of permitting redial. Both are covered by passing regressions.

### Verification

- [x] Rebased API suite: 31 files, 172 tests passed.
- [x] Targeted ESLint and `git diff --check` passed.
- [x] Final rebased normal type checks passed.
- [x] Final rebased normal desktop build passed.
- [x] Independent read-only review accepted the final feature-file hashes.
- [x] Owner built and ran a separate macOS development preview at `d893d8068ae2e957764bacb851b960fda98d1840`. Normal browser login, a reply in the original named-profile Bot Chat, and another reply after full quit/relaunch succeeded. Backend admission and stored-message checks confirmed the original canonical chat was used.

The PR was rebased after that Mac test; all four changed files remain byte-identical to the independently reviewed, Mac-tested feature files. Parent reruns above validate the new base. The Mac preview was not a signed/notarized release, and no permanent gateway migration is claimed. Separate controlled peer-DM and scheduled-delivery tests also succeeded after the history adoption prerequisite; they are operational evidence, not additional behavior implemented by this desktop PR.

The optional Linux HUD modifier helper was unavailable due to a missing XInput2 development header. The normal desktop build still completed successfully; no system packages were installed to suppress that warning.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing and repository guidance.
- [x] Conventional commit; one fix, no unrelated feature commits.
- [x] Searched existing PRs and documented overlapping work above.
- [x] Added regression tests.
- [ ] Full Python repository suite run. Not run for this TypeScript-only change.
- [ ] `python scripts/check` run. Not run; targeted desktop checks are listed explicitly.
- [x] No new configuration keys, tool schemas or dependencies.
- [x] Cross-platform behavior considered; automated Linux ARM checks and owner macOS development acceptance are distinguished above.

The anchor reaches the current plugin's standalone text and media sender, so delivery uses the reply API with `reply_in_thread` instead of treating a topic ID as a message destination.

Core routing uses an opt-in `StandaloneSendPolicy.forward_metadata` contract; Feishu declares the consumer. Explicit caller metadata wins, input dictionaries stay unchanged, and unlisted targets retain the existing fallback. Other platforms keep the default metadata behavior.

Based on main `6771d29e96fa`. Original PR commits and review history are preserved without a force push.

## Validation

- **162 tests passed** across the topic, directory, plugin-extensibility, send-message and Feishu suites (6 files, no retries).
- All **11 regression cases failed on main** before the update. They exercise real directory discovery, plugin discovery/dispatch and synthetic Lark SDK requests, covering state.db/JSON, explicit/friendly targets, text/documents and metadata precedence.
- `python scripts/check --staged --base upstream/main`: all **14 checks passed**; whitespace checks passed.

This PR stays independent of #49364. No live Feishu delivery/credentials or full-repository suite was used, and local validation does not claim remote CI approval.

Additional integration verification: a clean local merge with the updated #49364 direct-send path passed **179 combined tests across 11 files**, plus all 14 checks. This is a local compatibility proof, not an upstream merge.

prs.title: feat: draw images inline in the CLI and TUI
prs.body:
**ELI5:** Before, when you gave Hermes a picture in the terminal, or a tool took a screenshot, you only saw a file path. Now the picture is drawn right there in the chat: with real pixels in kitty and Ghostty, and as coloured blocks in every other terminal.

## What does this PR do?

Hermes accepts images (`/paste`, `/image`, drag-and-drop) but only ever shows a path. This PR draws them inline in both the classic CLI and the TUI: a turn's attachments under the user row, and the local image a tool produced or looked at (`vision_analyze`, browser screenshots, `read_file` on a PNG) under that tool's line.

It reuses the graphics stack the pet already had. The encoders move out of `agent/pet/render.py` into `agent/terminal_image.py`, and the CLI, the TUI and the pet all draw from it.

```text
agent/terminal_image.py        detection, encoders, render_inline_image, tool_image_path
├── agent/pet/render.py        spritesheet decode + PetRenderer (encoders moved out)
├── hermes_cli/cli_inline_images.py      CLI: rows into scrollback via _cprint
└── tui_gateway image.render  →  ui-tui <InlineImage>   TUI: kitty placeholders or half-block cells
```

Only the two forms a line-based renderer can measure are used: kitty Unicode placeholders (kitty, Ghostty) and truecolor half-blocks everywhere else. Image rows stay ordinary cells, so CLI scrollback replay and Ink layout/virtual scroll keep working. iTerm2, WezTerm and sixel terminals get half-blocks, because their protocols paint over rows nothing counted.

Which image a tool shows comes from named fields only (`image_url`, `url`, `path`, `image_path`, `screenshot_path`; result before args), the same rule as the desktop's tool preview. A `search_files` listing full of PNG paths shows nothing.

```yaml
display:
  inline_images: auto   # auto | kitty | unicode | off
```

## Related Issue

Closes #6675. Supersedes #85052 and #21546 (CLI-only, each with its own encoders), and the image-preview part of #40492 (raw escapes inside Ink, which it can't host).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change), commit 1 only

## Changes Made

Three commits, each green on its own:

1. **`refactor(terminal)`**: moves detection and the kitty/iTerm2/sixel/half-block encoders from `agent/pet/render.py` to `agent/terminal_image.py`; renames the Ink painters `petSprite.tsx` → `cellImage.tsx` (`HalfBlockImage`, `KittyImage`). No behaviour change.
2. **`feat(cli)`**: `render_inline_image` / `tool_image_path` / `resolve_inline_mode`; `hermes_cli/cli_inline_images.py`; hooks for attachments and the `tool.completed` progress event; `display.inline_images` default; docs.
3. **`feat(tui)`**: `image_path` on `tool.complete` from both the sidecar (`tool_progress.py`) and the shared gateway's local-viewer fields (`local_viewer_events.complete_fields`, so canonical sessions get it too); the `image.render` RPC + contract; `Msg.images` / `kind: 'image'`, `pushImageSegment`, `<InlineImage>` / `<MessageImages>`, height estimate; docs.

Two traps the CLI path works around (both are explained in commit messages and comments):

- `_cprint` prints at prompt_toolkit's default 256-colour depth, which rounds the placeholder colour that encodes the kitty image id (`38;2;224;70;113` → `38;5;167`) and turns the APC transmit into visible text. The kitty escapes ride prompt_toolkit's zero-width `\001…\002` brackets; half-block colours still follow the output's colour depth like the rest of the scrollback.
- A whole truecolor image in one `_cprint` overruns the Windows console write and loses the tail rows (7 of 16 arrived). Rows print one call each, like the diff printer.

## How to Test

1. `display.inline_images: auto` (default). In any terminal: `hermes`, then `/image path/to/pic.png` and a question. Half-blocks appear under "📎 1 image attached".
2. Ask the agent to `read_file` / `vision_analyze` a local PNG: the image appears under the tool line. In kitty or Ghostty it's the full-resolution image.
3. Same in `hermes --tui`. In a canonical session, `/image` works once the session exists, which is current behaviour.
4. `display.inline_images: off` brings back paths only.

## Live A/B (maintainer, rebased onto main 07274ac6543)

Real `hermes chat` (classic CLI) and `hermes chat --tui` in real kitty 0.39.1 and Konsole 25.12 under Xvfb. A loopback model calls `vision_analyze` on a 480×300 PNG. Base is `origin/main`, head is this branch rebased cleanly onto it.

| Surface / terminal | main | head |
|---|---|---|
| CLI, kitty | tool line only, no image | real pixel image under the tool line |
| CLI, Konsole | tool line only | half-block colour image, layout intact |
| TUI, kitty | — | real pixel image under `Vision Analyze` |
| TUI, Konsole | — | half-block colour image |

CLI main, kitty: ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/8a326fd00929c5c263aeb3e4e84c54b6/raw/8a7b8da90c392dfe948cea868cd48a8b36cb6833/main-kitty.png)
CLI head, kitty: ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/8a326fd00929c5c263aeb3e4e84c54b6/raw/8a7b8da90c392dfe948cea868cd48a8b36cb6833/head-kitty.png)
CLI main, Konsole: ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/8a326fd00929c5c263aeb3e4e84c54b6/raw/8a7b8da90c392dfe948cea868cd48a8b36cb6833/main-konsole.png)
CLI head, Konsole: ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/8a326fd00929c5c263aeb3e4e84c54b6/raw/8a7b8da90c392dfe948cea868cd48a8b36cb6833/head-konsole.png)
TUI head, kitty: ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/8a326fd00929c5c263aeb3e4e84c54b6/raw/8a7b8da90c392dfe948cea868cd48a8b36cb6833/tui-head-kitty.png)
TUI head, Konsole: ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/8a326fd00929c5c263aeb3e4e84c54b6/raw/8a7b8da90c392dfe948cea868cd48a8b36cb6833/tui-head-konsole.png)

Gates: `scripts/check` 14/14 ok; 40 Python tests (`test_terminal_image`, `test_cli_inline_images`, pet suites, `tui_gateway` image + contracts) pass; `ui-tui` `inlineImage.test.tsx` 3/3; TUI build ok.

## Evidence

**Real `hermes chat --cli` on a Windows 11 PTY** (pywinpty, fake LLM provider from `tests/fakes`, isolated `HERMES_HOME`, `inline_images: unicode`), screen replayed through `tests/e2e/core/terminal/_vt.py`:

```text
⚙  /image …\deku.png
  📎 Attached image: deku.png
❯ what is in this picture?
  📎 1 image attached
  ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀   x16 rows (52x16 cells, truecolor)
✗ Read deku.png  0.9s [Cannot read binary file …]
  ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀   x16 rows
☤ Hermes
That is a stylized anime character with leafy green hair.
```

- **Before (one `_cprint` per image):** 7.3 of 16 rows reached the terminal per image. A 20-line inline diff in the same run was intact.
- **After (one per row):** 32 half-block rows (both images complete), and the diff is still intact.

**Real `hermes --tui`** in the same harness (canonical shared gateway): the final frame holds 33 half-block rows, both 16-row images, after the full `tool.complete.image_path` → `image.render` → Ink path. This emulator can't reproduce Ink's ConPTY output faithfully enough for a screenshot (it garbles the text rows the same way), so this part rests on the count plus the renderer test below.

Tests, each checked against the defect it guards:

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_inline_images.py`: kitty rows reach a `Vt100_Output` at default depth with the exact id colour and the transmit. Without the zero-width wrapping: `38;5;167`, and the APC leaks as text. Rows measure as their cell width.
- `ui-tui/src/__tests__/inlineImage.test.tsx`: placeholders paint and the transmit is written once for two copies. Red when the send-once guard is removed. Half-blocks under a user turn; nothing when `off`.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_image_render.py`: `image.render` modes, `off`, non-image and missing files; `image_path` on `tool.complete` from both emitters; none for a `search_files` listing.
- `tests/agent/test_terminal_image.py`: mode resolution (tmux, WezTerm, iTerm2 → half-blocks; `kitty` pin), field rule, caps, no upscaling, ids above the pet's range, a new id for an edited file.

Results:

- `python scripts/check`: ok, 0 blocking.
- Related pytest files: 313 passed.
- TUI vitest: 1900 passed.
- Pre-existing failures that also fail on `main` on this Windows box: `test_config.py::TestEnvWriteDenylist` (2), `test_todo_state_events.py` (1), vitest `canonicalImages`, `slashAttachmentRenderer`, `terminalParity` (5).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Display-only: no stored data, no prompt or message changes (prompt caching untouched), and `inline_images: off` restores the old output.

**Blast radius:**

- Every CLI/TUI user on the default `auto` now sees images where paths used to be. Terminals without truecolor (macOS Terminal.app) get the CLI's normal 256-colour quantization.
- Kitty and Ghostty receive a PNG transmit of up to ~350 KB per image; over a slow SSH link that's noticeable.
- Tool images aren't kept on resume or rehydrate; they're live only.
- Remote image URLs (for example FAL `image_generate` results) aren't fetched; that's a follow-up.
- New `image_path` contract field and `image.render` RPC are additive.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs (see Related Issue)
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this feature
- [x] Related test files pass; full-suite failures listed above also fail on `main`
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 (real CLI and TUI on a PTY). kitty/Ghostty paths are covered by byte-level tests only.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Updated docs: `website/docs/user-guide/cli.md` (Inline Images), `tui.md`
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A (its `display:` block doesn't list neighbouring keys like `inline_diffs`)
- [x] `AGENTS.md`: N/A
- [x] Cross-platform: Windows console write limit handled; tmux/WezTerm/VS Code fall back to half-blocks
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A

prs.title: catalog: tabella 2.0.7 — macOS verified by CI
prs.body:
SHA bump for tabella **2.0.7**: `449e754` → `4922d16` (release-lane merge commit; tagged `2.0.7`), and `platforms` gains **macos**.

## The platform change

`platforms` was `[linux, windows]`. Both were backed by a lane that actually ran; `macos` was absent because nothing had ever executed the suite there, even though the README documents `brew install pandoc basictex` and `brew install cairo pango gdk-pixbuf` for macOS readers.

So the claim and the docs contradicted each other. `tests.yml` now has a `pytest-macos` job that installs exactly the packages the README names and runs the full suite on `macos-latest`: **73 passed, 0 failed** — create, read round-trip, OCR, convert and the security gates all exercised.

The first run of that job is why this entry is honest rather than optimistic. It failed 2/71 with:

```
OSError: cannot load library 'libgobject-2.0-0'
```

`brew` had installed pango and cairo; Homebrew's lib directory simply is not on the default dyld search path for a Python that Homebrew did not install. Same class as the Windows `WEASYPRINT_DLL_DIRECTORIES` requirement. The README now tells a python.org/pyenv user to export `DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH="$(brew --prefix)/lib"`, and the CI lane does the same — which is what makes `macos` a verified claim instead of an expectation.

## The rest of the release

Docs and CI only; no library code changed. 2.0.6's transport work (a malformed `Content-Length` no longer ends a stdio session; an unknown tool answers `-32602` instead of returning a success-shaped result; HTTP bearer compared in constant time, 4 MB body cap, lazy token) is described in the earlier revision of this PR.

**Verification:** `pytest` 73 on ubuntu-latest and 73 on macos-latest, cold-`bootstrap` green, all on `5ff5cb7` then `1f346bd`; PyPI `tabella-docs` 2.0.7 published; `validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes.

Note: this touches `sha`, `version` and `platforms`. The description rewrite is a separate open PR (#141476).

## Summary

Adds three Ponytail-inspired software-development skills:

- `ponytail`: task-scoped minimal-code implementation discipline
- `ponytail-review`: diff-focused, read-only over-engineering review
- `ponytail-audit`: repo/subsystem read-only over-engineering audit

The skills are adapted from [DietrichGebert/ponytail](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail) under the MIT License. Each skill preserves the upstream MIT copyright and permission/warranty notice.

## Relationship to existing skills

- `simplify-code` is a broader multi-reviewer cleanup workflow that may apply changes.
- These skills are narrower, task-scoped/read-only where applicable, and focus specifically on avoiding unnecessary dependencies, abstractions, wrappers, and custom code.

prs.title: Bots list: gateway Group Chats are normal rows; no Refresh button or raw error text
prs.body:
Gateway Group Chats now show up in the Bots list as ordinary rows, next to the other group chats. Before, the pane opened with a stray "Refresh gateway groups" button. Some remote setups also printed an internal error ("Canonical groups require an explicit connection") in the same spot, and a group you had just created didn't appear until you clicked Refresh.

Gateway rooms now look and behave like every other roster row, keep themselves up to date, and never show raw transport errors.

Reported in Discord by merky (screenshot of the button and the error text above their bots).

## What changes

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Top of the Bots pane | Bare "Refresh gateway groups" ghost button | Nothing; the toolbar is first |
| A gateway Group Chat | Unlabeled strip above the toolbar, small avatar-stack button | Normal roster row: group tile, name, age ("now", "3h"), avatars + "2 bots"; sorted, searched and filtered with the rest |
| Room you just created in the dialog | Missing until you click Refresh (live run below: main never listed it) | Listed at once |
| Window on an env / legacy remote (no registry id) | Plain text "Canonical groups require an explicit connection" | No rooms, no text |
| Backend without gateway Group Chats | Error text | No rooms, no text |
| A re-read fails (network blip) | Error line, list emptied | Keeps the last good list |
| Right-click a gateway room | Open / Delete | Open / Delete (unchanged) |

## Screenshots (real Desktop on a real local gateway, same spec on both trees)

Before (origin/main): the Refresh button on top, and no "Release crew" row even after creating it.

![before](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/f2a38ed62fe7cad60026c7ca83a5ad1d/raw/1823631ac7c3484f1d47be8278d5dea9e0413ca9/before-bots-pane.png)

After: "Release crew" is a normal row at the top of the list, no button.

![after](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/f2a38ed62fe7cad60026c7ca83a5ad1d/raw/1823631ac7c3484f1d47be8278d5dea9e0413ca9/after-bots-pane.png)

After: right-click keeps Open Group Chat / Delete.

![menu](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/f2a38ed62fe7cad60026c7ca83a5ad1d/raw/1823631ac7c3484f1d47be8278d5dea9e0413ca9/after-row-menu.png)

After: the room opened from the row, no error banners.

![room](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/f2a38ed62fe7cad60026c7ca83a5ad1d/raw/1823631ac7c3484f1d47be8278d5dea9e0413ca9/after-room-open.png)

**Live repro:** Playwright drives the built Desktop (Xvfb) on a sandbox HERMES_HOME with a real `hermes gateway` and a mock inference server. It creates two bots and a Group Chat named "Release crew", then reads the Bots pane. On main the pane text starts with `Refresh gateway groups`, has no `Release crew`, and the run stops when it tries to right-click the missing row. On head the pane reads `BOTS / Release crew / now / 2 bots / Scout …`, the buttons list has no Refresh, there are no `role=alert` nodes, and the run passes.

## Changes

- `canonical-group-registry.tsx`: `useGatewayGroupRooms()` (a React Query read of `groups.list` that polls every 10 s, re-reads on socket/source change, and re-reads right after a create or disband here) replaces the `CanonicalGroupList` component. Without a registry connection id it lists none; on JSON-RPC method-not-found it lists none.
- `roster-pane-derivation.ts` / `roster-pane.tsx`: gateway rooms become `RosterGroupRow`s (with `gateway` set), so they share the roster's ordering, search, the bots/groups kind filter, the activity filter and user sections. A gateway filter naming another source hides them.
- `canonical-group-row.tsx`: same markup as a Desktop group row (tile, name, age, avatars + member count), plus the live working / failed / needs-you glyph.
- The create dialog and "Start gateway group" trigger an immediate re-read.
- Removed: the button, its `refreshGroups` copy in all 10 locales, and the callerless `captureCanonicalGroupRoute` (whose throw was the raw text).
- `rpcMethodMissing` and `rowAge` moved into tiny leaf modules (`rpc-errors.ts`, `row-age.ts`), so the room row doesn't pull `data.ts` / `bot-row.tsx` into every room test.

## Tests

- New `gateway-group-rooms.test.tsx` (red on main, 3/3): rooms appear when the socket opens with no Refresh button and no alert; a failed re-read keeps the list; no registry id or no gateway Group Chats lists nothing and renders no text.
- The existing delete-from-row and disband-from-workspace tests now drive the new rows.
- `npx vitest run src/plugins/hermes-bots/`: 128 files, 970 tests pass. `tsc` clean. `scripts/check --only health` ok.
