prs.title: fix(agent): keep OpenCode Go keys on a per-model upstream 429
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

OpenCode Go returns HTTP 429 for two unrelated conditions:

| Body | Meaning | Correct recovery |
|---|---|---|
| `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"GoUsageLimitError",...},"metadata":{"limitName":"weekly"}}` | the key's plan window (5-hour / weekly / monthly) | bench the key, rotate (already classified `billing` on main) |
| `{"error":{"type":"server_error","message":"Upstream request failed: Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later."}}` | one model's upstream throttle | keep the key, defer to fallback |

On main both bench the key for the 429 hour. Repro with a two-key `opencode-go` pool where the primary has hit its weekly window: the main agent's model gets the per-model upstream 429, the pool logs `marking <backup> exhausted (status=429)`, and then every auxiliary task pinned to a *different* model on the same provider (approval, vision, compression) fails with `credential pool: no available entries`, although a direct call with the backup key on that other model returns 200.

## Changes

- `plugins/model-providers/opencode-zen/__init__.py`: the `opencode-go` profile sets `classify_api_error` (the existing provider-profile seam) and maps a 429 whose message contains `upstream request failed` to `upstream_rate_limit`. Every other error declines (`None`), so `GoUsageLimitError` keeps its built-in `billing` verdict.
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py::_recover_provider_pool`: the main path (`recover_with_credential_pool`) already skips rotation for `upstream_rate_limit`, but the auxiliary path only used substring predicates and benched anyway. It now consults `classify_api_error` and skips the bench for an `upstream_rate_limit` verdict. That also covers OpenRouter-wrapped upstream 429s on the aux path, which had the same gap.

## How to test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/model_providers/test_opencode_go_rate_limit_scope.py`: red on main (2 failures: upstream body classified `rate_limit` and benched on the aux path), green with the fix.
- Directly affected suites: `test_opencode_go_profile.py`, `test_auxiliary_error_classification.py`, `test_provider_profile_recovery_seam.py`, `test_auxiliary_client_cache_eviction.py`, `test_error_classifier.py`: 239 passed.
- Main-path E2E against a temp `HERMES_HOME`: a real `CredentialPool` with two mock entries fed through `recover_with_credential_pool`. Upstream body → no rotation, both entries `ok`. Plan-wall body → primary `exhausted`, rotated to the second entry.
- `scripts/check`: ok.

Platform: Linux (Debian 13).

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep a session's subagents visible after its cached parent agent is rebuilt
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A session's delegated children disappear from `subagent.list` once the gateway rebuilds the cached agent for that route, while the children are still running. `subagent.tail`, steer and interrupt then report the child as unavailable, so the Ctrl+T monitor and the dock show an empty roster for work that is still in progress.

Root cause: `gateway/session_ancillary.py::subagent_records` ties a child to the session only through the parent agent object (`registry._is_descendant_of(record['agent'], parent)`). A child keeps a weakref to the agent that spawned it. After a cache rebuild, `authority.agent(ref)` returns the replacement agent, the old weakref no longer matches it, and the roster comes back empty. The lineage fallbacks don't cover this either, because they only list rows read-only.

The fix carries the gateway's own `LiveSession` record, which survives a parent rebuild but not a replaced conversation, and matches on that exact object:

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`: `wire()` binds the turn's `LiveSession` on the agent as `_canonical_session_owner` (added to `_TURN_ATTRS`, so `restore()` puts back the previous value).
- `tools/delegate_tool.py`: `_build_child_agent` copies it onto the child when it is built, because a detached child can register after the parent turn has unwired.
- `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`: `_register_child` stores that record as `owner_session_record`, and nested children inherit it.
- `gateway/session_ancillary.py`: `_owner_objects` passes the session's `LiveSession`, and `subagent_records` checks `record['owner_session_record'] is session_owner` before the existing parent and lineage matches.

This keeps the existing rule that an identical durable session id never transfers access to old objects. The match is object identity on `LiveSession`, so a different `LiveSession` that reuses the same id gets an empty roster. A child that carries no token is still invisible after the rebuild (`owned` in the fixture).

Overlap checked: #114420 carries owner authority across a background-thread hop, #116204 shares the roster across processes, and #135874 lists sibling sessions in `delegate_task(action=list)`. None of them covers a parent cache rebuild within the same process.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. The searches I ran are listed under Overlap checked above.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`, `gateway/session_ancillary.py`, `tools/delegate_tool.py`, `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`, as described above.
- `tests/gateway/test_subagent_live_session_owner.py` (new, 2 tests):
  - The roster and controls keep the owned child after a parent rebuild and after the parent is gone. A foreign token and an unstamped child stay hidden. Reusing the durable id with another `LiveSession` returns nothing.
  - A child registered after the parent unwired still records the session owner.
- `tests/gateway/fixtures/ancillary_reads_peer.py` (real gateway daemon probe used by `test_session_ancillary_reads.py`): adds a `rebound` child stamped with the session's `LiveSession` under an old parent. It is listed and tailable, and after `_agent_cache[route]` is replaced with a new generation it is still the only child listed. `owned` (no token) stays hidden, as before.

## How to Test

1. Plant only the test hunks on `main`: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_subagent_live_session_owner.py tests/gateway/test_session_ancillary_reads.py` gives 3 failed, including `assert [] == ['owned']` and `test_activity_snapshot_requires_current_owner_objects`.
2. Same command on this branch: 4 passed.
3. Related files (`tests/gateway/test_session_ancillary*.py`, `test_subagent*.py`, `test_local_viewer*.py`, `tests/tools/test_delegate*.py`, 51 files): 418 passed, 0 failed.
4. `python scripts/check`: 14 checks ok, 0 blocking health findings.

I've been running this change on a long-lived gateway since mid-October. Before it, a rebuilt parent left the CLI subagent monitor empty while its children kept running. With it, the children stay listed and steerable.

prs.title: fix(desktop): load canonical groups when the gateway becomes ready
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Hermes Bots plugin's gateway groups list showed a "disconnected gateway" error on startup until the user pressed Refresh.

`CanonicalGroupList` runs its groups read in an effect that depends only on `connectionId`, `profile` and the refresh counter. At startup the connection route is published before its socket opens, so the first read fails, the error is shown, and nothing re-runs the effect when the socket opens.

The fix adds `host.state.gateway` to the effect's dependencies and skips the read until there is a `connectionId` and the gateway is `'open'`. A read that finishes after a disconnect is still discarded, and a real server error is still shown.

Behavior notes from review: on a reconnect the list empties and refills after the new read (the stale list is no longer shown while disconnected). Pressing Refresh while the gateway is not open now waits for the gateway instead of showing the disconnected error.

## Related Issue

None found (searched open and merged PRs and issues).

## Type of Change

- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/canonical-group-registry.tsx`: wait for gateway readiness; depend on `host.state.gateway`.
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/canonical-group-registry.test.tsx`: new tests (load on readiness without a manual refresh; discard a disconnected read, retry on reconnect, still show a real server error).

prs.title: catalog(pass-secrets): declare the real platform matrix (linux, macos)
prs.body:
catalog(pass-secrets): declare the real platform matrix

`platforms: []` is not neutral here. The site renders
`plugin.platforms?.length ? … : "Linux, macOS, Windows"`, so the empty list
advertises this entry as working on Windows, which it never has: `pass` is a
`#!/usr/bin/env bash` script (bash + gpg + git + tree) and the source calls it
through `subprocess.run(["pass", ...])` / `shutil.which("pass")`, neither of
which can execute a script on Windows outside WSL/Cygwin/MSYS2. There is no
`fcntl`/`getuid`/`termios` elsewhere in the path — the bash dependency is the
whole constraint.

`linux` and `macos` are both exercised: the GPG store, `pass init`, and the
`.gpg` subdir walk are the same on either.

Entry-only change: `sha` and `version` are untouched, still `485f105` / 1.0.0.
The platform claim is about the package's capability, not about this pin, and
1.0.0 had the same bash dependency.

Related: #146751 carries the same line as part of the 1.1.0 bump. That PR is
blocked on the `/s` sender-gate rework, which is unrelated to this field, so
landing the one-line correction separately keeps a false OS claim off the
listing in the meantime. Whichever merges first, the other needs a one-line
rebase.

prs.title: fix: self-heal a live-mounted local session from its receipt on resume
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #146344.

A local session mounted live **without** its store entry — the state a pre-scope-era listing/restore leaves legacy desktop-lane chats (`agent:main:local:dm:*`) in — refused every `session.resume` with `admission_conflict`, even though the validated `gateway.local_policy.v1:<id>` receipt in hand holds the complete entry. Only the desktop's focused tab survived each gateway restart; messages sent to a refused session queued forever (`session_admissions` stuck `queued`, eternal turn timer in the UI) because the admission executor's resume takes the same path.

## Change

In `restore_local_session`'s live-branch, when the store entry is missing (`current is None`), bind the receipt's validated entry instead of raising — mirroring what the fresh-mount branch two lines above already does with the same `entry` object:

```diff
-            if current is None or (current.session_id not in receipt.get('lineage', [sid])
-                                   and not _stray_route_target(authority, receipt, current.session_id)):
-                raise RuntimeStoreError('admission_conflict')
-            current.session_id = target
+            if current is None:
+                # Self-heal: the session is live-mounted (e.g. a history view from a
+                # pre-scope-era listing) without a bound store entry. The receipt has
+                # passed validation and the live source/policy already matched; bind
+                # its entry instead of refusing (#146344).
+                entry.origin = source
+                entry.session_id = target
+                store._entries[route] = entry
+            elif (current.session_id not in receipt.get('lineage', [sid])
+                  and not _stray_route_target(authority, receipt, current.session_id)):
+                raise RuntimeStoreError('admission_conflict')
+            else:
+                current.session_id = target
```

Safety: only the entry-missing case changes. The stray-route-target protection is preserved; the live mount's source and policy equality are already verified by the `storage_unavailable` guard two branches earlier; the bound entry is the same object the fresh-mount branch binds.

## Validation

Live system (a production install with three affected legacy sessions, days of repro before, multiple clean cycles after):

- Before: every gateway restart left exactly one resumable legacy chat (the desktop's focused tab); the other two refused `admission_conflict`; queued turns hung forever (no `session_turn_leases` row, `Session <id> paused: admission_conflict` repeating in the journal).
- After: all three resume normally regardless of tab focus, order, or prior parks; queued turns admit cleanly; fast-persisted routing rows behave normally. Verified via DB-side checks (`session_admissions` status, message flow, `gateway_routing` rows) without scripted probes.

## Test

`tests/gateway/test_local_live_mount_self_heal.py` follows the `test_local_receipt_missing_profile.py` harness: create a local session, drop its store entry while it stays live-mounted (the failing state), and assert `restore_local_session` heals — returns the ref, re-binds the entry, and is repeatable.

Note for reviewers: the full gateway authority test family is red on a *live install* machine (the home-io guard trips on the real home's `manifest.json` during `initialize_gateway_runtime`), identically with and without this change — that is environmental, which is why the regression test is written against the house harness for CI to run.

prs.title: feat(gateway): count turns that end without a reply
prs.body:
Counts every chat turn that finishes without the user getting a reply, with a reason that separates real losses from silence by design. It adds an opt-in shared-metrics counter, `hermes.gateway.no_reply` (`platform`, `reason`), and one content-free log line per such turn:

```
turn ended without a reply: platform=telegram session=<key> reason=delivery_failed
```

## Why

A chat turn that ends without a reply is invisible today. The reply clock it started is dropped without a count, and an empty response is logged only at DEBUG. Operators cannot see how often users get no answer, or tell a real loss (delivery failure, dropped content, an empty answer) from silence by design (a silence marker, an interrupted or steered turn). On one deployment about 8% of Telegram turns ended without a final reply before the user's next message, and the data could not say which kind they were.

## Change

- **Counter and vocabulary.** `hermes.gateway.no_reply` joins the v4 gateway counters in the contract and schema (additive). `reason` is one of:
  - `silent`: the agent answered with the silence marker, or a post-admission plugin consumed the message without replying.
  - `interrupted`: the turn was interrupted before it answered.
  - `empty`: the turn produced nothing to send.
  - `dropped`: the response had content but nothing was sent.
  - `delivery_failed`: sending was attempted and failed.
  - `error`: the turn raised before answering. The user may still see the generic error notice; that notice is not an answer and does not stop the reply clock, so each turn lands in exactly one of `reply_latency` and `no_reply`.
- **Only the turn's own clock.** `start_reply_clock` returns its start time and the claim stores it on the turn's event. The end of a turn pops the pending clock only when it carries that exact token, so a busy follow-up, a queued message or a concurrent turn in the same chat never claims another turn's clock. When ownership is unclear the turn is not counted: an undercount, never a false no-reply.
- **Session authority path.** Turns admitted through the session authority run on an event rebuilt from the FIFO row. The existing turn-marker hand-over (`_hand_over_turn_marker`) now also moves the token and a "reply delivered" flag to the waiting adapter event, only on the adopter branch. `_MARKER_FIELDS` and marker release are unchanged.
- **Replies that do not stop the clock still count as replies.** Media-only and TTS replies, a streamed media-only final, and a voice reply sent from the persistence step all count as replied. Voice delivery is recorded on the event; it does not change `reply_latency`.
- **Turn path untouched.** Classification runs in `shared_metrics_gateway.py` and never raises. `_process_message_background` gains two unconditional calls and no branches; base.py does not grow (a small platform-name helper moved to the existing `base_log_safety.py` sibling). The platform label is normalized once, in the owning profile's home, as `reply_latency` does.
- Counting follows the existing shared-metrics opt-in; the log line is written either way. Docs: the metrics table gets the row, with `no_reply / (reply_latency + no_reply)` as the per-platform rate.

Known limits:
- On a relay connector whose wire message names no platform, `no_reply` is labelled `relay` while `reply_latency` resolves the fronted platform, so that lane's rate splits across two labels.
- A streamed reply that is only attachments counts as replied even if every upload then fails (an undercount).

Not counted: turns that never finish (wedged before the agent starts: #138358, #131145, handled by #138535 / #138383), API-server turns, and turns whose reply is owed by a recovered delivery with no adapter waiting.

## Tests

- `tests/gateway/test_platform_no_reply.py` runs the real `_process_message_background`: `empty`, `dropped`, `delivery_failed`, `interrupted` and `error` each count once with a WARNING (INFO for interrupted). Text, streamed, media-only, TTS and voice replies count nothing, and neither do busy follow-ups, rescued events and unfinished turns. A raising classifier leaves the reply and the processing outcome untouched.
- `tests/gateway/test_no_reply_authority_claim.py` runs a real `SessionAuthority` admission and drain: the executed turn's token reaches the waiting adapter event before the adapter finishes, and a streamed media-only reply on that path counts as replied. It also drives the real claim: a silent plugin consume counts `silent`, a plugin reply counts nothing.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_shared_metrics_gateway_no_reply.py`: vocabulary, contract dimensions, v4 schema validation, exact-token ownership, owning-home routing, relay fronting, catalog platform labels matching `reply_latency`, and collection off (log line only).

The new tests fail on the base commit and pass with the change. The shared-metrics, platform-metrics, session-authority, ingress and turn-marker suites show no new failures, and `scripts/check` is clean.

Exact-head CI for head `6a3761bbfe` (current main `50d2adf1cd` merged in), on GitHub's standard runners from a fork because CI here waits for approval: the full Linux suite in four slices, the Windows lane and the Nix flake check show no failures beyond those main shows on the same runners ([head](https://github.com/100yenadmin/hermes-agent-for-upstream-PR-only/actions/runs/41170373697), [main](https://github.com/100yenadmin/hermes-agent-for-upstream-PR-only/actions/runs/41170193691)). The one exception is a Windows case, `test_failed_setup_never_runs_child_and_releases_handles[resume]`; its `[assign]` sibling fails on main with the same assertion, and this PR does not touch that code.

## Related

Refs #138358, #131145, #138535, #138383 (wedged turns, complementary), #112000 (opt-in silence would make `silent` more common, hence the reason dimension), #144818 (relay shared-metrics smoke), umbrella #145440.

prs.title: Plugin hooks learn where a turn came from: gateway, TUI/Desktop and cron (salvage #143260)
prs.body:
Plugins' `pre_llm_call`/`post_llm_call` hooks now learn where each turn came from (`turn_origin`), on gateway, TUI/Desktop and cron turns.

## Changes
- **Salvage #143260** (cherry-picked, @100yenadmin's authorship kept): keyword-only `turn_origin` on `pre_llm_call` and `post_llm_call`, derived per turn for gateway admitted and direct turns (`native` / `viewer` / `cli` / `api` / `automation` / `peer` / `None`). Conflicts resolved against main: the hooks doc tables now carry `side_question_token` too, and the side-question test drops an assertion main had already removed.
- **Wider coverage**: turns run by the `tui_gateway` engine (TUI, Desktop, and synthesized turns) and cron jobs used to report `None`.
  - A client submit (typed, or queued while a turn ran) is `viewer`; a hidden row is `automation`; a relayed bot author is `peer`.
  - `/loop` ticks, heartbeats, goal continuations, kanban/delegation/process notices and crash auto-continue are `automation`.
  - Cron job turns are `automation`.
- Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/features/hooks.md` (the `turn_origin` table and the fence format) and `developer-guide/observer-hooks.md`.

## Live A/B (real `hermes chat`, scratch home, throwaway plugin that logs hook kwargs, `google/gemini-3.8-flash` on Nous)

| Probe | origin/main `be32e2110df` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `chat -q` turn: `pre_llm_call` / `post_llm_call` `turn_origin` | absent / absent | `cli` / `cli` |
| Interactive classic CLI `/loop 10s ...`: 6 ticks | `turn_origin` absent on all 12 hook calls | `cli` on all 12 (see NOT_COVERED) |

## Tests
- 9 touched test files via `scripts/run_tests.sh` (shared clone, fake HOME): all of #143260's tests pass on this head.
- From #143260: `tests/agent/test_llm_call_hook_turn_origin.py`, `tests/gateway/test_session_turn_origin.py`, plus the retry and side-question test updates.

## NOT_COVERED
- **Fencing `pre_llm_call` context is parked.** It is built (a `<plugin-context>` fence plus a system note, the plugin's own fence tags stripped, cache-safe), but 7 existing tests in `tests/agent/test_api_content_sidecar.py` pin the raw `content + "\n\n" + ctx` bytes (#71998 / bb87e6abce98, 7b3dcee928e6). Changing those tests is a maintainer call, so the commit is held back from this PR.
- **Classic CLI `/loop` ticks report `cli`, not `automation`.** The classic CLI puts the wakeup into its input queue and submits it like typed text (`hermes_cli/cli_loops_mixin.py`), so the gateway admits it as a plain `cli_turn_v1` row. To fix it, the CLI submit needs an automation mark carried through `admit_cli_turn` into `row_turn_origin`. That is a follow-up commit on this branch.
- No live run of the Ink TUI or Desktop: the `tui_gateway` origins in this PR are not live-verified yet.
- `chat -q` (local one-shot) reports `cli` through the gateway path. The in-process ACP server, subagents and managed workers still report `None`, as in #143260.
- Plugin tool handlers get call context (`tool_call_id`, `turn_id`, `platform`, `agent_context`), and `_no_user_can_answer` becomes public: this goes in a separate PR, not started yet.

Refs #127973, #142321. Salvages #143260.

## Infographic

![turn-origin-hooks](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafe5f0/b2JCcP4yEemcHAKVkWcIO_X86L9HQV.png)

prs.title: feat(gateway): hold new turns when memory is nearly full and make children the OOM victims
prs.body:
On a small VPS or Docker host, a memory-hungry terminal command or browser no longer takes the gateway (and every session on it) down with it: the kernel now kills the child, and new turns wait for memory instead of starting into a host that is about to OOM.

## Before / after (live, real `gateway run --force` in a 400 MB `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=400M -p OOMPolicy=continue`, api_server + loopback tool-calling provider)

**OOM victim** — turn 1's `terminal` tool runs a process that grows until the scope OOMs:

| | gateway `oom_score_adj` | child `oom_score_adj` | kernel log | turn 1 reply | gateway after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base `5239b13` | 200 | 200 | `Killed process 1904139 (hermes) anon-rss:242888kB oom_score_adj:200` | empty (connection dropped) | **killed** |
| head | 200 | **700** | `Killed process 1919011 (python3) anon-rss:133196kB oom_score_adj:700` | `TOOL RESULT >> ... 1919011 Killed ...` | **alive** |

**Admission** — a holder process inside the gateway's cgroup fills it to 0 MB headroom for 20 s, then a turn is sent:

| | turn started | turn returned | gateway log |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | immediately, at 0 MB headroom | 1.4 s (holder still alive) | — |
| head | after the holder exited | 18.5 s | `INFO gateway.run: Holding person turn for agent:main:api_server:dm:...: host memory is low` and, while the person waited, `kanban dispatch: system memory pressure is critical; spawning no new workers this tick` |

`hermes status` (head):
```
  Memory:       ok · 43099 MB free of 64142 MB (meminfo) · no gateway running
```
With a live gateway it reads through the gateway's own cgroup and shows `N waiting`.

## Root cause

Nothing in Hermes looked at memory before starting a turn (`gateway.max_concurrent_sessions` is a fixed count; `agent.agent_cache.memory_high_mb` only sheds idle transcripts), and every spawned child inherited the gateway's `oom_score_adj` (`grep oom_score` on main: empty). In a memory cgroup OOM the kernel kills the process with the most memory, which on a small host is usually the long-lived gateway.

## What changed

- `hermes_platform/memory.py` (new) reads headroom as the tighter of cgroup v2 (`memory.max`/`memory.high` minus `memory.current`, `inactive_file` credited back, walked from the gateway's cgroup up to the root so slice/container limits count) and `MemAvailable`. `gateway/admission_memory.py` (new) is the admission policy on top of it, a process-wide FIFO gate: people wait below `critical_mb`; background work (internal events, cron) already below `low_mb` and never ahead of a waiting person. Each admitted turn reserves `reserve_mb` for 30 s so a released queue cannot stampede into the same headroom. The gate publishes `state/memory_guard.json` for `hermes status`.
- Inbound turns (`run_inbound` → `_hm_pre_turn_gates`): the hold runs inside the already-claimed session slot, so follow-up messages queue behind it under `busy_input_mode` exactly as behind a running turn. People get one "waiting for memory" message; after `max_wait_seconds` a resend notice (nothing ran). `/stop` or `/new` abandons the wait (run-generation check); a Stop through the session (API, Desktop, TUI) or a gateway stop latches the claim's pending Stop, and the wait then leaves the queue and settles the turn interrupted before any agent is built; a gateway restart refuses a held chat turn like any new turn.
- Cron (`cron/scheduler_memory_hold.py`): waits as background work before the job's pre-run script or a script-only job starts. On expiry the run is recorded as failed with a plain reason.
- Managed-worker turns (bypass/config-only sessions, kanban cards; `gateway/session_managed_memory.py`) wait before the worker spawns. Kanban cards wait as background work and the rest as people. A background waiter never starts while any person waits. Kanban: the dispatcher spawns nothing while a person waits.
- `hermes_platform/oom.py` (new): raises a spawned child's `oom_score_adj` by 500 relative to the spawner (capped at 1000), right after spawn. Wired into the local terminal (foreground + background, pipe and PTY), the Chrome launcher and the browser CLI (its daemon and Chrome inherit it). Relative, because an unprivileged process cannot lower its own score below the floor its service manager set, and a gateway already at 200 must still be well below its children.
- `hermes status`: `Memory:` row (summary and `--full`). Gateway liveness comes from verified PID/lock discovery, and the status file only carries queue statistics. One coalescing writer thread writes that file outside the admission lock and off the event loop.
- Config `gateway.memory_guard: {enabled, critical_mb, low_mb, reserve_mb, max_wait_seconds}`; docs in `user-guide/configuration.md`. Strings in all 17 locales.

**Default: on, conservative.** `auto` floors are 10% / 20% of the ceiling capped at 256 / 512 MB, so on a large host the guard only engages right before an OOM, when the alternative is the kernel killing the gateway; a 512 MB container is not permanently "critical" because of the gateway's own footprint. Running turns are never touched. `enabled: false` turns the hold off. The `oom_score_adj` change is unconditional on Linux: it changes nothing until the kernel is already choosing a victim.

## Tests

`tests/gateway/test_admission_memory.py` (fix round adds: background never ahead of a waiting person, status write off the lock, verified liveness, config.yaml through the gateway loader, cron hold before the script, managed worker held before spawn; the OOM-victim tests moved to `tests/tools/test_local_env_oom_victim.py` and `tests/hermes_platform/test_oom.py`; round 2: `tests/gateway/test_admission_memory_stop.py` drives a real local session through the FIFO drain, Stops it while it waits for memory and asserts it settles `interrupted` within the wait (red on the round-1 head: still queued after 10 s), plus a restart ending a held chat turn; the cgroup reader test is in `tests/hermes_platform/test_memory.py`, the cron holds in `tests/cron/test_scheduler_memory_hold.py`) (11 originally): cgroup ancestor limit + page-cache credit, people-before-background ordering, reservation vs burst, bounded wait + published waiting count, unknown/disabled admit, the inbound hold (notice then refusal; notice then start), cron failure on expiry, terminal child `oom_score_adj` (red on base: `assert 200 == 700`), relative raise capped. Plus `test_kanban_memory_guard.py`, `test_kanban_per_profile_cap.py`, `test_max_concurrent_sessions.py`: 37 passed. `scripts/check --only health` ok.

## Credit

The queue-under-resource-pressure idea and the `min(MemAvailable, cgroup headroom)` reading follow #97739 by @djpapzin. That PR is a much broader production change (per-worker systemd scopes, a FIFO across API/cron/background, health-guard scripts) with commits under a placeholder identity, so this PR re-implements the admission + OOM-preference slice on current main rather than cherry-picking it. Related: #123176, #56865 (terminal memory guard, #57121), #118117.

## NOT_COVERED

- Docker run (`scripts/hermes_docker_probe.sh` is not in this tree); verified with a cgroup v2 user scope instead, which exercises the same `memory.max` path.
- A messaging platform's "waiting" notice was not seen on a real chat (api_server has no side channel for it); the notice path is covered by the unit test, the hold itself by the live log.
- macOS/Windows: reads `unknown`, admits everything; not run there.
- The child score is written right after spawn, so a grandchild forked in the first microseconds keeps the parent's score (documented in `hermes_platform/oom.py`).

## Infographic

![memory guard](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafe24b/rdhIGocAC9GyCzPebJUkh_jA8HRE1Z.png)

releases.name: Hermes Agent v0.22.7
releases.body:
# Hermes Agent v0.22.7

**Release Date:** November 3, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~174 PRs merged since v0.22.6 into a stable release for the GitHub release (CLI and installers), the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes for this window ship with v0.23.0.

<!-- HERMES_BUILDS_TABLE -->

## About this release

Measured at commit `b200f5bc60e`, the window since v0.22.6 contains **581 non-merge commits** across **554 changed files** (+24,012 / −3,144), **174 merged PRs** and **29 closed issues**.

Also in the window, undocumented here on purpose: opt-in lead routing for Desktop Group Chats (with a Lead badge on the room header), cron jobs that post into Group Chats, room purpose and shared notes, group rooms laid out in one chat column with each member's live state, pinned Kanban boards as quick-switch tabs, `$$TeX$$` diagram labels and mermaid diagrams rendered through Pele, a Desktop update error box that shows the failed update's output with a report link, Web Access naming the step Start is on with a running clock, Telegram on Team Gateway set up by linking an account to the shared bot, an opt-in Slack `thread_followup_silence` for unaddressed thread replies, a Daybreak switch for catalog-listed ChatGPT subscription models, and a batch of new plugin-catalog entries.

**Full curated release notes for this window ship with v0.23.0**, which will document everything from v0.22.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- Microsoft Store app: updates through the Store.
- Desktop app installed from the installer (.exe / .dmg): no change in this release; it updates with the next bundled release.
- CLI: `hermes update`, or re-run the installer one-liner.
- Docker / Hermes Cloud: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:stable` (or `:latest`).

**Full Changelog**: [v0.22.6...v0.22.7](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v0.22.6...v0.22.7)

issues.title: [Feature] Web UI: chat folders to organize launcher session history
issues.body:
## 🎯 The Goal / Use Case

The launcher Web UI keeps **every** chat in one flat, time-ordered list:

- `GET /api/sessions` (`web/backend/api/session.go` → `handleListSessions`) returns a flat `[]sessionListItem`.
- The UI renders that list in a 300px-tall dropdown (`components/chat/session-history-menu.tsx`, `w-72` / `max-h-[300px]`).

There is no way to name, group, or otherwise organize chats. After a few weeks of daily use the history is a wall of "Привет", "Проверь логи", "Сделай плагин…" entries, all sorted only by `updated`, and the only available action is a hard `DELETE`. Users who want to keep their history have to scroll and guess; users who want a tidy list end up deleting chats they still need.

**What I want:** user-defined **folders** for chats in the launcher, and a way to put a chat into a folder, so that related work (one project, one topic, one experiment) stays together and survives restarts.

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Add a lightweight "chat folders" layer on top of the existing session store — **no changes to the session JSONL format**, folders are pure metadata.

### Data model

```json
// <workspace>/state/session_folders.json
{
  "version": 1,
  "folders": [
    {
      "id": "f_01J9ZK3M",
      "name": "PicoClaw plugins",
      "icon": "📦",            // optional, emoji
      "order": 0,
      "created": "2026-10-27T01:02:03Z",
      "updated": "2026-10-27T01:02:03Z",
      "session_ids": ["2fe8311d-...", "9a12..."]
    }
  ]
}
```

- One chat belongs to **at most one** folder (simple, predictable; nested folders are out of scope).
- Chats that are in no folder stay in the existing flat "Ungrouped / Recent" list.
- A folder id is authoritative even if the session file is deleted later — dangling ids are dropped lazily when the list is built.

### HTTP API (launcher backend)

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/session-folders` | list folders (folders only; chat titles still come from `/api/sessions`) |
| `POST` | `/api/session-folders` | create `{name, icon?, color?}` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/session-folders/{id}` | rename / re-icon / reorder |
| `DELETE` | `/api/session-folders/{id}` | delete folder (chats are **not** deleted) |
| `PUT` | `/api/session-folders/{id}/sessions/{sessionID}` | move chat into folder |
| `DELETE` | `/api/session-folders/{id}/sessions/{sessionID}` | remove chat from folder |

`GET /api/sessions` items gain an optional `folder_id` field so the UI can group a single, already-paginated list without a second round-trip.

### UI

- In the history dropdown, chats are grouped: each folder is a collapsible section (name + chat count), followed by "Ungrouped".
- Each chat row gets a "Move to folder…" submenu (radio-style folder list + "New folder…").
- A "＋ New folder" item at the top of the dropdown, and rename/delete in the folder's own submenu.
- Folder state is per-workspace (it lives next to `sessions/`), so the same workspace on another machine/launcher shows the same folders.

Nice-to-have follow-ups (not in the first patch): drag & drop between folders, pinning, searching inside folders, and "auto-file a chat into the last used folder" heuristics.

## 🛠️ Potential Implementation (Optional)

1. `web/backend/api/session_folders.go`
   - `sessionFolderStore` with `sync.Mutex`, load-modify-save under a temp-file + `os.Rename` (same pattern as other launcher state writes), file at `resolveSessionsDir(...)/../state/session_folders.json`.
   - Validation: name length 1..80 runes, unique folder ids, unknown folder id → 404, unknown session id → 404 (resolved through the existing `findPicoJSONLSession`).
   - Register the routes in `registerSessionRoutes` (`router.go` already calls it).
2. `web/backend/api/session.go` — read the store once inside `handleListSessions` and set `FolderID` on each item.
3. `web/frontend/src/api/session-folders.ts` — typed client using `launcherFetch`.
4. `web/frontend/src/hooks/use-session-folders.ts` — CRUD + optimistic move, `react-query`-free like the existing `use-session-history`.
5. `web/frontend/src/components/chat/session-history-menu.tsx` — render grouped sections, add `DropdownMenuSub` for "Move to folder…".
6. i18n: new `chat.folders.*` keys in `en.json`, `zh.json`, `pt-br.json`, `bn-in.json`, `cs.json`.

The feature is local to the launcher: gateway, channels, and session compaction are untouched.

## 🐠 Impact & Roadmap Alignment

- [x] This is a Nice-to-Have / Enhancement
- [ ] This is a Core Feature
- [ ] This aligns with the current Roadmap

Related prior art: #3406 / #3413 proposed a global multi-channel session sidebar with grouping (stale-closed, not merged). Folders are complementary to that direction: the sidebar can group by *source*, folders group by *user intent*. This proposal is deliberately small and self-contained so it does not conflict with a future session-sidebar rework.

## 🎨 Alternatives Considered

- **Rename a chat instead of folders** — helps a bit, but does not scale past a couple of dozen chats.
- **Archive instead of folders** — good for decluttering, not for organizing; also destructive-ish in the sense that archived chats disappear from view.
- **Tags / multi-label** — more flexible, but a much bigger UI surface (filter bar, tag editor, multi-select) and harder to make compact in a dropdown.
- **Frontend-only, `localStorage`** — trivial, but does not sync across browsers/devices and would be invisible to the agent (an agent can't put a chat into a folder, and the state dies with a browser profile).
- **Do it as a workspace skill** — possible (a skill + local web UI can manage folders over `workspace/sessions`), but the launcher dropdown would still be flat, which is exactly the thing being complained about.

## 📖 Additional Context

Prototype status: I have a working prototype of the backend store + API in a branch and I am happy to open a PR if the shape of the API above is acceptable. I am also fine with someone else implementing it and stealing this design — the important part is the `state/session_folders.json` shape + `folder_id` on `/api/sessions`, so that a skill-based UI and the launcher UI can share the same data.

issues.title: 智能路由：turn 中途不重判、无重复调用熔断，轻量模型可空转烧掉千万 token
issues.body:
## 现象

智能路由（`agents.defaults.routing`）把一轮简单对话交给轻量模型后，该轻量模型在**单轮内空转 222 次 LLM 调用**，约 9 分钟内累计消耗约 **1310 万输入 token**（约 13,098,285 tokens），输出内容几乎恒定、无任何有效进展。整轮最终被手动中止。

## 复现数据（真实事故 trace）

| 指标 | 值 |
| --- | --- |
| 时间窗口 | 09:00:27 – 09:09:48（约 561 秒） |
| LLM 调用次数 | 222 次（`iterations_total=222`） |
| 命中模型 | 100% 为轻量模型（一次都未切回主力） |
| prompt tokens | 从 11,218 逐步涨到 78,679 |
| 累计输入 tokens | ≈ 13,098,285 |
| 每次输出 tokens | 恒定 75 / 76（退化循环） |
| turn.end 状态 | `aborted`，`duration_ms=563919` |

特征：每一轮响应都带着几乎相同的工具调用（同名工具、近似参数），模型在"调用工具 → 得到结果 → 再调用同一个工具"之间循环，上下文随工具结果不断膨胀（prompt tokens 持续上涨），但没有任何收敛迹象。

## 原因分析（四个叠加因素）

1. **turn 中途不重判模型**
   路由只在 turn 开始时判定一次并选定模型档位，之后整轮固定不变。即使上下文已经从 1 万 token 涨到 7 万+、工作明显是工具密集型，也不会升级回主力模型。

2. **没有重复调用熔断**
   对"连续多轮返回完全相同的工具调用"没有任何检测。模型退化循环时只受 `max_tool_iterations` 约束，默认 50 轮仍会消耗大量 token；本例中循环甚至在校验之外持续了 222 轮。

3. **插话消息可绕过硬性迭代上限**
   迭代循环的继续条件类似：

   ```go
   for iteration < max_tool_iterations || len(pendingMessages) > 0 || graceful
   ```

   pending（steering）消息存在时循环不受 `max_tool_iterations` 限制，等于没有硬上限，一个坏循环可以无限延长。

4. **轻量模型池整体失败时直接报错**
   轻量模型的候选全部失败（服务不可用、密钥失效）时，本轮直接以错误结束，而不是退回主力模型。

## 建议

- **轮内升级（escalation）**：轻量模型单次响应 prompt tokens 超阈值（如 32k）或连续 N 轮（如 3）调用工具时，本轮剩余请求切换到主力模型；每轮最多升级一次。
- **重复调用熔断（repeat breaker）**：连续 N 次（如 5）出现"同名工具 + 相同参数（规范化后）"即中止本轮，并返回明确提示；对所有模型档位生效。
- **steering 硬顶**：插话延长轮次需有绝对上限（例如 `max_tool_iterations × 3`，且不低于 `max_tool_iterations + 20`）。
- **轻量池失败回退**：轻量模型候选全部失败时自动改走主力池，而不是直接失败。

上述四项守卫已在 fork 中实现并附集成测试（重复熔断、prompt 升级、工具强度升级、轻量池失败回退），可作为参考：

- 实现提交：`cnbillsomeday/picoclaw@24382d7c`
- 发布：https://github.com/cnbillsomeday/picoclaw/releases/tag/session-header-v1.3.1

prs.title: feat(channels): add Sendblue iMessage and SMS transport
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

Adds a native Sendblue channel so users can text a PicoClaw agent over iMessage/SMS and get its answer on the same phone. The guide covers fresh free-account setup, human phone/contact verification, model prerequisites, secrets, and receive-webhook registration.

This draft proposes a self-contained channel through the existing factory and shared webhook server. It validates the secret, receiving line and sender; normalizes direct-message context; deduplicates the last 4096 accepted handles in memory; and uses the existing outbound workers. Configuration supports named instances, redacted secrets, environment overrides, persistence, and credential-triggered reloads.

Scope is direct-message text. Groups/status callbacks are ignored; incoming attachments produce an explicit unsupported-attachment notice. There is no durable inbox or exactly-once guarantee. Ambiguous sends are not automatically retried, because the provider endpoint has no idempotency key.

## 🗣️ Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 📖 Documentation update

## 🤖 AI Code Generation

- [x] 🤖 Fully AI-generated (100% AI, 0% Human)

Independent human review is still pending.

## 🔗 Related Issue

No existing issue. Draft integration proposal; upstream design acceptance is pending.

## 📚 Technical Context

- **References:** [Send API](https://docs.sendblue.com/api/resources/messages/methods/send), [receiving/free-plan contact verification](https://docs.sendblue.com/getting-started/receiving-messages), [webhook registration](https://docs.sendblue.com/api/resources/webhooks).
- **Reasoning:** the channel exposes hosted phone messaging through PicoClaw's existing interfaces without requiring an Apple device on the gateway host. No new dependencies are added.
- **Base:** `bbf6893ca7afad27f1d00a0f5a45982a549c6ed6`
- **Head:** `4cacb17d68fdd0ebb685c1afa00fbc6aeb00f01d`

## 🧪 Test Environment

- **Hardware / OS:** macOS arm64
- **Runtime:** Go 1.25.13; CI build tags `goolm,stdjson`
- **Model / Provider:** deterministic local model fixture and fake Sendblue HTTP/TLS endpoints
- **Channel:** Sendblue, loaded through the normal factory/configuration registry

Validation:

- The same config probe rejects Sendblue as an unknown channel on the unmodified base and accepts it on head. Base `go test ./pkg/config ./pkg/channels` passes.
- `go test -tags goolm,stdjson -race ./pkg/channels/sendblue ./pkg/config ./pkg/channels ./pkg/gateway`: **passed**.
- Two-turn conversation exercises the real agent loop, channel dispatcher, bus and session history. Both replies use the configured line and original sender; the follow-up retains the first conversation turn.
- Tests cover duplicate concurrent callbacks, wrong secret/sender/line, malformed/oversized JSON, outbound/group callbacks, failed bus publication, provider HTTP/semantic failures, secret save/reload, environment overrides, and named-instance credential reload hashes.
- Golangci-lint **v2.10.1**, CI tags, affected packages: **0 issues**. Repository formatter applied to changed Go files. `scripts/lint-docs.sh`: **passed**.
- Full `go test -tags goolm,stdjson ./...` was attempted. Four failures were independently reproduced on the unmodified base: `TestShellTool_RelativePathWithSlashAllowed`, `TestShellTool_DevNullAllowed`, `TestShellTool_FileURISandboxing` (macOS path/safety-guard behavior), and `TestEvolutionBridge_TurnEndUsesExplicitAttemptTrail` (background work racing TempDir cleanup). No waiver is claimed; upstream maintainer review of these baseline failures remains pending. No existing tests were changed or skipped.

**Draft evidence limit:** no live account verification or handset delivery is claimed. Local fixtures prove framework routing and adapter behavior; iMessage and SMS carrier delivery must be verified separately using the guide's checklist. A QUEUED response is API acceptance, not delivery confirmation.

issues.title: bug: stranded outbound.db-journal after host reboot is never recovered; readonly poll fails every tick forever
issues.body:
## Summary

If the host (or the whole VM) goes down while a container is mid-write to `outbound.db`, the stranded `outbound.db-journal` is **never recovered**, because nothing re-opens that DB read-write until a new container spawns. The host's readonly delivery poll then fails with `SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK` ("attempt to write a readonly database") **every tick, indefinitely**. For a session that only runs scheduled tasks, no message arrives to trigger a respawn, so it stays stuck until someone intervenes. Observed: **~509,000 identical error lines over 5 days** (532 MB error log), and the session's every-10-minutes scheduled task silently did not run for that whole period.

This is the same mechanism as #2516 / #2640, but a third trigger that the open fixes do not cover, and one where the proposed "downgrade to debug" would make the failure *invisible* rather than just quieter.

## How it happened

1. Host reboot (unattended kernel patching) at 03:00 while a scheduled-task container was writing to its session's `outbound.db`.
2. Result on disk: `outbound.db` last modified 02:50, `outbound.db-journal` modified 03:00, with a valid journal header (SQLite magic bytes, non-zero page count).
3. After boot, the `sessions` row still read `status=active`, `container_status=running`, with a stale `last_active`; no container existed for it.
4. Host `pollActive` -> `drainSession` -> `getDueOutboundMessages` -> `Database.prepare` threw `SqliteError: attempt to write a readonly database`, once per second (`ACTIVE_POLL_MS`), for 5 days.

Reproduced deterministically on a *copy*: copy `outbound.db` + `outbound.db-journal` to a temp dir and open with `mode=ro` -> same error. Opening the original read-write once (SQLite rolls the journal back and deletes it) fixed it immediately: `integrity_check` = ok, all rows intact; the next sweep then woke a container for the overdue task and the task series resumed.

Version: 2.2.0, `journal_mode = DELETE`.

## Why the open PRs don't cover it

- #2750 (fixes #2516/#2640) runs `recoverOutboundJournal` only as the `onExit` of `killContainer` (ceiling / claim-stuck / restart kill). A host reboot, OOM-killer, or Docker daemon restart never goes through those paths, so recovery never runs.
- #2750 and #4047 both classify the whole `SQLITE_READONLY*` family as "transient" and return quietly from the poll. That is right for the live-container commit-window race in #2640, but for a **persistent** hot journal with **no live container** it turns an obvious error flood into complete silence: the session never delivers, never recovers, and nothing logs at error level.

## Suggested fix

Distinguish the two situations the same error code covers:

1. **Transient race** (container alive, commit in flight): retry next tick, debug-level log. As proposed in #2640/#2750.
2. **Persistent** (journal present, **no running container for the session**, or the same session has hit this N consecutive ticks): run the existing `recoverOutboundJournal` (brief read-write open) for that session. It is safe whenever no container holds the DB.

Concretely, also call `recoverOutboundJournal` for every session at **host startup**, before the first delivery poll / sweep (covers reboot, crash, OOM, daemon restart), and have the poll escalate to `error` (with backoff, not 1/s) if the same session keeps failing after a recovery attempt.

Secondary: a log line per second per session with a full stack is what produced the 532 MB file; even when a real fault persists, repeated identical failures for one session should be rate-limited.

## Workaround

Open the session's `outbound.db` read-write once while no container is running (e.g. `python3 -c "import sqlite3; sqlite3.connect('outbound.db').execute('pragma integrity_check')"`), then confirm the `-journal` file is gone.

issues.title: [bug] add-onecli: one slow health probe stops every running session
issues.body:
**Affected version / commit:** NanoClaw 2026.10.1-rc.2, upstream base 57c4440a. The code is unchanged on main at 8797ad37 (`.claude/skills/add-onecli/payload/src/gateway-providers/onecli.ts`, `probeHealth`).

**Host platform:** Linux. Raspberry Pi 5, Debian 13 (trixie), aarch64, Docker 29.9.2, Node 22.23.4. Default provider (Claude), OneCLI 1.42.0.

## What happened?

`probeHealth()` polls the gateway's `/health` every 5 s with `AbortSignal.timeout(5_000)`. When a single probe fails, it marks **every** live lease unavailable. `container-runner` then calls `killContainer(sessionId, 'gateway-unavailable')` for each one. It doesn't retry, ignores how many probes failed, and doesn't check whether the sessions' own gateway traffic is still flowing.

On a host that is briefly short of resources, `/health` can take more than 5 s even though the gateway is still serving. Every running agent is then stopped mid-turn. Our error log shows **18 failed probes and 124 session kills** (about 7 agents per failed probe). In 15 of those the kills come in the same second as the probe failure.

The mass kill then makes things worse:

1. Each stop runs `docker stop`, `docker rm --force` and a `docker ps` probe through `execFileSync` (30 s timeout each), which blocks the host's event loop (the class in #2665). That makes the next probe more likely to time out too.
2. `docker rm --force` races `--rm` auto-removal (dockerd: `removal of container … is already in progress`). `stop()` throws `session realization failed: unknown`, and the runtime keeps its claim and gateway lease (`Session teardown incomplete`), which is #4057. The next wakes then fail for the same session.
3. A container stopped mid-write to `outbound.db` leaves a hot journal behind, so the host's read-only handle fails every sweep from then on (#4056). See the comment there: the sweep's wake path fails too, so the session stays stuck until a new inbound message arrives.

In our incident (3 Nov 2026, 13:48–14:38 UTC) two agents that had just received a brief were killed before writing a word, killed again on retry, and then stayed stuck. An answer that takes them 4 minutes to produce arrived after 56 minutes. It came only because a human re-sent the request.

The gateway was slow, not down: the OneCLI API returned `408 Request Timeout` and kept serving CONNECTs between stalls. containerd was showing the same strain at the same time (`DeadlineExceeded` on container deletes, `Container failed to exit within 10s of kill`).

**A second route to the same mass stop.** `gateway-approval-coordinator.ts` `superviseSubscription` treats one failed or ended approval long-poll the same way: `failSubscription` → `reportUnavailable` → `stopGatewaySessionsForUnavailability` stops every active session and closes admission. In the same incident:

```
[13:53:01.039] ERROR Gateway approval subscription failed gatewayProvider="onecli"
[13:53:01.041] ERROR Gateway unavailable; stopping active sessions
```

So a fix for the probe alone isn't enough: a slow gateway that times out one long-poll still stops every agent. Denying pending approval holds while the bridge is down is right, but stopping running sessions could share the probe's tolerance, or wait for the health probe to confirm the outage.

## What did you expect?

A short spell of gateway slowness should not end turns that are in flight. One timeout of a cheap health probe isn't evidence that the gateway has gone. Something closer to this:

- Declare the gateway unavailable only after N consecutive failures across a window of at least ~30 s, as a circuit breaker would. Count a failure only when the probe got no answer at all; for 5xx/408 responses, back off and keep probing.
- While the gateway is suspect, **close admission** (no new spawns; `gatewayUnavailableReason` already exists for this) but leave running sessions alone. A session whose gateway really is dead fails its own requests and exits by the normal path (the fail-fast in #2657 tier 3).
- Keep the monitor running after a failure (today it calls `stopHealthMonitor()`), so recovery is noticed and admission reopens without waiting for a new lease.

## How can we reproduce it?

Expected reproduction, from reading the code. It hasn't been run on our live install, because it would stop every running agent:

1. Install with `/add-onecli`, then start two or three sessions that hold a gateway lease.
2. Make `/health` slow for a little over 5 s once, e.g. `docker pause onecli; sleep 6; docker unpause onecli`.
3. All running sessions are killed with `reason="gateway-unavailable"`, even though the gateway is healthy again a second later.

## Relevant redacted logs

```
[13:48:39.824] ERROR OneCLI gateway unavailable err={ type: "DOMException", message: "The operation was aborted due to timeout" }
[13:48:39.824] ERROR Gateway session became unavailable; stopping agent runtime sessionId="sess-…ul0tns" reason="OneCLI gateway unavailable"
[13:50:12.152] ERROR Gateway session became unavailable; stopping agent runtime sessionId="sess-…4245mr" reason="OneCLI gateway unavailable"
[13:50:30.209] ERROR Failed to stop session sessionId="sess-…4245mr" reason="gateway-unavailable" err={ message: "session realization failed: unknown" }
[13:50:30.812] ERROR Session teardown incomplete; retaining its claim and gateway lease sessionId="sess-…4245mr"
[13:52:11.192] ERROR Gateway session became unavailable; stopping agent runtime sessionId="sess-…7qma68" reason="OneCLI gateway unavailable"
[14:03:00.158] WARN wakeContainer failed — host-sweep will retry err={ type: "OneCLIRequestError", message: "[URL=…/v1/agents] [StatusCode=408] OneCLI returned 408 Request Timeout" }
[14:22:41.528] INFO Killing container sessionId="sess-…7qma68" reason="gateway-unavailable"
```
dockerd, same window:
```
13:49:02 level=warning msg="Container failed to exit within 10s of kill - trying direct SIGKILL"
13:49:22 level=warning msg="failed to delete container from containerd" error="DeadlineExceeded: stream terminated by RST_STREAM"
13:49:45 level=error msg="error removing container" error="removal of container … is already in progress"
```

**Last version that worked:** not known. The single-shot probe has been there since the provider moved into the skill (d5c7cccc).

We're carrying a minimal fix locally: the gateway is declared unavailable only after 3 consecutive failed probes, the in-flight guard is tied to the monitor generation, and the probe releases the response body. Happy to open it as a PR, alongside or instead of the admission-only approach above.

Related: #2657 (gateway supervision; the opposite failure: no reaction to a gateway that is dead), #2665, #4057, #4056.

prs.title: feat(proton-mail): HTML tables read one row per line (stacked on #4218)
prs.body:
## Summary **Stacked on #4218.** Only the last four commits are new here; the rest are #4218's, and drop out of this diff once it merges. New in this PR: `src/channels/proton-mail.ts` and its test, +337/−6. html-to-text's default writes a whole HTML table on one line, with nothing between cells (`NameGradeSmithA*Jones…`). So an agent misreads report mails, timetables, invoices and lists. This adds a table formatter to the adapter's HTML worker: - **Data tables, one row per line.** Cells are split by ` | `, and a cell's own lines are joined by ` / `. A blank cell is shown as `–`, so rows stay aligned. Columns that are empty in every row (a template's spacers) are dropped. - **Cells on a real grid.** `colspan` keeps later columns in place, and a `rowspan` value is repeated in each row it covers. - **Each cell rendered on its own.** Cells go through html-to-text's own table builder, so a cell's paragraphs (Outlook writes every cell as `

`) can't split its row. - **Layout tables as paragraphs.** Newsletters are built of tables. A table with no row of two cells, or with a cell over 10 lines or 500 characters, is written as its cells' text, each as a block. - **Nothing a mail client shows is dropped.** Rows inside wrappers (`

`, `
`) are found, and a caption, loose text or a stray block is kept in place. A nested table is its cell's content. - **Hidden-text marks still hold.** - A hidden table, row group or row is marked piece by piece: each cell, plus whatever else the formatter keeps. - A hidden empty link is now marked too, anywhere in the mail. html-to-text prints its address, so it counts as content. - **No compiler can rewrite the formatter.** It is the worker's own JavaScript, not a compiled function taken with `toString()`. Under `tsx` (`pnpm run dev`), esbuild wraps inner functions in `__name()` calls the worker doesn't have. That made every mail with a table fail to convert, until a real-mail replay caught it. ## Related work Follow-up to #4218 (the Proton Mail adapter), kept separate so that review stays on its own scope; #4218's description lists table layout as out of scope. ## Change kind - [ ] `kind/bug` - [x] `kind/feature` - [ ] `kind/documentation` - [ ] `kind/cleanup` - [ ] `kind/hardening` ## Validation Run locally on this head (CI does not run tests on PRs into `channels`), after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: ``` $ pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/proton-mail.test.ts src/channels/proton-mail-adapter.test.ts \ src/channels/proton-mail-registration.test.ts src/test-utils/fake-imap.test.ts Test Files 4 passed (4) Tests 256 passed (256) $ pnpm exec tsc --noEmit (no output, exit 0) ``` - **eslint:** 0 errors. - **Tests:** 15 table tests run real HTML through the actual worker: data, Outlook, layout and nested tables; key/value rows with a blank; multi-line cells; colspan and rowspan; wrappers, captions and loose text; hidden tables, rows and empty links; spacer columns. One of them runs the conversion in a real `tsx` subprocess, the path vitest's own compilation hides. Each fix's tests failed on the commit before it. - **Production build:** the built `dist/` worker was checked by hand. - **Real inbox:** the old and new conversion compared side by side over a real inbox (637 mails, read-only, counts only). 114 of 121 mails with tables changed, giving 567 row lines. Total text is 0.3% smaller, the longest line is unchanged, and no hidden-text marks were lost. - [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not) ## User and release impact - [ ] No user-visible behavior change - [x] User-visible change — release note below - [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback ```release-note Proton Mail: HTML tables in mail reach the agent one row per line, cells split by " | ", instead of run together on one line. ``` ## Security and trust boundaries - The formatter changes how text is laid out, not what is trusted. Hidden HTML is still marked with the mail's random code: in tables, cell by cell, along with captions and loose text. Hidden empty links are now marked too. - No new dependencies. ## Skill delivery - [x] Not a skill - [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above `/add-proton-mail` (#3726) copies the adapter from `channels`, so it picks this up with no change of its own. ## AI assistance - [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change - [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(docker-driver): wait out in-flight --rm auto-removal on stop
prs.body:
## Summary

Stops `DockerHandle.stop()` from reporting a failed teardown when Docker's own `--rm` auto-removal is still finishing.

- **Problem**: agent containers are created with `--rm`. `stop()` runs `docker stop`, which starts Docker's auto-removal, then `docker rm --force`, which the daemon rejects while that removal is in flight. `#confirmRemoved` probes `docker ps` once, still sees the container, and throws `session realization failed: unknown`. The container is gone a few milliseconds later.
- **Evidence**: on one Docker Desktop install, 60 of 164 absolute-ceiling kills over several days logged `Failed to stop session`. In one incident the daemon log shows the `ps` probe at `21:31:59.861` and "A container has been removed" at `.876`. A second `stop()` from `finishAndResolve` succeeds, so nothing leaks; the cost is a false error and a teardown marked incomplete.
- **Fix**: `#confirmRemoved` polls the same probe up to 10 times, 200 ms apart, and returns once the container is gone. A failing probe (daemon down) still throws at once, unretried, so auto-removal stays distinguishable from an outage. The original `rm` error is thrown only if the container is still there after about 2 s.
- **Concurrency**: the poll makes `stop()` yield, so concurrent `stop()` calls on one handle now share one teardown promise. Without that, a second kill could finish first, let the session respawn under the same deterministic container name, and the first poll would then see the new container. A failed teardown is not cached, so the retry in `finishAndResolve` still works.
- **Out of scope**: a throw while removing the main container still skips auxiliary container and private network cleanup in `stop()`. That predates this change.

## Related work

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `confirmRemoved`, "removal in progress", "session realization failed"). The change is limited to the Docker driver's stop path and its fake CLI.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/drivers/` -> 5 files, 152 tests passed
- `pnpm test` -> 274 files passed, 2 skipped; 3357 tests passed, 15 skipped
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` -> clean
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the three changed files -> 0 errors, same 18 warnings as before the change
- New tests in `src/drivers/docker-driver.test.ts` (`removal racing Docker auto-removal`): in-flight removal resolves after 2 probes; a container that never goes rejects as `unknown` after 10 probes; a failing probe rejects as `runtime-unavailable` after 1 probe; concurrent stops issue one `stop` and one `rm`; a stop after a failed stop retries. The existing force-remove test now also asserts no probe runs when `rm` succeeds.
- With the `docker-driver.ts` change reverted, 3 of the new tests fail (in-flight removal, never removed, concurrent stops).
- `FakeCli` gains an optional `once` flag on a scripted response, used by the new tests.

## Summary

`/add-discord` installs adapter 4.41.1, which drops every server message that @mentions anyone. The skill now applies a pnpm patch with the upstream fix.
- **Merge order**: land https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4252 first. The skill now copies `src/channels/discord-gateway.test.ts`, which that PR adds to `channels`. Merged before it, `/add-discord` fails at its copy step, and until then the `registry-skills` job skips `add-discord` as unavailable.
- **Problem**: the adapter forwards each gateway packet after discord.js has patched it in place into a circular object (`MessageMentions.js:100`: `Object.assign(mention.member, { user: mention })`). `JSON.stringify` throws, the log says `Error forwarding Gateway event`, and the message is lost. Details and a regression test are in https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4252.
- **Fix**: the skill copies `patches/@chat-adapter__discord@4.41.1.patch` and registers it with `pnpm pkg set` before `nc:dep`, the way `/add-matrix` ships its patch. The patch is vercel/chat 81e1a8c (adapter 4.42.0) line for line, plus a comment. `REMOVE.md` unregisters it before uninstalling. When the adapter is already installed (a setup re-run, where `nc:dep` skips it), the same step reinstalls so the patch applies, as `/add-imessage` does for its override.
- **Check in every install**: the skill also copies and runs `src/channels/discord-gateway.test.ts`, which feeds the installed adapter a mention and goes red without the patch. The registration test alone passes with an unpatched adapter.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-proton-mail`: Proton Mail as a channel through a local Proton Mail Bridge built from source in Docker (arm64 and x86). After review, this PR is the skill only; the adapter, its tests and its deps are in #4218 against `channels`, which the skill copies from.
- **Skill**: copies the adapter from `channels`, appends the barrel line, pins five deps, builds Bridge, signs it in, stores its credentials, runs it, wires the owner.
- **Bridge password**: `bridge/store-secrets.sh` writes it straight to `.env` (mode 600) instead of an `nc:run capture`, which the setup engine logged verbatim. The vault is read inside the container (`bridge-secrets.sh`) and only single fields leave it, under `--log-driver none` — `vault-editor read` prints the whole decrypted vault, refresh token and key passphrase included.
- **Certificate pin**: the same script saves Bridge's own TLS certificate and sets `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE`, so the adapter verifies Bridge even on loopback.
- **Isolation**: Bridge runs on its own Docker network (`nanoclaw-mail`), out of reach of agent containers on the default network, as uid 10001 with `--cap-drop ALL` and `no-new-privileges`; ports published on `127.0.0.1` only.
- **Supply chain**: base images pinned by digest; the release pinned by commit and checked against its tag (Proton's tags are lightweight, so unsigned; the commits are signed).
- **Updates**: Bridge runs without its launcher and the entrypoint discards downloads — the updater fetches Proton's x86 binary, which replaces the pinned build and cannot run on arm64; login turns auto-update off.
- **Docs**: a Security section on what Proton verifies, what the adapter relies on, and how approval cards are bound to their answers; REMOVE.md removes only what apply creates, idempotently.
- **Out of scope**: a `secret` option for `capture:` (engine change); a generic IMAP/SMTP channel (maintainers' call).

## Related work

Adapter: #4218 (lands first). Review: see the comments on this PR.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/skill-directives.ts .claude/skills/add-proton-mail/SKILL.md` → no problems, no warnings
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts scripts/skill-directives.test.ts scripts/skill-policy.test.ts` → 331 passed (includes this skill's `apply-fixtures.json`)
- `pnpm skill-pins:check` → matches
- Bridge image built from this Dockerfile (v3.27.0, commit check passing). Throwaway containers: Bridge as uid 10001 under `--cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges` on its own network opens IMAP/SMTP; `store-secrets.sh` against a throwaway volume writes `.env` 600 and the certificate, and fails cleanly with no account; a pinned-CA `ImapFlow` verifies the real Bridge certificate while system CAs reject it
- Network probes: a container on Docker's default network reached #3726's socat listener; on `nanoclaw-mail` it cannot, from the default or an `--internal` network; the host still connects through the published port; socat bound to loopback inside the container breaks the published port (why loopback binding was not used)
- Manual, Raspberry Pi 5: an existing root-owned volume chowned to uid 10001 and run with the new flags — the existing login carried over, the adapter connects with the pinned certificate, SMTP STARTTLS + AUTH verified

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

On adapter 4.41.1 a Discord bot never receives a server message that @mentions anyone. This backports the upstream fix as a pnpm patch and adds a regression test.
- **Merge order**: land this before https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4251, whose skill copies `src/channels/discord-gateway.test.ts` from this branch.
- **Problem**: the adapter's gateway `raw` handler forwards each packet after an `await`. By then discord.js has handled the same object, and `MessageMentions.js:100` runs `Object.assign(mention.member, { user: mention })`, which makes the packet circular. `JSON.stringify` in `forwardGatewayEvent` throws, the log says `Error forwarding Gateway event … Converting circular structure to JSON`, and the message is lost. Edits of recent messages hit it too. DMs and messages without mentions get through, so with the default `mention-sticky` wiring a server channel never engages the bot.
- **Fix**: `patches/@chat-adapter__discord@4.41.1.patch` is vercel/chat 81e1a8c (adapter 4.42.0) line for line, plus a comment. It snapshots `packet.d` with `structuredClone` before the first `await`, and forwards the snapshot.
- **Delivery**: `/add-discord` copies and registers the patch before installing the adapter, the way `/add-matrix` ships its own, and reinstalls when the adapter is already present (a setup re-run). Installs read the skill from `main`, so the same skill change is in https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4251. This PR adds the branch's own registration, lockfile entry, and a regression test in `src/channels/discord-gateway.test.ts`, which the skill copies into installs and runs after install.
- **Why not bump to 4.42.0 or 4.43.0**: skill lint requires every `@chat-adapter/*` pin to equal the `chat` core version, and those adapters pin their own `chat` and `@chat-adapter/shared` exactly. So the bump moves core and all eight adapters, with behavior changes in Slack, Teams, Telegram, WhatsApp, GitHub and Linear. That deserves its own PR; this one changes Discord only.
- **When the cohort moves past 4.41.1**: delete the patch here and in the skill, and replace skill step 3 with a refresh step that unregisters it, as step 3 now says. pnpm refuses an unused patch (`ERR_PNPM_UNUSED_PATCH`), so installs that registered it would otherwise fail to update. `skill-pins:sync` also flags the leftover patch name.

## Related work

No issue here yet. I searched issues and PRs for "circular structure", "Error forwarding Gateway event", "structuredClone", mention reports and Chat SDK bumps. Upstream fix: vercel/chat#923 (for vercel/chat#912). Companion PR for `main`: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4251.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

CI does not run tests on PRs to `channels`, so everything below is local.

- New test `src/channels/discord-gateway.test.ts` drives `startGatewayListener` the way the bridge does. A stubbed `Client.prototype.login` emits one raw `MESSAGE_CREATE` or `MESSAGE_UPDATE` that @mentions the bot, then applies the `MessageMentions.js` mutation in the same turn. The test asserts one webhook POST carrying the message as sent, and no logged error.
- Without the patch both cases fail with `Error forwarding Gateway event … property 'user' closes the circle`. That happens both on this branch and in a real install made with today's skill. With the patch, both pass. The same test passes unchanged on the released 4.42.0 and 4.43.0 adapters, so it stays useful after the bump.
- Whole host suite (`pnpm exec vitest run`, Node 25, macOS) at this head: 4,808 passed, 8 failed, none in Discord code. The 8 are zsh-driven tests (`add-tavily-tool-upgrade`, `add-vercel-onecli`, `migrate-openclaw-vault`) that fail the same way on untouched `channels`.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `tsc --noEmit`, prettier, eslint on the test file, `skill-pins:check` and skill lint all pass.
- Live: the same patch has run on one Discord install since 2026-11-02. Server @mentions reach the agent there now; before the patch none did.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Discord: server messages that @mention anyone, including the bot, now reach the agent. Adapter 4.41.1 dropped them; `/add-discord` and `/update-nanoclaw` now apply a patch with the upstream fix.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Patches third-party code in `node_modules`: the 7-line upstream change from vercel/chat 81e1a8c, readable in the patch file. The lockfile pins the patch hash. No new permissions, credentials or network access.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

Footprint: the skill copies `patches/@chat-adapter__discord@4.41.1.patch` and `src/channels/discord-gateway.test.ts`, and sets `pnpm.patchedDependencies` in `package.json`. `REMOVE.md` deletes the registration before `pnpm uninstall`, then both files. Fresh-clone checks on `main` are in https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4251.

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

<!-- Required. -->
- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

<details>
<summary>Why the upstream fix is more than payload fidelity</summary>

vercel/chat#923 scoped its change to payload fidelity. Its author found no cycle from `Message.js`, which assigns a `User` (that serializes flat through `toJSON`). The cycle comes from `MessageMentions.js:100` instead: for each mention with a `member`, it sets `mention.member.user = mention`, where `mention` is an element of `packet.d.mentions`. That is a real back-reference into the packet. The line is in discord.js 14.25.1 (the adapter's floor) through 14.28.0, and runs for any guild message with mentions while the guild is cached.
</details>
