prs.title: feat(channels): add native Proton Mail adapter via Proton Mail Bridge
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The adapter half of #3726, moved to the `channels` registry branch as review asked; #3726 keeps the skill (`/add-proton-mail`) and the Bridge container on `main`.
- **What**: a native IMAP/SMTP adapter (`src/channels/proton-mail.ts`) for a local Proton Mail Bridge, its tests, a faithful fake IMAP server for them (`src/test-utils/fake-imap.ts`), the barrel import, and six exact-pinned deps.
- **Sender identity**: a mail counts as from its `From:` address only when Proton vouches for it. Mail from outside Proton needs exactly one `mail.protonmail.ch` DMARC verdict, `pass`, for the From domain. Mail from another Proton account (which carries no verdict) needs exactly one `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, no Proton DMARC verdict, and a From domain that is Proton's own (`proton.me`, `protonmail.com`, `protonmail.ch`, `pm.me`, or a subdomain), the Bridge account's own, or one listed in `PROTON_MAIL_INTERNAL_DOMAINS` (for Proton custom domains). The `From:` must be one plain address on one `From:` line. Mail from the Bridge account's own address is never delivered. Refused mail stays unread; internal mail from a domain not trusted is also flagged `$NanoClawFailed`, since it is almost always a real Proton user on an unlisted custom domain.
- **Approval cards**: each card mail carries an `[NC-…]` token in its subject. An answer counts only from the card's approver, quoting the token, `In-Reply-To` the card mail, with an option command on the first line. Every option gets a distinct command. Cards persist across restarts; `onAction` gets the card's Message-ID and address. A card core has closed, or no longer holds, refuses later replies with core's reason when it gave one. Unanswered cards are never pruned before their 7-day TTL; at 1000 open cards a new one is refused rather than pushing one out. Answers to an open card are not held by the hourly sender limit (a held answer would let a gateway approval time out); mail on a card's thread that turns out not to be an answer is counted.
- **Confirmations**: none of the adapter's own for gateway approvals (`deferResolution`): core's card edit is the confirmation, threaded onto the card; other cards get a neutral "Reply received".
- **Transport**: IMAP STARTTLS required; certificate verification on except on loopback; `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` pins Bridge's own certificate so loopback is verified too, and an unreadable pin stops the adapter.
- **Delivery**: no mail is read until core's `onHostStart` has run (the host releases inbound first), so nothing is marked read while the host still holds routing. The callback only sets a flag; an adapter set up after host start reads at once, and one still waiting after 5 minutes logs an error (mail stays unread on the server). The inbound id is the adapter's (UIDVALIDITY plus UID), never the sender's Message-ID. A reply that keeps the conversation's subject, or arrives on a card's thread, reaches core as its bare body, so core's free-text prompts get just the answer. Failures inside the adapter are retried with back-off up to five times, then left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`; routing failures inside the host are not retried (the mail is already handed over). Mail over 40 MB is flagged without being fetched. State is written atomically with a backup (`state.json.bak`); with both unreadable the adapter does not start, so no mail is skipped.
- **Reading mail**: parsing and HTML conversion run in worker threads with timeouts and a heap ceiling, so crafted mail cannot stall the host. When a mail has both bodies the HTML is read. html-to-text runs with no word wrap and no upper-casing. HTML hidden from a mail-client reader (`display:none`, `hidden`, zero-size, transparent text, `<template>`, …) is kept but marked `[hidden CODE: … /hidden CODE]` with a per-mail random code, and invisible or direction characters are marked too (a lone direction mark beside Hebrew/Arabic letters, or a zero-width space between Thai/Lao/Khmer/Myanmar letters, is ordinary text and left alone); when the body the agent gets carries any mark, a note tells it to treat marked text as suspect. Quoted history and signatures are cut; a forward keeps the forwarded mail (a forward's subject prefix, or a "Forwarded message" / "Begin forwarded message:" line before any quoted history). A forward sent as an attachment (`message/rfc822`) is read into the body. Attachment names are cleaned, made unique per mail and given extensions from their MIME type. A non-ASCII sender domain is shown with its punycode beside it. The body is capped at 50k characters, the subject at 300.
- **Limits**: attachments go through only once the sender's DM is wired to an agent, up to 15 MB each and 25 MB per mail. Bounces, auto-replies (`Auto-Submitted`, `X-Loop`, no-reply senders, …) and mailing-list mail (`List-Id`, `List-Post`, `Precedence: list`) are skipped before the router. `PROTON_MAIL_POLL_SECONDS` must be 10–3600.
- **Hourly limits and the hold queue**: at most 20 mails an hour from one sender reach the host; beyond that, mail waits unread (in the state's retry list) and is handed over as the hour frees up. **This is a throttle, not a loop breaker**: two agents mailing each other are slowed to about 20 mails an hour each, not stopped. Bridge drops every loop marker on outgoing mail (below), and core has no loop handling for any channel yet, so that risk stays open project-wide. New addresses not yet approved are limited to 10 an hour, 200 in any 7 days, and 20 per domain in the same 7 days, freed early when core settles (approves or denies) an address; a new address over its domain's share waits, re-checked hourly. Held mail is capped at 200, of which new senders may use 100 and any one domain 20, so approved senders' over-limit mail always has room. Past a cap, mail is left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`.
- **Headers that cannot be sent**: Bridge builds each outgoing mail from a draft template and drops custom headers, so `Auto-Submitted` (RFC 3834) and our `X-NanoClaw-Agent` loop marker never arrive. The own-address check, the inbound auto-reply filter and the hourly throttle are what remain.
- **Message kinds**: a `/command` by email is a command; `send_card` goes out as its fallback text plus links; an edit goes out as a correction on the edited mail's thread.
- **Out of scope**: shared email helpers (sender check, reply-card store) for `/add-resend` and #3743, a follow-up once their home is agreed; a generic IMAP/SMTP channel (maintainers' call); loop handling in core; laying out HTML tables row by row (html-to-text's default runs cells together; a small follow-up).

<details>
<summary>Why the sender check counts verdicts, not their position</summary>

Review asked for `Authentication-Results` "only as added by the trusted receiving server". Bridge adds no verdict of its own; it serves the headers Proton's inbound servers recorded. A position rule (only verdicts above the first `Received:`) was tried and dropped: across 60 real inbox mails, Bridge rebuilds every message with the whole `Received:` chain first, then Proton's verdicts, then `X-Pm-Origin`, so position says nothing about who added a verdict. A forged `mail.protonmail.ch` verdict beside Proton's makes two and is refused; all 60 external mails carried exactly one.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Why X-Pm-Origin: internal can be trusted, and why only for some domains (probes on Bridge 3.27.0)</summary>

Proton-to-Proton mail carries no Authentication-Results, so the DMARC rule alone refused all of it. Three probes:
1. **External mail with forged Proton headers.** A mail from Gmail carried a forged `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption`, `X-Pm-Internal-Id` and `mail.protonmail.ch; dmarc=pass`. Every one was stripped. What arrived carried Proton's own single `X-Pm-Origin: external` and Proton's real verdicts only.
2. **A separate Proton account to the Bridge account.** One `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption: end-to-end`, and no Authentication-Results.
3. **The Bridge account to itself.** The same as probe 2.

A Proton sender cannot set headers: Bridge's SMTP draft template drops them. The rule fails closed: a forged `internal` that ever survived would sit beside Proton's `external` and be refused as two values. Since a Proton account can also send as an address outside Proton's domains (a custom domain, or a connected external address), and nothing Proton adds says which, `internal` is trusted only for the domains above. On a real inbox, every internal mail without a verdict came from a Proton domain or a subdomain (`notify.proton.me`).
</details>

## Related work

Split from #3726 (skill half stays there; it copies these files from `channels`, so this lands first). Purely additive on `channels`: new files, one barrel line, six deps.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

CI does not run tests on PRs into `channels`, so these were run locally on this head (57d4a78e) after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` from this branch's own lockfile:

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/proton-mail.test.ts src/channels/proton-mail-adapter.test.ts \
    src/channels/proton-mail-registration.test.ts src/test-utils/fake-imap.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  241 passed (241)
$ pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
(no output, exit 0)
```

- `eslint`: 0 errors on the new files.
- The whole suite on the same install: no failures in these files (16 elsewhere, in setup scripts and other channels' registration tests, unchanged by this PR).
- `proton-mail.test.ts`, the helpers: sender check (DMARC, `X-Pm-Origin`, trusted domains), plain-address and display-name checks, card matching and distinct commands, quote, signature and forward handling, hidden-text and invisible-character marks, attachment names, header caps, poll bounds, TLS options, skip and mailing-list rules.
- `proton-mail-adapter.test.ts`, the adapter against the fake IMAP server, faked SMTP and real mailparser: sender identity; approval cards (late answers, restarts, closed cards, ceilings, gateway confirmations, answers past the hourly limit); startup on `onHostStart`; the cursor across restarts and UIDVALIDITY changes; retries and giving up; worker timeouts; the hourly limits, the hold queue's caps and per-domain shares, settled addresses freeing their slots; forwards, hidden text and attached forwards.
- Each fix from the third review has a test that failed on the head before it (fc9ecaec, then each fix commit in turn).
- A read-only replay of the old head's and this head's rules over a real inbox (638 mails, counts only): no change to any sender decision; the text changes are no word wrap, heading case, horizontal rules drawn 40 dashes long instead of 80, forwards kept whole, and the hidden-text note now added in the mails whose hidden HTML held block elements.
- Adapter tests run against a scratch working directory and refuse to run otherwise, so they never touch a real install's `store/`.
- Manual, Raspberry Pi 5 (Debian 13, Docker): the install's own build of this adapter has been live since 24 Oct with Bridge 3.27.0 (pinned certificate, required STARTTLS, card answers from Outlook).

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New channel: Proton Mail via a local Proton Mail Bridge (`/add-proton-mail`). Native IMAP/SMTP adapter; mail counts as from its sender only on Proton's DMARC pass (or Proton-internal mail from a trusted domain), and approval cards are answered by replying to the card email itself. Proton custom domains other than the Bridge account's own go in `PROTON_MAIL_INTERNAL_DOMAINS`.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Inbound email is untrusted. For outside mail, sender identity rests on Proton's DMARC verdict, which is domain-level, so the owner's domain must stop its users sending as each other: someone who can get a DMARC-aligned pass for the owner's domain (a shared ESP in its SPF record, a relay that doesn't enforce From) can write as the owner. Only card answers carry the extra token. For Proton-to-Proton mail it rests on Proton's `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, trusted only for the domains above; anyone with a free Proton account is verified as their own address, and unknown senders still go through the approval card.
- Hidden HTML and invisible characters are marked for the agent, not removed, with a code the sender cannot predict, so a mark without the code was written by the sender.
- Attachments from a sender who is not yet approved are held back, and new addresses are limited per hour, per 7 days and per domain, so strangers cannot fill `pending_channel_approvals` or the cards the owner's approvals need.
- Loops: throttled, not stopped (see Hourly limits); stated here and in SKILL.md (#3726).
- Credentials: the bridge password is read from `.env` only; IMAP requires STARTTLS and SMTP requires TLS; Bridge's certificate is pinned when `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` is set (the skill sets it).
- Deps pinned exactly — `imapflow@1.7.8`, `mailparser@3.9.47`, `nodemailer@10.1.7` (past the addressparser advisories below 10.1.4), `html-to-text@10.0.1`, `@types/mailparser@3.4.6`, `@types/nodemailer@8.0.1` — all past the 3-day `minimumReleaseAge`; no build-script approvals added.

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

Code for the `/add-proton-mail` skill in #3726, which copies the `src/channels/proton-mail*` files from this branch and appends the barrel line. The adapter test imports `src/test-utils/fake-imap.ts`, so #3726 is being updated to copy it (and its test) too.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): stage inbound media where the container can read it
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description
Inbound media was written to `<DATA_DIR>/attachments/` and reported as localPath `attachments/<file>`. The container mounts the session dir at `/workspace`, and the agent-runner renders attachments as `/workspace/${localPath}`, so that resolved to `<sessionDir>/attachments/`, which never exists. The download succeeded, the file sat on the host, and the agent was handed a dangling path — images and voice notes read as "I can't see it" even though the bytes were on disk.

Carry the bytes as base64 on the attachment entry instead and let the host stage them, which is what the architecture requires: the adapter sees one message, but the router fans it out to every engaged session, so at download time there is no session dir to write into — only the host knows where the file belongs. session-manager.extractAttachmentFiles already decodes `data` into `inbox/<message_id>/`, the location `docs/db-session.md` documents and the Chat SDK bridge has always used.

Filename sanitizing moves to that same host write site, so the guard lives where the path is built rather than being duplicated per adapter, and mimetype now rides along so the host can derive an extension for images and voice notes, which WhatsApp sends with no filename.

Two follow-on effects worth noting: attachments are no longer written before the router's access/scope gates run (the gate comment in router.ts assumes staging happens behind it), and per-message inbox dirs replace a single global attachments/ dir where filenames from different chats could collide.

## For Skills

- [ ] SKILL.md contains instructions, not inline code (code goes in separate files)
- [ ] SKILL.md is under 500 lines
- [ ] I tested this skill on a fresh clone

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): route inbound media through shared session inbox
prs.body:
## Problem

Inbound WhatsApp media (images, video, audio, documents) never reached the agent. `downloadInboundMedia` wrote the file to `data/attachments/` on the host and tagged the message with `localPath=attachments/<file>`, but agent containers only mount the **per-session** directory at `/workspace` — `data/attachments/` is never mounted in. The formatter then handed the agent `saved to /workspace/attachments/<file>`, a path that resolves nowhere, so only the filename appeared to arrive.

## Fix

Route the bytes through `session-manager.extractAttachmentFiles` as base64 `data`, exactly like the chat-sdk channels already do. Files land in `<sessionDir>/inbox/<msgId>/<file>`, reachable at `/workspace/inbox/<msgId>/<file>`, and inherit the existing path-traversal hardening for filenames.

Non-document media usually arrives with no `fileName`, so synthesize a typed name (`<type>-<ts>.<ext>`). Without it the extractor produces an extensionless attachment and `send_file`/`buildMediaMessage` re-sends it as a *document* instead of the original media kind.

## Test

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/whatsapp.test.ts src/channels/whatsapp-registration.test.ts` — 20 passing
- `tsc --noEmit` + eslint clean

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): route inbound media through shared session inbox
prs.body:
## Summary

WhatsApp inbound media (images, video, audio, documents) was being staged to `<repo>/data/attachments/<filename>` on the host and tagged with `localPath: attachments/<filename>` (`src/channels/whatsapp.ts` `downloadInboundMedia`). Containers only mount the per-session directory at `/workspace` (`src/container-runner.ts`), so `data/attachments/` is unreachable from inside any agent. Agents saw the formatter line "saved to `/workspace/attachments/<file>`" but the path didn't exist.

This fix routes WhatsApp media through the same path chat-sdk channels already use: hand the buffer to `session-manager.extractAttachmentFiles` via a base64 `data` field on the attachment object. The extractor writes files to `<sessionDir>/inbox/<msgId>/<filename>` (reachable at `/workspace/inbox/<msgId>/<filename>`) and applies the existing path-traversal hardening — `lstat`/`realpath` containment, `wx` flag, basename guard on message id and filename.

Net effect: WhatsApp document delivery actually works, and every channel now stages inbound attachments through one code path.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm test` — 423/423 pass (existing inbound-attachment safety tests at `src/host-core.test.ts:168-255` exercise the shared extractor path that WhatsApp now uses)
- [x] `pnpm run lint` — no new warnings in `src/channels/whatsapp.ts` (17 → 17 identical warnings, line numbers shifted only)
- [x] `pnpm run build` clean
- [ ] Manual: send a document via WhatsApp DM/group, confirm container sees the file at `/workspace/inbox/<msgId>/<filename>`

## Notes

- Removes now-unused imports: `isSafeAttachmentName` (sanitization happens in the shared extractor) and `DATA_DIR` (no more host-side staging).
- Base64 inflation through `inbound.db` is the same trade chat-sdk channels already pay; the row is short-lived (extractor writes to disk and rewrites the JSON before the container reads it).
- File naming behavior matches chat-sdk channels: `att.name` (from `documentMessage.fileName`) when present, else `deriveAttachmentName` synthesizes `attachment-<ts>.<ext>` from `att.mimeType` / `att.type`.

## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in \`.claude/skills/<name>/\`, no source changes)

prs.title: Add Trustabl agent reliability check to CI
prs.body:
Hi! We came across nanocoai/nanoclaw and like that it provides a framework for building and deploying AI agents.

We ran [Trustabl](https://trustabl.ai), an open-source agent reliability scanner, on the repo and it flagged a few things that may be worth a look:

- **Bundled skill script reads credentials or secrets** (`.claude/skills/add-atomic-chat-tool/SKILL.md`): A script bundled with this skill reads credentials or secrets (for example `gh auth`, `$AWS_*` variables or files under `~/`), which the agent could then expose at runtime.
- **Bundled skill script reads credentials or secrets** (`.claude/skills/add-codex/SKILL.md`): A script bundled with this skill reads credentials or secrets (for example `gh auth`, `$AWS_*` variables or files under `~/`), which the agent could then expose at runtime.
- **Bundled skill script reads credentials or secrets** (`.claude/skills/add-cursor/SKILL.md`): A script bundled with this skill reads credentials or secrets (for example `gh auth`, `$AWS_*` variables or files under `~/`), which the agent could then expose at runtime.

This PR adds a small GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/trustabl.yml`) so these checks run automatically:

- Runs on pushes to the default branch, on pull requests, and on demand
- Advisory only: the job uses `continue-on-error`, so it never fails your CI
- No secrets needed; findings show up in the repo's code scanning results
- Actions are pinned to commit SHAs, with read-only contents access

Some findings may be intentional. Happy to adjust the workflow, or to close this if it's not useful.

Add Trustabl to your CI · [trustabl/trustabl-action](https://github.com/trustabl/trustabl-action) · https://trustabl.ai

prs.title: fix(cross-session-context): copy attachments onto echo and backfill rows
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Agents now see the files on messages copied in from the conversation's other threads (live echoes and dm/channel-timeline backfill). Before this, those copies carried text only.

- **Problem**: a copy of a message in another session kept only `text`. Its files stay in the source session's `inbox/`, which the target container can't see. `formatEchoMessage` also never called `formatAttachments`, and media-only messages were dropped from fan and backfill (`if (!parsed.text) return 0`). Live-hit on Slack: a thread root with a screenshot reached the agent as `<channel-history …>see the screenshot</channel-history>`, with no file.
- **Fix (host)**: `copyEchoAttachments` (new `cross-session-context/attachments.ts`) copies each staged file into the target session's `inbox/<echo-row-folder>/` and lists it on the row in the usual `attachments` shape. Used by `writeEcho` (fan) and `backfillSession`.
- **Fix (router)**: `writeSessionMessage` now resolves to the content as written (staged `localPath`, no base64). The router fans that version instead of the raw event, so the fan copies files from disk.
- **Fix (container)**: `formatEchoMessage` appends `formatAttachments(content.attachments)`, the same format `<message>` uses.
- **Bounded**: at most 25 MiB copied per echo row (`ECHO_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` in `config.ts`). A file past the cap, or one that can't be copied, stays on the row by name only (`[image: x.png]`). One bad file never drops the row.
- **Cleanup**: when the pruner drops a pending echo row (past `ECHO_MAX_AGE_DAYS` or `ECHO_BACKLOG_CAP`), the files copied for it are removed too. `prunePendingMessages` now returns the deleted ids instead of a count. Copies on delivered rows stay, like the source session's own inbox files, because the agent may refer back to them.
- **Off the wake path**: copies run inside the existing fan (after `requestWake`, unawaited, through `mapConcurrent` with `ECHO_CONCURRENCY`) and inside backfill. No new await before the wake.
- **Out of scope**: files on the agent's own outbound posts (outbox `files`). Those echoes stay text-only, as before.

<details><summary>Why 20 files (≈350 lines of code incl. comments, ≈390 lines of tests)</summary>

- `attachments.ts`, `fan.ts`, `backfill.ts`, `config.ts`: the copy, its callers and the size cap.
- `prune.ts`, `mailbox/types.ts`, `mailbox/sqlite/index.ts`, `reconcile-session.ts`: the cleanup. The mailbox returns the pruned ids, and the pruner needs the session to find their folders.
- `session-manager.ts`, `router.ts`: `writeSessionMessage` returns the content it wrote, so the router fans what's on disk.
- `response-handler.ts`, `session-manager.test.ts`, `session-manager.feeds.test.ts`, `messaging-groups.test.ts`: one-line follow-ons of that return type (`Promise<void>` → `Promise<string>`).
- `container/agent-runner/src/formatter.ts`: render the files.
- The rest are tests.

Happy to split the router/return-type change or the cleanup into their own PRs if that's easier to review.
</details>

<details><summary>How the live case happens</summary>

In a per-thread room, an untagged message is stored in its thread's session. A later new session in the same conversation (another thread, or a reply that roots a new session) gets the conversation's top-level timeline through `backfillSession`, and live sibling messages through `fanInboundMessage`. Both wrote `{ text, sender, echo }` only.
</details>

## Related work

No existing issue; the bug is reproduced in the tests below. Nearby open PRs, each checked with `git merge-tree` against this branch, merge cleanly:

- #3711 (deferred inbound content) touches `deliverToAgent`. The two compose: this fans the content as written, so once #3711 lands, its resolved view is what gets copied.
- #4244 changes `writeSessionMessage` error handling in `session-manager.ts`.
- #4159 edits `container/agent-runner/src/cross-session-echo.test.ts`.
- #3674 touches `session-manager.ts` and attachment naming.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- The first commit adds only tests. Each failed on `main`:
  - `container/agent-runner/src/cross-session-echo.test.ts` › `attachments` (5): files on dm-history, channel-history and cross-session-context rows; name-only files; XML escaping
  - `backfill.test.ts` › `backfillSession — attachments` (4): the copy lands in the target inbox; a media-only root is kept; a planted symlink is not followed; an `inbox/../` source path is refused
  - `fan.test.ts` › `fanInboundMessage` › `attachments` (3): per-sibling copy; media-only fan; size cap
  - `host-core.test.ts` › `a sibling thread's echo of a message with a file carries its own copy of the file`: end to end through `routeInbound`
- `prune.test.ts` › `copied files` (4): "removes the inbox folder of each pruned row and keeps the rest" and "removes a symlink inside the folder without touching its target" fail with the cleanup reverted. The other two guard the edges (a row with no files; a row folder swapped for a symlink is not followed) and pass either way.
- `pnpm test` → 4247 passed, 2 failed, both in `setup/` and unrelated to this diff: `onecli-detection.test.ts` fails the same way on unmodified `main` here, and `slack-auto.test.ts` passes when run on its own.
- `bun test` (container/agent-runner, Bun 1.4.3) → 632 pass, 0 fail
- `tsc --noEmit` (host and container), `eslint` on touched files → clean (no new warnings)
- Real install: Slack's API shows 38 messages with files over 2 weeks. Every original row had its files, and every text-only copy in other sessions (`dm-timeline`, `channel-timeline`, `dm-thread`) had none. With the fix deployed, an image posted in one thread was visible to the agent from a sibling thread.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Agents now see images and files on messages from earlier in the conversation and from its other threads, not just the text.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Both session folders are writable by containers, so the host reads the source inbox and writes the target inbox only through `AnchoredDir`. Symlinked `inbox`/message folders are refused, and source files are opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` and must be regular files. The target is created exclusively, so no entry is followed or overwritten. Same pattern as `forwardAttachedFiles` (agent-route.ts).
- The source `localPath` must be exactly `inbox/<safe>/<safe>` (`isSafeAttachmentName`). The target folder comes from `inboxFolderName(echoRowId)`.
- Cleanup removes only folders named by pruned echo-row ids through `inboxFolderName`, through `AnchoredDir`: a symlinked folder is not followed, and `unlink` removes a symlink itself, never its target.
- No new audience: echoes still go only to sessions of the same agent group and messaging group, which already received the text. The size cap limits disk use; it is not a trust boundary.
- Tests: a symlink planted in the source inbox; a traversal path; a symlinked folder and a symlinked file at cleanup.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: fix(add-codex): supervise turn inactivity instead of total duration
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->
## Summary

Keeps active Codex turns alive beyond ten minutes while still aborting inactive turns.

- **Problem**: the fixed 600,000 ms timer interrupts a whole turn even when Codex is producing output or running a tool.
- **Fix**: use a monotonic 15-minute inactivity budget, refreshed by active-thread/turn notifications. Running native tools suspend idle enforcement and remain cancellable.
- **Liveness**: emit coalesced host activity every five seconds without resetting the inactivity budget. Preserve bounded RPC deadlines and immediate process-exit errors.
- **Failure**: request turn interruption on idle expiry, retain the continuation, and do not replay partially executed work.

## Related work

Depends on #4165; its commit is included with the original author preserved. Thread isolation is needed so child-tool events cannot change the parent watchdog's state. Rebase after #4165 merges.

Related: #3338. This removes the misleading fixed-duration cutoff, but does not claim to resolve WebSocket retries or recoverable-error handling.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `bun test --isolate ./container/agent-runner/src/providers/codex*.test.ts` after materializing the skill in an isolated upstream worktree: 70 passed.
- `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: passed in the isolated upstream worktree and the customized install.
- Regression proof: the 17 new watchdog cases yield 16 failures against the original fixed-timeout provider and all pass against this change. prs.title: feat: add Keenable MCP tool skill
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-keenable-tool`, a skill that registers Keenable web search and page fetch as remote MCP tools for selected agent groups.

- **Installs**: the pinned `mcp-remote` bridge in `container/cli-tools.json`, two guards copied into `src/`, and one `keenable` MCP server per selected group via `ncl`.
- **Tools**: `mcp__keenable__search_web_pages`, `mcp__keenable__fetch_page_content`.
- **No account, no key, no signup.** The server answers anonymously, so the happy path has no credential step. A key raises the rate limit and changes nothing else; when a user wants one it goes through OneCLI, gated on `/init-onecli`.
- **No upgrade phase.** The anonymous allowance is a rolling window (1,000/hour, 10/second, per host IP), so a `429` sends `retry-after` and heals itself. A Rate limits section and a troubleshooting entry cover it.
- **Guards both integration points**: the pinned bridge in the manifest, and the registered argument shape read out of `SKILL.md` (endpoint, attribution parameter, transport pin, `--enable-proxy`). The second one follows the approach in #3418.
- **Out of scope**: promoting the paid key from inside the agent, which would need the vault deeplink machinery and is a separate change.

## Related work

No issue: this adds an optional skill and changes no existing behavior, so the diff can be reviewed directly. It follows `add-tavily-tool` (#3190).

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/keenable-manifest.test.ts` -> **6 passed** with the skill applied. Mutation-tested one element at a time: removing the attribution parameter, `--enable-proxy`, or the `--transport http-only` pin each turns exactly 1 of 6 red; removing the manifest entry reds the dependency half; restoring returns 6 green.
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts scripts/skill-policy.test.ts scripts/skill-directives.test.ts` -> **274 passed** with the skill in the tree.
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/skill-directives.ts .claude/skills/add-keenable-tool/SKILL.md` -> no problems, no warnings.
- `pnpm exec prettier --check "src/**/*.ts"` and `pnpm exec eslint src/keenable-manifest.test.ts` -> clean with the guards copied in, so `format:check` stays green after install.
- Outside CI: drove `mcp-remote@0.1.38` over stdio with the exact args Phase 3 registers -> `initialize`, `tools/list` and a live `tools/call` all returned anonymously, with page text in the result. A 25-call burst returned 10 x `200` and 15 x `429`, matching the rate limit the skill documents.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

Per-group MCP registration is runtime state stored through `ncl`, so it has no in-tree line to guard; the argument shape it is built from does, and that is what the second guard covers.

## User and release impact

- [x] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
```

## Security and trust boundaries

No credentials. The server is called anonymously, `--env` is empty, and the default path stores nothing. An optional API key, if a user wants one, is stored through OneCLI so the gateway injects it per request and the agent never sees it. The bridge keeps `--enable-proxy`, so it stays proxy-aware under `NANOCLAW_EGRESS_LOCKDOWN=true`. Search results and fetched pages are untrusted web content and are consumed as data, same as any other web tool.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: feat(web_search): add Keenable provider (no API key required)
prs.body:
## Summary
Adds **Keenable** as a `web_search` provider: `src/tools/web_search_providers/keenable.zig`.

- **No API key required.** Without a key, the provider calls the free public endpoint, `POST https://api.keenable.ai/v1/search/public`. If `KEENABLE_API_KEY` is set, it calls `POST /v1/search` with `X-API-Key`. Every request sends `X-Keenable-Title: nullclaw`.
- `count` is sent as `max_results`. Each result's text is Keenable's short `description`, or its `snippet` truncated to 1000 bytes (UTF-8 safe) if there is no description. Results without a URL are skipped.
- **Explicit only.** Keenable is used only through `http_request.search_provider = "keenable"`, as a fallback entry, or as the tool's `provider` arg. It is **not** added to the `auto` chain, so default behaviour is unchanged.
- Wiring changes: the `SearchProvider` enum, `parseProvider` / `providerName`, `executeWithProvider`, config validation (`isValidSearchProviderName`), the config error message, the tool schema description, and the README provider list.

## Tests
- New unit tests in `keenable.zig` cover description/snippet fallback, URL filtering, the `count` limit, and UTF-8-safe truncation.
- Added assertions that `parseProvider("keenable")` parses and that the config accepts `keenable`.
- `zig build test` with Zig 0.16.0 ran 7396 tests: 7382 passed, 14 skipped (platform-specific), 0 failed.
- `zig fmt --check` is clean.

Disclosure: I work with the Keenable team. cc @DonPrus @manelsen

prs.body:
## Summary

Bump the bundled DeepSeek Harness (dsh) runtime from 0.1.5-rc.3 to 0.2.1-rc.5 and fix the integration issues dsh 0.2 introduced.

- **Runtime bump**: pin `@deepseek-ai/dsh` to 0.2.1-rc.5; mac-arm64, mac-x64 and win-x64 runtime archives all point at the new 0.2.1-rc.5 builds (sha256/size recorded in `package.json`).
- **Boot fix**: add a version-scoped patch so `dsh-app-boot` reaches Node internals through `--expose-internals` first; the require-builtin addon rejects Electron 43.5.0's V8 fingerprint and dsh exited during boot.
- **Settings sync**: dsh 0.2 retired `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml`. `dshConfigSync` now writes the `llm-pi-ai` and `agent-default-model` rows of `profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` directly before spawn:
  - providers are live on the first boot;
  - managed `lobsterai-*` routes are replaced as a set, so removed ones no longer linger;
  - the default model is seeded only for a brand-new profile instead of overwriting the user's pick on every launch;
  - a leftover `settings.yaml` has its two sections folded in, and writes take dsh's own profile lock.
- **Windows install**: retry rename/rmdir with backoff on EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES (up to five minutes) when a background scanner holds the freshly extracted runtime, and make the trailing cleanup best effort so it no longer masks the real error.

## Electron-specific behavior

- Runtime download/install path changes (new archives, Windows retry logic).
- dsh profile files under `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/` are now written by LobsterAI before each spawn.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm test -- dsh`
- [ ] Fresh install + launch on mac-arm64, mac-x64, win-x64
- [ ] Providers configured in LobsterAI show up in dsh on first boot; removing one removes it from dsh

prs.title: fix(openclaw): compact byte-bounded history instead of sliding it
prs.body:
## Problem

A user reported going from 8,000+ credits to ~800 overnight. Their WeChat DM session (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1M window) was billed ~60–130 credits per message.

OpenClaw v2026.8.1 hydrates each attempt with at most `contextTokenBudget × 8` stored bytes (8 MB for a 1M window). The bound counts stored event JSON, including inline `view_image` base64, so image-heavy sessions run at 12–20 bytes per prompt token and hit it long before the 980k token compaction threshold. From then on:

- compaction never runs;
- the newest-first reader drops the oldest events every turn, so the first model message changes each turn and the whole ~650k-token prefix misses the provider cache;
- the dropped history is never summarized.

In the user's logs the first full miss happened exactly when `activeTranscriptBytes` crossed 8 MB (7.59 MB → 8.04 MB). Upstream tracks this as openclaw/openclaw#159799 (open); the only merged mitigation, openclaw/openclaw#168157, landed after our v2026.8.1 pin.

## Change

Two version-scoped OpenClaw patches. No LobsterAI runtime code changes.

- `openclaw-bounded-history-chunked-window.patch` (port of #168157) changes the bounded reader:
  - the latest compaction/reset boundary is reserved before the tail is sized;
  - byte pressure is measured from the boundary's retained start;
  - the cut advances in quarter-capacity steps and starts at a user turn.
- `openclaw-bounded-history-compaction.patch` adds a `model_context_bytes` preflight compaction trigger at 80% of the same hydration bound. It is optional: a skip or failure keeps the turn running on the bounded tail, and retries wait for another quarter of the bound. A boundary whose retained tail alone is large does not re-compact every turn. Existing token and `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` triggers are unchanged.
- `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs` gets strong-validator snippets for both patches; the patch README documents the background, behavior and removal criteria.

## Verification

- OpenClaw unit tests:
  - bounded-context tests 12/12 and preflight tests 105/105; the new cases fail on the old code;
  - related session, attempt and caller suites (~260 tests) pass.
- Core typecheck: only the existing `managed-image-replay.ts` errors. oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- The full 80-patch series applies to a clean v2026.8.1 checkout; `npm run openclaw:runtime:host` builds and the runtime starts.
- Standalone gateway + mock model (100k window): turns survive a failing summarizer, retries back off, the window start moves only every quarter step, and the cache recovers after compaction.
- **In-app**, dev app on a real profile, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, ~820 KB of history per turn via `view_image`:
  - turn 8 at 6.55 MB triggered `model_context_bytes` compaction (~9 s), which brought history to 2.46 MB;
  - that turn's first request hit 93%, and turns 9–12 hit 99–100%;
  - 13 turns cost ~12.6 credits in total.

Not covered in-app: the IM (WeChat) channel itself. It shares the gateway and the same preflight function. The chunked window only matters when compaction fails, so it is covered by the mock run and unit tests.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): load Windows plugins natively and cache plugin realpaths
prs.body:
## Problem

On Windows machines with 360 Total Security (common for Chinese users), gateway startup reached 170–250 s, pinned in synchronous fs metadata calls while loading plugins. With 360, each metadata call under `%APPDATA%` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%` costs about 1 ms (`lstat` ≈ 890 µs under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\LobsterAI` vs ≈ 8 µs in a dev folder).

## Root cause

On Windows, OpenClaw never loaded plugins natively:

- `loader-module-runtime.ts` passes `toSafeImportPath(modulePath)` to the plugin loader. On win32 that is a `file:///C:/...` URL, the form ESM `import()` needs.
- `tryNativeRequireJavaScriptModule` hands that URL to `require()`, which rejects it with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. The loader reads that as "target missing" and falls back to jiti with `tryNative: false`.
- So every plugin, including bundled `dist/extensions/*`, was Babel-transformed together with OpenClaw's whole SDK graph, and each import went through jiti's uncached `realpathSync`/`stat` resolver. That is where the ~138k `lstat` calls came from. macOS and Linux pass plain paths and load natively.
- The same URL also made `clearPluginModuleRequireCache`'s `require.resolve` fail silently, so URL-keyed modules were never evicted.

## Changes

Two new OpenClaw v2026.8.1 patches, each with a strong-patch validator in `scripts/apply-openclaw-patches.cjs`, a README section, and an entry in `v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts`:

1. **`openclaw-windows-native-plugin-require.patch`**: converts `file:` URLs to paths before `require()` and `require.resolve()` in `native-module-require.ts`. The URL stays the cache key. Two new tests cover loading and evicting a module through a file URL.
2. **`openclaw-plugin-realpath-parent-cache.patch`**: `pluginCacheRealpathSync` and the installed-plugin index staleness checks cached realpaths by exact path only, so every new file still walked each path component. New `realpath-through-parent.ts` resolves a path as its parent's cached realpath plus its basename after one `lstat` (links and roots still go through `fs.realpathSync`). Cache lifetimes are unchanged. Two existing tests that counted `fs.realpathSync` calls to prove one lookup per path now count the `lstat` too.

This PR first carried a jiti resolver cache. With native loading fixed, jiti is no longer called at startup, so that patch was dropped.

## End-to-end measurements

360 machine. Full `npm run openclaw:runtime:win-x64` build with these patches, copied to `%LOCALAPPDATA%` so it sits on the slow path, gateway run by `LobsterAI.exe` as Node (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`). The baseline is the installed v2026.8.1 runtime (built 2026-10-30), with the same scratch config.

| | installed | built |
|---|---|---|
| `[plugins] loaded 7 plugin(s)` | 124.5 s | 16.0 s |
| HTTP listening | 129.8 s | 18.0 s |
| lstat (7 plugins) | 138,504 | 13,919 |
| All 16 allowed plugins enabled | 270.2 s | 44.7 s |
| jiti cache calls (16 plugins) | 6,508 | 0 |

- Same plugin list and the same `tools.catalog` plugin tools in both; no plugin load errors. lark, nim-channel and netease-bee load natively in the shipped layout.
- `/readyz` is ready with the default 7 plugins. With all 16 enabled it reports `internal` in both runtimes, because channels such as Email are not configured.
- A plugin hot reload applies and re-registers all plugins. A running gateway re-registers from the same module generation by design, so module eviction applies to restarts and CLI flows; the unit tests cover it.
- Patch 2 isolated, by reverting it in the loaded bundle: `lstat` 32,851 → 13,919, process start to plugins loaded 64–75 s → 50–51 s.

## Testing

- New and updated OpenClaw tests pass. Failures in neighbouring files (`plugin-module-loader-cache` path fixtures, one `discovery` case, `channel-entry-contract`, …) fail the same way without these patches on Windows. oxlint/oxfmt are clean; tsgo is clean apart from pre-existing errors in another patch's file.
- All 80 v2026.8.1 patches apply and pass strong validation.
- `v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts` and `openclawReplayDiagnostics.test.ts` pass.
- Plugin staging during the runtime build now logs `failed to load` for openclaw-lark, nim-channel and netease-bee, because their host-peer `node_modules/openclaw` does not export `./plugin-sdk`. Packaging removes that peer, as on macOS where these plugins always load natively, and the e2e above loads them without errors.
- Not yet verified through an installed `dist:win` package.

prs.title: fix(cowork): keep model selection in scheduled-task conversations
prs.body:
## Problem
On a scheduled-task result page, switching the model appeared to fail: the selector snapped back to 快速 and the next manual reply still used the agent default. The model-change divider also showed the raw id `yd-fast`.

## Cause
Channel polling resolves cron rows (`agent:main:cron:<jobId>[:run:…]`) to the scheduled-task conversation and ran `syncChannelSessionModelOverride` on them. The cron row has no explicit override and matches the agent default, so the local `modelOverride` was cleared right after every switch (`[ChannelSync] synced channel session model override … Model agent/default.`). The channel model sync was meant for IM `/model` switches only.

The divider recorded the agent default `lobsterai-server/yd-fast` without a preset id, so it fell back to the bare model id.

## Changes
- `openclawRuntimeAdapter.ts`: skip cron keys in the channel model sync; manual replies run on the managed key, and the local override owns them.
- `sessionModelChange.ts`: treat `yd-fast` / `yd-ultra` refs as their presets when recording a change (also avoids a "快速 → 快速" notice).
- `ModelChangeDivider.tsx`: same fallback for notices already stored.

## Electron behavior
Main process only changes when the polled OpenClaw cron rows are written to local session state; no IPC, storage schema, or config/restart changes.

## Verification
- New regression test (fails without the guard) plus `sessionModelChange.test.ts`
- `npm test` passes, touched files lint clean, `npm run compile:electron` passes
- Tested manually in the app

prs.title: fix(packaging): stop shipping bundled and debug-only files in the installer
prs.body:
## Summary

The Windows installer was carrying a second copy of most libraries plus files nothing loads at runtime. This trims about **42 MB** off the compressed installer; the full installer built from this branch is **239 MB** (the 2026.10.9 one was 348 MB, which also predates other recent trims). `app.asar` drops from 670 MB to 174 MB.

| Change | Compressed saving |
|---|---|
| Move 92 Vite-bundled libraries to `devDependencies` (asar `node_modules` 38.3 → 7.8 MB) | ~30.5 MB |
| Ship only the matching `better-sqlite3` prebuild on Windows (as on macOS) | ~6.9 MB |
| Leave web-search's dev-only packages (`typescript`, `@types`) out of the Windows skills payload, using each skill's lockfile `dev` flags | ~1.6 MB |
| Prune OpenClaw `typescript/lib/_tsc.js` and diagnostic locales, native `.pdb` files, and the root `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk` once `openclaw-lark` is bundled | ~2.6 MB |

### What must stay in `dependencies`

electron-builder copies every production dependency into `app.asar`, but Vite already bundles the main and renderer code, so only modules loaded or resolved outside the bundles belong there. Four of them are easy to miss:

- `protobufjs`: the bundled Lark SDK ESM build keeps a top-level `require("protobufjs/minimal")` in `main.js`; without it the app fails to start. It is now declared directly, pinned to the range the SDK declares.
- `pptx-preview`: the preview server serves its UMD build via `require.resolve`.
- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `zod`: imported by the spawned computer-use MCP server script.

`tests/electronBuilderAppFiles.test.ts` now pins the `dependencies` list with a reason for each entry, and `AGENTS.md` tells contributors to add new libraries with `npm install -D`. `sheet-third-party-notices.cjs` reads `devDependencies` too, so the Univer notices are unchanged.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run` on the 6 affected test files: 88 tests pass. ESLint clean on touched TS files.
- A fresh `npm run build` produces a `main.js` with the same external requires as before.
- Built the full NSIS installer and installed it silently over 2026.10.30 on Windows x64 with real user data, then exercised the app:
  - startup, main window and history; desktop companion windows (koffi, selection-hook)
  - a chat task using the web-search skill, with the packaged bridge server started by the app
  - skills page
  - PPTX preview of a 38-slide deck through the bundled `pptx-preview`
  - all 5 MCP servers (computer-use, word, excel, ppt, browser credentials) complete initialize + `tools/list`
  - `openclaw-lark` resolves its own copy of the Lark SDK
  - no `Cannot find module` / `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in the main log

## Not covered

- Feishu channel end to end (no Feishu channel configured on the test machine).
- Linux skills payload still ships web-search dev dependencies.
- OpenClaw gateway startup on the test machine was slower than earlier runs (plugin load ~106 s vs 6–24 s). All plugins slowed by a similar factor while the machine was under heavy disk and memory pressure, so it looks environmental, but it was not A/B-measured; worth re-checking startup time on a quiet machine before release.

prs.title: fix(desktop-companion): show selections the hook skips over the pointer shape
prs.body:
## Problem

Customer report (LobsterAI 2026.10.30, macOS 26.6 25G72, Apple Silicon): the companion selection toolbar never appears in any app (Safari, Notes, ...). Accessibility is granted, the log shows `Selection hook started`, no errors.

## Root cause

- selection-hook (2.1.1; 2.1.2 is identical) gates drag / double-click / shift-click on `IsIBeamCursor([NSCursor currentSystemCursor])`, an exact hot-spot match against `{4,9}`, `{16,16}`, `{12,11}`. When it misses, the gesture is dropped silently.
- On 26.6 the match fails. Likely triggers: a changed (fractional) I-beam hot spot, an enlarged pointer size, or `currentSystemCursor` returning nil (deprecated; the SDK says it will always be nil in a future macOS). Not yet confirmed on the customer machine.
- `recoverSelection` then read the selection 80 ms after the gesture and, when text was readable right away, assumed the hook chose not to report it and dropped it. Native AX apps are always readable right away, so nothing ever showed.

## Fix

- `SelectionGestureTracker.up()` returns the gesture's press and release points instead of a boolean.
- New `selectionCoversGesture()`: a read is the gesture's own when both points lie within the selection bounds (48 pt either side, one line above/below, line capped at 40 pt). Requires full position level.
- Recovery attempt 0 now shows such a selection (with a `console.debug` line). Selections without bounds, or left elsewhere (window / scroll-bar drag, dropped text), are still ignored. Later attempts are unchanged.

No IPC, storage, runtime, or OpenClaw changes. Main process only.

## Verification

- New Vitest cases for drag / double-click acceptance, the three rejection cases, and slop boundaries; the acceptance cases fail with the old attempt-0 behavior.
- `npm test`, ESLint on touched files, `npm run compile:electron` pass.
- Not verified on a real macOS 26.6 machine (dev Mac is 15.1, where the hook still works and this path is not reached). Needs a customer test build.

## Follow-up

Upstream selection-hook: compare against the runtime `[NSCursor IBeamCursor]` scale-invariantly and handle a nil `currentSystemCursor`. The packaged app loads the prebuilt `.node` (`npmRebuild: false`), so patching the `.mm` locally would not take effect.

prs.title: fix(web-search): run node without the env found on PATH
prs.body:
## Summary
uv's installer adds `~/.local/bin/env`, a sh script meant to be sourced that ignores its arguments and exits 0. When `~/.local/bin` is ahead of `/usr/bin` on PATH, every `env PREFIX node ...` call in the web-search scripts silently runs nothing:

- On Windows bash (Node fetch path), the health check always comes back empty. `search.sh` reports "Bridge Server still unavailable after start" while `/api/health` is healthy.
- On every platform, `build_search_payload` returns an empty payload (the POST falls back to `{}`), `verify_iconv_runtime` always passes, and `nohup env … node server` never starts the server.

Repro: `echo 'console.log(1)' | env node -` prints nothing, while `node -` prints `1`. `command env` does not help, because it still resolves `env` on PATH.

## Related Issue
None. Found during an end-to-end install test on Windows.

## Changes Made
- `search.sh` / `start-server.sh`: add `run_http_node` / `run_node`, which exec the runtime directly and export `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` in a subshell for the Electron case. These replace the foreground `env` calls.
- `start-server.sh`: the background launch exports the prefix in place before `nohup`. A function's subshell would make `$!` a wrapper instead of the server process.
- Test: a no-op `env` ahead on PATH must not make a broken iconv-lite look healthy.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

Tested on Windows Git Bash (bash 5), with the real uv shim first on PATH:
- `bash SKILLs/web-search/scripts/search.sh "test" 1` returns results (before: exit 1, "still unavailable").
- Electron path, with node hidden and a fake Electron that requires `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`: health check, payload and `nohup` launch all work, and the variable does not leak into the caller.
- The `start-server.sh` tests are skipped on win32, so I ran them unskipped under Git Bash: 7/7 pass. With the original script, the new test and the existing "iconv-lite … reinstalled" test both fail on this machine.
- The existing win32 failure "copying resets mtimes …" also fails on the base branch. It is unrelated.
- Not run on macOS. The constructs used are bash 3.2 compatible, and the scripts do not use `set -u`.

## Summary

- **Truncated replies**: OpenClaw `chat.history` caps each text block at 8000 chars and appends `...(truncated)...`. History sync was writing that preview over the complete local text. prs.title: fix(desktop-companion): keep the orb under the pointer while dragging
prs.body:
## Summary

A user reported that the companion orb flickers on their Mac. In the frames of their video, the cursor sits still while the orb jumps about every 113 ms between its rest spot and a spot where the cursor holds the press point. Something re-applied the drag position while another writer moved the window back.

## Root cause

- The drag took its starting cursor from `screen.getCursorScreenPoint()` when the `Start` IPC was handled. That is often 100–200 ms after the press, so a quick drag left the orb behind the pointer. In a real CGEvent drag on macOS 15, the cursor slipped 40 px off the orb.
- Every `Move` called `setBounds`, even when the cursor had not moved. Moving the window under a still cursor produces pointer events of its own. Re-applying the same bounds for those events can fight anything else that places the window, which matches the flicker.
- The drag ended only on `pointerup` or `pointercancel`. If the release never reached the orb, the orb kept following a free pointer.

## Changes

- The renderer reports where the press landed, as fractions of the orb window, so page zoom cannot skew it. Main places the orb at the cursor minus that grab point.
- Main skips a `Move` whose target is unchanged.
- The renderer ends the drag when a pointer move arrives without the primary button held, or when pointer capture is lost.

**Electron/IPC:** the `desktop-companion:drag` payload changes from a bare phase string to `{ phase, grab? }`. Preload, main and renderer are updated together. There is no storage, runtime or OpenClaw change.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 8237 passed, 157 skipped. Two regression tests cover a late press and repeated moves while the cursor is still; a geometry test covers the grab offset.
- ESLint passes on the touched files with `--max-warnings 0`. Both `tsc` projects pass with `--noEmit`.
- In `npm run electron:dev` with real CGEvent drags on macOS 15:
  - A fast drag lands exactly at the cursor minus the grab point.
  - Holding still changes nothing.
  - After release, the orb no longer follows the mouse.
- **Not verified:** the user's flicker itself did not reproduce on macOS 15. Their Dock suggests macOS 26.
- **Seen once, not explained:** right after a fresh launch, one drag kept following the mouse after release. Five retries did not reproduce it.

issues.title: [Bug]: Hub Local runtime cannot start on Windows (AppContainer skill staging, missing CPU architecture, reverse-tunnel readiness timeout)
issues.body:
# [Bug]: Hub Local runtime cannot start on Windows (AppContainer skill staging, missing CPU architecture, reverse-tunnel readiness timeout)

## Environment

- QwenPaw: `2.2.2.post1`
- Install: `pip install "qwenpaw[hub]==2.2.2.post1"`
- OS: Windows `10.0.26300.9711` x64
- Hub provisioner: `local`
- Hub process: started from an Administrator terminal
- Hub data root: clean `QWENPAW_HUB_DIR`
- User: normal Hub user, first runtime start

## Summary

On Windows, a Hub Local personal runtime cannot reach `running`. Startup fails at
three independent points. The Hub control plane, login, user management, and
model settings work; only the user runtime fails.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Initialize Hub and start it on loopback:

   ```powershell
   qwenpaw hub --init-admin admin
   qwenpaw hub --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8088
   ```

2. Create a normal user and start that user's personal runtime through the Hub
   UI/API.

## Failure 1: default skill staging gets WinError 5

```text
PermissionError: [WinError 5] 拒绝访问
working/tmp/qwenpaw_skill_stage_*/QA_source_index

qwenpaw/cli/init_cmd.py
  _sync_default_workspace_skills()
    pool.download_to_workspace()
      copy_skill_dir()
```

`.hub-initialized` is never written, so every retry fails the same way.

## Failure 2: CPU architecture is empty

After running `qwenpaw init --defaults --accept-security` on the host first and
writing `.hub-initialized`, startup proceeds further and fails at local-model
initialization:

```text
RuntimeError: Unsupported architecture:
```

`platform.machine()` is empty because the AppContainer child environment does
not contain `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE`; `system_environment()` does not pass it.
This is the same root cause as the open PR #7492.

## Failure 3: reverse tunnel / readiness timeout

After restoring `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` in the runtime interpreter, the runtime
log reaches:

```text
INFO:     Application startup complete.
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:1297 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
```

Hub still reports:

```text
Runtime personal-... failed to start: timed out
```

and kills the runtime. The Hub readiness probe cannot reach the AppContainer
runtime through `WindowsReverseTunnelBroker` /
`qwenpaw.hub.windows_runtime_bridge`.

## Expected

The personal runtime reaches `running`, Hub proxies `/api/version` and the
Console, and a first-time user can open QwenPaw.

## Actual

The runtime is marked `failed`; the user cannot open their QwenPaw. Hub login,
user management, and model settings still work.

## Workarounds tested

- Host-side `qwenpaw init` + `.hub-initialized`: fixes Failure 1.
- A `sitecustomize.py` shim restoring `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` for managed
  Local runtimes: fixes Failure 2.
- No deployment-layer workaround found for Failure 3.

## Related upstream items

- PR #7492 `fix(windows): fall back when CPU architecture is missing` — open,
  not merged; directly addresses Failure 2.
- PR #7270 `test: mark Hub local runtime E2E as xfail on Windows` — closed
  without merge; describes Windows readiness flakiness.
- PR #7273 `test(ci): allow slower Windows Hub cold starts` — merged; raises the
  E2E readiness budget from 60s to 120s, but does not change the Local
  provisioner/readiness path.

## Latest beta check

`v2.3.0-beta.2` (2026-11-02) was checked at source level. These files are
unchanged from `v2.2.2.post1`:

- `src/qwenpaw/hub/windows_reverse_tunnel.py`
- `src/qwenpaw/hub/windows_process_isolation.py`
- `src/qwenpaw/hub/windows_runtime_bridge.py`
- `src/qwenpaw/cli/init_cmd.py`
- `src/qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py`
- `src/qwenpaw/utils/system_info.py`

`local_provisioner.py` only adds `QWENPAW_RUNTIME_MODE=hub`;
`runtime_environment.py` changes pip/certifi handling. No fix for the three
failures above is present in the beta.

## Request

Please fix the Windows Hub Local path end to end:

1. make the AppContainer runtime able to create the default-skill staging
   directories under `working/tmp`;
2. preserve or fall back for CPU architecture detection in managed Local
   runtimes (PR #7492);
3. make the AppContainer reverse tunnel and Hub readiness probe reliable,
   including a realistic startup budget on Windows.

I can provide full runtime/Hub logs and a minimal reproduction script if useful.

issues.title: [Feature]: Support message retraction/editing and workspace rollback in WebUI

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body: ## Summary A feature to allow users to edit or retract their previously sent messages in the WebUI chat interface, automatically truncating subsequent conversation history and optionally rolling back file changes (snapshots) to ensure a clean context. （在 WebUI 聊天界面中允许用户编辑或撤回已发送的消息，自动截断后续对话历史，并可选回滚文件修改（快照），以保证上下文的干净。） ## Component(s) Affected - [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [x] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [ ] Documentation (website) - [ ] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy ## Problem / Motivation Currently, once a user sends a message in QwenPaw WebUI, they cannot edit or retract it. When users realize their prompt has errors or missed information after seeing the AI's response, they can only correct it by sending follow-up messages. This severely pollutes the conversation context, introduces noise, and leads to AI hallucinations and wasted tokens. This feature is highly requested for: 1. Prompt Engineering: Iteratively testing different prompts to fine-tune AI responses. 2. Clean Context: Avoiding "Lost in the Middle" issues caused by messy correction messages. 3. Workflow Efficiency: Similar to the "Edit" button in DeepSeek web UI and the "Retract + File Rollback" feature in TRAE IDE, which users become highly dependent on for coding tasks. （目前用户发送消息后无法修改。看到 AI 回复才发现提示词有误时，只能在后续对话中打补丁，污染上下文、引入噪音、浪费 Token。此功能可以极大提升 Prompt 调试效率和代码编写体验，类似 DeepSeek 网页版的编辑按钮和 TRAE IDE 的撤回+文件回滚。） ## Proposed Solution UI/UX Design: Add "Edit" (✏️) and "Retract/Delete" (🔄/🗑️) buttons below each user message (similar to DeepSeek WebUI). Behavioral Logic: 1. Clicking "Edit" opens the message in an input box. Upon sending the edited message, all subsequent conversation history (both user and AI messages) will be automatically truncated. 2. The AI will then generate a new response based on the edited prompt. Workspace Rollback (Crucial for Coding Agents): When retracting a message in a coding session, a confirmation dialog should appear asking the user if they want to rollback the file workspace to the snapshot taken right before this message was sent (similar to TRAE IDE's checkpoint system). Technical Boundaries: Since side effects of executed Shell commands (e.g., rm, external API calls, database writes) are irreversible, the UI should clearly warn the user about this limitation. Workspace rollback should only apply to file-level snapshots. （UI 设计：消息下方增加编辑和撤回按钮。交互逻辑：编辑后发送自动截断后续历史并重新生成。工作区回滚：结合代码快照机制，撤回时弹窗询问是否恢复发送前的文件状态。技术边界：明确提示已执行的 Shell 命令等不可逆，UI 上应给出明确警示。） ## Alternatives Considered 1. Sending follow-up correction messages (current behavior, pollutes context). 2. Starting a brand new conversation (loses previous context and requires repeating all prior steps). （1. 发送后续修正消息，污染上下文；2. 开启全新对话，丢失上下文，需要重新复现之前的步骤。） ## Additional Context Reference: DeepSeek WebUI's message edit feature. Reference: TRAE IDE's "Retract and rollback" feature. Related existing issues in the community: #6408, #5503 (if applicable, search to link). (You can drag and drop the screenshot of DeepSeek or TRAE here to help illustrate the UI). （提供参考产品的截图，或关联社区已有的相关 Issue，比如之前提到的 #6408）。

issues.title: [Bug]: Desktop window is forced always-on-top (WS_EX_TOPMOST) in 2.3.0-beta.2 - covers fullscreen apps
issues.body:
## What happened

After updating to **2.3.0-beta.2**, the QwenPaw Desktop main window is permanently **always-on-top**. Any fullscreen window (a browser kiosk page, a fullscreen video player, a game in borderless mode, a presentation in slideshow) is drawn *behind* the QwenPaw window and cannot be seen.

On **2.3.0-beta.1** this did not happen — the same fullscreen page covered everything normally.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11, build 26300
- QwenPaw Desktop: **2.3.0-beta.2** (`/api/version` returns `2.3.0b2`)
- Installed: 2026-11-03 01:28 (previous build was 2.3.0-beta.1, exe dated 2026-10-27)

## Evidence

1. `GetWindowLong(hwnd, GWL_EXSTYLE)` on the main window returns **`WS_EX_TOPMOST` set**.
2. Calling `SetWindowPos(hwnd, HWND_NOTOPMOST, ...)` immediately clears it — but **within ~0.5 s the app sets it back** (re-checked every 2 s for 32 s: `topmost=True` in all 16 samples).
3. There is **no UI toggle** for this. Searching the console frontend bundle for "置顶 / alwaysOnTop / topmost" only finds per-session "pin conversation" strings; the Chinese docs contain no such setting; the profile JSONs contain no such key.
4. The v2.3.0-beta.2 release notes contain no mention of a window always-on-top change.

=> Looks like an unintended side effect rather than a designed feature.

## Expected

The main window should behave like a normal window (or at least there should be a setting to disable always-on-top).

## Actual

The main window stays above every other window, including fullscreen ones. On a 1920x1080 display the only workaround I found is `ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_MINIMIZE)` — i.e. the user has to minimize QwenPaw to see any fullscreen content.

## Impact

Any user who runs a fullscreen app while QwenPaw is open will lose that app's window. This is easy to hit: fullscreen video, game (borderless), slide show, or any kiosk-style page.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows 11, run QwenPaw Desktop 2.3.0-beta.2.
2. Open any fullscreen window, e.g. `msedge.exe --kiosk file:///C:/temp/test.html`.
3. Observe: the QwenPaw window stays in front of the fullscreen window.
4. (Optional) With a small Win32 helper, read `GetWindowLong(hwnd, GWL_EXSTYLE)` -> `WS_EX_TOPMOST` is set; clear it with `SetWindowPos(..., HWND_NOTOPMOST, ...)` and poll again -> it is re-set within half a second.

## Workaround

Minimize the QwenPaw window (`ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_MINIMIZE)`) while the fullscreen app is needed, then restore it afterwards.

issues.title: [Bug] Desktop build omits visual_compression assets → "FileNotFoundError: atlas-gray-native.ts", Visual Compact silently no-ops
issues.body:
## Summary

On the **desktop / PyInstaller build** of `2.3.0-beta.1` (Windows), Visual Compact never runs: the glyph atlases are not shipped, so every eligible model call raises

```
FileNotFoundError: <install>\binaries\qwenpaw-backend\_internal\qwenpaw\agents\context\visual_compression\assets\atlas-gray-native.ts
```

The middleware catches it and **fails open** (`Visual compression failed; sending the original request`), so the conversation continues unchanged and nothing is surfaced to the user.

`pip install qwenpaw` is **not** affected: `pyproject.toml` declares these files as `package-data` (`include-package-data = true`). Only the PyInstaller/Tauri bundle misses them.

## Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop `2.3.0-beta.1`, Windows 11 26H2 (build 26300.9807)
- default config: `light_context.visual_compact.enabled = true`, `effort = "low"`
- any model that reports `supports_image: true`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install QwenPaw **Desktop** `2.3.0-beta.1` (Windows).
2. Keep the defaults (`enabled = true`, `effort = "low"`).
3. Build a conversation with **≥ 3 real user turns** and at least one image in a turn older than the last two (`HISTORY_KEEP_RECENT_TURNS = 2`).
4. Send one more message.
5. The log shows `Visual compression failed; sending the original request (model=… effort=low)` plus a `FileNotFoundError` traceback for the atlas path above.

## Root cause

`scripts/pack-tauri/qwenpaw.spec` collects package data from a **hard-coded directory whitelist**:

```python
_data_dirs = [
    ("agents/skills", "qwenpaw/agents/skills"),
    ("agents/md_files", "qwenpaw/agents/md_files"),
    ("tokenizer", "qwenpaw/tokenizer"),
    ("security/tool_guard/rules", "qwenpaw/security/tool_guard/rules"),
    ("security/skill_scanner/rules", "qwenpaw/security/skill_scanner/rules"),
    ("security/skill_scanner/data", "qwenpaw/security/skill_scanner/data"),
    ("app/channels/yuanbao/proto", "qwenpaw/app/channels/yuanbao/proto"),
    ("providers/data", "qwenpaw/providers/data"),
]
```

`agents/context/**` is not in the list, so `_internal/qwenpaw/agents/` ships only `md_files` and `skills`. The runtime resolves the atlas relative to the frozen module:

```python
# rendering/renderer.py
_ASSET_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "assets"
_DENSE_ATLAS_PROFILES = {
    "low":    (_ASSET_ROOT / "atlas-gray-native.ts",   8, 16),
    "medium": (_ASSET_ROOT / "atlas-gray-readable.ts", 6, 13),
    "high":   (_ASSET_ROOT / "atlas-gray.ts",          5,  8),
}
```

→ the path it looks for cannot exist in the bundled layout. The same whitelist is on `main`, so the next desktop build will most likely miss it as well.

## Suggested fix

```diff
 _data_dirs = [
     ("agents/skills", "qwenpaw/agents/skills"),
     ("agents/md_files", "qwenpaw/agents/md_files"),
+    (
+        "agents/context/visual_compression/assets",
+        "qwenpaw/agents/context/visual_compression/assets",
+    ),
     ("tokenizer", "qwenpaw/tokenizer"),
```

(≈23 MB; the three `*_LICENSE.txt` files in that directory should be shipped too.)

## Two further suggestions

1. **Startup self-check**: if `visual_compact.enabled` is true but the configured atlas is missing, log one `WARNING` at boot (optionally auto-disable the feature) instead of raising on every request.
2. **Rate-limit the log**: the fail-open path currently emits a full traceback per model call; one line per session plus a counter is enough.

## Workaround for other desktop users

Copy the three atlases (and the three license files) from the tag into
`<install>\binaries\qwenpaw-backend\_internal\qwenpaw\agents\context\visual_compression\assets\`.
They exist in the source tree at `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/visual_compression/assets/` (`atlas-gray-native.ts` = 12,157,200 B, `atlas-gray-readable.ts` = 7,576,000 B, `atlas-gray.ts` = 4,093,877 B). Desktop upgrades recreate the `binaries` folder, so the copy has to be redone afterwards.

Raw logs can be provided on request if useful.

issues.title: [Bug]: QQ channel plugin fails to activate with DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED when a hub plugin (aliyun-hub) has no dependency environment
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0b2

## Description

The `qq` channel plugin (`dependency_mode: shared`) fails to activate on startup. Activation aborts inside the shared-dependency audit:

```
DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED: qq: host aliyun-hub: environment evidence unavailable.
Consumers: declaration qq, host aliyun-hub, runtime qq.
Stop environment consumers before explicit repair and re-audit.
Source rollback does not restore dependency packages.
```

The QQ channel never comes online. The Console "repair dependencies" action returns **409 Conflict** every time, because the repair path re-runs the same failing audit — and its instruction ("stop environment consumers before explicit repair") is unsatisfiable, since `qq` itself is one of the consumers. That is a deadlock with no UI path out.

`aliyun-hub` is an unrelated built-in **hub**-type plugin (Aliyun Skill marketplace source). It has no Python requirements and provides no dependency environment, so it should not be able to block a channel plugin.

## Environment

- QwenPaw **2.3.0b2** (PyPI `2.3.0b2`)
- Armbian aarch64 (TV box), Python 3.12.3
- One active agent, one workspace with the `qq` channel enabled
- Workspace plugins present: `aliyun-hub`, `qwenpaw-hub`, `clawhub-hub`, `modelscope-hub`, `memory-console`, `qq`
- `qq` channel: `enabled: true`, official QQ bot `app_id` + `client_secret` configured, previously working on 2.3.0b1

## Reproduction

1. Install 2.3.0b2 with the stock `aliyun-hub` plugin present in the workspace `plugins/` directory.
2. Enable the `qq` channel (`dependency_mode: shared`, `process_mode: runner_process`).
3. Restart qwenpaw.
4. Observe the activation failure above; the QQ channel stays offline.
5. Click "repair dependencies" in the Console → HTTP 409.

## Logs

```
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: aliyun-hub
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: qwenpaw-hub
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: qq
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: clawhub-hub
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: modelscope-hub
INFO  plugins/registry.py:538 | Registered startup hook 'channel_qq_qq' from plugin 'qq' (priority=80)
INFO  plugins/api.py:1329 | Plugin 'qq' registered startup hook 'channel_qq_qq' (priority=80)

ERROR plugins/loader.py:5002 | Failed to activate plugin 'qq': DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED:
      qq: host aliyun-hub: environment evidence unavailable.
      Consumers: declaration qq, host aliyun-hub, runtime qq.

INFO  ... "POST /api/plugins/qq/repair-dependencies HTTP/1.1" 409 Conflict
```

There is no `channel_qq` startup line and no runner connection attempt after the failure.

## Root cause analysis (from reading 2.3.0b2 source)

**1. `plugins/dependency_usage.py` — `DependencyUsageRegistry.observe_host()`** only attaches an environment when an observation succeeded:

```python
self._host[token] = deepcopy(
    replace(
        declaration,
        active=True,
        origin="host",
        snapshot=snapshot,
        environment=(
            DependencyEnvironment.from_snapshot(snapshot)
            if observed and (previous is None or previous.environment is not None)
            else None
        ),
    ),
)
```

**2. `plugins/python_backend.py:963`** — when host dependency observation is inconclusive it explicitly records an unknown state:

```python
def unknown():
    if valid():
        usage.observe_host(token, None)
```

So a host plugin whose imports/requirements can never be resolved ends up in `_host` with `snapshot=None` and `environment=None`.

**3. `plugins/dependency_usage.py` — `snapshot()`** includes every `_host` entry in `uses` unconditionally:

```python
uses = [
    use for token, use in self._declarations.items()
    if use.pending or token is admission_token
] + list(self._host.values())
```

**4. `plugins/dependency_gate.py` — the audit loop** treats any use with `environment is None` as a hard failure:

```python
for use in uses:
    environment, evidence = use.environment, use.snapshot
    ...
    if environment is None:
        unsupported.append(f"{use.origin} {use.plugin_id}: environment evidence unavailable")
        continue
```

**5.** `unsupported` being non-empty yields `DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED` for the whole shared plan, so **every** `dependency_mode: shared` plugin in that environment is refused activation.

In short: a hub-type plugin with no dependency involvement is registered as a host dependency user, can never produce environment evidence, and that missing evidence is treated as a fatal condition for an unrelated channel plugin's shared plan.

## Suggested fix

Any one of:

- Do not register `type: hub` plugins in `_host` (they have no dependency environment by design); or
- In `snapshot()`, keep host entries with `environment is None` out of the audited `uses`; or
- In `dependency_gate.py`, treat `environment is None` for a use that declares no requirements as "no dependency involvement" instead of `unsupported`.

## Workaround

Moving the `aliyun-hub` plugin directory out of the workspace `plugins/` folder and restarting makes the QQ channel activate with zero errors:

```bash
mv <qwenpaw_home>/working/plugins/aliyun-hub /tmp/aliyun-hub.bak
systemctl restart qwenpaw
```

After this, `Failed to activate plugin 'qq'` disappears, `Plugin 'qq' registered startup hook 'channel_qq_qq'` runs, and the QQ bot connects normally.

Downside: the Aliyun skill marketplace source disappears from the Console until the plugin is restored.

issues.title: [Bug]: edit_file converts all CRLF line endings to LF during a targeted edit

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

Tested source revision: `27d22cd18d6e7fe610536ef1375cebf7aea89215`.

## Description

QwenPaw's edit_file reads the file through read_file_safe, which normalizes all \r\n/\r to \n, applies the replacement and atomically rewrites the whole file with newline='\n', so a one-line edit of a CRLF file silently converts every line ending while reporting success.

Observed behavior:
edit_file(build.bat, 'set TARGET=staging' -> 'set TARGET=production') returns 'Successfully replaced text in build.bat.'; the final build.bat has 0 CRLF (fixture had 7); the agent tells the user nothing else changed.

Tested source revision: `27d22cd18d6e7fe610536ef1375cebf7aea89215`.

Model/provider: deepseek-chat via the recorded test harness.

## Steps to Reproduce
