issues.title: [Task]: show retired environment-variable warnings in zeroclaw config migrate
issues.body:
### Task

Make `zeroclaw config migrate` show the warning for a retired `ZEROCLAW_*` environment variable, as every other command does.

### Context

Follow-up from the review of #11218 (schema V4), raised by Greptile on that PR's `src/main.rs`.

At startup, `main.rs` prints the load's `migration_notices` unless the command is `config migrate` (`reports_own_migration`), because that command reports its own notices as changes it wrote. But `ConfigCommands::Migrate` then prints only `report.notices` from `migrate_file_in_place`, which come from the file. A `MigrationNotice::IgnoredEnvOverride` is raised at load time from the environment (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/env_overrides.rs`), not from the file, so `config migrate` never mentions it. That includes the "already at the current schema" branch.

Nothing is written incorrectly, and the variable has no effect either way. But `config migrate` is the command an operator runs to see what still needs cleaning up, and it's the one command where this warning is missing.

`MigrationNotice::changes_file()` already separates the two kinds: it is false only for `IgnoredEnvOverride`.

### Acceptance criteria

- With a retired `ZEROCLAW_*` variable set, `zeroclaw config migrate` prints its warning once, both when the file is migrated and when it is already current.
- File-change notices are still printed once, by the migrate command itself, not twice.
- `config migrate --json` includes the environment notice in its `notices` output, or the issue records why it should not.
- A test covers the already-current case with a retired variable set.

### Likely files or areas

- `src/main.rs`: the `reports_own_migration` block in startup, and the `ConfigCommands::Migrate` arm.
- `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/migration.rs`: `MigrationNotice::changes_file`.

### Contributor fit

good first issue candidate

### Mentor, reviewer, or contact

@tidux

### Risk notes

Low. Output only: no config is read or written differently. Keep the warning text on its existing Fluent path.

prs.title: fix(agents): admit env-defined agents at load and refuse tool-side agent removal
prs.body:
> **Stacked on #9745.** This branch carries #9745's content and integrates its current head (`e1e067643f`) by merge. Review only `f6597da57b` (the change), `0ec48844fe` (the Fluent key in the runtime catalogue the generated tools mirror is rendered from) and the one-paragraph docs resolution in the merge commit; everything else is #9745's and lands with that PR. Draft until #9745 merges, after which this diff shrinks to those commits.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `env_overrides::resolve_path` created `agents.<alias>` entries through the raw generated `create_map_key`, so `ZEROCLAW_agents__default__*` vivified the reserved `default` agent that every request-driven creation path refuses. The walker now admits a map key the environment would create: an absent reserved `default` is withheld with every variable naming it, the load still succeeds, and the refusal is one `WARN` per alias with `error_key` `config.env_agent_override_refused` plus `AppliedOverrides::withheld_agents`. An existing entry is never checked, so a migration-synthesized `agents.default` still takes env overrides; a malformed alias still fails the load with the validator's message.
  - The retired-knowledge rule the other creation paths apply is deliberately not applied at load. An env-defined agent is absent from the file on every boot and owns the knowledge it captured in earlier runs, and nothing durable distinguishes that from a retired alias whose purge failed (`committed_residue_exists` is residue-based too, the delete archive leaf is left by successful purges as well, the graph has no retired-owner record). Applying it would withhold every env-defined agent after its first run; #9745's test `upsert_agent_admits_env_defined_agent_that_owns_knowledge` catches exactly that. Docs now say env variables define an agent again at the next load, over retained knowledge too, and to remove an agent's variables before deleting it.
  - `model_routing_config remove_agent` removed the config entry and saved the file directly, skipping the delete lease and config commit, the hard-reference refusal and soft-reference scrub, and the owned-state cascade (memory, knowledge, cron, ACP), so the agent's owned state was orphaned under its alias. That path lives in the runtime, which the tools crate cannot depend on, and the tool is built with only `(Arc<Config>, Arc<SecurityPolicy>)`. The action is now refused unconditionally, before the write gate and without reading config, with a Fluent message naming `zeroclaw agents delete <alias>`, the dashboard's agent controls and RPC `agents/delete`, and a `WARN` with `error_key` `tools.model_routing_remove_agent_refused`. The schema no longer advertises it; the string is still dispatched so an older prompt gets the explanation rather than "Unknown action".
- **Scope boundary:** no change to the request-driven admission rule from #9745, to `upsert_agent`, to the delete cascade, or to how env overrides are masked at save. No load-time knowledge probe (see above). The tool still writes its other actions outside config-commit admission, as `config-lifecycle.md` already records.
- **Blast radius:** config load (`Config::load_or_init`, `prepare_from_migrated_toml`, the channel orchestrator reload, and the tool's `agent_defined_by_env` all share `apply_env_overrides`), and any prompt or SOP that called `model_routing_config` with `action: remove_agent`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #9745. Related #9647.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw agents can be created three ways: in `config.toml`, through a config write at runtime (CLI, dashboard, RPC, or the agent's own `model_routing_config` tool), or from `ZEROCLAW_agents__<alias>__*` environment variables when the daemon starts. #9745 made every runtime creation path share one rule: never the reserved `default` agent, and never an alias whose deleted predecessor still owns knowledge rows. The environment path had no rule at all, so a stray `ZEROCLAW_agents__default__enabled=true` quietly created the one agent nothing else is allowed to create. Now that variable is set aside with a warning and the daemon starts without it.

The second half is about deleting agents. The supported ways (`zeroclaw agents delete`, the dashboard, RPC) refuse while something still points at the agent, scrub references, and archive and purge the agent's memory, knowledge, cron jobs and ACP sessions. The `model_routing_config` tool's `remove_agent` just deleted the config line, leaving all of that behind under a name that no longer existed. The tool cannot run the real delete from where it lives, so it now says so and points at the surfaces that can.

One thing this PR does not do, on purpose: it does not refuse an environment-defined agent because knowledge rows exist for its name. Such an agent legitimately has rows after its first run, and there is no record that tells a live agent's rows apart from a deleted one's leftovers. Refusing would remove working agents on every restart. The docs now tell operators to remove an agent's variables before deleting it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the env-override half; the tool half is covered by unit tests and is a refusal with no state change.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a config with no `[agents.default]` entry (a fresh `zeroclaw init` config is fine).
- **Steps to run:** `ZEROCLAW_agents__default__enabled=false zeroclaw agents list`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** no `default` alias is listed; the log carries one `WARN` with `error_key=config.env_agent_override_refused`, `alias=default`, `env_var=ZEROCLAW_agents__default__enabled`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `default` is listed, created from the environment with no warning.

### How I tested

Focused tests, both crates' full lib suites, clippy and the docs gates locally on the original commit `f6597da57b`; after merging #9745's `e1e067643f` (one docs conflict in `relationship-memory.md`, resolved by keeping both PRs' sentences), fmt, clippy, the focused tests and the docs and hygiene gates were run again on the merge result. The comment hygiene checker was run as `python3 scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.py <nul-separated list of the changed files>` because the wrapper script needs `rg`, which is broken on this machine; `rust_quality_gate.sh` was not run end to end for the same reason, so its provider-dispatch step is left to CI.

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# (no output)
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings
#     Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 58.79s
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- env_overrides alias_refs::tests
# test result: ok. 73 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1756 filtered out
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- model_routing_config i18n
# test result: ok. 45 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1342 filtered out
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib
# test result: FAILED. 1828 passed; 1 failed  (policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception; fails on the base commit too, macOS host)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib
# test result: FAILED. 1375 passed; 9 failed; 3 ignored  (all content_search::tests::*, which need rg)
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
# No prose em-dashes in changed docs files. ... Summary: 0 error(s)
scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
# Collected 0 added link(s) from 5 docs file(s).
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Linux `Test` job runs both crates' unit tests, including the new ones; `Lint` covers the clippy surface with `--features ci-all`; `Docs Style` covers the five changed Markdown files; the comment hygiene gate covers the new comments.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `Report proposed PR risk` fails closed on this PR ("PR file evidence is not bound to the captured head SHA") and on #9745 for the same reason: #9745 removes `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/agent_owned_state.rs`, GitHub binds a removed file's `contents_url` to the merge base rather than the head, and `scripts/github/pr_risk_label.py`'s `file_bound_to_head` rejects that. The workflow fetches that script from master, so this branch cannot fix it; a separate script fix is proposed. The check is report-only.
- **Commands run and tail output:** above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That the one failure the first implementation produced was #9745's `upsert_agent_admits_env_defined_agent_that_owns_knowledge`, and why (see Summary); that `alias_refs::tests::rename_agent_rewrites_every_ref_kind`, which failed once in a full run, passes alone and in two further full runs: its fixture is `Config::default()`, so #9745's rename probe reads the developer's real `~/.zeroclaw/knowledge.db` and a concurrent local writer makes it refuse (worth a temp path in #9745). Not verified: the daemon end to end with the variable set; the reviewer steps above are the A/B for that.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`; no rendered interface changed. The additions are a log record and a tool error string, both asserted by unit tests.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the branch head after the #9745 merge (change commit `f6597da57b`), unit tests in `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/env_overrides.rs` and `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/model_routing_config.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `rust_quality_gate.sh` end to end and the full-workspace clippy: `rg` is broken on this host and a fresh full-workspace build did not fit the disk; CI runs both.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No` (the tool loses a capability: `remove_agent` no longer writes config)
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No` (withheld variables are never applied, so they never reach the save-masking snapshots either)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No` (the new tool error text is a fixed Fluent message; the alias it echoes comes from the tool call's own argument)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `No` for two narrow cases, listed below; `Yes` otherwise.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users:
  - A deployment that relied on `ZEROCLAW_agents__default__*` to create `agents.default` when the file had no such entry now boots without that agent and logs `config.env_agent_override_refused`. Define the agent under a non-reserved alias, or let the schema migration synthesize `agents.default` in the file, after which the same variables apply to it.
  - A prompt, SOP or automation that called `model_routing_config` with `action: remove_agent` now gets a failed tool result naming the supported surfaces. Use `zeroclaw agents delete <alias>`, the dashboard, or RPC `agents/delete`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert f6597da57b 0ec48844fe`. Observable symptoms if the env change misfires: `WARN` records with `error_key=config.env_agent_override_refused` for an alias the operator expected to exist, and that alias missing from `zeroclaw agents list`.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A

prs.title: fix(config): migrate retired keys at schema version 4 and warn on a missing schema_version
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **Credit:** this builds on @singlerider's #8754, opened 2026-07-06, which first identified these inert keys and proposed the move to schema version 4. Its still-valid retirements, its version 3 layout pin for the filesystem relocation, and its version 4 fixture and tests are carried forward here, with a `Co-authored-by` trailer on the retirement commits. This PR also folds #11217, which reads an unversioned config in the version 3 format as version 3.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11082 retired `[security.nevis]` but left `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` at 3, so no migration ran. The table was discarded at load with a warning hidden unless `-v` was passed, and it stayed on disk with any plaintext `client_secret`. This PR bumps the schema to version 4 and adds a version 3 → version 4 step driven by a new `RETIRED_KEYS` table.
  - Each table entry names a key path, the version that retires it, and the reason shown to the operator, with a Fluent id so the CLI prints the reason in the operator's locale (logs and `--json` keep the English text). A retired key is removed with everything under it. A path segment `ANY_KEY` (`"*"`) matches every key at its level, so one entry retires a key in every `[agents.<alias>]` block or every runtime profile. Each concrete match is reported under its real path.
  - Retired keys are applied during migration and again on every load of a current-version config. A retired key that reappears in a version 4 file is dropped with a notice, not silently ignored by serde.
  - The same table also drives incremental saves. #11191 made `save_dirty` remove `[security.nevis]` from the on-disk document, since an incremental save rewrites only dirty paths and would otherwise carry a retired table and its secret forward. This PR replaces that Nevis-only helper with `apply_retired_keys_to_doc`, so `save_dirty` and migration share one retirement policy. Wildcard entries work there too, so the eight agent-inline tunables are removed from disk as well. The edit touches only retired keys, keeps comments and unrelated ciphertext byte for byte, and logs each removal only after the atomic write succeeds. #11191's tests are kept against the table-driven cleanup. A save first reads the version of the file on disk. A version 1 or version 2 file is not edited as it stands, because keys retired at version 3 (`[identity]`, an agent's `max_tool_iterations`) are still live inputs to its version 2 → version 3 step. An incremental save first carries the file on disk through the typed migration chain, then applies the dirty paths to the result, so those inputs are converted and keys another handle saved after this config loaded survive. A file whose version cannot be determined (an unversioned file that mixes layouts or reads both ways) or is newer than this binary is refused by both save paths, so a load that fell back to defaults cannot relabel it and write over it.

A table matched by a wildcard is an operator-named alias such as `[agents.coder]` and is always kept, so a reference to it never dangles. `toml_edit` writes nothing for an empty implicit or dotted table, so an alias that existed only as a prefix of retired dotted keys (`runtime_profiles.slow.context_compression.summary_model = …`) is written back as its own `[runtime_profiles.slow]` header, or as `slow = {}` inside an inline table.

The copy is owner-only (0600 on Unix) whatever the source's mode, because it can hold the plaintext secrets of retired keys, and it is never replaced or removed. It is written and synced under a private name, then published with a hard link, which never replaces an existing path, so a file at that name is never an unfinished copy. An existing file there counts only when it holds exactly the bytes about to be rewritten; it is then synced and, if an older build left it readable by others, made owner-only, or the rewrite is refused. Where the filesystem has no hard links, the synced copy is renamed to a name of its own, `config.toml.v<version>-<uuid>.backup`, so no writer counts on a copy another writer might still fail to finish. `config migrate` names the copy, and `--json` reports it as `version_backup_path`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's config file carries a version number, so that when a setting is removed an upgrade can rewrite old files and say what it changed. Several settings had been removed without that happening, so they were quietly ignored. Some had been ignored from the start, like tuning knobs written under an agent instead of under its runtime profile. This PR adds a list of retired settings. The upgrade removes each one it finds and prints a plain warning saying why and what to use instead. One entry can cover a setting under every agent or every profile. The first entries are the removed Nevis login block, eight agent knobs that never did anything, and an old summary-model setting. A config file with no version number is no longer read as the oldest version when it is plainly written in the current shape, which used to silently merge your named channels into one called `default`. It warns either way.

With its `schema_version` line removed, it is read as version 3 with the inferred-version notice rather than as version 1, and the resilient load resets no section.
- **Unversioned-file and channel-retirement tests:** `a_plainly_v3_file_without_the_key_is_read_as_v3`, `an_inferred_v3_file_is_migrated_to_v4_and_keeps_every_channel_alias` (aliases kept on load, `config migrate` and the resilient load), `an_inferred_v3_file_still_loses_its_retired_keys`, `an_explicit_version_is_never_reported_as_inferred`, the version 1-reading cases (version 2 shape, version 1-only key, no alias-keyed section, the bundled version 1 fixture) and `the_legacy_catalog_names_every_v1_setting`. `v3_to_v4_retires_top_level_twitter_and_reddit_but_not_the_channels` and `v3_to_v4_removes_the_unread_notion_table_and_keeps_poller_references` run a version 3 fixture through both the value chain and the in-place migration, checking that the table goes, every `notion` reference stays, and the comment on an untouched section survives. `notion_references_in_a_current_file_are_not_retirements` covers a version 4 file with dotted and inline tables. `a_retirement_never_names_a_key_the_schema_still_reads` guards the table. `a_map_only_v2_provider_profile_requires_an_explicit_version` (with version 2 and version 3 stated, each keeping its data), `a_map_only_v2_channel_requires_an_explicit_version`, `an_ordinary_v2_profile_with_a_map_field_keeps_the_v1_reading`, `a_v3_alias_named_like_a_map_field_requires_an_explicit_version` and `a_schema_version_beyond_u32_is_refused_not_wrapped` cover the inference edges. `save_keeps_notion_poller_references_in_a_new_file`, `save_keeps_notion_poller_references_in_an_existing_file`, `save_dirty_keeps_notion_poller_references_on_an_unrelated_edit` and `save_dirty_on_a_missing_file_keeps_notion_poller_references` check the written file and its reload. With the probe, the full-save pass or the checked cast removed, these seven fail and the ordinary version 2 and clearly version 3 controls pass.
- **Cross-review regression tests:** `save_dirty_over_a_v2_file_migrates_it_before_editing` (identity and the agent's iteration limit survive, as does a key another handle saved after load; version 2 original kept), `saves_refuse_a_file_of_unknown_or_newer_version`, `the_first_save_over_a_v3_file_keeps_it`, `config_migrate_keeps_the_pre_upgrade_original`, `an_env_override_for_a_retired_key_is_ignored_not_fatal`, `save_dirty_over_an_unmigrated_v1_file_keeps_its_agent` (the #11579 reproduction), `retirement_reasons_and_their_ids_correspond`, `every_retirement_reason_is_in_every_cli_locale`, `a_v2_only_setting_beside_v3_sections_requires_an_explicit_version`, `an_empty_map_field_still_makes_the_shape_ambiguous`, `v2_only_agent_keys_are_not_v3_agent_fields` and the gateway's `migration_reports_its_notices`. With each fix removed, the eight tests guarding them fail.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Against a debug build of this head with an isolated temp `HOME`: the three steps above; a version 3 config with `[security.nevis]` and a `client_secret` (the secret is gone from `config.toml` and kept only in the backups); a version 4 config that still holds `[security.nevis]`; and a config with no `schema_version`. Every warning appeared without `-v`, and every second load was silent.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output`
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `34f5e905a6` (the head adds only doc comments), debug build, Linux x86_64; `zeroclaw` CLI stdout and stderr, locale `en`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

```text
$ zeroclaw config get runtime_profiles.fast.max_tool_iterations
warning: dropped retired config key `agents.coder.max_tool_iterations` from <tmp>/cfg/config.toml: agent-inline runtime tunables are no longer read; runtime profiles are authoritative, so set this key on the agent's `[runtime_profiles.<profile>]` instead
warning: dropped retired config key `runtime_profiles.fast.context_compression.summary_model` from <tmp>/cfg/config.toml: the deprecated bare model id had no provider identity and was never read; `summary_provider` replaced it (context compression itself is not currently implemented in the runtime)
warning: these changes apply to this run only. Run `zeroclaw config migrate` to write them to <tmp>/cfg/config.toml.
12
```

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** As above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The dashboard typecheck (`cargo web check`), the Nix module evaluation and the markdown lint half of `docs_quality_gate.sh` (its em-dash check passed) were not run locally; CI runs them as `Web Permission Tests`, `Nix Module Eval` and `Docs Style`. No dashboard source names a retired key. In `zeroclaw-runtime` this PR changes only the Fluent files and `schema_version` literals in test configs.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: `zeroclaw config migrate` now removes `[security.nevis]` from disk, including any plaintext `client_secret`; before, it stayed indefinitely. The backups still hold it: `config.toml.backup`, and the pre-upgrade copy `config.toml.v3.backup` described under Rollback. That lasting copy is created owner-only, and the authentication guide and the config lifecycle page now name both copies and say to delete them once a downgrade is no longer needed. Notices carry key paths and reasons only, never values; a unit test asserts this. The pinned filesystem relocation removes a risk this bump would otherwise have introduced: re-running the version 2 → version 3 workspace move on version 3 installs.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users:
  - After upgrading, run `zeroclaw config migrate` once. Until then configs load normally, migrated in memory, but `config set`, `config init`, `config patch` and `models set` refuse, as with every earlier schema bump.
  - `[security.nevis]`, the eight agent-inline tunables and `summary_model` are no longer config keys. Set tunables on the agent's `[runtime_profiles.<profile>]`; configure `[oidc.<alias>]` with `[users]` and `[permission_profiles]` in place of Nevis.
  - A config with no `schema_version` prints a warning on every command until it has one. One plainly in the version 3 shape is read as version 3 rather than version 1, so its channel aliases and provider entries are no longer reshaped.
  - Top-level `[twitter]` and `[reddit]` and the `[channels.notion]` table are dropped. References to the `notion` channel (the `[notion]` poller) are kept.
  - A save over a config whose version cannot be determined, or that is newer than this binary, now fails instead of writing over it. A `ZEROCLAW_*` variable naming a retired key is ignored with a notice.
  - An unversioned config that mixes the version 3 layout with an older one, or whose shape reads both as version 2 and as version 3, is refused until `schema_version` is added; the error names what it found. Before, the first was read as version 1 and its version 3 sections were reshaped. A `schema_version` past the `u32` range is refused as newer than the binary instead of being narrowed.
  - `zeroclaw config migrate --json` gains a `notices` array.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits. #11191's Nevis-only save cleanup then returns with it. A config already migrated to `schema_version = 4` is then newer than the binary supports. A version 4 body is a subset of version 3, so setting it back to `schema_version = 3` by hand works; to restore the file as it was, use `config.toml.v3.backup` (or `.v1`/`.v2`). This binary writes that copy the first time it rewrites a file of that version, through `config migrate`, the dashboard's migrate, or a save, and never replaces it. `config.toml.backup` is not a reliable rollback copy: each `config migrate` replaces it, including a later retirement-only one of a version 4 file. The dashboard migrate's `config.toml.bak` is replaced by the next save.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** An unexpected `dropped retired config key` line on stderr for a key that is still in use. `config migrate --json` shows the same entries under `notices`.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #8754 by @singlerider (its version 4 step and its still-valid retirements); #9809 by @NiuBlibing (its version 3 → version 4 and version 4 → version 5 steps only, which are superseded rather than ported: no code from #9809 is carried, so there is no trailer, and the multi-model provider change stays in #9809); #11217 by @JordanTheJet (closed in favour of this PR; its change is folded here).
- Scope materially carried forward: the inert agent-tunable and `summary_model` retirements, the version 3 layout pin for the filesystem relocation, and the version 4 acceptance fixture and its tests.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? Yes

v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(shell): reap the process group a returned command left running
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Every `shell` command runs in its own session, so its process group is its own. `ChildGroupGuard` already tears that whole group down on timeout or cancellation, but a command that returned normally disarmed the guard. A child the command had backgrounded (`sleep 300 &`, `yes > /dev/null &`) then kept running with nothing to bound it: the tool timeout no longer applies once the command has answered, and the process is reparented to init, so it outlives the turn, the job and a daemon restart. On one busy host a single agent run left 368 `yes` processes behind at load 376.
  - After a normal return the tool now terminates whatever is still alive in that group: `SIGTERM` to `-pgid`, a bounded grace, then `SIGKILL` for what has not exited, and it logs how many processes it swept. Only `-pgid` is signalled; a group id that is not positive or that names the daemon's own group is refused.
  - The sweep runs before the post-exit pipe drain, not after. A background child normally holds the tool's stdout/stderr open, so draining first spent the whole drain budget waiting on a process that was about to be killed. A command with a background sleeper now returns in about 30 ms instead of about 280 ms. Output the command itself produced is untouched.
  - Two new `[shell_tool]` keys: `reap_background_on_return` (default `true`) and `reap_grace_secs` (default `2`).
- **Scope boundary:** the shell tool and its config section only. Timeout and cancellation cleanup are unchanged. A descendant that calls `setsid()` or `setpgid()` itself still escapes, exactly as on the timeout and cancellation paths today.
- **Blast radius:** commands that deliberately start a detached daemon through the shell tool. They are now stopped when the command returns unless the operator sets `reap_background_on_return = false`.
- **Linked issue(s):** none.

### What this does, simply

If an agent runs `some-command &` through the shell tool, the command finishes, the tool reports its result, and the background process keeps going forever. Nothing watches it any more. This change kills those leftovers when the command returns, the same way the tool already does when a command times out.

Operators who really do start long-lived background services from the tool can turn the new behaviour off with one config line.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` - covered by the unit tests below.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** none directly; this is the `shell` tool.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zeroclaw-config` tests and clippy cover both crates touched.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the tests are Unix process-group tests; the Windows path is unchanged.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux, head `4701cc999`, rebased on master `4f3ca7c38`):

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output)

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::shell
test result: ok. 81 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib shell_tool
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile
```

- **Tests added or changed:** the shell tool reaps a backgrounded child on return; a command with nothing to sweep returns well inside the grace; a background child holding the tool's pipe does not cost the drain budget; the config defaults and a partial `[shell_tool]` section keep the remaining defaults.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `4701cc999`; no interface capture.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace test run was not repeated for this change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- Process signalling changed? Yes: the tool now sends `SIGTERM`/`SIGKILL` to the command's own process group after a normal return. Mitigation: only a positive `-pgid` is ever signalled, the daemon's own group is refused, and the group is the one the tool created for that command.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Mostly: the default changes behaviour for commands that background work and expect it to survive the command. They need `[shell_tool].reap_background_on_return = false`. Documented in `docs/book/src/security/sandboxing.md`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: two new optional keys in `[shell_tool]` with defaults.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: the keys are additive and default to the safe behaviour; no migration is needed.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Rollback strategy:** set `[shell_tool].reap_background_on_return = false`, or revert the two commits.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a background service started through the shell tool disappears when the command returns.

prs.title: feat(tools): add agy_cli coding-CLI tool for Antigravity CLI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Google has moved terminal Gemini use from Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI (`agy`), and Gemini CLI has stopped serving most accounts (Google Developers Blog, June 2026). ZeroClaw can delegate coding tasks to Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, but not to `agy`.
  - Adds `agy_cli`, a peer of `codex_cli` / `claude_code` / `gemini_cli` / `opencode_cli`. It is built on the shared coding-CLI executor, so it inherits the same authorization, working-directory validation, timeout, output bounding and runtime-executor routing.
  - Headless `agy` exits 0 and reports `status: SUCCESS` even when it auto-denies a tool permission, so the exit code alone would report a blocked task as a success. `agy_cli` requests JSON output and decides success from it. A run succeeds only when the process exits 0, `status` is `SUCCESS`, and `denied_actions` is empty. Non-JSON or status-less output fails closed.
  - Tool-owned flags are attached (`--print=<prompt>`, `--model=<id>`, `--print-timeout=<n>s`) and placed after operator `extra_args`. A model-supplied prompt that starts with `-` cannot be parsed as a flag, and the tool's own settings take precedence over operator arguments.
- **Scope boundary:** `gemini_cli` is not changed or deprecated here. There is no `agy` model provider. The shared coding-CLI executor is unchanged apart from recognising the new tool name in the env-boundary helper. The sandbox and permission defaults of `agy` itself are left to the operator's agy settings.
- **Blast radius:** Opt-in only. The new `[agy_cli]` section defaults to `enabled = false`, and nothing changes for existing configs. Shared test fixtures changed in two places: the budget-test fake now returns agy-shaped JSON, which the other adapters pass through unchanged, and the runtime routing test now expects `agy_cli` to fail closed on its plain-text probe.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11075. Related #4879, whose closing comment suggested Antigravity CLI support as the follow-up. Related #10381 (merged): `agy_cli` builds its command through the shared `CodingCliCommand`/`CodingCliExecutor` path, so it inherits that PR's host-launcher resolution before the workspace working directory is applied.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw agents can hand a coding task to an external coding CLI. Google has replaced Gemini CLI with a new tool called Antigravity CLI (`agy`), so Gemini users had no supported way to do that. This PR adds an `agy_cli` tool that works like the existing Codex and Claude Code tools. It stays off until you turn it on in config.

The main difference from the other CLIs is how failure is detected. When `agy` runs without a terminal and wants to do something that needs permission, such as running a shell command, it refuses automatically but still exits successfully. `agy_cli` reads agy's JSON result, reports those refusals as a failure, and tells the user how to allow the action in agy's own settings.

ZeroClaw checks that the requested working directory is inside the workspace, but it does not sandbox what `agy` does once it is running. That is governed by agy's own permission settings. The docs section added in `tools/overview.md` states this plainly.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behaviour is covered by unit tests with fixtures copied from real agy 1.2.9 output. Manual testing needs an authenticated `agy` install, which most reviewers will not have.

### How I tested

- **Revision (2026-10-11):** one commit, which supersedes `76275ecf6`. It was authored and validated at `34d7aea0825a1e7cd7701135e4dc3f341271a56b` on master `0f8fb9d372a5cf850e87f9464c7f5c216a717fee`. **Rebase note (2026-10-11):** the then-current head `6239f29f26fcbe1e6b520016cb98b9eade20f329` was a base-only rebase of that commit onto master `d03325172eb6c64272f01042b60fd7f66d74c711` with GitHub's update-branch (`git range-diff` shows the commit identical; the local validation and review below were recorded on `34d7aea08`). **Rebase note (2026-10-14):** the then-current head `dc09ad4048d50e3960e9d8c44132a8fec3b4b1cd` was a base-only rebase of `6239f29f2` onto master `329e66f76` with GitHub's update-branch. Master had moved 32 commits and four files this PR touches changed upstream (`orchestrator/acp_server.rs`, `orchestrator/mod.rs`, `config/schema.rs`, `docs/book/src/tools/overview.md`); a trial merge was clean and the rebase applied without conflicts. `git range-diff` shows the commit unchanged apart from one context line in `docs/book/src/tools/overview.md` (the neighbouring heading was renamed upstream); the file set is unchanged (18 files). The local validation and review below were recorded on `34d7aea08`; required CI runs on the current head. **Rebase note (2026-10-17):** rebased again with GitHub's update-branch onto master `4e82ce46e` (32 commits, including the rustls/Wasmtime advisory fix #11755 that the earlier Security failure was waiting on). `git range-diff` shows the commit identical, with no content change; the new head is `91da937b6051c182654f7ba5d0cc240b722cece8`. A trial merge was clean; five files this PR changes were also touched on master (`zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs`, both `tools.ftl` files, `zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs`, `docs/book/src/developing/tool-inventory.md`) without conflict. What changed:
  - Inventory: `agy_cli` is registered in `BUILTIN_TOOLS` as a Host-tier tool, listed in the tier table and prose of `tool-inventory.md`, and enabled in the runtime maximal-config inventory test. This fixes the `matrix_safe_policy_names_only_inventoried_tools` failure that appeared after master's typed tool inventory landed, and Greptile's inventory finding.
  - i18n: the tool description, parameter descriptions and errors are Fluent `tool-agy-cli-*` keys in the canonical English catalogue, with the generated tools-crate mirror regenerated. This addresses Greptile's localization finding.
  - Hardening of `agy_cli`'s own contract: a bare `--` in `extra_args` is dropped from the agy argv and flagged by config validation, so it can no longer turn the tool-owned flags into positionals. An explicit JSON `null` for `response`, `denied_actions` or `error` no longer breaks parsing, so agy's real status and error are reported; success still requires `status == SUCCESS` and no denied actions. The `--print-timeout` margin scales with small timeouts instead of collapsing to `1s`. The attached form `--dangerously-skip-permissions=<value>` now triggers the risky-flag warning (agy only; Codex matching is unchanged). Stderr appended to errors is capped like stdout. `agy_cli` is added to the Integrations-group test.
  - Not changed: the shared coding-CLI workdir refactor, Codex helper naming, the model-visible remediation text, and tolerance for non-JSON banner lines.

- **Rebase note (2026-10-18):** rebased onto master `c473221313341a853e04122f93bb9bd26b5e6c47` (8 commits after `4e82ce46e`). GitHub's update-branch could not be used: master's #11221 (`8ed287bd4`) moved the coding-CLI tools behind per-tool Cargo features and conflicted in `zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs` and `zeroclaw-tools/src/coding_cli.rs`. I resolved it locally in an isolated worktree, starting from master's versions of both files and re-applying this PR's change on top. The new head is `400553d30eed7e316b68860003553e61700825c5` (previous head `91da937b6`). `agy_cli.rs` is byte-identical to the previous head; the previously approved behaviour is unchanged. What changed:
  - New `tool-agy-cli` feature, chained like its peers (`zeroclaw-config` -> `zeroclaw-tools` -> `zeroclaw-runtime` -> root) and added to the full-tool feature list.
  - `OptInTool::AgyCli` (`ALL` is now 13 entries) with section `agy_cli` and feature `tool-agy-cli`; the inventory entry now carries `compilation: OptIn(AgyCli)`.
  - `agy_cli` module, attribution and runtime registration are gated on the feature, with `warn_tool_compiled_out` otherwise; `any_coding_cli_tool_enabled` and the shared coding-CLI executor gates include it.
  - `collect_agy_cli_extra_arg_warnings` returns early when the tool is not compiled in (as the Codex collector does), so a build without `agy` reports only the compiled-out warning. Tests that need the feature are gated, and one new test covers the compiled-out case.
  - `tool-agy-cli` is added to the 13 generated feature lists (`Containerfile`, the Dockerfiles, `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`, `dist/aur/PKGBUILD`, `flake.nix`, `setup.bat`); `cargo run -p xtask --bin generate -- installers --check` reports every surface in sync.
  - The file set grows from 18 to 31 files: 13 additional files, namely the Cargo manifests, the packaging surfaces and `opt_in_tools.rs`.

prs.title: fix(channels): re-apply the system prompt cap after per-turn skill refreshes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The channel-turn system prompt is modified after the initial `max_system_prompt_chars` finalization (skills refresh splice on fresh sessions or mode changes, per-message signal block, peer-map append, thinking prefix prepend), so the operator's cap silently stopped applying exactly when the prompt was largest.
  - Re-apply `finalize_system_prompt` with the agent's cap as the last step before the system message enters history (message-processing path), and at the provider-switch retry path (`refresh_channel_history_skills`) and after the startup builder's own post-finalize additions (tool instructions, deferred section, receipts addendum), so startup and refreshed prompts share the budgeting path. Mandatory additions are preserved whole even when they alone meet or exceed the cap; that case logs a warning and can exceed the budget.
  - `finalize_system_prompt` now strips trailing `TIMESTAMP_ORIENTATION` copies before head-retention truncation, preserving user-authored quotes. An older runtime orientation can still repeat when later channel additions leave it inside the retained head.
- **Scope boundary:** no new settings, no canonical-source duplication; the no-op path of `finalize_system_prompt` (prompt within cap) is untouched; compaction/history trimming behavior unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** channel system-prompt assembly only. Agents whose prompts already fit the cap see no change (finalization is a no-op for them). Complete-section skill refreshes are capped when the reserved additions fit. A skills section already truncated at startup can still move refreshed optional content into the reserved tail and escape the cap; this remaining case can reach the context-floor budget refusal (`context_floor_exceeds_budget`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12044 (deferred bootstrap sections), Related #12056 (separate identity-head truncation work; this PR uses the current head-retaining finalizer).

### What this does, simply

`max_system_prompt_chars` is the operator's system-prompt budget. This implementation preserves mandatory additions whole, with a logged overflow when those additions alone meet or exceed the budget. It was enforced only when the prompt was first built at startup. Later, on the first message of a new conversation (or after a skills-mode change), the runtime replaces the skills section with a freshly rendered one — in Full injection mode that is every skill's full instructions — and appends per-message extras. None of those steps re-checked the ceiling, so a fresh conversation could dispatch a system prompt several times larger than the configured cap. In production this surfaced as a hard refusal for brand-new conversations (`system prompt and tool definitions (148706 tokens) exceed context budget (100000)`) while long-lived conversations kept using the older, capped cached prompt and worked fine. This PR reapplies head-retaining truncation after those modifications while reserving the detected text-tool tail. It removes trailing runtime timestamp-orientation copies before truncation; interior copies can still repeat.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — new regression tests cover skill refresh into an initially small cached prompt and text-tool retention; they do not cover every capped prompt shape.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (telegram path in the repro test, mechanism is channel-generic)
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

- New `process_channel_message_reapplies_prompt_cap_after_skill_refresh` (zeroclaw-channels): builds a real startup prompt under a 4000-char cap, drops a ~26KB-body skill on disk in Full mode, and asserts (1) the refresh splice really exceeds the cap (incident reproduction), (2) the refreshed history prompt is ≤ cap with exactly one timestamp orientation, (3) end-to-end, the provider receives a system prompt ≤ cap with one orientation.
- New `refinalizing_an_over-cap_prompt_keeps_a_single_timestamp_orientation` (zeroclaw-runtime): re-finalizing an already-finalized prompt does not duplicate the orientation.
- Before the fix the e2e assertion fails (~26K chars vs cap 4000 reaching the provider); after, green.

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib process_channel_message_reapplies_prompt_cap_after_skill_refresh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib refinalizing_an_over-cap_prompt_keeps_a_single_timestamp_orientation
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI on this PR (build/test/clippy across feature matrix) — the change touches the channel orchestrator and system-prompt finalization used by all channels.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** local run covered lib targets of the two touched crates; full-workspace integration binaries were not built locally (CI covers them).
- **Commands run and tail output:** both new tests and neighbors (`final_prompt_budget*`, `timestamp_orientation_respects_budgets`, full `agent::system_prompt` module — 35 tests, `process_channel_message_refreshes_available_skills_after_new_session`) pass; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --lib` exits 0 with no new warnings in the changed lines.
- **Beyond CI, what did I manually verify?** Idempotence of the added finalization on under-cap prompts (no-op path) via the orientation-count assertions; not verified: full workspace integration binaries and non-Linux platform runs.

prs.title: feat(tools): send files through send_via under the read policy
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `send_via` gains `attachments`, a list of file paths, for an immediate send (`target` + `body`). Today an agent on the email channel cannot send a file at all. Since #9993, outbound attachment bytes come only from `MediaAttachment.data`, and nothing loads a workspace file explicitly for the agent.
  - **Loading.** A new helper (`helpers/outbound_attachment.rs`) checks each path in this order:
    1. Refuse an empty path, a NUL byte or a `..` component.
    2. `is_path_allowed`, then `resolve_tool_path`, then canonicalise.
    3. `is_resolved_path_readable`, the read check `file_read` uses. It is deliberately not the write check the upload tools use, which admits write-only roots.
    4. Refuse runtime config files, and require a regular file.
    5. Open without following symlinks and read with a bounded reader, so the size check applies to the bytes actually read.

    It then builds the `MediaAttachment` directly. `MediaAttachment::from_file` is never called, so the file isn't opened a second time after the check.
  - **Gates, all checked before any file is read.** Any failure sends nothing:
    - the call is an immediate send;
    - the channel declares the new `Channel::supports_outbound_attachments()`;
    - the recipient's peer group sets `attachments_enabled` (default `false`);
    - the call stays within the `[tools.send_via]` limits (default 10 files, 10 MiB each, 20 MiB per call).
  - **Capability.** `Channel::supports_outbound_attachments()` defaults to `false`. Email (IMAP+SMTP), Slack and Matrix return `true`, and `PacedChannel` forwards it. Every other channel, including WASM plugin channels, is refused by name rather than silently dropping the files.
  - **Text in a `send_via` body never becomes an upload.** `SendMessage` gains `inline_attachments` (default `true`, so ordinary replies keep their markers). When it is `false`, every channel that turns message text into uploads sends the text as text instead: Slack, Matrix, Telegram (markers, and its bare-path and `file://` fallback), WeChat, QQ, Lark, WhatsApp Web, WhatsApp Cloud and Discord. Explicit attachments are unaffected. `send_via` sends with it off, so files go through `attachments` and the gates above, and nowhere else. This replaces a body detector, because channels parse markers in too many ways to mirror: rescanning inside unrecognised brackets, joining text after stripping tool-call tags or embeds, and uploading a body that is just a path.
  - **Approval prompts go out with inline attachments off** too. They are built by a shared `approval_prompt_message` helper on Slack, Discord, WhatsApp Web, WhatsApp Cloud and Matrix. Their text includes a tool's arguments, so a file marker in an argument is now shown, not uploaded.
  - **Plugin channels** receive the body as written: the plugin interface has no field for the switch, and adding one changes the plugin ABI. Plugins run with no access to host files. The docs say so.
  - The refusals this change adds use Fluent keys, and the attachment load runs in one `spawn_blocking`.
  - **Slack checks its own limits before posting.** That means at most 8 explicit files, none empty and none over 20 MiB. Before, it posted the text and then failed on a bad file, or silently dropped files beyond 8.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No attachments on a routed reply (`send_via` without `body`).
  - Telegram and the other chat channels are left for later. Telegram already has `send_document_bytes`, so it can opt in by returning `true` and sending `SendMessage.attachments`, with no change to `send_via`.
  - No HTML body (#11992), no CC (#9506), no inbound attachments (#11745, #11746).
  - Recipients stay limited to peer groups.
- **Blast radius:**
  - `zeroclaw-api`: one trait method with a default, and `SendMessage.inline_attachments` (default `true`) with a builder.
  - `zeroclaw-config`: `PeerGroupConfig.attachments_enabled`, and `[tools.send_via]` inside `BuiltinToolsConfig`. Because that struct denies unknown fields, `migration.rs` now drops a malformed `[tools.<name>]` table on its own instead of the whole `[tools]` table. The tool selection survives a bad limit value.
  - `zeroclaw-tools`: `send_via`, the helper, and `detect_mime` made `pub(crate)`.
  - `zeroclaw-channels`: the three capability overrides, the `PacedChannel` forward, Slack's checks before posting, the `inline_attachments` gate in nine channels, and the approval-prompt helper.
  - `zeroclaw-runtime`: the registry passes the limits to the tool.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11996. Related #9993, Related #11992, Related #11990

### What this does, simply

An assistant can now send a file with a message it sends to a known contact, for example "email the client the report", as long as the operator allowed it for that contact. The file has to be one the assistant may read anyway, configuration files are refused by path, sizes are capped, and if anything is wrong nothing is sent at all. Channels that can't carry files are refused up front, not silently dropped. Text the assistant writes in such a message is always sent as text, so a `[FILE:...]` code or a bare path in it can't make the channel upload a file. Every file goes through the checks above.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional. The unit tests cover every gate with a channel stub that records what it was asked to send.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (`email`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** an IMAP+SMTP email channel, a peer group for it with `attachments_enabled = true`, and a PDF in the agent's workspace.
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to send the PDF to that peer with `send_via`. Then ask it to send `config.toml`, and to send the PDF to a peer group without the opt-in.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The PDF arrives as a real attachment. The other two are refused, and nothing is sent.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `send_via` has no way to attach the file. The agent pastes text or says it cannot.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on the five touched crates, and Docs for the two pages.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `markdownlint-cli2` can't run on my machine (no Node); CI's docs job covers it.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                          ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib                                  ok. 1378 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib                                 ok. 1817 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test migration                      ok. 99 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-api --lib                                    ok. 323 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features "channels-full channel-matrix channel-wechat whatsapp-web channel-telegram channel-email"
                                                                    ok. 3815 passed; 0 failed; 6 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::                     ok. 767 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
cargo check -p zeroclaw --tests                                     ok
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-plugins -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings   ok
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps --features "<same as above>" -- -D warnings    ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools   ok
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                             passed
# after the review changes, at 718aed5636
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib                                 ok. 1819 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test migration                      ok. 99 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings     ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-config   ok
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The new tests cover:
  - **`send_via`, success:** delivery through a capable, opted-in channel, with file name, MIME and bytes checked; an empty list sends a plain message.
  - **`send_via`, refusals, with nothing sent in each case:**
    - an incapable channel, and a group that hasn't opted in. Both ask for a missing file, which proves the check runs before any read;
    - the opt-in through the channel-alias target path;
    - routing mode, and a wrong argument type;
    - each of the three limits;
    - the read policy: outside the workspace, `..`, a directory, a symlink pointing outside, and a runtime config file;
  - **`send_via` sends its body with inline attachments off:** `"report [FILE:/x]"`, a tool-tag splice and a bare path all arrive as unchanged text with no attachments.
  - **Each gated channel:** a marker body (and on Telegram and WeChat a bare path or `file://` URL) with the switch off goes out as literal text with no upload, while explicit attachments still go out. Slack and Matrix check this end to end against a mock server.
  - **Approval prompts:** a file marker in a tool argument stays in the prompt text and is not uploaded (Slack end to end, WhatsApp Web through its send hook, Matrix and the shared helper directly).
  - **Schema:** the description shows the configured limits.
  - **The loading helper:** 4 unit tests.
  - **Slack:** more than 8 files, an empty file and an oversized file are each refused before any request reaches the mock server.
  - **Config:** a malformed `[tools.send_via]` value, or a misspelt key such as `max_attachment_byte`, drops that table on its own and keeps the tool selection. The drop counts as degraded security, so the daemon won't start without `--allow-degraded-security`: the defaults can be looser than a tightened limit such as `max_attachments = 0`. The same holds when this table is set and a mistake elsewhere drops the whole `[tools]` table.

  Not verified: a live send through a real mailbox on this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the commands above at `bbbac5a019`, and the `zeroclaw-config` tests, clippy and docs again at `718aed5636` after the review changes. Tool and channel unit tests, and the Slack and Matrix mock servers; no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A, as above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A; the behaviour checks are the tests listed above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `markdownlint-cli2`, because Node isn't installed on my machine; CI's docs job runs it. A live send through a real mailbox wasn't run on this branch.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. A model-called tool can now read files to send them. This is limited to `file_read`'s read policy, with runtime config refused by path (a copy or hard link inside the workspace is not recognised, and `file_read` could read it anyway), a per-group opt-in that is off by default, and size caps. The read is bounded, happens once after the check, and doesn't follow symlinks.
- New external network calls? No. Files go to recipients the agent could already message.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Runtime config files are refused explicitly.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (`example.com` and temp dirs).
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes, and this narrows the risk. An injected instruction can no longer get files out through text in a `send_via` body or in a tool's arguments shown in an approval prompt, and the explicit path is off by default per recipient. #11990 lets an operator remove `send_via` from an untrusted channel's turns entirely.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes, with two changes in behaviour. A `send_via` body is now always sent as text: a file marker or bare path in it is no longer uploaded. And approval prompts show file markers from tool arguments as text instead of uploading them.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Two new optional settings: `attachments_enabled` on peer groups (default `false`), and `[tools.send_via]` with three limits. Existing configs load unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`, or leave `attachments_enabled` off, which is the default.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `attachments_enabled` per peer group.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - A `send_via` refusal naming the channel ("cannot carry attachments"), the peer group ("not enabled"), a limit, or the path.
  - A file marker or path showing as plain text in a `send_via` message or an approval prompt is the intended behaviour.

prs.title: fix(channels): honour a channel instance's excluded_tools
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `ChannelsConfig::excluded_tools_for(channel, alias)` reads the `excluded_tools` list of a channel instance. `channel` is the runtime kind (`voice-call`) or the config key (`voice_call`). It covers every channel type listed by `ChannelsConfig::channels()`. Twitch and plugin channels have no such field and return an empty list; an unknown type returns `None`.
  - In the orchestrator, one helper, `channel_turn_excluded_tools`, computes a turn's excluded tools: the risk profile's list (lifted for CLI turns and `Full` autonomy, exactly as before) plus the list of the instance the message arrived through. Both places that built the per-turn list now use it, so the channel's list reaches the native tool specs, tool execution and the skills section, the same as the profile's.
  - Until now the per-channel setting was documented (channels overview table, security/autonomy.md) and present on every channel config, but nothing read it.
  - The restriction also follows the work a turn starts. It travels with the task (`security::channel_restriction`, modelled on the SOP step scope), and every tool loop merges it into its excluded tools in `run_tool_call_loop_impl`. So a bounded delegate, a sub-agent or an inline `cron_run` launched from a restricted channel can't use what the channel excludes, whatever tool set it assembles. Background and parallel delegation capture it before the spawn and restore it inside.
  - A skill wrapper is excluded with the tool it runs. `Tool::wrapped_tool_name` (a new default method, which the `Arc` wrappers forward) names the tool a wrapper such as a skill's builtin tool runs. The turn's excluded list takes in every wrapper of an excluded tool, so it is neither offered nor listed in the skills section. Dispatch refuses a wrapper whose target is excluded. `SkillBuiltinTool` also refuses before calling a target that the task's channel restriction excludes.
  - Work the restriction can't follow is refused on a channel that sets `excluded_tools`: cron and scheduled jobs, SOP steps, peer and A2A messages, external agent CLIs, and `execute_pipeline`. The new `[channels] restricted_channels_allow_detached_work = true` allows it again.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - The channel's own list applies at every autonomy level, including `Full`. It's an explicit restriction on that channel, not part of the risk profile; autonomy.md now says so.
  - A message that names no instance gets the union of all instances of its type, so it is never less restricted than the strictest instance.
  - The agent's startup prompt tool list is built once per agent and is not per channel, so in text-protocol tool mode an excluded tool can still be described there. It's still neither offered as a native spec nor executable.
  - No change to risk profiles, approvals or peer groups.
- **Blast radius:** channel turns of any agent whose channel instances set `excluded_tools`. Configs that don't set it behave exactly as before.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11989. Related #12113, the holding-crate exception for the runtime part of this fix, which must merge first.

### What this does, simply

Each chat or mail channel has a setting to hide certain tools from the assistant when it answers on that channel, for example "no web requests on the public inbox". The setting was documented but did nothing. Now it works. It adds to the agent's usual restrictions and applies even to an agent that otherwise has full autonomy.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The unit tests cover the lookup across every channel type and the merge used by both per-turn call sites.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-channels`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** On 0ba0a0d50ced28f4ac7d0db9495fbf6a2a164a70, Zerocode RPC Boundary was cancelled during checkout before tests ran, leaving CI Required Gate failed. Lint, Security, Test and Parallel Runtime Test passed; rerun the cancelled job before merge.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                         ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- every_listed_channel_type_answers_excluded_tools channel_excluded_tools_are_read_per_instance
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- a_channel_turn_drops_the_tools a_channel_exclusion_holds assemble_channel_agent_tools excluded
  test result: ok. 12 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings    ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config   ok
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                             passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests:
  - `every_listed_channel_type_answers_excluded_tools`: every kind and config key from `channels()` has a lookup arm, so a new channel type without one fails this test.
  - `channel_excluded_tools_are_read_per_instance`: per-instance lists, an unknown alias, and the union without an alias.
  - `a_channel_turn_drops_the_tools_its_channel_excludes`: profile plus channel list for the right instance only, and not for another channel type.
  - `a_channel_exclusion_holds_at_full_autonomy_and_without_an_alias`.
  - `a_restricted_channel_refuses_detached_work_unless_allowed` and `a_loop_started_from_a_restricted_turn_inherits_the_restriction`.
  - `security::channel_restriction` tests: no restriction outside a channel turn, merge into a loop's exclusions, a captured restriction surviving a spawn.
  - Skill wrappers:
    - `a_channel_exclusion_reaches_through_a_skill_wrapper`: an excluded wrapper's target is never called, while a permitted wrapper's target runs.
    - `execute_one_tool_blocks_a_skill_wrapper_of_an_excluded_tool`
    - `a_channel_exclusion_drops_the_skill_wrappers_of_an_excluded_tool`
    - `wrappers_of_an_excluded_tool_are_excluded_with_it`
  - The existing `delegate`, `spawn_subagent` and SOP scope tests (291 in the filtered runtime run) still pass.

  Not verified: a live channel turn on this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. It only removes tools from channel turns.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. This narrows what a turn from an untrusted channel can do, which is the mitigation the setting was documented to provide.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for configs that don't set the field. A config that already sets per-channel `excluded_tools` now gets the restriction it asked for.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: an existing field starts working, and one new optional key, `[channels] restricted_channels_allow_detached_work` (default `false`).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Rollback: `git revert <sha>`, or remove the per-channel `excluded_tools` entries.

- **Observable failure symptoms:** a tool missing on a channel that should have it would mean a per-channel `excluded_tools` entry is listing it.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** cron run history with final output is retained in `cron_runs.output` and exposed via the gateway API (`/api/cron/runs`), but the CLI offers no way to read it — `cron list` shows status only, so terminal operators and scripts must query the SQLite DB directly.
- Adds `zeroclaw cron runs [--job <id>] [--limit N]` (default 10, clap-validated range 1..=50) printing runs newest-first: `started_at | job prefix | status | duration | output preview` (first line, ≤80 chars).
- Read-only: reuses the runtime cron store API (`list_runs` for `--job`; new `list_recent_runs` for the unfiltered view). No changes to retention, scheduling, delivery, or the gateway endpoint.
- Added strings in all five locale catalogs (`cli-cron-runs-header`, `cli-cron-runs-none`); runtime falls back to English where a catalog lacks a key.
- **Scope boundary:** no new write paths, no schema/migration changes, no gateway surface changes.
- **Blast radius:** additive CLI surface only.
- **Linked issues:** none.

### What this does, simply

When a scheduled job finishes, ZeroClaw keeps its final output in the cron database and the web dashboard can show it — but from a terminal there was no command to see "what did the 06:10 job actually answer". This adds `zeroclaw cron runs`, the missing read side of the cron store for CLI operators.

## Testing (required)

Not verified: end-to-end run against a live daemon DB (source-only change; behavior follows the same store path as the existing gateway endpoint).
- **Visual interface evidence:** exact plain-text output (noninteractive, unstyled CLI text):
  ```
  🕒 Recent cron runs (3):
  - 2026-10-19T08:30:00+00:00 | a1b2c3d4 | ok | 1520ms | Backup completed successfully
  ```

prs.title: fix(runtime): enforce the system prompt size budget (fail closed)
prs.body:
Fixes #11908.

## What

The `max_system_prompt_chars` runtime-profile limit was advisory only. This makes it a hard gate and removes the unlimited default:

- **Fail closed in the turn gate** (`turn/mod.rs`): when the assembled system-prompt floor reaches/exceeds the context budget, the turn returns a typed `SystemPromptFloorExceedsBudget` error **before dispatch** — the over-budget request no longer reaches the provider. The historical WARN keeps its `error_key: context_floor_exceeds_budget` so existing trace dashboards still match.
- **Finite safe default** (`schema.rs`): `default_max_system_prompt_chars()` 0 → 50000. An explicit `= 0` in a profile keeps opt-in unlimited.
- **Workspace bootstrap respects the cap** for `compact_context = false` sessions (oversized-bootstrap regression test: 5×200K files under a 50000 cap).

## What this is NOT

The budget is resolved atomically with the rest of the profile from one generation-stamped config snapshot (`resolved_agent_config`), and the new gate measures the provider-bound request — the suspected snapshot-race and history-vs-request divergence paths were inspected and do not reproduce as independent defects; the gate now rejects any such bypass regardless.

## Tests

New regression tests (prefix `prompt_budget_cap_`): gate trip conditions, typed+localized refusal, capped workspace bootstrap with `compact_context = false`, finite schema default.

## Notes for reviewers

- Behavior change: a turn that would previously dispatch with a flooded system prompt now fails with a clear, localized error. Operators see the remediation text instead of a silent confabulated reply.
- `turn/mod.rs`/`outcome.rs` touched — happy to add the ADR-016 exception row if required (per #11578/#11625 precedent).
