prs.title: fix(channels): classify telegram transcription failures and bound transient retries
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Every error from `manager.transcribe` in the Telegram voice path became `UpdateDisposition::RetryTransient`, so a terminally rejected voice update pinned the long-poll offset and head-of-line blocked every later message until an operator intervened (#10863; production incident reported in #10640, where an ASR endpoint's persistent HTTP 413 wedged the channel for ~8 minutes and survived restarts).
  - Transcription providers now classify failures: substantiated payload-specific terminal rejections (HTTP 413/415, plus local pre-flight byte-cap and format rejections) are `Permanent`; credential (401/403), rate-limit, 5xx, transport, and unrecognised failures stay `Transient` — the same conservative philosophy as the `getFile` classifier (#9314/#9315): retrying a recoverable failure is safe, skipping a recoverable one loses a message.
  - The Telegram voice parser acknowledges terminal rejections with a new sender notice (`VoiceDropReason::TranscriptionRejected`, Fluent key added in en/es/fr/ja/zh-CN) instead of retrying forever — the same contract as the existing duration and file-lookup drops.
  - A bounded transient budget applies only to voice/audio updates. After 10 consecutive failures, the channel attempts a bounded resend notice, logs the update id and attempt count, and acknowledges the update so later messages can progress. There is no automatic replay. If the notice fails or times out, the recording can be skipped without the sender receiving a notice; recovery is to resend the Telegram recording after the service recovers or send text. Photo/document attachments retain transient retries beyond this budget.
- Deepgram, AssemblyAI (upload step), and Google STT now check `!status.is_success()` before JSON deserialization, so a proxy/gateway 413/415 with a plain-text or HTML body classifies as `Permanent` instead of falling into an untyped JSON-parse failure (misread as retryable `Transient`). Error bodies are read as text, extracting the vendor JSON message when present. AssemblyAI `create`/`poll` carry no audio bytes, so their non-success statuses stay explicitly `Transient` instead of masquerading as a payload rejection.
- **Scope boundary:** media-group batch retry machinery unchanged; `getFile`/download classification unchanged; other channels' transcription call sites unchanged (they do not acknowledge vendor offsets); no config, CLI, or schema changes; `TranscriptionProvider` trait signature unchanged (classification rides inside the `anyhow` chain).
- **Blast radius:** Telegram channel update-disposition path (voice parse + single-update retry gate); transcription error construction sites in `zeroclaw-channels/src/transcription.rs`; two new Fluent keys in runtime locale catalogs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10863. Related #10640, #9314, #9315.

### What this does, simply

When someone sends a voice note, the Telegram channel downloads the audio and hands it to a transcription endpoint. If that call fails, the channel used to retry the update forever — including failures that could never succeed, like the endpoint rejecting the recording as too long. Because Telegram redelivers unacknowledged updates first, one poisoned voice note blocked every message behind it, for every chat of the bot, and restarts did not help.

This PR makes the failure handling distinguish two cases. If the endpoint rejected *this recording* (too large, unsupported format), retrying is pointless: the channel now tells the sender why their voice note was dropped and moves on — the same way it already handles over-duration recordings and expired files. If the failure might recover (endpoint down, rate limit, bad credentials awaiting an operator fix), the update is still retried as before. After ten consecutive voice/audio failures, the channel attempts a bounded resend notice, logs the failure and acknowledges the update. The recording remains in Telegram, but the bot does not replay it automatically. The sender can resend it after recovery or send text. A failed or timed-out notice can leave the sender unaware that the bot skipped the recording. This limit counts failed attempts, not elapsed time.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the behavior boundary is covered by new wiremock-driven listener tests that replay the production incident shape (persistent 413) and the recovery shape (500 then 200); no manual Telegram setup adds signal beyond them.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `telegram` (voice transcription path)
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

New focused tests, all at the real behavior boundary:

- `listen_terminally_rejected_transcription_does_not_block_later_updates` — the incident replay: voice update, ASR endpoint consistently answers 413 `audio duration exceeds limit`; the voice update is acknowledged with exactly one sender notice, and the text update behind it is delivered with the offset advancing past both.
- `listen_recoverable_transcription_failure_retries_and_delivers` — 500 once, then 200: the same update is retried at the same offset and delivered as `[Voice] recovered words`.
- `process_update_acknowledges_update_after_transient_budget_exhausted` — the transient budget gate: an update at the attempt cap is acknowledged with no further I/O; below the cap or for a different update id, routing is unchanged.
- `try_parse_voice_message_terminally_rejected_transcription_notifies_sender` — the sender notice carries the new dedicated wording to the right chat.
- `transcription.rs` unit tests: status classification (only 413/415 permanent; 400/401/403/408/409/422/425/429/451/5xx transient), local validation rejections classified permanent, `failure_kind` recovery through `anyhow` context layers and its transient default, and a wiremock pass over the Groq provider proving 413 → permanent while 500/429 → transient.
- Provider-path regressions (wiremock, added with the review fix): `deepgram_non_json_413_is_classified_permanent` (HTML 413 body → `Permanent`; vendor-JSON 413 keeps the readable message), `assemblyai_upload_413_is_permanent_but_metadata_413_stays_transient` (upload-step 413 → `Permanent`; create-step 413 → `Transient`), `google_stt_non_json_413_is_classified_permanent`.

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** workspace `fmt` / `clippy` / test jobs cover `zeroclaw-channels` and the locale catalogs; the new tests run in the standard channels suite.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** 5 `link_enricher` tests fail in this Windows/localhost/VPN environment — pre-existing on clean `master` (localhost networking restriction), unrelated to this diff. CI (Linux) is expected green.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean (after one `cargo fmt --all` normalization pass over the new tests).
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` → `Finished dev profile` (no lints in the crate; `--no-deps` because path-dependency `zeroclaw-config` trips pre-existing Windows-only `collapsible_if` lints on this host that Linux CI never compiles).
  - `cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram` → `test result: FAILED. 1958 passed; 5 failed` — the 5 failures are the pre-existing `link_enricher` localhost cases above; every telegram/transcription test passes.

  - `cargo fluent check` → all catalogs `ok`, including the 5 edited `cli.ftl` files.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The classification mirrors the existing `FileLookupError::classify` philosophy and the voice-drop notice plumbing (`notify_voice_drop`, bounded notice timeout) is shared with the three existing drop reasons. Not verified: a live Telegram bot end-to-end run (covered instead by the wiremock listener tests at the same boundary the existing offset tests use).

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(channels): Gemini speech-to-speech broker channel (PR1: daemon-side core)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** PR1 of the accepted Gemini speech-to-speech broker
  RFC (#8780, tracker #10406). Adds a feature-gated `speech_to_speech` channel
  where a realtime voice model (Gemini Live) owns the caller audio and reaches
  the ZeroClaw agent through exactly one bridge function, `consult_agent`
  (+ `end_session`) — the voice model never sees tools; only the agent does.
  Vendors a small MIT `gemini-live` crate for the wire protocol. Adds config
  surface (`channels.speech_to_speech.<alias>`), broker-persona resolution
  confined to the agent workspace, consult-history binding, and a startup
  retention/cost privacy warning.
- **Scope boundary:** No audio-frame transport (mic in / speaker out) yet — the
  channel ships its session engine and config surface and stays inert (parks
  until cancelled) until the transport lands in a follow-up PR. No changes to
  existing channels, the tool pipeline, or provider wiring.
- **Blast radius:** Off by default (`channel-speech-to-speech` cargo feature).
  When the feature is off, nothing compiles in. Touches `zeroclaw-channels`,
  `zeroclaw-config` (new optional section + one warning), `zeroclaw-api`
  (`ChannelKind::SpeechToSpeech`), and adds the vendored `gemini-live` crate.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8780, Related #10406.

### What this does, simply

A phone call is answered by a voice model, not by the agent. It chats with the
caller and, whenever something needs the agent, passes the question through one
bridge function and speaks the answer back in its own words. The agent's tools
stay out of the voice model's reach entirely.


- **Review rounds addressed (refreshed onto current master).** The branch was
  re-applied on top of master; the conflicts were content conflicts
  (workspace members, the config warning collector, the generated feature
  lists) and were resolved keeping master's side plus this branch's addition.
  The blocking findings are answered as follows.
  - *Control messages lost on reconnect.* Every `ClientText` and
    `ToolResponse` now carries a receipt the transport driver resolves to
    `Written`, `Discarded` or `Failed`: written once the transport accepts the
    frame, discarded when the command is dropped in the backoff window, failed
    when the transport refuses the write. Commands queued during reconnect and
    setup stay queued and are written after the reopen, so nothing is replayed
    twice. `Channel::send` waits for that verdict (bounded) and reports a lost
    reply as a delivery failure instead of a silent success; no backlog is
    re-sent behind the caller's back, and an older turn completion no longer
    retires a newer reply because there is no shared pending list to clear.
    A tool acknowledgement has no caller to answer, so a discarded or refused
    one is logged with its call id and listed again when the call ends.
    Exactly-once across a broken connection is not attempted.
  - *A timed-out reply written late.* The queued command and its receipt now
    share one claim. When `send()` runs out of time it expires the receipt:
    a reply the driver has not started writing is withdrawn (the driver skips
    it when it reaches it), so a reply reported undelivered is never spoken
    after the agent has answered again; a write already in progress cannot be
    withdrawn and is reported as undecided, not as a confirmed failure.
    Teardown gives the acknowledgements still undecided the same budget before
    counting any of them lost: the session handle is released so the driver
    drains, the verdicts are awaited up to the deadline, and only an
    acknowledgement the driver never started is reported as unanswered.
  - *History and delayed replies.* Every attached call mints its own identity
    and carries it in `sender` and `reply_target`, so two calls on one alias no
    longer share a conversation history. The orchestrator echoes that address
    back as `SendMessage::recipient`, and a reply naming a call that has ended
    is dropped with a log instead of being spoken to whoever is on the line.
  - *Staged outbound surfaces.* Both spellings are declared in the one-shot and
    announcement intentional-unsupported dispositions, so the feature-enabled
    registration guards pass without new outbound functionality.
  - *SOP identity.* `ChannelKind::VoiceBroker` is renamed to `SpeechToSpeech`,
    so configuration, inbound topics (`speech_to_speech/<alias>`), attribution
    and discovery all use one token; the sender label follows the same name. A
    configured alias now appears in the trigger projection with its setup path,
    covered by a new registry test.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the channel has no audio transport
  yet, so there is no end-to-end caller flow to exercise; behavior is covered
  by unit tests on setup assembly, the security tool-set invariant, persona
  confinement, history binding, and the parked-listen contract.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Historical test evidence for `00bad6402b1e6e209862ba37b7d05d0f5fa7cefc` is preserved in the [fork run](https://github.com/metalmon/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39140694835). The [November 2 repair return](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10430#issuecomment-6566441271) reports the feature-enabled cancellation, queue-deadline and in-flight tests for the subsequent repair; the [follow-up](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10430#issuecomment-6573205020) identifies the current `b39a388dc7da7499caa091e62208cac8b540ef00` head and manifest/doc fixes. At review refresh on November 4 UTC, the only reported failing check is the alpine amd64 Source Image Build. Its job log was unavailable to the reviewer, so the older arm64/OOM and prefetch diagnoses are not asserted for this current failure. Workspace tests use the local vendored dependency; registry package compatibility requires a separate repair.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live audio round trip was run; audio transport remains deferred. The lifecycle follow-ups the last round listed as nonblocking (an awaited queue send delaying `stop()`, cancellation of `run_session` skipping detachment, `goAway` after a successful connection counting toward the reconnect budget) are not addressed here and are carried into the audio-transport PR.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo test -p gemini-live                                   # 45 passed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-speech-to-speech --lib speech_to_speech
```

- **Tests added for this round:**
  - `an_expired_control_is_never_written_and_an_in_flight_one_says_so`
    (`gemini-live`) — with the transport stalled on one write, expiring the
    queued control reports `Unwritten` and the driver skips it once the stall
    lifts, while expiring the stalled one reports `InFlight`; `FakeTransport`
    gained `stall_writes_after` so a hanging write is actually exercised.
  - `a_reply_that_expires_during_the_reconnect_is_never_written_after_the_reopen`
    — the gated reconnect outlasts `CONTROL_ACK_TIMEOUT`; `send()` reports the
    reply undelivered, and after the reopen the reply never reaches the new
    connection.
  - `a_reply_whose_write_is_still_in_progress_is_reported_as_unknown_not_lost`
    — a write the transport has taken and not completed is reported as
    undecided, not withdrawn.
  - `model_end_session_closes` now asserts the final acknowledgement is on the
    wire before `run_session` returns, which is the bounded teardown settle.
  - `a_written_control_reports_written_and_a_refused_one_reports_failed`
    (`gemini-live`, previous round) — the receipt resolves to `Written` when the transport
    accepts the frame and to `Failed` when it refuses it; `FakeTransport`
    gained `fail_writes_after` so a refused write is actually exercised rather
    than ending through the idle timeout.
  - `a_reply_enqueued_while_the_driver_reconnects_is_written_once_after_the_reopen`
    — a reply queued during connect/setup reaches the reopened connection
    exactly once; a control dropped in the backoff window reports `Discarded`
    and is not replayed.
  - `an_earlier_turn_completion_does_not_cancel_a_newer_reply` — a buffered
    `TurnComplete` from the previous turn does not affect a reply queued after
    it.
  - `a_reply_the_provider_refuses_is_reported_as_a_failure` — `send()` returns
    an error naming the refusal instead of `Ok`.
  - `an_acknowledgement_that_is_never_written_is_reported_with_its_call_id` —
    a tool acknowledgement discarded with the dead connection shows up in the
    call's unanswered-tool-call report under its id.
  - `a_reply_for_an_ended_call_is_not_spoken_into_the_next_one` and
    `speech_to_speech_alias_projects_under_its_ingress_identity` carry over
    from the previous round.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The setup builder emits exactly `{consult_agent, end_session}` in `setup.tools[]` (security invariant test); the broker persona path is resolved relative to and confined to the agent workspace and never falls back to `AGENTS.md`; `listen()` parks until cancelled rather than returning `Ok(())` immediately; the configured `model` id is threaded onto the wire via `SetupConfig.model_id_override` without the crate guessing api-version compatibility (Gemini rejects an incompatible combo itself). Reconnect: a `sessionResumptionUpdate` with `resumable: false` now clears the stored handle so a stale handle is never replayed; the crate discards commands during backoff and emits `SessionOpened { is_reconnect, resumed }`. Not verified: live audio round-trip (no transport yet).
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes** — reads a
  broker persona file, resolved relative to and hard-confined within the agent
  workspace (path canonicalized and checked to stay under the workspace root);
  it never reads `AGENTS.md` or escapes the workspace.
- New external network calls? **Yes** — the session API opens a connection to a fixed `wss://` Gemini Live endpoint. The configured channel listener remains inert in this slice, so enabling an alias does not yet open that session. The separately exported raw `connect_ws` helper accepts a supplied URL and does not enforce `wss://` on its direct, no-proxy branch.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes** — adds a channel-local `api_key: Option<String>` field marked `#[secret]` and `x-secret`. This slice does not yet wire that key into a live session; production credential resolution is deferred with the listener integration. It does not currently resolve an existing Gemini provider profile.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?
  **No**.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes,
  bounded** — the voice model can only reach the agent through `consult_agent`;
  it never receives tool schemas or results, so a compromised/confused voice
  turn cannot invoke tools. Caller audio flows to the provider; a startup
  warning (`speech_to_speech_provider_retention`) discloses provider retention
  and that enabled transcription is billed as text tokens on top of audio.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — new optional config section; absent config and
  the default build are unaffected (feature off by default).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes** — adds
  `[channels.speech_to_speech.<alias>]` (all fields optional with defaults).
  No env or CLI changes.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No** — vendored crate is edition 2021;
  workspace crates stay edition 2024 on the existing floor.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge-sha>`; or simply build
  without `--features channel-speech-to-speech` — the channel is off by default.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `channel-speech-to-speech` cargo feature
  (off by default); per-alias `enabled = false`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** startup warning
  `speech_to_speech_provider_retention` per enabled alias; a live session logs a
  `wss://` connect. With the feature off, no code path is reachable.

prs.title: fix(tools): per-agent ownership scoping for session tools and discord_search
prs.body:
## Summary

### What this does, simply

Each agent can only list, read, and write its own conversations, and only search the Discord archive rows its own Discord bots recorded. Which conversations are "its own" comes from trusted facts (who the runtime is, which channels the live config assigns to it, and what the storage layer recorded when the conversation was created), never from what the model asks for. Conversations recorded before this release had no owner stamp; the one agent that could have written them adopts them on the next message, and an install with several agents is told how to assign them instead of losing messages.

- **Base branch:** `master`; this head includes `master` through `3c18211b9f` (#11811).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Binds `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `sessions_send`, and `discord_search` to trusted per-agent ownership. Ownership is checked inside the storage critical section of each read and write, so a check/use race cannot admit a foreign session, and Discord namespace predicates run inside SQLite before ranking and limits.
  - Routing a message to an agent is not permission to take over a transcript. The inbound path *claims* a session: an absent key is created, an explicitly or channel-owned key is admitted only for its owner, and a foreign key refuses the turn before any hydration or append.
  - Authority is resolved at effect time, not captured ahead of storage. `ChannelAuthority` and `NamespaceAuthority` are callbacks the backend invokes after acquiring its connection or mutation guard; the policy read guard is held through the read or commit, so a channel reassigned or an agent disabled during a wait stops being admitted on the same turn.
  - Transcripts written before ownership attribution existed (master stamped nothing on the channel path, so every existing channel conversation is one) are handled by the claim itself. The live policy reader hands the backend a `SessionClaimGrant`: the channels the agent owns plus `adopt_unattributed`, which is true only when the caller is the sole enabled agent (`Config::is_sole_enabled_agent`, the same rule the Discord archive already applied to legacy rows). A sole agent adopts such a transcript and continues the conversation with its history. With several enabled agents the claim refuses, nothing is read or written, and the refusal is logged as `session_owner_unattributed` with the enabled-agent count and the operator remedy. The adoption bit never widens an explicit agent or a channel the caller does not own.
  - Makes typed live config the single agent/channel ownership source. Disabled aliases grant nothing; ambiguous duplicate enabled owners fail closed. The alias view is a typed walk of the channel maps (`map_alias_entries()` from the `Configurable` derive), so resolving ownership never serializes config on a caller's stack.
  - Preserves trusted session attribution across SQLite and JSONL restart, migration, retention, purge, and empty-transcript cases. Startup hydration touches only channel-marked sessions, so gateway and RPC sessions keep their owners.
  - Enforces Discord alias/channel provenance on search and on every archive write; a row already claimed by another alias or channel is never moved.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change `sessions_current`, `send_via`, peer-group semantics, the knowledge graph, or dormant session-tool registration. It adds no CLI; the explicit adoption step for multi-agent installs is a documented manual edit until a migration command lands (see Compatibility and Merge order).
- **Blast radius:** Per-agent tool registration, channel routing/collection, both session backends and hygiene, Discord archive/search/mutation paths, SQLite memory mutations, the `Configurable` derive's generated surface, and affected Fluent tool descriptions.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #9646. Related #9647. Related #8290.

The authorization inputs remain trusted runtime/config identity plus persisted provenance. Model-supplied session IDs and Discord channel IDs are selectors, never grants. A single-agent install, legacy or not, stays deterministic: it owns everything it wrote before and after the upgrade. Duplicate enabled owners are configuration ambiguity and are rejected.

### Review history on this head

- @JordanTheJet's 2026-09-30 blockers (F1 foreign claim of a channel-owned legacy transcript, F3 disabled caller inheriting the legacy Discord archive, F5 grants resolved before storage admission) were fixed in `040046750`, `344b610be`, `a6557147a`, and `0119cfe64` (now `e593ce5b7a`, `27063a7749`, `ba0d69c848`, and `5677f53b3e` after the history rewrite below); @tidux confirmed each on 2026-10-01.
- @tidux's 2026-10-01 blocker (pre-upgrade transcripts without attribution permanently drop their next inbound message) is fixed by the legacy adoption described above, with upgrade regressions on both backends.
- @tidux's `try_read` contention warning no longer applies after the master merge: the live config is now a `LiveConfigHandle` whose publish path holds its write lock only for the pair install and never across storage, so the authority callbacks take a short blocking `read()` instead of dropping the turn when a writer is queued. There is no longer an "authority unavailable" path on the inbound claim.
- The `.gitignore` entry @tidux flagged has been removed from this branch's diff.
- History was force-pushed once on 2026-10-23 to replace the merge commit `a6744b2b56`, which was authored as Claude with an attribution trailer and a session URL (AGENTS.md working rule 9), with the tree-identical `679755cf88` under my identity. Every descendant was re-created with its tree, message, author, and dates unchanged and only its parent re-pointed, so every SHA from that merge on moved; `git diff 6f0fdccc3b d1d9d03d27` is empty. The reviewed head `0119cfe64f` is now `5677f53b3e`, and the three commits on top are `9cc1a14780` (drift-only master merge), `fbbac6880e` (the fix), and `d1d9d03d27` (`.gitignore` chore).

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; the deterministic regressions exercise the security, retention, and upgrade boundaries without credentials.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` tool registration and `channel` persistence/search.
- **Setup / preconditions:** None for automated tests. A manual Discord A/B needs two neutral agents with distinct enabled, archive-enabled Discord aliases that both watch one channel. A manual upgrade check needs a `data/sessions` directory written by a pre-ownership release (any channel transcript without `agent_alias`).
- **Steps to run:** Run the session ownership, retention, and upgrade tests. For the upgrade path by hand: start a build of this branch with one enabled agent over an old sessions directory and send a message on an existing conversation (the reply uses the old history and `agent_alias` is now set); then enable a second agent and send a message on a different old conversation (no reply, one `session_owner_unattributed` error with the remedy, transcript unchanged). For Discord: let the first alias archive a message and a reaction from the shared channel, let the second alias observe the same two events, and run scoped `discord_search` as each agent.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Foreign sessions and Discord rows remain inaccessible; a sole enabled agent continues pre-upgrade conversations and adopts them; a multi-agent install refuses them with a logged remedy instead of silently dropping them; the owned Discord row stays in the first alias's namespace; archived JSONL sessions cannot reappear through metadata; ambiguous duplicate channel owners expose no scoped grant.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Session tools and the shared Discord archive lacked a complete per-agent boundary, JSONL ownership metadata could outlive retention, and the second observer's archive write took over the first alias's row.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Hosted CI covers the repository matrix (strict lint, workspace tests, Landlock, security, supported targets, MSRV, and the parallel runtime/channel gate). The previous head `0119cfe64f` had `CI Required Gate` green but was reviewed as 7 commits behind master and later became CONFLICTING; this head merges current master (`3c18211b9f`) so the PR runs against the base it would land on. Hosted CI on this head: `Quality Gate` run [40047833401](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40047833401) started on the push of `640f1c3c47` and was in progress when this body was written. The previous run 40042714043 on `d1d9d03d27` failed on two things: master's `every_inventoried_tool_registers_under_a_maximal_config` (the maximal config inserted its archiving Discord alias with `enabled` off, so under the ownership-gated registration the sole agent owned nothing and `discord_search` never registered; fixed in `640f1c3c47` by enabling the alias), and the `Security` job, which is the repo-wide RUSTSEC-2026-0385/0386 advisory affecting every PR until the dependency bump lands on master. GitHub reports the PR as mergeable again. The four commits on top of `5677f53b3e` (formerly `0119cfe64f`) are the drift-only master merge `9cc1a14780` (checked standalone: `cargo check --locked` on the five touched crates with all targets, 0 errors, 0 warnings), the fix `fbbac6880e`, `d1d9d03d27`, which drops the `.gitignore` patterns, and the test fix `640f1c3c47`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live two-bot Discord deployment and no real pre-upgrade data directory; both are covered deterministically (the upgrade regressions seed exactly what master writes: a SQLite metadata row with NULL agent and channel, and a JSONL transcript with no sidecar). `cargo fluent check` and `cargo deny` were not run locally.
- **Commands run and tail output** (aarch64 macOS, `rustc 1.97.1`, at `d1d9d03d27` (tree-identical to the pre-rewrite `6f0fdccc3b` the commands ran on) plus the inventory test re-run at `640f1c3c47`, dedicated target dir, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`):

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all --check
    -> clean

Confirmed `Config::is_sole_enabled_agent` returns the same answer as the inline count it replaces in the Discord archive grant, including for an empty agent map. I did not exercise a real Discord account or a real pre-upgrade install.

- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `./dev/ci.sh all`, `cargo fluent check`, and live Discord were not run locally. The changed Fluent catalogues are unchanged since the previously green exact-head run, and the remaining external gap would require credentials.

**Historical evidence (previous heads).** Exact-head `CI Required Gate` was green at `0119cfe64f` (run on 2026-09-30) and at `c1c14d91f9` (run 34549879212). Exact-head [run 34189025680](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34189025680) covered `6cef56af45` and exact-head [Quality Gate run 33805478225](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/33805478225) was fully green at `a6744b2b56`. None of those runs covers the master merge or the legacy adoption on the current head. Those SHAs predate the 2026-10-23 history rewrite; their trees are unchanged under the new SHAs listed in Review history.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**; access is narrowed. The only widening is the legacy adoption, and it is available to exactly one principal: the single enabled agent of a single-agent install, for transcripts that agent is the only possible author of.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**; the channel alias view no longer serializes any config section at all, so the transient copy it used to make of decrypted channel values is gone.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Static tool descriptions are model-visible Fluent strings. The ownership denial messages (`denial_message` in `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/sessions.rs`) are `format!` literals, following master's existing tool-error convention; the earlier claim that Fluent owns them was wrong. Denials name the owning agent or channel, matching the shipped reset/delete tools. Authorization comes only from trusted runtime identity, live config, and persisted provenance, never model arguments. The new `session_owner_unattributed` log line and its remedy are operator-facing log text, not model-visible.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No**; vulnerable cross-agent access and ambiguous ownership are intentionally denied.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`:
  - Existing attributed SQLite and JSONL sessions need no action.
  - **Pre-upgrade channel transcripts (no `agent_alias`, no `channel_id`; every channel conversation master wrote):** in an install with exactly one enabled agent, nothing to do; the agent adopts each conversation on its next inbound message and continues with the history. In an install with several enabled agents, those conversations are refused until attributed, and each refused message logs `session_owner_unattributed` with the remedy. To attribute one, with the daemon stopped: SQLite, `UPDATE session_metadata SET agent_alias = '<alias>' WHERE session_key = '<key>';` in `data/sessions/sessions.db`; JSONL, write `{"agent_alias": "<alias>"}` to the transcript's `.metadata.json` sidecar in `data/sessions/`. Archiving or deleting the transcript is the other option; the next message then starts a fresh, attributed conversation. The docs page `runtime-state-and-persistence.md` has the same steps under "Legacy session attribution".
  - Ambiguously owned data (two enabled agents bound to one channel) stays fail-closed; restore a unique enabled channel binding.
  - Scoped `sessions_send` no longer creates an unknown session key; establish the session through its owning runtime first. `sessions_list` and `discord_search` enforce the profile's `Read` operation, so restrictive profiles must permit it.
  - Where two enabled Discord aliases watch the same channel, the alias that archives an event first keeps the row and the later observer no longer replaces it.

## Merge order with the overlapping session-backend PRs (proposed)

Several open PRs add authority contracts to `SessionBackend`. Proposed order, so the backend ends up with one claim contract and one effect-time authority shape:

1. **This PR first.** It defines `SessionClaimGrant` / `SessionClaimAuthority` for the inbound claim and `ChannelAuthority` / `NamespaceAuthority` for effect-time reads and writes.
2. **#10412 (@REL-mame)** rebases its `claim_session_agent_alias` / `adopt_session_agent_alias` onto this PR's `SessionOwnerClaim` and `SessionClaimGrant`; its `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership` adopt operation then becomes the command this PR's `session_owner_unattributed` remedy points operators at, replacing the manual edit above.
3. **#11230 (mine)** rebases onto this PR and updates its guard test to the `SessionsListTool::for_agent(backend, security, scope)` constructor; principal scoping and agent/channel scoping compose.
4. **#11234 (mine)** adopts the effect-time callback shape from this PR instead of a parallel `SessionEffectGuard` contract.
5. **#11301 (mine)** and **#10407 (@vrurg)** resolve their `session_sqlite.rs` (and, for #10407, `sessions.rs` / `tools/mod.rs`) textual overlaps at rebase; neither changes the ownership contract.

#11205 is closed. If maintainers prefer #10412's contract to land first, this PR will rebase onto it instead; the adoption rule and the regressions here transfer either way.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the eventual PR landing commit from current `master`; no schema down-migration is required. Transcripts adopted by a sole agent keep their `agent_alias`, which the previous release ignores.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Disabling the affected channel/tool is the immediate containment option.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unexpected ownership-denial errors, a missing scoped tool for a uniquely configured owner, empty owned Discord results, channel startup errors reporting ambiguous enabled owners, repeated `session_owner_unattributed` errors in a multi-agent install (expected until the legacy transcripts are attributed), or `discord archive row belongs to another alias or channel; not overwritten` debug events for rows an operator expects a given alias to own.

**Earlier validation head:** `640f1c3c47`

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(providers): add Opper model provider
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add a typed provider slot `opper` for Opper, an EU-hosted, OpenAI-compatible AI gateway. Operators select it by name, and ZeroClaw fills in the endpoint and bearer auth.
  - The endpoint lives in one constant, `OpperEndpoint::DEFAULT_URI`. The factory's `DEFAULT_URL` reads it, and a test guards the pair.
  - Opper is already on models.dev as `opper`, so the slot sets `MODELS_DEV_KEY = "opper"`. The model picker lists Opper models before a key is set, through the existing models.dev path. With a key, the shared client reads the live `/models`.
  - The API key comes only from the typed alias. A test checks that the constructor does not read `OPPER_API_KEY`.
- **Scope boundary:** No new client implementation, no `ModelProviderKind` variant, no context-window discovery, no alias shims, no `wire_api` handling. Other providers and existing configs do not change.
- **Blast radius:** The provider registry, the config schema (a new `providers.models.opper` map), the catalog source table, the generated "All slots" table and the provider list. The slot is inactive unless an operator configures it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11583. Related #8396.

### What this does, simply

Before this PR, an Opper user had to write a `custom` provider with the URL. Opper did not show in the provider list, and the model picker stayed empty until a key was pasted.

This PR adds a named `opper` slot. The operator sets `model` and `api_key`. ZeroClaw then sends Chat Completions requests to `https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat`. Model ids are bare names such as `claude-sonnet-4-6`, and Opper picks the route for each request. The slot is for chat only.

### Why a first-class family (not `providers.models.custom`)

- **Model list before a key is set.** Opper is already listed on models.dev as `opper`. The slot reuses the existing models.dev catalog path, as `vercel` and `synthetic` do. A `custom` alias has no catalog source, so its picker stays empty until a key is pasted.
- **Maintained defaults.** The endpoint and bearer auth come from one constant, so operators cannot mistype the base URL. The `/v3/compat` path is easy to get wrong by hand.
- **Discoverability.** Opper shows in the provider list and in the generated catalog next to the other gateways.
- **No new client code.** The slot is data on the shared OpenAI-compatible client. The intake decision is in #11583.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. You need an Opper key from https://platform.opper.ai.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:**

  ```toml
  schema_version = 3

  [providers.models.opper.default]
  model = "claude-sonnet-4-6"
  api_key = "..."

  [agents.opper]
  model_provider = "opper.default"
  risk_profile = "default"

  [risk_profiles.default]
  level = "supervised"
  ```

- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw models refresh --model-provider opper.default`
  2. `zeroclaw agent -a opper -m "hello"`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The model list loads and the agent replies. Without `api_key`, step 1 lists the models.dev `opper` catalog.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `opper` is not a known provider slot, so `model_provider = "opper.default"` does not resolve and config validation fails.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Format`, `Check`, `Test` and clippy cover both changed crates. That includes the slot coverage tests `every_canonical_family_has_a_catalog_table_entry` and `listed_model_providers_match_canonical_slots`, and the 9 new tests. `Docs Style` covers `catalog.md`.
- **Mock request coverage (added in b488e30a5):** `opper_factory_sends_bearer_and_model_ids_to_compat_endpoint` in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/factory.rs` points the Opper provider at a local mock server under `/v3/compat`. It asserts that chat requests go to `/v3/compat/chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, that the pool name `claude-sonnet-4-6` and the pinned id `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` are sent unchanged, and that the model list goes to `/v3/compat/models` with the same header and returns both ids.
- **CI result on b488e30a5:** run 37914489616 concluded success with no failed jobs, including Format, Lint and Test, and the Test log shows the new test passing.
- **Live smoke from #11583 (run 2026-10-30):** tested commit `b488e30a5` (`zeroclaw 0.8.5 (b488e30)`), release build with rustc 1.98.0 on Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 (a GitHub Actions runner), the config above with a real Opper key in `api_key`, `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR` pointing at it. Sanitized output:

  ```text
  $ zeroclaw models refresh --model-provider opper.default
    [opper.default]
      ✅ 1250 models
    Summary: 1 ok, 0 skipped, 0 auth/access, 0 errors
    opper.default      ok           1250     catalog fetched

  $ zeroclaw agent -a opper -m "hello"
  Hello! How can I help you today?
  ```

  1250 is the live `GET /v3/compat/models` list with the key. Without a key the same command lists the 55-model models.dev catalog.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI makes no live provider request; the live smoke above covers that once.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```sh
  git diff --check origin/master HEAD
  # exited 0, no output

  curl -s https://models.dev/api.json | jq -c '.opper | {id, api, env, models: (.models | length), has_default: (.models | has("claude-sonnet-4-6"))}'
  # {"id":"opper","api":"https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat","env":["OPPER_API_KEY"],"models":57,"has_default":true}

  curl -s "https://api.opper.ai/v3/models?limit=2000" | jq -c '[.models[] | select(.model == "claude-sonnet-4-6" and .pooled == true and .type == "llm")] | length'
  # 5
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The models.dev `opper` entry and the model id used in the tests and docs, shown above. The live chat and keyed model list are covered by the smoke above.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No rendered interface changes. The new provider list entry is data from `list_model_providers()`.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I did not run `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy` or `cargo test` locally, because this machine has no Rust toolchain. This PR relies on required CI for them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `Yes`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Only when an operator configures `providers.models.opper`, ZeroClaw sends requests to `https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat` through the shared OpenAI-compatible client. The keyless model list uses the existing models.dev fetch. Credentials stay on the typed alias `api_key` or the `ZEROCLAW_*` schema-mirror override.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: This adds the `providers.models.opper.<alias>` slot. It is additive. `ModelProviders` is a public exhaustive struct, so a downstream struct literal needs `..ModelProviders::default()` for the new `opper` field. Existing `custom` configs keep working. To move to the typed slot, create `[providers.models.opper.<alias>]`, set `model`, and set `api_key` directly or bridge it with `ZEROCLAW_providers__models__opper__<alias>__api_key="$OPPER_API_KEY"`. `opper-ai` and `opper_ai` are not runtime aliases.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` this commit, or remove the `opper` slot from `providers.rs`, `schema.rs`, `factory.rs`, `catalog.rs`, `lib.rs` and the catalog doc entry.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Without a configured `[providers.models.opper.<alias>]` entry, the provider is inactive.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Provider construction errors that mention `opper`, failed `/models` calls to `https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat/models`, or chat errors from the compatible provider path.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line): N/A
- Scope materially carried forward: N/A
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? `No`
- If `No`, why (inspiration-only, no direct code/design carry-over): N/A

Disclosure: Opper is my startup.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Record the bounded runtime holding-crate exception for the existing native-thinking setting in feature request #12054.
  - Name the permitted adapters, their extraction destination and review condition, and record the Core Team approval by @Audacity88 on 2026-10-29.
- **Scope boundary:** One table row in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`. This PR adds no runtime behavior; its approval cell records the existing Core Team approval. Canonical types, budget policy and OpenAI model/wire mapping remain with their API, config and provider owners.
- **Blast radius:** Governance for the twelve named runtime files. The row records Core Team approval; this exception PR must still merge through normal review before the implementation can rely on the record on `master`. Implementation review remains separate.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12054. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12054
- **Implementation PR:** #12059 depends on this exception request. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12059

### What this does, simply

The OpenAI profile-thinking fix needs to carry an existing setting through the runtime's current request paths. The runtime is a transitional holding crate whose scoped `AGENTS.md` requires a recorded Core Team exception. This PR names the narrow scope and records [@Audacity88's approval in #12057 on 2026-10-29](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057#issuecomment-6502718792). That approval expressly covers the row at `6bc0024679e692e4f8b76b322b395bf51ccb59e9`; the update changes only its approval cell. The exception remains bounded by the named paths, destination and reconsideration condition. It does not approve the implementation or merge either PR.

The permitted slice covers existing CLI, Agent/RPC, delegate, tool-round, summary, recovery and streaming adapters; the response-cache bypass; required request-constructor updates; explicit core-turn future `Send` contracts; and focused regressions. `cost.rs` and `vision_route.rs` have test-only constructor changes, while `skills/creator.rs` initializes the new request field to `None`.

The intended destination is the agent-loop and delegation owners in the planned `zeroclaw-kernel` extraction; auxiliary skills construction follows its existing owner. Review the exception at the agent-loop or delegation extraction design review, whichever comes first, or before widening supported turn surfaces, retained state, mapping ownership or native thinking beyond OpenAI.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: this changes only the governance table; inspect the row's scope, destination, recorded authority and review condition.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Docs Style` succeeded on `8ade0d52dacda6e0d68c384b788bad21d68a02a4` ([job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41204095638/job/124545625925)). The [Quality Gate run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41204095638) is terminal with 43 successful, 3 skipped and 2 failed jobs. `Security` and `CI Required Gate` failed; this is not a green required-CI result. Fixing these advisories requires a Wasmtime dependency update outside this one-row governance PR; required CI remains blocked. The added-link collection policy includes this changed `.md` file. The resulting tree equals the proposed contributor patch at `379ddd9d5d9943055551fe5679cb9155a9198f9c`. The public Core Team roster lists @Audacity88; the linked comment explicitly approves this bounded scope and destination and asks that the approval be recorded. The full PR still adds only the OpenAI exception row relative to its upstream merge base. Implementation #12059 is separate. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12059

prs.title: fix(release): embed the dashboard in Linux and Windows desktop kernels
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The bug.** The Linux and Windows desktop jobs in Release Stable stage their kernel sidecar with `scripts/desktop/prepare-kernel.sh --target <triple>` and no features, and they never restore the `web-dist` artifact. The macOS job does both (`needs: [validate, web]`, `--features embedded-web`). `prepare-kernel.sh` adds no features by default, and the standard distribution feature set does not include `embedded-web`.
  - **The effect.** A fresh Linux or Windows desktop install has a kernel with no compiled-in dashboard and no dashboard files on disk for the gateway to fall back to. The dashboard root answers 503 "Web dashboard not available". The negative control below reproduces this with the release's current Linux staging command.
  - **The fix.** Both jobs now:
    1. wait for the `web` job;
    2. restore `web-dist` at `web/dist/`;
    3. stage the kernel with `--features embedded-web`;
    4. run `scripts/desktop/smoke-dashboard.sh` against the staged sidecar before `cargo tauri build`.

    This mirrors what the macOS job already does with an inline step.
  - **The smoke script.** `scripts/desktop/smoke-dashboard.sh` starts a staged kernel the way a fresh desktop install does: from an empty working directory with an isolated config directory. It requires the dashboard root to return the SPA, so a kernel built without `embedded-web` fails with the gateway's 503. It is a cross-platform version of the macOS job's inline check, so the Windows job can run it under Git Bash. It used to arrive with #11270; it now lives in this PR, next to its only callers, and there is one copy.
  - `tests/architecture/desktop_release.rs` now pins those invariants for the Linux and Windows jobs, as it already does for macOS. It also pins the smoke script's fresh-install launch and SPA check.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - The Linux and Windows jobs stay `continue-on-error`, and the macOS dmg remains the only required desktop asset. Promoting Linux and Windows is a separate maintainer decision.
  - The macOS job and its inline smoke step are unchanged.
  - Release triggers, permissions, signing, and the published asset and feature lists are unchanged. No new workflow or job is added.
  - No Rust product code changes.
- **Blast radius:**
  - Release Stable only: the two best-effort desktop jobs.
  - They now start after the `web` job (about six minutes in the last stable run).
  - If the new smoke test fails, that platform's installer is withheld from the release instead of shipping without a dashboard.
  - `publish` already lists both jobs in `needs` and does not require their assets, so a failure there still cannot block the release.
- **Linked issue(s):**
  - Part of #11004.
  - #11270 merged on November 3; this branch is refreshed onto master. The aggregate diff now contains only this PR's changes. This PR's own changes are the commits `fix(release): embed the dashboard in Linux and Windows desktop kernels` and `ci(release): ship the dashboard smoke script with the release jobs that use it`.

### What this does, simply

The Mac desktop installer ships a copy of ZeroClaw with the web dashboard built in. The Linux and Windows installers were built from the same recipe minus that one ingredient. Someone who installed ZeroClaw Desktop on Linux or Windows and opened it would get a "Web dashboard not available" error page instead of the dashboard.

This PR builds the Linux and Windows copies the same way as the Mac one. Before packaging, it also starts each copy once and checks that the dashboard really loads. Those two installers are still "best effort": if one fails to build, the release goes out without it, exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

Current head `12f662d575b150aed11550bd2c98e43e37f7db26` follows the merged #11270 parent and repairs the desktop runner assertion. [Current CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41602024261/job/125809088355) passes. The [November 3 author report](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11272#issuecomment-6598706004) records refresh validation. Older commands and output below retain their original revision provenance.

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A for manual steps. The edited release jobs run only during a stable release. See the validation note below.

### How I tested

- **Validation of the release jobs before a release run.** Release Stable runs only on a stable tag or a release dispatch, and it publishes, so the edited jobs cannot run on this PR.
  - Historical head `8ce4244c06656f364675dca180c305f9fecd5a33` was checked on Linux x86_64 with a private build that runs the release's own commands from an exact archive of the head commit: `cargo web build` for the real dashboard (the release `web` job's command), then `prepare-kernel.sh` twice, then `smoke-dashboard.sh` against each staged kernel. The kernel staged with the fixed command serves the dashboard; the kernel staged with the release's current Linux command is refused with the gateway's 503.
  - At the earlier revision `17d5f355bb`, this PR also ran the bundle dry run that #11270 used to add. Its Linux and Windows legs built release-profile kernels with `--features embedded-web`, logged `smoke-dashboard: http://127.0.0.1:42618/ served the embedded dashboard` (Windows under Git Bash), and produced `.deb`/`.AppImage` and `.msi`/`-setup.exe` installers. That workflow no longer exists, and `smoke-dashboard.sh` remains byte-identical to what it ran. The current staging script also resolves the distribution feature set before appending `embedded-web`.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The architecture suite in the current `Test` job covers the release job structure and the smoke script's contract.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No PR check runs the edited Release Stable jobs. The `needs: [validate, web]` edge and the `web-dist` restore inside Release Stable stay unexercised until the first release run; the architecture test pins both statically.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

Historical dashboard smoke at `8ce4244c06` (Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.0). Source is `git archive 8ce4244c06`; `git get-tar-commit-id` on the build host reads `8ce4244c06656f364675dca180c305f9fecd5a33`. Before the run, `/zeroclaw-data/web/dist` and `/usr/share/zeroclawlabs/web/dist` had no `index.html`, so neither kernel had dashboard files on disk to fall back to.

```text
$ cargo web build
WEB_BUILD_EXIT:0        (web/dist: 69 files; index.html contains id="root")

# release's current Linux staging command (negative control)
$ scripts/desktop/prepare-kernel.sh --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
prepare-kernel: cargo build --profile release --bin zeroclaw --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
NEG_STAGE_EXIT:0        (46M, sha256 e408ec6968581dd913786a2b49d5244f1ada9eabb7205c2666829ad3d4a0334a)

# this PR's staging command
$ scripts/desktop/prepare-kernel.sh --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --features embedded-web
prepare-kernel: cargo build --profile release --bin zeroclaw --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --features embedded-web
POS_STAGE_EXIT:0        (50M, sha256 a2bccfd7d0e922637f10c7933f5e492663f25723752cb7d91aa8ab4a3ad07642)

$ scripts/desktop/smoke-dashboard.sh apps/tauri/binaries/zeroclaw-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu 42691
smoke-dashboard: http://127.0.0.1:42691/ served the embedded dashboard
EXIT:0   (3 s)

$ scripts/desktop/smoke-dashboard.sh <negative-control kernel> 42692
smoke-dashboard: http://127.0.0.1:42692/ did not serve the dashboard within 120s (last HTTP status: 503)
Web dashboard not available. Reinstall with the supported installer so the dashboard is built and placed where the gateway looks for it: ...
EXIT:1   (122 s)
```

After both runs nothing was listening on either port, no staged kernel was still running, and the smoke script's temporary directories were gone.

Historical architecture tests at `8ce4244c06`, same host and toolchain:

```text
$ cargo test --locked --test architecture
test desktop_release::desktop_app_check_runs_the_desktop_unit_tests ... ok
test desktop_release::desktop_dashboard_smoke_launches_like_a_fresh_install ... ok
test desktop_release::macos_desktop_sidecar_embeds_the_web_artifact ... ok
test desktop_release::linux_and_windows_desktop_sidecars_embed_the_web_artifact ... ok
test desktop_release::windows_desktop_manifest_selects_common_controls_v6 ... ok
test result: ok. 58 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

From the earlier revision `17d5f355bb`, the Linux/Windows release test failed against `master`'s release workflow (`Linux desktop release must wait for the canonical web-dist artifact`) and against a partial fix with only Linux fixed (`Windows desktop kernel must enable the embedded-web Cargo feature`). That test and the release workflow change are unchanged since then.

Static checks:

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                              -> EXIT:0
$ git diff --check                                                        -> EXIT:0
$ cargo clippy --locked --test architecture -- -D warnings   (Rust 1.98.0) -> EXIT:0, no warnings
$ shellcheck -S warning scripts/desktop/smoke-dashboard.sh                -> EXIT:0
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh tests/architecture scripts/desktop .github/workflows -> Comment hygiene gate passed.
$ actionlint .github/workflows/release-stable-manual.yml .github/workflows/desktop-check.yml
    -> the same 6 pre-existing shellcheck infos as master's release-stable-manual.yml, none new
$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh -> Summary: 0 error(s)
$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh   -> OK
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `smoke-dashboard.sh` here is byte-identical to the version that ran in the earlier dry run (same Git blob).
  - In the last stable release run (v0.8.5), the Linux and Windows desktop jobs completed with these staging and bundling commands, minus `--features embedded-web` and the smoke.
  - This PR's CI at head `8ce4244c06`: `Desktop App Check` passed on all three OS. `Docs Style`, `Lint`, `Test`, and `Parallel Runtime Test` passed. On the first attempt, `CI Required Gate` was red only because `Check (32-bit)` timed out installing its apt packages before any compilation (`apt install: attempt 2/2 timed out (status: 124)`); every other job passed. That job was rerun once, and on the rerun `Check (32-bit)` and `CI Required Gate` passed.
  - **Not verified at this head:**
    - The Windows release leg's smoke. On this head the script has run only on Linux; its last Windows run was the earlier dry run under Git Bash.
    - A native Windows installer. The first proof there is the next stable release, where the Linux and Windows legs stay `continue-on-error`. The macOS job is unchanged.
    - An installed Linux or Windows desktop package opening the dashboard. The 503 on current packages is reproduced on a staged kernel built with the release's current command, not on an installed package.
  - The dashboard for the smoke was built with Node 20.20.2, while the release pins Node 24 (`.nvmrc`). npm warned about the engine version and the build succeeded. The smoke only needs a 200 with the SPA root element, which this build provides, but the asset is not byte-for-byte the release's.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The two jobs gain no secrets.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The same installers are produced; the kernel inside now includes the dashboard.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` of this PR's squash commit. Both jobs stay best-effort, so a bad release leg drops only that platform's installer.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
