prs.title: feat(rpc): dispatch plugin webhooks over the core RPC
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`03b29bcc68`). **Depends on #11319** (core ingress, which itself now builds on #11339) and **#11165** (`zeroclaw-rpc-proto`). The branch merges #11319 at its current head `c352574198` and #11165 at its current head `19e41b09fa` (restacked 2026-10-23, see below); their commits show in the diff until they land, so review this PR's own commits, `7962184961` (the methods), `b5d9ebd577` (channel scoping), `fcf4f6121c` (the review's two non-blocking warnings), `4e9a208600` (channel rename and delete carry `allowed_channels` grants), `d6ef5dc0af` (the removed-binding interval test) and `1147d81ac2` and `2aeb57ae9b` (test adaptation to master: config edits go through `publish_test_config` on the read-only live config, `RpcContext::for_authority` sets the ingress handle, the WSS refusal test selects its audit record by reason too, and master's channel WebSocket e2e spreads the plugin channel default), `f3364f9c67` (the RPC socket guide says a rejection record carries the plugin name, channel alias and error key, not the path or the plugin's rejection text; from Greptile's review), `ad161acc03` (admission re-resolves the caller's live grants; from Greptile's and Audacity88's reviews), `13fd6a42e1` (the two denial-record tests drain past a lagged broadcast receiver instead of stopping at it) and `864b58d76e` (a rename or delete refuses a cascade outside the caller's config write grants; from Greptile's review). **The holding-crate exception in #11317 is approved and records the approval; it must land before this implementation.**
- **Refresh of 2026-11-02 (`d2479d7f2f`):** merges master `03b29bcc68`, which carries the Wasmtime 48.0.8 bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424 (#12129) and so clears the `Security` job for this branch. The one conflict was the workspace `members` line in the root `Cargo.toml`: this branch adds the `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` member and master appends `tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer`; both kept. No change to this PR's own slice.
- **Fixes after the refresh (`5d17864f14`, `d93d67f79c`, `d4517a7845`):** master's new `runtime-composition-consumer` fixture refuses any `zeroclaw-*` dependency of the runtime that its retained-dependencies policy does not name, and this branch carries #11165's `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` edge, so the policy gains that entry the way the relay wire contract is recorded (owner `rpc/types.rs`, which re-exports the wire-stable types; the reason names the dispatcher's import). #11165 will need the same line when it refreshes onto master. The parallel runtime gate then failed in master's `persisted_log_reads_refuse_a_scoped_principal`: the two in-flight-cap tests here send `MAX_PLUGIN_WEBHOOK_DISPATCHES_PER_CONNECTION` (1024) dispatches in a tight loop, each leaving a rejection record, and the log writer hands records to its disk worker through a bounded queue of the same size, dropping what it cannot take, whichever test emitted it. Under the gate's 16 threads those tests sort right after the persisted-log tests, so the four denial records that test reads back were dropped and the administrator's query found none. The two burst tests now hold the writer's test lock, which the persisted-log tests hold while they read their records back, so a burst never shares the writer with a test that reads it; the capture tests read the broadcast stream, whose channel is far larger than a burst, and are unaffected. From Greptile's review of this refresh, `d4517a7845` takes the cascade refusal's message from the catalog (`rpc-auth-config-cascade-write-denied`, with the refused path as a Fluent argument) instead of an English literal.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-03 (`e331fc224c`):** merges master `ee8a753dff`, which is #11318 squash-merged, so #11318's changes no longer show in this diff. The four conflicts were all in files #11318 added or edited (`.github/workflows/README.md`, `golden_frames.rs`, the plugin backend change filter and its test): master's version of each is exactly #11318's final content, and this branch's version is that content plus the lines #11319 and this PR add on top of it, so every conflict resolves to this branch's side. The rest of the merge is master's own work since `03b29bcc68` (#11054, #11739, #11270, #12003).
- **#11165 (restack of 2026-10-23, `534a7e41c3` and `82dc407331`):** #11165's head `19e41b09fa` merges master and moves #11132's `session/*` methods into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`, so the master conflicts in `dispatch.rs`, `session.rs` and `types.rs` are resolved there and this branch merges it without conflict in those files. The hand-resolved files are the CI workflow, its gate registry, the CI guide and the plugin backend change filter, where master, #11165 and #11319 each add their own lines (every side's lines are kept), plus the regenerated OpenRPC document (`cargo generate openrpc`, 107 methods, `--check` clean). #11165's `session/prompt` fix (`SessionPromptAck`) comes along with its head. The branch is now mergeable with master.
- **Channel scoping (maintainer decision on this PR):** `channels:execute` and `channels:read` reach only the channel instances a profile names, and config can close the path for a channel or an agent whatever the grants. Field names and defaults:
  - `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels = ["plugin.<alias>", ...]`: a channel selector like `allowed_agents`. Entries are `<type>.<alias>` names of configured instances, validated at load; `"*"` grants every instance; empty (the default) grants none. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches all.
  - `[channels.plugin.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses webhooks delivered through `plugin-webhook/dispatch` to that instance.
  - `[agents.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses such a delivery to any channel the agent handles.
  - Checked at dispatch, not only when routes are listed: `PluginWebhookIngress::dispatch_admitted` runs the check on the owner the request would be queued to, before anything is queued or reserved, so a republished route cannot redirect an admitted request. A refusal is `FORBIDDEN` with an audit record. `plugin-webhook/routes` lists only granted channels.
  - The docs say what `channels = ["execute"]` and `["read"]` unlock (authentication guide and RPC socket guide), and that a route path can be a vendor's shared secret.
  - From the review's non-blocking warnings (`fcf4f6121c`): the refusal for an ungranted channel names no channel, while its audit record still does, and a route whose channel instance the live config no longer binds is refused (fail closed) until the next reload retires it. `d6ef5dc0af` proves that interval: a route admitted while its instance is bound is refused `FORBIDDEN` once a live config write removes the instance, while the route is still published, and its worker receives nothing (asked for in Audacity88's review of #11322).
  - Admission does not trust the grants the spawned dispatch task copied at the read loop's check (`ad161acc03`): `admit_plugin_webhook` re-resolves the caller's live grants with `recheck_authority_after_admission`, the same check `session/new` and `session/prompt` run after admission, so a credential revoked or a profile narrowed between the check and the task's admission refuses the delivery. `plugin_webhook_admission_rechecks_the_live_grants` narrows `allowed_channels` and then drops `channels:execute` after `spawn_handle` and asserts both refusals while the copied grants still allow.
  - Renaming or deleting a channel instance carries its `allowed_channels` grants along (`4e9a208600`): a rename rewrites them to the new name, a delete drops them, and the changed profiles are saved, so a grant never blocks the change. A caller does not reach a profile through that cascade (`864b58d76e`): the rename and the provider-model alias delete check every entry the cascade dirties against the caller's live config write grants and refuse the whole change, with nothing saved, when one of them is outside those grants, the write-set rule the gateway's config routes already follow (`config_map_key_rename_refuses_a_cascade_outside_the_callers_write_paths`: a `channels.*` writer is refused FORBIDDEN naming `permission_profiles.ops`, then succeeds once `permission_profiles.*` is granted).
- **What changed and why:** A gateway in another process needs to hand channel-plugin webhook requests to the core that owns the route table. Three daemon RPC methods over the core ingress:
  - `plugin-webhook/dispatch` (`channels:execute`): method, raw query, headers, and the body as standard base64 under a caller-chosen `request_id`; answers a typed outcome (`ack`, `reply` with `body`, `not_found`, `queue_full`, `unavailable`, `unauthorized`, `bad_request`, `invalid_response`, `timeout`, `cancelled`). Validated by the same shared constructor the HTTP adapter uses.
  - `plugin-webhook/cancel` (`channels:execute`): cancels an in-flight dispatch on the same connection; the dispatch response stays authoritative.
  - `plugin-webhook/routes` (`channels:read`): current route owners, for diagnostics.
  - Local IPC only: an exhaustive transport match refuses all three on WSS with FORBIDDEN and an audit record.
  - Dispatch runs in a task spawned from the dispatcher like `session/prompt`, so the serial read loop stays live for cancel and other requests. Each connection tracks in-flight dispatches for cancel and duplicate-id checks and holds at most 1024 until their responses are queued; the next gets `queue_full`. Connection close and daemon reload cancel in-flight work and send nothing; shutdown joins the tasks and never waits on a full writer queue.
  - The daemon registry hands the generation's ingress to the RPC context, and the daemon always builds one ingress.
- **Scope boundary:** No gateway change (the forwarder is the next PR). No new principal or credential. Runtime edits stay within the #11317 row: `src/rpc/{dispatch,context}.rs`, `src/daemon/{registry,mod}.rs`, and the denial message keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`. The new config field also updates `PluginChannelConfig` literals inside the test modules of `src/plugin_runtime.rs` and `src/tools/mod.rs` (mechanical, test-only). The grant selector and config fields live in `zeroclaw-api` and `zeroclaw-config`.
- **Blast radius:** runtime RPC dispatcher (new arms, per-connection state, shutdown join), daemon registry, `RpcContext` (all 14 literals), the OpenRPC document (regenerated), `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` (8 wire types, 3 `Method` variants), `zeroclaw-api` (route listing, the `allowed_channels` selector), `zeroclaw-infra` (route listing, `dispatch_admitted`), `zeroclaw-config` (three fields).
- **Follow-ups from the review, not in this PR:** one local-only gate shared with `file/upload/*`, with a per-method "local only" classification `xtask` can emit (#11566), and `schemars` bounds on the dispatch wire fields so the OpenRPC document states them (#11567).
- **Merge-order note:** #11186 adds `TransportKind::Inproc`. The transport match here is deliberately exhaustive, so whichever of this PR and #11186 lands second must add the `Inproc` arm (refused, with its test; #11322 carries both). #11289 replaces the free-text `AuthDenied::forbidden(message)` with `RpcDenialReason`: whichever of this PR and #11289 lands second needs variants for this PR's four refusals (for example `local_ipc_only`, `channel_not_granted`, `channel_refuses_injected_webhooks`, `agent_refuses_injected_webhooks`) and the updated audit assertions, which now read `reason` as a stable identifier.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000. Related #11001. Depends on #11165.

### What this does, simply

The daemon already answers RPC calls from local clients such as zerocode. This PR teaches it three more calls so a separate web gateway can say "here is a webhook request for this plugin URL, what should I answer?" and get back the same result the in-process gateway gets today. Only local connections may use them, and only callers allowed to operate the specific channels they ask for. An operator can also switch the path off for one channel, or for one agent, in config, whatever access a caller has.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** local RPC socket.
- **Steps to run:** start a daemon with a configured channel plugin that claims a webhook path, then over `socat READLINE UNIX-CONNECT:<data_dir>/daemon.sock` send `initialize`, then `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"plugin-webhook/routes","params":{},"id":2}` and a `plugin-webhook/dispatch` for that path.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** routes lists the owner; dispatch answers `{"outcome":"ack"}` or the plugin's reply.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `METHOD_NOT_FOUND`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` (runtime `rpc::` and `daemon::` suites, proto tests), `Parallel Runtime Test` (runtime/channels interference), `Installer Drift` (OpenRPC `--check`), plugin legs for the ingress and gateway parity.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows named pipes are not exercised by a required job.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `b5d9ebd577`: this PR with #11319 `98e1666b31` and #11165 `ec00bf0a12` merged, on master `a0f70b7925`; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::
test result: FAILED. 784 passed; 1 failed   (configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook   (x3)
test result: ok. 26 passed   (includes plugin_webhook_dispatch_reaches_only_granted_channels and plugin_webhook_dispatch_honors_channel_and_agent_refusal)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib daemon::
test result: FAILED. 101 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored   (a_live_config_write_reaches_the_daemon_pricing_refresher_without_a_reload, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib
ok. 295 passed, ok. 335 passed ; ok. 1760 passed   (channel selector, allowed_channels validation, accept_injected_webhooks defaults, dispatch_admitted)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto --features schema-export
ok. 29 passed ; ok. 32 passed
$ cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- openrpc --check ; cargo test --locked -p xtask openrpc
openrpc: docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync ; ok
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib ; --test golden_frames plugin_webhook
ok. 653 passed ; ok. 5 passed (fixtures unchanged)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib plugin_runtime:: ; cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e ; --test architecture
ok. 17 passed ; ok. 5 passed ; ok. 57 passed
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets ; cargo check --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --tests ; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
Finished ; Finished ; Finished, no warnings
$ cargo clippy (api, infra, config, gateway, rpc-proto; with and without zeroclaw-gateway/plugins-wasm; root bin and e2e) --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings
$ TMPDIR=/private/tmp ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh ; ZEROCLAW_PARALLEL_TEST_SCOPE=channels ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
runtime run 1/3: 5466 passed; 1 failed (peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget; the gate stops there) ; channels x3: ok. 1967 passed
$ comment hygiene, change filter, docs quality and docs links gates
all pass
```

The three failing runtime tests fail identically on untouched master `a0f70b7925` in this environment (two runs each), and this PR does not touch them. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops only on the pre-existing macOS `unused import std::sync::mpsc` in `service/mod.rs`; no lint in any changed runtime file.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutations caught by the new tests: releasing the permit before the send, shutdown not joining dispatch tasks, releasing the id after the send, allowing WSS, removing the send's race against connection cancel, and skipping the denial audit record.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Restack onto #11165 `19e41b09fa` and #11319 `c352574198` (head `2aeb57ae9b`, 2026-10-23):** the whole suite again on this head: proto (30, schema export 33), api and infra (339), config (1821 of 1822), channels listing (8), gateway with `plugins-wasm` and the plugin webhook golden frames (5, fixtures unchanged), runtime `rpc::` and `daemon::` (104), plugin admission (34), `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` (5), architecture (81), `cargo generate openrpc --check` in sync, workspace and root `plugins-wasm-cranelift` checks, `--no-default-features` with `-D warnings`, clippy on the touched crates, the root binary and e2e, and runtime clippy, the comment hygiene, change filter, docs and links gates, and the parallel runtime gate (runtime x3 at 16 threads, channels x3), all green. The one failure is `policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception`, a master test that fails on macOS (PR 11646) and that this PR does not touch; the earlier pre-existing runtime failures no longer reproduce on this master.
- **Refresh for the #11322 review (head `d6ef5dc0af`):** the same suite again: `rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook` 27 passed (with the new test), and the only failures are the same three pre-existing runtime tests and the macOS `std::sync::mpsc` clippy warning described above. The new test fails if a missing binding is admitted.
- **The parallel-gate failure of `plugin_webhook_dispatch_reaches_only_granted_channels` (`13fd6a42e1`):** the test reads its audit record from the process-wide log broadcast, and its drain stopped at the first lagged-receiver error, which the channel reports once a noisy neighbour floods the window between the subscription and the drain under 16 threads, so the record was never reached; the WSS refusal test had the same latent stop. Both now subscribe right before the call under test, drain past a lag with a two-second deadline for a late record, and report on a miss whether the capture layer was active and whether the broadcast hook changed since the subscription. `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook -- --test-threads=16` x3 passes (28 tests); the parallel gate's result on this head is in CI.
- **The cascade write-set check (`864b58d76e`):** `rpc::` 865 passed at 16 threads, with `config_map_key_rename_refuses_a_cascade_outside_the_callers_write_paths`; runtime clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; the docs quality and link gates pass on `authentication.md`, whose RPC selector bullet now says a cascade's rewrites are checked too.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-02 (head `d2479d7f2f`):** fmt and `cargo metadata --locked` on this tree, with cargo-audit 0.22.2 and `cargo deny check advisories` on its merged `Cargo.lock` (no vulnerabilities; RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424 are gone with Wasmtime 48.0.8). The build and test evidence for this merge ran on #11322's tree, which carries this branch's commits unchanged plus the gateway forwarder: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` with and without `plugins-wasm-cranelift`, workspace clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`), the two-process `plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e` 3 passed, `cargo generate openrpc --check`, and the docs gates; the runtime `rpc::` suite 884 passed at 16 threads on that tree, which includes this branch's dispatcher unchanged
- **Fixes after the refresh (head `d4517a7845`):** on the #11322 tree that carries this head unchanged: fmt; `rpc::dispatch::tests` 588 passed at 16 threads (the cascade test reads the refusal from the catalog); `runtime-composition-consumer` 10 passed, `dependency_boundary` included; runtime clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; the two burst tests and the two persisted-log tests together at 4 threads, ten runs, no failure; the parallel runtime gate script itself (three passes each of the runtime suite, 6044 tests, and the channels suite, 2031 tests, at 16 threads) green on this tree, as it was on the unfixed tree: the drop only shows under CI's slower disk, so the fix rests on the writer queue's mechanism rather than a local reproduction
- **Refresh of 2026-11-03 (head `e331fc224c`):** on the merged tree: fmt; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` with and without `plugins-wasm-cranelift`; the runtime `rpc::` suite 867 passed at 16 threads; runtime clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; `runtime-composition-consumer` 10 passed; `cargo generate openrpc --check`; gateway lib `plugin_webhook` with `plugins-wasm` 15 passed and the plugin webhook golden frames 5 passed against the recorded fixtures; the parallel runtime gate script green (three passes each of the runtime and channels suites at 16 threads); `plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh` and `windows_test_scope.test.sh` pass; the docs quality and link gates on the changed docs
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --no-default-features --features agent-runtime` fails on six pre-existing dead-code helpers in `src/main.rs` whose only caller is gateway-gated; unrelated, reproduces on master.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: `Resource::Channels` gains its first RPC consumers, scoped to named channel instances through `allowed_channels`. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches every route; any other profile reaches only the instances it names. `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or an agent refuses the path whatever the grants. Plugins still verify vendor signatures.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (headers pass through to the guest as they do over HTTP)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new path: dispatched messages enter the same plugin channel listener as HTTP webhooks.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: local IPC only (WSS refused with an audit record); grants checked at admission; the core enforces the shared request bounds, so a local caller bypassing the gateway's rate limit still cannot exceed them; 1024 in-flight dispatches per connection; no diagnostic detail in results.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (additive methods). Builds with plugins but without the gateway now build the ingress, so webhook-capable plugin channels validate and publish their route claims instead of activating poll-only. A worker that drops its reply after the caller cancelled now reports `cancelled` instead of `unavailable`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes, additive: `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels` (default empty, so a profile with `channels` grants but no selector reaches no channel; nothing consumed `channels` before this PR), and `accept_injected_webhooks` on `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` and `[agents.<alias>]` (default `true`).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the methods disappear (`METHOD_NOT_FOUND`) and nothing persisted changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** remove `channels:execute` or the channel from a profile's `allowed_channels` to deny dispatch; `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or agent closes the path whatever the grants; `plugins.enabled = false` publishes no routes.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `RPC authorization denied` records for `plugin-webhook/*`, with reasons naming the channel or agent that refused; `queue_full` answers at the per-connection cap; WARN `plugin_webhook_dispatch_notification` for notification-form dispatches.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(providers): refresh MiniMax text model choices
prs.body:
Reason: MiniMax's discovered text-model choices still include older models and can recommend M3 before the current M3.1 Flash model.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Define the direct MiniMax fallback catalog as `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`, then `MiniMax-M3`, using one ordered source for fallback recommendations and ranking.
  - Rank the shared provider-owned chat catalog without removing or rewriting returned IDs. Flash and M3 sort first; other IDs retain their order. The pre-existing non-chat filtering is unchanged. The runtime-specific integration is removed.
  - Update the MiniMax configuration example and cover the configured HTTP catalog path, empty/legacy catalogs, gateway availability, and explicit legacy selection.
- **Scope boundary:** No saved-config migration, pricing lookup changes, request serialization, thinking controls, or media-input changes. This does not add gateway routes or import code from #11383.
- **Blast radius:** Consumers of the shared provider-owned chat catalog. Explicit configured or manually supplied model IDs continue to pass through.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11383, which tracks separate MiniMax media-input work. This PR neither depends on nor supersedes it.

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw recommends MiniMax text models, it now offers Flash first and M3 second. A gateway retains all chat models that its catalog returned, including legacy IDs; for example, an existing Flash `:free` route stays intact, and a catalog with only M3 does not gain an invented Flash route. Existing configurations can continue to select older or custom models explicitly.

The upstream model reference is https://platform.minimax.io/docs/guides/models-intro.md. Pricing and model metadata continue to come from the existing pricing sources.

## Testing (required)

The October 30 narrowing removes the runtime integration and its test. The local command/output inventory below describes the earlier filtering revision, not a fresh execution on the narrowed head. Current [Test CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41145581896/job/124370083102) passes the provider catalog/factory regressions, including legacy-ID preservation. Claims below about runtime execution or removing advertised legacy IDs are historical and superseded by this narrowing.

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Deterministic catalog and tool-output regressions cover the changed selection policy without provider credentials.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Exact-head Test, Lint, Format and Docs Style pass on `ce771ba2604ee7c2bfa59fe0588ab8cbd793c8f3`. Security and Required Gate remain red for inherited Wasmtime advisories. Historical local checks are listed below.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live provider call or interactive web/TUI picker was exercised. The configured HTTP test uses a local mock server through the real provider factory and dispatch path; the runtime regression exercises `Tool::execute` and checks its JSON model list. The direct MiniMax chat capture verifies the default Flash request carries the exact model ID and omits an unsupported reasoning-effort field, relying on the provider default.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers catalog::tests --lib
  test result: ok. 27 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers factory::tests::minimax_default_flash_chat_serializes_model_without_injecting_reasoning_effort --lib
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime tools::model_switch::tests::minimax_list_models_refreshes_choices_but_explicit_legacy_selection_survives --lib
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
Earlier full scoped runtime suite: 19 passed; 0 failed
./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D clippy::correctness
  provider dispatch gate clean
cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
  Finished successfully; generated workspace API documentation
BASE_SHA=e8d2e5fc81a01e6dc7d76428e07168e583b43039 ./scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)
BASE_SHA=e8d2e5fc81a01e6dc7d76428e07168e583b43039 ./scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  Ran 6 tests: OK; no added links in changed documentation lines
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected the catalog consumers and confirmed the pricing/configuration paths remain independent. Tests verify that a saved legacy model and explicit legacy `model_switch set` selection remain intact. No live API request was made.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A for rendering: this changes catalog policy and tool JSON, with no renderer/layout changes. Interactive picker presentation remains untested.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** follow-up changes are locally validated on the amended PR revision, Linux, Rust 1.98.1. Catalog and serialization regressions live in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/{catalog,factory}.rs`; tool-output regression lives in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/model_switch.rs`. The final provider suite, targeted runtime test, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The OpenCode catalog regression asserts `opencode/minimax-m3.1-flash-free` before `opencode/minimax-m3`, removes `opencode/minimax-m2.1-free`, and preserves `custom/minimax-m2.1-free`. The gateway regression preserves returned `minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash:free`, music/embedding/speech/video entries, and the saved legacy selection. The direct HTTP capture asserts `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` in `model`, no `reasoning_effort`, and a user message body.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The current provider catalog preserves returned legacy IDs and puts Flash before M3. Explicitly selecting the legacy model still succeeds.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests and live/UI checks were not run; focused tests, the workspace quality gate, and rustdoc cover this catalog-only scope. Generated translations were not refreshed for this small English documentation change.

- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes: `model_switch` returns a refreshed list of model IDs from the existing catalog source. The current change only orders identifiers; it adds no new transport, prompt interpretation, or execution permission.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Returned older model IDs remain discoverable; saved and explicit selections remain accepted.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No schema, environment variable, or flag changes.

- Upgrade steps: None.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 3f56de01fed95f9a041c74da9aa33437cc49380d`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None; explicitly configured model IDs remain available.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A current MiniMax model is missing from discovered choices, or its returned gateway ID is altered. The focused catalog tests guard both cases.

prs.title: fix(cli): honour [gateway.tls] for local admin HTTP commands
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #12091

When `[gateway.tls] enabled = true`, CLI admin commands (`gateway get-paircode`, `sop pending|logs|approve|deny`, and `gateway restart`'s graceful `/admin/shutdown`) still built `http://…` URLs with `reqwest::Client::new()`, so they failed against a TLS-only listener and restart treated the gateway as absent.

### Changes

- `gateway_admin_url` takes `use_tls` and emits `https://` / `http://` accordingly; wildcard binds `0.0.0.0` / `::` rewrite to `127.0.0.1` / `::1` respectively for the outbound host.
- `gateway_admin_http_client` trusts `[gateway.tls].cert_path` as a PEM trust anchor (no silent plaintext fallback).
- Required `[gateway.tls.client_auth]` fails with an explicit error (CLI does not present a client certificate yet).
- Documented in `docs/book/src/gateway/api.md`.

## Tests

```sh
cargo test --locked --bin zeroclaw --features agent-runtime gateway_admin_
```

The original local run passed 6 tests, including `gateway_admin_shutdown_reaches_tls_listener`. On head `dd5ae50abc45bd306b77e108a4ddb89564d6fa01`, the [Linux Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41310037900/job/124858289004) passes all 12 gateway-admin helper tests and 3 CLI component tests, including real TLS listeners and refusal paths.

prs.title: fix(oidc): bind enrollment callbacks to the initiating browser
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, true-rebased onto `6ac37f60f142bca5e1e629f59e809a5cee6aaf3e`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Bind gateway OIDC enrollment to the browser that started it. A copied callback URL can no longer reveal a token in a different browser.
  - Generate a separate 32-byte random secret for each flow. Keep only its hash in the existing `PendingPkce` record. Check the cookie before code exchange; refuse and consume mismatched flows.
  - Preserve concurrent tabs, one-time consumption, issuer/provider checks, and the original deadline for a valid capacity retry. The cookie grants no session or API access.
  - Add four endpoint regressions, update existing callback tests to carry their actual issued cookie, and document cookie scope and recovery.
- **Scope boundary:** Enrollment start/callback and their documentation. Dashboard sign-in remains in #11965. Configured origin (#12048), same-host HTTP ports (#12088), broader availability (#12049), and response zeroization (#12090) remain separate.
- **Blast radius:** Clients that complete `/oidc/login/<alias>` through `/oidc/callback` must keep the issued browser cookie. Device flow and bearer-authenticated API routes retain their current behavior. The existing gateway `rand` dependency moves from dev to normal dependencies; no new package or lockfile change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12050. Related #11965 and #8289.

### What this does, simply

The browser login page returns a token that a user can copy into a client. Before this change, someone could start a login under their own account, then send its final URL to another person. That person could receive and use the wrong account's token.

The gateway now gives the starting browser a short-lived cookie. The final page requires that cookie. A different browser gets the existing refusal page, and no code is exchanged. Start a new login in the intended browser after a refusal; do not forward callback URLs.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: independent review of the callback boundary and an A/B browser check are useful for this security change.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, gateway enrollment HTTP routes and the callback page. No messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a test OIDC alias and two isolated browser profiles. Use dedicated test accounts. Keep the gateway scheme/host consistent. The captured mock-provider recipe and source hashes are in [the evidence bundle](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/README.md).
- **Steps to run:** Start a login in browser A. Capture the final callback URL before following it. Open that URL in browser B. Then retry it in A. Start two fresh flows in separate tabs of A and finish both normally.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** B receives `Sign-in not completed`, with no token exchange. A cannot replay that consumed flow. Both fresh tab flows succeed, each once. A normal same-browser return succeeds and clears only its flow cookie.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The callback lacks this browser check. The guard-removal negative control reproduces acceptance of a missing-cookie callback (200 instead of 400). A live provider or a full unpatched-daemon A/B run was not performed.

### How I tested

### Current integration after #12200 - 2026-11-02

Current head: a0b660c198c9a8aef8f00b3a2c2096af671ce127. Both original commits were true-rebased onto master 6ac37f60f142bca5e1e629f59e809a5cee6aaf3e, which includes merged #12200 and #11174. Both range-diff entries are unchanged; no manual conflict resolution or extra feature work was added. Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml and deny.toml match this master, including pulldown-cmark 0.13.6. The own scope remains 5 files.

The enrollment source, gateway manifest, locale loader and enrollment client are byte-identical to the previous head. The new master catalog keys are retained alongside the single enrollment error key, with no duplicate message keys. Focused rustfmt and whitespace checks pass. The callbacks, cookie parsing, consume-before-refusal and original-TTL capacity retry were traced again. Local Rust execution remains unavailable under Windows Application Control; the current-head upstream compilation and test results are recorded below. Earlier mock-provider/browser evidence remains historical and is not live-provider or combined dashboard evidence.

Two adversarial self-review passes and a final source review found no new supported defect. These are not independent Core approvals. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531182801/job/125581473661) passes on this exact head, including Security, Lint and Test. The [Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531182801/job/125571496498) records all 32 OIDC tests passing, including all four browser-binding regressions. Parallel Runtime Test also passes. No new private workflow or live-provider run was used.

### Earlier Fluent follow-up — 2026-11-02

Earlier head: `1bf288ffa29d00ac13a53bfe9304ee4d315e147a`. Both new enrollment-start errors now use `get_required_cli_string("cli-oidc-browser-start-failed")`. The canonical English catalog keeps the exact existing text, `could not start sign-in`. Other locales inherit that English fallback until translated. This uses the existing runtime locale; it does not add per-request language negotiation.

Local `rustfmt --check --edition 2024 crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_oidc.rs` and `git diff --check` pass. An exact inverse source comparison confirms that only the import, these two lookups and one English catalog entry changed. Status 500, the generic JSON error shape and early-return behavior remain. I traced the existing helper, catalog fallback and immediate JSON serialization; this was source validation, not a fresh gateway execution.

Historical CI on 1bf288ffa29d00ac13a53bfe9304ee4d315e147a failed Security on inherited pulldown-cmark 0.13.5 (RUSTSEC-2026-0433), with the aggregate gate also red. The merged #12200 repair is now inherited by the current head above. Historical results do not replace new-head checks.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Historical evidence: a bounded Ubuntu 24.04 job applied the exact patch to base `1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29`, checked all four source hashes, and ran Rust 1.98.0 tests, strict Clippy and the native browser fixture. Fresh upstream CI on the rebased head is recorded below. Independent Core/CODEOWNER security approvals remain required.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The native browser check uses production enrollment routes, prefix and security headers over loopback HTTP, with a mock IdP. It is not the complete daemon, native TLS, dashboard popup integration, or real-provider acceptance. HTTPS cookie attributes and rejection of an unprefixed cookie have router assertions.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0
git diff --check
exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib api_oidc::tests:: -- --nocapture
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.95s
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
exit 0

# Temporary guard removal; require the selected regression to fail:
enrollment_binding_refuses_other_browsers_before_exchange_and_consumes_the_flow ... FAILED
left: 200
right: 400
# Exact bytes restored; repeat the OIDC suite:
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.89s

# Native browser fixture, then exact restoration and final suite:
5 browser assertions passed; same browser, isolated context, consumed replay and concurrent tabs
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 6.96s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial source passes checked missing/wrong/duplicate cookies, consume-before-refusal, cookie-only API denial, concurrent flows, provider changes, issuer checks, original TTL and capacity retry. Source and dependency hashes were checked again. Both changed Markdown files passed pinned lint. No added documentation links need a new link target check.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshots of the existing success and refusal pages after the changed browser interaction; no layout redesign.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Historical source head `759ae4a5f1e4dffaa5d995503b222fc863e863d8`, exact four-file patch hash `945c228cff4dd8bf0a046630f7df1a22d3a14b34e6981eb64290d1e3fc9d55a9`; native Chrome `Chrome/156.0.8078.47`, Ubuntu 24.04, gateway `localhost`, mock IdP `127.0.0.1`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Same-browser success](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-same-context.png), [other-browser refusal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-other-context.png), and [machine receipt](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/receipt.json). All data is synthetic.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Follow the mock IdP page's link back to the prefixed callback: success with one exchange. Open a copied callback in another browser context: refusal with zero extra exchanges. Replay in the original context: refusal. Complete two fresh tab flows: both succeed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Windows Rust execution was blocked by Application Control, so this source was validated on Linux. No full workspace suite or live IdP run is claimed. The first Linux attempt passed the Rust checks but failed because the mock page had a plain-text MIME type. That fixture was corrected; the complete successful run above uses the corrected harness. No browser assertion was relaxed.

### Earlier rebase and dashboard integration — 2026-11-02

Earlier rebased head: `4ef9abef542eb90153587669f2650cefc1abcb1d`. This is a true rebase onto `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`, which includes #12129. All four enrollment files and the exact patch are byte-for-byte unchanged from the historical tested revision above; range-diff reports the same single commit. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125043937233) passes, including Security, Lint and Test. The [hosted Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125040616464) records all 32 OIDC tests passing, including all four new browser-binding regressions. Its checkout `0b80216b67e102089eebff5e2f6b7ff598a1e2bb` was verified to include this exact head. The earlier browser captures retain their named revision; no new native-TLS or real-provider acceptance run is claimed.

I also compared #11965 at `13486a064d2be1c05086e4ceaf6b08e94f2bc8b5`. At that historical snapshot, its delayed-start browser-family finding was open. It is now repaired at 02314854b32eb45a55d9d9c004f0bd73bb7b51e8, as recorded in [the repair review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11965#pullrequestreview-5731811340). That dashboard repair is separate from this per-flow enrollment binding. The branches overlap in `api_oidc.rs`; integration must keep one canonical binding in `PendingPkce`, checked before either exchange mode, with shared cookie parsing/cleanup and the original retry deadline. Preserve the dashboard's required ID token, provider pin, return/popup behavior and separate session-family/sign-out repair. Binding cleanup must coexist with the dashboard session cookie. This PR does not contain or validate that combined integration.

@IftekharUddin's [dependency and native-TLS proposal](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12157#issuecomment-6553383007) remains useful, separately attributed candidate evidence. The dependency repair is now inherited from master; no proposal commit was cherry-picked and no contributor source was replaced.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; the existing discovery and token endpoints remain the only provider calls.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A new per-flow secret is sent only in an HttpOnly binding cookie; its hash is stored with the pending flow and compared in constant time. Cookies use SameSite=Lax and root Path with no Domain; HTTPS adds Secure and the __Host- prefix. A terminal consumed-flow response clears its cookie. The recorded transport scope preserves the cookie attributes chosen at issuance. A valid 503 retry keeps its original expiry. Remote deployments should use HTTPS; plain HTTP does not isolate applications on different ports of the same host.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for callers that complete an enrollment callback without the starting browser's cookie; this is the intentional security correction.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps: Finish enrollment in the same browser that starts it and permit its cookie. If a callback was copied, the gateway restarted, or the cookie expired/was blocked, start a new login. Existing bearer clients and the device flow require no migration. The new field creates the browser-binding fact in the existing pending-flow store; it does not copy live policy.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the resulting squash commit through a reviewed PR, then restart the gateway. This restores the login-CSRF exposure, so use only as an incident response with an explicit exposure decision.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Device flow is the alternative if browser cookies cannot be used.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A fresh same-browser login reaches `Sign-in not completed`; investigate cookie blocking, scheme/host changes and callback provenance. Do not log cookie secrets or token-bearing callback URLs.

The refreshed head now passes its required upstream CI; earlier results remain attached to their named revisions. This remains open for independent Core/CODEOWNER security review, with Jordan for the manifest and Audacity for the gateway and documentation. I have not approved my own change. After adoption, #11965 should use one binding fact in `PendingPkce` for both modes while preserving its dashboard-specific return, popup and ID-token behavior.

prs.title: fix(tools): return MCP tool names in sorted order
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `McpRegistry::tool_names()` now returns its names sorted. Before, it returned `HashMap` keys, whose order is random for each registry instance.
  - The deferred-tools section of the system prompt and the eager MCP tool registration are both built in this order. A new registry, and in practice a new gateway connection, shuffled the `<available-deferred-tools>` list and the MCP tool specs. That changes the prompt early on, so prefix caching (llama.cpp, vLLM, hosted automatic caching) misses on almost every turn.
  - Sorting at the source fixes every caller at once: `DeferredMcpToolSet::from_registry`, eager registration in `tools/scoped.rs`, and `collect_mcp_elevation_arcs`.
- **Scope boundary:** this does not change which tools are listed or loaded, how activated tools are filtered out of the deferred section (#11703), the summary text, or how built-in tools are ordered.
- **Blast radius:** anything that iterates `McpRegistry::tool_names()`. All in-tree callers either render the names or look each one up, so none depend on the old order, which was random anyway. Sorting a few dozen strings per registry build costs effectively nothing.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12176. Related #11703.

### What this does, simply

With MCP deferred loading on, ZeroClaw lists the MCP tools the model can load in the system prompt. That list came out shuffled each time a session was set up, even when nothing had changed. Model servers cache the start of a prompt so they don't have to process it again, so a shuffled list near the top means the whole prompt is processed from scratch every turn. On a local model with a ~17k-token prompt, the first token took about 10 s instead of about 1 s. This PR lists the tools in alphabetical order, so the prompt is the same from one session to the next.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The new unit test covers the ordering at its source. A live A/B check needs a request-logging provider; the steps are in #12176 if wanted.

### How I tested

prs.title: fix(tools): reject send_message_to_peer to Discord external peers with an actionable error
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `send_message_to_peer` hands any known non-agent target (an entry from a
    peer group's `external_peers`) to announcement delivery. On Discord that
    delivery posts to `/channels/{recipient}/messages`, but Discord external
    peers are user IDs, so the send fails with Discord's opaque
    `404 Unknown Channel (10003)` and the agent cannot tell what to do instead.
  - The tool now rejects that case before delivery, using configuration only:
    the target has already been validated as a configured external peer (not an
    agent alias), and the channel ref's type is `discord` (same case-insensitive
    `<type>.<alias>` split that delivery uses). No ID-syntax guessing and no
    network calls; Discord user and channel IDs are both snowflakes.
  - The error explains why (user ID vs channel/thread ID, bots cannot DM bots,
    peer groups carry no channel mapping) and what to do: post in a channel or
    thread shared with the peer and mention the peer there.
- **Scope boundary:** No new config keys, no peer → channel/thread routing, no
  DM path. Peer-agent targets (in-process delivery) and external peers on other
  channel types are unchanged. `send_via` is not changed: it resolves its
  recipient from the first `external_peers` entry through `Channel::send` in
  `zeroclaw-tools`, a separate path whose recipient semantics belong to the
  routing design discussion in #10926.
- **Blast radius:** `send_message_to_peer` calls whose target is an external
  peer on a Discord channel. Those sends could not be delivered before; they
  now fail earlier with a clearer message.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10926 (identity vs. delivery-destination
  design; the Discord evidence for this failure is in
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10926#issuecomment-6511170110).
  This PR does not resolve it.

### What this does, simply

Agents can message configured peers with `send_message_to_peer`. For a human
or bot that is not a ZeroClaw agent, the tool sends through the channel's
normal delivery, which on Discord needs a channel or thread ID. Peer lists on
Discord hold user IDs, so the message went to a "channel" that does not exist
and Discord answered with a bare 404. This PR stops that send up front and
tells the agent to talk to the peer in a shared channel or thread instead. How
peers should be routed on Discord is left to the separate design discussion.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the change is a pre-delivery rejection
  covered by a unit test that exercises `SendMessageToPeerTool::execute`;
  reproducing the live 404 needs a Discord bot pair.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the runtime crate's
  lib tests, clippy and fmt cover the changed file.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live Discord round-trip in CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - RED on master 5a51398dd with only the new execute tests applied:
    `discord_external_peer_is_rejected_before_channel_delivery ... FAILED`
    (`a Discord user target must not report delivery`: master hands the user
    ID to announcement delivery; in the unit test no live Discord handler is
    registered, so it reports success where production gets the 404).
    `non_discord_external_peer_still_reaches_delivery ... ok`.
  - GREEN, `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --skip tunnel::tailscale`
    on default features and again with every `tool-*`/`tools-external`
    feature: all three new tests pass and every other `send_message_to_peer`
    test passes. 5846 and 5861 passed respectively, 0 failed, 8 ignored
    (run with `umask 077`; under a group-writable umask, three `rpc::local`
    endpoint-lock tests reject the temp dir, which is unrelated to this change).
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`,
    `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh <changed file>`: clean.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The original failure was seen
  on one deployment: a `send_message_to_peer` call targeting a second bot's
  Discord user ID returned `404 Unknown Channel (10003)`. The new error path
  was not exercised against live Discord.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `tunnel::tailscale` lib
  tests were skipped locally because they reconfigure the host's Tailscale
  Serve state.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No

- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No (the
  error echoes the target the model itself passed, already Debug-quoted)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (the rejected sends could not succeed before)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Prefer successful `getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION` or a glibc/GNU-libc `ldd --version` result before checking installed musl loaders. A glibc host can have musl installed for cross-compilation.
- **Scope boundary:** Installer libc detection and its existing target-test suite. The updater's separate target selection (#12156) is unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** x86_64/aarch64 Linux archive and feature-target selection. Existing musl/distro fallbacks, unknown-host GNU fallback, ARM32, macOS and Termux rules remain.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12153.

### What this does, simply

Installing musl alongside glibc should not change which ZeroClaw archive a glibc host receives. The installer now checks the system libc first. Alpine still selects musl.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, if a native Alpine or glibc-with-musl host is available.

prs.title: fix(memory): add per-agent attribution and scoping to the knowledge graph
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds mandatory agent ownership to the shared SQLite knowledge graph. `KnowledgeScope` is bound from trusted registration; writes keep caller ownership and directional `read_knowledge_from` grants widen reads only.
  - Makes legacy attribution explicit and fail-closed, with a sole-agent automatic path or configured `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` for ambiguous multi-agent upgrades.
  - Makes agent delete/rename recovery lifecycle-specific: delete probes exported memory while rename detects even an empty agent identity row; filesystem inspection errors retain residue; workspace/knowledge archives surface failures; cron and ACP rows are purged only after durable export.
  - Makes the fail-toward-residue rule uniform across surfaces. The gateway workspace mover and committed-rename probe no longer collapse a metadata error into absence, and the CLI deletion path archives through the shared helper instead of a hand-rolled copy that swallowed its errors.
  - Makes that fail-toward-residue rule platform-independent. A workspace whose parent is a file surfaces as an error on Unix and as an ordinary "not found" on Windows, so every surface now classifies a path through one shared `inspect_lifecycle_path` helper that re-walks the ancestors of a negative probe. An uninspectable workspace is residue on every supported platform, and the regressions assert that classification instead of the platform's error shape.
  - Gives every deletion archive an exclusively created leaf, so a duplicate delete inside the same clock second cannot adopt another attempt's directory, and writes the archive artifacts with `create_new` so a shared leaf could not replace a durable export even if one were reached.
  - Prevents shared inbound edges from suppressing the caller's own relation and requires a scope-visible anchor for every direct graph-neighbor query after grant revocation.
  - Validates lifecycle aliases before any recovery probe or filesystem path derivation, keeps unreadable RPC rename workspaces retryable, and serializes the global node cap across per-agent SQLite connections.
  - Boxes the RPC map-key delete future, which the master merge showed is needed to keep `process_line` inside the two-megabyte stack budget `master` now pins.
  - Resolves grants from live policy for each graph operation after acquiring the database connection. Purge verifies the archived snapshot in an immediate transaction, using durable edge generation identities to distinguish recreated relations.
  - Refuses to recreate an agent over a retired agent's knowledge on every config creation path. Explicit creation and property writes that would create the agent (`zeroclaw config set` and `config patch`, gateway PUT and PATCH, RPC `config/set` and `config/set-many`) share one admission rule: never the reserved `default` agent, and never an absent alias whose knowledge remains or whose store cannot be inspected without waiting. The refusal is a 400 `validation_failed` on HTTP (explicit creation previously reported it as 404) and a localized message on RPC and the CLI. The `model_routing_config` tool's `upsert_agent`, which inserts agents directly, runs the same retirement check against the store the runtime opens; an agent defined by environment overrides is live and is not probed. The probe re-walks the ancestors of a store reported as missing, so a store under a regular-file parent is refused on Windows as on Unix.
  - Merges current `master` (`5d4b18d335`) and ports the knowledge-ownership paths onto its atomic live-config publication: the live knowledge scope reads a `LiveConfigHandle`, and agent delete and its committed-delete retry admit a `ConfigCommit` and publish only when config changes.
- **Scope boundary:** Knowledge ownership is per agent alias, not per authenticated principal; different principals using the same agent share its knowledge. The unwired Postgres graph is unchanged. Knowledge tool schema/shape is unchanged, but row visibility is intentionally narrowed by `KnowledgeScope`. Gateway and RPC can retry committed rename residue; CLI cannot yet, and #10373 owns that shared recovery follow-up. Lifecycle requests now enforce the canonical alias grammar before touching recovery state. #10149 owns durable recovery for a failed custom workspace archive. Not changed here, and predating this PR: an environment override that names a new agent is applied at config load without the retirement check (documented as an operator caveat), and the `model_routing_config` tool's `remove_agent` removes an agent without the owned-state cascade.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-memory`, tools/runtime registration, config, gateway/RPC/CLI alias lifecycle, SQLite knowledge/session/memory stores, cron and ACP cleanup, workspaces, and documentation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #9647. Related #9646. Related #10149. Related #10373.

Agent aliases remain the canonical ownership key already used by configuration, workspaces, grants, and lifecycle operations. The storage API requires scope so foreign rows behave as absent even if a caller knows an ID. Disabled configured siblings remain valid explicit read sources; they do not become writers.

### What this does, simply

Agents previously shared the same knowledge graph. This change gives each row an owning agent and limits an agent to its own knowledge unless an operator grants read access to another agent's rows. Deletion archives owned knowledge before removing it, and rename moves its ownership. The latest repair makes revoked sharing take effect for retained tools and stops cleanup from purging rows that differ from its archive. If cleanup fails, creating that agent again through any config surface is refused until a retried delete removes the old knowledge, so a new agent with the same name never inherits it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` and `tui` through the registered `knowledge` tool and alias lifecycle RPC/CLI paths.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Enable knowledge and configure neutral agents `agent_a` and `agent_b`.
- **Steps to run:** Capture a unique node as `agent_b`; search, inspect statistics, traverse, and relate by ID as `agent_a`; then add `read_knowledge_from = ["agent_b"]`, restart, and repeat. Exercise rename/delete once with a temporarily unavailable configured memory/workspace path, restore it, and retry. For the archive path, issue the same `agents delete` twice inside one second and inspect `<data_dir>/agents/_deleted`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Foreign rows are absent before the grant; reads become visible after the directional grant while writes remain caller-owned. Failed lifecycle cleanup retains retryable residue. Creating the alias again, explicitly or through a property write such as `zeroclaw config set agents.<alias>.enabled true`, is refused while its knowledge remains or the store cannot be inspected, and is admitted once a retried delete converges. The duplicate delete lands in its own archive leaf and the first attempt's export is untouched.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Agents shared one unscoped graph, and several committed lifecycle failures could be mistaken for completed cleanup.

### How I tested

- **Earlier validation head:** `e248cfe531`. `959cb698a3` merges `master` at `5d4b18d335`, and `e248cfe531` is the alias-recreation fix. Results below are from macOS arm64 at that head unless noted. Hosted CI was still running on this head when this was written.

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
    -> clean
  cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
    -> clean
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --features channel-linq -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --all-targets --features gateway,agent-runtime -- -D warnings
    -> clean
  cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
    -> no warnings
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test-threads=1
    -> 5951 tests run: 5951 passed, 9 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features channel-linq
    -> 727 tests run: 727 passed, 7 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --test component
    -> 263 tests run: 263 passed
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --features gateway,agent-runtime
    -> 526 run: 525 passed; filesystem_adapter_drives_a_run_with_maintenance_disabled
       timed out under full-suite load and passes alone
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-memory
    -> 2531 run: 2530 passed; policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception
       fails identically on master on macOS (open PR #11646)
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-tools -E 'test(/model_routing_config|knowledge/)'
    -> 56 tests run: 56 passed
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
    -> no prose em-dashes; 0 errors
  ```

- **Not run as scripted here:** this machine's `rg` cannot load `libpcre2`, so `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` and the provider-dispatch step of `rust_quality_gate.sh` abort, and nine `content_search` tool tests fail for the same reason. The comment hygiene checker passed when given the same file set through `git ls-files`, and the fix adds no `ModelProvider` method calls. Hosted CI runs both gates.
- **Regression coverage for the blocker:** a failed knowledge purge followed by recreation is refused at each boundary: config unit (`auto_create_refuses_retained_knowledge_and_uninspectable_store`), gateway PUT, PATCH and explicit create (`property_writes_cannot_recreate_agent_with_retained_knowledge`), RPC `config/set` and `config/set-many` after a real committed delete with a blocked store, then admitted after the retried delete converges (`config_set_cannot_recreate_agent_until_retired_knowledge_converges`), the CLI binary (`config_patch_refuses_to_recreate_agent_with_retained_knowledge`), and the `model_routing_config` tool (`upsert_agent_refuses_alias_with_retained_knowledge`, `upsert_agent_admits_env_defined_agent_that_owns_knowledge`). Busy and uninspectable stores fail closed; the Windows-shaped not-found branch is driven directly (`missing_store_under_a_file_ancestor_is_uninspectable`).
- **Mutation checks:** restoring the old auto-create path (retirement check skipped, reserved check kept) makes the config, gateway, RPC, and CLI regression tests fail; probing the tool's env-free file config or skipping its probe fails the tool test; disabling the env-defined-agent check fails its test.
- **Known gap:** no Windows execution here; the gateway and RPC uninspectable fixtures rely on the new ancestor walk on Windows and are untested there until the advisory Windows job runs.

### Earlier validation (historical)

- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** for ambiguous multi-agent legacy knowledge; it remains hidden until assigned. Single-agent upgrades are automatic.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes**; adds `agents.<alias>.workspace.read_knowledge_from` and `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent`; alias lifecycle commands now cascade owned state and reject noncanonical/reserved aliases before recovery I/O. milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

The old warnings fire on normal release binaries and no longer identify a useful limit. The script now reports the size and enforces the caller's actual cap. A binary exactly at the cap still passes; one byte over still fails.

prs.title: fix(gateway): key rate limits on the proxy-appended XFF hop
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `forwarded_client_ip` now prefers the rightmost parseable non-loopback `X-Forwarded-For` entry instead of the leftmost client-supplied value. It decodes each hop separately so an opaque prefix cannot hide the proxy-appended suffix.
  - For a loopback-only forwarded value, `client_key_from_request` uses a non-loopback peer or the non-exempt `unknown` key, so remote clients cannot inherit a loopback peer's limiter exemption.
  - Docs note the nginx directives operators should use and the loopback-forwarded behavior.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not add a trusted-proxy CIDR list or change limiter thresholds; only how the client key is derived when `trust_forwarded_headers` is on.
- **Blast radius:** Pairing lockout, webhook auth limits, and OIDC enrollment per-client budgets that key through `client_key_from_request`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12052

### What this does, simply

When the gateway sits behind a reverse proxy with `trust_forwarded_headers`, it used the first address in `X-Forwarded-For`. Most proxies append the real client after any client-supplied value, so a remote caller could put `127.0.0.1` first and skip pairing lockouts and enrollment budgets. This PR takes the rightmost usable non-loopback address, and never treats a forwarded loopback value as the local exemption.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — covered by focused unit tests; no user-visible UI change.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** gateway HTTP auth path (pairing / rate-limit key derivation)
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Gateway unit tests for `client_key_from_request`
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Full pairing integration against a real appending proxy not run locally
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib client_key_
# running 4 tests
# client_key_defaults_to_peer_addr_when_untrusted_proxy_mode ... ok
# client_key_uses_forwarded_ip_only_in_trusted_proxy_mode ... ok
# client_key_ignores_spoofed_loopback_forwarded_header ... ok
# client_key_falls_back_to_peer_when_forwarded_header_invalid ... ok
# test result: ok. 4 passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source review of callers of `client_key_from_request`; did not spin a live nginx proxy.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible interface state changed
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `aa19064ac` / gateway unit tests
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** see command output above
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test` skipped; focused lib filter covers the changed helpers

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A — this hardens rate-limit keying against client-controlled forwarded headers.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes` for correctly configured single-hop appending proxies; deployments that relied on leftmost XFF with multi-hop lists will now key on the rightmost hop)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Prefer `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;` or set `X-Real-IP $remote_addr;` while clearing `X-Forwarded-For`, as shown in the updated proxy guidance.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)
